issues.title: [BUG] Windows: a file edited through \wsl.localhost is re-read on every turn, which restarts a stopped WSL distro

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

labels.name: platform:wsl
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on WSL

issues.body:
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Reproduced_with_Procmon-1f883d?style=flat-square&logo=windows)](.) [![Claude Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-2.1.309-0969da?style=flat-square&logo=anthropic)](.) [![Host](https://img.shields.io/badge/Host-Windows_10_22H2_+_WSL2-8250df?style=flat-square&logo=linux)](.) [![Workaround](https://img.shields.io/badge/Workaround-transcript_edit-ff69b4?style=flat-square&logo=github)](.)
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet - [x] This is a single bug report (please file separate reports for different bugs) - [x] I am using the latest version of Claude Code ### What's Wrong? Claude Code runs on the Windows side. Earlier in the session it edited one file inside a WSL distro through its UNC path, `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\\win7-lab\compose.yaml`. From then on, after `wsl --shutdown`, the WSL VM (`vmmem`) comes back as soon as Claude answers a prompt, every single time. #### 🔬 What Process Monitor shows With a Procmon filter `Path contains wsl.localhost`, the only process touching the share is `claude.exe`, once per turn, always on that one file: | Time | Operation | Detail | |---|---|---| | 03:36:42.386 | CreateFile | Read Attributes | | 03:36:42.387 | QueryAllInformationFile | LastWriteTime 22/10/2026 23:55:31, EndOfFile 445 | | 03:36:42.388 | CloseFile | | | 03:36:42.401 | CreateFile | Generic Read | | 03:36:42.404 | ReadFile | Offset 0, Length 445 | | 03:36:42.406 | ReadFile | END OF FILE | | 03:36:42.407 | CloseFile | | The same seven operations repeat at 03:37:52 and 03:39:17, one burst per reply. The file's `LastWriteTime` never moved (23:55:31 the day before), yet it is read in full each time. Accessing `\\wsl.localhost` starts the distro, so every reply ships with a free virtual machine (0.8 to 1 GB of `vmmem` here). #### 🧭 Which files, and where the list comes from | Observation | Result | |---|---| | Files only **read** through `\\wsl.localhost` in the same session (two logs, a PNG) | never touched again | | The one file **edited** through `\\wsl.localhost` | metadata + full read on every turn | | After `/compact` | still read every turn | | After quitting and `--resume` (new process) | still read every turn | | After `--resume --fork-session` (new, slim transcript) | still read every turn | | Transcript of the fork | 30 `file-history-snapshot` / `file-history-delta` lines carry the UNC path | So the tracked list is rebuilt from the `file-history-*` entries of the transcript, and it survives compaction, restart and fork. `/compact` forgets a great deal; this, it remembers. ### What Should Happen? Starting a stopped WSL distro should not be a side effect of answering a prompt. Without claiming to know the internals, any of these would avoid it: - skip the content re-read when `LastWriteTime` and size are unchanged, since the metadata call alone already shows nothing moved; - treat `\\wsl.localhost\…` and `\\wsl$\…` paths as not worth a per-turn check, or check them only when the distro is already running. The same goes for remote paths in general: the volume answers `Characteristics: Remote`; - let `/compact`, or a command, drop files from the tracked list. ### Error Messages/Logs ```shell 03:36:42,3862446 claude.exe CreateFile \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\\win7-lab\compose.yaml SUCCESS Desired Access: Read Attributes, Synchronize 03:36:42,3874138 claude.exe QueryAllInformationFile ...\compose.yaml BUFFER OVERFLOW LastWriteTime: 22/10/2026 23:55:31, EndOfFile: 445 03:36:42,3878516 claude.exe CloseFile ...\compose.yaml SUCCESS 03:36:42,4014373 claude.exe CreateFile ...\compose.yaml SUCCESS Desired Access: Generic Read 03:36:42,4037504 claude.exe ReadFile ...\compose.yaml SUCCESS Offset: 0, Length: 445 03:36:42,4059123 claude.exe ReadFile ...\compose.yaml END OF FILE Offset: 445 03:36:42,4067269 claude.exe CloseFile ...\compose.yaml SUCCESS (same sequence at 03:37:52 and 03:39:17) ``` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. On Windows with a WSL 2 distro, run Claude Code on the Windows side (not inside WSL). 2. Ask Claude to edit any file in the distro through its UNC path, e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\\test.txt` (Edit tool). 3. Run `wsl --shutdown` and wait until `vmmem` disappears from Task Manager. 4. Send any prompt, even one that triggers no tool. 5. `vmmem` is back. Procmon with `Path contains wsl.localhost` shows `claude.exe` opening and reading the edited file. Repeating steps 3 and 4 reproduces it on every turn. ### Claude Model Opus 5.5 ### Is this a regression? I don't know ### Last Working Version _No response_ ### Claude Code Version 2.1.309 (Claude Code) ### Platform Anthropic API ### Operating System Windows ### Terminal/Shell Windows Terminal ### Additional Information #### 🧪 Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Host | Windows 10 Home 22H2, build 19045.7807 | | WSL | 3.0.4.18 (a build of microsoft/WSL#41914), kernel 6.18.54.1-1, distro Ubuntu-22.04 | | `.wslconfig` | `networkingMode=virtioproxy`, `autoMemoryReclaim=gradual` | | `WSLService` | set to Manual, and the distro still comes back. Only Disabled stops it, which also disables WSL | #### 🛠️ Workaround that worked With Claude Code closed, I rewrote, in the session transcript only, the two strings of the `file-history-snapshot` / `file-history-delta` lines that pointed into WSL: the tracked path (`\\wsl.localhost\…\compose.yaml` → `/home//win7-lab/compose.yaml`) and its `realParentDir`. 32 lines, 64 replacements, every line still valid JSON, a backup kept beside it. After `--resume`, `wsl --shutdown` and a new prompt, `vmmem` stayed gone. Nobody should need this, and a `/rewind` to that edit would now aim at a path that does not exist on Windows. #### 🔗 Same mechanism elsewhere farion1231/cc-switch#6975 describes the same symptom in another tool: periodic access to a `\\wsl.localhost` config path keeps relaunching the distro after shutdown. 🦎

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro

labels.name: platform:macos

issues.body:
## What happens

In the Desktop app's Code tab, while I am typing in a session's composer (or reading it), the app leaves that session and shows the new-session screen by itself. I end up typing into the new-session composer ("another textbox") instead of the session I was in. No click, key press or shortcut from me causes it. It happens many times an hour.

## Environment

- Claude Desktop 3.6556.1, Code tab (local sessions)
- Bundled Claude Code 2.1.308 (2.1.299 also installed; the 23:29 events below ran on 2.1.299)
- macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), Apple M3 Pro
- Heavy use: about 20 local sessions in the sidebar, many in git worktrees; the CLI governor sits at its cap (`[CliGovernor] at cap=6` logged 55 times since 21:41 yesterday); several MCP servers per session; the sidebar polls PR checks every few seconds.
- macOS "Swipe between pages" is off (`AppleEnableSwipeNavigateWithScrolls = 0`).

## Evidence: input timing vs. main.log

To rule out my own input, I ran a small logger that records only the time and kind of each input event (key, modifier, click, scroll, trackpad gesture), using `CGEventSource.counterForEventType(.combinedSessionState, …)` polled every 40 ms. I compared it with `~/Library/Logs/Claude/main.log` (times GMT+8, 2026-10-23).

Since the logger started at 09:13, every move between two sessions came less than 1 s after a click, so those were mine. But 4 times the app left the focused session for a non-session screen with no click and no key press in the 1.5 s before:

| Time | Click/key in prior 1.5 s | Scroll in progress |
|---|---|---|
| 09:15:26 | none | no |
| 09:29:29 | none | no |
| 09:38:01 | none | no |
| 09:48:06 | none (I had typed up to 09:47:55, not sent) | yes, a trackpad scroll began within ~50 ms |

The same thing happened at 08:56:25, before the logger was running.

Every event has the same signature in main.log, with nothing app-related logged in the seconds before:

```
09:48:06 [info] [CCD] LocalSessions.setFocusedSession: sessionId=null
09:48:06 [info] [CCD] LocalSessions.setFocusedSession: sessionId=null
09:48:06 [info] [WarmLifecycle:preview] Starting idle timeout for local_<the session I was in>: 1800s
09:48:07 [info] [CCD] temporary query on required_version:2.1.308:…: 1 plugin(s) go to Claude Code over stdin (initialize request, --await-initialize)
09:48:07 [info] Config file written
09:48:09 [info] [CCD-SessionRecovery] Scanning for recoverable CLI transcripts (…)
```

At 08:56:25 the same lines also included `LocalSessions.checkTrust: cwd=<my repo root>`, which is what the new-session composer runs for its default folder. A normal click to another session looks different: `setFocusedSession: sessionId=null` immediately followed by `setFocusedSession: sessionId=local_<target>` in the same second.

A related flicker last night: four times between 23:29 and 23:33 the view jumped from the session I was in to an old stopped session and back within 1 s (`setFocusedSession` → other session, then back), each a few seconds after I sent a message. Each time `temporary query … (command menu query)` ran for the session it flicked to.

## What I ruled out

- Another session navigating the window: no session called `open_session_in`, `show_pane`, `start_session`, `hand_off_to_session`, `unarchive_session` or `clear_session` at those times (checked every tool call in 146 session transcripts). Cross-session `send_message` calls do not move focus.
- New sessions taking focus: since 21:41 yesterday all 5 sessions that took focus on creation were ones I started, and I had not moved elsewhere first.
- Account switching / app relaunch: no quit or relaunch at those times.
- Keyboard shortcuts or swipe navigation: no key or click in the 1.5 s before; 3 of 4 events had no input at all.
- `Failed to toggle remote control … "Remote Control initialization failed"` is logged on nearly every send, with or without a jump, so it does not look like the trigger.

## Expected

The app never changes the focused session, or opens the new-session screen, unless I ask it to. At the very least, never while the composer has focus or holds an unsent draft. (#103105 shows the app already refuses `open_session_in` while the caret is in a text field; whatever causes this skips that guard.)

## Related

#102169, #95295, #91993 (new-session view and focus bugs), #97917 (draft lost when the session changes), #102066 (focus stealing).

Happy to run a debug build or turn on more renderer logging. The renderer logs in `~/Library/Logs/Claude` (main-window.log, claude.ai-web.log) are empty, so the reason for the navigation isn't visible from here.

issues.title: [Desktop] Allow start_session from automated/session-triggered turns when the user pre-authorizes it

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## What I wanted to do

In Claude Desktop (Code tab), a coordinator session runs unattended overnight and starts worker sessions with `start_session` as each stage finishes. The user explicitly authorized this before leaving.

## What happened

`start_session` with `initiation: "user_asked"` is refused on any turn that was triggered by another session's message, a background-task notification, or a scheduled (cron) wakeup:

> Start sessions only on the user's own words to you here; this turn runs an automated event, another session's message, or the task another session gave you.

So a coordinator cannot start the next worker when a previous worker reports back, and a worker cannot start its own successor when its context gets large. The only workaround is to pre-create every session (including spares) in a turn where the user is present, and have them idle until a `SendMessage` "start" signal. That wastes sessions and requires guessing the count in advance.

## Request

Let the user grant a durable, scoped authorization (e.g. per session family, with a time limit or a maximum count) so that `start_session` can run from automated / session-triggered turns, for example:

- a setting or a one-time card: "allow this session and the sessions it starts to start up to N more sessions until <time>"
- or allow a session to start a successor of itself (same brief, fresh context) without a user turn

This keeps the safety default while enabling unattended multi-session work.

issues.title: [BUG] Desktop sessions get nothing back from cloud sessions they start: no completion note, no reply channel

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

issues.body:
### Summary

A Claude Code Desktop (Code tab) session can start cloud sessions as workers, but it has no supported way to hear back from them. Local side sessions send the parent a note when they finish a turn. Cloud sessions send nothing, and the parent's own tool text says *"a cloud session cannot message other sessions back yet -- do not ask it to reply"*. So the parent can hand work to the cloud, but it cannot receive a result, answer a question, or learn that the work is done.

The parent needs two-way communication with the cloud sessions it starts, on the same terms it already has with local side sessions.

### Use case: fanning a batch of work out to cloud builders

We run a local "manager" session that takes a numbered batch of backlog items and starts one worker per item. With our `/batch cloud NN` command, each worker is a cloud session started with `start_session` and `target: "cloud"`:

1. The manager verifies the batch locally (it needs local-only state: a workbook, claim locks, a private repo).
2. It starts N cloud sessions in one turn, one brief each. Each builds, runs checks and a code review, pushes a branch, and opens its own PR.
3. Then the manager should collect results: which items landed, which PR each opened, which hit a blocker, and what question a worker could not answer from its brief.

Step 3 does not work today. The manager:

- **gets no completion note** when a cloud worker ends a turn (a local side session does send one);
- **cannot receive a question.** A worker that finds an ambiguity cannot ask the parent, so our briefs have to say "nobody can answer you mid-run: write the question in your PR body and stop". Then the manager must find the PR to learn there was a question;
- **cannot get a report.** It has to poll GitHub by branch name or label to learn whether each worker finished, and it learns nothing about a worker that failed before pushing;
- **cannot send a follow-up the worker will act on.** `SendMessage` to a cloud session is one-way and reports nothing back, so the parent cannot tell whether its correction arrived.

With local side sessions the same flow works end to end: the parent gets the worker's report as a note and can reply. Moving the workers to the cloud (for parallelism and to keep the user's machine free) loses the whole return path.

### Expected

For a cloud session started by a Desktop session (at least `start_session` with `target: "cloud"`), the parent should have the same channel it has with a local side session:

1. **Completion notes.** When the cloud session ends a turn, the parent gets a note quoting its latest report, as for a local side session.
2. **Cloud to parent messages.** The cloud session can message the session that started it. A blocking question, a progress report, or a final result arrives in the parent as a cross-session message.
3. **Parent to cloud messages with delivery state.** `SendMessage` to a cloud session reports whether it was delivered or held, and the tool text no longer tells the model not to ask for a reply.
4. The existing safety rules still apply: per-session permission modes, held messages needing the user's approval, and no permission laundering through the channel.

### Current behaviour

- The Desktop system prompt says a cloud session "receives your message but cannot message any session back yet", and that a cloud session "sends none" of the turn-end notes that local sessions send.
- The `SendMessage` result to a cloud session says the route is one-way and "do not ask it to reply here".
- #98897 reports that a cloud session can sometimes reply through the Remote Control `send_message` tool. That route depends on the parent having Remote Control on, is undocumented, and contradicts the tool text, so a parent cannot rely on it to run a batch.

### Related

- #98897 -- the `SendMessage` one-way wording, and an informal reply path.
- #103124 -- the reverse topology (a cloud session managing Remote Control CLI workers), which needs the same two-way channel and completion events.

### Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.301 in the Claude desktop app (Code tab), Windows 11
- Parent: local Desktop session. Workers: cloud sessions started with `start_session`, `target: "cloud"`, same account.

issues.title: [BUG] User-tier prompt.attachment hooks no longer run since 2.1.299 when sec-default seats itself by default

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

issues.body:
### What's Wrong?

Since 2.1.299, a user-installed mod's `prompt.attachment` hooks never run when `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin` is seated. They ran on 2.1.296. The mod is admitted and its other hooks (`tool.describe`, `command.run`, `ui.render`) still run.

My mod (context-lean) uses `prompt.attachment` to hide deferred connector tool names (`deferred_tools_delta`) and move the agent listing (`agent_listing_delta`). On 2.1.296, deferring the connector tool names alone saved about 17k tokens per request in one session. On 2.1.301 the full lists go to the model on every request.

The user can't turn this off. `"cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin": false` in user `enabledPlugins` is ignored. My org sets no `prependPlugins` (its managed settings hold only attribution and one env variable), so sec-default seats itself by default, and the only way out is an org-wide `prependPlugins` change that drops every other protection.

The 2.1.299 changelog doesn't mention `prompt.attachment`.

### What Should Happen?

As on 2.1.296: a user-tier `prompt.attachment` hook runs for attachments that carry no managed or organization content, such as the deferred tool list and the agent listing. If skipping it is intended, there should be a user or admin setting that allows it, and the changelog and docs should say so.

### Error Messages/Logs

```
cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin seated outermost: this machine has managed settings
plugin.register: context-lean (user, context-lean@local-mods), judged by cc-plugin-sec-default: admitted
context-lean: prompt.attachment bypassed by cc-plugin-sec-default (tier user); beneath runs
```

The last line appeared 14 times in one turn on 2.1.301 and never in 2.1.296 debug logs on the same machine.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a Team or Enterprise account, or any machine with managed settings and no managed `prependPlugins`.
2. Install a user-tier mod with a hook such as `on('prompt.attachment', { type: 'deferred_tools_delta' }, ...)`.
3. Optionally set `"cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin": false` in user `enabledPlugins`.
4. Run `claude -p 'Reply with: pong' --debug-file run.log`.
5. On 2.1.301, `run.log` shows `prompt.attachment bypassed by cc-plugin-sec-default (tier user)` and the hook never runs. On 2.1.296 the hook runs.

### Claude Model

Opus

### Is this a regression?

Yes, this worked in a previous version

### Last Working Version

2.1.296

### Claude Code Version

2.1.301 (Claude Code)

### Platform

Anthropic API

### Operating System

macOS

### Terminal/Shell

Other

### Additional Information

- Terminal: tmux on macOS 27.0.1. Reproduced in a headless `-p` run.
- The sec-default README lists `prompt.attachment` as continuing past the user tier: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/94506ff0d3bd9185f1752da36e968775021fb48f/mods/sec-default/README.md
- Related: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102134 (`session.compact`, same version) and https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102470 (`tool.check`, same version).

prs.title: mods: the declarations carry process.run's truncation flags and list entries' mtimeMs; the test fakes answer them
prs.body:
Arm when the released npm CLI carries both fields (`isStdoutTruncated` / `isStderrTruncated` on a `$.process.run` result, `mtimeMs` on a `$.fs.list` entry): until then these declarations would promise what the installed CLI does not answer yet.

The engine's `$.process.run` result now says, per stream, whether its output was cut at the limit (`isStdoutTruncated`, `isStderrTruncated`), and its declaration states that limit as a number: 4194304 bytes each. A `$.fs.list` entry now carries `mtimeMs`: a regular file's own, as `$.fs.stat` spells it, and 0 for a directory, a link or any other kind, as `size` is.

The declarations in `mods/types` follow (the `ProcessRunResult` and `FsEntry` types, and the `run` and `list` docs), and every test fake that builds one of those values answers the new fields: the scripted git results and `gitIn` in `mods/diff/tests`, the telemetry probe and listing fixtures, the README's example test, and the recording backend host, whose runner hands on the mod's own narrower run result and so fills the two flags in. No mod reads the new fields yet; the diff mod's own output-cap arithmetic can move to `isStdoutTruncated` in a later change.

Checked:

- `tsc -p mods/tsconfig.json` passes at this branch's head. It checks against the declarations in this folder, so the change is consistent on its own; without the fixture edits it fails once in each of the ten fixture files.
- The added fields are inert under a CLI that does not know them, so `claude plugin test mods/diff` and `claude plugin test mods/telemetry` are unchanged by them.

prs.body:
**Merge order: after the engine has `session.append` on main AND no live engine release branch lacks it (the engine's build links this mod; the name does not scan on an engine without the event).**

**The `test` check is red by construction until a released CLI carries the event, not by accident.** This repository's CI installs the released CLI from npm and runs each mod's suite with it; on a CLI without `session.append` the scan refuses this mod's hooks module (`"session.append" is not an event`), so sec-default's suite fails there while agents-md, diff and telemetry pass. It turns green on its own with the first release that carries the event, and this merges only after that release is the one CI installs, so that `main`'s CI never goes red for the pull requests that follow.

sec-default: `session.append`, the event raised once for each row a conversation keeps (a prompt, a tool result, a settings hook's context, a reminder) whose hooks may rewrite what is stored and sent from then on, joins the rows that continue past the user tier (`next.to(e, "append")`), beside `prompt.section` and `prompt.context`. Where an organization seats sec-default, the rows are kept as the organization's tiers and the built-ins left them; everywhere else a person's plugin hooks the event like any other.

- `mods/sec-default/hooks/register.ts`: one line, the mirror of the `prompt.section` one.
- `mods/sec-default/tests/register.test.ts`: one case beside the `prompt.section` one. A plugin the person installed rewords a settings hook's context row; it is passed over, and the organization's append-tier plugin and what is beneath it stand.
- `mods/sec-default/README.md`: a row for the event, the list of hooked events names it, and the rows that pass say `session.*` other than `session.append`.
- `mods/types/claude-code.d.ts`: the declarations carry `session.append` (its input, message, door, origin and result types, the content block type they use, and `$.session.append` on the test kit's engine).

Checked:

- `tsc -p mods/tsconfig.json` is clean against the declarations in this branch.
- The new case has not been run yet: no CLI that carries the event was at hand here. It is written as the mirror of the `prompt.section` case and is to be run, with and without the new line, on the first build that carries the event before this merges.
- On a CLI without the event this mod does not load at all: the scan of a hooks module refuses a name under an engine noun that is not one of the engine's events, and the name has to be a string literal. That is the reason for the merge order above; nothing fires early and nothing can be feature-tested from inside the module.

prs.title: sec-default: collector records continue past the user tier
prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: where an organization seats sec-default, a person's plugin can no longer drop or rewrite records sent to its collector.

`telemetry.log` for the collector's stream now continues past the user tier, as `classic.*` and `settings.read` do. The organization's own `prepend` and `append` plugins still may hook it.

## Notes

The row is one line in `hooks/register.ts`: `on('telemetry.log', { to: 'collector' }, ($, e, next) => next.to(e, 'append'))`. The matcher is the literal stream, so the `anthropic` stream is not touched.

Inert in a CLI whose own event records do not travel this event: there the row meets only what a plugin logs through `$.telemetry.log`. It takes effect with the release that routes the CLI's own collector records through `telemetry.log`, and merges after that release.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `mods/sec-default/tests/register.test.ts`: the new case "a collector record passes over the plugins the person installed" loads a user-tier plugin that denies one record and marks every other one `edited`, logs two records, and expects both to arrive as logged; with the row taken out, that case is the one that fails
- [ ] the mod's tests pass 14 of 14 at this branch's head
- [ ] README: the row in the table, and the event in "What it hooks"

prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: other plugins' toasts show while the /diff pane or dialog is open, where they were held until it closed

## Notes

`/diff` opened its pane and its dialog with `holdToasts: true`. That option holds every transient toast while the pane is the one shown: each other plugin's `$.ui.toast` and the app's own, not only this plugin's. A plugin that toasts on a timer showed nothing for as long as `/diff` was open, and its toasts came out in a burst on close.

- The option goes from both opens. Nothing else in the mod changes, and nothing in it relied on the hold.
- Why it is safe to drop: docked, the notification row is drawn inside the transcript's column and the toast stack sits beside the dock; without the fullscreen layout a toast is one line in the footer. Neither lands between the pane and the prompt.
- One visible effect: a very long toast wraps the footer by one row while the dialog is up, as it does with no pane open. The dialog's own rows do not move.
- The README's sentence on toasts says what now happens.

## Test Plan

- [x] `claude plugin test mods/diff` passes: 210 pass, 0 fail
- [x] A second plugin toasts every 1.5 s, at 80 and 120 columns, in both renderers, with `/diff` open for 7 s: toasts show throughout, docked and in the dialog
- [x] The same before this change: no toast shows while `/diff` is open, and the held ones burst out on close
- [x] Docked: no toast is drawn in any row of the dock
- [x] The dialog's border and footer rows stay where they are under short toasts; a long toast grows the footer by one row

> Revert-proof: 3 tests fail with the mod's hooks reverted (the mod's own suite, with the new expectations, run against the unchanged hooks)

Fixed other plugins' toasts staying hidden while the `/diff` pane was open

prs.title: sec-default: a person's plugin may tighten, never loosen, what holds over it
prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: Where sec-default is seated, a person's plugin no longer lifts a deny or an ask rule, nor changes a pinned variable.

Needs no new engine: it reads nothing the published one does not carry.

## Notes

| What | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `tool.check`, any deny | the verdict reached past the user tier is returned when it is a deny, whatever decided it. Before: only a deny naming a settings rule. A deny that names nothing can stand in front of a rule's ask: lifted, the call would run with nobody asked |
| `tool.check`, an ask rule | an ask that names the settings rule behind it holds over an allow. The mode's own ask is still theirs to allow: that is what such a plugin is for |
| `ui.log` (new) | a line a plugin in `prepend` or `append` logs, this one's included, continues past the user tier. A user hook that heard this plugin's own notice ran inside its `tool.check` hook, and the engine leaves a hook out of whatever is raised from inside it: the notice was a way round the hold, deny rules included |
| `env.set` (new) | a variable managed settings set in `env` (its name in any case) is pinned: a user-tier caller is refused by name, setting or unsetting; any other caller continues past the user tier. With no policy to read every variable counts as pinned. Its `.catch` fails closed |
| The notice | once for each plugin and kind: a deny rule, an ask rule, a refusal |
| The option | `allowModsToOverrideDenyRules` covers all that holds on `tool.check`. It does not unpin `env` |
| Cost | every `$.ui.log` and `$.env.set` of any plugin now runs a chain where this plugin is seated; an `env.set` waits on the policy read |
| Not reached | an ask that names no rule is not held: the mode's own, a settings hook's, a check of the engine's own, an organization's plugin's. A held ask is still an ask: a classic `PermissionRequest` hook of the person's answers it (`allowManagedHooksOnly` is the control). A command hook decides only if its command runs: a variable its spawn depends on (`PATH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX`) that managed `env` does not set is a person's to change. The README says each |
| Typings | none change |

## Test Plan

- `claude plugin test mods/sec-default` on the published 2.1.288: 86 pass (57 before).
- The same suite on the unpatched hooks, 2.1.288: 28 of 86 fail, among them the ask rule, the unnamed deny, the notice as a way round, the dropped notice, one notice a kind, and each `env.set` case.
- 33 planted bugs on 2.1.288: 32 red. The one green is `env.set`'s `.catch`: only a hook that overruns its budget reaches it, and the kit cannot shorten a budget.
- `tsc -p mods/tsconfig.json`: clean. `claude plugin validate`: passes.

prs.title: diff: a pane nothing can draw yet is kept, and shows once something can
prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: /diff opened before anything can draw its pane keeps the pane, and it shows as soon as something can.

Stacked on #99118: its one commit shows here until that merges.

## Notes

Where nothing is attached that draws a pane yet (a host whose page has not attached), the engine answers an open `isPlaced: false` with a reason that starts `no-surface`. The mod read every unplaced open as one left waiting for width and withdrew it, so the pane was lost: it never showed once the page attached.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| An open answered `no-surface` | kept; `/diff` answers "Nothing here can draw the diff panel yet; it opens as soon as something can" |
| While no one sees it | nothing polls and nothing refreshes; an edit reads nothing |
| Its first drawing | reads the repository again, and counts the pane shown with the trigger it was opened by |
| An open left waiting for width | withdrawn, as before |
| An engine that resolves nothing, or never gives that reason | reads as before: placed, or withdrawn |

## Test Plan

- [x] `claude plugin test mods/diff` passes: 215 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `/diff` typed where nothing draws yet: the pane is kept, HEAD is read once and not polled, nothing is counted shown; the first drawing has what the open read, reads again, and counts it
- [x] An edit while the pane waits unseen runs no git
- [x] `/diff` again closes it, as an open pane
- [x] In a terminal the pane is placed as before, with no new line

> Revert-proof: 2 new tests fail with the mod's hooks reverted (the mod's own suite, run against the unchanged hooks)

## Changelog

<!-- CHANGELOG:START -->
Fixed the `/diff` pane being lost when `/diff` ran before the page that draws it had attached
<!-- CHANGELOG:END -->

prs.title: sec-default: an organization's ceiling on a tool holds over the plugins a person installs
prs.body:
## Summary

> TLDR: The policy mod holds an organization's ceiling on a tool, and every hook of it that decides carries a `.catch`.

An organization can require approval for a connector's tool. Seated, the policy mod now holds that ceiling over the plugins a person installs, as it holds a deny rule.

## Notes

| Hook | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| `tool.check` | When the chain's answer is more permissive than the question's `ceiling`, the dispatch is run once more past the user tier, and a stricter verdict there is the answer. The person is told once for each plugin. No option lifts it. |
| `ui.log` | A line from a caller in `prepend` or `append`, this mod's own included, continues past the user tier. What a person's plugins, the built-ins and the engine log is theirs to hook as before. |
| `classic.*`, `settings.read`, `tool.describe`, `command.describe`, `agent.offer`, `agent.spawn`, `tool.register`, `tool.list` | Each carries a `.catch` that decides as its hook does. None depends on a call on `$` succeeding: a policy read that rejects or throws counts as a policy in force. |
| `plugin.register`, `tool.check` | Their `.catch` handlers are named functions with tests of their own; a line that cannot be logged changes no answer. |

`mods/types/claude-code.d.ts` names `ceiling` on `tool.check`'s input and result. The engine sets it from the tool and pins it; a hook's own is dropped.

The five hooks that only pass prompt content and attribution text over the user tier carry no `.catch`, and the README says so.

## Test Plan

- [x] `claude plugin test mods/sec-default`: 107 pass, 0 fail (57 before)
- [x] each new `.catch` deleted alone, and each replaced by `next(e)` alone: at least one case fails every time
- [x] the other mods in this tree pass as before, and the mods typecheck
- [x] `claude plugin validate mods/sec-default` lists the gating hooks with their `.catch`

releases.name: v2.1.309
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
- Fixed macOS sandbox `denyWrite` glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
- Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with `--mcp-config`
- Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions
- Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open
- Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the `cd` is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain `cd`
- Fixed an `Edit(path)` deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell
- Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
- Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
- Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
- Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
- Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
- Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
- Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from `!` mode
- Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
- Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that `jq` could not parse
- Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's `/proc`
- Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed
- Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization
- Fixed the `claude remote-control` status line showing `HEAD` as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository
- Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and `--tools` rules given on the leader's command line
- Fixed sessions renamed with `/rename` appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive `--resume`
- Fixed the `/rewind` list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through `/code-review --fix`, a subagent or a shell command
- Fixed `/privacy-settings` showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched
- Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug
- Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript
- Fixed a skill in an `--add-dir` folder being unreachable when another skill already held its name; it is now offered as `<folder>:<name>`
- Fixed `/verify` and `/code-review` not finding a nested package's own skill when its files were changed from the shell
- Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that `ant beta:worker poll --on-work` passes trace context to the command
- Fixed the /claude-api skill's C# tracing setup missing spans from the cloud platform clients
- Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that API spans for requests to Claude Platform on AWS can't join the caller's trace
- Fixed hooks that run in PowerShell not blocking when the hook's program exits with code 2, and on Windows `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest` hooks with `"shell": "powershell"` failing open when Git for Windows isn't installed
- Fixed a mod's `turn.step` hook that names a model by alias, such as `haiku`, failing every request with a model error: the alias now resolves to its model
- Fixed plugins and skills synced from claude.ai being removed, sometimes mid-session, after a disk read error
- Fixed artifact publishes and updates being refused for some ordinary pages, such as pages with certain minified scripts or artifacts Claude could not read first
- Fixed Claude asking for permission on each artifact update for the rest of a turn after the conversation was compacted in that turn
- Fixed fine-grained tool streaming staying off on Amazon Bedrock when `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL` is set to the default `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com` endpoint
- Fixed the "Waiting for API response" hint flickering behind gateways that send only keepalive pings: routes off Anthropic's backend now wait 45 seconds
- Fixed Claude notifying unrelated GitHub users by writing role names and placeholders as mentions in PRs, issues and comments
- Linux: Fixed sandbox write denies lifting when a background command outlived the session
- Windows: Fixed PowerShell permission checks auto-approving some `Set-Location` or `cd` commands that target the current directory and carry extra arguments; these now prompt for approval
- macOS: Fixed the "Install Command Line Developer Tools" dialog opening each time Claude Code starts on a Mac without Xcode or the Command Line Tools
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed `--startup-timeout-min` stopping a session whose first prompt, such as `/code-review`, was still working in a subagent; a frozen process is still stopped
- Improved the speed of many git commands Claude Code runs for itself on Windows; on every platform, errors from those commands now show in English even when git is set to another language
- Improved the error when a hooks module is nested too deep to load: it now names the file instead of showing a bare stack-overflow message
- Improved disk-full handling: a Bash command cut off by a full disk now says so and names the folder to free up, and starting on a full temp volume prints a clear message, not a raw ENOSPC error
- Improved the /claude-api skill to offer API tracing alongside SDK tracing when asked to add OpenTelemetry
- Improved the /claude-api skill to check the live docs before saying a feature is unsupported
- Self-hosted runner: Improved sessions that move to a new runner: Claude now sees the tool call that was interrupted, marked as outcome unknown
- Updated the bundled dataviz skill to accept APCA as a text-contrast measure (keeping WCAG 2 ratios where AA conformance is required), add an `apca(text, background)` function to its palette validator scripts, and say whether a label inside a colored chart fill should be white or near-black
- Updated the /claude-api skill: service account keys and Workload Identity Federation tokens can now manage OpenTelemetry destinations
- Changed `sed -i` to get the standard Bash prompt and run as written, not a simulated file-edit preview; like other Bash edits, it is no longer restored by `/rewind`
- Changed `claude ultrareview` to require workspace trust: it asks on a terminal, else refuses; scripts pass `--trust-workspace`, which takes no value (put a PR number or base branch before it), or set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRAREVIEW_TRUST_CHECK=1`
- Changed the dangerous `rm` and `rmdir` prompt in bypass permissions mode in the Desktop app and VS Code to deny the command at once with a rewrite hint, so unattended sessions keep going
- Changed commands the settings exclude from the sandbox to ask before writing to its write-list paths while the sandbox is enabled but cannot run; the unsandboxed fallback is refused there
- Changed worktree creation and reuse so git no longer fetches objects on demand, in ordinary clones and in partial clones with a Bash sandbox configured; such a partial clone fetches them first
- Changed the `/claude-api` skill to build Managed Agents subagent teams on `multiagent_20261001` with dynamic workflows on by default, instead of `coordinator`
- [VSCode] Added a log warning that says what to do when dictation or the extension's own requests fail certificate verification, such as behind a TLS-inspecting proxy
- [VSCode] Fixed the Claude panel staying blank after the editor cached an incomplete copy of its files; it now recovers by itself, or says what went wrong and how to fix it
- [VSCode] Fixed Session history filling up with empty "Untitled" sessions each time you start a new session without sending a message
- [VSCode] Fixed long slash-command messages such as `/goal` filling the chat panel; they now fold behind Show more like other prompts (anthropics/claude-code#97469)
- [VSCode] Fixed long messages not folding behind Show more after the chat panel is made narrower
- [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+J in the chat input always inserting a newline: it is now left to VS Code and the OS when "ctrl+j" is set to null in the Chat context of ~/.claude/keybindings.json
- [VSCode] Fixed a mod's "From the … plugin" label above the prompt being drawn over the slash command and @-mention menus (anthropics/claude-code#102981)
- [VSCode] Fixed an empty list item, paragraph or code block, and list items renumbered from 1, when pasting copied LaTeX math
- [VSCode] Fixed the feedback error showing only an HTTP status when your organization does not accept feedback
- [VSCode] Improved Edit and Write speed in the chat panel: the wait for new problems after each edit is now 0.75 seconds in most cases, down from 1 to 1.5 seconds
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the Add connector list in routine forms saying no connectors were available while they were still loading
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the cloud environment editor shuffling environment variables and adding backslashes to values that contain both kinds of quote
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the self-hosted environment details dialog in admin settings so its title, tabs and buttons stay in view while only the content scrolls
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the "read documentation" tool row in cloud sessions, which showed escaped JSON instead of a readable page
- [Cloud sessions] Improved a cloud session's Changes pane, which now says when it lists only pushed commits or only Claude's edits
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack posting a draft you approved for a channel into your DM by mistake; a post with no channel is now refused so it can go to the approved channel
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Allow and Deny on Claude's approval cards in Slack doing nothing when the session had stopped; your answer now restarts the session
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude ignoring untagged messages in a Slack channel after its workspace moved to a different Claude organization, including unshared channels on Enterprise Grid
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in a Slack channel posting a threaded reply before reading a newer message someone had just added to that thread
- [Claude Tag] Fixed the Slack page in Claude Tag admin settings saying no workspaces were connected when the list failed to load; it now shows an error with a Retry button
- [Code Review] Fixed a finished review showing no check on the pull request when earlier tries to create it failed; a final try now adds a completed check
- [Code Review] Fixed a push queued behind a running review still starting a review after `@claude review stop`; its check now closes and says why

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.818.8289.0

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary
After switching from Codex to ChatGPT (Chat/Work) inside the unified Desktop app, all Codex chats and projects become visible in the ChatGPT view. This contradicts OpenAI's own documentation, which states Codex history is kept separate from ChatGPT history.

## Evidence
This was straightforward to confirm unambiguously: I currently have only a small number of chats/projects in Codex, so there was no risk of mistaking pre-existing ChatGPT items for leaked Codex ones. Immediately after switching views, the same small set of Codex chats/projects appeared listed under ChatGPT.

## Impact
Breaks the documented separation between Codex (development work) and ChatGPT (general use) — same category of privacy/context-boundary concern raised in #32494 for the reverse direction (ChatGPT history appearing in Codex).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the Desktop app, select Codex from the top-left menu.
2. Confirm Codex has its own chats/projects listed (a small number, in my case, made this easy to verify unambiguously — no risk of confusing them with pre-existing ChatGPT items).
3. Switch to ChatGPT (Chat/Work) from the same top-left menu.
4. Observe: all Codex chats and projects are now visible in the ChatGPT view as well.

### What is the expected behavior?

Per OpenAI's own Help Center documentation ("ChatGPT Work and Codex"): "Codex remains a separate view. Its workflows are unchanged, and its history remains separate from ChatGPT history." Codex chats and projects should not appear in the ChatGPT (Chat/Work) view after switching.

### Additional information

Related but not identical reports on the same Chat/Work/Codex separation boundary — flagging in case this is a symptom of the same underlying sync/attribution mechanism, though the direction and trigger differ:
- #32494 — opposite direction: personal ChatGPT history appearing inside Codex.
- #33087 — general feature request for separating histories, no specific reproduction steps.
- #33910 — Codex CLI sessions misattributed to ChatGPT/Work, a different trigger (CLI session creation) than plain UI switching.

This report is specifically about: switching views inside the Desktop app surfaces existing Codex chats/projects inside ChatGPT, with no CLI or external trigger involved.

issues.body:
### Environment
- Windows 11, Codex desktop app (exact app version not yet collected)
- ChatGPT web conversations and Codex Chat mode work normally
- Codex web task execution has **not** been tested because it asks to connect a GitHub repository
- Reported on October 21, 2026

### Problem
Every selectable model in Codex task/execution mode repeatedly returns:

`Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`

The UI counts down and automatically retries, but the same error recurs. Selecting other models does not resolve it. Starting a new ChatGPT Work task also produces exactly the same capacity error immediately, while ordinary chat continues to work.

### Reproduction
1. Open Codex desktop on Windows 11.
2. Select any available model and try a simple task in execution/agent mode.
3. Observe the capacity error and retry loop.
4. Switch models; the error persists.
5. Start a fresh ChatGPT Work task; the same error occurs.

### Expected behavior
An available model should execute tasks successfully, or the service should return an actionable account/quota/capacity diagnosis rather than looping indefinitely.

### Request
Please investigate backend capacity, account-level model admission/routing or entitlement state affecting Codex and ChatGPT Work. There is insufficient evidence yet to distinguish account-level from service-wide issues. We have not deleted application data, reinstalled, or modified proxy settings in order to preserve local history and projects.

### Related report
Similar symptoms: #55583 (2026-10-20), including Work mode failure. This report adds a separate reproduction across Codex desktop and freshly created ChatGPT Work tasks.

*Submitted on behalf of the affected user; no local logs, identifying account data, or precise client version are included.*

### Clarification: browser reproduction (October 21, 2026)
The same `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.` error also occurs **in ChatGPT in a web browser when switching to Work mode and starting a new Work task**. This is not restricted to the Windows Codex desktop application. Ordinary ChatGPT web chat continues to work. The separate Codex web interface cannot be used for testing because it requires connecting a GitHub repository. Please prioritize a backend/entitlement/account routing investigation over Windows-only troubleshooting.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244 (build 13536); bundled codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64; uname -mprs: Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm; UTM 5.0.6 (125), Apple Virtualization, VirtualMac2,1; Host: Apple M2 Max, macOS 27.0 (26A428)

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating to 26.1002.52244 (13536), I cannot send messages from Codex Home in my macOS VM. The composer shows “Не удалось загрузить настройки рабочей области” / “Повторите попытку, чтобы продолжить общение” (“Couldn't load workspace settings”; retry to continue chatting). Retry does not help.

My profile and other account-backed screens also fail to load. Usage limits are visible, but their freshness is unknown.

Version 26.930.61225 worked before the update. I am now completely locked out of my VM workflow. I use the VM to isolate my work environment; running Codex on the host is not a usable workaround.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use Codex with ChatGPT sign-in inside the macOS VM described above.
2. Update from 26.930.61225 to 26.1002.52244.
3. Open Codex Home and try to send a message.
4. Click Retry on the workspace-settings error. Sending remains blocked. Help/Feedback is not working either.

### What is the expected behavior?

With a valid session, DeviceCheck failures should not lock users out of core app functionality in a VM, as they did not in the previous version. Please restore that behavior while preserving required authentication and workspace-policy enforcement.

### Additional information

The logs show 86 DeviceCheck request failures across three launches between 10:56:45 and 11:05:00 UTC on October 7. Routes include `/accounts/check/{version}`, `/me`, `/profiles/me`, and `/settings/user`.

```text
2026-10-07T10:56:49.748Z sa_server_request_failed
errorCode=devicecheck_token_generation_failed
errorMessage="DeviceCheck token generation failed"
routePattern=/accounts/check/{version} status=500
```

Bundle inspection shows this error occurs locally, before the account request is sent. No 401/403 or session-expiry markers were found in the inspected logs. Sign-out, cookie deletion, and login tests were not performed.

Comparing signed builds 13232 and 13536 found a likely regression:

- Both builds have the same one-second native DeviceCheck timeout. The older session already logged DeviceCheck failures.
- Build 13536 adds `codexHomePolicyBlocking`. Unavailable account data now blocks the Codex Home composer, even when workspace-policy enrollment is still unknown. Build 13232 lacks this Codex-home path.
- The new selector is in `webview/assets/app-initial-61c077dcc1af.js` (`qhi` / `Jhi`); its composer integration is in `app-primary-15d1279f1ff0.js`.

This explains how an existing account-loading failure could start blocking messages after the update. Six isolated checks of the extracted selectors passed; a runtime fix has not been tested. The affected renderer's enrollment value and the private desktop commit SHA are unknown. Public app-server/CLI attestation files are unchanged between 0.160.1 and 0.162.0-alpha.2.

Suggested approach:
1. Treat DeviceCheck failure separately from an expired session or a workspace-policy denial.
2. Provide a server-supported, VM-compatible validation path so core features remain usable with valid authorization; retry DeviceCheck in the background with bounded timeouts.
3. Apply workspace-policy restrictions according to the actual policy, and show a recoverable error when required validation cannot succeed.

Please also review VM authentication across account loading, profiles, and messaging, and add regression coverage for unavailable DeviceCheck, timeouts, session refresh, and recovery. Related DeviceCheck report: #49556.

issues.title: [Windows][26.901.1978.0] `cua_node` `rename_staging` EPERM loops indefinitely, freezes desktop UI, and consumes ~59 GB

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Codex version

- Codex desktop: `26.901.1978.0` (Microsoft Store/MSIX, x64)
- Bundled Codex CLI: `0.153.0-alpha.5`
- A similar relocation failure also occurred after updating version `26.820.7780`.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build `26200.8457`, AMD64
- Runtime root: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node`
- Affected runtime content ID: `ad3b5049246cde44`

## Description

After an app update, Codex desktop starts but becomes extremely slow and eventually enters Windows' "Not responding" state. This is not ordinary renderer lag: the desktop main process repeatedly tries to materialize its bundled Node runtime and fails at the final staging-directory rename with Windows `EPERM`.

Each failed attempt creates another large `.staging-*` directory. In this incident, the loop produced **591 staging directories** and consumed **58.96 GB** before remediation. The retries were approximately three seconds apart. Windows also recorded `MoAppHang` for the app.

## Sanitized log evidence

```text
event=bundled_executable_relocation_failed
destinationPath=%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\ad3b5049246cde44
errorCode=EPERM
operation=rename_staging
executableName=node.exe   # also observed for node_repl.exe
originalError={"errno":-4048,"code":"EPERM","syscall":"rename",
  "path":"%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\.staging-ad3b5049246cde44-<uuid>",
  "dest":"%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\ad3b5049246cde44"}
```

The relocation failure is followed by errors equivalent to:

```text
Unable to locate the Codex CLI binary / bundled Node runtime
```

## Reproduction sequence

1. Update Codex desktop on Windows and launch it.
2. The app reports an Electron/PATH-related startup error; retrying can eventually open the UI.
3. The UI then freezes or becomes unresponsive.
4. Observe `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node` while the app is running.
5. A new `.staging-ad3b5049246cde44-*` directory appears roughly every three seconds, while the finalized `ad3b5049246cde44` directory never appears.
6. Disk usage and main-process blocking continue to grow until Codex is terminated.

## Implementation-level findings

Inspection of the installed desktop bundle indicates this failure is amplified by the materialization logic:

- The app recursively copies the bundled runtime synchronously, then calls a synchronous directory rename from staging to the content-addressed final directory.
- If the rename throws, staging cleanup is attempted, but any cleanup failure is swallowed.
- The resolved-runtime cache is populated only after successful finalization, so a transient failure is not remembered.
- Separate startup consumers request `node.exe`, `node_repl.exe`, and `node_modules`; after each failure they can re-enter the full copy-and-rename path.
- There is no bounded retry, exponential backoff, lock coordination, or failure circuit breaker for transient `EPERM`.
- Because recursive copy/rename work is synchronous in the desktop main process, the retry loop directly contributes to UI hangs.

This explains both the repeated staging-directory creation and the user-visible freeze. The initial process that briefly held the file/directory handle cannot be proven retroactively without ProcMon/ETW data, but the persistent app hang and disk exhaustion are caused by the unbounded failure/retry behavior.

## Recovery verification

With Codex fully stopped, constructing the complete runtime in a single staging directory and atomically renaming it to `ad3b5049246cde44` succeeded. After restarting:

- the staging-directory count remained at `0`;
- bundled Node (`v24.19.0`) was usable;
- Codex processes remained responsive;
- no new hang/crash events appeared;
- the desktop UI became immediately smooth again.

Deleting the orphaned staging directories recovered **58.96 GB**. No Codex settings or project data were removed.

## Expected behavior

- Treat `EPERM` during final rename as a transient Windows sharing/scan condition and retry the rename itself with bounded exponential backoff and jitter.
- Coordinate concurrent runtime requests so only one materialization is in flight per content ID.
- Never repeat the entire synchronous recursive copy every few seconds from the main process.
- Surface cleanup failures and reliably remove orphaned staging directories on the next launch.
- Add a retry/circuit-breaker limit so runtime relocation cannot indefinitely freeze the UI or exhaust the system drive.

## Related reports

- #41850 — Windows runtime staging does not finalize after a clean reset
- #41654 — Windows desktop update regressions involving protected runtime relocation

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; raw logs may contain local paths and account/session metadata.

issues.body:
### Summary

My dot can create a Slack channel canvas and discover its sections, but cannot update that same canvas. I can manually edit it in Slack. Recreating the canvas did not resolve the problem.

### Environment

- ChatGPT dot with its connected Slack bot identity
- Slack Free workspace
- Requested through the ChatGPT macOS app; the integration targeted the intended Slack channel
- Latest reproduction: October 23, 2026, approximately 03:08 UTC
- Client build and underlying Slack API error code are not available in the returned diagnostic information

### Minimal reproduction

1. Ask dot to create a canvas in a Slack channel using a heading and a single harmless test paragraph.
2. Creation succeeds and returns a new canvas ID.
3. List the channel's canvases. The newly created canvas appears in the list as a canvas tab (`is_primary: false`).
4. Look up the test paragraph's section ID. This succeeds.
5. Ask dot to replace that paragraph with another short test sentence, using the newly returned canvas ID and freshly retrieved section ID.

### Actual result

The edit fails with this exact message:

> Slack denied the canvas edit before making any changes. Check the requester's permission.

The edit is reported as not applied. I can manually edit the same canvas in Slack's UI. Earlier attempts in both a channel and a DM also encountered this edit failure, despite successful creation and section discovery. In earlier testing, Slack's UI displayed Dot Agent as the canvas owner.

### Expected result

The integration should be able to edit a canvas when its acting identity has write access. If it does not, the error should identify the missing permission or relevant restriction clearly enough to resolve it.

### What has been ruled out / remains unknown

- The fresh reproduction did not reuse a deleted canvas ID or stale section ID.
- The new canvas was present in the target channel's canvas-tab list when editing was attempted.
- Manual editing works, so this is not a generally read-only document for my Slack user.
- It is not yet established whether creation and editing use the same Slack actor, whether that actor has the required scope and document access, or whether a Free-plan canvas classification restriction is involved.
- No raw Slack error code, acting identity, or scope diagnostics were exposed by the failing operation. The root cause is unconfirmed.

Could the team inspect the creation/edit identity and request routing, and surface the underlying Slack error rather than only the generic requester-permission message?

Private workspace/channel/canvas IDs, private links, and actual workspace content are intentionally omitted. The reproduction uses only nonsensitive test text.

issues.body:
# [Windows][26.1016.8622.0] Three Crashpad-confirmed browser/main crashes immediately after IAB tab.close(), including non-final-tab closure

## User impact and request for action

I am reporting three whole-app crashes across three consecutive Windows Codex packages within about 14 hours. These crashes interrupt my development workflow. The first also coincided with termination of my terminal and a long-running local training job. I have had to spend substantial additional time and Codex usage allowance repeatedly diagnosing the crashes and reconstructing my normal workflow. This is unacceptable.

My complaint in my own words, submitted with my explicit authorization:

> 我因为软件的崩溃，浪费了很多额度来回到我正常的工作流，这是不可忍受的！

Please investigate this as a serious reliability issue, provide a verified fix or supported mitigation, and explain how I can request a review and appropriate remediation/credit for usage spent recovering from these product crashes. The exact amount of wasted allowance has not been measured; please do not interpret this as a quantified billing claim. Please provide a private support channel for account identification and usage review, and respond to the reporting GitHub account.

Related symptom reports: #42006, #36674, #35210. This report adds local evidence for packages 26.1016.6573.0, 26.1016.8120.0, and **26.1016.8622.0**, including closure with another managed browser tab still open. It does not claim that all reports share a proven native root cause.

## Environment

- Component: Windows Codex desktop app, native Windows local tasks, built-in Browser/IAB through `cua_repl`.
- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, x64, OS version/build `10.0.26300`.
- Microsoft Store/MSIX packages: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1016.6573.0_x64`, `26.1016.8120.0_x64`, `26.1016.8622.0_x64`.
- Time zone: Asia/Shanghai, UTC+08:00.
- The latest incident occurred after the successful update to 26.1016.8622.0 at 2026-10-23 09:02:11 local time.

## Three confirmed incidents

All times below are local UTC+08:00. The Crashpad column is the sidecar file creation timestamp, not a decoded native exception timestamp. The close column is the recorded tool-call invocation, not instrumented native destruction entry.

| Date / package | Explicit close call | Last desktop-log entry | Crashpad sidecar created | Codex AppModel container destroyed | App Browser / Browser Use tabs after closure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-22 / 26.1016.6573.0 | 20:01:52.892 | 20:01:53.015 | 20:01:53.6196385 | 20:01:54.3059464 | 0 / 0 |
| 2026-10-22 / 26.1016.8120.0 | 20:44:53.009 | 20:44:53.265 | 20:44:53.7179942 | 20:44:53.8945183 | 0 / 0 |
| **2026-10-23 / 26.1016.8622.0** | **10:07:59.278** | **10:07:59.359** | **10:08:00.0149507** | **10:08:00.3582150** | **1 / 1** |

Each final tool invocation explicitly awaited `tab.close()` (variable names normalized). These were ordinary cleanup operations after verifying a local web application. The application subsequently disappeared and its main desktop log stopped. No deliberate crash reproduction was performed during the investigation.

## Crashpad evidence

Three retained 60-byte sidecar files contain exactly:

```json
{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}
```

| Incident | Local Crashpad report ID |
|---|---|
| 1 | `20628979-94a0-4e01-b278-e4ad55094a28` |
| 2 | `c2b663ea-0ebf-459b-9b41-656e283525c7` |
| 3 | `bf2ab438-af99-4a78-9e86-d0a70999b2f5` |

The sidecars are from `%APPDATA%\Codex\web\Codex\Crashpad\reports`. Their identical content SHA-256 is `34da0ce5ef437eed829a85f48a89050e6079cbc58ee759a285ec3d13a49e0c3f`. These are local report IDs; server-side receipt has not been verified. No matching native `.dmp` remains in the inspected directory, so the exception code, faulting module and native stack are unavailable.

## Latest incident: selected log sequence

Below are redacted and abridged entries retaining the original UTC timestamps; local paths, project names, session IDs and unrelated fields are omitted.

```text
2026-10-23T02:07:59.278Z  tool call: ... await tab.close();
2026-10-23T02:07:59.311Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE unregistered debugger listener reason=target-close tabId=1 webContentsDestroyed=false
2026-10-23T02:07:59.314Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE renderer disposed browser sidebar webview
2026-10-23T02:07:59.324Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE browser sidebar guest torn down
2026-10-23T02:07:59.333Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE renderer removed browser sidebar webview tabType=closed
2026-10-23T02:07:59.333Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE closed browser sidebar page
2026-10-23T02:07:59.334Z  IAB_TAB_ANALYTICS action=closed appBrowserTabCount=1 appBrowserUseTabCount=1 threadBrowserTabCount=0 threadBrowserUseTabCount=0
2026-10-23T02:07:59.346Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE created browser use host
2026-10-23T02:07:59.346Z  IAB_LIFECYCLE iab rejected tab for route tabId=1 tabRouteKey=null
2026-10-23T02:07:59.346Z  request=getCommittedTabUrl error="Tab 1 is not part of browser session <redacted>"
2026-10-23T02:07:59.358Z  Received Browser Use PiP metadata backend=iab browserID=2 tabID=undefined
2026-10-23T02:07:59.359Z  Received item/completed for unknown conversation <redacted>
2026-10-23T02:08:00.0149507Z  Crashpad sidecar file created: capture_kind=crash, ptype=browser
2026-10-23T02:08:00.3582150Z  AppModel-Runtime/Admin 217: Codex container destroyed
```

The sidecar time above has been converted from its local filesystem creation timestamp to UTC. The final JS stack names `requireBrowserUseTab`, `getTab`, and `getCommittedTabUrl` in bundled `main-CT5a1yCd.js`. This is a JavaScript cleanup error, not a native crash stack, and is not sufficient on its own to prove the native fault.

Earlier incidents show the same target-close / guest teardown / invalid tab-route sequence:

```text
2026-10-22T12:01:52.908Z  reason=target-close
2026-10-22T12:01:52.931Z  action=closed appBrowserTabCount=0 appBrowserUseTabCount=0
2026-10-22T12:01:52.941Z  tabRouteKey=null; request=getCommittedTabUrl; Tab 4 is not part of browser session <redacted>
2026-10-22T12:01:53.6196385Z  Crashpad sidecar created

2026-10-22T12:44:53.041Z  reason=target-close
2026-10-22T12:44:53.045Z  tabRouteKey=null; request=getCommittedTabUrl; Tab 1 is not part of browser session <redacted>
2026-10-22T12:44:53.074Z  action=closed appBrowserTabCount=0 appBrowserUseTabCount=0
2026-10-22T12:44:53.7179942Z  Crashpad sidecar created
```

## Windows cross-check and concrete impact

- AppModel-Runtime/Admin event 217 records the three Codex container destructions with Record IDs 32269, 32328, and 32405. These corroborate process-container teardown but do not themselves provide an exception cause.
- At the first incident, Windows Terminal container destruction was also recorded at 20:01:53.9297671, Record ID 32268. Training updates stopped at 20:01:52, at step 7284; the latest committed checkpoint was step 7168. The precise OS mechanism connecting the app and worker termination is not established.
- A separate recovery queue launched afterward survived the second and third Codex crashes. At 2026-10-23 11:14 local, its worker was still advancing. I am not claiming all training was lost at every incident.
- No corresponding conventional Application Error / Windows Error Reporting / Application Hang entries were found in the inspected incident windows. This does not negate the positive Crashpad evidence.
- Inspected System logs did not show a reboot, resource-exhaustion event or display-reset event corresponding to the crashes. Security process-audit records were inaccessible without elevation; Sysmon was not present. Transient resource/driver involvement is not comprehensively excluded.
- Successful app-package updates were recorded separately at October 22 20:07:34 and October 23 09:02:11. They do not coincide with the three documented crashes.

## Expected behavior and requested investigation

Closing or cleaning up a Browser Use tab should close the tab or safely fail the tool request, while leaving Codex and unrelated tasks running. Investigate IAB debugger detachment, WebView/guest disposal, stale-route handling, `getCommittedTabUrl` requests racing with closure, and PiP updates. These are investigation directions, not a proven C++ root cause.

Please cover both final-tab and non-final-tab closure in regression tests. Leaving another tab open was insufficient in the third incident. Please identify a verified fixed Windows package or supported mitigation and a supported private procedure to retain the next native dump without risking active work.

Original local logs, hashed extracts and sidecar copies have been preserved. The minimized technical evidence is included above; fuller material and account details can be supplied through an authenticated private support channel. No private project contents, credentials, raw transcripts or account email are included in this public report.

issues.title: Automatically redeem unused banked resets before they expire

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS

### What feature would you like to see?

#### Problem

A banked Codex rate-limit reset can expire unused if the user saves it for later but forgets to redeem it before the displayed expiration time.

Once the reset is about to expire, allowing it to disappear provides less value than applying it as a final fallback.

#### Proposed behavior

When a banked reset remains unused immediately before its expiration time, Codex should automatically redeem that specific reset.

This should be the default behavior:

1. Keep the reset available for manual redemption until expiry.
2. Do not redeem it early.
3. Automatically redeem it as the expiration fallback, even if the ChatGPT desktop app is closed.
4. Notify the user that the reset was redeemed automatically.

### Additional information

This is distinct from #32218, which proposes letting users queue a reset for redemption when a usage limit is exhausted.

That request addresses unattended limit exhaustion. This request addresses a reset reaching its expiry unused. Both behaviours could coexist, with expiry redemption acting only as the final fallback.

```json
          "type": "agentMessage",
          "id": "<assistant-message-id>",
          "text": "::chatgpt-content-reference{index=\"1\" source_message_id=\"<assistant-message-id>\"}"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected Windows Desktop session:

1. Use an existing ChatGPT conversation containing completed assistant replies.
2. Invoke the official `mcp__codex_app__read_thread` tool with the following arguments:

```json
{
  "threadId": "<chatgpt-conversation-id>",
  "turnLimit": 10,
  "includeOutputs": true,
  "maxOutputCharsPerItem": 20000
}
```

3. Inspect the returned assistant items' original `agentMessage.text`, rather than `thread.preview` or the user messages.
4. Observe that the assistant items contain only content-reference directives, despite the completed turn statuses.

This was reproduced on the existing affected conversation. We are not claiming that every account, conversation, or desktop build is affected.

### What is the expected behavior?

A supported way for the calling agent to obtain the readable content of the referenced assistant message: either resolved text in the read result or a documented public resolver.

If reference-only or summary-only output is intentional, please clarify that contract and the supported way to retrieve the underlying message content. A successful read returning only an opaque reference is insufficient for a workflow that must inspect the actual answer.

### Additional information

**Historical comparison:** A retained September 12, 2026 result for the same ChatGPT conversation and the same read parameters contains ordinary assistant text and stable message IDs. September 26 checks returned references, and the October 2 direct retest above still does. The exact first failing release/date is unknown; the earlier desktop package version was not independently established here.

**Related external evidence, not a confirmed shared root cause:** Another browser integration reported the identical directive while its ChatGPT tab displayed normal replies: [chat-on-steroids #574](https://github.com/totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids/issues/574). Its [PR #579](https://github.com/totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids/pull/579) uses a complete, resolved page capture for model-facing text readers; the change appears in [v2.1.20](https://github.com/totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids/releases/tag/v2.1.20). That is a separate browser-based path and does not establish how the official desktop tool should resolve the reference.

We have not completed a same-time browser/DOM comparison in our own environment. No private endpoints, content-reference dereferencing, browser cookies, or session-database edits were used in the direct test.

Questions for maintainers:

1. Is this expected representation, or a regression in ChatGPT-backed `read_thread` content resolution?
2. Does `read_thread` support resolved assistant content for these messages? If so, what supported call or option should be used?
3. If it does not, is there a public resolver for `source_message_id`, or another supported first-party retrieval path?

Existing issue #40300 concerns a ChatGPT-backed read causing a crash; this report concerns successful calls returning reference-only bodies.

Conversation titles, real conversation/message IDs, private message bodies, local paths, credentials, and full session logs are omitted. Codex assisted with the investigation and this report; the user explicitly authorized submission.
