prs.title: fix(cli): stop continuation stream processing and auto-nudge after request cancellation
prs.body:
When a user cancels an active turn in interactive mode (by pressing `Escape`) while a continuation stream is running after a tool batch completes (for example, right after `SearchText` finishes for an `explain @<dir>` prompt), the CLI prints `ℹ Request cancelled.` but continues executing subsequent model turns and tool calls (`Shell git status`, `Shell git worktree list`).

In `processGeminiStreamEvents()` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`), `ServerGeminiEventType.UserCancelled` only broke out of the `switch` statement instead of returning `StreamProcessingStatus.UserCancelled`, and the post-loop logic did not check `signal.aborted || turnCancelledRef.current`. Because the cancelled continuation stream had `isContinuation === true`, `toolCallRequests.length === 0`, and `hasVisibleText === false`, `processGeminiStreamEvents()` mistook the user cancellation for an empty model response and triggered the auto-nudge continuation (`submitQueryRef.current([{ text: nudgeMessage }], { isContinuation: true }, prompt_id)`). That `submitQuery` call created a new `AbortController`, reset `turnCancelledRef.current = false`, and sent the nudge prompt to the model, causing the agent to continue running and scheduling new tool calls after `ℹ Request cancelled.`.

This change returns `StreamProcessingStatus.UserCancelled` immediately on `UserCancelled` or when `signal.aborted || turnCancelledRef.current` is set, prevents auto-nudging after terminal stream events, and checks cancellation state across async boundaries in `submitQuery` and `handleCompletedTools`.

## Details

- **`processGeminiStreamEvents` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`)**:
  - Flushes any pending history item, clears `pendingToolCallRequestsRef.current`, and returns `StreamProcessingStatus.UserCancelled` immediately when `ServerGeminiEventType.UserCancelled` is received or when `signal.aborted || turnCancelledRef.current` is true after the stream loop exits, preventing both post-cancellation tool scheduling and post-cancellation auto-nudge continuation queries.
  - Tracks terminal stream events (`Error`, `AgentExecutionStopped`, `AgentExecutionBlocked`, `MaxSessionTurns`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `InvalidStream`, and `LoopDetected`) so the empty-response auto-nudge only runs when a continuation stream completes normally.
- **`submitQuery` & `handleCompletedTools` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`)**:
  - Guards `submitQuery` after `await prepareQueryForGemini(...)` and `handleCompletedTools` before `submitQuery(..., { isContinuation: true })` against `turnCancelledRef.current || abortSignal.aborted`.
- **Tests (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx`)**:
  - Adds a regression test reproducing (cancelling during the continuation stream after `SearchText` completes and verifying that `Request cancelled.` halts execution without triggering the auto-nudge turn or scheduling `Shell` tool calls).
  - Adds a regression test verifying that buffered `ToolCallRequest` events are not scheduled if the stream is cancelled before completion.




## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx -t "User Cancellation"
   ```
2. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Build and launch the interactive CLI from the repository root:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      node packages/cli/dist/index.js
      ```

prs.title: fix(a2a-server,core): preserve extended token usage metadata and align per-turn reporting
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Updates token usage metadata handling across `@google/gemini-cli-a2a-server` and `@google/gemini-cli-core` to preserve `thoughtsTokenCount`, `toolUsePromptTokenCount`, and `cachedContentTokenCount`, compute `totalTokenCount` across all token components, and report per-turn context window usage once per final status transition.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
- **Per-Turn Usage Metadata Lifecycle & Aggregation (`packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts`)**:
  - Extended `Task.usageMetadata` to include `thoughtsTokenCount` and `toolUsePromptTokenCount`.
  - Updated `Task._createStatusUpdateEvent` to clear `this.usageMetadata` once attached to a `final: true` status update so subsequent `final: true` updates without a new LLM stream (such as sequential tool confirmation waves or tool cancellations) do not re-emit prior usage metadata.
  - Updated `Task.acceptAgentMessage` on `GeminiEventType.Finished` to retain the latest sub-turn `promptTokenCount` and `cachedContentTokenCount` while accumulating `candidatesTokenCount`, thoughtsTokenCount`, and `toolUsePromptTokenCount` across un-emitted sub-turns within the turn, and compute `totalTokenCount` as `promptTokenCount + candidatesTokenCount + toolUsePromptTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount`.
- **Extended Usage Metadata Preservation in Core (`packages/core/src/code_assist/converter.ts`,   `packages/core/src/hooks/hookTranslator.ts`)**:
  - Updated `fromGenerateContentResponseUsage` in `converter.ts` to preserve `thoughtsTokenCount`, `toolUsePromptTokenCount`, and `cachedContentTokenCount` and align `totalTokenCount` with the component sum.
  - Extended `LLMResponse['usageMetadata']` and `HookTranslatorGenAIv1.toHookLLMResponse` in `hookTranslator.ts` to preserve `cachedContentTokenCount`, `thoughtsTokenCount`, and `toolUsePromptTokenCount`.
- **Unit Tests (`task.test.ts`, `converter.test.ts`, `hookTranslator.test.ts`)**:
  - Added unit tests covering extended token field preservation, `totalTokenCount` calculation, single-emission consumption on `final: true` status updates, and multi-step sub-turn usage aggregation.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

prs.title: fix(core): prevent path traversal in legacy checkpoint fallback
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the path-traversal vulnerability in `Logger._getCheckpointPath()` and `Logger.deleteCheckpoint()` when falling back to the legacy unencoded checkpoint filename (`checkpoint-${tag}.json`).

While `_checkpointPath(tag)` safely percent-encodes special characters (including `/` and `\`) via `encodeTagName(tag)`, both `_getCheckpointPath(tag)` and `deleteCheckpoint(tag)` previously fell back to constructing `path.join(this.geminiDir, `checkpoint-${tag}.json`)` directly from the raw `tag`. A tag containing `../` segments (for example, `x/../../target`) caused `path.join` to normalize the `checkpoint-x` prefix away and resolve to `../target.json` outside `this.geminiDir`, allowing `loadCheckpoint`, `checkpointExists`, and `deleteCheckpoint` to read, probe, or delete arbitrary `*.json` files outside the checkpoints directory.

### Key Changes
- **Legacy Path Guard (`packages/core/src/core/logger.ts`)**: Added `_legacyCheckpointPath(tag)` to validate that the legacy candidate filename is a flat basename within `this.geminiDir` with no path separators before `_getCheckpointPath` or `deleteCheckpoint` touches the filesystem.
- **Unit Tests (`packages/core/src/core/logger.test.ts`)**: Added regression coverage verifying that `checkpointExists`, `loadCheckpoint`, and `deleteCheckpoint` reject `../` traversal tags on the legacy fallback path while preserving backward compatibility for flat legacy tags with special characters.

## Related Issues

Closes #29191

## How to Validate

```bash
npx vitest run --root packages/core src/core/logger.test.ts
npx eslint --max-warnings 0 packages/core/src/core/logger.ts packages/core/src/core/logger.test.ts
npm run typecheck --workspace=@google/gemini-cli-core
```

prs.title: refactor(core): replace tree-sitter Bash parser with unbash
prs.body:
## Summary

Replace the tree-sitter Bash parser with the synchronous `unbash` parser. This removes the WASM runtime, Bash grammar, asynchronous initialization and fallback plumbing while preserving the command-detail API and the native PowerShell AST path.

A fresh bundle comparison from the same `origin/main` commit reduced top-level JavaScript from 26,808,108 to 24,665,148 bytes (8.0%) and gzip size from 4,834,570 to 4,452,446 bytes (7.9%). The two tree-sitter chunks and all tree-sitter references are gone.

## Details

The Bash command collector now walks structured commands, compound syntax, redirections, substitutions, tests and arithmetic expressions from the unbash AST. It preserves the existing command details used by policy and sandbox callers, including source text and offsets.

The replacement also corrects two command-root results from the previous parser:

| Input                                       | Previous roots | New roots |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------- |
| `if [[ -f package.json ]]; then npm ci; fi` | `[[`, `npm`    | `npm`     |
| `coproc mycop { sleep 1; }`                 | `coproc`, `}`  | `sleep`   |

Command substitutions inside arithmetic syntax are collected as executable roots. Parse errors from both the root script and nested substitutions continue to fail closed.

This removes `web-tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-bash` and `esbuild-plugin-wasm`, along with the WASM loader utilities and parser lifecycle calls. It also addresses the loading overhead discussed in #12135 and removes the published `?binary` WASM imports reported in #25651. Both issues were closed by stale automation rather than a code change.

Disclosure: I maintain [unbash](https://github.com/webpro-nl/unbash) and [knip](https://github.com/webpro-nl/knip), which depends on it. For npm's 2026-07-27 through 2026-08-02 reporting window, unbash recorded 9,056,581 downloads and knip recorded 12,240,135. unbash is an ISC-licensed, zero-dependency, synchronous package and supports every Node.js version supported by Gemini CLI.

## Related Issues

Related to #12135 and #25651.

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts`
  - 67 passed, 2 skipped
- Affected policy, sandbox, shell and utility tests
  - 472 passed, 5 skipped across 11 files
- Full core test suite

- `npm run typecheck`
  - Passed for all workspaces, evals, integration tests and memory tests
- `npm run lint`
  - Passed with zero warnings
- `npm run bundle`
  - Completed successfully with no tree-sitter chunks or references

prs.title: fix(core): keep the unsent request when loop recovery starts before a turn
prs.body:
## Summary

When the loop check at the start of a turn reports a loop, `_recoverFromLoop` sends only the loop feedback and drops the pending request. That request is usually the `functionResponse` of a tool that already ran, so the call is closed as `"Response was lost or interrupted."` and the model loses the record of what the tool did.

## Details

`processTurn` now passes the unsent request to `_recoverFromLoop`, which sends the request parts first and the feedback text after them, in one user turn. `isFunctionResponse` matches a turn with any `functionResponse` part, so `closeUnansweredToolCallsTurn` no longer replaces the real result.

The loop check during streaming is not changed, because there the request was already sent. I did not postpone the check while a tool response is pending: late in a prompt a response is almost always pending, so the check would almost never run.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29815

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/client.test.ts`. The new test `should keep an unsent tool response when the loop is found before the request is sent` fails on `main`, because the recovery request contains only the feedback text.
- The `--fake-responses` script in #29815: `step-29.txt` is answered with its real `functionResponse`, followed by the loop feedback.

issues.title: Voice server segfaults (signal 11) on WSL2 after updating to 1.0.100; /voice stuck on 'Fetching voice models'

issues.body:
## Summary
After updating to Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (which also pulled a new voice runtime), voice input no longer works on WSL2. The voice server process segfaults (signal 11) a few seconds after starting, so `/voice` stays on "Fetching voice models" and no model can be downloaded.

## Environment
- Copilot CLI: 1.0.100 (linux-x64), latest at time of report
- OS: Ubuntu (glibc 2.39) on WSL2, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- CPU: x64 with AVX2, 8 cores, 16 GB RAM
- Audio: WSLg PulseAudio available (`/mnt/wslg/PulseServer`)
- Voice worked on earlier versions (e.g. 1.0.98) with the older runtime (`Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.Core.so`, ~645 MB)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Update to 1.0.100; the update installs a new voice runtime (`libfoundry_local.so`, ~85 MB).
2. Start `copilot` and run `/voice`, choose Continue.
3. Status shows "Fetching voice models" indefinitely.

## Actual behaviour
Process log:
```
[INFO]  voice server: boot pid=1708 endpoint=/run/user/1000/copilot-voice/<id>.sock
[INFO]  voice server: connected to spawned voice server pid=1708
[WARNING] [VoiceEngine] connection error: read ECONNRESET
[ERROR] [VoiceEngine] fatal: Engine connection closed.
[WARNING] [VoiceEngine] start failed: Engine connection closed.
```
WSL kernel log (repeated on every attempt, ~6-15s after the voice server starts):
```
copilot: MainThread: potentially unexpected fatal signal 11.
WSL (CaptureCrash): Capturing crash for pid: 1708, executable: .../@github/copilot-linux-x64/copilot, signal: 11
```

## Already tried
- Removed stale `/run/user/$UID/copilot-voice/*` socket/pid files
- Deleted `~/.cache/copilot/foundry` and `~/.github-copilot-cli/cache/models`, then re-ran `/voice` to reinstall the runtime. The crash still occurs with the freshly downloaded runtime.
- `ldd` on `libfoundry_local.so` reports no missing libraries.

## Expected behaviour
The voice server stays running, the model list loads, and dictation works.

Possibly related: #4024

issues.title: Secret redaction is too agressive and redact legitimate content.
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I have a spec file that contains the following line

```
- Rover's `supergraph.yaml` supports Router-style variable expansion (e.g. `Authorization: "Bearer ${env.AUTH_TOKEN}"`), so the token can be injected via an environment variable at compose time without hand-editing the config file per run.
```

The security feature redact the `Bearer ${env.AUTH_TOKEN}`, to `******` causing agent to get confused.

That's really not ideal. It prevent reading completely valid specification. As you can see, no actual secret are being exfiltrated.

I understand why the feature exists,  clearly the PII protection should be on by default but it would be nice to be able to configure the level of redaction. Certain type of task demand that we edit Authorization Header code, it is part of programming. The current security settings make this impossible.

That's quite blocking for my current work 

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.69

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Use plan mode or similar to create a markdown file containing specification on how to construct an Authorization Header
In a fresh session, ask the agent to review the file and see if there is ambiguities

The agent will complain about the ******. Sometime he will be smart about it and use xxd to read the ****** , meaning the secrets aren't really protected.

### Expected behavior

The agent can ream understand and work in code and text that contains text that look like authorization code, and the redaction does not throw it off. 

EDIT: 2026-10-22  changed the expected behavior to avoid specifying the solution too much

### Additional context

Couple suggestion on how to fix this
- Turn off secret redaction with a flag. e.g. `--no-secret-redaction`. Opt-in only so no secret are leaked by default
- Allow the user to define path without redaction in the configuration. If the `docs/` directory is known to be safe, it can be excluded from secret redaction. Again, opt-in only.

issues.title: Installed plugin custom agent cancels its own HTTP MCP calls while default agent succeeds
issues.body:
### Summary

An HTTP MCP server packaged with an installed Copilot plugin is discovered and its tool can be selected, but the connection is immediately cancelled whenever the plugin's custom agent is active. The same MCP tool succeeds from the default agent in the same repository project session and from a general chat.

This is a controlled custom-agent/default-agent difference, not a general MCP endpoint outage or malformed plugin configuration.

### Environment

- GitHub Copilot app on Windows 11
- Copilot CLI `1.0.100`
- Installed plugin version: `0.6.0`
- Custom agent is manually selected and has:
  - `target: github-copilot`
  - `disable-model-invocation: true`
  - `user-invocable: true`
- Plugin MCP declaration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "microsoft-learn": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

The installed `.mcp.json` is byte-identical to the source declaration.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a plugin that contains both a custom agent and the HTTP MCP declaration above.
2. Create a repository project session.
3. Select the plugin custom agent.
4. Ask the agent to invoke `microsoft-learn.microsoft_docs_search` once.
5. Observe that the tool is discovered and a tool execution starts, but it completes almost immediately with a cancelled connection.
6. Create another project session for the same repository without selecting the custom agent.
7. Invoke the same tool and query using the default agent.

### Actual behavior

Two independent fresh sessions with the plugin custom agent selected reproduced:

```text
MCP server 'microsoft-learn': MCP server "microsoft-learn" connection was cancelled
```

Observed execution timings:

```text
Custom-agent session A, attempt 1: 20:12:37.554Z -> 20:12:37.604Z, failed (50 ms)
Custom-agent session A, attempt 2: 20:16:53.996Z -> 20:16:54.059Z, failed (63 ms)
Custom-agent session B:            20:24:45.594Z -> 20:24:45.660Z, failed (66 ms)
```

The tool request is emitted correctly. Cancellation occurs during host execution after `tool.execution_start`.

### Controlled comparison

The same `microsoft-learn.microsoft_docs_search` tool and endpoint succeed when the custom agent is not selected:

```text
Default-agent project session in the same repository:
20:27:31.533Z -> 20:27:34.017Z, success

General chat:
20:24:40.107Z -> 20:24:43.164Z, success
```

The project session, repository, branch, installed plugin state, MCP endpoint, and query type were held constant for the project-session comparison. The controlled difference was custom-agent selection.

### Expected behavior

A plugin custom agent should be able to execute tools from the MCP server packaged by that same installed plugin. Selecting the custom agent should not cancel an otherwise healthy MCP connection.

### Impact

The custom agent can route to the MCP tool, but cannot execute it. This prevents the plugin from using its declared grounding capability, while the default agent can use the same server successfully.

### Additional context

- No OAuth is involved in this MCP server.
- No repository, plugin, or Copilot configuration mutation occurred during the tests.
- The failure reproduced after creating a second clean custom-agent session.
- Related but distinct from #1756: that issue concerns inheritance of globally configured MCP servers. Here, the MCP server is packaged with the installed plugin, its tool is discoverable, and execution is cancelled only under the plugin custom agent.
- Related but distinct from #5195: this is not deferred-tool context loading or token growth. The selected tool starts execution and is immediately cancelled.

Full session identifiers and sanitized event excerpts can be provided privately if needed for host-side tracing.

issues.title: Trusted folders silently auto-approve shell execution in manual mode, even for commands with unpredictable side effects (scripts, sqlcmd, curl)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In `manual` permission mode, any shell command whose referenced file paths all lie inside a trusted folder is executed without any permission prompt. Path-based gating cannot determine what a command will actually do.

Concretely: the agent ran
```
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\someScript.ps1
```
from inside a trusted folder. The session event log contains no `permission.requested` event for this execution - it went straight from tool request to execution. 




### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a folder to `trustedFolders` in `~/.copilot/config.json` (or accept the trust prompt with the persistent option).
2. Start a session in that folder with permission mode `manual`.
3. Ask the agent to run any script in the folder, e.g. a `.ps1` that connects to a local database or the network.
4. Observe: the command executes immediately; `events.jsonl` contains a `tool.execution_start` but no `permission.requested` event.

### Expected behavior


In `manual` mode, shell command execution should require approval regardless of folder trust.

At minimum, provide a setting that decouples the two, e.g. `"trustedFolderAutoApprovesShell": false`, so users can keep folder trust while retaining per-command prompts.

However, neither pure path-based nor pure command-based gating is sufficient on its own. Suggested combination, evaluated in order:

1. A built-in read-only tier: provably side-effect-free commands (`git show`, `git log`, `Get-Content`, `ls`, ...) never prompt, regardless of path or folder.
2. Per-folder command-pattern rules: `(folder, command-pattern) -> allow | ask | deny`, persisted via the existing per-folder structure of `permissions-config.json` and populated through the familiar "allow always (for this folder) / allow for session / deny" prompt choices.
3. Unclassifiable executions default to ask: invoking scripts or interpreters (`powershell -File *.ps1`, `cmd /c`, `bash`, `python`), database clients (`sqlcmd`, `psql`), service control (`systemctl`, `Stop-Service`), and network tools (`curl`, `Invoke-WebRequest` to URLs outside allowedUrls) always prompt unless explicitly allowlisted for that folder — their effect cannot be predicted from the command line.

Prior art: Claude Code uses per-command-pattern allow/ask/deny rules (folder trust does not grant execution); Codex CLI pairs auto-approval with OS-level sandboxing (network off, writes confined to the workspace) so unpredicted effects fail instead of succeeding silently; JetBrains Junie and VS Code agent mode prompt per terminal command with allowlists. Copilot CLI's "trusted folder implies unprompted shell" is the outlier among these.



### Additional context

**Environment**

- Copilot CLI 1.0.83 through 1.0.101 (long-lived session, behavior identical across versions)
- Windows, PowerShell tool
- permissionMode: `manual`, agentMode: `interactive`
- No entries for the folder in `permissions-config.json`; no `/allow-all`; no launch flags

issues.title: Remote MCP (OAuth): active session keeps resending an expired access token instead of refreshing or prompting sign-in
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A Copilot CLI session connected to a remote OAuth-protected MCP server keeps sending the same expired access token after its first HTTP 401. The client makes no request to the token endpoint and does not prompt the user to sign in again. The rejected requests repeat about every four minutes for hours.

We run the MCP server at `https://api.plori.ai/mcp` and observed this from the server side:

- Session A (`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2`): the server rejected one bearer token (same fingerprint on every request) 581 times as expired, from 2026-10-19 00:56 UTC to 2026-10-21 06:50 UTC.
- Session B (`copilot-cli`): successful MCP pings until 2026-10-20 19:38 UTC, which is one hour after the token was issued (our access tokens live one hour). From 19:42 UTC the server rejected the same expired bearer 82 times, about four minutes apart, until 2026-10-21 05:55 UTC. Between 19:30 and 20:00 UTC our authorization server received no token-endpoint request.

Every rejection is HTTP 401 with:

```http
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", resource_metadata="https://api.plori.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

The authorization server advertises `grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]` and issues rotating refresh tokens when `offline_access` is requested. The token response sizes we logged before each session match a response that contains a refresh token, so we believe the client held one. We cannot inspect the client's credential store, so this is an inference.

### Affected version

`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2` (session A). Session B's user agent was `copilot-cli` without a version.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a remote MCP server whose authorization server issues one-hour access tokens and rotating refresh tokens (`offline_access` advertised).
2. Sign in through the CLI's OAuth flow.
3. Keep the session open past the access token's expiry, with the server connected (background pings or subscriptions running).
4. Watch the server logs: requests continue with the expired bearer and receive 401 `invalid_token`; no `refresh_token` grant reaches the token endpoint.

### Expected behavior

On a 401 with `error="invalid_token"`, the client uses its refresh token (RFC 6749 §6), stores the rotated credentials, and retries with the new access token on the active transport. If refresh is not possible, the client tells the user that the server needs authentication again, instead of resending the rejected token.

### Additional context

This looks related to #4203, which describes an expired access token at session start forcing interactive sign-in instead of a refresh. Here the token expires during an active session, and the client neither refreshes nor asks for sign-in; it keeps retrying the same token. We are happy to provide more server-side detail (timestamps, request counts) if it helps.

— Plori AI team

issues.title: web_fetch fails DNS validation in proxy-only environments despite working native HTTP transport (1.0.102)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in `web_fetch` tool fails for public HTTPS URLs in a corporate proxy-only environment where local DNS does not resolve public destination hostnames. The configured HTTP CONNECT proxy can resolve and fetch those destinations successfully.

Both `curl` and the same installed Copilot CLI native HTTP transport can retrieve the page through the existing proxy without local destination DNS resolution.

### Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI: **1.0.102**
- OS: Linux on WSL2 / Windows
- Installation: npm (`@github/copilot`)
- System Node.js: **v24.18.0**
- Corporate HTTP CONNECT proxy: Zscaler
- `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and lowercase equivalents are configured and inherited.
- `no_proxy` does not exclude the tested public destinations.
- `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` points to the trusted system CA bundle.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an environment where public Internet access works through an HTTP CONNECT proxy, but local DNS returns `NXDOMAIN` for public destination hostnames.
2. Configure `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and required CA trust.
3. Ask Copilot CLI to fetch `https://docs.github.com/` or `https://example.com/` using built-in `web_fetch`.
4. Compare with the following request from the same environment:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
  --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 \
  -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}; TLS verify %{ssl_verify_result}\n' \
  https://docs.github.com/
```

### Actual behavior

Both tested destinations fail in `web_fetch` with:

```text
WebFetchBlockedUrlError: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known
```

### Diagnostic evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in `web_fetch` for GitHub Docs and example.com | DNS lookup error above |
| `curl` through configured proxy | HTTP 200; TLS verification result 0 |
| Local DNS lookup in WSL | Fails; A query returns NXDOMAIN |
| Windows `Resolve-DnsName docs.github.com` | DNS_ERROR_RCODE_NAME_ERROR |
| Direct query to configured corporate DNS | Authoritative NXDOMAIN for docs.github.com A |
| Installed CLI native HTTP transport through same proxy | HTTP 200, final URL https://docs.github.com/en |

For the last comparison, I loaded `runtime.node` from the installed CLI 1.0.102 package and invoked `networkFetchStreamStart` with a GET request, `redirect: "follow"`, `pinnedAddresses: []`, and `allowLocalhost: false`. The proxy environment was unchanged. This was a diagnostic transport probe, not a proposed replacement for URL validation.

This isolates the observed failure to local destination resolution in the built-in tool's validation path, rather than missing proxy variables, TLS trust, or a WSL-only DNS problem. The precise internal validation implementation has not been verified from source.

### Expected behavior

Please provide a supported, security-preserving way for `web_fetch` to work when the configured proxy handles destination DNS and local public-name resolution is unavailable.

If local destination DNS is an intentional prerequisite, please document that limitation and return an actionable error distinguishing it from proxy connectivity or TLS problems.

This is not a request to disable SSRF protection, allow private/loopback/metadata destinations, or bypass corporate network policy. Any solution needs appropriate destination and redirect validation.

### Related issues

- #5180: related conflict between local address validation and proxy-managed DNS, but concerns Fake-IP addresses rather than unavailable resolution / NXDOMAIN.
- #3948: previous proxy failures were marked resolved as of 1.0.88; this failure reproduces on 1.0.102.
- #4019: previous built-in web_fetch proxy support report.

### Workaround

Use shell `curl` through the configured proxy. No system DNS settings, CLI package files, TLS verification settings, or URL-safety checks were modified during investigation.

issues.title: ACP mode: expired MCP OAuth access token opens the browser authorization page instead of using the stored refresh token
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), when a remote HTTP MCP server answers 401 because the stored access token has expired, the CLI goes straight to `[acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`. It never tries a `refresh_token` grant, even though a refresh token is stored and works.

The same config, same Keychain entry and same machine, a minute apart:

- `copilot` (interactive) and `copilot -p`: 401, then silent refresh, server connected in ~200 ms, no browser.
- `copilot --acp`: 401, then the authorization page opens. Nothing in the log shows a refresh attempt.

ACP does read the stored token: right after the interactive CLI refreshed and persisted it, an ACP session connected to the server without a browser. It just never renews an expired one.

Server used: Sentry remote MCP (`https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`), dynamic client registration (`clientId` `https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json`), token in the macOS Keychain (service `copilot-mcp-oauth`).

## Affected version

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102 (latest stable; 1.0.103-0 prerelease release notes mention nothing related)
- Same pattern in my logs going back to 2026-10-19 (1.0.100 and 1.0.101)
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a remote OAuth MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "sentry": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp" } } }
   ```
2. Sign in once from the interactive CLI so an access token and refresh token are stored.
3. Wait until the access token expires (about an hour for Sentry). Don't run the interactive CLI in between.
4. Start `copilot --acp` over stdio and send `initialize` then `session/new` (`cwd` set to any temp dir, `mcpServers: []`).
5. The browser opens the Sentry authorization page. Log: `opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`.
6. Close the ACP process, then run `copilot -p "reply with ok"` from the same directory. The server connects after a 401 with no browser.

Minimal driver used for step 4:

```js
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
const cwd = process.argv[2];
const child = spawn('copilot', ['--acp'], { cwd, stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] });
const send = (id, method, params) => child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params }) + '\n');
let buf = '';
child.stdout.on('data', d => {
  buf += d; let i;
  while ((i = buf.indexOf('\n')) >= 0) {
    const m = JSON.parse(buf.slice(0, i)); buf = buf.slice(i + 1);
    if (m.id === 1) send(2, 'session/new', { cwd, mcpServers: [] });
  }
});
send(1, 'initialize', { protocolVersion: 1, clientCapabilities: {} });
setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGTERM'), 45000);
```

## Expected behavior

On a 401 for a server with a stored refresh token, ACP does what the interactive CLI and `-p` already do: silently POST `grant_type=refresh_token`, persist the new tokens, reconnect. Only fall back to the authorization page if the refresh fails (`invalid_grant`, revoked, no refresh token).

## Actual behavior

### ACP, expired token (2026-10-22, live repro)

```
11:45:55.601Z [INFO] Starting ACP server (stdio)
11:45:56.976Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "******"OAuth\", resource_metadata=\"https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\"", response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, header_count: 10, has_body: true } })
11:45:57.315Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:45:57.315Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (WWW-Authenticate: ******"OAuth", resource_metadata="https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp") {"server":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth authorization failed"}
11:45:57.414Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:45:57.458Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:46:39.891Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_client::session_authorizer] MCP OAuth login did not complete {"server_name":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed."}
```

Two authorization pages per `session/new`, one per challenge. The ACP client got no `session/update` or request about auth; the CLI opened the browser on its own.

### `-p`, same token, 60 s later

```
11:46:50.753Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:46:50.955Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

No browser, connected 200 ms after the 401.

### Interactive CLI, earlier the same day

```
07:54:03.670Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
07:54:03.761Z [ERROR] Refreshing authentication for sentry...
07:54:04.340Z [ERROR] Successfully authenticated with sentry
07:54:04.413Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

The Keychain item's modification date is 07:54:04Z, so this refresh was persisted. An ACP process that had already opened the page at 07:53:30 and again at 07:54:29 finally connected to Sentry at 07:54:34, using the token the interactive CLI had just stored.

### Across all my logs

I went through every process log in `~/.copilot/logs` (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22) that has a Sentry OAuth challenge:

| Mode | Processes | With a refresh attempt | Opened the authorization page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--acp` | 32 | 0 | 30 (in the other 2 the client disconnected before the page opened) |
| interactive | 2 | 2 | 1, only after its refresh attempt failed (2026-10-21, `Refreshing authentication` then `Opening browser for sentry authentication`) |

No ACP log contains `Refreshing authentication`, `Successfully authenticated` or anything else showing a refresh attempt.

## Impact

ACP clients (Kepler, editors) spawn short-lived `copilot --acp` processes: one per new chat, plus background ones for titles, model lists and similar. Once the access token expires, which for Sentry is about an hour, every one of them:

- pops one or two Sentry authorization tabs the user didn't ask for, at session start, before any Sentry tool is used;
- cancels the flow a moment later when the process exits (`MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed.`), or leaves it hanging until `OAuth callback timeout` after 5 minutes;
- starts the session without the server's tools.

The only workaround is to open the interactive CLI now and then so it refreshes and persists the token for ACP to pick up.

## Possibly related: `-p` refresh is not persisted

The silent refresh in `-p` runs never updated the stored token. After two `-p` runs at 11:46 and 11:50 that both refreshed, the Keychain item's modification date was still 07:54:04Z and nothing under `~/.copilot` changed. So every `-p` run refreshes again from the stored refresh token. That works with Sentry, but against a server that rotates refresh tokens it would break the stored grant (same class of problem as #5079). It also means a `-p` refresh doesn't help ACP the way an interactive refresh does.

## Related issues

- #4203: generic "expired access token forces interactive re-auth instead of refresh_token grant" (1.0.71). On 1.0.102 the interactive CLI and `-p` refresh fine for me; ACP still doesn't, so what's left of #4203 may be this ACP path.
- #4994: the authorization page opens on every ACP session since 1.0.89, with a valid token and no refresh token. Different trigger (an expired token with a working refresh token), same ACP handler that goes straight to the browser.
- #5192: tokens from an ACP sign-in are never persisted. Here the token is persisted (by the interactive CLI) and ACP reads it, but never refreshes it.

issues.title: `copilot --resume` without an ID drops into a new empty session; the Sessions list is auto-replaced after ~2s and the trust prompt takes the first Enter
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since the unified Sessions browser became the default, `copilot --resume` without a session ID no longer lets me pick a session. Each launch creates a new empty session ("Session 1"). The Sessions list is shown for only ~2 seconds, then the UI switches to that new session's "Current" tab. In a folder that is not remembered as trusted, the "Confirm folder trust" dialog then appears on top of the empty session and consumes my first Enter, so I end up in a blank new session before I can use ↑/↓ on the list.
 
 The list is still reachable with Tab or /resume, but this is not obvious, and it makes `--resume` look like it simply creates a new session.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

 1. cd into a local folder that has earlier Copilot sessions and is not remembered as trusted.
 2. Run `copilot --resume` (no session ID).
 3. After a "Resuming session…" spinner, the Sessions tab appears. The highlighted first row is a brand-new empty "Session 1".
 4. About 2 seconds later the UI switches to the "[Current]" tab and shows "Confirm folder trust".
 5. Press Enter ("1. Yes").
 6. Result: I am in the new empty session. ↑/↓ does nothing here. Pressing Tab (footer: "tab next tab") or typing /resume brings back the Sessions list, where ↑/↓ works.

### Expected behavior

`copilot --resume` without an ID should keep the session list focused until I choose a session or cancel. It should not auto-switch to the newly created placeholder session, and the folder-trust prompt should not take focus or Enter from the picker. Alternatively, it should reopen the most recent session for the current repository, as the 1.0.64 changelog describes for --continue/--resume.

### Additional context

- macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), x86_64; Terminal.app 470.2; zsh; installed via Homebrew cask, auto-updated to 1.0.102.
 - Timeline from a 120x40 pty capture: ~0.7s "Resuming session…"; ~1.1s Sessions tab with list; ~3.0s switch to "[Current]" plus the trust dialog. I could not test a remembered-trusted folder, so I don't know whether the auto-switch is caused by the trust prompt.
 - Each launch also creates an empty session directory (only workspace.yaml, no events.jsonl). Related: #3908, #5204.
 - Changelog 1.0.100: "Use the unified Sessions browser by default for /sessions, /session, and /resume." I did not bisect other versions.
 - Workarounds: `copilot --continue`, `copilot --resume <name|id>`.

issues.title: Gemini continuation and /compact fail with "Tool name is required" on mixed-model history
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A long-lived, mixed-model Copilot CLI session fails to continue with Gemini:

```text
400 Tool name is required for Gemini requests
{"message":"Tool name is required for Gemini requests","code":"invalid_tool_call_format"}
```

Multiple normal prompts fail before any new tool executes. Manual `/compact` also fails with the same error, so compaction does not provide recovery in this session.

The captured **failed compaction request** provides a useful triage lead: its history contains three GPT-originated `type: "custom"` / `custom.name: "apply_patch"` calls among ordinary function calls. All tool results have matching, preceding calls with nonempty names when both call types are accounted for. This is not evidence of a missing tool name in the persisted call itself.

**Suspected area:** cross-model history normalization / Gemini request adaptation. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause or an assertion that two independent bugs exist.

### Affected version

- Copilot CLI **1.0.86**, verified from the running process's loaded `.../1.0.86/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node`.
- Session originally created under 1.0.83 and subsequently resumed across updates; the version that introduced the failure is unknown.
- Model at failure: `gemini-3.8-flash`.
- Earlier turns used `gpt-6-astra`, including built-in `apply_patch`.
- macOS **26.7**, Apple Silicon (`arm64`), tmux.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**Observed workflow, not yet a clean-room/minimal reproducer:**

1. Continue a long-lived session that has used both GPT and Gemini, with previous compactions and tool calls.
2. GPT turns in that history use built-in `apply_patch`, persisted as custom tool calls.
3. Continue later with Gemini. Conversation-only rewinds and process resume/restart occurred before the reported failures. Their causal role has not been isolated; switching models alone is not claimed to reproduce this.
4. Submit a normal follow-up prompt. It fails with `invalid_tool_call_format`.
5. Retry later: the same error recurs.
6. Run `/compact`: it also fails, with `session.compaction_complete.success: false` and `error: "host-rethrow: 400 Tool name is required for Gemini requests"`.

The real environment includes user hooks, plugins, and MCP servers. These have not been eliminated in a fresh configuration. This report does not establish reproducibility in a stock installation.

### Expected behavior

A session created through supported model switching, tool use, resume, and rewind should remain usable. Historical custom tool calls should be translated into a supported representation when replayed to another provider, or the CLI should provide an actionable compatibility/recovery error without silently discarding history.

### Additional context

#### Captured request metadata

For the failed manual compaction, `model.model_call_failure` records:

```json
{
  "model": "gemini-3.8-flash",
  "status": 400,
  "api_endpoint": "/chat/completions",
  "transport": "http",
  "failure_kind": "api",
  "badRequestKind": "structured_error",
  "errorCode": "invalid_tool_call_format"
}
```

Parsing that event's JSON-encoded `requestMessages` locally:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Messages | 506 |
| Assistant tool calls | 258 |
| Function calls with nonempty `function.name` | 255 |
| Custom calls with nonempty `custom.name` | 3, all `apply_patch` |
| Tool-result messages | 258 |
| Results without a matching preceding named call | 0 |

The three custom calls are at zero-based message indices 85, 107, and 115; their matching results immediately follow. All 258 result messages omit a standalone `name`; each has a `tool_call_id` that resolves to its preceding call. This alone is not asserted to be invalid in the OpenAI-shaped intermediate format.

**Synthetic structural illustration only** (not an executed reproducer; IDs, input, and output replaced):

```json
[
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "",
    "tool_calls": [{
      "id": "custom_call_example",
      "type": "custom",
      "custom": {
        "name": "apply_patch",
        "input": "<synthetic patch placeholder>"
      }
    }]
  },
  {
    "role": "tool",
    "tool_call_id": "custom_call_example",
    "content": "<synthetic result placeholder>"
  }
]
```

Please check whether the Gemini adapter handles `custom.name`, rather than assuming every historical call has `function.name`. The captured request does not establish which field the server rejected; it is not a capture of the final native Gemini payload.

#### Trace correlation

| UTC time, 2026-09-19 | Operation | Request ID | Service request ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21:44:48 | Normal prompt: HTTP 400 | `7B0D:345026:2C3E730:36BEE94:6AAF024C` | `138e7b2d-aebe-4123-97f2-8b61e81f383e` |
| 22:07:00 | Later normal prompt: HTTP 400 | `7F6E:178245:2FFDC9D:3C2C1FB:6AAF077F` | `4b9439d5-7085-490b-8815-a43414f9cea4` |
| 22:07:20 | Manual compaction: HTTP 400 | `4DFE:3B6359:2FDC2F9:3C0B645:6AAF0797` | `90eafc3c-9e21-4633-a126-9f3bfc45a047` |

#### Important limits / ruled-out inference

- Some persisted event `parentId` links are dangling, but following those links alone incorrectly suggested an orphaned image-view result. The actual captured request contains both image-view calls, their names, and their results. Therefore, an orphan caused by rewind is **not established**.
- Successful later Gemini turns exist after the original custom-tool turns. This is not established as an immediate model-switch failure; resume/replay or runtime-version differences may matter.
- No controlled retry with only the custom calls normalized has been performed. No successful model-switch workaround is claimed.
- The live session was inspected read-only. No repair, event deletion, or history rewrite was performed for this investigation.
- No original conversation, image, patch contents, filesystem paths, or configuration is attached. Only structural findings and request-correlation metadata are included.

Related but not established as duplicates: [broader Gemini 400 report](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4155) and [older tool-use/result corruption report](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2543).

issues.title: Feature request: option to pin input box to the top of the screen
issues.body:
## Problem

The Copilot CLI input box is always rendered at the bottom of the screen. During long sessions, everything the user cares about — the line being typed, the latest output — is at the very bottom edge of the display. This forces a constant downward gaze / neck angle, which is genuinely fatiguing on large monitors.

Add a setting (e.g. `/settings input_position top` or a config key) to pin the input box to the **top** of the screen, with the conversation/output flowing below it — similar to Warp's "pin input to top" option or chat-style interfaces.

## Alternatives considered

- Shrinking the terminal window so the bottom edge sits at eye level (workable but ugly)
- Using the desktop app / VS Code chat instead (but the CLI TUI is the preferred workflow)

## Context

- Copilot CLI 1.0.102
- macOS, running in Canario/Warp

Thanks for considering!

issues.title: Voice: make the transcription language configurable (currently hard-coded to `"auto"`)
issues.body:
## Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Voice dictation (`/voice`) works with the multilingual Nemotron streaming model, but the voice worker always starts
the live transcription session with automatic language detection. For non-English speakers this means the first
sentence of every dictation is recognised noticeably worse.

**Environment:** Copilot CLI 1.0.101 (the same code is in 1.0.96–1.0.100), foundry-local-sdk 2.1.0, model
`nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b-generic-cpu:3`, macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon).

`voice-engine.worker.js` → `openStreamingSession()` sets the language before starting the session (minified):

```js
let r = t.createAudioClient().createLiveTranscriptionSession();
r.settings.language = "auto";
try { await r.start() } catch (i) { … }
```

The model is prompt-conditioned on a language id (`lang_id`). With `"auto"` it commits to a language only at the end
of the first sentence (it emits a `<de-DE>` tag there), so the first sentence is decoded without the language prior.

Measured with a small Node script that makes the same SDK calls as the worker (`createLiveTranscriptionSession`,
`settings.language`, `start`, `append` in real-time-paced 100 ms chunks of 16 kHz mono s16le) on German TTS samples,
each with 1 s of leading silence so that the whole first sentence reaches the model. Reference: *"Bitte prüfe, warum
der Build in der Pipeline fehlschlägt. Schau dir dazu die Logs im Kubernetes-Cluster an …"*. First sentence of the
result:

| `settings.language` | First sentence                                              |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `"auto"`            | Bitte prüfe, warum der Bult in der Pipeline **fehlt**.      |
| `"de-DE"` or `"de"` | Bitte prüfe, warum der Bult in der Pipeline **fehlschlägt**. |
| `"en-US"`           | German speech is dropped                                    |
| unset or numeric    | no text at all                                              |

The difference is reproducible; the rest of the text is identical once the model has detected the language.

## Proposed solution

Make the language configurable: a setting (e.g. `voice.language`, default `"auto"`) and/or `/voice language de-DE`,
passed to `settings.language`. Validate the value against the tags the model supports, since invalid values silently
produce no text and a wrong language drops speech.

## Additional context

- Related: #3658 (multilingual voice input). This request is narrower: the bundled model already handles other
  languages; only the language hint is hard-coded.
- A user-level workaround exists: patching the minified worker in the CLI package cache, replacing
  `X.settings.language="auto"` with `X.settings.language="de-DE"`. It works, but has to be re-applied after every CLI
  update.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

If I have a hook that keeps agents from doing a dangerous command and then tell Copilot to run the command via a background/task or general-purpose agent, the sub-agent can run the command no problem.

This feels like a security vulnerability: just jailbreak the agent or even have it get frustrated that something doesn't work, and have it spawn a new agent to do the dirty deed for it.

Any `preToolUse` hook that enforces policy (file permissions, lock checks, security scanning) is bypassed entirely by sub-agents. This applies to all sub-agent types tested: task (Haiku), general-purpose (Sonnet). Both global (~/.copilot/hooks/) and project-level (.github/hooks/) hooks are affected. `sessionStart` hooks also do not fire for sub-agents.

### Affected version

1.0.37

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a global hook that logs all preToolUse invocations:
File: ~/.copilot/hooks/hooks.json
```json
 {
   "version": 1,
   "hooks": {
     "preToolUse": [
       {
         "type": "command",
         "powershell": "$i = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd() | ConvertFrom-Json; $ts = Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss'; Add-Content -Path 
\"$env:USERPROFILE\\.copilot\\hooks\\hook-test.log\" -Value \"[$ts] preToolUse | tool=$($i.toolName) | sid=$env:COPILOT_SESSION_ID\"",
         "timeoutSec": 5
       }
     ]
   }
 }
```
2. Create a test file:
```
 echo "// original" > test-hook.txt
```
3. Start a new Copilot CLI session (restart if needed to pick up hooks).
4. Verify the hook fires for the main session:
  - Ask Copilot: Edit test-hook.txt and change the comment to "// main session"
  - Check the log: `Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.copilot\hooks\hook-test.log"`
  - Expected: Log entry showing `preToolUse | tool=edit` (main CLI session logs show up).
5. Now ask Copilot to dispatch a sub-agent that edits the same file:
  - Ask Copilot: Use the task tool to dispatch a sub-agent that edits test-hook.txt and changes the comment to "// sub-agent was here"
  - Check the log again: `Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.copilot\hooks\hook-test.log"`
  - Expected: New log entry showing `preToolUse | tool=edit` from the sub-agent's edit call. Actual: ❌ No new entry. Only the parent session's `preToolUse | tool=task` is logged (for dispatching the task), but the sub-agent's edit call within that task produces no hook invocation.
6. Verify the sub-agent's edit went through unguarded: `Get-Content test-hook.txt`
  - Shows: `// sub-agent was here`

### Expected behavior

All hook triggers (preToolUse, postToolUse, sessionStart, etc.) should fire for tool calls made by sub-agents (spawned via the task tool) with the same semantics as the parent session. A preToolUse hook that returns {"permissionDecision":"deny"} should block the sub-agent's tool call, not just the parent's.

In my case, only parent session gets any hook controls. Sub-agents are uninhibited and untraceable.

### Additional context

- Windows 11
- Windows Terminal

issues.title: Session wedged: task subagent with unknown model id falls back to 128k default caps and fails the whole turn with 'Request exceeds the model's prompt budget'

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running interactive session, the session gets stuck. On every turn where the main agent delegates to a `task` subagent, the whole turn fails with a prompt-budget error. The main context is far below its own limit. The cause appears to be a `task` call with a `model` id that isn't in the catalog. The runtime doesn't reject it. Instead it quietly falls back to default capabilities (128k), and the request then goes over that limit.

**What we saw (from local process logs and session events):**

1. The main agent model is `claude-opus-5.5`, picked in the model picker, with `contextTier` long_context (1M context, `maxPromptTokens` 968000). The main context is about 177k tokens, well within budget. Auto-compaction is measured against the long-context limit (earlier compactions logged `tokenLimit` 922000), so compaction never triggers.
2. The main model's response contains a `task` tool call (usage record `toolCounts {"task":1}`, and `{"task":2}` on the retry). Both responses also had `finishReason: "content_filter"` / `contentFilterTriggered: true`. That may or may not be related, but it looks suspicious.
3. Right after that, the process log shows this warning twice per turn:
   ```
   [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::native_message_turn] turn model is in neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog, nor the session's excluded-model capture; falling back to default capabilities and the chat-completions wire {"model":"claude-opus-4.8","latest_model_list_fetch_succeeded":true,"picker_models":23,"unfiltered_models":39,"catalog_only_models":6}
   ```
   So the subagent was requested with a model id (`claude-opus-4.8`) that isn't in the catalog. The `task` tool's own `model` enum doesn't list it either, but tool-argument validation didn't reject it.
4. Then a session-level error ends the user's turn:
   ```
   session.error {"errorType":"query","message":"Execution failed: Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (143299 tokens; limit 128000). Reduce context or compact before continuing."}
   ```
   No `subagent.started` event is emitted. When the user prompts again, it fails the same way (143360 / 128000).
5. **Result:** the session is stuck. Every turn where the model delegates fails. The error tells the user to compact, but the main context is nowhere near its own limit. `/compact` doesn't fix the real cause, so the advice is misleading.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.100, macOS arm64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an interactive session on a long-context model (for example `claude-opus-5.5` with the long_context tier).
2. Build up a moderately large context (about 140k+ tokens), still well under the main model's limit.
3. Have the main agent call the `task` tool with a `model` value that isn't a valid catalog id (seen here: `claude-opus-4.8`).
4. The turn fails with `Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (~143k tokens; limit 128000)`, and the warning above appears in the log. Every later turn that delegates fails the same way.

### Expected behavior

- An unknown `model` value on the `task` tool is rejected at argument validation and returned to the model as a tool error, so it can retry with a valid id. It should not be silently mapped to default 128k capabilities.
- If a subagent request goes over its model's budget, that shows up as a failure of that one `task` tool call, not as a fatal session/turn error.
- The error message says which request and model hit the limit (subagent vs. main), so users aren't told to compact the wrong context.
- It would also help to know why the subagent prompt reaches about 143k tokens. Does a subagent inherit or fork the parent context?

### Additional context

Workaround: start a new session, or make sure subagent model ids are valid catalog ids.

Possibly related: #5201 (prompt-budget rejection has `errorType: "query"` and no stable error code) and #5127 (the same "neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog" fallback, in BYOK/SDK mode).

issues.title: Non-PTY interactive build spins indefinitely and WSL process tree survives editor restart

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

A Copilot SDK session in VS Code launched an OpenWrt prerequisite check through a non-PTY shell into WSL. With no build configuration, the build system invoked its interactive configuration menu implicitly. The menu process ran continuously on one CPU for approximately 10.5 hours with no further log output, while the chat continued to show background work.

The process tree was later found orphaned inside WSL after the editor had been restarted. This is a report about detecting and recovering from non-interactive background work, not a request to terminate intentionally detached services.

## Affected version and environment

* Windows x64, VS Code, Copilot SDK agent session, WSL Ubuntu 22.04.
* The installed VS Code version at reporting time is 1.143.0. The exact editor and bundled runtime versions at the start of the incident were not captured.
* The standalone `copilot --version` shim cannot find a standalone CLI installation. This does not identify the version of the runtime bundled with VS Code.
* This was not the built-in Agent mode's interactive terminal tool.

## Observed sequence

1. A fresh OpenWrt v24.10.8 source tree had no `.config`.
1. The agent ran the equivalent of the following command in a non-interactive WSL process. Paths below are placeholders, not original local paths:

   ```sh
   cd /tmp/repro
   make prereq > /tmp/repro-prereq.log 2>&1
   ```

1. The observed process chain was:

   ```text
   sh
     make prereq
       make V=s menuconfig
         sh -c .../mconf ...
           scripts/config/mconf
   ```

1. OpenWrt's configuration prerequisite fell back to `make menuconfig` because `.config` was absent and the default configuration could not be copied. Consequently the requested prerequisite checks had not actually started.
1. The `mconf` process's stdin was a pipe, not a TTY. It remained runnable, accumulated approximately 10.5 CPU hours, and produced no further log output after the initial menu output.
1. A later inspection found the outer shell's parent was WSL's `/init`; the editor had been restarted, but the Linux process tree remained.
1. Sending TERM to the individually verified processes stopped them. There was no compiler output, package output, or successful prerequisite result to recover.

After the diagnosis was supplied to the agent, it launched an equivalent unconfigured `make prereq` command again, producing the same `mconf` chain and several more minutes of CPU activity. That repetition is an agent execution/reasoning failure; it is not evidence of a particular runtime lifecycle bug.

## Reproduction guidance

The sequence above is the observed reproduction, not a newly verified reproduction on the latest runtime.

To investigate independently, use only a disposable checkout of public OpenWrt v24.10.8 sources, without a `.config`, and invoke the prerequisite target through a non-PTY SDK shell. A source checkout alone is not sufficient: build-host dependencies must be present so that execution can reach `mconf`.

**Do not repeat the unbounded command above.** On a Linux host with GNU `timeout`, bound the experiment, for example:

```sh
cd /tmp/repro
timeout --kill-after=2s 30s make prereq </dev/null > /tmp/repro-prereq.log 2>&1
```

This EOF-input variant is a proposed diagnostic, not a claim that its stdin conditions exactly match the original runtime's open pipe. If the timeout expires before `mconf` starts, that does not reproduce the incident.

For lifecycle investigation, record the task's execution mode, attachment mode, task ID and process tree before using the host's task-specific termination action. Verify termination of the descendants in WSL, not just the Windows launcher or the chat spinner. If testing editor restart, preserve the hard timeout.

## Expected behavior

* Non-PTY execution should clearly explain that an interactive menu cannot be completed through that execution channel.
* A long-running task should expose enough state to distinguish an active build from a terminal-dependent process that is not making progress. Lack of output alone is not proof of a hang.
* A task-specific stop operation should provide a verifiable result for the task and its owned subprocesses, including subprocesses across the Windows/WSL boundary.
* The host should document what happens to attached work when the editor/session disconnects and how to find and stop surviving work after reconnecting. Intentionally detached work should remain distinct.
* A command deadline should be distinct from the initial wait before a synchronous shell is reported as background work.

## Limits of the diagnosis

* I cannot establish from the available record whether the host successfully invoked task cancellation before the restart.
* The original shell's attachment mode was not captured. I am not claiming that an explicitly detached task violated its documented lifetime.
* `mconf` consuming CPU is established; the exact ncurses input-loop mechanism has not been instrumented.
* This is not evidence of continuous model inference or a quantified token charge during those hours.
* I have not reproduced this on the latest Insiders build.
* Public SDK wrappers and VS Code integration code do not by themselves establish the root cause of runtime process ownership or WSL descendant cleanup. Please route this to the runtime or host owner as appropriate.

The application-level mitigation is to initialize and verify the build configuration non-interactively before running prerequisites, with an explicit deadline. Merely redirecting output or changing a shell's initial wait does not solve the interactive fallback.

## Related reports

* github/copilot-sdk#2859: companion documentation mitigation for non-PTY execution and recovery; not a runtime cancellation fix.
* microsoft/vscode#341333: non-PTY commands cannot receive terminal Ctrl+C; the maintainer points to background-task termination instead.
* microsoft/vscode#341462: interactive terminal access in Copilot SDK sessions.
* github/copilot-sdk#2822: cancellation of background **agents**, a different lifetime from the shell process reported here.

All paths are generic. No private project sources, firmware, device identifiers, screenshots, session IDs, raw logs, or original local directories are included.

issues.title: Interactive autopilot stops after 600s while a background subagent is still running (regression in 1.0.102)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since 1.0.102, interactive autopilot stops whenever a background subagent runs for more than 600 seconds. The subagent is still working normally when this happens. The CLI shows:

> Autopilot stopped after 600s waiting for background tasks. Set COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to change the limit.

A common pattern is for the main agent to start a background agent (for example, to implement part of a feature) and then end its turn to wait for the result. Any subagent that needs more than 10 minutes now ends the autopilot run, and I have to continue it manually.

This worked in 1.0.101 and 1.0.100. The 1.0.102 changelog doesn't mention any change to this behavior, so it looks unintended.

### Affected version

1.0.102

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start Copilot CLI interactively and turn on autopilot (`/autopilot` or shift+tab).
2. Give it a task where the main agent starts a background subagent (`task` with `mode: "background"`) that takes more than 10 minutes.
3. Let the main agent end its turn to wait for the subagent.
4. After 600 seconds, autopilot stops with the message above, even though the subagent is still running.

### Expected behavior

Interactive autopilot keeps waiting for in-flight background agents and continues when they finish, as it did in 1.0.101. If a cap is needed, a running subagent that is making progress shouldn't count as stuck, or the cap should be opt-in for interactive sessions.

### Additional context

- In 1.0.101, `COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` / `autopilot_background_timeout` appear to apply only to prompt mode (`-p`). In 1.0.102 the native runtime adds new autopilot continuation logic, and the stop message and `autopilot_background_timeout` warning first appear there.
- Workaround: `export COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600` (or higher) before launching.
- The limit can't be turned off. `COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0` gives a 0 ms wait, not an unlimited one. Negative or non-numeric values fall back to 600 s.
- Related but different: #4628 (prompt mode on 1.0.80, closed).

issues.title: Startup reports disabled MCP servers as “blocked by policy” and repeats the warnings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Description

Copilot CLI displays organization-policy warnings at startup even though every configured third-party MCP server is explicitly disabled through `disabledMcpServers` in the user settings. The same pair of warnings appears twice during startup.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI: **1.0.101**
- OS: **Windows**
- Shell: **PowerShell**
- MCP configuration includes user-configured and plugin-provided servers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have third-party MCP servers configured.
2. Disable all of them through the CLI, persisting their names in `disabledMcpServers`.
3. Start a new interactive CLI session with an account for which the CLI reports that third-party MCP servers are disallowed by organization policy.
4. Observe the startup warnings.

### Actual behavior

Startup displays:

```text
Third-party MCP servers are disabled by your organization's Copilot policy. Only built-in servers are available.

9 MCP servers were blocked by policy: ...
```

Both messages appear twice in the observed startup. Every server named in the warning is already explicitly disabled in the user settings.

### Expected behavior

- Already-disabled servers should not be counted as servers blocked by policy at startup.
- An unchanged policy notice should not be repeated during startup refreshes.
- If a general policy notice is intentional, it should be clearly informational and distinguish organization restrictions from user-disabled servers.

### Investigation notes

Read-only inspection of the locally installed **1.0.101** bundle found:

- In `cli-main.js`, `reloadMcpServersExclusive()` passes the configured server map to the policy filter without disabled-server settings. Disable settings are handed to the native lifecycle afterward.
- The interactive initialization path emits the general policy warning based on policy allowance, without checking whether any third-party servers are enabled.
- The general and filtered-server warnings have no deduplication at these emission points, allowing repeated initialization/reload calls to emit them again.

These observations explain the reporting behavior; **they do not establish that disabled servers are launched**. The exact trigger for the second initialization/reload has not been identified.

### Related issues

- github/copilot-cli#2567 - incorrect startup "blocked by policy" reporting in a different configuration scenario.
- github/copilot-cli#4907 - repeated MCP lifecycle notifications.

issues.title: Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (5-minute cache expires during normal interactive use)

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Claude prompt caching in Copilot CLI appears to use Anthropic's default **5-minute** cache TTL. In normal interactive use (read the answer, think, write the next prompt) gaps of more than 5 minutes are common, so the full conversation gets re-written to cache on almost every turn instead of being read from cache.

I measured this with `copilot -p` / `--resume` in fresh sessions (~35k-token context), sending a follow-up after different idle gaps, and reading `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` from the local session usage data. Two independent runs gave identical results:

| Idle gap | Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1-sol / GPT-6-sol / GPT-5.6-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 2 min | ~95% cache read | ~95% cache read |
| 11 min | **0% cache read** (~100% cache write) | ~95% cache read |
| ~85 min | 0% | 0% |

My broader session history (Claude 5.x, CLI) shows the same pattern: 98% cache read for gaps < 4 min vs ~1% for gaps of 6–60 min.

Anthropic supports a 1-hour TTL (`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}`). VS Code Copilot Chat already has experimental settings for this (`github.copilot.chat.anthropic.promptCaching.extendedTtl` / `extendedTtlMessages`), though they currently miss Claude 5.x models (microsoft/vscode#340830, fix in microsoft/vscode#340831). Copilot CLI has no equivalent option.

### Proposed solution

Add an option in Copilot CLI (config setting and/or env var) to use the 1-hour cache TTL for Claude models, covering the Claude 5.x family. Consider making it the default for interactive sessions, since the higher write cost (2x vs 1.25x) is usually recovered after one or two follow-up turns with a pause longer than 5 minutes.

### Example prompts or workflows

Any interactive session with a large context where the user pauses longer than 5 minutes between prompts (reviewing diffs, testing changes, meetings).

### Additional context

- Related: #3808 (prompt caching for Claude), #4724 (auto-compact on idle aligned to cache TTL)
- Triggered by this discussion: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xauf3s/anthropic_caching_is_this_a_bad_joke/
- Tested with Copilot CLI 1.0.102-1 on Windows.
