issues.title: TUI: a user-scrolled chat viewport shifts on every append (overflow-anchor forced to none)
issues.body:
**What happens**

Scroll up in the chat so you're reading something, then let the agent keep working. The text under your view marches upward — you have to chase it back down. It happens on every append, so with a streaming agent it's effectively impossible to read anything that was produced more than a few seconds ago.

This is *not* the auto-follow-to-bottom behaviour: that is correctly disengaged. The problem is that a user-scrolled viewport is anchored to the *bottom* of the scrollable content rather than to the content you're looking at.

**Why**

The chat message view builds its scroll hook with anchoring forced off:

```js
const Sn = e$e({ working: () => !0, overflowAnchor: "none" });
```

and the hook's setter takes that literally and returns early, so the dynamic branch is never reached for the chat:

```js
w = x => {
  const k = <overflowAnchor option>;
  if (k === "none") { x.style.overflowAnchor = "none"; return }   // ← taken
  if (k === "auto") { x.style.overflowAnchor = "auto"; return }
  x.style.overflowAnchor = o.userScrolled ? "auto" : "none"       // ← dead for the chat
}
```

With `overflow-anchor: none` the scroll container preserves `scrollTop` absolutely, so appending to the transcript shifts the visible content up by the height of each appended block.

Secondary, but related: `userScrolled` (which gates the auto-jump to the bottom) is only ever set from a `wheel` listener with `deltaY < 0`:

```js
y = x => { if (x.deltaY >= 0) return; ... p() }      // only wired to "wheel"
p = () => { ... o.userScrolled || (a("userScrolled", true), e.onUserInteracted?.()) }
```

There is no `scroll` listener on the container, so the `messages_page_up` / `messages_half_page_up` / `messages_line_up` actions never set it. That's a separate issue, but it's moot for the symptom above, because that view can never anchor at all.

**Environment**

- opencode 1.18.35
- kitty + zellij, Wayland
- Checked 1.19.4's release notes: no scroll/follow/viewport fix mentioned.

**What I verified locally**

The literal `overflowAnchor:"none"` occurs exactly once in the shipped binary, and `"none"` → `"auto"` is the same byte length, so I applied it as a 4-byte, single-site patch (no other byte changes; file size identical) to confirm the diagnosis rather than assume it. Result worth recording: **it substantially improves things but doesn't fully fix it.** Before, the view shifted every few seconds; after, it only shifts on very large appends (a big tool result landing at once). So browser scroll anchoring alone isn't sufficient here — which is the actionable part below.

**Suggested fix**

1. Stop forcing `overflowAnchor: "none"` for the chat: pass `"auto"`, or omit the option and let the dynamic `userScrolled` branch apply.
2. For large appends, don't rely on CSS anchoring alone. Measure `scrollHeight` before and after the append and compensate `scrollTop` by the delta when the user is not at the bottom. That is robust for a single very large block, where anchoring can fail (the anchor node itself may be replaced or re-keyed by the list render).

I'm not submitting a PR since I only have the minified bundle, but the call site is unique, so it should be easy to find in source: the `e$e({ working, overflowAnchor: "none" })` construction in the session/message view (the same object that calls `Sn.resume()` on session change), plus the `overflow-anchor` setter in the scroll hook.

issues.title: server: GET /api/vcs returns {"branch":{}} until the location's plugins activate, while /api/vcs/branch already answers
issues.body:
### Description The first `GET /api/vcs` for a directory that the server has not served yet returns `200 {"branch":{}}`. It keeps returning that for about 1 s, until the location's plugin activation registers the git provider and the cached summary refreshes. During that window, `GET /api/vcs/branch` for the same location already returns `["main"]`. A client that reads the summary once gets an answer that looks like "no branch" or "not a repository", with no signal that the answer is not final. ``` [ 311 ms] vcs.get {"branch":{}} vcs.branch.list [] [ 766 ms] vcs.get {"branch":{}} vcs.branch.list ["main"] [ 1061 ms] vcs.get {"provider":"git","branch":{"current":"main","default":"main"}} vcs.branch.list ["main"] ``` The window reopens for every directory that the server has not seen before, not only after a server start. What I found: - `vcs.get` returns a cached value ([handlers/vcs.ts#L11-L18](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/server/src/handlers/vcs.ts#L11-L18) → `info()`, [vcs.ts#L169-L171](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L169-L171)). The cache starts as `{ branch: {} }` ([L61](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L61)). - Only `refresh()` fills the cache ([L122-L143](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L122-L143)). `refresh()` runs from the state notify after a provider registers ([L84](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L84)), or on a `HEAD` change. The git provider registers during the location's asynchronous plugin activation ([plugin/vcs/git.ts#L34-L35](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/git.ts#L34-L35)). [plugin/service.ts#L29-L33](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/plugin/service.ts#L29-L33) describes this exact early-request case. The handler does not wait for activation. - `branches()` reads the provider on every call ([L177-L187](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L177-L187)), so it answers as soon as the provider is registered. The summary waits for the deferred `refresh()` and the git calls that it runs. - During that window, the response has no `provider`. After a refresh, a detached HEAD is `{"provider":"git","branch":{"default":"main"}}`. So `provider` is the only thing that separates "not known yet" from a real answer, and that is not documented. This looks like the same class as #36117 (catalog reads return 200 with intermediate activation state), for a different route. Possible fixes, in order of preference: 1. In `vcs.get`, wait for plugin activation and for the first `refresh()` to finish before it answers, in the same way that `worktree` and the session entry points already wait on `Plugin.awaitActivation`. 2. Or compute `info()` from the provider when the cache has never been refreshed, as `branches()` already does. 3. At a minimum, document on `Vcs.Info` that an absent `provider` means "not determined yet". ### Plugins None (isolated config, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={}`). ### OpenCode version 2.0.15 (`opencode serve`). The relevant code is unchanged in v2.0.16 and on `v2` at `19a9e41c28`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start `opencode serve` with its working directory outside the repository. 2. Create a git repository with one commit on `main`. 3. Poll `GET /api/vcs?location[directory]=` and `GET /api/vcs/branch?location[directory]=` every 100 ms. 4. The first samples of `/api/vcs` are `{"branch":{}}`, while `/api/vcs/branch` already returns `["main"]`.
Script (bun; starts an isolated opencode serve) ```ts // bun vcs-cold-location.ts (starts an isolated `opencode serve`, then touches a git repo it has not seen yet) import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs" import { tmpdir } from "node:os" import { join } from "node:path" const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "oc-vcs-")) const repo = join(root, "repo") mkdirSync(repo) Bun.spawnSync(["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main"], { cwd: repo }) Bun.spawnSync(["git", "-c", "user.name=r", "-c", "user.email=r@r", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "init"], { cwd: repo }) const port = 20000 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 20000) const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}` const headers = { authorization: "Basic " + btoa("opencode:repro") } const server = Bun.spawn([process.env.OPENCODE_BIN ?? "opencode", "serve", "--hostname", "127.0.0.1", "--port", `${port}`], { cwd: root, // not the repo, so the repo's location is cold on first request stdout: "ignore", stderr: "ignore", env: { ...process.env, OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD: "repro", OPENCODE_DB: join(root, "opencode.db"), XDG_DATA_HOME: join(root, "data"), XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(root, "config"), XDG_STATE_HOME: join(root, "state"), XDG_CACHE_HOME: join(root, "cache"), OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: "{}", OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH: "1", }, }) const get = (path: string) => fetch(`${base}${path}`, { headers }).then((r) => r.text()) while (!(await fetch(`${base}/api/info`, { headers }).then((r) => r.ok, () => false))) await Bun.sleep(100) const at = `location[directory]=${encodeURIComponent(repo)}` const t0 = performance.now() let last = "" for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) { const vcs = await get(`/api/vcs?${at}`) const branches = await get(`/api/vcs/branch?${at}`) const line = `vcs.get ${JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(vcs).data)} vcs.branch.list ${JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(branches).data)}` if (line !== last) console.log(`[${Math.round(performance.now() - t0).toString().padStart(5)} ms] ${line}`) last = line if (JSON.parse(vcs).data.provider) break await Bun.sleep(100) } server.kill() ```
### Screenshot and/or share link Not applicable (HTTP API). ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200. The same raw `{"branch":{}}` was seen on Linux with 2.0.2. ### Terminal Not applicable (HTTP API; the script runs under bun 1.3.8).

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### Description
Currently, OpenCode Go provides a feature to configure permissions for each API key, while the model execution location (Global vs. Europe&United States) is managed separately as a global system setting. 

I would like to request an enhancement to **integrate the model execution location toggle directly into the existing API key permission settings**.

## Summary

Please re-land Brave Search as a built-in websearch provider. PR #48222 implemented it completely and was closed by the automated stale-PR cleanup (>1 month old, <2 positive reactions) — it was never reviewed on its merits. Brave is also the provider used as the worked example for the pluggable WebSearch API in #35558.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.2
- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (darwin arm64)
- Install/channel: release (Homebrew tap, `channel=latest`)

## Reproduction

This is a feature request; the repro is the current ecosystem state:

1. `opencode api get /api/websearch/provider` → exa, firecrawl, parallel, tavily, tinyfish — no brave, despite `BRAVE_API_KEY` being set in the environment.
2. PR #48222 ("feat(core): add brave web search") shipped: key-gated registration (`BRAVE_API_KEY` / Brave integration, re-registering on credential change), result mapping to `WebSearch.Result`, integration with the existing rate-limit case, tests (`packages/core/test/plugin/websearch.test.ts`) and live verification against the real API via `opencode serve`.
3. It was closed 2026-10-09 by "Automated PR Cleanup" (age >1 month + fewer than 2 positive reactions). The bot's own comment invites a reply when the closure seems incorrect — this is that reply, in issue form, since the tracking issue #35038 is closed.

## Expected Behavior

Brave sits alongside the five current first-class providers: selectable via `"websearch": { "provider": "brave" }`, part of `"random"` selection and of the 429 → cooldown → failover path.

## Actual Behavior

No built-in Brave. Users must write their own plugin provider via `ctx.websearch.transform` — and plugin providers currently cannot participate in failover at all (#58327).

## Additional Context

- Demand evidence: we maintain a production Brave websearch provider plugin (key-gated registration, `WebSearch.Result` mapping, Brave→Tavily fallback) for a paying Brave Search API subscriber. Happy to contribute it back as a built-in.
- API quirk worth documenting: Brave authenticates with the custom `X-Subscription-Token` header (not `Authorization: Bearer`); endpoint `GET https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search`.
- Proposal: reopen #48222 (the implementation looked complete; the author disclosed Brave affiliation), or accept a resubmission against current v2 — I'm willing to prepare the PR if a maintainer confirms the shape.
- Related: #58327 (custom/plugin providers excluded from rate-limit failover — the same mechanism this PR wired Brave into).

issues.title: Mistral-family tool-call ID normalization collapses GLM call IDs to "chatcmplt" (400 "Duplicate tool call id" on Mistral Large)
issues.body:
### Description

Chat tool-call ID normalization (`packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`, from #45056) turns every ID into its first 9 alphanumeric characters when the model ID contains `mistral`, `devstral`, `codestral`, `pixtral` or `mixtral`. Mistral's own IDs are 9 random characters, so they come through intact, but IDs that share a prefix all collapse to the same value.

That happens with GLM served by Mistral (`zai-glm-5-3`, `zai-glm-5-3-flash`) through a gateway that names models by provider, e.g. magpie's `mistral/zai-glm-5-3-flash`: the model ID contains `mistral`, and GLM's call IDs look like `chatcmpl-tool-99557ad68a6e6efc`. Every call and every tool result in the history then goes out as `chatcmplt` (all 30 IDs in one captured request). As a result:

- Parallel calls in one assistant message share an ID, so their results can't be paired with them.
- Mistral's own models reject the history. A session that has used GLM fails on every request after a switch to `mistral/mistral-large-4-0`: `Mistral: Duplicate tool call id in assistant message` (400).

Mistral doesn't need the shortening for these IDs. Sent directly to api.mistral.ai (an assistant message with two `read` calls and their results):

| Tool-call IDs | mistral-large-4-0 | zai-glm-5-3, zai-glm-5-3-flash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| both `chatcmplt` (what OpenCode sends now) | 400 `Duplicate tool call id in assistant message` | 200 |
| GLM's originals (`chatcmpl-tool-<16 hex>`) | 200 | 200 |
| unique 9-character alphanumerics | 200 | 200 |

Keeping the normalized IDs unique would fix it, for example 9 characters derived from a hash of the whole ID instead of its prefix.

### Plugins

tokentracker (usage logging only)

### OpenCode version

2.1.3 (same code on `dev` at 33726e8)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use GLM on Mistral through a gateway that names it `mistral/...`, e.g. magpie's `magpie/mistral/zai-glm-5-3-flash` (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`).
2. Let it make a few tool calls, including parallel ones.
3. Switch the session to `mistral/mistral-large-4-0` and send a message (`opencode run --session <id> --fork -m 'magpie/mistral/mistral-large-4-0#high' "Please continue"`).
4. The request fails with `Mistral: Duplicate tool call id in assistant message` (400). Captured with a local endpoint, every `tool_calls[].id` and `tool_call_id` in the request is `chatcmplt`.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0.1

### Terminal

Ghostty 1.3.1

issues.title: openai: ChatGPT OAuth reports 400k context for long-context models
issues.body:
## Summary

When OpenAI models are used through a ChatGPT OAuth connection, OpenCode overwrites their effective context limits with 400,000 tokens. This affects multiple long-context OpenAI models whose catalog limits are approximately 1.05 million tokens, causing the TUI to substantially overstate context usage.

For example, approximately 140,000 tokens are shown as 35–36% usage instead of approximately 13–14%.

## Environment

- opencode version: `v0.0.0-beta-19192`
- OS: `Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)`
- Terminal: Ghostty (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`)
- Shell: `/bin/zsh`
- Install/channel: beta
- Active plugins: none found in project or global configuration

## Reproduction

1. Connect the `openai` provider using ChatGPT OAuth.
2. Select a long-context OpenAI model such as `openai/gpt-6-astra`, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, or `openai/gpt-5.5`.
3. Inspect the effective model metadata with:

   ```sh
   opencode2 api get /api/model |
     jq -r '.data[] | select(.providerID=="openai" and .limit.context==400000) | [.id,.limit.context,.limit.input,.limit.output] | @tsv'
   ```

4. Grow a session to approximately 140,000 tokens.
5. Observe the context usage percentage in the TUI.

## Expected Behavior

OpenCode should use the actual context limit supported by each model and connection rather than applying a blanket 400,000-token limit.

Models whose catalog metadata declares a 1,050,000-token context should report approximately 13–14% usage at roughly 140,000 tokens.

## Actual Behavior

The affected models report an effective limit of 400,000 context tokens and 272,000 input tokens. On the tested installation, this includes:

```text
gpt-6-astra
gpt-6-astra-fast
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-sol-fast
gpt-5.6-luna
gpt-5.6-luna-fast
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-terra-fast
gpt-5.5
gpt-5.5-fast
gpt-5.4
gpt-5.4-fast
```

For example, the API reports:

```json
{"id":"gpt-6-astra","providerID":"openai","limit":{"context":400000,"input":272000,"output":128000},"baseURL":"https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"}
```

The TUI percentage arithmetic appears correct: it divides the latest token count by `model.limit.context`. The inflated percentage comes from the effective model limit.

## Additional Context

The OpenAI provider's ChatGPT OAuth catalog transform applies a blanket override to eligible models:

```ts
draft.limit = { ...draft.limit, context: 400_000, input: 272_000 }
```

This discards model-specific catalog limits. For example, several affected models declare:

```json
{"context":1050000,"input":922000,"output":128000}
```

This is consistently reproducible across multiple OpenAI models connected through ChatGPT OAuth. No user-defined model or provider limit overrides are configured.

issues.title: MCP OAuth: missing scope in token response causes repeated browser re-authentication
issues.body:
### Description

# MCP OAuth: missing `scope` in token response causes repeated browser re-authentication

## Summary

When an OAuth provider omits the optional `scope` field from its token response, OpenCode skips the stored refresh token after the access token expires and opens the browser for a full authorization flow.

This occurs with **AWS Cognito + Bedrock AgentCore Gateway**, causing re-authentication approximately every hour despite a valid refresh token with a 30-day lifetime.

## Environment

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenCode | `2.1.3` |
| OS | Linux `7.0.0-38-generic` (`x64`) |
| Shell | `/usr/bin/zsh` |
| Terminal | `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor` |
| Install/channel | `latest` |
| Active plugins | `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest` |
| MCP server | AWS Bedrock AgentCore Gateway |
| OAuth provider | AWS Cognito User Pool |
| OAuth client | Pre-registered public client with PKCE |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a remote MCP server backed by AWS Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, using a Cognito User Pool and a pre-registered public PKCE client.
2. Authenticate through `/mcps`:
   - The authorization code exchange succeeds.
   - The access token and refresh token are persisted.
   - The token response omits `scope`.
3. Wait for the access token to expire—one hour with the current Cognito configuration.
4. Trigger a connection to the MCP server.

## Expected behavior

OpenCode exchanges the stored refresh token for a new access token and reconnects without browser interaction.

## Actual behavior

1. OpenCode sends the expired access token.
2. The gateway returns `403 insufficient_scope`.
3. OpenCode opens the browser for a full authorization flow.
4. **No refresh token exchange is observed in the logs.**

This repeats approximately every hour, even though the refresh token remains valid.

## Suspected root cause

The behavior appears to result from missing scope metadata interacting with the newer MCP SDK’s step-up authorization logic.

### 1. Requested scope is not retained when the token response omits it

In `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts`, `toCredential()` (around line 248) stores scope from `input.scope`, which comes from the token response.

Cognito omits this field, so the persisted credential has no scope metadata, even though scopes were requested during authorization.

### 2. Missing scope triggers forced re-authorization in the MCP SDK

In `@modelcontextprotocol/client` v2.0.0, `streamableHttp.ts`, `_stepUpAuthorizeInner()` (around line 416):

1. Reads `tokens.scope`, which is `undefined`.
2. Computes `unionScope` from the stored scope and the challenge scope.
3. Evaluates `isStrictScopeSuperset(unionScope, tokens?.scope)` as `true`: the missing stored scope is treated as an empty set.
4. Sets `forceReauthorization = true`.

In `auth.ts`, `authInternal()` (around line 1305), the refresh-token branch requires `!forceReauthorization`. Consequently, the refresh-token exchange is skipped and browser authorization is triggered.

## Regression context

This began after the SDK migration in **PR #48937**, shipped in **OpenCode v2.0.4+**:

| OpenCode version | MCP SDK | Relevant behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `2.0.3` and earlier | `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` v1.29.0 | Attempted a refresh-token exchange on `403 insufficient_scope` without this step-up scope check |
| `2.0.4+` | `@modelcontextprotocol/client` v2.0.0 | Can force re-authorization when stored scope metadata is missing |

## Suggested fix

In `toCredential()`, persist the scope from the original authorization request when the token response omits `scope`. Continue to use the response’s scope when explicitly provided.

This follows RFC 6749 §5.1: when `scope` is omitted from the token response, the granted scope is identical to the requested scope.

Proactively refreshing access tokens before expiry could also help avoid this failure path, but preserving scope metadata would address the underlying ambiguity during scope checks.

### Suggested regression coverage

- A token response without `scope` preserves the originally requested scope.
- An explicitly returned `scope` takes precedence.
- An expired access token with a valid refresh token and sufficient scope triggers a refresh without browser interaction.
- A challenge requesting genuinely additional scopes still triggers step-up authorization.

## Additional observations

- Other MCP servers in the same OpenCode instance successfully perform refresh-token exchanges.
- The affected credentials correctly retain the access token, refresh token, issuer, and `client_id`; only `scope` is missing.
- The issue appears specific to providers whose token responses omit `scope`.

issues.body:
### Description


OpenCode Desktop freezes on session load when the host event table grows without bound. On my DB, 3.47 GB total / 2.94 GB (85%) was event (174,758 rows). The server uses better-sqlite3 synchronously; the session list took 4.2 s and two launches hung after booting location services. Offline .backup + DELETE FROM event + VACUUM reduced the DB to 519 MB, the list query to 3 ms, and three consecutive cold boots were clean.

Environment
OpenCode Desktop 1.19.0 (session records report version=1.19.0; app installed 2026-10-22), Linux Mint 22.3, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, x86_64, 4 cores, 8 GiB RAM.
/dev/sda4 ext4 on a rotational HGST  (ROTA=1); SQLite 3.45.1, WAL, 4096-byte pages.
DB: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-desktop.db; 265 sessions.
Evidence
2026-10-22: DB 3.47 GB (848,540 pages, freelist 0); dbstat: event 2.94 GB, part 316 MB, message 179 MB; 174,758 events.
Session-list query: 4.2 s on 265 sessions.
Launches at 09:20:39 and 09:27:58 hung for 2–3 minutes after booting location services, with no plugin initPlugin line; 09:36:28 was usable after ~45 s.
Offline on a copy: .backup + PRAGMA quick_check + DELETE FROM event + VACUUM → 3.77 GB → 519.4 MB; 190,718 events deleted; 265 sessions / 17,804 messages / 79,181 parts intact; quick_check=ok.
After the shrink: list query 3 ms; three consecutive cold boots clean (0 subscribe errors, refresh 0.8–4.0 s); no freeze.
The table regrew to 2,767 rows within ~90 minutes of normal use.
Schema
CREATE TABLE `event` (
  `id` text PRIMARY KEY,
  `aggregate_id` text NOT NULL,
  `seq` integer NOT NULL,
  `type` text NOT NULL,
  `data` text NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (`aggregate_id`) REFERENCES `event_sequence`(`aggregate_id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX `event_aggregate_seq_idx` ON `event` (`aggregate_id`, `seq`);
CREATE INDEX `event_aggregate_type_seq_idx` ON `event` (`aggregate_id`, `type`, `seq`);
The shipped app.asar contains this schema but no DELETE FROM event and no retention path. Rows are per-session append-only streams; the top aggregate IDs had 42,482 / 33,906 / 21,305 / 17,104 rows.

Reproduction / inspection
SELECT name, SUM(pgsize) AS bytes
FROM dbstat GROUP BY name ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10;

SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT aggregate_id) FROM event;

SELECT aggregate_id, count(*) AS c FROM event GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 5;
Then close the app, copy the DB, delete the event rows on the copy, VACUUM, and compare session-list latency.

Additional finding
The existing maintenance aborted 3× at 4.2–5.2 GB with backup quick_check failed (2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15), so no prune/VACUUM ever ran.

Requests
Add retention/compaction for event (prune completed sessions or enforce a max age/size; run in maintenance; compact safely).
Move heavy SQLite work off the server event loop / avoid synchronous checks on the boot path; add a large-DB guard.
Fix the maintenance backup quick_check failed abort.

issues.title: V2: compaction fires on first request / loops when compaction.buffer >= model context limit
issues.body:
## Summary

With `compaction.buffer` set to a value greater than or equal to the model's context limit, V2 starts automatic compaction on the **very first request** and re-triggers it on every turn. This emits meaningless structured summaries at session start and sometimes surfaces an internal `Session.StepFailedError: Nothing to compact yet`.

## Environment

- opencode `v2.0.32` (Linux x64; also confirmed config is read by V1 `1.19.0`)
- Session model: `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`

## Reproduction

`opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "compaction": {
    "auto": true,
    "buffer": 600000,
    "keep": { "tokens": 15000 }
  }
}
```

1. Start a V2 session (any directory with an `AGENTS.md`).
2. Send a single first message.
3. Observe the message stream: a `compaction` message is created immediately after the user message (`reason: "auto"`), summarizing an empty history, and repeats every 1-2 turns.

Startup log line:

```
ERROR "Failed to drain Session" cause="Session.StepFailedError: Nothing to compact yet
    at SessionRunner.runStep
    at SessionRunner.drain
    at ServerProcess.start"
```

## Expected

- An oversized `buffer` should be clamped to `< context limit` (or rejected with a clear warning at config load).
- Compaction should not run when there is no older history to compact.
- The internal `StepFailedError` should not surface as a user-facing failure at server start.

## Actual

The trigger is `estimated_tokens > context_limit - max(requested_output_tokens, buffer)` (docs state `buffer` default = 10% of the limit). When `buffer >= context_limit`, the right-hand side is negative, so the condition is always true and compaction fires on every step, including the first. Because `buffer` is a single global value evaluated against each model's own limit, a value chosen for a large-context model (e.g. `400000` for a 1M model) breaks every smaller model.

## Additional context / feature request

`buffer` and `keep.tokens` are only configurable globally in the top-level `compaction` block; per-model `settings.compaction` only accepts `type: native|summary`. This forces a single compaction policy across models with very different context windows. It would help to allow a per-model (or per-provider) `buffer`, and/or support an absolute "compact at N tokens" threshold, so users can pick different compaction points for a 200k model vs a 1M model without a global value that is unsafe for one of them.

issues.title: tui: /cd directory Tab-completion appends backslash on Windows (name/\ instead of name/)
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, Tab-completing a directory for the `/cd` slash command appends a backslash, producing `name/\` instead of `name/`. The completed argument is invalid/awkward to pass to `cd`.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.31 (channel: latest, autoupdate enabled)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable — `TERM`/`TERM_PROGRAM`/`COLORTERM` are not set (Windows / PowerShell 7.6.6)
- Shell: `pwsh` 7.6.6 (`COMSPEC=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`); opencode config sets `"shell": "pwsh"`
- Install/channel: latest (auto-update on)
- Active plugins: `@mohak34/opencode-notifier@latest`, `opencode-tps-meter`

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, open the opencode TUI.
2. Type `/cd ` (slash command followed by a space) so the directory argument autocomplete opens.
3. Filter to a directory (or accept the first suggestion).
4. Press Tab (`prompt.autocomplete.complete`).

## Expected Behavior

The directory is inserted with a forward slash, e.g. `Desktop/`, matching how the completion list already renders it.

## Actual Behavior

A backslash is appended, e.g. `Desktop/\`.

## Additional Context

Root cause is `expandDirectory()` in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`:

```ts
if (store.visible === "directory") {
  insertDirectory(selectedPath.endsWith(path.sep) ? selectedPath : selectedPath + path.sep)
  setStore("selected", 0)
  return
}
```

Directory completion values are always built with a forward slash in `packages/tui/src/prompt/directory-completion.ts`:

```ts
value: directoryAutocompleteResultValue(path.basename(absolute) + "/", search)
```

On Windows `path.sep === "\\"`, so `selectedPath.endsWith(path.sep)` is `false` and a backslash is appended, yielding `/\`.

Note: absolute Windows paths coming from directory recents can legitimately contain `\`; a fix should treat either separator as already-terminated (e.g. `/[\\/]$/.test(selectedPath)`), or normalize directory values to `/`.

`expandDirectory` currently has no test coverage (`packages/tui/test/prompt/autocomplete.test.ts` does not reference it).

Reproducible consistently.

issues.title: Unified Real-Time Usage Dashboard for All AI Models
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Hello OpenCode Team and Community,

I have already contacted OpenCode support about unclear free-tier usage limits, and I would like to share a practical solution with the community.

My concern is not the existence of usage limits, but the lack of a simple, unified way to understand them.

Users should not have to search through multiple documentation pages or manually calculate how much usage remains, whether limits are shared across models, or when their allowance resets.

### My Proposal: A Built-In Live Usage Dashboard

Add a small dashboard directly inside OpenCode that automatically tracks usage and updates when users switch models.

For example:

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│        MODEL USAGE METER        │
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│ Model: Nemotron Free             │
│ Daily Requests: 30 / 100        │
│ Remaining: 70 requests          │
│ Usage: 30%                      │
│ [██████░░░░░░░░░░░░] 30%        │
│ Input Tokens: 30,000            │
│ Output Tokens: 15,000            │
│ Total Tokens: 45,000             │
│ Reset Time: 03:00 AM             │
└─────────────────────────────────┘

These figures are illustrative only, not actual model limits.

The dashboard should:
- Automatically count requests and track token consumption.
- Display remaining allowances and usage percentages.
- Update automatically when switching models.
- Clearly distinguish model-specific limits from shared account or provider limits.
- Show applicable daily and monthly allowances and reset times.
- Distinguish verified figures from estimates or unavailable information.

Different models have different restrictions. Where exact provider information is unavailable, OpenCode should explain this clearly rather than leave users guessing.

### Why This Matters

Unexpected restrictions can interrupt hours of development work and force users to investigate multiple sources just to understand their remaining usage.

Users should not need to ask other AI assistants to calculate limits using incomplete information.

I am not asking for unlimited free usage. I am asking for transparent, predictable limits and a practical way to monitor them directly inside OpenCode.

OpenCode already brings multiple models into one environment. A unified usage dashboard would make that experience significantly more practical and user-friendly.

I have contacted support privately and am sharing this proposal to encourage community discussion and help improve the platform.

Thank you!

issues.title: shell tool description names the backend shell, so models call a non-existent `bash` tool
issues.body:
### Symptom

Models routinely call a tool named `bash`. This build registers only `shell`, so the call fails immediately:

```
No tool named "bash" is currently available. Please use a tool from the available tool list.
```

The model then retries with `shell` and the command runs. Cost: one wasted tool call, and an error surfaced to the user mid-task.

### Why the model does it

Ranked, from the actual signals a model reads:

1. **The `shell` tool's own description uses "bash" as the verb.** On Windows the description reads:

   > Commands run on Windows using bash.

   This text is read at tool-selection time on every turn, and it names the interpreter rather than the tool. It is the strongest single cause.

2. **V2 documents `bash` as an alias of `shell`** (docs: "shell tool named `shell` (bash kept as alias)"), so `bash` looks like a legitimate name in this ecosystem.

3. **Model prior**: nearly every other coding agent names its command tool `bash`.

### What this is not

Not a relay/proxy renaming tools. This is not the `shell_client` pattern from #56193 / #56794 - nothing rewrites the tool list here; the model reads the description above and types `bash` itself. Related, though: in #56193 a maintainer confirmed the description embeds the backend shell name (there, "using powershell"), the same text-vs-registration mismatch.

### Reproduction

1. Windows, `opencode.json` with "shell": "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\bash.exe".
2. Ask the agent to run a shell command in a fresh session.
3. Observe the tool-selection step: the model emits `bash` a percentage of the time (intermittent, model-dependent).
4. The call fails with `No tool named "bash" is currently available`; the retry with `shell` succeeds.

### Suggested fix (either is enough)

- Expose `bash` as a real entry in the tool catalogue (an alias of `shell`), so the name the description advertises actually resolves; or
- Reword the description so the tool name is unambiguous, e.g. `Run a shell command (this tool is named "shell"; it executes via bash on Windows).`

### Environment

- opencode v2.0.32 (bundled with OpenChamber 2.0.1)
- Windows 11, Git Bash at `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`
- `opencode.json` shell field points at that bash.exe
- Plugins cannot work around it: the V2 plugin API only exposes `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", event)`; there is no tool-registration or tool-rename hook.

issues.title: desktop: zh locale has unreviewed machine-translation errors (壳牌, 出口, 个贝壳)
issues.body:
### Description

The Simplified Chinese (`zh`) catalog in desktop 2.0.18 contains a few machine-translation errors, and 93 of the 1828 keys in the English base catalog have no `zh` entry, so those strings fall back to English.

#### Wrong translations

| key | English | current zh | suggested |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.timeline.category.shell` | Shell | 壳牌 | `shell 命令` |
| `ui.promptInput.exitShell` | Exit | 出口 | `退出` |
| `session.background.shell.other` | {{count}} shells | {{count}}个贝壳 | `{{count}}个shell` |
| `settings.timeline.title` | Timeline | 时间表 | `时间线` |
| `settings.timeline.preset.detailed` | Detailed | 详情 | `详细` |
| `settings.timeline.description.quiet` | Group edits and subagents. Hide other activity. | 对**已使用**的编辑和子代理进行分组。隐藏其他活动。 | 对**编辑**和子代理进行分组。隐藏其他活动。 |
| `settings.timeline.description.detailed` | Expand shell output and edits. Show subagents separately and group other activity. | 展开shell输出和编辑。 单独显示子代理，并在**已使用**中对其他活动进行分组。 | …并在**编辑**中对其他活动进行分组。 |

壳牌 (the Shell oil company), 出口 (customs/export exit) and 个贝壳 (a seashell) are clearly unreviewed machine translation. For reference, the rest of the catalog keeps "shell" in English in every sentence it appears in (`输入 shell 命令…`, `Shell 命令`, `{{count}}个shell`), so `settings.timeline.category.shell` is also inconsistent with the catalog's own convention. `description.detailed` additionally has a stray space after `。`.

#### Missing keys: 93

English base catalog 1828 keys, `zh` 1735 keys (94.9%). Most are the new provider-connect flow:

- `provider.connect.*` — 39 (the entire "Sign in to OpenCode Console" flow)
- `settings` — 18, `pair` — 10, `file` — 10, `session` — 8, `command` — 4, `home` — 2, `common` / `server` — 1 each

Happy to paste the full key list if useful.

#### Application menu bar is always English

The main-process catalog (`/out/main/translations-*.js` inside `app.asar`) contains no CJK at all, so the Windows menu bar (File / Edit / View / Go / Window / Help) is never localized even when the renderer UI is Chinese. Looks like an oversight rather than an intended limitation.

#### Where the catalogs live

Inside `resources/app.asar`: the `zh` catalog is `/out/renderer/assets/zh-*.js` (2 chunks, 13 KB + 81 KB) and the English base is inlined in `/out/renderer/assets/main-*.js`. The counts above come from parsing the asar and diffing the `"key": \`value\`` maps.

#### Suggestions

1. A build-time check that diffs each locale catalog's key set against the English base and fails (or warns) on missing keys, so new features cannot ship untranslated.
2. A review pass on `zh` additions — the three failures above are characteristic of raw machine translation.


### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

2.0.18 (desktop app @opencode/desktop 2.0.18)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop 2.0.18, UI language zh (system display language Chinese Simplified).
2. Settings > Timeline: the Shell category reads 壳牌.
3. Prompt input > Esc: the exit hint reads 出口.
4. Settings > Providers > Add account: the whole connect flow is in English.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

Windows 11 Home (zh-CN) 10.0.26200.8457, x64

### Terminal

OpenCode desktop integrated terminal (TERM=xterm-256color)

prs.title: fix(desktop): give dev builds their own server and keep beta off dev servers
prs.body:
Dev builds shared the released channels' server: one `service.json`, one port, one `opencode.db`. A dev desktop pins its exact CLI version, so starting it replaced the stable/beta server with a dev build. The beta app adopts any running server (#57309), so it then kept that dev server. On adais the Beta app (`0.0.0-beta-21669`) ran against `0.0.0-dev-21146`, which predates the heap-dump endpoint.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
  <style>
    .d{animation:m 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes m{0%,15%{transform:translateX(-52px);opacity:.25}45%,100%{transform:translateX(0);opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.d{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <rect x="20" y="16" width="80" height="40" rx="0" stroke-opacity=".9"/>
  <circle cx="44" cy="36" r="5" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".85"/>
  <circle cx="60" cy="36" r="5" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".55"/>
  <circle cx="76" cy="36" r="5" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".35"/>
  <g class="d">
    <rect x="140" y="16" width="80" height="40" stroke-dasharray="4 3" stroke-opacity=".6"/>
    <circle cx="180" cy="36" r="5" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".5"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

| | Stable, beta, next | Dev builds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registration | `service.json` | `service-dev.json` |
| Database | `opencode.db` | `opencode-dev.db` |
| Default port | `0xC0DE` (Windows `0x70DE`) | `0xC0E0` (Windows `0x70E0`) |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  B[Beta app] -- "service.json, version: releasedBuild" --> S[(stable/beta server)]
  D[App running a dev CLI] -- "service-dev.json, exact version" --> V[(dev server)]
  B -. "0.0.0-dev-* in service.json: replace" .-> S
```

- **CLI** (`service-config.ts`, `database-path.ts`): `dev` leaves the shared set. It gets `service-dev.json`, port `0xC0E0` and `opencode-dev.db`. It no longer migrates `service.json`, which it never owned; a dev server still registered there is left for a released client to replace.
- **Desktop** (`cli-version.ts`): `serviceFile` picks the registration from the CLI the app runs, not the app's channel, matching the CLI: a `0.0.0-dev-*` build reads `service-dev.json`, a released one `service.json`. A source build of the desktop can run either (`bun dev --download-server 2.0.32`), and so can the sidecar probe. Beta still keeps an older or newer server so a beta update does not kill running sessions, but only a released build's: `serviceVersion` now returns `releasedBuild`, which rejects `0.0.0-dev-*`, instead of `undefined`. `shouldRetryEnsure` takes whether the version is pinned, so the unpinned-beta retry is unchanged.
- **Transition:** a dev server an older dev CLI left in `service.json` is replaced the next time the beta or stable app starts. The dev app then starts its own server on its own port and database.

```ts
// packages/desktop/src/main/service/cli-version.ts
if (input.channel === "beta" && !input.isolated) return releasedBuild

export function releasedBuild(version: string) {
  return !version.startsWith("0.0.0-dev-")
}
```

### Impact

- Dev builds (the dev desktop app, and the `@opencode/cli@dev` npm tag) start with an empty `opencode-dev.db`. Sessions they made before this stay in `opencode.db`, visible in stable and beta. `OPENCODE_DB=…/opencode.db` points a dev build at the shared database when needed, as long as no released server is running on it.
- Dev's service config moves to `~/.config/opencode/service-dev.json`, so saved dev settings (password, remote access) start fresh.

Shared registration came from 9e22c40 ("feat: align V2 beta release channels"); beta adopting any version from #57309. Docs: `troubleshooting.mdx` lists both sets of files.

prs.title: fix(client): keep a live service that stalls across a suspend
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58111

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A client no longer kills a healthy background service just because its health probes did not answer, and it no longer waits forever on a registration whose process is gone.

`ensure()` treated three consecutive 2 s `/api/info` timeouts as proof that the registered service was dead: it cleared the PTY handoff, sent `SIGTERM` (then `SIGKILL`) and spawned a replacement. After a resume from sleep the probes can be sent on a pooled socket the server already dropped, so the timeouts arrive while the process is healthy and answering. Reproduced on 2.1.2 against a sandboxed service frozen with `SIGSTOP`: `Background service is unresponsive`, the frozen process killed, a replacement registered, and the calling client exiting `0` — the user only loses the running turn and the persistent terminals.

What changed:

- `service-probe.ts` probes `/api/info` with `connection: close`, so a half-dead pooled socket cannot answer for the service, and classifies a sample whose deadline passed by more than a second as `stalled` instead of `timedOut`.
- `service-recovery.ts` holds the replacement decision in one place, shared by the Effect and Promise clients so they cannot drift. A live but silent owner is replaced only after a continuous `unresponsiveAfter` (30 s) window. An answered probe, a stalled sample, or a different registration restarts the window; a process that is gone never opens one.
- `service-contender.ts` no longer starts attempts against a live owner. A live owner holds its port, so a contender could only fail to bind and report that failure for the whole `ensure()`. A gone owner still gets one spawn delay before an attempt competes with its exit — without that delay a stale registration would wait forever.
- The destructive path attempts `PtyHandoff.prepare` so persistent terminals survive a restart, instead of clearing the handoff.

The 30 s window also bounds the respawn storm from #57038 more tightly than before, since a recovered service answers long before the window closes.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/client` cover the recovery window (answered sample, stalled sample, gone process, a different owner, a replaced owner), the contender gate for `absent` / `alive` / `dead` owners, a live service that answers again before the window (same process reused, no signal, no attempt started), and a service whose process is gone (replaced without waiting for the window). Both the Effect and Promise clients are exercised.
- Manual check against a real `opencode serve --service`: frozen with `SIGSTOP` for 12 s, the same process is kept and reused; frozen past the window, it is signalled and replaced.
- `bun test` in `packages/client` (240 tests), `bun typecheck` and `oxlint` on `packages/client`, and the `packages/cli` service tests pass.

### Screenshots / recordings

_Not a UI change._

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep chrome-sandbox setuid in Linux packages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58157

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The deb installs `/opt/OpenCode/chrome-sandbox` as 0755, so on AppArmor-confined systems (Ubuntu 24+) Chromium falls back to user namespaces, the main process gains NoNewPrivs, every child inherits it, pkexec can never elevate, and in-app updates die with `pkexec must be setuid root` (exit 127).

The mode does not come from staged files: electron-builder's default postinst probes `unshare --user true` in dpkg's unconfined context and deliberately resets 0755 on every install/update. So this replaces the postinst for deb/rpm (all channels) with `scripts/after-install.sh` — the default template with the sandbox block forced to unconditional `chmod 4755`, matching what other Electron debs ship. A root-owned 4755 helper is safe with and without working user namespaces.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Contract table in `electron-builder.config.test.ts`: every channel's deb/rpm resolves to the script and the script carries the unconditional setuid line. Full file 10 pass, 100/100 over `--rerun-each 10`; `bun typecheck` clean in `packages/desktop`.
- Rendered the script with prod vars and ran it twice against a staged 0755 helper: 755 -> 4755 on install, stays 4755 on update (other errors in the log are sandbox artifacts: no /usr/bin write, no real executable — the script continues past them as designed).
- `bash -n` clean on source and rendered script.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change. Functional proof from the rendered-script run:

```
$ stat -c '%a' sbtest/opt/TestApp/chrome-sandbox
755
$ bash sbtest/rendered.sh   # install
$ stat -c '%a' sbtest/opt/TestApp/chrome-sandbox
4755
$ bash sbtest/rendered.sh   # update
$ stat -c '%a' sbtest/opt/TestApp/chrome-sandbox
4755
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(app): animate the timeline like iOS while a session runs
prs.body:
**Head:** `d68e8840a41d88ae06484183bb26aa64191146d3` · 2 commits on `beta` `5c95abcf34` · 14 files · code +1156/−105, tests +135/−7

## Why

While a session runs, the desktop timeline lands every change in one frame. Streamed text adds a line and everything above it jumps, a new tool row pops in at full height, a row that leaves takes its space with it at once, and Working pops in and out, sometimes twice. The iOS app animates the same moments, and this brings that model to Desktop.

## What changes

**Timeline** (`packages/app/src/session/timeline`)

- **Rows grow instead of landing.** While the timeline follows its end, a row's displayed height springs to its measured height (`row-growth.ts`, 0.32 s, no bounce) behind a soft bottom edge. The end stays put and the rows above glide. A new growth takes its first step in the frame that measured it.
- **Rows that leave fade where they were.** A copy of the row fades out in place, keeping the opacity its own animations had reached, while the rows above close the gap on the same spring. Growth fills the gap first. The gap only starts closing once nothing has grown for 120 ms, so a pause between streamed chunks can't start it and then stop it again.
- **Space the composer frees is held.** When the queue closes as its prompt arrives, the end stays where it is and the freed space waits under the last row for the reply to rise into. Before, the end sank with the composer and the reply then pushed it back up.
- **Scroll stays on the layout grid.** Chromium rounds a written `scrollTop` to a whole pixel, which made row edges tremble on every write. Each write now takes the whole pixel below and draws the remainder as a `translate`, which clears as soon as the user scrolls or the timeline stops following.
- **Streamed markdown never shrinks mid-stream.** While its text streams, a followed row never shrinks below what it shows; a lower target that is still above that just bends the growth down, and a growth bent toward a nearer target lands there instead of passing it and coming back. Once the text completes, the row takes whatever it measures in the next frame.
- **Your own send flies into its bubble.** A steer sent from the composer flies from the composer into its bubble, drawn above everything else. Queued and remote deliveries just grow in.
- **Working and the background hint** fade in one lane from whatever opacity they've reached, so they never show twice.

**Composer** (`packages/app/src/session/composer`, `composer/editor`)

- The queue panel springs open and closed. While it moves, it clips behind a soft edge, and at rest it clips nothing, so its skirt under the composer stays drawn. It keeps its last prompts while it closes, and a refreshed queue row keeps its element.
- The activity pill fades out still naming the last work, the placeholder crossfades, and the Queue hint no longer flashes on every send.

**Reduced motion** drops all travel. Status, placeholder, activity pill and hover footers keep short opacity fades (0.11–0.2 s); the queue panel lands at once.

## Scope

Desktop timeline and composer region only. No row redesign and no new production UI. The tuning controls only appear in the debug bar's Motion workspace.

## Verification

- **Strict motion trace** of a recorded 4-turn session at 60 fps with stepped frames (2145 frames, every timeline row, the status lanes and the composer edges). It covers streaming, tool rows, steer and queue sends, both deliveries and the turn ends. Edges are compared only while they are an element's own edge, not a clip line.
  - The previous draft of this branch, same harness: 55 jumps over 1 px, 9 visible unmounts, 1390 reversals and 3163 sub-pixel reversals, and the composer gap drifted 79.52–80.5 px.
  - Now: 0 jumps, 0 unmounts, 0 reversals, 0 sub-pixel reversals (steps over 1/64 px), and the composer gap is exactly 80 px in every frame.
- **First load and session switch:** frame-by-frame probe, with and without reduced motion. No animations on timeline or status elements, and no visible row moves after it first paints.
- **Reduced motion:** a full replay animates opacity only (tailwind fades carry identity transforms).
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/app` and `packages/session-ui`, `row-growth.test.ts` (7 pass), `bun run lint:changed origin/beta` (0 problems).
- Recordings (2880×1800, 60 fps, dark): one full turn at 1×, plus the send and the turn end at 0.25×. They're on the Problems board review R-51.

**Not verified:** a real Electron build, a real model stream (replayed tape in headless Chromium only), trackpad momentum during growth, and other window widths.

prs.title: feat(core): add goal round driver and goal verification
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of the goal/todo series. **Stacked on #55744** (the endpoints) and #54799 (the durable contracts) — review those first.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds the goal round driver, the independent verification round, and the model-facing tools.

**No new loop.** A round is one synthetic inbox row plus one `SessionExecution.wake`. The only place a round is scheduled is the `session.execution.succeeded` subscription, and it re-checks before scheduling: the process-local arm, the durable phase, the verifier's verdict, the todo gate, `rounds < maxGoalRounds`, and no human item waiting. The upper bound is `maxGoalRounds` (default 8).

**The verifier is a second, independent LLM request** — the shape of `SessionTitle.generate`: no conversation history, its own prompt entry, its own `UsageRecorded{source:"goal-verify"}`. Its input is only three kinds of evidence: the session's file diff, the results of finished tool calls (exit code and output), and the todo rows' `acceptance` text. The assistant's prose never enters. The output is decoded from one `llm.stream`; anything that does not decode is `incomplete` (fail-closed).

**`completed` is the verifier's alone.** The model's todo tool cannot write `completed`, and the gate is in code: `todo.every(s => s === "completed" || s === "cancelled")`.

**The model cannot resume.** The goal tool's `action` set is `set|edit|pause|clear` — `resume` is not constructible.

**Fail-closed disarm list**: execution failure, shutdown interruption, a verifier throw, session move/fork, compaction failure. `armed` is process-local and never persisted, so a restart is always disarmed.

### Notes

- `SessionGoalVerify` is a global node with `verify(sessionID, context)` parameter injection — putting `SessionContext.node` in its requirements makes `Instance.Services` self-referential.
- The human-yield check uses `Session.inbox()` rather than `nextPromotable`, because `nextPromotable` only returns the head and would miss a user row queued behind a steer.
- Known limits: the verifier can be fooled by a model that edits tests or the diff; `armed` is process-local.
- If the loop should be reviewed on its own, this splits cleanly into the verifier + tools and the driver + disarm list.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/server`: exit 0.
- New tests (`session-goal-verify`, `tool-goal`, `session-goal-driver`): 29 pass.
- Regression (`session-goal`, `plugin/command`, `session-projector`, `session-title`): 48 pass.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve line endings in patch tool
prs.body:
Closes #45926
Closes #54605

## Problem

The patch tool rewrote every line it touched with `\n`, so a CRLF file ended up with mixed endings after any update.

```diff
 file:   foo\r\n bar\r\n      patch: foo -> FOO
-before: FOO\n   bar\r\n
+after:  FOO\r\n bar\r\n
```

## Change

```text
line the patch didn't touch        -> kept byte for byte
line marked as context (" x")      -> kept byte for byte
changed or added line              -> file's first line ending (LF if none)
unterminated last line             -> gets the file's first line ending
```

Uniform files stay uniform, and mixed files stay mixed outside the edited lines.

To keep context lines verbatim, the parser now records which old/new lines are context (`contextIndices` on each chunk). The ACP preview, which reverses chunks, swaps those indices too.

## Out of scope

- A lone `\r` is still part of the line text, matching how Read shows the file.
- New files from `*** Add File` are still written with LF.

Builds on #45931 and #56128, both authors are credited as co-authors.

prs.title: feat(core): move ChatGPT context caps into a separate plugin
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem:** The ChatGPT context caps were hardcoded inside the OpenAI plugin. They only covered the legacy Codex sign-ins, so **Sign in with ChatGPT** (token sharing) got each model's full 1.05M window. They also couldn't be turned off and weren't documented.

**Change:** Move the caps into their own plugin, `opencode.provider.openai-context-caps`. It applies to all three ChatGPT sign-in methods. API-key connections are untouched.

```diff
 packages/core/src/plugin/
 ├── provider.ts                    # registers the new plugin
 └── provider/
     ├── openai.ts                  # keeps filtering, cost, headers; no longer sets limits
+    └── openai-context-caps.ts     # only lowers limits
```

```text
when the active openai connection is chatgpt-browser, chatgpt-headless, or chatgpt-token-sharing
  for each openai model
    cap = 500k if the model is gpt-6.1 or newer (or not a gpt-N name), otherwise 272k
    if the model's window is already <= cap: leave it alone
    else: input = cap, context = cap + output
on credential switch: reload so the caps follow the active connection
```

| model | before (Codex sign-in) | before (token sharing) | after (both) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-sol-fast | 500k | 922k | 500k |
| newer models, such as gpt-7 | 272k | not listed yet | 500k |
| gpt-6-*, gpt-5.6-* | 272k | 922k | 272k |
| gpt-5.5 (token sharing only) | n/a | 922k | 272k |

The 272k and 500k values are the `context_window` defaults returned by the live ChatGPT model list. That list also reports a 872k `max_context_window`. When probed directly, the backend accepted 921,522 input tokens and rejected 921,922, so it enforces only the model's real ~922k window. The caps are a usage choice, not a backend requirement.

Users can opt out with `"plugins": ["-opencode.provider.openai-context-caps"]`, or override one model's `limit` in config, which applies after the plugin.

**Docs:** a new **ChatGPT** section in `providers.mdx` covers the sign-in methods, why the limits exist, the limit table, and both ways to change them.

**Out of scope:** model sync for token sharing is still commented out in `chatgpt.ts`. When it returns, it can record the server's default and this plugin can apply it instead of its fixed values.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run script/test.ts test/plugin/provider-openai-context-caps.test.ts test/plugin/provider-openai.test.ts test/plugin/provider-chatgpt.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 31 pass. The new test covers all three sign-in methods, the 6.1+ rule, an unchanged smaller model, and an API key that keeps the full window.
- `--rerun-each 10` on the new test file: 40 pass.
- `bun run check` from the repo root: 34/34 tasks successful.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): show MCP elicitation forms in desktop and web
prs.body:
## Problem

An MCP server can ask the user for input partway through a tool call (`elicitation/create`). Since #58184 the TUI shows these forms, but the desktop and web app only render forms of kind `question` and `websearch.provider`. In the app the form never appears, and the tool call waits until the server gives up.

App support was originally added in #35064, lost in the #35080 revert, and not reapplied when #35115 restored the core side.

## Change

```diff
 createSessionRequestModel
   formRequest          // session tree: question | websearch.provider
+                       //               | mcp-elicitation
+  elicitationRequest   // session-tree form, else a "global" form for the session's Location
+  sync("global", session.location)
   blocked = permission || question || elicitation || websearch

 <SessionComposerRegion>
   <SessionWebSearchDock />
   <SessionQuestionDock />
+  <SessionElicitationDock />   // new
   <SessionPermissionDock />
```

- **New `SessionElicitationDock`.** Shows the form title, the server's message, and one control per field: a switch for booleans, number inputs for number and integer fields, a select for string choices, text inputs for free strings, checkboxes for multiselect, and the URL with an Open button for URL-mode elicitations. **Submit** replies and **Dismiss** (or Escape) cancels.
- **Global forms.** Elicitations are owned by the `"global"` sentinel session, so the model also lists and syncs global forms for the session's Location. Replies and cancellations go through `data.session.form.reply`/`cancel`, which add the Location header for global forms.
- **Strings.** Adds one English string, `session.elicitation.selectPlaceholder`. Everything else reuses existing keys.
- **Stories.** Adds two Storybook stories, *MCP elicitation request* and *MCP URL elicitation request*. The Storybook data mock gains no-op `form.reply`/`cancel`.

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4616de5-c78b-493f-88a9-53230f4aa8a8

This is the production web build against a local backend. A stdio MCP server's `deploy` tool asks for `approve` (boolean), `environment` (`staging | production`) and `notes` (string). The server received:

```json
{ "action": "accept", "content": { "approve": true, "environment": "production", "notes": "Ships the MCP elicitation dock." } }
```

## Out of scope

prs.title: fix(core): ignore a compaction buffer that leaves the model no room
prs.body:
A `compaction.buffer` set for a large model can be bigger than a smaller model's whole window. The ceiling is `window - buffer`, so it goes to zero or below and automatic compaction is due on every step.

```diff
-  if (buffer !== undefined) return window - buffer
+  if (buffer !== undefined && buffer < window) return window - buffer
```

A buffer that leaves no room is now ignored, and the default reserve (15% of the window, at least 16k) applies. The docs note it next to `buffer`.

Fixes #56783
Fixes #58146

prs.title: feat(desktop): add native memory breakdown to heap captures
prs.body:
A heap snapshot only holds objects the garbage collectors own, so on adais the app window's 1,186 MB showed up as ~300 MB of heap and 886 MB of nothing. **Capture heap snapshots** now also records Chromium's per-process, per-allocator memory dump and summarizes it, and the server reports its own memory.

## What the folder holds now

```text
opencode-heap-2026-10-23T023312345Z/
  memory.json                  where the memory is, per process, in MiB: start here
  memory-infra.json            Chromium's raw memory dump trace (Perfetto / chrome://tracing)
  heap-24792-…heapsnapshot     server
  window-1-24924.heapsnapshot  app window
  main-22204.heapsnapshot      Electron main
  gpu.json                     GPU and driver
  manifest.json                files, snapshots, metrics before and after; written last
```

```jsonc
// memory.json (dev build, fresh window)
{
  "unit": "MiB",
  "native": [
    { "name": "GPU Process", "pid": 30340, "totals": { "privateFootprint": 154.3 },
      "allocators": { "malloc": 28.8, "cc": 9.9, "gpu": 9.5 },
      "detail": { "gpu/shared_images": "…", "cc/resource_memory": "…" } },
    { "name": "Renderer", "pid": 24924, "totals": { "privateFootprint": 127.8 },
      "allocators": { "partition_alloc": 37, "malloc": 35.1, "v8": 27.3, "cc": 24.3, "blink_gc": 4.3 },
      "detail": { "cc/tile_memory": 24.3, "partition_alloc/partitions/buffer": "…", "v8/main/heap": "…" } }
  ],
  "server": { "rss": 304.5, "heapTotal": 86, "heapUsed": 99, "external": 50.7, "arrayBuffers": 0.1 },
  "pages": [{ "window": 1, "title": "OpenCode", "contentSize": [1280, 802], "scaleFactor": 1.5,
    "page": { "elements": 773, "images": { "count": 0, "decodedMiB": 0 }, "canvases": { "count": 0, "MiB": 0 },
              "svgUses": 13, "jsHeap": { "usedJSHeapSize": 40316740 } } }]
}
```

## How

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as main (debug/main.ts)
  participant C as Chromium tracing
  participant W as app windows
  participant S as server
  M->>M: getAppMetrics, memoryUsage, v8 heap stats, system memory (before)
  M->>C: startRecording(memory-infra, detailed dump every 1s)
  C-->>M: memory-infra.json after 2.5s
  M->>M: summarize → memory.json
  M->>W: executeJavaScript: DOM size, images, canvases, performance.memory
  par
    M->>S: POST /api/debug/heap-dump?directory=…  → { path, pid, memory }
  and
    M->>W: takeHeapSnapshot, one window at a time
  end
  M->>M: writeHeapSnapshot(main), getGPUInfo, metrics (after), manifest.json
```

- **Measurements before snapshots.** Writing a snapshot raises the memory of the process it serializes, so metrics, the memory-infra dump and page stats are read first; `manifest.json` also keeps metrics after.
- **memory-infra.** One `contentTracing` recording covers every Chromium process (browser, renderers, GPU, utility). `summarize` (`debug/memory-infra.ts`) takes the latest complete dump: totals and allocators arrive in separate events per dump id, and the browser splits its allocators over two. It reports effective sizes (shared memory counted once), top-level allocators, and sub-allocators of at least 1 MiB up to three levels deep. If another trace is running (DevTools recording a profile), the manifest records the error and the snapshots still run.
- **Server memory.** `HeapSnapshot.write` reads `process.memoryUsage()` just before writing and the endpoint returns it as `memory`; the SIGUSR1 log line includes `rss` and `heapUsed`. The desktop records it per server snapshot; servers released before this leave it out.
- **Page stats** per window: element count, images and their decoded size (4 bytes per pixel), canvases, `<use>` count, viewport, device pixel ratio, zoom, `performance.memory`.
- **Also recorded:** main's `v8.getHeapStatistics()` and heap spaces, `process.getSystemMemoryInfo()`, `app.getGPUInfo("basic")`, app uptime.

Follow-up to #58259. Docs (`troubleshooting.mdx`) and the `opencode-dev` skill describe the new files.

prs.title: feat(app): add a timeline width setting
prs.body:
Adds **Settings → Preferences → Timeline → Timeline width** with three options. The session column was ~105 characters per line, well past the 45–75 range that readability research recommends. **Focused** brings it to ~66.

| Option | `--container-session` | Text column | ≈ chars/line | Composer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Focused (new) | 488px | 440px | **66** | 464px |
| Comfortable (default, unchanged) | 744px | 696px | **105** | 720px |
| Wide (the pre-#54020 width) | 1000px | 952px | **144** | 976px |

The character counts use Inter at 14px, which averages 6.62px per character (spaces included) on technical prose, after the 24px side padding. I measured the text columns in the app: 440, 696, and 952px.

### Why 66

- **45–75 characters per line.** Bringhurst's range, and the one Google Fonts Knowledge quotes. Material Design suggests 40–60 on screen.
- **About 70 at most.** From the Nanavati & Bias review (2005).
- **55 characters per line rated easiest.** Dyson & Kipping (1998). Lines of 95–100 characters read slightly faster, but readers rated them the hardest (also Shaikh 2005).
- **WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.8:** no more than 80 characters.
- Wide stays available for people who prefer to see more at once. The Readability Consortium (Google, Adobe, UCF) found that the best format differs from reader to reader.

### How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[settings.general.timelineWidth] --> A[":root[data-timeline-width]"]
  A --> V["--container-session"]
  V --> T[timeline rows]
  V --> C[composer dock]
  V --> D[drop target]
  V --> B[btw panel]
```

- The setting works like `reduceMotion`: the settings model writes it as an attribute on the root element. CSS then overrides the one shared token, so the timeline, composer, and drop target keep the same edges.
- Rows already get remeasured through their `ResizeObserver`, so the change applies live, the same as a window resize.

```css
:root[data-timeline-width="focused"] { --container-session: 488px; }
:root[data-timeline-width="wide"]    { --container-session: 1000px; }
```

prs.title: feat(app): show the web sources a reply used (experiment)
prs.body: ### What it does Under a reply that searched the web, an "N sources" chip with up to three site icons. Clicking it opens a Sources panel in the side panel with each search (query, result count, expandable to its results) and each page opened, in the order they ran. Results open in the in-app browser when there is one. Site icons are Letters or real favicons, chosen in Knobs. Off by default: Knobs → Experiments → Sources. ### How it works 1. `turnSources` (session-ui) reads a turn's `websearch` and `webfetch` tool parts. The search tool's structured output isn't stored in messages, so results come from its `## [title](url)` text. URLs dedupe on host (without `www.`), path and query. 2. The chip renders in the finished turn's footer only, so nothing shows or shifts while the turn streams. It fades in when the turn finishes. 3. A new built-in `sources` extension lists one transient side-panel tab per turn, titled "Sources · N". It lists nothing while the experiment is off, so turning it off closes any open panel. Provider-native web search citations (Anthropic, OpenAI) aren't stored in messages yet, so they don't show here. ### Risk Client-only, behind an off-by-default experiment. With it off, no chip renders, the panel never lists and no favicon is requested. With "Site icon" on, the panel and chip request `https:///favicon.ico` directly, with no referrer and no third-party icon service. ### Proof The Sources story in the components lab, dark: - `bun test src/sources` in `packages/session-ui`: 5 pass (order, dedupe, titles, empty and failed steps, turn slicing) - `component-tests/sources-experiment.spec.ts`: turning the experiment off closes the open panel and removes its site icons (passes) - `bun typecheck` in session-ui, gui-extensions and app: clean ### Visual ```svg ```

prs.title: fix(cli): isolate background service per config profile
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58141

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Previously, the managed background service registered a single per-user state file (`~/.local/state/opencode/service.json`) and bound a single default port (`49374` / `0xc0de`) regardless of `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. Launching a second profile with a different `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (and profile-specific environment variables) discovered and attached to the first profile's background server instead of starting its own.

This change:
1. Detects when `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` resolves to a non-default config directory (`ServiceConfig.activeProfile()`).
2. Deterministically derives a profile-specific registration filename in `global.state` (`service-<hash>.json` / `service-<channel>-<hash>.json`) and a profile-specific default port (`ServiceConfig.defaultPort`) from the resolved `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` path, while keeping the default profile (`service.json` and port `49374`) unchanged.
3. Canonicalizes `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` before `ServerProcess` changes directory to `$HOME` and passes it in `ServiceConfig.options().env` so spawned background services and CLI commands (`service start`, `status`, `restart`, `stop`) consistently resolve the same profile.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added unit tests in `packages/cli/test/service.test.ts` covering per-profile port derivation, registration filename derivation, and `ServiceConfig.options()` isolation in a shared state directory.
- Added an end-to-end multi-profile CLI test in `packages/cli/test/service.test.ts` verifying that two `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` profiles start on distinct ports, report independent `service status`, and stop independently without affecting each other.
- Ran `bun test test/service.test.ts` and `bun run check`.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(app): show live Thinking instead of hiding reasoning-only turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** With grouped thinking (the default `compact` preset, and `detailed`), a turn whose only output so far is reasoning showed a bare **Working** row. There was no thought, no elapsed time, and nothing to expand, for as long as the model kept thinking. #51090 added this to avoid a premature "Used 1 Thought".
- **Fix:** The reasoning-only group renders again. While it is the live group, it reads **Thinking · 8m 13s** with a shimmer and a ticking duration, and it replaces Working. The row stays as compact as before.
- **Expand:** Opening the group shows the thought text directly, without a second collapsed "Thinking" row inside it.
- **Hand-off:** When the turn produces a tool, text, or finishes, the group becomes the usual "Used N …" and Working comes back for tool activity.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[busy turn, only reasoning] -->|before| B[Working]
  A -->|after| C[Thinking · 8m 13s ▸]
  C -->|tool or text arrives| D[Used 1 Read ▸ + Working]
```

- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/projection.ts`: remove the `thoughtOnly` early return that dropped the whole assistant segment.
- `packages/session-ui/src/tools/tool-renderer.tsx`: `CurrentContextToolGroup` labels a busy, reasoning-only group "Thinking", shows the elapsed time since the first thought (s, m s, h m), and opens its thoughts by default.

### What does this PR do?

Implements the preset interface proposed by @Dante-dan in #58054.

{ "tabs": { "marquee": "slow" } }
```

prs.title: fix(core): recover unclassified oversized rejections through text-only compaction
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related #46564, #53107. Resolves the #54690 repro (default config: compact-then-send image-heavy session dies on a generic 400 with no recovery).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Proxies and gateways often reject oversized HTTP bodies with a generic 400 instead of a classified size error, while media counts flat toward tokens and dominates bytes. Neither the overflow nor the payload path triggers, so the session dead-ends: every continuation (even content-free) resends the same oversized body and fails the same way.

This treats an unclassified 4xx against a request at or above 4 MiB as a payload rejection: one text-only compaction rebuild before durable output, reusing the existing single-rebuild limit and opt-out. Small requests and non-4xx failures behave exactly as before. It complements #53108, which covers the classified 413 path only.

Note: with `compaction.auto: false` recovery still declines per existing opt-out semantics, so the exact #46564 env (auto:false + third-party context plugin) needs a separate policy decision.

### How did you verify your code works?

New runner scenarios: recovery with media stripped from the summary request while stored history keeps the image; no recovery for small requests; no recovery for 5xx. Plus a classifier unit test locking in that generic 400s stay unclassified. Full suites pass: packages/core 6665 pass, packages/ai 1811 pass; both typechecks and oxlint clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change. Uses synthetic fixtures (a generated 4.5 MB PNG data URI); no private session data.
