prs.title: fix(app): run the web app on Safari 16.4
prs.body:
The web app targets `esnext` for both JS and CSS, so the iPhone Safari versions people still use (a 16.6 report in #48610) hit missing APIs and drop whole CSS rules.

**How the gaps were found.** The production bundle was scanned against MDN browser-compat-data for iOS Safari 16.4, and every hit was traced back to our source. Syntax is fine: the bundle passes `es-check es2022`.

| Gap | iOS Safari | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `URL.parse` | 18 | pairing link parsing | `core-js/modules/web.url.parse` |
| `URL.canParse` | 17 | server addresses, `openExternal`, extensions (~8 sites) | `core-js/modules/web.url.can-parse` |
| `AbortSignal.any` | 17.4 | client RPC and event calls that take a caller's `signal`, extension host | `anySignal` (below) |
| CSS nesting | 17.2 | 14 shipped stylesheets (toast, switch, select, shell, connect screen, …) | `build.cssTarget: "safari16.4"` |
| `light-dark()` | 17.5 | elevation shadows (`theme.css`) | same |

- The URL modules add only the static methods. The `core-js/*/url` entry points would also swap in core-js's `URL` constructor.
- No maintained package adds `AbortSignal.any` to a native `AbortSignal`: core-js has no AbortSignal modules, and `abortcontroller-polyfill` installs only where `AbortController` itself is missing. So `runtime/abort-signal.ts` provides it (aborts with the first input's reason, and removes its listeners once it fires), installed from `polyfills.ts` only when `AbortSignal.any` is absent.
- Lightning CSS lowers `light-dark()` using the `color-scheme` declared on `[data-color-scheme]`, which the theme always sets. In Chromium the resolved `--v2-elevation-raised` shadow is identical before and after, in light and dark.
- After the change, Lightning CSS rewrites nothing more for a Safari 16.4 target (before: 280 `&`, 10 `light-dark()`).
- `vite.config.ts`: the conditional spread and `as any` were replaced to keep the touched file lint-clean. Builds with and without `VITE_OPENCODE_TEST_FIXTURES` produce the same inputs.
- **Diff colours.** `@pierre/diffs` 1.5.1 ships its stylesheet as a JS string (`dist/style.js`) that uses `light-dark()` for every diff colour (syntax tokens, text, added and removed rows) and 120 nested selectors. `build.cssTarget` does not reach it. The new `vite.diffs.ts` build plugin adds a copy lowered by Lightning CSS and picks it only where `CSS.supports("color", "light-dark(#000, #fff)")` is false. Modern browsers keep Pierre's CSS unchanged.
  - Before lowering, token backgrounds that fall back to `light-dark(inherit, inherit)` become `transparent`. Browsers reject that `light-dark()`, so those backgrounds stay transparent. Lowered as is, `inherit` would apply and repaint word highlights.
  - Our own diff CSS (`session-ui/src/pierre/index.ts`) is also a JS string: its nested rules are now flat (Lightning CSS produces the same rules), and its 4 `light-dark()` values get an `@supports not (color: light-dark(…))` fallback chosen by `prefers-color-scheme`. That matches native behaviour, because the diff host's `color-scheme` is `light dark`.
  - Checked against real Pierre SSR markup in current Chromium and WebKit, light and dark: the fallback path (plugin output plus our block forced on) resolves the same color, background, font and decoration on all 187 elements as the modern path, and the screenshots are pixel-identical. A wrong fallback value fails this check.

## Before

Production build in Chromium with the APIs iOS 16.6 lacks removed, against a real `opencode serve`: pasting an expired pairing link throws in `URL.parse`, and the screen reports a generic connection failure.

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a6b9cb7-2223-41db-a3e2-0ced7f1bdab5)

## After

Same setup: the link is parsed and the server's answer is shown.

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55205095-4bc2-43ab-97ef-0da08160c4d3)

## Diffs before

Current WebKit with every `light-dark(` renamed to an unknown function, so it treats them as Safari before 17.5 does. Pierre's shipped CSS:

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0710692-9606-405e-ae31-b74c8b69dcda)

## Diffs after

Same approximation with the lowered copy and our fallback:

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/192235c3-67fb-44ae-b6b6-c29c418717d5)

issues.title: pi-durable: defineDoc accepts a missing checkpointWhen; first change commit crashes

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

In `packages/durable`, `defineDoc()` and `defineDocFamily()` should reject a definition whose `checkpointWhen` is missing or not a function, at define time. `validateDefinition()` in `src/documents.ts` currently only checks `version`, so the omission passes silently. The change is five lines there, plus a regression test in `test/session-definitions.test.ts`. It is ready on a branch (linked below); I would like to open the PR if approved.

**Why?**

1.4.0 made `checkpointWhen` required with no default, but that is only enforced by the TypeScript types. A plain-JavaScript caller, or any code building definitions dynamically, gets no error at define time. The definition is accepted, the creation commit succeeds, and the first ordinary change commit throws from inside the transaction (`src/session/transaction.ts`):

```
TypeError: change.definition.checkpointWhen is not a function
```

That message names an internal field, not the document kind or the missing predicate. Minimal repro against the published `@earendil-works/pi-durable@1.4.0` dist (plain JS, MemoryStorage): define a conversation doc without `checkpointWhen`, commit a change that creates it, then commit a second change:

```
1. defineDoc() accepted the definition without checkpointWhen (no error)
2. first doc change (creation) committed fine
3. second doc change (ordinary delta) threw: TypeError: change.definition.checkpointWhen is not a function
```

I hit this in real use: after upgrading a crash-resume agent built on pi-durable to 1.4.0, a doc write inside a recovered run failed with this error, so the run's remaining state never landed. For a durability library, the failure surfaces at the worst place: late, mid-commit, potentially after a restart. Failing at define time, with a message naming the kind and the remedy (`() => false` keeps the old delta behavior), turns it into a one-line fix.

**How?**

Extend `validateDefinition()` with a `typeof definition.checkpointWhen !== "function"` check that throws a `TypeError` in the style of the existing version check. Add a runtime regression test, "rejects a missing checkpoint predicate at runtime", next to the existing definitions tests (the current checkpoint test only exercises the types; its calls are never invoked).

Prepared branch: https://github.com/Darren-dev141/pi/tree/fix/durable-checkpointwhen-validation (diff: `documents.ts` +5/-0, `session-definitions.test.ts` +29/-0). Verified locally against main's source: with the patch, missing and `undefined` predicates throw at define time for both `defineDoc` and `defineDocFamily`, while valid definitions and the version checks behave as before; against unpatched main, the new checks fail with "did not throw". Version: `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.4.0, Node 24.

issues.title: Empty bracketed paste from Windows Terminal is dropped, so image paste does nothing on WSL

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

On WSL, Windows Terminal handles `Ctrl+V` itself. With an image on the clipboard it sends an empty bracketed paste (`ESC[200~ ESC[201~`) and leaves the image on the WSLg Wayland clipboard. The editor ignores empty pastes (`if (pasteContent.length > 0)` in `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`), so `app.clipboard.pasteImage` never runs. Screenshot, `Ctrl+V`, nothing happens.

I'd like an empty bracketed paste to mean "check the clipboard" instead of being dropped.

**Why?**

Reading the clipboard already works — `readClipboardImage()` from the running process returns the PNG through `wl-paste`. Only the trigger is missing, because the key never reaches pi. On Windows Terminal + WSLg that leaves image paste permanently broken.

**How?**

Don't return early on an empty payload; run the same path as `app.clipboard.pasteImage`, but only when the clipboard actually has an image. Tests in `packages/tui` (empty paste calls the callback) and `packages/coding-agent` (wiring).

I wrote this as an extension first — [pi-image-paste-cards](https://github.com/ImSven/pi-image-paste-cards) — and can send a PR if it belongs in core. OSC 5522 is the cleaner long-term answer for kitty, but that's a separate and bigger change.

issues.title: Set a startup-time budget targeting jcode-comparable latency and memory
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Set a startup-time budget for pi that targets jcode-comparable latency and memory, and close the gap measured by jcode's README benchmark against pi 0.62.0:

| Metric (median; 10 interactive PTY launches, Linux) | jcode v0.9.1888-dev | pi (same table) | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time to first frame | 14.0 ms (10.1–19.3) | 590.7 ms (369.6–934.8) | 42.2× |
| Time to first input | 48.7 ms (30.3–62.7) | 596.4 ms (373.9–955.2) | 12.2× |
| Idle RAM, 1 session (PSS) | 27.8 MB | 144.4 MB | 5.2× |
| Idle RAM, 10 sessions (PSS) | 117.0 MB | 833.0 MB | 7.1× |
| Extra RAM per added session | ~9.9 MB | ~76.5 MB | 7.7× |

Notes: jcode numbers come from jcode's own README ("Performance & Resource Efficiency"; RAM rows are with local embeddings off). pi 0.62.0 is the version listed in the README's version list for the RAM tables; the timing rows carry no stated version there. Pi's own best measured cold start is 2.55 s (`--no-extensions`, pi 0.78.0, #5402); ~2.7 s was reported in #7639.

### Why?

Startup latency is paid on every spawn, and current pi workflows spawn it constantly:

- Multiplexer setups (tmux/zellij; pi-mux, dmux) run one pane per session; each switch back pays the first frame plus a ~2.5–2.7 s cold start and multi-second extension reloads (#5905).
- `pi -c` one-shots and subagent fan-out multiply the cost: 16 concurrent spawns × 0.59 s ≈ 9.4 s before agents render, and 1000 one-shots at ~2.7 s each total ~45 min. Running many sessions at once also costs ~76.5 MB PSS per session vs ~9.9 MB for jcode.
- Session resume and switch sit on the same path: listing and parsing session files adds to per-switch latency (#5804, #6594).

Nielsen Norman Group response-time limits put 0.1 s at "instant" and 1.0 s as the limit for uninterrupted flow. jcode's 14 ms first frame sits far below the instant threshold; pi's 590.7 ms and 2.5 s cold start break flow on every spawn. For pane-per-session workflows, spawn speed decides whether multiplexers feel like background processes or warm tabs.

This builds on prior work rather than duplicating it: #7639 (startup benchmark, closed no-action), #6530 (Node CLI startup cost, unmerged), #5402/#5405 (138 MB eager provider SDK loads), #5380/#6892 (extension transpile cost), #2522 (bundled entrypoint), #5804/#6594 (fast session load). The ask is a jcode-parity budget on top of those.

### How? (optional)

- Add the CI startup gate #7639 proposed: benchmark cold start and TUI first frame with a hard budget — e.g. first frame < 150 ms, or a 4× improvement over the current baseline — measured like jcode's README (10 interactive launches).
- Lazy-load the remaining eager work: provider SDKs at top level (#5402/#5405), jiti extension transpilation with a persistent disk cache (#5380/#6892), sequential package resolution.
- Investigate an entrypoint that skips the Node bootstrap path where possible: bundled single-file CLI (#2522) and fast paths for version/RPC (#6530), working toward a compiled artifact like jcode's Rust binary.

issues.title: Public tool-presentation API or built-in one-line tool mode
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Either:
- A public, display-only API so an extension can control the presentation of **all** tool rows, including built-ins, MCP, codemode, and custom extension tools.
- A built-in one-line mode showing the tool name, a short call summary, and running/success/error status, with full details available on demand.

For the API option, I want to build an extension with a shortcut that cycles between full output, a compact preview, and a one-line view. It should work for live calls and resumed history without replacing tool execution or patching Pi internals.

### Why?

Even with Ctrl+O collapsed, commands, diffs, and tool-result previews take up most of my screen and push the conversation out of view. The minimal-mode example helps with built-ins, but does not cover every MCP or custom tool.

This is only a display preference. Tool execution, model context, and stored results should stay unchanged.

### How? (optional)

A global tool-presentation hook would let extensions handle this without adding UI preferences to the core. A built-in one-line mode would also solve my problem.

Related: #5137, #9638, and #10011. I know these requests overlap; is either approach something maintainers would support?

issues.title: A split mouse report leaves its tail in the prompt: the escape timeout flushes half a sequence and the editor types the rest

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Disclosure: I drafted this text with an AI agent. I reproduced the split-read case locally with the shipped StdinBuffer and Editor and pasted the observed output above.


### Steps to reproduce

```
   ```ts
   const buffer = new StdinBuffer({ timeout: 10, escapeTimeout: 10 });
   const editor = new Editor(tui, theme);
   buffer.on("data", (sequence) => editor.handleInput(sequence));

   buffer.process("\x1b[<35;4");                 // first half of an SGR motion report
   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 40));  // longer than the timeout: head is flushed
   buffer.process("8;27M");                      // second half arrives as new input

   editor.getText();  // "8;27M"
   ```

   Observed: emitted sequences are ["\u001b[<35;4","8",";","2","7","M"] and the editor ends up containing
   8;27M. A report that arrives in one read is consumed by the fullscreen mouse handling as expected; only the
   split case leaks.

   In a terminal: run pi, move the mouse while it is busy (the escape timeout is 10 ms, so a busy event loop
   splits the report), and fragments like 8;27M appear in the prompt.
 ```

### Expected behavior

```
   Half of a terminal control sequence should never reach the editor. Either StdinBuffer keeps the fragment out of
   the input stream and swallows the continuation that follows, or Editor.handleInput() refuses to type a string
   that is an obvious control-sequence remnant (an ESC-less report such as [<35;48;27M is typed as-is today).
   Today a moving mouse fills the prompt, and Ctrl+C only clears the line, which reads as "pi prints garbage and
   will not exit".
 ```

### Version

1.3.0, also on main (73f8de8). Windows 11, Windows Terminal, PowerShell; the input path is the same everywhere.    Related: #11170 is the other half of the same symptom (an exiting pi leaves the terminal in mouse-tracking    state, so the shell echoes the reports). They are independent: this one is pi typing the fragments itself while it is still running.

issues.title: Feature request: per-message assistant footer API for extensions

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

Extensions can add commands, tools, status text, and global widgets, but there is no supported way to attach an interactive component to each finalized assistant message in the transcript. A global widget is not equivalent: it cannot reliably control or annotate the particular message it belongs to. This blocks row-local actions such as Play/Pause/Stop/seek, citations, and message-specific review controls.

I confirmed that my installed Pi 1.4.0 package does not expose a per-message assistant footer extension API. I built a local extension that needs one for manual, per-message TTS controls.

## Proposed capability

Please consider a public extension API for registering assistant-message footers. A factory could receive the finalized message snapshot, session and entry IDs, active theme/keybindings/output padding, a render callback, and a lifecycle `AbortSignal`; it could return a TUI component (or `undefined`). Core would render that component immediately beneath its owning message.

Important behavior:

- Keep the message snapshot immutable and tied to its persisted entry, not to “the latest answer.”
- Preserve the logical footer across transcript rebuilds, scrolling, resizing, and theme changes; abort/dispose it when its message leaves the rendered active branch or its session is replaced/reloaded/shut down.
- Isolate factory/render/input/disposal errors so one extension cannot break transcript rendering.
- Route fullscreen mouse events to the footer without stealing editor focus. Respect regular-mode terminal mouse ownership and provide keyboard/command alternatives.
- Do not construct interactive footers in print, JSON, or RPC modes that cannot render them.

The exact API shape is open to maintainer preference; this is the behavior that proved useful in the prototype.

## Prototype and implementation notes

In a separate local Pi source checkout, I prototyped `registerAssistantMessageFooter(factory)`. Core attaches a footer component to each eligible finalized `AssistantMessageComponent`, keeps instances keyed by session/entry, supplies a cloned and recursively frozen message snapshot, and reconciles/disposes instances against the complete rendered branch. The host dispatches fullscreen mouse events through the footer component while leaving focus unchanged. Factory and component failures are contained.

The prototype includes tests for footer creation/lifetime, branch removal and cleanup, error isolation, rendering/invalidation, focus retention, fullscreen mouse routing, regular-mode behavior, and headless modes. It is a local patch, not a change to the installed Pi package.

## Offer to help

I can contribute a PR adapting the prototype to the current upstream architecture, add or revise tests and docs, and work with maintainers on the API/lifecycle details. I would be happy to split this into a small host API change and a follow-up example extension.

## Example: poem with its own controls

![Illustration of a poem followed by its own italic playback controls](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/leoscricca/234f4ae54f0588ed3b4a5824f775bfd5/raw/b1c32b884c8c363f37600fad265c202425de1ce7/pi-per-message-poem-widget.svg)

This is an illustrative mockup (not a live Pi screenshot): the Pause/Stop/progress/time/speed row belongs to the poem above it.

issues.title: modelOverrides are silently ignored for classifier models
issues.body:
### What happened?

`modelOverrides` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` are silently ignored for classifier models. No error, no warning.

`docs/models.md` says they change metadata for "an existing built-in or extension-provided model", and that only unknown IDs are ignored. This model is built-in and the ID matches.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point Pi at a llama.cpp router serving a decision model (GGUF `architecture.output_modalities: ["decisions"]`), so Pi registers it as `type: "classifier"`, `api: "typesafe-system-one"`. ID here: `clef-flash`.
2. In `models.json`:

```json
{"providers":{"llama.cpp":{"modelOverrides":{"clef-flash":{
  "name":"Clef Flash Q8_0 (Spark)","contextWindow":8192}}}}}
```

3. Restart Pi, then in codemode:

```js
const m = await models.getModelOfType("classifier","llama.cpp","clef-flash");
return m.name; // "clef-flash", not "Clef Flash Q8_0 (Spark)"
```

The identical override on a chat model in the same file does apply, so the file, merge and reload are fine; only the model type differs. Loading `ModelRuntime` with a temp `models.json` reproduces it with no extensions involved.

### Cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts`, `composeModelProvider()`:

```ts
const override = config?.modelOverrides?.[model.id];
return override && isModelType(model, "chat") ? applyModelOverride(model, override) : model;
```

`rawModelHeaders()` has the same chat-only gate, so `modelOverrides[...].headers` is dropped as well. Present in 1.2.0, 1.3.0 and `main`. #5021 and #6367 covered dynamically registered/extension providers, a different path.

### Expected behavior

Either apply overrides to every model type (at least `name`, `input`, `contextWindow`, `cost`, `headers`), or say in the docs that `models.json` overrides are chat-only and warn instead of silently ignoring them.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Fix thinkingLevelMap?.off type guard causing 400s on OpenRouter reasoning models

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

Models with `reasoning: true` and `thinkingFormat: "openrouter"` but no `thinkingLevelMap` (e.g. `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free`) fail with HTTP 400 from upstream providers (AtlasCloud) when invoked via `--model`, even though they work via direct API calls. The model appears in `--list-models` and responds to direct API calls, but fails when supplied via `--model` in pi.

## Root Causes

### 1. Phantom reasoning parameter

In `buildParams` (openai-completions.ts and 4 other API implementations), the expression `model.thinkingLevelMap?.off !== null` evaluates to `true` when `thinkingLevelMap` is `undefined` (`undefined !== null` → `true`). This causes pi to send `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` on every request for these models, even when thinking is off. Upstream providers like AtlasCloud reject this parameter with HTTP 400.

**Fix:** Change `model.thinkingLevelMap?.off !== null` to `model.thinkingLevelMap != null && model.thinkingLevelMap.off !== null` in all affected API implementations.

### 2. Unconditional max_completion_tokens

`buildParams` always sends `max_completion_tokens` set to `model.maxTokens` (460800 for some OpenRouter models) even when the user didn't request a specific token limit. Providers like AtlasCloud reject this large value with HTTP 400. Without the parameter (letting the provider use its default), the request succeeds.

**Fix:** Only send `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` when the value differs from `model.maxTokens` (i.e. when context clamping actually reduced it).

## Affected Files

- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts` — 3 thinkingLevelMap guards + 1 maxTokens guard
- `packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts` — 1 thinkingLevelMap guard
- `packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts` — 1 thinkingLevelMap guard
- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts` — 1 thinkingLevelMap guard
- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts` — 1 thinkingLevelMap guard

## Testing

Verified (runtime patches applied to bundled files):
- `pi --provider openrouter --model "dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free" -p "hello"` — works
- `pi --provider openrouter --model "dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free" --thinking off -p "hi"` — works
- `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` — works
- `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free` — works

issues.title: Allow configuring the idle cache-warming horizon
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Allow configuring the maximum age of idle cache warming, for example 60 or 120 minutes, while keeping the current 30-minute default.

### Why?

With `cacheWarming: "idle"` and a 30-minute prompt-cache TTL, refreshes would be due at roughly 27 and 54 minutes. The hard-coded 30-minute horizon prevents the later refresh even when warming would pass the cost check. A finite, user-selected window would support returning to a large-context session after a longer break without patching Pi.

`cache_warming_decision` cannot extend this horizon: `onAgentSettled()` and `schedule()` enforce it before the decision hook runs. This is present in Pi 1.3.0 and current [`cache-warmer.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/cache-warmer.ts).

### How? (optional)

Expose a global duration setting, defaulting to 30 minutes, and use it instead of `MAX_IDLE_WARMING_AGE_MS`. Preserve the existing clock origin, TTL-based scheduling, economic checks, late-refresh protection, and cancellation behavior.

Related: #9868. This proposal asks for an opt-in duration setting, not a longer default or unlimited warming.

*AI-assisted draft; disclosure follows in a comment.*

issues.title: Context files: strip whole-line HTML comments to match Claude Code

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Problem

Claude Code skips whole-line HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) in `CLAUDE.md`. Pi reads context files verbatim. So a context file written for Claude Code sends its maintainer notes to the model as prompt text.

## Real case

A `CLAUDE.md` in use today holds a 44-line AVOID list: 33 lines, each giving a banned phrasing and the plain phrasing to write instead. The block states its own purpose at line 74:

> `<!-- Claude Code doesn't load them, so the bad words never reach an agent. -->`

That sentence is true for Claude Code and false for pi. A pi session reads all 33 banned phrasings.

The cost is also context. In that file:

| | bytes |
|---|---|
| total | 8683 |
| the 44 comment lines | 4782 |
| rule text | 3901 |

55% of the prompt is a note for a human reviewer.

## Why it matters beyond one file

The same file is now used as `AGENTS.md` so that pi can load it. Without this change, the only ways to keep the notes out of the prompt are:

1. delete the notes, and lose the reviewer guidance; or
2. keep a second copy of the file with the notes removed, and let the 2 copies drift.

Neither is good. Option 2 is exactly the "second home for a rule" problem that makes 2 copies disagree.

## Proposed behaviour

Drop a line when its first non-whitespace characters are `<!--`.

- A comment that shares a line with rule text is **kept**, so no rule is lost.
- The blank lines a removed block leaves behind collapse to one.
- A file with no comment is returned unchanged.

## Pull request

#11249 implements this in `loadContextFileFromDir`, with 6 tests.

## Scope

This is the only behaviour gap I found between the two agents on context-file *content*. The remaining differences are by design:

| | Claude Code | pi |
|---|---|---|
| file names | `CLAUDE.md` | `AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.MD`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.MD` |
| folders | `~/.claude/`, project | agent dir, worktree root, cwd upward |

I am not proposing to change those. This issue is only about making the content of a context file mean the same thing to both agents.

issues.title: durable: MCP extension for Harness hosts

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

A durable MCP extension, next to `@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode` and `/tool-search`: it connects MCP servers and registers their tools as `ToolRegistration`s, so a Harness can offer MCP tools the way the coding agent does.

- Tools as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, deferred or `callers: ["tools"]` by exposure, with a codemode namespace per server carrying its instructions.
- Replay policy from annotations: `readOnlyHint` or `idempotentHint` tools are `replay: "safe"`, everything else unsafe.
- Connections owned by the extension, opened on first use, with reconnects and `McpOAuthStateStore` for credentials.
- The resource tools (`list_mcp_resources`, `read_mcp_resource`, ...).
- `mcp.json` loading shared with the coding agent, so hosts honor the same files and project trust.

### Why?

Agents in [pi-agents](https://github.com/mavam/pi-agents) run on pi-durable and can't use MCP servers. pi-durable already has the pieces: nested calls, `callers`, deferred tools, `tool_search`, and codemode namespaces, and its README mentions an "MCP bridge". But the bridge itself lives only in the coding agent's `AgentSession` extension. Each durable host would otherwise rebuild config loading, exposure, OAuth, and the tool mapping, and Pi's own durable session will need the same.

### How? (optional)

Port the coding agent's MCP extension the way codemode and tool search were ported, as `@earendil-works/pi-durable/mcp` or a durable entry point in `pi-mcp`, e.g., `createMcpExtension({ servers, exposure?, auth? })`. The Harness core stays MCP-agnostic, as with codemode.

Short of that, exporting `loadMcpConfig` (or moving it to `pi-mcp`) would let hosts build the bridge on the same `mcp.json` files and project trust.

Sharing a client with the host's own connections would let pi-agents avoid a second `stdio` process per server, but isn't required.

issues.title: Compaction file lists grow without bound across compactions

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What happened?

Each compaction appends `<read-files>` and `<modified-files>` lists to the summary. `extractFileOperations` in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts` seeds the next compaction's `fileOps` from the previous compaction's `details.readFiles` and `details.modifiedFiles`, so the lists only ever grow. They are never pruned, capped, or filtered.

In a long session (15 days, 95 compactions, heavy subagent use) the latest summary is 225,233 characters. The model prose is 19,640 characters. The remaining ~205,000 characters are 2,102 file paths, 1,312 of them under `/tmp/`. Those ~50k tokens are carried into every context after compaction, so the context refills fast and compaction fires every 30 to 60 minutes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run a session that reads or edits many distinct files over time (subagents writing to `/tmp` make it fast).
2. Let auto-compaction run several times.
3. Compare `summary.length` on successive `compaction` entries in the session JSONL. The prose stays near the summarizer's `maxTokens`; the file lists keep growing.

## Expected behavior

The appended file lists stay bounded. Options: cap each list to the newest N paths, drop paths under the OS temp directory, or do not seed from the previous compaction's details and only list files touched since the last compaction.

Verified in the current `main` source (`compaction.ts` lines 69-78 and `utils.ts` `formatFileOperations`).

## Version

1.4.0

issues.title: registerMarkdownTransformer context lacks message identity - extensions cannot decorate per-message content
issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Add message identity to the transformer context: `messageId` (and `timestamp`, which already exists in the session entry) alongside the current `messageType`, `isStreaming`, and `availableWidth`. Display-only semantics stay exactly as today - the transformer just gets to know which message it is rendering.

## Why?

Without identity, extensions cannot attach per-message data (timestamps, correlation ids, per-message state) to built-in user/assistant messages:

- Streaming: partial assistant updates re-render the same markdown repeatedly, and redraws of older messages happen on width changes - a transformer without identity cannot distinguish "same message, new frame" from "new message", so any stateful workaround corrupts older messages with newer state.
- Multi-block: one assistant message renders through several transformer calls; without identity there is no way to know they belong together.
- Restored/history rendering: resumed sessions re-render without event history, so identity cannot be reconstructed.

The full-message renderer path (`registerMessageRenderer`) covers only custom messages, so built-in messages have no identity-bearing hook at all. Concrete casualty: per-message timestamps (requested in #4859, which was closed as not planned) are unbuildable as an extension.

## How? (optional)

Add `messageId`/`timestamp` to the transformer context object. The session entry already carries a timestamp; a per-session monotonic id (or the entry id) is sufficient. No renderer changes needed - extensions get the data, the built-in renderer stays untouched.

issues.title: Have `/reload` reload `AGENTS.md` for the current session

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

When I edit `AGENTS.md` during a session, the running agent keeps using the version loaded at startup. `/reload` does not pick up the changes, so I have to start a new session. Until then, the LLM follows the stale instructions and can push back against the changes I just made.

## Expected behavior

`/reload` should reread `AGENTS.md` and apply its current contents to the active session, so the next turn follows the updated instructions without requiring a new session.

Related: #9760 discusses refreshing cached context files between turns.

issues.title: HTML export never renders system messages (initial prompt and mid-session section updates)
issues.body:
### What happened?

The HTML session export does not render `role: "system"` entries. The initial prompt and every later section update are in the session JSONL and in the embedded `session-data` of the exported HTML, but nothing shows them on the page.

Reproduced on 1.4.0 with no extensions:

```
pi -ne -ns -p 'reply with ok' --session-dir /tmp/x/sessions
pi --export /tmp/x/sessions/<file>.jsonl /tmp/x/out.html
```

The session has one system message with sections `preamble, tools, rules, docs, addendum, cwd`; it is present in the export's `session-data`, but the preamble text is absent from the rendered HTML. `renderEntry` handles user, assistant, bashExecution and toolResult, with no system branch.

Same for mid-session updates: after editing `AGENTS.md` and running `/reload`, my session had a later system entry patching only `project_context`; it is in the export data and invisible on the page (`getSystemMessageText` / `renderSystemMessageUpdate` produce that text for the model).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the two commands above (any single turn).
2. Open the HTML: no block for the system entry, though it is in the embedded `session-data`.
3. Or: in a fresh session edit `AGENTS.md`, run `/reload`, export, compare entries against the page.

### Expected behavior

System entries render in the transcript, e.g. collapsed on first appearance with the full prompt, and named section updates ("updated section: project_context") where they occur. Or an explicit note that system prompt updates are omitted.

### Why it matters

The export is what gets shared and used to debug a session, but the instructions the model actually received, including mid-session `/reload` updates, are the one part you cannot see. Related but narrower: #3464 (CLI export lacking prompt/tools), #8896 (hidden custom messages).

### Version

1.4.0; still absent in `template.js` on main (2685de7).

issues.title: macOS: aborting a bash command can still run the next command in a; b

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

When a bash tool call is aborted (Esc or timeout), Pi kills the shell's process group with one process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"). On macOS under CPU load, the shell sometimes outlives its foreground child by a few milliseconds and runs the next command. So aborting long_step; next_step can occasionally start next_step. I checked with ps right before the kill: bash is the group leader and both sleeps are in its group.



### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `sleep 30 & sleep 30; echo never` through `createLocalBashOperations().exec` (with no extensions) and abort after 200 ms. Script in the first comment.
2. Run 6 copies in parallel while the machine is busy.
3. `never` showed up in 7 of 135 aborts. With no extra load I got 0 of 90.


### Expected behavior

Aborting stops the whole command line. When I sent SIGSTOP to the group first and then SIGKILL, it went to 0 of 135 under the same load.

### Version

1.4.0

issues.title: forkFrom copies sessions with one appendFileSync per entry, very slow on large sessions
issues.body:
### What happened?

`--fork` on a large session (73 MB, 3,322 entries) took over 30 s before pi answered any RPC, so our host timed out the handshake.

`SessionManager.forkFrom` copies the source with one `appendFileSync` per entry, so every entry reopens and closes the target file. On machines where open/close is expensive (here an endpoint security agent watching file events, ~10 ms per open/close) the fork cost becomes entries × open/close.

Same source file, the copy loop replicated standalone in Node 24 on macOS (no pi, no extensions):

- per-entry `appendFileSync` (current code): 33.5 s
- one `writeFileSync` of the joined lines: 0.19 s

With the security agent excluded for the sessions directory, the per-entry loop drops to 0.43 s, so the cost is per open/close, not data size.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a session with a few thousand entries.
2. Start pi with `--fork <id>` on a machine with an EDR/AV filesystem monitor.
3. The fork takes tens of seconds; nothing answers until the copy finishes.

### Expected behavior

Forking should cost about as much as loading the same file with `--session` (~1 s here). `_rewriteFile` already writes all entries through one fd; `forkFrom` could do the same, or join the lines and write once. Happy to send a PR.

### Version

1.3.0. The loop is unchanged in 1.4.0 and on main (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts`).

issues.title: Extension api providers wiped by mid-session settings reload: 'No API provider registered' uncaughtException

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Mid-session, after pi reloads its settings (file watcher fires on a settings.json write — e.g. `setModel` persists the model), any stream for a model whose `api` is provided by an extension dies with an uncaughtException and the process exits:

```
Error: No API provider registered for api: claude-bridge
    at resolveApiProvider (…)
    at streamAssistantResponse (…)
```

Observed 6 times in one day (pi 1.4.0 and 1.3.0). The model stays selectable the whole time, so the crash lands on the *next* user message after the reload.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load an extension that registers a custom api provider via `registerApiProvider` (I hit this with pi-claude-bridge, but any extension api should do).
2. While a model on that api is active, trigger a settings reload — `/reload`, or any settings.json write the file watcher picks up (a model switch does this: setModel persists settings).
3. Send the next message.

The extension module re-runs on reload, but registration guards (a process-global "already registered" marker survives the reload) or the absence of a second `session_start` leave the api provider unregistered.

### Expected behavior

Reload should preserve extension api registrations, or give extensions a hook/event to restore them after reload; and a missing provider at stream time should surface as a caught, reportable error — not kill the process. Note: `pi -ne` can't show this because no extension api exists without extensions; the defect is in core's `resetApiProviders()` (wipes all non-built-in apis) plus the uncaught escape in the stream path.

### Version

1.3.0, 1.4.0

issues.title: `transformMessages` + `isSameModel === false` thinking block normalization interacts poorly with `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` compat flag

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

When the user switches models, `transformMessages` will normalize non-redacted/plain-text thinking content [by inlining it in to the assistant message content](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/927e98068cda276bf9188f4774fb927c89823388/packages/ai/src/api/transform-messages.ts#L98-L114), with no delimiters or control tokens, in an attempt to be provider agnostic.

But this strips the reasoning content from the assistant message block before it arrives at the checks around `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages`. This means that if you switch from any previous reasoning model to a reasoning model with `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true`, the historical message prefill is a little wonky. Specifically, [the actual attached reasoning content ends up being an empty string](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/927e98068cda276bf9188f4774fb927c89823388/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1000-L1004). This doesn't fundamentally *break* anything, but in my experience, it *does* make the model a wee bit confused about what's going on (or at least it makes `glm-5.2-fp8` via vLLM a little confused).

### Steps to reproduce

- Use a reasoning model with thinking enabled
- Do some work
- Switch to another model/provider with reasoning enabled and `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true` in its compat configs
- Enable reasoning
- Send a prompt
- Observe the outbound REST messages

### Expected behavior

In the case that reasoning context is available as plaintext, the cross-provider normalization should probably try to remain aware of the destination model's `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` configs and adhere to that when possible.

### Version

0.80.2

issues.title: Allow global and per-package overrides of native tool exposure in settings.json

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let users override native extension tools’ exposure through `settings.json`, globally or per package/extension, using existing modes such as `direct`, `deferred`, and `codemode`.

In particular, let users choose **deferred by default**, with direct-exposure exceptions for selected packages. Tools should remain registered and discoverable through `tool_search` and codemode search.

### Why?

Installing a package can add substantial tool schemas and guidance to every session’s initial context, whether those capabilities are needed or not. Users cannot selectively override that exposure through standard settings; they must modify or disable the package, rely on package-specific controls, or use broad codemode-only presentation.

Users should be able to keep capabilities installed without accepting each package’s upfront context cost. A deferred-by-default policy would build on Pi’s existing tool discovery mechanisms: load schemas when needed rather than requiring every package author to opt into deferred exposure.

For example, locally changing process/debugger tools to `deferred` preserved discovery and execution without upfront declarations. That workaround is overwritten by package updates.

### How? (optional)

Apply a configurable global exposure default and per-package overrides when native tools register, including late registration and reload. Preserve `model-only` restrictions.

Related: #8583 and #9796. This request concerns user-controlled exposure, not merely disabling tools.

issues.title: Editor swaps via setEditorComponent drop prompt history (text/appearance copied, history not)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What happened?

When an extension swaps the composer editor via `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()`, `InteractiveMode.setCustomEditorComponent()` builds a new editor instance and copies the current text, callbacks, appearance, and action handlers to it -- but not the prompt history. `Editor.history` is private (only `addToHistory` is public), so the extension cannot carry it over either.

Every swap therefore discards the accumulated prompt history. With an install-then-restore choreography (decorate editor on demand, restore the previous factory later):

- prompts submitted while the decorated editor is live vanish from history browsing afterwards;
- if the restore goes through a factory (a custom editor or another extension's composer), the rebuilt instance starts with an empty history, so Up/Down browsing hard-stops at the first post-restore entry -- the boundary reads to the user as "history browsing broke".

## Repro

1. An extension registers a custom editor wrapping the previously configured factory (e.g. to decorate rendering), then restores the saved factory later.
2. Submit prompts before, during, and after the swap window.
3. Press Up in the composer: entries from the swap window are gone; with a factory-based restore, browsing stops exactly at the swap boundary.

Verified in pi 1.3.0, `dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js`, `setCustomEditorComponent` (around line 2242): `currentText`, `onSubmit`/`onChange`, border/padding/autocomplete settings, and action handlers are copied; `history`/`historyIndex`/`historyDraft` are not.

Related prior reports that were auto-closed without action: #8798 (same root cause via `/reload`), #5466 (asked for `addToHistory` on `ExtensionUIContext`).

## Suggestion

Either:

- carry `history` across swaps in `setCustomEditorComponent` (both directions, like text), or
- expose `getHistory()`/`setHistory()` (or `addToHistory` on `ExtensionUIContext`) so extensions can migrate history themselves.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): render deep session exports iteratively
prs.body:
## What changed

- replace the three recursive session-tree traversals in the HTML export template with explicit iterative stacks
- preserve child ordering, newest-leaf navigation, and active-subtree ordering
- add a 20,000-entry parent-chain regression covering tree construction, active-path flattening, and newest-leaf lookup

## Why

A valid deeply chained Pi Session can overflow the browser JavaScript stack while initializing an otherwise successfully generated export. The failure was observed in `sortChildren`, but the same template also recursively built the node lookup and marked active subtrees, so fixing only the first stack trace would leave the failure class open.

## User impact

Deep native Session exports now render instead of leaving a blank page with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The Session format and shallow-tree presentation are unchanged.

## Validation

- four focused exporter test files passed, 17 tests total
- the new 20,000-entry regression passes all three formerly recursive traversals
- a real 3,039-entry, depth-2,847 sanitized local Session exported successfully with the patched template and rendered in Chrome

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): start when a configured package fails to install
prs.body:
## Summary

- A package configured in settings that cannot be installed no longer aborts startup. Resource resolution records the failure per source, skips that package the way offline mode does, and loads the packages that do install.
- The failure is reported through the extension warning channel: `Extension package "npm:...": failed to install (...). Run "pi remove npm:..." to remove it from settings.json.` Project entries point at `pi remove <source> --local`. Temporary `-e` sources are skipped the same way, with a hint to check the source.
- `--help` and `--list-models` now report runtime diagnostics, so the warning appears on every command the issue lists. Diagnostics go to stderr and exit codes are unchanged.
- A source that failed once is not retried for the rest of the process. Startup resolves packages twice when project trust is resolved, so without that a failing package cost a second npm attempt and printed npm's error twice.
- `pi install` and `pi update --extensions` still report the failure and exit non-zero. `pi config` prints the warning too, so a skipped package is not silently missing from the list.
- `docs/packages.md` documents the behavior.

Fixes #11088

## Validation

- Repro from the issue on unmodified main (936e5f40): `pi -p hello`, `pi --help` and `pi --list-models` all exit 1 with `Error: npm install @example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz --prefix /tmp/p/agent/npm --legacy-peer-deps failed with code 1` and a raw Node stack. With this branch: one warning line, startup continues, `--help` and `--list-models` exit 0.
- A healthy local package next to the broken npm entry still loads: its `--good-pkg-flag` appears in `--help`.
- `git:github.com/example/definitely-not-a-real-repo` warns, is skipped, and leaves no partial checkout under `<agentDir>/git`.
- `pi install npm:@example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz` and `pi update --extensions` still exit 1 with a single error line.
- With a trusted project and a failing project package the hint is `pi remove <source> --local`. An untrusted project never installs the package and prints nothing.
- Interactive startup shows the warning and continues.
- `npm run check`
- `node "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js" --run test/package-manager.test.ts test/resource-loader.test.ts` from `packages/coding-agent` (190 tests).
- `./test.sh` was run. The affected tests pass. Baseline failures in this environment, all present on unmodified main or environmental: `test/auth-storage.test.ts` "keeps a coalesced reload alive while another credential reader is waiting" (also fails on main), `packages/env` ssh suites (the Rust daemon is not built locally), and `packages/durable` timeouts under load (pass when rerun in isolation).

prs.title: Fix thinkingLevelMap?.off type guard and spurious max_completion_tokens
prs.body:
## Problem

Models with `reasoning: true` and `thinkingFormat: "openrouter"` but no `thinkingLevelMap` (e.g. `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free`) fail with HTTP 400 from upstream providers (AtlasCloud) when invoked via `--model`, even though they work via direct API calls.

## Root Causes

### 1. Phantom `reasoning` parameter

`model.thinkingLevelMap?.off !== null` evaluates to `true` when `thinkingLevelMap` is `undefined` (`undefined !== null` → `true`), causing pi to send `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` even when thinking is off. Upstream providers like AtlasCloud reject this.

**Fix:** Changed to `model.thinkingLevelMap != null && model.thinkingLevelMap.off !== null` in all 5 API implementations.

### 2. Unconditional `max_completion_tokens`

`buildParams` always sends `max_completion_tokens` set to `model.maxTokens` (460800 for some OpenRouter models) even when the user didn't request a limit, causing 400 from providers with smaller output limits.

**Fix:** Only send `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` when the value differs from `model.maxTokens` (i.e. when context clamping actually reduced it).

## Files Changed

- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts` — thinkingLevelMap guard (3x) + maxTokens guard (1x)
- `packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts` — thinkingLevelMap guard (1x)
- `packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts` — thinkingLevelMap guard (1x)
- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts` — thinkingLevelMap guard (1x)
- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts` — thinkingLevelMap guard (1x)

## Testing

Verified with installed pi binary:
- `pi --provider openrouter --model "dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free" -p "hello"` — ✅ works
- `pi --provider openrouter --model "dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free" --thinking off -p "hi"` — ✅ works
- `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` — ✅ works
- `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free` — ✅ works

prs.title: fix(tui,coding-agent): rank contiguous fuzzy matches and search session fields separately
prs.body:
Closes #11220. Also addresses #10552, #10065, #11024.

## Problem

`fuzzyMatch()` matched each query character at its first occurrence after the previous one (greedy leftmost) and scored only that alignment. A query could be scattered over an earlier unrelated part of the text, while the real match later in the text ranked last.

`/model` search text is `provider provider/id provider id name`. Scores before (lower = better):

```
query "opus"
41.1  openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b        o,p,u from "openrouter", s from "oss"
41.6  openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
57.9  openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.1   last

query "astra" (provider radius)
27.7  gpt-5.4        "radius radius/gpt" already contains a,s,t,r,a
39.9  gpt-6-astra    last
```

`/resume` matched one string `id name allMessagesText cwd`. `allMessagesText` is the full text of every user/assistant message (MBs per session), so:

- nearly any short query matched scattered letters somewhere (`opus` in "lorem ipsum dolor sit"),
- digits matched scattered inside UUIDs (`1024` in `019e9024-...`, #11024),
- the `i * 0.1` position penalty buried a real word deep in a transcript.

## Changes

**`packages/tui/src/fuzzy.ts`**: also score every contiguous occurrence of the query and keep the best alignment (greedy or contiguous). No flat substring bonus, so existing ranking rules hold (e.g. `fb` still prefers `foo-bar` over `afbx`). Only short strings use it now, so the extra `indexOf` loop is cheap.

After:

```
query "opus"
-28.6  anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
-23.8  openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.1
 29.1  anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5
 41.1  openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b
 41.6  openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5

query "astra"
-49.0  gpt-6-astra   first
 27.7  gpt-5.4
```

**`packages/coding-agent/.../session-selector-search.ts`**: match fields separately, so a token never spans fields (different tokens may match different fields).

| Field | Match |
|---|---|
| name | fuzzy |
| cwd | fuzzy |
| id | exact substring, anywhere |
| messages | exact substring, no position penalty |

Ranking per token: text in name > text in id/messages/cwd > scattered match in name/cwd. Ties: most recently modified first. Quoted phrases and `re:` regex use the same fields and tiers (no position penalty). Lowercased message text is cached per session (`WeakMap`), not recomputed per keystroke. `allMessagesText` stays uncapped (it was never capped).

Examples:

```
query "1024"
before: 019e9024-... (scattered in UUID) ranked above session named "#1024 TDD ..."
after:  only "#1024 TDD ..." matches; "9024-aa" still finds the UUID session

query "opus"
before: session with "opus" deep in messages scored ~3000 with a substring bonus,
        below sessions where o,p,u,s are scattered
after:  sessions containing "opus" match, ordered by modified time;
        scattered-only sessions do not match

query "cache"
after:  name "Cache work" > message "...the cache." > name "c-a-c-h-e notes"
```

## Performance

500 sessions, 23 MB message text, ms per keystroke (median / p90):

| Typing | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `opus` ... `opus cache` | 11.2 / 12.5 | 0.3 / 0.5 |
| `xylophone`, `日本語` (rare / no match) | 7.3 / 8.6 | 4.9 / 9.5 |
| `"opus cache"` phrase | 8.1 / 307.6 | 1.9 / 2.5 |

## Relation to #11145

#11145 prefers the first contiguous occurrence with a flat -100 bonus in the shared matcher. That fixes `/model` but changes ranking for every `fuzzyMatch` caller (its `fb`/`afbx` test was rewritten) and makes `/resume` worse for words deep in a transcript. Its scoped-order option is not included here.

## Tests

- `packages/tui/test/fuzzy.test.ts`: opus vs sonnet/gpt-oss, best vs first occurrence, astra with radius prefix
- `packages/coding-agent/test/model-search.test.ts`: opus and firerouter (#10065) via `getModelSelectorSearchText`
- `packages/coding-agent/test/session-selector-search.test.ts`: position independence, UUID scatter (#11024), tier order, per-field tokens, regex name priority

prs.title: fix: preserve scoped model order and prefer substring matches
prs.body:
This makes two changes to fuzzy scoring:

1. Add an option to ignore match-position penalties and enable it in the scoped model picker. Equivalent matches then receive equal scores, so the existing stable sort keeps their configured sequence. There is no separate scoped-ordering step; better-scoring matches still rank higher.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): render HTML export for sessions deeper than the call stack
prs.body:
The HTML export viewer built its session tree with recursive walks (`sortChildren`, `mapNodes`, `markActive`) that recurse once per entry. A long session is mostly a single parent chain, so ~6k+ entries overflowed the call stack and the page rendered blank.

Changes in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js`:
- `sortChildren`: sort each node's children in a flat loop over all nodes.
- `mapNodes` (`findNewestLeaf`): explicit stack.
- `markActive` (`flattenTree`): iterative post-order.
- `getPath`: `push` + `reverse` instead of `unshift` (avoids O(n^2) on long chains).

Regression test `test/export-html-deep-tree.test.ts` exports a 20,000-entry chain and runs the viewer's tree functions. It fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on the old template.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): write forked session through one fd
prs.body:
`SessionManager.forkFrom` wrote the new header with `writeFileSync`, then called `appendFileSync` once for every copied entry. Each of those calls opens and closes the target file. Forking a 3,000-entry session therefore opened the new file about 3,000 times. Where open/close is expensive, for example under an endpoint security file monitor, a fork took tens of seconds. In the issue, a 73 MB session took over 30 s.

The change opens the new file once with `wx`, writes the header and all non-header entries through that fd, and closes it in `finally`. This is the same pattern `_rewriteFile` already uses. The `wx` flag still makes the fork fail if the target file already exists.

Testing:
- Added `test/session-manager/fork-from.test.ts`. It forks a 50-entry session and checks three things: the new file is opened for writing exactly once (`wx`), `appendFileSync` is never called on it, and the content is copied unchanged. The test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- All tests in `test/session-manager/` pass, and `npm run check` passes.
- Ran `strace -e openat` while forking a synthetic 3,000-entry session. Before the fix the target file was opened 3,002 times; after it, 2 times (one write, one load).

Fixes #11253

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(extensions): preserve ctx.ui getters through wrapUIPromptContext
prs.body:
## Problem

`ExtensionRunner.wrapUIPromptContext` spreads the UI context:

```ts
return {
    ...ui,   // getters resolved here, once
    select: ...,
};
```

Object spread evaluates `get theme()` **at bind time**. A host that binds the extension UI context before initializing its global theme (pi-web-ui binds sessions on creation, `initTheme()` happens later in its startup) freezes `ctx.ui.theme` as `undefined` **for the whole session** — later access never re-evaluates the getter.

Extensions that guard on the theme then silently degrade forever. Real case: [ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail)'s `syncStatus` has `if (!theme?.fg) return;` — its 🐴 status indicator never appeared in pi-web-ui's web footer, with zero errors anywhere. Took ~1h of probe-based debugging (comparing `Object.keys(ctx.ui)`: has `setStatus`, no `theme`) to find.

## Fix

Prototype-chain the original context instead of spreading, so accessors stay live:

```ts
const wrapped = Object.create(ui) as ExtensionUIContext;
wrapped.select = ...;
```

The five dialog methods keep their exact `withUIPrompt` wrapping; only the getter resolution changes. `Object.create` also keeps own properties (widgets, statuses maps) reachable via the prototype chain.

## Docs

Added a note in `extensions.md` — hosts may never initialize the theme, so extensions should still treat `ctx.ui.theme` as optional and degrade gracefully.

## Testing

- `vitest --run test/extensions` — 96 passed (incl. all 56 runner tests)
- Repo `check` (biome, tsc, import/entry-graphs, install-lock) passed in pre-commit

Reported downstream: ponytail received a local hotfix; this removes the trap for every extension author.

prs.title: fix(ai): use OpenRouter-reported total cost
prs.body:
OpenRouter reports the actual amount billed for each request. This will often differ from Pi’s catalog estimate because OpenRouter routes requests to differently priced providers. OpenRouter's [Usage Accounting docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting) explain how this works; we've referenced those docs and the type schemas for making this change.

This commit adds `applyOpenRouterReportedCost` such that for OpenRouter requests, we make `cost.total` be the reported cost. This means
- `cost.total` is the best available total cost
- `cost.input`, `cost.output`, `cost.cacheRead`, and `cost.cacheWrite` remain catalog-derived estimates.
- If the cost is missing or invalid, `cost.total` falls back to the sum of those estimates.
- For BYOK requests, the total includes both OpenRouter’s fee and the upstream inference cost.

We have confirmed for non-BYOK and BYOK (OpenAI and Anthropic) that the cost.total is now correct, where it would in a few cases have been incorrect.

But I'm not sure this is the best solution since now cost.total may intentionally differ from the sum of the component fields.

This fixes #9980, partially addresses #8940 although that also asks for some more metadata like which provider served the request.

issues.title: feat(serve): support per-session working directories within a shared workspace

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Issue needs to be triaged and labeled

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Allow ordinary `qwen serve` sessions to use independent working directories while remaining bound to one registered workspace.

For example:

```text
/work/project/                  # one registered workspace
  QWEN.md
  .qwen/                        # shared workspace configuration and skills
  sessions/
    session-a/                  # effective working directory of Session A
    session-b/                  # effective working directory of Session B
```

The requested behavior is:

- Register and prepare `/work/project` once. Sessions reuse its workspace-level configuration, instructions, and skills.
- Create A and B under that same workspace, with separate effective working directories. Relative file operations in A use `session-a`; those in B use `session-b`. Changing or loading one session must not change the other's directory.
- Keep workspace ownership and session-history storage associated with `/work/project`. The session directories must not become additional registered workspaces.
- When loading an existing session after a daemon or container restart, allow the caller to reapply its working directory before any prompt or tool execution. The caller may have already restored the session records and working files. Loading A should not require loading B.
- Support both the primary workspace and dynamically registered secondary workspaces.

The API shape is open: a directory option on create/load, or an existing directory-selection operation with the required ordering, would both satisfy the need. A new registration per session would not.

### Why is this needed?

Applications embedding `qwen serve` can run many conversations against the same project configuration. Each conversation needs its own working files, but registering every session directory as a separate workspace multiplies workspace initialization and consumes the workspace registration limit.

The desired separation is between the registered workspace/configuration scope and each session's effective working directory. Normal session initialization can still happen; the goal is to avoid a new workspace initialization and registration for every session.

Ordinary directories are sufficient. Git repositories, worktrees, commit-history recovery, and index/staging-state recovery are not required for this use case.

### Additional context

In the source checked at main commit `32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e`, [`POST /session/:id/cd` is still classified as primary-workspace-only](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e/packages/cli/src/serve/routes/session.ts#L428), so that public operation does not currently cover dynamically registered workspaces.

File backup and transfer remain the caller's responsibility. The requested Qwen capability is to create/load a session under its registered workspace and establish the correct execution directory before it runs.

Related: #15298 concerns configuring the built-in Conversations root. This request concerns independent directories for ordinary sessions within an existing registered workspace.

issues.title: Web Shell: move Create group into the workspace More menu to avoid confusion with new sessions

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In the Web Shell sidebar, move **Create group** from the inline `+` button on each workspace row into that workspace's **More (`⋮`) menu**.

- Remove the inline `+` button that currently creates a group.
- Add **Create group** to the same workspace's More menu, preserving its existing localized name, including the Chinese label **新建分组**.
- Keep the existing group-creation flow and behavior, including which workspace receives the new group. This is an entry-point relocation only.

### Why is this needed?

Creating a new session is the most frequent action users intend to perform at the workspace level. The prominent `+` icon is easily interpreted as “new session,” but actually creates a group. This mismatch causes repeated accidental clicks and gives a lower-frequency organizational action too much visual prominence.

Group creation is used relatively infrequently. Keeping it in the workspace More menu preserves access while reducing ambiguity and accidental activation in the primary workspace actions.

### Additional context

**Current behavior / how to observe**

1. Open the Web Shell sidebar and hover over a workspace row to reveal its actions.
2. The row shows a `+` button next to the new-session action and the `⋮` menu.
3. The `+` button is labeled **Create group** and starts group creation, although users can mistake it for session creation.

The reported screenshot shows this `+` immediately to the right of the `qwen-code` workspace name, with a **Create group** tooltip. This request concerns the workspace's `⋮` actions menu, rather than its hover overview panel.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The workspace row no longer shows the inline Create group `+` button, including on hover.
- [ ] The workspace More (`⋮`) menu contains the existing localized **Create group / 新建分组** action.
- [ ] Selecting the menu item opens the same group-creation flow and creates the group in the workspace whose menu was opened, including when multiple workspaces are present.
- [ ] Existing availability and permission restrictions for group creation remain unchanged.
- [ ] The existing new-session action remains available and keeps its current behavior; existing groups and sessions are unaffected.

**Related work**

- #9398 (closed) / #9400 (merged) added the Create group tooltip. That explains the icon on hover but does not address its prominence or the recurring confusion with new-session creation.
- #10399 describes broader workspace overview and More-menu improvements. This request is a focused usability adjustment to the group-creation entry point, without expanding that broader scope.

**中文说明**

工作区层级下，用户最高频的操作是新建会话，但当前工作区行内的「+」实际用于「新建分组」，视觉上过于突出，容易被误认为新建会话，造成反复误操作。新建分组属于相对低频的整理操作，因此应移除工作区行内的该「+」按钮，将「新建分组」迁移至对应工作区的「更多（⋮）」菜单中。名称、功能、创建流程、所属工作区及现有可用性限制保持一致；现有新建会话入口和已有分组、会话不受影响。

issues.title: Web Shell: standardize display terminology on Workspace and Session

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/ui
labels.description: User interface and display

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Standardize the Web Shell's user-facing terminology on **Workspace / 工作区** and **Session / 会话**, following the [recorded meeting conclusion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14988#issuecomment-6340677765) to align with DSH naming.

This replaces the original two-option proposal: **Project versus Workspace is no longer an open choice in this proposal, and ordinary conversational work items should be called Sessions rather than Tasks.** The intended implementation is the smallest practical change to existing display strings and their tooltips/accessibility labels.

### Final terminology

- **Workspace / 工作区:** the existing directory-backed object shown in the sidebar, including its existing registration and management actions.
- **Session / 会话:** an ordinary conversation opened or created in that workspace, or an existing conversation without a workspace association.
- **Recent / 最近:** the recent-session view; its creation action is **New session / 新建会话**.
- A filesystem directory remains a path associated with the workspace. This proposal does not introduce another organizational entity or change the directory selection flow.

### Observed wording → final wording

The current main-branch strings were checked while preparing this revision. The two Recent rows refer to the #14904 preview, which is still an open draft at the time of this update.

| Existing surface | Observed wording (EN / 中文) | Final wording (EN / 中文) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar container section | Project / 项目 | Workspaces / 工作区 |
| Existing add action | Add workspace / 添加工作区 | Add workspace / 添加工作区 — retain |
| Existing add dialog title | Add Workspace / 添加工作区 | Add workspace / 添加工作区 |
| Add dialog submit button | Register / 注册 | Add workspace / 添加工作区 |
| Existing path field | Directory path / 目录路径 | Directory path / 目录路径 — retain |
| Management entry | Manage workspaces… / 管理工作区… | Manage workspaces… / 管理工作区… — retain |
| Management page | Workspaces / 工作区总览 | Workspaces / 工作区总览 — retain |
| Rename dialog | Rename Workspace / 重命名工作区 | Rename workspace / 重命名工作区 |
| Remove action | Remove workspace / 移除工作区 | Remove workspace / 移除工作区 — retain |
| Top sidebar creation action | New task / 新建任务 | New session / 新建会话 |
| Creation action on a workspace row/menu | New task / 新建任务 | New session / 新建会话 |
| Worktree conversation creation action | New worktree task / 新建 Worktree 任务 | New worktree session / 新建 Worktree 会话 |
| Recent heading in #14904 preview | Recent sessions / 最近会话 | Recent / 最近 |
| New icon beside Recent in that preview | New task / 新建任务 | New session / 新建会话 |
| Existing group for conversations without a workspace | No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话 | No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话 — retain pending a separate naming decision |
| Workspace-specific Memory scope label | Project / 项目级 | Workspace / 工作区级 |
| That Memory description | Saved to this workspace memory file / 保存到当前 workspace memory 文件 | Saved to this workspace memory file / 保存到当前工作区的记忆文件 |

Apply the same nouns to existing confirmation text, errors, counts, expansion/collapse tooltips, and accessible names reached by these flows. Singular **Workspace** is appropriate for one object; the section containing several uses **Workspaces**. Prefer sentence case for English actions and dialog titles.

### Scope and open follow-up

**In scope:** copy/i18n changes for these existing surfaces. “New session” changes the label of the existing ordinary-conversation action; it does not change how or where a session is created. Recent's label can follow this decision when that feature lands; this naming issue does not require its aggregation implementation.

**The unassociated-conversation group still needs a separate label decision.** The earlier “Standalone tasks / 独立任务” candidate is superseded by the Session terminology and must not be treated as an agreed final name. Keep **No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话** for the minimal change. If the group is renamed later, its noun should remain **Session / 会话**.

The suggestion to move this group out of Projects/Workspaces and make it a peer section remains a **separate hierarchy proposal**, as discussed in the comments. It is not required for this copy change. Retain the existing placement, collapse behavior, routing, ownership, and standalone capabilities here.

Do not rename SDK/API fields, stored identifiers, configuration keys, internal symbols, or unused translation keys as part of this work. **Scheduled tasks, todo items, agent/tool executions, external services' Projects, and Git worktrees retain their actual domain meanings**; do not globally replace every occurrence of “task” or “project.”

The original Agent-creation example was inaccurate: its rendered scope selector already says **Workspace / 工作区**. Leave that correct label in place; unused keys are not evidence of visible inconsistency.

## Why is this needed?

The sidebar currently places Workspace actions under a Project heading and calls ordinary conversation creation New task. Using Workspace and Session consistently makes the existing object and action names match across a single flow, while retaining the product behavior users already have.

## Additional context

### Acceptance criteria

1. In English and Chinese, the sidebar and its existing add/manage/rename/remove flows consistently use Workspace terminology.
2. The top, workspace-row/menu, and worktree conversation creation entries use Session terminology. Matching tooltips and accessible names agree. Recent's action follows the same rule where that view is available.
3. The workspace Memory scope label and description agree on Workspace.
4. The no-workspace group remains available under its existing label and placement. No migration, new fields, additional hints, or behavior changes are required.
5. Scheduled-task and other genuine domain terms remain distinguishable from ordinary sessions.

### Earlier discussion and images

The original mockups illustrate the earlier alternatives and are **superseded for final naming**, especially their “New task” / “Standalone tasks” labels and proposed group placement. They are not acceptance criteria for this revision. The [product reference screenshots](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14988#issuecomment-6339116677) remain background only; the final vocabulary follows the recorded meeting conclusion.

Related: #14901 / #14904 (Recent), #10399 (workspace management surfaces), #12444 (workspace pinning). Their feature work is independent of this terminology change.

issues.title: Tell the model which shell it uses, instead of letting it assume bash

labels.name: status/need-information
labels.description: More information is needed to resolve this issue.

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: category/tools
labels.description: Tool integration and execution

labels.name: scope/shell
labels.description: Shell command execution

labels.name: scope/windows
labels.description: Windows specific issues

labels.name: type/enhancement
labels.description: Non-bug improvement or optimization

issues.body:
On Windows, Qwen Code runs shell commands through cmd.exe, but nothing in the system prompt says which shell is in use, so the model assumes a POSIX shell and writes commands that cannot work there. Each failure costs a full turn.

I saw this twice in one unattended run on Windows 11, against a local model served by an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The agent called `node --version; npm --version; echo "---"` and the answer was `node: bad option: --version;`, because in cmd a semicolon does not separate commands and the rest of the line becomes an argument of node. It also called `curl -sI https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/... | head -n 3` and the answer was `"head" non è riconosciuto come comando interno o esterno`, because cmd has no head.

The model recovered on the next call both times, so this is not a loop and not a broken tool. What is missing is a fact: which shell will execute the command. The environment section mentions the platform, but Platform win32 is not enough to decide the syntax, because a Windows machine can run cmd, PowerShell, or a POSIX shell inside WSL.

I would like Qwen Code to state the effective shell in the system prompt on every platform. On Windows that would mean saying that commands are executed by cmd.exe, and that forms like chaining with a semicolon, head, grep, wc and single quotes do not work there. On Linux and macOS the same sentence would say that bash is used. Removing the guess is more useful than replacing one guess with another, so the sentence should describe what the harness really does, not what is common on that platform.

This is a request about the information given to the model, not about how commands are executed. A user should not have to discover that the shell has to be named in a prompt of their own before the agent stops wasting turns.
