issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Discuss a clearer name and sidebar placement for the existing **No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话** group, separately from the copy-only Workspace/Session terminology update in #14988.

The agreed core nouns are **Workspace / 工作区** and **Session / 会话**. Any replacement name should use Session, not Task. **Standalone sessions / 独立会话** is one candidate, not a decided label. Keeping the current name is also an option if it communicates the association more clearly.

There are two decisions:

1. **Naming:** what should users see for conversations that are not associated with a registered workspace? Please compare the clarity of “No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话” and “Standalone sessions / 独立会话”, or suggest a better Session-based name.
2. **Placement:** make this group a peer of **Workspaces**, instead of nesting it inside that section. Expanding Workspaces should show the actual workspace entries and their sessions; conversations without a workspace association should have their own peer group.

Illustrative structure, with the candidate label explicitly provisional:

```text
Workspaces
  qwen-code
    Review sidebar wording
  design-notes
    Draft release notes
Standalone sessions  ← candidate name, not yet decided
  Discuss a technical question
Recent               ← where the Recent feature is available
  …
```

The peer group should retain its own existing expand/collapse interaction independently of Workspaces. Collapsing Workspaces should not hide these unassociated sessions. Moving the group should preserve existing host/daemon ownership, visibility restrictions, search behavior, selection, pagination, and creation/opening behavior; it should not make a previously hidden session source visible in a host mode that does not support it.

## Why is this needed?

A category named “No-workspace sessions” inside the workspace/project section makes its organizational relationship hard to understand. In current main, collapsing that section hides the group, and the collapsed state is persisted across reloads. Expanding the section or using its search action restores visibility, so this is a discoverability issue, not lost data or permanently inaccessible conversations.

A clearer label and independent placement would explain that these are ordinary sessions without a workspace association. “Standalone” must not imply that the session has no execution environment or change its filesystem permissions or capabilities.

## Additional context

This is the explicit follow-up requested in #14988. The parent issue's final copy-only plan leaves **No-workspace sessions** unchanged; its PR should not implement either this rename or this layout change.

Source checked at main `32b4234b849c`: [the shared Workspaces collapse boundary and standalone group](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.tsx#L6977-L7043). This is static source verification, not a new runtime reproduction.

Related work has different scope: #14901 / #14904 add a recent-session view; #11878 concerns Session Overview; #15304 concerns when newly created standalone sessions first appear in the existing list. This issue concerns the existing group's name and hierarchy. No matching dedicated placement/naming issue was found in searches for standalone/sidebar/group/collapse and 无工作区/分组.

Suggested acceptance criteria after the product decisions:

- The chosen name is consistent in English and Chinese and uses Session terminology.
- Workspaces and the unassociated-session group are peers; each can be collapsed independently, including after reload.
- Existing source restrictions and host ownership remain intact. Search, opening, selection, pagination, and existing session capabilities are preserved.
- No task storage migration, new backend entity, or automatic workspace association is introduced.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 希望调整什么？

从 #14988 的纯文案修改中拆出，单独讨论目前“无工作区会话”分组的**名称与位置**。核心名词已确定为“工作区 / Workspace、会话 / Session”，所以新的候选名称应使用“会话”，不再使用“独立任务”。

需要分别确定：

1. **叫什么：**“独立会话 / Standalone sessions”只是候选，名称尚未确定。请比较它与现有“无工作区会话”的清晰程度，也可以提出其他基于“会话”的名称。
2. **放哪里：**建议将该分组移出“工作区”，与工作区放在同一级。展开工作区后只列出具体工作区，各工作区下面再展示其会话；未关联工作区的会话拥有单独的同级分组。

分组应独立展开和收起，折叠工作区不应再隐藏未关联会话。调整时保留既有主机/daemon 归属、可见性限制、搜索、选中、分页、创建及打开行为，不应在原本不支持该来源的宿主模式中额外暴露会话。

## 为什么需要？

“无工作区会话”放在工作区分类内部，组织关系难以理解。当前代码中折叠工作区会隐藏该分组，且折叠状态跨刷新保留。展开或点击搜索可以恢复显示，因此属于可发现性问题，不是数据丢失或永久不可访问。

“独立”仅描述未关联工作区的组织关系，不表示没有运行环境，也不应改变文件权限及现有能力。

## 范围与验收

#14988 的文案 PR 暂时保留原名称和原位置，不在其中实现本 Issue 的改名或层级调整。本 Issue 的产品决策完成后，应确保：中英文名称统一使用“会话”；两个同级分组可独立折叠并保持刷新后的状态；既有来源限制、归属、搜索、打开、选中、分页和运行能力保持一致；不新增后端实体、存储迁移或自动绑定工作区。

已核对上面链接的 main 源码，本次未新增运行时复现。#14901 / #14904、#11878、#15304 分别关注最近列表、会话总览、创建后列表刷新，与本 Issue 不同。

issues.title: Shell safety parser triggers ~1.6 GiB transient WASM compiler allocation on Node 24.16.0

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/performance
labels.description: Performance and optimization

labels.name: scope/shell
labels.description: Shell command execution

labels.name: scope/memory-usage
labels.description: Memory consumption

issues.body:
### What happened?

Shell safety classification in Qwen Code 0.25.2 can trigger a transient native-memory spike during V8 optimization of the bundled Bash WASM parser. On Linux x64 with Node v24.16.0, 100 calls to the real published `classifyShellCommandSafety('ls -la /tmp')` raised sampled process RSS to **1777.89 MiB**, while JavaScript heap usage after the loop was **47.33 MiB**. RSS fell again after compilation.

No shell command was executed. The reproduction requires no model, credentials, Python process, upload, or external service. This is a memory-performance/stability bug: the transient allocation can exhaust the remaining memory budget of a constrained process/container. The isolated runs reproduced the allocation spike, **not an ACP crash or cgroup OOM kill**.

#### Minimal reproduction

Use Linux x64 and Node **v24.16.0**, in a scratch directory with enough free memory for a roughly 1.8 GiB process. Download the published package without installing it globally:

```sh
npm pack @qwen-code/qwen-code@0.25.2 --ignore-scripts
tar -xzf qwen-code-qwen-code-0.25.2.tgz
```

Save this as `repro.mjs` beside the extracted `package` directory. The chunk name is specific to this pinned release; it directly exports the real classifier.

```js
import { classifyShellCommandSafety } from './package/chunks/chunk-IFAUFERF.js';

const input = 'ls -la /tmp';
console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: 'before', memory: process.memoryUsage() }));
const results = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
  results.push(await classifyShellCommandSafety(input));
}
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  event: 'after',
  calls: results.length,
  classifications: [...new Set(results)],
  memory: process.memoryUsage(),
}));
const timer = setInterval(() => {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: 'retained', memory: process.memoryUsage() }));
}, 1000);
await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20000));
clearInterval(timer);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: 'done', memory: process.memoryUsage() }));
```

Run these sequentially in fresh processes using the pinned Node binary, with `NODE_OPTIONS` unset:

```sh
env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --trace-wasm-compilation-times repro.mjs
env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --trace-wasm-compilation-times --no-wasm-tier-up repro.mjs
env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --trace-wasm-compilation-times --no-wasm-tier-up --no-wasm-dynamic-tiering repro.mjs
```

Keep the process alive after parsing: the optimization runs in the background. One classification of this simple input did **not** trigger the spike in the initial control; 100 sequential classifications did. The input string is only parsed, never executed.

#### Measured results

Each condition used one fresh process. RSS and kernel high-water marks were read from `/proc/<pid>/status` approximately every 50 ms (411 samples per repeated-call run). The one-second memory prints above are useful for observing the transient pattern but can miss its maximum.

| Node flags | Sampled peak RSS (MiB) | Kernel RSS high-water mark (MiB) | JS heapUsed after loop (MiB) | Function #28 TurboFan compilation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Default | 1777.89 | 1780.73 | 47.33 | Yes |
| `--no-wasm-tier-up` | 1767.55 | 1771.68 | 47.22 | Yes |
| `--no-wasm-tier-up --no-wasm-dynamic-tiering` | 162.52 | 162.52 | 47.28 | No |

All 100 classifications in each condition returned `read-only`. All processes exited 0 without hitting the test's timeout or RSS guard. The guard was 2560 MiB sampled RSS and 45 seconds per child; tests ran sequentially with at least 4 GiB host memory available before each run.

The default run logged the following (process address omitted):

```text
Compiled function <address>#28 using TurboFan, took 1428 ms and 1732255216 / 1888562064 max/total bytes; bodysize 212599 codesize 300788 name wasm-function#28
```

The single-flag run reported the same maximum allocation, with 1392 ms compilation time. That is **1,732,255,216 bytes (~1.61 GiB)** of maximum temporary compiler allocation. With both flags disabled, function #28 used Liftoff and did not log a TurboFan compilation. Compiler allocation accounting and process RSS are separate measurements.

### What did you expect to happen?

Classifying small shell commands should not require a multi-gigabyte process memory budget because of background parser optimization. Shell safety checks should remain enabled, with memory usage that is practical in constrained environments.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

- Qwen Code: published npm package `@qwen-code/qwen-code@0.25.2`
- Runtime: Node.js `v24.16.0`
- OS/architecture: Linux x64
- Entrypoint: directly exported classifier from the unmodified published bundle
- npm tarball SHA1: `8a391f83d9ab4db18b2bde024ad67afd890b40cc`
- Embedded `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` SHA256: `807dcdb1380a59befb112ed8fbd3d3872c7fadaf5903a769282b50973b30696d`
- Embedded asset: `tree-sitter-bash-TGZOTF7S.js`

`qwen -p '/about'` was also attempted with an isolated empty configuration. It exited 1 with the following output, so the environment above is recorded from the actual test runtime and package instead:

```text
No auth type is selected. Please configure an auth type (e.g. via settings or `--auth-type`) before running in non-interactive mode.
```

</details>

### Anything else we need to know?

The two Node flags are a verified workaround for this parser workload on the tested Node version, not a validated product-wide fix. Disabling optimized WASM compilation may affect other WASM workloads; no general performance claim is made. A JavaScript old-space limit does not directly bound native compiler allocations.

This report uses a synthetic, non-sensitive input and independent measurements. It does not replay an application-specific incident or establish behavior on other Node versions or the latest development build.

I searched existing issues and PRs for WASM, tree-sitter memory, TurboFan, and the tiering flags. #9198 and #11724 concern memory/OOM symptoms without evidence identifying this compiler spike; #2740 concerns a missing WASM file. PR #6747 defers loading the parser runtime at startup rather than addressing optimization-time memory allocation. I did not find a dedicated report for this reproducible signature.

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: roadmap/platform-distribution
labels.description: Roadmap: Platform and distribution

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

A generic, opt-in **HTTP-backed Runtime provisioner** for the Managed Agent Runtime Broker: `qwen.managed-agent.runtime-broker.provisioner=external`. The Broker delegates the physical lifecycle of a Session-exclusive tool worker to an operator-run HTTP service, and keeps everything it owns today — seed/credential minting, attestation, lease/epoch fencing, the binding ledger, reconciliation and the tool protocol.

The point is to let a deployment run each Session's `managed-runtime-worker` on infrastructure it already operates (a managed sandbox platform, ECI, an internal container pool, …) **without** Kubernetes, without SSH, and without vendor code in this repository.

**Proposed contract (Broker → provider), all POST, bearer-authenticated:**

| Route | Request | Response | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/provision` | `provisionRequestId`, scope (tenant / workspace / generation / cwd / storageId), the full worker **boot document** (v1 or managed-context v2), previously saved `handle` if any | `{ handle, endpoint }` — `handle` is an opaque provider identity (≤ 4 KiB JSON), `endpoint` is the worker's HTTP(S) origin | `ensureResource` / `provision(request, seed)` |
| `/observe` | `provisionRequestId`, `handle` | `{ state: RUNNING \| GONE \| UNKNOWN, endpoint? }` | `reconcile` |
| `/release` | `provisionRequestId`, `handle`, `reason` | `{ stopped: true \| false }` | `release` / `stopDrained` |

The provider starts the worker with the existing container entry, `qwen managed-runtime-worker --container-boot <file>`, which already listens on `0.0.0.0:43190` and enforces the bearer + lease-id + epoch headers. The Broker then attests the returned endpoint exactly as it attests a local-process or Kubernetes worker; a provider can never inject an identity the Broker did not mint. `provision` must be idempotent on `provisionRequestId` (same handle back on retry); observe/attest mismatch keeps the existing fail-closed `runtime_reconciliation_required` / LOST semantics; the provider is never asked to replay an execution.

### Why is this needed?

Today a Hosted tool worker can only be placed by:

- `local-process` — same host as the Java service (the only accepted path);
- SSH — needs a pre-provisioned host reachable over SSH (#11746, `docs/design/2026-10-15-managed-ssh-runtime.md`);
- Kubernetes — experimental, and `EmbeddedRuntimeBroker.provisioner()` refuses it in Spring ("supported: local-process, static").

`static` is not an escape hatch either: preflight rejects it for Workspace files ("Workspace files cannot use the static provisioner"), and it is one fixed worker for every Session.

So a deployment that has a sandbox/container platform but no Kubernetes cluster has no way to give each Session its own isolated worker. The selection is a hard-coded `if/else` with no Spring extension point (unlike `HarnessConnector` or `ToolPublicationObjectStore`, which are `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`), so the only option is forking the Broker.

This also matches the direction already stated in #11695 / #11698: the executor is pluggable, the protocol lives here, and "any managed control plane — provisioning, multi-tenancy, scheduling — ships elsewhere". An external provisioner is the Broker-side half of that boundary.

**Evidence that the remaining pieces already work across machines (v0.26.0, two separate sandbox instances, no shared network except their public HTTPS endpoints):**

1. Java service + Hosted Harness + MySQL with `local-process`: a Workspace Session ran `write_file` + `read_file` end to end (`ma_runtime_binding.provisioner_kind=local-process`, `binding_state=READY`).
2. In a second instance, `managed-runtime-worker --container-boot boot.json` (boot v1) bound `0.0.0.0:43190` and printed `ready`.
3. From the first instance, through the platform's HTTPS endpoint for port 43190, `POST /internal/managed-runtime/v2/attest` returned **200** with the matching identity; a wrong token returned **401** and a wrong epoch **409**. `BrokerValues.requireOrigin` already accepts `https` origins, so the lease/transport path needs no change.

### Additional context

**Scope I'd suggest for a first PR (deliberately narrow):**

- `ExternalRuntimeProvisioner` (kind `external`) in `runtimebroker.provisioning`, plus a small bounded JSON HTTP client, following the `KubernetesRuntimeProvisioner` structure (seed → boot document → ensure → handle → attest; `release` never treated as authority to stop a worker another Broker may own).
- Wiring in `EmbeddedRuntimeBroker.provisioner()` and config: `external.base-url`, `external.token`, request timeout.
- Session isolation, **scratch workspace only** — the same boundary K1 Kubernetes uses. Managed-context / registered Workspace storage on a remote worker needs a storage-identity story (the `LOCAL` path verifies device/inode/birth time and the marker on the Java host; `SSH_LOCAL` does it through `managed-runtime-bootstrap`). That deserves its own follow-up rather than being folded in here.
- Opt-in and off by default; no change to `local-process`, SSH or Kubernetes behavior.
- Tests: provider contract against a fake HTTP provider (idempotent provision, observe GONE → LOST, mismatched attestation refused, lost provision reply converges on the same handle), plus one opt-in real-worker test reusing the container boot path.

Two things worth agreeing on before code:

1. Is `external` (HTTP contract) preferred over a Spring `@ConditionalOnMissingBean RuntimeProvisioner` hook? The HTTP contract keeps providers language-neutral and out of the JVM; the bean hook is smaller but ties providers to this Spring build. I lean HTTP, but either unblocks the use case.
2. Should the worker boot document travel in the `/provision` body (simplest; the provider writes it to a private file) or should the provider only receive a one-time fetch URL? The body is strictly no worse than the Kubernetes immutable Secret today, but a fetch URL keeps the token out of the provider's request logs.

Related: #11695, #11698, #11746, #13395, #12380.

I'm happy to implement this.

issues.title: Allow explicit WebSearch opt-in for DashScope-compatible custom gateways

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/tools
labels.description: Tool integration and execution

labels.name: scope/web-search
labels.description: Web search functionality

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Please provide a supported way to explicitly configure the built-in `web_search` tool for a custom HTTPS gateway that implements DashScope Responses search, even when its hostname is not recognized by Qwen Code.

The existing automatic detection can stay unchanged. When configuring a search backend explicitly, users should be able to declare that the endpoint supports DashScope Responses search. With an otherwise valid configuration, Qwen Code should register the tool and use that endpoint without requiring its hostname to match the built-in allowlist.

The exact configuration field is open to discussion. The requested behavior is:

- Make the declaration specific to the configured provider or search backend, so different endpoints can be configured independently.
- Use the configured gateway, credentials, and search model.
- Report an actionable error if the endpoint cannot execute the search request. An explicit declaration does not guarantee that the gateway implements the required API correctly.

### Why is this needed?

We access Bailian/DashScope through our own gateway and configure it as a custom model service. The gateway has our own domain, so Qwen Code cannot identify its upstream from the hostname.

Currently, the hostname restriction also applies to explicitly configured search backends. Even with `tools.webSearch.enabled: true`, a search model, and credentials configured, specifying a custom endpoint through `modelProviders` or `WEB_SEARCH_BASE_URL` does not provide an override. An unrecognized hostname prevents the built-in tool from being registered before a search request can be attempted.

Conservative automatic detection is understandable. However, applying the same restriction when users explicitly configure a known compatible backend leaves no supported opt-in for this deployment pattern. Users cannot reuse their gateway for the built-in search tool and instead have to configure a separate search route or patch the client.

This request is specifically about declaring **DashScope Responses search compatibility**. A gateway supporting ordinary chat requests is not sufficient; it must also forward the search tools and their responses correctly. Our gateway's compatibility with this Responses search path still needs verification, but the client-side hostname restriction prevents testing that configuration through the built-in tool.

### Additional context

- [#4138](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/4138) proposed an explicit provider type for DashScope-compatible custom endpoints. It was closed, with the [maintainer response](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/4138#issuecomment-4458651325) preferring domain detection for known cases while leaving room to revisit explicit opt-in for additional custom gateway scenarios. This request is narrower: allowing an explicitly configured **search backend**, without requiring all DashScope-specific provider behavior to be enabled.
- [#11348](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/11348) added automatic search activation for supported providers, but retained the known-host requirement for custom endpoints.
- Codex provides a source-level design precedent for avoiding this hostname restriction. At `e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023`, its [provider capabilities default to allowing web search](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023/codex-rs/model-provider/src/capabilities.rs#L21), and its [hosted Responses search path](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs#L690) can include the server-side search tool for a custom provider without requiring a recognized hostname, subject to model and search-mode settings. This comparison concerns hosted search only; Codex's separate standalone search path has different requirements. It does not establish that our gateway has passed an end-to-end Codex search test.
- Claude Code provides a documentation-backed comparison. Its [official gateway guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#how-the-connection-method-changes-client-behavior) explains that, when configured through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` using the Anthropic Messages format, the client treats the gateway as the Claude API and sends the full capability set, leaving protocol compatibility to the gateway. [Bailian's search documentation](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/web-search) explicitly supports Anthropic-format server-side `web_search` for Claude Code. We have also observed Claude Code search working through a custom gateway, although the exact upstream route remains unverified. This is a useful example of retaining search capability behind a custom hostname; it does not establish compatibility with the separate Responses search API used by Qwen Code.
- Source review at `7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3` confirms that both the [explicit base URL path](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3/packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts#L575) and the [configured search-model path](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3/packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts#L649) reject unrecognized hosts.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

### 希望增加什么功能？

希望提供一种受支持的显式配置方式：当自定义 HTTPS 网关实现了百炼 Responses 搜索协议时，即使域名不在 Qwen Code 的识别范围内，也可以使用内置 `web_search` 工具。

现有的自动识别逻辑可以保持不变。用户显式配置搜索后端时，应能够声明该端点支持百炼 Responses 搜索。在其他配置有效的情况下，Qwen Code 应注册搜索工具并使用该端点，无需其域名匹配内置白名单。

具体配置字段可以讨论，期望的行为是：

- 声明作用于具体的 provider 或搜索后端，使多个端点可以独立配置。
- 使用用户配置的网关地址、凭证和搜索模型。
- 如果端点无法执行搜索请求，返回有助于排查的错误。显式声明并不保证网关已经正确实现所需接口。

### 为什么需要？

我们通过自有网关访问百炼，并将其配置为自定义模型服务。网关使用自己的域名，因此 Qwen Code 无法通过域名判断背后的服务。

目前，域名限制同样作用于显式配置的搜索后端。即使已设置 `tools.webSearch.enabled: true`，并配置了搜索模型和凭证，通过 `modelProviders` 或 `WEB_SEARCH_BASE_URL` 指定自定义端点，也无法覆盖这项限制。不被识别的域名会使内置搜索工具无法注册，甚至没有机会尝试发出搜索请求。

自动识别保持保守是可以理解的。但用户已经明确配置兼容后端时，仍受同样的域名限制，就缺少了受支持的自主启用方式。这类部署无法让内置搜索复用现有网关，只能额外配置搜索通路或修改客户端。

这里希望声明的是 **百炼 Responses 搜索兼容性**。网关仅支持普通聊天请求还不够，还需要正确转发搜索工具及其返回结果。我们自己的网关是否兼容这条 Responses 搜索链路仍需验证，但当前客户端的域名限制使我们无法通过内置工具测试该配置。

### 补充背景

- [#4138](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/4138) 曾提出为兼容百炼的自定义端点增加显式 provider 类型。该 issue 已关闭，[维护者回复](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/4138#issuecomment-4458651325) 倾向于先通过域名识别覆盖已知场景，同时表示遇到更多自定义网关场景后可以重新讨论显式配置。本请求范围更小：允许显式配置 **搜索后端**，无需同时启用所有 DashScope provider 专有行为。
- [#11348](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/11348) 增加了受支持 provider 的自动搜索启用，但自定义端点仍需满足已知域名要求。
- Codex 的源码可以作为不依赖这一域名限制的设计参照。在 `e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023` 上，其 [provider 能力默认允许 web search](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023/codex-rs/model-provider/src/capabilities.rs#L21)，[hosted Responses 搜索路径](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e103bbc06f2f516afe47eb9b1d8d172128912023/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs#L690) 在模型和搜索模式等条件满足时，可以为自定义 provider 下发服务端搜索工具，无需匹配已知域名。这里仅比较 hosted 搜索；Codex 独立的 standalone 搜索路径有不同要求。这项源码证据不代表我们的网关已经通过 Codex 搜索的端到端验证。
- Claude Code 提供了官方文档支持的参照。其 [官方网关指南](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#how-the-connection-method-changes-client-behavior) 说明，通过 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` 使用 Anthropic Messages 格式时，客户端将网关视为 Claude API，发送完整能力集合，由网关负责协议兼容。[百炼联网搜索文档](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/web-search) 也明确支持面向 Claude Code 的 Anthropic 格式服务端 `web_search`。我们也观察到 Claude Code 可以通过自定义网关搜索，但具体的上游调用路径尚未确认。这可以作为自定义域名下保留搜索能力的参照，但不能据此认定网关兼容 Qwen Code 使用的另一套 Responses 搜索接口。
- 在 `7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3` 上检查源码可以确认，[显式 base URL 路径](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3/packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts#L575) 和 [搜索模型配置路径](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7547326f3a746c0897e61815a70ff0bf9dc9a3b3/packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts#L649) 都会拒绝未知域名。

</details>

issues.title: bug(web-shell): new standalone session appears in sidebar only after its first turn completes

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/ui
labels.description: User interface and display

labels.name: roadmap/session-management
labels.description: Roadmap: Session management features

labels.name: status/ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified; an AFK coding agent can pick this up with no human context

issues.body:
## What happened?

A newly created **no-workspace (standalone) session** is missing from the sidebar's **No-workspace sessions** list throughout its first running turn. The row appears only after that turn finishes.

The session has already been allocated an ID and the conversation pane shows the request running. This is a list-refresh delay, rather than the expected behavior of keeping an unsubmitted draft out of history. Workspace-backed sessions do not exhibit the same delay in the reported scenario.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Web Shell connected to a daemon supporting standalone sessions.
2. Let the sidebar finish its initial session-list load.
3. Start a new task and explicitly select **No workspace**, or use the no-workspace new-task entry where available.
4. Submit a first message, for example: `Please reply only "Test complete". Do not call tools or read or write any files.`
5. While the first turn is still running, inspect the **No-workspace sessions** list.
6. Wait for the turn to finish and inspect the same list again, without reloading the page.
7. As a comparison, repeat with a workspace-backed session.

**Actual:** the conversation runs with a real session ID, but its standalone sidebar row is absent until the turn ends.

**Expected:** once standalone session creation succeeds, its row should appear promptly, independently of how long the first model response takes. Completion can still refresh the title and other metadata.

### Observed sequence

In a browser reproduction, the new session was still absent at about 31 seconds into the first turn. It appeared after that turn completed at about 48 seconds. These timings are illustrative, not a timeout threshold; the source condition is the transition back to `idle`.

## Client information and verification scope

- Surface: embedded Qwen Web Shell in Chrome on macOS.
- Source baseline examined: Qwen Code **v0.26.0**. The relevant standalone-list and sidebar component files match that release.
- The same refresh logic was also checked in upstream `main` at `32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e` (2026-10-23).
- The browser observation above is from an embedded deployment. A separate reproduction against an unmodified `qwen serve` deployment has **not** been run; the upstream attribution below is based on the shared component code.
- CLI `/about` output and provider/auth configuration were not collected for this UI investigation. No provider-specific cause is asserted.

## Root cause in the current source

### 1. StandaloneRecents has no creation-time refresh

In [StandaloneRecents.tsx](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/StandaloneRecents.tsx#L198-L234):

- Changes to `currentSessionId` / `currentSessionReady` clear open-error state, but do not reload the list.
- The initial-load effect reloads only when the component has not loaded yet or `refreshKey` changes.
- The streaming effect reloads the active standalone list when the previous state was non-idle and the new state is `idle`.

Consequently, when the list was already loaded before the new session was created, starting the first turn does not fetch the new row; finishing the turn does.

### 2. The sidebar refresh key is not advanced by creation

In [WebShellSidebar.tsx](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.tsx), `standaloneRefreshKey` is advanced by standalone lifecycle mutations and the archived-list retry action. There is no corresponding notification from successful standalone session creation.

### 3. Workspace creation follows a different path

In [App.tsx at v0.26.0](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/ac97ce7a70d9b2ea5d62b357e3d9b0851423afc9/packages/web-shell/client/App.tsx), `onSessionAllocated` calls `sessionCatalogController.sessionCreated(catalogWorkspaceCwd, sessionId)` only when `catalogWorkspaceCwd` exists. Standalone creation has no workspace catalog owner and skips this path.

The [catalog controller](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/ac97ce7a70d9b2ea5d62b357e3d9b0851423afc9/packages/web-shell/client/session-catalog/session-catalog-hooks.ts) invalidates the workspace catalog and coordinates its refresh. StandaloneRecents maintains a separate list and does not receive that signal.

Existing [StandaloneRecents tests](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/32b4234b849c229b0e5ed9ec6ddf987f3318c67e/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/StandaloneRecents.test.tsx) cover both "does not reload when the selected session changes" and "refreshes on standalone completion but not workspace completion", but do not cover a newly created standalone session appearing before completion.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit **successful standalone creation → active standalone list invalidation/refresh** notification inside Web Shell.

- Fire it after creation is confirmed and the session is listable, before awaiting first-turn completion. Wire it into the standalone list's refresh mechanism or a shared standalone catalog.
- Retain the completion refresh to reconcile generated titles and final metadata.
- Prefer a creation-specific signal over refreshing on every selected-session change; opening an existing conversation should not require an unnecessary full-list fetch.
- Preserve the existing pagination, deduplication, and stale-response guards.
- Handle deferred creation, create-result recovery, and failed attachment carefully: refresh confirmed/listable sessions without inserting phantom rows for failed or unresolved creation.

This should be owned by Web Shell rather than requiring each embedding host to implement its own sidebar workaround. The precise signal/API is open to maintainer preference.

### Suggested regression coverage

1. Mount an already-loaded standalone list, successfully create a new standalone session, keep its first prompt pending, and assert that the new row appears **before** the prompt resolves.
2. Finish the turn and verify that title/metadata reconciliation still works without duplicate rows.
3. Verify that merely opening an existing session does not introduce redundant list reloads.
4. Verify failed/unresolved creation does not leave a phantom row, and a stale list response cannot overwrite the newer refresh.
5. Retain workspace-backed creation behavior and pagination coverage.

## Related, but different scope

- #10514 introduced standalone chats.
- #11878 / #13679 concern standalone sessions in **Session Overview**, rather than this existing sidebar group's first-turn refresh.
- #14901 / #14904 concern a unified **Recent sessions** section. The current issue is the creation-time refresh of the existing **No-workspace sessions** list.

issues.title: [Bug] XML recovery repeats prefix scans on large multi-call responses

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/performance
labels.description: Performance and optimization

labels.name: scope/latency
labels.description: Response time optimization

issues.body:
## What happened?

XML tool-call recovery becomes increasingly slow when a completed response contains many valid calls. A bounded direct-parser reproduction confirms the cost on current main `e3c5360e5a71` and PR #13579 at `f6f8af8be25f`.

| Blocks | Plain input bytes | Main plain ms | PR plain ms | Quoted-content bytes | PR quoted-content ms |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 17,100 | 16.10 | 17.44 | 22,400 | 24.01 |
| 200 | 34,200 | 87.03 | 80.86 | 44,800 | 139.85 |
| 400 | 68,400 | 565.04 | 575.06 | 89,600 | 989.68 |

The plain-block cost already exists on main. PR #13579 correctly recovers outer calls whose content contains literal XML call examples; that newly accepted input class encounters the same repeated prefix scanning. Main rejects these identical quoted-content inputs without recovery, so its shorter timings for them are not equivalent feature performance.

All 2,100 recovered outer calls across the nine positive measurements had exact arguments and empty remaining text. The inner `read_file` examples stayed inside the outer content and were never dispatched. This is a source-level postprocessing measurement, not a live-model or CLI latency benchmark. Each size was measured once; the data shows strongly superlinear growth without establishing an exact asymptotic degree. The reviewer's larger 2,000-block workload was not rerun.

### How to reproduce

Run this read-only probe with `npx tsx parser-perf.ts` from the repository root at either pinned revision:

```ts
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { tryRecoverXmlToolCalls } from './packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts';

const plain = [
  '<invoke name="write_file">',
  '<parameter name="content">Anonymous plain payload.\nAnonymous marker\n</parameter>',
  '<parameter name="file_path">anonymous.md</parameter>',
  '</invoke>',
  '',
].join('\n');
const quoted = plain.replace(
  'Anonymous plain payload.\nAnonymous marker\n',
  'Usage:\n<invoke name="read_file"><parameter name="file_path">anonymous.txt</parameter></invoke>\n',
);
for (const blocks of [100, 200, 400]) {
  for (const [kind, block] of [['plain', plain], ['quoted', quoted]] as const) {
    const input = block.repeat(blocks);
    const start = performance.now();
    tryRecoverXmlToolCalls(input);
    console.log({ kind, blocks, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(input), ms: performance.now() - start });
  }
}
```

Calling the parser does not execute tools or write the named fixture files. The observed mechanism is the final per-block fence/example filtering, which repeatedly slices and splits the preceding response and searches parameter ranges. PR #13579 also uses that helper while classifying quoted values. [Exact current-main source](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e3c5360e5a718549f7ace9be61ef830ed097a81a/packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts), [review follow-up](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#pullrequestreview-5472672743).

## What did you expect to happen?

Large valid multi-call responses should recover the same outer calls and preserve literal argument content without repeatedly scanning every preceding block.

## Client information

Controlled parser reproduction: macOS arm64, Node v22.22.0, tsx 4.20.3; unmodified Git-object copies of both pinned TypeScript modules using the same existing dependencies. One child process completed in 3.32 seconds; no repeated runs or tool execution. Main module SHA256: `a6052efbda59bc1bf27367ac5de28a0c1834b43b1abfb9aa9cfb6af22024a505`; PR module SHA256: `711fab51837d8ce64f12d93389b06091d90cae61ccbb4d5905ae09f8ef6f0ab1`.

<details>
<summary>Installed client information (sanitized; not the parser benchmark target)</summary>

```text
Qwen Code v0.25.0-nightly.20261007.8003d28042
Model: [redacted]
Fast Model: [redacted]
Auth: openai
Platform: darwin arm64 (27.0.0)
Node.js: v22.22.0
Session: [redacted]
Git commit: cce7fed039
LSP: disabled
```

Local model/provider identifiers, session identifier and unrelated local execution configuration are omitted or redacted.

</details>

This records the non-blocking performance follow-up separately from #13579's correctness repair after repeated review rounds.

中文：已在准确 main/PR 源码上有界复现，main 本身已有普通多调用块耗时增长；PR 新支持的内容引用场景进入同一过滤路径。400 个引用内容块约 990ms，所有外层参数保持正确、内层示例未派发。仅一次受控纯解析器观察，没有真实模型/CLI 延迟或精确复杂度结论；作为非阻塞后续性能项跟踪。


## Round-5 review finding recorded here: R5-1

PR #13579 round-5 review raised this same cost as `[Critical]` R5-1 ([thread](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#discussion_r4234229508)). It is recorded here instead of being fixed in that PR, whose scope ledger limits it to fully-closed quoted-value recovery. Line numbers below are verified at PR head `6d9ebdc46da79a1bec7015ffde642cbf529541e1`, `packages/core/src/core/xml-tool-call-fallback.ts`.

**Which passes are unbounded.** Six `positionInsideFence` call sites (`:205`, `:222`, `:552`, `:553`, `:576`, `:577`); each one slices `text.slice(0, index)` and walks every line of that prefix against the whole `parameterRanges` list.

- `maskValuesBefore` (`:201`) restarts that scan from offset 0 once per quoted value (`:205`) and pushes a span (`:206`) that lengthens the list every later line test walks — the two costs compound.
- `isEligibleBlock` (`:552`, `:553`) and `passesFenceGuard` (`:576`, `:577`) pay it twice per **candidate** block, so the cost is reachable on turns where most documentation is correctly suppressed.

`MAX_LEXER_SCAN_LENGTH` (`:21`) is used at exactly one place, `:153`, and bounds only marked's inline-lexer pass. It does not bound any `positionInsideFence` pass, so an oversized turn pays the fence scans in full.

**Measurements.** R5-1's A/B witness (identical bytes, measured at PR head `f6f8af8be25f`, before the round-5 guard landed): 23.8 KB 2 ms → 28 ms, 63.4 KB 6 ms → 440 ms, 158 KB 41 ms → 6410 ms, 237 KB 55 ms → 20786 ms; controls: 640 plain sibling calls BASE 546 ms / HEAD 543 ms. The PR author separately measured the compiled parser on a different corpus at 1,378 ms for 93,887 bytes and 29,174 ms for 250,387 bytes ([thread reply, 2026-10-09](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#discussion_r4234229508)). Both are source/parser-level measurements, not live-model latency. The table at the top of this issue is a third independent measurement of the same mechanism.

**Why the reviewer's incremental rewrite is not a drop-in fix.** The suggestion is to carry the fence cursor and `openFence` state across calls because the requested positions increase monotonically. But `parameterRanges` is mutated *while* it is being scanned (`maskValuesBefore` pushes at `:206`), then pushed to again from the eligibility loop (`:603`), then re-sorted and merged in place (`:614`) before a second `computeExampleRanges` pass runs over it. Any cached cursor or fence state has to be invalidated by every one of those mutations, so bounding these passes means restructuring the range-list lifecycle, not adding a cache. The alternative the reviewer offers — bound the passes the way the lexer is bounded and fail closed past the bound — changes which blocks stay eligible, i.e. it changes recovery behaviour, and `exampleTagPositions`' existing over-cap `null` sentinel already shows how that interacts with the intent guard.

**Scope for a fix.** Bound or incrementalise all six call sites together, and pin the bound itself with a test that counts the helper's iterations or scanned characters on a many-block input — a pure complexity refactor reddens no existing assertion. R2-7 on the same PR asked for this shape. `sequential documentation masks` (test:1477) and `reviewed XML ownership and documentation regressions` (test:1385) must stay green, which is what would prove a cached-cursor version is equivalent rather than merely faster.

中文：第 5 轮 review 的 R5-1（`[Critical]`，无上限同步扫描）记录在本 issue，不在 PR #13579 内修。已核实该 head 上共 6 处 `positionInsideFence` 调用（`:205` `:222` `:552` `:553` `:576` `:577`），每处都从偏移 0 重扫整个前缀；`MAX_LEXER_SCAN_LENGTH` 只在 `:153` 门控 marked 词法分析，不管这些扫描。reviewer 建议的「跨调用携带游标」不是即插即用：`parameterRanges` 在被扫描期间就被 `:206` 修改，之后又在 `:603` 追加、在 `:614` 原地重排合并，再跑第二遍 `computeExampleRanges`，缓存必须被每次修改失效，因此要重排 range 列表的生命周期；改成「超长度即失败关闭」则会改变恢复行为。修的时候六处要一起收，并用测试固定上限本身。

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Session listing in Managed Agent should support an archived filter and a title search.

Today `GET /v1/agents/sessions` and the WebShell list route return only live Sessions, paged by an opaque cursor. Two fields that users expect are declared but not implemented:

- An archived filter (the field exists in the contract as planned, so archived Sessions can never be listed).
- A title search, which has no field at all.

The request is to implement the archived filter on both the public and WebShell surfaces, and to add a title search that works without loading every Session into the client.

## Why is this needed?

Managed Agent already supports archiving and renaming Sessions. Archiving without a way to list archived Sessions makes the operation one-way from the user's point of view: the Session disappears and cannot be found again through the API.

Search matters more as the Session count grows. A user with a few hundred Sessions can only page through them to find the one called "investigate checkout failure". The legacy daemon already offers `sessions/search`, so users moving to Managed lose this ability.

## Additional context

The contract file already reserves the archived field with a "planned" implementation status, which suggests the shape was decided and only the query work remains. The search field is new, so its shape is open: a case-insensitive substring match on the title is probably enough for a first version, with the exact matching rules stated in the contract rather than left to the storage engine.

Whatever is chosen must stay tenant-scoped and must page consistently with the existing cursor behavior, so a search result set cannot leak a Session from another tenant or shift while the client pages through it.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 希望增加什么？

Managed Agent 的会话列表应支持归档过滤与标题搜索。

目前 `GET /v1/agents/sessions` 与 WebShell 列表路由只返回活跃会话，使用不透明游标分页。用户期望的两个字段存在缺口：

- 归档过滤：契约中已有该字段但标记为 planned，因此归档会话永远列不出来。
- 标题搜索：完全没有对应字段。

希望做到：在公开接口与 WebShell 两个面上实现归档过滤，并新增标题搜索，且不需要客户端把所有会话拉到本地再筛。

## 为什么需要？

Managed Agent 已经支持归档与重命名会话。能归档却不能列出归档会话，从用户角度看这个操作就是单向的：会话消失了，通过接口再也找不回来。

会话数量增长后搜索更重要。有几百个会话的用户想找名叫「investigate checkout failure」的那个，只能一页页翻。旧守护进程提供 `sessions/search`，迁移到 Managed 的用户会失去这个能力。

## 补充信息

契约文件已为归档字段保留了位置并标记为 planned，说明形状已经确定，剩下的是查询工作。搜索字段是全新的，形状待定：首版用标题的大小写不敏感子串匹配大概足够，但匹配规则应写进契约，而不是留给存储引擎决定。

无论选择哪种方案，都必须保持租户隔离，并与现有游标分页行为一致，确保搜索结果不会泄露其他租户的会话，也不会在客户端翻页时发生漂移。

</details>

prs.title: fix(runtime): deliver bounded provider images and PDFs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Enables bounded image and PDF delivery through the existing managed runtime provider protocol. Each prepared file read uses its own image/PDF capability snapshot for both the tool description and actual content delivery. Supported images use the existing safe image handling; PDFs can return native bytes, extracted text, or rendered pages as appropriate. Execution workers remain independent of model initialization and do not inherit Omni media uploads. Audio and video remain disabled for this provider profile.

Media reads enforce an aggregate 768 KiB base64 ceiling and a 896 KiB complete tool-result ceiling within the existing 1 MiB response envelope. Oversized reads settle as explicit `FILE_TOO_LARGE` tool errors. Accepted media-bearing results retain their content, captions, and display across execution and settled status/cancel observations; response fitting may remove progress or auxiliary Hook details while preserving Hook stop decisions. PDF cancellation propagates through page counting, extraction, and rendering, and waits for child-process exit and renderer cleanup.

Adds regression coverage and integration fixtures for capability isolation, byte boundaries, media validation, chunked Java transport, lost replies, and Broker restart recovery. Updates the provider-control design and dependency notices. The public Hosted raw file loop remains outside this change.

## Why it's needed

The provider worker has no content generator. Previously, its declared media capabilities influenced the tool description, but actual file reads consulted content-generator modalities, so supported images and native PDF bytes could remain unavailable. Oversized responses could also replace inline media with a generic text stub after the Runtime had already retained the original result, producing inconsistent observations of the same invocation.

Using the prepared capability snapshot for delivery and applying media limits before settlement allows provider integrations to receive actual workspace media or an explicit bounded error while retaining consistent execution evidence.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Prepare reads of real PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF files with image support enabled, disabled, and omitted, including concurrent invocations and Sessions. Enabled reads should return decodable image content with the expected MIME and dimensions; disabled or omitted support should return the existing unsupported-image response without inline bytes. An inherited Omni opt-in must not cause uploads.
2. Read a small PDF with native PDF support enabled and no page range: its decoded bytes should match the workspace document. With a page range or native PDF support disabled, confirm text-first behavior and image rendering when extraction fails and image support is enabled. Explicit ranges must not silently lose pages; an implicit rendered prefix must announce omitted pages.
3. Exercise exact media boundaries and one-byte-over cases. A native PDF of 576 KiB can meet the 768 KiB base64 ceiling if the complete result also fits; one decoded byte over must return a settled `FILE_TOO_LARGE` error. Include escaped and multibyte metadata in the 896 KiB result calculation. Text, SVG, notebook content, and text-only PDF results should retain their existing handling.
4. Compare accepted tool results across execution and settled status/cancel responses, including large progress and Hook payloads. Media, captions, and display must remain identical, Hook stop decisions must survive fitting, and malformed MIME/base64 or unadmitted media must fail explicitly. Change the source file after settlement and confirm observations do not reread it.
5. With functioning Poppler tools, cancel page counting, text extraction, and rendering after the child starts. Cancellation must propagate without starting another fallback, and the owned child and rendering directory must be cleaned up.
6. After obtaining a successful build and bundle, run the added Java/MySQL provider-media integration scenario with an isolated MySQL instance. Verify the original seven-field provider reference, correct outbound media bytes and tool-call correlation at the deterministic Chat Completions fixture, exactly one physical execution after lost start/execute replies, unchanged persisted results after Broker restart, and released ownership. Treat native PDF handling through Responses as the documented unsupported case. These are proposed checks; the Java/MySQL scenario is covered by the maintainer run recorded under Evidence.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Maintainer verification at head `d44304c390` on 2026-10-23 (Beijing) reproduced the behavior flips end-to-end over a real managed-runtime socket and reported 804 assertions/checks: 772 harness assertions, 30 mutation kills, and 2 lint-liveness probes. A follow-up Java/MySQL M4 run at head `c4d1f04a04` passed locally against an isolated MySQL instance: 12 cases, 24 model requests, one dropped start, and every reference dispatched exactly once and released after Broker restart. Verification report: [#issuecomment-6354304828](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13606#issuecomment-6354304828).

The following validation was recorded by the author during the earlier commit workflow on 2026-10-07:

- From `packages/core`: `npx vitest run src/tools/managed-tool-runtime.test.ts src/tools/read-file.test.ts src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts src/utils/inline-media.test.ts src/utils/pdf.test.ts src/utils/pdf.poppler.test.ts` — 6 test files passed, with 455 tests passed and 4 real-Poppler tests skipped.
- From `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/serve/managed-runtime-provider-protocol.test.ts src/serve/managed-runtime-provider-worker.test.ts` — 2 test files passed, with 141 tests passed.
- From the repository root: `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='cleanup|promisify|image fixtures' integration-tests/helpers/provider-media-fixtures.node-test.ts` — the selected 4 fixture tests passed. The PDF fixture case was not selected.
- The commit's Prettier/ESLint hook passed. `npm run build` failed in the unchanged email channel with missing `imapflow`, `mailparser`, `nodemailer`, and `html-to-text` dependencies and related type errors. `npm run typecheck` failed with workspace errors, including `TS2540` for assigning to the readonly `text` property in the newly added protocol test at line 942.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested — maintainer verification at `d44304c390`; full gates green, real-Poppler tests executed, Java/MySQL M4 passed locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Maintainer verification on macOS with Node.js v22.18.0 and Vitest v3.2.7, against the packaged CLI and a real managed-runtime socket. The Java/MySQL M4 scenario used JDK 21, Maven 3.9.16, and an isolated MySQL instance. Author's original source: commit `205dd4b282c9936b228e79960fe7b7268e520407`, compared with its single parent `9a02f40567237ea3003becac4e6fb3b64c893d45`; maintainer-verified head: `d44304c390`; docs-only follow-up: `c4d1f04a04`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the shared effective-modality read path also affects local CLI and local managed tools. Provider media is intentionally a smaller bounded subset of local CLI media; PDF rendering and retained invocations can consume more memory and disk than the response size, and this change introduces no global quota.
- Not validated / out of scope: no real-model request, Windows/Linux arm, or production deployment was exercised; the Java/MySQL M4 scenario passed locally, not in a deployment. Public Hosted raw-file media delivery, its separate 64 KiB persistence limits, audio/video, object-storage transport, zoom, and native PDF support through Responses are outside scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no protocol-version, public API, or database-schema migration is introduced by this diff. Invalid or over-budget provider media now produces an explicit protocol fault instead of a successful stub; normal oversized reads are settled tool errors. Existing [English provider-control design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/205dd4b282c9936b228e79960fe7b7268e520407/docs/design/2026-09-27-broker-provider-control.md) and [Chinese provider-control design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/205dd4b282c9936b228e79960fe7b7268e520407/docs/design/2026-09-27-broker-provider-control.zh-CN.md) are updated. Both the [English media design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/c4d1f04a04bfec1da7a2a79ea93f16379851908b/docs/design/2026-10-07-managed-runtime-provider-media.md) and the [Chinese media design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/c4d1f04a04bfec1da7a2a79ea93f16379851908b/docs/design/2026-10-07-managed-runtime-provider-media.zh-CN.md) are included.

## Linked Issues

Related to [#13039](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13039) and its [root-cause comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13039#issuecomment-5895577269). No closing keyword is asserted because the documented end-to-end acceptance has not been established by the available validation.

---

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## What this PR does

通过现有 managed runtime provider 协议提供有界的图片和 PDF 交付。每次准备的文件读取使用独立的图片/PDF 能力快照，同时决定工具描述和实际内容交付。支持的图片复用既有安全处理；PDF 按条件返回原生字节、提取的文本或渲染页面。执行 worker 保持独立于模型初始化，也不会继承 Omni 媒体上传行为。该 provider profile 仍禁用音频和视频。

媒体读取在既有 1 MiB 响应包装内，限制聚合 base64 为 768 KiB、完整工具结果为 896 KiB。超限读取以明确的 `FILE_TOO_LARGE` 工具错误结算。已接受的含媒体结果在执行和已结算的 status/cancel 观察中保持内容、说明文本和展示不变；响应适配可以删除进度或 Hook 辅助内容，但保留 Hook 停止决定。PDF 取消会传递到页数查询、文本提取和渲染，并等待子进程退出及渲染清理完成。

增加回归覆盖和集成 fixture，覆盖能力隔离、字节边界、媒体校验、Java 分块传输、应答丢失和 Broker 重启恢复。更新 provider-control 设计及依赖声明。公开 Hosted raw 文件循环不属于本次改动范围。

## Why it's needed

provider worker 没有 content generator。此前，声明的媒体能力影响工具描述，但实际读取依赖 content-generator 模态，导致支持的图片和原生 PDF 字节仍可能无法交付。超限响应还可能在 Runtime 已保留原始结果后，把内联媒体替换为通用文本占位，从而让同一 invocation 的观察结果不一致。

使用准备时的能力快照决定交付，并在结算前应用媒体上限，使 provider 集成能够获得真实 Workspace 媒体或明确的有界错误，同时保留一致的执行证据。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. 使用真实 PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF 文件，分别在图片能力开启、关闭和省略时准备读取，包括并发 invocation 和 Session。开启时应返回可解码、MIME 和尺寸正确的图片内容；关闭或省略时应返回既有的不支持图片提示，不含内联字节。继承的 Omni 开关不能触发上传。
2. 开启原生 PDF 能力、不指定页范围，读取小型 PDF：解码字节应与 Workspace 文档一致。指定页范围或关闭原生 PDF 能力时，确认文本优先行为，以及提取失败且图片能力开启时的页面渲染。显式范围不能静默丢页；隐式渲染前缀必须说明省略的页面。
3. 检查精确媒体边界和超出一字节的情况。576 KiB 原生 PDF 在完整结果也可容纳时，可以满足 768 KiB base64 上限；多一个解码字节必须返回已结算的 `FILE_TOO_LARGE` 错误。896 KiB 结果大小计算应包含转义和多字节元数据。文本、SVG、notebook 内容和纯文本 PDF 结果应保留既有处理方式。
4. 比较执行和已结算 status/cancel 响应中的已接受工具结果，包括较大的进度及 Hook 负载。媒体、说明文本和展示必须相同，Hook 停止决定必须保留，畸形 MIME/base64 或未经准入的媒体必须明确失败。结算后修改源文件，确认观察不会重新读取文件。
5. 在 Poppler 工具可用时，等待子进程启动后取消页数查询、文本提取和渲染。取消必须向上传递，不能启动另一条回退，所属子进程及渲染目录必须完成清理。
6. 构建和打包成功后，使用隔离的 MySQL 实例运行新增的 Java/MySQL provider-media 集成场景。验证原始七字段 provider 引用、确定性 Chat Completions fixture 收到的媒体字节及工具调用关联、start/execute 应答丢失后只发生一次物理执行、Broker 重启后持久结果不变，以及所有权已释放。Responses 的原生 PDF 处理应被视为文档说明的不支持情形。这些是建议检查；Java/MySQL 场景已在 Evidence 中记录的维护者运行中覆盖。

### Evidence (Before & After)

维护者于 2026-10-23（北京时间）在 head `d44304c390` 上通过真实 managed-runtime socket 复现了行为翻转，共 804 项断言/检查：772 项 harness 断言、30 个突变杀死、2 个 lint 活性探针。随后在 head `c4d1f04a04` 上于隔离 MySQL 实例本地跑通 Java/MySQL M4 场景：12 个场景、24 次模型请求、1 次 start 丢包，所有 reference 均只派发一次并在 Broker 重启后释放。验证报告：[#issuecomment-6354304828](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13606#issuecomment-6354304828)。

以下验证为作者在 2026-10-07 较早提交流程中记录：

- 在 `packages/core`：`npx vitest run src/tools/managed-tool-runtime.test.ts src/tools/read-file.test.ts src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts src/utils/inline-media.test.ts src/utils/pdf.test.ts src/utils/pdf.poppler.test.ts` — 6 个测试文件通过，455 项测试通过，4 项真实 Poppler 测试跳过。
- 在 `packages/cli`：`npx vitest run src/serve/managed-runtime-provider-protocol.test.ts src/serve/managed-runtime-provider-worker.test.ts` — 2 个测试文件通过，141 项测试通过。
- 在仓库根目录：`node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='cleanup|promisify|image fixtures' integration-tests/helpers/provider-media-fixtures.node-test.ts` — 选中的 4 项 fixture 测试通过。未选择 PDF fixture 用例。

prs.title: feat(mods): skip hooks for Claude Code events this runtime does not run
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A Mod that registers a hook for a Claude Code event this runtime does not run yet now loads, instead of failing initialization. Examples are `prompt.submit`, `ui.render`, `classic.Stop`, or a prefix such as `prompt.*` that matches nothing supported. The skipped hook never runs and the rest of the Mod works. At startup each plugin reports its skipped patterns once, in the same place as transcript logs. Recognized names come from Claude Code 2.1.308: its engine events, `$` API events and `classic.*` settings hook events. Names Claude Code does not define, such as `tool.calls`, still reject initialization.

A plugin's `unsupportedEvents` setting, read from user or system settings like `toolDialect`, restores the previous refusal with `"reject"`. The default is `"skip"`.

`$.session.version()` lets a Mod adapt. It reports:

- the Qwen Code version;
- the Claude Code release whose event names are recognized;
- the events hooks can receive and the `$` methods a Mod can call.

Like the other `$` methods, it passes through the middleware chain as an API event, so another plugin can observe, answer or deny it.

This implements the first change in the compatibility baseline proposed in #15270.

## Why it's needed

Mods are written against Claude Code, which adds and renames events often: 2.1.296 to 2.1.308 took two weeks. Until now, any registration outside the supported subset rejected the whole plugin. A Mod that uses one prompt-box or drawing hook therefore could not run its supported commands or tool middleware here.

An external Mod author asked for this on #13749. They asked for the hook to be skipped with a diagnostic and for the supported events to be listed beside `$.session.version()`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Install a Mod that registers commands plus hooks for `prompt.submit`, `ui.render` and `classic.Stop`, then run one of its commands with `qwen -p`. The command should run.
  - In text mode, stderr shows `[Mod <name>] Hooks for unsupported events will not run: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render`.
  - In JSON output, the same text arrives as one `system/ui_log` message.
- Start the terminal UI with the same Mod, in Ink or OpenTUI. The same line appears once at startup, and the Mod's commands run.
- Set `pluginConfigs.<name>.unsupportedEvents` to `"reject"` in user settings. Initialization should fail and list the skipped patterns.
- Register a misspelled name such as `tool.calls`, an unknown namespace such as `models.*`, or an unknown classic event. Initialization should fail as before.
- Call `$.session.version()` from a command. It should return the Qwen Code version, `claudeCode: "2.1.308"`, the eight supported events and the three supported methods. A second plugin hooking `session.version` can rewrite or deny the answer.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Linux, Node 24.21.0. Before is the exact base `3d65e23cf6`; After is this PR's head. Both bundles were built locally and run with an isolated home, workspace and settings against a loopback model endpoint. Every case below made zero model requests.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Headless text, Mod with 3 unsupported hooks, `/hello Qwen` | exit 1: `Mod a1-mod: Error: Mod event not supported: prompt.submit` | exit 0: `Hello Qwen!`; stderr `[Mod a1-mod] Hooks for unsupported events will not run: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render` |
| Headless JSON, same Mod | exit 1, error result | exit 0; one `system/ui_log` with the line above; result `Hello Qwen!` |
| `$.session.version()` from a command | `Mod API not supported: $.session.version` | `{"version":"0.26.0","qwen":{"claudeCode":"2.1.308","events":[8 names],"methods":["command.register","session.version","ui.log"]}}` |
| `unsupportedEvents: "reject"` | (refused) | exit 1: `Mod events not supported: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render` |
| Misspelled `tool.calls` | exit 1: `Mod event not supported: tool.calls` | exit 1, same message |
| Ink PTY (tmux, 140×45) | `Mods failed to initialize: … Mod event not supported: prompt.submit`; `/hello Qwen` stays blocked in the input | startup line once; `/hello Qwen` → `Hello Qwen!`; `/version-info` → `VERSION 0.26.0 claudeCode=2.1.308 events=8`; `/quit` exit 0 |
| Strict OpenTUI PTY (Bun 1.3.13) | same failure as Ink | same as Ink |

Automated checks:

- Mods core suites: 274 passed, 1 skipped, including the existing tool permission check suite. New real-QuickJS cases cover:
  - prefixes, negations, matchers and `.catch` on skipped hooks;
  - misspelled, unknown namespace, unknown classic and negated unknown names;
  - the reject policy;
  - `session.version` interception and denial.
- CLI Mod service and settings schema suites: 145 passed, including policy precedence, invalid values and version forwarding.
- Also run: the Mod worker bundle test, the workspace build and bundle, the full workspace typecheck including integration types, and ESLint, Prettier and whitespace checks on the changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Built bundle under Node 24.21.0; strict OpenTUI under Bun 1.3.13 with renderer fallback disabled; tmux 3.4 PTYs. The E2E report is posted as a separate comment.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a Mod that guards something through an unsupported event, for example a `prompt.submit` filter, now runs without that guard. This includes its `.catch`. Two things mitigate it: the startup line names every skipped pattern, and `unsupportedEvents: "reject"` keeps the old refusal for that plugin.
- Not validated / out of scope:
  - Running any of the newly recognized events; only the eight listed events run.
  - Other `$.session` methods.
  - The `tool.check` alignment proposed in #15270, which comes in a separate PR.
  - macOS and Windows runs, and hosted CI, are separate from this local validation.
- Breaking changes / migration notes:
  - Plugins that were refused for an event Claude Code defines now load.
  - Names that are not Claude Code events are still refused.
  - Users who prefer the refusal can set `unsupportedEvents: "reject"` per plugin.

## Linked Issues

Part of #13749. Design: #15270.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

如果 Mod 为运行时尚未运行的 Claude Code 事件注册了 hook，现在会照常加载，不再导致初始化失败。例如 `prompt.submit`、`ui.render`、`classic.Stop`，或 `prompt.*` 这类匹配不到任何已支持事件的前缀。被跳过的 hook 永远不会运行，Mod 的其余部分照常工作。启动时，每个插件只报告一次被跳过的 pattern，输出位置与 transcript 日志相同。可识别的名字取自 Claude Code 2.1.308：它的引擎事件、`$` API 事件和 `classic.*` settings hook 事件。Claude Code 没有定义的名字（例如 `tool.calls`）仍会导致初始化失败。

插件的 `unsupportedEvents` 设置和 `toolDialect` 一样从用户或系统设置读取，设为 `"reject"` 可以恢复原来的拒绝行为。默认值为 `"skip"`。

`$.session.version()` 让 Mod 可以自行适配。它返回：

- Qwen Code 的版本；
- 可识别事件名所依据的 Claude Code 版本；
- hook 能收到的事件，以及 Mod 可以调用的 `$` 方法。

与其他 `$` 方法一样，它作为 API 事件经过中间件链，其他插件可以观察、代答或拒绝。

本 PR 实现 #15270 所提兼容基线中的第一项改动。

## 修改原因

Mod 是按 Claude Code 编写的，而 Claude Code 经常新增和改名事件：从 2.1.296 到 2.1.308 只用了两周。此前，只要有一个注册不在支持子集内，整个插件就会被拒绝。因此一个用到提示框或绘制 hook 的 Mod，连它已支持的命令和工具中间件也无法在这里运行。

一位外部 Mod 作者在 #13749 提出了这一需求：跳过这类 hook 并给出诊断，并在 `$.session.version()` 旁边列出支持的事件。

## 评审测试计划

### 验证方式

- 安装一个注册了命令、并钩住 `prompt.submit`、`ui.render` 和 `classic.Stop` 的 Mod，然后用 `qwen -p` 运行它的某个命令。命令应正常运行。
  - 文本模式下，stderr 显示 `[Mod <name>] Hooks for unsupported events will not run: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render`。
  - JSON 输出中，同样的文本作为一条 `system/ui_log` 消息出现。
- 用同一个 Mod 启动终端 UI（Ink 或 OpenTUI）。启动时同样只出现一次这行提示，Mod 的命令可以运行。
- 在用户设置里把 `pluginConfigs.<name>.unsupportedEvents` 设为 `"reject"`。初始化应失败，并列出被跳过的 pattern。
- 注册拼错的名字（如 `tool.calls`）、未知命名空间（如 `models.*`）或未知的 classic 事件。初始化应和以前一样失败。
- 在命令中调用 `$.session.version()`。它应返回 Qwen Code 版本、`claudeCode: "2.1.308"`、八个已支持事件和三个已支持方法。第二个钩住 `session.version` 的插件可以改写或拒绝这一答复。

### 修改前后证据

Linux，Node 24.21.0。修改前是精确基线 `3d65e23cf6`，修改后是本 PR 的 head。两个 bundle 都在本地构建，使用隔离的 home、工作区和设置，并连接本地回环模型端点。下列所有场景的模型请求数都为零。

| 场景 | 修改前 | 修改后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| headless 文本，Mod 含 3 个不支持的 hook，`/hello Qwen` | 退出码 1：`Mod a1-mod: Error: Mod event not supported: prompt.submit` | 退出码 0：`Hello Qwen!`；stderr `[Mod a1-mod] Hooks for unsupported events will not run: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render` |
| headless JSON，同一个 Mod | 退出码 1，错误结果 | 退出码 0；一条包含上述文本的 `system/ui_log`；结果为 `Hello Qwen!` |
| 在命令中调用 `$.session.version()` | `Mod API not supported: $.session.version` | `{"version":"0.26.0","qwen":{"claudeCode":"2.1.308","events":[8 个名字],"methods":["command.register","session.version","ui.log"]}}` |
| `unsupportedEvents: "reject"` | （被拒绝） | 退出码 1：`Mod events not supported: classic.Stop, prompt.submit, ui.render` |
| 拼错的 `tool.calls` | 退出码 1：`Mod event not supported: tool.calls` | 退出码 1，消息相同 |
| Ink PTY（tmux，140×45） | `Mods failed to initialize: … Mod event not supported: prompt.submit`；`/hello Qwen` 停在输入框无法执行 | 启动提示只出现一次；`/hello Qwen` → `Hello Qwen!`；`/version-info` → `VERSION 0.26.0 claudeCode=2.1.308 events=8`；`/quit` 退出码 0 |
| 严格 OpenTUI PTY（Bun 1.3.13） | 与 Ink 相同的失败 | 与 Ink 相同 |

自动化检查：

- Mods core 测试：274 个通过、1 个跳过，其中包括现有的工具权限检查测试。新增的真实 QuickJS 用例覆盖：
  - 被跳过的 hook 上的前缀、取反、matcher 和 `.catch`；
  - 拼错的名字、未知命名空间、未知 classic 事件，以及取反的未知名字；
  - reject 策略；
  - `session.version` 的拦截与拒绝。
- CLI Mod 服务与设置 schema 测试：145 个通过，覆盖策略优先级、非法取值和版本传递。
- 另外运行了：Mod worker 打包测试、工作区构建与打包、包含集成测试类型在内的完整类型检查，以及对改动文件的 ESLint、Prettier 和空白检查。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

在 Node 24.21.0 下运行构建好的 bundle；严格 OpenTUI 运行在 Bun 1.3.13 上，并关闭了渲染器回退；PTY 使用 tmux 3.4。E2E 报告另以评论发布。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：通过不支持的事件实现守卫的 Mod（例如过滤 `prompt.submit` 的 Mod），现在会在没有该守卫的情况下运行，它的 `.catch` 也不会运行。缓解措施有两点：启动提示列出了每个被跳过的 pattern；`unsupportedEvents: "reject"` 可以为该插件保留原来的拒绝行为。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：
  - 运行任何新识别的事件；只有列出的八个事件会运行。
  - 其他 `$.session` 方法。
  - #15270 中提出的 `tool.check` 对齐，将在单独的 PR 中提交。
  - macOS 和 Windows 上的运行，以及托管 CI，都不在本次本地验证之内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：
  - 以前因注册了 Claude Code 已定义事件而被拒绝的插件，现在可以加载。
  - 不是 Claude Code 事件的名字仍会被拒绝。
  - 偏好拒绝行为的用户可以按插件设置 `unsupportedEvents: "reject"`。

## 关联 Issue

属于 #13749。设计：#15270。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): Replace synthesized tool-result placeholders with late real results
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a model stream dies after tool-call chunks were already yielded (a transient SSE cut, a stream guard firing, etc.), the session keeps the partial tool-call turn, and the next unrelated send's orphan-repair pass synthesizes a placeholder error response ("Tool execution result was not recorded…") so the wire stays well-formed. The tools themselves keep running and usually succeed. Previously, when the scheduler's real result then arrived, it was discarded as a duplicate because the placeholder already answered the call id — so the model permanently believed a successful edit/write/command had failed, re-applied landed edits, and announced failures that never happened. With this change, the tool-completion handler checks whether the existing answer is one of those synthesized placeholders: if so, the real result replaces it in place (same slot, pairing preserved) and is recorded to the session transcript; only a genuine duplicate — a real response already present for the same id — is still dropped.

## Why it's needed

Issue #15297 measured this at scale: 43 of 1275 tool calls in a five-hour window lost their results to the model even though client telemetry recorded success and side effects were on disk, producing exactly the false "edits were not recorded" belief and costly re-read/re-apply loops. The placeholder-versus-real ordering gap turned every transient stream cut into a durable false belief about the working tree. This PR closes that gap; it deliberately does not attempt to address whatever cut the reporter's streams in the first place — that investigation continues in the issue (the reporter's debug logs, specifically the `error=` field on `[PARTIAL_PUSH]`, remain the discriminator).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The race itself needs a provider stream cut mid-turn, so the verification is mechanism-level: `packages/core` gains a regression test that plants the placeholder in history, replaces it with the real result, then sends and asserts the outbound request carries the real output exactly once and never the sentinel; `packages/cli` gains a regression test driving the tool-completion handler with a synthesized placeholder present, asserting the real result replaces it (and is recorded) instead of being dropped. Both fail without the production change (mutation-checked). Existing repair/dedup suites (`llm-chat.test.ts` 614 tests, `use-llm-stream.test.tsx` 321 tests, `client.test.ts` + `session-recovery.test.ts` 546 tests) pass unchanged. A reviewer can confirm by reading the dedup branch in the tool-completion handler and running the two new tests.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no TUI-visible surface change; the fix changes what the model sees in history and on the wire, pinned by the new wire-level unit test). Before: debug log shows `[REPAIR] Dropping N late tool result(s)` and the transcript keeps a phantom unanswered functionCall. After: the log shows `[REPAIR] Replaced synthesized placeholder(s) with late real tool result(s)` and the transcript records the real result.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build of the branch (`npm run build`); unit/integration suites via vitest. No live provider was involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: when the placeholder was already included in an intervening request, the model may have already reacted to the "not recorded" error; after replacement its next request carries the real result, so it can self-correct. This late correction is the intended trade-off and strictly improves on the previous permanent false belief.
- Not validated / out of scope: the original stream-cut trigger (needs the reporter's debug logs; provider- and platform-specific), Windows/Linux runtime behavior, and a live end-to-end staging of the race in the TUI (the interleave timing is not deterministically stageable through the interactive admission path; the wire contract is pinned at request-construction level instead).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New internal accessors are additive; behavior for genuine duplicates is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Related to #15297 (fixes the result-delivery half; the stream-cut trigger investigation stays open there).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当模型流在工具调用 chunk 已经产出之后中断（瞬时 SSE 断流、流守卫触发等），会话会保留这个半截的工具调用轮次，而下一条不相关发送的孤儿修复流程会合成一个占位错误响应（"Tool execution result was not recorded…"）以保证线协议格式合法。工具本身仍在运行且通常成功。此前，当调度器的真实结果随后到达时，会因为占位响应已经应答了该 call id 而被当作重复项丢弃——于是模型会永久认为一次成功的编辑/写入/命令失败了，从而重复应用已落盘的编辑、并宣告从未发生的失败。本次修改让工具完成回调检查既有应答是否为合成占位符：如果是，真实结果将原位替换它（位置不变、配对关系保持），并写入会话转录；只有真正的重复——同一 id 已存在真实响应——才会继续被丢弃。

## 为什么需要

Issue #15297 给出了量化的影响：5 小时窗口内 1275 次工具调用中有 43 次结果未送达模型，而客户端遥测记录为成功、副作用已落盘，由此产生了完全错误的"编辑未记录"认知以及昂贵的重读/重做循环。占位符与真实结果的时序缺口把每一次瞬时断流都放大成对工作区状态的持久错误认知。本 PR 闭合了这个缺口；但它刻意不处理最初切断报告者流的原因——该调查仍在 issue 中继续（报告者的 debug 日志，尤其是 `[PARTIAL_PUSH]` 上的 `error=` 字段，仍是判别依据）。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

该竞态需要 provider 在轮次中途断流，因此验证在机制层面进行：`packages/core` 新增回归测试，先在 history 中植入占位符，再替换为真实结果，随后发送并断言出站请求恰好携带一次真实输出且不再包含哨兵文本；`packages/cli` 新增回归测试，在存在合成占位符的情况下驱动工具完成回调，断言真实结果替换占位符（并被记录）而非被丢弃。两个测试在没有生产代码改动时都会失败（已做变异验证）。既有修复/去重测试套件（`llm-chat.test.ts` 614 个、`use-llm-stream.test.tsx` 321 个、`client.test.ts` + `session-recovery.test.ts` 546 个）全部通过。评审者可阅读工具完成回调中的去重分支并运行这两个新测试来确认。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（无 TUI 可见界面变化；本修复改变的是模型在 history 和线上协议中看到的内容，已由新的线级单元测试锁定）。修复前：debug 日志出现 `[REPAIR] Dropping N late tool result(s)`，转录里留下一个没有应答的幽灵 functionCall。修复后：日志出现 `[REPAIR] Replaced synthesized placeholder(s) with late real tool result(s)`，转录记录真实结果。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

分支本地构建（`npm run build`）；单元/集成测试经 vitest 运行。未接入真实 provider。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：当占位符已包含在介入请求中时，模型可能已经根据"未记录"错误做出反应；替换后它的下一次请求将携带真实结果，因此可以自我纠正。这种延迟纠正是有意为之的权衡，且严格优于此前永久性的错误认知。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：最初的断流触发原因（需要报告者的 debug 日志；与 provider 和平台相关）、Windows/Linux 运行时行为，以及在 TUI 中对竞态的实时端到端复现（交互式准入路径无法确定性地编排该交错时序；线协议契约改在请求构造层面锁定）。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增内部访问器均为增量；对真正重复项的行为不变。

## 关联 Issue

相关：#15297（修复结果送达这一半；断流触发原因的调查在该 issue 中继续）。

</details>

Existing add/rename/remove dialog copy and session-creation errors are aligned in English and Chinese.

Production changes are limited to values of existing translation keys. Existing tests only update their displayed-text selectors/expectations, and the adapter documentation records the terminology. No identifiers, translation keys, component structure, APIs, storage, or runtime logic are renamed or refactored.

## Why it's needed

The sidebar currently calls the same directory-backed object Project in its heading and Workspace in its actions, while ordinary conversation creation says New task. This implements the final Workspace/Session vocabulary recorded in #14988 with a small copy-only change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- In English and Chinese, confirm the sidebar says Workspaces / 工作区 and the top, workspace-row/menu, worktree, and workspace-overview actions use New session / 新建会话 terminology. Their existing destinations and callbacks should behave as before.
- Check the existing add, rename, and remove dialogs and the workspace Memory label/description. The legacy add-dialog submit label becomes Add workspace / 添加工作区; the folder-browser flow still uses its existing Add this folder action.
- Confirm No-workspace sessions / 无工作区会话 stays named and placed as before, and Scheduled Tasks / 定时任务 retains its domain name.

Validation: repository build and typecheck passed. A TypeScript AST comparison verified that all 11 changed TSX files differ only in string literals; a separate comparison verified that production translation keys, symbols, and logic are unchanged. prs.title: fix(managed-agent): drop removed publication constructor argument
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Restores compilation of the managed-agent hosted tool-turn fixture by removing an argument that the publication store no longer accepts. The fixture is test-only; production wiring, the database schema, and the public contract are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

The post-merge fast Java lane on main died during test compilation, before any test could report. An earlier refactor removed the pre-release `journalHeadAuthorization` switch and collapsed the publication store's two constructors into one, but the hosted tool-turn fixture — added by a change authored in parallel — still passed the deleted trailing boolean. Because the fast tier compiles every test source before running the suite, that single stale argument failed the whole lane and produced a red main.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the managed-agent test tree compiles, which is what the failing lane stopped on. Running `mvn clean test` in `packages/managed-agent-server` (JDK 21) compiles the hosted tool-turn fixture during `test-compile`; before this change that phase fails on the publication store constructor, and after it the compile proceeds. A reviewer can also inspect the constructor declaration and confirm it takes six parameters while the fixture previously supplied seven; the removed value was the obsolete authorization flag, and the surviving constructor already defaults it to `false`, so no runtime behavior changes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — not a user-visible change. Before: the fixture passes a seventh argument to a six-parameter constructor and `test-compile` fails. After: the fixture passes six arguments and compiles.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

The Java suite was not run locally: this runner has no JDK, Maven, or Docker. The repository's TypeScript checks (`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`) pass on Linux; CI's Linux Java 21 lane owns the Java compile and suite.

### Environment (optional)

Repository checks ran from the project root on Node.js 22. The local sandbox could not hold Maven state, so Java verification is delegated to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none beyond relying on CI to execute the Java compile this change exists to fix; locally only static signature checks were possible.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full hosted-harness MySQL integration profile, which does not run in the fast tier and is unrelated to this compile-only fix.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15307
