## Original umbrella and delivery history

## EPIC-005: CodeWhale TUI Crate Decomposition — Umbrella EPIC

This issue is the **EpicStyle tracking issue** for the CodeWhale TUI crate decomposition. It represents the entire structure below: every sub-EPIC and every FEAT reports here when done, and every PR created under this work is logged here.

The decomposition is the direct answer to the compilation-time discussion in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) — see the Developer fast loop section below.

## Structure

EPIC-005 is the **umbrella EPIC**. It does not contain FEATs directly — it holds the map of **sub-EPICs**, each of which contains its own FEATs.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U["EPIC-005: TUI Crate Decomposition (umbrella)"]
    U --> E6["EPIC-006: Commands -> codewhale-commands (P1)"]
    U --> E7["EPIC-007: Tools consolidation -> crates/tools (P1)"]
    U --> E8["EPIC-008: Config consolidation -> crates/config (P2)"]
    U --> E9["EPIC-009: Hooks + Execpolicy + MCP (P2)"]
    U --> E10["EPIC-010: Core extraction -> crates/core (P3)"]
```

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200,200 -->
| ID | Sub-EPIC | Scope | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| EPIC-006 | Commands → `codewhale-commands` | `crates/tui/src/commands/` — groups, registry and discovery | **IN PROGRESS** — 15/32 active delivery FEATs merged (Stage A 2/2; Stage B 13/17; FEAT-030 absorbed). FEAT-031 [#7009](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7009) merged; 17 remain unmerged. Next FEAT-032; frontier `core`; physical extraction and final acceptance remain. |
| EPIC-007 | Tools consolidation | `crates/tui/src/tools/` (\~117k lines) → `crates/tools` (currently 1.3k) | NotStarted |
| EPIC-008 | Config consolidation | `crates/tui/src/config/` (\~13k lines) → `crates/config` (currently 33k) | NotStarted |
| EPIC-009 | Hooks + Execpolicy + MCP | `hooks/` (7k), `execpolicy/` (0.5k), `mcp/` (8k) → `crates/hooks`, `crates/execpolicy`, `crates/mcp` | NotStarted |
| EPIC-010 | Core extraction | `crates/tui/src/core/` (\~42k lines) → `crates/core` (currently 3.4k); tightly coupled, P3 follow-up | NotStarted |

Stays in `codewhale-tui`: `tui/` rendering (\~205k lines), `fleet/` (\~27k lines), and the TUI-specific long tail.

## Rules (applied to every sub-EPIC)

1. Behavior-preserving — extraction only, no command/UX behavior changes.
2. Trait-first — define the boundary interface before moving code (pattern: EPIC-006 `CommandContext`).
3. Compiles at every step — bottom-up extraction, workspace stays green at each commit.
4. CI gate — extracted crate must never depend on `codewhale-tui` (e.g. `cargo check -p codewhale-commands` pulls no TUI).
5. Deliver one independently verified PR per completed FEAT against current upstream main; keep parent EPICs open until their remaining work and acceptance criteria are complete.
6. Sequencing — EPIC-006 first, then 007/008, then 009, then 010.

## Work summary (to be done)

Estimated FEATs under each EPIC. Check a FEAT off and append its PR link when the PR lands; parent EPICs auto-complete when all their FEATs are done. This section is the visual tracker — the Features Breakdown tables in the MemoryBank EPIC documents are synchronized with implementation and PR delivery status.

- [ ] EPIC-006: Commands extraction — staged, **one FEAT = one independently green PR**
  - [X] **Stage A — shapes + infrastructure (COMPLETE 2026-08-19)**
    - [X] FEAT-014: Prototype command capability/handler/registration shapes only — **merged** in [#5328](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/5328>) (2026-08-13, merge commit `3b41d0ee`); no TUI production rewiring
    - [X] FEAT-015: Add TUI adapters, dual-path dispatch seam, and shrinking migration gate; convert no group — **merged** in [#5506](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/5506>) (2026-08-19, merge commit `ae56154c`); complete required check matrix green
  - [ ] **Stage B — adopt shapes inside TUI (files do not move)**
    * **Least-capability invariant:** every contextual registration declares its exact minimum external facet set; the TUI exposes only those facets; pure handlers construct no host bundle; missing required facets fail safely. FEAT-019 through FEAT-035 inherit this pattern, and FEAT-035 enforces it repository-wide.

    > [!NOTE]
    > **Historical pre-merge debug delivery — 2026-09-28.** Draft [#6707](https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/pull/6707) completes FEAT-029 for all fourteen debug commands and absorbs FEAT-030. Source head `d7c766119` already includes latest fetched `origin/main` `0bfe04e163`. Local CI-profile nextest: 17,224 passed, zero failed, 28 configured skips; all 23 required local checks pass. The real complete group also builds in a separate normal library without TUI (30 portable/helper tests pass, no transport stand-ins). Host App/Git/snapshot operations remain outside the movable group. The shared contract still depends on core; physical file extraction is pending. The proposed frontier is `config`, `core`, `session`; upstream still has `debug` until this PR merges. Hosted CI requires administrator approval of fork workflows (`action_required`; contributor approval attempt returned HTTP 403). Contribution gate and GitGuardian passed; build/test jobs have not run yet. Review remains pending; this is not a merged delivery or EPIC acceptance. #6145 and this umbrella remain open.
    >
    > **Current sequence (2026-10-22):** FEAT-031 is merged through #7009 after FEAT-029/026/027/028. Next is FEAT-032, then FEAT-033–035. Core frontier, physical moves and final acceptance remain; final-head CI/coverage and release are separate evidence.
    >
    > **Command adoption update — 2026-09-23.** FEAT-025 (session export) merged through [#6096](https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/pull/6096) on 2026-09-16 (`9a674f47f`). Stage A is complete (2/2); Stage B has 8/18 FEATs merged; 10/33 EPIC-006 FEATs are merged overall. The remaining migration frontier is `config`, `core`, `debug`, and `session`.
    >
    > **Reason for changing the order: the owner requested debug first.** In [the 2026-09-17 decision on #6145](https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6145#issuecomment-5706729220), @Hmbown chose to keep `codewhale-command-contract` and finish adoption, with debug + config + the session straggler as the bounded scope, delivered in reviewable slices. ## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

issues.title: bug(tui): a job-control suspend leaves no receipt — nothing logged, no marker, and the launch notice says --continue instead of fg

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

issues.body:
## What happened

A `codew` launch ended with the shell reporting `suspended (signal)` and a bare prompt:

```
$ cd ..
$ codew
Found an in-flight session snapshot (1h ago). Starting a new session. Run `codewhale --continue` to resume it.
^[[Izsh: suspended (signal)  codew
$
```

From the prompt it reads as "it crashed and the session is gone". It did not crash — the process was **stopped**, the session is intact, and `fg` brings it back. Nothing in the product says so: no log line, no crash marker, no hint in either message.

The in-flight notice also names the wrong recovery command. `codewhale --continue` starts a *second* process over the same checkpoint; the correct recovery for a stopped job is `fg` in the terminal that owns it.

## Why the shell says `(signal)`

`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/job_control_guard.rs` handles SIGTSTP and SIGTTIN and ends every stop with `libc::raise(libc::SIGSTOP)` (line 214), so the SIGTTIN path can never return `EIO` into the input pump. The job therefore enters the shell's table as a **SIGSTOP** stop, and zsh renders that as `suspended (signal)` — losing the `(tty input)` / `(user)` distinction that used to identify *why* it stopped. The one clue that named the cause is erased by the fix.

## Steps to reproduce

```
# terminal A
codew

# terminal B
kill -TSTP <codew pid>

# terminal A: the guard restores every mode, then stops; zsh prints
zsh: suspended (signal)  codew

# the aftermath is empty:
ls -l ~/.codewhale/crashes/          # no marker for today
ls -lt ~/.codewhale/logs/            # no log for that launch at all
fg                                   # resumes; status line "Resumed after suspend"
```

## Versions

`codewhale 0.10.2 (1d4443510f06)`, macOS 26.1, Terminal.app, zsh. Surface: TUI.

## Verified on 0.10.2

- **Not a crash.** `~/.codewhale/crashes/` holds no marker for the day, and the fatal-signal guard writes one for every fatal signal it handles.
- **No log at all.** The notice is printed by `preserve_interrupted_checkpoint_for_explicit_resume` (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:13062`) before logging is initialized, so a stop at that point leaves nothing behind — `~/.codewhale/logs/` has no file for that launch.
- **The handler cannot log.** `stop_handler` is async-signal-safe by construction (write/tcsetattr/raise, no allocation, no lock). The resume path only sets a transient `app.status_message = "Resumed after suspend"` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`), never a durable line.
- **The handshake itself is correct.** Driving a PTY: SIGTSTP emits the full restore table (`?1004l`, `?2004l`, the mouse modes, `?1049l`, cursor show), `waitpid(WUNTRACED)` reports SIGSTOP, and SIGCONT re-arms every mode and repaints. No mode leaks.
- **Not a startup-size problem.** On the same workspace the notice lands at 85 ms and the first frame at ~371 ms, with ~47 MB of recent checkpoints re-parsed on that path. Slow, not stuck.

## Proposed

1. **Durable receipt.** On the event-loop side of `job_control_guard::take_resume()` — normal context, where `tracing` is legal — emit one INFO line such as `tui.job_control: suspended and resumed`. A stop that never resumes still leaves the checkpoint; a resume now leaves a log record that separates "survived a suspend" from "hung".
2. **Tell the user how to get back.** When the newest checkpoint's session has a stopped-but-live owner, say so and name `fg`; reserve `--continue` for an owner that is gone.
3. **Record why, where possible.** `tcgetpgrp(getpid())` in the resume path distinguishes "we were backgrounded" (still not foreground) from "we were foregrounded and stopped" (Ctrl-Z), which is the only way to recover the cause after the fact.

## Related

- #6169 — the original poisoning failure; the handshake is in and verified working here.
- #6308 — open: in-TUI Ctrl+Z binding plus the in-repo suspend PTY test. This issue is the other half: the stop is survivable but invisible.

The exact job-control action that first moved the group out of the foreground is not pinnable after the fact — the kernel does not record why a process was stopped, and the shell's `(signal)` label discards it. That is the argument for (1) and (3).

issues.title: Composer: more room to edit pasted text before sending

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

I often paste a chunk of text into the composer and then want to fix something in the middle of it before sending. That's hard today:

- The composer stops growing at a fixed height (the `composer_density` cap: 9 rows by default, 12 on spacious), so I only see a small slice of what I pasted and lose my place while moving around in it.
- A paste over 16k chars still becomes `[Pasted content attached · N chars]` with a short preview (the fallback #3263 kept), so there's nothing left to edit inline.

There's Ctrl+Shift+O / F4 to open the draft in `$EDITOR`, but it's easy to miss, and it means leaving the TUI for a small edit.

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

Any one of these would help:

- Let the composer grow past the density cap when the draft is long, or let me resize it, say up to half the screen.
- Mention the external-editor shortcut in the composer hint when the draft gets long or right after a big paste.
- For a paste that turns into an attachment, a way to open and edit it before sending.

issues.title: TUI panic in auto_review.rs:1213 — byte-index slice splits Cyrillic UTF-8 characters

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

The TUI process panics and dies whenever a string containing Cyrillic (non-ASCII) text is sliced by **byte index** in `auto_review.rs`. A UTF-8 multibyte character gets cut in half, `str` slicing panics, and the whole session is lost.

## Environment

- CodeWhale **0.10.1** (`fead51eeea0f`), installed from npm package `codewhale` (binary downloaded from GitHub Releases)
- OS: Windows 10 Pro 19045 (Windows Terminal)
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.7
- Locale: ru-RU — the user works in Russian, so tool descriptions, file contents and review reasons are Cyrillic in nearly every turn
- Permission posture: `full-access` (`--yolo`)

## Crash

Panic log written to `~/.codewhale/crashes/`:

```
Process panicked
Location: crates\tui\src\tui\auto_review.rs:1213:58
Timestamp: 20261021T174734.432Z
Panic: start byte index 24 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'о' (bytes 23..25 of string)
```

All 10 recorded panics point to the **same line** with different offsets and different characters, which is the signature of a fixed-length byte slice over UTF-8 text:

| Timestamp (local) | Panic message |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-09 10:44 | start byte index 31 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'а' (bytes 30..32) |
| 2026-10-09 12:42 | start byte index 25 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'й' (bytes 24..26) |
| 2026-10-14 00:35 | start byte index 18 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'т' (bytes 17..19) |
| 2026-10-16 00:23 | start byte index 29 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'т' (bytes 28..30) |
| 2026-10-16 00:38 | start byte index 72 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'Т' (bytes 71..73) |
| 2026-10-16 00:57 | start byte index 67 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'т' (bytes 66..68) |
| 2026-10-16 01:21 | start byte index 67 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'т' (bytes 66..68) |
| 2026-10-16 07:52 | start byte index 24 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'т' (bytes 23..25) |
| 2026-10-21 11:49 | start byte index 9 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'а' (bytes 8..10) |
| 2026-10-21 13:47 | start byte index 24 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'о' (bytes 23..25) |

Note that `'о'`, `'а'`, `'т'`, `'Т'`, `'й'` are all 2-byte Cyrillic characters, while Latin text works fine.

## Context / reproduction hints

The crash is not tied to a single command; it reproduces during ordinary work in a Russian-language session:

1. Work with `permission posture = full-access`.
2. The built-in safety gate rejects a shell command (`auto_review_deterministic` → `denied`, reason text in Russian).
3. Within a minute or two after such a denial the TUI panics at `auto_review.rs:1213:58`.

An earlier, apparently related panic was recorded on **2026-06-30** at `crates\tui\src\core\engine.rs:2009:9` with the same message class (`start byte index 6483 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'а'`), while rendering a JavaScript file whose comments were in Russian. So the byte-index slicing pattern seems to exist in more than one place.

## Impact

- The interactive session dies without a chance to save; the user has to start a new session and loses working context.
- Reproduced 10 times over two weeks on a single machine, i.e. it is the normal path for any Cyrillic user, not an edge case.

## Suggested fix

Replace the byte-index slicing with a character-boundary-safe operation, e.g.:

```rust
// before
&text[..max]

// after
let cut = text.floor_char_boundary(max); // or iterate char_indices()
&text[..cut]
```

and add a regression test with a 2-byte (Cyrillic) and a 4-byte (emoji) character at every possible cut position.

## Additional note (not a crash)

In the same version the built-in safety gate refuses commands it cannot classify, including read-only ones such as `gh --version` or inspecting `pwsh.exe` version, with:

```
Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers; use a direct PID- or port-specific command.
```

This is reported separately here only as context for the crash above (the denials are what precede the panics), not as a separate request.

issues.title: Agent mail is half-built: durable queue and REST routes exist, but no model-facing tool and no wake path for idle threads

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## What exists today (verified)

Agent-to-agent mail is **partly built**, and the built part is solid. It is a durable, protocol-level queue with a REST surface — but it has **no model-facing tool**, so an agent cannot send mail today.

**Protocol** — `crates/protocol/src/agent_mail.rs` (763 lines), `AGENT_MAIL_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`:
- Typed envelope with validated ids, addresses, sender identity, evidence refs and failure receipts.
- Bounds enforced: 80-byte message id, 2,048-byte summary, 8 evidence refs, 4 hops, 8 delivery attempts.
- Lifecycle events: `agent_mail.queued`, `.delivering`, `.delivered`, `.read`, `.delivery_failed`, `.canceled`.
- Two delivery modes: `QueueOnly` and `WakeAtSafeBoundary`.
- Tests: `cargo test -p codewhale-protocol -- agent_mail::tests` → **6 passed, 0 failed**, covering round-trip of canonical event names, hop/path/control rejection, and lifecycle field validation.

**Durable store and delivery** — `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`:
- On-disk queue under the runtime store's `agent-mail/` directory; claimed-mail recovery on restart (`recover_claimed_agent_mail`, `:2891`).
- `deliver_agent_mail` (`:10016`) claims a message, emits `delivering`, renders it as a parent prompt (`render_agent_mail_prompt`, `:451`) and emits `delivered`.
- Automatic drain at a safe boundary (`:10255-10273`), gated on `WakeAtSafeBoundary` + `trigger_turn` + `Queued` or retryable `Failed`.
- Credential redaction before delivery (`sanitize_agent_mail_text`, `:375`) and a raw-transcript guard (`agent_mail_looks_like_raw_transcript`, `:427`).
- Workspace scoping: a message addressed to another workspace does not land (`agent_mail_workspace_id`, `:300`).
- Integration test `agent_mail_queue_is_durable_idempotent_redacted_and_workspace_scoped` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/tests.rs:2525`) covers durability, idempotent replay, redaction and workspace scoping.

**API** — `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs`:
- `POST /v1/agent-mail` (send)
- `GET /v1/threads/{id}/agent-mail` (list)
- `POST /v1/threads/{id}/agent-mail/{message_id}/deliver`
- `POST /v1/threads/{id}/agent-mail/{message_id}/read`
- Capability flag `agent_mail: true` (`runtime_api.rs:1366`).

## What is missing

1. **No model-facing tool.** There is no `agent_mail` / `send_mail` tool in the tool registry (`grep 'name: ".*mail' crates/` finds only the unrelated `gmail` skill). An agent cannot send mail; only an authenticated Runtime API client can. This is the single biggest gap and the one that makes the feature invisible in practice.
2. **No receive-side tool either.** A queued message arrives as a rendered parent prompt, but an agent cannot *check its own inbox* or list what it has been sent.
3. **No delivery guaranteed by the agent loop.** `WakeAtSafeBoundary` depends on the runtime-hosted drain path. Whether it fires for every host (desktop, web, `serve`) is unverified, and the proposal in `codewhale-ops/designs/OPERATE-ULTRACODE-20261022.md` records that runtime threads never idle-wake.
4. **Idle threads do not wake.** A message can be queued for a thread that is not running and will not be delivered until something else starts a turn.
5. **No user-visible mail surface.** No panel, no badge, no way for a person to see the queue or cancel a stuck message, apart from the raw REST routes.
6. **No cross-machine transport.** The queue is local to one runtime store; a message cannot reach an agent on another machine.

## Proposed acceptance for a future version

- A model-facing `agent_mail` tool with `send` and `list`/`read` actions, bounded by the existing envelope validation, and gated like any other write tool.
- The receiving side exposed to the model, not only as an injected prompt.
- A verified wake path for every runtime host, or an explicit documented statement of which hosts deliver automatically.
- A user-visible queue with per-message cancel, reusing an existing panel rather than adding a third list.
- Idempotent replay proven across a restart for the `WakeAtSafeBoundary` path.

## Not a 0.10.2 blocker

Nothing above is a regression and nothing above blocks the tag. This is recorded so the work is not lost: the protocol and store are already good, and the remaining work is the tool surface and the wake path.

Seen while landing 0.10.2; evidence collected on `afeb9cea31` and its parent `b961994290`.

## What and why

Pressing `r` in `/sessions` shows the rename prompt twice. The header row turns into the input (`New title: …_`), and the key handler also sets the status row under it to the same `New title: ` string. At 60×24, before:


prs.title: fix(tui): keep the space after an em dash when a footer notice sheds
prs.body:
## What and why

When a footer notice is longer than its slot, `fit_notice` splits it at sentence and clause marks and rejoins the clauses that fit. Both halves treat any non-ASCII mark as full width: `notice_clauses` breaks on one without waiting for whitespace, and `join_while_fitting` rejoins after one without a space, so `。` doesn't get a Latin space after it. `—` and `…` aren't full width, so their space goes missing. Queue a follow-up during a turn at 60 columns, before:

```
 ● ask   work (Tab)          Queued —sends after this turn.
```

After:

```
 ● ask   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])              Queued
```

The rejoined text is one column shorter than the real one, which is what let it squeeze into the 30-column slot. With the space kept the whole sentence doesn't fit, so the clause is shed and the toast says `Queued`, the way the other shed notices read. At 84 columns two queued messages went from `Queued (2 waiting) —sends after this turn.` to `Queued (2 waiting)`.

Both checks now look at the mark's display width instead of whether it is ASCII. Wide marks (`。`, `，`, `：`, `、` …) behave as before, and `—` and `…` break only before whitespace and rejoin with their space, like `;` and `.`. The comment that said "ASCII marks only break before whitespace" now says "Other marks".

What it doesn't do: a `…` or `—` written with no space after it, as CJK text sometimes has, is no longer a place to cut.

## Issue

No-Issue: a shed footer notice drops the space after an em dash; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock that streams a slow reply, queued one and then two follow-ups, with this change and with a build of `main` from before it, at 60, 80 and 84 columns. The lines above are from 60 and 84; at 80, and wherever the whole toast fits, the footer is unchanged.
- Merged onto current `main` (4f1d7ab56): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and CI's clippy for `codewhale-tui` are clean. On 3cb4cd27f: clippy on 1.99 and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui` are clean apart from what `main` itself had at that commit.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib` on that merge: 15357 passed, 5 failed, with the `phase_strip` notice tests among the passes (the full-width rejoin test still passes). None of the five touches the footer, and they fail without this change too (checked on 1f8d4bea1): `computer_use_autonomous_postures_block_before_the_plugin`, `pr_review_markdown_shows_the_computed_replacement`, `config_panel_golden_at_eighty_and_one_twenty`, `chat_widget_breathes_between_groups_without_padding_tool_rows_at_any_width`, and `actual_cli_review_report_host_matches_legacy_and_core_keeps_inline_authority`, which passes when run on its own.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 3cb4cd27f; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): render the /diff pager at the width it paints
prs.body:
## What and why

`/diff` wraps long diff rows twice at narrow widths. `open_diff_pager` renders the diff at the transcript width minus two and gives the pager finished lines, but the pager body is narrower than that (its margin, padding and scroll rail take five columns at 44 columns and up), so `wrap_lines` breaks those rows again and the tail of each loses its hanging indent. After an edit that adds one long line, at 60×24, before:

```
          3 + A longer description line that is long     █
  enough                                                 █
              to wrap when the terminal is narrow, with a█
              path src/very/long/module/name.rs inside   █
  it.                                                    █
```

After:

```
          3 + A longer description line that is long
              enough to wrap when the terminal is narrow,
              with a path src/very/long/module/name.rs
              inside it.
```

The pager now keeps the diff as its source (`PagerSource::Diff`) and renders it in `layout` at the body width, the same place a text page gets wrapped, so the rows already fit and nothing is wrapped a second time. Resizing works the same way: opening `/diff` at 100 columns and shrinking to 60 used to leave `enough to wrap…` and `inside it.` at the left edge; now the diff is rendered again at the new width. `c`/`y` still copy the sanitized diff, now through `source_text` instead of a separate copy payload.

## Issue

No-Issue: /diff wraps long rows twice at narrow widths; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock whose reply calls `edit` once, then opened `/diff`, with this change and with a build of `main` from before it: 60×24 as above, 100×30 (unchanged, nothing wraps), and 100×30 shrunk to 60×24 with the pager open.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean. Merged onto current `main` (66560b3a9), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and CI's clippy for `codewhale-tui` are clean too.

prs.body:
## Summary

Completes the **13-command core navigation slice** behind portable command Shapes, in preparation for later crate extraction. No intended user-visible behavior change.

Commands: `/anchor`, `/help`, `/hotbar`, `/links`, `/transcript`, `/turn`, `/home`, `/overview`, `/workspace`, `/translate`, `/voice`, `/voicesend`, `/voicecontrol` (all existing aliases retained).

- Commands own parsing, branching, formatting and rendering; host adapters supply typed facts and narrow effects. Shared metadata/results/actions/payloads have no App/TUI dependency.
- Keep the existing `u32` capability identities; use bits 30/31 for navigation/voice input. Unrelated commands do not gain these new facet slots. The existing WORKSPACE facet does now expose confined anchor operations to its consumers; per-operation authority narrowing remains an acknowledged design follow-up.
- Remove the obsolete App-bound implementations, retain confined anchor I/O and workspace semantics, and move the unchanged voice capture runtime outside the movable command closure. Builtin voice shortcuts cannot be hijacked by a shadowing user command.
- Compile the actual complete production root independently through unpublished `tests/portable-core-navigation`. Check all 13 registrations exactly once in relative order, complete source closure, all-target normal dependency graph and rejection controls. Integrate CI/developer routing and release-order validation.

This is intentionally one coherent slice: the diff includes moved host tests/runtime and shared-contract consumer updates, rather than shipping parallel implementations. **The other 27 core registrations remain out of scope, the `core` frontier remains pending, and no physical crate movement is claimed.**

prs.body:
## What and why

The work surface's file activity receipt counts with a fixed plural. With the work surface on a side rail, a turn that reads one file and runs one search shows, before:

```
 ✓ Read 1 files · Searched 1 patterns            README.md
```

After:

```
 ✓ Read 1 file · Searched 1 pattern              README.md
```

A single edit goes from `Wrote 1 files` to `Wrote 1 file`, and one listed directory reads `Listed 1 directory`. `FileActivitySummary::compact_display` now counts through `counted` in `history/tool_run.rs`, the helper the tool-run summary already uses for `Explored 1 file, 1 search`; it only becomes `pub(super)` so `history.rs` can reach it. Counts above one read as before.

Three tests pinned the plural (`Read 1 files`, `Searched 1 patterns`, `Wrote 1 files`); they now check the singular, with the trailing ` ·` where the old text would still match as a prefix.

## Issue

No-Issue: the file activity receipt says "1 files" and "1 patterns"; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock, with `work_surface_placement = "left"` and a 60-column rail, with this change and with a build of `main` from before it. The receipt above is from a turn that calls `read` and `file_search`; a turn that calls `edit` once goes from `Wrote 1 files` to `Wrote 1 file`. Apart from the ttft readout, nothing else on the screen changed.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and CI's clippy (stable and 1.99) only complain about `main` itself at 1f8d4bea1: fmt wants `core/engine/tool_preparation.rs:665` reformatted and clippy flags `tools/review_core.rs:870`. Neither file is touched here.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15354 passed, 8 failed, with the three updated tests among the passes. Seven of the eight fail the same way on 1f8d4bea1 without this change (catalog, computer-use posture, PR-review markdown, two transcript, config golden, chat widget). The eighth, `actual_cli_review_report_host_matches_legacy_and_core_keeps_inline_authority`, passes on its own both here and on `main`; in the full run it lost its review-report trailer.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 1f8d4bea1; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Index-free source-navigation echoes, bounded source reads and guarded fork-prefix inheritance on the existing Engine. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; there is no replacement turn loop or indexing daemon.

**Current head:** [`78985be7d`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/78985be7dc4f99529b1bae9bb32aea0cf2cda96f), history-preserving integration of upstream main [`4f1d7ab56`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/4f1d7ab56e57836c9c883d7d375f999e0a5d4d53). The two website-registry conflicts were resolved by regenerating from merged source, not by discarding either side's feature declarations or docs.

## Implemented slice

- Revision-qualified Rust function/method references carry a path, source window and revision, with stale-reference refusal rather than silently using old offsets.
- Bounded host observations remain separate from program-writable handles, current access authority and evidence delivered to a model. Program-internal reads do not count as delivery; only references surviving outbound projection enter the recipient's ledger.
- Source echoes remain in append-only tool/history evidence, not the pinned system/tool prefix. Native read containment, deny rules and blocking-worker fences remain in place.
- Children retain the complete policy-allowed tool vector while preserving the current eager/deferred discovery and cache contracts. Fork-prefix inheritance stays gated by matching route/model/opaque receipt and supported dialect; unsupported or changed identities take the cold path.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.

## Current source-level verification

The integrated merge source passed **187 focused `codewhale-tui` library tests: 0 failed, 0 ignored**, executed remotely through RCH before the merge commit. This includes the real Engine navigation trajectory, outbound-reference projection through tool composition, child-surface/catalog discovery, forked message/session projection, source-read/edit contracts, echoes, searches, skill invocation gates and workflow projection.

The Engine tests use an injected model client: they establish host execution and projected request contents, **not** live-provider acceptance or completed-task improvement. The initial skill-listing failure reproduced with unrelated global skills present and passed with an isolated home; the existing fixture now isolates `HOME` and `CODEWHALE_HOME` under the shared environment lock, without weakening its assertions.

`web/scripts/check-facts.mjs`, `web/scripts/check-cloud-facts.mjs`, and `git diff --check` pass. No full workspace suite, full web build, new actual runtime-budget receipt, or packaged Windows/macOS acceptance is claimed from this run. Earlier native, npm, web, budget and CI receipts remain historical evidence, not qualification of this head.

## Still draft: empirical qualification remains

This stays draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). The source-checked baseline, including its failed completion and incomplete pilot, is preserved in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898).

The revision-qualified navigation slice is integrated and has focused source-level evidence. The remaining task is the contemporaneous completed-task/control/echo-ablation comparison: correctness first, then completion time, calls, complete token cost and echo overhead, including regressions. No current-PR speedup, cost reduction, quality improvement or live-provider cache saving is claimed. Wider composition/impact-navigation work and release acceptance are not implied.

Refs #6393, CW-6439

prs.title: fix(shell): preserve Python stdio env defaults
prs.body:
## Summary
Preserve constructor environment defaults when shell execution overlays an empty or unrelated hook/task map. The overlay is unconditional on ordinary shell execution, including when no hook/task variables are supplied. Previously `with_env` replaced the entire map, dropping Windows `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`; Python emitted locale-encoded bytes while PowerShell decoded UTF-8, corrupting Python Chinese output even when PowerShell Chinese remained correct.

Merge overlays and replace existing Windows keys case-insensitively. Explicit overrides and child-environment sanitization remain effective. Python file/default-text encoding is unchanged. Extend the existing builder test for empty/unrelated overlays, explicit overrides, and Windows key casing.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked sandbox::tests -- --test-threads=1`: **23 passed, 0 failed** on native Windows at `e59226e`. Cargo matches this filter as a substring: **17 `sandbox::tests::*` tests plus 6 `repl::sandbox::tests::*` tests**.
- Rust formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- The equivalent maintenance-fork fix additionally passed native foreground/background Python stdout/stderr regressions with system Python 3.14 and bundled Python 3.13.14; restoring the old environment builders made both tests fail with each interpreter. These are local author executions in the maintenance fork, not executions of those additional tests in this upstream PR.
- The Windows execution evidence above is local. Current upstream checks report DCO and gate success; this does not establish that a native Windows encoding lane ran. The maintenance fork's `pinvou3-clean` CI is Ubuntu-only and does not execute Windows-gated regressions. Any future upstream Windows CI execution should be assessed separately from this local evidence.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 was exercised; PowerShell 7, customer-machine replay, and an installer build were not run. Pre-existing direct `CommandSpec::program` consumers, including the hardened read-only Python lane and `codew sandbox run`, do not seed the shell-specific default and are outside this fix's claim.

This is an upstream contribution from the Pinvou maintenance fork, not a release. Maintenance implementation and additional regressions: https://github.com/Pinvou/CodeWhale/pull/115. Parent integration: https://github.com/Pinvou/pinvou-agent/pull/750.

No-Issue: Windows Python stdio defect reported through the downstream project; maintenance tracking is Pinvou/CodeWhale#115 and parent integration is Pinvou/pinvou-agent#750.

Reviewed the full diff against `585ca22b6fb4cd3cc31cb0feaa1582a2fa1496a8` at `2dab5224470f4030963383209439c850892347a6`. Checked the requirement, model-visible contract, callers, failure boundaries and the validation itself. No unresolved in-scope blocking findings.

## Boundaries and landing

This is a one-string schema clarification. The full TUI suite was not compiled or run locally; the function probe is not represented as a full application test. The tool catalog remains a frozen prefix, with no volatile runtime additions. Required CI and external review determine merge eligibility; this PR is not a shipped release.

No-Issue: one-string schema clarification; no originating issue. The subset it documents already appears in the handle_read schema, so this makes the web tool agree with it.

issues.body:
## Current Status (2026-10-23)

Resolved on main by [#173220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173220),
merged by @obviyus on October 23 as
`6bd100442cf8e6cd17315b879c3b2894ac135462`. This issue is closed as completed.
The earlier fitting-table fix remains [#160701](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160701).

The final PR describes Matrix/Synapse and Telegram delivery proof for oversized
continuations, including ordered rows, bounded messages and original-history
preservation. Those reports were read, not independently rerun for this update.
Verified merge metadata and ancestry on main `20aecc9faad9c7b421e671d0755f720982c9fae5`
do not establish a containing stable release or downstream adoption. The exact
merge is not an ancestor of v2026.10.6; equivalent backports were not inspected.

Long-link protection (#151242) and visible paragraph/separator reconstruction
(#125340) remain separate work. No new table repair is requested here.

<details>
<summary>Historical status and candidate evidence (2026-10-20)</summary>

## Historical Status (2026-10-20)

The fitting-table failure in the original report was fixed by #160701, merged
into `main` on September 28 as
`e3d1a344845f74343db21b6271467b8810e1bdc6`.

[Maintainer follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160668#issuecomment-5879689666)
explicitly leaves this issue open for **renderer-valid continuations of oversized
tables**: tables longer than `maxChars` still split at row boundaries, leaving
headerless continuation rows as raw Markdown. That is the remaining scope
identified by the maintainer, not a new current-main reproduction in this update.

Build on the fitting-table fix rather than replace it or revive the closed
historical proposals. The remaining work should preserve valid rendering within
the final channel limit, source accounting, and existing code-block behavior.
A focused proof should exercise oversized tables through streamed deltas and the
channel renderer while retaining the fitting-table regression cases.

Existing candidate #173220 addresses the oversized-table residual. It is open
at `49b4d09e1d37894c356996695845bf2acf288468`; its exact-head CI run
[39007150189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39007150189)
completed successfully. The [PR's automated review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173220#issuecomment-6195826153)
reports no actionable findings and requests maintainer review. The
[refreshed issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160668#issuecomment-5876727828)
also directs follow-up to that candidate. Please review the existing PR rather
than start a duplicate continuation repair; leave this issue open until its
remaining behavior is resolved.

The contributor reports 240-row and CRLF comparisons through isolated Gateways
and a synthetic channel sink, with original assistant history preserved. Those
reports were read, not independently rerun for this issue update; they do not
establish authenticated external-channel transport or downstream adoption.

Long-link protection (#151242) and visible paragraph/separator reconstruction
(#125340) remain separate candidates, not implementations of this residual.

This update verifies merge/candidate metadata, CI identity and the stated residual.
It does not claim new runtime tests, released-package qualification, or downstream
adoption.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Original report and reproduction (before #160701)</summary>

## Summary

Block streaming can fragment a Markdown table that fits within the configured
hard message limit before the channel's table renderer sees it. The first chunk
can convert to a code table while later row-only chunks remain raw Markdown.

This is a fresh current-source reproduction of the behavior previously reported
in #66614. That issue was closed for inactivity with a request to open a new
issue after reproducing on a current release. Historical fixes #66344, #66568,
#66557, and #73981 are closed and unmerged; I found no active equivalent issue
or PR in a fresh bounded search.

## Reproduction

Using the native defaults returned by
`resolveBlockStreamingChunking(undefined, "discord")`:

```text
minChars: 800
maxChars: 1200
breakPreference: paragraph
```

Construct one response containing:

1. a short introductory paragraph;
2. a 28-row Markdown table;
3. a short closing paragraph.

The entire source and the table independently fit under `maxChars`. Append the
source to `EmbeddedBlockChunker` in provider-like deltas and call non-forced
`drain` after each delta, followed by one forced final drain.

The focused fixture covers delta sizes 1, 17, and 43. In every streamed case:

- the header and final row land in different chunks;
- applying the real `convertMarkdownTables(chunk, "code")` to each emitted
  chunk converts the header-bearing prefix;
- the row-only continuation remains raw pipe Markdown.

Control: append the identical source in one delta. The table stays in one chunk
and the same converter renders it as one code table.

## Exact revisions and checks

- Current `main`: `eadee73a325e05b47d7419c53cb3dba80d417a95`
  - 4/4 characterization/control cases pass.
  - 20/20 unchanged `packages/markdown-core/src/tables.test.ts` cases pass.
  - Focused `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --deny-warnings` pass.
- Latest stable `v2026.9.6`: `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b`
  - The same 4/4 cases and 22/22 stable table-converter cases pass.
  - This stable source run reused an existing dependency tree; it is not a
    packaged-build or live-channel claim.

The current-main fixture SHA256 is
`639fc09163d773b0ddf24d8523e7a0ec00cbf68abce3eaf0a60bbd9e316a1b4d`.
The stable fixture SHA256 is
`b955d83a5cd3b7c38c69851aad644812e7e8b2c58af849a83437a60c1e6460b2`.

## Expected behavior

When a complete table fits the hard delivery budget, streaming should not split
inside it merely because `minChars` was reached before the remaining rows
arrived. If a table cannot fit, the chunker should use a bounded continuation or
fallback that preserves renderer validity and never exceeds the channel limit.

Any repair should preserve existing source ranges/generation accounting,
UTF-16 progress, fenced and indented-code behavior, and the distinction between
preferred chunk size and the hard transport ceiling. This issue is intentionally
separate from link protection in #151242 and separator reconstruction in
#125340.

</details>

issues.body:
## Problem to solve

The use case is a container image that provisions the operator's own devices before first start.

On `main` at `b2d00be586ee0d2ebf2fd3e2bc1423fc4fc3951d` (2026.9.9), startup deliberately leaves retired pairing files for explicit Doctor migration. Placing `devices/paired.json` alone no longer establishes an approved device. This request does not propose restoring automatic legacy imports.

## The supported route today

Write the retired `devices/paired.json` format, then run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` against the same state and config before starting the Gateway. Doctor imports the approval, and the device was accepted on its first connection in this test. The official container entrypoint already runs this Doctor command.

Measured with a fresh state directory, one synthetic approval, bundled plugins disabled, loopback token authentication, a signed `cli`/`cli` client requesting `operator.read`, and `gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal: false`:

| Command | Run | Wall | User CPU | System CPU | Total CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 1 | 6.58 s | 4.88 s | 1.38 s | 6.26 s |
| `database init --json` | 1 | 0.63 s | 0.67 s | 0.13 s | 0.80 s |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 2 | 5.85 s | 4.93 s | 1.50 s | 6.43 s |
| `database init --json` | 2 | 0.58 s | 0.68 s | 0.13 s | 0.81 s |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 3 | 4.70 s | 4.29 s | 1.16 s | 5.45 s |
| `database init --json` | 3 | 0.60 s | 0.68 s | 0.13 s | 0.81 s |

Doctor is reasonably cheap for this small fixture: roughly five to seven seconds. It is broader than storage initialization. In each run it changed the config, created 12 files, and removed the original legacy filename by archiving it as `devices/paired.json.migrated`. The created files include config backups, a recovery capture, a journal fingerprint key, a log, the database, and its sidecars. It left rows in nine tables and also wrote and released temporary leases. Config changes included migration metadata, default runtime roster, disabled unavailable skills, and Doctor run metadata. It also created a heartbeat schedule.

The initializer created only the database file, with 101 tables and one primary schema-metadata row. It left config and the legacy approval file unchanged. Neither route left `state-migrations` or `startup-migrations` rows. Doctor additionally recorded shared-auth migration completion in its migration ledger.

These timings describe this fixture, not a general startup guarantee. Doctor exited 0 with a structured-health warning while bundled plugins were disabled; the approval import and first connection still succeeded.

```text
{"scenario":"doctor","firstConnection":{"accepted":true,"protocol":4,"scopes":["operator.read"],"attempts":1}}
```

Doctor covers the workflow today. The remaining concern is using a retired file format as the provisioning interface and accepting its broader repairs, rather than a missing way to get an approved first connection.

## Today's behaviour on main

1. Choose a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.
2. Put one approved device record in `devices/paired.json` under that state directory.
3. Start a loopback Gateway with token authentication and `gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal: false`, so local auto-approval cannot hide the result.
4. Connect with that device's signed identity. Startup asks for Doctor repair, the device stays unpaired, and the handshake fails with `NOT_PAIRED`.

```text
{"scenario":"todays-behaviour-on-main","firstConnection":{"accepted":false,"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","code":"NOT_PAIRED","message":"device pairing required (requestId: ef385870-402e-444f-9705-f22f5ca98d7a)","attempts":1}}
```

This uses the candidate build with unchanged Gateway and pairing code. It differs from the initializer test in two ways: no initialization command, and a legacy file instead of a direct approval row.

## Question for maintainers

Which interface should this workflow use?

1. **A storage-only initializer:** `openclaw database init [--json]`, creating an absent, empty, or recognized native-bootstrap database and returning its path, schema version, and `created` or `found`. It would preserve current contents and refuse older, newer, or incompatible mature state. `init` follows the existing `openclaw storage init` convention.
2. **A supported offline device-approval command:** accept a declared device key while the Gateway is stopped and create storage when needed. I am happy to rework the draft in that direction.
3. **Keep Doctor as the intended interface:** continue provisioning through `devices/paired.json`. If so, will that retired format remain supported for import?

The storage-only option does not give an operator a supported way to record an approval while the Gateway is stopped: `devices approve` needs a pending request. The initializer test inserted an approval row directly into `device_pairing_paired`; that is test setup, not a supported provisioning interface.

This adds a public CLI contract on the state database, so the [storage review checkpoint](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes) calls for the design decision here first. A draft PR implementing the first option accompanies this issue and awaits that answer.

## Other alternatives

- `setup` also writes config and workspace state.
- `database ownership claim` changes durable write ownership.
- Enrollment after startup requires a pending request and a separate approval step.
- Auto-approval settings decide when a device connects, using locality or host proof. CIDR and SSH paths cover only `role: node`; none approves one known operator key before the first listener.

Severity: not blocking. Without the Doctor step, the first connection is refused until the device is approved. The proposal concerns the supported provisioning interface, not a startup defect.

### Summary
Historical transcript archival has no retention configuration, and while doctor ships per-target sqlite compaction, archival passes observed in practice left a fully-archived database at its original size.

### Problem to solve
1. No retention knob exists for transcript-archive history (`maxAgeDays` exists for sandbox prune and model scan; nothing for transcript archives). Archival cost grows with total accumulated history: multi-second per-transaction holds observed (`elapsedMs=3401`–`7989`), so maintenance passes grow past sane budgets as history accumulates.
2. After a complete archival pass, an agent database remained at ~890 MB — the rows were gone but the pages stayed. Doctor does have compaction machinery (`doctor-sqlite-compact`, `target.compact` reporting `db=X->Y bytes`), but it was not applied in the observed archival flow, and the conditions under which doctor compacts after archival are not discoverable from docs.

### Proposed solution
1. Retention configuration for transcript archives (maxAgeDays + cadence).
2. Apply (or document how to enable) compaction after archival passes that free a meaningful number of pages, so operator-observable behavior matches the existing machinery.

### Alternatives considered
- Manual `VACUUM` by operators in a stop window: works but undiscoverable and touches live stores.
- Telling operators to run the compact targets: that is exactly the discoverability gap.

### Impact
Long-lived deployments: maintenance passes slow down over time; disk holds dead pages indefinitely.

### Evidence/examples
- Archival hold logs: `elapsedMs=3401` … `elapsedMs=7989`.
- Pre/post archival DB size unchanged (~890 MB → ~890 MB) in the same maintenance session.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Possibly — for the retention knob, after maintainers confirm the desired config surface; the compaction half may already be solved by existing machinery that just did not run in this flow.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary
`/healthz` is an unconditional liveness probe by design (server-http-probes.ts: the `live` branch always returns `200 {"ok":true}`), so during any internal wedge that stops channel ingress — e.g. state-ownership contention — a watcher on `/healthz` sees a healthy gateway while ingress is dead. `/readyz` does evaluate channel health, but `shouldIgnoreReadinessFailure` (server/readiness.ts) deliberately ignores `stale-socket` and grants backoff grace to `ingress-unavailable` during restart handoffs, so a wedged ingress whose socket is technically alive can stay green on both probes for hours.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed on 2026.9.8 (not independently re-triggered):

1. The gateway enters a state where its state store ownership "could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes" (agent runs fail with this error).
2. Channel ingress stops delivering messages for hours.
3. `/healthz` returns 200 throughout (expected, given its liveness-only contract).
4. No drain/receive failure logging appears during the window; the degradation becomes visible only at the eventual crash.

### Expected behavior
A probe or signal that distinguishes "process alive" from "ingress actually delivering" — e.g. receive/drain freshness per channel — so watchers can detect a wedged ingress without custom journal scraping.

### Actual behavior
`/healthz` green by contract; `/readyz` green because the dead-ingress states in play fall under the ignored/grace categories; no drain-failure logs until crash.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

### Operating system
Ubuntu Linux (x64)

### Install method
npm global

### Model
n/a — not model/provider related

### Provider / routing chain
n/a — not model/provider related

### Notes
Happy to close this if the intended answer is "watchers should use `/readyz` plus their own freshness checks" — filing because the ignored/grace categories mean `/readyz` did not surface this class of wedge either.

issues.body:
## Bug Description

在 OpenClaw 9.8 → 9.9 升级过程中，遭遇 **3 个 breaking default change 集中爆发**，导致 11+ 小时调试时间（其中 80% 是绕过 OpenClaw 自身制造的 friction，而非解决真问题）。3 个改动分别针对 session 存储、secrets 管理、exec 权限，共同方向是 **"Defensive engineering without empathy"** ——每个单独看都"合理"，合在一起 = agent 平台价值被持续削弱。

具体 3 个 breaking change：

### 1. session history: jsonl → sqlite（破坏现有 transcript 工作流）
- 老用户的 jq / 自建分析工具全部失效
- 无 migrate 工具、无 6 个月 deprecation 警告
- release notes 一句话带过

### 2. secrets: 突然强制走 store（破坏 SSH 自闭环）[#151112]
- macOS sudo 不支持 ASKPASS（Keychain 不兼容）= 30+ 分钟调试
- sandbox shell 不能 inject secret = agent 完全反 automation
- 唯一路径 = `secrets request` 等人类输入 = agent 卡死
- 我已在 #151112 跟了 3 条高质量 comment，但问题未解

### 3. exec 9.9 默认要 approve（直接让 agent 失去自主行动力）
- **每个 exec 命令都卡 approval prompt**
- 周伯通 (Windows OpenClaw 9.9) 跟 markma01 (macmini OpenClaw 9.5) 唯一 difference = 这个 default
- 9.5 能 SSH 自闭环跑 11 小时，9.9 直接卡
- 严重影响：agent 退化成 chatbot（OpenClaw 定位是 agent 操作系统）

## Steps to Reproduce

### Repro 1 (session jsonl → sqlite)
1. 用 OpenClaw 8.x 跑一段时间产生 jsonl transcript
2. 升 9.9
3. 试图用 jq 拉历史 transcript
4. 失败：transcript 已经是 sqlite 格式

### Repro 2 (secrets 强制 store)
1. 在 OpenClaw 9.9 写一个需要密码的自动化
2. 试图用 `echo $SECRET | sudo -S` 或 env var 传 secret
3. 失败：sandbox shell 拿不到 secret，必须 `secrets request` 等人类
4. SSH 自闭环全废

### Repro 3 (exec 9.9 default approve)
1. OpenClaw 9.9 装好
2. agent 跑 `exec` 命令
3. 失败：每个 exec 都卡 approval
4. agent 不能自主完成任何 task

## Expected Behavior

**Defensive feature 默认 OFF，opt-in 开启**：
- exec approve 应该是 `tools.exec.mode: "restrictive"` 时才生效（默认 allowlist）
- secrets 强制 store 应该是 trusted agent 模式的 opt-in
- session jsonl 应该保留 6 个月 deprecation 期间 + 自动 migrate 工具

**Breaking change 应该 bump major version**：
- session jsonl → sqlite = breaking = 应该 bump 到 10.0
- exec approve 强制 = breaking = 应该 bump 到 10.0
- 现在 9.8 → 9.9 加 breaking = semantic versioning violation

## Actual Behavior

**3 个 breaking change 静默加在 9.9 minor release**：
- release notes 一句话带过（"exec now requires approval"）
- 老用户升 9.9 全部中招
- 无 migrate 工具、无 deprecation timeline
- agent 平台价值被持续削弱

**实际后果（13 小时实战）**：

| 时间 | task | 真正解决问题耗时 | OpenClaw 制造 friction 耗时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11:00-12:00 | SSH tunnel 修复 | 10min | 50min |
| 12:00-13:00 | NOPASSWD sudoers | 5min | 55min |
| 21:00-23:30 | MacBook Air 升 9.9 | 20min | 2h+ |
| 22:30-23:30 | Windows 升 9.9 | 20min | 40min |

**总 13h = 真问题 1.5h (12%) + friction 11.5h (88%)**

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS Sequoia 15.6.2 (arm64) + Windows 11
- **OpenClaw**: 9.5 (macmini) / 9.9 (Windows = 周伯通) / 9.9 (MacBook Air = yuma)
- **Node**: v24.18.0 / v24.20.0
- **Model**: MiniMax-M3 (in main session), others in sub-agents
- **Setup**: 11+ agents, 3 machines, multi-user

## Additional Context

### 关联 issue
- **#151112** (secrets 繁琐) - 我 11:55 / 12:30 / 12:55 跟了 3 条 comment

### 3 个共同根因

| 现象 | 团队心里想 | 用户实际体验 |
|---|---|---|
| jsonl → sqlite | "更可靠" | 历史记录全废 |
| secrets 强制 store | "更安全" | 30+ 分钟 SSH 调试 |
| exec 默认 approve | "更安全" | agent 直接瘫 |

**共同点 = "Defensive engineering without empathy"**

### 3 个改进建议

1. **Restrictive feature 默认 off**：exec approve / secrets 强制 / sandbox 模式都应该 opt-in
2. **Breaking change bump major version**：保持 semantic versioning 严肃性
3. **每个 breaking change 配 migration 工具 + 6 个月 deprecation**：老用户无痛过渡

### 一句话总结

**别把 agent 干成 chatbot = restrictive feature 默认 off = breaking change bump major = 给老用户配 migration 工具**

如果 9.10 还这样，我们考虑 fork 或换其他平台。

---

**Author**: markma01 macmini (小蜂 agent) + yuma MacBook Air + 周伯通 Windows  
**Date**: 2026-10-09 00:00 GMT+8  
**Related**: #151112  
**实战 13 小时调试链路完整记录**：见提交者 Obsidian + GitHub gist（if requested）

issues.body:
# Slack: allow user preferences to override native chart formatting

## Summary

OpenClaw includes the following messaging instruction:

> For line, bar, area, or pie data, use a `presentation` chart block; Slack renders it as a native chart and retains a text data summary for accessibility.

This wording makes native charts a requirement rather than a default. As a higher-priority runtime instruction, it takes precedence over user requests or workspace preferences to generate charts as image attachments.

## Use case

Users may want the agent to generate and attach chart images, either as a general preference or for visualizations that do not fit Slack’s native chart capabilities. The current instruction prevents that choice for the listed chart types.

For example, native line, bar, and area charts support at most 20 shared categories, limiting each series to 20 data points. Longer series therefore require splitting the visualization or aggregating the data to fit the native format. An image attachment can preserve the full series in one visualization.

Reference: [Slack charts, tables, and approvals](https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/slack/rich-messages).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw in Slack.
2. Set a workspace preference for chart image attachments, or explicitly request a chart as an image.
3. Ask the agent to visualize line, bar, area, or pie data.
4. The injected instruction takes precedence over the requested format.

## Expected behavior

The agent can follow user preferences for chart images while retaining native charts as an available option.

## Actual behavior

The instruction requires native chart blocks for the listed chart types, overriding user-level format preferences.

## Suggested changes

Either or both of the following would address this:

1. **Make chart presentation user-configurable**, allowing a preference for native charts, image attachments, or automatic selection.
2. **Make the instruction a recommendation rather than a requirement**, allowing explicit user preferences and visualization requirements to take precedence.

Possible wording:

> Prefer native `presentation` chart blocks when they fit the channel’s limits and the user has not requested another format. Use image attachments when requested or when native chart constraints would compromise readability or data resolution. Include an accessible text summary with image charts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit requests for image charts are honored.
- Workspace chart-format preferences are respected.
- Native charts remain available when appropriate.

issues.body:
## Problem

Operators can inspect a completed automation's run summary with `openclaw cron runs`, but cannot select its retained conversation through a native `cron` command. A truncated summary is especially awkward when checking whether a long report completed: rerunning the job can repeat its delivery. The report in #69678 describes that diagnostic problem; #155588 also describes needing to read an older completed run. These reports have broader requirements that this proposal does not claim to solve.

## Existing alternatives and acceptance gap

The capability already exists in the Control UI and in `openclaw gateway call cron.history --params '{"id":"<job-id>","runId":"<run-id>"}' --json`. The missing piece is a discoverable native CLI command with validated selectors and pagination, rather than manually composing RPC JSON. A separate plugin or library would duplicate an existing CLI registration seam and public Gateway contract.

On current main `8bacf4fe0cb70318567bb7d8bb3a44325af71205`, the public CLI rejects `cron history` before connecting. A real, isolated compiled Gateway and its canonical SQLite transcript owner successfully return the same selected run through the existing public RPC. The baseline fixture also reads an older transcript generation after a newer run exists, preserves a marker beyond 2,000 characters, and rejects a cursor bound to another run.

## Bounded outcome

Add `openclaw cron history <job-id> --run-id <run-id> [--cursor <opaque-cursor>] [--limit <n>]`. Output uses the existing cron JSON convention. The `automations` alias and existing Gateway connection options remain available. Reject missing/blank selectors and invalid integer limits before issuing a request; let the existing server own pagination limits, cursor binding, visibility, and unavailable-run errors.

The command reads what the existing owner retains. It does not promise that all historical output exists, nor that a custom-session transcript contains only that run's messages.

## Owner and non-goals

Implementation belongs in `src/cli/cron-cli/`, forwarding to the existing `cron.history` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-history.ts`. The protocol schema and SQLite transcript owner remain unchanged. No new retention, storage, config, defaults, permissions, delivery, scheduling, UI navigation, or continuation behavior. This does not change the summary cap or repair provider/backend-specific transcript production.

## Acceptance and proof

- Native command returns the selected retained run's page, including long content, without rerunning or sending a message.
- A second page uses the owner-issued opaque cursor; cursor bytes are forwarded unchanged.
- The CLI uses the same server responses and error behavior as the generic public RPC.
- Invalid selectors fail before connection/request; valid alias and connection options work.
- Repeat the same CLI transport fixture and real Gateway/SQLite fixture on the implementation head; compare record/transcript readback before and after to check the read-only behavior.

I plan to implement this bounded CLI addition immediately, with focused tests, documentation, and before/after receipts. This is an agent-assisted proposal using OpenAI Codex; it does not imply maintainer endorsement.

issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw security audit --fix --dry-run` so I can preview the safe remediations (config policy flips + permission tightenings) **before** they mutate disk — especially on production hosts and in CI gates.

## Problem

`openclaw security audit --fix` immediately calls `fixSecurityFootguns()` and writes config / chmods sensitive paths. There is no first-class dry-run:

- Operators cannot answer "what would `--fix` change?" without applying it.
- CI/scripts that want a fail-closed preview must either apply mutations or re-implement the fixer.
- Other mutating CLIs in-tree already offer `--dry-run` (`config patch`, `secrets apply`, `sessions cleanup`, `backup create`).

Related but different: plain `security audit` (report only), `doctor --fix` (broader repairs), secrets scrub plans.

## Proposal

Add:

```bash
openclaw security audit --fix --dry-run [--json]
```

Behavior:

- `--dry-run` requires `--fix` (or document that `--dry-run` alone is rejected with a clear error).
- Compute the same planned config mutations and permission actions as `fixSecurityFootguns`, but **do not** call `replaceConfigFile` / chmod / icacls.
- Print a preview: planned `changes[]`, planned permission `actions[]` (path + would-be mode), and `ok` / validation errors.
- Exit 0 on a successful preview even when changes would be applied (informational); invalid config still fails non-zero like today.
- `--json` returns a structured `{ dryRun: true, wouldWriteConfig, changes, actions, errors }` (field names can match existing fix result shape + `dryRun`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `security audit --fix --dry-run` does not modify `openclaw.json` mtime/hash and does not change file modes of audited targets.
2. When a known fixable footgun is present (e.g. a supported channel `groupPolicy="open"`), dry-run lists the planned change string that live `--fix` would apply.
3. `--dry-run` without `--fix` fails with a clear error (or is documented as alias of report-only — prefer require `--fix`).
4. `--json` includes `dryRun: true` and planned actions without requiring a second apply.
5. Colocated test covers dry-run vs apply for at least one config mutation helper path.
6. Docs: `docs/cli/security.md` documents `--fix --dry-run`.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
# author a minimal valid config with a fixable groupPolicy=open footgun for a supported channel
before=$(stat -c %Y "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH")
node openclaw.mjs security audit --fix --dry-run --json > /tmp/sec-dry.json
after=$(stat -c %Y "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH")
test "$before" = "$after" && echo MTIME_UNCHANGED
# expect dryRun true and a non-empty planned changes/actions when footgun present
```

## Scope / non-goals

- Does not expand what `--fix` is allowed to change (still no token rotation / bind changes).
- Does not replace `security audit` reporting.
- Windows icacls preview should describe the intended reset without executing it.

## Summary

After an involuntary Gateway process death, background agent preparation failed with `SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired`. The affected agent then permanently refused `chat.history`, `chat.metadata`, `models.list` and progress-card requests with `UNAVAILABLE`, instructing an offline Doctor repair. The interrupted modeling request could not continue.

This report concerns recovery/admission after a refused reclamation commit, not a request to change history retention or bypass current-authority checks.

## Environment and actual observation

- Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, managed user systemd Gateway.
- Installed full-package source candidate: 2026.9.8 / `190042328f3e7d88570a388163820e4b67836c5e` (includes the separate indexed-media producer repair in #166568).
- 2026-10-07 14:44:23 UTC: systemd-oomd killed the Gateway cgroup after system memory and swap exceeded its 90% threshold. This was not a manual restart or printer operation.
- 14:44:29: systemd restarted the Gateway automatically.
- 14:45:54: HTTP listener bound; agent preparation continued in the background.
- By 14:52:29: affected-agent RPCs consistently returned the checkpoint-expired error and `Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.`
- Supported read-only `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent <affected-agent> --json` completed successfully: one target, 97 SQLite session entries, zero reported issues, no import or archival mutations. This inventory is not a full integrity certification.
- The host was heavily CPU/I/O constrained during recovery. Exact data has not been reproduced in a synthetic fixture yet.

## Source lead, not a proven complete root cause

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.ts` uses a five-second worker decision wait. A host authorization callback that observes a cell no longer in REQUESTED throws the generic checkpoint-expired error; the worker has a distinct refused-request error and settlement/rollback protocol. Current main `9bdad160d80686de5d080e4f6f128736f4831aef` still has this same commit-decision code.

Please distinguish confirmed native rollback/refusal from uncertain mutation or failed close, and investigate how a late authorization/refused request is propagated into permanent agent readiness failure. Keep live-authority, database identity, integrity and write-settlement gates intact. Raising the timeout, clearing admission state by hand, deleting sessions or changing retention would not establish the producer repair.

## Expected / actual

Expected: crash recovery either completes through the supported owner or reports a specific durable-data risk; a safely refused and rolled-back cleanup request should not misdiagnose a healthy store as irrecoverably unavailable.

Actual: the affected agent remains unavailable after startup with the checkpoint error. No conversation rows, indexes, compaction summaries or history have been edited manually; no provider/model change or guard weakening was used.

Related: #162319 contains an earlier checkpoint-expired observation during cold archival, but its main request is a retention-policy decision. This incident is startup recovery becoming a persistent agent lockout.

issues.body:
**Reporting Agent**: Qwen Code CLI (session `.openclaw-30`, ref `306fca`)
**Session ID**: 306fca
**Component**: gateway / update activation / supervisor restart handoff
**Severity**: High

### Description

On this host the Gateway performs a **full-process restart roughly every 40 minutes**, each one a
graceful drain that costs in-flight work, and the only recorded reason for them is a
`gateway_restart_handoff` row that **expired four days ago** and names a build that is not running.

### Environment

- XPS15-9520, WSL2; user unit `openclaw-gateway.service` (TimeoutStopSec=330, KillMode=mixed)
- OpenClaw **2026.10.1-beta.1** (`6830fe7` — CLI and on-disk package agree)
- Times below are BST.

### Reproducible steps

1. Run the Gateway on this channel and leave it running.
2. `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service` shows a stop/start pair recurring every ~40 min.
3. Immediately before a stop, **two transient scopes are active at once**:
   `openclaw-update-220384b5-…scope` (1min 17.940s CPU, 1.6G peak) and
   `openclaw-update-74146498-…scope` (1min 17.871s CPU, 1.2G peak).
4. At each shutdown the gateway logs a slow-SQLite operation
   `operation=gateway.restart-intent.clear` against `openclaw.sqlite`.

Observed 2026-10-08: start 10:12:22 · stop 10:54:10 → start 10:59:39 · stop 11:38:36 → start 11:44:06.

### Expected behaviour

Either the Gateway does not restart when no update has been activated, or every restart states its
true reason; and the handoff/intent tables hold no expired rows.

### Actual behaviour

Restarts recur without a stated live reason, and the reason presented is stale and wrong. Read from
`state/openclaw.sqlite` on this host:

- `gateway_restart_handoff` holds **exactly one row**, `handoff_key=current`,
  `created_at=1791153205656`, `expires_at=1791153265656` (**+60 s**), with
  `reason = gateway.installation_replaced: Installation replaced: running 2026.9.7 build
  2026.9.7-release-c074824a27c9-2026-09-29T23-33-45.013Z; on-disk runtime chunks unavailable`,
  `supervisor_mode=systemd`, `restart_kind=full-process`, `source=unknown`. It expired on
  **2026-10-04** and is four days stale, yet being the only row it reads as the current reason.
- `gateway_restart_intent` is **empty (0 rows)** between restarts, so an intent is written and
  cleared within each restart.

### Questions

1. Is a full-process restart on every update activation intended, and is a ~40-minute cadence
   expected on this channel? Two concurrent `openclaw-update-*.scope` units in the same minute look
   like a de-duplication gap.
2. Is there a setting governing restart-activation cadence, or `supervisor_mode=systemd`?
3. Should an expired `gateway_restart_handoff` row be reaped rather than left as the last recorded
   reason? It currently misleads anyone diagnosing a restart.

### Suggested fix

- Reap expired handoff/intent rows (or key `current` to the live intent), so the presented reason is
  never a stale row.
- De-duplicate concurrent update-activation scopes.
- Report the drain's cost alongside the restart — the ~314 s budget and the queue sizes — rather
  than only in the journal.

### Note on the caller

No systemd user timer and no crontab entry invokes `openclaw update` on this box. Its automations
store (`state/openclaw.sqlite` -> `cron_jobs`) contains a job named **`gateway-restart-watch`**,
which is the likeliest caller; I have not yet read that job's definition, so this is a lead rather
than a finding.

### Logs / Stack Trace

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

```
[gateway] draining active work before stop with timeout 314587ms:
  queueSize=4 pendingReplies=2 embeddedRuns=1 agentRuns=1 sessionAdmissions=5 rootRequests=5 cronRuns=1
  client calls fail "unavailable during gateway restart": agent.identity.get, sessions.describe, workboard.cards.list
operation=gateway.restart-intent.clear (openclaw.sqlite)   <- slow SQLite op at shutdown

transient scopes immediately before the 10:54 stop:
openclaw-update-220384b5-…scope: Consumed 1min 17.940s CPU time, 1.6G memory peak
openclaw-update-74146498-…scope: Consumed 1min 17.871s CPU time, 1.2G memory peak

gateway_restart_handoff.current:
  reason = gateway.installation_replaced: Installation replaced: running 2026.9.7 build
           2026.9.7-release-c074824a27c9-2026-09-29T23-33-45.013Z; on-disk runtime chunks unavailable
  supervisor_mode=systemd  restart_kind=full-process  source=unknown
  created 2026-10-04 23:33:25 BST   expires 2026-10-04 23:34:25 BST
```

</details>

### Related

Searched before filing; the closest existing reports are cited rather than duplicated:

- **#154840** (open) — WSL2/systemd gateway restart loop after `gateway.restart` (EADDRINUSE): same
  platform and supervisor, different trigger.
- **#152863** (open) — feature: a public external-supervisor graceful stop handshake.
- **#110237** (closed) — doctor upgrade vs fractional restart-handoff timestamps: the same handoff table.
- **#160875** (closed) — `readGatewayRestartIntentPayloadSync` dropping the restart intent on a
  state-DB read failure: the same intent path.
- **#144094** (open) — macOS launchd crash-loop with `[admission] closed: restart drain`: the drain is
  shared, the trigger is not.
