## Summary

Investigate an intermittent empty copy-status assertion in the real-browser file-path tooltip test. During a paired full-UI runtime qualification, the baseline passed and the candidate had one failure in 22,785 executed assertions. A bounded follow-up of 20 whole-file runs on each of Node 24.21.0, Bun 667c and Bun fc53 produced no failures.

Disposition: **known intermittent, recorded per the CI known-failure policy**. Neither a candidate runtime regression nor an equal-rate pre-existing race is established. The passing focused runs do not prove a fix; the original failure remains recorded for owner investigation.

## Failing row

Source: [`986a594e3da344c7127a68d1fcbc170abc65a3c9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/986a594e3da344c7127a68d1fcbc170abc65a3c9).

File: [`ui/src/components/markdown-file-tooltip.browser.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/986a594e3da344c7127a68d1fcbc170abc65a3c9/ui/src/components/markdown-file-tooltip.browser.test.ts#L31).

Case: `file path tooltip > keeps the popup reachable and copies the exact path without opening the file`.

The assertion expected the status element to contain `Copied!` but received empty text until the ordinary 60-second browser-test deadline. The baseline case took 832 ms; the failed candidate case took 60,115 ms. The test already awaits the status assertion and click concurrently with `Promise.all` (the change landed in #165912).

The subsequent clipboard-payload and no-navigation assertions were not reached. The evidence therefore does not establish whether the clipboard spy was called, success feedback was published then cleared, or tooltip ownership retired before feedback.

## Qualification evidence

Linux x86-64; identical source, canonical Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and the repository's UI test configuration, with the existing four-worker ceiling and native deadlines.

| Full UI lane | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Files |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bun 667c | 22,785 | 0 | 6 | 1,644 |
| Bun fc53 | 22,784 | 1 | 6 | 1,644 |

| Bounded whole-file classification | File runs passed | Assertions passed | Failed | Skipped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Node 24.21.0 | 20/20 | 260 | 0 | 0 |
| Bun 667c | 20/20 | 260 | 0 | 0 |
| Bun fc53 | 20/20 | 260 | 0 | 0 |

The 60 runs used ten cyclically rotated cold/warm blocks, with private state and verified matched cache custody. All 13 original cases ran every time. No source instrumentation, timeout change, tolerance change or skip was introduced. The unchanged standalone file does not reconstruct the full lane's style/animation history.

Baseline release: [`openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156).

Candidate release: [`openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b).

## Retained capture references

The original paired evidence archive has SHA-256 `21c34d9f245f9e38817a70f54b7880876b8ee0920249dfebf08a2173daabeab0`.

Screenshot reference: `p035-tooltip-failure.png`, SHA-256 `928b547129c7061b269bb16d4e0f5d02c24c29ffb7210fdb24fbd0bb4a531a69`. It shows a synthetic example file path, an open popup, a copy icon and an empty status at the failed assertion. The 414×896 viewport is Vitest's default; it is not evidence of leaked viewport state. The still image contains no event-transition history.

Before the valid classification, a harness temporary-directory path exceeded Chromium's Unix socket limit. Those startup attempts executed zero assertions and are excluded from the table. Restoring the short private temporary path allowed the single valid bounded cohort to run; all invalid logs remain archived separately.

## Investigation boundary

A browser-local timeline around the original failure is needed: actual click and clipboard-spy activity, status text mutations, tooltip open/close and owner generation, and assertion/action settlement. Distinguish missed transient feedback from absent feedback or ownership retirement before selecting a synchronization repair. Preserve the real interaction, payload/navigation checks and existing deadlines.

issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw config explain <path>` so I can see **why** a config value is what it is (authored vs runtime default, which `$include` owns it, env/SecretRef state) without dumping the whole tree or guessing from `config get` alone.

## Problem

Today:

- `openclaw config get <path>` prints the **redacted runtime value** only.
- `openclaw config diff` (#178016) lists authored-vs-effective differences across many paths.
- `openclaw config export --safe` (#178014) dumps the full redacted tree.

None of these answer a single-path support question: "Did this come from my file, an include, an env SecretRef, or a runtime default?" Operators dig through include files and `${ENV}` by hand, and sometimes mistake a default for an authored secret/plaintext value.

Related but different: #178016 (bulk diff), #178014 (full export), #103606 (externally managed hot-reload).

## Proposal

Add:

```bash
openclaw config explain <path> [--json]
```

Behavior (v1):

- Load the same config snapshot as other read-only config commands.
- For `<path>`, report structured provenance, for example:
  - `path`
  - `runtimeValue` (redacted via existing `redactConfigObject` / UI hints — same as `config get`)
  - `authoredPresent` (bool: present on `sourceConfig` after include/env)
  - `source` enum: `authored` | `default` | `unset` (and optionally `include` when include ownership applies)
  - `include` (when `includeProvenance` owns the path): include file path + ownership fields already tracked on the snapshot
  - `secretRef` summary when resolution facts / SecretRef metadata exist for the path: `{ source, provider, id, state }` **without** resolving or printing the secret value
- Missing/invalid config fails clearly (same policy as `config get` / `config validate`).
- Unknown schema paths fail like `config get`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For an unset schema path that has a runtime default, `config explain` reports `source=default` (or equivalent) and a redacted runtime value when one exists.
2. After `config set <path> <value>`, explain reports `authoredPresent=true` / `source=authored` for that path.
3. When the path is owned by a `$include` file, explain names that include path (from snapshot `includeProvenance`).
4. When the path is backed by a SecretRef / env ref, explain shows ref identity fields and does **not** print the resolved secret; plaintext secrets still redact like `config get`.
5. `--json` emits a stable machine-readable object; human mode is readable without requiring jq.
6. Colocated unit/integration test covers at least authored vs default for one path; docs update `docs/cli/config.md`.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
printf '%s\n' '{}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
node openclaw.mjs config explain agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
# expect source=default (or unset+default filled), no crash
node openclaw.mjs config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '"30m"'
node openclaw.mjs config explain agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
# expect authoredPresent=true / source=authored, runtimeValue visible as 30m
```

## Scope / non-goals

- Not a bulk authored-vs-runtime listing (that is #178016 `config diff`).
- Not a full redacted export (#178014).
- Does not resolve/print secret material; SecretRef identity only.

issues.body:
We are building a governed model-selection workflow around OpenClaw and are looking for a supported way to associate structured task metadata with a specific agent execution before model resolution.

We have tested the supported `before_agent_run` hook in OpenClaw 2026.9.3. It appears suitable as a non-blocking observation point, but the runner context does not provide enough information to identify an externally governed task or reconstruct its authority and workflow requirements. In particular, we need to carry fields such as:

- external task ID and revision;
- immutable task/envelope reference or digest;
- authority/admission state;
- workflow role and stage;
- validation and independent-review requirements;
- model/reasoning constraints and cost/fallback constraints.

We would then like the resulting execution evidence to link that external task identity to OpenClaw's host-generated execution/run/context identity and the provider/model/reasoning actually used.

The desired transaction is roughly:

`structured governed task → committed/verified immutable envelope → per-request fail-closed admission → task/role/stage-scoped model resolution → agent execution → receipt linking external task identity to actual provider/model/reasoning and OpenClaw execution identity`

We are specifically trying **not** to implement this by parsing natural-language prompts, using session side channels, patching OpenClaw source, or creating a plugin-owned parallel dispatcher.

We have also looked at `before_dispatch`, `reply_dispatch`, Gateway `agent` RPC, `/hooks/agent`, and execution/audit identities. They provide useful pieces, but we have not found a supported mechanism that composes the complete transaction above.

Two questions:

1. Does OpenClaw already provide a supported first-class mechanism for attaching immutable external task metadata to a particular agent run before model resolution/admission and carrying that identity through execution receipts?
2. If not, would you consider a host capability that allows a structured per-run metadata/envelope reference, task-scoped fail-closed admission, role/stage model options, and an execution receipt containing both external task identity and actual provider/model/reasoning?

An important requirement for our use case is preserving **independent reviewer separation**. For example, an implementation stage may deliberately use one model while a subsequent independent review stage is required to use a different model. A task-level model override should therefore not silently propagate to the reviewer role.

We are happy to provide a more concrete proposed schema if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow custom decision-model providers in `models.providers` with `type: "decision"`, a custom endpoint, API key or SecretRef, and operator-defined model IDs.

## Problem to solve

Custom chat models can be configured through `models.providers`, but typed decision models currently require a plugin-owned provider and static manifest model catalog. Adding `type: "decision"` to a custom provider is rejected by the config schema. Removing the field does not register a decision provider or add its models to the separate Decision picker.

This prevents an operator from configuring their own native decision endpoint and model IDs using the familiar provider configuration flow. This is a configuration support gap; no previously working version is claimed.

## Proposed solution

Add an explicit decision provider type to the existing configuration surface. Keep `baseUrl`, `apiKey`/SecretRef, headers, timeout, and model IDs with that provider. Select an installed decision adapter separately from the model role so plugins continue to own native wire protocols, while the host owns catalog separation, provider binding, lifecycle, deadlines, and result validation.

Illustrative proposed configuration (currently unsupported):

```json5
{
  models: {
    providers: {
      custom: {
        type: "decision",
        decisionProvider: "typesafe",
        baseUrl: "https://decisions.example.com/v1",
        apiKey: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "CUSTOM_DECISION_API_KEY" },
        models: [{ id: "custom-decision-model", name: "Custom decision model" }],
      },
    },
  },
  agents: { defaults: { decisionModel: "custom/custom-decision-model" } },
}
```

The endpoint must implement the selected adapter's native decision protocol. Decision models must stay out of chat/primary/fallback/utility catalogs. Configuration and credential changes must invalidate outstanding requests and reset provider health appropriately. Preserve actual probability estimates and score distributions; do not manufacture decisions from chat completions.

## Alternatives considered

- Author a separate plugin for every private endpoint/model: unnecessary duplication when an existing wire adapter can be reused.
- Reuse a chat model with JSON output: a different capability with different probability semantics.
- Change only the schema: leaves decision catalog discovery and runtime dispatch broken.

## Impact

Affected: operators using private or custom hosted decision endpoints and model IDs. The missing config path consistently blocks this setup. Existing ONNX and TypeSafe plugin-defined models remain available through their documented setup.

## Evidence/examples

Inspected upstream `83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7` (`2026.9.8`). Directly reproduced with `ModelsConfigSchema.safeParse` using a synthetic endpoint/key/model:

```text
code: unrecognized_keys
path: providers.custom
keys: [type]
message: Unrecognized key: "type"
```

`src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-capabilities.ts` currently enumerates manifest decision models only. `src/decisions/runtime.ts` dispatches only registered plugin decision providers. See [Decision models](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7/docs/concepts/decision-models.md) and [custom providers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7/docs/concepts/model-providers/custom-providers.md).

Related context: #166320 adds an OpenAI Decisions adapter and endpoint overrides under its existing provider identity. This request covers operator-defined provider/model declarations and reusable adapter binding.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
## Problem

`model.usage`'s `costUsd` (and its `usage` token totals) appear to reflect only the **final real model API call** of an agent turn, not the sum across every real call that happened within that turn — even when the turn involved several real calls in a tool-use loop. This means turns with multiple real calls likely have their true cost (and token total) under-reported by this event, systematically, for any multi-call turn.

## Evidence

Captured live against a production Claude Sonnet 5 session with prompt caching enabled, using a plugin that separately logs both `model.usage` (once per turn) and `model.call.completed` (once per real API call, confirmed call-scoped via `observer.usageField()` — see #166623).

**The per-call event shows a strictly growing, then-resetting, token total across one turn's real calls** (one real turn, successive real API calls in a tool loop):

```
tokens=77626
tokens=78192
tokens=80043
...
tokens=130803
tokens=131702
tokens=132127
tokens=133398
tokens=133567
tokens=133960
```

**The `model.usage` event logged for that same turn reports `tokens=133960`** — exactly the last value in the sequence above, not a sum of the sequence (which would be far larger, since each entry already includes the growing resent context from prior calls in the loop).

**Cost cross-check:** using published per-token pricing for the model in question (including its cache-read/cache-write discount tiers) against the actual per-call token breakdown (fresh input vs. cache-read vs. cache-write vs. completion, all available from the per-call events), the *estimated* true cost for this turn's full sequence of real calls comes out roughly an order of magnitude higher than the `costUsd` value `model.usage` actually reported for the turn. The gap tracks almost exactly with "last call only" vs. "all calls in the turn."

## Why this matters

`model.usage` is the only event that carries cost at all (no per-call cost field exists anywhere in the plugin-facing API — see #166692). If its cost silently reflects only the turn's last real call rather than the full turn, every multi-call tool-use turn under-reports true spend, and the undercount grows with how many real calls happen in the loop. This is a correctness gap in the existing, official cost-reporting mechanism — not something a plugin can work around, since no per-call cost is exposed elsewhere.

## Ask

Confirm whether `model.usage`'s `usage`/`costUsd` is sourced from only the turn's terminal real call rather than accumulated across every real call dispatched during that turn, and if so, fix it to reflect the full turn.

## References

- #166623 — established that `model.call.completed`/`model.call.error` fire once per real call with call-scoped usage, which is what made this cross-check possible.
- #166692 — separate ask (attach cost to those per-call events too); this issue is about the existing turn-level cost being incomplete even before any per-call cost exists.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
The macOS app's local device-pairing WebSocket connections (`clientId=openclaw-macos`, modes `ui` and `node`, `role=operator`) fail with `authReason=token_missing` / `authProvided=none` on every reconnect attempt (~every 30s) against the local Gateway (`ws://127.0.0.1:18789`), even though the device holds a valid paired token both in the Gateway's `device_pairing_paired` table and in the app's own local `device_auth_tokens` sqlite store. The loop persists indefinitely and survives a full app quit/relaunch.

### Steps to reproduce
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO for the original trigger (first observed already in-progress). However, the following did **not** stop the loop once it was occurring, each tested in isolation while the bug was actively reproducing:
1. Fully quit the macOS app (⌃/⌘Q) and relaunch it — new process, identical failure starting on the very first reconnect attempt.
2. `openclaw doctor --repair --generate-gateway-token` (rotates the shared `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` secret) + Gateway service restart.
3. `openclaw devices rotate --device <id> --role operator` (rotates that specific paired device's token).
4. `openclaw devices remove <id>` — Gateway log immediately showed `device pairing removed` followed by `device pairing auto-approved` for a fresh pairing of the same device id (loopback connections auto-approve) — the `token_missing` loop resumed within the next ~30s poll cycle regardless.

### Expected behavior
The app should attach its stored device token (present locally in `~/Library/Application Support/OpenClaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`, table `device_auth_tokens`, and recognized by the Gateway's `device_pairing_paired` table) when opening `ui`/`node` connections — as it evidently did before: the last successful auth for this device/role is logged at `2026-10-06T18:03:32.364+02:00` (`[gateway] ... lastSeenReason=connect`), matching the `updated_at_ms` of the same row in the app's local token table to the millisecond.

### Actual behavior
Continuous pairs of `[ws] unauthorized ... reason=token_missing ... authProvided=none` + `[ws] closed before connect ... authReason=token_missing` logged roughly every 30 seconds, for both `mode=ui` and `mode=node`, `role=operator`, same `instanceId`, `hasDeviceIdentity=true` throughout. Over the ~46 hours before mitigation attempts this produced over 12,000 log lines. Sample pair:

```
2026-10-07T20:17:21.938+02:00 [ws] unauthorized conn=c26d2631-8202-4e18-be74-45ebf9b0e3db peer=127.0.0.1:59400->127.0.0.1:18789 remote=127.0.0.1 client=MBP Marko ui v2026.9.8 role=operator scopes=6 auth=none device=yes platform=macOS 26.7.1 instance=f2a69036-5c94-4d66-8110-883b9f40ae2b host=127.0.0.1:18789 origin=n/a ua=OpenClaw/2609000890 CFNetwork/3860.700.1 Darwin/25.6.0 reason=token_missing guidance=unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
2026-10-07T20:17:21.955+02:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=c26d2631-8202-4e18-be74-45ebf9b0e3db peer=127.0.0.1:59400->127.0.0.1:18789 remote=127.0.0.1 ... authMode=token authProvided=none authReason=token_missing allowTailscale=true ... role=operator scopeCount=6 hasDeviceIdentity=true client=openclaw-macos clientDisplayName="MBP Marko" mode=ui version=2026.9.8 platform="macOS 26.7.1" deviceFamily=Mac modelIdentifier=Mac14,9 instanceId=f2a69036-5c94-4d66-8110-883b9f40ae2b
```

The app's own Connection tab surfaces this as two different-looking symptoms that are the same root cause:
- "Local Gateway" tile: `Gateway listener found on port 18789 (pid <pid> node @ /usr/local/bin/node) but health check failed: Gateway health probe timed out after ~800ms`
- "Gateway local" tile: `Health check failed: This gateway requires an auth token. Run openclaw gateway auth-token --show on the gateway host.`

The Gateway itself is healthy throughout: `openclaw health` reports a 9ms probe duration, and a direct `curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/` returns `200 OK` in ~5ms.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.8 (fc23bc8) — confirmed identical across the CLI (`openclaw --version`), the Gateway service, and the macOS app (`CFBundleShortVersionString`). Already the latest release per the app's own Sparkle appcast at the time of filing.

### Operating system
macOS 26.7.1, Mac14,9 (Apple Silicon)

### Install method
Gateway: npm global (`openclaw` installed via `npm install -g`, service run via launchd). macOS app: official OpenClaw.app, configured as "Gateway gestionado de forma independiente" (app connects to the existing CLI-managed Gateway rather than bundling its own).

### Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not a model/provider-related issue — purely a Gateway/device-auth transport bug, reproduces independent of any agent/model activity)

### Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not applicable — issue is in the Gateway's device-auth WebSocket handshake, not in model routing)

### Additional provider/model setup details
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Impact and severity
- Affected: the macOS app's own "Local (este Mac)" Gateway connection mode, on a host where the Gateway is managed independently (npm-global CLI/launchd) rather than bundled by the app.
- Severity: does not interrupt the Gateway's own channels/agent runtime (Telegram etc. kept working throughout via the Gateway process itself), but per the app's own UI text, "chat rápido, la voz y las actualizaciones" and permissions in `Panel → Configuración → Este Mac` depend specifically on this connection, so those app-embedded features are unusable while the loop persists. It also continuously grows the Gateway's log file (a new failed-connect pair every ~30s, indefinitely).
- Frequency: continuous since onset; observed for 24h50m+ without self-recovery, across an app relaunch and four independent server-side auth remediation attempts.
- Consequence: app-embedded quick chat/voice/permissions panel unusable; steady background log growth; recurring "Local Gateway" red-banner health warning in the app with no in-app remedy (no credential field is exposed for the "Local (este Mac)" mode — only "Remoto (otro host)" exposes a manual token field, and using that mode as a workaround is not viable: it rewrites the shared `openclaw.json`'s `gateway.mode` to `"remote"`, which per `openclaw config schema` stops the host from running channels/agent runtime locally).

### Additional information
- Last known good: `2026-10-06T18:03:32+02:00` (last successful `operator` auth for this device, confirmed in both the Gateway's `device_pairing_paired.last_seen_at_ms` and the app's local `device_auth_tokens.updated_at_ms`, to the millisecond). First known bad: the next scheduled reconnect after that timestamp. No app/CLI version change occurred between good and bad — same build (2026.9.8) throughout — so this does not appear to be an upgrade-triggered regression; the actual trigger is unknown.
- A separate connection in the same app session — the "Gateways" tab, using the `openclaw-control-ui` client in `webchat` mode, manually configured with the Gateway's Tailscale Serve URL and a token obtained via `openclaw gateway auth-token --show` — authenticates successfully (confirmed via `[ws] webchat connected ... client=openclaw-control-ui webchat` in the Gateway log) and stays connected with normal ping stats. This confirms the bug is isolated to the `openclaw-macos` client's `ui`/`node` connection code path, not the Gateway, not the app's networking in general, and not device pairing/approval (which the Gateway grants instantly on loopback).
- No workaround currently preserves both correctness and functionality (see Impact section above for why the "Remoto" + manual token workaround is not acceptable).

issues.body:
## Summary

Feature request: attach cost to the `model.call.completed`/`model.call.error` diagnostic events, the same way `model.usage` carries cost today — not a new mechanism, just the existing price-table lookup running on an event that's structurally decoupled from whatever currently prevents `model.usage` from firing in some session types.

## Background

#166623 asked for per-call token usage and was closed as already-implemented: `model.call.completed`/`model.call.error` carry real per-call `usage` (tokens) via `observer.usageField()`, independent of the turn-aggregated `model.usage` event. We adopted this in our plugin and it works exactly as described — real per-call token granularity, finally.

#164562 (still open) describes `model.usage` never firing for sessions running under a channel/topic-level model override — cost silently missing for those sessions, tokens still visible via a separate path.

## The gap this FR targets

Since adopting the `model.call.completed`/`.error` events, we now have live evidence of the practical shape of the gap between those two issues. For a real session affected by #164562 (a channel/topic model override), we observed:

- **Zero** `model.usage`-sourced metrics for the entire session (confirming #164562 — that event never fires here).
- **Correct, internally consistent** token counts from `model.call.completed`/`.error` for the same session (prompt=47216, completion=190, total=47406 — exact).
- **No cost** anywhere for this session, because the only place cost is ever computed is inside whatever code path also emits `model.usage` — and that path doesn't run here.

So this specific session has fully correct token accounting and zero cost visibility, for no reason other than cost not being attached to the one event that's already proven to work independently of the #164562 bug.

We understand (and have independently confirmed, since custom/self-hosted OpenAI-compatible providers' raw API responses carry no cost field at all) that `costUsd` on `model.usage` must come from a core-side price-per-token table, not from the provider response itself. The ask here is simply to run that same lookup when emitting `model.call.completed`/`model.call.error`, and attach the resulting cost to those events too.

## Why this is worth doing even with #164562 still open

This wouldn't replace fixing #164562 — `model.usage` firing correctly is still the right long-term fix. But since `model.call.completed`/`.error` already don't depend on whatever's broken for #164562, giving them cost too would mean sessions hitting #164562 get full cost visibility as a side effect, the same way they already incidentally got full token visibility once we moved onto this event. It also just closes an odd asymmetry: the two numbers that used to travel together (tokens, cost) now take genuinely different paths for no documented reason.

## References

- #166623 — precedent: this mechanism (per-call diagnostic events carrying real usage, independent of `model.usage`) exists and was accepted as sufficient for tokens.
- #164562 — live evidence of the practical gap: a real session with correct per-call tokens and zero cost, because of this exact asymmetry.

issues.body:
## Problem

`web_fetch` can return an extracted access-denied, login, CAPTCHA, bot-check, or navigation-only page as an ordinary successful result. Agents then spend attention on content that cannot answer the user's question.

## Proposed behavior

Add an opt-in, web-fetch-owned Decision page-quality check after extraction. `shadow` would report a proposed judgment without withholding content; `apply` would withhold only a strong unusable-page judgment on a complete excerpt. Both require the existing Decision assistance opt-in and the owning agent's selected Decision model. Unavailable, uncertain, cancelled, stale, and truncated cases must preserve the original page or normal cancellation behavior. The fetch cache must retain the original result.

This is not a global web-search filter or page-change classifier. The selected Decision provider may receive bounded extracted page text, so setup and privacy/cost implications need to be explicit.

## Acceptance evidence

A PR should include direct and fallback `web_fetch` path tests, stale-config/cancellation/fail-open checks, and pre-labelled page-quality observations including false drops and missed junk. The experimental threshold should be reviewable, not described as calibrated accuracy.

Inspired by the page-quality experiment in <https://x.com/ethank_6/status/2107576429928169934>.

issues.body:
Multi-agent gateways make it common to keep several agents open simultaneously in split panes. Currently the only per-agent visual identity is name + emoji + avatar, which is hard to distinguish at a glance across panes, especially in multi-pane layouts or for users with low vision.

**Proposal:** Allow an optional accent color per agent (e.g., `agents.entries.*.identity.accentColor`), applied as a tint or stripe on:
- split-pane headers
- sidebar session rows grouped by agent
- avatar ring / message bubbles (optional)

**Why:** with 5 agents (main + personal + course + two projects), pane-glance recognition is the main usability friction. Themes are global; agents need identity. Accent colors are a small, orthogonal addition that composes with existing themes.

Suggested behavior: agent config overrides > agent-derived hash color > theme default. Respect increased-contrast / forced-colors modes by falling back to non-color markers.

issues.body:
## Summary

Request design acceptance for allocation-owned execution-host identity, so Systems can group disposable workers under the machine that actually runs them. Initial acceptance is two simultaneous workers on two hosts; larger fleets are a later validation target.

## Problem to solve

A flat worker list does not tell an operator which machines or cloud services are in use. With a local macOS container backend and a remote Linux container backend, a worker's enrolled telemetry node identifies the guest, not its physical parent. Backend/profile names alone are not proof of host identity.

Existing shared-host node relationships are useful, but cannot truthfully express the physical parent of a disposable container. Inferring that parent from a display name, IP address, current profile configuration, or Gateway hostname risks incorrect grouping and historical attribution.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional bounded execution-host receipt to the existing worker-provider lease contract, retain it through the existing worker environment owner, and expose it to Systems for host-first grouping.

```ts
type WorkerExecutionHost = {
  id: string;          // Provider-scoped stable identity, 1–128 ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._:-].
  displayName: string; // Nonsecret label, 1–120 characters, no control characters.
};
```

- Add optional `executionHost` to `WorkerLease` and the public worker environment summary through existing seams, not a new tool or SDK subpath.
- Persist versioned JSON in a proposed nullable `worker_environments.execution_host_json TEXT` column, admitted by the canonical database owner. Regenerate database types through existing tooling.
- The allocation owner obtains host identity through the authenticated allocation path and binds the receipt to the exact lease. A friendly label supplements identity; it does not establish it.
- Scope grouping keys by canonical provider identity plus host ID. Never join on display names. Providers must namespace host IDs adequately for their allocation domains.
- For a provider that cannot identify a physical host, preserve provider-level grouping with an explicit unknown-host state. Do not invent a machine parent from a cloud service name.
- Preserve the existing core-owned shared-host/node relation. Do not allow a provider-supplied arbitrary node/environment ID to attach a worker to a paired node. Physical-host rows may coexist with paired-node rows until an authoritative binding exists.
- Keep active workers and retained history distinguishable under each parent, with search retaining parent context and compact/mobile labels retaining host context.

### Ownership, trust, and lifecycle

This is **provider-attested presentation provenance**, not authorization, placement authority, or a routing target. It does not independently prove the provider is truthful.

Validate only named fields. Do not forward arbitrary provider labels, addresses, usernames, SSH options, credentials, raw hardware UUIDs, or provider settings. Obtain an opaque provider-scoped ID or suitable namespaced digest instead.

Record the receipt in the same owner-authorized transition that adopts the lease and transport, after checking current ownership following awaited work. Use the existing worker broker/store and committed projection; no additional state owner, sidecar store, list-time database mutation, or Gateway-main-thread database access.

Keep the fact stable for that allocation. A conflicting later observation must not silently rewrite history. Retain it with the environment under existing retention rules. Existing records remain unknown; no guess-based backfill from current configuration. Exclude this field from authority decisions and review any relevant digest construction.

Recommended malformed-optional-field policy: omit the invalid presentation fact with a bounded nonsecret diagnostic, keeping the worker lifecycle available. Please confirm this choice versus rejecting the receipt.

### Upgrade and rollback

Propose a same-version, bare nullable TEXT addition, with no default, index, NOT NULL, or CHECK constraint. This is subject to explicit design acceptance and compatibility proof, not assumed safe because it is additive.

Prove previous-version database admission, reads and writes against a candidate-created copy, preservation of the unknown column, and subsequent candidate reopening. Binary rollback must not drop the column. Old workers remain unknown, and older UIs ignore the new metadata.

Storage cost is one bounded JSON value per worker. Host discovery happens during allocation, not on every UI refresh. No added per-row network lookup or new retention service.

## Alternatives considered

- **Treat the guest telemetry node as its physical host:** incorrect for disposable containers.
- **Use profile names or current profile settings:** request/configuration inputs are not an allocation receipt and may change after allocation.
- **Reuse profile snapshot, desktop, or bootstrap receipt fields:** changes those fields' existing meanings and creates mixed ownership.
- **In-memory or inspect-only metadata:** useful only while the lease can be inspected; loses attribution after restart or resource destruction.
- **Separate metadata table/store:** adds another lifecycle/join surface without an established need.
- **Provider-only grouping:** retain as the honest fallback, but it does not identify different machines served by the same backend.

## Impact

Affected: operators using workers across multiple local, LAN, and cloud backends.

Severity: blocks reliable host-first fleet inspection, although it does not itself block task execution.

Frequency: whenever multiple worker destinations are in use.

Consequence: operators must cross-reference provider inventories to locate resources and understand failures or retained history. The first milestone is two real hosts; scaling to tens/hundreds will need separate rendering, search, pagination, and telemetry-cost measurements, not an unsupported scalability claim.

## Evidence/examples

Related UI/lifecycle context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165873.

Source inspection baseline: `079f019294fb`.

- `src/plugins/capability-provider.types.ts`: `WorkerLease` currently records lease/transport/shared-account facts, not container physical-parent identity.
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/environment-summary.ts`: existing shared-host node linkage cannot be reused to identify a disposable guest's physical parent.
- `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-inspect.ts`: named inspect fields are projected; arbitrary host labels are not a durable provenance contract.

A local host-tree UI prototype has focused and synthetic desktop/mobile validation for existing shared-node and provider-grouping facts. **It is not deployed, and synthetic screenshots are not live two-host proof.** The proposed persistence/SDK extension is not implemented.

A bounded CAD workload executed successfully in a remote Linux container, but automatic result reconciliation and normal reclaim failed; artifacts were manually recovered and exact resources were reclaimed through supported forced teardown. That is execution evidence only, not successful end-to-end worker qualification. The lifecycle failure is a separate prerequisite for the eventual live acceptance test, not evidence that this metadata change repairs it.

### Required implementation proof

- Absent, valid, malformed, oversized, and control-character receipt fields; arbitrary labels never forwarded; mismatched lease rejected.
- Guest node never treated as physical parent; same-label/different-ID hosts remain distinct; multiple workers on one host group together.
- Profile edits cannot relabel history; older records stay unknown; host facts survive reopen and terminal cleanup under existing retention.
- Stale/canceled owners cannot publish; metadata commits atomically with lease adoption.
- Nullable-column admission, previous binary read/write, candidate reopen, and rollback/recovery coverage.
- One live worker on a Linux host and one on a Mac host simultaneously; correlate lease-bound receipts with independent host probes and the actual connected UI; inspect desktop/mobile evidence.
- Verify automatic artifact return and normal cleanup for both exact test resources. Preserve unrelated resources.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, following maintainer acceptance of the storage/SDK design and the required implementation proof.

## Decision requested

Please confirm whether this optional allocation-owned receipt, same-owner persistence, nullable-column approach, and presentation-only public projection are acceptable before implementation. Feedback on the narrower existing contract to use instead is welcome.

This request follows the design-acceptance checkpoint in `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` and the SDK boundary guidance in `src/plugin-sdk/AGENTS.md`. Filing this issue is not acceptance of the design.

AI-assisted proposal, reviewed and published with the operator's authorization.

issues.body:
Gateway-methods exhausted the Linux qualification host's memory under the source-owned Bun pin. The complete owner remains on Node; the failed Bun run was not replayed for admission.

### Reproduction scope

- Source: [`cb01febf9fa4fbda271d10b3adff3b384c6ece76`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cb01febf9fa4fbda271d10b3adff3b384c6ece76).
- Published fork: [`openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156) (`1.4.3-canary.1+667c4ab22`). Linux x64 executable SHA256: `76ede220307e41e36c6f4981abf203536de469d2a6628a7ce503616fd477c467`.
- Linux x64, eight logical CPUs, 33,084,002,304 bytes observed RAM (about 30.8 GiB), no swap; four non-isolated fork workers.
- Complete `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts`, 447 files, no file filters. Fresh private state and runtime caches, canonical current-head `qaRuntime` preparation, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`.
- Existing test/hook deadlines stayed at 120,000/180,000 ms; the outer bound stayed at 2,562 seconds. No skips, worker limits or deadlines were changed to obtain a passing result.

The consumer command was:

```sh
CI=true OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4 \
  NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts --maxWorkers=4
```

The exact fork binary was staged on PATH. The full qualification also retained resource, JSON and sealed per-file reporters.

### Observed failure

The Bun arm began at 2026-10-07 15:38:53 UTC. At 15:57:38 UTC, the kernel recorded global OOM and killed a Bun worker with `anon-rss:12299036kB` (about 11.7 GiB) and `total-vm:28994680kB`. The workload cgroup peak was 32,033,415,168 bytes; its OOM-kill count was one and CPU throttling counters were zero. The time-specific kernel record associates the OOM with this run; the cgroup counters alone are cumulative.

The final collection contains 415 completed files, 5,628 passing assertions and 16 existing skips, with no observed assertion failure. Thirty-two files have no completed receipt. There is no complete Bun Vitest report or completed candidate cell, so these partial passes do not qualify the owner.

The workspace-owner renewal subsequently failed closed. The command transport exited 7 and the interrupted execution pipeline recorded 141. Source/runtime identities and process closure were checked directly afterward, and both the original archive and a separate final post-join archive were retained.

### Node comparison

The first, previously unexecuted Node 24.21.0 control completed on the same frozen source, host, CPU/worker/memory profile and unchanged deadlines: **447 files, 5,700 passes, 16 existing skips, exit 0, 1,028.066 seconds**. Its wrapper and process cleanup also completed successfully, with no OOM recorded in the control window.

Independent verification confirms exact unredacted case identity/status parity for the 415 files observed in both engines. The other 32 Bun files remain unobserved. The preserved failed Bun artifacts were checked unchanged after the Node control. This is a single control and an observed candidate-side resource failure; it does not establish the memory-growth root cause or qualify the owner.

### Investigation boundary

The root cause of the memory growth is unclassified. A prior source, `fbac0bec89805765cba15e2bc146be9f6c88217a`, completed two full passing Bun/Node pairs on the same runtime/profile. The newer source changes native SQLite worker admission, session-reader lifetimes, and async placement/worktree ownership. These are investigation leads, not a proven cause or an engine-versus-fixture conclusion.

This was the complete unfiltered owner. The result does not establish that every smaller CI include stripe would exhaust memory. Whole-owner admission remains blocked; narrowing the proof, adding skips, or widening memory/timeouts is not the proposed resolution.

Please identify the owning retained-memory/lifetime boundary, produce a bounded reproducer and fix, then perform fresh admission qualification on the then-current shared pin. The failed candidate and first Node control must remain recorded rather than being replayed to green.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `decision_evaluate` tool declares support for all three TypeSafe question types (`boolean`, `choice`, `score`) — its own description states *"The selected provider supports boolean, choice, score questions."* However, the `score` branch is unreachable in practice: any `score` question is rejected by **local input-schema validation** before the provider is called, including when `criteria` is supplied in exactly the shape the tool's own input schema declares.

`boolean` and `choice` questions work correctly on the same tool, same config, same session.

> 中文注：工具自称支持 boolean / choice / score 三种题型，但 `score` 分支实际不可用——任何 `score` 问题都会在**本地 schema 校验**阶段被拒，压根到不了 provider，哪怕 `criteria` 完全按工具自己声明的形状给。同一工具、同一配置、同一会话下，`boolean` 与 `choice` 均正常。

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | `2026.9.8` (build `fc23bc8`) |
| OS | Windows |
| Plugin | `typesafe` (enabled) |
| Config | `agents.defaults.decisionModel = "typesafe/jev-latest"` |
| Tool access | `tools.alsoAllow` contains `"decision_evaluate"` |

> 中文注：复现环境为 OpenClaw 2026.9.8 / Windows，typesafe 插件已启用，决策模型指向 `typesafe/jev-latest`，且 `decision_evaluate` 已在 `tools.alsoAllow` 中放行（即不是"工具没注册/没放行"这类环境问题）。

## Declared input schema (from `tool_describe`)

The tool advertises three question shapes under `questions.<id>`. The `score` branch declares:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "const" /* "score" */,
  "criteria": {
    "type": "array",
    "minItems": 2,
    "items": { "anyOf": [ { "type": "string" }, { "type": "object" }, { "type": "null" } ] }
  }
}
```

i.e. `criteria` should be an **array with at least two string / object / null items**.

> 中文注：工具自己声明的 `score` 题目形状是——`type` 固定为 `"score"`，`criteria` 是一个**至少 2 项的数组**，元素可为字符串/对象/null。换言之，按声明这里给数组是合规的。

## Reproduction

Minimal payload (no real data):

```json
{
  "state": { "status": "error", "error": "command exited with code 1" },
  "questions": {
    "urgency": {
      "type": "score",
      "instructions": "How urgent is this failure?",
      "criteria": [
        "Low: ignorable or already self-recovered",
        "Medium: does not break delivery",
        "High: affects delivery or will worsen"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

> 中文注：最小复现 payload，不含任何真实数据。三档评分 criteria 用**扁平字符串数组**，完全按上一节声明的形状。

## Actual result

Rejected locally, with **no provider call** (so no `429` / auth / rate-limit explanation applies):

```
Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:decision_evaluate":
  questions.urgency.type: must be equal to constant (allowed: "boolean");
  questions.urgency.criteria: must be null;
  questions.urgency.criteria: must not have additional properties: "item";
  questions.urgency.criteria: must match a schema in anyOf;
  questions.urgency.type: must be equal to constant (allowed: "choice");
  questions.urgency.criteria: must not have fewer than 2 properties;
  questions.urgency.criteria: must be array.
Expected input: { questions: { ... }; state: unknown }.
```

Note the last clause: **`criteria: must be array`** — while the payload supplies exactly that.

> 中文注：报错在本地校验阶段产生，**未发出任何 provider 请求**，所以与鉴权/限流/网络无关。注意最后一句是 `criteria: must be array`（"必须给数组"）——而请求里给的**就是**数组。

## Why this looks like a discriminator defect, not a caller error

1. **The error is byte-identical regardless of the array's shape.** A flat `["a","b","c"]` and a nested `[{"item":["a","b","c"]}]` both produce the same message, including the same `must not have additional properties: "item"` clause.
2. **The message enumerates failures for all three `anyOf` branches.** The final clause is the `score` branch's complaint — i.e. the branch is reached, but its constraint is applied against an already-array value.
3. **`boolean` and `choice` succeed** on the same tool with object-form `criteria`, so the plugin registration, the credential path, and the provider round-trip are all healthy.
4. **The same `score` question succeeds over the provider's HTTP API** (`POST /v1/systemone`), returning `score` + `confidence` normally — so the provider and the model support the primitive; only the tool's local validation blocks it.

Reproduced consistently across multiple attempts (4/4) and independently in two separate sessions.

> 中文注：判断这是工具缺陷而非调用方写错，四条对照证据：① 数组无论扁平成 `["a","b","c"]` 还是嵌套成 `[{"item":[...]}]`，报错**一字不差**；② 报错把三个 anyOf 分支的失败都列了出来，最后一条正是 score 分支的抱怨，说明分支确实被走到了，只是约束被套在了一个本来就是数组的值上；③ 同工具的 boolean / choice 正常，证明插件注册、凭据链路、provider 往返都没问题；④ 同一个 score 问题改走 provider 的 HTTP API 则正常返回 `score` + `confidence`，说明模型与 provider 都支持，是工具的本地校验把它挡住了。跨两个独立会话、4/4 次稳定复现。

## Impact

- Agents configured with the TypeSafe plugin cannot use the `score` primitive through the sanctioned tool path. `score` is one of the three primitives advertised by the tool.
- The documented fallback — switching `score` questions to `choice` — is workable but lossy for callers that need an ordered rubric, and it forces a rewrite of question definitions.
- The only remaining route is a hand-written HTTP call from the agent, which moves credential handling and retry logic outside the plugin — exactly what the tool exists to centralize.
- The failure mode is confusing: the error names a constraint (`must be array`) that the payload satisfies, so it reads as a caller mistake rather than a tool defect, costing real debugging time.

> 中文注：影响面——① 工具宣称的三原语之一被自己的校验封死；② 官方建议的退路（改用 `choice`）对需要"有序评分表"的调用方是有损的，且得重写题目定义；③ 剩下唯一出路是让 agent 手写 HTTP，凭据处理与重试逻辑全部溢出插件，而这正是该工具要集中化的东西；④ 最麻烦的是报错指着一条请求**已经满足**的约束（"必须给数组"），读起来像用户自己写错了，实际是工具坏了，白白浪费排查时间。

## Suggested direction

Since `boolean` (object criteria) and `choice` (object criteria, ≥2 keys) validate fine while `score` (array criteria) does not, the `anyOf` branch discrimination for `score` looks worth checking — e.g. the `type` discriminator may not be narrowing the branch before `criteria` is validated, or the array branch may be losing to the object branch during `anyOf` evaluation.

Not sure whether this is version-specific (observed on `2026.9.8`) or still present on `main` — happy to re-test against a newer build if that helps triage.

> 中文注：方向建议——boolean（对象型 criteria）和 choice（对象型、≥2 键）都校验通过，唯独 score（数组型）不过，怀疑是 `anyOf` 分支判别的问题：`type` 判别式可能没在校验 `criteria` 前先把分支收窄，或者数组分支在 `anyOf` 求值时被对象分支压过去了。不确定这是版本相关（我在 2026.9.8 上观察到）还是 main 上仍在，若换新版本能加速定位，我可以再测。

## Related

- #155115 — Provider-neutral `decision_evaluate` tool and capability discovery
- #162875 — `decision_evaluate` always fails in scheduled/CLI-started runs

> 中文注：#155115 讨论的是 decision_evaluate 工具的 provider 中立化与能力发现（我 10-01 在该帖留过两条实测评论），#162875 报的是定时/CLI 场景下 decision_evaluate 恒失败（根因不同）。本 issue 与 #155115 属同一片功能区域，一并列出便于维护者归拢处理。

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm global install, node v24.16.0; gateway as systemd user unit, Ubuntu (kernel 7.0.0-3x), single host
- 15-agent organization; mixed tool profiles (`full` and `coding` per agent; root tools.profile=coding); `tools.sessions.visibility=all`; `agentToAgent` enabled
- Session kinds in daily use: main lanes, an interactive dashboard lane, isolated cron runs, collector subagents

## Symptoms
1. The agent-side `automations` tool (documented in docs/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md) disappeared from the per-turn tool inventory of **every** observed session: a `full`-profile main lane, a `coding`-profile main lane, and a **fresh isolated minimal-context subagent probe** (lightContext, ~200 input tokens).
2. The flip happened **mid-session during normal operation**: last confirmed successful tool call 2026-10-04 ~13:0x local; first confirmed absence 2026-10-05 ~01:4x. In that window: **zero gateway restarts, zero host restarts, zero config-file changes** (config mtime 2026-10-04 12:12 precedes the last successful use — the tool worked after that write).
3. **Persistent across cold restarts**: a host reboot (10-06 12:39) and a gateway-only restart (10-07 06:16) did not restore the tool.
4. **Silent**: no error/warn lines in gateway logs at flip time; post-restart boot logs show no registration errors; plugin inventory identical across four gateway generations spanning the window (15 plugins, stable list).
5. Discovered days later only because an agent reported "tool absent in all turns today"; the org had silently fallen back to the CLI.

## Code-level gate (read from the installed dist bundle)
- Tool-injection filter (agent-tools module) drops `automations` when `!(cronCreatorAuthorityResolver || cronManagementGrant)`.
- Resolver binding: `cronCreatorAuthorityResolver = bindActiveCronCreatorAuthorityResolver(options?.runId)` (agent-runtime-identity-token module) — a **per-run authority binding**.
- State DB: table `worker_turn_tool_authorities` (session_id, environment_id, owner_epoch, placement_generation, claim_id, run_id, tool_names_json, updated_at_ms) holds **0 rows** — no per-run tool authority is persisted for any session.
- `device_auth_tokens`: single operator token with scopes `operator.admin/approvals/read/write`, **unchanged for ~3.5 weeks** (long before the flip) — operator auth stable.

## Non-causes excluded (with evidence)
- **Config deny/allow**: full-text config grep for "automations" = 0 hits; per-agent deny lists cover browser/canvas/messaging/calendar tools only; `agents.defaults.tools=null`; `agents.defaults.experimental=null` (lean mode not set).
- **Plugin registry**: boot-line plugin inventory identical across four gateway generations before/after the flip.
- **Context-size tool trimming**: fresh minimal-context isolated probe also lacks the tool.
- **Operator auth**: device token unchanged since well before the flip.
- **Version**: same build (2026.9.4 / 3a9d69d) throughout — the tool was present under the identical binary hours before the flip.

## Expected vs actual
- Expected: `automations` availability stable for authorized sessions (as it had been for weeks), and any entitlement flip to be logged/auditable and recoverable (restart or re-auth).
- Actual: silent, org-wide, mid-session flip; no audit trail (authority table empty); unrecoverable across cold restarts; only the per-run resolver outcome appears to have changed.

## Mitigation in place (our side)
- Org-wide migration to `openclaw cron` / `openclaw automations` CLI — full functional parity for our usage (one-shot `--at`, `--delete-after-run`, `--model`, best-effort delivery, agent-run wrapped payloads). Zero operational loss, but in-turn tool ergonomics are gone and the entitlement state remains flipped.

## Asks
1. What populates `worker_turn_tool_authorities`, and what does `bindActiveCronCreatorAuthorityResolver(runId)` resolve against? Under what condition does it start returning falsy for **all** runs, persistently, with no config change, no restart, and no log line?
2. Should entitlement flips emit an audit/log event? Is there a supported re-grant or re-auth path short of a version upgrade (e.g., operator.admin re-authentication)?
3. Known issue in releases after 2026.9.4?
4. Domain-separation note: filed separately from #166035 (supervisor child-process accumulation) and #166137 (egress sentinel substitution) — distinct subsystems, separate issues for triage hygiene.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm global install, node v24.16.0; gateway as systemd user unit, Ubuntu (kernel 7.0.0-3x), single host
- Protected secret store in use; two entries relevant here: a search-API key (allowedHosts = its API host) and a GitHub PAT (allowedHosts = api.github.com). Egress proxy enabled with exact allowedHosts.
- Affected consumer: agent `exec` tool runs issuing curl one-liners with injected sentinel env vars. Gateway-side consumers (an MCP server shelling out to curl with the same sentinel mechanism) were observed working **in the same minute** exec-side failed (Occurrence 1).

## Observed occurrences (local times)
**Occurrence 0 (prior, 2026-09-22 ~18:0x)** — search-API calls from long-lived exec runs returned 401 while the stored key was valid. Layered tests at the time: a **fresh** exec run with the same sentinel → 200; gateway-side MCP path → 200; direct key check → valid. Internally attributed to per-run egress proxy credential snapshot expiry; workaround adopted since: run external queries in fresh/short runs.

**Occurrence 1 (2026-10-04 18:26-18:28)** — within ~2 minutes, exec curl failed for **both** secrets: GitHub `GET /user` → 401 Bad credentials (two separate runs), search API → 401. Same-minute controls: anonymous `GET /rate_limit` → 200 (network fine); **gateway-side MCP search tool → 200 with real results** (gateway egress substitution fine); secret-store entries verified unchanged (update timestamps). No config change preceded; no restart between.

**Self-heal (2026-10-05 09:00)** — identical exec-path tests → both APIs 200. **No restart and no config change in between** (same host boot).

**Occurrence 2 (2026-10-06 16:56-16:58)** — three-run sequence, no credential/config/restart change throughout:
- 16:56 run: GitHub `POST /repos/.../issues` → 401 Bad credentials.
- 16:57 run (fresh): search API → 401 **and** GitHub `GET /user` → 200 **within the same run, minutes apart** (per-host mixed substitution).
- 16:58 run: GitHub `POST /repos/.../issues` → 201 Created (issue #166035 filed successfully).
Note: host was under heavy legitimate CPU load at the time (load ~30 on 6 cores) — correlation unknown, listed as context only.

## Pattern summary
- Failure signature: upstream rejects the credential (401) although the store entry is valid and unchanged — consistent with the opaque sentinel (or a stale substitution value) reaching upstream unsubstituted. Per the store design, sentinels are opaque: **no plaintext secret exposure was observed** at any point.
- Granularity: varies **per exec run** and **per destination host within a single run** (16:57 mixed result); gateway-side substitution can work while exec-side fails in the same minute (Occurrence 1).
- Duration: hours-scale (18:26 → next-day 09:00 self-heal) and minutes-scale (16:56 fail → 16:58 success on retry).
- Silent failure: gateway journal shows **no** proxy/substitution error lines at any failure timestamp (checked 10-06 17:07 for the 16:50-17:00 window) — the miss is invisible server-side.

## Impact
- Intermittent 401s on valid credentials invite misdiagnosis as expired/revoked tokens (we nearly re-rotated a healthy PAT in Occurrence 1); automation retries mask incidence; any agent workflow calling external APIs from exec is exposed.
- Security-adjacent: substitution reliability is a core guarantee of the sentinel design; a silent, variable miss erodes the auditability of "which value actually left the host".

## Asks
1. Root-cause the per-run/per-host substitution variance: lifecycle of the exec-run env snapshot vs the egress proxy substitution table; is there a rotation/expiry race between them?
2. Known issue? Fixed or changed in releases after 2026.9.4?
3. Could a failed substitution be made non-silent (proxy-side warn log, or an opt-in strict mode that fails the request locally instead of letting the raw sentinel egress)?
4. Cross-reference: observed on the same host/deployment as #166035 (supervisor child-process accumulation) — distinct defect domains, filed separately for triage hygiene.

issues.body:
# Windows: managed Gateway service (schtasks) will not start; update to 2026.9.8 rolls back

## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8) — also reproduced on 2026.9.6; npm global install
- OS: Windows 11 (win32 x64, build 10.0.26200)
- Node.js: 24.19.0
- Service: Windows Scheduled Task "OpenClaw Gateway" -> gateway.vbs -> gateway.cmd
- Gateway: mode=local, bind=loopback, port=18789

## Symptoms

### 1) `openclaw gateway start` aborts a slow-but-healthy boot
```
Gateway start timed out after 90s waiting for /healthz and /readyz.
Tip: openclaw gateway status --deep
Tip: openclaw doctor
```
The CLI then stops the service it just started:
```
{\"subsystem\":\"gateway/task-supervisor\"} {\"exitCode\":1,\"exitSignal\":null,\"reason\":\"exit\",\"stderr\":\"\"} "Gateway child failed"
```
A gateway started manually boots fine, but takes ~40-70 s here (log: `http server listening (18 plugins: ...; 69.7s)`), so the 90 s readiness window is hit.

### 2) `schtasks /Run /TN "OpenClaw Gateway"` (the CLI's own tip) -> child refuses
```
Another gateway (pid <N>) already owns this state directory; refusing to run automatic startup
migrations or report the gateway ready. Stop it with "openclaw gateway stop" (or select a
different OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR), then retry startup.
```
Child exits 1, nothing listens on 18789. Observed repeatedly (different pid each time).

### 3) Repair refused before reinstall
```
Gateway repair failed: Error: Refusing to repair the managed Gateway service because its installed
state directory cannot be determined from the service definition. Run `openclaw gateway install --force`
to repair it intentionally.
```
After `openclaw gateway install --force` the task is re-registered, but (1) and (2) still reproduce.

### Workaround that works
Foreground gateway, no task supervisor:
```
openclaw gateway --port 18789
```

## Related: update 2026.9.6 -> 2026.9.8 rolled back
Reason: `doctor-failed`. Post-install `openclaw doctor` exits 1:
```
Candidate executor binding does not match its parent.
```
(thrown from the managed update handoff as UpdateCommandRecoveryPendingError.) Plus doctor lint:
```
core/doctor/lint-inspection update-validation-budget: Doctor lint inspection deferred until after
activation: 1 agent scopes need a 2000ms inspection allowance, with 0ms remaining in the validation
inspection window (validation-ledger).
```
Also on this box `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw status` hang when run interactively. 2026.9.8 was
installed as a workaround with `npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.8`.

## Evidence
- Sanitized diagnostics archive (log tail, config shape, gateway status/health) — available on request.
- Update failure/lint reports: `openclaw-update-failure-*.json`, `openclaw-update-lint-*.json`.
- Key log lines (local time +08:00):
  - 02:08:47 service child starts -> 02:09:59 readiness timeout -> 02:10:21 `Gateway child failed`
  - 02:23:05 `schtasks /Run` -> `Another gateway (pid <N>) already owns this state directory...`
  - 02:12:01 `http server listening (... 69.7s)` (manual run)

## Notes
- Likely two independent issues: (a) readiness window too short for slow Windows boots, and
  (b) supervised child refusing on state-dir ownership during service start.
- Reproducible; happy to provide more logs.

issues.body:
**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.9.7, `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.7 (Codex app-server harness).

**What happens**
A parent agent spawns native Codex children (`spawn_agent`). A child finishes its first task normally. Later, in a
**new** parent turn, the parent sends that same (now idle) child a new task through the collaboration message path.
The child's new turn starts and its **first model request** is rejected:

```
unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Codex cannot verify the owner of this model request. Start a fresh request before retrying.
```

The child turn ends immediately. The parent is not told in a way it can act on, so from the parent's point of view the
task was delegated and nothing happens. In our case work silently stalled for ~25 minutes until someone checked.

**Evidence (10 of 10 cases over 4 days)**
- Every real failure (we excluded the error string quoted inside later context) happened in a **child thread whose turn
  number was ≥ 2**, and that turn was **triggered by an inter-agent message**.
- It never happened on a child's first turn.
- It happened with and without our local relay patches, so it is not caused by them.

**Where it comes from**
`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts` → `createCodexInferenceModelBinding`. For a child request,
`captureModelSource({ threadId, turnId, parentThreadId, parentTurnId, rootTurnId })` fails or returns no source, and the
binding throws `CodexInferenceAuthorizationError("owner")`, which becomes a 403 `model_permission_denied`. Our reading
is that the re-tasked child's model custody is still tied to the parent turn that originally spawned it. That turn is
over, so there is no current owner to bind to.

**Expected**
One of these:
- (a) Re-tasking an idle child from the current parent turn re-binds its model custody to the current parent turn.
- (b) The send or re-task call is rejected **up front**, with a clear error to the parent ("child is bound to an
  ended turn; spawn a new child").

Either way, the failure should not be silent for the parent.

**Workaround we use:** always spawn a fresh child for each new task, and never re-task children from earlier parent
turns. Since adopting it, no recurrences.

# [Bug]: Control UI context window widget renders stale `maxTokens` (128k) after model switch / gateway restart

- **Reporter**: DomotiGa (gateway-owner)
- **Date**: 2026-10-05
- **Severity**: low–medium (cosmetic; model still has full context, but UI misleads operator into thinking they are near limit, which can trigger premature compaction)

## Summary

The dashboard context-window widget for `minimax/MiniMax-M3` can render `120k / 128k` (~94% "full") even though:

- The model's actual `contextTokens` is **1,000,000** (configured and confirmed).
- The current input token count is **1,295** (less than 0.2% of the real context window).

The UI appears to read `maxTokens` (≈131072) for the widget denominator instead of `contextTokens` (1M), after certain lifecycle events (model switch, gateway restart, session reset).

## Reproduction

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.9.8.
2. Set `minimax/MiniMax-M3` as default model.
3. Use gateway normally (token usage low, ~1k input tokens).
4. Switch model to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` for a few turns, then switch back to `minimax/MiniMax-M3`.

Expected: widget denominator = `1,000,000`, fill = ~0.13%.
Actual: widget denominator = `128,000` (or `131,072`), fill = `120,768 / 131,072` ≈ 92%.

Same symptom can be triggered by gateway restart after a model switch. The `kill -s SIGKILL` → systemd auto-restart with a fresh PID often restores the correct `980k` (1M − 20k reserve) widget denominator.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **v2026.9.8** (`build=2026.9.8-release-fc23bc864e45-2026-10-02T18-22-33.858Z`)
- Model: `minimax/MiniMax-M3`, `contextTokens: 1000000` in `openclaw.json`, confirmed via `openclaw models list` and `openclaw sessions list --json`.
- Source value: `dist/extensions/minimax/provider-discovery.js` defines `DEFAULT_MINIMAX_MAX_TOKENS = 131072` and `MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_CATALOG["MiniMax-M3"].contextWindow = 1e6`. The widget can render either field depending on cache state.

## Workaround (manual)

```
systemctl --user kill -s SIGKILL openclaw-gateway.service
sleep 5
systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway.service --property=MainPID,ActiveState,SubState
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18789/health
```

After auto-restart, hard refresh the Control UI tab — `980k` returns.

This works but should not be necessary: model is correct, config is correct, CLI is authoritative.

## Suggested diagnostic

Maintainer-side:

- Identify the Control UI widget that draws the progress arc / fill percentage.
- Determine which field the widget reads (`contextTokens`, `maxTokens`, or another).
- Check whether the widget reads from a per-session cache or a global model-definition cache, and whether that cache is invalidated on model switch.
- Confirm that `providerContextTokenCache` (`dist/worker/...`) and `CONTEXT_WINDOW_CACHE_STATE.contextWindowCache` are cleared on model switch + on session reset + on gateway restart.

## Related

- #165391 — Dashboard shows N session rows, sessions.list shows M (separate symptom, same dashboard, separate code path)
- #158900 — Mid-turn auto-compaction fails when prompt exceeds `contextTokens` (different UI symptom, related fallback chain)

issues.body:
### Summary

Move the generated Control UI translation memory (`ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl`) out of `main` so the repository's history stops growing by ~4 MB file versions on every locale refresh.

### Problem to solve

The translation-memory files are now most of the repository's clone size. In a full clone of `openclaw/openclaw` (all branches, 105k commits, 5.24 GiB pack), the on-disk blob size breaks down as:

| Path | On-disk size |
|---|---|
| `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` | **3.53 GiB** |
| everything else | 1.30 GiB |
| `mantis/` QA gifs (`qa-artifacts` branch) | 0.08 GiB |
| committed Swift `.build/` caches | 0.06 GiB |
| committed `.serena/` cache | 0.01 GiB |

On `origin/main` alone:
- 20 TM files, 85 MB in the current tree (~4 MB each)
- 813 commits touching them since 2026-04-05 (343 `github-actions[bot]`, 327 `openclaw-mantis[bot]`)
- 9,307 distinct TM blob versions

Each refresh only changes a few lines per file (for example, #165213 is +100/-20 across 20 files, and #165010 is +20/-20). But every refresh stores a new version of each ~4 MB file, and the `control-ui-locale-refresh` workflow runs on a daily cron plus on pushes. That adds up to 20 large blob versions per run, indefinitely.

#159032 reported the clone size and was closed as needing a GitHub-side repack. That repack would help existing clones. This issue is about the source-side cause, which a repack doesn't fix: the workflow keeps adding history at this rate.

### Proposed solution

Keep the translation memory out of `main`'s tree. Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Dedicated orphan branch or separate repo for TM** (for example, `i18n-memory`). The locale workflow reads and writes TM there and only commits the generated `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts` output to `main`. The TM history still exists but no longer comes with every clone of `main`, and `--single-branch` clones skip it entirely.
2. **Store TM as a CI artifact or cache** (Actions cache or a release asset), restored at the start of `control-ui-locale-refresh.yml` and saved at the end. This only works if TM loss is recoverable, for example by retranslating with the existing "retranslate every source string" input.
3. **Git LFS for `*.tm.jsonl`.** This is the smallest workflow change, but it adds an LFS dependency for contributors and bandwidth costs on GitHub.

`ui/AGENTS.md` already treats these files as generated and workflow-owned rather than hand-edited, so moving them shouldn't affect contributors.

### Alternatives considered

- **GitHub support repack only (#159032):** shrinks the current pack (the reporter there saw 6.2 GiB → 1.2 GiB after a local repack) but does nothing about future growth.
- **History rewrite (filter-repo) to purge old TM versions:** would fix past history too, but breaks every fork and open PR. That seems out of proportion.
- **Shrinking each file (shard per namespace, drop `updated_at`):** reduces per-version cost but keeps the unbounded growth.

### Impact

- **Affected:** anyone doing a full clone. That includes contributors, forks, people self-hosting from source, and CI jobs without `--filter`/`--depth`.
- **Severity:** annoying to workflow-blocking on slow or metered connections or small disks.
- **Frequency:** every full clone. Growth continues on every locale refresh (at least daily).
- **Consequence:** multi-GB clones and fetches, slow `git gc`, and disk pressure on dev machines.

### Evidence/examples

Measured on a full clone fetched 2026-10-05:

```sh
# on-disk blob size by category
git rev-list --objects --all \
  | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectsize:disk) %(rest)' \
  | awk '$1=="blob" && $3 ~ /\.tm\.jsonl$/ {s+=$2} END {printf "%.2f GiB\n", s/2^30}'
# -> 3.53 GiB

git log --oneline origin/main -- 'ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl' | wc -l          # 813
git rev-list --objects origin/main -- ui/src/i18n/.i18n/ | grep -c 'tm.jsonl$'   # 9307
```

Workflow: `.github/workflows/control-ui-locale-refresh.yml`. It stages `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/${LOCALE}.tm.jsonl` (around line 205) and publishes `*.tm.jsonl` via the `automation/control-ui-locale-refresh` branch (around line 277). The cron is `23 4 * * *`.

Related: #159032 (clone size report, closed as needing a GitHub-side repack).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Separately from this change, a server-side repack via GitHub support (as #159032 suggested) would still be worthwhile for the existing history. Until then, contributors can use `git clone --filter=blob:none` or run `git repack -a -d -f --depth=50 --window=250` locally.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- Workflow unchanged. `.github/workflows/control-ui-locale-refresh.yml` still crons on `23 4 * * *` (line 36), stages `*.tm.jsonl` (line 207), and publishes via the `automation/control-ui-locale-refresh` branch (lines 276–279).
- 20 `.tm.jsonl` files currently tracked on `main`, totalling **84.1 MiB** (`git ls-tree -l -r origin/main ui/src/i18n/.i18n/`).
- **13 refresh commits touching `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` on `main` since this issue was filed on 2026-10-05** — the daily cron keeps running and keeps adding ~4 MB × 20 blob versions per refresh.
- No mitigation landed: no `.gitattributes` LFS rules for `*.tm.jsonl`, no orphan-branch migration, no alternative storage.

## Summary
On macOS, OpenClaw **2026.9.8** `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --json` fails during `finalize:plugins` after `finalize:doctor` completes. The plugin lifecycle lease verifier reports that the shared state database is still undergoing offline maintenance. A prior 2026.9.7 package activation remains `prepared`, so future native updates remain blocked despite a healthy 2026.9.8 Gateway.

## Environment
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64; Node 26.8.x; npm global installation in an unprivileged user prefix; managed launchd Gateway.
- Core CLI and Gateway: 2026.9.8 (release build fc23bc8); previous installed release: 2026.9.7.
- A verified OpenClaw state backup was created before manual installation. No recovery journal, migration marker, database row, or staged package was removed or edited.

## Reproduction and observed timeline (October 4, 2026, EDT)
1. A native 2026.9.7 → 2026.9.8 update left package activation `prepared`. The original sealed helper refused its package fingerprint with `Package publication object changed`.
2. Following the documented manual installation hop, install 2026.9.8 in the same npm prefix. The CLI and Gateway both report 2026.9.8; Gateway health and Telegram/WhatsApp channel probes pass.
3. From an independent Terminal, stop the managed Gateway, then run `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --json`. Do not manually restart the Gateway before finalization. This pass reaches Doctor, then fails in plugin convergence.
4. `finalize:doctor`: **completed**, 11:13:13–11:14:53 EDT (about 100 seconds). `finalize:plugins`: **failed**, 11:14:53–11:15:04 EDT (about 11 seconds). The Gateway process later started at 11:15:05 EDT, *after* the plugin failure. The previous Gateway shutdown separately recorded `gateway.stop_close_failed`; causality is not established.
5. The final run records `status=failed` and `reason=OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_STORAGE_FAILED`. Package activation remains `prepared`; plugin data/settings upgrades remain unfinished. The serving 2026.9.8 Gateway is healthy after restoration.

Exact sanitized failure:
```text
failed to verify plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global |
OpenClaw state at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance; retry when it finishes.
```

## Expected
The post-Doctor plugin phase should acquire its lifecycle lease after Doctor's offline state maintenance releases ownership (or wait/report the actual owner safely). `update repair` should then settle the pending package operation and plugin migrations without requiring journal/database edits or a repeated CLI loop. If the shutdown-close warning is material, the error should identify that prerequisite distinctly.

Potentially related but not identical: #164066 (activation Doctor offline-maintenance refusal), #161921 (Doctor/plugin convergence cycle), #164074 (retained package fingerprint recovery). This report covers the **post-Doctor `finalize:plugins` lease-storage failure** on the published 2026.9.8 build.

issues.body:
# Bug: Forra provider tool calls fail deterministically — "Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call"

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.9.7 (c074824) — npm install, stable channel, macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), Node v26.10.0
**Provider:** `forra` (models.json, secretref-managed)
**Models affected:** `forra/azure-kimi-k3`, `forra/gpt-5.5` (both fail with the identical error hash)

## Summary

Any agent turn that attempts a tool call fails deterministically with:

```
⚠️ Agent run failed (model: forra/azure-kimi-k3). rawErrorPreview=Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call
rawErrorHash=sha256:d872f1dd4375 providerRuntimeFailureKind=unclassified
```

The user sees only the "[This turn failed before it completed]" notice. Plain text turns (no tools) succeed. Direct shell/exec turns succeed. Turns invoking memory/session recall tools (memory_search, sessions_search) fail 100%.

Same failure signature as #157469 (xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro), but here it affects **both** Forra models with the **same error hash** (`sha256:d872f1dd4375`), suggesting the broken tool-call parse happens in a shared provider-stream path rather than anything model-specific.

## Reproduction rate

Observed 6+ times within 2 hours on 2026-10-03, across two models and multiple sessions of the same agent:

| Time (EDT) | Model | Turn type | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 08:12 | forra/azure-kimi-k3 | memory/session recall | ❌ 3/3 retries failed, same hash |
| 09:33 | forra/azure-kimi-k3 | memory/session recall | ❌ 3/3 retries failed, same hash |
| 09:41 | forra/azure-kimi-k3 | memory/session recall | ❌ failed, same hash |
| 09:43 | forra/gpt-5.5 | memory/session recall | ❌ failed, same hash |
| 09:44 | forra/gpt-5.5 | memory/session recall | ❌ failed, same hash |
| 09:45 | forra/azure-kimi-k3 | tool use | ❌ failed, same hash |

Note: retries produce byte-identical errors (same hash), i.e. deterministic, not transient.

## Evidence

Gateway log excerpts (timestamps EDT, 2026-10-03):

```
09:33:43 embedded run agent end  isError=true model=azure-kimi-k3 provider=forra
  rawErrorPreview="Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call"
  rawErrorHash=sha256:d872f1dd4375 providerRuntimeFailureKind=unclassified
09:33:43 [empty-error-retry] stopReason=error non-visible-output; resubmitting attempt=1/3
09:33:46 embedded run agent end  isError=true (same hash) — attempt 2
09:33:50 embedded run agent end  isError=true (same hash) — attempt 3
09:33:51 message dispatch completed outcome=error duration=24752ms
```

```
09:43:24 embedded run agent end  isError=true model=gpt-5.5 provider=forra
  rawErrorPreview="Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call"
  rawErrorHash=sha256:d872f1dd4375
09:43:25 message dispatch completed outcome=error duration=8660ms
```

Also on every failing run: `[model-fallback] configured fallbacks disabled by user model override` — so the session-pinned model leaves no failover path, and the user gets a hard failure.

## Expected

Tool-call turns parse and execute, or fail over to a fallback model when the provider stream is malformed.

## Workaround in use

Bypassing the failing tool path entirely: answering recall-type questions via direct `exec` against local data (e.g. querying local sqlite databases) instead of memory_search/sessions_search. This works but defeats the memory tooling.

## Related

- #157469 — same error text on xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro under code mode (open, P1)
- #126389 — provider streams can execute malformed terminal tool calls (closed)
- #161072 — broader retry/recovery concerns (open)

issues.title: Feature: `openclaw sessions storage status|run` (expose existing cold-transcript Gateway RPCs)

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:feature
