issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw sessions storage status` and `openclaw sessions storage run` so I can inspect per-agent hot/cold transcript inventory and trigger the existing cold-archive maintenance batch without hand-writing `gateway call` JSON — especially when agent SQLite growth and cold-storage policy need a first-class terminal check.

## Problem

Cold transcript storage already has a supported Gateway contract:

- `sessions.storage.status` (`operator.admin`) — per-agent hot/cold counts, database/WAL/archive byte sizes, and background maintenance status
- `sessions.storage.run` (`operator.admin`) — start or join the existing archival batch; returns promptly; poll status while `maintenance.running`

Docs already describe these RPCs ([session control protocol](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control), [cold transcript storage](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance#cold-transcript-storage)). Operators investigating unbounded `openclaw-agent.sqlite` growth (e.g. #180532, #162319) must either open Control UI paths or compose:

```bash
openclaw gateway call sessions.storage.status --json
openclaw gateway call sessions.storage.run --json
```

`openclaw sessions cleanup` is a different surface (session-store cap/stale cleanup). It does not replace cold-transcript inventory or the archival worker.

## Proposal

Add native CLI verbs that forward the existing Gateway methods only (Alix / #148903 pattern — complete the terminal adapter; no new query engine, schema, permissions, or storage behavior):

```bash
openclaw sessions storage status [--json] [--url ...] [--token ...] [--timeout ...]
openclaw sessions storage run [--json] [--url ...] [--token ...] [--timeout ...]
```

Behavior:

- Call `sessions.storage.status` / `sessions.storage.run` with empty/validated params matching the existing Gateway validators.
- Print the Gateway JSON payload (`--json` or default machine-friendly JSON, consistent with sibling `sessions` RPC-backed commands).
- Exit non-zero on RPC/auth failure; do not invent local aggregation of SQLite files.
- Docs: mention under `docs/cli/sessions.md` next to cleanup / cold-storage notes; point to the existing protocol page.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a running Gateway with `operator.admin`, `openclaw sessions storage status` exits 0 and returns an object with `agents` (per-agent inventory) and `maintenance` (running/idle fields already returned by the RPC).
2. `openclaw sessions storage run` exits 0, returns the same shape, and either starts or joins the existing maintenance owner (idempotent join as today).
3. Without Gateway / without admin scope, the command fails with the same class of error as other admin RPC CLI verbs (no partial local scan that bypasses Gateway auth).
4. Packaged/registered CLI proof: before → missing `storage` subcommand under `sessions`; after → RPC observed with method `sessions.storage.status` / `sessions.storage.run` and successful JSON.
5. Colocated CLI registration test covers forwarding + option plumbing; no production LOC beyond the thin CLI adapter and docs.
6. Explicit non-goals: does not change cold-storage policy, does not replace `sessions cleanup`, does not add new Gateway methods.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
# With a local Gateway already running and admin credentials available to the CLI:
openclaw sessions storage status --json
# expect: agents[].{agentId,hotTranscripts,coldTranscripts,databaseBytes,...}, maintenance.{running,...}

openclaw sessions storage run --json
openclaw sessions storage status --json
# expect: maintenance.running true while the batch is active, then settles

# Wire/parity check (existing escape hatch must keep working):
openclaw gateway call sessions.storage.status --json
```

Independent reread: Command registration + Gateway client request only; canonical inventory/maintenance ownership stays in existing `sessions.storage.*` handlers (`getSessionColdStorageStatus` / `requestGatewaySessionColdStorageMaintenance`).

## Scope / non-goals / related

- Not a duplicate of #178014 / #178015 / #178016 (config export / heartbeat status / config diff).
- Not #154482 permanent MAIN history lifecycle (product policy); this only exposes the already-shipped cold-storage admin RPCs.
- Not changing `session.maintenance.coldStorage.*` defaults.
- Closely analogous to #148903 (`automations runs --all` exposing existing `cron.runs` scope).

Prepared against current `main`. Runtime proof and review will be linked from the implementation PR; no maintainer sponsorship is claimed.

issues.body:
## Requested native behavior

Workboard should reclaim eligible metadata through its native history/attachment custody before refusing a mutation for the 24 KiB card metadata budget. If safe reclamation cannot create enough room, refuse atomically and leave the card unchanged.

## Observed environment and distinction

OpenClaw 2026.9.6 on Linux. Our downstream installation currently has a frozen, version-specific guard that replaces destructive metadata trimming with a WORKBOARD_METADATA_BUDGET refusal. The refusal below describes that guarded installation, not an assertion that unmodified upstream emits this error.

The shipped trimming path removes historical metadata collections under pressure; historical proof durability is already covered by #113309. This request must not reintroduce silent deletion of proofs, attempts, attachments or failure history.

## Small reproduction / acceptance scenario

1. Create an isolated Workboard card whose serialized metadata is just below 24,576 bytes.
2. Include historical text eligible for native archival, plus proof IDs, attempt IDs, dependency conditions and a current owner/claim.
3. Make a bounded unrelated mutation that would otherwise cross the budget, such as a claim or a short comment.
4. Before refusing, preserve the eligible history in durable native attachment/history custody, read it back and match it, then retain a bounded pointer/current-state projection.
5. Commit the requested mutation only if the resulting metadata fits; verify original history is still accessible and all authoritative identities/conditions are unchanged.
6. With no eligible reclaimable history, refuse atomically without losing evidence. A stale concurrent update must also refuse or retry through existing CAS.

## Required preservation

Keep full ordered evidence and attachment content retrievable, retain failures and rework cycles, and preserve active claims, proof/attempt IDs, dependency and owner holds. Do not merely evict canonical proof rows or select the newest contradictory control comment as authority.

## Why upstream

A bundled-dist patch is fragile across upgrades. We are freezing the existing downstream patch, using native notes/attachments and finite card splits for immediate budget pressure, and seeking a maintained native archive/evict-before-refuse path instead of extending the patch or raising the budget.

Related: #113309 (historical proof durability) and #143842 (no-start dispatch metadata churn). This request is specifically for safe admission under metadata pressure, rather than an unrestricted eviction policy.

issues.body:
### Summary
On an ordinary (non-compaction) inbound channel message, when every auth profile for the **primary** model's provider is in cooldown, the reply-resolver pre-flight auth check rejects with a plain `Auth profile ... is temporarily unavailable` error **before a turn is created**. That rejection is never handed to the cross-provider model-fallback runner, so a **configured and healthy fallback model is never attempted**. The ingress retry layer then retries the same cooled-down primary 8× and dead-letters the message with no reply. Cron jobs on the *identical* config fall back correctly, because they route through `embedded-agent` / `model-fallback-runner`.

### Version
OpenClaw **2026.9.7** (also present on 2026.9.4 — not introduced or fixed by that update).

### Config (already correct per docs)
```
agents.defaults.model:
  primary:   openai/gpt-5.6-terra
  fallbacks: [anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, cursor-cli/composer-2.5]
```
The `main` agent (handles Discord) has **no model override** — it inherits `agents.defaults.model` cleanly, identical to what cron uses. There is no missing `fallbacks:` array and no channel/agent setting to flip; the gap is in code, not config.

### Expected behavior
Per `concepts/model-failover` ("Which errors advance fallback → Continues on: auth failures"; "all profiles in cooldown" = exhausted profile rotation → advance to next model in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`), an inbound channel message whose primary provider is all-cooled should advance to the configured fallback and reply.

### Actual behavior
Reply-resolver pre-flight rejects before any fallback attempt; 8 identical retries against the same cooled-down primary; dead-letter; no reply ever sent. No `model_fallback_decision` event appears in the trace.

### Failure path (source trace, 2026.9.7 dist)
1. Inbound message dispatches through the reply-resolver (logged `source=replyResolver`).
2. `selectProviderModelAuthSources()` (`provider-model-route-auth-*.mjs`) returns a `rejected` disposition with `kind="all-cooldown"`: `Auth profile "<id>" is temporarily unavailable for <provider>.` This function's own `fallback` field is **same-provider only** (an alternate credential) — structurally unaware of `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`.
3. That rejection surfaces as a **dispatch-level error** (~150–250 ms, no network round-trip) rather than being handed to `model-fallback-runner-*.mjs` (the cross-provider engine used by `embedded-agent-*.mjs`, which cron turns reach and which emits `model_fallback_decision`).
4. The generic ingress layer (`ingress-drain-*.mjs` / `src/channels/message/ingress-retry-policy.ts`) has only two outcomes — `release` (retry same call) or `fail` (dead-letter after `maxAttempts=8`). It has no "try a different model" outcome.
5. Result: 8 identical retries against the same cooled-down primary, zero attempts against the configured fallback, then `reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered`.

### Why cron works but channels don't (identical config)
A cron job's `payload.model` is a distinct selection source that explicitly inherits `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` and runs through `embedded-agent`/`model-fallback-runner`. The channel reply path's pre-flight auth-profile check short-circuits before that runner is ever invoked.

### Logs
```
message dispatch completed: ... source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=246ms
  error="Error: Auth profile \"<id>\" is temporarily unavailable for openai/gpt-5.6-terra."
discord ingress: spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry: Auth profile ... (×7 more, same error, same model)
discord ingress: spooled update <id> on lane channel:<id> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered
```
(No `model_fallback_decision` event anywhere in the trace for these messages.)

### Recurrence
4 confirmed dead-lettered Discord events over 12 days, same `retry-limit-exceeded` reason each time.

### Relationship to existing issues
- **#1522** (closed/fixed): added `FailoverError` on all-cooldown in the **embedded runner** — but the channel reply pre-flight rejects *before* reaching the embedded runner, so that fix does not cover this path.
- **#150388 / PR #150400**: same dead-letter-on-preflight mechanism, but scoped to the **compaction** auth-planning path. This report is the **ordinary (non-compaction) reply path** with a healthy configured cross-provider fallback.

### Suggested fix direction
Either (a) have the channel reply dispatch pre-flight consult `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` before rejecting, or (b) route channel replies through the same `embedded-agent`/`model-fallback-runner` entry point cron uses, so the documented "auth failures advance fallback" behavior applies to channels too.

### Environment
macOS; Homebrew install; gateway + CLI 2026.9.7.

## Summary
Please let Workboard remember its search and filter selections across a browser reload or a later visit in the same browser.

## Current behavior and evidence
Source/build inspection on OpenClaw 2026.9.7 and current upstream main on 2026-10-01 shows search and status/priority/attention/archive/completion-period filters held in in-memory Workboard state. A fresh state starts with an empty query and default filters. This is source-only validation, not an interactive browser reproduction.

The relevant owner is [runtime.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/98d3fdae44490b268f536a14f5f9a14de2112f62/extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/runtime.ts#L105-L174); the [plugin activation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/98d3fdae44490b268f536a14f5f9a14de2112f62/extensions/workboard/browser/index.ts) creates the shared capability. Same-app navigation can retain that live state; this request specifically concerns reload/new activation, not a claim that every navigation resets it.

## Synthetic reproduction to verify
1. Open Workboard with ordinary synthetic cards.
2. Search for `sample` and select a status or priority filter.
3. Reload the page and reopen the same board.
4. Compare the search and filter selections with those before reload.

Expected: restore the chosen presentation filters, with visible active chips and a reliable Clear filters action. Current initialization returns the empty/default filter state. No card data should change.

## Scope
A per-browser, gateway-scoped preference (or documented URL state) would avoid repeatedly reconstructing a view. Please keep canonical board routing and shared agent scope authoritative; do not add board orchestration fields or a per-board default agent override. Search-query persistence and its privacy/lifetime policy need an explicit choice.

- #162850 requests an exact label selector, not persistence.
- #119531 concerned a per-board default agent view and was declined; this request does not seek that override.
- #153447 proposed layout/density persistence but is closed without merge, and does not supply search/filter persistence.

Searched open and closed Workboard issues/PRs for filter persistence, reload/reset, remember, and search persistence; no exact duplicate found.

## PR
A bounded implementation can be prepared after the preference owner and lifetime are agreed. No PR opened yet.

issues.body:
### Summary

Opt-in load-time check that recomputes an installed plugin's payload digest and compares it against the integrity pinned in its install record, refusing (or warning on) load when they diverge.

### Problem to solve

Install records already pin a registry integrity hash for npm/ClawHub installs (`PluginInstallRecord.integrity`, resolved at install and preserved across updates). Today that pin is only audited for *presence* — doctor reports `plugins.installs_missing_integrity` — and compared against the registry during install/update flows. Nothing at startup or module load re-reads the on-disk payload and compares it to the pin.

The load path does two other checks, but neither is anchored to the pin:

- the static payload smoke check (`src/plugins/payload-verification.ts`) verifies payload presence and manifest structure, not content hashes;
- the generation-receipt comparison (`src/plugins/loader-module-runtime.ts`, `expectedSourceDigests`) compares against a digest captured by a *previous load in the same process generation*, so a fresh process start has no anchor — the first load after an at-rest payload swap is unverified.

Net effect: a plugin payload that is substituted or tampered on disk after install loads silently on the next gateway start, and the pinned integrity value is never consulted.

### Proposed solution

A config-gated check, e.g. `plugins.load.integrity: "enforce" | "warn" | "off"` (default `off` or `warn` so current behavior is unchanged), that at plugin load:

1. recomputes a digest of the installed payload with the algorithm recorded at install time (sha512/256 per registry metadata);
2. compares it to `PluginInstallRecord.integrity`;
3. on mismatch, refuses to load (or warns) and records a structured rejection — `{ pluginId, expected, actual, decision, timestamp }` — persisted so it survives restarts, surfaces in `doctor`, and the recovery path stays the usual `plugins update`.

Bundled and source-checkout plugins skip the check since they carry no registry pin, mirroring how the existing smoke check excludes them.

### Alternatives considered

- Extending the generation-receipt sourceDigest check: it detects changes *between* loads within one process, but the initial anchor is whatever was loaded before, so a tampered-at-rest payload passes its first post-tamper load.
- Doctor-only verification: doctor is manual/periodic and today only checks that the pin exists, never that disk content matches it.

### Impact

- Affected: operators running npm/ClawHub-installed plugins on shared or externally reachable machines.
- Severity: high — substituted plugin code runs with the host's full capability surface (channels, tools, credentials).
- Frequency: rare per machine, but silent when hit; update-flow drift checks only catch swaps that coincide with an update, not at-rest tampering between updates.
- Consequence: no signal at load, no persisted record, and recovery depends on someone noticing misbehavior rather than the loader refusing the plugin.

### Evidence/examples

On current `main`: install writes `integrity` into the record (`src/plugins/install-*`); `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts` audits only that the pin exists; load-time content checks are the structural smoke check (`src/plugins/payload-verification.ts`) and in-session receipt digests (`src/plugins/loader-module-runtime.ts`); npm registry integrity resolution (`src/infra/npm-integrity.ts`) is consumed only by install/update paths.

### Additional information

Happy to implement behind the default-off flag with regression tests (mismatched payload rejected and recorded, matching payload loads unchanged, bundled plugins unaffected) if maintainers want the loader boundary hardened this way.

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

After upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.9.8, the Gateway starts initialization but consistently exits during sessions.projection with:

Gateway failed to start: Shared-state reader requires a captured state location and read command.

### Steps to reproduce

Run OpenClaw 2026.9.8 on the affected system.
Start the Gateway.
Observe that initialization proceeds through HTTP/health startup.
The Gateway then fails during session projection and shuts down.
Systemd subsequently retries the service until the restart-loop breaker is reached.

### Expected behavior

The Gateway should complete startup and remain running, as it did on earlier OpenClaw versions.

### Actual behavior

Gateway failed to start: Shared-state reader requires a captured state location and read command.

The diagnostic bundle identifies the failure during:

sessions.projection

followed by gateway.request-runtime.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

### Operating system

Fedora 44 x86_64

### Install method

OpenClaw npm installation using the OpenClaw-managed Node runtime

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> ollama (local Ollama HTTP service)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Ollama is running locally as a system service on 127.0.0.1:11434.

The failure occurs during Gateway startup before model execution, so the configured model/provider does not appear to be involved in the immediate failure.

### Logs

```shell
Error: Shared-state reader requires a captured state location and read command
    at createError (.../openclaw-state-worker-error-CvUWzlTD.mjs:197:24)
    at Array.map (...)
    at decodeErrorGraph (.../openclaw-state-worker-error-CvUWzlTD.mjs:344:24)
    at add (.../openclaw-state-worker-error-CvUWzlTD.mjs:407:64)
    at hydrateOpenClawStateWorkerError (.../openclaw-state-worker-error-CvUWzlTD.mjs:420:15)
    at decodeTaskReply (.../openclaw-state-read-worker-N851KEmP.mjs:282:10)
    at run (.../openclaw-state-read-worker-N851KEmP.mjs:332:14)
    at async Object.read (.../openclaw-state-read-worker-N851KEmP.mjs:350:24)
    at async read (.../openclaw-state-db-readonly-DE3MB0wy.mjs:492:20)
    at async run (.../openclaw-state-db-readonly-DE3MB0wy.mjs:515:13)

The Gateway log sequence immediately before the failure includes successful config/auth initialization, Gateway startup, spawn broker initialization, HTTP server startup, and health-monitor startup, followed by the session projection failure and shutdown.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The shipped 2026.9.8 worker implementation explicitly raises this error when isReadRequest(input) rejects the worker request.

I also verified that the OpenClaw state-directory resolver itself returns the expected state directory (~/.openclaw), so an unset shell OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR is not the cause.

The error is therefore occurring at worker request validation before the SQLite read is performed.

No session databases or session history have been deleted, rebuilt, or reset during diagnosis.

The failure appeared after upgrading into the recent 2026.9.x series; 2026.9.8 is the currently failing version.

issues.body:
### Summary

On the **2026.7.x LTS line** (Windows, local Gateway), a message typed into the Control UI composer **while a turn is running** stays pinned in the composer queue as **"Queued (1)"** and is never delivered. The gateway is healthy and reports an **empty queue (`depth 0`)** for the same session. A page reload (F5) clears the pinned row, and the message is delivered afterwards.

Filed as a focused report **at the request of @azuretek** in #158190 — that issue tracks a different mechanism (a pane composer restore copying the stored `waiting-reconnect` alias into the visible queue); none of those attributes are present in our run.

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.7.35 (aa94808)** — npm global install
- OS: Windows 10.0.26300 (x64), Node **v24.16.0**
- Gateway: **local** (same host); UI: Control UI (webchat), desktop browser
- Queue mode: default (`steer`) at first observation; the mode was changed to `followup` later during investigation — the symptom was reproduced on both
- First observed: 2026-09-29 (evening); still reproducible on 2026-09-30

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a turn that takes a while (long tool run).
2. While it is still running, type a message into the composer and send it.
3. The message shows up pinned as **"Queued (1)"** and stays there.
4. `session_status` for the **same** session reports **`Queue: (depth 0)`** — the gateway does not have it pending.
5. There is **no** "Waiting for reconnect" label, and no "Reconnected before delivery was confirmed" copy; the pane is **never** re-shown / split / docked.
6. Reload (F5): the pinned row disappears and the message is delivered.

### Evidence

- **`inputReceipts` is not available on this line.** On 2026.7.35, `chat.history` returns only `sessionKey, sessionId, messages, defaults, sessionInfo, thinkingLevel` — so the pending-input receipt cannot be inspected here. (Confirmed as a 9.x-era field by @azuretek in #158190; our field list matched.)
- **Socket closes do not correlate with the stall.** In a 13-hour capture there were **17 `close` events** (`code=1012 / 1006 / 1001`), all attributable to our own gateway restarts / browser navigation — none of them at the time the row was pinned.
- **Pane state:** unchanged (single, live pane; no re-show/split/dock).
- **The core contrast:** the row is pinned in the composer queue **while** the gateway reports `Queue: (depth 0)` for the same session.

### Relation to other issues

- **#109040** — *"webchat: queued message stays in 'Queued (1)' and is never delivered after turn completes"* (2026.7.1, `steer`): the **same profile**. It is closed (2026-07-28) and its timeline carries **no linked fix PR**, so it is unclear which change, if any, was meant to reach the 7.x line.
- **#158190** — different mechanism (the reconnect/restore path). Our run lacks all of its attributes: no reconnect label, no pane restore, depth 0 rather than a blocked queue.
- **PR #158432** — the restore fix for #158190; it does not address this symptom.

### Questions

1. Which change (if any) was intended to reach the **7.x line** for #109040 — and **is it present in 2026.7.35**?
2. Is a fix planned for the **2026.7.x LTS line** at all, or is this only addressed on `main` (9.x)?
3. Is there a supported way on 7.35 to **reset the pinned composer row without a full page reload** (a workaround we can use in production until a fix lands)?

---

*Reported on behalf of a production user of the LTS line. We are happy to run any diagnostic you need on 2026.7.35 — e.g. `openclaw gateway call ...` or additional client-side captures — just say which method/output would be most useful.*

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow native feature plugins to register a collapsible parent navigation item with child page links in the Control UI's main left sidebar.

### Problem to solve

A feature plugin with several pages currently has two practical choices: add multiple flat sidebar entries, or provide its own navigation inside the page. The latter puts a horizontal navigation bar across the working area and separates plugin navigation from the host sidebar.

The public `ControlUiNavigationItem` contract exposes `id`, `label`, `page`, `icon`, `order` and `defaultVisible`, but no parent/child relationship. This was checked against OpenClaw 2026.9.6 source and current main on 1 October 2026.

A native way to group a plugin's pages would keep the sidebar compact and make multi-page feature plugins easier to navigate.

### Proposed solution

Extend the native Control UI navigation contribution API to support one level of child links under a plugin-owned parent. The exact API shape is open to maintainer guidance.

For example:

```text
Home
Agents
Plugins
Publishing
    Overview
    Content
    Board
    Calendar
    Review
    Distribution
    Analytics
    Profiles
    Authors
    Settings
Sessions
    ...
```

Suggested behaviour:

- A parent can have an optional landing page and a separate expand/collapse control.
- Children use existing native page targets and URL helpers.
- Opening a child reveals the group and highlights that child; the parent indicates that its section is active.
- Current-page matching can distinguish section parameters while ignoring unrelated filter or item-detail parameters.
- Expansion state uses the host's existing browser/Gateway preference scope.
- The group occupies one position in sidebar ordering and pinning. Child entries are not duplicated at the top level.
- Existing flat navigation registrations continue to work unchanged.
- Registration ownership, disposal and plugin reload remove or replace the complete group cleanly.
- Navigation uses semantic links and an accessible disclosure button, with keyboard operation, visible focus and usable collapsed-sidebar behaviour.
- Page changes preserve native links, modifier clicks, deep links and Back/Forward. Integration should also respect any page leave/unsaved-edit guard.

This should be an extension to the existing navigation surface; plugins should not need to replace the workspace or manipulate host DOM to express a page hierarchy.

### Alternatives considered

- Flat sidebar entries work today but make the main sidebar longer and do not express which pages belong to one plugin.
- A horizontal or vertical menu inside the plugin page keeps the implementation local, but consumes working space and creates a second navigation location.
- A workspace replacement has a much larger maintenance surface for this small navigation requirement.
- A downstream Control UI patch can bridge the gap, but requires ongoing compatibility testing against host releases.

### Impact

- **Affected:** Operators and authors of native feature plugins with multiple pages.
- **Severity:** Usability limitation; existing workflows remain available.
- **Frequency:** Every time a user switches between plugin pages.
- **Consequence:** Fragmented navigation, extra sidebar entries or duplicated in-page navigation, and custom shell maintenance for plugin authors who need hierarchy.

### Evidence/examples

- [Navigation SDK source at the inspected 2026.9.6 UI commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b/src/plugin-sdk/control-ui.ts).
- [Native navigation contribution renderer at that commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b/ui/src/plugins/control-ui-view.runtime.ts).
- [Feature plugin documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/feature-plugins).
- [W3C disclosure navigation guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/).

Related: #137107 requests nested groups for sessions/projects. This request concerns developer-registered plugin page navigation in the main sidebar, which is a separate contribution surface.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

### Additional information

A backward-compatible, one-level hierarchy would meet this use case. Arbitrary-depth trees, session organisation and a new routing system are not needed. Feedback on the preferred contribution contract would help avoid maintaining an incompatible downstream extension.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two related delivery-reliability defects observed in production, discovered while auditing a channel's ingress dead-letter queue and the subagent task backlog.

### 1. Swallowed subagent completion delivery

Subagent tasks can finish with status "succeeded" (all tool work completed, including cases where the deliverable was written to disk and the run produced a full progress summary) but the completion never reaches the requester. Two real examples from `openclaw tasks list --status blocked --json`:

- A subagent completed a multi-step repair, saved its report to disk, and returned a detailed progress summary — but deliveryStatus was "not_applicable" with error "prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for \<agent\>". The requester received nothing and had no way to know the work had finished.
- A separate subagent run returned deliveryStatus "delivered" yet was still classified terminalOutcome "blocked" with terminalSummary "Required completion did not produce a final deliverable." — an inconsistent combination (delivered + blocked) that makes it unclear whether the requester actually got the result.

In both cases the only visibility into the failure is `openclaw tasks list --status blocked`; nothing proactively surfaces these to the requester or logs them as user-facing errors. A requester has no signal that a task they dispatched silently stalled at the delivery layer rather than failing outright.

### 2. Payload-less channel ingress dead-letters

`openclaw channels dead-letters list` can return dead-lettered events with no payload field at all (reason: handler-timeout), alongside other entries for the same lane that do retain a full payload. When the payload is missing, resubmit has nothing to re-enqueue — the CLI's own error path ("has no retained payload and cannot be resubmitted") confirms this is a known, unrecoverable state, but nothing distinguishes why some failures retain payload and others don't, and there's no telemetry counter/alert surfaced for "dead-lettered with no recoverable payload" vs "dead-lettered but resubmittable".

### Impact

- Users cannot tell, from the outside, whether a dispatched subagent task's result was actually delivered, silently dropped at the delivery layer, or is sitting in a blocked state waiting on manual tasks retry/dismiss.
- Some ingress dead-letters are permanently unrecoverable (no payload) with no distinguishing signal, so operators can't tell resubmittable failures from truly-lost events without manually reading each entry.

### Suggested improvements

1. Treat "delivered" and "blocked" as mutually exclusive terminal states, or add a distinct state (e.g. delivery_ambiguous) when they disagree.
2. Surface a proactive notification/log line when deliveryStatus resolves to not_applicable/failed for a completed task, rather than requiring an operator to run tasks audit / tasks list --status blocked.
3. Add a payload_present boolean (or similar) field plus a counter/metric on channel ingress dead-letters so payload-less (permanently unrecoverable) failures are distinguishable from resubmittable ones at a glance.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6
- macOS 26.7 (arm64)
- Observed via `openclaw channels dead-letters list --json` and `openclaw tasks list --status blocked --json`

No private payload content, tokens, internal identifiers, or vendor source files are included in this report — only field names, states, and generic reason strings.

issues.body:
Found while investigating why three months of scheduled-job failure alerts never arrived. Observed in 2026.4.26, the version we run. The same code path is present in 2026.8.1 — read, not run.
Summary
When a scheduled job's `failureAlert` names `channel: "webchat"`, OpenClaw drops that channel without a warning, falls back to the last-used or single configured channel, and sends the message there with the original recipient string unchanged. The recipient means nothing in the fallback channel, so the send fails — and the error names only the fallback channel, never the substitution or the channel that was actually requested.
A configuration mistake becomes invisible at configuration time, at send time, and afterwards.
Why this may be worth your time
The area around this path has been hardened twice since 2026.4.26, and neither guard covers this case. In `2026.8.1`:

* a failed target lookup on the fallback channel is now fatal rather than falling back to the raw value — but it does not fire here, because the Slack resolver runs with `unknownTargetMode: "normalized"` and Slack declares no reserved literals, so an unrecognised name passes the lookup as `ok`;
* a new guard refuses implicit isolated cron delivery — but it fires only when no destination is given at all, and here one was given explicitly.

So the intent to catch bad destinations is clearly there. The gap is specifically the case where the caller named a channel and that channel cannot deliver.
And in 2026.8.1 the failure mode gets quieter, not louder. Because the fallback now resolves the name against the Slack directory, a recipient string that happens to match a real Slack channel would be delivered to it. Today the mistake at least produces `channel_not_found`. With a coincidental name collision it would deliver to the wrong place and say nothing.
Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a scheduled job with a failure alert addressed to the webchat channel:

```json
"failureAlert": { "channel": "webchat", "to": "<any-webchat-target>" }
```

2. Configure exactly one real delivery channel — in our case Slack.
3. Cause the job to fail.

What happens
`webchat` does not pass `isNormalizedMessageChannel`, so the requested channel resolves to `undefined`. The session has no last-used channel, so resolution falls through to the single configured channel, Slack. The `to` value is passed through verbatim. Slack returns `channel_not_found`, because the string was never a Slack identifier and was never meant to be one.
In `2026.4.26` the same thing happens through `isDeliverableMessageChannel`; the gate was renamed and reworked, the outcome did not change.
What we expected
Either the send fails immediately with an error naming the requested channel as undeliverable, or the fallback happens and says so, resolving the recipient for the channel it is actually sending to.
What it cost us
Twelve failure alerts queued over two days, none delivered; a thirteenth silently expired into the failed queue months earlier; three months in which the mechanism that reports a broken automation could not report anything. Found only because a gateway restart happened to print a recovery line while someone was reading the log for an unrelated reason.
Anyone who configures a webchat destination — reasonably, since the product presents a web panel — gets a system that looks configured and delivers nothing.
Suggested fix, in order of preference

1. Do not fall back from an explicitly requested channel. If the caller named a channel and it cannot deliver, fail with an error naming that channel. Implicit resolution, where no channel was specified, can keep falling back as it does today. This is the one that makes the class of mistake impossible rather than merely visible.
2. If the fallback is kept, do not carry the recipient across. An address is channel-scoped. Passing it verbatim guarantees a confusing downstream error — or, worse, a silent delivery to a coincidentally matching target.
3. Reject a non-delivering channel at configuration load. For a failure alert, the moment it fails is the worst possible moment to discover it.
4. Log the substitution at warning level, naming both the requested and the actual channel.

Notes

issues.body:
# [Draft] blocked_tool_call wedges the session queue: recovery=none, new messages pile up, only an app restart unblocks

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (also observed on 2026.9.4), macOS arm64, embedded agent (webchat dashboard session).

## Summary
When a session's in-flight tool call blocks, the stalled-session diagnostic flags it (`reason=blocked_tool_call`) but `recovery=none`. The tool call never completes, the session's queue wedges (`queueDepth` grows), **all new inbound messages are queued and never processed**, and the only way out is restarting the app/gateway. This is a session-availability deadlock, not a cosmetic stall.

## Evidence (gateway.log, 2026-10-01 01:09–01:11)
```
stalled session: sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:... state=processing age=484s queueDepth=0 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:exec:started lastProgressAge=177s activeTool=exec activeToolCallId=exec_232_dd2c71ee activeToolAge=177s lastAssistant="..." recovery=none
stalled session: ... state=idle age=207s queueDepth=1 reason=blocked_tool_call ... recovery=none
stalled session: ... state=idle age=237s queueDepth=1 reason=blocked_tool_call ... recovery=none
```
The tool call (`exec`) sat in `started` for 177–237s+ with no completion; `queueDepth` went 0→1 (messages piling up, unprocessed); `recovery=none`. The user had to restart the app to unblock the session. The in-flight call that blocked was an ordinary `exec` that had effectively completed on the model side (the reply had already streamed) — the runtime nonetheless wedged the queue.

## Impact
A single blocked tool call silently deadlocks the session's inbound queue. No timeout, no auto-recovery, no surface that the session is wedged except an eventually-stalled diagnostic. From the user's perspective the assistant "hangs" and stops responding until a manual restart.

## Ask
1. A recovery path for `blocked_tool_call` that unblocks the session queue without a restart: e.g. a deadline (`activeToolDeadlineAtMs`) after which the call is abandoned and the queue is released, or an explicit operator/auto "release queue" action.
2. The stalled-session diagnostic should be actionable (not just `recovery=none`) — at minimum a logged, recommended remediation, ideally an automatic one.
Related to our earlier report on recovery-limit / transcript persistence.

## Context
Follow-up to #138316 and #147283. The PR is limited to CLI cron Telegram-topic routing; durable source-generation fencing and downgrade are separate work.

## Design and compatibility
Bind a delayed completion to its exact source generation and resolved channel/account/recipient/thread. Enforce authorization before final transport effect, including recovery. Another process can change SQLite source ownership during an awaited dispatch; snapshots alone are insufficient. Use a nonblocking mechanism with cross-process invalidation or justify and measure a safe alternative. Reject plugin-supplied authority and fail closed on unavailable source facts.
Decide whether older binaries may run after new fenced queue rows exist: require owner-approved drain/reconcile procedure or compatible migration. Demonstrate published-version queue writer to candidate reader and explicit rollback behavior.

## Acceptance evidence
- Tests: correct Telegram group/topic/account and nearest wrong target, source reassignment during await, foreign SQLite commit before final I/O, direct and recovered channel rejection, fail-closed behavior.
- Upgrade fixture: actual queued rows from published driver recovered by candidate, legacy and fenced cases where supported.
- Real configured Telegram Test Server topic send and negative transport cases, redacted proof; spies alone insufficient.
- Focused/static/type/exact-head CI checks and event-loop throughput review.

Historical design and tests from #147283 may inform this work; no experimental queue contract is declared ready.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Preview, compaction can mark a check that already ran and returned a negative result as unfinished work. In the reproduction below, `verify()` reports missing release approval, but the summary puts “Release approval verification” under **In Progress** and says to check approval again.

This report concerns incorrect task state in the summary. Repeated tool calls are a separate observation; the tests do not establish that compaction caused them.

### Steps to reproduce

Use source commit `61732a9a36a510b175905f25393ca5bd5728f4e9` and the default `generateSummary` update path. The model output is nondeterministic; repeat the fixture 10 times. The standalone script below supplies these exact inputs:

1. Previous summary:
   ```text
   Owner: Maya. Launch date: October 8. Verification: pending. The launch preparation is not finished.
   ```
2. New user message:
   ```text
   Correction to the facts: the confirmed launch date is October 15, not October 8. Maya is still the owner. This date is already decided; no date-editing task is pending. Separately, check whether the release is approved.
   ```
3. Assistant tool call: `verify({})`, followed by its tool result (`isError: true`):
   ```text
   Verification FAILED: missing release approval.
   ```
4. Generate the updated summary before adding any final assistant answer. Inspect **Done**, **In Progress**, and **Next Steps**.

Maya and the dates are fictional fixture context. In the supplied transcript, the check has executed; missing approval is its finding. The user's answer is still owed.

### Expected behavior

Record the check as completed with its negative result, retain missing approval as the blocker, and retain the response still owed. Do not describe the check itself as unperformed. A new check after approval changes is legitimate.

Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra produced the expected check-state distinction in all 10 default-format trials each. No-execution and service-unavailable controls establish the other side: when the check did not run, it must remain unresolved.

### Actual behavior

Excerpt from the first baseline Nemotron output:

```text
### In Progress
- [ ] Release approval verification

### Blocked
- Verification FAILED: missing release approval

## Next Steps
1. Check whether the release is approved.
```

The same summary preserves the executed result under Critical Context. The inconsistency is task status, not simply loss of the error text.

Default-format summary-state defects, 10 trials per model per condition:

| Model | Original instructions | Partial prompt change in #161293 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Preview | 9/10 | 3/10 |
| Kimi K2.6 | 2/10 | 0/10 |
| Qwen3.8 Flash Next | 1/10 | 2/10 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 0/10 | 0/10 |
| GPT-6 Astra | 0/10 | 0/10 |

Counts include contradictory completed/pending labels, not only explicit rerun instructions. These are small synthetic samples, not general reliability estimates; Qwen's counts do not establish a statistically reliable regression.

### What I tried; what works and what does not

- **Explicit completed-check instructions (#161293):** the default-format results are above. The safeguard component fixture improved too, but still had mixed Nemotron status in 2/10 patched outputs. The patch is incomplete.
- **Longer instructions and examples:** a shared rule replacing the format-specific rules still reopened completed checks; revised format-specific rules had four clear errors in 10 Nemotron probes. I discarded those changes.
- **Controls:** never-run and service-unavailable cases correctly retained unexecuted status in 10 native cases each. Ten changed-approval cases allowed legitimate rechecks. A fix must preserve these distinctions; suppressing all repeat calls would be incorrect. Successful-check controls still exposed summary inconsistencies, so the broader suite was not a clean pass.

<details>
<summary>Native save/reopen/resume follow-up and its limits</summary>

On the partial-patch head, a different explicit-report fixture produced 20 saved summaries that all retained the failed result, blocker, and report still owed. None clearly instructed an unconditional rerun; one Qwen summary had stale contradictory wording. Yet 13 continuations checked again. Nemotron also checked again with the original tool result retained. This does not establish compaction-caused loops, and these results must not be pooled with the component A/B.

This follow-up used native SDK sessions and verified unchanged summaries after SQLite close/reopen. It forced verification history across the summary boundary with `keepRecentTokens: 0` and safeguard `recentTurnsPreserve: 0`. Default safeguard retention is three recent user turns, plus tool-failure receipts; the follow-up is a stress fixture.

</details>

### OpenClaw version

Source baseline: `61732a9a36a510b175905f25393ca5bd5728f4e9` (package version `2026.9.6`). Partial-patch/native follow-up: `58c9ba46ed2da971af498f57c62a6ed72019c52c`. Tested September 29; standalone snippet checked September 30. Current `main` has not been retested.

### Operating system / install method

macOS 26.7 (25G229), Node v24.19.0, pnpm source checkout. Component tests import the native summary generator and OpenAI-compatible provider adapter; the follow-up uses native SDK sessions.

### Model / provider routing

OpenClaw → OpenAI-compatible adapter → `https://inference-api.nvidia.com/v1`; thinking off, no fixed seed. Exact model IDs:

```text
nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-preview
nvidia/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
nvidia/qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next
azure/anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
openai/openai/gpt-6-astra
```

### Impact and severity

Intermittent incorrect compaction state in these controlled tests, most frequent with Nemotron. The checkpoint can tell the continuing agent that completed work is still pending. No production outage, data loss, or compaction-caused loop was established.

### Additional information

Related partial mitigation: #161293, submitted for maintainer review of the measured summary improvement. It does not resolve all summary-state errors or establish that repeated tool calls are prevented. Keep this issue open if that PR merges: it tracks the remaining compatibility problem. A complete fix should preserve execution status, the result, and the reply still owed. `isError: true` alone does not distinguish a completed negative check from a service failure preventing execution.

API errors were excluded and preserved separately: one Qwen HTTP 503 in the component A/B and three API errors in native controls, each separately replaced. Semantic failures were not retried.

<details>
<summary>Standalone component reproduction (JavaScript)</summary>

In a source checkout at one of the tested commits, install dependencies normally and save this as `repro-compaction.mjs`. With credentials for the NVIDIA route in `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, run from the checkout root:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./repro-compaction.mjs > compaction-results.jsonl
```

Defaults to 10 independent Nemotron calls. `MODEL` selects another exact model ID above. `FORMAT=safeguard` uses the native safeguard instruction builder, not the full registered safeguard hook. The script prepares a synthetic transcript and exercises real native summary generation; it does not execute `verify()` or simulate a Gateway session.

```js
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

// Run from the root of an OpenClaw source checkout with dependencies installed.
const load = relative => import(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(relative)).href);
const { generateSummary } = await load("packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts");
const { streamSimpleOpenAICompletions } = await load("packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts");
const key = process.env.NVIDIA_API_KEY;
if (!key) throw new Error("Set NVIDIA_API_KEY for the NVIDIA inference route.");
const model = {
  id: process.env.MODEL ?? "nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-preview",
  name: "compaction-repro", api: "openai-completions", provider: "nvidia-coopt",
  baseUrl: "https://inference-api.nvidia.com/v1", reasoning: true, input: ["text"],
  contextWindow: 131072, maxTokens: 16384,
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
};
const usage = {
  input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, totalTokens: 0,
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0 },
};
const previous = "Owner: Maya. Launch date: October 8. Verification: pending. The launch preparation is not finished.";
const messages = [
  {
    role: "user", timestamp: 1,
    content: "Correction to the facts: the confirmed launch date is October 15, not October 8. Maya is still the owner. This date is already decided; no date-editing task is pending. Separately, check whether the release is approved.",
  },
  {
    role: "assistant", timestamp: 2, api: model.api, provider: model.provider,
    model: model.id, usage, stopReason: "toolUse",
    content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "verify_1", name: "verify", arguments: {} }],
  },
  {
    role: "toolResult", timestamp: 3, toolCallId: "verify_1", toolName: "verify",
    isError: true,
    content: [{ type: "text", text: "Verification FAILED: missing release approval." }],
  },
];
let summaryPrompt;
if (process.env.FORMAT === "safeguard") {
  const { buildCompactionStructureInstructions } = await load("src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts");
  summaryPrompt = { kind: "custom", instructions: buildCompactionStructureInstructions() };
}
const repetitions = Number(process.env.REPETITIONS ?? 10);
if (!Number.isInteger(repetitions) || repetitions < 1) throw new Error("REPETITIONS must be a positive integer");
for (let run = 1; run <= repetitions; run++) {
  const result = await generateSummary(
    messages, model, 20480, key, undefined, AbortSignal.timeout(180000),
    undefined, previous, "off", streamSimpleOpenAICompletions, undefined, summaryPrompt,
  );
  if (!result.ok) throw new Error(String(result.error?.message ?? result.error).replaceAll(key, "<redacted>"));
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ run, model: model.id, format: process.env.FORMAT ?? "default", summary: result.value.replaceAll(key, "<redacted>") }));
}
```

</details>

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## U-1 Startup error names `doctor --fix`, but `--fix` doesn't run the session-sqlite import

**Observed**: gateway start fails with `Legacy session store requires migration: ... Run "openclaw doctor --fix" ...`. Running exactly that completes successfully ("Doctor complete") **without** performing the session migration; start fails again identically. The working command is `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite import --session-sqlite-all-agents` (confirmed in #134896 / #135038).
**Suggestion**: either include the session-sqlite import in default `doctor --fix`, or change the startup error text to name the exact subcommand. The current message sends users down a verified dead end.

## U-2 Preflight validates retired config keys before startup self-heal can migrate them

**Observed**: embedders/launchers that run `openclaw config validate` (or equivalent) before `gateway run` hard-fail on retired keys (e.g. `gateway.controlUi.allowInsecureAuth`), even though gateway startup would auto-migrate them. Result: any launcher-side preflight makes upgrades unbootable.
**Suggestion**: give retired keys a "auto-fixable" severity in the validator (exit 0 with warnings), or expose `--migrate-retired-keys` so launchers can heal before validating.

## U-3 `proxy_attribution_required`: document the same-host proxy escape hatch

**Observed**: a same-host launcher proxying over loopback (itself behind a unix-socket frontend that supplies no XFF) cannot satisfy attribution either way: `trustedProxies=[]` fails on "untrusted peer + forwarded headers"; `trustedProxies=[127.0.0.1]` fails because the XFF chain is loopback-only. The working fix is **stripping all forwarded headers** so traffic classifies as `direct-local` — but the guidance text only mentions "configure trustedProxies narrowly / overwrite or safely rebuild headers", which cannot succeed when no real client IP exists anywhere in the chain.
**Suggestion**: extend `PROXY_ATTRIBUTION_GUIDANCE` and the gateway security docs with the same-host recipe: *if the proxy and gateway share a host, prefer sending no forwarded headers at all (direct-local), since attribution by design requires a non-loopback client.*

## U-4 Migration re-entry blocking is opaque

**Observed**: a stale `main.sqlite.migrated` sidecar from an interrupted attempt blocks subsequent migrations with an indirect error ("Repair the retained source using the migration report's named file and validation error"), and `doctor --fix` skips the item silently (reports "complete").
**Suggestion**: `doctor --fix` should list blocked migrations explicitly (not skip silently), and offer `--archive-stale` to move stale `.migrated.*` sidecars aside automatically.

## U-5 Docs: reverse-proxy page should cover nested chains and unix-socket upstreams

Common NAS/embedded topology: browser → cloud relay → system nginx → app server (unix socket) → gateway (loopback). Current docs cover single-hop reverse proxies well, but not: (a) which hop must set/overwrite XFF, (b) unix-socket upstreams (no peer IP), (c) interaction between `x-forwarded-prefix` and `controlUi.basePath`, (d) the Bun/fetch transparent-decompression pitfall when forwarding `content-encoding` (affects many embedders' proxies, not just ours).

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

### Bug type

Regression / tool schema mismatch

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (`3928bad`), the agent-facing Automations tool advertises the `add` action in `/tools verbose`, but actual tool calls using `"action": "add"` are rejected during tool argument validation:

```text
Validation failed for tool "automations":
  - action: must be equal to one of the allowed values

Received arguments:
{
  "action": "add",
  "agent": "main",
  "sessionTarget": "isolated",
  "message": "AUTOMATION_ADD_OK",
  "delivery": "none",
  "timeoutSeconds": "60"
} 
```

This reproduces across multiple models and both Telegram and WebChat, so it does not appear to be model- or channel-specific.

The same Gateway can successfully create and execute an automation through the CLI, so the scheduler itself is working.

### Environment
OpenClaw: 2026.9.2 (3928bad)
Docker / TrueNAS
Main container: ix-openclaw-openclaw-1
Agent: main
Reproduced with OpenAI and MTPLX/Qwen models
Reproduced through Telegram and WebChat



### Control test

Creating an automation directly with the CLI succeeds and the job runs successfully.

Therefore:

- scheduler is enabled
- Gateway cron execution works
- agent `main` can execute the scheduled job
- failure is isolated to the model-facing Automations tool schema/authority path

### Relevant source investigation

In the bundled 2026.9.2 code:
```javascript
parameters: createCronToolSchema({
  ...
  management: managementAuthority
    ? managementAuthority.managementOnly
      ? "only"
      : "also"
    : undefined
})
```
and:
```javascript
action: stringEnum(
  managementOnly
    ? CRON_MANAGEMENT_METHODS.map((method) => method.slice(5))
    : CRON_ACTIONS
)
```
bindCronManagementGrant() sets:
```javascript
const managementOnly = scope.callerOrigin.kind === "unknown";
```
The actual case "add" implementation is present in the same tool, but schema validation rejects add before execution.

Normal channel-owner automation authority appears intended to use:

createCronCreatorAuthorityCapability(
  runId,
  { kind: "external", channel: messageProvider }
)

This suggests that some normal owner turns are receiving/binding a management-only authority surface even though /tools verbose advertises the full Automations action set.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a normal owner agent session.
2. Run /tools verbose.
3. Observe:
```
Automations - Gateway scheduler...
ACTIONS: status | list ... | get jobId | add job | update ... | remove ...
```
4. Ask the agent to call the Automations tool exactly once with action: "add".
5. Observe tool-schema validation failure:
```
action: must be equal to one of the allowed values
```

The request never reaches the `case "add"` implementation.

### Expected behavior

For a normal authenticated owner agent turn:

- `/tools verbose` and the actual JSON/tool schema should agree.
- `action: "add"` should be accepted when Automations advertises `add`.
- Control-UI management-only restrictions should not leak into normal owner agent turns.



### Actual behavior

The agent sees add, selects add correctly, but the runtime tool validator rejects it before execution.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2

### Operating system

Linux - TrueNAS Scale

### Install method

docker

### Model

openai

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

This resembles older schema-mismatch issues such as #9283, but the failure here is at the `action` enum / management authority layer introduced in the current implementation rather than the older nested `job` schema mismatch.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

In Discord Direct Messages (DM), when a user sends a normal text message, the agent says the message arrived empty ("context arrives without text content") but STILL executes the command correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a DM to the agent in Discord (normal text message, not forwarded)
2. Observe the agent's response

### Expected behavior

The agent should see the message text in its context and acknowledge it received the content.

### Actual behavior

- Agent says: "Juan — me llega el contexto pero sin texto del mensaje"
- But the agent STILL executes the command (e.g., deleted a section of a file successfully)
- This means the message WAS received and processed, but the model believes it arrived empty

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2

### Operating system

Truenas Scale 25.10.7

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

MiniMax-M2.7

### Provider / routing chain

minimax

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
From session history (seq 407):
- User message: "eliminala" — content exists in the JSON transcript
- Model response: "Bug #21439 — contexto llegó sin texto. Procedo:"
- Model then executed `sed -i '221d' AGENTS.md` successfully

The contradiction: The message content IS in the transcript (proved by the model's ability to execute the command), but the model says it arrived empty.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

- Confusing for users — bot says it didn't receive text when it did
- May cause incorrect behavior in more complex interactions

issues.body:
## Summary

Add one boolean, `dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards`, settable per agent (`agents.entries.<name>.dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards`) or globally (`security.dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards`). When it's on, OpenClaw skips a specific list of hardcoded refusals — the ones that fire even when `openclaw.json` already grants full trust. Correctness checks, consistency checks, and enforcement of user-configured policy (`modelPolicy`, `tools.deny`, etc.) all keep working normally.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw already offers plenty of ways to set trust per agent: `tools.profile`, `tools.deny`, `sandbox.mode`, `permissionMode`, `modelPolicy`. On top of those, more and more hardcoded guards keep landing that run *before* the config is consulted and refuse regardless of what's set. There is no config field, env var, or CLI flag that can turn them off.

A configuration that clearly expresses "trust these agents, restrict selectively" looks like this:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": { "sandbox": { "mode": "off", "workspaceAccess": "rw" } },
    "entries": {
      "trusted-agent":    { "tools": { "profile": "full", "deny": [ /* selective */ ] } },
      "restricted-agent": { "tools": { "profile": "full", "deny": ["exec","process","subagents","sessions_send", /* … */ ] } }
    }
  }
}
```

Several guards ignore that setup and refuse anyway, with no way to say "yes, it was intentional."

### Guards this flag would cover

These block real workflows, have a clear reason someone might want them off, and turning them off doesn't break anything the runtime actually needs to stay correct:

- **Exec-marker CLI refusal** — [#150499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150499), precursor [#150520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150520). `assertGatewayCliMessageContext` in `src/gateway/operator-cli-message-input.ts` refuses `sessions.send`, `sessions.steer`, `chat.send`, `sessions.create` (with an initial turn), and `agent` RPCs any time `OPENCLAW_SHELL=exec` or `OPENCLAW_SUBAGENT_EXEC=1` is set. The PR itself calls it *"denial-only, not authenticated identity"*. Result: shell/Python helpers launched from an agent's exec stop working (see #160289). Downside of turning it off: those messages show up as human input instead of attributed agent messages. That's a UX thing, not a broken state.
- **Sandbox-required HTTP session refusal** — [#155964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155964). `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` refuse to create sessions when the role requires sandbox and `sandbox.mode` is off. Users who deliberately run `sandbox.mode: "off"` can't use those endpoints. Downside of turning the refusal off: no isolation for HTTP-triggered work — which is what the sandbox-off setting already asks for.
- **Stateless `tools.invoke` role enforcement** — [#153881](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153881). `tools.invoke` now enforces the role's agent allowlist and required-sandbox rule even when there's no session row. Blocks scripting, one-shots, and tests that don't want to spin up a session. Downside of turning it off: the tool runs without session context — which is the whole point of using it statelessly.
- **Media capability fail-closed** — [#143521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143521). Media reads fail closed when trusted active-session context is missing. Blocks plugin-driven media reads where the session context can't be cleanly threaded through. Downside: minor cross-session read leakage in edge cases — bounded by whatever the plugin can already see.

### Guards this flag would NOT cover

Not every guard belongs on this switch. Some are actually doing useful work — turning them off wouldn't unblock a workflow, it would just silently break something. These stay in force no matter what the flag says:

- **Mid-op workspace-authority re-check** ([#147138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147138)) — this catches the case where permission is *revoked* while a write is in progress (via fs-safe 0.10). Turning it off means "keep writing after being told to stop." That's a bug, not a workflow.
- **Visitor invite revalidation** ([#153987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153987)) — a version-compatibility check. If the host doesn't have the "guarded store capability," turning off the check doesn't add it — the invite goes out but nothing can enforce it. Silent inconsistency, no new ability.
- **macOS file-tool alias rejection** ([#131434](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131434)) — path canonicalization. Skipping it means paths silently resolve outside the workspace the tool thinks it's in. That's a footgun for the tool, not a restriction on the user.
- **Native + Visitor role model-limit enforcement** ([#154893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154893)) — re-checks that model calls match the operator role's `modelPolicy`. But `modelPolicy` is *user-configured*; turning this off would silently let agents call models outside a user-maintained allowlist. If `modelPolicy` is too strict, the fix is to edit `modelPolicy`, not to bypass it.
- **Main-session recovery provenance requirement** ([#160130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160130)) — refuses to auto-resume a crashed session if the last input wasn't verified `external_user`. Fail-closed is the right default for state integrity; the "recover no matter what" case is a separate tradeoff that isn't what this request is about.

Listing what's *not* covered is intentional. The flag has a specific meaning ("skip hardcoded refusals that ignore user config"), and the excluded list is what defines that meaning.

### Community reports that match this pain

Directly overlapping:
- [#160289](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160289) — "Support attributed agent-to-agent messaging from CLI scripts" (filed after #150499; documents heartbeat agents whose shell/Python helpers broke with no supported workaround).
- [#150467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150467) — the original bug #150499 closed; gives context on why that guard was added.
- [#137299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/137299) — exec children carry no calling-agent identity, forcing wrappers to encode identity themselves.

Same general pattern — hardcoded refusal fires despite user-granted permission, no workaround in the error message:
- [#124946](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124946) — terminal tool bypasses exec policy and approvals on both runtimes.
- [#59006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59006) — 2026.4.1 broke exec completely for existing setups.
- [#45464](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45464) — Telegram DM exec parity broken; exec denied despite trusted sender + elevated + full/off approvals.
- [#59847](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59847) — "Allow always" popup approval doesn't persist for the next exec command.

The pattern across all of these: the user's config says one thing, a hardcoded guard says another, and the config loses without any way to override it.

## Proposed solution

### Config

Per-agent (primary):

```json
"agents": {
  "entries": {
    "trusted-agent": {
      "tools": { "profile": "full", "deny": [ /* … */ ] },
      "dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards": true
    }
  }
}
```

Global fallback:

```json
"security": {
  "dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards": true
}
```

Both default to `false`; leaving them out means `false`.

**How they combine:** per-agent wins over global. A per-agent `false` turns the bypass off even if the global is `true`. That way global trust can be declared once and individual agents can still be selectively locked down (matching the `restricted-agent` shape in the sample above).

Naming matches an existing convention in the repo — `sandbox.docker.dangerouslyAllowContainerNamespaceJoin` in `src/config/schema.labels.ts` — and mirrors Claude Code's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` so it's familiar.

### Behavior

When `dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards` resolves to `true` for an agent:

- The four guards in the "would cover" list above are skipped for that agent's operations.
- The guards in the "would NOT cover" list keep firing normally. So does everything the user configured — `tools.deny`, `modelPolicy`, `permissionMode`, per-agent `sandbox.mode`, plugin authz. The flag only turns off refusals that ignore user config; it doesn't turn off user config, and it doesn't turn off checks the runtime actually needs.
- When an in-scope guard *does* fire (because the flag is off or set to `false`), the error message should name both fields so users hitting it for the first time know how to allow it.

### This should be a principle going forward, not just a patch on today's four guards

The important part of this request is not just the current list — it's that whenever a new safety guard gets added later, the same test should be applied and the flag should be wired up (or explicitly not wired up, with a reason) before the guard lands. Otherwise the same pattern that produced these four will keep repeating and user config will keep getting overruled every release.

Concretely, for any new hardcoded refusal that fires *before* user config (`tools.deny` / `modelPolicy` / `permissionMode` / `sandbox.mode`) is consulted:

- Ask the same question used here: *does turning this off unblock a real workflow that users should be allowed to opt into, or does it silence a correctness check / user-configured policy?*
- If it unblocks a workflow → wire it to `dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards` and short-circuit when the flag is `true`. Landing without that is an incomplete implementation.
- If it's a correctness or consistency check → leave it in force, and say so in the PR description. Being explicit about the classification is what keeps things from drifting over time.
- A shared helper (something like `isSafetyGuardBypassed(agentId?: string): boolean`) would make the check one line to add and make the whole trust boundary easy to audit in one place.
- One extra line in the PR template — "Does this guard need to honor `dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards`? Why or why not?" — would make sure the question gets asked at authoring time, not surfaced later as a fresh issue after someone hits the refusal.

Today's four guards are the starting point. The rule for future guards is the real ask.

### Non-goals

- Not asking to weaken any default. Every guard listed (in or out of scope) stays fail-closed by default. The flag is opt-in only.
- Not asking for new credentials, transports, or auth surfaces. It's just about letting existing config be consulted before hardcoded refusals fire.
- Not asking to bypass correctness/consistency checks or user-configured policy — the excluded list makes that explicit.

## Alternatives considered

- **A flag per guard** (e.g. `security.allowAgentCliMessagesFromExec`, `security.allowSandboxOffOnHttp`, …): blows up the config surface, makes users learn each guard's name, and needs a schema change every time a new safety feature lands. Doesn't match how anyone actually thinks about trust.
- **One flag that turns off everything indiscriminately**: sweeps in the correctness/consistency checks and user-configured policy enforcement, silently breaking things that should stay enforced. The narrower list here does the same job without the footgun.
- **Env var only** (`OPENCLAW_SKIP_SAFETY_GUARDS=1`): loses per-agent granularity, encourages ad-hoc shell exports, doesn't survive service restarts cleanly.
- **Auto-derive from `sandbox.mode: off` + `tools.profile: full`**: the exec-marker guard fires at a place where the caller's agent identity has been intentionally erased, so there's no "which agent's config" to consult. The bypass would either be too broad or unavailable. Fragile, doesn't generalize.
- **Session-level `permissionMode: "unrestricted"`**: piggybacks on per-session state, and doesn't cover exec-launched helpers or HTTP session creation at all.
- **Migrate case-by-case**: as #160289 shows, this forces scope-changing refactors on existing helpers, and some paths (agents that explicitly deny `sessions_send`, for example) have no supported alternative.

## Impact

- **Who's affected**: users running exec-launched shell/Python helpers, cron-triggered agents, TUI-driven scripts, sandbox-off setups, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` HTTP integrations against roles that require sandbox, stateless `tools.invoke` for scripts and tests, and plugin-driven media reads without cleanly-threadable session context.
- **Severity**: workflow blocker for those paths; the error messages don't offer a workaround.
- **Frequency**: every affected call.
- **Consequences**: forced refactors, blocked workflows, or hard failure with no override. The four in-scope guards all landed between 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-23. If the trend continues (and the community reports above suggest it will), the practical value of user config will keep dropping unless there's an opt-out.

## Evidence / examples

In-scope guards, files, and PRs (all verified reachable):

- `src/gateway/operator-cli-message-input.ts` (`assertGatewayCliMessageContext`) — PR #150499, #150520
- `src/gateway/operator-session-run.ts`, `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/command/session-preparation.ts` — PR #155964
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts`, `src/gateway/session-sharing-policy.ts` — PR #153881
- `src/media/local-roots.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.ts`, `src/media/read-capability.ts` — PR #143521

Excluded guards for reference (not covered by the flag):

- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/provisioned-files.ts` — PR #147138
- `extensions/visitor-access/src/visitors.ts`, `src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.ts` — PR #153987
- `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts`, `src/agents/core-coding-tools.ts`, `src/agents/apply-patch.ts` — PR #131434
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-model-input.ts`, `src/agents/harness/host-source-authority.ts` — PR #154893
- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-replay-safety.ts` — PR #160130

Existing `dangerously*` naming precedent in the repo: `sandbox.docker.dangerouslyAllowContainerNamespaceJoin` (`src/config/schema.labels.ts`).

Consistent with what the guards themselves say. PR #150499's own body: *"This inherited marker only refuses accidental operator re-entry. It is not authentication, and must never mint provenance or grant a missing tool."* An opt-out honors that framing — the guard stays as the *default*, and explicit user trust becomes the intended way to override it instead of something out-of-scope.

Related community reports: #160289 (direct match), #150467, #137299, #124946, #59006, #45464, #59847.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

- The flag is deliberately coarse ("is this agent trusted?") and named to make the tradeoff obvious (`dangerously…`). Users who want fine-grained restriction still have `tools.deny`, `modelPolicy`, `permissionMode`, and per-agent `sandbox.mode` — those don't change and stay the right tools for locking things down.
- Suggested error-message tweak on the in-scope guards: append a line naming both `agents.entries.<name>.dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards` and `security.dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards` when the refusal fires, so first-time users know how to allow it.
- The "principle going forward" part above is the real point of this request — the four guards today are just the starting set.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still unfulfilled on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- No `dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards` / `skipSafetyGuards` key in schema or anywhere in `src/` or `extensions/` (`git grep -i 'dangerouslySkipSafetyGuards\|skipSafetyGuards' origin/main` returns zero hits).
- All four in-scope guards still refuse before user config is consulted:
  - **Exec-marker CLI refusal** — `src/gateway/operator-cli-message-input.ts` (`assertGatewayCliMessageContext`, throws at the entry).
  - **Sandbox-required session enforcement** — `src/gateway/session-sharing-policy.ts` `authorizeSessionAgentRun` (role-vs-sandbox check still present).
  - **Stateless `tools.invoke` role enforcement** — `src/gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts` → same `authorizeSessionAgentRun`.
  - **Media capability fail-closed** — `src/media/read-capability.ts` (active-session requirement unchanged).
- The "narrower" alternative clawsweeper recommended (attributed-CLI messaging via #160289) has not landed either; the pain is unresolved from both ends.
