### Bug type

Performance regression / slow startup

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On this Windows host the Gateway's plugin-load phase (`plugins.runtime-post-bind`, 23 plugins) takes **59,959.9 ms**, and **57.4 s of that is three channel plugins alone**. The cost is **module compilation**, not plugin logic: a single heavy channel plugin's entry costs **5.0 s (weixin)** to **7.4–13.2 s (feishu)** to import in a cold Node process, while its third-party SDK is **264 ms at most**. Pre-warming only the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` subpaths those plugins import drops the same import to **224–448 ms** (weixin: 5.0 s → 0.22 s, a 22x difference).

So the dominant startup cost is re-compiling a large shared `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` module graph, once per plugin instance, on the Gateway's single main thread. Related: #159499 (two sequential registry phases; this report isolates what one of them is spending its time on) and #157989 (the same source-capture machinery also rewrites GBs per start — the capture directory is per plugin *workspace*, and this issue is about the CPU cost of the per-instance module registry, not the I/O).

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.6 (eb377ac)**, npm global install, Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200), Node **v24.19.0**
- 23 enabled plugins; the three heavy channels: `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.9.6, `@dingtalk-real-ai/dingtalk-connector` 0.8.26, `@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin` 2.4.6 (all installed via npm into `<stateDir>/npm/projects/...`)
- Gateway started with `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` set and `--max-old-space-size=8192`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the three plugins above into an npm-based install and start the Gateway with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`.
2. Read the `startup trace: plugins.gateway-load.plugin.<id> ... loadMs= registerMs= loadAndRegisterMs=` lines.
3. In a separate cold Node process, `import()` the plugin's entry module (e.g. `@openclaw/feishu/dist/index.js` → `loadChannelPlugin()` → `dist/channel-plugin-api.js`) and time it.
4. Repeat step 3 after first `require()`-ing the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` subpaths that the plugin imports.

### Expected behavior

An installed, unchanged plugin's module graph should be compiled once per process (or once per build) and reused across plugin instances, so that enabling N channel plugins costs roughly the compile of the union of the graphs, not N × (shared graph + own graph).

### Actual behavior

**1. Gateway-side per-plugin cost (2026.9.6 eb377ac, Windows)**

| plugin | `loadMs` | `registerMs` | `loadAndRegisterMs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feishu` | 18,843.0 | 21,805.6 | **40,649.0** |
| `dingtalk-connector` | 12,112.8 | 10.1 | **12,123.0** |
| `openclaw-weixin` | 4,625.3 | 2.5 | **4,627.9** |
| (next 16 plugins combined) | — | — | **~0.6 s** |

`plugins.runtime-post-bind` = **59,959.9 ms**, `loadedPluginCount=23`. The phase's own liveness line says the main thread was saturated while it ran:

```
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization,cpu interval=61s degradedFor=62s
  eventLoopDelayP99Ms=60196.7 eventLoopDelayMaxMs=60196.7 eventLoopUtilization=0.999 cpuCoreRatio=0.914
  active=0 waiting=0 queued=0 phase=sidecars.control-ui-assets
```

**2. Cold-process cost of one plugin entry, measured outside the Gateway (5 runs each, min/median/max)**

| what was imported | wall time |
|---|---|
| `@openclaw/feishu/dist/channel-plugin-api.js` (a 92-byte file that re-exports one `.setup/channel-*.mjs`) | **7,212 / 7,303 / 7,497 ms** (one run during an active session: 13,186 ms) |
| `@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin/dist/index.js` | **4,932 / 4,968 / 5,040 ms** |
| `@dingtalk-real-ai/dingtalk-connector/dist/index.mjs` | ~835 ms (only 66 modules) |
| third-party SDK alone: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` / `axios` / `dingtalk-stream` / `zod` | **264 / 136 / 159 / 118 ms** |

Variance is small (weixin: 4,932–5,040 ms over 5 runs), so this is deterministic compile cost, not scheduling noise.

**3. Where inside weixin's 5 s it goes — cumulative cost of the SDK subpaths it imports**

| subpath (in import order) | cumulative |
|---|---|
| `openclaw/plugin-sdk/account-id` | 11 ms |
| `+ channel-config-schema` | 733 ms |
| `+ channel-runtime` | 1,564 ms |
| `+ command-auth` | 2,659 ms |
| `+ config-runtime` | 2,770 ms |
| `+ hook-runtime`, `infra-runtime`, `plugin-runtime` | ~5,400 ms |

The plugin's own entry is 716 bytes and imports 4 local files; the whole 5 s is the SDK graph behind it. (`feishu` imports 20 distinct `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` subpaths.)

**4. Control: warm the SDK graph, and the same import is 20x cheaper**

| case | cold | after warming only the plugin-sdk subpaths |
|---|---|---|
| weixin `dist/index.js` | 4,968 ms | **224 ms** (285 modules) |
| dingtalk `dist/index.mjs` | 835 ms | **448 ms** |
| feishu `dist/channel-plugin-api.js` | 7,303 ms | **3,121 ms** (still loaded 222 more modules beyond the 19 subpaths that were statically enumerable) |

**5. CPU profile of one such import** (`--cpu-prof`, weixin `dist/src/config/config-schema.js`, 6,015 ms sampled, 279 modules)

| self time | frame |
|---|---|
| 2,710.5 ms | `ModuleWrap` (ESM wrapping/compile) |
| 357.5 ms | `internalModuleStat` |
| 321.0 ms | `compileSourceTextModule` |
| 261.6 ms | `compileFunctionForCJSLoader` |
| ~1,300 ms | file I/O (`open` 153 / `read` 108 / `lstat` 115 / `realpathSync` 121 / `fstat` 54 / `readFileUtf8` 50) |
| 90.3 / 198.8 / 323.9 ms | `esm/module_job` / `esm/loader` / `esm/utils` |
| 63.7 ms | GC |

**6. `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` does not help this path** (2 controlled pairs, same module): 2,421 / 2,293 ms without the cache vs 2,609 (populate) / 5,021 ms (hit) with it. The 16 MB cache dir (4,332 files) is written but the compile cost stays — i.e. the cost is resolve + read + compile + instantiate of the graph, not V8 code-cache territory.

### Hypothesis (not proven)

The plugin instance isolation introduced with source capture gives each plugin its own module registry, so the *shared* SDK graph is compiled again for each instance instead of being reused process-wide. Consistent with the numbers: in one plain Node process the SDK graph is shared (`require.cache`), and weixin costs 224 ms after feishu warmed it, while in the Gateway the second and third heavy channel plugin still cost 12.1 s and 4.6 s. A build-time diagnostic would settle it.

### Available instrumentation for maintainers

`plugin.load-profile` already exists: `OPENCLAW_DIAGNOSTICS=plugin.load-profile` (or `diagnostics.flags`) makes `src/plugins/plugin-load-profile.ts` emit one stderr line per phase:

```
[plugin-load-profile] phase=bundled-register:loadChannelPlugin  plugin=feishu elapsedMs=… source=…
[plugin-load-profile] phase=bundled-entry-module-load elapsedMs=13186.6 sourceLoaderCreateMs=0.0 sourceLoaderCallMs=0.0 source=…/dist/channel-plugin-api.js
```

`bundled-register:*` (`loadChannelPlugin` / `registerChannel` / `setChannelRuntime` / `registerFull` / `registerCapabilities`) and `bundled-entry-module-load` give exactly the per-plugin split this report infers, and `sourceLoaderCallMs=0` tells you the native-require path was taken rather than the source-transform loader. We verified the flag works in a standalone process; we have not yet captured a Gateway boot with it (that requires enabling it and restarting, which we will do next and attach here).

One data point from that standalone harness: with the plugin's modules already warm, the entire `register(registrationMode="full")` call took **43 ms** — so feishu's Gateway-side `registerMs=21,805.6` looks like further *module loads* inside the same phase (its `registerFull` synchronously loads six tool modules: doc / chat / wiki / drive / perm / bitable), not registration logic.

### Honest limits

- All per-module timings are from the **reported release (2026.9.6 eb377ac)**, measured in standalone Node processes on this host, not from current main. The Gateway-side numbers (table 1) are from the Gateway's own startup trace on the same release.
- The "per-instance registry defeats sharing" explanation is a **hypothesis**; the per-plugin splits needed to confirm it require the `plugin.load-profile` run described above.
- The 13,186 ms outlier for the same feishu module was measured while the Gateway was serving a session; all other runs were on a quiet host.

## Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker
No

## Summary
On 2026.9.6, a guarded Skill Workshop apply from an agent-to-agent continuation fails at `plugin.approval.request` with `missing scope: operator.approvals`, but the agent receives `Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)` while the Gateway is healthy.

## Steps to reproduce
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Observed incident path (not a clean-install deterministic reproduction): an existing user-authorized skill repair was staged in Workshop; an agent received an A2A continuation via `sessions_send`; its guarded `skill_workshop` apply was rejected before approval creation. The exact provenance/scope conditions needed to reproduce on another installation have not been isolated.

## Expected behavior
The error presented to the agent should distinguish an authorization rejection from a transport outage, consistent with the actual Gateway error. If this continuation is ineligible to request approval, provide an actionable supported operator handoff. If eligible, route the request to the operator without granting the agent approval-resolution authority.

## Actual behavior
The tool returned `Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)`. The Gateway log instead recorded `GatewayClientRequestError: missing scope: operator.approvals`. Gateway connectivity was healthy. `openclaw approvals pending --json` returned an empty list; that list alone is not proof of plugin approval absence, but the logged request rejection establishes the earlier failure. The proposal remained pending and live skill files were unchanged.

## OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 (eb377ac)

## Operating system
macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon

## Install method
Global npm package

## Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Logs
Sanitized error text from the incident:
```text
plugin approval gateway request failed
GatewayClientRequestError: missing scope: operator.approvals
Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Installed bundle inspection:
- `agent-tools.before-tool-call-D6M7yTR3.mjs:989`: calls `plugin.approval.request`.
- Same bundle, line 1082: maps non-`INVALID_REQUEST` errors to the gateway-unavailable message.
- `gateway-C0WAS-zz.mjs:408` and `in-process-gateway-BV20ULlt.mjs:78` route through `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch-DeqbsaqC.mjs:166-218`, where source/operator authority is intersected.
- Method registry requires `operator.approvals`.

These observations do not establish whether the narrowed authority is intentional or a provenance propagation defect. No pairing defect or transport outage has been demonstrated.

## Impact and severity
Blocks one observed authorized managed-skill repair. Frequency across other contexts is unknown. The misleading error directs troubleshooting toward connectivity/restarts instead of the rejected approval request. No live skill mutation or data loss observed.

## Additional information
Related closed reports: #100212 (misleading rejection message) and #124314 (approval request authorization in a different deployment path). This is a current 2026.9.6 observation through the in-process/A2A path, not a claim that the older device-pairing root cause applies. Unlike #109278, this request is rejected before an operator decision, rather than successfully delivered but invisible to an independent poller.

Please confirm intended A2A approval-request semantics and the supported recovery path, and preserve the request-vs-resolution authority boundary. No permission widening, core patch, approval bypass, or restart was performed as a workaround. No known-good version established.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After updating OpenClaw to 2026.9.5 using `openclaw update` in administrator PowerShell on Windows, my previously working Slack integration prevents normal Gateway startup.

Startup initially failed with:
“prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out”.

Disabling Slack and DuckDuckGo allowed the Gateway to reach ready in 24–36 seconds. Re-enabling only Slack, with DuckDuckGo still disabled, reproduced a roughly 187-second event-loop stall and startup did not reach ready before the test was stopped. Disabling Slack again restored successful startup and dashboard chat.

Slack remains unusable. I need to restore it without losing my existing configuration or conversation history.

### Steps to reproduce

On my existing Windows installation with Slack previously configured and working:

1. Run `openclaw update` in administrator PowerShell, updating to 2026.9.5.
2. Start the Gateway. Startup fails with:
   prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out
3. With the Gateway stopped, run:
   openclaw plugins disable slack duckduckgo
4. Run `openclaw gateway run`.
   Gateway reaches ready in 24–36 seconds, and dashboard chat works.
5. Stop that foreground Gateway with Ctrl+C.
6. Run `openclaw plugins enable slack`, leaving DuckDuckGo disabled.
7. Run `openclaw gateway run` again.
   HTTP listening is reported after approximately 205 seconds, with an approximately 187-second event-loop stall. No ready message appears during several minutes of observation.
8. Stop the test, disable Slack again, and start the Gateway.
   It reaches ready in approximately 24 seconds.

This reproduces on my existing configuration; a fresh-install reproduction has not been tested.


### Expected behavior

The Gateway should complete startup with the Slack plugin enabled and continue receiving and replying to Slack messages, as it did before the update. My existing Slack configuration and conversation history should remain usable, without disabling Slack or encountering multi-minute event-loop stalls and startup timeouts.


### Actual behavior

With Slack enabled, Gateway startup stalls for several minutes. The original run exits with:
prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out

In a later test with only Slack re-enabled and DuckDuckGo still disabled, HTTP listening was reported after 205.1 seconds. Diagnostics showed:
- eventLoopDelayP99Ms=186696.9
- eventLoopUtilization=1
- cpuCoreRatio=0.92
- phase=sidecars.model-runtime

No Gateway ready message appeared before that test was stopped, and Slack remained unavailable.

With both Slack and DuckDuckGo disabled, the Gateway reached ready in 24–36 seconds. Scheduled Task startup and dashboard chat worked, but this workaround leaves my Slack workflow unusable.


### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), stable

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

npm global installation on native Windows; updated using openclaw update

### Model

openrouter/openrouter/free (via OpenRouter)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → OpenRouter → OpenRouter free-model router (openrouter/free). Underlying model/provider selected by OpenRouter is unknown.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Gateway logs show agent model openrouter/openrouter/free with thinking=medium and fast=off. The model configuration was unchanged during the Slack enable/disable tests.

Dashboard chat successfully returned replies with Slack and DuckDuckGo disabled. Logs also reported “Failed to fetch OpenRouter models: This operation was aborted”, but chat still worked afterward. It is unknown whether that warning is related to the startup issue.

### Logs

```shell
Original failed startup:
20:24:18 [gateway] sidecars failed to start: Error: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out
20:24:28 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 9683ms
20:24:28 Gateway failed to start: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out.

Later test: Slack enabled, DuckDuckGo disabled:
21:00:44 [gateway] http server listening (15 plugins: anthropic, browser, canvas, cua-computer, device-pair, file-transfer, geolocation, linux-node, memory-core, ollama, openai, openrouter, slack, talk-voice, xai; 205.1s)
21:00:44 [diagnostic] liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=160660ms elapsed=190660ms; deferring recovery decisions

Diagnostic values from that same test:
eventLoopDelayP99Ms=186696.9
eventLoopDelayMaxMs=186696.9
eventLoopUtilization=1
cpuCoreRatio=0.92
phase=sidecars.model-runtime

After disabling Slack again, with DuckDuckGo still disabled:
21:07:20 [gateway] starting...
21:07:44 [gateway] ready
21:07:45 [heartbeat] started

Full stability diagnostics retained locally, not attached pending privacy review.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

High impact on my primary workflow: my previously working Slack integration is unusable after the update. Enabling Slack causes severe Gateway startup stalls; the original startup attempt timed out and exited.

The available workaround is to disable Slack and use dashboard chat, which does not restore my Slack workflow. No data loss has been confirmed.
An in-place downgrade to the suspected previous version, 2026.6.8, is blocked by database-schema incompatibility. A current-state backup has been created and verified.


### Additional information

- Node version: 24.19.0.
- Native Windows npm installation; Gateway managed by a Scheduled Task.
- Slack plugin: @openclaw/slack 2026.9.5, origin reported as global.
- Updated using `openclaw update` in administrator PowerShell. Original update output is no longer available.
- Saved .pre-update and .last-good configuration files record 2026.6.8; the actual previous running version is unconfirmed.
- `openclaw plugins doctor` passed with Slack disabled.
- Automatic triage failed with the same model-runtime timeout.
- Update history queries returned only the later diagnostic downgrade dry run, not the original update.

Rollback assessment:
`openclaw update --tag 2026.6.8 --dry-run` refused because the current state database has schema 17 and the main agent database has schema 21, while the target supports schema 1. No downgrade was performed.

A current-state backup was created with `openclaw backup create --verify`; verification passed. Retained legacy session migration archives have not been deleted.
Current workaround: Slack and DuckDuckGo remain disabled; Scheduled Task startup and dashboard chat work. DuckDuckGo has not been tested independently and is not confirmed faulty. Slack configuration was not deleted.

I need guidance on restoring Slack while preserving configuration and conversation history.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Regression not fully covered by an existing fix (residual case of #133692)

## Summary

On 2026.9.6, the built-in system-owned monitor job **Skill collection review** (`skill-collection-review-<agentId>`, declarationKey `skill-collection-review:<agentId>`, isolated session target, `wakeMode: "next-heartbeat"`) fails deterministically on every run with:

```
prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agentDir>
```

The failure happens within ~250ms–3s of enqueue; the agent turn never executes. `openclaw cron run <jobId>` reproduces it 100% of the time, including right after a clean gateway restart.

## What still works on the same install (important for scoping the residual path)

- Interactive agent turns: fine
- Spawned isolated subagents (`context: isolated`): fine (verified)
- **User-owned isolated cron jobs with `wakeMode: "now"`: fine** — they succeeded on this install after the #133692 fix landed (verified on 2026.9.6)
- Other system-owned isolated monitors (`memory-core` dreaming job, `wakeMode` now): fine

So the #133692 fix covered the ordinary isolated-cron dispatch path, but the monitor's `next-heartbeat` preparation path still rejects a superseded prepared runtime generation before dispatch.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), npm/brew install, systemd user service
- Linux (fnOS, x64), node v24.21.0
- Active model: zai/glm-5.3 via the zai plugin (plugin still at 2026.9.5; core reports "no release reaches 2026.9.6 yet" for it)
- Skill Workshop config: defaults (`skills.workshop.autonomous.mode` unset → auto)

## Reproduction

1. Run 2026.9.6 with Skill Workshop defaults (`autonomous.mode: auto`) and a rooted runtime for the agent.
2. Wait for the weekly `skill-collection-review-<agentId>` monitor job, or force-run: `openclaw cron run <jobId>`.
3. Every run fails with the error above; `state.consecutiveErrors` keeps climbing and the scheduler backs off.

## What does NOT help

- Clean gateway restart (fresh boot) — force run ~50s after boot still fails
- `openclaw doctor --fix` with the gateway stopped (it cleared stale session routing state for the job's sessions, but the next force run failed identically)

## Additional friction

- The job is system-owned: `openclaw cron edit/disable` refuse with "system-owned monitor jobs cannot be edited by cron clients", so there is no per-job way to stop the error streak.
- Only workaround found: set `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode` to `off`/`propose`, which disables the monitor entirely (also loses the feature). Per #144515 this opt-out granularity is a known gap.

## Suspected area

Same class as #133692 / #139830: `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError` thrown on the run/borrow path when `configuredOwner.needsRefresh || configuredOwner.pluginGeneration !== options.pluginGeneration` (prepared-model-runtime borrow check, provenance "run"), but specifically reached via the `wakeMode: "next-heartbeat"` monitor flow (`skill-collection-review-monitor` → isolated agent turn). Interactive and `wakeMode: "now"` paths self-heal; this one does not.

## Related

- #133692 (canonical, closed/fixed — ordinary isolated cron path; this report shows the monitor path is still broken)
- #139830 (closed as duplicate of #133692; same residual symptom)
- #144515 / #141102 (no per-agent/per-job opt-out, which turns this runtime bug into recurring error noise)

issues.body:
**Version:** openclaw 2026.9.6, node 26.8.2, macOS; single-model lane (`anthropic/claude-fable-5-1`, fallbacks = same model); `agents.defaults.compaction.mode = safeguard`, `maxActiveTranscriptBytes = 768kb`, `recentTurnsPreserve 8`, `qualityGuard.enabled`.

**Observed (2026-09-26 ET):**
- 14:30:51 Telegram inbound (1010 chars) dispatched to `agent:main:main`; the lane was busy with the owner's previous long run → `lane wait exceeded … waitedMs=473786 … 520348` (three queued items).
- 14:32:13 `[compaction-safeguard] Compaction safeguard: finalized artifact truncated; loss=summary-tail,suffix-head` (main session compacted while the run was queued).
- 14:40:07–14:40:11 the queued run (`runId 9cedc381…`) started and died: `embedded run agent end … isError=true … rawError=Session transcript anchor was not returned: 6bcc98d5-…` ×3 (`[empty-error-retry] … resubmitting attempt=2/3, 3/3`), `failover decision=fallback_model … next=none`, then `Embedded agent failed before reply: Failed to persist terminal assistant error: session rebound for sessionKey: agent:main:main`, `message dispatch completed … outcome=error duration=561573ms`.
- The user received "⚠️ Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session." No alert anywhere; the user turn IS persisted in the transcript (14:32:14), so a later run can still see it.

**Reading:** the queued run captured its transcript anchor (the parent event id to append after) at dispatch time; the safeguard compaction that ran while it waited finalized a new artifact and rebound the session (`lifecycleRevision`), so the anchor no longer exists when the run finally executes. Retrying the same request 3× cannot help (same stale anchor); model failover is irrelevant (`reason=unknown`).

**Expected:** a run admitted after a compaction/rebind should re-resolve its anchor to the current transcript head (or the compaction should be deferred while runs are queued for that session); the failure should be classified as a session error, not a model failover, and surfaced to operators.

**Repro:** long active run on a session + a queued inbound message + `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` small enough that a safeguard compaction lands during the wait.

_Filed from a production single-operator deployment; happy to provide redacted logs or test a patch._

issues.body:
### Summary

Let plugins and the assistant mark individual outbound images (and eventually other media) as sensitive/spoiler so that channels which support it render them blurred / click-to-reveal, and the Control UI applies an equivalent blur-until-clicked treatment.

### Problem to solve

Plugins that generate imagery (e.g. AI image generation, meme/anime generators, screenshots that may contain personal info) currently have no way to opt individual outputs into the receiving channel's "sensitive content" affordance. The result is that every image is delivered fully visible, regardless of whether the plugin (or agent) knows the content is NSFW, spoilery, private, or just should be hidden until the recipient chooses to reveal it. Users on Telegram/Discord/Matrix have grown to expect this affordance, and its absence forces plugin authors to either not ship these tools, or to warn users out-of-band in text.

The plumbing is *partially* present already: `ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia?: boolean` exists (`src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.ts:109`) but is only consumed by delivery-queue spool logic — it does not reach any channel adapter, and no plugin-facing API surfaces it.

### Proposed solution

Introduce a single, channel-agnostic "sensitive media" flag that flows end-to-end:

1. **Plugin SDK surface**
   - `AgentToolResult.details.media.mediaUrls[]` items and `toolContext.delivery.send({ mediaUrl, sensitive?: boolean })` accept a per-media `sensitive: boolean` (or richer `{ sensitive: true, reason?: string }`).
   - Also allow declaring the flag at the tool-result level for "everything this tool returns is sensitive" ergonomics.

2. **Gateway propagation**
   - Carry the flag through `ReplyPayload` per-media (not just the existing payload-level `sensitiveMedia`) so mixed sensitive/non-sensitive batches survive.
   - Preserve it across the outbound delivery queue and any media-spool rehydration.

3. **Channel adapter mapping** — each adapter maps the flag to the closest native affordance, or drops it with a debug log if the channel has no equivalent:
   - **Telegram**: pass \`has_spoiler: true\` on \`sendPhoto\` / \`sendVideo\` / \`sendAnimation\` / \`sendMediaGroup\` items (\`extensions/telegram/src/outbound-media.ts\`).
   - **Discord**: set \`spoiler: true\` on the attachment / message file component, or fall back to the \`SPOILER_\` filename prefix (\`extensions/discord/src/send.message-request.ts\`, \`send.components.ts\`, \`internal/components.message.ts\`).
   - **Matrix**: use the client-side spoiler convention (\`<span data-mx-spoiler>\` on the message body / alt-text) so compatible clients render blurred.
   - **Slack / WhatsApp / iMessage / Signal / Feishu / Line / etc.**: no native spoiler primitive today — the adapter should either (a) leave the media as-is, or (b) optionally prepend a configurable text warning (opt-in per channel), so behavior is predictable rather than silently different.

4. **Control UI**
   - Render \`sensitive\` images with a blur / "Click to reveal" overlay in the assistant transcript and in the media lightbox, matching the Discord/Telegram UX.
   - Add a per-session or global "always reveal" toggle for users who don't want the affordance.
   - Currently the Control UI has no spoiler/sensitive-media concept at all — this would be net new.

5. **Config**
   - \`channels.<channel>.sensitiveMedia.mode\`: \`native\` (default) | \`text-warning\` | \`drop\`
   - \`ui.controlUi.sensitiveMedia.defaultRevealed\`: \`false\` (default) | \`true\`

### Alternatives considered

- *Plugin prepends a text warning*: doesn't blur the image, and text warnings are ignored/scrolled past. Also inconsistent per-plugin.
- *Global "this session is NSFW"*: too coarse — a single tool call may produce mixed content, and users want per-image control.
- *Only implement Telegram*: leaves plugin authors with a per-channel matrix they have to encode themselves, which is exactly what the SDK should abstract.
- *Only wire the existing `ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia`*: works for a single payload but breaks for mixed batches (some sensitive, some not) which is the common case for image_generate + follow-up screenshot combos.

### Impact

- Affected: any plugin/user shipping image-generation or screenshot-capture tooling; primarily Telegram + Discord users (largest install base of native-spoiler-capable channels), then Matrix.
- Severity: Medium — no data loss, but currently blocks a common UX affordance and forces workarounds.
- Frequency: Every image turn from opting-in plugins.
- Consequence: Plugin authors either don't ship NSFW-capable image tools, or ship them with clunky text warnings; users can't hide plot spoilers, private screenshots, or sensitive stills the way they can natively on Telegram/Discord.

### Evidence/examples

- Existing partial primitive: \`ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia\` at \`src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.ts:109\`, only consumed in \`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.ts\`.
- Discord already has \`spoiler\` on file components at \`extensions/discord/src/internal/components.message.ts\` — unused from the outbound payload side.
- Telegram Bot API \`has_spoiler\` param on \`sendPhoto\` / \`sendVideo\` / \`sendAnimation\` / \`sendMediaGroup\` items (Bot API 6.4+).
- Matrix spec: \`data-mx-spoiler\` HTML attribute in \`m.text\` / \`m.image\` bodies.
- Control UI: \`grep -Ri '\b(spoiler|sensitiveMedia|has_spoiler|nsfw|content[_-]?warning)\b' ui/\` returns nothing — feature is entirely absent from the transcript renderer today.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

- Related: #156548 — plugin \`toolContext.delivery.send\` media doesn't appear in Control UI. The two fixes should probably land in coordination so the sensitive-flag doesn't get stripped by the same filter path that currently drops plugin delivery media from Control UI transcripts.
- Backward compatible: absent flag = current behavior. The existing \`ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia\` field would be preserved (or aliased) so no serialized transcripts break.
- Non-image media (video, audio, files) can inherit the same flag with the same channel-adapter mapping table; scoping to images first is fine but the API shape should not preclude it.


---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still unfulfilled on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- No per-media sensitive flag added. `ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia` is still payload-level only; `ReplyMediaAttachment` carries no sensitivity field.
- No channel adapter consumes it for outbound rendering:
  - **Telegram** — `git grep has_spoiler extensions/telegram/` returns zero hits; `sendPhoto` / `sendVideo` / `sendAnimation` / `sendMediaGroup` still omit `has_spoiler`.
  - **Discord** — `send.components.ts` still only reads `block.spoiler` from inbound-authored components; nothing wires `ReplyPayload.sensitiveMedia` to the component spoiler flag.
  - **Matrix** — no `data-mx-spoiler` on outbound sensitive media (inbound spoiler parsing exists; outbound does not).
- Control UI still has no spoiler/blur/NSFW rendering (`git grep -E 'spoiler|sensitiveMedia|has_spoiler|nsfw|content[_-]?warning' ui/src/` → zero hits for outbound presentation).
- No `channels.<channel>.sensitiveMedia.*` or `ui.controlUi.sensitiveMedia.*` keys in schema.

issues.body:
## Summary

Isolated automation (cron) runs are capped at a fixed **8 concurrent runs per gateway** (`DEFAULT_CRON_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS = 8`, `src/cron/service/run-admission-capacity.ts` `resolveRunConcurrency()` returns the constant), and the former knob `cron.maxConcurrentRuns` is now dead config (`src/config/dead-config-keys.test.ts`). #87174 was closed in May as "default 8 + documented supported knob"; the knob no longer exists.

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (upstream main `359a8a35`), Linux x64, Node v24.21.0, 5 gateways on one host.

## Why 8 fixed does not fit a business workload

One gateway serves a whole company: ~20 recurring jobs (triage, hygiene, watchers, support checks) plus **work-loop jobs whose agent turn legitimately runs 1–2 h** (implementer + reviewer subagents, tests, deploy verification). We run 15 such queues (instance × kind of work).

- Every long work-loop run holds one of the 8 slots for its full duration. With 6 running, the remaining automations of *all* agents on the gateway compete for 2 slots; hourly jobs queue behind them.
- A trigger (`trigger.script`) evaluation also occupies a slot while it runs (measured: `runningAtMs` is set for the evaluation, ~2–3 s), so a 60 s gate on 16 jobs adds steady slot pressure.
- There is no per-agent or per-job concurrency class, so there is no way to say "work loops: at most N, never starve the watchers".

## Workaround we use (works, but it is orchestration we had to invent)

The trigger does not fire the cron run. It admits under a host lock and dispatches the work into an ordinary named session with its own code-mode tools: `sessions` patch (creates `agent:executor:lane:<queue>:<card>`, thinking) + `sessions_send` `mode: "followup"`, `timeoutSeconds: 0`. The turn runs in lane `nested:<key>`, outside the cron pool, and our gate enforces its own cap (8 work turns + 3 urgent). Side benefits: per-card persistent session (continuable later), subagent completions delivered reliably (vs. #44925). Costs: no per-run timeout on this route, a non-`NO_REPLY` final wakes a delivery turn in the trigger session, and admission/counting logic lives in our trigger script.

## Ask

1. Make run concurrency configurable again (global and ideally per agent/job class), or
2. document that long agent work should not run as cron runs and provide a first-class "dispatch a turn into a named session" action for triggers (with timeout and concurrency class), so this does not need custom admission code.

issues.body:
### Summary
On this Windows machine the update flow fails repeatedly, and every failure emits a user-visible notice. Five failure records accumulated in ~2 days. Three distinct failure modes were observed on the same box.

---
#### 1) `managed-service-preflight` — updater runs inside the gateway process tree
```
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: managed-service-preflight.
Phases: requested (22.91s) → staging (209ms) → validating (969.9s) → activating (18.85s)
Failed: activating
Failing check managed-service-preflight: This command is running inside the gateway
process tree (gateway PID <pid>).
```
The updater is spawned as a descendant of the gateway, so activation is refused. Refusing may be correct, but the auto-update path keeps producing this instead of handing the run to the managed helper.

#### 2) `runtime-verification-failed` — snapshot path contains an unexpanded env var
```
Failed: candidate snapshot — Exit code: 1;  directory, mkdir
'~\AppData\Local\Temp\openclaw-update-canary-XXXXXX\?\$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR\agents\main\agent' (13495ms)
```
Note the literal `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and the `\?\` prefix. The canary/snapshot copy cannot create the agent dir, so the run degrades to "repairing" and then fails.

#### 3) `reconcile:abandoned` / `inactive-driver-dead` after a gateway restart
```
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: abandoned. Phases: requested (1891.62s). Failed: requested.
Failed: reconcile:abandoned — inactive-driver-dead.
Recorded verification: gateway booted; service running.
```
An update queued at the same moment as a gateway restart sat in `requested` for ~31 minutes until the reconciler abandoned it because its driver process was gone (killed by the same restart). The user gets a failure notice for a run that was already superseded.

---
#### Related: validation is very slow and the inspection window is exhausted
```
Phases: requested (22.91s) → staging (209ms) → validating (969.9s) → activating (18.85s)
Warning: Doctor lint inspection deferred until after activation: 1 agent scopes need a 2000ms
inspection allowance, with 0ms remaining in the validation inspection window (validation-ledger).
```
Validating took ~16 minutes here (SQLite family ≈419 MiB + ~160 MiB of plugin files; snapshot needs ≈2.1 GiB scratch). The lint allowance was exhausted, so repairs were deferred post-activation.

### Workaround currently in use
`update.auto.enabled` was set to `false` to stop the recurring failed-update notices; updates are triggered manually via `/update`.

### Suggestions
- Always hand auto-update runs to the managed helper (never launch inside the gateway process tree), or detect the condition before spending ~17 minutes staging/validating.
- Fix snapshot path construction on Windows (expand `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; drop the literal `\?\`).
- Treat `reconcile:abandoned` after a restart as a quiet log entry rather than a user-facing failure notice.
- Make the validation inspection budget adaptive, or report an exhausted window as info instead of a deferred-repair warning.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) — also reproduced on 2026.9.5
- Windows 10.0.26200 x64, node v24.18.0, PowerShell 5.1
- Gateway managed by a Windows Scheduled Task via a generated `gateway.vbs` hidden WScript wrapper
- Install: npm global (`%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\openclaw`)

Receive these webhooks through Gateway plugin routes while retaining vendor signature and token verification. Validation should cover correctly and incorrectly signed requests for all four channels on an isolated Gateway, listening sockets, restart behavior, old-config migration, explicit legacy-port delivery, and a published updater installing the candidate. Keep the Node request/response handler ABI and channel ingress-spool ownership unchanged.

issues.body:
## Bug Report

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), macOS 26.4.1 arm64, node 26.9.0
**Runtime:** claude-cli agent runtime (model `claude-cli/claude-fable-5`), webchat channel (Control UI, single connected client)

**Describe the bug**
Since upgrading to 2026.9.6, assistant messages are intermittently delivered twice to webchat. The duplicate is not a UI rendering artifact: the same assistant message is recorded **twice in the session transcript**, ~293 ms apart, with the **identical idempotencyKey**, differing only in stopReason:

- record 1: timestamp `1790279252950`, `stopReason: "end_turn"`, `api: "cli"`, `provider: "claude-cli"`
- record 2: timestamp `1790279253243`, `stopReason: "stop"`
- both: `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:397f5a7e-274b-4b3d-815a-17e55bdc907b"`

So the CLI runtime double-emits the final assistant message (once on `end_turn`, once on `stop`) and idempotencyKey-based dedup does not collapse the pair; both records persist and both deliver to the channel.

**Frequency/pattern**
Intermittent within one evening session: 4 duplicated interim (pre-tool-call) assistant texts + at least 1 duplicated final message. Turns with tool calls seem overrepresented. Only one webchat client was connected (verified in gateway logs). Duplicates began immediately after the 2026.9.6 upgrade; the same session/agent had no duplicates before the upgrade.

**Context that may be relevant**
- The upgrade's first restart tripped a refused startup state migration (`codex:codex-app-server-orphaned-session-bindings`) and required `openclaw doctor --fix` before the gateway would start; duplicates appeared in the session that resumed afterwards.
- Several "OpenClaw resumed this CLI session after prompt content changed (changed=prompt-tools)" resumes occurred in the same session after config hot-reloads (plugin reinstall, per-agent subagents.allowAgents change).

**Expected behavior**
One assistant message per emit: either the runtime should not re-emit on `stop` after `end_turn`, or transcript/delivery dedup should collapse records sharing an idempotencyKey.

**Possibly related:** #125824 (idempotencyKey not honored as at-most-once delivery identity), #146472 (Control UI duplicated bubbles stream vs final — but in this report the duplicate exists in the transcript itself), #144918 (closed, UI duplicates).

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, a successful first-class `plugins.reload` of the Codex plugin returned `ok: true` and `restartRequired: false`, but the agent turn that initiated it then lost authority to call unrelated Gateway tools. Subsequent calls in that same turn failed *before dispatch*, including read-only plugin, cron and session inspection and a Discord thread-creation attempt. The Gateway still answered health requests. The assistant could not complete its own post-reload verification or create a recovery thread.

This is a single observed production sequence, not a claimed deterministic minimal reproduction or proof of a particular internal cause.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`), macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 26.9.0
- Managed LaunchAgent Gateway; Codex harness; Discord agent turn
- Reload target: `codex` only

## Observed sequence (24 September 2026, Europe/Amsterdam)

1. In an active agent turn, call the first-class plugin reload for `codex`.
2. The tool returns `ok: true`, `restartRequired: false`, runtime `generation: 3`, `pluginIds: ["codex"]`.
3. In the same turn, try post-reload readbacks. Independent calls return:

```text
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching plugins.list.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching cron.status.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching sessions.list.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching message.action.
```

The `message.action` failure prevented the assistant from creating a recovery thread. The Gateway health RPC still answered; this was not a total service outage. A separate gateway resource-pressure/catalog incident was occurring at the same time, so this report does not attribute the authority failure solely to reload internals.

## Expected behavior

A successful plugin reload should leave the initiating turn able to call unrelated Gateway tools against the current generation, or provide a supported, explicit continuation path. If re-binding authority within the turn is intentionally unsupported, the reload receipt should say so and the agent should still have a reliable way to report the state to the user. `restartRequired: false` was misleading for an operation that made the current turn unable to verify itself.

## Impact

An agent performing authorized maintenance cannot verify the successful reload or continue recovery from the same turn. This is especially costly when the operation is being performed to recover a degraded Gateway; a user must initiate a fresh conversation/thread to restore an actionable control path. No credential or policy bypass is requested: keep stale authority fail-closed, but make continuation possible and visible.

## Evidence and limits

- The reload receipt is preserved locally; no private config or raw transcript is attached.
- Four distinct methods failed with the same pre-dispatch authority error after that receipt.
- One observed sequence; no isolated replay and no identified introducing commit.
- Related but distinct: #155881 concerns exec auto-review retaining retired plugin inventory; #153572 concerns a bundled MCP loopback 500 after config hot reload; #144291 concerns in-flight model turns aborted by a superseded runtime. This report concerns first-class Gateway tool dispatch in the initiating agent turn after a successful explicit plugin reload.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow a deployment to disable cloud and paired-device session hosting as a capability while retaining local sessions and ordinary browser-node operation.

### Problem to solve

Our deployment runs sessions in the team Gateway's managed execution environment. We still need browser nodes, but do not offer remote session hosting. Today we maintain a substantial source-removal patch because selecting no worker providers is not a complete capability boundary across core startup, entry points and UI.

The downstream removal also exposed a dependency: local GitHub publication initialization shared worker startup wiring, and our removal initially broke it. That was a downstream regression, not evidence that stock OpenClaw currently breaks a supported disabled-hosting mode.

### Proposed solution

Give the existing session-hosting subsystem one authoritative availability decision. Startup, session placement/admission, RPC/HTTP, CLI, tools and UI should consume that decision. Preserve the standard default behavior.

Acceptance criteria:

- Once hosting has been safely disabled, it starts no provisioning, ready-pool maintenance or worker reconciliation. Configuration reload must not silently re-enable it; changes may require restart.
- New remote placements, dispatch/move operations and remote-session bootstrap paths reject before allocation or credential consumption.
- Local sessions/worktrees, browser-node enrollment and browser execution continue working. Generic node commands and terminal routing retain their separate controls.
- Local GitHub publication initializes independently; remote publication uses the hosting-specific dependencies only when that capability is available.
- Existing remote session/environment ownership remains recorded and visible as unavailable. A retained remote session cannot silently execute locally, and worker-owned nodes/credentials cannot bypass that state by appearing ordinary.
- Active sessions and existing provider resources have an explicit disable/drain policy. Reject disabling with actionable guidance if safe draining is not supported; do not silently abandon leases or destroy data.

A startup/restart-based control is sufficient for an initial slice; live switching need not be introduced. Exact configuration and plugin boundaries need maintainer agreement. This request concerns the hosting owner, not deleting worker source or disabling all node functionality.

### Alternatives considered

- Omit provider plugins: does not by itself define core hosting/UI/lifecycle behavior.
- Disable node browser support: removes a capability we need and addresses a different responsibility.
- Hide destination controls or filter RPC externally: leaves background work and alternative entry points unresolved.
- Maintain a removal patch: achieves our deployment choice at significant upgrade cost.

### Impact

Affected: deployments with a deliberate local-session execution model and separate browser nodes. The gap blocks expressing that model through supported native controls and creates recurring downstream maintenance. Existing hosted deployments should retain their defaults.

### Evidence/examples

Source inspected at [`0603d46c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470) on September 24, 2026. This is a feature/design request based on source inspection and downstream deployment experience; no fresh stock-upstream runtime reproduction or benchmark is claimed.

- [Cloud worker configuration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/src/config/zod-schema.cloud-workers.ts#L123) exposes profiles/pool/desktop settings rather than a complete hosting-availability contract.
- [Publication initialization is conditional on worker startup/module state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/src/gateway/server-runtime-state-prepare.ts#L173).
- Existing [`nodeHost.workerRuns.enabled`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/src/config/zod-schema.node-host.ts#L45) governs a node accepting work; the requested control concerns the Gateway's overall hosting capability and its other entry points.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

We are happy to contribute focused PRs once maintainers agree on the intended behavior and first implementation slice.

### Additional information

- Full native GitHub integration availability is tracked separately: #157509.

issues.body:
### Summary

Provide a coherent optional lifecycle for OpenClaw's native GitHub integration across account linking, publication, previews, credentials and background work.

### Problem to solve

We operate a team-oriented deployment whose users do not all need native GitHub functionality. That integration spans more than the existing `github` plugin: its manifest describes public previews/document reading, while core separately owns OAuth lifecycle and publication initialization.

Disabling selected tools or removing one UI entry does not express the deployment requirement: do not offer or start the native integration. Maintaining this choice downstream requires following multiple owners across upgrades.

### Proposed solution

Consolidate GitHub-specific behavior under one integration lifecycle, preferably using the existing plugin registration/configuration contracts. Keep generic workspace, publication and credential interfaces with their appropriate core owners; extend public plugin contracts narrowly where a concrete missing interface prevents this ownership.

Desired behavior when the integration is disabled:

- Account-linking flows, native publication actions, GitHub-specific readers/previews, tools and related settings are unavailable consistently.
- Direct native API/tool/CLI entry points return a clear unavailable result before GitHub-specific effects.
- OAuth/background maintenance and native GitHub credential injection do not start.
- Pending authorization/publication work drains or cancels through its existing owners, preserving uncertain outcomes. Stored accounts/publication records remain retained without automatic use; disabling is not implicit deletion or external credential revocation.
- Ordinary Git and independently configured `gh` remain usable. Unrelated workspaces, local sessions and remote hosting do not depend on GitHub being enabled.

Keep existing default behavior. Restart-required changes are acceptable for an initial slice. Start with a maintainer-agreed lifecycle boundary and implementation slice; this is not a demand for a single large extraction PR or a prescribed new flag.

### Alternatives considered

- Deny individual tools: useful per-agent policy, but leaves linking, previews and background services outside that choice.
- Remove the current `github` plugin: its declared scope does not encompass the whole integration.
- Hide UI or filter RPC at a proxy: leaves runtime ownership and other entry points inconsistent.

### Impact

Affected: customized team deployments that do not offer native GitHub integration. The gap affects setup and ongoing background behavior; implementing this choice otherwise requires coordinated downstream changes as upstream evolves. The requested control is product availability within OpenClaw's existing trust model, not a sandbox against administrator code.

### Evidence/examples

Source inspected at [`0603d46c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470) on September 24, 2026. This is a feature/design request based on source inspection and downstream deployment experience; no fresh stock-upstream runtime reproduction or benchmark is claimed.

- [Current GitHub plugin manifest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/extensions/github/openclaw.plugin.json#L1).
- [Core GitHub OAuth lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/src/gateway/server-lifetime-sidecars.ts#L122).
- [GitHub publication initialization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0603d46c1b7616efb6fe99225498487aea3e9470/src/gateway/server-runtime-state-prepare.ts#L173).
- Merged [PR #156865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156865) makes GitHub tools participate in Disable All. That fixes a narrower tool-catalog gap; this request concerns the complete integration lifecycle.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

We are happy to contribute focused PRs once maintainers agree on the intended behavior and first implementation slice.

### Additional information

- Independent session-hosting availability includes separating local publication startup: #157510.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a degenerate generation, an assistant turn can be delivered with only a `thinking` content part and no `text` part, causing raw model reasoning to reach the customer.

### Steps to reproduce

Not a deterministic repro — this is a rare degenerate generation on openrouter/auto. Observed once in production (customer-facing agent "Nexus", session 77186188). Trigger conditions from the captured turn:
1. Agent running openrouter/auto with fallbacks (claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.8).
2. A turn degenerates into looping reasoning and consumes the entire output budget as reasoning tokens (32000/32000), hitting stopReason: length before any answer text is emitted.
3. The persisted assistant message has one content part of type "thinking" and zero "text" parts; delivery renders the reasoning as the visible reply.

### Expected behavior

When a turn has no deliverable text (only a thinking part, or an empty visible answer), the system should not surface raw reasoning to the user. It should emit a graceful fallback message or auto-retry the turn.

### Actual behavior

Raw model reasoning was delivered to the customer. Captured turn: content = one part, type "thinking", ~124,000 chars of multilingual token salad, thinkingSignature "reasoning_details", stopReason "length", zero text parts. Usage: output 32000, reasoningTokens 32000 (100% of the output budget consumed by reasoning). The existing tag-based stripper (stripReasoningTagsFromText, reasoningMode strict) does not catch this because the content is a structured thinking part, not <thinking>-tagged or naked text — so this is a missing delivery-eligibility guard, not a stripping-regex gap.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

Linux 6.8.0-110-generic (x64)

### Install method

docker

### Model

openrouter/auto (fallbacks: openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openrouter (auto routing) -> resolved model (fallback to claude-sonnet-4.6 on timeout)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

```shell

```

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any customer-facing agent on openrouter/auto (all 9 agents in our consolidated deployment share this exposure).
Severity: High (raw model reasoning delivered to an external customer).
Frequency: Rare / intermittent (one observed occurrence tied to a degenerate generation).
Consequence: Garbled/internal content shown to customers; reputational risk. Guard belongs in the shared delivery path since it is model-agnostic.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading from 2026.7.1-2 to 2026.9.6, agents whose `model.primary` is a bare alias (`"opus"`, aliased to `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`) create sessions stored as `model: "opus"`, `modelProvider: "openai"`, `agentRuntime: {id: "codex", source: "implicit"}`. `openclaw models status --agent <id>` still resolves the same config to `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. Turns in those sessions go to the Codex runtime instead of Anthropic. Changing `model.primary` to the explicit `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` fixes it immediately.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a production host. This is not yet a minimal reproduction.

1. Configure an alias `opus -> anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with Anthropic runtime auth through `claude-cli`, and a configured OpenAI (Codex OAuth) profile.
2. Set `agents.defaults.model.primary: "opus"` and, per agent, `model: { primary: "opus", fallbacks: ["openai/gpt-5.6-sol"] }`.
3. Upgrade from 2026.7.1-2 to 2026.9.6.
4. Start a new session, for example `openclaw agent --agent <id> --session-id fresh-1 --message "Reply with exactly: pong"`, or a new Slack thread mention.
5. Run `openclaw sessions list --agent <id> --json` and inspect the new session.

### Expected behavior

The new session resolves `opus` through the alias to `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and selects the Anthropic runtime (`claude-cli` here), matching `openclaw models status --agent <id>`.

### Actual behavior

- `openclaw models status --agent <id>` prints `Default (agent): anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (from opus)`.
- Every session created after the upgrade is stored as `model: "opus"`, `modelProvider: "openai"`, `agentRuntime: {"id":"codex","source":"implicit"}`. That includes fresh sessions created with `openclaw agent --session-id <new>`. The pair `("opus", "openai")` does not correspond to any configured model.
- Turns in these sessions hung or failed with `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationSupersededError: prepared model runtime publication was superseded for <agentDir>`. When the OpenAI fallback was over its Codex usage limit, the channel showed `API rate limit reached` (the misleading-error path from #156975).
- A pinned session also blocks `sessions.patch`. Patching the model timed out after 90 s because the stuck turn held the session lane.
- Sessions created before the upgrade (stored as `claude-opus-5-5` / `anthropic` / `claude-cli`, `source: "session"`) kept working on the same gateway.
- Workaround: change `agents.defaults.model.primary` and every `agents.entries.*.model.primary` from `"opus"` to `"anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"`. After the hot reload, new and existing sessions show `claude-opus-5-5` / `anthropic` / `claude-cli` (`source: "model"`), and turns succeed.

I could not determine whether `modelProvider: "openai"` comes from alias resolution at session creation, or from a fallback attempt that persisted the provider without the model. Either way, the stored model/provider pair is inconsistent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac), upgraded from 2026.7.1-2

### Operating system

Debian 13, Linux 6.12 x64

### Install method

npm global (Node 26.10.0), systemd user service

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (configured as alias `opus`)

### Provider / routing chain

primary `opus` -> anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 via claude-cli runtime; fallback openai/gpt-5.6-sol via Codex OAuth

### Additional provider/model setup details

7 agents, all with the same `model` block. Aliases: `opus`, `sonnet`, `fable`, `OpenRouter`. The `agents.defaults.models` allowlist includes `anthropic/*` and the OpenAI fallback.

### Logs

```
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=slack ... outcome=error error="Error: prepared model runtime publication was superseded for <agentDir>"
[sessions] sessions.patch: target failed for <sessionKey>: prepared model runtime publication was superseded for <agentDir>
[diagnostic] stuck session: ... state=processing reason=stale_session_state lastProgress=reply_operation:queued
```

`openclaw sessions list --json` excerpt (before the workaround):

```
{"model": "opus", "modelProvider": "openai", "agentRuntime": {"id": "codex", "source": "implicit"}}
```

### Impact and severity

Every channel-originated session on every agent routed to the wrong provider after the upgrade, and Slack replies stopped for about 4.5 hours, from the upgrade until the config was changed. `models status` looks correct, which hides the cause.

### Additional information

Related: #156975 (superseded publication sent through provider fallback), #144291 (hot reload aborts in-flight turns with the same error family).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`@openclaw/codex` is resolved through an ephemeral `/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-<random>/package-N/...` "plugin source capture" sandbox (`createPluginSourceCapture` / `withPluginSourceCaptureDirectory` in `dist/plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs`) instead of the plugin's own persistent install directory; that sandbox intermittently fails to populate `package.json` before something reads it, and a resolved path into it can also get cached and reused after the sandbox has been disposed — both cases throw `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json'`, and in the harness-dispatch case this aborts the user-facing agent turn entirely.

### Steps to reproduce

Not fully deterministic on-demand — this is intermittent, observed over ~1.5 days of normal usage, not from a constructed minimal repro. What we directly observed:

1. Run a gateway (systemd-supervised, `openclaw gateway --port <port>`) with `models.providers` containing `anthropic`/`claude-cli` and `agents.defaults.models` containing an `openai/*` entry with `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}` (the bundled `codex` plugin, config `{"codexDynamicToolsLoading": "searchable", "codexDynamicToolsExclude": []}`), and let it run for an extended period (our case: ~2 days uptime) with normal Telegram/Slack/webchat traffic.
2. Inspect `/tmp` for `openclaw-plugin-build-*` directories. Over ~1.5 days we accumulated 106 such directories (7.9G total); only 19 of them had `package-N/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json` actually present — the rest were empty or partially populated (e.g. `package-0/node_modules/` present but no package installed under it, or only a different plugin like `@openclaw/zai-provider` at `package-0`).
3. At some point a background `codex.accountUsage` RPC call resolves `@openclaw/codex` via this mechanism, gets a path into one specific sandbox dir, and then reuses that exact path on every subsequent call — even hours later, after the sandbox directory no longer exists (confirmed: the directory referenced in the repeated error was not present in `/tmp` when checked).
4. Separately, dispatching an actual agent turn to a model with `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}` can hit a *freshly*-named sandbox dir (a new one per invocation) that also fails to have `@openclaw/codex/package.json` populated in time, aborting that turn.

### Expected behavior

`@openclaw/codex` resolves successfully every time (either from its persistent install location, which is already present and used successfully by the underlying `@openai/codex` process, or from a correctly-populated fresh sandbox), and a `codex.accountUsage` call or a codex-routed agent turn completes normally without `ENOENT`.

### Actual behavior

Two related failures sharing the same error text, both observed in the gateway journal on the same running instance:

1. `codex.accountUsage` RPC fails repeatedly over hours with the *identical* stale path (same random suffix reused across calls at 11:16, 11:20, and 12:27 UTC, no restart in between):
   ```
   [gateway] request handler failed: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-IXTSVn/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json': code=ENOENT
   [ws] ⇄ res ✗ codex.accountUsage ... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: ENOENT: ... code=ENOENT
   ```
   That exact directory (`openclaw-plugin-build-IXTSVn`) did not exist in `/tmp` at the time of the failures — it had already been cleaned up/disposed, but the resolved path was still being reused.

2. An actual agent turn aborted entirely (user-visible "turn ended before a reply") when dispatched to a model with `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}`, with a *newly*-generated sandbox path this time:
   ```
   [agents/harness] Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend harnessId=codex provider=openai modelId=gpt-6-astra error="ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-NKA9yj/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json'"
   [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=280 error="ENOENT: ..." errorName=Error
   Embedded agent failed before reply: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-NKA9yj/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json'
   ```
   Notably the log itself says "not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend" — the harness-failure fallback path does not appear to trigger here, so the failure is unhandled and surfaces directly to the user.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

Linux, GCP Compute Engine VM, kernel 6.17.0-1022-gcp, x86_64, Node 24.18.0

### Install method

npm global (`npm install -g openclaw`), gateway run as a systemd `--user` service

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-terra (also reproduced with modelId `gpt-6-astra` per the harness log above) — any model routed with `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}`

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw agent dispatch -> `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}` -> `@openclaw/codex` plugin (resolved via ephemeral `/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-*` sandbox instead of its own persistent install) -> `@openai/codex` app-server (ChatGPT subscription auth, separately and successfully installed/running from a persistent `npm/projects/openclaw-codex-*` directory)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Relevant config in `~/.openclaw-t81/openclaw.json` (custom profile via `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, otherwise stock):
```json5
"plugins": { "entries": { "codex": { "enabled": true, "config": { "codexDynamicToolsLoading": "searchable", "codexDynamicToolsExclude": [] } } } },
"agents": { "defaults": { "models": {
  "openai/gpt-5.6-terra": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "codex" } }
  // and similar entries for other openai/* models
} } }
```
The persistent, working `@openai/codex` install lives at `~/.openclaw-t81/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-<hash>__openclaw-generation__<id>/node_modules/@openai/codex` (and `-linux-x64`) — that one is not affected and has multiple long-running `app-server --listen stdio://` processes. Only the separate `@openclaw/codex` *wrapper* package is affected, and only when resolved via the `/tmp` capture sandbox.

### Logs

```
2026-09-24T11:16:31.282+00:00 [gateway] request handler failed: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-IXTSVn/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json': code=ENOENT
2026-09-24T11:16:31.285+00:00 [ws] res codex.accountUsage 224ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-IXTSVn/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json': code=ENOENT
2026-09-24T11:20:15.816+00:00 [gateway] request handler failed: Error: ENOENT: ... (identical path, same build dir, 4 minutes later)
2026-09-24T12:27:30.133+00:00 [gateway] request handler failed: Error: ENOENT: ... (identical path, same build dir, 71 minutes later)
2026-09-24T13:17:11.659+00:00 [agents/harness] Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend harnessId=codex provider=openai modelId=gpt-6-astra error="ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-NKA9yj/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json'"
2026-09-24T13:17:11.665+00:00 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=280 error="ENOENT: ..." errorName=Error
2026-09-24T13:17:11.667+00:00 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:dashboard:<id> durationMs=282 error="ENOENT: ..." errorName=Error
2026-09-24T13:17:11.682+00:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-NKA9yj/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/package.json'
```

Source of the sandbox mechanism (from the installed `dist/` bundle, `plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs`):
```
function createPluginSourceCapture(execute) {
  const directory = fs.realpathSync(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(sourceCaptureDirectory.getStore() ?? tmpdir(), "openclaw-plugin-build-")));
  ...
  const acquire = (capture) => {
    if (disposed) throw new Error("Plugin module capture has been disposed");
    ...
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

N/A — see Logs section and the directory-census evidence described in "Steps to reproduce" (106 leftover `/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-*` dirs, 19/106 with `@openclaw/codex` actually present, no automatic cleanup observed).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any gateway with an `openai/*` (or other) model routed via `agentRuntime: {id: "codex"}` — in our case this was the configured **default** agent model, so it affected every default-routed turn, not an edge case.
- Severity: High for the harness-dispatch case (blocks the turn entirely, user-visible "turn ended before a reply", no fallback triggered despite a log line implying one was expected); Low-but-persistent for the `codex.accountUsage` case (background RPC only, fails silently in logs but doesn't block a user-facing turn).
- Frequency: intermittent for the harness-dispatch failure (~18% of sampled sandbox dirs had `@openclaw/codex` successfully populated — 19/106 — though not all 106 were necessarily codex-resolution attempts specifically, so treat that ratio as directional, not exact); the stale-cache `accountUsage` failure was 100% reproducible on every call observed over a multi-hour window until the gateway was restarted.
- Consequence: failed agent turns on the default/configured model; ~7.9G of un-cleaned `/tmp` disk usage accumulated over ~1.5 days from abandoned sandbox directories, contributing to disk pressure (root filesystem was at 93%/20G-free at time of investigation).

### Additional information

Workaround we applied (not a fix, just restores service): delete the stale `/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-*` directories and restart the gateway process. This clears the in-process stale-path cache (fixes the `accountUsage` symptom immediately) but does not address the underlying intermittent sandbox-population failure, which could recur.

We cannot determine regression status from available evidence (no data on when this started, or a last-known-good version) — `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` for that specific point.

Two suggestions based on the observed evidence, not verified against the source beyond what's quoted above:
- `@openclaw/codex` resolution doesn't need to go through this ephemeral capture-sandbox mechanism at all when a persistent, already-installed copy exists (as it does here) — it could resolve there directly, the way `@openai/codex` itself is resolved.
- If the capture-sandbox path is intentional (e.g. for provenance/audit purposes), any code that caches a resolved path into it should either revalidate the path exists before use, or scope the cache lifetime to the same acquire/dispose cycle rather than holding it across unrelated later calls.

issues.body:
### Summary
`memory-lancedb` has no native way to compact or optimize its LanceDB table. Writes accumulate as many small data fragments, and `openclaw ltm` exposes only `list`, `search`, `stats` and `query` — there is no `compact`, `optimize` or `cleanup`. Operators are left choosing between an ever-fragmenting table and a hand-rolled script against plugin state, which is exactly the kind of out-of-band maintenance we try not to do.

### Observed (OpenClaw `2026.9.5`, Linux x86_64, local Ollama embeddings)
- The memory table holds **~2,425 rows across 4,837 data fragment files** — about two rows per fragment — and **`_indices = 0`** (no ANN index).
- Per the plugin docs, agent ownership is a predicate applied *before* vector ranking. With no index, an agent that owns **zero** rows still has to scan every fragment to establish that.
- A cold `openclaw ltm stats` open took **~41–44 s** whether the agent owned 2,425 rows or zero — consistent with a fixed cost that scales with fragment count rather than result size.

### What this is NOT
We are **not** attributing our auto-recall timeouts to this. We traced those to a separate cause (the local embedding runner oversubscribing its threads against a container CPU quota) and fixed it; recall latency dropped sharply with the fragment count unchanged. So we have no controlled measurement that fragmentation is currently a production bottleneck for us, and we don't want this read as one. It is a maintenance gap that will grow with every write.

### Request
Any of:
1. A native `openclaw ltm optimize` (or `compact`) command, ideally with a `--dry-run` that reports fragment and version counts before and after; or
2. Automatic compaction on a threshold (fragments per row, or fragment count); or
3. At minimum, documentation of the supported way to compact the table safely while the gateway holds it open — including whether version pruning is safe for a live reader.

Related, but distinct: #127425 (ordered `ltm` limits materialize the full corpus).

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug: an available OpenClaw tool is absent from the Codex dynamic-tool catalog.

## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.5 with the Codex app-server harness and `codexDynamicToolsLoading: "searchable"`, a fresh Codex-backed agent session cannot discover `image_generate`. The tool is absent from the native Codex dynamic catalog, even though the same Gateway accepts `tools.invoke` for `image_generate` and completes image generation through the configured provider.

## Environment

- OpenClaw and `@openclaw/codex`: 2026.9.5 (`ec9c1a1`)
- Node: 24.19.0
- Gateway: Ubuntu 26.04 WSL on Windows
- Model: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the Codex app-server harness
- Image model: `openai/gpt-image-2`, authenticated with OpenAI Codex OAuth
- `tools.profile: "coding"`; no global `tools.allow` or `tools.alsoAllow`
- One unrelated agent-level deny for an MCP tool is present. I have not run a no-deny A/B comparison, so a policy interaction is not ruled out.

Sanitized relevant configuration:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "mediaModels": {
        "image": { "primary": "openai/gpt-image-2", "timeoutMs": 180000 }
      }
    }
  },
  "tools": { "profile": "coding" },
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "codex": { "enabled": true, "config": { "codexDynamicToolsLoading": "searchable", "codexDynamicToolsExclude": [] } },
      "openai": { "enabled": true }
    }
  }
}
```

Gateway `config.get` reports this image model in `runtimeConfig`, a valid config, and equal current/applied revision hashes. Both the Codex and OpenAI plugins report `loaded`, with OpenAI registering its image-generation provider.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a fresh Codex-backed WebChat session with the configuration above and ask for one photorealistic generated image using the configured OpenClaw route.
2. Inspect that session's native Codex rollout `session_meta.payload.dynamic_tools`, or run the Codex Code Mode metadata search:

   ```js
   ALL_TOOLS.filter(x => x.name.includes("image_generate"))
   ```

3. Compare with the Gateway operator method in the same session, using a synthetic prompt:

   ```text
   openclaw gateway call tools.invoke --json --params '{"name":"image_generate","sessionKey":"<current-session-key>","args":{"action":"generate","prompt":"A ceramic pear on a plain background","count":1}}'
   ```

## Expected behavior

With a configured image model and a loaded provider, Codex should be able to discover and call OpenClaw's deferred `image_generate` tool through its `openclaw` namespace while dynamic tools remain `searchable`.

## Actual behavior

- `ALL_TOOLS.filter(...)` returns `[]`. The native session metadata contains other OpenClaw dynamic tools but no `image_generate` in either `openclaw` or `openclaw_direct`.
- The agent initially treated image generation as unavailable. Without explicit routing guidance, a separate canary substituted an unintended public image endpoint. No credentials were included in that request; the prompt was synthetic.
- The documented local Gateway `tools.invoke` call succeeds for `image_generate` and asynchronously delivers one structured image attachment to the same session. This was reproduced in two isolated sessions with synthetic prompts.
- Gateway health stays `ok=true`; no plugin error or pending config reload was observed.

This is a catalog/construction discrepancy, not a claim that the provider request or media attachment path is broken. I have not isolated the exact construction stage or tested without the unrelated MCP deny. A workspace instruction to call the local Gateway operator method is a working workaround, but leaves native deferred-tool discovery broken.

## Related reports

- #77244 and #77841 concern older generation-tool liveness/policy problems, but their direct provider path was also unavailable. Here direct Gateway invocation succeeds.
- #151964 concerns asynchronous media-completion waiting, not initial tool discovery.

issues.body:
### Summary

Android Chat dictation currently requires the platform on-device recognizer. On some Android 15 OEM builds, Google voice typing and the standard Android speech-recognition service work normally, while `SpeechRecognizer.isOnDeviceRecognitionAvailable()` returns `false`. In that situation OpenClaw dictation is unavailable even though the OS has a working recognizer.

Please consider an **explicit, opt-in fallback** from on-device dictation to the standard Android `SpeechRecognizer` service.

### Reproduction

1. Use the current Google Play build of the official Android app.
2. Grant microphone permission.
3. Confirm Google voice typing works in other apps.
4. Open OpenClaw Chat and tap the composer microphone.
5. OpenClaw reports that on-device speech recognition is unavailable.

This occurs on an Android 15 OEM build where the standard Google-backed recognizer is available but the dedicated on-device recognizer is not exposed to third-party apps.

### Current behavior

OpenClaw checks `SpeechRecognizer.isOnDeviceRecognitionAvailable()` and uses `createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer()`. When that API is unavailable, the app cannot provide text dictation. The voice-note recovery added for #125322 is useful, but it produces an audio attachment rather than a transcript in the draft.

### Requested behavior

Keep on-device recognition as the preferred default. When it is unavailable, offer an explicit option such as:

- **Use system speech recognition**
- **Record voice note**
- **Cancel**

If the user chooses system recognition, use `SpeechRecognizer.createSpeechRecognizer(context)` after checking `SpeechRecognizer.isRecognitionAvailable(context)`.

Because the system recognizer may use a network service, the UI should disclose that it may send audio to the configured speech provider and optionally remember the user's choice in Voice settings.

### Why this helps

It restores text dictation on Android devices where Google/system voice input works but the on-device-only API is unavailable, without weakening the existing offline-first behavior or silently changing privacy expectations.

### Privacy

This report intentionally contains no account identifiers, device identifiers, IP addresses, screenshots, logs, or user data.

### Related

- #125322 addressed recovery to voice-note recording when on-device dictation is unavailable. This request is specifically for an optional **text-dictation** fallback through Android's standard recognizer.
