issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.9.5, running 3 or more agent turns concurrently stalls the gateway event loop in ~5 s chunks (`eventLoopUtilization=1` at ~2% CPU) and logs `SQLite transaction admission was refused`; 1–2 concurrent turns are unaffected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (Docker) with the Codex app-server runtime and an idle gateway.
2. Launch N identical agent turns at once, each in a fresh session, e.g. for N = 1, 2, 3, 6:
   ```bash
   for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
     openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:probe-$N-$i \
       --thinking medium --timeout 360 --model <model> \
       -m "Use web search to find 3 notable news items from yesterday about topic #$i. Run one bash command 'date' too. Reply with a short bullet list with URLs." &
   done; wait
   ```
3. Watch the gateway log for `[diagnostic] liveness warning` and `SQLite transaction admission was refused`, and compare the wall time for each turn.

### Expected behavior

Concurrent turns finish in roughly the time a single turn takes, with no event-loop stall. On 2026.9.4 our daily job ran 6 of these turns in parallel every day (last good run 2026-09-22): each turn took 57–92 s and none timed out.

### Actual behavior

Measured on the same host, same prompt shape, minutes apart:

| concurrent turns | wall time per turn | liveness warnings / admission refusals |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 s | 0 |
| 2 | 15 s, 32 s | 0 |
| 3 | 49 s — all three end at the same second | 1 |
| 6 | 123–125 s — all six end within 2 s of each other | 1 warning + 4 `admission was refused` |

While the stall lasts, the Codex app-server itself stays fast. In the rollout JSONL, tool calls return in 0.1–2 s, and one turn logged `task_complete` after 246 s. The gateway, however, projected that turn's events about 80 s late. The turn then hit its 360 s deadline (`codex app-server execution budget timed out`) even though its answer was already complete. The whole gateway lags during the stall; for example, one `sessions.list` call took 5.1 s. Once concurrency drops to 2, the stall goes away.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS host (kernel 7.0), container Debian 12 bookworm, Node v24.19.0

### Install method

docker (image built `FROM ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.5`)

### Model

openai/gpt-6-luna (also seen with openai/gpt-5.6-terra)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> codex app-server (agentRuntime codex) -> OpenAI (ChatGPT subscription OAuth)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The app-server runs a global Codex 0.156.0 via `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` rather than the bundled 0.154.0; the log reports `codex app-server is newer than OpenClaw's managed runtime … detectedVersion=0.156.0 validatedVersion=0.154.0`. That override went in at the same time as the 2026.9.5 upgrade, so I can't rule it out as a factor. The per-agent SQLite DB (`openclaw-agent.sqlite`) is 1.5 GB.

### Logs

```shell
[diagnostic] liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=5s degradedFor=79s eventLoopDelayP99Ms=5091.9 eventLoopDelayMaxMs=5091.9 eventLoopUtilization=1 cpuCoreRatio=0.017 active=6 waiting=0 queued=0 work=[active=agent:main:probe-…(processing/tool_call,q=0,age=73s last=codex_app_server:notification:item/completed)|…]
[diagnostic] liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1453ms elapsed=31453ms; deferring recovery decisions
[sessions] slow session list operation=sessions.list … handlerElapsedMs=5139 phaseDurationsMs={"setup":0,"modelCatalog":5122,…} … yieldWaitMs=5122 yieldCount=1
[agent/embedded] agent cleanup failed: runId=… sessionId=… step=codex-native-hook-relay-release error=SQLite transaction admission was refused
[memory] sync failed (session update): SqliteWorkerError: SQLite transaction admission was refused

# production run of the same shape (6 parallel turns, 360 s timeout):
[ws] … stream=lifecycle … phase=finishing aborted=true error=codex app-server execution budget timed out
[ws] … stream=lifecycle … phase=error error=Codex cancellation could not confirm the turn stopped; background terminals may still be running.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`eventLoopDelayP99Ms` sits at ~5000 ms in every warning, which matches `ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 5e3` in `dist/sqlite-worker-operation-admission-*.mjs`. In that module the worker blocks in `Atomics.wait(decision, 0, REQUESTED, ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS)` until the owner thread grants admission through a `MessagePort` handler. The stall itself shows ELU = 1 at about 2% CPU. That pattern fits the owner thread blocking synchronously on the worker until the 5 s admission timeout refuses the request, but I have not confirmed this in source. It is a hypothesis from the numbers, not a verified root cause.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any deployment that runs ≥3 agent turns at once (parallel fan-out plugins, overlapping cron jobs, several busy chats)
- Severity: blocks workflow. The fan-out job failed outright (0/6 turns within the deadline), and every other session on the gateway lagged while it ran.
- Frequency: always at ≥3 concurrent turns (3/3 attempts); never at 1–2
- Consequence: turns that were effectively complete were aborted by the deadline, the scheduled job didn't deliver, and replies on other channels were delayed

### Additional information

Last known good: 2026.9.4, with 6 parallel turns every day up to 2026-09-22. First known bad: 2026.9.5, on the first scheduled run after the upgrade (2026-09-23). Workaround: cap concurrency at 2 in the fan-out. With that cap, 6 turns completed in 36–113 s each with 0 liveness warnings. Possibly related, but broader: #153257, which mentions `SQLite transaction admission was refused` among other 2026.9.5 symptoms, and #144460, a main thread in futex wait on 2026.9.2.

issues.body:
### Summary

Reduce the memory cost of starting an idle Gateway before its first agent turn. OpenClaw 2026.9.5 on macOS arm64 uses about **560 MiB physical footprint with plugins disabled, empty state, and no channel/model activity**. This is a performance improvement request with a measured baseline, not a demonstrated regression or unbounded leak.

### Problem to solve

The Gateway occupies a substantial part of workstation RAM immediately after launch. Removing user history and disabling plugins does not remove this baseline. A separate uninstrumented process confirmed that the footprint is not introduced by the heap profiler or measurement preload.

Environment: OpenClaw **2026.9.5 / ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9**, installed npm distribution; **Node v26.7.0**, macOS **27.0 (26A428)**, arm64, 24 GiB RAM. Measurements were taken on September 23, 2026.

### Evidence/examples

The plain run had no inspector, preload, patched APIs, `--expose-gc`, or forced GC. `vmmap -summary` at both 15 and 24 seconds reported:

```text
Physical footprint:         559.7M
Physical footprint (peak):  566.8M
App-Specific Tag 16:        423.0M resident / dirty
Malloc zones total:         86.1M resident / dirty
Page tables:                38.5M
```

A separate diagnostic run measured **562.5 MiB physical footprint before GC**, close to the uninstrumented run. After GC, the main isolate retained **175.8 MiB heapUsed**, and the SQLite store worker retained **27.5 MiB**. These isolate metrics do not account for the complete OS footprint.

The main-isolate heap snapshot contained:

| Snapshot node type | Self size, MiB |
|---|---:|
| Strings | 75.88 |
| Code, bytecode and associated metadata | 41.47 |
| Arrays | 23.05 |
| Objects | 13.12 |
| Closures | 7.59 |
| Object shapes | 7.50 |
| Hidden | 7.38 |

About **47.6 MiB of source-text strings** matched **3,061 distinct prefixes of installed dist modules**. The snapshot truncates long string names at 1,024 characters, so these were matched by their first 1,024 characters; seven prefix groups had ambiguous filenames. This establishes retained source text, not a complete module-execution trace.

Large retained sources include `builtin-openclaw`, `openclaw-tools`, `embedded-agent`, `agent-runner`, `state-migrations.doctor`, `resource-loader`, `get-reply`, and bundled channel configuration metadata.

**Reproduction:** use the version/platform above, create a fresh temporary home/state/workspace, and write this config, replacing `<TEMP_WORKSPACE>` with a path inside the temporary directory:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "mode": "local",
    "bind": "loopback",
    "auth": { "mode": "none" },
    "controlUi": { "enabled": false }
  },
  "plugins": { "enabled": false },
  "discovery": { "mdns": { "mode": "off" } },
  "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "<TEMP_WORKSPACE>" } }
}
```

Start the installed `dist/index.js` directly:

```text
/absolute/path/to/node --max-old-space-size=8192 \
  /absolute/path/to/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js \
  gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 19789
```

Use a clean subprocess environment: `HOME` points to the temporary home, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` point to the temporary state/config, and `TMPDIR` points inside it. Set `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1`, and `NO_COLOR=1`; retain only a basic executable `PATH` and `USER`. Do not pass production credentials or copy existing state. The startup log should report **0 plugins**. Send no messages. Run `vmmap -summary <new-gateway-pid>` after 15 and 24 seconds, then terminate only that temporary process.

This measures fresh process startup; filesystem caches were not flushed.

### Proposed solution

Profile and reduce the startup import graph, moving heavy agent/tool runtime loading to first use where behavior permits. One concrete candidate is the unconditional `sidecars.reply-runtime` prewarm:

- [Gateway prewarm caller in v2026.9.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.ts)
- [Reply runtime imports in v2026.9.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-helpers.ts)

The installed code calls `prewarmConfigDrivenReplyRuntime()`, which preloads the session-update, embedded-agent and agent-runner runtimes. A separate import-only probe observed roughly 45 MiB additional main heap for reply prewarm. **The full-Gateway memory benefit of deferring it has not been measured**, and it is not established as the sole cause of the footprint.

Please measure both idle footprint and first-turn latency when evaluating a change. A small empty-state startup memory regression benchmark would make the baseline visible.

### Alternatives considered

- Disabling plugins and using empty state: this is already the reported reproduction.
- Smaller V8 heap ceiling: in separate diagnostic runs, reducing old space from 8,192 to 512 MiB changed pre-GC RSS from 592.8 to 535.8 MiB, while post-GC main heap remained 175.8 vs 175.4 MiB. It changes allocation/GC behavior without removing the retained runtime. This is not a recommendation to cap a production Gateway at 512 MiB.
- Forced GC: after both measured isolates collected, RSS was still 548.1 MiB with the 8,192 MiB ceiling; physical footprint was 515.1 MiB at 24 seconds.

### Impact

Observed on one macOS workstation in both plain and instrumented fresh processes: hundreds of MiB are occupied before any user request. This is a resource-efficiency concern; these tests established no crash, failed reply, or data loss. Cross-platform prevalence and a supported minimum footprint are unknown.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

### Additional information

All figures are MiB. RSS, physical footprint and heap snapshot self sizes are different metrics and are not interchangeable or additive. Individual runs are not a statistical benchmark. The snapshot itself temporarily increased RSS; those samples are excluded above. No earlier release or current-main runtime comparison was performed.

Related: #145679 tracks broader startup/history/streaming work. This request isolates empty-Gateway memory. #155728 and #155773 concern large binary capture allocations; this reproduction has all plugins disabled and does not load Codex.

issues.body:
# Bug: App "Update" 按钮失败 - plugin-target-unavailable

## 现象
用户在 OpenClaw Desktop App 点击"更新"按钮，失败并提示：
```
plugin-target-unavailable
Exit code: 1; packages or registry are available, use openclaw update --tag <older-version>, 
or disable the affected plugin and retry.
```

## 根因
当用户安装了自定义插件（通过 `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/` 安装），且这些插件的 `package.json` 包含 `overrides` 字段时，`control-ui` 触发路径在 validating 阶段会因 npm peerDependencies 冲突而失败。

受影响的自定义插件示例：
- `@openclaw/deepseek-provider` (path: `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-deepseek-provider-*/package.json`)
- `@openclaw/duckduckgo-plugin` (path: `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-duckduckgo-plugin-*/package.json`)

这些插件的 `package.json` 中有 ~30 个 `overrides` 条目，用于锁定依赖版本。当 App 触发更新时，validation 步骤尝试解析这些插件与新 core 版本的兼容性，npm overrides 导致解析失败。

## 对比
- **CLI 路径** (`openclaw update --yes`)：✅ 正常工作
- **App control-ui 路径**：❌ 失败，plugin-target-unavailable

## 复现步骤
1. 安装带有 npm overrides 的自定义插件
2. 在 App 中点击"更新"按钮
3. 失败，错误码 plugin-target-unavailable

## 临时解决方案
```bash
# 1. 禁用自定义插件
openclaw plugins disable deepseek duckduckgo
# 2. 执行更新
openclaw update --yes
# 3. 重新启用
openclaw plugins enable deepseek duckduckgo
```

## 建议修复方向
`control-ui` 触发路径的 validation 步骤应跳过或宽容处理自定义插件（非 stock 插件）的 peerDependencies 冲突，与 CLI 路径保持一致。或者在 validation 失败时给出更明确的错误信息，指示用户禁用特定插件后重试。

## 系统信息
- OpenClaw 版本: 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
- Node 版本: v24.21.0
- 平台: macOS 15.8 (x64)
- 自定义插件数量: 3 (deepseek, duckduckgo, lean-offline)

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

## Summary

An observed gateway preparation pause delayed the first model request by about two minutes and coincided with a 122.8-second heartbeat timer overrun and channel reconnection.

## Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The same running gateway normally completes preparation in seconds. Later observed turns in the same conversation completed preparation in under four seconds; the observed two-minute heartbeat gap is abnormal relative to the recovered gateway.

## Actual behavior

One request reached the gateway, then the aggregate preparation interval labeled session-resource-loader took 124,108 ms. The model call started only after this interval. The gateway then reported a 122,811 ms heartbeat gap, and WhatsApp reconnected. The eventual reply was acknowledged about 167 seconds after arrival. Mac power logs did not show a corresponding sleep/wake transition.

## OpenClaw version

Observed release string: OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (2b26444). The deployment carries previously reviewed local changes. The new incident diagnostic patch has not been applied. These observations have not been reproduced on current upstream main.

## Operating system

macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon; gateway Node 24.21.0.

## Install method

Source checkout with a launchd-managed gateway and a versioned runtime build.

## Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw embedded agent through the configured OpenAI subscription route. The measured pause preceded the model call.

## Additional provider/model setup details

Durable SQLite-backed conversation. Exact private history is unavailable for public sharing. This report does not claim that database size or the aggregate preparation label identifies the underlying cause.

```text
original request: received t=0
preparation: session-resource-loader=124108ms
heartbeat overrun: gapMs=122811
model request starts after preparation
WhatsApp reconnect: approximately t=139s
reply send acknowledged: approximately t=167s
```
Durations and ordering are extracted from production logs. Identifiers and message contents are omitted.

A separate process loaded the exact runtime resource loader in 1.7 ms; settings preparation took 305 ms. A consistent database snapshot reproduced a 16.9-second event-loop block while opening the database, with CPU profiling showing about 16.6 seconds inside a full SQLite integrity check. No matching slow database-open record from the gateway process was found for the original incident, so this is a separate reproduced concern, not an established explanation for the 124-second pause.

2. Capture the delayed operation during a recurrence, or reproduce it with an isolated synthetic database/history fixture. Keep the separate integrity-check reproduction separate unless the live path is demonstrated.

issues.body:
## Environment

OpenClaw Gateway, multi-agent deployment (7 agents, heavy `sessions_send` inter-agent routing), lossless-claw context engine.

## What happened

During one week of operation, a gateway restart and a preflight-compaction failure left admitted inputs stranded as `interrupted` in `pendingInputs` across many sessions. Per current design (`docs/concepts/session-tool.md`: "Cancelled and interrupted inputs are retained for inspection and never run automatically"), these inputs never run, are never re-queued, and nothing notifies the sender.

Observed impact on one deployment:

- 37 interrupted items accumulated on one agent, 14–18 on another, 4 on a third
- a receipt that arrived **2.3 days late** because its send was interrupted and required manual re-send
- a 16-item queue only cleared by a full session reset

## Root-cause decomposition (three stacked factors, not a single bug)

1. **Design**: interrupted inputs never replay — safe default, but there is no opt-in recovery path.
2. **Trigger**: (a) gateway restarts interrupt in-flight/queued runs across all sessions simultaneously; (b) preflight compaction failure (full sessions near the context limit) rejects new runs, converting accepted inputs into `interrupted`.
3. **Amplification**: no owner-facing queue summary, no sender notification, no dismiss/bulk-dismiss path — interrupted items accumulate invisibly until someone inspects the session manually.

## Additional findings from the same incident

- With a context engine (lossless-claw) configured, sessions that were already full when the engine was enabled never bootstrap a conversation record. Preflight compaction then delegates to the engine, gets `no_conversation_found`, and rejects the run — a self-locking deadlock (full → cannot turn → cannot bootstrap → cannot compact). We had to reset the affected sessions to recover.
- The deadlock starts at a gateway restart (observed from 2026-09-18 21:50) and silently affects every session that was near its context limit at that moment (11–12 sessions in our deployment; hourly `compact: skipped ... reason=no_conversation_found` maintenance logs, 84/69/128 occurrences across three days).
- The built-in `migrate-sessions` tooling only imports JSONL-native transcripts; SQLite-backed session transcripts cannot be imported to pre-seed a context-engine conversation — there is no bootstrap/reingest CLI for row-less sessions.
- The compaction-size threshold appears to be keyed to the wrong model identifier in our setup (summary model `sglcompact/GraphenModel` vs runtime `sgl2/GLM5.3`), so thresholds don't match the session's real budget.
- `sessions_send` to a group lane requires the full route-suffixed session key; the base key fails with "No session found" — easy to misconfigure at call sites.
- Repeated empty route envelopes (no message content) arrive on group lanes — apparently announce/redundant delivery markers; hard to distinguish from real empty messages.
- Failed `sessions_send` calls (e.g. `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`, `sentBeforeError=true`) can leave a residual delivery that the receiving side sees — sender sees an error while the receiver sees noise; bookkeeping is inconsistent between the two sides.

## Workaround (manual recovery, verified in production)

Two paths unlock a deadlocked session:

1. **Surgical truncation** (does not destroy the session): export-trajectory archive (12 sessions, ~62,800 events) → `sessions compact --max-lines` truncate below the preflight threshold (observed: 300 lines insufficient, 50 lines passed; threshold ≈ effective context-engine budget 128K × threshold factor) → next run starts → ingestion auto-creates the conversation row.
2. **Session reset**: rebuilds context from scratch (persistent state in workboard/files unaffected), but loses in-session context and clears stranded pending inputs.

Both require an operator who already understands the deadlock — see feature request (e).

## Feature requests (fix suggestions)

- (a) **Opt-in auto-replay for interrupted inputs** — a per-agent or per-channel setting to re-queue interrupted (not cancelled) inputs on next successful run start, or an explicit "replay" action on a pending input.
- (b) **Queue visibility** — surface a count of queued/interrupted inputs per session in the Control UI (badge/banner) and/or via `session_status`, so accumulation is visible without opening each session.
- (c) **Sender notification on interrupt** — when an admitted input becomes `interrupted`, notify the sending session (or channel) with an actionable message, instead of the current silent strand.
- (d) **Context-engine fallback** — when the configured context engine has no conversation record for a session, preflight compaction should fall back to native compaction instead of failing the run.
- (e) **Out-of-band bootstrap** — support bootstrapping a context-engine conversation record for a full/inactive session — e.g. from existing transcript history (including SQLite-backed transcripts, not only JSONL) — without requiring a successful turn first; a CLI or `migrate-sessions` extension would cover the deadlock precondition. The truncation workaround above proves bootstrap can be achieved out-of-band, but only through manual surgery an operator must already know to perform — a built-in path would remove the deadlock precondition entirely.
- (f) **Threshold keyed to runtime model** — compaction-size thresholds should resolve against the session's runtime model id, not a summary/engine model id, so the effective budget matches reality.

## Evidence available on request

Per-session interrupted counts with timestamps, gateway/compaction error excerpts, the 2.3-day-late receipt chain (run IDs), and the reset-recovery transcript.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Regression (introduced by #128610)
**Beta release blocker:** No

## Summary

PR #128610 routes delivery-failure alerts to a fallback destination when the primary thread matches the announce route. For the PR's own target configuration (threaded primary announce + `delivery.failureDestination` set + no explicit `failureAlert.to`), the new condition flips `alternateRoute` to true and `maybeEmitDeliveryFailureAlert` fires on **every failed run** — there is no threshold, cooldown, or dedupe on this path. A broken topic + an every-minute job spams the fallback chat 1,440 alerts/day.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Job config: `every: 60_000`, primary delivery into thread 42 of a chat, `delivery.failureDestination` pointing at the same chat (top-level), no explicit `failureAlert.to`.
2. Delete topic 42 (or otherwise break primary delivery).
3. Let two consecutive runs finish with ok status + failed delivery.

## Expected behavior

Failure alerts should be policy-gated like every sibling path (threshold via `after`, cooldown via `lastFailureAlertAtMs`) so a permanently broken route produces bounded notifications.

## Actual behavior

Verified at pinned SHA:

- New condition `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts:170-176`: with failureDestination present + primary `threadId != null` + no `jobConfig.to`, `primaryRouteMatches` no longer suppresses the alternate-route flag (old code did).
- `maybeEmitDeliveryFailureAlert` (`failure-alerts.ts:313-326`) gates ONLY on `alertConfig.alternateRoute`; it never reads/writes `lastFailureAlertAtMs` and has no `after` check — contrast the sibling gated path at `:368-389`.
- Wiring fires on EVERY `status:"ok" && completionStatus:"failed"` outcome (`src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.ts:201-205`), and the gateway sender is unconditional (`src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:333-399`).

Unit repro: build that job, call the finalizer twice with ok/failed-delivery results spaced arbitrarily; assert `sendCronFailureAlert` called twice with nothing set in between. Contrast: two consecutive `status:"error"` runs inside `cooldownMs` emit once.

Related context: #128267 asks for conditioning/cooldown on the cron *announce* delivery path; this issue tracks the concrete unbounded-alert regression on the *failure-alert* path introduced by #128610.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: cron users relying on fallback failure alerts during outages (exactly when they fire).
- Severity: alert storms drown the very channel meant to surface failures; can trigger channel rate limits/costs.
- Frequency: one alert per failed run until fixed.

## 1. What changed vs #154971

- **(a) external probe** — out-of-process 5s polling monitor (WebSocket upgrade vs 127.0.0.1:18789); records `host_gap` events when its own timer skips >30s (= host frozen), plus per-tick attempt records with phase and timestamp
- **(b) the gateway's own `host timing gap detected` events** (frozenMs + detection timestamp)

Result:

| hold (UTC+8, 09-21) | duration | operation | verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 09:12:21 → 09:12:55 | **33.2s** | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 21:42:41 → 21:43:03 | 21.1s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 16:54:46 → 16:55:04 | 17.1s | cron.job-family-adoption | ✅ verified clean |
| 17:27:34 → 17:27:46 | 11.7s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 19:15:38 → 19:15:50 | 11.6s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 11:35:27 → 11:35:38 | 10.0s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 13:40:08 → 13:40:16 | 7.5s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 20:16:15 → 20:16:22 | 7.0s | agent.write | ✅ verified clean |
| 07:55:34 → 07:55:40 | 5.9s | (unlabeled) | ✅ verified clean |

Corrections: the **65.5s hold is withdrawn** as core evidence (external probe shows host awake and port answering — 811/812 upgrades OK in the surrounding window — but the gateway's freeze detector reported a 3246.7s "freeze" covering the hold; can't currently distinguish app-level hold from detector artifact). The **187.9s hold was already attributed host-level** in the OP (BitLocker volume decryption, System event Id 24580, 10:19:52). Full stats from the OP still stand: 70 WARNs in 2 days, P50 2.2s / P95 17.1s, 22 of 70 = `agent.write`, plus read-path ops (`sessions.history.read` ×4, `sessions.list.title-probes` ×1) appearing in slow-transaction warnings under WAL mode.

## 2. The verified problem

On a healthy awake Windows 11 desktop (i7-11700F, 32 GB, NVMe; single gateway via scheduled task; OpenClaw **2026.9.4** npm; Node 24.18.0; main agent WAL only **4.2 MB**, freelist=3 — not the giant-WAL pathology of #143524):

- 9 dual-monitor-verified single transactions hold the SQLite write lock **5.9s–33.2s**, all while the host is awake (0 probe host_gaps in every window) and no disk-level event is recorded
- `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` ⇒ every writer queued behind any of these holds is **guaranteed** a SQLITE_BUSY timeout by parameter design, then retries blind
- any such hold also blocks WAL checkpointing — the "original Windows holder" #154302 explicitly left unidentified. 9 verified occurrences in 2 days on one small, well-checkpointed DB says the holder is not rare or exotic

Per-tick probe records around a verified hold (09:12:21–09:12:55, verbatim from probe log):

```
09:12:01.012Z phase=upgraded
09:12:06.014Z phase=upgraded
... (continuous 5s upgrades throughout the hold window)
09:12:56.019Z phase=upgraded
```

## 3. New finding: `host timing gap detected` reports freezes the process did not have

- Window A: gateway logged `host timing gap detected: process was frozen ~3246668ms` (detected 12:39:41, claimed freeze start ~11:45:34). In that window the external probe performed **812 WebSocket upgrades: 811 OK** (single isolated 5s timeout). Gateway's own log stalled 3191s (11:45:18 → 12:38:29, 18 lines).
- Window B: gateway claimed `frozen ~3158634ms` (15:33–16:25). Probe: **647/647 OK**.

So `host timing gap detected` does not measure process liveness — it fires on the gateway's own log/heartbeat stall while the process keeps serving. Two consequences:

1. heuristics (including consumers of the new `checkpoint.readerDiagnostics`) that read `host timing gap` as "process was frozen" will mis-attribute stalls on Windows;
2. conversely, it's a cheap discriminator: log-stall + external prober served normally = logging/heartbeat pipeline stall, not a frozen process.

## 4. Toward reproduction (responding to the review of #154971)

1. **Live native capture on next occurrence** — the probe host has ETW/ProcMon capture scripts already wired to wedges; we can extend the trigger to any slow-transaction-hold >5s and attach the holding thread's native stack (directly addresses "the original Windows holder remains unidentified").
2. **Upstream one-shot instrumentation** — if `slow SQLite transaction hold` logged a bounded SQL digest or a minidump of the holding thread, every Windows user's logs would identify the holder class immediately. Happy to test a canary.
3. **We can run any repro script you provide** on this host and report results with the same dual-monitor verification.

## Raw records (gist)

- `holds-all-70.jsonl` — all 70 holds, parsed (time, elapsedMs, operation, pid, threadId, isMainThread, database, thresholdMs, traceId, spanId)
- `holds-over-5s-raw.jsonl` — verbatim raw log lines for every hold >5s
- `clean-holds-verified.json` — the 9 verified holds (start/end, operation, traceId, verifying monitors)
- `probe-vs-freeze-detector.md` — freeze-detector analysis with per-tick probe records

issues.body:
**Environment**
- Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.10 (2026-07-31); the mechanism is unchanged in our reading of 2026.8.1-beta.3 but not re-tested there
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; Mattermost + Telegram channels

**Symptom**
When a pending exec is approved from outside the requesting thread (e.g. `/approve <id>` typed at DM top level), the async completion event can be delivered into a *different* session than the one that issued the command. Observed: a fresh, context-free session received "An async command the user already approved has completed… Exec finished (gateway id=…, session=…)" with **no command echo and no output**, and the agent (correctly) answered "I don't have context on what task we were working on… I'd rather not guess." Separately, some completions report "(no output recorded)" with exit 0 for commands that must produce output.

**Why it matters**
Multi-flow concurrency is the normal state for an always-on agent (tasks + inbound email at once). Approval ids are surface-agnostic, so users approve from wherever they are; completions that do not return to the requesting session with their payload strand the original task and waste a turn asking "what were we doing?".

**Proposed direction**
(a) Route async exec completion events to the **requesting session** regardless of where the approval was typed; (b) include the **original command line** (and the requesting session/task label) in the completion event; (c) investigate the "(no output recorded)" exit-0 capture gap for approved async execs.

**Workaround we're using locally**
A local session-forwarding patch for `approvals.exec`, plus user practice of approving in-thread.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 running under WSL2 with a systemd user service enters a repeated Gateway restart loop after `gateway.restart`.

Related to #75115, but not identical: after the initial `gateway.restart`, the service continues entering a clean shutdown/restart loop even after `openclaw gateway install --force`, with no second persistent external Gateway process found.

The Gateway starts normally, begins serving HTTP, then shuts down cleanly after approximately 10 seconds. systemd starts it again, and the cycle repeats. `EADDRINUSE` appears to be secondary to the repeated restart lifecycle, rather than the initial cause.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.5
- Host: Windows with WSL2
- Service manager: systemd user service
- Node.js: OpenClaw-managed Node.js 24.19.0
- Service: `openclaw-gateway.service`
- Port: 18789
- `Restart=always`
- `RestartSec=5`
- `TimeoutStopSec=330`
- `KillMode=mixed`
- Single Gateway instance
- No additional legacy Gateway service detected

## Reproduction / observed sequence

The recurring sequence is:

1. `starting HTTP server`
2. Gateway remains alive for approximately 10 seconds
3. `gmail watcher stopped`
4. `shutdown completed cleanly`
5. systemd starts the service again
6. The same sequence repeats

The logs also show:

- `restart-loop breaker tripped`
- `gateway already running under systemd; waiting 5000ms before retrying startup`
- subsequent port-in-use/EADDRINUSE symptoms

One explicit lifecycle trigger was recorded:

`restart (SIGTERM: gateway.restart)`

After that trigger, the repeated cycles continued without a new external `openclaw gateway restart` command being observed.

No new external restart command or config mutation was observed between subsequent clean shutdowns.

## Checks already performed

- CLI and service configuration paths match.
- Only one Gateway service/process was found.
- No additional Gateway service was detected by OpenClaw diagnostics.
- `openclaw gateway install --force` was executed.
- The temporary operator `RestartSec=60` override was removed.
- The generated service definition now uses the standard `RestartSec=5`.
- The restart loop continues after reinstalling the managed service definition.
- Pairing, Companion, Telegram, models, OAuth, and CUA were not changed during this investigation.

## Related issues

This appears related to #75115, which describes a systemd `Restart=always` and `openclaw gateway restart` race causing competing Gateway processes and EADDRINUSE.

It may also be related to #17125, which describes a Gateway restart/update creating an orphan process outside systemd control.

The current case differs because the observed repeated shutdowns are logged as clean shutdowns, and the loop persists after `openclaw gateway install --force` restored the managed service definition.

## Expected behavior

Under systemd, a Gateway restart should be delegated to the service manager or otherwise terminate in a way that prevents competing Gateway processes and restart loops.

A healthy Gateway should remain running after one managed restart and should continue to own port 18789.

## Diagnostic attachments

Sanitized diagnostic bundle:

`openclaw-gateway-restart-loop.zip`

Sanitized stability export:

`openclaw-diagnostics-2026-09-21T12-46-52-245Z-4134.zip`

Additional systemd journal and Gateway logs are available if required.

No workaround or manual source patch has been applied.

labels.name: clawsweeper:needs-product-decision

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Native Ollama requests made through plugin `api.runtime.llm.complete()` preserve an explicit `reasoning: "off"` through the simple-completion path, but the raw Ollama `/api/chat` request builder does not serialize it as top-level `think: false`. Thinking models can therefore consume a small output allowance entirely as hidden reasoning and return empty visible text.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw `2026.9.6` from npm and configure native Ollama with `qwen3.5:2b`.
2. From a plugin, call `api.runtime.llm.complete()` with a small token limit and explicit reasoning disablement:

   ```ts
   await api.runtime.llm.complete({
     messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Classify this request as JSON." }],
     maxTokens: 24,
     reasoning: "off",
   });
   ```

3. Inspect the native Ollama `/api/chat` request. The call flows through:

   ```text
   api.runtime.llm.complete()
   -> completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel()
   -> completeSimple()
   -> createRawOllamaStreamFn()
   -> Ollama /api/chat
   ```

4. Observe that the request has no top-level `think` value, so Ollama uses the model default.

### Expected behavior

An explicit plugin request of `reasoning: "off"` should override any configured/default thinking behavior and serialize to Ollama's documented top-level request parameter:

```json
{ "think": false }
```

With that mapping applied locally, the same classifier request returned:

```text
text: "{\"category\": \"code\"}"
stopReason: "stop"
outputTokens: 7
```

### Actual behavior

`createRawOllamaStreamFn()` maps `maxTokens`, `temperature`, `topP`, penalties, `seed`, and stop sequences, then builds top-level request params from model configuration only. It does not translate the per-call `options.reasoning` value into Ollama's top-level `think` parameter.

Observed result with `qwen3.5:2b` and `maxTokens: 24`:

```text
text: ""
stopReason: "length"
outputTokens: 24
```

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Noble Numbat), release 24.04

### Install method

npm

### Model

ollama/qwen3.5:2b

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw plugin `api.runtime.llm.complete()` -> simple completion -> native Ollama transport -> Ollama `/api/chat`

### Additional provider/model setup details

Ollama server version: `0.33.2`.

Native Ollama transport (`api: "ollama"`). The issue is specific to direct plugin simple completions, not the normal agent streaming path.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

The published `2026.9.6` bundle preserves `params.reasoning` in `runtime.llm.complete()` and passes it into `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel()`. The simple-completion executor then forwards it as `options.reasoning`.

In the bundled Ollama transport, `createRawOllamaStreamFn()` constructs `requestParams` as:

```ts
const requestParams = {
  ...(isLocalOllama ? { truncate: false, shift: false } : {}),
  ...resolveOllamaTopLevelParams(model),
  ...(responseFormat !== undefined ? { format: responseFormat } : {}),
};
```

There is no per-call reasoning mapping. Current `main` at `5fd7c3d95e03c1acbbfe180991309fe99d6a9fa3` has the same gap in `extensions/ollama/src/stream.runtime.ts`.

Ollama's API contract defines `think` as a top-level `/api/chat` parameter. `false` requests no thinking; omission uses the model default. See:

- https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking
- https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md#generate-a-chat-completion

The narrow confirmed fix is to let an explicit per-call `reasoning: "off"` override model-level top-level params:

```ts
const requestParams = {
  ...(isLocalOllama ? { truncate: false, shift: false } : {}),
  ...resolveOllamaTopLevelParams(model),
  ...(options?.reasoning === "off" ? { think: false } : {}),
  ...(responseFormat !== undefined ? { format: responseFormat } : {}),
};
```

Placing the override after `resolveOllamaTopLevelParams(model)` is intentional: explicit request intent should win over configured `think: true`. Checking the exact `"off"` value also preserves configured behavior when reasoning is omitted.

Suggested regression cases:

- Explicit `reasoning: "off"` overrides configured `think: true` with top-level `think: false`.
- Omitted reasoning preserves the existing configured `think` value.

Broader effort mapping (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `adaptive`, `max`) should be handled separately with model-capability coverage. This report directly validates only `"off" -> false`.

Related issues #50702 and #50712 covered the normal agent streaming compatibility wrapper. That path receives `thinkingLevel` and injects top-level `think`. Plugin `runtime.llm.complete()` uses the direct simple-completion path and passes per-call `options.reasoning` to the raw transport, so the existing wrapper fix does not cover this case.

The local edit to the installed `dist/` bundle is only a workaround and will be overwritten by npm reinstall/update.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: plugin authors using `api.runtime.llm.complete()` with native Ollama thinking models.
- Severity: medium; short classifier/extraction calls can return an empty string without an error.
- Frequency: reproduced when explicit `reasoning: "off"` is combined with a thinking-default model and a small output limit.
- Consequence: plugins receive `stopReason: "length"` and no visible result even though they explicitly disabled reasoning.

### Additional information

This is not a request to change the normal agent streaming wrapper. The missing serialization is in the native Ollama simple-completion request builder used by plugin runtime calls.

issues.body:
**Two reproducible defects in the session lifecycle CLI on 2026.9.5 (Windows, Node 24.18.0), found while trying to slim a large agent DB without restarting the gateway.** Both make the "delete/archive old sessions to reclaim space" workflow unusable.

### 1. `sessions delete` / `sessions archive` report `not_found` for keys returned verbatim by `sessions list`

```
$ openclaw sessions list --agent <agent> --json --limit 1
{ "sessions": [ { "key": "agent:<agent>:subagent:2c9b9456-…", "sessionId": "e0a3c61b-…",
                  "status": "done", "ageMs": 196582, … } ] }

$ openclaw sessions delete --agent <agent> --dry-run --json "agent:<agent>:subagent:2c9b9456-…"
{ "ok": false, "results": [ { "key": "agent:<agent>:subagent:2c9b9456-…", "ok": false,
  "status": "not_found",
  "error": "Session not found. Run openclaw sessions list --agent <agent> --json to choose a valid key." } ] }
```

Same for `sessions archive`. The key was copied from the immediately preceding `sessions list` output, and the same failure occurs with a session that was updated **4.9 minutes** earlier, so it is not staleness. Several keys, all deterministic.

**Root cause looks like an internal param mismatch.** The lifecycle code resolves keys by paging `sessions.list` and matching `row.key` (`listRequestedSessions`). Calling that RPC the way the CLI does returns nothing:

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.list --params '{"limit":5,"agentId":"<agent>"}'
{ "sessions": [], "totalCount": 0, "hasMore": false }        # 0 rows

$ openclaw gateway call sessions.list --params '{"limit":5,"agentId":"<agent>","archived":"all",
    "includeGlobal":true,"includeUnknown":true,"configuredAgentsOnly":true}'
{ "sessions": [], "totalCount": 0, "hasMore": false }        # 0 rows
```

while the CLI list command on the same gateway returns 174 sessions for that agent. (`agent` is rejected: `invalid sessions.list params: at root: unexpected property 'agent'`, so `agentId` is the documented field — the CLI list path must be passing something else.) Because the resolver gets an empty page, `hasMore !== true` and it breaks out, then every requested key is reported as `not_found`.

### 2. `sessions delete` does not remove SQLite transcript rows

The delete itself succeeds when the RPC is called directly, but it only archives the session-store file:

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.delete --params '{"key":"agent:<agent>:subagent:6604d197-…","agentId":"<agent>"}'
{ "ok": true, "key": "agent:<agent>:subagent:6604d197-…", "deleted": true,
  "archived": ["…\\agents\\<agent>\\sessions\\6fc802cd-….jsonl.deleted.2026-09-21T06-30-54.097Z.….zst"] }
```

Measured around that call (SQLite transcript store):

```
before:                    after:
transcript_events rows for that session: 72     72
agent DB size:            1516.9 MB             1516.9 MB
```

So the agent SQLite DB — the thing that actually grows to GB and drives the WAL/stall issues — is untouched. If that is by design, it would help to say so in `sessions delete --help`; as written ("Delete stored sessions and their live artifacts … Retained archives can remain searchable") a user reasonably expects the stored session to shrink the store.

### 3. `sessions compact` fails on dashboard sessions, works on subagent sessions

```
$ openclaw sessions compact --agent <agent> --json --max-lines 50 "agent:<agent>:dashboard:bab27eb8-…"
{ "ok": false, "error": "Session agent:<agent>:dashboard:bab27eb8-… changed before compaction. Retry." }
# 3/3 retries, several minutes apart, same result

$ openclaw sessions compact --agent <agent> --json --max-lines 50 "agent:<agent>:subagent:f280fb79-…"
{ "ok": true, "compacted": true }
# rows for that session: 207 -> 50, 1.2 MB -> 0.35 MB
```

The dashboard variant fails even though the session is idle (status `done`/`timeout`, last updated 7–12 days ago) and nothing else is writing to it; `updatedAt` may be flickering for another reason (dashboard/heartbeat touches?), which would defeat the optimistic-concurrency guard. Subagent compaction works and is a genuinely useful, no-restart way to shrink a store — thanks for that path.

### Why it mattered here

This box has one agent whose SQLite store grew to ~1.5 GB (transcripts 798 MB, memory/embeddings 546 MB, trajectory 87 MB) with ~190 stored sessions, ~230 MB of it old synthetic subagent sessions and ~200 MB of dashboard sessions. The plan was to delete/compact the synthetic ones to cut the store — and every non-restart route was blocked: `delete` doesn't touch SQLite, `archive`/`delete` can't even resolve keys, `cleanup` correctly no-ops while under the disk budget (our budget had been raised on purpose, see the WAL thread), and `compact` only works for subagents. If any of these is expected behaviour, a note in the CLI help would save the next person the same afternoon.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Bug

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In Control UI, an assistant reply's text is rendered twice when that logical message is persisted as multiple records sharing one `message.id` — specifically when the message contains both a `text` block and one or more `tool_use` blocks. Turns that are pure text, or pure tool calls, render correctly.

This presents identically to #149221 but appears to be a **different cause**. That issue's signature error, `"Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot"`, occurs **zero times** in this installation's gateway logs across two days while the duplication was actively reproducing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.4 with Control UI open (local gateway, single client).
2. Send a message prompting a turn where the assistant emits narration text and then calls one or more tools in the same assistant message.
3. Observe the narration text rendered twice in Control UI.
4. Turns with no narration before tool calls, or with no tool calls at all, render once.

### Expected behavior

Records sharing a `message.id` are grouped into one rendered message; its single `text` block appears once.

### Actual behavior

The `text` block renders twice. Measured over one session:

```
logical assistant messages : 202
physical records           : 508
  single-record            : 40      (renders correctly)
  multi-record             : 162
    with exactly 1 text blk: 111     <-- duplicates
    with 0 text blocks     : 51      (nothing to duplicate)
messages with >1 text block: 0
```

No logical message ever contains more than one `text` block, so the duplication is a render-grouping failure, not duplicated content.

Concrete example — three records, one `message.id`:

```
message.id: msg_011Ceu78f3ynWMhqWwFKcKCK
  record 1: blocks=['text']      text="I'll take a look at that repo."
  record 2: blocks=['tool_use']  text=''
  record 3: blocks=['tool_use']  text=''
```

### Evidence this is distinct from #149221

- `grep -c "no active tool authority snapshot"` over `openclaw-2026-09-{16,17}.log` → **0**
- Single gateway process; single Control UI socket — duplicate processes and multi-client rendering both excluded
- The stored transcript is clean: 75 assistant text bodies, 75 unique. Content is not duplicated at rest, only in the rendered view
- `auto-reply/agent-turn-timing` fires twice for ~40% of runIds, but with *distinct* milestones (`assistant_output_started`, `tool_execution_started`) — normal telemetry, not duplicate delivery. Noted only because it correlates with the affected turns: those are exactly the runs that emit text *and* execute tools

### Workaround

Suppressing narration text in any assistant message that also carries `tool_use` blocks (emitting one or the other, never both) structurally avoids the multi-record-with-text shape. Offered as a diagnostic signal rather than a fix.

### OpenClaw version

`OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)` — build `2026.9.4-release-3a9d69db306c`

### Operating system

Linux 7.0.12+kali-amd64, gateway as a systemd **user** unit on `127.0.0.1:18789` (no Tailscale exposure, unlike #149221)

### Model / routing

`claude-cli` backend, `claude-opus-5`. Issue is in the Control UI render path, not model output.

## Summary

Recent OpenClaw releases increasingly make ordinary self-hosted administration feel less autonomous and less usable for non-technical owners. Security and approval mechanisms frequently turn the owner into a manual execution agent, even when the owner has explicitly delegated the task and controls the server, devices, subscriptions, and network.

This is a report from a long-time self-hosted user who previously set up much of the current system by securely delegating operational work through Telegram. The regression is not that safeguards exist; it is that there is often no practical, supported path from an owner's authorization to task completion.

## Concrete failure in OpenClaw 2026.9.2

Goal: onboard five identical NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices from an already managed office node.

1. The owner explicitly authorizes the work in a private Telegram conversation.
2. All five devices are online, reachable on the LAN, and expose SSH.
3. The owner provides the shared SSH credential in the private owner chat, as had worked in older operational workflows.
4. The current agent policy refuses to use it and deletes the message.
5. The owner is sent through Tailscale and the Control UI to create a protected `SSHPASS` entry.
6. The protected value is stored successfully.
7. The value cannot be consumed by `sshpass` or another arbitrary local SSH subprocess; `SSHPASS` is not present in that process environment.
8. The CLI exposes no supported protected-secret execution bridge for SSH.
9. The task remains impossible despite explicit owner authorization, a successfully stored secret, and full control of every involved machine.

The result is a long loop of prompts, UI switching, approvals, and explanations, without completing the delegated task.

## Broader usability regression

- Too many actions stop for repeated approvals even after the owner has clearly authorized a bounded task.
- Telegram, which is the owner's primary operational interface, can no longer complete common administration flows end to end.
- Protected credential intake is disconnected from practical local tools such as SSH, `sudo`, `rsync`, and bootstrap scripts.
- The system asks the owner to visit terminals, edit files, run commands, or perform physical steps instead of completing the delegated work.
- "Autonomous" operation becomes impractical because the owner must stay on the phone and approve or bridge each small step.
- The software increasingly feels optimized for an abstract security model rather than for a real owner operating trusted self-hosted infrastructure.

The owner's core question is: **Who is working for whom?** A self-hosted operator paying for the server and model subscriptions needs an explicit way to choose the risk posture for their own systems.

## Requested product changes

1. **Owner-controlled trust policy**
   - Provide an explicit, documented self-hosted operator mode for trusted private owner channels.
   - Let the owner decide whether credentials submitted through a designated private owner conversation may be used for a narrowly scoped task.
   - Keep secure defaults, but make stricter behavior an operator policy choice rather than an unavoidable dead end.

2. **Protected-secret execution bridge for local administration**
   - Allow a protected SecretRef to be attached to one explicitly authorized subprocess without exposing the value to the model, transcript, command line, logs, or child processes outside the approved scope.
   - Support common local tools and protocols, including SSH password bootstrap, `sudo`, `rsync`, and deterministic provisioning scripts.
   - The current HTTP-egress-only model is insufficient for self-hosted systems administration.

3. **Bounded approval grants**
   - Let the owner approve a whole clearly described task, target set, time window, and action class once.
   - Avoid repeated micro-approvals for every command in the same authorized workflow.
   - Surface a concise execution plan and audit log instead of forcing continuous supervision.

4. **Native credential UX in messaging channels**
   - Telegram and similar owner channels should receive a reliable one-tap link to a masked credential form bound to the exact requesting session and task.
   - The prompt must only be offered when the resulting secret is actually usable for the requested operation.

5. **Fail before burdening the owner**
   - Before asking the owner to switch apps and store a secret, OpenClaw should verify that the chosen execution path can consume that secret.
   - Do not guide the owner through a credential flow that ends in an unsupported sink.

6. **Migration transparency**
   - Release notes should explicitly call out workflow-breaking changes to approvals, credential handling, chat-channel behavior, and autonomous execution.
   - Provide a documented migration path for existing self-hosted installations.

## Desired outcome

Security should prevent accidental disclosure while still enabling authorized work. The owner should be able to delegate a bounded administrative task once, walk away, and receive a verified result. If the only supported outcome is that the owner manually performs the sensitive steps, the system is no longer functioning as an autonomous assistant for self-hosted operations.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.9.4

## Summary

Bundled plugin panels (Workboard, for example) render as **"Plugin panel unavailable — The plugin that owns this tab is not active on the connected gateway, or it did not provide a panel"** when the Control UI is reached through a reverse proxy in front of a loopback-bound gateway.

The same gateway process serves the same panel correctly over a direct connection to its loopback port. The plugin is enabled and its declared control-ui assets exist on disk.

## Reproduction

1. Gateway with `gateway.bind = "loopback"`, reached through a reverse proxy (in my case the managed Tailscale Serve ingress, `gateway.tailscale.mode = "serve"`).
2. Open the Control UI **through the proxy** → the plugin tab shows "Plugin panel unavailable".
3. Tunnel the loopback port and open it directly (`ssh -N -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port>`) → the same tab renders.

Same gateway process (verified by PID), same plugin, same browser. This isolates the proxied request path rather than remote access as such.

## What the gate is

The plugin tab grant is gated on `operator.read` in `listControlUiPluginTabAuthGrants`:

```js
function listControlUiPluginTabAuthGrants(callerScopes) {
  const registry = getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry();
  if (!registry || !authorizeOperatorScopesForRequiredScope("operator.read", callerScopes).allowed) return [];
  ...
}
```

With no `operator.read` (and no `operator.admin`, which short-circuits the check) in the caller
scopes, no plugin tab grants are produced, so `setControlUiPluginAuthCookieForRequest` issues no
cookie and the UI has no panel registration to render. That is consistent with the observed
"did not provide a panel" state, but I have **not** been able to capture the Control UI session's
own resolved scopes to prove it directly — at `logging.level = debug` the gateway logs the RPC
denials it issues, but not the handshake that produced the scope set. I would happily gather more
if there is a flag for it.

## Ruled out

- Plugin is `enabled`, `loaded`, bundled at the gateway's own version.
- Declared control-ui assets (`entry` + `styles`) exist on disk, no symlinks, within the size limits.
- Same gateway process serves both paths.
- All HTTP surfaces compared between the two paths are byte-identical, including the SPA build id.
- Paired operator devices carry `operator.admin` and `operator.read`.
- `doctor` reports nothing relevant.
- No `gateway.auth.trustedProxy` or `gateway.roles` configuration is present, so no role ceiling applies.

## Where I think it goes wrong

I could not determine from the outside which `authMethod` the proxied session resolves to, so I am not claiming a specific branch. The relevant resolution is in `setControlUiPluginAuthCookieForRequest`:

```js
const scopes = authenticatedScopes ?? (
  usesSharedSecretGatewayMethod(authMethod) ? [...CLI_DEFAULT_OPERATOR_SCOPES]
  : authMethod === "trusted-proxy" || authMethod === "tailscale"
      ? resolveTrustedHttpOperatorScopes(req, { trustDeclaredOperatorScopes })
      : []);
```

Two candidates:

1. The session does **not** resolve to `trusted-proxy`/`tailscale` and falls into the trailing `: []`, leaving it with no scopes at all.
2. It does take that branch, but `resolveTrustedHttpOperatorScopes` returns `[]` via its `shouldTrustDeclaredHttpOperatorScopes` guard — which, when no explicit `trustDeclaredOperatorScopes` is in the object, reduces to `!isGatewayBearerHttpRequest(req, auth)` and therefore yields `[]` for a bearer-authenticated request.

Either way the result is the same: a proxied Control UI session that is otherwise authenticated ends up without `operator.read`, which is the minimum the plugin tab grant requires.

## Why the documented workaround does not fit

The configuration surface for the proxied path is `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove`. Its own schema text says that granting `operator.admin` this way

> "lets every proxy-authenticated user auto-approve full admin and makes scope-less requests receive full admin automatically; it also triggers a critical security audit finding and Gateway startup warning."

That seems disproportionate for rendering a dashboard panel that only needs `operator.read`, and the default scope set deliberately excludes admin.

## Suggested direction

A proxied session that has already authenticated as an operator device should retain at least `operator.read` for plugin tab grants. If the intended contract is instead that the reverse proxy supplies `x-openclaw-scopes`, the managed Tailscale Serve ingress does not appear to set it, and that requirement is not documented.

Happy to test a patch against the reproduction above, or to supply more debug output.

issues.body:
## Summary
`openclaw memory index` (with and without `--force`) fails immediately with `Memory index failed (main): unable to open database file`
while `openclaw memory status` opens and even creates the same database without problems. The failure is inside the full-reindex path
(`extensions/memory-core`, `runInPlaceReindex`), not a permissions problem.

## Environment
OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4), Node 22.23.2 (`node:sqlite`), Linux aarch64, running inside an NVIDIA NemoClaw 0.0.123 sandbox as user `sandbox`.
`memory.search` provider `ollama-mem` (custom provider, api `ollama`) — the provider is *unavailable* (no plugin serves it; gateway logs the
FTS-only fallback). `sqlite-vec` is not installed in this runtime.

## Reproduction
```
$ openclaw memory status --json     # works, creates the DB
  dbPath /sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite, files 0, chunks 0, dirty true, provider ollama-mem, providerState pending
$ openclaw memory index --force --verbose
Memory Index (main)
Provider: ollama-mem (requested: ollama-mem)
Sources: memory (MEMORY.md + $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/workspace/memory/*.md)
[memory] sync: indexing memory files          <- debug log: {"files":0,"needsFullReindex":true,"batch":false,"concurrency":1}
Memory index failed (main): unable to open database file   <- ~10 ms later
```
Same result after deleting the database (a fresh one is created), after removing `openclaw-agent.sqlite.reindex-lock.sqlite`, after a gateway restart,
and with `workspace/memory/` present or absent.

What works from the same user in the same directory (so it is not permissions, `/tmp`, or the temp-file name):
```
$ node -e '
const {DatabaseSync}=require("node:sqlite"); const crypto=require("crypto");
const db="/sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite";
const tmp=db+".memory-reindex-"+crypto.randomUUID();           // the tempDbPath runInPlaceReindex uses
const t=new DatabaseSync(tmp,{allowExtension:true}); t.exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000"); t.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL"); t.exec("create table x(a)"); t.close();
const m=new DatabaseSync(db,{allowExtension:true}); m.exec("ATTACH DATABASE \x27"+tmp+"\x27 AS memory_reindex"); m.exec("DETACH DATABASE memory_reindex"); m.close();
console.log("temp db + attach ok")'
temp db + attach ok
```
Directory: `drwx------ sandbox sandbox /sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent`; `/tmp` writable; `TMPDIR` unset; disk 3.4 TB free.

## Expected
A full reindex on an empty memory set with an unavailable embedding provider should either build an FTS-only index or report *why* the
provider prevents it — not `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. Suspects: the provider-unavailable path or the sqlite-vec load path inside `runInPlaceReindex`
opening a path that does not exist; the error message hides which file failed.

## Ask
Surface the failing path in the error (`unable to open database file: <path>`), and make the FTS-only full reindex succeed when the embedding
provider is unavailable / sqlite-vec is missing.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Bug (something is broken)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a nested/subagent run finishes (`stopReason=stop`), its ephemeral model-runtime plugin generation is released. The next task scheduled on an affected lane still holds the old generation snapshot and fails within ~10–17 ms with `prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>`. The error is then treated as a model failure and slides the model fallback chain — but the failure is runtime-level, so every fallback candidate fails identically and the run fails before any reply is produced. The inbound user message gets no answer, and the UI surfaces "Request timed out before a response was generated", pointing the operator at timeout tuning instead of the real cause.

Three compounding defects:

1. A routine run-lifecycle boundary (subagent completion) poisons the next lane task — no config churn, hot reload, or external trigger is required.
2. A runtime-level error is classified as a per-model failure, so the whole fallback chain burns through candidates that were never going to work.
3. `run-failed-before-reply` consumes the user's message, and the timeout-framed notice misdirects diagnosis.

### Steps to reproduce

Racy but frequent on a busy multi-agent instance (95 occurrences in retained gateway logs since 2026-08-01; up to 36/day on high-activity days):

1. Run a Gateway with several agents (here: 4) doing concurrent, subagent-heavy work.
2. Let a nested/subagent run complete (`stopReason=stop`).
3. Send a user message to a session on an affected agent shortly afterwards (observed both ~2 min after a gateway restart and during normal operation with no restart involved).
4. The lane task for the new message fails in 10–17 ms with the superseded error; the fallback chain slides; no reply is produced.

### Actual behavior — logs

2026-09-12 12:14:22 — a user message was dropped; every fallback candidate failed with the same runtime error; whole burst ~80 ms end-to-end (hostnames/paths redacted):

```
12:14:22.602 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=nested:agent:<id>:main durationMs=14 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.603 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<id>:main durationMs=16 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.620 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=zai/glm-5.3 candidate=zai/glm-5.3 reason=unknown next=minimax/MiniMax-M3 detail="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.648 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=nested:agent:<id>:main durationMs=14 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.649 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<id>:main durationMs=15 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.653 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=zai/glm-5.3 candidate=minimax/MiniMax-M3 reason=unknown next=zai/glm-5.3-flash detail="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.681 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=nested:agent:<id>:main durationMs=15 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
12:14:22.682 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<id>:main durationMs=17 error="prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded for <agent-dir>"
```

2026-09-11 00:25:15 shows the identical 8-line burst shape. On that occasion our fallback chain additionally referenced a model id missing from the provider catalog (our config bug, since fixed), which turned the slide into a hard request failure — worth noting because it demonstrates how the per-model misclassification converts one transient race into total message loss whenever any fallback entry is unhealthy.

### Frequency

95 occurrences of the superseded message in retained gateway logs since 2026-08-01 on a single instance (journald retention limits how far back this count reaches); bursts track agent-activity days (36 on 2026-09-06, 26 on 09-10, 24 on 09-11). Not restart-only: reproduces during normal operation whenever a lane task starts right after a nested-run boundary.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm stable channel — current latest at time of filing
- Linux x64, Node v26.8.1
- Single gateway, 4 agents, multiple concurrent sessions; providers: zai (openai-completions) primary, minimax (anthropic-messages) fallback
- Source area per stack traces: `dist/prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs`, provenance=run/ephemeral branch (`PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError`)

### Expected behavior

- Releasing a run-scoped generation at run completion must not fail-close the next lane task: either defer the release until in-flight borrows drain, or retry against the new generation as neighboring supersede branches already do (same non-retrying throw as defect 1 in #139710, different trigger).
- A generation/runtime-level error should not be classified as a candidate model failure; the fallback chain must not slide on it.
- If a turn still fails, the user-visible notice should name the real cause instead of a timeout message, and the inbound message should not be silently consumed.

### Related

- #139710 — same error family; trigger there is a mid-turn config hot reload, symptom is the misleading "run `openclaw onboard`" advice. Here the trigger is the run-lifecycle boundary itself and the symptom is a dropped user message framed as a timeout. Both share the non-retrying throw inside the prepared-model-runtime loop.
- #139830 — cron-isolated variant on 2026.9.2, closed as not-planned.

issues.body:
### Summary

Automations cannot deliver their result to a paired node, so a scheduled report cannot reach the Android app as a notification even though the app already posts notifications for assistant replies and the node already exposes `system.notify`.

### Problem to solve

`delivery.channel` accepts only chat channel plugin ids. A paired node is not selectable as a delivery target, so an operator who wants a daily report on their phone must route it through Discord or Telegram purely to obtain a notification.

Every Gateway-side route into a node was tried, and each fails for a different structural reason:

- **`--session main`** rejects agent payloads outright: `Main jobs cannot use --message or --command; use --system-event or --session isolated.` A report that must be generated by an agent turn therefore cannot target the main session.
- **`--session session:<id>`** does not join an existing session. `normalizeSessionTarget` passes the value through `assertSafeCronSessionTargetId` and treats it as an opaque label, so targeting an existing session id mints a new session instead of appending to it.
- **`--session-key`** on an automation queues an awareness *system event* (`formatTargetCronDeliveryAwarenessText`, "A scheduled automation delivered this message to this channel:"). That is `role != assistant`, so by construction it cannot satisfy a final-assistant-reply notifier.
- **`delivery.channel`** accepts only chat channel plugin ids; there is no node target.

Additionally, `shouldDefaultCronDeliveryToAnnounce` treats `isolated`, `current`, and `session:*` alike, so such jobs default back to announce-to-a-chat-channel, and clearing the channel is not a valid "deliver nowhere" state — it fails the run: `Channel is required when multiple channels are configured: telegram, discord.`

The remaining workaround is to instruct the agent, in the job prompt, to call the `nodes` tool itself. That is unreliable in exactly the way this repo treats as the worst bug class. On a local model the tool call was emitted as literal text:

```
nodes:system.notify title="Ubuntu Security Report" body="Gateway: 6 upgradable / 0 security - shockwave: 15 upgradable / 0 security" node="OnePlus 12R"
```

No tool ran, no notification was sent, and the run still reported success — an action that silently produced nothing, with no recorded reason. A delivery target would fail loudly and be visible in automation history; a prompt instruction cannot.

### Proposed solution

Allow an automation's delivery target to name a paired node, so the existing notification path is reused rather than duplicated. Roughly `delivery.channel: "node"` with `to: "<nodeId|name>"`, resolved through the same node registry that `openclaw nodes notify` already uses, and recorded in automation history like any other delivery.

The notification half already works end to end and needs no new transport — only a way for an automation to reach it.

### Alternatives considered

- **A node channel plugin.** Duplicates a notification path the app already has, and would need its own transport, config, and delivery semantics.
- **Prompt-instructed `nodes` tool call.** Model-dependent and silently no-ops (evidence above).
- **Exec-based `openclaw nodes notify` from a `command` job.** Deterministic, but a `command` payload cannot compose the report, so it requires splitting one job into two and correlating them.
- **Keep a chat channel purely for notification.** What operators do today; the chat message is unwanted noise whose only purpose is to trigger a phone alert.

### Impact

Any operator who runs scheduled reports and wants them on a phone. Today that requires a chat channel as an intermediary, or a prompt-driven tool call that can fail silently and still report success. The capability exists on both ends — the node declares `notifications` and `system.notify`, the app posts `MessagingStyle` reply notifications with inline reply — but nothing connects an automation to it.

### Evidence/examples

Direct node notification works reliably today:

```
$ openclaw nodes notify --node "OnePlus 12R" --title "..." --body "..." --priority active --json
{"ok": true, "nodeId": "4df7cc13432e...", "command": "system.notify", "payloadJSON": null}
```

The app's own reply notifier also works, verified on Android app `2026.8.2` (`versionCode=2026080201`). Injecting an assistant turn into the app's node session with `openclaw agent --session-key agent:<agentId>:node-<shortNodeId> --message ...` posts a real notification; from `dumpsys notification` on the device:

```
NotificationRecord: pkg=ai.openclaw.app
  tag        openclaw.chat.<digest>
  channel    openclaw.chat.replies
  importance 4
  category   msg
  actions    1
```

So both halves exist. The gap is only that an automation cannot address either one.

Note `openclaw agent --session-key` *can* run an agent turn inside an existing node session, while an automation's `--session-key` only queues an awareness system event. That asymmetry between the CLI and the automation runner is the crux.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No

### Additional information

Related but distinct: #111360 requests multi-target cron delivery across several *chat* channels; this asks for a non-chat node target. #53228 requests an `openclaw notify` CLI pushing to connected UI sessions, which is a different surface (and `openclaw nodes notify` already covers part of it).

Discovered while trying to route a daily security report to a phone instead of Discord. The related notification report #142516 was closed as invalid: the app build under test predated the notifier feature. This request is unaffected by that, since it concerns Gateway-side delivery rather than app behavior.

issues.body:
## Summary

The agent-facing `dashboard` tool uses one flat schema for every action. In an empty dashboard tab, the model repeatedly emitted `after` for `widget_put` (usually equal to the widget's own name), making it impossible to add the first widget through the typed tool.

This also makes recovery difficult: `after` is optional in the implementation, but the model-facing call repeatedly included unrelated optional fields for the selected action.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.3 (`1391f7c`), current npm stable as of 2026-09-09
- Model: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`
- Surface: WebChat / Control UI
- Gateway: local loopback, reachable
- OS: Linux x64, Node 24.18.0

## Reproduction

1. Start with a session board containing no tabs or widgets.
2. Call `dashboard` with `action: "tab_create"`, `tabId: "finance"`, and a title. This succeeds.
3. Ask the agent to add the first trusted plugin widget:

```json
{
  "action": "widget_put",
  "tabId": "finance",
  "name": "finance.monthly",
  "size": "full",
  "pluginKind": "session:report",
  "props": {
    "blocks": [{"type": "text", "text": "test"}]
  }
}
```

4. The generated tool call repeatedly includes the flat schema's unrelated optional parameters, including:

```json
"after": "finance.monthly"
```

5. The server rejects the operation with:

```text
widget cannot be placed after itself
```

Using another placeholder value produces:

```text
board widget anchor not found on tab finance: <placeholder>
```

Because the tab is empty, no valid anchor exists. In this run, repeated retries continued to populate `after`; the final `dashboard read` remained at one tab and zero widgets.

## Expected

The first `widget_put` call should omit `after` and append the widget at position 0. The tool schema should make it difficult for a model to include parameters that do not apply to the selected action.

## Actual

The model-facing flat schema encourages/permits argument contamination across actions. The first widget cannot be created when the generated call self-anchors or references a nonexistent anchor.

A similar contamination happened with the `sessions` tool in the same run: a current-session `patch` repeatedly included `targets`, and the server rejected it because `targets` cannot be combined with `sessionKey`/`expectedSessionId`.

## Relevant implementation

`DashboardToolSchema` correctly marks `after` optional, but exposes every action's fields in one `Type.Object`. `insertBoardWidget()` calls `moveWidget()` when placement contains `after`, and `moveWidget()` correctly rejects a self-anchor.

## Suggested fix

Use action-discriminated schemas (`Type.Union` of per-action objects) for `dashboard` and similarly overloaded tools, so `widget_put` can clearly express placement as one of:

- no placement anchor (append/default),
- `position`, or
- `after`.

Alternatively, normalize `after === name` to omitted only when creating a new widget, though an action-specific schema would prevent more classes of invalid mixed arguments.

## Impact

Agent-authored dashboards can get stuck on an empty tab despite valid report data and a healthy board. The failure is especially confusing because tab creation, focus, presentation, and `dashboard read` all continue to work.
