issues.body:
## Summary

In Control UI `2026.9.3-release-1391f7cd2d40`, every assistant reply renders twice: once as the live-streamed text block(s), and again as the completed-run `turnRecap` block containing the same full text plus the duration footer.

The Gateway is not duplicating anything. One `chat.send`, one run, one persisted transcript record. This is purely a client-side rendering issue: the provisional streamed bubbles are not reconciled away when the final turn record renders.

## Environment

- Gateway: `2026.9.3 (1391f7c)`, mode `local`, macOS 26.3 arm64, node v24.19.0
- Control UI: `openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.3 build=2026.9.3-release-1391f7cd2d40-2026-09-08T07-46-00.264Z`
- Host: OpenClaw.app desktop shell `2026.9.2`, loading the UI from the local Gateway over `localhost:18789`
- Agent runtime: `claude-cli` (`anthropic/claude-opus-5`)
- Single agent, single session, single websocket connection

## What the user sees

For one reply, three bubbles:

```
Bubble 1:  "Path confirmed. Writing the memory file now."      <- preamble text block
           "Ran a command, created a file"                     <- tool activity indicator
Bubble 2:  [rest of the reply]                                 <- second text block
Bubble 3:  preamble + rest of the reply
           "Done in 2 minutes, 16 seconds"                     <- turnRecap
```

Bubbles 1 and 2 are the live stream. Bubble 3 is the completed-turn render. Both are retained, so the full reply appears twice on screen.

## Gateway-side evidence: single generation

```
22:19:40.872  [ws] res OK chat.send 109ms runId=f9ae78a8-06f9-4454-b9c5-ab9c0e66b46d conn=dd341ab1
22:19:41.324  [agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5
              promptChars=308 trigger=user useResume=true reuse=reusable-drift:prompt-tools
22:20:55.047  milestone=assistant_output_started runId=f9ae78a8 totalMs=74067
22:21:56.208  [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: durationMs=134881 outBytes=3869 outHash=74693f6d351f
```

One `chat.send`, one `runId`, one `cli exec`, one `cli turn`, one output hash.

`durationMs=134881` is 2m14.9s, which matches the "Done in 2 minutes, 16 seconds" recap footer, confirming bubble 3 is the completed-run render.

## Store-side evidence: single record, single content block

Querying `transcript_events` for the assistant record of that turn:

```
seq 61
content blocks: 1
  [0] text: "Path confirmed. Writing the memory file now.\n\nNot a duplicate. Two dif..."
  api: cli    stopReason: stop    length: 4490 bytes
```

The store holds the preamble and the reply already merged into a single text block on a single record. Records alternate `user` / `assistant` with no duplicates:

```
62 message user
61 message assistant
60 message user
59 message assistant
58 message user
57 message assistant
```

## Not a transport or double-mount issue

- Exactly one webchat connection for the whole period (`conn=dd341ab1`), no disconnects or reconnects
- 28 RPC calls post-restart with zero duplicated method calls
- `index.html` has a single script entry (`index-CbXUwLqm.js`); the three `control-ui-core-*.js` entries are `modulepreload` hints, not separate mounts

A separate, genuine double-mount bug did exist in `2026.9.2` (every RPC method issued twice with different ids from one socket, same millisecond) and was fixed by upgrading to `2026.9.3`. The duplicate rendering described here survived that fix and is distinct from it.

## Reproduction

1. Run the Gateway locally with the `claude-cli` runtime
2. Send a message that causes the assistant to emit a short preamble, then call a tool, then write a longer final answer
3. Observe the streamed blocks remain on screen after the `turnRecap` block renders the same content again

Turns that emit a single text block with no tool calls show the same doubling in a less obvious form, since the streamed block and the recap are identical.

## Expected

The completed-turn render should replace the provisional streamed blocks for that `runId`, leaving one bubble per assistant turn. A fresh page load already renders correctly, since it builds from the persisted store, which contains one record.

## Notes

- No server-side configuration affects this. `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault` is already at its `"off"` default and is not overridden, and `channels.webchat` has no schema since webchat is the Control UI transport rather than a configurable channel.
- The workaround is to fully quit and reopen the client, which rebuilds history from the store. It does not prevent the doubling on subsequent live turns.
- `l10n` key involved: `turnRecap.doneIn` (`"Done in {duration}"`), in `control-ui-core-BHfdLkse.js`.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add opt-in supervised TaskFlow episodes with structured goals, durable continuation ownership and explicit endpoints.

## Problem to solve

A model turn ending is not the same as a task finishing. If a coordinator disappears while a command survives, users can see activity but have no assurance that anything will collect its result or continue. Current TaskFlow intentionally persists records without automatically arranging restart continuation; controller-managed wakeups leave this responsibility fragmented.

## Proposed solution

A native controller should maintain transactional ownership of every admitted episode: executable work, a bounded durable wait/recovery action, or a recorded endpoint. Require structured goal/acceptance criteria supplied by the operator or inferred in a bounded model attempt. Endpoints are success, preaccepted partial success, input required, unrecoverable/policy-exhausted failure and cancellation. Input opens a new episode while preserving history.

Use exact owner/attempt/revision fencing, finite attempt/deadline policies and fresh status observations. Recover pre-dispatch work, but stop for reconciliation/input after an ambiguous potentially effectful dispatch rather than blindly replaying. This is an availability-qualified endpoint guarantee, not guaranteed semantic success or exactly-once external effects.

## Alternatives considered

- Progress text and Discord presence describe activity but cannot own continuation.
- Model-authored timers/heartbeats can rescue some failures but do not atomically transfer responsibility.
- A hook-only plugin cannot guarantee custody when the model/tool connection or hook itself fails.
- Preserve existing TaskFlow for legacy controllers; make stronger supervision opt-in rather than silently redefining all flows.

## Impact

Affected: operators using long-running agent workflows, including Codex and Claude CLI. Intermittent coordinator/connection failures can strand otherwise recoverable work and require repeated manual status checks and wakeups. This blocks unattended workflow completion; no urgency or universal incidence is claimed.

## Evidence/examples

Experimental implementation: https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/tree/feat/supervised-task-poc-ugqq at f79dde8f9d321e379e6acfaf1ecda494940c7955. Includes 69 focused tests and a real-process crash/reopen proof; actual Codex and Claude CLI endpoint matrices and built foreground commands passed locally. A draft PR will describe proof boundaries and the implementation for review.

## Implementation intent

An isolated PoC exists for architectural feedback, not merge approval. It is restricted to reasoning and permitted file tools; arbitrary background commands/children, an external-effect ledger, automated presence and automatic supervision of every chat are not implemented.

## Design questions

Is an opt-in native supervised controller the right extension of TaskFlow? Please review persistence/migration and retention requirements before considering merge. Material SQLite design acceptance is outstanding; this issue and draft seek that discussion, not claim prior approval.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.3 (1391f7c)** via npm global install
- Node v26.8.1, Linux 7.0.0-31-generic (x64)
- User systemd service (`openclaw-gateway.service`), `Restart=no` drop-in
- Single `main` agent, single workspace
- Agent database: 327.4 MiB · 48 markdown files · 2290 chunks

## Symptom

Gateway becomes **unkillable** during a memory reindex. SIGTERM via `systemctl --user stop openclaw-gateway.service` is queued behind an in-flight synchronous SQLite transaction and never executes. `TimeoutStopSec=330` elapses, process stays in `Ssl` state, `systemctl --user restart` has no effect. Only a hard reboot via `sudo reboot` recovers the host.

The two 0-byte lock marker files (`*.reindex-lock.sqlite`, `*.generation-lock.sqlite`) **survive the reboot** and continue to block every subsequent reindex attempt, so the freeze will recur on the next LCM compaction cycle.

## Evidence

Lock files (after reboot, 4+ hours old):

```
$ ls -la ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.{reindex,generation}*lock* *.writer*
-rw-r--r-- ... 0 Sep  8 23:20 .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.reindex-lock.sqlite
-rw-r--r-- ... 0 Sep  8 23:21 .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.generation-lock.sqlite
-rw-r--r-- ... 4096 Sep  9 01:43 .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.generation-writer.sqlite
```

WAL bloomed to **51 MiB** (normal: <1 MiB):

```
$ ls -la ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal
-rw------- ... 51326992 Sep  9 02:59 .../openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal
```

Memory index never settled:

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Dirty: yes
Indexed: 48/48 files · 2290 chunks
Agent database: 327.4 MiB · WAL 48.9 MiB
```

Journal excerpt during the freeze window:

```
Sep 09 02:59:04 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
Sep 09 02:59:28 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
Sep 09 02:59:58 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
Sep 09 03:00:48 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
Sep 09 03:02:37 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
Sep 09 03:05:46 node[2115]: [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold
...
```

Gateway process state at freeze (after reboot, fresh PID 2115):

```
$ ps -p $(pgrep -f 'openclaw.*gateway' | head -1) -o pid,stat,wchan,etime,cmd
   2115 Ssl  ep_pol   11:04 node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
```

`Ssl` = interruptible sleep, but `ep_pol` shows genuine polling — SIGTERM queued but never delivered.

## Related upstream issues (same bug class)

| Issue | Match |
|---|---|
| [#140620](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140620) (P0) | session-transcript reconciliation stalls at 27/~1500 sessions, lock file left over, sudo reboot needed |
| [#136311](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136311) (P1) | gateway reacquires reindex lock on every start; 19 GB orphans |
| [#115908](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/115908) (P1) | session transcript projection reconcile can livelock |
| [#119720](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/119720) (P1) | synchronous agent persistence blocks Gateway event loop at scale |
| [#138474](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138474) (P1) | node:sqlite transactions + memory-worker lock spin freeze gateway 45-90s |
| [#134337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/134337) (P1) | memory_search dirty maintenance repeatedly full-reindexes |
| [#124788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124788) (P0, closed) | event loop blocks ~100s every ~10 min |
| [#112758](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112758) (P1) | missing `mmap_size` and `cache_size` SQLite pragmas |

## Suggested fix

1. **Auto-release stale lock files on gateway start.** If `*.reindex-lock.sqlite` or `*.generation-lock.sqlite` is older than 30 minutes AND `fuser` reports no current holder, remove it before opening the database. This unblocks future reindex attempts. (See `openclaw-memory-recovery` skill.)

2. **Set SQLite PRAGMAs by default in `openclaw-agent-db-*.mjs`** (next to the existing `busy_timeout` line at ~line 603):
   ```js
   db.exec(`PRAGMA busy_timeout = ${OPENCLAW_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS};`); // already done
   db.exec(`PRAGMA mmap_size = 268435456;`);   // 256 MiB  — addresses #112758
   db.exec(`PRAGMA cache_size = -64000;`);     // 64 MiB   — addresses #112758
   ```
   `mmap_size` and `cache_size` are persistent in the DB file, so setting once is enough; `busy_timeout` stays per-connection.

3. **Bump default `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`** from `5e3` (5s) in `openclaw-state-db-contract-DGtx5mf2.mjs:74` to `3e4` (30s) so contended transactions retry instead of erroring during memory reindex.

4. **Make reindex truly async.** The current synchronous-SQLite write path is what blocks the event loop. Async writes via `node:sqlite` async API or a worker thread would prevent the entire gateway from stalling.

5. **Expose `sd_notify(WATCHDOG=1)` from the gateway loop** so user-level systemd `WatchdogSec=` + `Restart=on-watchdog` actually works. Currently the gateway does **not** call `sd_notify`, so `WatchdogSec` always fires and causes an infinite restart loop — there is no graceful recovery path today.

## Workaround (until upstream fix lands)

```bash
# 1. Hard kill the gateway (SIGKILL — SIGTERM is queued behind the SQLite transaction)
pkill -9 -f 'openclaw.*gateway'

# 2. Verify no current holder on the lock files
fuser -v ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.reindex-lock.sqlite
fuser -v ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.generation-lock.sqlite
# Both must return empty

# 3. Remove stale 0-byte markers (NOT the 4096-byte .generation-writer.sqlite — active session)
rm ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.reindex-lock.sqlite
rm ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.generation-lock.sqlite

# 4. Restart gateway and force full reindex
systemctl --user start openclaw-gateway.service
openclaw memory index --force --agent main
```

## Problem

The macOS app opens tapped chat/dashboard links in its embedded sidebar browser (`DashboardLinkBrowserView` — documented in `docs/platforms/mac/macos.md`). The only outs are per-link, per-tap:

- right-click → **Open in Default Browser** / **Copy Link**
- modified clicks / user-activated new-window links (which do open externally)

There is no way to set the default. Every link I actually want in my real browser (logged-in GitHub, extensions, sessions) costs a right-click. Verified in 2026.9.2: no `openclaw.*` preference key and no Settings toggle for link routing — the sidebar is the hardcoded tap destination.

## Why it matters

The sidebar webview is a logged-out context: no user sessions, no extensions. Links to PRs, issues, docs — anything behind auth — land as logged-out dead-ends unless remembered to right-click first. Related symptom on the widget side: #142606 (widget `host.open` fails closed entirely in native apps).

## Proposal

A **Links** preference in macOS app Settings (General feels right):

- **Open links in:** `Sidebar browser` (current behavior, keep as default — nobody's workflow breaks) / `Default browser`
- Applies to plain left-click/tap on http(s) links in chat and the embedded dashboard. Right-click menu keeps all three options regardless; modified-click behavior unchanged.

## Scope notes (from code/docs research)

- macOS-only ask: iOS/Android docs describe no in-app browsing surface, so there's nothing to align there.
- No sandbox or gateway changes needed — this is purely the app's `openURL` / navigation-policy routing decision. The `host.open` bridge (#142606) is a separate fix; this preference should govern its destination too once that lands (sidebar tab vs. system browser).
- Searched existing issues for `default browser`, `in-app`, `sidebar browser`: everything is the automation/control browser or gateway ports — no prior request for this. First filing.

## Labels suggestion

`enhancement`, `impact:ux-friction`

issues.body: ## Summary Links in dashboard HTML widgets (``) work in the browser Control UI but silently do nothing in native apps (confirmed: macOS app; likely iOS/Android Quick Chat webviews too). No error, no feedback — the tap is swallowed. ## Confirmed behavior - Same widget, same HTML: links open a new tab correctly in desktop Safari Control UI. - Same widget in the native macOS app: taps do nothing. - Likely same root family as #131406 (attachment `target="_blank"` links unresponsive in the macOS app). ## Architecture (traced through 2026.9.2 build + docs) The sandbox is not the bug — by design it never grants popup permission: 1. Widget HTML (whether via `show_widget` or `board.widget.put` → `buildWidgetDocument`) is wrapped in the canonical wrapper (`wrap.ts`), which intercepts primary-click on `target="_blank"` http(s) anchors (plus middle-click) and issues `request("host.open", {url})`. Script-initiated `window.open` is hard-locked to `undefined`. (`docs/tools/show-widget.md`: link forwarding "needs no grant and **never grants iframe popup permissions**".) 2. The Control UI host handles `host.open` (`board-view` bridge controller: validates `^https?://`, calls `this.openUrl(url)`, default `Ee` from the shared boot bundle). 3. There is **no `window.open` call anywhere** in the Control UI bundles — the final tab-open primitive lives in shared/native code, and evidently fails closed (returns null/falsy → `throw Error("widget link could not be opened")`, which the wrapper swallows: `then(()=>{},()=>{})`). So on surfaces where the open-URL primitive is unavailable (native webviews that block new tabs / lack external-open handling), every widget link silently dies. The failure is invisible by construction: the wrapper drops rejections silently and there is no fallback (no error toast, no copy-URL, nothing). ## Why not just `allow-popups` Per `docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md`, widget code is "arbitrary agent-authored HTML/JS in a hard sandbox… Capabilities over trust." Granting popup permission would bypass the user-gesture-gated, ticket-bound `host.open` path and enable scripted popups, phishing tabs, and URL-based exfiltration outside granted-`connect-src` containment. The fix should stay on the host side, not relax the sandbox. ## Suggested fix (host-side, no sandbox change) - Implement the open-URL primitive in native clients: route `host.open` to the system browser (or an in-app browser tab) instead of failing closed. - Alternatively/additionally: surface the failure — if `openUrl` returns falsy, show a toast / copy the URL to clipboard so the tap isn't a silent no-op. - Bonus: `sendPrompt`-style user-activation-gated fallback (e.g. long-press to copy link) for webviews that can't open tabs at all. ## Config consideration No config knob exists today for the sandbox attribute, `allow-popups`, or per-widget network (sandbox strings are hardcoded; only `mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin/sandboxPort` are configurable). This issue deliberately proposes **no new knob**: `host.open` already "needs no grant", so native clients just need to honor the contract the browser Control UI already honors. If maintainers want a kill-switch (e.g. `controlUi.widgetLinks: open|copy|disabled`), that's a product call — but the default should be working links everywhere. ## Repro 1. Push any HTML widget with `x` to a session dashboard (via `show_widget pin:true` or `board.widget.put`). 2. Open the dashboard in browser Control UI → link works. 3. Open the same dashboard in the macOS native app → tap does nothing. ## Labels suggestion `bug`, `bug:behavior`, `impact:ux-friction` (mirroring #131406); CC dashboard/widget maintainers.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a cron-isolated session runs an `agentTurn` payload that spawns sub-agents and yields via `sessions_yield`, the cron session's model is never woken back up when sub-agents complete. The cron observer's wait/grace/fallback sequence times out without producing the cron's own synthesis, and the fallback path delivers descendant replies (the sub-agent's findings text) as the cron's "final reply" via `cron-direct-delivery-context`.

This is the scheduler-lifecycle work that PR #140137 explicitly deferred.

## Reproduction

**Setup (any cron with this shape):**
- `sessionTarget: "isolated"`
- `payload.kind: "agentTurn"`
- Cron message instructs the agent to spawn 1+ sub-agents via `sessions_spawn` and wait via `sessions_yield`
- `delivery.mode: "announce"` (channel: any — the defect is in the text-selection, not the channel)

**Observed 2026-09-08:** forced a cron matching this shape on agent `main`. The agent spawned 2 search sub-agents, then called `sessions_yield`. The first yield returned `"Skipped due to queued user message."` (sub-agent 1's completion event was already queued). The agent resumed, read the findings, listed subagents, and yielded again. The second yield returned `{"status": "yielded"}`. From that point on, the cron session's model never produced another assistant message. Both sub-agents completed normally and wrote their findings to disk. ~5 seconds after the last descendant drained, the cron finalized. The cron delivery to Telegram contained the sub-agent's raw findings text (not the cron's intended summary block) — `openclawDeliveryMirror.kind: "cron-direct-delivery-context"`.

## Expected

The cron session's model is woken when sub-agents complete, so it can produce a synthesis reply. The cron's announced final text is what gets delivered; descendant replies don't masquerade as the cron's own final text.

## Actual

- Cron session is never woken.
- `cron-direct-delivery-context` picks up descendant reply text and delivers it as if it were the cron's final reply.

## Root cause

Two related defects in the cron-isolated-agent path. Neither is addressed by PR #140137.

### (a) Cron session is excluded from the requester-settle wake mechanism

`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled` in [`src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1391f7cd2d4/src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts) has a depth guard that skips wake dispatch for non-yielding nested requesters. PR #140137 correctly opened the gate for yielded nested requesters (depth ≥ 1 with `requesterYieldedAfterDelivery = true`). But the cron session is at depth 0, and the new doc [`docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1391f7cd2d4/docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md) — added in the same PR — explicitly notes:

> "The top-level cron exclusion also remains; starting an independent requester-settle turn for the cron session would compete with its scheduler-owned continuation."

So cron's model is never woken by this mechanism. There is no other mechanism in `src/cron/isolated-agent/` that wakes the cron session's model.

### (b) Cron-direct-delivery falls back to descendant replies

`readDescendantSubagentFallbackReply` in [`src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1391f7cd2d4/src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts) reads the descendant's terminal assistant reply and uses that as the cron session's "final reply." This means a successful sub-agent completion can masquerade as the cron's final delivery, even though the cron session itself never produced text. The 5-second grace (`finalReplyGraceMs = 5_000` in `resolveCronSubagentTimings`) gives the cron session's model time to produce a synthesis reply — but the model is never woken, so the grace always expires and the fallback always fires.

## Relationship to PR #140137

PR #140137 — [`fix(subagents): resume nested orchestrators after sessions_yield`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140137) (commit `038acb26`, on 2026.9.3) — fixed two specific defects in the nested-orchestrator path:

1. `maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled` now wakes yielded nested requesters (was: skipped at depth ≥ 1 unconditionally). The depth guard is now gated on `!requesterYieldedAfterDelivery && requesterDepth >= 1`.
2. `resolveGatewayAgentTaskTrackingMode` in [`src/gateway/server-methods/agent-task-tracking.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1391f7cd2d4/src/gateway/server-methods/agent-task-tracking.ts) now returns `'plugin_subagent'` for `inter_session` provenance targeting a paused `sessions_yield` run, so `adoptPausedSubagentRunForFollowUp` preserves `requesterSettleWake`.

The same PR's new doc explicitly defers the cron case:

> "Cron's existing observer follows active descendant run IDs and a bounded synthesis grace period. It does not wait for every registry settlement phase. A delay between the last worker ending and successor admission can therefore reach its existing fallback policy. **Making cron wait on full task settlement, and resolving reports of indefinitely pending delivery after a finalized cron run, require separate scheduler-lifecycle proof; this repair does not redefine those contracts.**"

This issue is the deferred work that PR #140137 documented but did not implement.

## Proposed fix direction

Both fixes are scheduler-lifecycle, not subagent-registry:

1. **Wake the cron session's model when descendants settle.** Either remove the "top-level cron exclusion" in `maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled` and route the cron wake through the existing `requesterSettleWake` + `adoptPausedSubagentRunForFollowUp` machinery (the same path PR #140137 enabled for nested orchestrators), or add an equivalent mechanism in `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts` that actively wakes the cron session instead of only polling for new assistant replies. The cron's `waitForDescendantSubagentSummary` already pushes through the agent-wait RPC; the missing piece is the wake path that re-admits the cron session's model.

2. **Don't fall back to descendant replies for `cron-direct-delivery-context` when the cron session has no synthesizing reply.** Either keep the cron session's announced-final text authoritative (even if empty), or distinguish "agent produced a synthesis" from "observer fell back to descendant text" so the channel knows which it's delivering. Today's fallback path means a sub-agent's terminal reply can be the cron's `cron-direct-delivery-context` payload.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (`1391f7cd2d4`)
- Cron session: `agent:main:cron:<cron-id>:<run-key>`
- Spawned sub-agents: `agent:main:subagent:<uuid>` × 2, both `status: "done"` with `expectsCompletionMessage: true`
- Cron delivery: `channel: telegram`, `kind: cron-direct-delivery-context`
- Delivery text: sub-agent's findings summary (e.g. `"Findings written to: ... 2 distinct items found ..."`), not the cron's intended summary block

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2026.9.2, `publishBootstrapFile` (`src/agents/workspace.ts`) publishes each generated bootstrap file by writing a staging file and then `fs.linkSync`-ing it into place, and treats a hard-link failure as fatal. On a workspace filesystem where `link(2)` is not supported, every fresh workspace fails on its first turn with:

```
Error: Workspace filesystem does not support atomic bootstrap publication. Use a workspace on a filesystem with hard-link support.
```

This was introduced by 216360ad87 (`fix: do not keep a partial workspace bootstrap file after a failed first write`, #131108, closes #127505) and is covered by the test `fails closed when the workspace does not support hard links` in `src/agents/workspace-bootstrap-publish.test.ts`, so it looks like a deliberate fail-closed choice. Its practical effect is that OpenClaw can no longer start on any FUSE-backed or network-mounted workspace that lacks hard links. We hit it running OpenClaw headless inside a container with `agents.defaults.workspace` on a Modal Volume (a FUSE network volume); every new conversation dies before the first model request. 2026.9.1 works on the same mount, and 2026.9.2 works on a workspace that already contains the bootstrap files, because the check is skipped when the target exists (`if (existing) return false`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Mount a filesystem on which `link(2)` fails with one of the codes `isHardlinkFallbackError` recognises (`EPERM`, `EXDEV`, `ENOTSUP`, `EOPNOTSUPP`, `ENOSYS`). A FUSE network volume (Modal Volume in our case) does this; locally, a vfat or exFAT mount reproduces it, since FAT has no hard links.
   Confirm with: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");fs.writeFileSync("WS/a","");fs.linkSync("WS/a","WS/b")'` → throws `EPERM`/`ENOTSUP`.
2. Point `agents.defaults.workspace` at an empty directory `WS` on that mount (no `AGENTS.md` etc. yet).
3. Install `openclaw@2026.9.2` and start the gateway / run one agent turn.

### Expected behavior

Bootstrap files are published (as they are on 2026.9.1, which used exclusive-create writes), or at minimum OpenClaw degrades to a non-hard-link publication path. `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s own `publishFileExclusive` already does this: it has strategies `"link-or-copy" | "link-required" | "rename-noreplace"` and falls through to an exclusive copy when the hard link fails with one of the fallback codes unless the caller asked for `link-required`. `publishBootstrapFile` bypasses that helper with a hand-rolled `linkSync` and turns the fallback case into a hard error.

### Actual behavior

The turn fails immediately with the error above. No bootstrap file is created, so every subsequent turn on that workspace fails the same way; the workspace is unusable until someone creates the bootstrap files by hand or downgrades to 2026.9.1.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (2026.9.1 is fine on the same mount)

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 (Debian slim container), Node 22. Workspace on a FUSE-backed network volume without hard-link support.

### Install method

npm (global, pinned version)

### Model

N/A — the failure happens before the first model request, with any model.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

Headless gateway in a sandbox; `agents.defaults.workspace` set to the network-volume mount. Nothing provider-specific is involved.

### Logs

```
Error: Workspace filesystem does not support atomic bootstrap publication. Use a workspace on a filesystem with hard-link support.
```

(from `publishBootstrapFile`, `src/agents/workspace.ts`; in the 2026.9.2 npm build it is in `dist/workspace-*.js`)

### Suggested fix

Publish bootstrap files through `publishFileExclusive` with `"link-or-copy"` (or `"rename-noreplace"`) so the partial-file guarantee from #131108 is kept where hard links exist and the exclusive-copy path is used where they don't; alternatively expose the strategy as a config knob. Happy to send a PR if you'd take either approach.

issues.body:
## What problem does this solve?

OpenClaw users who want short-form social video production currently need to assemble several manual steps: turn an idea into a spoken script, synthesize narration, generate or provide visuals, burn readable captions, reframe video vertically, and package post copy. Clipping a long owned video has a parallel gap: a user needs time-aligned captions, self-contained moment selection, mobile framing, and separate output assets.

The requested workflow needs both routes in one agent:

- caption or idea to a finished 9:16 short; and
- owned long video or timed transcript to multiple captioned highlight clips.

The workflow should draft and render automatically without a storyboard approval loop, preserve the user's language, target Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok, and never publish publicly without an explicit request.

## Proposed solution

Add a portable Agent Plugins-compatible example bundle named Viral Clipper. It uses configured OpenClaw TTS/video capabilities when present and a dependency-free Node + FFmpeg helper for deterministic local composition, vertical reframing, ASS caption burn-in, and time-range clipping. It accepts existing SRT captions or local Whisper for time-aligned long-video transcription.

The bundle should remain provider-agnostic, avoid storing credentials, use only local media paths, reject output/input path collisions, disclose a caption-led fallback when optional video generation fails, and keep publishing outside the default automation boundary.

## Alternatives considered

OpenShorts is an existing open-source MCP option for larger face-aware long-video workflows. It is intentionally preferred when already configured, but it has heavier operational requirements. A lightweight portable bundle is still useful for a few transparent local renders and for the caption-to-short route.

## Acceptance criteria

- An Agent Plugin exposes an autopilot skill for both requested routes.
- Caption-to-short produces narration-led, captioned 9:16 H.264/AAC output and post-package assets.
- Long-video clipping uses timed SRT/Whisper evidence and produces captioned, mobile-framed clips with source audio.
- The default master works for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok and gives multilingual/font guidance.
- The installer creates an isolated workspace without writing credentials.
- Public publishing remains explicit rather than automatic.

## Evidence

A proposed implementation includes focused Node tests for timestamps, SRT cropping, generated caption coverage, ASS escaping, strict plan validation, and a conditional real FFmpeg render. It also has plugin manifest/skill-loading and installer smoke coverage. The authoring sandbox lacks FFmpeg, so the real render test is intentionally skipped there; its preflight reports the exact missing capabilities.

AI-assisted implementation and validation.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw `2026.9.2`, Codex-backed OpenAI models show severe and highly variable latency during normal tool-using agent workflows.

The most important operational finding is that **the problem can be escaped immediately by switching to a non-Codex model/runtime**. On the same host, same Gateway, same tools, and same OpenClaw installation, switching from Codex/OpenAI to `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.2` removes the pathological pauses and restores normal interactive performance.

This is therefore not just a generic “large model is slow” report. The same OpenClaw installation performs equivalent workflows normally through another runtime.

I am not claiming the final root cause is proven to be inside the Codex plugin itself, but the A/B evidence strongly narrows the problem to the Codex/OpenAI runtime path rather than the host, Gateway, tools, or general OpenClaw agent loop.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.2 (3928bad)`
- `@openclaw/codex`: `2026.9.2`
- Codex CLI: `0.153.4`
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Gateway: local OpenClaw Gateway
- Codex runtime: bundled Codex app-server / stdio
- OpenAI models observed in this path:
  - `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`
  - `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`
  - `openai/gpt-6-astra`
- Non-Codex control:
  - `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.2`

## Observed behavior

### 1. Small canary — 3 sequential commands

| Metric | Codex / Sol | OpenRouter / GLM 5.2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total duration | 25.4 s | ~9.1 s |
| Failures | 0 | 0 |

GLM completed the same class of work about **2.8x faster**.

### 2. Multi-tool workflow — 6–7 tool calls

| Metric | Codex | OpenRouter / GLM 5.2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total duration | 82–109 s | ~16 s |
| Maximum observed gap between tools | 18.9–25.6 s | ~2.6 s |
| Tool failures | 0 | 0 |

The tools themselves were succeeding. The large delay was primarily between a successful tool result and the next model/tool action.

The OpenRouter control completed this class of workflow about **5–7x faster**.

### 3. Heavy workflow — ~10 tool calls

| Metric | Codex | OpenRouter / GLM 5.2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Time before first useful output | 303.4 s | <2 s |
| Total duration | 428.1 s | ~33.4 s |
| Tool calls | ~10 | 10 |
| Tool failures | 0 | 0 |

This is about a **13x total-duration difference**, and the 303-second pre-output stall disappears completely outside the Codex runtime.

### 4. OpenRouter transport control

During the GLM control test, Gateway logs showed successful OpenRouter requests around:

```text
elapsedMs ~= 1,000–6,200
status=200
```

No 429s, no timeouts, no anomalous queueing, and no equivalent 20–300 second pauses were observed.

## Additional Codex observations

The OpenAI models have different absolute speeds, but all share the Codex runtime path.

Representative real-world observations:

- GPT-5.6 Sol: often >60 s for simple work
- GPT-5.6 Luna: roughly 20–45 s
- GPT-6 Astra: also showed high latency and high usage

During Astra testing, the runtime eventually produced:

```text
gateway reconnected after transport loss
run error: codex app-server client closed before turn completed
```

The Gateway remained operational afterward.

## Why this matters operationally

The single most useful workaround discovered is extremely simple:

> **Switch away from the Codex-backed model/runtime.**

In this installation, doing only that immediately returned the system from multi-minute stalls to normal interactive timings.

That means operators who hit this failure mode do not necessarily need to spend hours or days debugging the host, network, tools, or Gateway before regaining a usable system.

A visible diagnostic hint such as “Codex runtime latency detected; test a non-Codex model/runtime” could save substantial operator time.

## Operational impact during diagnosis

This investigation consumed approximately:

- **1.5 working days of operator time**;
- **more than USD 20 in additional Codex credits**, on top of normal weekly subscription usage;
- approximately **EUR 11 in OpenRouter usage** during comparative testing.

The human diagnostic time was by far the most expensive part.

Without the non-Codex control, it was difficult to distinguish:

```text
“the reasoning model is inherently slow”
```

from:

```text
“the runtime path is introducing abnormal latency”
```

## Expected behavior

Codex-backed turns should not introduce tens or hundreds of seconds of unexplained idle time between:

```text
tool result
→ next model request
→ next tool call
```

If the model itself needs additional reasoning time, OpenClaw should expose enough phase-level timing to distinguish model inference from:

- app-server startup;
- request dispatch;
- transport wait;
- queue/service-tier wait;
- post-tool continuation delay;
- missing terminal-event wait;
- client lifecycle/reconnect delay.

## Requested investigation

Could the Codex harness expose or log timestamps for at least:

```text
OpenClaw turn admitted
Codex app-server request started
thread/start or thread/resume completed
turn/start sent
upstream model request sent
response headers / first byte received
first model event received
tool call emitted
tool result returned to Codex
next upstream model request sent
turn/completed received
```

Please also investigate why a successful tool result can be followed by 18–26 seconds of inactivity before the next action, and why some turns show ~300-second pre-output stalls.

## Related issues

Possibly related OpenClaw reports:

- #87744 — Codex turns repeatedly time out waiting for `turn/completed`
- #89742 — Codex app-server can wedge while an in-flight request remains active
- #95547 — `codex app-server client closed before turn completed`
- #140479 — same client-close symptom still present on OpenClaw 2026.9.2

Potentially relevant upstream Codex report:

- `openai/codex#23807` — Codex CLI stalls for exactly 300 seconds between a tool result and the next model request

This report is distinct because it provides a **same-installation, same-host, non-Codex control path on OpenClaw 2026.9.2**.

## Privacy

No API keys, OAuth tokens, business prompts, email content, private file paths, account identifiers, or session identifiers are included. Additional redacted Gateway/trajectory timing excerpts can be provided if maintainers need them.

   The turn then ran normally to completion (~4.5 min).

- Either boot-time restart recovery settles before admitting new inbound on the same lane, or a failed recovery does not wedge `claim→adoption` for the full handler timeout (300 s).

`DEFAULT_INGRESS_ADOPTION_STALL_MS` in `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts` is 300000 and only Telegram wires `adoptionStallTimeoutMs` to configuration. openclaw 2026.9.2, @openclaw/discord 2026.9.2, Codex runtime with turns that routinely exceed five minutes.

Wire `adoptionStallTimeoutMs` for the Discord channel (and other channels) or raise the default well above typical turn lengths. Related: #116547, #126842. Local workaround used: the default raised to six hours in the bundle.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression / message delivery and restart-recovery bug

### Summary

Since upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.9.1, a Telegram direct session frequently appears to stop responding. The gateway still receives inbound messages, but no reply reaches the user. Manually restarting the gateway makes the session responsive again, while at least one interrupted reply remains lost.

Logs from one incident show two interacting failure paths:

1. Telegram returns a long HTTP 429 flood-wait for sendChatAction/sendMessage.
2. A gateway restart occurs with pending reply delivery and an active Codex turn.
3. After startup, delivery recovery refuses to replay an entry in send_attempt_started state, so the reply is not recovered.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)
- OS: macOS
- Install: global Node/OpenClaw installation managed by LaunchAgent
- Node runtime: 25.9.0
- Channel: Telegram direct chat, polling
- Runtime/model: OpenAI Codex, openai/gpt-5.6-sol
- Gateway bind: loopback
- Config validation: valid
- Telegram probe after recovery: works

### Observed timeline

All identifiers below are redacted.

2026-09-08 12:48:33 +07:00
telegram sendMessage failed:
429 Too Many Requests, retry after 333 seconds

2026-09-08 12:48:33 +07:00
telegram final reply failed:
OutboundDeliveryError, 429 Too Many Requests

2026-09-08 13:09:28 +07:00
Inbound Telegram direct message received successfully.

2026-09-08 13:09:29 +07:00
telegram sendChatAction failed:
429 Too Many Requests, retry after 460 seconds

2026-09-08 13:10:21 +07:00
Gateway received SIGTERM and began restarting.

Drain state at restart:
- 2 queued or active operations
- 1 pending reply delivery operation
- 1 active embedded run
- 1 admitted session turn

During drain:
reconnect delivery drain failed:
gateway is draining for restart

After startup:
- one startup-orphaned main session marked for restart recovery
- restart-safe recovery dispatched for the Telegram direct session
- recovery run eventually reported completed

However, outbound recovery logged:
Delivery state is send_attempt_started;
refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation

The affected reply was not replayed.

### Expected behavior

- Telegram typing actions should not exhaust or unnecessarily extend the message flood-wait affecting final replies.
- A server-directed 429 should be respected without silently losing the final response.
- If the gateway restarts while a reply is pending, delivery recovery should reconcile the Telegram send state or surface a visible failure/retry notice.
- The user should not need to restart the gateway to make the direct session responsive again.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway receives inbound messages.
- Telegram channel health may still appear normal.
- No final reply is delivered.
- Manual gateway restart restores responsiveness.
- At least one delivery remains in send_attempt_started and is not replayed.

### Additional evidence

No matching liveness-warning, stuck activeAppServerTurnRequests, or "Codex stopped before confirming the turn was complete" signature was found for this incident. This suggests the primary observed path is Telegram 429 plus incomplete delivery reconciliation across restart, rather than a pure Codex terminal-idle wedge.

### Related issues / PRs

- #51620 — Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages
- #138763 — Telegram typing coalescing on OpenClaw 2026.9.1
- #139292 — Telegram shared limiter/action failure-state repair
- #90771 — Gateway restart during active Codex channel turn drops final reply

### Frequency / impact

## Summary

On OpenClaw `2026.8.2` we are seeing severe latency during technical/tool-heavy work when using `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the native Codex/OAuth app-server path.

Bounded tasks that previously completed in roughly 1–2 minutes can now remain `running` for 7–12 minutes.

We ran a controlled canary using the **same GPT-5.6 Sol model** through two different routes. The OpenRouter route was materially faster and followed the requested tool sequence exactly.

This does **not** prove that every 2026.8.2 Codex installation is affected, but it strongly suggests that the native Codex/app-server path contributes materially to the latency in our environment.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.8.2`
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Install: npm global
- Gateway: local
- Native model: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`
- Auth/runtime: Codex OAuth / app-server
- Managed Codex version: `0.151.0`
- Fast mode: off

Gateway health, configuration, OAuth, CPU, RAM and swap were checked and showed no obvious resource or authentication problem.

## Controlled canary

Exact task:

```text
Execute exactly three independent checks:
1. openclaw --version
2. openclaw config validate
3. openclaw gateway status --deep

Do not make any other query or tool call.
Summarize the result in five lines.
```

### Result A — GPT-5.6 Sol via native Codex

- Total time: `40.889 s`
- Tool calls: `5`
- Failed/recovery call: `1`
- Requested useful operations: `3`
- Approximate actual tool execution time: `3.75 s`
- Result: functionally correct

### Result B — same GPT-5.6 Sol via OpenRouter

Route:

`openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

- Total time: `24.395 s`
- Tool calls: `3/3`
- Failed calls: `0`
- Model/handoff wait: `18.657 s`
- Result: functionally correct

The same GPT-5.6 Sol model was therefore about **40% faster through OpenRouter** in this canary, while also following the requested three-tool sequence exactly.

For reference, DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter completed the same canary in `15.419 s`, with `3/3` successful calls.

## Longer runs

The same 2026.8.2 installation also showed bounded technical tasks with many sequential model → tool → model cycles taking several minutes.

Examples observed:

- `762 s`, 58 tool calls
- `711 s`, 35 tool calls
- `472 s`, 32 tool calls
- `444 s`, 57 tool calls
- `351 s`, 26 tool calls

In these traces, actual tool execution represented only a minority of total elapsed time; most of the delay accumulated between tool results and subsequent model/runtime continuation.

## Expected behavior

A simple three-tool read-only task should not take ~41 seconds or require extra recovery calls when the same GPT-5.6 Sol model completes the identical workflow substantially faster through another provider/runtime path.

Longer bounded technical tasks should not accumulate several minutes of model/runtime wait between otherwise fast tool executions.

## Actual behavior

The native Codex/app-server route introduces substantially more latency and, in the controlled canary, additional tool-call recovery compared with the same GPT-5.6 Sol model routed through OpenRouter.

## Temporary workaround

For users affected by similar latency, using the same GPT-5.6 Sol model temporarily through OpenRouter may be a useful **diagnostic and operational workaround**.

In our environment:

- GPT-5.6 Sol / native Codex: `40.889 s`
- GPT-5.6 Sol / OpenRouter: `24.395 s`

This avoids changing the actual model while bypassing the native Codex/app-server path.

## Related

Possibly related to #86961, which reported a large latency difference when the Codex plugin was enabled vs disabled on an earlier OpenClaw version and GPT-5.5. Our report differs by comparing the **same GPT-5.6 Sol model** over native Codex vs OpenRouter on `2026.8.2`.

We are preparing an upgrade to `2026.9.2` and intend to repeat the **exact same canary** after the upgrade, since that release also updates the managed Codex runtime. We can add the before/after result here.

Raw timing/trajectory details can be provided if useful. No secrets are included.

## Summary

OpenClaw 2026.9.2 webchat: after an update + `openclaw onboard`, the Control UI WS connection enters a permanently pending state where **every profile-dependent RPC** fails with:

> `UNAVAILABLE: Authenticated profile verification is unavailable. Retry shortly; if this continues, contact a gateway administrator.`

Affected methods seen in gateway ws logs (all, repeatedly, ~2 s after connect): `chat.startup`, `sessions.list`, `sessions.groups.list`, `sessions.catalog.list`, `sessions.describe`, `sessions.subscribe`, `sessions.messages.subscribe`, `sessions.viewers.set`, `sessions.observer.visibility`, `tasks.list`, `taskSuggestions.list`, `workboard.cards.list`, `progressCard.get`, `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe`, `openclaw.approval.list`.

Notably `chat.send` kept working, so the agent stayed reachable while the UI looked dead — very confusing UX.

## Root-cause pointer

`isGatewayClientProfilePending(client)` = `client.authenticatedGitHubIdentitySync && !client.authenticatedUserProfile` (src/gateway/server-methods/gateway-client-identity.ts) never clears for the connection — the async GitHub identity sync presumably fails silently and the client is stuck "pending" for its lifetime. Every gated method returns retryable UNAVAILABLE.

## Workaround that fixed it

Restarting the gateway (and hard-refreshing the tab). Per-connection state, so there is no self-heal retry for the user.

## Suggestions

1. Retry profile sync on the connection (with backoff) instead of wedge-until-restart.
2. Surface a one-click "reconnect" (new WS) affordance in the UI error.
3. If chat.send must stay allowed while profile is pending, make the UI clearly show "degraded" instead of blank panels.

## Environment

- 2026.9.2 (3928bad), gateway on Linux/Debian 13, webchat over Tailscale serve HTTPS
- Same build also produced intermittent `exec` child SIGTERM kills (separate issue) and the `openclaw` plugin tool error `prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded` (resolved by `openclaw onboard`).

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior/performance regression

### Summary
OpenClaw 2026.9.2 appears to regress the Experience Review prompt-cache reuse intentionally added by merged PR #130013 (`fix(skills): keep the experience review on the foreground prompt-cache prefix`).

An autonomous Skill Workshop Experience Review can still rebuild a different prompt prefix from the foreground turn, producing `cache_tokens=0` and a full re-prefill of a long local-model session. In the observed case the review hit its hard 120-second timeout before generating a token.

This is distinct from review cancellation/starvation (#139351). The failure here is the cache-prefix mismatch itself.

### Reproduction / failing evidence
1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.2 with Skill Workshop autonomous mode at its default `auto` behavior.
2. Use a long foreground session on an OpenAI-compatible local backend that exposes cache metrics.
3. Complete an Experience-Review-eligible turn (>=10 model iterations).
4. Wait for the 30-second review idle trigger.
5. Inspect the detached review request and backend cache metrics.

Observed failing review:

```text
messages        = 429
request JSON    ~= 554 KB
cache_tokens    = 0
input_tokens    = 0
output_tokens   = 0
duration        = 118.766 s
```

The zero usage is because the request was aborted during prefill. Gateway timing:

```text
19:10:18.279 model-fetch start
19:12:18.194 embedded run timeout
runId=skill-workshop-review:...
timeoutMs=120000
```

### Expected behavior
Per PR #130013, the detached Experience Review should preserve the foreground prompt-cache prefix and foreground advertised tool catalog, while actual execution stays gated to `skill_workshop` only.

### Prefix divergences observed in the 2026.9.2 installed bundle

1. The review opens the foreground model context but runs with an internal review `sessionId/sessionKey` from `resolveInternalSessionEffectsIdentity(...)`.
2. `skillWorkshopProposalOnly` still passes through `appendProgressCardSystemPrompt(...)`, changing the system-prefix content.
3. `toolExecutionAllow: ["skill_workshop"]` participates in tool-surface construction and changes the model-visible schema. One concrete mismatch was the `sessions_spawn` swarm-enabled schema.

Any of these can break prefix equality. Together they reproduced a full cache miss.

### Local production workaround / proof
I tested a narrow local patch that:

- runs the detached review against the foreground `sessionId/sessionKey`;
- skips progress-card system-prompt injection for `skillWorkshopProposalOnly`;
- keeps the complete foreground tool schema visible to the model;
- gates execution after schema construction so only `skill_workshop` can actually execute.

The execution gate preserves tool names/descriptions/parameter schemas but replaces disallowed executors with execution-denied behavior.

First proof:

```text
ID118 foreground
cache_tokens = 0
input_tokens = 43,536
output       = 91
duration     = 31.671 s

ID119 Experience Review
cache_tokens = 43,534
input_tokens = 438
output       = 414
duration     = 21.009 s
```

This is ~99.995% foreground-prefix reuse.

Production-shaped regression proof after restoring the normal trigger (`10` iterations, `30s` idle) and leaving the 120-second review timeout unchanged:

```text
ID120 foreground system hash = b77f88fb253e132a
ID121 review     system hash = b77f88fb253e132a

ID120 foreground tool hash   = 6e7b09439ae04f29
ID121 review     tool hash   = 6e7b09439ae04f29

tools advertised: 52 / 52
```

Review result:

```text
ID121
cache_tokens = 43,589
input_tokens = 439
output       = 193
duration     = 16.755 s
```

Normal foreground continuation after the patch:

```text
ID122
cache_tokens = 43,594
input_tokens = 48
output       = 37
duration     = 2.810 s
```

### Why increasing the timeout is not the fix
The timeout is not the root cause. A cache-missed 190K-token local review can spend minutes re-prefilling, whereas a cache-hit review only processes the appended review instruction. Increasing the timeout would simply allow the redundant prefill to continue longer.

### Related upstream work
- PR #130013 explicitly added foreground prompt-cache-prefix reuse while retaining `skill_workshop`-only execution.
- #131791 states that foreground prefix/catalog reuse is intentional and should remain.
- #139351 concerns timeout/cancellation and scheduler starvation; this report is about the prefix regression before that timeout.
- #141202 is a separate `process.poll` / `notifyOnExit` duplicate-wake race.

### Suggested regression test
For an eligible Experience Review, assert:

```text
foreground system prompt digest == review system prompt digest
foreground advertised tool schema digest == review advertised tool schema digest
review cacheRead > 0
```

while also asserting that non-`skill_workshop` execution remains denied.

The local workaround was against bundled JS only; upstream should implement the source-level equivalent at the review/session/tool-surface boundaries.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.2
- Windows 10 x64
- Node 22.23.2
- OpenAI-compatible local provider via llama-swap / llama.cpp
- 262K configured model context

### Impact
On local long-context inference, this regression can turn a small background review into a complete tens- or hundreds-of-thousands-token prefill. In the observed long-session failure, the review never reached generation before the 120-second abort, wasting compute and making autonomous Skill Workshop review unreliable.

{
  "primary": "commandcode/meituan/LongCat-2.0:free",
  "fallbacks": [
    "openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free",

    "openrouter/thinkingmachines/inkling:free",

}

## Expected vs Actual
| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Primary returns 429 | Try next model in fallbacks | Session fails: "failed before producing a reply" |

Manually set primary to a non-rate-limited model:

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With state on the PostgreSQL backend, an invalid `openclaw.json` makes `openclaw gateway run` fail with an unrelated database error instead of the config issue. On SQLite the same config reports the problem and exits 78. On PostgreSQL the process exits 1 with "Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.", which points operators at the database instead of their config.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure PostgreSQL state (`database.engine: "postgres"` with a reachable `database.postgres.connection`) and start the Gateway once.
2. Make the config invalid, for example add a second agent without `agents.ownership: "explicit"`:
   ```json
   { "agents": { "entries": { "main": { "workspace": "..." }, "helper": { "workspace": "..." } } } }
   ```
3. `openclaw config validate --json` reports `agents.ownership: multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership="explicit" or one legacy default=true marker`.
4. Run `openclaw gateway run`.

### Expected behavior

The Gateway refuses to start and reports the config issue (`agents.ownership: ...`), as it does with SQLite state.

### Actual behavior

```text
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.
```

With `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1`, the stack runs from the config preflight's legacy-issue collection into a synchronous state read:

```text
at readConfigMachineState
at readBundledDiscoveryMode
at readBundledDiscoveryModeMemoized
at resolveInstalledPluginIndexPolicyHash
at resolvePluginMetadataSnapshotCacheKey
at loadCachedPluginMetadataSnapshot
at loadPluginMetadataSnapshotForRegistry
at loadContributionRegistrySnapshot
at loadPluginManifestRegistryForPluginRegistry
at collectDoctorConfigRepairPluginIds
at collectPluginLegacyConfigRules
at findDoctorLegacyConfigIssues
at addDoctorLegacyIssues
```

For an invalid config there is no plugin metadata snapshot, so collecting legacy issues derives the plugin registry synchronously, and that reads the bundled-discovery machine state on the main thread. SQLite allows that read; a PostgreSQL Gateway refuses it.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5, `main` `f5521bca76e` (CLI transcript) and `d238c0e5ce7` (regression test); the path is unchanged between them

### Operating system

macOS 27, PostgreSQL 18 (`pgvector/pgvector:pg18`); first seen on Linux containers.

### Install method

pnpm build from source

### Model

Not applicable; this happens before any model call.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

See above.

### Impact and severity

An operator who mistypes or migrates config on a PostgreSQL deployment is told the database is unreachable and goes looking in the wrong place; the actual config issue is never shown.

### Additional information

A fix is proposed in a linked PR.

A failed publication should leave the previous complete version of that launcher available for the existing task/login entry. Only publish the replacement after its bytes have been written successfully.

The original 38-byte CMD fixture becomes an 11-byte `@echo off` prefix after the injected partial write. `readScheduledTaskCommand` no longer returns the original command. The caller reports failure but the old launcher has already been damaged.

Source main at `00fd5d6a404939da829ceae80e01d941a729cf06`.

### Bug type

Bug — WebChat UI / streaming delivery (native agent runs, non-ACP)

### Summary

Assistant reply text appears duplicated (×2–×3) as separate bubbles in Control UI WebChat. Verified two related manifestations:

1. **Live-stream duplicates when the reasoning-only retry fires.** With `zai/glm-5.3-flash`, a turn whose reply text had *already streamed* to the UI gets retried by the reasoning-only guard:

   ```
   reasoning-only assistant turn detected: runId=0f99… sessionId=<…> provider=zai/glm-5.3-flash — retrying 1/2 with visible-answer continuation
   ```

   Up to 2 retries + the original attempt = 3 attempts, and the already-emitted commentary text is (re-)delivered for each, so the UI accumulates 2–3 identical bubbles. If the run is then aborted, **zero copies are committed** — the duplicates exist only in the live event stream.

2. **Completed turns also render commentary segments more than once.** Even normal completed runs show inter-tool commentary text ×2–×4 (partially merged variants) in WebChat. The committed assistant events carry text blocks alongside `openclawStreamFallback: {source: "segment", itemId: "commentary-0"}` records, which suggests the streamed partial, the fallback replacement, and the committed text are each appended as separate bubbles instead of superseded ones being replaced.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.8.2 (0965053); gateway loopback on macOS; Control UI WebChat
- Model: `zai/glm-5.3-flash` via `openai-completions` (reasoning enabled) — a model that frequently produces reasoning-only terminal turns, so the retry path fires often ("every reply shows three times")

### Reproduction (case A)

1. Use a reasoning model that intermittently returns reasoning-only turns (z.ai glm-5.3-flash does this frequently).
2. Send a prompt in WebChat that produces inter-tool commentary text followed by a tool call.
3. When a phase ends reasoning-only, OpenClaw retries with visible-answer continuation (up to 2 retries → 3 attempts total).
4. WebChat shows the same text 2–3× as separate bubbles.

### Evidence for case A (aborted run)

- Run window: `chat.send` 19:05:49 → `chat.abort` 19:06:59 — 1m1s, exactly matching the WebChat usage footer ("1m1s · 787 output tokens").
- Afterwards the tripled text was searched in durable state: the `transcript_events` SQLite store contains **0 copies** of that text in any session, while the tool call executed in the same run *is* committed. So all three bubbles came from the live stream only — nothing was ever committed.
- The retry mechanism itself was confirmed active on this gateway/model (log line quoted above; the aborted run matches the 1 original + 2 retries = 3 copies budget).
- Refreshing the WebChat page clears the duplicates — consistent with them living purely in the delivery/streaming layer.

### Expected behavior

- Text deltas already delivered for a superseded attempt should not be re-delivered by a retry (or the UI should replace the superseded attempt's bubbles rather than append).
- Committed turns should render each commentary segment exactly once.

### Actual behavior

- Identical text bubbles ×2–×3 during streaming; for aborted runs the duplicates are phantom (page refresh removes them). Users reasonably conclude the model repeated itself or the message was sent multiple times.

### Impact

- Confusing UX; erodes trust in the transcript.
- No context pollution for aborted runs (nothing committed), but provider output tokens are wasted across retry attempts.

### Related

- #110368 — ACP sessions show duplicate identical replies (transcript double-persist, ×2 with committed rows; our case is native runs, ×3, zero committed copies — different layer)
- #125267 — reasoning-only retry path and z.ai reasoning-only turns (confirms the retry mechanism this bug surfaces through)

### Summary

Today only `sessions_spawn` creates a job-ledger row. Native Task/Agent CLI sub-agents run invisibly — no ledger row — so an agent can claim work is "running" with zero authoritative record, and there's no way to detect or block that claim at the source.

### Problem

The job ledger is the source of truth a self-hosted app relies on to answer "is this run real?" When a sub-agent primitive that isn't `sessions_spawn` starts work, nothing is written to the ledger. That makes it possible for an agent turn to assert a background run is in flight while no authoritative record exists — the confabulated-"running" failure class. App-side Stop hooks can only detect this after the fact; they can't make visibility a structural guarantee.

### Request

A gateway lifecycle hook that fires on **any** sub-agent primitive start/stop (including native Task/Agent CLI sidechains, not just `sessions_spawn`) and writes a ledger row. That makes the invariant *"a run is legit iff it's visible in the ledger"* structurally true, closing confabulated-"running" claims at the source rather than catching them downstream.

### Environment

- OpenClaw gateway (self-hosted), Claude-CLI live-session backend.
- Consumer: a backend that treats the job ledger as authoritative for run state and renders it to users.

issues.body:
## Summary

In our Windows OpenClaw exec environment, running `openclaw status 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 50` in a fresh PowerShell runspace was reported to print three XML errors:

```text
openclaw.cmd: Cannot process the XML from the 'Error' stream of
'<OpenClaw state directory>\tmp\agent-cli\openclaw.cmd':
Data at the root level is invalid. Line 1, position 364.
```

The local diagnostic report records exit code 0 and usable stdout, but error-stream noise and a failed-looking process status in Control UI. This report is based on that diagnostic record; the underlying serialization cause still needs maintainer confirmation.

## Reproduction

In a fresh Windows PowerShell exec runspace managed by OpenClaw, run:

```powershell
openclaw status 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 50
```

Compare with a fresh runspace running the native command without merging stderr or piping:

```powershell
openclaw status
```

Expected: normal status output without XML deserialization errors. Actual in the reported environment: the merged/piped form prints the error above, despite exit code 0.

## Recorded local observations

- Bare `openclaw status`: exit 0 without the XML parse errors; raw `#< CLIXML` progress records were observed on cold runs.
- Merged/piped status command: three XML errors and exit 0; status output remained usable (the example intentionally selects only the first 50 records).
- Prefixing `$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'` inside the command did not suppress the reported errors.
- `openclaw status --help 2>&1 | Select-Object` did not reproduce the errors in the local test.
- Progress payload included the localized message `正在準備模組以便第一次使用。` (preparing modules for first use).

## Suspected cause / investigation areas

The observations suggest an interaction between fresh-runspace module initialization, CLIXML progress records, and merged stderr handling. They do not conclusively establish whether the defect belongs to PowerShell, OpenClaw's host/wrapper, or their interaction. The meaning of the reported position 364 and any encoding involvement are unconfirmed.

Potential areas to investigate:

1. Initialize progress preferences before module initialization/user code.
2. Preserve stdout/stderr separation in the exec host.
3. If decoding CLIXML, handle complete framed records and preserve actual errors rather than indiscriminately stripping stderr.

## Workaround

Run the native command without `2>&1 | Select-Object`, allowing the exec host to capture stdout and stderr separately. This avoided the XML parse errors in the local diagnostic report.

## Reported environment

- OpenClaw 2026.8.2 (0965053), local Gateway
- Windows build 10.0.26300, x64
- PowerShell 7.6.5
- Node 26.8.1
- Local diagnostics recorded on 2026-09-04

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)
**Version:** 2026.9.2 (3928bad); reproduced at function level on 2026.9.2, incident observed on 2026.8.1

## Summary

When a session's stored last route holds the Telegram topic **out-of-band** (`context.to = "telegram:<chat>"`, `context.threadId = <N>`), a subsequent inbound from the **General** topic makes the reply go to topic `<N>`. General is the one topic whose inbound can never carry a thread id (Telegram rejects `message_thread_id=1`, so `buildTelegramRoutingTarget` addresses it as the bare chat), and `resolveSessionDeliveryTarget` treats "turn source has no thread" as "inherit the session's thread".

Observed: owner wrote in General; the agent's reply was delivered to the Finance topic (`outbound send ok … threadId=49`), where the inbound before it had come from.

## Steps to reproduce

Function-level, against the installed bundle (no bot needed):

```js
const G = "telegram:-100123";
const entry = { delivery: { kind: "external",
  route:   { channel: "telegram", accountId: "default", target: { to: G }, thread: { id: 49 } },
  context: { channel: "telegram", to: G, accountId: "default", threadId: 49 } } };

resolveSessionDeliveryTarget({ entry, requestedChannel: "last",
  turnSourceChannel: "telegram", turnSourceTo: G, turnSourceAccountId: "default" });
// → { to: "telegram:-100123", threadId: 49, threadIdSource: "session" }   ← wrong: the inbound was General
```

Live, the shape arises because `persistOutboundSessionEntry` (`src/infra/outbound/outbound-session.ts`) stores `route.to` and `route.threadId` separately — e.g. a `message` tool send to the bare chat with an explicit `threadId`. (The inbound path now writes topics in-band, `…:topic:<N>`, which is why the same session shape from before #113063 reproduced more often.)

## Expected behavior

A reply to a General-topic inbound goes to General. The turn source is the authority on its own thread: when it names a concrete target and carries no thread, the reply carries no thread. The session's stored thread should only fill in when there is **no turn source at all** (cron / `agent --deliver`).

## Actual behavior

`lastThreadId` falls through to `parsedSessionTarget.threadId` because `channelRoutesShareConversation` (`src/infra/outbound/channel-route.ts`) returns true when either side lacks a thread id — so the bare General target "matches" the bare-`to` session route and inherits its stale thread. The same line makes an explicit `to` in a *different* chat inherit the session thread when the turn has no thread.

## Root cause / proposed fix

`src/infra/outbound/targets-session.ts`, the `lastThreadId` expression:

```diff
+const turnSourceOwnsThread = hasTurnSourceChannel && typeof params.turnSourceTo === "string" && params.turnSourceTo.trim() !== "";
 const lastThreadId = hasTurnSourceThreadId
   ? parsedTurnSourceTarget?.threadId
-  : hasTurnSourceChannel && (params.turnSourceChannel !== sessionLastChannel || !turnToMatchesSession)
+  : hasTurnSourceChannel && (params.turnSourceChannel !== sessionLastChannel || !turnToMatchesSession || turnSourceOwnsThread)
     ? undefined
     : parsedSessionTarget?.threadId;
```

Running with this patch: General→Finance, Finance→General, Finance→Finance, no-source (session fallback preserved), and explicit-target cases all behave as expected. Happy to open a PR with a test if the approach is acceptable.

issues.body:
# Bug report: @openclaw/google-meet 2026.9.2 — Meet-DOM/UI incompatibilities break agent voice sessions

**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.9.2, `@openclaw/google-meet` 2026.9.2 (global extension)
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Chrome via `chrome-node` transport, `mode: agent`
- Google Meet current web UI (uses Google Closure/Soy `__soy` DOM objects)
- Audio: BlackHole 2ch virtual device (verified working via sox loopback)

**Summary:** An agent joins the Meet call successfully but stays silent. Three distinct Meet-compatibility defects in `google-meet-platform-adapter-*.js` block the audio path. Fixes/workarounds below; #1 is a clean fix.

---

## Bug 1 (CRITICAL, clean fix) — in-call inspection crashes on circular JSON

The injected in-call inspection script ends with `return JSON.stringify({...})`. One of the serialized fields (caption/transcript extraction) holds a live Meet DOM node. Google Meet's DOM attaches a `__soy` property whose object closes a cycle back to the node, so `JSON.stringify` throws:

```
TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
  --> starting at object with constructor 'HTMLDivElement'
  |     property '__soy' -> object with constructor '_.AGx'
  --- property 'node' closes the circle
```

**Effect:** `page.evaluate` returns HTTP 500; the plugin can never confirm in-call (`inCall` reported `no` despite the agent being a participant), never establishes the audio bridge, and reports `manualAction: browser-control-unavailable`. `recover-tab` fails with the same error.

**Fix (verified):** make the final serialization circular-safe and drop DOM nodes. At the end of the in-call inspection object in `google-meet-platform-adapter-*.js` (~line 507):

```diff
-  });
+  }, (function(){var seen=new WeakSet();return function(k,v){if(v&&typeof v==='object'){if(typeof v.nodeType==='number')return undefined;if(seen.has(v))return undefined;seen.add(v);}return v;};})());
```

After this, `inCall` is correctly detected. (Better long-term: never place raw DOM nodes into the returned object — extract `.textContent` for caption fields.)

## Bug 2 (HIGH) — audio-routing verification depends on a fragile Meet Settings-UI scrape

`routeMeetAudioInput()` finds the correct virtual mic via `enumerateDevices()` (`audioInputDeviceLabel: "BlackHole 2ch (Virtual)"`), but then only sets `audioInputRouted = true` if `selectedMicrophoneLabel()` matches — and `selectedMicrophoneLabel()` relies on `findMicrophoneDeviceControl()` scraping Meet's Settings→Audio panel, which returns nothing on the current Meet UI. So `audioInputRouted`/`audioOutputRouted` stay `false` even when BlackHole 2ch is correctly selected as both mic and speaker, which keeps the mic muted and blocks the bridge (`meet-audio-choice-required`).

**Workaround applied:** trust a recognized virtual device from `enumerateDevices()` instead of the UI scrape (set `audioInputRouted`/`audioOutputRouted` true when a recognized device family is present). A robust fix should verify selection via the active `getUserMedia` track / `sinkId`, not the settings DOM.

## Bug 3 (HIGH, unresolved) — realtime bridge never starts; audio-choice check is non-deterministic

Even with Bugs 1–2 patched and both Meet devices on BlackHole 2ch:
- `googlemeet status` reports `audioInputRouted: True`, `audioOutputRouted: True`, `manualAction: None`, `meet output routed: yes`.
- but `googlemeet test-speech` on the **same** session returns `speechBlockedReason: meet-audio-choice-required`.
- `audio bridge: none`, `last input/output: 0 bytes`, `provider connected: unknown`, and no realtime connection appears in gateway logs.
- A related log line recurs: `unknown session key "agent:meet-consult:main"`.

The per-action re-inspection returning different routing answers points to remaining Meet-DOM assumptions. Net result: the realtime provider is never connected and no audio flows, so the agent is a silent participant.

---

## Repro
1. Configure a `meet-consult`-style agent, `chrome-node` transport, `mode: agent`, BlackHole 2ch.
2. `openclaw googlemeet create` / `join` a Meet space.
3. Observe: agent joins (visible as a participant) but is silent; `googlemeet doctor` shows `audio bridge: none`, `in call: no` (pre-Bug-1-fix) or `meet-audio-choice-required` / no bridge (post-fix).

## Impact
Agent voice mode in Google Meet is non-functional on current Meet with plugin 2026.9.2. BlackHole and OpenClaw config are not at fault (loopback verified).
