### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), npm install, Linux x64 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.17)
- Slack channel plugin, socket mode, streaming: off
- DM conversation (bot → user)

### Timeline (same session, same day, controlled A/B)
- 09:21–09:44 local on 2026.9.1's predecessor **2026.8.2 (0965053)**: assistant replies authored with single-asterisk Slack mrkdwn bold (`*text*`) rendered correctly as bold in Slack client. No formatting complaints all morning.
- ~09:55: upgraded to **2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)**, gateway restarted.
- 10:01 first reply containing `*text*` bold → delivered **literally** (stars visible).
- 10:04 A/B follow-up with standard markdown `**text**` → delivered **literally, stars included**.

### Interpretation
Under 2026.9.1 the Slack outbound path appears to send message text as plain text without invoking the markdown→mrkdwn conversion at all (both mrkdwn single-asterisk and standard double-asterisk pass through untouched). This matches the symptom family of:
- #22769 (message sent as rich_text block; conversion pipeline not called)
- #55460 (blocks path bypasses markdownToSlackMrkdwnChunks)
- #137129 (my earlier 8.2-era report; closed as unresolved/not reproducible — but rendering was intermittently broken there too)

Notably, on this same install 8.2 rendered the exact same authoring style correctly earlier the same morning, which points at a 9.1 outbound-pipeline regression rather than client/environment config.

### Question
Open PR #133136 ("fix(slack): render authored presentation text once across sends and edits") touches this area — is the 9.1 regression related to that change, and does it fix this?

### Requested fix
Restore (and keep) a single authoritative markdown→mrkdwn conversion on the Slack send path for assistant-authored text, regardless of blocks/rich_text presentation mode.

issues.title: [Bug]: 2026.9.1 official plugin update can time out on npm metadata while direct npm view succeeds

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

labels.name: impact:other
labels.description: This issue has meaningful maintainer-visible impact outside the owned taxonomy.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Plugin update / transient registry timeout

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.1, updating an official external npm plugin from the previous release cohort failed on npm metadata timeout even though:

- direct `npm view` against the same public registry succeeded;
- `openclaw plugins update ... --dry-run` correctly resolved the intended update;
- the exact package/version existed;
- `openclaw plugins install npm:<exact-version> --force` later succeeded immediately and produced a healthy post-upgrade state.

The same installation also repeatedly emitted a hard **3500 ms** timeout from `doctor --post-upgrade` while resolving the official plugin drift target.

This looks related to transient npm metadata handling, but does not appear to be an exact duplicate of #77616 or #127448.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)**
- OS: Ubuntu, Linux `6.8.0-138-generic` x64
- Node: `22.22.3`
- Install: npm global
- Plugin: official `@openclaw/searxng-plugin`
- Installed plugin before repair: **2026.8.2**
- Desired/release-cohort version: **2026.9.1**

### Reproduction / observed commands

After the core update to 2026.9.1, Doctor reported official plugin drift:

```text
Plugin searxng is 2026.8.2, but OpenClaw is 2026.9.1.
```

The package is present and resolves normally through npm:

```console
$ npm view @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 version \
    --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
2026.9.1
```

OpenClaw dry-run also resolves the update:

```console
$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 --dry-run
Would update searxng: 2026.8.2 -> 2026.9.1.
```

But the actual update failed:

```console
$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1
Failed to update searxng: npm view failed: termination timeout (no output from npm)
```

`doctor --post-upgrade` also repeatedly failed to confirm the exact repair target:

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 3500ms (elapsed 3502ms)
operation=npm-registry-update-check
url=https://registry.npmjs.org/%40openclaw%2Fsearxng-plugin/2026.9.1

[warn] plugin.version_drift: Plugin searxng is 2026.8.2, but OpenClaw is 2026.9.1.
No confirmed repair target is available; check registry availability and rerun this command.
```

Running repair with a larger outer timeout completed but did not move the exact-pinned plugin:

```console
$ openclaw update repair --timeout 60
...
Updating plugins...
npm plugins: 0 updated, 1 unchanged.
Update finalization completed.
```

The install record still pointed to the old exact version:

```json
{
  "spec": "@openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.8.2",
  "resolvedVersion": "2026.8.2"
}
```

A forced exact install through the OpenClaw plugin manager succeeded:

```console
$ openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 --force
Installing @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 ...
Installed plugin: searxng
```

After Gateway restart:

```json
{
  "packageVersion": "2026.9.1",
  "version": "2026.9.1",
  "builtWithOpenClawVersion": "2026.9.1"
}
```

and:

```text
openclaw doctor --post-upgrade
post-upgrade: no findings
```

### Source-level observation in v2026.9.1

`src/infra/update-check-package-target.ts` defaults the npm package target lookup to 3500 ms:

```ts
export async function fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus(params: {
  ...
  timeoutMs?: number;
  ...
}): Promise<NpmPackageTargetStatus> {
  const timeoutMs = params.timeoutMs ?? 3500;
  ...
}
```

For exact-pinned plugin drift, `src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.ts` calls this helper without a timeout override:

```ts
await fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus({ packageName, target: requestedTarget })
```

That matches the observed `npm-registry-update-check` timeout at ~3500 ms.

This does not necessarily prove that the separate `npm view failed: termination timeout (no output from npm)` from `plugins update` has the exact same timeout owner, but both failures occurred in the same official-plugin repair flow and direct npm metadata access succeeded.

### Expected behavior

- A transient >3.5s npm registry response should not prevent Doctor from resolving a valid official release-cohort repair target.
- Registry target checks should probably retry/back off or use a less aggressive deadline for maintenance/update workflows.
- An outer maintenance timeout such as `openclaw update repair --timeout 60` should ideally be able to influence nested registry metadata checks, or the nested timeout should be documented separately.
- `openclaw plugins update <exact official package@version>` should tolerate brief npm startup/registry stalls similarly to a normal direct npm invocation instead of failing on a no-output timeout when the package is reachable.

### Actual behavior

A valid official plugin update was blocked by transient metadata deadlines. Manual exact reinstall through the same OpenClaw plugin manager was required to converge the plugin to the core release cohort.

### Related issues

- #77616 — transient `npm view` failure produced a misleading unsupported-spec error. Closed/fixed; this report is about the update still failing on timeout in 2026.9.1 and the 3500 ms drift target lookup.
- #127448 — preserved timeout/signal termination identity for npm metadata/pack failures. Closed/fixed; in this report the termination identity is now visible (`termination timeout`), but the operation still fails under ordinary transient latency.

### Impact

Low-to-medium availability/maintenance impact:

- core update can finish with an official plugin still on the previous release cohort;
- `doctor --post-upgrade` may be unable to provide an actionable exact repair target due to a short registry deadline;
- users may repeatedly retry update/repair even though npm itself is reachable;
- workaround requires a more invasive forced exact plugin reinstall.

issues.body:
# OpenClaw 移动端 UI/UX 反馈

## 问题描述

聊天界面在键盘弹出后，大量关键内容被遮挡，严重影响使用体验。

## 截图说明

**设备**: LIO AN00 (华为)  
**系统**: Android  
**时间**: 2026-09-04

## 具体问题

### 1. 顶部筛选标签占用过多空间
- `leader_agent`、`aether_agnes_2_5_flash`、`主智能体`、`Memory Dreaming Promotion` 等标签横向排列
- 键盘弹出后这些标签完全被遮挡
- **建议**: 折叠为下拉菜单，或仅显示当前选中的会话名称

### 2. 输入区控件冗余
- 模型选择器 (`Agnes 2.5 Flash`) 和上下文滑块 (`上下文 8%·中`) 放置在输入框正上方
- 占据宝贵的聊天区域
- **建议**: 移至设置页或顶部导航栏，聊天时不需要频繁调整

### 3. 输入框设计过于复杂
- `+`、附件图标、视频图标、麦克风、发送按钮一排
- 文字提示 "向 OpenClaw 发送消息" 占空间
- **建议**: 
  - 简化为纯文本输入 + 发送按钮
  - 附件功能用 `+` 展开面板
  - 移除占位的提示文字

## 核心诉求

**键盘弹出时，聊天记录区域应保持可见。**

这是移动端聊天的基本要求，目前的设计导致用户无法看到历史消息，体验很差。

---

## 提交建议

请在 GitHub Issues 页面创建新 Issue，标题建议：
> [Mobile UI] 键盘弹出后聊天内容被遮挡，输入区控件布局不合理

附上此截图和问题描述。

issues.body:
## Summary

Same bug class as #123265 (Slack), #134240 (Telegram), #115978 (Feishu), #108409 (Discord) — the internal `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>` runtime-context carrier is being serialized as a standalone, visible **`user`-role turn** on the **Microsoft Teams (msteams)** channel, instead of staying attached/internal to the real inbound message. No msteams-specific issue exists yet for this class, filing one so it's tracked per-channel like the others.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.8.2** (`0965053`)
- Surface: Microsoft Teams, direct message (1:1)
- Model: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`
- Session kind: main agent, `msteams:direct:*`

## What was observed

Across a single ~40-minute live conversation, this exact block arrived as its own **top-level inbound turn** well over a dozen times, including:

1. **Fully bare**, with zero accompanying human-authored text — just the wrapper itself, e.g.:
   ```
   OpenClaw runtime context for the active user request in this turn. Do not reply to or describe this context. Use it to continue answering the active user request now. Do not wait for another message.
   This context is runtime-generated, not user-authored. Keep internal details private.

   <<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>
   Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
   {"chat_id":"conversation:a:<redacted>","message_id":"<redacted>","sender":{"id":"<redacted>","name":"<name>"},"timestamp":"Wed 2026-09-02 10:21:24 EDT","inbound_event_kind":"user_request","was_mentioned":true}

   System: [2026-09-02 10:21:24 EDT] Teams DM from <name>
   <<<END_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>
   ```
2. **Immediately following a tool result**, not a user message — e.g. it fired directly after an `exec` tool call returned (`openclaw --version` output), with the block itself appearing as the very next turn, before the human had sent anything new.
3. At least once with **no `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` header at all**, just plain text: `Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.` — suggesting the leaked carrier can also lose its own metadata wrapper and render as an even more ambiguous bare instruction.

Each occurrence:
- Declared `inbound_event_kind: user_request` and `was_mentioned: true`, i.e. self-identifies as a genuine new user message.
- Carried a live-looking `message_id` (differs from prior occurrences, unlike the pinned/stale message_id in #123265 — worth noting this may be a distinct variant where the carrier is regenerated per-turn rather than replayed).
- Instructed the model in-band not to reply to or describe it and to "continue now" without waiting — which is indistinguishable, from the model's position in the transcript, from a prompt-injection attempt impersonating system context.

## Why it matters

- **Security/trust impact**: because this is textually indistinguishable from a malicious actor injecting fake system-context blocks via the channel (same delimiter format, same "don't describe, don't wait" instruction pattern an attacker would use), a model has to choose between (a) treating it as a real hidden instruction and silently complying, or (b) refusing to comply and burning a large amount of the conversation on trust-verification with the actual user, which is what happened here — the agent correctly declined to act on it, but had to stop and explicitly interrogate legitimacy multiple times, degrading the interaction.
- **Channel coverage gap**: msteams doesn't yet have a tracked issue for this bug class, so it may not be in scope for whatever fix lands for Slack/Telegram/Feishu/Discord.
- Distinguishing detail vs. #123265: in this msteams case, `message_id` changed on each occurrence rather than staying pinned to one original message, and at least one occurrence dropped the `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` JSON header entirely, rendering as unstructured plain text. Might indicate either a different code path than the Slack case, or the same underlying carrier-placement bug with channel-specific serialization differences.

## Suggested next step

Treat as part of the same root-cause investigation as #123265 / #134240 / #69208 (umbrella), scoped additionally to the msteams delivery/inbound-event-assembly path. Happy to provide the full redacted session transcript if useful — reporting via a user request in the live session rather than filing directly, so I don't have direct repo write access context beyond this issue.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80); first observed on 2026.6.10
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; Mattermost + Telegram channels

**Symptom**
The scheduler has no end conditions. `openclaw cron add --help` / `cron edit --help` expose no until / max-runs / expire flag (re-checked on 2026.8.1-beta.3, 2026-08-26), so every recurring job runs until someone disables it. Job `state` carries `lastRunAtMs` / `nextRunAtMs` / `lastRunStatus` and *consecutive* error/skip counters, but **no cumulative run count**, so "stop after N runs" cannot be enforced externally either without keeping a counter elsewhere.

**Why it matters**
"Ends after N occurrences / ends on a date" is standard recurrence vocabulary and the natural shape for finite delegated work ("check this daily for two weeks", "remind me 5 times"). Without it, bounded chores become unbounded standing jobs that need manual cleanup.

**Proposed direction**
(a) `--until <ISO>` and `--max-runs <N>` on `cron add` / `cron edit`, plus a `state.runCount` counter; at the bound the job **disables** (not deletes) so the audit trail survives. (b) Failing that, just `state.runCount` — external tooling can then enforce bounds cheaply.

**Workaround we're using locally**
A sidecar sweep that counts fires from the tasks ledger and disables the job at the bound.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80)
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; control container + Playwright Chromium (CDP attach, `attachOnly:true`) in a shared netns; Mattermost + Telegram channels

**Symptom**
On a public Airtable form behind a Transcend "Cookie Preferences" modal, the browser tool's `snapshot` (default `ai` extraction) returned an **empty** tree twice while the modal was up, so the agent had no refs to act on. `openclaw browser snapshot --interactive` on the same tab returned the modal's controls (`button "Accept All" [ref=e2]`, `button "Reject All, Except Strictly Necessary" [ref=e3]`, …); `click e2` succeeded; a fresh `navigate` then rendered the form in the default snapshot. `browser.snapshotDefaults.mode` only admits `"efficient"`, so there is no config-level way to prefer the interactive extraction or an automatic fallback.

**Why it matters**
Consent modals are the most common overlay on public sites. An empty snapshot reads to the model as "nothing on this page", and it starts guessing (coordinate clicks, key presses) — in our case 39 identical retries before giving up.

**Proposed direction**
1. When the default snapshot is empty (or the document is `inert` / `aria-hidden` under a modal), fall back to the interactive extraction automatically and say so in the result.
2. Or surface modal/dialog controls in the default snapshot regardless of extraction mode.
3. Expose `interactive` / `fallback` under `browser.snapshotDefaults` so operators can set the policy once.

**Workaround we're using locally**
AGENTS prose: on an empty snapshot, re-snapshot with `interactive:true`, click the consent ref, then navigate again. Works, but every tenant has to know the trick.

issues.body:
## Summary

After a post-compaction memory-flush failure, a Telegram group session entered a state where **every inbound message dispatched a turn that produced zero transcript events and zero replies** — a silent swallow, with no error surfaced anywhere.

`sessions.reset` reported success but did not actually reset the session. Only `sessions.delete` recovered it.

## Observed

- `sessions.reset` returned `{ok: true, sessionId: ...}`.
- `session_windows` still showed the **same single window from 7 days earlier**; the call had only appended a `reset` marker to the existing window.
- Inbound messages continued to vanish exactly as before the reset (turn dispatched, zero transcript events, zero replies, no error).
- `sessions.delete` recovered the chat — it was rebuilt from its deterministic key on the next inbound message and behaved normally from then on.

## Why this matters

`sessions.reset` is the documented operator escape hatch for a wedged session. When it reports success while changing nothing observable, the operator has no signal that the session is still broken — meanwhile the channel is silently eating user messages.

## Requested

1. Make `sessions.reset` create a new session window (or report explicitly that it did not).
2. Surface silent-swallow sessions (turn dispatched, zero transcript events, zero reply payloads, repeatedly) as an error/health signal rather than nothing.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.7 (build dabe191), Node v26.5.0, macOS (Apple Silicon), single gateway under launchd
- Workload: ~100 cron jobs + Telegram DMs/groups + Slack; embedded (direct-API) runs
- Observed 2026-08-06/07 during a multi-day production investigation; not yet re-verified on 2026.8.x

issues.body:
## Summary

Compaction progress feedback (implemented in v2026.4.22 for Telegram via #56378) is not visible to webchat users. When auto-compaction triggers during a webchat session, the user experiences complete silence for 10-180+ seconds with no indication of what's happening. Additionally, there's no diagnostic API to determine whether a stalled compaction is caused by: (a) slow model response, (b) memory/context rebuild, (c) write-lock contention, or (d) provider timeout.

## Current Behavior (webchat)

1. User sends message → context exceeds threshold → auto-compaction triggers
2. User sees: nothing. No typing indicator, no status message, no progress bar
3. Compaction can take 10-180s depending on context size and model latency
4. User assumes system is frozen, may refresh or resend messages
5. If compaction times out (see #92043, #53008), session appears dead

## What Telegram Already Has (from #56378)

- Tool events start/refresh typing indicator
- Compaction drives explicit "Compacting..." / "Thinking..." feedback
- Live "Working..." message reused for tool/progress updates

## Proposed: Three Additions

### 1. Webchat Compaction Progress Events
Expose compaction lifecycle stages as SSE/WebSocket events to the webchat frontend:
- `compaction:start` — compaction triggered, include estimated token reduction
- `compaction:summarizing` — LLM summarization in progress
- `compaction:rebuilding` — context reconstruction in progress  
- `compaction:complete` — done, include actual token reduction + duration
- `compaction:timeout` — exceeded expected duration, include diagnostic info

This mirrors what Telegram already has, but through the webchat channel's native event mechanism.

### 2. Compaction Watchdog Diagnostic API
A `/api/diagnostics/compaction` endpoint (or `openclaw diagnose compaction` CLI) that reports:
- Last N compaction events: start time, duration, trigger reason (threshold/memoryFlush/midTurnPrecheck), model used, token count before/after
- Current in-progress compaction: elapsed seconds, current stage, model response status
- Write-lock state: holder, age, queue length
- Average compaction duration over last 24h/7d

This addresses the "black box" problem where operators can't determine why compaction is slow without digging through logs.

### 3. Async Pre-Compaction via Plugin Hooks
#85675 was closed as NOT_PLANNED for core, with the suggestion to use ClawHub plugins. The hooks exist (`afterTurn`, `compact` lifecycle). This issue requests:
- Documentation of the exact plugin API surface for implementing a "Session Memory" / "running summary" context engine
- A minimal example or reference implementation

This would allow background summarization at natural breaks (afterTurn), reusing the summary during compaction to skip the expensive LLM summarization call — making compaction near-instant.

## Environment
- OpenClaw v2026.4.27
- Channel: webchat
- Model: xfyun-coding/astron-code-latest (128K context)
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Related Issues
- #56378 (COMPLETED) — Telegram compaction progress feedback
- #85675 (NOT_PLANNED) — Session Memory / async compact (plugin path suggested)
- #92043 (OPEN) — Compaction timeout no partial-progress reuse
- #53008 (OPEN) — Compaction blocks main processing lane
- #45522 (COMPLETED) — Long-running task progress feedback

issues.body:
## Problem

A local image-context probe showed that OpenClaw can send a native image to the model and `openclaw infer image describe` can produce a good durable summary/OCR-style description, but the agent/LCM path did not persist any attachment metadata or media-understanding output for reuse. Follow-up turns can only recover image content if the assistant happened to mention it later.

## Desired behavior

- Agent image attachments should expose/persist durable media memory alongside the raw image reference: filename/source label, MIME type, byte size, dimensions/hash when known, attachment provenance, and `image.description` text/OCR output.
- Reuse existing media-understanding output when OpenClaw already produced it.
- If no prior summary exists, run `image.describe` once at ingest or maintenance time, not repeatedly during hot context assembly.
- Default summary budget should be about 512 tokens, with an OCR-heavy flyer/screenshot cap around 2,000 tokens.
- Fresh turns can still send the native image to capable models, but old/compacted/tool-stubbed context should receive a metadata+summary stub by default; raw image replay should be explicit.
- If summary generation fails, persist a metadata-only stub and raw reference so the agent still knows media existed.

## Why now

`Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#775` is being hardened so LCM can store image files and assemble bounded image-memory stubs instead of replaying raw base64. For best results, OpenClaw should hand lossless-claw the media-understanding summary/metadata directly instead of requiring LCM to infer it later from assistant prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deterministic image with visible text is sent through a local agent session.
- The first model call can use the native image.
- The durable context path stores/reuses image metadata and summary without retaining base64 in normal assembled context.
- A follow-up turn can answer from cached image memory after raw image replay is disabled.
- OCR-heavy flyer text is preserved under the 2,000-token cap.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.1-beta.1 (Windows), a file-transfer allowReadPaths policy reload timed out behind five retained work items, and the official --wait reload remained pending with the same count and no supported owner-level inspection available.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The installed runtime's waitForRetainedWork() and reload drain logic wait for applicable owners to settle before activating the replacement generation. A supported diagnostic/remediation is needed to identify and safely settle the retained owners; forcing counters to zero is not a safe expected outcome.

### Actual behavior

Automatic reload exceeded its 60-second drain budget and explicitly kept the previous generation active. A later official `openclaw plugins reload file-transfer --wait --json` again reported five retained work items and did not complete before the wait request was cancelled. Gateway remained responsive. These five references are NOT five identified transfers; owner identities and completion states remain unknown.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1-beta.1 (CLI commit 6830fe7); bundled file-transfer 2026.10.1-beta.1; Node 24.21.0

### Operating system

Windows; managed Gateway runs as a Scheduled Task

### Install method

System npm installation (bundled runtime code inspected locally)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See sanitized diagnostic report in Additional information. No raw logs/configuration or personal data attached.

### Impact and severity

Policy activation and safe recovery are blocked: owner settlement cannot be verified, so a further restart and CSV read validation remain deferred. This is one observed environment, not a demonstrated regression or clean-room reproduction.

### Additional information

# Bug report: file-transfer policy reload blocked by uninspectable retained work

Submission prepared from a sanitized local diagnostic report.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.10.1-beta.1` (CLI reports commit `6830fe7`).
- Host: Windows; managed Gateway runs as a Scheduled Task.
- Node runtime reported by Gateway logs: `24.21.0`.
- Plugin: bundled `file-transfer`, enabled, version `2026.10.1-beta.1`.
- Gateway remained responsive to read-only status/inspection requests.
- Times below are Asia/Seoul (UTC+09:00), 2026-10-07.

## Impact

A change to the file-transfer plugin's node `allowReadPaths` policy failed to apply during a plugin replacement. The failure explicitly reported that the previous plugin generation stayed active. Operators cannot determine whether the retained count represents transfers, consumers, or runtime custody, and cannot safely reconcile the owners before restarting.

The current policy state after subsequent lifecycle events has NOT been verified with a CSV read. This report does not claim that the old policy is still active now.

## Confirmed evidence

### Automatic policy reload

At 21:09:17.744:

```text
Plugin replacement queued behind 5 retained work item(s) for plugin file-transfer; applies when they finish within the 60s drain budget.
```

At 21:10:17.786:

```text
config reload failed: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during drain: plugin file-transfer admitted work did not settle within 60s; the previous plugin generation stays active. Use `openclaw plugins reload file-transfer --wait` to wait until it finishes. | plugin host cleanup timed out: retained plugin work
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.
```

### Later managed lifecycle event

Managed Gateway restart was recorded at 21:23:18.247; HTTP startup was recorded at 21:24:40.338. These events predate the latest constrained recovery attempt. They do not prove that all preceding work settled safely or that the requested policy was applied.

### Official manual reload

Command run:

```powershell
openclaw plugins reload file-transfer --wait --json
```

At 22:51:55.079:

```text
Plugin replacement queued behind 5 retained work item(s) for plugin file-transfer; waiting until they finish or the request is cancelled.
```

The request did not complete. Only the matching reload CLI processes were terminated to cancel the wait; the Gateway process was preserved. Server confirmation at 22:53:43.811 (connection/request identifiers removed):

```text
plugins.reload 110682ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=This operation was aborted
```

The active-only session inventory during diagnosis returned one running main conversation. This is NOT an inventory of runtime consumers or transfers and does not prove there are no other retained owners.

## Related failures; causality unproven

Previous management/setup attempts reported:

```text
Inference setup probe cleanup did not finish safely.
Prepared plugin generation cleanup failed
CLI cleanup timed out: shared-state after 5000ms
```

A management attempt made during the manual reload wait was rejected with:

```text
Model runtime replacement is in progress; admitted plugin work cannot wait for the reload. Retry after the plugin reload completes.
```

After cancellation, the management tool could enter successfully, but did not expose per-reference owner inspection or release capabilities. Whether the setup/cleanup failures share the same underlying owner leak remains unknown.

## Installed runtime code observations

These are observations from installed bundled code, not a proven root cause or an upstream fix.

- `dist/plugin-setup-module-nAV3303O.mjs`, around lines 1690–1708:
  - `retainWork()` adds an anonymous `{}` token to `this.retainedWork` and returns a release callback.
  - `retainedWorkCount` adds `retainedWork.size` to consumers whose `kind` is `work`.
  - `waitForRetainedWork()` waits for the applicable counts to reach zero.
- `dist/runtime-plugins-2JwehrGU.mjs`, around lines 25–48:
  - `retainRuntimePluginWork()` retains work across registry invocation instances.
  - `releaseRuntimePluginWork()` does not release the work token if cleanup throws an error marked as retaining runtime resources. This may be intentional resource custody; it is not evidence that the reference is safe to discard.
- `dist/server-plugin-reload-CbQVxS81.mjs`, around lines 282–308:
  - Reload sums retained counts and waits for settlement; `--wait` removes the normal drain deadline.

Consequently, the observed number 5 must NOT be presented as five identified file-transfer jobs. Their IDs, start times, file paths, initiating actors, and individual status classifications are currently unknown.

## Requested maintainer assistance

1. Provide a supported, payload-free diagnostic for each plugin generation's retained work, ordinary calls, and consumers: opaque reference ID, owner kind, lifetime, originating operation/session where available, completion/release state, and whether cleanup is still physically pending.
2. Establish whether these five references are live transfers, completed-but-retained custody, or failed cleanup owners. Provide safe owner-level completion/cancellation/release rather than forcibly clearing counters.
3. Investigate possible runtime/setup cleanup ownership cycles. Do not assume a leak solely from a nonzero counter.
4. Provide a supported remediation or fixed release, and a way to prove settlement and policy generation activation.
5. Regression coverage should include completed/failed/cancelled owners, reload cancellation preserving the previous generation, and path-policy activation only after safe drain.

## Observed sequence, not a minimal clean-room reproduction

1. A paired-node file-transfer read policy was changed.
2. Automatic reload hit the 60-second drain limit and kept the preceding generation.
3. A later managed restart occurred, but safe settlement/policy activation were not proven.
4. Official `plugins reload file-transfer --wait --json` again reported five retained items and remained pending until cancelled.

No additional transfers were started to reproduce this report. A minimal reproduction has not yet been established.

## Recovery constraints

- No deletion/modification of user analysis outputs, CSVs, locks, or checkpoints.
- No retry of failed/stuck file transfers.
- No force-clear of reference counters or state files.
- No additional Gateway restart until safe settlement is proven.
- After settlement and a managed restart, only one small read test against the same CSV path is authorized.
- Analysis and trading remain stopped; no orders were executed.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes raw configuration/log attachments, credentials, personal filesystem paths, hostnames, node IDs, account/session IDs, CSV contents, and connection/request identifiers. The displayed errors and bundled filenames were selected manually. Do not attach the original raw logs/configuration to a public issue without a separate privacy review.

The installed package metadata declares its issue tracker as:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A WhatsApp group's session acquires a spurious `conversations` row with kind="direct" but peer_id equal to the group's own JID, gets promoted to role="primary" in session_conversations, and every subsequent inbound message for that group then fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'`.

### Steps to reproduce

No confirmed deterministic manual repro. Observed correlation (not proven causal) across two independent occurrences on the same long-lived WhatsApp group session, both times while Control UI/dashboard `chat.history`/`chat.metadata` RPC calls against that session were failing with errorCode=UNAVAILABLE, errorMessage="session history is rebuilding; retry shortly" — i.e. dashboard access to the session's history while the WhatsApp channel is actively processing a message for that same session.

### Expected behavior

Inbound messages for a WhatsApp group should always resolve to the existing kind="group" conversation row for that peer_id. No kind="direct" row should ever be created with a peer_id that is a group JID, and session_windows.chat_type for a group session should remain "group".

### Actual behavior

conversations table ends up with two rows for the same peer_id (120363429459936309@g.us): one kind="group" (correct, original) and one kind="direct" (spurious). The spurious row is promoted to session_conversations.role="primary" for the session, demoting the correct group row to role="related". session_windows.chat_type for that session then reads "direct" instead of "group". Every subsequent inbound message for the group fails with:
Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'
Reproduced twice in one calendar day on the same session_id, both times yielding the identical spurious conversation_id hash (conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148) — consistent with the conversation-ref hash being deterministic over (channel, accountId, kind, peerId, parentConversationRef, threadId), so the same wrong inputs regenerate the same wrong row.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (first occurrence), 2026.8.2 (second occurrence, same day, after upgrading)

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro

### Install method

npm global install (openclaw package). Gateway run as a Windows Scheduled Task service, loopback bind.

### Model

deepseek-v4-flash (custom-registered model entry, not in built-in catalog)

### Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp channel -> OpenClaw Gateway (local, loopback) -> agent "wa" -> DeepSeek API (openai-completions-compatible, api.deepseek.com). Fallback chain (gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-5) not implicated; failure occurs at the conversation/session bookkeeping layer, before any model call.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Custom deepseek-v4-flash model entry with manually-declared contextWindow/contextTokens. session.dmScope="per-channel-peer". tools.sessions.visibility="self". tools.agentToAgent enabled. No custom hooks touch conversation identity resolution.

### Logs

```shell
"message":"message processed: channel=whatsapp chatId=+52XXXXXXXXXX messageId=3AD1AC718294DC014478 sessionId=be37c314-124e-4823-9466-cb86754e8ef3 sessionKey=agent:wa:whatsapp:group:120363429459936309@g.us outcome=error duration=178ms error=\"Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'\""

Preceding, repeatedly, at the time of both occurrences:
"message":"⇄ res ✗ chat.history 133ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=session history is rebuilding; retry shortly"

conversations table excerpt (sanitized):
{"conversation_id":"conv_2954465dff82db10951e6b76b19da7a5","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"group","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
{"conversation_id":"conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"direct","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Sanitized SQLite excerpts and a full trajectory export (openclaw sessions export-trajectory) are available on request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: a single WhatsApp group channel used for team/business communication (one agent, one account). Severity: blocks workflow entirely — total inbound-message outage for the affected group until a manual database repair (delete the spurious row, restore role="primary" on the correct group conversation, respecting the partial unique index on session_conversations.role='primary'). Frequency: intermittent, but recurred twice within roughly 9 hours on the same session_id. Consequence: missed incoming business messages until manually detected and fixed; no automated alerting surfaces this failure mode.

### Additional information

Jarvis is the display name/persona of the WhatsApp bot as seen by the group's human participants, not an OpenClaw-internal name — included for context since it appears in session labels/logs. Not confirmed as a regression: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO on last-known-good version, as this was not deliberately bisected. Suspected root cause (unconfirmed): the dashboard/session-resolution code path may create conversation rows without the WhatsApp admission context (group vs. direct) available, defaulting to kind="direct" keyed by whatever raw JID it has, instead of resolving the existing kind="group" conversation for that peer_id.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw config patch` / `config set` / gateway `config.patch` should return deterministic, machine-readable feedback about whether a config change is active in the running gateway.

Today the operator/agent often sees generic text such as `Restart the gateway to apply.` and then has to infer the real state by reading logs, checking health, or restarting defensively.

## Why this is distinct from #81409

#81409 and merged PR #81612 add `reloadKind` metadata to `config.schema.lookup`, which is useful before making a change.

This request is about the post-apply acknowledgement after the write/reload actually happens:

- Was the config written to disk?
- Did the gateway see the change?
- Was hot reload attempted?
- Did hot reload complete?
- Is a gateway restart still required?
- Which exact paths/reasons caused that status?

## Current operator failure mode

A user asks an OpenClaw agent to change config. The agent applies a patch and gets generic restart guidance. The system is deterministic, but the feedback exposed to the agent/user is not deterministic enough, so the agent cannot confidently say one of these:

- `config write done; hot reload done; effective now`
- `config write done; reload not applicable; restart required`
- `config write done; hot reload failed/deferred; restart required`
- `config write rejected; runtime unchanged`

That ambiguity caused avoidable churn during a `2026.5.18` troubleshooting session: the agent could not tell whether message/tool-error config changes were live, whether they needed a restart, or whether the restart instruction was only conservative CLI copy.

## Suggested response shape

For `--json` CLI output and gateway RPC responses, return something like:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "writeId": "cfg_...",
  "changedPaths": ["messages.suppressToolErrors"],
  "reloadPlan": [
    {
      "path": "messages.suppressToolErrors",
      "reloadKind": "hot"
    }
  ],
  "apply": {
    "configWrite": "done",
    "hotReload": "done",
    "restartRequired": false,
    "restartReasons": []
  },
  "effectiveRuntime": {
    "verified": true,
    "checkedAt": "2026-05-19T01:xx:xxZ"
  }
}
```

For human CLI output, make the terminal state explicit:

```text
Applied 1 config update.
Reload: hot reload done.
Effective now: yes.
Restart required: no.
```

or:

```text
Applied 1 config update.
Reload: not applied to running gateway.
Restart required: yes (gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs).
Effective now: no.
```

## Why this matters

OpenClaw agents are now first-class operators of OpenClaw itself. They need deterministic config feedback so they do not guess, restart unnecessarily, or tell users a setting is active when it is only written to disk.

The core ask: after a config write, expose `reload done` / `restart required` / `reload failed` as an explicit contract, not something inferred from logs.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary After a Codex-native parent has already received successful child results via wait_agent and produced its final response, OpenClaw can still create a second synthetic announce:codex-native Main that repeats the final answer; the same failure chain was independently observed through both Telegram and WebChat. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use an existing OpenClaw conversation/session backed by Codex. 2. Restart the OpenClaw Gateway / Codex app-server lifecycle. 3. Continue using the same conversation after the restart. 4. Send a request that first produces a normal user-visible progress message, then spawns one or more Codex-native children, waits for their terminal results with wait_agent, and produces a final answer after receiving all child results. 5. In the failing observations, the native child or children complete successfully and the original Main receives their results and produces the correct final answer. 6. Immediately afterward, inspect the gateway log. 7. In the failing runs, OpenClaw logs: Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion; falling back to requester-agent handoff: active requester session could not be woken: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming 8. A separate announce:codex-native:::succeeded Main run is then created and produces the same final answer again. This sequence was independently observed once through Telegram and once through WebChat / Control UI. In the current WebChat case, immediately repeating an equivalent orchestration request in the same session did not reproduce the duplicate. The exact reproduction rate has not been established. ### Expected behavior When the active parent has already received the successful terminal child result through wait_agent and incorporated that result into its final response, the same child completion should not create another requester-visible Main execution. As a known-good comparison, an immediately repeated equivalent WebChat orchestration in the same session produced only one final response. ### Actual behavior The native child or children complete successfully, the original Main receives their results, and the original Main produces the correct final response. After that response is already complete, OpenClaw attempts to wake the requester for subagent completion. The wake fails with: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming OpenClaw then falls back to a requester-agent handoff and creates a separate: announce:codex-native:...:succeeded Main run. That second Main produces the same final answer again. This is not one assistant message being rendered twice. The two visible responses correspond to two distinct Main executions. ### OpenClaw version 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1) ### Operating system Windows 11 host / Linux WSL (OpenClawGateway) ### Install method npm global installation using the OpenClaw-managed Node.js runtime inside WSL ### Model codex/gpt-5.6-sol (parent); openai/gpt-5.6-luna (native children) ### Provider / routing chain OpenClaw -> Codex app-server parent -> OpenClaw native Codex subagents -> OpenAI child models ### Additional provider/model setup details Current WebChat reproduction: Parent: codex/gpt-5.6-sol Native children: openai/gpt-5.6-luna Two independent native children were used. Child 1 calculated: 17 x 23 = 391 Child 2 calculated: 19 x 29 = 551 Both children completed successfully. The original parent received both results and produced: FINALITY_MULTI_OK 391 551 before the later synthetic announce:codex-native Main produced the same final result again. The earlier independent reproduction occurred through Telegram using the same Codex-native child / wait_agent execution path. Node.js: v24.19.0 ### Logs ```shell WebChat reproduction on OpenClaw 2026.9.5: 2026-09-23T01:48:29+09:00 [warn] Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion; falling back to requester-agent handoff: active requester session could not be woken: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming sessionId= gatewayHealth=live 2026-09-23T01:48:29+09:00 [warn] Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion; falling back to requester-agent handoff: active requester session could not be woken: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming sessionId= gatewayHealth=live 2026-09-23T01:48:46+09:00 [agents/agent-command] [agent] run announce:codex-native:::succeeded ended with stopReason=stop ------------------------------------ The two not_streaming wake failures occurred in the two-child WebChat reproduction. The announce:codex-native entry is a separate synthetic Main execution that followed the already completed original Main response. ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Cross-surface visual evidence **Telegram reproduction** The first screenshot shows the original successful Codex-native child execution and final response, followed by the same final response again with a separate Main execution footer. **WebChat / Control UI reproduction** The second screenshot shows the original Main response with two successful native Luna children, followed by the identical final response from a second Main that has no child executions of its own. Together, these screenshots show the same duplicate-final behavior through two different requester surfaces. The corresponding gateway logs show: `queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming` → `requester-agent handoff` → `announce:codex-native` → second Main This makes a channel-specific Telegram or WebChat rendering defect unlikely. ### Impact and severity Affected systems/channels: Codex-backed OpenClaw sessions using native child agents. The same failure chain has been observed through both Telegram and WebChat / Control UI. Severity: User-visible behavior defect. The system creates a real second Main execution and shows the same final answer twice. Frequency: Intermittent. Two independent failures have been observed across two different requester surfaces. In both investigations the failure occurred around the first relevant native-child orchestration after a Gateway / Codex app-server restart. In the current WebChat case, an immediately repeated equivalent request completed normally without duplication. Observed consequences: - duplicate user-visible final response - an additional synthetic Main execution - additional model execution for a result that had already been delivered by the original Main ### Additional information ## Cross-surface reproduction This behavior has been independently observed through two different requester surfaces. ### Earlier Telegram reproduction The observed sequence was: ```text Codex-native child completes successfully -> parent receives the child result -> original Main sends its final Telegram response -> requester completion wake fails with reason=not_streaming -> requester-agent fallback -> announce:codex-native synthetic Main -> the same final answer is sent again

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

Yes

### Summary

Environment

OpenClaw: 2026.9.7 (c074824)

Node.js: v24.21.0

OS: Linux x86_64

Kernel:
Linux [vps].de 5.2.0 #1 SMP Mon Sep 30 15:36:27 MSK 2024 x86_64 GNU/Linux

Gateway: system-wide systemd service

Service file: /etc/systemd/system/openclaw.service

Gateway stopped during all migration/repair attempts

OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external

Summary

After upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.9.7, two agent databases require session-identity migration:

~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite

~/.openclaw/agents/openclaw/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite

Both use schema version 19.

Running openclaw doctor --fix while the Gateway is completely stopped reproducibly damages the existing shared-state database:

~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

The command creates its normal pre-migration backups, then aborts with:

Doctor could not complete maintenance.
Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
Existing shared-state database generation changed:
/home/superadmin/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

After the failed repair, the live openclaw.sqlite has been observed as a 0-byte file.

Restoring the shared-state database from the automatically generated pre-migration backup makes read-only OpenClaw commands work again.



### Steps to reproduce

Reproduction

Stop the Gateway completely:

sudo systemctl stop openclaw.service
ps -ef | grep '[o]penclaw'

No OpenClaw process remains.

Verify the restored shared-state DB:

file ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

Result:

SQLite 3.x database, user version 19, ...

Current state:

size=7892992

Read-only doctor succeeds:

OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external \
openclaw doctor --lint --json

The remaining relevant findings are only that the two agent databases use schema version 19 and require doctor --fix.

Session SQLite inspection also confirms both agent databases are healthy:

openclaw doctor \
  --session-sqlite inspect \
  --session-sqlite-all-agents \
  --json

Results:

main

DB size: 81571840

integrityCheck: "ok"

11 SQLite session entries

no issues

openclaw

DB size: 602112

integrityCheck: "ok"

no issues

Run the requested repair:

OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external \
openclaw doctor --fix

Doctor creates pre-migration backups and then exits with:

Existing shared-state database generation changed:
/home/superadmin/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

After a failed run, the live shared-state DB has been observed as:

-rw------- ... openclaw.sqlite

with size:

0 bytes

No process has the DB/WAL/SHM files open according to lsof.

Recovery

Restoring the automatically generated pre-migration backup restores normal read-only access:

cp \
  ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak \
  ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

After restoration:

file ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite

again reports:

SQLite 3.x database, user version 19

and:

OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external \
openclaw doctor --lint --json

works again without the generation changed error.

Current shared-state file

dev=1533064801
inode=2758105
birth=-
size=7892992
mtime=2026-09-30 22:30:02.630829665 +0000
ctime=2026-09-30 22:30:02.630829665 +0000

Relevant code path

The failure appears to originate from the existing shared-state generation guard in the 2026.9.7 build:

if (
  !current.isFile() ||
  current.dev !== original.dev ||
  current.ino !== original.ino ||
  current.birthtimeNs !== original.birthtimeNs
) {
  throw new Error(
    `Existing shared-state database generation changed: ${params.pathname}`
  );
}

The existing DB is opened through the existing-only path and the generation is checked again after schema maintenance.

The issue therefore appears to be that some operation during doctor --fix changes/recreates/truncates the canonical shared-state DB while the repair still holds the original generation admission.

Expected behavior

doctor --fix should migrate the agent databases while preserving the existing healthy shared-state database.

If a migration cannot safely proceed, it should abort without modifying or truncating the canonical openclaw.sqlite.

Actual behavior

doctor --fix reproducibly aborts with:

Existing shared-state database generation changed

and the canonical shared-state SQLite DB has been observed truncated to 0 bytes.

Additional observations

Gateway is fully stopped during the repair.

No OpenClaw process remains.

lsof shows no process holding the shared-state DB, WAL, or SHM files.

Read-only doctor works after restoring the backup.

Both agent DBs pass SQLite integrity inspection.

The issue is reproducible.

Downgrading is not a viable workaround because the restored state DB already uses schema version 19.

Manual schema editing has not been attempted.

The automatically generated pre-migration backups successfully preserve the original data.

This looks like a data-loss-risk issue in the 2026.9.7 repair/migration path.

### Expected behavior

Update should have run through without any errors and resulting in an operataional updated OpenClaw instance.

### Actual behavior

openclaw System is down.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (c074824)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

### Install method

global npm install

### Model

none bc update lead to system crash; before Qwen3.8 flash via open router

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openrouter -> Qwen3.8 flash

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: OpenClaw Users who want to migrate to OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (c074824)
Severity: High (full system crash)
Frequency: always, no way backwards
Consequence: Openclaw is nonoperational

Last known good version was 2026.9.5 but I could not downgrade anymore.

issues.body: ### Bug type Regression (worked before, now fails) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary First, credit where due: 2026.9's Control UI is a big step toward a real Claude Desktop-style web interface. The points below are interaction/information-architecture friction on top of an otherwise strong redesign, not a complaint about the direction. ## 1. "Home" is not a root "Home" reads as the website/app convention: one root, where the app opens. In the Control UI it's actually the current agent's default session, and it can't be deleted. With multiple agents there are multiple "Home"s, each one changing silently when you switch agent in the picker directly above it — the opposite of what "root" implies. There is a difference between new empty main session and creating a new session. Different capabilities. Unclear why though. Suggestion: rename to "Main session", "Main" or similar. (Loosely related to #150382, where Home also routes wrong after visiting Dashboards — different bug, same underlying fuzziness.) Still the function of Home is quite ambiguous. I think you should seperate new session and configuration into multiple controls. Explicit and unique function in the UI > "Edit sidebar" and "New" ## 2. "Groups" is actually three different mechanisms, none of which agree with each other Sessions and Groups are shown as if Groups nests inside Sessions, when conceptually it's the reverse (a group is a set of sessions, so they should be siblings). Worse by implmentation, "assigning a group" can mean three different things depending on how you do it: - A gateway-wide `session_groups` table (name + cwd), independent of any agent. Why would you create a group on gateway-level?! Just type the group twice or three times. Way too complicated for simple experience. - A per-agent, per-session `category` field, set via right-click → "New group". - `pinned_at` on the session — reached by dragging a row **above** the "SESSIONS" header, which looks like it should mean "ungroup" but is actually an unrelated pin flag. Reproduced live: a group "Appelflap" existed in the gateway table from testing on one agent. Dragging two sessions into "Appelflap" on a *different* agent (Grease-monkey) never touched that table — it wrote `category: "Appelflap"` into Grease-monkey's own per-agent database. Separately, dragging those same two sessions above the "SESSIONS" header set `pinned_at` on them, which made the "Appelflap" group header disappear from the sidebar entirely (not because the group is empty — it has two members — but because both are now rendered in the pinned zone instead). So a group with real members can silently vanish as a side effect of an unrelated pin action, and nothing in the UI names what any of these three stores actually is. I believe assigned groups should stay within the agent always no exlusion and never escape it's (agent) context. It's an ingredient for headache. A group is a container for sessions within the container agent. You could implement Tags which live among agents but that's a whole different direction of classification. ## 3. "Other" and "Group": entries I never created, can't delete or rename After the 2026.9 migration, my sidebar shows groups called "Other" and "Group" that I never made. Neither exists in any agent's `session_nodes.category` values nor in the gateway `session_groups` table, so they're most likely client-side placeholders, not real stored groups — which would explain why there's nothing to rename or delete. If so, the UI shouldn't render them with the same right-click affordances (rename/delete) as real, user-created groups. ## 4. A group's "Delete" option disappears with its last visible row "Delete group" lives only in the right-click menu on the group's own header row. Whether that row renders depends on "Hide empty groups" (`filtering` / `always` / `never`); unless it's `always`, a group with zero *currently displayed* sessions draws no header at all, so its only delete affordance is unreachable. There's no group-management list elsewhere (e.g. Settings) as a fallback. This is exactly how "Other" and "Group" (point 3) and "Appelflap" (point 2) became permanent. ## 5. New session in Agent A assign agent B and workspace C - Users can start a new session in Agent A and able to select agent B for new chat. Why when we have seperate Agents? Quite more disturbing if you ask me when I'm able to select a workspace that actually configured for another agent. Less is more. Keep it simple. ## Ask - Rename "Home" to name what it is (a per-agent default session). Function of 'home' is ambigues though. I truly think you should seperate controls/settings and sessions/chats. A default new session make more sense then home with hidden controls for settings and a special chat state. Seperate into at least 2 controls: "Edit sidebar" and "New"/"New Session". - place jail agent sessions in agent! - Give Sessions and Groups clear hierarchy and simplify group concept. Do we really need a Swiss army knife for group concept? issues.body:
## Summary

Proposing a new `doctor:secret-resolve-preflight` health contribution that walks the user's secret target registry and warns on shape-coverage gaps the CLI's apply path can't handle.

Today, when the gateway emits a secret assignment for a target whose `secretShape` is `sibling_ref` and whose value path doesn't exist in source config, the CLI's `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` crashes via `setPathExistingStrict` ("Cannot set value at non-existent path"). PR #78555 fixes that specific instance by introducing a `setPathCreateStrict` path for sibling_ref. **This issue asks the orthogonal question: should doctor _also_ catch the general class proactively, so future shape additions don't reopen the same hole?**

## Motivation

The bug class is **shape coverage drift** — the gateway emits shapes the CLI's apply path hasn't grown a handler for. The user finds out by hitting a crash during `openclaw status`, `openclaw channels list`, or doctor itself, not by anything diagnosable from their config.

`sibling_ref` is the first concrete instance, but the same class can recur whenever a plugin registers a new `secretShape` or the gateway introduces a new resolution path the CLI hasn't switched on yet. Doctor is the natural place to surface this — it already loads the user's config and runs diagnose-only contributions for adjacent concerns (`doctor:gateway-config`, `doctor:gateway-auth`).

## Proposed design

A new contribution `doctor:secret-resolve-preflight`, slotted right after `doctor:gateway-auth` in `resolveDoctorHealthContributions()`. For each target returned by `discoverConfigSecretTargets(ctx.cfg)`:

- If `secretShape === "sibling_ref"` and `getPath(ctx.cfg, target.pathSegments) === undefined` → warn. Suggested remediation: upgrade to a CLI build that resolves sibling_ref SecretRefs via `setPathCreateStrict` (i.e. a build including PR #78555 once merged).
- If `secretShape` is anything other than the values this CLI build recognizes (`secret_input`, `sibling_ref`) → warn with the path + the unrecognized shape. Defense-in-depth for future shape additions that ship in the gateway before the matching CLI handler lands.

It does **not** mutate the config — the user's config is correct; the remediation is always a CLI upgrade.

## Draft

A draft implementation is on a fork branch for evaluation:
<https://github.com/octocore-autonomous-systems/openclaw/tree/feat/doctor-secret-resolve-preflight> (commit `27898c0f6f`)

Diff: +51 lines in `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts`, +108 lines in `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`. No framework changes; six new tests covering registration ordering, empty-config, populated/absent value paths for both shape branches, and unknown-shape defense-in-depth. All tests pass locally on `upstream/main`. Happy to convert into a PR if maintainers prefer to evaluate at that surface.

## Relationship to PR #78555

This is **orthogonal** to PR #78555. #78555 fixes the specific sibling_ref crash by changing the apply primitive; this proposal adds a defensive doctor surface for the general class. They don't conflict — merging this without #78555 just means doctor warns affected users while they wait for the fix, and merging both keeps doctor catching any future shape additions where the CLI handler list falls behind the gateway.

If you'd prefer a different remediation entirely (e.g. exhaustiveness-typed `secretShape` at the registry boundary so missing CLI handlers fail at build time), I'm equally happy to abandon this branch in favor of that direction — wanted to surface the proposal while the shape is fresh.

15:39:24.506 [model-fetch] start provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-5
15:39:25.630 [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic model=claude-opus-5 status=200 elapsedMs=1124

issues.body:
## Summary

`MAX_OVERFLOW_COMPACTION_ATTEMPTS = 3` is a hardcoded const at `pi-embedded-Bcz04p2i.js:1955` (verified in 2026.5.7 tarball). When a long-lived agent hits context-overflow, the runtime tries up to 3 LLM-summarizer compactions before bubbling the error. Each attempt is a billable model round-trip. For agents on per-seat ChatGPT Team/Pro/Enterprise quotas, a sustained overflow loop burns the seat very fast.

## Real-world impact

A long-lived `agent:<bot>:main` session running `openai-codex/gpt-5.5`:
- 7 context-overflow events in 17 hours.
- Each triggered up to 3 compaction calls.
- ~21 billable compaction calls × ~34K tokens each, on top of normal traffic.
- Seat hit 66-hour cooldown.

The 2026.5.4 post-compaction loop guard helps when the agent is repeating the same `(tool, args, result)` triple, but it does not protect against compaction itself running 3× per overflow on a session where the summary is structurally too large.

## Proposed fix

Expose as `agents.defaults.compaction.maxOverflowAttempts` (default 3, lower to 1 to fail-fast on overflow). Sibling keys (`compaction.mode`, `compaction.reserveTokens`, `compaction.recentTurnsPreserve`) suggest this slot is the natural home.

## Related

- #63216 (repeated hard resets on same session key) — adjacent failure mode
- #45505 (post-timeout compaction reconciliation)

(Re-filed from `badlogic/pi#4` — filed in wrong repo originally.)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After hand-editing `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env` and running `openclaw gateway restart`, the systemd unit restarts genuinely (new `MainPID`, new `ActiveEnterTimestamp`), yet the agent's `exec` tool calls keep serving the *old* environment variable value. The stale value is confirmed to differ from the current file contents via direct sha256 comparison, and the mismatch persists across repeated retests minutes apart — it is not a race/timing artifact. The gateway's own child process tree for tool execution (`service-child-relay.js` → `service-child-group-anchor.js`) appears to hold a cached environment snapshot that a normal restart does not refresh.


### Steps to reproduce

- On OpenClaw 2026.8.2, edit a manually-added (non-plugin-managed) variable in `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env`, e.g. change `SOME_TOKEN=<old-value>` to `SOME_TOKEN=<new-value>`.
- Run `openclaw gateway restart`.
- Confirm the restart is genuine: `systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway -p ActiveState -p ActiveEnterTimestamp -p MainPID` shows a new `MainPID` and a fresh `ActiveEnterTimestamp`.
- From an agent `exec` tool call (a child of the gateway process), compare the live env var against the file, without printing either value:
  ```bash
  echo "Live: $(printf '%s' "$SOME_TOKEN" | sha256sum)"
  echo "File: $(grep '^SOME_TOKEN=' ~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env | cut -d= -f2- | sha256sum)"
  ```
- Observe the hashes differ, even though the file and the systemd unit both reflect the new value.

### Expected behavior

After a genuine gateway restart (new PID, new activation timestamp), every process in the gateway's own process tree — including whatever handles `exec` tool calls — should reflect the environment as loaded from `EnvironmentFile=` at that restart. A restart should not leave any part of the gateway's own subprocess tree running with a stale pre-restart environment snapshot.


### Actual behavior

Concrete repro from 2026-09-06, verified twice (initially and again several minutes later, same result both times):

- File value hash (from `gateway.systemd.env` directly): `720bad96...`
- Live `exec`-call env value hash (same variable name, same process tree, post-restart): `3d6ba3a4...`
- These do not match.
- A CLI tool that reads the same variable directly from the environment (not typed/interpolated by the agent) — `ntn whoami` / `ntn doctor` — failed with an authentication error using the live (stale) value, while the exact same command succeeded when the file was explicitly re-sourced first: `(set -a; source ~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env; set +a; ntn whoami)`.
- This rules out the credential itself being the problem — the file's current value is correct and valid; only the inherited environment in the tool-execution path is stale.
- Process tree observed at time of repro: gateway `MainPID` (post-restart, matching `systemctl show`'s `MainPID`) → `.../dist/process/supervisor/service-child-relay.js` → `.../dist/process/supervisor/service-child-group-anchor.js`, with the relay/anchor processes' own PPID chain rooted at the *current* (post-restart) gateway PID — so they were spawned fresh after the restart, yet still served the pre-restart value.
- **Workaround that reliably works:** any command needing the fresh value must explicitly re-source the env file in a subshell rather than rely on inherited process environment, e.g. `(set -a; source ~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env; set +a; <command>)`.


### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (0965053)

### Operating system

Debian 13 (trixie)

### Install method

npm global (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-specific — reproduced with a Notion CLI (`ntn`) credential (`NOTION_API_TOKEN`), but the mechanism is about environment propagation to the `exec` tool's process tree, independent of which variable or provider is involved.

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via a systemd `--user` unit (`openclaw-gateway.service`) with `EnvironmentFile=/home/<user>/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env`.
- The affected variable (`NOTION_API_TOKEN`) is a manually-added entry in `gateway.systemd.env`, not one of the plugin-declared "managed" keys tracked in `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` — so this does not look like the same mechanism as #118503 or #124847 (both of which are about `~/.openclaw/.env` vs. generated systemd-env-file precedence/staging). Here there is only one file, hand-edited directly, and the *systemd unit itself* is confirmed to have reloaded it (`ActiveEnterTimestamp` updated) — the staleness is isolated to the tool-execution subprocess chain.
- Side observation, not confirmed as related: `systemctl --user list-units --all` showed the unit description as "OpenClaw Gateway (v2026.7.1-2)" even though the installed package (`package.json`) was already 2026.8.2. This may just be a static description string that isn't updated per-version and unrelated to the env staleness; flagging in case it's a symptom of the same underlying process-tree/restart issue rather than a coincidence. The host had done an in-place upgrade from 2026.7.1-2 → 2026.8.2 prior to this repro.

### Logs

```shell
$ systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway -p ActiveState -p ActiveEnterTimestamp -p MainPID
ActiveState=active
ActiveEnterTimestamp=Sun 2026-09-06 11:42:45 JST
MainPID=109621

$ echo "Live exec env value hash: $(printf '%s' "$NOTION_API_TOKEN" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
Live exec env value hash: 3d6ba3a40e0a163c2d66ff98c8f322d616b2d2024e18fb3923214026c4989c26

$ echo "File value hash: $(grep '^NOTION_API_TOKEN=' ~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env | cut -d= -f2- | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
File value hash: 720bad965b3d1f498e38ac6690fde9c2aa69275ae14a135e2ca797e9cb63f2f2

$ ntn whoami
error: Failed to fetch /v1/users/me: API token is invalid.
  hint: Set NOTION_API_TOKEN, or run `ntn login` to reuse a saved workspace token.

$ (set -a; source ~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env; set +a; ntn whoami)
<succeeds, same token, same file>
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any agent workflow that relies on a manually-managed secret in `gateway.systemd.env` and needs to pick up a rotated/edited value without a full host reboot.

Severity: Medium — not a crash or data loss, but silently defeats the documented remediation path ("edit the env file, restart the gateway") for credential rotation. Someone rotating a credential and restarting the gateway would reasonably believe the new value is live; it is not, in at least this configuration, until either a further, harder restart or a manual re-source workaround is used per command.

Frequency: Reproduced twice, consistent both times, several minutes apart.

Consequence: A rotated/edited secret can appear "not to have taken" after a documented restart, leading to unnecessary secondary troubleshooting (in this case, briefly suspecting a bad credential rotation when the credential was fine).

### Additional information


Related but distinct issues found during a search for duplicates before filing this:
- #118503 (closed) — "Managed env keys in systemd env files don't sync when `.env` is edited." Different mechanism: `.env` → generated systemd-env-file sync for plugin-declared managed keys.
- #124847 (open) — "Generated `gateway.systemd.env` retains keys deleted from `~/.openclaw/.env` and silently overrides it." Different mechanism: dotenv-loader precedence between `.env` and the generated systemd file.

This issue differs from both: there is a single, hand-edited file; the systemd unit itself demonstrably reloaded it; the staleness is specific to the process tree that services `exec` tool calls, not to `.env`/systemd-file precedence.

Happy to provide the full process tree dump or repeat the repro with a throwaway variable if that's more useful than the redacted excerpt above.

issues.body:
## Summary

In the OpenClaw control UI at `OpenClaw › main › Agents › Overview`, the Primary Model and Fallbacks fields require operators to **type model identifiers as raw strings** (e.g. `claude-cli/claude-opus-4-7`, `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `openai/gpt-5.5`). The fallbacks render as pill-style chips with `×` close buttons, but the chips are **not reorderable** — to change priority the operator has to remove and re-add them in the right sequence, retyping each one.

For any user who's tuning their fallback chain non-trivially (cost optimization, plan-quota-aware ordering, post-incident reconfiguration), this is painful enough that operators end up editing `openclaw.json` directly. Both surfaces — the UI and the JSON — share the same cognitive cost: "remember the exact provider/model slug and the exact ordering."

## Requested

Two UX changes in the `Agents > Overview` page:

### 1. Model picker (autocomplete dropdown) instead of free-text

Replace the free-text input fields for both Primary Model and Fallbacks with a typeahead dropdown that lists all configured providers and their models. Source of truth is already present in `openclaw.json` under `agents.defaults.models` (the operator's catalog) plus the provider plugin registrations under `plugins.entries.*`. The picker should:

- Group by provider (`claude-cli`, `openrouter`, `openai`, `google`, `anthropic`, `ollama`, etc.).
- Show each model's full slug (`claude-cli/claude-opus-4-7`) plus the operator's alias if defined (`claude-cli-opus 4.7` for that example).
- Optionally show a small indicator next to plan-covered models (e.g. "plan" badge for `claude-cli/*`, "paid" for `openrouter/*` and `openai/*`) so the operator sees cost implications at a glance.
- Filter by substring as the operator types (so `"opus"` narrows to opus variants).

### 2. Drag-to-reorder for the fallback chain

The Fallbacks pill row should support **click-and-hold drag** to reorder. The current first → last sequence is the priority order (Hermes/OpenClaw both treat earlier entries as higher priority), so visual position should match priority directly. After a drag:

- Update the order in-memory and persist to `openclaw.json` automatically (with the existing "You have unsaved config changes" → Save flow OR a debounced auto-save).
- No need to retype anything.

A library like `dnd-kit` (React) or `Sortable.js` handles the heavy lifting if the dashboard is React-based. Should be a small lift relative to how much pain it removes.

## Why this matters

Fallback ordering is a **frequent operator-tuning surface**, especially when:

- A primary provider auth fails (covered separately in `#80514`) and the operator needs to temporarily reshuffle.
- The operator adds a new lower-cost option (e.g. dropping `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` between Opus and OpenRouter to spill plan-covered work to Sonnet before paid fallbacks).
- A provider becomes flaky (rate-limited, deprecated, etc.) and needs to be demoted, not removed.
- Post-incident reconfiguration after diagnosing the failure cascade in `#80040` / `#80509` / `#80514`.

Every one of those situations currently requires either (a) typing exact model slugs in the UI or (b) editing JSON directly. The UI should be doing the slug-completion work.

## Related

- `openclaw/openclaw#80065` — surface `auth.cooldowns.*ProfileRotations` knobs in the configure wizard. Same general theme (expose model/auth config in UI rather than forcing JSON edits).
- `openclaw/openclaw#80514` — the billing-misclassification bug that motivated tonight's fallback-chain audit and underscored how often operators need to touch this surface.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.7 (gitSha `b8fe34a`)
- Surface: control dashboard, `OpenClaw › main › Agents › Overview`
