issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On iOS and macOS, Gateway-relay realtime Talk ends the call once 48 `talk.session.appendAudio` requests are waiting
(about 2 s of latency), or when one append takes longer than 8 s. The close aborts the agent consult already in
progress. Control UI and Android drop the late audio and keep the call, and detach accepted work when a failure does
end Talk.

### Steps to reproduce

Reproduced in the shared Apple kit on main `5a9fa922f96`:

1. On macOS, run `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests`.
2. The existing test `microphone saturation terminates once without sending the frame past the cap` passes. It holds 48
   appends, admits one more frame, and asserts that the relay ends with `audioInputFailed("Realtime audio input fell
   behind. Reconnecting…")` and sends `talk.session.close`.
3. With a test transport whose append answers after 10 s, the kit's 8000 ms deadline fires and the relay ends with
   `audioInputFailed`. The test is included in the upcoming fix; it fails on main (log below).

On a device: an iPhone on App Store build 2026.9.20 in a Gateway-relay Talk call over Wi-Fi hit a 5.5 s upload stall
(see Actual behavior).

### Expected behavior

The same contract that browser Gateway-relay Talk already documents in `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`:

- at most about 3 s of microphone audio in flight;
- frames over that budget are dropped, with a notice asking the user to repeat the last part;
- the call ends only when nothing is acknowledged for 30 s, on an explicit Gateway error, or when the connection is lost.

When a failure does end the call, the close detaches accepted agent work if the Gateway advertises
`talk-session-close-disposition`. `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md` describes this for Control UI and
the Android phone app; explicit Stop still aborts.

### Actual behavior

Code path at `5a9fa922f96`:

- [`RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L163`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L163):
  `guard self.pendingSends < RealtimeTalkRelaySession.maxPendingAudioSends else { return .saturated }`, with
  `maxPendingAudioSends = 48` at
  [`#L259`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L259).
  Each append uses an 8000 ms deadline
  ([`#L176`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L176)).
- `.saturated` and `.failed` both call `handleAudioInputFailure`
  ([`#L1280-L1289`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L1280-L1289)),
  which calls `close(sendClose: true)`
  ([`#L1228-L1244`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L1228-L1244)).
- `beginServerClose` sends `{ sessionId }` only
  ([`#L507-L516`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift#L507-L516)).
  The Gateway therefore applies the default `abort`
  ([`operations.ts#L661-L668`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/src/gateway/talk/relay/operations.ts#L661-L668))
  and retires accepted runs with `"relay-closed"`
  ([`operations.ts#L186-L189`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/src/gateway/talk/relay/operations.ts#L186-L189)),
  which aborts them
  ([`state.ts#L485-L513`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/src/gateway/talk/relay/state.ts#L485-L513)).
- The kit cannot gate `detach` today: `GatewayServerCapability` has no case for `talk-session-close-disposition`
  ([`GatewayPush.swift#L3-L13`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/GatewayPush.swift#L3-L13)).
- On iOS, three rapid terminations within 30 s switch Talk to the native fallback
  ([`TalkModeManager.swift#L403-L406`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift#L403-L406)).
  macOS uses the same kit session
  ([`TalkModeRuntime+Realtime.swift#L283`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a9fa922f96f23c99627553cc22a122c1c643f12/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/TalkModeRuntime+Realtime.swift#L283)).

Device observation on App Store 2026.9.20: a 5.5 s upload stall was followed by four appends completing in the same
millisecond. The relay closed with "Realtime audio input fell behind", and the consult that was running ended with an
AbortError. That build still had the four-request cap (upload ref `refs/openclaw/mobile-releases/ios/2026.9.20-1` →
`d69752a1c9`). The same stall exceeds the current 48-request cap after about 2 s; that part comes from reading the
source and has not been re-measured on a device.

### OpenClaw version

main `5a9fa922f96` (source and kit tests); the same logic is in v2026.10.5 and v2026.10.10-beta.3. Device observation:
iOS App Store 2026.9.20.

### Operating system

iOS on iPhone for the device observation (iOS version not recorded); kit tests on macOS 27.0.1 with Xcode 27.

### Install method

iOS App Store app connected to a self-hosted Gateway in Docker; kit tests from a source checkout.

### Model

Not model-specific: the failure is in the Apple client's microphone send path, before any provider.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw iOS/macOS app -> Gateway relay (`talk.session.*`) -> realtime provider

### Logs

```shell
# main 5a9fa922f96 with the upcoming 10 s stall test applied (no fix)
✘ Test "a ten second append stall keeps the call" recorded an issue at RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests.swift:277:9: Expectation failed: terminations.isEmpty
↳   terminations → [OpenClawKit.RealtimeTalkRelayTermination.audioInputFailed(message: "Realtime audio failed: The operation couldn’t be completed. (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.)")]
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

How the other clients already handle the same problem:

- Control UI: #155839 (3 s input budget, drop frames), #173490 / #173388 (30 s no-progress watchdog instead of the 8 s
  per-append deadline), #171377 / #171310 (failure closes detach).
- Android phone app: `Channel(capacity = 4, onBufferOverflow = DROP_OLDEST)`; #172276 / #172275 (failure and
  background closes detach).
- Apple: #163146 raised the cap from 4 to 48 and kept the fatal path (related issue #163122).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: iOS and macOS users of Gateway-relay realtime Talk, which is every realtime provider except OpenAI WebRTC,
  plus explicit `gateway-relay` setups.
- Severity: blocks the workflow; the call drops and the answer of the consult in progress is lost.
- Frequency: once on a device; deterministic in the kit tests above. Triggered by about 2 s of append latency, for
  example during a Wi-Fi handoff or while the Gateway is busy.
- Consequence: lost answer and a reconnect cycle; after three rapid failures iOS falls back to native Talk.

### Additional information

Client-only patches are ready and PRs will follow after an iOS simulator build and a device check:

1. Failure closes detach accepted work when the Gateway advertises `talk-session-close-disposition`: add
   `GatewayServerCapability.talkSessionCloseDisposition` and wire it through `RealtimeTalkRelayTransport` on iOS and
   macOS. Explicit `stop()` keeps aborting.
2. Bound in-flight microphone audio by time instead of request count: a 3 s budget, admitted before the send task
   starts, with frames over budget dropped behind one notice and one recovery notice. Raise the per-append deadline to
   a 30 s liveness bound; the Gateway answers appends in order.

`swift test --filter RealtimeTalkRelaySession` on macOS passes with each patch: 64 tests for (1) and 62 for (2), against
62 on main. The rewritten tests fail on main. A device run on a build that contains #163146 has not been done yet.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An isolated cron run rejects two nonexistent tool calls without execution, then suppresses its explicitly configured model fallbacks after a provider error because the rejected calls are classified as potential side effects.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed sequence on the build below:

1. Run an isolated cron `agentTurn` with an explicit primary model and a nonempty `payload.fallbacks` array.
2. During the primary attempt, the model emits two calls to the nonexistent tool `malformed_tool_call`. Both receive `Tool malformed_tool_call not found`; neither tool executes.
3. The subsequent model request fails with a provider auth error delivered through an OpenAI-compatible SSE stream.
4. Observe the cron terminate with an error, without dispatching any configured fallback candidate.

This is a production observation plus installed-code inspection and a zero-write pure-function check. It has not been reduced to an end-to-end automated reproducer or retested on newer upstream main. The relevant condition is authoritative `executionStarted:false`, not the particular nonexistent tool name.

### Expected behavior

Preserve authoritative evidence that a tool never began execution when deciding replay safety. If the attempt has no other replay-unsafe activity, a subsequent eligible provider failure should reach the configured fallback chain.

The installed tool dispatcher already emits `executionStarted:false` for a missing tool, and the installed model-selection code correctly carries the explicit fallback array. These are the concrete references for the expected behavior. This is not a request to bypass replay protection after actual or uncertain side effects.

### Actual behavior

The primary route received three HTTP-200 SSE responses. The first two resulted in the rejected tool calls. The third ended with a recognized provider auth error. The run updated the primary auth-profile failure state and terminated; none of the three configured outer fallback candidates were invoked.

The provider router did perform its own internal fallback: it progressed past unavailable Mistral targets to Gemini. On the final request its available pool was exhausted and it emitted a terminal error. Therefore the missing transition reported here is OpenClaw's **outer** model fallback, not the router's internal pool traversal.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4, installed build-info commit `6f867819c16f2466be711e0616ee538263ca09b9`

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux x64; Node 24.21.0

### Install method

Managed package installation, Gateway launched as a systemd service; diagnosis performed against the running installation's bundled dist files.

### Model

`omniroute/free-final-fallback` (OpenAI-compatible `openai-completions` API)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw isolated cron → OmniRoute pool → upstream providers.

Configured outer chain:
`omniroute/free-final-fallback → openai/gpt-6-luna → xai/grok-4.6 → omniroute/nr-deepseek-41f`

### Additional provider/model setup details

`payload.kind=agentTurn`, `sessionTarget=isolated`, `lightContext=true`; `payload.fallbacks` explicitly names all three alternatives. Installed-code inspection confirmed the array propagates through `fallbacksOverride` and `modelFallbacksOverride`: it is not lost or replaced by agent defaults.

### Logs

Redacted, shortened excerpts from one run:

```text
toolResult: Tool malformed_tool_call not found
toolResult: Tool malformed_tool_call not found

[model-fetch] provider=omniroute api=openai-completions model=free-final-fallback status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
[model-fetch] provider=omniroute api=openai-completions model=free-final-fallback status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
[model-fetch] provider=omniroute api=openai-completions model=free-final-fallback status=200 contentType=text/event-stream

embedded_run_agent_end:
  isError=true
  failoverReason=auth
  providerRuntimeFailureKind=unclassified
  rawErrorPreview="mistral/mistral-large-latest: auth — [403]: This model is not available in your subscription tier (HTTP 403); ..."

auth_profile_failure_state_updated: provider=omniroute reason=auth
message dispatch completed: channel=cron source=cron-isolated outcome=error
cron: job run returned error status
```

No subsequent candidate request appears in the same correlated trace. HTTP 200 describes the SSE transport, not successful completion.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Installed-code reconstruction (bundled filenames identify the tested build):

1. `dist/agent-core-qvRE9fDN.mjs:1149` rejects a missing tool immediately. Lines 983–994 attach `executionStarted:false`; lines 1455–1463 carry it into the tool-end event.
2. `dist/builtin-openclaw-CntTfMHf.mjs:3018–3039` computes `executionStarted`, but terminal replay metadata records `replaySafe:callSummary.replaySafe` without retaining or incorporating the non-execution fact. Unknown tools lack a replay-safe contract (2171–2179), so that value is false.
3. The same bundle's normalization (7923–7937) retains that false value. Replay aggregation (3508–3513, 8015) treats any tool metadata with `replaySafe !== true` as `hadPotentialSideEffects:true,replaySafe:false`. Current-attempt metadata takes precedence over the more accurate accumulated replay state (3499–3501).
4. `dist/embedded-agent-wyJhS-wg.mjs:1975–1979` returns `action:"proceed"` when `!isCurrentAttemptReplaySafe(input.attempt)`, before the normal auth-error `FailoverError` throw (2156–2183).
5. The returned result has `meta.error.kind="incomplete_turn"` and `fallbackSafe:false`. `dist/result-fallback-classifier-BGNih4it.mjs:163–165,178` declines fallback. `dist/model-fallback-attempt-B2iFV_mZ.mjs:309–336` treats the unclassified returned result as completion, and `dist/model-fallback-runner-XfYT3d5_.mjs:473–479` returns without dispatching the remaining candidates.

**Evidence boundary:** tool results, provider requests, auth classification and terminal job state were directly observed. Internal replay flags above are reconstructed from installed code, not logged variable snapshots. A zero-write check of the installed pure function bodies with the observed unknown-tool shape confirmed `replaySafe:false`, a false replay gate and outer classification `null`. No live replay or corrective patch was performed.

### Impact and severity

Affected: an isolated scheduled agent turn with configured fallback providers.

Severity: blocks the scheduled workflow despite configured alternatives; no successful business-tool call was observed in this run.

Frequency: one investigated run, with two rejected tool calls followed by one terminal provider error. Broader frequency is not established.

Consequence: the job ends in error without attempting the remaining configured models.

### Additional information

Related but distinct: #151572 requests continuation after **actual replay-unsafe tool activity**. This report concerns a false-positive veto where the dispatcher explicitly knows the rejected tools **never executed**. #149785 discusses provider failures bypassing fallback more generally.

Please preserve the conservative veto for actual or uncertain side effects; the missing information is authoritative non-execution evidence. No known-good version or regression range has been established.

issues.body:
# GitHub Issue 草稿（待Lucas批准后才发布）

**标题:** Restart recovery lacks token budget guard and balance alerting — one silent recovery turn burned 127M+ tokens

**仓库:** openclaw/openclaw

---

## Summary

On 2026-10-22, a Gateway restart interrupted an in-flight turn in our main session. When the Gateway came back, automatic main-session recovery resumed that turn silently. The recovery run executed **344 model calls over 52 minutes**, consuming **~127.7M raw tokens** on our Zhipu (BigModel) GLM-5.3-Flash resource pack — with **no warning, no budget cap, and no notification**. Two 50M resource packs plus part of a third were drained before we noticed the balance drop manually.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), Windows 10 (26200), x64
- Model provider: zhipu/glm-5.3-flash (resource pack billing; packs deduct **raw** total tokens, including cache reads at full count)
- Session: `agent:main:main` (Control UI home session, ~265k token context)

## Timeline (from local SQLite transcript `usage` records)

| Time (CST) | Event |
|---|---|
| ~10:20 | Gateway restart interrupts an assistant turn mid-flight |
| 10:20–16:25 | Session sits in "restart recovery pending" state; no operator-visible alert |
| 16:26:03 | Recovery turn auto-triggers and resumes the interrupted work |
| 16:26–17:17 | 52 min run: 344 model calls, context ~265k re-read each step (cacheRead-dominated) |
| 17:17:10 | Run ends. Total: input 893,220 / output 17,834 / cacheRead 127,694,272 ≈ **128.6M raw tokens** |
| 17:21 | User notices balance crash (150M pack bought that morning → 9.28M left), manually stops/clears the session |

Full-day reconciliation: pack deduction (150M − 9.28M = 140.7M) matches raw transcript usage sum (≈141.4M) to <1%. No key leak, no third-party traffic — 100% of the burn was this single recovery turn plus normal usage.

## Why this hurts so much

1. **Cost scales as `window_context × steps`** for a recovery turn. Our 265k-context home session multiplied that by 344 steps. A recovery turn on a large session is effectively unbounded spend on the operator's API key/pack.
2. **"Recovery is always on"** (docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md) — there is no config to disable or bound it, no per-turn token/step budget, no spend ceiling.
3. **Zero signaling.** No log surface, notification, or channel message fired during or after the 52-minute burn. The only symptom was the provider balance cratering. The user's own assistant was the attacker, and the user found out by checking the billing page.

## Requests

1. **Recovery budget guard:** a configurable cap for automatic recovery turns (max steps / max tokens / max cost estimate), e.g. `agents.defaults.recovery.maxTokens` or similar. Exceeding it should tombstone the turn pending operator inspection, same as the existing delivery-budget tombstone path.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Updating OpenClaw from 2026.10.5 to 2026.10.6 ended with `state-migrated-no-rollback` after Gateway readiness verification timed out. The update also refused to refresh the systemd user service because doing so would omit an operator-provided `OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN`.

Subsequent checks confirm that 2026.10.6 is running and the configured Telegram channels work, but the recorded update still prominently says “failed” and suggests `gateway install --force`. It is difficult for an operator to distinguish the historical verification failure from the current operational state, or to know that forcing a reinstall may change a protected service setting.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with OpenClaw 2026.10.5 installed globally via npm under a user-owned `~/.local` prefix, with a systemd user Gateway service containing an operator-provided `OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN`.
2. Update to 2026.10.6.
3. Observe service-definition reconciliation refused with `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN` because the installer would omit that setting.
4. Observe Gateway verification time out and the update finish as `state-migrated-no-rollback`.
5. After the Gateway settles, check `openclaw update status`, `openclaw gateway status --deep --require-rpc`, `openclaw gateway health --port 18789`, and `openclaw channels status --probe`.

This is one observed installation; I have not reproduced it on a clean setup.

### Expected behavior

Do not mark a timed-out verification as successful or weaken the service-definition safeguard. However, subsequent status output should clearly separate:

- **Update attempt:** failed verification at the time; recovery artifacts retained.
- **Current state:** target version now serving and independently healthy.
- **Outstanding action:** service refresh was skipped to preserve an operator setting; explain how to reconcile it safely, rather than presenting `install --force` as an uncomplicated fix.


### Actual behavior

The update exhausted its 1806-second readiness budget. The recorded verification said the service was running but channels and HTTP were not ready. `openclaw update status` continues to report `state-migrated-no-rollback` and retained backups, although it now says the 2026.10.6 Gateway answered on the recorded port and the saved runtime-verification failure no longer applies.

The service warning says the existing definition was preserved because the installer would omit `OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN`, then suggests `openclaw gateway install --force` and restart.

### OpenClaw version

CLI version: 2026.10.6 (`fe06181`).

### Operating system

Linux

### Install method

Install method: global npm installation under `~/.local`

### Model

minimax

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw update

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

Current: <redacted>; installer: <absent>.. Run openclaw gateway install --force, then openclaw gateway restart.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Last recorded update (2026-10-22T17:41:45.663Z):

The target release appears operational now, but the combination of a prominent failed-update result, retained rollback warnings, and a force-reinstall suggestion leaves users unsure whether the upgrade succeeded or what action is safe. issues.body:
### Summary

On a gateway state with ~810 configured agents (939 agent databases), `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` from schema v28 to v31 needed three passes and about 110 minutes on current `main`. The second pass died of V8 heap exhaustion at a 6 GB heap during the `contributions` phase, on both builds tested. For a single shared gateway, that is upgrade downtime: the gateway cannot start until doctor finishes.

### Environment

- `main` at `bc9b82033`, and the same commit with #173994 merged on top (both arms behaved the same through doctor)
- Node 24.21.0, Linux x64, 4 vCPU / 16 GB, `NODE_OPTIONS`-equivalent `--max-old-space-size=6144`
- State: a copy of a production gateway, ~176k files, 939 agent databases at v28, egress blocked (no model calls)
- Two hosts in parallel, the same result on each

### What happened (control arm; candidate within a few minutes of it)

| Pass | Result | Time | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | rc=1 | 1,115 s | `Plugin migration obligations changed while their inputs were being prepared ... run "openclaw doctor --fix" after the other repair finishes` (same error as #180350) |
| 2 | rc=134 | 3,009 s | `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`, about 20 minutes into `Doctor: contributions` (after `config-flow` 841 s and `legacy-cron.inference` 377 s) |
| 3 | rc=0 | 2,462 s | succeeded; agent databases at v31 |

The candidate arm's pass 2 OOMed at the same point (`config-flow` 919 s, `legacy-cron.inference` 440 s, then `contributions`); its pass 3 was still running when our 2-hour cap stopped it.

Startup-trace phase times from the successful pass 3:

```
doctor.contributions                        1096088 ms
doctor.config-flow                           730011 ms
doctor.maintenance.begin                     421183 ms
doctor.maintenance.preserve-original-state   420321 ms
doctor.legacy-cron.inference                 254501 ms
doctor.archive-preparation                   181892 ms
doctor.database-migrations                    76268 ms
doctor.heartbeat-migration-backups            57439 ms
```

The last GC lines before the abort:

```
Scavenge 6112.4 (6145.5) -> 6097.9 (6146.2) MB ... allocation failure;
Mark-Compact (reduce) 6113.6 (6146.7) -> 6083.2 (6114.0) MB ...
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

### Expected

One bounded `doctor --fix` pass whose memory does not grow with agent count past a 6 GB heap, and a total time a gateway operator can plan a maintenance window around. The gateway itself, once migrated, booted in 35 s and served `/health` 200 at 52 s on the same host, so doctor is now the long pole of an upgrade at this size.

### Notes

- `contributions` (18 minutes when it succeeds) and `config-flow` (12-15 minutes) look like the per-agent work; `contributions` is where the heap runs out.
- Pass 1's obligations conflict cost 19 minutes before failing and leaving the work for a rerun; #180350 covers that error's diagnostics, and here it occurred with no concurrent repair running (one doctor process, gateway stopped).
- Happy to rerun with a heap snapshot or extra tracing if that helps.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.9.7 (c074824). The same code is on `main`. Linux, `claude-cli` runtime, `tools.profile: "coding"`, `tools.alsoAllow` lists the 26 `workboard_*` tools, `plugins.entries.workboard.enabled: true` (loaded at startup).

### Repro
```
openclaw gateway call tools.effective --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:<id>:main"}' --json
```
No `workboard_*` entries appear, and neither do file-transfer or talk-voice tools. Only memory-core's plugin tools show up. At the same time the gateway logs:

> tools.profile (coding) allowlist contains unknown entries (workboard_list, …). These entries won't match any tool unless the plugin is enabled.

`tools.catalog` lists all 35 workboard tools, and real agent turns do get them once the policy allows it. We verified this in a sandboxed session after adding `workboard_*` to `tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow`.

### Cause (from reading dist)
- `acquireEffectiveToolInventoryRuntimeModelContext` acquires `acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime({ loadRuntimePlugins: true, runtimePluginSelections: [...] })`.
- In `prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries`, `loadRuntimePlugins` forces `basePluginIds: []`. The generation therefore only holds provider, memory and harness owners (here `agentsapi, anthropic, google, memory-core`).
- The inventory then runs inside `withPluginRuntimeGenerationScope(lease.snapshot)`. `resolveOpenClawPluginToolsForOptions` picks up that registry and metadata snapshot as `preparedRuntime`.
- `resolvePluginToolLoadState` computes `onlyPluginIds` from the narrowed snapshot, so tool-only plugins are never selected.

### Evidence
- In a separate process with the same config, `resolveEffectiveToolInventory` called outside the lease reports all 26 `workboard_*` tools as available.
- The same call inside `acquired.run(...)` returns only `memory_search`/`memory_get`, and logs the identical "unknown entries" warnings.

### Impact
Operators check `tools.effective` after granting optional plugin tools, as the docs recommend. They see the tools as absent and revert config that was correct; we did exactly that. The warning also wrongly says the plugin isn't enabled.

### Expected
The inventory should build plugin tools from the full enabled plugin set, or from the Gateway's active registry, and use the narrowed lease only for model and runtime facts.

Related: #167351, #157396, #156864

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Managed workers cannot send to their valid global parent or sibling when the parent belongs to a non-default agent. A shared session store also exposes a target-owner mismatch before core send admission.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use global session scope with separate `main`, `ops`, and worker agents. Create an `ops` global parent and ordinary managed child/sibling sessions through the Gateway session-creation path.
2. Dispatch the child to a paired worker with an active placement and turn claim, then admit its worker WebSocket connection.
3. Call `worker.sessions.send` for the recorded global parent and sibling.
4. Repeat with a shared fixed session store whose canonical owner is `ops` and a qualified worker-owned child/sibling.

### Expected behavior

The authorized child can message its exact live parent and siblings, including Gateway-local targets. Existing worker-family support is documented by #132818. Parent/target incarnation and source authority must still validate.

### Actual behavior

The ordinary global-owner reproduction rejects both parent and sibling as outside the authorized session tree. A separate shared-store reproduction of the initial repair reaches core target lookup but rejects the owner before dispatch; no provider request occurs.

### OpenClaw version

Source baseline `36092853807a72cbbad6e2f7feddbf87679b1fbb` for the original reproduction. The shared-store second reproduction used the initial local owner-routing candidate before its core handoff was corrected.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0; Node 26.8.1.

### Install method

Isolated source checkout with real Gateway session creation, worker dispatch/admission, and worker WebSocket RPC.

### Model

Synthetic loopback Responses fixture using public model ID `gpt-5.4`; the failing calls never reach inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Worker WebSocket RPC -> Gateway session tool -> core sessions_send -> target admission -> OpenClaw runtime -> loopback synthetic Responses provider for after-fix verification.

### Logs

```text
Worker sessions_send target is outside the authorized session tree
agent "worker" does not match session key agent "ops"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The original before-fix WebSocket proof completed at 2026-09-04 10:08:53 UTC. The shared-store before-fix proof completed at 10:27:54 UTC with zero provider requests. Regression coverage also fails against the old owner lookup and old core handoff.

The candidate passes 49 focused cases and both real WebSocket after-fix runs, with the parent and sibling transcripts containing the sent message plus synthetic assistant reply. An unrelated owner's transcript stays untouched. Revoking source authority after a real sibling-resolution response prevents further transcript/provider effects.

Proof limits: bundle installation and workspace-sync transport are simulated. Generic node handshake, a separate remote worker process, and external inference are not exercised.

### Impact and severity

Blocks valid worker-family messaging in the tested multi-agent global-session configurations. Both attempted family destinations failed in the original reproduction. No cross-owner data modification was observed.

### Additional information

The repair carries the existing canonical owner through exact parent lookup and core send admission. No schema, persisted representation, migration, configuration, dependency, or protocol field is added. The exact introducing commit is not established.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Crabbox Windows cloud worker (native `windows_mode=normal`), the workspace directory that `crabbox exec` runs commands in is 171–187 characters long before the command creates a single file:

```
C:\Users\<user>\.openclaw\cloud-workers\cbx_<12 hex>\node-host\gateway-<32 hex>\workspaces\<16 hex>\<32 hex>\<generation>
```

(171 characters with `C:\Users\crabbox`; 187 on the machine measured, where the profile folder had the usual `crabbox.<COMPUTERNAME>` suffix). That leaves 72–88 characters below the classic 260-character `MAX_PATH` (259 usable) for anything a command resolves relative to its working directory. Installers and many desktop programs are not long-path aware, so `LongPathsEnabled` does not help them; an installer started from that directory failed with "Error 206: The filename or extension is too long".

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Crabbox cloud worker on a native Windows profile and let it bootstrap (Windows Server 2022, `windows_mode=normal`).
2. Run any command through the worker's `crabbox exec` and print the working directory, e.g. `(Get-Location).Path.Length`; or read `workspaceDir` from the exec result.
3. From the same exec, download an installer that is not long-path aware (observed with an Inno Setup installer) and start it with `Start-Process -FilePath $env:TEMP\<installer>.exe -ArgumentList '/S'`, inheriting the working directory.

### Expected behavior

Worker commands on Windows run from a short working directory (for example `C:\ocw\<lease>\<n>`, or a junction created with `mklink /J` onto the deep workspace), so a program started from it has the normal `MAX_PATH` headroom. `LongPathsEnabled=1` in the Windows worker bootstrap is a useful addition but only helps long-path-aware tools.

### Actual behavior

- Step 2: the working directory is the 187-character path above (`workspaceDir` in the exec result; every segment except `<user>` and `<generation>` has a fixed length).
- Step 3: the installer window opened, then showed "Error 206: The filename or extension is too long" and aborted. Observed on 2026-10-04 on v2026.9.8. The installer was not re-run from a short working directory in that session, so the inherited directory is the strongly indicated cause rather than an isolated one; the path composition below is from source.

### OpenClaw version

Observed on v2026.9.8 (`fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943`); the path composition is unchanged on v2026.10.1-beta.1 (`6830fe76b3db05ad59e8ff7f0f872d4e2639a1fe`) and main `c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886` (2026-10-06).

### Operating system

Gateway on Linux amd64; worker on Windows Server 2022 (AWS, Crabbox 0.71.0, `windows_mode=normal`).

### Install method

Docker image based on `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw`; Crabbox worker provider (`extensions/crabbox`).

### Model

Not applicable.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable (worker workspace layout, no model routing).

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

The exec result carried `workspaceDir` = the path above. The installer's own dialog read:

```
Error 206: The filename or extension is too long
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Path composition (main; line numbers for beta / v2026.9.8 in parentheses):

- `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.ts` [L104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.ts#L104) (103 / 102): `stateDir = path.join(home, ".openclaw", "cloud-workers", leaseId)`, exported as `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` for the node host.
- `src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts` [L110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts#L110) (112 / 111): root `<stateDir>/node-host`; [L237-L238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts#L237-L238) (240 / 239): `<root>/<gatewayNamespace>/workspaces`; [L67-L68](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts#L67-L68): environment hash `^[a-f0-9]{16}$`, session hash `^[a-f0-9]{32}$`; [L571](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts#L571) (572 / 576): `workspacePath = path.join(sessionRoot, String(input.generation))`.
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/node-worker-gateway-namespace.ts` [L4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/gateway/worker-environments/node-worker-gateway-namespace.ts#L4): `gateway-${sha256(gatewayDeviceId).slice(0, 32)}`.
- `src/node-host/node-worker-workspace-commands.ts` [L116-L126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c656ee5227cdfc8930c6eff095937e53e0516886/src/node-host/node-worker-workspace-commands.ts#L116-L126): workspace commands run with `cwd: params.workspaceDir`.

Fixed-width budget: `\.openclaw\cloud-workers\cbx_` + 12 + `\node-host\gateway-` + 32 + `\workspaces\` + 16 + `\` + 32 + `\1` = 155 characters after the profile directory, so even `C:\Users\Administrator` (22) gives 177.

Related: #113227 / #113228 (SQLite snapshots past `MAX_PATH`, fixed with long-path support inside OpenClaw), #154734, #152992 and #165518 (update canary paths on Windows), and #162660 (docs clarifying workspace paths on native Windows). Those fix OpenClaw's own file operations; this report is about the directory handed to arbitrary programs the agent runs.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** every Crabbox Windows worker; any program the agent starts from the workspace that is not long-path aware (installers, many desktop apps).
- **Severity:** medium. Nothing in OpenClaw crashes, but installs and some tools fail with a confusing error.
- **Frequency:** deterministic for affected programs; the budget shrinks further with a long user name or a `.<COMPUTERNAME>` profile suffix.
- **Consequence:** the agent needs an explicit `Set-Location $env:TEMP` (or similar) before running installers, which it has no way to know.

### Additional information

Workarounds in use: `LongPathsEnabled=1` in the worker setup (covers long-path-aware programs only), and prompting the agent to `cd $env:TEMP` before starting installers. A short Windows workspace root (or a junction handed to `exec` as its working directory) removes the need for both.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Native Windows Doctor rejects its original-state capture because an effective ancestor ACE grants DELETE on the local volume root, although that root cannot be renamed and the ACE grants none of the other rights in the replacement mask.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on one existing installation, rather than a new clean-state fixture:

1. Use a private native capture repository beneath a genuine local Windows volume root. The capture repository has a protected DACL containing only the current user, SYSTEM and Administrators; intermediate user directories are protected.
2. The existing volume-root ACL has an effective Authenticated Users (`S-1-5-11`) allow ACE with mask `0x1301bf` (Modify | Synchronize). It is inherited but **not inherit-only**, with no OI/CI flags. A separate inherit-only ACE is not the rejected entry.
3. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive`.
4. Observe the ancestor ACL refusal below before native original-state capture succeeds.

No volume, home or intermediate-ancestor ACL was changed for this observation. No rename/delete probe or safety bypass was used.

### Expected behavior

DELETE-self alone on a positively identified local volume-root ancestor should not be treated as authority to replace that ancestor. Microsoft documents that a volume's root directory cannot be renamed. Keep repository-root privacy and ordinary ancestor checks, including DELETE_CHILD, WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER and unknown-rights rejection. [Microsoft FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION remarks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/ns-ntifs-_file_rename_information)

### Actual behavior

Doctor reports:

```text
Original state capture was unavailable: Windows ACL permits untrusted SQLite staging access on ancestor: path=C:\ principal=S-1-5-11 rights=(RD,WD,AD,REA,WEA,X,RA,WA,D,RC,S). Remove the untrusted grant or choose a private local directory; do not use a shared or synced root.. Doctor will continue; inspect retained evidence manually before restoring state.
```

The observed ACE intersects the ancestor replacement mask only at DELETE-self:

```text
observed ACE mask:          0x001301bf
ancestor replacement mask:  0x120d0040
intersection:              0x00010000  (DELETE)
```

There is no DELETE_CHILD, WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER or unknown-bit intersection. The rejected entry is not an inherit-only flag parsing case.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.6, official target `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`; locally repaired candidate `839b6796f331b780fa34c9113737bac4850d311d`.

The installation retains unrelated runtime/browser/memory/reply/auth/MCP repairs and SQLite diagnostics. The affected staging-policy file is unchanged from the official target, blob `6ace9c129436fc90da1df4b61f0684ea8cb5e86f`. Current main was also inspected and retains the same guard; no current-main runtime reproduction was performed.

### Operating system

Windows 11, 10.0.26200, x64; Node 26.12.1.

### Install method

npm-global package, built through the canonical source packer for the disclosed repair candidate.

### Model

Not applicable: native CLI capture admission, before inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: native CLI capture admission, before inference.

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

The exact safe refusal and mask comparison are included above. Account-specific SIDs, home paths, configuration and credentials are omitted.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

[Official target policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc/src/snapshot/local-repository-directory-policy.ts#L343) applies the same replacement mask to every ancestor, including the volume root. Its inherit-only exception is already present. [Current-main policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/snapshot/local-repository-directory-policy.ts#L346) was checked on 22 October 2026.

Native ACL facts and independent .NET ACL inspection agree on the effective mask and flags. Private raw receipts are retained. This is an availability false positive, not a demonstrated security bypass.

### Impact and severity

Observed once on this native Windows installation after the capture repository's separate privacy issue was corrected. Native original-state capture remains unavailable while Doctor continues maintenance. The current Doctor process is still running, so its terminal outcome is not claimed. No corruption, data loss or exposure was established.

### Additional information

No matching issue or merged fix was verified in bounded core/fs-safe searches. [#173484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173484) is adjacent but concerned an unsafe ancestor FullControl grant and MSIX support; it does not cover this volume-root DELETE-self case. Last known-good version and regression boundary: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

AI-assisted investigation and report, prepared with the operator's authorization.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

While an OpenAI-compatible (Chat Completions), Azure Responses, ChatGPT Responses or Kimi model streams a large tool call, the malformed tool-call argument repair wrapper re-parses the whole argument buffer on almost every streamed delta, so Gateway CPU per large `write`/`edit`/`exec` call grows quadratically up to the 64,000-character repair cap.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `844b03541a8` (same code in `v2026.10.3`).
2. Configure a model provider with `api: "openai-completions"` (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, for example OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Groq, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM or a custom provider).
3. Ask the agent for a large file write, so the model streams a `write` call with about 60 KB of arguments at token granularity.
4. Measure Gateway CPU for the turn, or count `JSON.parse` calls on inputs of 4 KB or more.

### Expected behavior

Per-delta work in the repair wrapper stays proportional to the delta until the streamed arguments could actually be repaired.

### Actual behavior

`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-call-argument-repair.ts` runs `tryExtractUsableToolCallArguments(state.partialJson)` whenever a delta contains `}` or `]`, and for every short (1-3 character) delta once the buffer has seen a closer (checked with a full-buffer regex each time). Each attempt runs `JSON.parse` on the whole buffer, a balanced-JSON scan from the start, and a smart-quote scan. Every success path, however, returns an object whose closing `}` is followed only by whitespace and at most three allowed trailing characters, so while the buffer ends inside a string or after a comma all of that work is guaranteed to fail.

Measured through an isolated Gateway (QA channel, a Chat Completions mock provider, one `write` call per turn with 60,000 content characters streamed in 4-character chunks, about 15,700 deltas; warm turns):

| | `main` 844b03541a8 |
| --- | ---: |
| `JSON.parse` calls on inputs >= 4 KB, per turn | 4,084 |
| characters parsed by those calls | 136.6M |
| Gateway process CPU per turn, median / p95 (50 turns, 5 boots) | 2,959 / 3,478 ms |
| inbound to first outbound, median | 1,692 ms |

Fed the same events directly, the wrapper alone spends 700 ms per 60 KB TypeScript write. With token-sized deltas from a GPT-2 style tokenizer the count rises to about 8,430 large parses (274.7M characters) per call.

### OpenClaw version

`main` at `844b03541a8`; `v2026.10.3`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64 (Node 26.12)

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Any model on the affected APIs

### Provider / routing chain

`openai-completions` (OpenAI-compatible providers), `azure-openai-responses`, `openai-chatgpt-responses`, and Kimi on `anthropic-messages` (the APIs `shouldRepairMalformedToolCallArguments` enables). The default OpenAI Responses path is not affected.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default config otherwise.

### Logs

No errors; the tool call succeeds and the written file is correct.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Counts and CPU come from an isolated Gateway with a local mock provider; the written file matches the streamed content byte for byte on every turn.

### Impact and severity

Coding-agent turns that write or edit large files on OpenAI-compatible providers spend more than a second of extra Gateway CPU per 60 KB tool call while the arguments stream, which competes with every other session on the same Gateway. Always reproduces for tool calls with large arguments; no data risk.

### Additional information

A fix can keep every existing repair and the per-delta invalidation of a cached repair (#43824) by skipping only the attempts that cannot succeed.

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Add a bundled-only skill filter to `openclaw skills list`

## Summary

Add `openclaw skills list --bundled` (and `--no-bundled`) so operators can list only the skills that shipped with OpenClaw, or only the ones they added.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw skills list` shows a `Source` column, and the values include `openclaw-bundled` and `openclaw-custodian`, alongside user-installed and workspace skills. The JSON output also carries a boolean `bundled`. There is no way to filter the list by that fact.

Scenario: an operator wants to know which skills came with OpenClaw before deciding what to remove, or wants to check whether a workspace skill shadowed a bundled one. They read the Source column across 56 rows, or pipe `--json` through a script.

Frequency: every skill audit or cleanup; on a stock install 54 of 56 listed skills are bundled, so the unfiltered table is mostly noise for this question.

Current workarounds: `skills list --eligible` filters by readiness, not by origin; `skills list --json` needs an external filter; `skills check` prints counts only and no source breakdown.

## Proposed solution

```bash
openclaw skills list --bundled          # only openclaw-bundled / openclaw-custodian
openclaw skills list --no-bundled       # only workspace / managed / extra skills
openclaw skills list --bundled --json   # same filter, same JSON shape
```

The filter composes with the existing `--eligible` and `--verbose` flags and does not change the output shape.

### Design details

- `src/cli/skills-cli.format.ts`: `formatSkillsList` already receives `bundled` on every `SkillStatusEntry`; add the filter next to the `eligible` check.
- The CLI option lives with the other `skills list` options; `--bundled` and `--no-bundled` are mutually exclusive.
- Tests: extend the existing skills list format tests in `src/cli/` next to `formatSkillsList`.

## Alternatives considered

- Option A: add a `B` marker to the Skill name column. Why weaker: it makes every row noisier, and the Source column already says `openclaw-bundled`.
- Option B: add a count line to `skills check`. Why weaker: it answers "how many", not "which ones", and does not compose with `--json`.
- Option C: document a jq one-liner. Why weaker: the core CLI already exposes `--eligible`; origin is the same kind of filter.

### Why not a plugin?

`skills list` is a core CLI command; a plugin cannot add a flag to it. The filter needs only the `bundled` fact that the skill status owner already computes.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: operators auditing or cleaning up skills on any deployment.
- Severity: annoying, turns into extra work during cleanup.
- Frequency: every skills audit.
- Consequences: manual scanning of a table that is mostly bundled rows, or a throwaway JSON script.

## Evidence/examples

On `main` (a6c561f954c), an isolated state directory:

```text
$ openclaw skills list
Skills (22/56 ready)
│ Status │ Skill │ Description │ Source │
│ △ needs setup │ 🔐 1password │ ... │ openclaw-bundled │
...
```

54 of the 56 rows use `openclaw-bundled` or `openclaw-custodian`. `openclaw skills list --json` exposes `"bundled": true` per entry, but there is no CLI flag that filters on it. `openclaw skills check` reports totals (56 total, 22 eligible) with no origin breakdown.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- Read-only, no config, no migration.
- Flag naming (`--bundled` / `--no-bundled`) is open; the filter semantics are not.

issues.body:
Side chat is currently one conversation per session, shared by everyone who can view that session (`src/gateway/session-companion.ts`). In multiplayer sessions this means:

- other viewers see your Side chat questions and answers
- anyone who clears it clears it for everyone

The panel itself is already per person (layout is stored per browser profile), so nothing in the UI suggests the conversation inside is shared.

**Proposal**

- Key Side chat threads by session **and** operator, so each person gets their own private thread.
- Reset/clear only affects the caller's thread.

**UX: make privacy obvious**

Users must be able to tell at a glance that only they can see the Side chat they create, especially in multiplayer sessions. For example:

- lock icon plus "Only you can see this" in the Side chat tab and header
- the same in the empty state and composer placeholder (e.g. "Ask privately…")
- clear visual contrast with shared surfaces (main chat, Browser, Terminal), so the private and shared areas aren't confused

Observed on deployed release `4039ebd5`.

name: Bug report
title: '[Bug]: tools.github.configure swallows the real failure cause and always reports "GitHub identity setup failed"'

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Gateway handler for `tools.github.configure` (`src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts`, ~line 228) catches every failure in a bare `catch {}` and responds with only the generic `UNAVAILABLE` error `GitHub identity setup failed`. The caught error is neither logged nor reflected in the response, so the Gateway log shows the failure envelope but never a cause — in a one-hour session, 10 consecutive failures produced zero cause-bearing log lines.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed in normal use — no special setup or artificial repro needed (10/10 failures during the recorded session):

1. Run an OpenClaw Gateway (2026.10.5, npm-global install, systemd user service) with the GitHub identity setup flow available.
2. Trigger a failure inside the `tools.github.configure` setup path — e.g. save an agent GitHub identity from the Control UI when the one-use setup handoff is missing/expired (no valid handoff, the call fails without performing any network work and returns the generic error).
3. Observe the client response and inspect the Gateway log around each failure.

The covered `try` block spans several unrelated fallible steps — `consumeGitHubSetupHandoff`, `installManagedGitHubProfile`, the `updateGitHubToolIdentityConfig` commit callback, and identity-status resolution — and every one of them collapses into the identical generic message.

### Expected behavior

When setup fails, the cause is visible to the operator: at minimum the Gateway logs the caught error, and ideally the response carries an actionable code/message. Precedent exists in the codebase: `mcp-app.ts` uses `logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage` in catch paths, and the fix for #135028 made the sibling `tools.github.authorize.start` handler distinguish `GitHubCliUnavailableError` specifically. The `tools.github.configure` handler was not given equivalent treatment.

### Actual behavior

The client receives only `errorShape(ErrorCodes.UNAVAILABLE, "GitHub identity setup failed")`, and the Gateway log contains no cause line before or after each failure — the response envelope is the entire trace. Verified against 2026.10.5:

- 10 failed `tools.github.configure` calls observed (2026-10-22 01:44–02:00 UTC), durations 1–468 ms.
- Full journal context inspected around each failure: only unrelated routine lines (memory embeddings, heartbeat, model-fetch); no error entry at all.
- The installed 2026.10.5 bundle (`dist/tools-github-CLW68rQL.mjs`) contains the same bare `catch {` immediately preceding the generic response, matching source `main` at `d5ce64b7` (`2026.10.5` package version).

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 — Gateway build `2026.10.5-release-1b58cb9a1b4f-2026-10-18T17-23-40.943Z` (the same `catch {}` was verified present in the installed bundle's `dist/tools-github-CLW68rQL.mjs`).

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux x86_64), Gateway host

### Install method

npm global install (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), run as systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service`.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Redacted Gateway journal excerpt (representative of the 10 observed failures; request/connection ids truncated, no auth data on these lines):

```shell
2026-10-22T01:44:07.729+00:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ tools.github.configure 346ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed" bytes=145 conn=1c521fd3…e887 id=338:da3800b5…c8bf
2026-10-22T01:45:47.160+00:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ tools.github.configure 61ms  errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed" bytes=145 conn=1c521fd3…e887 id=392:e347e4c8…df74
2026-10-22T01:46:40.990+00:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ tools.github.configure 1ms   errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed" bytes=145 conn=1c521fd3…e887 id=417:7e17f481…99c3
2026-10-22T01:55:04.374+00:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ tools.github.configure 381ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed" bytes=145 conn=1c521fd3…e887 id=661:bfb706c0…653d
```

No cause-bearing Gateway log line precedes or follows any of the ten failures; only the response envelope appears. Full unredacted journal context is available on request.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any operator using the GitHub identity setup flow (Control UI / CLI save path), and the support/maintainer team triaging the same.
- Severity: moderate — diagnosability loss, not a data risk; the flow fails visibly but stays silent about its reason.
- Frequency: 10/10 failures observed during a single one-hour session on 2026-10-22; every failure of the covered setup path produces the same opaque result.
- Consequence: transient, user-fixable (missing `gh` CLI, expired handoff), and hard failures are indistinguishable; troubleshooting requires reproduction and guessing across the several fallible steps instead of reading a log line.

### Additional information

Security: this is not a security report — the generic client-facing response stays generic; the ask is only that the caught error be logged server-side before the same response, e.g.:

```ts
logWarn(`tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: ${formatErrorMessage(error)}`);
```

A minimal patch (bind the error in the catch, one `logWarn` line, response byte-identical) is prepared locally against source `main` at `d5ce64b7`; I can open the PR against this issue.

Possible follow-up beyond logging: map `GitHubIdentityError` to more specific error codes while keeping the generic fallback.

**Related issues (checked 2026-10-23; none are duplicates):**

This report covers that remaining gap.
- #140576 (closed) describes a different defect (saved agent identity silently not updating in Control UI); it touches the same UI surface but does not report the swallowed-error/logging problem filed here.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Benign Chinese equipment-loan questions in an OpenClaw + OpenViking memory workflow intermittently end without a complete final answer when Alibaba's streamed DeepSeek response is rejected by output inspection. Direct API isolation reproduces the upstream rejection without OpenClaw or OpenViking executing any tools. Please help triage provider-error handling and whether a supported, opt-in same-model non-stream retry exists; this is not a claim that OpenClaw performs the moderation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.1 with an OpenAI-compatible model route through LiteLLM to Alibaba Model Studio's `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
2. Run an ordinary Chinese equipment-return / handover question with recalled business records. In our run, the final-answer model requests contained `stream=true`.
3. Inspect the raw API response: the provider can return an in-band output-inspection error after HTTP 200 and partial output. The agent does not obtain a complete final answer.
4. Use the minimal direct API isolation below to separate the upstream behavior from memory tools. Repeat independently with response caching disabled and compare non-stream output. The complete original histories are not attached; they contain extensive unrelated test context.

### Expected behavior

The benign test text should be answerable: the unchanged short sentence and one full question were observed to complete on non-stream calls. For an upstream content rejection, preserve and surface the actual failure rather than treating partial text or HTTP 200 as a completed answer. Is there a supported per-request/provider setting or extension point for an **opt-in, at-most-once, same-model non-stream transport retry**, while retaining completed tool results and leaving safety settings unchanged? A second rejection should remain a visible failure.

### Actual behavior

The original Lex Q104 and official-OV Q108 final-answer attempts ended without complete answers after provider output-inspection errors. Our benchmark controller recorded the missing final answer; that controller wording is local and is not asserted to be an OpenClaw error string. No network-failure inference should be made solely from LiteLLM's `APIConnectionError` wrapper.

### Isolated transport results (2026-10-23)

Model alias: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; route: OpenAI-compatible client → LiteLLM 1.105.0 → Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / Beijing MAAS. The model alias and provider route were unchanged. Safety and thinking settings were not disabled. Request-local response caching was disabled for the repeated diagnostics.

A minimal equipment-loan test sentence was:

> 约6月4日，当前只余赵棠的CAM-01未还。

It describes an equipment-loan status. In an additional small diagnostic, two streamed requests were interrupted with the output-inspection error; one non-streamed request returned this exact sentence with `finish_reason=stop`.

We also replayed two captured, full failed terminal requests three times each, changing only the response transport (`stream=false`, removing `stream_options`) plus request-local cache controls:

| Captured request | Non-stream outcomes |
|---|---|
| Official OpenViking integration, Q108 | 3/3 returned nonempty final answers with `finish_reason=stop` |
| Lex integration, Q104 | 1 final answer; 1 valid `tool_calls` response with no final answer; 1 HTTP 400 output-inspection rejection |

The original tool schemas remained present; diagnostic tool calls were not executed. A `tool_calls` response is an intermediate step, not a content rejection or proof that a complete agent run would fail. These were direct API replays, not six fresh end-to-end OC/OV runs. Normal termination was checked separately from answer correctness. In particular, non-streaming is **not** a guaranteed workaround, and generation variability prevents attributing every difference to transport alone.

### Errors observed

Stream: HTTP 200 was already committed, then the SSE contained an error and lacked a successful terminal answer:

```json
{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - Output data may contain inappropriate content.","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}}
```

One non-stream replay also failed (routing-detail suffix omitted from the message below):

```json
{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Custom_openaiException - Output data may contain inappropriate content.","type":"data_inspection_failed","param":null,"code":"400"}}
```

Alibaba's [official error reference](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/error-code#inappropriate-content) associates this message with provider content inspection. We do not have the provider's internal moderation category or audit logs.

### Minimal API isolation request

Send this body to the configured **LiteLLM** `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with your own authorization header:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "请逐字转写下面这段设备借还业务记录，不添加解释：\n约6月4日，当前只余赵棠的CAM-01未还。"}],
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "cache": {"no-cache": true, "no-store": true}
}
```

For the paired diagnostic, set `stream=false` and remove `stream_options`. The `cache` field is LiteLLM-specific. No content-inspection headers are added or disabled. This reproducer isolates the provider path; rejection can vary by account, generated text, and context, so it is not a deterministic assertion for every deployment.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.1, pinned Docker deployment. Not retested on current main/latest; no regression range established.

### Operating system

Linux container on a macOS host. Exact container distro version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

Docker. Two integrations were present: the official OpenViking plugin with local OC 9.1 compatibility adaptation, and a separate Lex memory integration. The direct API isolation did not load either plugin.

### Model

`deepseek-v4.1-flash` (configured alias, not an independently verified immutable upstream model build).

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → read-only diagnostic/metering forwarder → LiteLLM 1.105.0 → Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Beijing MAAS, OpenAI-compatible API).

### Impact and severity

Intermittent workflow-blocking failure: normal office questions sometimes end without a final answer. In the original Q108 original/fresh attempts, six individual model requests were rejected; these are not six separate question retries. Other streamed questions completed normally. Failed streams often omitted usage, making their complete cost unknown rather than zero.

### Additional information

Related but not identical: #32622 (Bailian input inspection on ordinary conversation), #152000 (provider content-guard classification/recovery).

We have not changed production transport/safety settings, replaced formal answers, reset sessions, or modified stored memory to work around the issue. The request is for accurate provider-error handling and a documented recovery boundary, not for disabling moderation.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a run fails with a billing error, the session row's `lastRunError` says "The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes." (the rate limit copy). The transcript entry for the same run correctly says "reported a billing problem".

### Steps to reproduce

`resolveSessionRunError` runs `renderUserFacingText(error, { errorContext: true })` on `outcome.error`, and by then that is already the text from `formatBillingErrorMessage`:

```
⚠️ openrouter (moonshotai/kimi-k3) returned a billing error — check your account's balance and usage limits before trying again. | 402
```

Feeding that string to `renderUserFacingText` (`repro.ts` in the gist: https://gist.github.com/eliavb43/f75d92a8109718fcb196a31e93fa755f):

```
reason: rate_limit
out   : ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.
```

A raw provider 402 body classifies as `billing` fine, so only the already formatted copy flips.

### Expected behavior

The billing copy ("The AI service reported a billing problem. …"), same as the raw 402 case.

### Actual behavior

`classifyFailoverReasonCore` returns `rate_limit`. I think two things add up: `isBillingErrorMessage` is false for this text (no billing pattern knows "returned a billing error", and the trailing `| 402` isn't read as a status), while the rateLimit table has the soft hint `"usage limit"` and the copy says "usage limits".

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (also reproduced on v2026.10.6 and main c133b02)

### Operating system

Ubuntu (WSL2)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openrouter

### Logs

Same output on v2026.10.6 and main, files in the gist (out-wt-106.txt, out-wt-main.txt).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

![repro output on v2026.10.6 and main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/eliavb43/f75d92a8109718fcb196a31e93fa755f/raw/billing-misclassified.png)

### Impact and severity

Affected: anyone who looks at session rows / run failure notices after a billing failure. Severity: low, it's just misleading text ("try again in a few minutes" when the account needs credit). Frequency: every time, for the formatted billing copy.

### Additional information

Adding `/\breturned a billing error\b/i` to `ERROR_PATTERNS.billing` in `message-patterns.ts` fixes it in my local run (reason becomes `billing`). I'll open a small PR with a test as a suggestion, happy to change the approach (another option is to not re-render text that is already user-facing copy).

Thanks!

Side chat today is a separate, read-only companion: hard-coded `read`, `sessions_history` and `sessions_search` tools, the utility model, and the OpenClaw runtime even when the parent uses the Codex harness (`src/gateway/session-companion-ask.ts`, `session-companion-policy.ts`).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When an adapter's unknown-send reconciliation throws, the queue always records the failure as retryable, so a permanent provider error consumes the retry budget instead of settling terminally.

### Steps to reproduce

Queue a delivery that is in an unknown-after-send state (a crash after the platform send started) for a channel whose adapter advertises the reconcileUnknownSend capability (for example Slack, Matrix, or ClickClack), and make that adapter's reconciliation throw a permanently-invalid error.
Trigger recovery drain (startup or periodic), which calls reconcileUnknownQueuedDelivery from the recovery loop.
Observe the returned reconciliation result: it is { status: "unresolved", error, retryable: true } regardless of the error text, so recovery re-queues the entry for another attempt up to the default retry budget of 5.

### Expected behavior

A permanent reconciliation failure should be classified as terminal (non-retryable) and settle the entry as failed, matching how the direct-send failure path classifies permanence.

### Actual behavior

The reconciliation result hardcodes retryable: true. In outbound/delivery-queue-reconciliation.ts:105-108 the catch block returns { status: "unresolved", error: message, retryable: true } for every thrown error. By contrast the direct-send failure path consults isPermanentDeliveryError at outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts:965-968 (and :1152), so the same class of permanent error is treated as terminal there but as retryable on the unknown-send reconciliation path.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output without crash)

## Summary

`openclaw update` and its repair/finalize paths interpolate invalid `--channel` values into diagnostics without escaping quotes or control characters, so one invalid argument can forge extra stderr lines and make JSON-mode error text ambiguous.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-invalid-channel-state \
HOME=/tmp/openclaw-invalid-channel-home \
openclaw update --json --channel $'beta"\nFORGED'
```

## Expected behavior

The rejected value is rendered as one unambiguous JSON string, for example `"beta\\"\\nFORGED"`. This matches the existing process-test oracle in `src/cli/update-cli.invalid-channel.process.test.ts`, which uses `JSON.stringify(channel)`.

## Actual behavior

The diagnostic contains a literal quote and newline:

```text

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
`openclaw backup record --bytes` silently accepts non-decimal numeric forms (`0x10`, `1e3`, `0b101`, `0o17`) via raw `Number()` coercion and records the coerced value, even though the command's own error message promises the value "must be a nonnegative integer."

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run from a source checkout with a writable state dir:
   `openclaw backup record --status ok --target t --bytes 0x10 --json`
2. Observe output records `"bytes": 16` instead of rejecting the input.

### Expected behavior
`--bytes 0x10` (hex), `--bytes 1e3` (exponent), `--bytes 0b101` (binary), and `--bytes 0o17` (octal) should be rejected as invalid because they are not plain decimal integer strings, consistent with `--bytes 12abc` and `--bytes -5`, which are correctly rejected with "--bytes must be a nonnegative integer." The rest of the CLI rejects these forms via `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`/`parseStrictPositiveInteger` (e.g. `worktrees retire-snapshot --removed-at`).

Note: signed and zero-padded decimal strings (`+5`, `010`) are intentionally accepted and interpreted as decimal integers by the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` contract, so they are out of scope for this issue.

### Actual behavior
```
$ openclaw backup record --status ok --target t --bytes 0x10 --json
{
  "kind": "external",
  "archivePath": "t",
  "target": "t",
  "status": "ok",
  "bytes": 16
}
$ openclaw backup record --status ok --target t --bytes 1e3 --json
{ ... "bytes": 1000 }
```
The coerced value is written into the backup outcome ledger (manifest) instead of the CLI rejecting the invalid input.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.5 (source checkout, `dist/index.js`)

### Operating system
Windows 11

### Install method
pnpm dev / source build

### Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no model involved; pure CLI command)

### Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no provider involved)

### Impact and severity
Affected: operators/scripts that use `openclaw backup record --bytes` with a size expression that is not a plain decimal integer (e.g. a script passing `0x...`, a binary/octal literal, or a shell `$((...))` arithmetic that emits an exponent form).
Severity: Low (edge case) — the value is silently wrong rather than rejected, so recorded backup sizes can be incorrect.
Frequency: edge case.
Consequence: incorrect byte counts recorded in the backup outcome ledger; silent data-quality defect.

issues.body:
## Bug: MiniMax M3.1 Flash (Ollama Pro) tool calls fail 100% — "Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call"

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9) — npm, stable channel, macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Node v26.8.1
**Provider:** `ollamapro` (baseUrl: `https://ollama.com/v1`, api: `openai-completions`)
**Model:** `ollamapro/minimax-m3.1-flash` (free tier until Oct 22, 2026)

### Summary

Every agent turn that requires a tool call fails with `Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call`. Plain text turns succeed. The same error affects multiple providers (#164341 — forra, xiaomi), suggesting a shared stream-parsing defect.

### Evidence

**Raw SSE from Ollama Pro (curl, no OpenClaw):**
Flash emits valid OpenAI-format tool calls:
```
chunk 1: {"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"I'll read that"}}
chunk 2: {"delta":{"content":" file for you."}}
chunk 3: {"delta":{"content":"","tool_calls":[{"id":"call_function_...","index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":"read_file","arguments":"{\"path\":\"/tmp/test.txt\"}"}}]},"finish_reason":null}
chunk 4: {"delta":{},"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}
```

**OpenAI SDK v7.27.0 passthrough:**
Identical chunks — SDK does not modify tool_calls. Accumulated `partialArgs` = `{"path":"/tmp/test.txt"}`, `name` = `"read_file"`. Both non-empty.

**Gateway log (2026-10-20, post-upgrade to 2026.10.5):**
```
18:56:45 tool-search: cataloged 91 tools behind compact prompt surface
18:56:47 [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=1904 contentType=text/event-stream
18:56:50 embedded run agent end isError=true rawError=Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call
```

No intermediate log lines between response receipt and error. ~3s gap.

**Tested with 91 tools:** Flash correctly selects and calls the right tool from 91 options in raw tests.

### Root cause hypothesis

The error is set in `finalizeOpenAICompletionsToolCalls` (openai-completions-transport) when:
```js
toolCalls.some(call => typeof call.name !== "string" || call.name.trim().length === 0 
  || typeof call.partialArgs !== "string" || call.partialArgs.trim().length === 0)
```

Since the raw stream has valid name and partialArgs, the issue is likely:
1. A stream wrapper between the SDK and `finalizeOpenAICompletionsToolCalls` is dropping or corrupting the tool call block, OR
2. The `normalizeToolCallDeltas` function is not correctly accumulating tool calls when content precedes them in the same stream, OR
3. A text-tool-call promoter wrapper is creating a spurious malformed tool call from Flash's visible text output

### Reproduction

```
model: ollamapro/minimax-m3.1-flash
prompt: "Use the read_file tool to read /tmp/test.txt"
expected: tool call to read_file with path=/tmp/test.txt
actual: "Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call"
```

### Workaround

None found. Setting `compat.supportsTools: true` explicitly did not help (already the default). Disabling code mode is not relevant (not enabled).

### Related issues

- #164341 — same error, forra provider, deterministic
- #157469 — same error, xiaomi provider, closed as fixed by #164274 (but that fix targets malformed calls *after earlier tools ran*, not first-call failures)
