prs.title: perf(ui): consolidate chat and New Session route CSS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session fetch eight and six bundled stylesheets during boot, adding requests before the page is ready.

## User Impact

Both routes fetch three bundled stylesheets, including the unchanged initial shell sheet, and total CSS gzip drops by 4,189 B in the original matched build. Chat timing remains outside the agreed acceptance band; this PR is held from merging pending that decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracted CSS disappears from JavaScript source maps, so the boot manifest omitted styles scattered across multiple chunks. Retain reachable external CSS, exclude inline style strings, and consolidate through the existing route groups. Optional component styles remain lazy, and no CSS declarations or selectors change.

## Evidence

Current landing status: **held by the timing acceptance rule; auto-merge is not armed.** The byte/request target and focused tests pass. On this shared Mac, Chat's completed twenty-pair result has composer median +6.15% (limit +5%), composer p95 +1.49%, and transcript p95 +2.06% (required: no p95 regression). New Session passes after twenty pairs: composer median +1.40% and p95 -35.64%. All eighty cold-load samples are retained. CI is requested to validate the complete code change, including the inline-style regression.

| Cold-cache metric | Pairs | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 | Median / p95 change | Timing rule |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Chat: composer ready | 20 | 6086.8 / 12233.3 ms | 6460.9 / 12415.5 ms | +6.15% / +1.49% | Not met |
| Chat: transcript visible | 20 | 8297.7 / 14379.3 ms | 8515.0 / 14676.1 ms | +2.62% / +2.06% | Not met |
| New Session: composer ready | 20 | 4292.1 / 9957.4 ms | 4352.1 / 6408.6 ms | +1.40% / -35.64% | Met |

Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, 32 available CPUs, 512 GiB RAM. Load averages are recorded before/after every pair and by each measured run. The unchanged startup CSS is also slower in this sample set (Chat median arrival 1,495.5 → 1,916.1 ms), so these loaded-host results do not establish a CSS-caused regression. They also do not waive the stated timing rule. No local Docker or live operator Gateway is used.

Acceptance rule recorded before timing: each route uses at most three asset CSS requests in total (one startup plus at most two route sheets); startup stays at one CSS request; total CSS raw/gzip bytes do not grow beyond 64 B. Measure ten alternating baseline/candidate cold-cache first-load pairs per route with the committed cold-load benchmark, the same fixture time, 35 ms network latency, 10 Mbps download, and 4x CPU throttling on one host. The requested Testbox retry queued again, so the coordinator explicitly authorized the same workload on this Mac with host load recorded per pair. Compare enabled-composer and first-nonempty-transcript medians and nearest-rank p95 (transcript for Chat only). Accept median regression at most 5% with no p95 regression; collect ten more pairs if needed to resolve the acceptance band. Any regression above 20% blocks. Inspect separate filmstrip captures for unstyled flashes; traced captures do not supply timing results.

Each pair runs the baseline and candidate serially with this committed workload (a fresh process/browser for each sample):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --bundle-dir <base-or-head-bundle> --first-load --runs 1 \
  --boot-route <chat-or-new> --face chat --cold-http-cache --untraced \
  --color-scheme light --network-latency-ms 35 --download-kbps 10000 \
  --cpu-throttle 4 --fixture-now-ms 1792717200000 --output <sample-directory>
```

The benchmark serves production assets with synthetic bootstrap, WebSocket RPC, and fixture media; it does not measure real session authorization, server CPU, or service-worker caching.

Original matched build (same source/toolchain/machine as the baseline; the timing series above uses these bundles):

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 315,877 B | 315,632 B |
| Startup CSS requests / gzip | 1 / 41,124 B | 1 / 41,124 B |
| Chat CSS requests / gzip | 8 / 145,924 B | 3 / 141,910 B |
| New Session CSS requests / gzip | 6 / 106,434 B | 3 / 104,228 B |
| All CSS files / gzip | 111 / 315,108 B | 105 / 310,919 B |
| All CSS raw | 1,594,317 B | 1,594,311 B |
| Deferred stylesheets outside both boot graphs | 101 | 101, byte-identical |
| Largest stylesheet gzip | 41,124 B | 57,154 B |

Refreshed exact-head comparison after merging current main: candidate `09ced2869a6d6d0010d837d7a1e8b5cb9363a67d` against merge base `38f070553d67c3b30de6fd2670103341080024fb`, built with fixed identity on the same Mac and installed toolchain using `pnpm ui:check-performance:base <base-sha>`:

| Surface | Refreshed base | Refreshed head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip / requests | 315,661 B / 7 | 315,375 B / 7 |
| Startup CSS gzip / requests | 41,143 B / 1 | 41,143 B / 1 |
| Chat CSS gzip / requests | 145,976 B / 8 | 141,950 B / 3 |
| New Session CSS gzip / requests | 106,486 B / 6 | 104,268 B / 3 |
| All CSS gzip | 315,157 B | 310,956 B |
| Largest head stylesheet gzip | — | 57,175 B (cap 58,315 B) |

The refreshed comparison removes 4,201 B total CSS gzip and reports no budget violations. It preserves main's newer JavaScript deferrals and stricter route JS caps. The original timing series remains labeled with its original head/base above; no additional timing samples were substituted.

The largest-sheet cap is 58,315 B: the measured 57,154 B plus the same relative headroom used by the previous cap (53,400 / 52,337, about 2.03%; see #136186). The startup checks remain unchanged. The old largest-file growth check is replaced by a 64 B total-CSS gzip growth allowance so regrouping cannot disguise additional bytes.

Coordinator decision (2026-10-22):

> The per-file CSS cap exists to stop runaway shared chunks. Here you merge stylesheets that always load together, total CSS gzip drops by 4,189 B, and route CSS requests go 8 → 3 (chat) and 6 → 3 (New Session). Raise the largest-shared-sheet cap to the measured 57,154 B plus the cap's normal relative headroom, in the same PR, with a reason that names this consolidation and the total-byte decrease. Quote this decision in the PR body. If the merged sheet contains rules that aren't needed on both routes, say so in the PR and leave them; the request count matters more.

The shared sheet includes conditional assistant-panel, transcript, camera, and other component rules that are not all painted on both routes. Those styles were already fetched by both routes and intentionally remain together. Optional styles outside the two boot graphs remain deferred.

Every original route stylesheet is accounted for below. Sizes are shipped gzip bytes; hashed filenames are shortened to their stable prefix. Conditional styles remain necessary for the page-owned loading shell or restored content even when absent from the empty fixture.

| Original asset | Gzip | Owner / first-frame use | New owner |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| control-ui-core.css | 41,124 B | Initial shell, tokens, shared primitives; both routes | Unchanged initial sheet |
| control-ui-boot-shared-styles.css | 40,611 B | Composer, text, rail/header, picker and shared route styles; both routes | Shared route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-shared.css | 7,550 B | Sidebar rail/reorder/pinned agents, identity and assistant-panel shell; sidebar rules apply immediately, closed-panel rules are conditional | Shared route sheet |
| chat-transcript-styles.css | 11,024 B | grouped.css + message-layout.css; Chat transcript, New Session restored draft previews | Shared route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-chat-styles.css | 27,841 B | Chat layout, attachment/detail/attribution/subagent/selection surfaces; layout applies immediately, content-dependent rules apply when present | Chat route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-chat-DutuGsya.css | 1,879 B | Message reaction chips/picker; rendered reaction controls | Chat route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-chat-_TJ_Cs4g.css | 695 B | Header presence and usage-limit modal; presence applies immediately, modal is conditional | Chat route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-chat-D7ZwJo6b.css | 15,200 B | Person/file references, source previews, tool/board/split-view/mobile/composer-status rules; conditional on first-frame content | Chat route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-new-styles.css | 5,857 B | New Session hero, draft, composer and recent rows | New Session route sheet |
| control-ui-boot-new.css | 268 B | New Session attachment-panel shell; absent in the empty fixture, needed before its lazy contents | New Session route sheet |

The table and performance budgets count emitted `/assets/*.css` in the boot graph, matching the campaign's 8/6 starting counts. The cold-load HTTP waterfalls also contain these unchanged requests:

| Stylesheet | Bytes | Owner / first-frame use |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| fonts/instrument-sans.css | 2,422 B raw; about 685 B encoded | Typography owner; selected Claw theme face, used by both routes |
| fonts/jetbrains-mono.css | 2,413 B raw; about 690 B encoded | Typography owner; shared code face declaration, glyph downloads remain lazy |
| context-breakdown.css | 2,987 B gzip | Lazy Chat context breakdown / details content |
| chat-pull-request-presenters.css | 3,053 B gzip | Lazy pull-request details and branch actions |
| chat-outputs.css | 2,941 B gzip | Lazy Chat outputs content |
| session-progress-card-solid.css | 2,275 B gzip | Lazy session task-progress card |
| chat-details-session.css | 1,443 B gzip | Lazy Chat session details |
| lobster-pet-identity.css | 4,924 B gzip | Lazy pet identity; New Session fixture requests it after composer readiness |
| Seven fixture plugin index.css files | 37 B encoded each | Synthetic plugin widgets; independent plugin styles, outside the application boot bundle |

The deferred application sheets above belong to the 101 byte-identical stylesheets outside both boot graphs. In the first bounded Chat captures they complete after composer readiness; optional content keeps its existing CSS boundary. Selected fonts and independent plugin stylesheet requests are not being consolidated or claimed as removed.

Local synthetic screenshots and sampled filmstrips show styled shell/content transitions. All boot CSS completed before the visible enabled composer and nonempty transcript in those captures. This is visual evidence, not a timing acceptance claim. Consolidation also restores the source-defined circular Chat avatar: previously the later generic identity `border-radius: inherit` overrode the chat avatar radius.

Validation: UI typecheck passed; all 37 performance-checker cases are covered by the first run (32 passed) and corrected boundary-case rerun (10/10 passed). The five old-policy expectations were updated for the approved total-byte limit, without changing production code after review. Chunking tests pass 6/6, including the inline/external-style fixture; formatting passes. Script lint did not reach lint because Plugin SDK declaration preparation timed out at 300 seconds. Production Knip reports the pre-existing `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs` unused file (same Git blob on baseline and current main). No ignores were added.

Both Testbox requests queued before any command ran and were stopped under the remote proof policy. Their backends report completed with no host; GitHub cleanup association remains pending. Twenty alternating pairs per route completed (eighty samples total). No samples are excluded. These timing samples compare original base `22338ef3220a6598bcf893e86018b1446c07ab63` with original head `1753deb419a54a1385f9655a4f9a0ee66e66db61`; they are not relabeled as measurements of a later merge head.

LOC: production tooling/config 1,456 -> 1,473 (+17); tests 1,242 -> 1,297 (+55); generated manifest 1,851 -> 1,881 (+30); docs 327 -> 333 (+6); total changed files 4,876 -> 4,984 (+108), against refreshed merge base `38f070553d67c3b30de6fd2670103341080024fb`.

The initial independent review identified the unapproved per-file budget increase. After the explicit coordinator approval, fresh isolated autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent edits only corrected old-policy test expectations; the new boundary cases pass. No production rendering code, owner state, or Solid lifecycle constructs changed.

prs.title: fix: defer draft storage loading until needed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Draft storage runtime initialization currently starts as soon as the chat recovery and persistence modules are imported, even when no storage operation has been admitted.

## User Impact

Draft restoration, persistence, recovery confirmation, and error handling retain their existing behavior. Optional storage code starts loading when those operations actually need it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the three eager runtime imports to their existing operation boundaries. The two plain persistence owners retain first-demand cached readiness: fresh import promises changed settled-operation ordering and caused five New Session race tests to fail; preserving the shared promise fixes those regressions. Recovery retains the same first-demand promise and original namespace access/control flow: the direct-import version changed Solid action readiness and broke retry/remount confirmation. Current owner and generation checks remain unchanged.

The manual stored/chained import census remains **66 → 66**, while eager runtime initializations decrease **3 → 0**. These three caches belong to storage owners and preserve demonstrated ordering contracts; removing a proven readiness cache would misrepresent the cleanup. Touched production files contain no `onCleanup`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner`, or `flush` calls; those counts remain zero. No new abstraction, dependency, component loader, markup, or CSS is introduced.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| `new-session/draft-persistence.test.ts` | 23 passed; same 23 pass on exact base |
| `chat/chat-outbox-recovery.test.ts` | 1 passed on final source; new assertion fails on exact-base implementation because an unadmitted owner initializes storage |
| `chat/chat-outbox-recovery-owner.test.ts` | 4 passed on final source, including both retry/remount confirmations that failed on the initial PR head |
| `chat/composer-persistence-restore.test.ts` | No assertion result: pinned Bun worker hit the runner's 120-second no-output guard; retained child PIDs confirmed gone |
| `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` | Passed; manual imports 66 → 66, other controller baselines unchanged |
| `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --prune` | Passed; explicit mock-isolation explanation removes one obsolete exact-factory allowance |
| Targeted lint / format / `git diff --check` | Passed; one warning on an unchanged recovery subscription line |
| Production Knip | Head reports one unused Telegram test-support file; the broader same-config production scan on exact base reports the identical file |
| Independent Codex review through P2 | Scoped-clean; no actionable findings |

The local test commands use the pinned Bun runtime, `--pool=forks --maxWorkers=1`, and Node 26.12.1 for the wrapper. Full UI coverage runs through `ci:full`; no local E2E suite or build was run for this nonvisual runtime-only change.

LOC against `16920345c8785c5b3d79efbd3499984d51292b68`: production **1,443 → 1,453** (+10); recovery tests **352 → 366** (+14); shared E2E helper **259 → 262** (+3). The added production lines defer initialization while preserving cached readiness; the test readiness precondition waits for durable preparation before counting subsequent owner refreshes.

Knip attribution: `pnpm deadcode:knip` on this head reports `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs`. On clean exact base `16920345c8785c5b3d79efbd3499984d51292b68`, `pnpm dlx --package knip@6.40.0 knip --config config/knip.config.ts --production --no-progress --reporter compact --no-config-hints --exclude duplicates` reports the same unused file (plus the broader scan’s export/type findings). The base command includes the files/dependencies detectors; these are different command scopes, not a claim that the narrower command ran twice.

Initial `ci:full` run `39892137428` exposed the recovery action-ordering regression and the missing mock-isolation explanation; both are repaired in the follow-up head. Two UI E2E failures (progress-card hiding and mobile Panels reachability) passed on the latest completed scheduled main run `39890895258`, so they remain owned/unresolved until the repaired head's CI proves them. The real-Gateway session-PR reader assertion fails identically on that scheduled main run. UI unit shard 2's retained failure log contains setup output but no assertion failure; no test verdict is inferred from that gap.

The initial dark-mobile Panels failure also exposed a setup race in `openChatPanels`: it picked desktop controls when the mobile header had not rendered yet. The helper now waits for a visible header and uses the existing layout-settlement helper before selecting mobile or desktop controls, matching the sibling layout-action helper. The original mobile assertions and timeouts remain unchanged; the next full CI run provides browser proof.

prs.title: fix(secrets): reject malformed UTF-8 plans before applying them
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `secrets apply --from` silently replaces malformed UTF-8 bytes before parsing a plan, which can change a provider path and apply the altered value.

## User Impact

Malformed UTF-8 plans fail before apply runs. Valid Unicode plans, including literal replacement characters, retain their contents. Existing regular-file and 16 MiB limits remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `decodeUtf8Input` helper at the bounded plan-file reader instead of maintaining another UTF-8 validator. Original fix and regression coverage by @Alix-007.

## Evidence

The two malformed-input regressions fail on baseline `b4031b2954c7984754a2c375ab528162b795654b` because apply succeeds. Both pass with the fix, and the valid Unicode/CRLF control passes. The unchanged baseline secrets suite also passed all 20 tests.

Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'UTF-8 secrets plans'`. The post-integration run selected three secrets cases: 3 passed, 20 skipped, 213.79 seconds in Vitest (246.18 seconds for the wrapper), including cold CLI imports. After the first import, the truncated-sequence and valid controls took 22 ms and 15 ms.

Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, core and test-graph typechecks, and whitespace checks pass. Final isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head [CI run 39896103143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39896103143) passed for `6f17e8acefcee9165fccc60f149275a9c38f8bdd`; the repository watcher reports GREEN with no pending checks. Dependency review briefly published “Security review has not completed,” then changed to “No dependency changes require review” four seconds later in the same [security run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39896732709). No CI rerun or code change was needed.

The final [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167379#issuecomment-6066233248) found no code defects and requests additional shipped-CLI proof. That proof remains unrun for the bounded-live reason below.

A fresh standalone CLI/live Gateway proof was not run: generated CLI runtime artifacts are absent and a cold build exceeds the bounded live-proof effort. The regression invokes Commander and the real bounded file reader, with only the downstream apply operation mocked. Earlier contributor Linux CLI proof applies to its recorded historical head, not this head.

Production delta: +3/-1 (net +2); tests: +47/-0. The two added production lines connect the existing decoder without weakening file admission or adding another validation implementation.

prs.title: refactor: remove unused runtime arguments and result metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal runtime helpers still carry arguments, branches, and result metadata their production callers never use.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, public API change, migration, or operator action. This removes 130 net production lines across 13 files; tests/support shrink by 166 lines.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hook npm installation has one archive installer and one workspace prefix, so the hook owner now runs its pack, prerelease, integrity, and install sequence directly. The generic callback, forwarding bag, result types, and orphan module disappear. The existing lazy runtime facade remains the boundary for installation tooling.

CLI launchers use their actual process facts rather than test-only process/platform/environment bags. Asset health checks use the package root every production caller already supplies; rebuilds retain their fixed production timeout and stop returning unread `built` metadata. Smaller cuts remove unused restart-attempt metadata, a private verbose-duration mode, an unread media-completion summary, and an unused retained-tree progress callback.

Production caller searches include extensions, packages, UI, scripts, aliases, and SDK barrels. The installed-wrapper `moduleUrl` fixture seam is deliberately retained. Public config/CLI/Gateway/SDK and persisted shapes, live authority checks, source/standalone/Windows launch handling, cancellation, installation integrity/policy, transaction receipts, and workspace settlement stay intact. The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Internal argument bags are stable during a call. Mutating hook-install options during an awaited npm pack is not a production caller behavior; installation policy and effect-boundary callbacks still run. No extra snapshots or mutation fences are added.
- Synthetic process, formatter, and health-discovery variants with no production caller are no longer injectable. Tests use existing process/module mocks or the actual discovery owner instead.
- No security, normal crash/restart durability, realistic-concurrency, or resource-bound guard is removed.

## Evidence

- Hook installation: 43 focused cases across three files pass, including real archive extraction, policy rejection, deferred transactions, work deadlines, integrity/prerelease admission, and real temporary-workspace cleanup. Vitest 33.44 s including cold compilation; wrapper 42.73 s. The migrated npm admission file has no real network calls.
- Asset health/rebuild consumers: 64 focused cases across six files pass. Native targeted no-emit checks, typed lint, format, and whitespace checks pass.
- CLI invocation/shims and their consumers: 29 focused cases pass; five existing native-Windows skips remain an explicit platform-proof gap. No timeout, retry, or skip was added.
- Earlier restart, formatter, completion, and retained-tree cuts retain their focused passing proof and independent clean reviews. The retention proof includes after-await authority rejection; those checks are unchanged.
- Independent P0–P2 reviews are clean for each cut; the final hook specialization is scoped-clean. Suppression guard: 14 cases pass. Runtime and Madge import-cycle checks both find zero cycles.
- Fresh main has no intervening edits to these production owners. PR CI on the exact head supplies broad/platform proof; no local build, broad suite, live Gateway, or whole-graph typecheck was run.

prs.title: perf(ui): load mascot motion on first visible use
prs.body:
Mascot motion was bundled into Chat and New Session even when its host was hidden. Load the deterministic animator on first visible use, while the existing canvas, static pose, sizing, theme, and playback owner remain synchronous. Hiding and reopening retain the same canvas and animator. Reduced-motion and hidden-document rules stay intact; import failure retains the static pose. Browsers without IntersectionObserver retain eager motion startup.

| Production boot surface | Base gzip | Candidate gzip | Change | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,324 B | 316,317 B | −7 B (build variance) | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,349,072 B | 1,346,578 B | −2,494 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 823,291 B | 820,819 B | −2,472 B | 17 → 17 |

Matched production builds compare main `82c46546765f97edea22f0d9fea65f97ed7d67b2` with runtime head `6a60c51f4059b07c9b00394349866d585ccb2392`; the follow-up changes only cap numbers. Both builds use identical explicit metadata and 29 checksum-verified plugin inputs. CSS is unchanged and the strict check has zero violations. Keep the stricter existing startup baseline; lower Chat/New Session caps to 1,397,842 / 831,850 B, preserving relative headroom. No new boot request, dependency, tag, selector, artwork, or presentation change.

Before timing, acceptance is fixed: the baseline's committed cold-load workload, 240 messages, 20 alternating cold-HTTP-cache samples (10 pairs), untraced; transcript/composer medians may regress at most 5% and p95 must not worsen. Fresh exact-head timing passed on Blacksmith run [39896502503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39896502503), using the same base/head source trees, explicit build metadata, and 29 plugin inputs. The requested 16-class runner provided 4 CPUs and 16.6 GB RAM; observed load was recorded with each sample.

| Cold-load outcome | Base median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First visible transcript | 540.35 / 635.90 ms | 523.60 / 600.30 ms |
| Enabled composer | 539.30 / 634.60 ms | 522.35 / 599.20 ms |

Both medians improve about 3.1%, and both p95 values improve about 5.6%. This synthetic transport benchmark does not measure live provider/network latency.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Integrated `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Mascot and chunk contracts | 10/10 passed; unchanged by main integration |
| Matched production builds and strict comparison | Passed, zero violations |
| Independent integration and numeric-cap reviews | P0–P2 scoped-clean |
| Production `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Exit 1: sole unused Telegram ingress test-support file, identical on exact82c base |
| Fresh full CI | Run [39893810689](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893810689) complete: all unit and regular E2E jobs pass; sole real-Gateway failure matches scheduled main (below) |
| Fresh cold-load timing | 20 alternating samples passed both transcript/composer median and p95 gates |

The focused regression verifies that a hidden mascot draws immediately without scheduling motion and keeps its identical canvas through reveal/hide/reveal. Existing motion tests wait for the asynchronous animator, and the chunk contract keeps motion out of boot even when an older boot manifest contains it.

One owner remains responsible for drawing and playback, with a one-way first-use latch. Solid refactor counts are unchanged: effects 1→1, onSettled 1→1, untrack/direct listeners/queries/cleanup/owner APIs 0→0. Production LOC in touched modules, including the budget checker: 1,290→1,321 (+31); the growth handles optional readiness and failure, with no duplicate renderer. No live Gateway or private data. The timing lease is being released after evidence download.

Current CI attribution: the sole root failure is `Session PR readers through a real Gateway > keeps session PR and CI results with the current workspace and reader`, in `session-pr-reader-lifetime.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:465`: the workspace title is null. The same exact name and assertion fail in latest completed scheduled main [39890895258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890895258), job 120210444912. No passing-CI claim is made. The required timing gate also passed; this CI failure is retained for native inherited-failure admission.

The initial allocation, run 39895494703, was stopped too early after its transient queued status; it had reached normal hydration. It produced no samples and was cleaned up. The replacement run above completed the full proof. Its lease is being released after evidence download.

Private setup, parser, lifecycle and rendering work still crosses argument/result frames or modules used by only one production owner.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep each responsibility in its existing consumer: Feishu's invitation callback, OpenCode's stream adapter, StepFun's registration loop, LINE's card handler, completion installation and Mantis's desktop runner. Remove private forwarding frames and StepFun's single-consumer setup module. Shared SDK owners, substantive parsers, lazy boundaries, validation, cancellation, authority, durability and settlement remain.

StepFun's four direct-helper preservation cases now call the actual registered noninteractive auth methods. They passed before and after the production fold; runtime-owned ordinary catalogs, exact replace catalogs, aliases and repeat-setup idempotency stay covered. Existing primary/fallback and method-registration tests remain. Incoming Step5 proposals #153525/#156412 are not implemented here; their future alias-preservation logic belongs in the retained SDK resolveParams callback.

Net production reduction: **155 lines** (+370/-525 across seven production paths). Tests grow by 17 lines (+44/-27). No assertion, timeout, retry, skip, suppression or allowance is weakened.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None: no guards or supported scenarios are removed. Only private single-consumer parameter/result and forwarding frames disappear.

## Evidence

Focused serial runs with one worker and isolated state: Feishu invitation/account lifecycle17 cases (56.0s wrapper), OpenCode stream plus prompt-prefix11 cases (35.4s), StepFun registration/setup8 cases (33.9s after fold;31.8s baseline), LINE parser/blank fields/lazy registration/card siblings40 cases (30.5s), completion27 cases (2.8s;four existing Windows-only skips are not Windows proof), Mantis runner/shared lifecycle30 cases (12.0s). prs.title: perf(ui): defer dictation capture until voice starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Composer dictation eagerly loads microphone capture, audio conversion, and transcription-session code even when the user only reads or types a message. Load that runtime on the first dictation or Split Talk interaction. The existing owner still performs gesture admission and playback preparation synchronously, then checks current cancellation, client, and session identity before starting capture after the import.

One explicit capture chunk prevents the shared dictation/Split Talk dependency from being merged back into the eager route graph. The error formatter remains a small shared leaf. Import/start failure uses the existing visible error path; stop, reset, disconnect, and final-transcript settlement stay with the current owner.

## Performance

Matched production builds on the same machine: base `82c46546765f97edea22f0d9fea65f97ed7d67b2`, runtime candidate `f77a496afb617a4781edbf62b4f2ddd00470888a`, identical fixed build metadata and the same checked 29 packaged-plugin inputs. Both use build ID `solid2-boot-comparison`; physical source identity is verified separately. The final commit only ratchets performance caps; it does not change these runtime build inputs.

| Surface | Base | Candidate | Change | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,324 B | 316,313 B | −11 B | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,349,072 B | 1,345,818 B | −3,254 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 823,291 B | 820,084 B | −3,207 B | 17 → 17 |

CSS is byte-identical; startup remains 41,128 B / one request. Strict base comparison has zero violations or warnings. Route caps preserve prior relative headroom: `ceil(candidate × old cap / base)`, yielding Chat 1,397,054 B and New Session 831,106 B. The existing stricter 315,881 B startup baseline remains unchanged. The regenerated boot attribution excludes capture/audio from both route graphs.

Production owner modules: 859 → 889 lines (+30), plus four build-boundary lines. The growth handles cancellation and current-context validation around the new asynchronous import. No new reactive owner, cache, effect, listener, or DOM query. This changes no visual design, host tag, selector, or layout.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` on integrated source | Passed |
| `composer-dictation.test.ts` | 27/27 passed, covering synchronous playback preparation, cancel→restart, session replacement during loading, startup failure, stop/reset/disconnect and final transcript settlement |

prs.title: fix(plugins): fence enqueueNextTurnInjection by plugin generation and global side effects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a Plugin SDK generation can retain `api.session.workflow.enqueueNextTurnInjection` (or deprecated `api.enqueueNextTurnInjection`) after `register()` returns, allowing retired generations to recreate durable next-turn injections. After disable cleanup removes the generation's state, the stale API can still enqueue model-visible text under a replacement generation's identity. Sibling late-callable mutators (`emitAgentEvent`, run context, attachment delivery, schedule/unschedule) are already generation-fenced via `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` and `activateGlobalSideEffects`; the enqueue handler was the only gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair adds the same two guards the sibling handlers use:

- When `activateGlobalSideEffects` is `false`, return the existing nonthrowing `{ enqueued: false, id: "", sessionKey }` shape so global opt-out still applies.
- When `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` is `false` (registry retired or generation not active), return the same inert shape so a retired generation cannot recreate durable state.
- Valid activation-time calls remain aligned with `emitAgentEvent` and pass through to the durable enqueuer.

The fence is checked before policy diagnostics, config reads, and state writes, so the retired generation can no longer commit new workflow side effects. The check uses the workflow-side-effect guard rather than the stricter live-registry helper so valid activation-time calls remain aligned with `emitAgentEvent`.

## User Impact

Trusted in-process plugin code can no longer accidentally or asynchronously mutate durable session state after disable. Re-enabling a plugin no longer lets a new generation consume retired-generation text as model-visible prompt context, and a stale idempotency key can no longer occupy the replacement generation's queue. The repair is a Plugin SDK lifecycle and model-input integrity fix; it is not a plugin sandbox or privilege-escalation change.

## Evidence

Files changed:
- `src/plugins/registry-api.ts` — `enqueueNextTurnInjection` handler now checks `activateGlobalSideEffects === false` and `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` before policy diagnostics, config reads, and state writes; returns the same inert shape the existing `allowPromptInjection === false` path uses (+14 / -0 production LOC).

Reproduction from issue #127396: a temporary session store, real plugin registries/APIs, real registry retirement, real disable cleanup, a stale retained enqueue API call, and the production next-turn drain. The production proof showed `pendingAfterDisableCleanup: null`, `staleEmit: { emitted: false, reason: "plugin is not loaded" }`, and `staleEnqueue: { enqueued: true, id: "retired-proof", sessionKey: "agent:main:main" }`. After this fix, the `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` check returns false for the retired generation so the handler returns the inert shape and `staleEnqueue.enqueued` becomes `false` while `staleEmit` continues to be correctly rejected.

CI must validate: full vitest lane + lint + typecheck on the PR head SHA.

prs.title: fix: wait for keyboard progress hide before resize
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The progress-card E2E checks that a locally hidden card stays hidden after a responsive resize. Its keyboard path dispatched Enter on “Hide this card” and immediately resized the viewport, even though first-open menu navigation can defer keyboard selection until its runtime finishes loading. Because that resize intentionally closes the old menu, the test could cancel its own pending action and report a progress-pill failure before local hiding had completed.

## User Impact

There is no production behavior change. The E2E now starts its responsive persistence check only after the keyboard menu action has completed, while preserving the saved Details card, local-only hide behavior, pointer coverage, no-write checks, peer isolation, reload behavior, focus expectations, timeouts, and final pill assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completing Playwright’s Enter dispatch does not prove that a deliberately deferred menu callback has run. The existing menu item becoming hidden is the action’s public semantic completion signal: menu activation invokes the selection callback before closing the overlay. Waiting for that state keeps intentional cancel-on-close behavior intact and separates keyboard-action completion from the independent resize under test.

## Evidence

The exact candidate passed remote changed-file format, lint, and Control UI i18n checks, plus the canonical `core-test-ui-e2e` type graph. The full existing `session-progress-live-placement.e2e.test.ts` file passed all 7 tests. A separate fresh invocation of `hides active progress locally without clearing the saved card` also passed its one selected case, ensuring full-file ordering did not warm the cold menu path.

Hosted CI and automated review remain pending on this initial non-draft head. Screenshots are not applicable because this changes test sequencing only; no rendered UI behavior changes.

Fixes the real-Gateway restart recovery fixture hanging during its `SIGTERM` case after saved chat inputs begin replaying. prs.title: fix: bound stalled session archive and reconciliation work
prs.body:
Related: #176080

## What Problem This Solves

Stuck archive work can hold its FIFO indefinitely, and timed-out archive or transcript-reconciliation workers can retain native/database custody forever if termination never finishes. This completes the reporter's requested bounded retirement and recovery through the existing Gateway service lifecycle.

## User Impact

Archive admission is bounded to 128 outstanding claims. Active archive and reconciliation tasks request retirement after 180000ms. FIFO and database ownership remain held until physical settlement; expiration never admits overlapping replacement work.

If native settlement remains pending after the existing 5000ms retirement grace, the Gateway recovery owner verifies its live native service and Node command, then requests forced fresh-process recovery through the existing shutdown and hard-exit path. Required fresh-process recovery cannot fall back to an in-process restart. Concurrent requests coalesce and a worker that settles during verification cancels recovery. Unmanaged, external-supervisor, embedded, disabled-respawn or unavailable-native-service instances remain report-only.

The accepted native recovery records and awaits the existing boot-lifecycle completion before shutdown watchdogs or teardown. That native reason survives forced process death, so a successor with another stuck worker within five minutes remains report-only. The existing consumed boot ID prevents a later generic shutdown deadline overwriting the native reason.

Native systemd capability is prepared before workers start: lazy dependency initialization otherwise calls Node's diagnostic-report API, which waits for the stuck worker and deadlocks recovery. Actual service/Node verification remains live at recovery time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses the archive FIFO, scoped archive worker, reconciliation WorkerTaskPool and Gateway process lifecycle. Schemas, canonical transcript bytes, retention and final archive-publication rules are unchanged. Whole-process death may leave an unreferenced staging artifact; no new orphan-cleanup policy is introduced. Existing best-effort boot-history persistence policy is preserved.

## Evidence

Final source and actual runtime build: `989b30680025e029885e77e6aeefb3c1cc7626a5`.

[Immutable evidence index, complete logs, drivers, receipts, hashes and limitations](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/README.md).

- **Permanent archive recovery:** real native fsync remains blocked through the unchanged 180-second budget and five-second grace. FIFO/native/staging custody remains held. The service replaces PID 629111 with 632652 without releasing the fault; both archive retries match exact canonical rows, retained history is readable and SQLite integrity passes.
- **Forced-death cooldown RED/GREEN:** the pre-repair production baseline kills its successor again 225.2 seconds after the first death and queues another service restart. Final head records the native planned-restart row durably while the old process is still alive. After its physical death, the successor holds a second permanent native fsync for 205.125 seconds without restarting, logs the five-minute report-only cooldown, and retains native custody and canonical rows. [Baseline failure](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-baseline/cooldown-successor.json), [pre-kill durable row](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/durable-native-recovery-before-kill.json), [successor result](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/cooldown-successor.json).
- **Permanent reconciliation recovery:** startup SQLite pread stays blocked, and the durable lease/canonical rows remain held without cleanup overlap. After physical death, PID 629566 is replaced by 632844; the dead lease is reclaimed, successor reconciliation and authenticated history rebuild the index, and canonical rows and SQLite integrity remain intact. A separate pre-fault credential migration restart is explicitly distinguished in the receipts.
- **Official stable upgrade:** verified npm `2026.10.6` creates two conversations/four canonical rows and non-default settings. Candidate Doctor succeeds. Both candidate boots retain every original JSON/compressed transcript byte and selected settings; authenticated history works, and a third conversation's two new rows survive another clean restart. [Stable package identity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-install/install.receipt.json), [upgrade/restart receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/upgrade-v2.receipt.json), [final settings/history/integrity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/candidate-restart-v2-integrity.json).
- The new ordering regression fails before the repair and passes after; all six runtime-unavailable cases pass. Scoped type-aware core lint, config-cli types, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent P0-P2 review of the final delta is scoped-clean, with its context/execution limitations retained. Earlier custody, retirement, FIFO, import-closure and service-recovery validation remains linked in the evidence index.
- Failed fixture admission, a lint prerequisite timeout, and the first upgrade comparison's null-prototype-object mismatch are retained and explained. The corrected upgrade comparison normalizes representation while still comparing every original byte; no product code or expected data was changed for that proof correction. Final native scenarios use unchanged production timeouts and never release injected faults to obtain a passing result.

The actual main merge conflict is resolved using exact current-main hook-fixture bytes; that fixture is no longer part of this PR's diff. The final cooldown repair adds 10 production lines and 48 test lines. Permanent recovery and its cooldown remain one coherent availability repair.

## Maintainer Decision

The contributor recommends bounded admission, retirement and verified-service recovery. Upstream acceptance of the fixed limits and automatic escalation remains outstanding: overload can be rejected and slow healthy work can be retired. This PR does not claim authority to grant that owner decision.

The incident's underlying memory-growth cause is not established by this availability repair. Final-head CI and ClawSweeper's verdict remain separate gates, not implied by evidence publication.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(plugins): let Gateway close after forced retirement settles
prs.body:
Fixes #181106

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown repeatedly failing after a plugin generation times out during hot-reload retirement, even after its cleanup has finished.

## User Impact

Later Gateway closes can complete once the retired plugin's work settles. Unfinished work remains awaited, and failed host cleanup prerequisites still block a clean close. No configuration changes or migration are required.

Drain budgets still use wall time, so arbitrary main-thread stalls can still force retirement. Current main already drains before replacement registration and yields between registrations; residual stall sensitivity is the accepted timing edge case for this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inspection release previously cached a bounded timeout report as retained resource custody. Final release now joins the instance's existing physical-disposal promise. Completed callback failures remain diagnostics; physical-disposal rejection remains retained. Setup cleanup stays under the cache owner, preserving admission closure and registry/setup/native-source cleanup order. Rolled-back instances are joined without duplicating construction diagnostics, and self-retirement still acknowledges without waiting on itself.

This removes the blanket timeout-to-retained classification and avoids adding retry state to the prepared runtime's resource and lifetime owners.

## Evidence

- **Red on main:** both new forced-retirement cases failed independently on `22338ef3220a6598bcf893e86018b1446c07ab63`, whose owning source was unchanged through fetched main `49e32cbda0c277b83bf3a77d2d618f7427ccec1c`. Real inspection acquisition → prepared generation retirement → timeout → physical cleanup settlement → process close failed with `PluginRuntimeCloseRetainedError` at `loader-runtime-load.ts:255–256`. The cases cover successful cleanup and a late callback failure, including a close attempt before settlement.
- Each baseline run used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.instance-cleanup.test.ts -t 'closes after forced retirement.*false' --maxWorkers=1` (then `true`) with the supported Node backend. Both exited 1 at the expected assertion; no live Gateway was involved.
- **Green:** 94/94 tests passed with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.instance-cleanup.test.ts src/plugins/registry-inspection-resources.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-cache.test.ts src/plugins/setup-registry.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` using the Node backend. Both new regressions pass; close remains pending before settlement and repeated close succeeds afterward. The unchanged `src/plugins/plugin-instance.test.ts` suite also passed all 34 cases in the preceding focused run.
- The preceding run exposed an existing Doctor discovery test's one-second registration poll (78/79 passed). It now waits for the fixture's existing disposal-start signal, raced against operation completion; the final run preserves all assertions and passes.
- Changed-file oxfmt and type-aware oxlint passed, as did `git diff --check` and normal commit hooks. Removing the unused `vi` import was the only edit after the final test run.
- Deslop completed. Exact numstat: production **+38/-20** (net +18), tests **+90/-27**, docs **+4/-2**. The production growth preserves the bounded observer contract while exposing existing physical completion to final owners; it adds no retry state or competing cleanup owner.
- Codex autoreview completed with one P2, declined after caller audit; no accepted findings. It proposed upgrading an already-started cache retirement. Here `acquireRegistryResources` creates a private cache and returns only registry/release; its last-claim finalizer is the sole retirement caller. CLI, update inspection, lifecycle leases, supplemental tool inspection, and Gateway metadata each own separate caches; `resetPluginCache` retires only the process cache. `inheritPluginNativeAdmissions` shares payload custody, not cache retirement. The current inspection caller always selects physical settlement on its first cache-retirement request; the earlier bounded retirement assumed by the finding has no supported entry point.

Fresh main `49e32cbda0c277b83bf3a77d2d618f7427ccec1c` was fetched by URL and merged without conflicts before push. All seven affected files were unchanged from the tested base.

Live Gateway/channel e2e, remote leases, broad local suites, and full local typechecks were skipped per maintainer policy. PR CI supplies broad validation.

prs.title: perf(infra): reuse immutable worker reply facts
prs.body:
**Status:** code review and exact-head CI are green, but the performance evidence is not an unqualified pass. The required third retained pair crossed the stated maximum-pause envelope (minor 75.704 ms versus 50 ms; major 173.254 ms versus 151.126 ms), and native/root survivor bytes rose in all three pairs (mean +0.561 MB; +22.05% against mean baseline). These are measured-window results, not profiler cleanup. Leave this PR open for the lead's acceptance decision; the 50% decoded-and-retained target is not established.

## What Problem This Solves

Session row reads clone already-immutable nested facts, and actor commit receipts carry a second pending-delivery payload that no consumer reads.

## User Impact

Less allocation when projecting resident session rows and publishing actor receipts, with the same session-list values and delivery behavior. No configuration, schema, migration, or authority changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replica already freezes retained entry facts. Row readers now own fresh outer row/entry objects while borrowing those frozen nested facts. Pending final delivery remains in its canonical entry postimage; the unused receipt-level copy is removed. Runtime production code is net −1 line, with no new cache or retained prepared objects.

The additional benchmark-only tooling measures this owner and attributes previously unsized worker-message envelopes through the existing message-metrics and admission owners. Attribution is opt-in, uses bounded labels, and records missing sizing explicitly. Its reserialization overhead is excluded from acceptance runs; serialized bytes are never presented as deserialized heap bytes. The complete diff adds 918 net benchmark-code lines, 268 net test lines, and 44 net documentation lines while deleting one net runtime-production line; the tooling growth supplies the requested reproducible attribution and owner measurement, not another production path.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement: compare owner work/allocation first, then concurrent baseline/candidate Gateway pairs with swapped CPU placement, matched rounds/resets, and separate allocation and five-minute live-retention profiles. Report absolute as well as relative differences, tail sample counts, maximum GC pauses, promotion per turn, and GC per unit of work. Opposite-sign deltas or baselines differing by more than 5× are inconclusive and require a third pair if gating. Small-owner changes qualify as simplifications only; the 50% retained-byte target is a goal, not a measured claim.

Two concurrent, swapped owner pairs are complete on Node 26.12.1. Each side performs 20,000 row reads and 20,000 receipt creations after 2,000 warmups, using 32 synthetic admitted replicas. Sampling includes collected objects at a 512-byte interval; timing/GC use a separate unprofiled pass. The shared guard did not interrupt either pair.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Mean paired delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total allocation B/row read | 28,914.86 → 11,843.82 | 28,901.62 → 11,850.91 | −17,060.87 B (−59.02%) |
| Allocation B/receipt | 14,440.25 → 488.35 | 14,445.58 → 500.87 | −13,948.30 B (−96.58%) |
| V8 serialized B/receipt, not heap | 63,037 → 50,079 | 63,037 → 50,079 | −12,958 B (−20.56%) |
| Read p95 µs (n=20,000/side/pair) | 27.682 → 6.760 | 29.865 → 7.281 | −21.753 µs (−75.60%) |
| Read p99 µs (n=20,000/side/pair) | 34.913 → 10.967 | 51.016 → 12.870 | −31.046 µs (−71.68%) |
| GC ms/20,000 reads | 10.772 → 6.483 | 11.645 → 5.413 | −5.261 ms (−46.67%) |
| Maximum GC pause ms (59 → 124 collections/pair) | 0.428024 → 0.152990 | 0.444378 → 0.192059 | Context; no major collections |

Row allocation profile samples: 900,514 → 408,638 and 900,282 → 408,956. Receipt profile samples: 76,685 → 16,089 and 76,883 → 16,630. Low-count GC pause percentiles are context only. All four row goldens are byte-identical; canonical receipt payloads have matching byte counts and SHA-256 digests. Mutable outer-row isolation and frozen nested ownership remain covered by the regression.

Measured source is baseline `9f89542dafed5af10322f0a4d3b5eb58b48f3eed` plus candidate runtime patch `2abd97738502a140399dd999bd0865f55462099e`. The runtime patch is unchanged at current PR head `3cc2374effb0de2a780a9afe59a20466ebd8801c`; range-diff and owner source hashes verify equivalence. Follow-up changes extend diagnostic attribution, fix benchmark types and native Worker flag inheritance, and snapshot completed cron history before benchmark cleanup. The measured driver stays pinned to the original workload plus these reviewed harness corrections; it is not a full-tree benchmark of the rebased PR head.

The isolated real-Gateway `sessions.list` correctness capture also passed: 20 filter/paging variants and 1,701 returned row instances have identical stable payload bytes, including property order, row order, and counts. Canonical UTF-8 JSON is 3,668,635 bytes, SHA-256 `2080b366f5a74a773cf9cfbc8948aa3d83bfc36d88ff1fa021f87a2bb8e947bd`. The raw captures differ only in 20 `payload.ts` timestamps, 20 isolated `payload.path` values, and 1,701 `sessions[].snapshotAt` timestamps per side. Only those fields were normalized; `presentSessionRow` explicitly stamps `snapshotAt` from the presentation clock. This is stable payload equivalence, not raw wire-byte identity. The two correctness captures ran sequentially under sandbox prep limits; their timing is excluded from performance evidence.

The corrected whole-Gateway allocation comparison passes its specified gates. Three valid five-minute retained pairs and a separate diagnostic attribution run are complete. Total live-survivor bytes fall by a mean 1.068 MB (2.28%), while native/root survivor bytes rise; the retained-phase pause envelope is not clean. The initial unequal-work allocation comparisons were discarded because the baseline-only wrapper disabled its config watcher. The first retained attempt was discarded because teardown cancelled a cron turn before the harness read history. Both harness defects were corrected and independently reviewed; all accepted runs keep both watchers active and validate completed cron outcomes before disabling the synthetic job.

<details>
<summary>Corrected Gateway allocation results and decision rules</summary>

## Corrected Gateway allocation pairs

Both pairs use Node 26.12.1, interleaved slot-A CPUs, swapped placement, and independent synthetic state. All four arms complete 20 measured cohorts, 80 foreground turns, 8 total / 4 measured resets, 20 successful subagent cohorts, 80 tool calls/results, and 10 cron runs. All exits are zero, guards empty, watcher startup valid, and sampling/capture drops zero. Diagnostic reserialization is disabled. MB means 1,000,000 bytes. Each cell gives baseline → candidate and sample counts; means are paired differences, not pooled quantiles.

| Metric | Pair 1 (n baseline / candidate) | Pair 2 (n baseline / candidate) | Mean absolute Δ | Mean relative Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Allocation MB/turn | 326.4357 → 288.3069 (n=49,480/43,696) | 330.6613 → 330.4059 (n=50,121/50,074) | -19.1921 | -5.88% |
| Promotion MB/turn | 70.2372 → 37.3784 (n=980/827) | 69.3553 → 68.4840 (n=1,016/1,045) | -16.8650 | -24.02% |
| Total GC ms/turn | 63.6795 → 50.3113 (n=1,019/856) | 63.7030 → 62.1795 (n=1,056/1,084) | -7.4458 | -11.69% |
| Loop p99 ms | 37.2900 → 36.1431 (n=14,310/14,430) | 38.8628 → 38.4369 (n=14,268/14,305) | -0.7864 | -2.09% |
| Minor GC p95 ms | 5.5980 → 5.4060 (n=941/798) | 5.4700 → 5.1500 (n=976/1,006) | -0.2560 | -4.64% |
| Minor GC p99 ms (context) | 9.0220 → 8.4460 (n=941/798) | 9.0220 → 7.8700 (n=976/1,006) | -0.8640 | -9.58% |
| Major GC s/min (context, inconclusive) | 0.3571 → 0.2498 (n=39/29) | 0.3305 → 0.3345 (n=40/39) | -0.0516 | -14.41% |
| Major GC p95 ms (context) | 68.6060 → 73.7260 (n=39/29) | 70.6540 → 71.1660 (n=40/39) | +2.8160 | +4.09% |
| Major GC p99 ms (context, inconclusive) | 83.4540 → 80.8940 (n=39/29) | 99.3260 → 157.6940 (n=40/39) | +27.9040 | +27.85% |
| Minor GC maximum ms (inconclusive; guard passes) | 9.9324 → 39.8264 (n=941/798) | 12.6694 → 10.6079 (n=976/1,006) | +13.9163 | +142.35% |
| Major / overall GC maximum ms (inconclusive; guard passes) | 83.2097 → 80.7848 (n=39/29) | 98.8361 → 157.0430 (n=40/39) | +27.8910 | +27.99% |

All primary gates improve in both pairs. The allocation result is −11.68% in pair 1 and −0.08% in pair 2; promotion is −46.78% and −1.26%. These large differences in effect size are not a causal production estimate. The changed owner is small relative to turn allocation, so acceptance rests on the independently proven owner saving and net-negative runtime simplification with no new cache.

Major-GC time has opposite signs (−0.107283 s/min, −30.04%; +0.004052 s/min, +1.23%). Under v5 it is context-only because counts are 39/29 and 40/39, so mark it INCONCLUSIVE rather than adverse; total GC/work carries the gate. Minor p99 is also context because not every side reaches 1,000 collections. Minor p95 and loop p99 have sufficient samples and improve in both pairs. No baseline disparity exceeds 5× for a gate metric, and no eligible gate has opposing signs; a third allocation pair is not required.

Maximum-pause guards pass: pair 1 overall 83.2097 → 80.7848 ms, pair 2 98.8361 → 157.0430 ms (candidate below 197.6721 ms guard). Minor maxima are 9.9324 → 39.8264 and 12.6694 → 10.6079 ms, all below their 50 ms guards. The maximum-pause deltas are opposite-signed: minor +29.8940 ms (+300.98%) then −2.0615 ms (−16.27%); major −2.4249 ms (−2.91%) then +58.2069 ms (+58.89%). Those comparative metrics are INCONCLUSIVE; only the specified maximum-pause guard applies, and it passes. Major p99 is also opposite-signed and context-only. Do not gate on a relative maximum dominated by a small baseline.

Foreign-worker message counts now have coverage on both sides: 40,098 → 38,228 in pair 1 and 37,493 → 38,042 in pair 2, per direction. This background polling variation is reported; no missing watcher remains. Explicit V8-deserialize input bytes are 68,120,235 → 68,005,185 and 68,023,775 → 68,100,324. Their deltas are −115,050 bytes (−0.169%) and +76,549 bytes (+0.113%): INCONCLUSIVE context, separate from allocated heap bytes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Three retained pairs, pause limits, and unresolved native/root retention</summary>

## Retained-survivor results

**Conclusion:** average total survivor bytes, promotion, total GC per foreground turn, and event-loop p99 improve across three valid pairs; minor p95 rises modestly. **The maximum-pause envelope is not clean:** pair 3 exceeds the stated minor and major maximum thresholds. Native/root survivor bytes also rise in every pair. These results do not establish the requested −50% decoded-and-retained target or an unqualified whole-Gateway performance pass. Lead acceptance is still required.

## Workload and validity

Three concurrent pairs used slot B, interleaved 16-CPU placements; pair 2 swapped pair 1, and pair 3 repeated pair 1. Every arm ran Node 26.12.1 with 20 measured + 2 warmup cohorts, 80 foreground turns, 8 total / 4 measured session resets, 20 successful subagent cohorts, and 80 tool calls/results. Successful measured cron runs were 10/10, 11/11, and 10/10; work matches within each pair. All six arm exits and three outer exits are zero; guard logs are empty. Every memory observation includes the foreign config watcher, without invalid-worker-argument/watcher failure signatures. Worker reserialization attribution is disabled for acceptance profiles.

Live-only profiles use 32,768-byte sampling, `includesCollectedObjects:false`, and final forced collection. They measure allocations made in the capture that survive its end, **not the full live heap**. Actual windows are 301,025/300,969 ms, 300,888/300,850 ms, and 301,048/301,033 ms. Raw tree self-byte totals match results, with zero unmapped samples. GC/promotion/loop use whole-soak windows ending before final forced collection. All diagnostic error/drop/clamp counters are zero.

## Primary metrics

MB is decimal. Delta means candidate minus baseline. Means are arithmetic means of the three paired absolute and relative deltas. Promotion, total GC, and loop p99 had opposite signs after two pairs, requiring pair 3 under v5.2; their decisions use the final absolute means. Counts are heap samples, main-isolate trace GC events for promotion, observer GC events for total GC, and observations for tails.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 2 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 3 baseline → candidate; delta | Mean paired absolute / relative delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live-survivor MB | 46.997864 → 46.713440; -0.284424 (-0.61%); n=1258/1254 | 46.899488 → 46.080816; -0.818672 (-1.75%); n=1268/1232 | 46.838800 → 44.739000; -2.099800 (-4.48%); n=1246/1193 | -1.067632 / -2.28% |
| Promotion MB/foreground turn | 68.709651 → 69.036266; +0.326614 (+0.48%); n=1025/1045 | 68.465713 → 33.086359; -35.379354 (-51.67%); n=1041/834 | 69.093952 → 32.020396; -37.073556 (-53.66%); n=1036/838 | -24.042099 / -34.95% |
| Total GC ms/foreground turn | 73.231393 → 74.012137; +0.780744 (+1.07%); n=1066/1088 | 73.006138 → 58.797614; -14.208524 (-19.46%); n=1082/863 | 74.880951 → 61.923656; -12.957294 (-17.30%); n=1078/867 | -8.795025 / -11.90% |
| Event-loop p99 ms | 40.927231 → 42.762239; +1.835008 (+4.48%); n=14164/14147 | 40.763391 → 38.535167; -2.228224 (-5.47%); n=14199/14321 | 42.958847 → 39.256063; -3.702784 (-8.62%); n=14148/14268 | -1.365333 / -3.20% |
| Minor GC p95 ms | 5.726000 → 5.982000; +0.256000 (+4.47%); n=984/1002 | 6.046000 → 6.558000; +0.512000 (+8.47%); n=1000/805 | 6.462000 → 6.270000; -0.192000 (-2.97%); n=994/809 | +0.192000 / +3.32% |
| Major GC seconds/minute (context) | 0.387477 → 0.383347; -0.004130 (-1.07%); n=41/43 | 0.373138 → 0.270498; -0.102640 (-27.51%); n=41/29 | 0.384465 → 0.283517; -0.100948 (-26.26%); n=42/29 | -0.069239 / -18.28% |

All loop p99 counts exceed 1,000 and minor p95 counts exceed 200. Minor counts change +1.83%, −19.50%, and −18.61%, so none uses the ≥20% reduced-count exemption. Minor p95 deltas are +0.256, +0.512, and −0.192 ms; absolute mean +0.192 ms is below adverse criteria. Major counts are 41/43, 41/29, and 42/29, all below 50; major time rate and percentiles remain context, with total GC carrying the gate.

## Maximum-pause measurements

| Pair / kind | Baseline max ms | Candidate max ms | Threshold max(50 ms, 2×baseline) | Collections baseline / candidate | Crossed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 / minor | 19.002910 | 37.050509 | 50.000000 | 984 / 1002 | No |
| 1 / major | 108.368467 | 77.225980 | 216.736934 | 41 / 43 | No |
| 2 / minor | 11.880965 | 11.594795 | 50.000000 | 1000 / 805 | No |
| 2 / major | 73.251064 | 78.538645 | 146.502128 | 41 / 29 | No |
| 3 / minor | 16.516299 | 75.704398 | 50.000000 | 994 / 809 | **Yes** |
| 3 / major | 75.562865 | 173.254369 | 151.125730 | 42 / 29 | **Yes** |

Pair 3 candidate minor max **75.704398 ms exceeds 50 ms**; major max **173.254369 ms exceeds 151.125730 ms**. They occurred within the main-isolate measured window. Candidate stdout whole-soak markers are lines 5871–10813, containing exactly 838 main collections (809 minor, 29 major). Line 6060 records major trace pause 173.113 ms at uptime 182,226 ms; line 8812 records minor trace pause 75.579 ms at 339,917 ms. Observer durations are slightly larger. First/last measured trace events occur at 180,062/468,840 ms. Neither long pause is final forced collection.

The literal v5.1 maximum threshold affects per-pause tail gate eligibility; it does not erase v5 sample minima or independently specify unconditional single-pause rejection. Minor p95 remains eligible and within average limits; major tails still lack sufficient samples. The evidence has improving primary averages but an unresolved maximum-pause risk requiring lead judgment. No valid pair is discarded or rerun to chase a better maximum.

## Retained allocation families

Families attribute allocation stacks, not retaining-object dominators. They may overlap; do not add them as disjoint totals. Native/root counts only direct-root native self bytes, excluding child JS subtrees. Missing stacks are unobserved, not zero. Percentile sample cutoffs do not apply to these byte totals.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 2 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 3 baseline → candidate; delta | Mean paired absolute / relative delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native/root survivor MB | 2.983560 → 3.103328; +0.119768 (+4.01%); n=86/89 | 1.932776 → 2.935104; +1.002328 (+51.86%); n=54/84 | 2.716944 → 3.277928; +0.560984 (+20.65%); n=78/95 | +0.561027 / +25.51% |
| Decoder subtree survivor MB | 0.306800 → 0.133384; -0.173416 (-56.52%); n=9/4 | 0.297136 → 0.164032; -0.133104 (-44.80%); n=9/5 | 0.165872 → 0.268248; +0.102376 (+61.72%); n=5/8 | -0.068048 / -13.20% |
| Row-facts subtree survivor MB | unobserved → unobserved; n=unobserved/unobserved | unobserved → 0.057384; n=unobserved/1 | unobserved → unobserved; n=unobserved/unobserved | unavailable |
| Freeze subtree survivor MB | 1.119080 → 1.082256; -0.036824 (-3.29%); n=3/2 | 1.180088 → 0.134144; -1.045944 (-88.63%); n=5/4 | 1.114488 → 1.147920; +0.033432 (+3.00%); n=3/4 | -0.349779 / -29.64% |

**Native/root retention rises in every pair:** mean +0.561027 MB, paired-relative mean +25.51%, or +22.05% relative to the mean baseline. Baselines differ less than 5× and signs agree; this is an adverse attribution signal, not v5.2 opposite-sign ambiguity. It remains materially relevant to the lane goal. The dominant `(V8 API)` bucket has no JS stack and cannot establish worker deserialization or retaining ownership exclusively. Its contextual classification follows the preregistered whole-survivor gate and uncertain provenance, not sparse-sample dismissal.

Decoder and freeze deltas have opposite signs across three pairs, so their relative means do not prove uniform improvement. Freeze totals are sensitive to one 1,048,616-byte `add` allocation under `freezeTrustedJsonSnapshot`, present in both pair-1 arms and pair-2 baseline but absent in pair-2 candidate. Row-facts appears only in pair-2 candidate (57,384 bytes / one sample), preventing comparison against an unobserved baseline. **The −50% decoded-and-retained target is not established.**

## Supplemental tails

Per-kind p99 and mixed all-GC tails remain visible below. The mixed distribution is supplementary to preregistered per-kind tails and total-GC cost, not a newly added gate; it combines changing collection-type proportions. Every cell has its sample count. p99 needs ≥1,000 per side; p95 needs ≥200.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 2 baseline → candidate; delta | Pair 3 baseline → candidate; delta | Mean paired absolute / relative delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Minor GC p99 ms | 7.838000 → 9.406000; +1.568000 (+20.01%); n=984/1002 | 8.574000 → 8.830000; +0.256000 (+2.99%); n=1000/805 | 9.662000 → 8.574000; -1.088000 (-11.26%); n=994/809 | +0.245333 / +3.91% |
| Major GC p95 ms | 72.702000 → 64.766000; -7.936000 (-10.92%); n=41/43 | 69.630000 → 71.678000; +2.048000 (+2.94%); n=41/29 | 70.142000 → 79.870000; +9.728000 (+13.87%); n=42/29 | +1.280000 / +1.96% |
| Major GC p99 ms | 108.542000 → 77.310000; -31.232000 (-28.77%); n=41/43 | 73.726000 → 78.846000; +5.120000 (+6.94%); n=41/29 | 75.774000 → 174.078000; +98.304000 (+129.73%); n=42/29 | +24.064000 / +35.97% |
| All-GC mixed p95 ms | 7.646000 → 9.342000; +1.696000 (+22.18%); n=1066/1088 | 8.510000 → 7.614000; -0.896000 (-10.53%); n=1082/863 | 9.150000 → 8.030000; -1.120000 (-12.24%); n=1078/867 | -0.106667 / -0.20% |
| All-GC mixed p99 ms | 53.758000 → 48.894000; -4.864000 (-9.05%); n=1066/1088 | 53.758000 → 48.126000; -5.632000 (-10.48%); n=1082/863 | 51.454000 → 47.870000; -3.584000 (-6.97%); n=1078/867 | -4.693333 / -8.83% |

Minor p99 lacks ≥1,000 observations on both sides in every pair. Major p95/p99 lack both major-count and percentile minima. Mixed all-GC p95 is sample-eligible but supplementary, with conflicting paired signs. Mixed all-GC p99 is sample-eligible only in pair 1; candidate counts are 863/867 in pairs 2/3. Do not present them as fully qualified three-pair percentile gates.

## Provenance and limits

Inputs are `.local/buf-l/evidence/gateway-retained-v3-pair-{1,2,3}/`. All source-hash files are byte-identical across pairs. Three production session-actor owners and three preload/instrumentation files match the local lane source. Measured driver SHA-256 is `0472a839bbc2a31c8f13f00ccf692a2bb37caf95f99192b4954848967fccd666`, copied to `.local/buf-l/evidence/runners/measured-transcript-broadcast-measure.ts`. Inspected differences from rebased driver add unused authority/session-event benchmark modes and metadata; retained workload/cron correction agree. This is production-patch-equivalent evidence on a pinned base/candidate experiment, not an exact-current-main whole-tree benchmark.

Original allocation pairs were discarded for baseline-only watcher failure; retained-v2 was discarded for cron teardown validation failure. Only corrected allocation-v2 and retained-v3 enter acceptance. Serialized input/reserialization bytes are not deserialized heap bytes and do not replace profile evidence. Final acceptance belongs to the lead; the native-retention rise and maximum-pause crossings preclude an unqualified performance recommendation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Diagnostic worker-message attribution and sizing limits</summary>

## Worker-message attribution

Separate diagnostic baseline run, Node 26.12.1: 20 measured cohorts / 80 foreground turns, 8 total resets, 10 successful cron runs, exit 0. All four source hooks loaded; both overflow counters are zero. One isolated guard warning did not interrupt the run. Messages, known bytes, and unmeasured counts reconcile exactly with the existing worker metrics. The instrumented capture is excluded from allocation, retention, promotion, GC, and latency acceptance.

MB below means decimal **V8 reserialized envelope estimates**, including transferred buffer contents. These are not deserialized heap bytes. The foreground-turn denominator also contains subagent and cron work.

| Inbound category | Messages | Serialized MB | MB/foreground turn | Share of sized bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Task replies | 6,120 | 304.364 | 3.805 | 56.93% |
| Authority | 25,974 | 203.010 | 2.538 | 37.97% |
| SQLite replies | 6,124 | 19.656 | 0.246 | 3.68% |
| Other | 38,022 | 7.061 | 0.088 | 1.32% |
| All inbound | 81,119 | 534.618 | 6.683 | 100% |

The following task drilldown overlaps the task-reply row; it must not be added to transport totals. Its complete totals match exactly: 6,120 replies and 304,364,308 bytes, all validated outcomes `ok`.

| Worker / operation | Replies | Serialized MB | MB/foreground turn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Provider prompt state / `task` | 365 | 71.915 | 0.899 |
| Session transcript / `model-context` | 165 | 31.217 | 0.390 |
| Session transcript / `session-exact-entries` | 822 | 13.544 | 0.169 |
| Session transcript / `task` | 1,187 | 8.159 | 0.102 |
| Session transcript / `history-page` | 1,198 | 4.783 | 0.060 |
| Discovery / `task` | 51 | 1.753 | 0.022 |
| Session transcript / `session-row-facts` | 242 | 0.463 | 0.006 |

Hydration is 32.14% of all sized inbound bytes. The foreign-worker `other` subgroup has 37,962 messages but only 5.717 MB. Authority includes 1,265 committed actor receipts / 91.504 MB; `appendTranscriptEvent` contributes 1,085 / 87.023 MB. Overlapping entry sections total 50.455 MB for 2,730 authority snapshots and 23.396 MB for 1,265 postimages. Skills snapshots and system-prompt reports account for approximately 88.1% of each entry section. These section estimates are included in the envelopes, not extra traffic.

Sizing covers 78,221/81,119 inbound messages (96.43%), versus 17,625 with preexisting known payload lengths. Remaining gaps: 1,100 serialization failures (1,097 admission messages) and 1,798 unavailable values. Outbound sizing is 8,065/54,060 messages, with 6,396 failures and 39,599 unavailable values; outgoing foreign values remain untouched. `task` is a bounded fallback label. Explicit main-isolate `v8.deserialize` separately observes 7,400 calls / 68.081 MB of input (0.851 MB/foreground turn); it excludes native MessagePort structured-clone decoding and overlaps transport payloads.

Source-backed retention ownership: hydration feeds the bounded transcript replica/context; authority admissions and committed postimages feed actor replicas; row facts feed Gateway row projections; catalog hotspots map to revision-scoped entry-wrapper arrays. Provider-prompt replies already contain transferable encoded bodies. Their serialized size cannot be equated with object churn. This capture does not establish per-operation decoded-heap totals or a 50% retained-byte reduction.

</details>

Focused checks completed:

- `src/config/sessions/session-actor-replica.test.ts`: 15 tests; the added regression fails on baseline and passes with the change.
- `src/config/sessions/session-actor-receipt.test.ts` and `session-actor-worker.test.ts`: 23 tests; `src/gateway/session-row-projection.actor.test.ts`: 2 tests.
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`: 22 tests. `gateway-bench-profile.test.ts`: 14 tests after the final Worker-inheritance regression was added.
- Targeted `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreviews for the original change, attribution follow-up, and Worker-inheritance fix: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Extended real-worker attribution coverage: `gateway-bench-profile.test.ts`, 14/14 including the real-Worker regression (red before the inheritance fix, green after); scoped script/test lint and formatting passed.
- Exact-head CI for `3cc2374effb0de2a780a9afe59a20466ebd8801c` is fully green: [run 39892645394](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892645394), including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Across the PR there are 71 successful checks, 52 skips, one neutral result, and no failed or pending checks. Initial benchmark type errors were fixed. A previous head's unrelated hook-test TS2353 matched scheduled-main run 39890895258 exactly; the final rebase includes main's repair. No CI reruns were requested.
- The final cron-cleanup ordering correction passed scoped lint/format and fresh independent P0–P2 review. The real retained pair that reproduced cleanup cancellation was discarded; all three corrected pairs complete successfully without filtering any failed history.
- ClawSweeper found no concrete defect in the original runtime change; it correctly identified the pending Gateway evidence. The original change, attribution follow-up, Worker-inheritance fix, and cron-cleanup fix each received an independent clean review.

No Testbox lease or broad local suite was run. PR CI supplies the broad checks.

## Production follow-through and limits

After deployment, compare owner stack allocation and promotion per completed turn at similar traffic and reset cadence. The expected direct signal is less `readSessionActorRowFacts` cloning and less duplicate pending-delivery receipt serialization. Watch total GC per turn, major-GC seconds/minute, event-loop p99 with sample counts, and the post-GC heap floor. Whole-Gateway means from two noisy pairs are not a production forecast.

Native/root allocation has no JavaScript operation stack, and a sampling profile does not identify retaining paths. Message serialization counters cannot fill that gap. Actor replicas retain immutable facts; transcript contexts, Gateway row-fact maps, and revision-scoped catalog snapshots have separate retention owners. This change does not claim to remove all of those sources or halve decoded-and-retained bytes.

Leave this PR open for the lead's acceptance decision. Green CI does not resolve the measured pause-envelope and native-survivor concerns.
