prs.title: fix(slack): keep progress updating after native streams expire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack native progress can freeze or look failed after Slack expires a stream while the agent continues working. Later progress and the final answer can then fail or arrive separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a bounded projection of the stream from its first append. After an explicit `message_not_in_streaming_state` rejection with a known timestamp, use `chat.update` on that same message for later progress, final text and metadata, following the [Slack SDK recovery guidance](https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/pull/2611).

The existing scoped writer and native Stop handling remain authoritative. Ambiguous writes are not replayed. If a full-message projection cannot fit, or a definitive editing rejection prevents recovery, only the undelivered tail uses ordinary chunked delivery. Successful fallback retires its retained projection so cleanup cannot replay it onto the original card.

`chat.update` cannot retain custom username/avatar overrides. For customized streams, explicit expiry instead retires the stream and sends only its unacknowledged tail through the existing identity-aware sender.

## User Impact

Progress and eligible final replies continue on the existing message after expiry. Task state, narration order, details, outputs and source links remain available. Recovered task details/outputs use plain rich text; embedded Markdown is not interpreted. Custom authorship, cancellation and existing delivery policy are preserved. No new option or default is introduced.

## Evidence

Current head: `6dce715c8478e7d62c98aa31a74074f8dea0164b`.

- Ordinary merge of fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa`; prior head `fe91f0cf4045cea136254caed46f893c923a8813` remains the first parent. No force push. The production `streaming.ts` and `streaming-projection.ts` bytes remain unchanged from that previously reviewed head.
- The two trace-test conflicts preserve main's shared successful acknowledgement and `wirePayloads`, plus the one-shot append rejection and `recoveryTraceParams` controls. **163 tests across the same three Slack files passed** with the native wrapper, Node24.22.1, a dedicated transform cache, one worker, and an independently owned frozen-lockfile install.
- Touched-file type-aware lint (including official Plugin SDK declaration preparation), formatting, `git diff --check`, and outgoing-content Gitleaks pass.
- Fresh AutoReview at P0-P2 found no actionable defect in the patch-bearing pass. Its context-only status passes do not independently certify unseen code. No second review was run for a cleaner result.
- Current-head CI is pending; prior-head CI remains historical evidence only.
- Landing note: upstream main was `cc16d8d655332a71b13bd505c0b738de87ecd6bd` at fetch. This repair intentionally integrates the measured conflict set against fixed main228b5e9e; later main advancement is not repeatedly folded into this branch.

### Real Slack transport evidence

The earlier live proof executed compiled production stream/client owners from measured revision `2fec06eb352ffb4fc89178b5130aa594c7c1a4d0`, real Slack SDK8.0.0 and installed public OpenClaw SDK modules. API responses were not mocked. A separate `chat.stopStream` closed only each synthetic server-side test stream, leaving the SDK object active so its next real append received the expiry rejection.

| Measured owner | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline `4d7a33874` | Start and external stop succeed; append receives expiry rejection; rejected tail absent on readback |
| Candidate `2fec06eb` | Same rejection followed by successful same-message progress update, final answer and complete task, then final metadata |

Independent native-CLI readback verified the expected bot, same message timestamp, complete tasks, one acknowledged prefix, one final answer and retained final metadata. Task details, outputs and source links survived recovery; executed bundle hashes matched after the run. Only synthetic content was used.

That is historical evidence for the declared measured default-identity recovery path, supported by source comparison and later owner/dispatch regressions. It is not a fresh live run on this integrated head, a measurement of undocumented natural-expiry timing, or screenshot-based rendering proof. The later custom-identity branch has focused production-owner and dispatch proof; it deliberately avoids `chat.update`. No employee plugin, Gateway, channel or authentication configuration was changed.

prs.title: feat(exec): save command output for post-failure diagnosis
prs.body:
Related: #176116

## What Problem This Solves

Failed or timed-out shell commands can lose their diagnostic output when bounded process results expire or the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

Gateway-hosted `exec` can opt into `saveOutput: true` and return a workspace log path for later inspection. Saving is off by default. The log retains sanitized stdout/stderr up to the first 2 MiB, survives process-result eviction and Gateway restart, and reports capture failures without preventing command execution.

The path precedes large results so it survives the model-visible persistence cap. Timeout, exit status, approvals and completion routing retain their existing owners. Unsupported sandbox/node saving is rejected before launch. The irreversible-loss warning remains when the retained file does not cover discarded in-memory output.

## Scope and Tradeoffs

This proposes the explicit workspace-artifact stage of #176116. Files require manual cleanup: there is no automatic expiry or aggregate quota. Explicit saving also writes files during incognito sessions. These lifetime/storage/incognito choices still need maintainer product acceptance. Logs do not recover running processes or promise durability across power loss.

## CI Repair

- Integrated main `292ca7a1f`, including the upstream Custodian history-fixture fix [#177988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177988). The previously failed onboarding locale test had no default `openclaw.chat.history` response. No UI assertion or test timeout is changed here.
- Added two exact-rule-ID `nosemgrep` annotations to the existing trusted-host `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` reads. Caller overrides are normalized and rejected before this block; the reads retain host-owned Git policy. These are explicit false-positive exceptions, not a runtime security fix. The global detector correction remains with [#176328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176328); no rulepack, workflow or ignore list is changed here.
- Added a real exec rejection test for canonical and padded lowercase caller Git-config keys with `saveOutput`, checking that neither the command marker nor an output artifact is created.

## Evidence

Windows / Node 26.10.0, with OpenGrep 1.30.2 running under WSL:

- Actual scanner reproduction: two findings before annotation, zero afterward; `--disable-nosem` still reports the original two. Both dangerous sanitizer-override controls remain detected. The unchanged full rulepack scans all 14 feature production TypeScript files with zero findings/errors.
- Production core and agents-tools test typechecks, focused type-aware lint, formatting, the 19-source line-cap ratchet and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Independent canonical autoreview of the two-file repair, with complete relevant sources supplied, found no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is static review, separate from scanner/test execution.

- The previously failing onboarding locale E2E passes locally (one actual Chromium test, unchanged assertions), using the official matching Headless Shell. Initial setup was interrupted during cold compilation; that attempt is not counted as proof.
- All 11 saved-output cases pass, including the new rejection-before-launch case. The real Git partial-clone/host-policy case also passes: 12 cases across two files, with five unrelated GitHub identity cases filtered by the selected test-name pattern. Both Vitest shards completed successfully.

The previous integration head `128ef4f` passed 62 cases across saved output, notifications, process registry and cancellation. Prior production Gateway proof is pinned to `923ef07ad`: actual agent/tool execution retained 250,042 bytes after a nonzero exit, retained timeout output, and read both files after Gateway restart. That proof used an isolated Gateway and deterministic loopback provider, not a live model; it is not new exact-head Gateway proof.

Before the conflict refresh, head `7647a2446f36e7e4f1979c2b826d33d9be72a032` had the following CI evidence. [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39369714233) completed successfully: 58 jobs passed and 28 were scope-skipped, including all three UI E2E shards, production/test types, lint and baseline checks. The [OpenGrep PR-diff scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39369714260/job/118454599811) also passed. Required `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses are successful. This is CI clearance, not maintainer approval or a merged PR.

## Conflict Refresh

Conflict-integration head: `72de4acb50cd8605433a52f52f77663950fe88f4`. Merged main `1c787f912131cd0440db781a74330c538359c7db` to resolve four content conflicts. The resolution preserves main's `resolveExecHost` entrypoint, secret-egress bindings, deadline-bearing structured `followUp`, diagnostics formatting, and updated continuation tests, while retaining the saved-path/capping regression and output-log fields. The capture-file implementation is unchanged.

The four conflict files pass syntax checks under Node 26.12.1; the candidate diff passes whitespace checks. Canonical independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the supplied staged diff. This was static diff review: the metadata-only chunks do not prove runtime behavior, unchanged source was not supplied to the reviewer, and it ran no tests. This source-only worktree has no dependency installation, so refreshed-head type/lint/test proof was delegated to PR CI; subsequent results are recorded below, with each result tied to its own head. Prior-head Gateway evidence remains identified above; no new Gateway run is claimed for this refresh.

Follow-up head `3d05b09d1e6df4c996d16a55df85933d1ae1e1cf` repaired those two findings. The first refreshed-head CI run exposed a retained test import from the retired heartbeat completion path and an unused max-lines disable after the runtime file became shorter. Current published head: `eade44adbc4f5f8c539f933ff34608a5848d7d4b`. prs.title: fix(ui): Enter in a new chat silently does nothing while the session setup is still loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a new chat, pressing Enter (or Start) in the first moments after the composer appears can do nothing at all — the text stays in the box, the Start button still looks enabled, and no message, error, or explanation appears — while the page is still restoring the last session setup or refreshing agent defaults.

## User Impact

User impact: while a new chat is not ready to start, the composer shows why ("Restoring your last session setup…" or "Refreshing agent defaults…") and the Start button is visibly disabled; the text stays editable, and Enter or Start sends it as soon as preparation finishes. A submit attempt never silently disappears.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new-session submit owner already rejects a start while agent defaults or saved model preferences are being prepared, but its explanation was bound to the single rejected attempt and vanished as soon as that gate changed or cleared, and the composer exempted reasoned gates from native disabling, so Start kept its enabled look. The composer now shows the current gate's reason for as long as it applies and uses native disabling with the existing muted style. The attempt-bound tracker, its terminal notification callback, and the special blocked-button styling are removed. No queueing, protocol, config, persistence, or cancellation change.

## Evidence

- Live, real Gateway with a built-in and a Codex agent: opening a new chat and pressing Enter immediately after the composer appeared dropped the message 4 of 4 times on `main` with no explanation in 3 of 4 and an enabled-looking Start in 2 of 4; with this change all 4 showed the reason ("Restoring your last session setup…" / "Refreshing agent defaults…") with Start disabled, and the next Enter sent each message. Earlier timing probe on `main`: the Codex agent dropped Enter at 0 ms and 300 ms after the composer appeared and accepted it from 600 ms.
- Browser regression (`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.early-submit.e2e.test.ts`, mocked Gateway holding `agents.list` / `models.list`): real composer, native paste+Enter and Start click during the blocked window; checks the visible reason, preserved text, zero accidental sessions, then exactly one creation with the exact message after release. Fails on the original production code (no explanation), passes with the fix; with the existing draft-handoff and config/startup e2e files, 10 passed. Unit: 147 passed across the composer, submit gates, native terminal start, command-palette attachments, and submission flow.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` pass. Autoreview (Codex): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Production +5/-30.

After (same moment — reason shown, Start disabled):

prs.title: fix(slack): report silent receiver processing failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack event admission fails, the wrapped receivers suppress the processing-error diagnostic. Socket Mode leaves the event unacknowledged without that diagnostic; HTTP reports only a generic acknowledgement timeout.

## User Impact

Operators get an immediate `Slack receiver event processing failed` message for either transport. The fixed message omits event and error details. Acknowledgement behavior remains unchanged; this change does not recover failed events.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both wrapped receivers replace Bolt's default processing-error handler. A shared handler now logs the fixed message and returns the same `false` value as before.

## Evidence

- Against the previous implementation, the new interop tests produced **26 passes and three expected diagnostic failures**. With this change, **50 tests passed**: 29 interop, 19 ingress and 2 startup-cleanup tests.
- Local listener probes using durable admission and a synthetic queue found no processing diagnostic on main and one per failed transport with the change. HTTP returned an empty 404 after about three seconds, then an empty 200 for a successful control. Socket acknowledgement counts were zero for the failure and one for the control. No synthetic canary appeared in the captured output.
- The refreshed-head probe used signed buffered HTTP input and an invoked Socket listener, not a running network receiver or Slack service. Earlier loopback HTTP/WebSocket proof compared baseline `6487c6e6` with old head `1f53ee44` using an older dependency graph; it does not establish wire behavior for the refreshed head.
- Formatting passed for both changed files. A targeted strict TypeScript check passed for both changed files and their imported source, using the repository’s normal compiler wrapper in a self-contained checkout. Full-repository typechecking and hosted CI are still unverified.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop model fallback when native threads are active
prs.body:
Fixes #181046

Related: #176177 (broader change that also includes this typed error; it can drop that hunk after this lands)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary model fallback when a Codex thread is still claimed by active work and a policy change needs to release it.

## User Impact

OpenClaw preserves the thread and stops the fallback chain instead of attempting another model against the same busy thread. Wait for or stop the active work before retrying. The actionable diagnostic remains available under the existing error-detail settings; this change does not add public channel copy. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing global `AgentHarnessPreflightError` contract at the refusal producer, as the fallback owner already treats it as a coordination failure. Apply the same classification to the session-retirement sibling and remove manual adoption's duplicate plain-error check so its existing typed authority check owns the refusal. The warm-thread and retirement messages are unchanged; adoption retains the canonical wait-for-completion guidance.

Thanks to @Stronggenetics for the typed-error idea in #176177. This separates that narrow correction from its broader native-tool catalog changes, following the coordination-error approach in #179347.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation on main `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2`: `thread-lifecycle-warm.ts:215` throws an ordinary `Error`; the fallback runner advances unknown failures but stops global harness preflight errors.
- The real warm-thread lifecycle regression requires an unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError`, the original message, unchanged binding, and successful reuse under the original policy. Existing core fallback tests own the one-attempt/no-fallback contract for this public error type. Adoption and session-retirement cases now require typed refusals too.
- **Local execution gap:** host Node 26.12.0 is below the required 26.12.1, so `pnpm install` was refused. Per maintainer policy, local tests (including red/green runs), lint, formatting, and typecheck are deferred to PR CI. No local passing-test or timing claim. Live Gateway/channel e2e was skipped per maintainer policy.
- `git diff --check` passes. Simplification removed a duplicate claim check without adding new error classes, codes, fallback policy, or state. Exact numstat: production +9/-9 (net 0), tests +11/-3, docs +5/-0.
- Independent Codex branch autoreview through P2 completed `scoped-clean`: no actionable findings. This is static review, not runtime proof.
- Merged fresh main `08b5a12ddd5173d2ef5e3e4668c94f748c77efb5` without conflicts. The corrected patch is unchanged after integration; current head is `498bb5772caa1fc09dadcf0d4103465a1599a763`. Fresh full-candidate P0–P2 autoreview is `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings.

- Initial-head CI (`b96e5b6`) passed the composed lifecycle-to-fallback regression (96 ms) and the adoption/retirement suites, but rejected its direct core import from an extension test. The follow-up keeps the regression on the public preflight contract; production is unchanged. The failed boundary job is [120203614256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888765208/job/120203614256).
- Review scope: main already returns generic copy for this ordinary ownership error when external error details are disabled (`agent-runner-failure-reply.ts` and `renderCodexAppServerFailureCopy`). Curated non-verbose channel copy is a separate improvement; this PR preserves the existing diagnostic-disclosure behavior while fixing fallback classification.
- **Current-head CI is green:** [run 39891710031](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891710031) completed successfully on `498bb5772caa1fc09dadcf0d4103465a1599a763` (28 successful jobs, 29 skipped). Lint, formatting, production/test types, boundary checks, and the CI gate pass. All 110 cases in the three changed suites pass; key CI case timings are 53 ms (warm refusal/reuse), 131 ms (claimed manual adoption), and 22 ms (retirement refusal). No local wall-time measurement is claimed under the host policy.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): separate the message_tool_only reply decision from its delivery path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `message_tool_only` chats, an agent must call `message(action=send)` for a visible text reply to reach the user; its ordinary final answer is private. The existing prompt mixed that delivery mechanism into the decision about whether to reply:

> If no visible group response is needed, do not call message(action=send). Your normal final answer stays private...

On a production gateway, 185 of 193 long `source-reply/private-final` warnings (96%) came from turns that called no tools even though the resolved delivery mode and prompt were correct. The wording made the “whether to reply” gate and “how to deliver it” rule easy to conflate.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared helper now separates those concerns for group, channel, and direct surfaces:

- **Mechanism:** `message(action=send)` is the only visible text-reply path; reactions and other non-text message actions remain valid visible outcomes, while a final answer reaches nobody.
- **Decision gate:** if no text reply is needed, use an appropriate non-text action when warranted or end the turn; if a text reply is needed, send it before ending.

Group prompts still end on the selectivity instruction. An earlier ordering ended on “deliver it” and increased ambient replies in weaker models; the final ordering retains the delivery clarification while preserving the no-reply control.

The change is scoped to `message_tool_only`. Automatic-delivery prompts remain byte-identical.

## User Impact

The text-delivery contract becomes explicit and consistent across direct, group, and channel prompts without changing routing or transport behavior. Models still receive the existing instruction to react or stay quiet when a text response is unnecessary. The exact-head wording explicitly keeps reaction-only outcomes actionable instead of turning every no-text decision into an immediate exit.

The measured benefit depends on the surrounding harness. An isolated wording A/B improved delivery substantially; the production Codex path was already saturated by separate harness-level guidance and showed no additional gain. This PR therefore improves clarity and consistency while preserving behavior on the already-correct Codex path.

## Evidence

### Field signal

The production gateway recorded 193 long private-final warnings; 185 (96%) came from zero-tool turns. That establishes the user-visible failure boundary: substantive final text existed, but no `message` call delivered it.

### Isolated wording A/B

`scripts/dev/message-tool-only-prompt-live-proof.ts` isolates the changed chat-context wording while exposing the production message-tool descriptor. Across 600 real-model turns per run:

| Prompt | Reply-required visible delivery | Ambient sends |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline → first draft | 63% → 78% (p=0.001) | 20% → 31% (p=0.037) |
| Baseline → shipped ordering | 63% → 80% (p<0.001) | 21% → 19% (p=0.638) |
| Independent replication | 62% → 79% (p<0.001) | 18% → 23% (p=0.191) |

The first draft’s significant ambient increase is why a regression test pins the final ordering. GPT-4.1 direct delivery moved from 0/20 to 20/20; GPT-4o-mini remained 0/20, so the result is not presented as universal.

### Production Codex path

`scripts/dev/message-tool-only-codex-app-server-proof.ts` drives the real embedded Codex app-server attempt and production dynamic-tool bridge. The earlier full-turn run measured 120 real turns with 0 errors under the prior counter:

- reply-required delivery: 40/40 baseline and 40/40 patched;
- ambient sends: 0/20 baseline and 0/20 patched;
- all 80 message invocations completed with `deliveryStatus: "sent"` at the embedded run’s production settle point.

That null result is important: Codex’s separate harness-level visible-reply guidance already saturated this path, so this PR does not claim an additional Codex delivery-rate gain.

The proof harness now also:

- defaults the baseline argument to immutable pre-fix commit `3dd3003f49ce71f38c0ecf84dbdbc95023498a69` rather than moving `origin/main`;
- prints both resolved commit identities before credential preflight and fails if they coincide;
- passes the production `currentInboundContext` field into the embedded runner;
- verifies those bytes reach the actual Codex `turn/start` input;
- reports exact baseline/patched commits and context digests; and
- fails when the two rendered prompt arms are identical;
- scores delivery through the production current-source route predicate;
- requires the `internal-ui` source sink, a settled delivery receipt, and terminal intent; and
- runs startup self-checks that reject both a successful off-target send and a non-final progress send.
- encloses auth-file creation and client startup in unconditional cleanup guards, so startup failures cannot leave temporary credential directories behind.

The corrected harness was not rerun on this head because no model credential was available to the test environment. The previous 40/40 result is retained only as historical full-turn evidence; it is not represented as exact-head validation of the new classifier.

### Validation

- Focused prompt and message-tool suites: 252/252 on the current upstream merge.
- Credential-free proof startup: pass, including the exact pinned baseline identity plus canonical, off-target, and non-terminal classifier cases.
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check`: pass; all seven generated fixtures are current.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: pass after a frozen-lockfile refresh, including core and core-test typechecks, scripts typecheck, core/scripts lint, prompt drift, boundaries, and all repository guards.
- Script erasability, formatting, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Current head: `2d9528c6386b31d01548c6cbf19b3f82d5434818` (GPG-signed).

### Limitation

The evidence does not include post-deployment warning-rate measurement on live user traffic or a real Telegram/Discord wire send. The production Codex run settles at the embedded runtime’s `internal-ui` source-reply sink; it does not exercise an external channel adapter.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): avoid redundant freshness probes on admitted databases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite's pre-schema setup probes `page_count` even after schema admission has already established that the file is nonempty. The probe cannot enable incremental auto-vacuum on those files.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. SQLite opens avoid a redundant statement when existing admission already proves that the file is nonempty. Fresh-file initialization and existing auto-vacuum modes are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the admission owner's existing, non-refreshing lookup to skip that probe when retained facts contain a positive user version, a table, or a view. Missing or empty facts keep the native probe and fresh-file initialization. No new cache, schema, connection setting, checkpoint policy, or admission exchange is introduced. Existing FULL auto-vacuum mode remains unchanged.

## Acceptance rule (recorded before measurements)

- Flow: isolated Gateway boot, same-fixture restart, idle and both shutdowns, plus warmed turns over the frozen v3.1.4 real-transport workload. Baseline is `9c29902212c54ebcfbc73324043af3923aa42f2f`; candidate is this PR's exact head.
- Metric: successfully executed SQL statements, worker requests, and main-thread SQL. Count native executions, excluding prepares, and split compound exec calls.
- Samples: one alternating baseline/candidate pair, as approved for this bounded cut. Keep boot and restart separate from warm turns; report each count with n=1 and no statistical or latency claim.
- Win: remove the redundant nonempty-file freshness probes (s44 attribution predicts up to seven per workload), with no additional requests or main-thread work from this change. Fresh-file initialization and persisted auto-vacuum modes must hold.
- Regression: any new target-path SQL/request, any warm-path increase attributable to this patch, or changed persistence/admission behavior is a stop. Attribute unrelated background-count variation explicitly. No wall-clock or CPU improvement is claimed from these samples.

## Evidence

Independent Codex review completed with no actionable findings. Production delta: +10 lines; test delta: +38 lines. The small branch is necessary to retain fresh-file initialization while removing unnecessary work from admitted opens.

### Validation

- Baseline regression fails with exactly one redundant probe; candidate passes. WAL, reclamation, checkpoint-tick and schema-admission suites: 94 passed, seven existing skips. Fresh-file initialization and existing FULL mode/data across reopen pass.
- Frozen v3.1.4 pair: both full real-Gateway workloads pass, including boot, ten warm turns, idle, compaction, restart and both shutdowns. All 36 frozen hashes verified. One sample per arm for full/phase counts; warm statistics use ten causal turns per arm. Nearest-rank p95; no latency or CPU claim.

| Count | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Target freshness probes | 8 | 1 |
| Target probes on MAIN | 2 | 0 |
| All PRAGMA statements | 233 | 227 |
| Whole SQL | 2,936 | 2,957 |
| Whole requests | 795 | 799 |
| Whole MAIN SQL | 98 | 95 |
| Warm causal SQL median [range]; p95 | 45 [44–48]; 48 | 45 [44–48]; 48 |
| Warm causal requests median [range]; p95 | 11 [10–12]; 12 | 11 [10–12]; 12 |
| Warm causal MAIN | 0 | 0 |

The seven removed probes are boot 2→0, initial connect 2→1, and restart boot 4→0. The remaining probe initializes the fresh agent; the independent integrity probe also remains. This proves a target-family saving, not a whole-workload SQL reduction.

The coordinator accepted the raw-cell movements as background-placement scatter: background `installStatusTracking` adds 30 statements in the restart-first-turn window (temporary transcript-index status/trigger setup). Restart-first-turn causal work is identical at 124 SQL / 39 requests; background SQL is 35→64. Control-plane raw SQL is 7→18 (+157.1%), consisting of unchanged history-page work, seven projection statements and four statements from the preceding turn. Raw warm SQL moves beyond 20% in turn 3 (−24.6%), turn 4 (+38.6%), turn 5 (−31.2%), and turn 6 (+44.4%); causal tracking puts periodic background work in adjacent windows. The movements beyond 20% were explicitly reviewed and accepted; they are not described as within spread. The target freshness probes improve from 8 to 1, target MAIN from 2 to 0, and the warm causal distribution remains 45 SQL / 11 requests / 0 MAIN.

- Exact-head CI: 39 jobs passed, including type, lint and architecture jobs. The sole failing test is the mocked-Gateway image-lightbox E2E (`chat-image-lightbox.e2e.test.ts:402`, duplicate rendition request), which fails the aggregate gate. [Run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39886184561). The baseline exact-case replay passes; latest scheduled main also passes this shard. Matching-main inheritance has not been established. Another independent PR hit the same assertion; that is supporting evidence, not a waiver. Both baseline and candidate exact-case replays pass (one case each; three existing skips), which neither repairs nor proves inheritance of the original CI failure. Local worker/T1 (170→170; compatibility 15→15) and dialect (14→14) ratchets pass. The local typecheck refuses the campaign-required internal pnpm virtual store because its declarations are outside the checkout; no guard was bypassed. All exact-head CI type jobs pass. The complete local `check:changed` sweep finished: targeted type-aware lint, runtime imports, dependency/format/schema guards, and worker/dialect ratchets pass. Its aggregate exit is nonzero because of the declaration-containment refusal and inherited Knip findings. Knip has 10 production / 7 full-tree / 0 script findings, exactly matching scheduled main run 39885503944 (job 120192944836), with no additions. Madge reports zero cycles.
- Open-main-PR coverage: 2,892/2,892 at the final comparison snapshot; 65 new/moved heads checked, 2,827 unchanged heads reused, with no gaps. Base-only versus candidate merge-tree comparisons add no conflict paths or target-file conflict hunks for the 11 unchanged overlaps: #172220, #167048, #156924, #156348, #156200, #155667, #151346, #144984, #137097, #135400 and #134173.

### Accepted edge

If another process deletes and recreates a database at the same path while this process retains its schema admission, this shortcut can skip INCREMENTAL auto-vacuum initialization for the replacement. This affects the vacuum mode only; Doctor's offline VACUUM owns changes to existing databases. The edge is accepted for this optimization and is recoverable.

This is a SQLite-only setup path. PostgreSQL connections and SQL are unchanged. The coordinator accepted the disclosed raw-count cells. The lightbox failure follows the approved flake route: one full-file replay on exact current main with pinned Bun, then either matching-main inheritance or one failed-job CI rerun. Landing is pinned to `1da437d4be78fbd261ab6fb3d5f09c9b82b59f26`.

prs.title: fix: answer /login cancel during chat sign-in on channels without command source
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175344

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/login cancel` goes unanswered until the chat sign-in is dropped, about 5 minutes after `/login` (4 minutes after the cancel in the run below), when an owner starts `/login github-copilot` (or another device sign-in) on a channel that does not mark typed commands, such as IRC, Signal, LINE, Feishu, MS Teams or Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

User impact: during a chat sign-in on these channels, `/login cancel` answers within a second, as the sign-in prompt promises, and the sign-in no longer stalls the sender's channel lane.

On these channels, every authorized typed active-run-safe command now runs beside an active turn, as it already does on channels that mark commands (Discord, Mattermost, Matrix, iMessage, Tlon, SMS). That set includes the state-changing `/new`, `/reset` and `/stop`, not only `/status` and `/help`. Unauthorized senders, ordinary messages, and typed commands on a surface with `commands.text: false` still wait in order.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cancel was held back in two places, and both are needed for it to get through:

- **Ingress adoption.** The channel `/login` turn waits for the provider inside the turn without marking its durable ingress claim adopted. The claim keeps the sender's ingress lane until the 5-minute adoption watchdog releases it for retry. `runChannelProviderLogin` now adopts after the authorization check and before the provider flow, the same way `/compact` does. The flow still rechecks current authority first. Once the claim is adopted, a Gateway restart during the sign-in does not replay `/login`; the user sends it again.
- **Reply admission.** Reply admission (it picks the `command_resolution` phase, which may run beside the active turn) and the foreground reply FIFO let an active-run-safe command pass only when it is a native or text-slash turn. A channel that passes command authorization without setting `CommandSource` yields a normal turn, so the cancel queued behind the sign-in. The two checks now resolve the turn with `resolveExplicitCommandTurnContext`, which treats an authorized control command from an unmarked channel as an authorized text-slash turn. It reuses the existing `isExplicitCommandTurnContext` fallback that the first check already used as its outer gate, and promotes only where `shouldHandleTextCommands` accepts typed commands for the turn's surface.

Design note: the turn resolution owns this decision, so `isActiveRunSafeCommandTurn` and its unit contract stay unchanged, and no `/login cancel`-only branch is added to the callers. Marking commands in each channel would also work, but it touches every unmarked channel plugin.

## Evidence

Tested at `4f132e1b82c`, which merges `upstream/main` `287b38a78d2` into this branch. Before and After both ran on 2026-10-23 with Node 24.22.1.

Built CLI, `openclaw gateway run` with an isolated state directory and no outside network. The real IRC channel plugin connects to a loopback IRC server. A local stand-in for the GitHub device-code endpoints hands out a code and never approves it. The owner sends `/login github-copilot` (owner joins at +75 s), then `/login cancel` 60 s later.

Before (`upstream/main` `287b38a78d2`):

```text
+75.0s >> PRIVMSG ocbot :/login github-copilot
+76.0s << ... :Sign in with Copilot. Return here after approving access. Send /login cancel to cancel. https://github.com/login/device
+76.0s << ... :Authorize GitHub Copilot  ... Code: FAKE-0409 Code expires in 15 minutes. ...
+135.0s >> PRIVMSG ocbot :/login cancel
+376.9s << ... :No provider login is active in this chat.

[diagnostic] stuck session: … sessionKey=agent:main:main state=processing age=130s … recovery=controller_owned
[irc] Channel ingress claim→adoption stalled for event local:…:000000000001 on lane direct:owner after 300001ms; applying retry policy (handler-timeout).
```

The cancel ran only after the stall watchdog ended the sign-in turn (`totalMs=299546`), so it found no sign-in to cancel.

After (this PR):

```text
+75.0s >> PRIVMSG ocbot :/login github-copilot
+76.1s << ... :Sign in with Copilot. Return here after approving access. Send /login cancel to cancel. https://github.com/login/device
+76.1s << ... :Authorize GitHub Copilot  ... Code: FAKE-0645 Code expires in 15 minutes. ...
+135.0s >> PRIVMSG ocbot :/login cancel
+135.2s << ... :Provider login cancelled for this chat.
+135.2s << ... :Copilot login did not complete. Send `/login github-copilot/github-copilot` to try again.
```

Observed result: the cancel answers in 0.2 s, and the sign-in turn ends right after it (`totalMs=59673`). The 720 s run logs no `claim→adoption stalled` and no `stuck session` line. The After run used `26b392b3789`; the later amend to `4f132e1b82c` changed only a test file, and so does `3a5b9ce67e0`.

In the first run of this PR (base `19c5e58c2e8`), the same run with only the adoption fix still waited `reply.wait_admission_ticket:434111ms` for the cancel. Both fixes are needed.

Checks at `4f132e1b82c`, repeated at `3a5b9ce67e0` for the one test file it changes (that file, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo` on every `src` test shard and the ratchet): the touched tests and the other auto-reply and channel-turn tests that import the four changed production files (21 files), type-aware `oxlint` (`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, as CI runs it) and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, `tsgo` on the core project and every `src` test shard, and `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet` (baseline unchanged). One of the 21 files, `route-reply.delivery-result.test.ts > preserves session writer authority through route normalization`, fails the same way on `upstream/main` `287b38a78d2` without this change. These ran through the repo scripts directly.

Each changed test file, timed with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file> --maxWorkers=1` (what `pnpm test` runs) and a warm transform cache:

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-login.ingress.test.ts` | 24.7 s (test 0.4 s) |
| `src/auto-reply/command-turn-context.test.ts` | 5.9 s (new cases < 1 ms) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.active-command.test.ts` | 8.9 s (new case 0.10 s) |
| `src/auto-reply/dispatch.delivery-order.test.ts` | 7.8 s (new cases < 10 ms) |

The merge follows two main changes. The reply admission ticket is gone (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175837, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176447), so the admission case moved from `dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts` to `dispatch-from-config.active-command.test.ts`, next to main's `/login cancel` admission cases. Main also rewrote the same-session `/status` fence test, which now covers the marked command, so this PR keeps only its unmarked rows.

Tests (before/after run against `287b38a78d2`: 6 fail on the base and pass here, 31 guard tests pass on both; no added test uses a wall-clock race):

- `commands-login.ingress.test.ts` (new): drives the real channel ingress drain and its SQLite queue into `handleLoginCommand` on a fake clock. It fails on the base because the stall watchdog releases the `/login` claim (`expected "release" to not be called at all`).
- `dispatch-from-config.active-command.test.ts`: with a turn active on the session, an authorized unmarked IRC `/login cancel` reaches its reply resolver and gets its reply while that turn stays active. The case waits on a deferred the resolver settles, within the test signal. On the base, the command waits behind the active turn, so the resolver is never reached and the case runs into the test timeout.
- `dispatch.delivery-order.test.ts`: the same-session `/status` fence case runs for an unmarked command and for an unmarked command with `commands.text: false`. The older turn is released when `/status` sends its final. The unmarked case fails on the base (`expected [ 'old', 'status' ] to deeply equal [ 'status', 'old' ]`); the disabled-text case expects `['old', 'status']`.
- `command-turn-context.test.ts`: the resolver promotes an authorized unmarked control command, keeps an unauthorized one a normal turn, and leaves a marked turn unchanged.

Simplification pass: production +38/−4 in 4 files, tests +238/−3 in 4 files, plus one Vitest database-worker list entry. The admission fix is one resolver plus two one-line call changes. A `/login cancel`-only branch at both callers was dropped for it. Main's reply admission has a third active-run-safe check (`dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts`); the run above shows the cancel already gets through without changing it, so it is left alone. `command_resolution` admission returns ready while another turn holds the mailbox (`allowActiveResolution`), so the third check is not reached for this turn.

Not covered:

- Ordinary messages (`hello`) sent during the sign-in still wait until the sign-in turn ends or is cancelled. This is the existing order for normal turns. In the run above, `hello` reached the agent but could not answer, since no model was reachable.
- Ordinary turns that queue behind a sign-in that is neither approved nor cancelled keep waiting behind it. Detaching the wait from the turn, as the Telegram native login does, is a separate change.
- On unmarked channels (IRC, Signal, LINE, Feishu, MS Teams, Nextcloud Talk and others), all authorized active-run-safe commands now run beside an active turn, including the state-changing `/new`, `/reset` and `/stop`. This is intended: it matches channels that mark commands.
- Having each channel pass command facts to the shared inbound builder would retire the fallback, and is left for a separate change.

prs.title: fix(talk): agent consults fail after a Discord call changes its voice
prs.body:
Closes #181269
Related: #171013, #171029

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every agent consult in a Discord realtime call fails with "Gateway is temporarily unavailable" after `talk_voice set` changes the voice.

## User Impact

Callers can change the voice and keep using the agent (search, tools, answers) for the rest of the same call, without leaving and rejoining. No configuration, protocol, or SDK changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`talk.voice.set` runs inside its WS request root. The replacement realtime connection is created during that request but outlives it, so its later consults inherited a root that was released when the RPC returned, and gateway admission rejected them. The voice-selection host now starts the owner's replacement with `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission`, the existing primitive for work that outlives the request creating it (the same one channel startup uses). The RPC still holds its own root while it waits for the replacement, so restart drain and suspension still see it. This complements #171029, which restored the channel's plugin-instance scope on the same path but not the gateway root-work context.

## Evidence

- Regression: `admits later consults after the voice change request root is released` in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/voice-channel.test.ts`, shaped like the #171029 case. It runs `talk.voice.set` inside a `ws:talk.voice.set` root admission (as `server-methods.ts` does), binds a deferred consult from the replacement callback, releases the root, then checks `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()`.
  - base (`main` 58992a473b): **fails**, `expected true to be false`
  - head: **passes**, 8/8 in the file
- `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-voice-selection.test.ts`: 22/22 pass on head.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files pass. `tsgo` with `tsconfig.core.json` passes. Node 24.22.1.
- Live: on 2026.10.2 the call log showed `talk.voice.set` ✓ at 11:11:52, then 8 consults rejected ~30 ms after start with `Gateway is temporarily unavailable` until the caller left (log excerpt in #181269). An equivalent local patch (rebuilding the replacement outside the request context) is now deployed on that gateway. **Live proof pending**: no voice call has been made since it was deployed. I will add the result here.

prs.title: fix: peer steering fails after native consumption
prs.body:
## Author investigation update

**This PR is not ready for acceptance. The claimed native root cause is unproven.** The completed review exposed a material omission in the original reproducer, rather than a publication delay.

The actual native adapter calls `markSentToProvider()` before persisting accepted internal guidance. The real recorder deliberately exempts that delivered input from `assertOriginalInputCommit`; this behavior was introduced by merged #173458 (`815a0bd3b7eef4d7b7e64d302c03d30c2a0602ec`) to preserve faithful accepted history after source disposal. The earlier admission fake omitted that transition. Its failing-base result therefore does not establish the claimed native failure.

A new combined diagnostic exercises the production Gateway custody helper, registered Codex adapter, production wire client, `markSentToProvider()` and actual SQLite-backed recorder in one path. It is in-process with a scripted wire peer, not a native executable or shipped Gateway. All three scenarios pass with **both** the original settlement-only custody owner and this PR's proposed join:

| Scenario | Original owner | Proposed join |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allowed input: one accepted history append | PASS | PASS |
| Sender revoked after native consumption: delivered history still records once | PASS | PASS |
| Receiving physical session replaced after consumption: stale-target append refused | PASS | PASS |

The original-owner control changes only the custody implementation in the same retained integrated checkout. Candidate run: 3/3, 52.96 seconds wrapper; original-owner control: 3/3, 42.33 seconds wrapper. Both use repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de` with Node24 orchestration. Source was restored and task-only test/config diagnostics removed after capture. Two preliminary collectors failed because their initial test classifications did not provide the required host SQLite broker; those are setup failures, not product verdicts.

**Limits:** this collector calls the actual custody helper directly rather than the full `sessions_send` delivery path. Other retained local runtime source differs, including the separately qualified reply-identity patch. These observations invalidate the original native-path reproducer; they do not prove that every full-tool steering failure is absent. The initial synthetic reproducer remains evidence for its synthetic queue contract only.

The next justified step is a failing reproduction through the complete real delivery path before retaining or changing this production authorization-lifetime patch. I am not adding a stricter post-delivery sender gate merely to satisfy an incorrect negative assertion, and am not requesting another review until that reproduction exists. No native security bypass or local production repair is established by these diagnostics.

No live Gateway restart, configuration change, production data write, deployment, dependency install or external model inference was performed. Inputs and identities are synthetic; no private endpoints, credentials or production captures are published.

<details>
<summary>Prior submission and revision-qualified supporting evidence, superseded as a native root-cause claim</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `sessions_send(mode: "steer")` to a running native session failing with `session changed before sessions.send; retry the request` when consumption settles before the adapter saves the accepted message.

## User Impact

Accepted guidance can finish saving to the existing session. Device revocation, replacement of the receiving session, and exact receiving-attempt termination retain their existing authority and cleanup boundaries. Admission timing and peer-message scheduling policy are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex steering queue can invoke `onQueueSettled` on consumption before its outer adapter finishes `userTurnTranscriptRecorder.persistApproved()` for internal guidance. Releasing sharing authorization on that callback alone invalidates the pending transcript write.

The existing custody owner now waits for both consumption settlement and the adapter result. Exact physical-attempt teardown remains the independent escape path when an adapter never returns. No new authority owner, public API, setting, or permission exception is introduced.

This is a narrow lifecycle follow-up to merged #177698. Merged #180728 repairs a different recovered-child authority problem.

## Evidence

### Post-consumption authority controls

Evidence follow-up at `f622883e5e3282d849af4ffbb640107e38e32e9b` adds tests only; the production fix is unchanged.

The actual `sessions_send` admission fixture uses its real isolated SQLite transcript recorder and Gateway continuation authorization. Its synthetic queue backend pauses after `onQueueSettled` and before persistence:

- **Allowed:** the message persists once and returns accepted/steered after the adapter returns. The original settlement-only implementation reproduces the exact session-change error at this boundary.
- **Device revoked:** canonical `invalidateGatewayDeviceRevocation` runs before the append; the actual recorder rejects current authority and neither saves the message nor reports success.
- **Receiving session replaced:** canonical `replaceSessionEntry` installs a new physical session before the append; the recorder soft-refuses the stale target. The fixture mirrors Codex's existing `hasPersisted()` check and reports that refusal as an error. Both original and replacement transcripts contain zero matching source messages.
- **Cleanup:** selected physical-attempt teardown releases custody while an adapter receipt is held; sibling-attempt teardown does not. Rejected controls release their retained continuation.

All **16 admission tests pass**: 12.05 seconds wrapper / 10.25 seconds Vitest. Preliminary negative-control collectors stalled because the fixture omitted the adapter's persistence-result check; they were stopped and are not passing product evidence. Canonical replacement itself returned promptly; no synchronous mutation or raw database bypass was used.

### Production native adapter ordering

The existing registered Codex harness fixture now uses the production `CodexAppServerClient` with its request-admission path and a scripted wire peer. A correlated `item/completed` user-message receipt exercises the real notification controller, native steering queue, active-turn adapter and isolated SQLite append. The added case observes:

```text
native-consumed
persistence-start       # held: no message committed yet
persistence-committed   # released: exactly one source message
turn/steer: 1
turn/interrupt: 0
normal final: confirmed
```

All **4 native steering-settlement tests pass**: 14.95 seconds wrapper / 13.06 seconds Vitest, including the existing human-before-dispatch and degraded-completion cases. The prior two supplemental collectors used a fake client that skipped request admission and never established consumption; neither is credited as a pass.

**Scope:** these are separate, complementary boundary tests. The native case uses a scripted transport, not a Codex executable or full Gateway. Its recorder is the native fixture's actual SQLite appender; final-write revocation/replacement are tested through the actual Gateway authority owner and recorder in the admission suite. They are not one combined native/Gateway authority trace. A full native-app-server/Gateway capture and local deployment remain unproved.

### Revision and validation limits

The production custody fix and both existing test-file baselines match prior public head `7d99006e39967dcb6e9a63414c35aa19815ea67e` byte-for-byte. The added tests were executed in the retained integrated local checkout, then copied byte-for-byte to this PR. Other local runtime source differs: in particular its separate reply-identity patch uses `isInboundUserReply ?? isInboundUserMessage`; this native case supplies `isInboundUserMessage: false`, selecting the same post-consumption branch in both versions. This is not whole-head upstream-environment proof.

Focused core/extension lint, formatting, whitespace, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The earlier production typecheck and 12 queue-authority tests remain qualified to local candidate `9fc43634d11b`. The local test-type graph had an untouched missing `seedCanonicalAcpSessionMeta` reference. Fresh-checkout dependency/declaration/lint setup failures remain recorded; no installation or configuration bypass was used to turn them into passes.

At prior public head `7d99006e3996`, hosted source/lint/production-type and changed-node checks passed, while test-types reported an untouched `managedHooksDir` fixture/type mismatch in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts`; its aggregate CI gate also failed. This PR does not include a speculative hook repair. New-head CI remains the broad gate.

All content, identities and credentials are synthetic. No live Gateway was restarted or modified and no production conversation, private endpoint, credential or raw capture is published. Maintainer security review remains required; passing isolated controls are not an assertion of owner approval.

</details>

prs.title: fix(plugins): reject embedded runs whose sessionId disagrees with the key's persisted identity
prs.body:
Closes #120787

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveRunSessionExecutionOwner()` derives the ownership scan scope (`agentId`, `storePath`) from the plugin-supplied session key. `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned()` then scans only that one scoped store, so a plugin-supplied `sessionId` that actually lives in a *different* agent/store is never observed - the ownership check silently passes. The caller's key then binds to a bogus fresh window in its own store instead of executing the foreign session (downstream binding anchors to the key-derived store), but the identity guarantee is broken and integrity-polluting windows get created.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scoped scan cannot see cross-store ids by design, so absence there must not imply safety when the caller also supplied a concrete id. This adds a fail-closed check after the existing scan in `src/plugins/registry-runtime-session-ownership.ts` (reached from `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` via `loadSessionOwnership()`):

```ts
if (directSessionId && sessionKey && entry && entry.sessionId !== directSessionId) {
  throw new Error(
    `Plugin "${pluginId}" may execute session "${sessionKey}" only with its exact persisted identity.`,
  );
}
```

Deliberate ordering and scope:
- Placed **after** `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned` so same-store mismatches keep their richer pre-existing ownership error (the scan finds locked foreign rows in the same store).
- Only fires when the plugin supplies both a session key with a resolvable entry *and* a differing explicit id; fresh-session create flows (id absent from stores, no key/entry) are unaffected.
- Locked-session flows return earlier with their own stricter identity rules.

## User Impact

- Embedded runs that pair an owned key with a foreign/differing session id are now rejected up front instead of silently creating a bogus execution window.
- Legitimate flows (matching id/key pairs, create-on-run, incognito scans) behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Focused proof (Windows, Node v24.15.0): `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ``src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.sqlite.test.ts`` src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.test.ts` -> 2 passed + 16 passed.

Update: the production guard landed after review feedback (it was correctly flagged as missing from the initial head) — the check above is now in the diff. New regression test uses real per-agent SQLite stores: victim harness-locked session lives in agent `main`'s store while the caller owns a key in agent `researcher`'s store; `{sessionId: victimId, sessionKey: ownKey}` previously resolved (mock executed), now rejects with the exact-identity error and never reaches `runEmbeddedAgent`. The pre-existing same-store case still asserts its original `'owned by plugin "harness-owner"'` error.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session titles show the model's explanation instead of the title
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic dashboard session titles show the title model's own explanation ("Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nic…") or a label prefix ("Session title: …", "Titel: …") when the first message is vague, e.g. "Explain whether this could be useful for us too" or "What do you think about this?".

## User Impact

User impact: new dashboard, iOS and node chats get the title the model actually proposed instead of a cut-off explanation sentence or a "Title:"-style prefix. Saved titles also name worktree branches, so the same fix applies there.

Affected: setups where titles run on the Claude CLI runtime with the automatic utility model (Haiku 5.5, since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168603 ), i.e. no explicit `agents.defaults.utilityModel`. Measured on an isolated Gateway with 15 first messages × 5 runs: 13 of 75 titles were unusable on 2026.10.5, 9 of them in the two shapes this PR targets. Other utility models may produce the same shapes; I only measured Haiku.

## Why This Change Was Made

The title model often answers in two parts: a sentence about its task, a blank line, then the title. Two things in the existing owner dropped the title:

1. `runLabelAttempts` cut the answer to the 60-character title cap *before* calling the caller's `normalizeLabel`, so the dashboard normalizer only ever saw the start of the explanation.
2. `normalizeDashboardSessionTitle` took the first line and only stripped an English `title:` prefix.

Now the generator normalizes the whole visible answer and truncates afterwards. The dashboard normalizer skips lines ending with `:` (they introduce the next line), prefers a line the model introduced as the title, otherwise keeps the first line — unless that first line is over the title budget and contains a later line exactly as a quoted span (`… a fitting title is "X".\n\nX`; open and matching close quote directly around the text, using the quote pairs of the existing wrapper removal from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167584 , now a shared constant) —, strips a closed set of title introductions ("Title:", "Session title:", "Conversation title:", "Concise title for this session:", "Label:", "Titel:", "Sitzungstitel:", "Richtiger Titel:" …) and unwraps a title wrapped in `**bold**`. Topics that merely contain these words stay intact (`Fix button label: Save changes`, `Fix subtitle parsing: "Invalid cue"`, `PR 177777: Proof for the title fix`). Single-line outputs keep today's behavior, except that a line ending in `:` is rejected so the existing fallback chain (regular model, then slug) runs.

| | Production | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | +58 / −27 (2 files; includes moving the existing quote-pair table to module scope) | +77 (1 file) |

No prompt change. `normalizeLabel` has one caller (`src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.ts`).

## Evidence

**Live, isolated Gateway** (loopback, own state, agent on `claude-cli`, utility model resolved automatically to `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` via Claude CLI), driver `gateway call sessions.title.prepare`, same 15 messages (10 vague, 5 clear controls, German and English), 5 runs each. Before = installed 2026.10.5 package, after = package copy of this branch's build (`d3249a9` before review round 1, `3864f35` after round 1). The live runs were not repeated for `0311964`: review round 3 only tightens which later line may replace the first one (exact quoted span instead of plain substring), so it can only keep more first lines than `3864f35`; it is covered by the tests and the replay below. Classification of the saved title by hand from the JSONL output:

| Build | Calls (UTC, 2026-10-20) | Explanation or "Title:"-prefix instead of title | Answer instead of title | Over-long title cut at 60 chars | Model call failed (`null`) | Usable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) | 75, 19:27–19:33 | **9** | 2 | 2 | 0 | 62 |
| `d3249a9` (before review) | 75, 20:45–20:52 | **2** | 6 | 3 | 1 | 63 |
| this PR (`3864f35`) | 75, 21:29–21:35 | **2** | 1 | 3 | 0 | 69 |

Haiku varies a lot between runs, so only the targeted column is a fair comparison. Review round 1 found that the length/punctuation preamble rule in `d3249a9` could replace a long punctuated first-line title with the explanation after it; `3864f35` drops that rule. A long first line is now kept (truncated, as on `main`) unless it quotes the later line. Cost of that change: one long explanatory sentence followed by the bare title (no `Title:`, no quote) keeps the base behavior; on `3864f35` this was 1 of the 2 remaining targeted misses (`Erkennung: Die Aufgabe ist … etwas wie "Nutzen für unser Team prüfen" oder ähnlich.\n\nNutzen für uns prüfen` — the quoted phrase differs from the final line). The other one uses an introduction outside the closed list (`Ein Titel für diese Sitzung: **…**`); I kept the list closed rather than guess more phrasings. Answers instead of titles are single-line replies to the user and pass through unchanged before and after.

<details><summary>Examples (raw model output → saved title)</summary>

```text
2026.10.5
"Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nicht die Frage zu beantworten. … Ein passender Titel wäre: „Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen“.\n\nNützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
  → "Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, nic"
"Concise title for this session: **Assessing usefulness for our team**"
  → "Concise title for this session: **Assessing usefulness for o"
"Session title: Gateway Docker persistent state volume"
  → "Session title: Gateway Docker persistent state volume"

this PR (3864f35)
"Die Aufgabe ist, einen kurzen Sitzungstitel zu erzeugen, … Ein passender Titel wäre: „Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen“.\n\nNützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
  → "Nützlichkeit für unser Team prüfen"
"Fix Docker startup failures on Windows. Restore volume permissions\n\nThis captures the main topic."   (review example, test row)
  → "Fix Docker startup failures on Windows. Restore volume permi"
"Generiere einen kurzen Sitzungstitel (3–6 Wörter, max. 60 Zeichen) …\n\nIch antworte auf deutsch, aber für diese Aufgabe gebe ich nur den Titel zurück.\n\nTitel: Nützlichkeit für unser Team erklären"
  → "Nützlichkeit für unser Team erklären"
"Conversation title: Checking a request"
  → "Checking a request"
```

</details>

**False positives:** replaying the old and new line/prefix selection (head `0311964`) over 227 existing dashboard titles from a real installation changed 0 of them. Over 475 raw outputs collected in all runs it changed 34: 28 unusable → usable, 5 only by trailing whitespace (trimmed afterwards anyway), 1 usable → a different usable title (the model returned two candidate lines and introduced the second with "Session title:").

**Tests** (`src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.transport.test.ts`, real OpenAI-compatible transport through `maybeGenerateDashboardSessionTitle`, asserts the persisted `displayName`): 17 new rows in the existing "persists a usable title" table — an English and a German explanation quoting the title before it (`… Ein passender Titel wäre: „X“.\n\nX`), an introduction ending in `:`, explanations before an introduced `Title:` line, `Titel:`, `Session title:`, quoted and bold titles after an introduction, an introduction without a title (falls back to the slug), and eight titles that must stay unchanged (a long title that merely contains the next line, unquoted (review round 2: `Investigate intermittent Docker startup failures caused by Permission denied\n\nPermission denied`), a long punctuated title before an explanation (review round 1), `PR 177777: …`, `Debug Docker: "Permission denied"`, `Fix subtitle parsing: …`, `Fix button label: …`, a long quoted title before a short explanation, a title before an explanation).
Counter-check: with only the two production files reset to the merge base, the 9 rows that need extraction fail and the 8 unchanged-title rows pass (41 tests, 9 failed). Against the previous head `3864f35`, only the new review-round-2 row fails (41 tests, 1 failed).

```text
pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1 (VPS, 2 CPUs, head 0311964)
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.transport.test.ts            41 passed  106 s
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts                      32 passed   21 s
src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.incognito.test.ts             2 passed   17 s
src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts        19 passed   22 s
src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-title-preparation.test.ts    5 passed   33 s
src/gateway/server.sessions.create.titles.test.ts                 9 passed   41 s
src/gateway/server-methods/session-discussion.test.ts             8 passed   22 s
src/commands/doctor-session-title-repair.test.ts                  6 passed   35 s
pnpm test <transport> <dashboard-session-title> <conversation-label-generator> --maxWorkers=1: 92 passed, 81 s
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` and `git diff --check` clean on the changed files. The branch merges into current `main` without conflicts; `main` has not touched these three files since the merge base.

**Gaps:** single-line answers to the user, over-long single-sentence titles, and a long explanation followed by an unquoted bare title are unchanged; they need a different signal than this normalizer has. Title phrasings outside the closed introduction list still pass through. Measured with Haiku 5.5 only.


## Maintainer follow-up

### Maintainer proof

Reviewed and validated head `03119648fea381d4f38525be21583d076dc22d1b` without changing the contributor's commits. Thanks @holgergruenhagen. The full PR remains production **+58/−27** (net +31, two files) and tests **+77/−0** (one file). No prompt change; prompt-token delta **0**.

**Sidebar before/after.** The PR changes no UI files. These captures use the actual PR-head Control UI with a mock Gateway returning the exact title results derived from merge base `996d77cd1b3460d45c14babe0703d618396ae5e4` and this head, respectively. Rows are the same introduced, German quoted, and plain-title cases below. All six full DOM strings were asserted; long labels still receive the UI's normal visual clipping. One browser test passed in **44.82s**. Both full frames and these same-frame sidebar crops were inspected: synthetic content only, no secrets, private data, or internal identifiers.

|---|---|

prs.title: refactor(ui): remove redundant Solid lifetime snapshots
prs.body:
Related: #168114

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI rows and imperative input dialogs carry redundant reactive-prop snapshots even when their owners already supply stable identities or immutable opening requests.

## User Impact

No intended visual or user-facing behavior change. Tabs, command-palette options, transcript rows, sidebar panels, and selection annotations retain their existing keys, focus behavior, and synchronous registration/cleanup. MCP app content continues to retain its admitted launch while teardown is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve keyed identity inside Solid's native ref factory, where the runtime already evaluates under `untrack` with the owner intact; callbacks then use the captured plain key. Reuse the existing `elementRef` lifecycle. Capture the shell observer and picker registration in their existing settled setup. Derive the retained MCP launch and sidebar branch instead of snapshotting them. The Solid lessons now document why moving the same read into an unowned callback is insufficient: rc.16 preserves the surrounding strict-read diagnostic scope.

The sidebar now iterates canonical serialized row keys directly. Input dialogs render their immutable opening request inside the existing modal owner, removing an unnecessary reactive prop boundary. The newer confirmation and file-draft recovery lazy entry points are preserved unchanged from main. The unused automation inventory injection path is deleted; production already creates its inventory locally.

The full effect audit found real external responsibilities at the remaining sites. This PR does **not** claim the requested targets of 30 feature effects and 15 `untrack` calls are met. It keeps required router/request admission, DOM commit, foreign widget, media, credential, and teardown synchronization rather than hiding calls behind new wrappers. There are no new shared primitives, dependencies, routes, or lazy imports.

Touched production-file checklist: `createEffect` 2 → 2; `untrack` 18 → 2; direct `onCleanup` 3 → 1; raw listeners, DOM queries, `getOwner`, and `flush` remain 0; `runWithOwner` and manual imports are unchanged. Async request and mutation ownership stays with the existing owners.

prs.title: fix(cli): escape rejected --channel values in update diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #181212

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update`, `update repair`, and `update finalize` render a rejected `--channel` value into their diagnostic with plain interpolation:

```text
--channel must be "stable", "extended-stable", "beta", or "dev" (got "<value>")
```

The value is inserted verbatim instead of as an escaped string, so a channel carrying a quote and a newline closes the quoting, breaks the line, and appends text that reads like a separate diagnostic. With `--channel $'beta"\nFORGED'` the one-line rejection becomes two lines:

```text
--channel must be "stable", "extended-stable", "beta", or "dev" (got "beta"
FORGED")
```

In `--json` mode the message is still JSON-encoded, so the payload parses, but `error.message` now contains a raw newline. Anything that reads one line per error, or that forwards that message into its own line-oriented log, sees an ambiguous value.

The accepted-channel list and the guard itself are intentional and unchanged; only the rendering of the rejected value changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing oracle in `src/cli/update-cli.invalid-channel.process.test.ts` already expects `(got ${JSON.stringify(channel)})`, but it only feeds `""` and `"unrecognized-channel"`, where raw interpolation and `JSON.stringify` produce identical output. The test therefore never distinguished the two, and both production branches drifted to raw interpolation.

This change renders the rejected value with `JSON.stringify` in both validation branches, which is exactly what the oracle already describes, and adds cases with a quote plus newline and with a quote plus tab so the distinction is locked in.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-run.ts` | root `update` guard renders the rejected value with `JSON.stringify` |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts` | `repair` / `finalize` guard renders the rejected value with `JSON.stringify` |
| `src/cli/update-cli.invalid-channel.process.test.ts` | new process-level cases: 3 entry points × 2 hostile values |

The new cases assert the escaped rendering is present, the raw value is absent from stderr, and the JSON-mode `error.message` equals the escaped message exactly.

## Evidence

### Real CLI before and after

Executed against the source entry (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `--channel $'beta"\nFORGED'`. `before` is the same tree with only the two source lines reverted.

```text
[root] before: stderr_lines=4  json_message="...(got \"beta\"\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='[openclaw] The CLI command failed.\n[openclaw] Reason: --channel must be ... (got "beta"\nFORGED")\n[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.\n'
[root] after:  stderr_lines=3  json_message="...(got \"beta\\\"\\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='[openclaw] The CLI command failed.\n[openclaw] Reason: --channel must be ... (got "beta\\"\\nFORGED")\n[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.\n'

[repair] before: stderr_lines=2  json_message="...(got \"beta\"\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='--channel must be ... (got "beta"\nFORGED")\n'
[repair] after:  stderr_lines=1  json_message="...(got \"beta\\\"\\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='--channel must be ... (got "beta\\"\\nFORGED")\n'

[finalize] before: stderr_lines=2  json_message="...(got \"beta\"\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='--channel must be ... (got "beta"\nFORGED")\n'
[finalize] after:  stderr_lines=1  json_message="...(got \"beta\\\"\\nFORGED\")"
  stderr='--channel must be ... (got "beta\\"\\nFORGED")\n'
```

The forged `FORGED")` line is gone in all three paths, and `error.message` is a single escaped line.

### Regression test

`src/cli/update-cli.invalid-channel.process.test.ts` gains `it.each` over `update`, `update repair`, `update finalize` × `beta"\nFORGED`, `dev\t"[error] forged`. Each case runs the real CLI child, then asserts `stderr` contains the escaped message, does not contain the raw value, and that `JSON.parse(stdout).error.message` equals the escaped message.

With the two source lines reverted, the cases fail on both `not.toContain(channel)` and the `error.message` equality; with the fix they pass.

### Checks

- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the three files: clean.
- `oxlint` on the three files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

### What was not run here

The vitest file itself could not be executed on this Windows host: the runner's worker namespace cleanup is blocked in this environment. The captures above are direct executions of the real CLI source entry, and the added assertions mirror the existing cases in the same file (whose `--json` path already relies on `JSON.parse(result.stdout)`).
