prs.title: fix(config): preserve whitespace in secrets provider file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`, and resolution/exec validation previously re-trimmed via `resolveUserPath`, so a whitespace-bearing trusted directory could authorize the wrong neighbor executable.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Whitespace-bearing `trustedDirs` authorize only executables literally inside that directory; the nearest neighbor without the trailing space is rejected before process creation. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. File/exec resolution used trimming `resolveUserPath`. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder and adds `resolveUserPathLiteral` for resolution + `assertSecureExecCommandPath`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPathLiteral`), `src/secrets/exec-provider-path-validation.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.ts`; regressions in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI on head `bd8f2287fe3`: **shipped file-provider consume** (literal path beats distinguishable neighbor) + **real upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`** (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: file+exec providers still load/validate/resolve) + exec allow/deny-before-start (below)
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. `--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally.
2. **Shipped CLI must consume that literal file-provider path** (not a trimmed neighbor): `node openclaw.mjs config set … --dry-run` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readSecureFile(resolveUserPathLiteral(path))`.
3. Existing `secrets.providers` written by published **v2026.10.5** must still load, validate, and resolve after upgrading the same state dir to this PR head.
4. (Already shown) Whitespace-bearing trustedDirs authorize only the literal helper; neighbor rejected before process creation.

### Canonical reachability path (file-provider consume)

Packaged `node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.<alias> --provider-source file --provider-path '<path with trailing space>' --provider-mode json` → persist literal path → `config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider <alias> --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json` → `collectDryRunResolvabilityErrors` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readFileProviderPayload` / `resolveUserPathLiteral` → `readSecureFile`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses `readNonBlankString` for builder persistence and `resolveUserPathLiteral` for file (and exec) resolution. No direct library `resolveSecretRefString` call in this proof — only the packaged CLI entrypoint.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, OpenClaw 2026.9.9) on head `bd8f2287fe3` with Node v24.16.0; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Paths redacted to `/tmp/oc168261.*/…`.

### Exact steps — shipped file-provider consume + neighbor

```bash
# Node 24.16+ (packaged CLI) on head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"
SECRET_SPACE="$ROOT/secret "          # trailing space
SECRET_NEIGHBOR="$ROOT/secret"        # no trailing space
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"GOOD"}' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' 'NOT_JSON_WRONG' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"   # distinguishable: INVALID JSON
chmod 600 "$SECRET_SPACE" "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"

node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$SECRET_SPACE" --provider-mode json

# Shipped consume (resolvability via packaged dry-run — neighbor is invalid JSON)
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json

# Flip: corrupt spaced file; leave neighbor as VALID {"token":"WRONG"}
# Expect dry-run FAIL (still targets literal spaced path; trim would succeed via neighbor)
printf '%s\n' 'CORRUPT_NOT_JSON' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"WRONG"}' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
```

### Evidence after fix — shipped file-provider consume

```text
=== SETUP (file-provider consume) ===

head=bd8f2287fe3
secret_space_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
secret_neighbor_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret'
space_content= {"token":"GOOD"}
neighbor_content= NOT_JSON_WRONG

=== A1) Persist file provider with trailing-space path ===
Updated secrets.providers.vault. No gateway restart needed.
stored_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
stored_source= file
stored_mode= json

=== A2) Shipped consume: config set --dry-run (neighbor INVALID JSON) ===
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
consume_dryrun_exit=0
# Success with invalid neighbor ⇒ packaged CLI read the literal spaced file (GOOD).

=== A3) Flip: spaced file CORRUPT; neighbor VALID {"token":"WRONG"} ===
{
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [{
    "kind": "resolvability",
    "message": "Unexpected token 'C', \"CORRUPT_NOT_JSON\\n\" is not valid JSON",
    "ref": "file:vault:/token"
  }]
}
flip_dryrun_exit=1
flip_result=DENIED_AS_EXPECTED (literal spaced path still targeted; neighbor not used)

=== A4) Restore spaced GOOD; consume green again ===
restore_ok= True
restore_dryrun_exit=0
```

### Exact steps — data-model compatibility / existing settings

```bash
# Simulate pre-fix stored settings (stable-style: no edge whitespace on provider path)
STATE2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-compat.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE2" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE2/openclaw.json"
LEGACY_SECRET="$ROOT/legacy-secret.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"apiKey":"LEGACY_OK"}' > "$LEGACY_SECRET" && chmod 600 "$LEGACY_SECRET"
# write openclaw.json with secrets.providers.legacy.path = $LEGACY_SECRET (no edge whitespace)
# and channels.discord.token SecretRef → legacy:/apiKey

node openclaw.mjs config get secrets.providers.legacy
node openclaw.mjs config validate --json
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider legacy --ref-source file --ref-id /apiKey --dry-run --json

# Ordinary (no-whitespace) path still works via CLI; legacy provider retained
ORD="$ROOT/ordinary.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"ORDINARY"}' > "$ORD" && chmod 600 "$ORD"
node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.ordinary \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ORD" --provider-mode json
```

### Evidence after fix — compatibility / upgrade retention

```text
=== B) COMPAT: legacy provider paths (no edge whitespace) on this head ===
wrote_legacy_config= /tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json
legacy_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/legacy-secret.json'

--- config get (loads existing stored provider) ---
{ "source": "…", "path": "…", "mode": "…" }   # redacted by CLI; loads OK

--- config validate ---
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json", ...}
validate_exit=0

--- shipped consume of legacy file provider ---
legacy_consume_ok= True
legacy_resolvability= True
legacy_refsChecked= 1
legacy_consume_exit=0

--- ordinary no-whitespace provider + legacy retained ---
Updated secrets.providers.ordinary. No gateway restart needed.
ordinary_path= /tmp/oc168261.*/ordinary.json
legacy_still_present= True
legacy_path_unchanged= True
ordinary_consume_ok= True
ordinary_consume_exit=0
```


### Exact steps — real upgrade from published v2026.10.5

```bash
# Authentic release binary (npm registry, not a hand-built fake):
#   npm install openclaw@2026.10.5
#   → OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
#   npm pack shasum 158d80b43644e2feba2a50647803562aa394e080
#   tarball sha256 dbb1bdcf2346292e25f672822b6a9928c234909abe6fee0df5fc4556e769d40e
export PATH="/path/to/node-v24.16.0/bin:$PATH"
OC_OLD=…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs   # 2026.10.5
OC_NEW=…/openclaw.mjs                         # PR head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"

# 1) ON v2026.10.5 — create real secrets.providers (file + exec)
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"UPGRADE_OK","apiKey":"LEGACY_KEY"}' > "$ROOT/vault.json" && chmod 600 "$ROOT/vault.json"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/helpers"
# exec helper speaks protocolVersion 1
cat > "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' '{"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"secret":"EXEC_OK"}}'
EOF
chmod 755 "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh"

node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ROOT/vault.json" --provider-mode json
node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.execvault \
  --provider-source exec --provider-command "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" \
  --provider-trusted-dir "$ROOT/helpers" --provider-json-only

node "$OC_OLD" config validate --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider execvault --ref-source exec --ref-id secret --dry-run --json --allow-exec

# 2) UPGRADE: same OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR / openclaw.json → PR head packaged CLI (no rewrite)
node "$OC_NEW" --version
node "$OC_NEW" config get secrets.providers.vault
node "$OC_NEW" config get secrets.providers.execvault
node "$OC_NEW" config validate --json
node "$OC_NEW" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
node "$OC_NEW" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider execvault --ref-source exec --ref-id secret --dry-run --json --allow-exec
```

prs.title: fix(slack): retry isolated invalid_auth before disabling a socket-mode channel
prs.body:
Closes #180942

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: a Slack Socket Mode channel is permanently disabled for the life of the process after a single `invalid_auth`, even though the configured tokens still pass `auth.test`.

## User Impact
A transient Slack-side `invalid_auth` no longer takes an account offline until a manual gateway restart (the linked report lost inbound DMs and mentions for 3.5 hours). The channel now retries with the normal reconnect backoff and recovers on the next successful connection; definitive credential failures (revoked token, deactivated account, missing scope) still stop the channel immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made
The auth-error classifier treated `invalid_auth` like a revoked token: one occurrence published terminal status, and the health monitor skips terminal channels forever. Slack can emit an isolated `invalid_auth` while the credentials still verify, so it is not a definitive verdict. `invalid_auth` (when not accompanied by a definitive code) now counts toward a consecutive-failure limit of 3 via `nextSlackAuthFailureState`; a successful reconnect resets the count, and reaching the limit keeps today's terminal behavior. The limit check, status publication, and terminal rejection live in `provider-support.ts` so the already over-cap monitor provider does not grow.

Follow-up after review: the limit check now compares the incremented count, so the channel turns terminal exactly at the 3rd consecutive failure (previously the 4th), and `trackSlackAuthFailure` accepts the optional `setStatus` callback like the sibling status publishers. The persistent-failure regression now asserts the exact attempt cutoff and the post-reconnect counter reset instead of only eventual rejection.

## Evidence
- Regressions in `provider.reconnect-loop.test.ts`, red before the threshold fix: persistent `invalid_auth` makes exactly 3 start attempts before blocking (the pre-fix PR head made 4; base main makes 1), and the counter reset after a successful reconnect requires a fresh run of 3 consecutive failures (pre-fix head needed 4 post-reset; the reset test also drives the post-connect `unable_to_socket_mode_start` auth-failure branch).
- Suites: reconnect-loop 7/7 plus consumers of the touched helper/policy — provider interop, ingress-start-cleanup, monitor history-policy and tool-result suites all green (node 24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --run`). `provider.auth-test-token.test.ts` shows the same 2 failures with and without this change on this host (real-stall HTTP timing on a proxied, loaded box; unrelated to the diff) — CI `checks-node-*` covers them.
- Real behavior proof (localhost Slack stand-in + isolated `openclaw gateway run`, placeholder tokens, Linux, node 24.22.1):
  - Isolated `invalid_auth`: the stand-in answers the first `apps.connections.open` with `invalid_auth`, then ok. The gateway logs `socket mode failed to start; retry 1/∞ in 2s` followed by `socket mode connected`; the stand-in then delivers a DM envelope over the real Socket Mode WebSocket, the gateway acks it and processes it to an outbound reply (`[slack] delivered reply to channel:DPROOF1`; the reply text is the no-model-configured notice, expected in this isolated setup).
  - Persistent control: every `apps.connections.open` answers `invalid_auth`; the gateway logs retries `1/∞` and `2/∞`, then stops at exactly the 3rd failure with `auth: start failed, skipping channel` and `auto-restart skipped, terminal disconnect` — no 4th connection attempt.
  - Consistent with the independent live-run evidence @wr-web posted below on an equivalent branch.
- oxfmt and `git diff --check` clean. Not run locally: `pnpm tsgo:extensions*` typecheck lanes — the tsrs binary requires GLIBC 2.32+ and this host's libc is older; CI typecheck lanes cover the diff (1-line comparison change plus test-only code).

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): preserve pending MCP app setup [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link repeatedly cancels and restarts the same MCP App setup before showing the widget. The final baseline issued a median 15 identical `mcp.app.view` requests for one widget; the candidate issues one.

**Experiment stopped: the final comparison failed the pre-declared chat LoAF secondary gate. This PR is not a landing candidate.**

## Why This Change Was Made

`restartAfterTeardown()` treated absence of mounted resources as evidence of retirement. Resources are also absent while setup awaits its first HTML response. The change requires the owner's existing `retired` fact before restarting. Changed bindings, reconnects, explicit retirement, and the visible Retry action retain their existing paths.

Separate unprofiled call instrumentation mapped the repeated calls to `BoardMcpAppContent`'s ready publication at line 49. Two steady baseline runs recorded 32 and 31 restart calls with one unchanged client/revision/scope/session/view binding, no retirement, and no iframe yet. Candidate runs received 32–34 publications but made one HTML request each. Instrumented timing is not used for the gate.

Production LOC delta: **0** (one existing guard changed). No new state, cache, configuration, schema, or permission behavior.

## User Impact

The candidate removes repeated MCP setup and paints charts sooner. It does not clear the campaign's no-regression gate: the final chat LoAF intervals separate in the wrong direction. Chat made zero MCP view requests on both builds; a causal link between this guard and the chat change has not been established. No A/A follow-up or broader optimization was attempted after the stop condition.

The separate HTML-widget path made one HTTP HTML fetch and zero MCP view calls on every control reload (three per build). Its existing active-load guard prevents this same pending-load restart pattern.

## Evidence

Final head: `8a0de4777594971f8ecd3f5ec5a80aad160a9c7f`, based on `974c99df3832ce3b50afc6b70fd45189aa6f017a`. Baseline/candidate bundles came from the same checkout and differ only in the one-line owner guard. AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease **cbx_1ee3380fa823**, run [run_c37943663459069bcddfe07f604a4667](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c37943663459069bcddfe07f604a4667), Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, repository Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Synthetic Team-scale fixture, 1719×1179, warmed storage/cache; no real account or private capture.

Delivery: challenge no earlier than 340 ms, connect reply after 220 ms, ordinary RPC replies after 20 ms, session resolve/describe after 195 ms. These are simulated delays. This measures the production renderer against a synthetic Gateway, not live server/proxy latency.

Pre-declared acceptance: **11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs per route**; request count target one per widget; paint improves with non-overlapping IQR or at least 9/11 better pairs and a negative median paired delta. Secondary regression requires non-overlapping IQR, or at least 9/11 worse pairs with a median rise greater than max(10 ms, 3%). Values below are ms from navigation unless marked as counts. Intervals are Q1–Q3; paired deltas are candidate minus baseline.

The primary metrics improve, but chat LoAF fails by the independent non-overlapping-IQR rule: **235 [222–241] → 246 [244.5–251] ms**. Its paired median is +10 ms with 8/11 worse pairs. The earlier pre-rebase round passed (17 → 1 requests; chart pixels 1,840 → 1,790 ms; overlapping chat LoAF intervals), but it is not substituted for final-head evidence.

| Primary metric | Baseline | Candidate | Median paired Δ | Better pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MCP view requests (count) | 15.0 [14.5–23.0] | 1.0 [1.0–1.0] | -14.0 | 11/11 |
| First visible chart pixels | 1,901.3 [1,891.0–1,929.0] | 1,778.4 [1,761.0–1,852.3] | -128.1 | 10/11 |

| Route / secondary metric | Baseline | Candidate | Median paired Δ | Worse pairs |

prs.title: fix: automatically retire old recovery copies after successful updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recovery copies accumulated indefinitely even after later successful updates made them eligible for the existing `openclaw update cleanup` retirement. Operators had to remember to run cleanup manually.

Related: #174253 #162622 #173564

## User Impact

Successful updates automatically retire superseded recovery copies, while retaining the just-finished update's rollback generation. Cleanup failures leave the update successful and surface advisory diagnostics in output/JSON and update history. Manual cleanup remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

- CLI terminal publication invokes cleanup **after durable success and executor settlement**, using the existing local-state-owner router. A stopped state gets exclusive offline custody; a running Gateway receives an owner-bound admin request and runs the same retirement in a worker with live owner checks before effects. Cleanup never stops/restarts the Gateway or bypasses the manual command's offline lock.
- Gateway-owned restart completion invokes the same operation after success, including later observation of managed completion. The macOS app already uses these CLI paths; `--no-restart` does not imply ownership.
- The existing eligibility, dependency, manifest, and identity checks remain authoritative. Current-generation, pending-recovery, unfinished, unresolved-failed/rolled-back, orphan/unmanifested, and blocked artifacts remain protected under those rules. If any retained historical reference lacks artifact proof, automatic cleanup conservatively defers migration-original disposal as a group because dependency edges may span manifests. This uses underlying references, not final classification, so already-protected/incomplete originals cannot hide missing proof. Independently eligible captures still retire; manual cleanup retains its existing verification/classification. Doctor retention is unchanged.
- Post-success cleanup diagnostics may extend a terminal record but cannot change its outcome. No config switch, new retention schema, or new scheduler is introduced. The prewritten update report artifact remains the settled update report; late cleanup diagnostics are included in terminal output/JSON and update status.

## Evidence

Validated head: `1a65852c3ab6ae4252c321ad6fcbc2390f6307b4` (2026-10-22).

### Exact-head local checks

Commands ran in the task worktree with isolated HOME/state/config/TMPDIR. The actual handoff resolver was asserted to resolve inside the private temporary root, never the live handoff store. The existing install and global pnpm package store were reused. Vitest selected the repository-pinned Bun fork; Node subprocess fixtures used supported Node 24.22.1. No live Gateway/service operation was performed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-disposal.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-mutations.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-terminal-record.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-terminal-authority.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/progress.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-ledger.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-restart-update-run.test.ts \
  src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.since.test.ts \
  src/gateway/update-recovery-cleanup.authority.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**156 passed**, 10 files, 4 shards; **204.86 s wall**. Includes all 13 automatic-retirement cases, 38 manual-retirement mutation/disposal cases, terminal/cancellation/ledger/progress consumers, and the real authenticated cleanup RPC test. The latter took 54.13 s of test time: it boots an isolated real Gateway and exercises real clients, dispatcher, worker and filesystem, not a substituted handler.

Authenticated RPC trace:
> Allowed deletion; non-admin and wrong owner denied; real device revocation after one removal prevented subsequent deletion; current capture and successful outcome retained.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **19 passed**, **152.50 s wall**.
- `node --experimental-vm-modules --test scripts/tests/update-restart-module-outcome.mjs` — **19 passed**, **2.07 s wall**, including real synthetic-package swap/retirement.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.manifests.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **20 passed**, **20.57 s wall**. Covers historical V2 indexes, retained/changed/missing archives, shared duplicate-retirement interruption/recovery and preserved rollback bytes. This adds bounded stored-data compatibility proof, not a claimed released-driver upgrade.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <config> --incremental` — passed for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json`, and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json`.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -E '\.(ts|mjs)$' | xargs node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` — **27 files, 0 warnings/errors**, 26.3 s lint time.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-retirement.ts src/commands/update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts` — passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-protocol-registry.mts`, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/protocol-gen.ts`, and `git diff --check` — passed.

An initial prior-head CLI run selected unsupported Node 24.20.0 for Node-specific fixtures and refused at `node-runtime-preflight`, before two intended boundaries. Selecting the already-installed supported Node 24.22.1 cleared both; the final-head run above also passes. No test expectation or production runtime gate was weakened.

### Independent review and repair

Fresh full-diff GitHub-API-only review of the final SHA is **clean through P2**. The reviewer read all 29 changed-file diffs, every touched test file in full, and the pinned authority/retirement helpers. Whole-file test audits retained distinct behavior, cancellation, ownership, failure and consumer contracts; no new source-text mirrors, tautologies or mocks replacing cleanup decisions/deletion were found.

The preceding independent review found **P1: migration-original deletion could continue after caller/physical-owner revocation**. The shared retirement owner had checked authority once before a synchronous batch and did not propagate the guard through awaited claim publication. The final repair rechecks live authority after publication before source-name removal, before each final unlink, and before each manifest publication. It reuses the existing retirement owner and helper callback; no new authorization or retention mechanism was added.

Two real-worker regressions replace the actual physical state owner after a claim appears and after the first original is removed. Both failed on pre-fix production code (the original source name had already disappeared; both originals were removed rather than one remaining), then passed with the fix. They verify remaining bytes, current capture and settled success, and require the successor owner to resume the durable partial-disposal receipts successfully. The final API review explicitly confirmed this P1 resolved. Earlier historical-dependency, late-warning and consumer-fixture findings remain covered by the passing suites.

Manual cleanup still refuses a live Gateway lock. The regressions also preserve current-generation, failed/pending/unfinished and cross-manifest historical recovery; filesystem/bookkeeping failures stay advisory in human output, JSON and history, and backward clocks cannot select the triggering capture.

Limits: no full published-stable-driver-to-candidate upgrade or native macOS-app flow was executed in this finishing pass. Sequential terminal updates, production migration fixtures and authenticated Gateway-worker proof are the bounded behavioral evidence. No new local full-build claim is made; exact-head CI owns broad build proof.

### Exact-head CI

All **207** current check/status entries are terminal: **136 SUCCESS**, **70 SKIPPED**, **1 NEUTRAL**; no pending/failing entries. Required `openclaw/ci-gate` check and commit status both pass. `openclaw/dependency-review` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` commit statuses pass on this exact head. [CI run 39881117535](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39881117535), attempt **2**, reports `head_sha` equal to the validated head and `conclusion: success`; both exact-head build-artifacts jobs pass.

Infrastructure recovery: attempt 1's [Android Access 4096 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39881117535/job/120178976493) failed while `sdkmanager` downloaded/unpacked Google's API 36 system image: `Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel`. It never reached Gradle/application tests; the missing-report upload error was consequential. After inspecting the raw log and allowing the original run to settle, one targeted `gh run rerun 39881117535 --job 120178976493 --repo openclaw/openclaw` recovered that job and dependent gates on the unchanged SHA. All other original CI jobs passed. No code changes, baseline exemptions, broad reruns or blind retries were used. An earlier mid-run retry was refused (`job ... cannot be rerun`) and did not execute.

The final ClawSweeper review of this SHA reports **no correctness or security findings**. It still requests broader fresh-install / v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade evidence; that scenario is not claimed here. The touched contracts have production migration, historical V2 receipt, preserved-current-SQLite, sequential update and authenticated worker proof above. There is no schema migration in this PR. The broader release scenario remains a disclosed proof limitation, not an invented successful result.

prs.title: refactor: fold private callback and presentation frames into their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several internal preparation and presentation steps still expose a separate module or parameter/result frame to exactly one production consumer.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Public plugin SDK, CLI, configuration, protocol, authentication, migration, and memory-backend contracts remain unchanged; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the private work with its existing owner: embedding adapters, the Hermes planner, Kimi's sanitizer, the OAuth wrapper, QA artifact/CLI handling, and status presentation. Remove the redundant argument/result packets and three single-consumer modules rather than introduce new abstractions. Preserve lazy imports and every existing validation, authority, cleanup, and error-reporting boundary.

The embedding and Hermes tests now exercise their public adapter/planner entry points instead of the retired helpers. Additional OAuth wrapper cases protect delayed manual entry and the rendered Homebrew certificate repair path.

Net production reduction: **154 lines** (+390/-544 across 11 production paths). Tests grow by 124 lines (+194/-70); no assertion, timeout, retry, skip, suppression, or allowance was weakened. Phase E standalone session memory and its machinery/tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No guards or supported behavior were removed; this cut only retires private single-consumer frames.

## Evidence

Preservation tests passed before the embedding, Hermes, and OAuth production folds, then were rerun afterward. prs.title: fix: restore error messages dropped by Bun bare-header stacks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: user-visible diagnostic messages (version resolution failures, help display errors, unhandled rejections, main-session recovery warnings) are printed without their error message when the CLI/Gateway runs on Bun.

Bun's GC can materialize `Error#stack` with a bare header (`"Error\n    at ..."`) that drops the message V8-style stacks carry. Diagnostic paths that read `error.stack ?? error.message` then render a stack with no message, hiding what actually failed.

## User Impact

User impact: failures on Bun report the actual error message again; stacks that already embed the message are unchanged. Node-only installs are unaffected (their stacks already carry the message).

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical fix already exists upstream as `formatErrorStackWithMessage` in `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.ts` (upstream PR #172774, already merged into base, already used by `formatUncaughtError`). This PR routes the remaining `src/` production `stack ?? message` reads through that helper: on a bare-header stack it restores `"Name: message"` and keeps the rest verbatim; otherwise it returns the stack/message exactly as before, so every replacement is equivalent-or-strictly-better.

`node-runtime-recovery.mjs` mirrors the helper inline because the pre-compile bootstrap cannot import compiled packages; the inline copy is byte-for-byte consistent with the canonical implementation and the file header documents the dependency constraint.

The 5 extension call sites (reached via the plugin-sdk error seam) still use the old expression; fixing them requires widening a frozen plugin-sdk export surface, so they are tracked as a follow-up for the next stable cycle rather than included here.

## Evidence

- Helper unit tests (5 cases) cover: bare-header restore, V8-style stack unchanged, custom error name on a bare header, no-name-line prefix, and no-stack fallback — `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.test.ts`.
- `unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts` uses an independent bare-header fixture (`"Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"`) and asserts the exact restored output instead of re-applying the production formatter (ClawSweeper Tests feedback); all 12 tests pass.
- Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (`11d0c854192`); branch head is `58f53d53c9c`.
- Red-on-base/green-on-head on the revised registry test: HEAD passes 12/12; with `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`, the same test fails with the bare `Error` header (`1 failed | 11 passed`), exactly the regression this PR fixes.
- Shipped Gateway proof: the built `dist/index.js` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`) loads a standalone plugin through `plugins.load.paths`; the plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws a bare-header-stack error, and the migrated `diagnostic-events` reporter prints `Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded` with the frame preserved. Full output above.
- Type/lint/format on the 14 changed files: oxlint 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; fallback `tsc` reports no diagnostics in any changed file. The repo `tsgo` wrapper could not run in this checkout because the local install predates the `tsrs` dependency; CI's production and test type lanes cover that gap.
- CI on `58f53d53c9c`: all product checks pass except two unrelated failures. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-4` times out in the untouched `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-transcript.test.ts`; the same test fails locally with all 12 PR source files reverted to base, so it is pre-existing/environmental. `Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code` fails before scanning with `Error: Missing or ambiguous ios Periphery producer`; this PR changes no iOS/Swift files.
- `security-sensitive-review` / `ci-gate` still require a maintainer approval for the security-sensitive path change (`/allow-security-sensitive-change`); that is an approval step, not an author code action.

### Real behavior proof (Bun, newly migrated reporter)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was proof from a **newly migrated** reporter, not the pre-existing `formatUncaughtError`. This exercises the changed **handler-failure reporter** in `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` end to end: a real Bun process imports the real module, registers a handler that throws a bare-header-stack error (the exact shape Bun's GC materializes, per the `error-coercion.ts` docstring), installs the real `unhandledRejection` handler, and triggers a genuine rejection, so the changed `catch` block formats the thrown error through `formatErrorStackWithMessage`.

Runtime: Bun 1.4.3, Linux x64. Driver (uncommitted temp script): installs the real listener, registers a throwing handler, then runs `Promise.reject(new Error("orphaned background compaction rejected"))`. BASE = `upstream/main` `11d0c854192`, HEAD = this PR `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
## BASE — upstream/main reporter (`err.stack ?? err.message`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20

## HEAD — this PR reporter (`formatErrorStackWithMessage`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20
```

The BASE reporter prints a bare `Error` header with the message dropped; the HEAD reporter restores `Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store` and keeps the stack frames verbatim. Both runs exit 1. This is the revised regression shown failing on the base and passing on the head.

### Real behavior proof (shipped Gateway entry point)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was a newly migrated reporter reached through a shipped CLI/Gateway entry rather than a direct module import. This run uses the built Gateway from this PR (`dist/index.js`, `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`, Node v24.18.0) and a standalone plugin enabled through `plugins.load.paths`. The plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws an error whose `stack` is the exact bare-header shape Bun materializes (`"Error\n    at ..."`), then emits a real `webhook.received` diagnostic event. The migrated `diagnostic-events` listener-error reporter formats the caught error:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:39.991+08:00 [diagnostic-events] listener error type=webhook.received seq=79: Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded
    at pluginDiagnosticListener (diagnostic-failure-plugin.cjs:10:13)
```

The same Gateway process loaded the plugin and shut down cleanly:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:40.066+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (1 plugin: diagnostic-failure-plugin; 11.0s)
2026-10-20T09:59:42.179+08:00 [gateway] [shutdown] completed cleanly in 162ms
```

Command (isolated HOME/state/config; plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` and enabled through `plugins.entries`):

```bash
OPENCLAW_HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 \
  node dist/index.js gateway --port 19031 --bind loopback
```

### Red-on-base / green-on-head (revised registry test)

HEAD `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
$ pnpm test src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

Same test file with only `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`:

```text
FAIL  src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts > process error handlers > continues past declining and throwing handlers, then stops at the first claim
- Expected: "Error: bare header message\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
+ Received: "Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

### Real behavior proof (Bun, pre-existing formatter surface)

Bun-run real behavior on the pre-compile `src/infra/errors.ts` public `formatUncaughtError` surface (already migrated before this PR), feeding the exact bare-header stack shape and comparing against the old `err.stack ?? err.message` expression:

```text
runtime: bun 1.4.3
error.message: "version resolution failed"
error.stack: "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

BEFORE — old expression `err.stack ?? err.message`:
  "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

AFTER — production formatUncaughtError (formatUncaughtError -> formatErrorStackWithMessage):
  "Error: version resolution failed\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"
```

Unit tests for the helper run under both Node and Bun (identical string logic, runtime-independent).

prs.title: fix: keep starting while an inherited auth owner prepares
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A PostgreSQL Gateway can fail startup when an admitted agent inherits auth from an owner whose database inspection is still pending.

Supersedes #180632 (thanks @ceckert).
Closes #180631.

## User Impact

This is the regression-only baseline for the fix. Production code is unchanged; the pending-owner tests are intentionally expected to fail before the repair is added. This PR must not merge in this state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The real PostgreSQL regression blocks the owner's schema inspection, starts the Gateway, sends a model turn using the admitted agent's own credential, then releases inspection and requires inherited credentials to arrive through the existing admission-completion refresh. No production polling or explicit model refresh is added. Reader controls preserve genuine admission, schema, and read failures and existing SQLite behavior.

## Evidence

- [Baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888160537): pending-owner reader regression is RED on unchanged production; 15 sibling cases pass, including SQLite and genuine-error controls. PG shards 1 and 2 passed. PG shard 3 found a fixture close outside synchronous admission before Gateway startup; this is not a product RED. The reviewed fixture correction in `ded9231e7a0a` closes seeded native handles under admission before async drainage; the [corrected baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891188653) timed out in the real-PG fixture after 90 seconds, without a verified Gateway failure. The timeout came from omitting the CLI readiness preflight that creates the five-second deferral scheduler. The reviewed correction in `48a92301e0bd` now invokes that preflight and waits for normal chat readiness while the owner remains locked. [Current baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894580308) is running. The current baseline now proves the real-PG product RED: the Gateway startup regression fails in 49.975 seconds with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError`, code `agent-database-inspection-pending`, through the PostgreSQL auth reader. A separate local real-Gateway run reproduced the same pending-owner startup rejection. The pending-only repair and automatic-recovery proof are in progress.
- Local PostgreSQL schema and migration preflight passed, but the local test worker stalled before test entry under both available runtimes. No product verdict is claimed from those attempts. CI PostgreSQL shards will establish the real Gateway baseline.
- Independent Codex review precedes the baseline commit. Local lint is blocked by a pre-existing artifact-owner lock, left untouched; CI owns that check.

Release-note context after the repair: PostgreSQL Gateways keep starting with admitted agents' own credentials while an inherited auth owner is still preparing, then add inherited credentials when the existing admission owner completes.

prs.title: perf: keep the New Session composer out of Chat boot
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Chat imports the accepted-composer registry from the New Session composer module, so opening an existing conversation also downloads the composer class and attachment draft. Move the existing registry unchanged into `creation-composer-registry.ts`, with type-only imports of the composer. All three runtime consumers use that boundary; only New Session imports the class. Accepted initial turns, attachment custody, recovery, and account-change disposal retain their existing behavior.

The registry remains the single owner of accepted composers. This changes module reachability, not state authority or rendering. Reuse the existing submission-handoff type to keep the submission owner within its file-size limit. No markup, dependencies, or lazy route boundaries change.

## Matched boot measurement

Exact baseline: `35637f41d8207bd58409304d8ba778b4a7d3e2bd`. Candidate runtime: `de72a012558fa550f72ef8bd59b3dfa924db3ab3`; final commit `35965659ffc21bca4b8221a95a39e2bd08927045` only updates budget constants/comments and the baseline reason. Both production builds used the same machine, Node 26.12.1, fixed build metadata, dependency tree, and 29 canonical plugin inputs. The strict performance comparison reports zero warnings and zero violations. Standalone module attribution confirms `creation-composer.ts` and `attachment-draft.ts` leave Chat boot; module gzip estimates are diagnostic, not additive. The campaign's full graph attribution is in #181052.

| Surface | Base gzip B | Candidate gzip B | Change | JS requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup | 316,324 | 316,294 | −30 | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,349,072 | 1,347,441 | −1,631 | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 823,291 | 822,816 | −475 | 17 → 17 |

CSS is unchanged: startup 41,128 B / 1 request, Chat 145,939 B / 8 requests, New Session 106,449 B / 6 requests. No boot surface grows.

Caps preserve incoming relative headroom: `ceil(1347441 × 1400431 / 1349072) = 1398738` for Chat and `ceil(822816 × 834356 / 823291) = 833875` for New Session. The stricter 315,881 B startup baseline is unchanged; its reason is refreshed through `--update-baseline --startup-js-bytes 315881 --reason`.

## Validation

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| UI typecheck on integrated candidate | Pass |
| `creation-composer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 7/7 pass; existing acceptance, custody, reconnect, and disposal assertions retained |
| Targeted lint and formatting / diff check | Pass; final cap files formatted |
| Matched production builds and strict performance comparison | Pass; values above |
| Production Knip on final candidate | One inherited unused file, `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs`; identical diagnostic from the same production command on exact base `35637f41d8207bd58409304d8ba778b4a7d3e2bd` |
| Simplification and isolated autoreview | Registry logic moved unchanged; integration and final cap-inclusive reviews scoped-clean at P0–P2 |
| Full PR CI | Current-head [39893048501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893048501), with `ci:full`: 46 jobs passed, 24 skipped; sole real-Gateway failure plus aggregate gate. The exact session-PR reader case also fails on [scheduled main 39890895258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890895258), at the same line 465 title assertion (replacement workspace expected, null received); inherited-failure route. |
| Cold-load timing | Pass on exact final head: ten interleaved cold-cache pairs; median and p95 gates pass (details below) |

Timing acceptance, fixed before the run: ten interleaved baseline/head cold-cache pairs, 240 synthetic messages, using the committed cold-load benchmark without tracing. Transcript-visible and enabled-composer median regression must each be ≤5%, and neither p95 may worsen. One further ten-pair batch is allowed if needed; all twenty pairs then count. Both exact revisions must use the same host and fixed inputs, with CPU/RAM/Node and host load recorded.

No visual screenshot pair is needed for this source import split: no JSX, markup, classes, CSS, or visible state changes. Production TypeScript LOC: 2,053 → 2,060 (+7); direct tests: 269 → 266 (−3); generated boot manifest: 1,851 → 1,852 (+1). The added lines form the import boundary; the registry implementation itself is unchanged.

Refactor-checklist census across the five touched production modules is unchanged: `createEffect`, `createRenderEffect`, `untrack`, direct listeners, DOM queries, and Solid owner/flush APIs are all 0 → 0. Existing `listen` calls are 8 → 8 and `onCleanup` is 1 → 1. The textual `flush()` occurrence belongs to the existing panel-action owner, not Solid's flush API. This performance-only extraction adds no reactive or lifecycle mechanism.

## Cold-load timing result

[Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893356770), lease `tbx_01m5kbnhcyj0cwam3wc1s03eba`: requested the existing check profile; observed AMD EPYC with 4 available CPUs and 16,555,134,976 B RAM, Node 24.22.1. prs.title: improve: make large chat session switches more responsive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching back to a large chat repeated transcript preparation and invalidated layout and style in the session header, sidebar, and composer.

## User Impact

Returning to recent sessions is faster while keeping the existing three-pane retention bound, Markdown cache, virtualized rows, and Gateway request behavior. Selected sidebar titles retain their active color/background and use the same 500 weight as other titles; text color changes immediately while the existing background transitions remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep prepared transcript rows across parking and invalidate only rows that consume changed presentation, tool-roster, question-generation, or retry-action facts. Retained video previews follow the presentation owner. Preserve the roster pagination button, stop enumerating the entire drawer for initial focus, defer marquee measurement until its existing dwell delay, and avoid a style flush through `document.fonts.ready`. Narrow two `:has()` rules and remove unavailable versions-menu hosts so session switches do not dirty unrelated layout.

No cache, dependency, state owner, or lazy boundary was added. The benchmark fixture now supplies the valid empty `progressCard.get` response for both revisions.

Acceptance: the committed `session-switch` workload, two retained 400-message sessions, desktop/mobile, ten interleaved baseline/head pairs, task medians at most 200/300 ms, no p95 regression. prs.title: fix(telegram): multiline directive commands drop the task after the first line
prs.body:
Closes #141998

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users sending a multiline text directive would have the task silently discarded. Sending

```
/think high
summarize the release notes
```

in a Telegram DM set the thinking level but never delivered `summarize the release notes` to the agent — the model received only the bare directive, with no indication that a line had been dropped.

#138545 fixed this at the core boundary, but the fix could not take effect on Telegram: the tail was already gone before the core ever saw the message. Channels that pass raw text through were unaffected, which is why this survived as a Telegram-only gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram inbound projection called `normalizeCommandBody(rawBody, …)` without `preserveArguments`. Without that option the helper cuts the text at the first newline and applies a per-command tail policy that keeps the tail only for `skill`, `learn`, and `reset` — every other command, including text directives such as `/think`, drops it. That truncated value becomes `ctx.CommandBody`, which the core prefers as `commandText`, so the `preserveArguments` re-normalization added in #138545 was handed `/think high` with the task already removed.

The ingress projection now passes `preserveArguments: true`, matching the option the core boundary already uses for text-slash directives.

Non-goals, and what deliberately did **not** change:

- **Native argument ownership stays strict.** The strict command view is recomputed independently at the core layer without `preserveArguments` (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-context.ts:44`, `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-command.ts:255`), so the per-command tail policy — including the `reset` flatten from #117143 — still applies there. This change only widens what the directive pipeline is able to see.
- No command was renamed, and command detection is untouched: `hasControlCommand` is computed upstream from the raw body, not from this projection.

## User Impact

Telegram users can send a directive and its task in one message and have both take effect:

```
/think high
summarize the release notes
```

now sets thinking to `high` **and** passes `summarize the release notes` to the agent, matching the behavior other channels already had. No configuration change is required, and no existing single-line command behavior changes.

## Evidence

New regression test: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.command-multiline.test.ts`, driving the real `buildTelegramMessageContext` harness and asserting on the `CommandBody` the core consumes.

**Before the fix** — three of four cases fail for the reported reason (tail dropped at ingress):

```
AssertionError: expected '/think high' to be '/think high\nsummarize the release notes'
  /think high
- summarize the release notes

AssertionError: expected '/reset keep this line' to be '/reset\nkeep this line'

AssertionError: expected '/think high' to be '/think high\nsummarize the release notes'

 Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)
```

**After the fix:**

```
 ✓ preserves the task tail of a multiline text directive
 ✓ preserves the tail raw for /reset so core keeps ownership of flattening
 ✓ still canonicalizes text aliases on the command line
 ✓ leaves single-line commands unchanged

 Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The `/reset` and `/t` cases are there on purpose: they pin that flattening and alias canonicalization keep working, so preserving the tail at ingress does not quietly relax per-command argument policy.

Regression scope:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src` — **218 files, 4060 tests passed**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/commands-registry.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.levels.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.auth.test.ts` — **67 passed**
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — **exit 0**, including the `typecheck extensions` and `typecheck extension tests` lanes

**Proof gap:** validation is the isolated harness covering the changed path, not a live Telegram client — I do not have bot credentials for the QA lane. Per `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md` this path is command-body projection rather than transport, streaming, topics, callbacks, or reply context, but live confirmation of the `/think high\n<task>` DM would still be stronger proof if a maintainer can run it.

prs.title: fix(plugins): surface dropped prompt-build context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins use `before_prompt_build` to add context that can determine what an agent does next. When that context is dropped, the resulting prompt looks exactly like the plugin had nothing to report. A task or memory plugin can therefore fail while the agent incorrectly concludes that its queue or context is empty.

The silent-loss paths include a handler failure or timeout, a nested prompt build that is prevented from recursively dispatching hooks, a dispatch rejection, and a failure in the later tool-authorized enrichment phase.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime now appends one bounded `<dropped_plugin_context>` marker when a contribution is lost. It identifies the affected plugin and one fixed reason code: `handler-failed`, `nested-prompt-build`, or `dispatch-failed`.

The implementation deliberately preserves existing policy:

- prompt-build hooks remain fail-open;
- surviving plugin contributions still reach the prompt;
- error details remain in operator logs and never enter model context;
- authority-only handlers are reported only by the authorized phase that can actually run them;
- exact raw plugin identities are counted before labels are sanitized and truncated, so display collisions cannot understate the number of losses;
- the marker lists at most five entries and is capped at 640 bytes, with `+N more` accounting for every omitted contribution.

Pre-dispatch preparation failures remain marker-free because no plugin contribution was dispatched or dropped.

## User Impact

Agents can distinguish “the plugin had nothing to add” from “the runtime lost the plugin’s context.” That prevents false empty-queue conclusions and gives the agent a safe recovery instruction without exposing exception text, credentials, endpoints, or plugin-authored prompt injection.

No configuration or public plugin SDK change is introduced.

## Evidence

Current topic head: `2fb1637ed675e9615d92730f9d83087aa58a9485`.

- The complete changed-file gate, config-schema check, Plugin SDK surface check, and unused-file scan passed on that refreshed candidate.
- Focused validation passed 223 tests across four repository-runner shards (12 + 17 + 172 + 22). These are the saved refresh results, not a claim of a new run caused by this description update.
- `scripts/proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` passes all 55 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`). Its CLI scenarios now run inside `withTestRunAdmission`, so the CLI preparation path's own live-authority assertions execute for real rather than being bypassed by a no-audit fixture carrier. It exercises the real hook runner and production embedded, agent-harness, and CLI prompt-consumer functions: healthy contributions, failures/timeouts, nested builds, dispatch rejection, redaction, bounds, hostile identities, and pre-dispatch negative controls.
- Review regressions cover sanitized-label collisions, authority-only nested hooks, and failed authorized enrichment.
- `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` passes all 26 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`, four consecutive runs). It closes the installed-plugin and provider-edge gap described below: the fixture plugins are installed through `installPluginFromPath` (the entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses), loaded by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins` through the loader's real conversation-hook consent gate, and the assertions are made on the **stdin of a real spawned provider process**, not on a returned value.

### Installed-plugin proof at the outgoing provider request

The earlier proof boundary — constructed registrations and a returned prompt value — is now closed by a second harness, `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts`.

**What is real.** Each fixture plugin is packaged on disk and installed through `installPluginFromPath` (`src/plugins/install.ts`), the same programmatic entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses; the install really validates the package, and the run asserts a committed artifact exists before proceeding. The plugins are then discovered and registered by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins`. The loader's own consent gate applies unchanged: `before_prompt_build` is a conversation hook, so a non-bundled plugin does **not** register without `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess`. The harness sets that key in its own isolated config the way an operator would, rather than bypassing the gate.

**Where the request is observed.** One installed fixture registers a CLI backend via `api.registerCliBackend` whose `command` is a small recorder process. `runCliAgent` then runs end to end, and `resolvePromptInput` (`src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`) routes the assembled prompt to that process's stdin under `input: "stdin"`. The runtime performs a real spawn, so the recorder's stdin is literally the request that left the process. Substituting the provider binary is the stub at the very edge; every step between the installed plugin's handler and that spawn is production code.

**Isolation.** `OPENCLAW_HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` are redirected to a fresh temporary tree before any OpenClaw module is imported, which is why every import in the harness is dynamic. Installs, state, and sessions land in that tree, a configured install is never read or written, and the tree is removed on exit.

**Scenarios and results** (26 assertions, `EXIT 0`):

1. **Healthy-only turn** — the installed plugin's block and the user's ask are both in the outgoing provider request, and there is **no** loss notice. This is the negative control the review asked for by name.
2. **Installed healthy/throwing pair** — the throwing plugin raises an error carrying credential-shaped text. The outgoing provider request retains the healthy plugin's content, carries **exactly one** notice (384 bytes, within the 640-byte cap) naming `proof-throwing (handler-failed)`, contains **no** exception text, does not contain the dropped plugin's own block, and does not blame the healthy plugin.
3. **Bounded under load** — one healthy plus seven throwing installed plugins: still exactly one notice, five plugins named, `+2 more`, 515 bytes, healthy content retained, no exception text.

The outgoing provider request captured verbatim in scenario 2:

```
<plans_and_tasks><ready_issues><issue id='openclaw-beads-201'/></ready_issues></plans_and_tasks>

latest ask

<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">
The runtime dropped this turn's before_prompt_build contribution from proof-throwing (handler-failed).
That context is MISSING from this prompt, not empty — do not read its absence as "nothing to report" (for example, an empty task or work queue). Re-read anything you need from its source before acting.
</dropped_plugin_context>
```

**The proof can fail.** Run unchanged against pristine `origin/main` (`38c3edcc4caf692bbb9ff0078bda002587528036`, which has no `src/plugins/prompt-build-drop.ts`), the harness completes scenario 1 green — including `healthy: content is RETAINED`, so the fix is shown not to alter healthy behavior — and then fails at `pair: outgoing provider request carries EXACTLY ONE loss notice`, `EXIT 1` after 9 checks. That failure is the silent drop this PR fixes, observed at the provider boundary.

### Line-cap ratchet: coherent extraction (September 18, 2026)

The previous head grew three already-over-cap files, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` rejects *growth against a grandfathered baseline*, not absolute size. Three cohesive extractions erase that growth without touching behavior or coverage:

- `src/plugins/hooks-prompt-build.ts` — both `before_prompt_build` dispatch phases (ordinary and tool-authorized), the `AsyncLocalStorage` nesting token, and the loss collection they share. The hook runner injects its merger, its registration list, and its modifying-hook dispatcher, so the new module never imports back into `hooks.ts` and `check-import-cycles` still reports 0 runtime value cycles.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/hook-prompt-build.ts` — the CLI's two prompt-build hook resolutions, including this PR's deliberate asymmetry: preparation failures stay marker-free, dispatch failures become the bounded marker.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.prompt-build-drop.test.ts` — the five CLI drop-marker tests, moved verbatim beside the existing `prepare.context-window` / `durable-context` / `model-routing-authority` / `rooted-execution` siblings. No assertion was weakened or deleted.

Counted lines (oxlint `max-lines` with `skipBlankLines`/`skipComments`, the measurement the gate itself uses) against the baseline each file is ratcheted to:

| File | Before | After | Baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 6872 | **6721** | 6736 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | 2361 | **2325** | 2353 |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | 1397 | **1289** | 1364 |

Neither new module nor the new test file reports a `max-lines` diagnostic. CI confirms it: `Line-cap ratchet OK: 19 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`

**Behavior and coverage preserved, measured rather than asserted.** The *unmodified* `prepare.test.ts` from the previous head passes **191/191** against the extracted production code; the reduced file passes **186/186** and the five moved tests pass **5/5** in their new home (186 + 5 = 191). Both proof harnesses still pass on the new head — `proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` 55/55 and `proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` 26/26, both `EXIT 0`. `pnpm check:changed` is `EXIT 0` across every lane, including the core/extensions/scripts oxlint shards and the Knip dead-export and unused-file scans.

The earlier partial-gate failure and old-head evidence are superseded by the successful refresh checks above. No unrelated CI failure is being claimed as fixed by this PR.

---

prs.title: fix(gateway): run CLI bridge tool calls in their own run's request scope
prs.body:
## Current disposition — October 11, 2026

The implementation in this PR has been incorporated into main by [#165432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165432), commit `fdcbcf5c2ebd83316f411d406315f08225949c59`, which credits Amrit Chana and adapts this PR's authority-chain regression. There is no remaining production fix to merge from this branch.

Current main uses a detached process context for listener startup, retains the Gateway's worker resources, records each grant's minting request scope, and restores that scope for its tool calls. Its HTTP coverage checks starter isolation, fresh replacement scopes, allowed owner dispatch, the write-only ceiling, closed requester refusal, and revoked-grant rejection.

Fresh verification on main `cbe0b272883c68210aee33b67e4bdf66d9106587`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts` passed **6/6 tests** on macOS/Node 24.16.0. Vitest reported **221.45 s**, including cold transformation. This was HTTP/in-process authority boundary proof, not a new live Claude or channel test. No production or test changes were needed.

The v2026.10.1 tag predates the merged detached-context implementation, so the release-pinned follow-up remains relevant to that tag. The original branch's old CI/conflict state is historical; rebasing it would duplicate the implementation and weaker coverage already on main. This PR remains open and non-draft for maintainer disposition; no merge or closure was requested or performed.

---

## Original contributor proposal and historical evidence

Closes #157126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart that resumes an in-flight CLI-runtime turn (for example `claude-cli`), the owner's later chat turns fail admin-only tools with `missing scope: operator.admin` until the Gateway restarts again. The same leak also breaks a second owner turn once the first turn's connection has closed (`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching ...`).

## User Impact

User impact: owners of CLI-runtime agents keep their normal tool authority after a restart. Admin-only tools (automations with triggers, secrets, system and config tools) work from chat again. Lower-authority runs keep their own ceiling: the write-only restart-recovery run is still refused admin tools, and a run whose device was revoked mid-turn is still refused before its action. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loopback MCP listener is process-owned but starts lazily inside whichever Gateway request first needs it. Its handlers kept that request's scope and tool-caller identity. So every bridge tool call ran with the authority of whichever run started the listener, not the run making the call. If the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) started it, every later owner call was capped at `operator.write`.

The fix has two parts:

1. **The listener no longer inherits its starter.** It starts outside the tool-caller identity (`withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`) and outside the request scope (`withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver(..., { inheritRequestScope: false })`), keeping only the Gateway context resolver. This matches the rule already applied to follow-up and scheduled runs.
2. **Each bridge call runs in its own run's request scope.** A CLI client grant now records the Gateway request scope it was minted in (`mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant`, called while the run's request is active), and the handler re-enters that scope for the grant's tool calls. That is what in-process runtimes already get implicitly, so dispatch sees the calling run's own client: its scopes stay the ceiling, and its `hasCurrentClientAuthority` liveness still applies.

Part 1 alone would have removed the accidental ceiling without restoring the intended one. With no scope, a write-only recovery run and a revoked run both completed an admin-only call in live testing. Part 2 is why those runs are still refused (see the proof below).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Setup.** This PR's branch at `3ff6fbe1d78`, built, running as an isolated foreground Gateway (`openclaw --profile <test> gateway run`, loopback, its own state dir, clean environment). macOS arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw `2026.9.6 (3ff6fbe)`. Agent `main` runs `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5`. Owner turns come from `openclaw agent --agent main` on a local CLI device paired with `operator.admin` (`senderIsOwner: true`). The admin-only action is the `secrets` tool with `action: "list"` (`secrets.store.list`, needs `operator.admin`). Heartbeat, Bonjour, and dreaming are off, so no other system run can start the bridge first.

Steps:
1. **step0**: owner turn on a fresh Gateway calls `secrets` list.
2. **step0b**: a second owner turn in the same process.
3. **step1**: an owner turn runs a 90 s probe script, then calls `secrets` list. Mid-probe the Gateway is restarted (`gateway restart --wait 5s`). The drain runs out, the turn is marked for recovery, and the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) is the first CLI run after startup, so it starts the bridge. It then calls `secrets` list itself.
4. **step2**: after recovery settles, a new owner turn calls `secrets` list.
5. **step3** (fresh Gateway process): an owner turn runs the probe, and 5 s in the owner device's operator token is revoked (`devices revoke --role operator`, connection closed `4001 device removed`). After the probe, the run calls `secrets` list.

Results are the exact tool results the agent received, from the Claude Code stream in the Gateway log and `chat.history`. The "unpatched" column is the same checkout with `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` reverted to `6907f58b136` (upstream main) and rebuilt. "Part 1 only" is this PR's first commit, `3b3536613b4`.

| Step | Caller | Unpatched main | Part 1 only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| step0 | owner | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step0b | owner, 2nd turn | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step1 | restart recovery (system, write-only) | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`missing scope: operator.admin`** |
| step2 | owner, after recovery | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`The secret store is empty.`** |
| step3 | owner, device revoked mid-run | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.`** |

On unpatched main, step1 and step3 are refused only because each of those runs happened to start the bridge itself. On this PR they are refused by their own run's scope, whichever run started the listener.

Restart and recovery on this PR (Gateway log, local time, redacted):

```text
17:37:19.641 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:37:56.086 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
17:38:01.088 [gateway] restart drain budget 4999.5ms exhausted; cutting short queueSize=1 embeddedRuns=1 activeTasks=1 sessionAdmissions=2 rootRequests=1
17:38:01.129 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (gateway restart shutdown)
17:38:05.456 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:38:05.460 [main-session-restart-recovery] started interrupted main session: agent:main:main
```

`secrets` tool results on this PR, in order (step0, step0b, recovery, step2):

```text
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":"missing scope: operator.admin","is_error":true
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
```

The refused call belongs to the recovery turn: in `chat.history` it follows the `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart ...` continuation message, and step2's owner turn after it succeeds.

step3 on this PR (device revoked mid-run):

```text
17:41:27.494 [gateway] device token revoked device=<device-id> role=operator
17:41:27.495 [ws] → close code=4001 reason=device removed ... lastFrameMethod=agent
17:42:54.300 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5 durationMs=102068
"tool_result","content":"Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.","is_error":true
```

**Differences from the issue's scenario.** Owner turns come from the local CLI (`openclaw agent`, a device with `operator.admin`), not Control UI webchat. The restart is the supported foreground restart (`gateway restart --wait 5s`, in-process SIGUSR2 with a 5 s drain), not a LaunchAgent handoff. The admin-only tool is `secrets` list only.

### Tests

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts`:
  - "does not retain the Gateway caller of the request that started it": the listener started inside a write-only request scope and a tool-caller identity; a later owner-token call sees neither, and the Gateway context resolver is preserved. Fails before part 1.
  - "runs each CLI grant's tool calls in the request scope that minted it": the listener is started under a write-only recovery scope; grants minted under an owner scope, under the recovery scope, and under no scope each see exactly their own client (`[owner, recovery, undefined]`). Fails without part 2 (`[undefined, undefined, undefined]`).
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/mcp-http src/gateway/mcp-grant-store src/agents/cli-runner/prepare`: 275 of 276 pass. The one failure, `mcp-http.keepalive.test.ts` › "keeps a GET notification stream alive and releases it during shutdown", fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` at `6907f58`.

prs.title: fix(qa): verify subagent handoffs in order on the visible transcript branch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The source-checkout QA runner could time out when transcript metadata appeared between a child’s successful completion and the assistant’s reply. An answer recorded before the child’s result must still be rejected, even if a legacy transcript reuses an entry ID.

## User Impact

The check accepts a reply across intervening metadata only when public session history shows that same assistant message, with matching ID and text. This changes the QA runner only. Agent runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check follows the same transcript branch as session history. From the expected child’s successful completion to the reply, every step must move forward in stored order, within the same turn. Checking just the two endpoints would miss a link that runs backward between them.

## Evidence

In the [scheduled QA job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39724512539/job/119647320029), the requester’s transcript recorded an assistant reply 1.8 seconds after settlement, with two metadata entries in between. We don’t know what public history returned when the check timed out.

On base `6676ef1f`, the [new SQLite regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b108783b4b224342dae68780100efa74e9b59b9f/extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-session.test.ts#L96) failed its positive case: it expected the delivered reply and got `undefined`. On this head, all 51 tests in the two complete affected files passed. 34 local history cases passed.

The stock source-checkout QA suite passed `subagent-handoff` once in 38 seconds with a real Gateway and a local mock provider. The child settled at row 13, directly linked through `custom` metadata at row 14 to the assistant reply at row 15; the actual public `chat.history` reply matched that transcript reply’s ID and text. This run exercised one metadata entry; it did not recreate the historical two-entry sequence.

To reproduce with a prepared source checkout and the default local mock fixture:

```sh
OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1 pnpm openclaw qa suite --runner host --transport qa-channel --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario subagent-handoff --concurrency 1
```

Type-aware lint, a focused strict TypeScript check, and the complete affected private QA host and plugin build passed. The full cross-platform local artifact was not built.
