prs.title: fix(telegram): release account throttlers for retired bot tokens
prs.body:
Related: gap finding `gap-telegram-throttler-token-leak` (hot-update token rotation / repeated account add-remove, evidence level A — real Gateway process logs + unit/integration tests)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: rotating a Telegram bot token or removing a Telegram account leaks the old token's limiter — Bottleneck heartbeat timers and memory grow monotonically until the Gateway is restarted.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now rotate bot tokens and remove Telegram accounts on a long-running Gateway without leaked Bottleneck heartbeat timers and cache entries accumulating for every retired token; the retirement runs inside the Gateway process on the config hot-reload stop, settling queued sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions before disconnecting the old token's limiter while in-flight requests finish. A chat action sleeping in its 401 authorization backoff settles immediately at retirement — for group and DM dispatch alike — and never sends on the retired token. No config or behavior change for steady-state operation; the per-token shared throttling contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` caches one throttler per bot token in a process-global map with no eviction path, and grammY's `apiThrottler()` never exposes its Bottleneck instances, so each retired token left 3 perpetual `setInterval` timers (250 ms reservoir heartbeat + two group auto-cleanup loops) plus its object graph in memory forever. This change mirrors the upstream `apiThrottler()` defaults in an owned factory (`grammy-api-throttler.ts`) so the limiters can be disconnected, and retires the token's throttler in the process that owns the map:

- **Gateway-side retirement:** the CLI lifecycle hooks (`onAccountConfigChanged` / `onAccountRemoved`) never run inside the Gateway that holds the map. All three account lifecycle hooks (config change, removal, `gateway.stopAccount`) now release the throttler once the token is no longer configured for any account. Unchanged-token reloads and manual stops keep the limiter so flood penalty state survives restarts; a shared token used by another account is never released.
- **Settling queued work:** retirement stops admissions first (a `retired` gate rejects later calls on the captured transformer and prevents new group limiter creation), rejects queued group sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions immediately, re-checks retirement after the action pacing sleep and again at the shared final dispatch boundary — including after the 401 authorization backoff, for DM and group actions alike — then `limiter.stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` — queued sends reject with a clear BottleneckError while running sends finish — and only then disconnects, clears the group auto-cleanup intervals, and drops the map entry. Disposal is idempotent. Backing-off group actions stay tracked for retirement settlement until their transport dispatch actually begins, so their callers settle right away instead of waiting out the backoff.
- **Thin channel hooks:** the rotated/removed/stopped release operations live in `account-throttler-lifecycle.ts`; `channel.ts` returns under its 700-line cap.

## Evidence

### Waiting requests settle during retirement (production client, real timers)

A production-client script (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-settlement-169536.mjs`) drives the shipped `account-throttler` module through the real production undici transport (`resolveTelegramTransport` + `createTelegramClientFetch`, the same stack the Gateway uses) against the loopback Bot API stub, with real timers and real Bottleneck. It parks one send in flight, queues a second send behind it, arms the 401 authorization backoff with a group action, parks a second action in that backoff, and retires the token:

```
PROOF live intervals after throttler create: 3
PROOF send A dispatched and held in flight by the stub (3s)
PROOF send B queued behind the in-flight send
PROOF action C failed with 401 (backoff armed)
PROOF action D sleeping in authorization backoff
PROOF releaseAccountThrottler -> true after 1428ms (waits for the in-flight send to finish)
PROOF in-flight send A: fulfilled
PROOF waiting send B:   rejected: This limiter has been stopped.
PROOF backing-off action D: rejected: Telegram throttler for this token has been released
PROOF intervals: after create=3 before release=3 after release=0 (created=3, cleared=3)
PROOF stub sendMessage requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF stub sendChatAction requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF OK: waiting sends and actions settled, in-flight send preserved, intervals reclaimed

=== STUB LOG ===
stub listening on http://127.0.0.1:19877
2026-10-13T02:44:50.265Z  sendMessage      111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T02:44:50.332Z  sendChatAction   111:proof-token  first-action=401
```

The waiting send settles with Bottleneck's "limiter has been stopped", the backing-off action settles immediately with the released error, the in-flight send completes through the real transport after its 3 s hold, all three live intervals are reclaimed, and the stub records exactly one sendMessage and one sendChatAction — no dispatch ever reaches the retired token after retirement. Tokens are synthetic (`111:proof-token`); no credentials appear.

### Real Gateway process (built from this branch, this revision)

A full build of this branch (rebased on current upstream main) was run and the Gateway launched from that build with an isolated state directory and port (`gateway run --port 19876 --auth none`), talking to a local loopback Bot API stub (`apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:19877`). Tokens are synthetic (`111:...`/`222:...`); no credentials appear in the logs. Both retirement paths were driven through the real config hot-reload.

**Rotation with an in-flight reply.** An unpaired DM reached the Gateway; its pairing reply `sendMessage` was held in flight by the stub (3 s). The token was rotated while the reply was still held:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:26.XXXZ  (stub) sendMessage 111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T12:21:04.187+08:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:04.286+08:00 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete
2026-10-13T12:21:27.926+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:27.962+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
2026-10-13T12:21:27.966+08:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.001+08:00 [telegram] [default] starting provider (@proof_bot_222)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.004+08:00 [telegram] Detected bot identity change for account "default" (was 111, now 222); discarding stale update offset 1 and starting fresh.
```

The hot reload deferred until the held `sendMessage` completed, the in-flight request succeeded (no failure logged), and only then did the retirement release the throttler — the "preserve already-running I/O" contract through the real transport client.

**Account removal.** Dropping the whole `channels.telegram` section produced the second release on the same Gateway run:

```
2026-10-13T12:21:30.596+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:30.612+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
```

**Clean token cutover (stub log).** The stub recorded every authenticated request: exactly one `sendMessage` on the retired token (completed after the hold), none on the new token, and no retired-token request after the rotation:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:27.168Z  getUpdates   111:proof-token   <- last long poll by the retired token
2026-10-13T04:21:27.984Z  getMe        222:proof-token   <- restart one second later
```

After rotation no `111:proof-token` request appears again: the retired token stops polling entirely instead of leaking a live long poll — the same leak class this PR eliminates for the throttle limiter.

Full redacted logs in this checkout: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-gateway-169536.log` and `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-stub-169536.log` (driver: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-driver-169536.mjs`, stub: `.openclaw/.tmp/telegram-proof-stub.mjs`).

### Waiting actions settle and never dispatch after retirement (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` regressions for the action lane, covering the retirement windows:

- `settles a pacing action and never dispatches it when the account is retired` — the successor is sleeping out its one-second pacing window when the token is released; its caller settles immediately and the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles actions queued behind a running predecessor when the account is retired` — retirement while the predecessor's dispatch is in flight settles the queued successor immediately; the in-flight I/O completes; the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles a backing-off action immediately when the account is retired` (revised in this revision) — the successor parks in the 401 authorization backoff after pacing; releasing the token during that backoff settles its caller **at release time** (asserted before any further timer advancement), and advancing 10 minutes afterwards still produces no dispatch.
- `never dispatches a DM action whose authorization backoff outlives retirement` (new in this revision) — the DM successor parks in the 401 backoff; retiring during the backoff rejects it with the released error and the final dispatch never reaches the API.

Baseline: both new/revised regressions fail on the pre-fix source (previous commit `ba17964a2af`): the group regression reports `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` (no immediate settlement) and the DM regression reports `promise resolved "true" instead of rejecting` (the retired token dispatched). The low-value `keeps releasing other tokens independent` test was removed per review.

### Queued sends settle on release (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `stops timers and settles queued sends on release`: with the default owned limiter, a second DM send queued behind a running one rejects with `This limiter has been stopped` when the token is released, the live `setInterval` handle set returns to zero (all heartbeats/cleanup timers cleared), and a later call on the captured transformer rejects with `Telegram throttler for this token has been released` without creating new limiters.

### Retire gate blocks queued group sends and fresh work (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `rejects queued group sends and new work once the account is retired`: retirement settles the group sends already queued on the group limiter, rejects a later group send with a clear `BottleneckError`, clears the group engine timers, and a subsequent call on the captured transformer is rejected by the retired gate without creating a new group limiter.

### Before/after timer probe

Probe counting `setInterval`/`clearInterval` against the real code path (`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` + `releaseAccountThrottler`):

```
baseline:                          created=0  cleared=0
after create (1 token entry):      created=3  cleared=2
after 2 rotations (3 entries):     created=9  cleared=6
after releasing all 3 entries:     created=9  cleared=15   (+9 real clears, net 0 leaked timers)
```

Before the fix the same rotation sequence left all 9 timers firing until process exit. The production-client trace above re-confirms the same balance with real timers (`after create=3 … after release=0`).

Behavior parity with upstream grammY defaults is anchored by the pre-existing reservoir tests (e.g. "preserves the group message budget while sending topic actions": 30/msg-min global + 20/msg-min per group chat).

### Local verification on this revision

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/account-throttler.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 23/23; `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/channel.gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 27/27 (includes the restored removal-hook regression `releases the removed account's throttler`); `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 17/17
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: 0 errors; oxlint clean on the changed files; `pnpm format` clean on the changed files
- Ratchets: `check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` OK (channel.ts stays under its baseline) and `check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main` OK
- Branch rebased onto current upstream `main` (`7f4197068b3` at rebase time). The previous head's `checks-node-compact-small-6` failure was an inherited red-main window (duplicate `transcript-entry-anchor.ts` wrapper-inventory entry on main between 12:04–12:36 UTC, fixed upstream by `30b2ef35d02`); the rebase clears it, and the test passes locally (17/17).

### What was not tested

- Live Telegram end-to-end (no real Bot API traffic): the change is transport-independent lifecycle plumbing; the Gateway-process proof above uses a loopback Bot API, the production-client trace uses the real undici transport, and existing HTTP-conformance suites cover the throttling contract.
- Waiting-send settlement and the chat-action lane through the Gateway transport require a model-backed turn (typing keepalives / streamed replies), so they are covered by the production-client trace and the owning-boundary unit regressions above rather than a Gateway run.
- Accepted edge case: after retirement settles a backing-off action's caller, the bounded one-shot backoff timer (≤ 5 min) can still run to completion in the dead scheduler; it finishes into the final dispatch guard and can never send on the retired token. Reaching into the caller's AbortSignal to reclaim that timer would cross the grammY/undici signal-type boundary for a timer that is bounded and harmless.
- Bottleneck running-job completion at stop: `stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` is Bottleneck's documented settlement (drops queued, waits for running); the pinned 2.19.5 source was read to confirm.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `grammy-api-throttler.ts` deep-imports the Bottleneck class from `@grammyjs/transformer-throttler/dist/deps.node.js` (the package has no `exports` map; the repo already deep-imports `dist/` paths in production, e.g. `extensions/slack/src/streaming.ts`). Adding `bottleneck` as a direct dependency was rejected to avoid a lockfile change.
- `dispose` clears the Bottleneck Group auto-cleanup interval through a documented private handle — Bottleneck v2 exposes no public stop API and `Group.disconnect()` only handles shared connections. The dependency is pinned at 2.19.5; a code comment flags this for any future upgrade.
- The final dispatch guard is a shared wrapper (`finalDispatch`) applied to both the DM branch and the group action branch; group actions additionally hand it a `markDispatched` hook so retirement settlement tracking ends exactly when transport I/O begins.
- Maintainer decision noted by ClawSweeper (approve the narrow disposable factory that mirrors upstream quota defaults) is still open for maintainers; this revision addresses the two P2 action-retirement findings, the test cleanup, and the real-behavior proof ask.
</details>

ClawSweeper review: the CLI lifecycle hooks never run inside the Gateway that owns the throttler map, and disconnecting an exhausted reservoir strands queued sends.   re-check retirement after pacing and before the final dispatch, so a

- Restore throttler retirement in onAccountRemoved via a thin delegation

- Annotate the two new type assertions with SAFETY invariants.

* fix(telegram): settle DM chat-action backoff immediately on retire

prs.title: fix: restore missing Telegram replies in conversation context
prs.body:
Related: #166482

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing completed Telegram replies in restored conversation context, which can make an already answered request look pending on a later turn.

## User Impact

Delivered final answers remain beside their questions when the next turn restores conversation context, preventing this source of repeated answers to old requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared recent-text reader discarded confirmed final message-tool replies as delivery bookkeeping. Session-generated chat windows now opt into those replies using the existing terminal-delivery metadata. Native channel windows continue to own their delivery history; progress updates and uncorrelated legacy mirrors remain excluded.

The cache keeps its existing memory-pressure subscription strongly referenced, preserving its behavior on Bun. No SQL schema or storage format changes.

## Evidence

The SQLite → channel-turn → rendered-context regression was reproduced against unchanged production: both prior questions remained while both delivered final answers disappeared, for successful and aborted tool-result cases. The candidate tests retain native-window deduplication and verify that reading context does not rewrite stored history.

The focused regression and sibling checks cover the SQLite history reader, channel context restoration, memory-pressure eviction, native-window deduplication, and prompt-prefix stability. Targeted core lint and formatting checks pass. The independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Broad local checks pass production and test-graph typechecking, but the unused-export scans report unrelated unchanged exports; exact-head PR CI is tracked below.

Against the merge base: production **+9 lines**, tests **+184 lines**, documentation **+6 lines**. The small production increase adds the explicit opt-in and retains the cache subscription; the simplification pass found no useful adjacent deletion without obscuring those responsibilities.

After merging current main, all 87 tests across seven files pass through the repository runner, including its final source-integrity verification (four Vitest shards, 1300.42 seconds). The two SQLite boundary cases fail on the unchanged base and pass with this fix. Exact-head CI is pending after this push.

A prior live Telegram run on `f4c4222c17b9` recorded the delivered answer exactly once in the next accepted model input; details below preserve that evidence and its head. A fresh live channel round trip was not run in this pass because QA broker credentials are unavailable on the test host. This fix addresses one demonstrated cause of repeated recaps, so the broader issue remains related rather than closed.

Thanks to @sobolevbel for the fix and original proof.

<details>
<summary>Previously recorded live Telegram + Codex proof on f4c4222c17b9</summary>

Executed on 2026-10-21 using an isolated Gateway built from `f4c4222c17b9e848042df04eb018eefed480a4d6`, separate OpenClaw state/workspace/port, disabled cron/heartbeat, and the operator's Telegram bot. A human sent both messages from the real Telegram client. The agent used Codex app-server with an existing ChatGPT subscription. No personal conversation history was copied into the test state.

Sanitized launch shape:

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PROOF_STATE" pnpm openclaw gateway run --port "$PROOF_PORT"
```

The two messages were sent in order, waiting for the first answer:

```text
OC179399_TASK_A2. Join the tokens FIXED and 166482 with a colon. Use the message tool with action=send and final=true to send exactly the resulting text to this conversation. Do not send a second visible answer.

OC179399_TASK_B2. A new, unrelated question: what is 2 + 2? Reply with exactly 4.
```

Observed Telegram replies: `FIXED:166482`, then only `4`. The human confirmed both and supplied a screenshot of the two exchanges. Both turns ran in the same Gateway process, with no restart between them.

The read-only transcript extraction checked the successful Telegram receipt and final delivery mirror, then read B2's `message.__openclaw.upstreamUserText`. The Codex integration records this from the text inputs of the accepted native `turn/start` request ([request boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f4c4222c17b9e848042df04eb018eefed480a4d6/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.ts#L297), [transcript annotation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f4c4222c17b9e848042df04eb018eefed480a4d6/extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts#L252)). The full answer was absent from A2's input, so its later presence cannot be explained by replaying the first question.

Redacted terminal output from that extraction:

```json

  "transport": "real Telegram Bot API; human Telegram client",

  },

    "acceptedCodexTurnInputCaptured": true,

```

Accepted B2 input excerpt, with the original mirror ID and timestamp replaced by aliases:

```text

```

The extractor verified that this line refers to the actual A2 delivery-mirror event ID, and counted `FIXED:166482` once across the entire accepted B2 user input. The exactly-once claim concerns this current input and its restored Conversation context, rather than historical tool-call arguments in the native thread.

prs.title: fix(gateway): setup stays busy on every device after a setup wizard is abandoned
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144969

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: setup stays unavailable on every device, with `OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.`, after a client starts a setup or channel wizard and goes away without cancelling it. Only a Gateway restart clears it.

## User Impact

User impact: an abandoned setup wizard releases setup after 25 minutes without client activity, so another device (or the same one, after a reload) can start setup again without restarting the Gateway. A client that comes back to an expired wizard gets the same "not found" answer it already shows as an expired session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A `wizard.start` session holds setup admission until its runner settles, and nothing settles it when the starting client disappears: the session is intentionally not bound to its connection, and only that client knows the session id needed for `wizard.cancel`.

This change gives hosted `wizard.start` sessions a 25-minute idle window, reusing the session's existing expiry timer (`WizardSession` now takes either a fixed `timeoutMs` or a renewable `idleTimeoutMs`). Each `wizard.next` call restarts the window, and so does the step a waiting `wizard.next` receives. Expiry closes the wizard's input the same way closing the Control UI setup window does (`wizard.cancel` with `closeInput`). A configuration write already in progress still finishes, and a channel session left waiting on a prompt after its durable commit is released too. Other `WizardSession` users (provider sign-in, prepare) keep their fixed deadlines. An expired session is removed once its runner settles, so a returning client gets `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND` rather than a generic "wizard not running".

Design note: I chose idle expiry over binding the session to its connection, because setup sessions are deliberately not connection-bound, so a reconnecting client can resume. The tradeoff: a tab left open on a prompt for 25 minutes also expires, and so does a client waiting on a step that takes more than 25 minutes with no progress output; the wizard then has to be started again. A pending `wizard.next` does not count as activity on purpose, because a long-poll left behind by a closed tab would otherwise hold setup forever. A busy-message cancel action, also suggested on the issue, would need UI and protocol changes and is left out of this change.

This builds on the approach of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133848 by @SebTardif (renewable idle timeout on hosted wizards), which was closed for inactivity. Thanks to them for the original design.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163527 (setup runner honors session cancellation) edits the same `wizard.start` session block, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. The two are complementary: with it, idle expiry can also interrupt provider sign-in polling in the setup flow.

## Evidence

Tested at `d762d1fbde3` (base `upstream/main` `f9d5447c594`), the exact head of this PR.

A built Gateway ran on Linux (Node 24) with an isolated home and port, once per side, using the same steps on the channel setup flow the issue reports (`wizard.start` with `flow: "channels"`). Each line is a separate `openclaw gateway call --json` over a new WebSocket connection that closes when the call returns, which matches a Control UI tab closed mid-wizard. Client A opens channel setup and leaves, client B tries at once, nobody touches A's session for 26 minutes, then B tries again and A asks about its own session. The production 25-minute value was not shortened. Each line shows the call time, the method, the CLI's exit code, and the CLI's JSON answer, reduced to its status and error fields.

Before (base `f9d5447c594`):

```text
2026-10-13T03:46:43.404Z wizard.start {"exit":0,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-13T03:46:44.040Z wizard.start {"exit":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","details":{"code":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}}}
2026-10-13T04:12:44.606Z wizard.start {"exit":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","details":{"code":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}}}
2026-10-13T04:12:45.169Z wizard.status {"exit":0,"status":"running","done":null,"step":null}
```

After (this PR):

```text
2026-10-13T04:12:54.600Z wizard.start {"exit":0,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-13T04:12:55.235Z wizard.start {"exit":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","details":{"code":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}}}
2026-10-13T04:38:55.801Z wizard.start {"exit":0,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-13T04:38:56.371Z wizard.status {"exit":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"wizard not found","details":{"code":"WIZARD_NOT_FOUND"}}}
```

Observed result: on the base, 26 minutes after client A left, client B is still refused with `SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY`, and A's abandoned session still reports `running`. With this change, B starts channel setup, and A's expired session answers `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND`. While A's session is live, B is refused on both sides.

Checks: locally, the touched tests, `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (23 tests, 10.4 s wall, vs 22 tests and 10.3 s on the base, both with a warm transform cache) and `pnpm test src/wizard/session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (38 tests, 2.3 s wall), plus `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint, format and the changed-file guards). The three new tests use fake timers and take a few milliseconds each. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

The three new tests fail on the base and pass here: the handler-level test in `wizard.test.ts` (polling renews, idle expiry releases admission, a returning client gets `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND`), and two `WizardSession` tests (the window restarts when a waiting `wizard.next` receives its step, and expiry releases a session parked after `lockCancellation()`).

Not covered: no Control UI browser run. The live run used CLI calls that disconnect after each request, which is the same server path a closed tab takes. The classic setup flow (`flow: "setup"`) shares the same expiry code and is covered by the handler test, not by this live run.

prs.title: fix(telegram): return structured suppressed result when sendMessage is cancelled by hook
prs.body:
Closes #143461

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and automated agents using Telegram would experience transport errors when a `message_sending` hook intentionally cancelled an outbound message. The Telegram action runtime threw a generic Error (`Telegram sendMessage was suppressed before delivery.`), which the Gateway converted into an `UNAVAILABLE` transport failure, discarding the hook's `cancelReason` and causing agents to treat intentional suppressions as channel outages (triggering retry storms and painting healthy scheduled cron runs with `lastRunStatus: error`).

## Why This Change Was Made

When `sendDurableMessageBatch` completes with `status: "suppressed"`, `extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.ts` previously threw a generic `new Error("Telegram sendMessage was suppressed before delivery.")`.

We now return a structured `jsonResult` carrying `{ ok: true, messageId: "suppressed", status: "suppressed", deliveryStatus: "suppressed", reason: durableResult.reason, cancelReason, receipt }`. This matches the direct-delivery contracts used by core (`message.ts`), preserving the suppression reason and hook effect without raising false transport errors or confusing callers into retrying.

## User Impact

Scheduled runs and agents whose messages are intentionally filtered or deduplicated by `message_sending` hooks receive a clean suppressed status with the exact suppression/cancel reason, avoiding retry loops and false job error statuses.

## Evidence

- Added unit tests to `extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`:
  - Verified structured suppressed result containing `reason`, `cancelReason`, and `receipt` when cancelled by a hook.
  - Verified structured suppressed result when suppressed without `cancelReason`.
- Vitest results:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`: 131/131 passed.
  - `src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.plugin-dispatch.test.ts`: 21/21 passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary agent turns and `agent exec` can silently read the wrong prompt when `--message-file` names a file with leading or trailing spaces and a trimmed-name neighbor exists.

## User Impact

Quoted, nonblank message-file paths are opened exactly as supplied. Whitespace-only options remain invalid, and only the exact `agent exec --message-file -` value selects stdin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both input adapters trimmed the path before opening it. They now use the existing `readNonBlankString` helper, which checks for blank input without changing the filename. The tests create both filenames with different contents, so opening the neighboring file cannot pass. Nearby single-use aliases and a wrapper were removed while preserving their behavior.

Thanks to @Alix-007 for the original fix and reproduction.

## Evidence

- Regressions fail on the current-main baseline: `agent exec` returns the neighboring file's prompt, and ordinary Gateway dispatch receives that same wrong file's content. Both pass with this fix; the existing symlink case also passes.
- Targeted owner regressions pass: both literal filename paths, the symlink sibling, and blank-target rejection. The existing `/compacting` sibling remains an unresolved load-sensitive local timeout: it passed on base in 102.886 seconds and timed out on the candidate at 120.147 seconds. Its lazy session-worker routing path is unchanged; no timeout or assertion was weakened.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-count checks, and `git diff --check` passed on the reviewed candidate. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. `check-changed` completed the selected core and test typechecks; its remaining repository-wide coercion scan was not completed.

prs.title: fix(config): report invalid config on PostgreSQL state instead of a main-thread read failure
prs.body:
Closes #180686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with state on PostgreSQL, an invalid `openclaw.json` makes `openclaw gateway run` exit 1 with "Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker ..." instead of reporting the config issue and exiting 78 as SQLite does.

## User Impact

An operator who mistypes or migrates config on a PostgreSQL deployment is told the database connection failed and goes looking at `database.postgres.connection` and the server. The real config issue (for example `agents.ownership`) is never shown. With this change, PostgreSQL reports the same issue and exit code 78 as SQLite. Valid configs and SQLite state are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

For an invalid config, `readConfigSnapshot` collects legacy issues before any plugin metadata snapshot exists. `collectInvalidConfigLegacyIssues` derives the plugin registry synchronously (`collectDoctorConfigRepairPluginIds` → `loadPluginManifestRegistryForPluginRegistry` → ... → `readBundledDiscoveryMode`), and that derivation reads the `plugins.bundledDiscovery` machine state on the main thread. SQLite allows that read; a PostgreSQL Gateway refuses it, and the refusal escapes as the CLI failure.

The valid-config path already avoids this. `io.plugin-metadata.ts` prepares the machine state with `preparePluginMetadataMachineStateAsync` ("one worker read before synchronous metadata derivation") and only then derives synchronously. This change does the same for invalid configs, inside `collectInvalidConfigLegacyIssues`: after the known core repairs return (the #178289 fast path stays first and touches no plugin state), and only when no plugin metadata snapshot is available. `core-only` validation and the available-snapshot branch are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, before and after.** The same script runs on each build: a first start with a valid config, then a second agent without `agents.ownership` (which `openclaw config validate` rejects), then `openclaw gateway run`. PostgreSQL 18 (`pgvector/pgvector:pg18`), macOS, built from source.

| State | Base `f5521bca76e` | This PR `fb7357d127d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite | exit 78, `agents.ownership: multi-agent rosters require ...` | exit 78, same issue |
| PostgreSQL | exit 1, `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker ...` | exit 78, same issue as SQLite |

<details>
<summary>PostgreSQL transcripts (paths, DSN and token redacted)</summary>

Base:

```text
base (postgres state): OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (f5521bc)
== 1. first start with a valid config
  [base] gateway healthy on loopback after 10s
  gateway stopped
== 2. openclaw.json gains a second agent without agents.ownership (invalid: multi-agent rosters need ownership="explicit")

$ [base] openclaw config validate --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "agents.ownership",
      "message": "multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership=\"explicit\" or one legacy default=true marker; add agents.ownership=\"explicit\" or run openclaw doctor"
    }
  ]
}

== 3. gateway run
  [base] gateway exited (code 1) after 4s
    [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
    [openclaw] Reason: Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.
```

This PR:

```text
fix (postgres state): OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (fb7357d)
== 1. first start with a valid config
  [fix] gateway healthy on loopback after 9s
  gateway stopped
== 2. openclaw.json gains a second agent without agents.ownership (invalid: multi-agent rosters need ownership="explicit")

$ [fix] openclaw config validate --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "agents.ownership",
      "message": "multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership=\"explicit\" or one legacy default=true marker; add agents.ownership=\"explicit\" or run openclaw doctor"
    }
  ]
}

== 3. gateway run
  [fix] gateway exited (code 78) after 4s
      - agents.ownership: multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership="explicit" or one legacy default=true marker; add agents.ownership="explicit" or run openclaw doctor
```

</details>

**Upgrade from the latest release.** v2026.10.6 has no PostgreSQL backend: it rejects the `database` key (`<root>: Unrecognized key: "database"`), so no released install has PostgreSQL state to carry forward. The upgrade proof therefore uses the released SQLite state. The same state and saved settings run under 2026.10.6 and then under this PR, which still reports an invalid config and keeps the retired-setting fast path. After step 2 the state schema is newer than 2026.10.6, so that build refuses it as a downgrade, as intended.

```text
stable: OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181)
pr:     OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (fb7357d)

== 1. latest stable on sqlite state, two agents with explicit ownership and a saved agent timeout setting
  [stable] gateway healthy after 9s
  gateway stopped
  state: sqlite file inode 1202509195, 103 tables

== 2. upgrade: the PR build starts on the same state and config
  [pr] gateway healthy after 10s
  gateway stopped
  state: sqlite file inode 1202509195, 103 tables
  saved setting: agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds=600

== 3. config becomes invalid (agents.ownership removed from the two-agent roster)
  [pr] gateway exited (code 78) after 4s
      - agents.ownership: multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership="explicit" or one legacy default=true marker; add agents.ownership="explicit" or run openclaw doctor

== 4. config repaired; the PR build starts on the retained state
  [pr] gateway healthy after 9s
  gateway stopped
  state: sqlite file inode 1202509195, 103 tables

== 5. a known retired setting with an unreadable local state database
  config validate --json: valid=false, issue skills.workshop: Unrecognized key: "approvalPolicy" (Doctor repair hint), with state/openclaw.sqlite at mode 000
  validate finished in 1s
```

prs.title: fix(agents): stop model fallback on CLI history owner changes
prs.body:
Related: #179979 (this addresses its remaining source-proven defect: a CLI history-owner refusal advances provider fallback as `reason=unknown`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a claude-cli turn silently switches to another provider and model when the session's history is owned by another live run (`CLI history owner changed before preparation`).

When a claude-cli turn starts while another live run holds the session's writer claim, or the session lifecycle changed during preparation, `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` refuses with `CLI history owner changed before preparation`. That refusal was a plain `Error`. `resolveModelFallbackError` therefore returned `kind: "unknown"`, and `runWithModelFallback` replayed the turn on the next configured candidate. The agent silently switched provider and model family for a local session-ownership fault that another model cannot repair. The reporter counted 40 of these in two days. The failover docs already say pre-admission session-state changes stop fallback.

## User Impact

User impact: when another run owns the session, the turn now stops with the original local error instead of being answered by a different model family.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Fix

- `history-boundary.ts`: both refusal sites throw a typed `CliHistoryOwnerChangedError`. The message is unchanged, so existing log matching and tests keep working.
- `failover-error.ts`: the error name joins `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES`, which is the same path as `ActiveTurnClaimError` and `GatewayDrainingError`. It is matched through wrappers and causes, classified `coordination`, and fallback stops with the original error.

Out of scope, as in the ClawSweeper review on the issue:

- The MCP cleanup "could not confirm closure" path needs its own replay-safety proof and is tracked by #157062.
- Transcript admission identity is already typed by #179347.
- No generic `runtime_fault` same-model retry is added.

## Evidence

Local runs: local run, Windows 11, Node 26.

This is a production-path harness, not a mock of the guard. A real SQLite session store is created with the repo's history-boundary fixture. A prior run (`orchestrator-prior`) claims the session writer, then a claude-cli turn calls the real `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` through the real `runWithModelFallback` with `fallbacksOverride: ["openai/gpt-6-sol"]`. The rows below are the raw JSON the harness wrote.

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/179979/proof-179979.png)

main f3f7a8a (fix reverted):

```
{"step":"writer claimed","activeWriterRunId":"orchestrator-prior"}
{"step":"candidate failed","candidate":"claude-cli/claude-sonnet","errorName":"Error","message":"CLI history owner changed before preparation","classified":"unknown"}
{"step":"turn outcome","outcome":"completed on fallback","provider":"openai","model":"gpt-6-sol","runCalls":["claude-cli/claude-sonnet","openai/gpt-6-sol"]}
{"step":"session after","activeWriterRunId":"orchestrator-prior"}
```

This branch:

```
{"step":"writer claimed","activeWriterRunId":"orchestrator-prior"}
{"step":"turn outcome","outcome":"stopped","errorName":"CliHistoryOwnerChangedError","message":"CLI history owner changed before preparation","classified":"coordination","runCalls":["claude-cli/claude-sonnet"]}
{"step":"session after","activeWriterRunId":"orchestrator-prior"}
```

| build | classification | candidates run | turn outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | unknown | claude-cli → openai/gpt-6-sol | silently answered by another provider |
| fix | coordination | claude-cli only | stopped with the original error; the live writer's claim is untouched |

### Tests

The existing "admits a finished writer's successor while refusing the live writer" case in `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.test.ts` now drives the real refusal through `runWithModelFallback` with a fallback configured. It asserts that the turn rejects with `CliHistoryOwnerChangedError` and that only one candidate ran.

- On main it fails: `promise resolved "{ outcome: 'completed', … }" instead of rejecting`, because the turn was replayed on the fallback.
- On this branch it passes.

Checks run locally:

- The `history-boundary`, `failover-error`, `model-fallback.terminal-boundary` and `model-fallback` suites pass 150/150.
- oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- The changed-path core test typecheck shards pass 29/29. The script still exits 1 on the pre-existing advisory shard root-budget check, which fails the same way on main.
- `pnpm check:changed` was not run locally because of a Crabbox DNS issue on this machine.

prs.title: fix(agents): settle consumed yield cohorts without retry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, a fleet parent could deliver its final answer twice.

When a parent is killed mid-turn and resumed, two settle cohorts can wake it back to back: the interrupted originals, and the replacements it spawned in the recovered turn (an explicit `sessions_yield` cohort). The first wake often consumes both cohorts' results in-turn and writes the complete final answer. The second, yielded cohort still owes one continuation under #178104, and settle policy required that continuation to produce a visible final. The parent correctly answered `NO_REPLY`, since it had already reported everything. Direct delivery classified that as "completion agent did not produce a visible reply", and missing-answer recovery re-ran the wake with the same payload, producing a duplicate final answer.

Live sequence, from the Gateway raw model stream (embedded OpenClaw runtime):
1. Wake A writes the full final table at 01:26:58.
2. Wake B (`:yield-1`) answers `NO_REPLY` at 01:27:01.
3. `:yield-1:retry-1` writes the same table again at 01:28:13. The parent's report said "duplicate completion announcements arrived".

Direct delivery also re-derived the reply requirement from the channel instead of using the settle owner's decision.

## User Impact

A yielded cohort whose results were already consumed can complete silently without replaying the parent's final answer. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The settle policy (`resolveRequesterSettlePolicy`) requires a visible reply for a yielded cohort only while some member still needs delivery or restart reconciliation.
- Direct delivery and the response classifier both use that owner decision for `subagent_settle`.
- When nothing is left to deliver, the continuation still runs exactly once, and a silent or `NO_REPLY` completion settles it without missing-answer recovery.
- Unchanged: mixed cohorts still require a visible reply; ordinary child missing-answer recovery; and failed, suppressed or ambiguous delivery evidence.

`docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md` documents the optional continuation.

## Evidence

- `subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts` has consumed-cohort regressions: red on base (2 failed, 19 passed) and green with the fix (21/21). These pass, run on a Crabbox host: requester-settle dispatch, wake and restart, yielded-settle (17), direct delivery (48), announce delivery (124), and `agent-command-restart-recovery` (29).
- Live Crabbox A/B, Gateway `kill -9` while operator CLI parents were still in their first turn, embedded runtime:
  - main: 1 "completion agent did not produce a visible reply" plus 1 `:retry-1` settle wake in the A/B batch of 6 parents, and the same in an earlier single-parent run.
  - this branch: 0 of either. Its second settle wake answered `NO_REPLY` at 02:57:48 and was settled once, with no re-delivery.

### Landing validation

- Local changed-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The first PR CI run exposed an outdated `progress only` recovery fixture: every child was marked delivered while the test expected missing-answer retries. The fixture now retains pending delivery for that case, preserving all retry assertions and production behavior.
- The corrected real-Gateway recovery harness passed all 18 tests on the supplied Crabbox runner. The initial CI harness took 93.99 seconds; it covers persisted recovery, Gateway restart, and source admission across the restart boundary.

prs.title: refactor: fold private preparation frames into their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private preparation operations still shuttle argument/result objects through functions and modules with one production consumer.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change or operator action. Public SDK, protocol, config, CLI and persisted contracts remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep Activity instance lookup with its HTTP route and X attachment preparation with delivery. Localize the sole-use Google credential-home, selected-template and lazy configuration frames; Copilot Azure mapping; xAI streaming URL setup; Matrix account setup; QA reply preview and child reader; and custom-provider model selection in their existing callers. Shared helpers, lazy imports and actual lifecycle owners remain separate.

The Activity cancellation tests now enter the real HTTP token route instead of importing the private API donor. All other public boundary suites stay unchanged. The obsolete Activity location assertion allowance shrinks; no replacement allowance is added.

Net production reduction: **156 lines (+697/-853)** across 13 production paths. Tests: 32 net lines removed (+33/-65). One obsolete assertion-baseline row is removed separately. Implementation body relocation earns no deletion credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No guard or supported edge case is removed. This is private API/frame consolidation, not a relaxation of validation, authorization, durability or concurrency behavior.
- Google retains deferred atomic credential/settings publication and identical cleanup, including the queue-race and failed-publication fixes. Its post-await tool-availability observation is not replaced by an earlier snapshot. Public synchronous voice configuration remains supported through 2026-12-31.
- Matrix setup stays inside the admitted local-state command callback, with awaited config publication in the same finally after profile/device/bootstrap work. QA child listeners/timers still attach before completion registration and stdin; process-tree settlement and redaction remain unchanged.
- X retains both original signal-read phases and all media/authority limits. xAI retains native-origin HTTPS/credential/path refusals before opening a socket. Activity membership, SSRF, body/time limits and cancellation/release order remain.
- Custom discovery keeps manual/Anthropic fallback and reads the current retry endpoint/key on each existing selector invocation. Selected Google family templates remain lazy.

Phase E standalone memory is untouched. No dependency, schema, permission or migration change. No live provider/channel acceptance is claimed.

## Evidence

- Activity public HTTP/endpoint suites: 46 cases pass; the moved cancellation cases passed on unchanged production first. xAI TTS/guarded HTTP: 34 cases pass. Google model/registration/import guards: 42 pass. Google credential-home/isolation: 42 pass. Copilot mapping: 15 pass.
- Matrix CLI/publication/local-state-owner: 49 pass. QA inbound/lifecycle: 29 pass. X delivery/reply/upload/authority: 52 pass. QA real child-command/bootstrap: 19 pass. Custom-provider public wizard: 20 pass.
- Targeted native types and formatting pass for every touched owner. Typed lint passes except four local SDK error-type diagnostics (one Google model and three Google auth) reproduced on their actual unchanged preimages; candidate restored afterward. No lint suppression or assertion allowance is added.
- The initial Google lazy voice run passed 55 assertions but exited 2 because an unrelated source edit occurred during its compiled subprocess. That wrapper result is not counted as clean proof; the focused frozen-source rerun passed all 55 cases with wrapper exit 0 (26.6s).
- Author simplification pass complete. Fresh isolated independent review through P2 is scoped-clean, final source verification passed (0.98). Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad proof. No broad local suite, build or E2E was run.

Suppression audit (14 cases), assertion/mock ratchets, wrapper/import-closure (4 cases), zero runtime cycles, zero static cycles, line caps and diff check pass. Changelog is release-owned.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes invalid Gateway configuration reporting a misleading PostgreSQL connection error when PostgreSQL state is selected.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway run` reports the actual configuration issue and exits 78, consistently with SQLite. No configuration migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Invalid-config diagnostics can derive Doctor plugin contracts before a metadata snapshot is available, reaching the synchronous `plugins.bundledDiscovery` machine-state read. Prepare their cold policy and inventory facts through the existing worker, then activate those facts immediately before synchronous diagnostics. Known core repairs and available metadata snapshots retain their existing paths; the PostgreSQL main-thread guard is unchanged.

## Evidence

The real CLI regression on trusted main reproduced PostgreSQL exit 1 with the main-thread connection error; the separate SQLite control passed exit 78 and the exact ownership diagnostic. The same regression is green with the fix on disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 and SQLite. Both engines now report the expected ownership diagnostic and exit 78.

Final independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. All 13 config snapshot tests, the repository core type-check, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on the exact final head in [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890188199/attempts/2), including the real Gateway CLI regression.

CI currently fails `check-test-types-core-1` in the untouched `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57`: newer main removed the `managedHooksDir`/`bundledHooksDir` options while its test still passes them. The CI log checks out our head merged with main `4f44cc7d`; current main [`b8d8c220` retains the incompatible call](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8d8c220af0b6bbee84b8768ab7378a394c0c910/src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts#L55) and [the narrowed signature](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8d8c220af0b6bbee84b8768ab7378a394c0c910/src/hooks/loader.ts#L71). This PR changes neither hook file. [Scheduled main fails with the identical diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890895258/job/120210446157). [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890188199/job/120208930798); all final-head PostgreSQL shards are green.

The focused change is 14 added/1 removed production lines, 50 added test lines, and one documentation-line replacement. It reuses the existing worker and cache lifecycle, with no new state owner or public contract.

Supersedes #180687 (thanks @ceckert).
Closes #180686.

The first PostgreSQL shard-2 attempt exceeded its 30-minute job deadline after broad build/test slowdown. Its exact-job rerun passed without source changes. prs.title: fix: long HTML answers still stall Gateway streaming at partial tag boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long streamed ordinary HTML reply can still spend 4.8-5.2 seconds of blocking Gateway CPU at a delta boundary that leaves a partial tag prefix such as `<p`, delaying every channel, session, cron turn, and tool call in the same process. Fixes #180720.

This is a follow-up to #175472 and its source report #175439. The merged optimization skips complete ordinary tags and partial prefixes inside settled fences. Outside those cases, `<p` is still a prefix of `<parameter>`, so every four-character delta that ends there sends the whole accumulated reply through the canonical Markdown ownership resolver again.

## User Impact

User impact: long HTML, JSX, XML, SVG, and comparison-heavy answers no longer stall unrelated Gateway work at partial tag boundaries. On a 64 KB fixture streamed in four-character deltas, the shipped `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` path drops from 4,840.5 / 5,175.8 ms to 655.0 / 631.0 ms (multiline / single-line) on the same Windows host. The deterministic 16 KB regression drops from **5,417,280 parsed characters** against a **31,980-character budget** (169x over) to within budget. Tool-call stripping, fenced-code ownership, and one-shot output remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Streaming mode now holds only an unresolved tag prefix just long enough to see whether the next delta completes it. Ordinary markup is released to the existing projector; a completed tool-call candidate still goes through the canonical resolver. The carried protection scan disables holding for fences, ambiguous paragraph ownership, and structural uncertainty, preserving the existing Markdown semantics.

The fast path also disables itself permanently once any complete tool-call candidate is found, so later deltas cannot hide or reorder tool-call XML.

## Evidence

Pre-fix regression on upstream code:

```text
expected 5417280 to be less than 31980
```

Post-fix regression and the same real-entry probe on final head `093313d4b43` (rebased to `bee83199e15`):

```text
multiline chars=65520 wallMs=655.0 cpuMs=563.0 visible=65519
single chars=65536 wallMs=631.0 cpuMs=673.0 visible=65536
```

The same probe on the pre-fix code produced:

```text
multiline chars=65520 wallMs=4840.5 cpuMs=4891.0 visible=65519
single chars=65536 wallMs=5175.8 cpuMs=5188.0 visible=65536
```

Validation run on final head:

- Independent review found one remaining interaction: a fenced literal `<tool_call>` example permanently disabled the fast path. The new regression failed first with `expected 5447844 to be less than 32082`, then passed after the fix in `093313d4b43`.
- 3 Vitest shards, 157 tests passed, including all shared-text and embedded-agent-utils owners.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` exited 0.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/shared/text/tool-call-xml.ts src/shared/text/tool-call-xml.streaming-work.test.ts`: `All matched files use the correct format.`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: no output, exit 0.
- Targeted type-aware `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` exited 0.
- A differential check over 2,500 complete HTML/JSX/XML documents with randomized 1-9 character chunks produced identical final text to the pre-fix streaming projector.

Validation gap: targeted oxlint used the wrapper-supported `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1` path because this Windows host timed out while generating plugin-SDK boundary declarations at both 300 seconds and 900 seconds. The same declaration preparation completed successfully before the rebase, and the rebase did not touch either target file. PR CI will rerun the full declaration and lint lanes.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.


## Maintainer follow-up

The unfinished-indented-line regression is fixed at the XML projection owner. The final implementation classifies a copy of the current protection state before retaining a trailing prefix, so literal indented/inline/fenced code keeps canonical ownership. It retains prefixes in the existing conditional projector and removes the second output buffer and separate fence scan. Ambiguous Markdown continues through the canonical resolver. The generic projector is unchanged; the broader hold API proposed in #180775 is not needed and was not merged.

The bounded regression covers 54 adversarial inputs in both modes, every two-chunk split (including empty chunks), and one-character/four-character streams: **3,608 schedules and 10,924 prefix comparisons**, with delta reconstruction checked as well. It covers indentation/tabs/list continuation, fences, inline code, HTML blocks/tags, partial `<p`/`<pre`/tool/function tags, entities, references, malformed adjacent candidates, and CRLF. The committed sweep took **496 ms**; the complete owner file passed 9 tests in **8.182 s wall time**. A standalone run of the same corpus took 352 ms. The new table is red against both original owners: main fails the work budgets and list/fence parity; contributor `093313d4b43` loses `<p` from `    <p`. Both are green with this repair.

Local validation: **240 targeted tests passed**, including the visible-text projection and embedded-agent delivery consumers (consumer run: 86.271 s wall across three shards). Core and shared-test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc and plugin-inventory checks pass. Source **+28/-28 (net 0)**; tests **+150/-0**, relative to the tested main base `87aada17522b`.

Built Gateway proof used the same **65,536-byte HTML fixture in 16,384 four-character provider SSE deltas per request**, through the public `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint in separate clean builds of baseline `87aada17522b` and repaired head `205117ed252`. Source, streamed delivery, and batch delivery match byte-for-byte on both heads (SHA-256 `0f7afdd7770dca424be28c5353056d58fe9f0132122a5101d7fd00f19ee6d7c1`). Across each stream/batch pair:

| Ownership work | Baseline | Repaired head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Resolver calls | 1,474 | 1,043 |
| Resolver input characters | 52,538,312 | 37,289,212 |
| Parser calls | 1,472 | 1,041 |
| Parser input characters | 52,538,200 | 37,289,100 |

This is **29% less ownership-parse work** through the built delivery path, including the fixture's deliberately ambiguous Markdown that still uses canonical parsing. In-memory instrumentation counted both the resolver and actual parser across the Gateway and its workers; no repository or build artifacts were modified by instrumentation. Both runtimes verified Node 26.12.1. The failed first Qwen leg interrupted final timing serialization, so the recovered head fixture receipt records request timings and ephemeral provider request metadata as unavailable; no before/after request-latency claim is made.

Real local-model smoke through the same built public Gateway endpoint: native Ollama **`qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-instruct`**, requested and returned model verified, HTTP 200, **112 bytes / 29 SSE frames in 53.179 s**, delivering a paragraph, `&`, and a preformatted block without an SSE error. Two earlier prompts produced pseudo-tool calls and no visible answer; the final literal-HTML prompt passed the requested smoke. The harness still exited nonzero on an additional zero-advertised-tools assertion: it observed three tools despite deny-all/code-mode-off configuration. That assertion and the earlier failed attempts remain recorded; this proof makes no tool-free-provider claim.

Codex branch autoreview returned **scoped-clean: no actionable P0–P2 findings**. It reviewed the diff and supplied owner context statically; the separate full-module parity review and executed tests provide additional coverage.

The existing contributor commits are preserved, with JasonBuildAI credited in the maintainer commit. This is a macOS arm64 / Node 26.12.1 proof; request timings are instrumented, single cold/warm samples on a shared host, and include Gateway/session/provider overhead. Work counts and exact delivered bytes are the primary comparison. Conservatively unclassified Markdown still uses full ownership parsing.

prs.title: fix: reduce repeated parsing in streamed final answers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes streamed final answers exposing tool-call text when a supported inline-link title closes across chunks, including titles after balanced or multiline destinations.

Fixes #175264

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream reuses parsed Markdown ownership across appended chunks and refreshes it when link titles, image descriptions, reference definitions, GFM table delimiters, or indentation can change code ownership. HTML invalidation was removed because the canonical parser disables HTML flow and text nodes.

## User Impact

Tool-call syntax stays hidden as Markdown syntax completes, while literal examples in indented, list, and fenced code remain visible.

## Evidence

- Exact base `2c5b726` and head `2d394cf`: the same `openclaw agent exec` loopback Responses SSE proof matched canonical output, hid resolved tool calls, and preserved literal code. It recorded 351 ms on the base and 49 ms on the head for one run.
- The 4,143-character open-call work-budget regression uses four-character appends and matches visible output: the merge base scans 4,297,278 characters against a 66,288-character budget; the head scans 16. It fails on the base and passes on the head. The focused streaming suite passed 16/16 cases.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node npm_config_manage_package_manager_versions=false node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-final-answer-stream.mts
entrypoint: openclaw agent exec via src/entry.ts
provider: one local OpenAI Responses SSE request
phase: final_answer
pending-call workload: 4,096 payload characters in 256-character deltas; measured 351 ms on base `2c5b726` and 49 ms on head `2d394cf`
response events: 84; tool-call deltas: 17
quoted-title transitions after balanced and multiline destinations: tool-call hidden
result: resolved link/image/reference calls hidden; list, indented, and fenced code calls preserved
status: ok
```

AI-assisted: built with Codex

## Maintainer follow-up

The open-table checkpoint returned before applying canonical Markdown retention. An earlier image description could therefore be settled as literal code before a later reference definition revoked that code ownership, leaving a tool marker visible. The follow-up takes the earliest of the table boundary, canonical image/title retention, and long-label retention. This keeps the mutable-image/reference intent of #172832 (`a8a67b01`) intact instead of weakening literal-code preservation. Contributor commits and @sunlit-deng's ownership are preserved.

The added eight-case table-driven regression checks every two-chunk split, one-character and four-character chunkings, canonical output at each prefix, and delta reconstruction. It fails on the original production code in the three image/table cases and passes with the fix. The broader lane-only deterministic sweep covers escaped brackets and backslash runs, nested labels, one-to-three-backtick spans, reference titles, images, angle destinations, tables, ordinary/list/tilde/four-backtick fences, CRLF, tool markers, model control tokens, and long normalized labels: **439 documents, 37,836 chunkings, 119,743 prefix checks, zero divergences, 88.484 seconds**. The original contributor head produced 418 divergences on that corpus.

Validation on macOS:

- Five focused suites: **149 tests passed, 112.19 seconds wall**. The changed streaming test file used **3.365 seconds** of test execution; CI timing is pending.
- Core types, scoped lint/format, max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks passed. Merging current main cleared a reproduced inherited max-lines baseline failure; the reviewed projection patch is byte-identical after that merge.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in **49m33s** on the shared Mac.
- Built-CLI fixture: `pnpm openclaw --profile projection-table agent exec` sent one streaming Responses request (seven SSE events), produced the exact expected sanitized final output, and preserved fenced tool/model-control examples (**103.584s**, including startup). This checks transport/final rendering; the production-projector differential sweep checks prefix/delta parity.
- Real local-model control: built `openclaw agent exec` with native Ollama `llama3.2:latest` returned the exact requested text in **106.530s**, including startup. The first control with minimal tools instead returned a tool error; the recorded passing control uses the documented deny-all tool policy and exact-text assertion. Ollama is an unphased control, not a reproduction of Responses `final_answer` phase handling.
- Isolated Codex autoreview: clean through P2, with no actionable findings.
- A single 4,140-character pending-call sample through the production projector took 919 ms on main and 94 ms with this branch; ordinary prose controls took 4 ms and 7 ms. These are observations, not a statistical benchmark.

Follow-up LOC: production **+2/-5 (net -3)**, tests **+37**. Full PR relative to current main: runtime production **+615/-22**, tests **+499/-48**, existing proof script/inventory **+762**. The contributor's cache machinery accounts for the production growth and avoids repeatedly parsing settled Markdown while retaining canonical invalidation.


### Remote check follow-up

CI run [39892893645](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892893645) passed the text checks and baseline ratchets, but `checks-ui-e2e (6/9)` failed `chat-image-lightbox.e2e.test.ts:402`: navigating back to `after.png` recorded a duplicate 1920px rendition request. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` remains red. The entire UI and media-core source trees are unchanged from merged main `87aada17522b`; the test routes all media requests (Playwright documents that routing disables HTTP cache), while the gallery retains the loaded URL through this navigation. The focused local scenario passed (10.423s test, 173.22s Vitest duration), which does not prove a CI repair. CI’s automatic pre-existing label names a main run with a different failure, so it is not matching-signature evidence; this remains an inherited-source UI/harness limitation for maintainer review. No retry or test weakening was used.

ClawSweeper re-review was requested after the push. After the requested 15-minute polling window, its published review still names the prior `2d394cf75428` head; no exact-head ClawSweeper verdict is available yet.

prs.title: fix: native worker supervisor crashes when a resource attachment endpoint is rejected
prs.body:
Closes #180581

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native worker lifecycle supervisor crashes (exit code 1) and takes down every native worker it owns when a resource attachment endpoint is rejected synchronously by `net.connect` (for example an out-of-range port).

## User Impact

User impact: a malformed resource attachment now fails only the worker that requested it. That worker reports an error and stops, and the supervisor and its other native workers keep running. No production configuration is known to produce a malformed endpoint today, so this hardens a defensive path rather than fixing a reported crash.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resource attachment client already turns asynchronous connection failures into a failure report plus cleanup. A synchronous `connect()` throw skipped that path, and the supervisor's close-and-rethrow catch let it escape the message listener. The client now reports a synchronous throw the same way, one microtask later, after the supervisor has installed the attachment owner and child listeners. The same change covers the startup-retry timer, which calls the same `start()` and could also throw uncaught. The supervisor's catch can no longer be reached, so it is removed.

The fix deliberately does not send `create-error`. The parent treats `create-error` as "the constructor refused and there is no child to join", but here the child Worker already exists. The failure goes through the existing post-construction path instead: `created`, then `error`, then the child stops and joins. This matches the custody concern raised in the ClawSweeper review.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: fault-injection trace on the production supervisor

A standalone script (not part of the diff) starts the production supervisor, `src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.worker.ts`, in a real `worker_threads.Worker` over its private port. It injects the fault from the issue (a `create` with `resource.attachment.endpoint = 70000` plus a `taskPort`) and logs every reply the supervisor emits. It then creates a second worker, round-trips a message, and stops it. The secret is redacted and local paths are stripped. Environment: Node v24.22.1 on Darwin arm64, head `14ec3d9a77`.

**Before (main's `resource-client.ts` and `worker-native-lifecycle.worker.ts`):** the supervisor dies, the requester gets no reply, and the second worker never runs.
```
[+   2ms] supervisor started (threadId=2)
[+   3ms] send   id=1 create with resource.attachment.endpoint=70000 (+taskPort)
[+2314ms] supervisor ERROR event: RangeError: Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (70000).
[+2326ms] supervisor EXIT code=1
[+2327ms] RESULT supervisorAlive=false id1=[] id2=[] createError=false
```

**After (this PR):** worker 1 fails on its own and the supervisor keeps serving.
```
[+   2ms] supervisor started (threadId=2)
[+   5ms] send   id=1 create with resource.attachment.endpoint=70000 (+taskPort)
[+ 315ms] reply  id=1 created threadId=4
[+ 321ms] reply  id=1 error RangeError: Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (70000).
[+ 323ms] reply  id=1 execution-exit code=0
[+ 323ms] send   id=2 create (no resource)
[+ 323ms] reply  id=1 stop-error RangeError: Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (70000).
[+ 323ms] reply  id=2 created threadId=5
[+ 324ms] send   id=2 post "ping"
[+ 401ms] reply  id=2 message value="ping"
[+ 402ms] send   id=2 stop
[+ 404ms] reply  id=2 execution-exit code=1
[+ 404ms] reply  id=2 stopped code=1
[+ 404ms] RESULT supervisorAlive=true id1=[created,error,execution-exit,stop-error] id2=[created,message,execution-exit,stopped] createError=false
[+ 407ms] supervisor EXIT code=1 (trace script called terminate())
```

Reading the after trace:
- **Worker 1:** the endpoint is rejected and reported as `error`, and the child is stopped and joins (`execution-exit`). There is no `create-error`, because the child exists.
- **Worker 1's `stop-error`:** the resource attachment never connected, so the supervisor cannot confirm its cleanup and reports `stop-error` with the original failure. The parent keeps custody of the resource for its existing recovery path. This is the same outcome an unreachable broker produces today through the asynchronous connection-error path.
- **Worker 2:** created, round-tripped `"ping"`, and stopped normally while the supervisor stayed alive.
- **Final `EXIT code=1`:** this is the trace script's own `terminate()` call at the end; Node reports code 1 for a terminated worker.

### Tests

A new real-supervisor regression test is in `src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.test.ts`. It starts `worker-native-lifecycle.worker.ts` in a real `worker_threads.Worker` with a private port and sends `create` with `resource.attachment.endpoint = 70000` plus a `taskPort`. It asserts that the supervisor stays alive, that the request gets `created`, then `error` (a `RangeError`, "Received 70000"), then `execution-exit`, and never `create-error`, and that a sibling worker then creates, round-trips a message, and stops.

- **Red on main** (fix reverted, same test): the supervisor exits with code 1 from an uncaught exception.
  ```
  × keeps the supervisor alive when a resource attachment endpoint is rejected synchronously
    → expected 1 to be undefined
  Uncaught Exception: RangeError: Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received 70000
   ❯ start src/process/spawn-broker/resource-client.ts:116:23
   ❯ attachBrokerNativeResource src/process/spawn-broker/resource-client.ts:159:3
   ❯ create src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.worker.ts:211:16
  Serialized Error: { code: 'ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT' }
  ```
- **Green with the fix:** the same test passes.
- **Suites from the issue's acceptance criteria:** `pnpm test src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/worker-native-handle.test.ts src/process/spawn-broker/resource-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 15/15 (9 + 2 + 4).
- **Static checks:** core typecheck and every core test typecheck shard pass, including `infra`. `oxlint` on the touched files reports 0 warnings and 0 errors. Format check and `git diff --check` are clean.

Gaps:
- `pnpm check:changed` was not run to completion locally. It hit failures that already exist on `main` and are unrelated to this change: the max-lines suppression ratchet in `ui/`, the dead-export scan, and the advisory core test-shard root budget (`infra` 735, `gateway-root` 726). The regression test was added to an existing test file so this change adds no test root. CI is the broad proof.
- No live Gateway end-to-end run. No supported configuration produces a malformed endpoint, so the fault-injection trace on the production supervisor above is the behavior proof for this path.

prs.title: fix(chat): show tool cards for external Codex transcripts
prs.body:
Closes #180940
Related: #147378

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plain Tool call/Tool result labels and JSON when browsing external Codex app/CLI transcripts in the Control UI.

## User Impact

Recorded commands, file changes and explicit outcomes use ordinary chat cards while browsing and retain the same presentation after import and reopen. Imported history adds its provenance notice and normal session controls.

Existing imported copies are not backfilled. Output previews and transport/import limits remain; older node readers retain their own bounded text. Dashboard folding and native continuation are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Codex harness's argument, result and activity helpers, then share one display conversion between catalog browsing and preserved history. Keep inputs and file changes structured until the existing renderer consumes them. The Gateway derives optional display facts once for local and released-node pages without changing their source text, identity, rows or cursor.

Preserved imports retain canonical trust-framed reference text alongside display metadata. Recorded Canvas/app/embed references remain inert. No new renderer or component is introduced.

## Evidence

- Eight built-browser scenarios pass, including browse → menu Open → actual durable import → Open → reload. Commands, a 48-row diff, titles and outcomes match across recorded-history stages and the same six normal-harness reference tools. Trust framing, idempotent import and absence of native full-output fetch are checked.
- Focused native/local/paired-node, import/display and UI tests pass. After integrating upstream's test cleanup, all 57 affected owner tests and all eight browser scenarios pass again. Production UI types pass on that base.
- French durable browse/import/reopen and mounted French/German/English switches verify localized truncation receipts while preserving source text.
- Targeted types/lint/format, docs lint (1,365 files), protocol registry/generation and Swift/Kotlin determinism checks pass. Full build and base-relative bundle checks passed before upstream integration; startup raw bytes/request count were unchanged (+24 B gzip). The broader UI editor/test graph has identical missing-declaration/native-bridge diagnostics on unchanged main.

Synthetic captures of the same native fixture:
