prs.title: fix(ui): let operators dismiss retired pending inputs
prs.body:
Closes #134887

## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted and cancelled messages stay pinned at the bottom of a chat forever. Nothing in the Control UI (or `/reset`, `/clear`, `openclaw sessions cleanup --enforce`) lets an operator clear them.

## User Impact

Each interrupted or cancelled message now has a **Dismiss** button, and the retained-input footer has **Dismiss all** for the interrupted and cancelled messages on the page being viewed (older ones stay behind **Show earlier messages** and are not touched). The controls appear only for people who can change the conversation; view-only collaborators do not see them. A dismissed message disappears right away on this device and, after the next history read, on every other device viewing the conversation. If the Gateway refuses, only the rows from that request come back, with the error shown in the footer.

Queued and running inputs never change. Dismissed messages do not resume after a restart, and no browser resends its saved copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the owner decision on the review of the first revision: dismissal is persisted on the Gateway, nothing is deleted, retained content is preserved, and it is complementary to #156625's browser-local hide (that PR hides rows in one browser; this one records the dismissal once so every device sees it and the receipt fence stays intact).

The first revision hard-deleted `session_pending_inputs` rows. That removed the receipt fence other owners rely on: restart recovery keeps cancelled receipts, `chat.history` keeps withdrawn rows so client copies retire, and a missing receipt lets an outbox copy resend under the same idempotency key and be admitted as a fresh turn. This revision tombstones instead.

- **Tombstone, matching the queued-input withdrawal.** `chat.pendingInputs.dismiss` does exactly what `chat.abort`'s queued-input withdrawal (`discardSessionPendingInputInWorker`) already does to a row: it sets `state = "cancelled"` and adds `display: false` to the stored message. Interrupted rows therefore become cancelled; that is what stops restart recovery (which only resumes `interrupted` rows) and what the existing `chat.history` projection already hides. The row, its message content, and its attachments stay in the database. Its receipt keeps reporting `{ state: "pending", cancelled: true }`, which the Control UI outbox already treats as retired, not resendable.
- **No schema change.** No column, table, or migration is added. Rows written before this change load and render exactly as before; a dismissed row round-trips through `chat.history` as a content-less `display: false` row.
- **Scope gate:** the descriptor row uses `OWN_SESSION_WRITE`, the same gate as `chat.predict`: `operator.write`, or `operator.sessions.write` limited to the caller's own session through the standard session-access check (unlike `chat.abort`, which has no own-session alternative). The Control UI shows both controls only when the session-access presentation policy (`readChatPaneMutationAccess`, the same policy as the model and permission controls) allows the method, the session row's `sharingRole` is not `viewer` (a view-only collaborator in a shared session stays hidden even with a broad `operator.write` grant, matching the Gateway's sharing refusal), and the sharing participation gate does not block the caller. A writer can still dismiss when sending is unavailable (for example, no model configured).
- **Authority at the commit boundary.** The handler passes the live session-access assertion into the store, which carries it into the agent-database worker's transaction and commit admissions exactly as the withdrawal does. If access is revoked after RPC admission, the worker transaction rolls back at commit and the RPC returns `FORBIDDEN` with no row changed and no `sessions.changed` event.
- **Refusals:** any requested input that is still queued, or held by a turn that is still settling (a registered pending-input owner), refuses the whole request with `INVALID_REQUEST`, `details.code: "PENDING_INPUT_NOT_RETIRED"`, and the affected `inputIds`; nothing changes. A replaced session is refused. Incognito sessions are refused at session-access admission.
- **Idempotent, partial-safe result:** success returns `{ dismissedIds, runIds, missingIds }`. Already-dismissed inputs are reported again, so a retry after a lost response is safe. Inputs no longer retained (consumed or gone) go in `missingIds` instead of failing the batch, and the UI treats them as done.
- **Outbox copies:** the UI retires local copies by the Gateway's returned `runIds` (stable submission identities), not by the displayed page. Retirement runs before the request is marked complete and still runs if a history refresh replaced the page or the operator switched conversations mid-request. Copies on other devices, or ones missed after a lost response, retire on their next reconcile through the cancelled receipt.

**Security review:** this adds a row to `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts`, which the security-review policy classifies under `gateway-auth`, so the guard will ask for `/allow-security-sensitive-change`. The method adds no new scope and reuses the existing own-session write gate.

## Evidence

- **Store** (`src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-dismissal.test.ts`, 7 tests): tombstones through the database worker with no host SQL, keeping every row, its content, and `display: false`; the receipt keeps reporting `cancelled: true` after dismissal; a repeat dismissal is idempotent and reports no-longer-retained ids as missing without failing the batch; queued and replaced-session targets change nothing; an interrupted input reclaimed by a resend (`retryInterrupted`) is refused; a retired row with a registered settling owner is refused; revoking authority at the worker commit rolls the transaction back with no row changed.
- **Registered RPC through `handleGatewayRequest`** (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-pending-inputs-dismiss-handler.test.ts`, 5 tests): success returns `{ dismissedIds, runIds, missingIds }`, emits one `sessions.changed`, keeps every row, and `chat.history` then returns the row as hidden with a `cancelled: true` receipt; queued input and a replaced session are refused with no `sessions.changed`; view/none roles and a read-only scope are refused, a different session's caller holding only `operator.sessions.write` gets `FORBIDDEN`, and own-session `operator.sessions.write` succeeds; rows written before this change load through `chat.history` with their content; revoking session write access between RPC admission and the worker commit returns `FORBIDDEN` with no row changed. Incognito sessions are refused with a structured `FORBIDDEN` at the registered RPC (`src/gateway/session-control.incognito.test.ts`).
- **Control UI** (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-inputs-dismiss.test.ts`, 12 tests, plus `chat-pane-session-controls.pending-inputs.test.ts`): named controls only on visible retired rows; no controls for callers without session mutate access, while a writer whose composer cannot send still gets them; text-less inputs are named by attachment or image labels; Dismiss all sends exactly the displayed ids; two in-flight requests where one fails restore only that request's rows; a missing id is treated as done; outbox copies retire by the Gateway's `runIds` even after the view moved to another conversation, and through a history refresh that replaced the page mid-request; an outbox copy whose input another client dismissed is never resent on reconcile (no `chat.send`). The access policy test pins the own-session write gate (`operator.write`, owner with `operator.sessions.write`, member refused, read-only refused, older Gateway without the method refused) and hides both controls from a shared-session `viewer` even with `operator.write`.
- **New plus sibling suites together:** the new files above and queued-input withdrawal, `chat-pending-inputs`, `chat-system-notice`, outbox receipt attention and restart-input reconcile, `session-send-recovery` (+ upgrade), pending-input pagination, and session-control permission tests: 231 tests across 16 files pass.
- **All 112 test files under `src/gateway` that call `handleGatewayRequest`:** 1,496 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, Swift/Kotlin determinism, since guard), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm db:worker-inventory:check`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, and oxfmt pass. oxlint on the changed files reports only the pre-existing `max-lines` note below and two pre-existing Solid reactivity warnings on unchanged lines.
- **Screenshots** (mocked Gateway E2E harness, built bundle, 1100x760): before (unchanged from main), the interrupted and cancelled rows sit under the conversation with no way to clear them; after, each row has **Dismiss** and the footer has **Dismiss all**; clicking **Dismiss all** sends one `chat.pendingInputs.dismiss` request and leaves only the real conversation. 

  Before (no controls on the retired rows):

  ![Before: interrupted and cancelled rows with no way to clear them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/f5451867f94f398626f6f2efe10e87dd94a40e91/pending-input-discard/before-1-retired-rows.png)

  After (Dismiss on each row, Dismiss all in the footer):

  ![After: each retired row has a Dismiss button and the footer has Dismiss all](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/66981c91f54525f8808bbb51e8b09396f43f819d/pending-input-discard/v2/after-1-retired-rows.png)

  After Dismiss all (only the conversation remains):

  ![After Dismiss all: the retired rows are hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/66981c91f54525f8808bbb51e8b09396f43f819d/pending-input-discard/v2/after-2-cleared.png)

<details>
<summary>Known lint note</summary>

`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts` is already over the 700-line `max-lines` budget on main (701 counted lines); the new descriptor row makes it 702. The file is the canonical append-only method table, so the row cannot move elsewhere, and this PR does not refactor it.

</details>

### Real Gateway, real agent, real worker

Isolated branch Gateway on loopback (own state directory, `trusted-proxy` auth with a throwaway local password so every teammate is a real profile with a role; `gateway.roles` for writer, teammate, viewer, read-only and sessions-only identities), OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini`, the branch's served Control UI driven by headless Chromium, and the merge base built and served separately for the "before" phase. Full capture set with redacted RPC transcripts, sqlite dumps (`session_pending_inputs` state, `display`, content hash and size per row), `chat.history` excerpts and gateway logs: [`pending-input-discard/live/`](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/tree/b97d8d8f1ee3d878626bceb4c3e7bc2fe33eb5b5/pending-input-discard/live) ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/b97d8d8f1ee3d878626bceb4c3e7bc2fe33eb5b5/pending-input-discard/live/README.md)).

- **Retired rows created the way the issue describes.** Five follow-ups were queued behind a tool run (`messages.queue.mode: followup`); two writers had their role revoked while queued (rows became `cancelled`), then the Gateway was SIGKILLed mid-run and the teammate role lost write access while it was down, so recovery refused the other three (rows stayed `interrupted`). sqlite and `chat.history` agree (`after/01-create-retired.txt`).
- **Controls.** Every retired row shows **Dismiss** with a named label and the footer shows **Dismiss all**; the merge base renders the same rows with no control, and calling `chat.pendingInputs.dismiss` there returns `unknown method`.

  ![Before, merge base: retired rows with no control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/b97d8d8f1ee3d878626bceb4c3e7bc2fe33eb5b5/pending-input-discard/live/before/02-writer-rows-bottom.png)
  ![After: retired rows with Dismiss on each and Dismiss all in the footer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/b97d8d8f1ee3d878626bceb4c3e7bc2fe33eb5b5/pending-input-discard/live/after/02-writer-rows-bottom.png)

- **Dismiss one, reload.** The row is gone and stays gone after a reload. In sqlite the row still exists as `cancelled` with `display: false`, content intact; `chat.history` returns it hidden and empty (`after/02-dismiss-one-*.png`, `02-sqlite-dismiss-one.txt`, `02-history-after-dismiss-one.txt`).
- **Dismiss all, reload.** One request carrying exactly the four visible ids; after reload nothing renders and no footer; every row is kept, cancelled and hidden (`after/02-dismiss-all-*.png`, `02-sqlite-dismiss-all.txt`).

  ![After Dismiss all and a reload: only the conversation remains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/b97d8d8f1ee3d878626bceb4c3e7bc2fe33eb5b5/pending-input-discard/live/after/02-dismiss-all-3-after-reload.png)

- **Dismissed rows survive a restart.** After another SIGKILL and restart they stay `cancelled` + `display:false`, nothing resumes, no user turn is added (`after/05-dismissed-survive-restart.txt`).
- **Off-page browser copy is not resent.** Browser B held an unconfirmed outbox copy of its accepted follow-up (its `chat.send` response was dropped in the page), went offline, and the input ended `interrupted`. Writer A dismissed it from the UI. B came back online and reloaded: no `chat.send` for that input, outbox copy retired, no new user turn in the transcript. As a control, B's never-accepted local message did send on reconnect, so the outbox was draining (`after/03-offpage-*.png`, `03-offpage-copy.txt`).
- **Refusals, sqlite row identical before and after each** (`after/rpc/04*.txt`):

  | Caller | Result |
  |---|---|
  | read-only scope (`operator.read`) | `FORBIDDEN` missing scope: operator.write |
  | `operator.sessions.write` only, on a session it does not own | `FORBIDDEN` (`SESSION_ACCESS_CHANGED`); its session reads still work |
  | input still queued (also a mixed queued + interrupted batch) | `INVALID_REQUEST` `PENDING_INPUT_NOT_RETIRED`, nothing changed |
  | view-only collaborator, revoked writer, teammate demoted while the Gateway was down | `FORBIDDEN` |
  | repeat of an already-dismissed id | same id returned again in `dismissedIds` with its `runId`; unknown ids in `missingIds` |

- **Found by this proof and fixed in this revision:** a view-only collaborator in a shared session (`sharingRole: "viewer"`) still saw the controls; the Gateway refused the call and the rows came back unchanged (`after/04e-viewer-ui-*.png`, `04e-viewer-ui-click-sqlite.txt`). The UI gate now also hides both controls for `sharingRole: "viewer"`, with a failing-first test.

Not shown live: a revocation landing between RPC admission and the worker commit (a role change closes the caller's connection at once, so one in-flight call cannot span it live; the commit-boundary rollback is covered by the store and handler tests), and own-session success with `operator.sessions.write` only (covered by the handler test).

prs.title: fix(ui): bind the Working timer to the active run's own start
prs.body:
Closes #133545

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI's live Working timer counts time from an earlier turn when a new run starts outside the open pane, such as through `sessions.send`.

## User Impact

User impact: the Working timer for an externally started run counts from when that run began, not from the previous run's activity. Recorded per-run durations and the final history row are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

An externally started run first reaches the pane through the session row, before the pane knows its run id (the id arrives only through a local send or a reconnecting outbox entry). The retained activity that backdates it comes from an earlier run whose tool rows were never removed; live, that happens when the earlier run received a follow-up message while it was still working, because the post-finish history reload then keeps its tool row (see the real-Gateway section). During that window, the working progress took both its run identity and its start time from tool rows and stream segments the previous run had left behind. The timer then showed the previous run's start, plus the idle gap, and the indicator attached to the previous run's reply.

The pane now records when it sees the session idle. While no run identity is given, it ignores activity received before that point, both for identity and for the start time. A run identified by id still uses only its own timing. Activity that arrives after the idle point still times an unidentified run, so its own early tool rows keep counting.

## Evidence

- Failing-first unit tests at the `resolveWorkingProgress` boundary and through `buildChatItems`, which is the production caller. On main they fail: an unidentified second run starts at the first run's segment (900 instead of 60000) and the first run's tool row (1100 instead of 60000). They pass with the fix:
  - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.test.ts`: a run admitted after an earlier run left activity. Cases: identity missing; identity arriving later, with the start and key kept; the run's own activity received after idle; identity present.
  - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts`: two runs in one pane. Run 1 is identified, the pane goes idle, and run 2 is admitted from the session row alone.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat --maxWorkers=1`: 439 files and 5475 tests passed. This includes the handoff and preamble contracts that inferred identity still covers.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm check:test-types`, and targeted oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files all passed.
- Browser replay with the mock Gateway (local control-ui e2e harness, not committed). Run 1 is started externally with a tool call, then finishes, the session goes idle, and the clock advances 60 seconds. Run 2 is then admitted from the session row.
  - Before: run 2's Working row reads **1m 31s**, attached to run 1's reply. It snaps back to 1s only when run 2's first tool event arrives.
  - After: run 2's Working row reads **6s** in its own row.

Before (run 2 admitted, timer reads 1m 31s on run 1's reply):

![Before: Working row reads 1m 31s attached to the previous reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/f5451867f94f398626f6f2efe10e87dd94a40e91/working-timer-backdate/before-external-run-2-admitted.png)

After (run 2 admitted, timer reads 6s in its own row):

![After: Working row reads 6s in its own row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/f5451867f94f398626f6f2efe10e87dd94a40e91/working-timer-backdate/after-external-run-2-admitted.png)

### Real Gateway and real agent

Isolated branch Gateway (`6c0068f1e8d`, loopback, own state directory, token auth), OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` on the Codex runtime; the "before" UI is the merge base `8e1fafd407f` built in a throwaway worktree and served through `gateway.controlUi.root`. Every run was started from outside the pane with `openclaw gateway call sessions.send`; a headless Chromium sampled the Working row every 100 ms. Full capture set with redacted gateway frames, history stamps, the sampler logs and the read-only instrumentation patch used to confirm the mechanism: [`working-timer-backdate/live2/`](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/tree/3d4d0c2cf10d1849431ac77cc3387093cf6d9888/working-timer-backdate/live2) ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/3d4d0c2cf10d1849431ac77cc3387093cf6d9888/working-timer-backdate/live2/README.md)).

Sequence: run 1 calls a tool (`sleep 15`); about 8 s in, a second `sessions.send` reaches the same session and is delivered into the active run; run 1 finishes; about 80 s idle; run 2 is a plain external `sessions.send`.

| | Before (`8e1fafd`) | After (`6c0068f`) |
|---|---|---|
| Run 2 admitted | 19:59:00.5Z | 20:01:58.4Z |
| First Working label | **`288 output tokens · 1m 37s`**, sitting on run 1's reply | **`1s`**, own row, no run-1 token count |
| When run 2's id arrives | snaps to `1s` | continuous, no jump |
| Run 2 span per Gateway history | 17.9 s | 18.9 s |

![Before: at run 2 admission the Working row reads 1m 37s on run 1's reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/3d4d0c2cf10d1849431ac77cc3387093cf6d9888/working-timer-backdate/live2/before/run2-admission-011-195900655Z-1m37s.png)

![After: at run 2 admission the Working row reads 1s in its own row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceckert/openclaw/3d4d0c2cf10d1849431ac77cc3387093cf6d9888/working-timer-backdate/live2/after/run2-admission-011-200158647Z-1s.png)

The `1m 37s` is run 1's age plus the idle gap, counted from run 1's leftover tool row. Without the mid-run follow-up, the post-finish history reload removes run 1's rows and plain back-to-back `sessions.send` runs show `1s` on both builds (first capture set, `live/`).

Gaps: on loopback the backdated value lasts only until run 2's id reaches the pane (about 0.2 to 0.5 s), so the live defect shows as a flash and grows with each further external run; the issue's long-held values need a slower path for the id, such as a remote Gateway. The follow-up-while-working case is the one trigger found that leaves a tool row behind; other ways a row could outlive its run were not enumerated. If no idle render happens between two back-to-back runs, the earlier run's cached start can still carry into the next run until the new run's identity arrives; the pane then rebinds to the new run's own start.

CI note: the earlier `checks-ui (3/3)` failure on this PR was `sidebar-attention-lazy-failure.test.ts`, which this diff does not touch; it passes locally three times in a row and the same shard passed on sibling PRs. This push is rebased on current main.

prs.title: feat: preview Control UI themes before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #151479 (reuse of shared radio/option-card controls; this does not complete the consolidation tracker).

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a Control UI theme needs a compact, keyboard-friendly way to try it across the window before saving, including matching colors in the embedded terminal.

## User Impact

Users can hover, focus, or tap a theme to preview the current window; Apply theme or Enter saves it, while Cancel, Escape, or leaving Appearance restores the current selection. Other windows and saved preferences are unchanged during preview. All 11 built-in names/IDs are preserved, with palette descriptions and Beacon identified as the high-contrast option.

Arrow keys browse, Home/End jump, and Space previews without saving. The visible keyboard guide is scoped to the picker, not text fields. Plugin and personal palettes use the existing catalog, including cancellation when a previewed plugin disappears.

Themes may optionally author 16 ANSI colors. Existing terminals and scrollback repaint without restarting the shell; explicit true-color output remains application-owned. No database migration or operator configuration change is required. The approved temporary ghostty-web 0.4.0 repair includes rebuilt embedded WASM and generated ESM/CJS/declarations, with pinned sources, hashes, rebuild instructions, and removal gates in patches/README.md and the packaged source patches.

This is Omarchy-inspired groundwork, not an official collaboration or an installed Catppuccin/Tokyo Night theme pack. New wallpapers, continuous animation, and external CLI theming are outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing application theme owner now holds transient preview state separately from canonical preferences and rejects stale palette completion after cancellation. The picker reuses shared native radio navigation instead of adding a second keyboard model; the previous floating miniature was removed. Preview and commit share the font/accent reset policy.

The terminal updates native color defaults directly rather than injecting OSC into the PTY parser, preserving split escape sequences and active-theme reset baselines. The canvas also paints literal-black cell backgrounds correctly. Existing clipboard-success and disposal repairs remain intact. Most patch bytes are reproducibly generated dependency output, not a second terminal implementation.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI browser flow: window preview, all scoped navigation keys, explicit Apply/Enter, Escape/Cancel/route exit, no writes before Apply, a second window retaining its selection, touch, plugin preview/withdrawal, and saved-profile persistence.
- Chromium Appearance consumer suite: 20 tests. Focused keyboard/preview consumer also passed in WebKit. Focused owner/preference/configuration suites: 169 tests, including late palette completion and Gateway-scope retirement. Contrast matrix retains AA, with Beacon AAA for the sampled text pairs.
- Full terminal browser suite: 6 cases, including cold authored palettes, live reload/fallback, clipboard outcomes, input, memory isolation, and disposal. Native regressions cover all 16 colors, scrollback, explicit RGB, cursor preservation, fragmented CSI/OSC, and reset defaults.
- The literal-black canvas regression was red before the renderer repair and green afterward: SGR 40 paints [0,0,0], while untouched default background remains [30,30,46]. A fresh-store frozen install reproduced both generated runtime formats and the native WASM hash.
- UI production typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, docs MDX, and i18n verification passed. Independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving the black-background finding. PR CI provides the broad suite; no remote CI or whole-repository typecheck success is claimed.

- After GitHub reported an actual conflict, integrated main at `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd`. Kept the new canonical Settings preference owner rather than restoring duplicate bindings. On that exact base, all 9 browser cases, affected Settings/preview owner regressions, UI production typecheck, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0-P2 review passed. The integrated After capture is byte-identical to the image below. Earlier unchanged-contract proof is retained, not relabeled as remote CI.

- Hosted-review follow-up: completed the remaining browser-only `ApplicationTheme` fixture and corrected the radio test callback's return contract. The UI-components test typecheck leaf now passes, along with that browser test and all 5 shared-radio tests. These follow-up edits are test-only; production behavior and the inspected images are unchanged.

Existing persisted preference and theme-definition shapes are unchanged, and ANSI tokens are optional. A full v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade run was not performed; it remains an explicit qualification gap rather than a claimed pass.

The earlier editor/test type graph (before base integration) reported errors in untouched native-desktop, quota-reset, and regexp declaration inputs. That broad graph was not rerun or claimed fixed; this is not a clean full-project gate run. No live Gateway was modified or deployed. Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway fixtures.

### Visual proof

**Before — existing picker**

![Existing Appearance picker without window-local preview or Apply/Cancel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b6536cd-be32-486b-ac03-37fdf69ea075)

**After — current window previewing Tide while Claw remains saved**

![Window-local Tide preview with Apply, Cancel, and keyboard navigation guide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f3e0979-688d-4c1c-bb18-213dbcf42f85)

The captures use synthetic data. The After image shows an unsaved preview, not a deployed change.

Concept, UX direction, and feature request: Chris Eckert (@ceckert).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5c6bc88f-6d89-40f8-9bad-41b563880ac3)

## Worked on by

- @ceckert

prs.title: fix: tool-free agents fail to run in ordinary sessions
prs.body:
Related: #157790

## What Problem This Solves

An intentionally tool-free agent fails before answering ordinary messages when it inherits a nonempty `tools.allow` or `tools.alsoAllow` setting.

## User Impact

Agents configured with `tools.deny: ["*"]` can answer ordinary first and subsequent turns without exposing tools. An explicit per-run `toolsAllow` request that conflicts with that denial still fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog already distinguishes intentionally disabled tools from an allowlist that accidentally matches nothing. Include the resolved wildcard denial in that existing check; tool construction, filtering, execution authority, and prompt schemas keep their existing owners.

Original fix and live proof by @enki (Paul Bohm). No configuration migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Base regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-search-run-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the Node runtime failed exactly the two deny-all cases; 20 existing and explicit-runtime-request checks passed.
- Integrated candidate: all 22 catalog tests passed. Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and diff whitespace checks passed. Independent Codex review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- All six prompt-prefix stability tests passed; the complete targeted run passed both Vitest shards (28 tests).
- [Exact-head CI run 39894941285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894941285) passed on `ab22c87a41285169342817ec843473571fe9d17e`; the pinned watcher reported GREEN with no current pending or failing checks. Older cancelled/superseded runs remain in GitHub's broad rollup.
- The contributor recorded two ordinary authenticated `chat.send` turns through an isolated compiled Gateway on the original PR head. Both completed in the same session with zero exposed tools and retained replies. This lane has not independently rerun live Gateway/model traffic; a separate runtime build on the loaded host is outside the bounded live-proof budget.

Production +3/-1 (net +2); tests +45/-4 (net +41) against the integrated main base. The source growth is one condition in the existing validation owner.

prs.title: fix(hooks): preserve concurrent session-memory captures
prs.body:
Closes #159826

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost session-memory captures when concurrent resets or rollovers select the same date/slug filename.

## User Impact

Each capture keeps its own memory file and matching provenance. Existing file contents, numeric suffix naming, and manual-reset admission behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existence check and overwriting write previously ran independently, with asynchronous provenance recording between them. The existing workspace file-lock owner now keeps filename allocation, provenance recording, and exclusive atomic creation together. Transcript capture and optional slug generation remain outside the lock. Provenance still precedes file visibility and rolls back if creation fails.

Thanks to @jason-allen-oneal for the fix and Gateway reproduction.

## Evidence

- Regression red → green: six simultaneous automatic resets retained only one file on the unchanged baseline; the fix retains all six exactly once with matching hashes, session identity, and trust classification.
- All 24 focused tests passed across the hook, rollover, admission, and slug suites. After integrating main, the three changed files matched the reviewed/tested candidate byte for byte, and the three rollover tests passed again. The final regression file took 14.96 seconds of test time and 375.62 seconds wall time under heavy host contention. The first Bun attempt timed out during startup; the supported Node runner completed without weakened assertions.
- Targeted lint, formatting, production typecheck, and affected test typechecks passed. Independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The broader local `check-changed` passed every selected check except its unused-export scan: ten reported owner files were unchanged from baseline, and its full-tree scan timed out.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893021016) for `18ea9065fdd8c1b300a9bce1952769a998b0a016`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. No CI rerun was requested.
- [Contributor Gateway receipts and portable driver](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/b557f72c258c3f3fe7fa16ae3990e579bc77bd4b/README.md): six concurrent real `sessions.reset` calls lost one capture on the baseline. The contributor head retained all six new captures, matching provenance, and prior files across restart. This predates the final atomic-publication refinement.
- The fresh final-head Gateway run requested by ClawSweeper remains deferred: CI supplied no reusable runtime artifact, and a separate runtime build was skipped under heavy host contention. Only the contributor-head live receipts are claimed; no final-head model/channel round-trip was run, and channel credentials were unavailable.
- Production: +23/-10 (net +13); tests: +69/-0; docs: +2/-1. The production increase preserves provenance ordering using existing owners without new storage or configuration.

prs.title: fix: finish reply recording before resetting sessions
prs.body:
Related: #134498

## What Problem This Solves

A canonical session reset can fail after the transport has already accepted a reply. Delivery becoming idle releases lifecycle custody before the transcript mirror and cleanup finish, allowing `SqliteSessionMutationConflictError` while the accepted reply is being recorded.

## User Impact

Session reset waits for the existing recording and cleanup owner. The accepted reply remains durable before the reset boundary and is excluded from the new context. Transcript writer fences and delivery authorization remain unchanged; no new schema, retention policy, or configuration is introduced.

The reported CLI-backed reset/rebind paths and accepted-reply crash boundary have now been exercised on this exact head. Unfinished CLI work is canceled before stale delivery; supported deletion/recreation changes the physical session ID; accepted CLI/model replies already have canonical records before the HTTP acknowledgment. The patch repairs the demonstrated reset/settlement conflict within those existing owners. No new historical append destination or transactional outbox is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registered dispatcher settlement tasks remain joinable until they finish, run once through their existing owner, and participate in the existing lifecycle after-clear barrier. Source-owned events retain their operation until transport settlement before clearing it. No duplicate send or competing persistence owner is added.

Affected low-level test callers now finish the same outer dispatcher settlement lifecycle that the production facade owns. Intermediate producer/transport assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

Exact final head: `a7f5cc2f35fb2e0254207492149d52d3923c0cbc`.

[Immutable execution proof, raw logs, receipts, scripts, model/build identity, and SHA256 manifest](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/tree/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0).

- **Baseline RED → final GREEN through the shipped Gateway:** a real loopback HTTP receiver accepts the reply and holds HTTP 200; real `sessions.reset` is observed waiting in the existing lifecycle owner before HTTP 200 is released. Baseline delivery succeeds with one durable reply, but reset fails `SqliteSessionMutationConflictError`. The final build completes both RPCs with one physical send and one durable reply before the reset boundary; new-context `chat.history` excludes it. [Baseline receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/baseline/receipt.json), [final receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/candidate/receipt.json).
- **Actual agent and model:** a separate final-head run removes the synthetic reply resolver and uses the default agent path with existing local Ollama `qwen3:0.6b`, no cloud fallback. Actual inference produces all three replies; physical HTTP delivery, durable assistant-row recording, reset, and progress after retained-state restart pass. [Model receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/candidate-real-model/receipt.json), [model Gateway log](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/candidate-real-model/gateway-first.log), [model identity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/model-identity.json).
- Both final lanes stop and restart the built Gateway with retained isolated state, verify prior history and every retained transcript event byte, and repeat the held-receipt/reset overlap afterward. Both Gateway processes exit 0. Build: 148.01s; deterministic runtime: 63.89s; model runtime: 97.11s. Executable hashes and `dist/build-info.json` bind both runs to the exact final commit.
- **Reported CLI reset/rebind and abrupt crash:** the documented CLI backend launches a real Node subprocess that calls local Ollama and holds stdout before finalization. Through the actual originating-channel adapter (direct dispatcher deliberately throws), reset and delete/recreate suppress stale output; recreated physical session IDs differ. A real CLI reply accepted by HTTP has one canonical assistant row while HTTP200 is withheld. After actual Gateway SIGKILL, the fresh Gateway reads that reply through `chat.history`, preserves every prior canonical event JSON/compressed byte, and delivers/persists a new CLI reply. [117.26s passing receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/candidate-cli-origin-crash/receipt.json).
- **Accepted delivery plus actual replacement:** with the default agent/model and originating-channel transport, delete first returns the existing retryable UNAVAILABLE while transport is active, preserving storage. After settlement, delete/recreate changes the physical session ID; the accepted reply remains durable and is excluded from the new context. The same sequence passes after retained-state restart. [Receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/candidate-origin-rebind/receipt.json). The first fixture's structured-error assertion failure is retained and explained in the proof bundle.
- **Affected consumers: 45/45 passed** on the final head across owner settlement, tool-authored transcripts, pending-final dispatch, and pending-final delivery ([log](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/final-consumers.log), 80.83s). Initial raw-fixture hangs and the intermediate 15-pass/2-timeout result are retained. Completing the fixture's missing settlement lifecycle fixes them; the owner suite also passed 17/17 under a stricter 15s diagnostic bound. No assertions were weakened or timeouts increased.
- **[Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39881320624) passed**, with no failed or pending PR checks at publication ([snapshot](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/final-ci-snapshot.json)). Committed real HTTP/SQLite/controller regression covers the reset overlap; dispatcher regression covers concurrent settlement and joinability. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean P0–P2 for the production change. The subsequent test-only migration received its own review; its one failure-cleanup finding was fixed and the final review is scoped-clean ([reports and exact test-only delta](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/tree/d03bac5b15e0b00b741dd6e45bfa86daa2356fe0/fixture-repair)). Final-head native runs were rebuilt/replayed after that commit; prior-head proof remains separately labeled.

The baseline executable is `2975dedca83e94d3530fdb339077bfe040d1b560`; its auto-reply, sessions, and Gateway sources match task base `a8ead196291935d24c44a4f40b67397d88c70256`. The deterministic baseline and candidate use the same driver bytes. The real-model run is a separate sibling-path proof. All state and prompts are synthetic. Supported physical session replacement and abrupt process death at the accepted CLI reply boundary are proved; real Discord delivery, OOM, raw-database rebinding and arbitrary new outbox/destination policies are not claimed.

prs.title: refactor(ui): load application chrome through Solid boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional application pages, panels, and dialogs still use manual custom-element registration and loading state alongside Solid rendering.

## User Impact

The same pages, shortcuts, panels, and dialogs load on demand, keeping their native tags, routes, and selectors. The command palette retains its live input, selection, attachments, and composition custody while its implementation loads. Sidebar navigation keeps its original native element through desktop, drawer, and settings transitions.

After dismissing an import error, reopening that surface shows the retained error with an explicit Retry action. Retry attempts the import again; stale-build recovery keeps the existing unsaved-work and current-action checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Solid `lazy()` and its loading/error boundaries now own component loading. The existing plain shell owner keeps pending commands and persisted replay; connected shell-owned hosts decide when a command can be delivered. Requested components record retention only, without a second loading or readiness store.

The sidebar uses a small lazy adapter that returns its precreated native host after registration. Its bridge still owns rendering and lifecycle. This preserves early property assignments and native identity while removing the final shell registration loader. Delayed mounts notify the existing readiness owner. The public terminal readiness flag describes whether the connected shell can accept the first terminal command; it does not eagerly import the terminal just to expose a host. Native bottom docking is replayed through that same shell owner.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before measurement: compare production builds of the exact base and candidate on the same machine with the strict performance checker. Preserve lazy entry points, the single startup CSS request, and every enforced budget. An over-budget surface may not grow beyond the checker's 64 B build-variance allowance.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui`, the Gateway core leaf, and the UI-app/UI-components core leaves passed. |
| Formatting and lint | Targeted formatting and type-aware lint passed. One duplicate type import found during repair validation was consolidated and its targeted recheck passed. One existing tracked-async test warning remains. |
| Shell action custody, shell view, and readiness tests | 49 initial focused tests passed. Repair runs exercised 113 passing cases, then 41 passing cases in affected suites. The two remaining lazy-ready fixture failures were corrected and each passed individually. Runs use the pinned Bun forks pool. |
| Production build and strict base/head performance comparison | Final repair build and strict comparison passed with no warnings or violations. Exact base and head built on the same machine; the final follow-up only consolidates erased type imports. |
| Production Knip | Final repair census and exact base `4b07579bee3` logs are byte-identical with 11 existing findings. Three migration-caused type/export findings were removed; no new ignores. |
| Independent review | Full cutover, cleanup, and complete repair diff independently reviewed, scoped-clean through P2. Sidebar mount/readiness finding fixed; JSX error details and conditional label remain reactive. |
| Full UI and real-Gateway CI | Repair head awaiting full `ci:full` results. Initial run `39892182176` exposed the cold-host and lazy fixture contracts repaired here; remaining failures require current-head attribution. |

| Touched production metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Manual component-registration descriptors | 17 | 0 |
| Application manual request-loader instances | 3 | 0 |
| `onCleanup` | 1 | 1 |
| `getOwner` / `runWithOwner` / `flush` | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Production UI LOC | 6,947 | 7,207 |
| Test LOC | 8,543 | 8,551 |

| Production surface | Base gzip / requests | Head gzip / requests | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 315,876 B / 7 | 315,378 B / 7 | −498 B |
| Chat boot JS | 1,353,107 B / 23 | 1,355,462 B / 24 | +2,355 B |
| New Session boot JS | 826,135 B / 17 | 828,484 B / 18 | +2,349 B |
| Startup CSS | 41,128 B / 1 | 41,128 B / 1 | 0 B |

Chat and New Session remain below the measured source’s JS caps (1,405,102 B and 837,725 B), with the same 8 and 6 CSS requests. Component imports retain their existing lazy timing; the added loading/error presentation explains the small route-size increase.

CI repair preserves the onboarding attention entry point, Gateway recovery footer during a sidebar import failure, native terminal docking, and cold-terminal readiness. The E2E fixtures now distinguish a held component import from a mounted native host while retaining retry, stale-build, exactly-once attachment, and reconnect assertions. A type-only `es2024.collection` reference keeps the existing `Map.groupBy` use visible to the newly reached core typecheck leaf. The i18n baseline removes seven obsolete raw-copy entries.

The retained cleanup belongs to the palette custody primitive, which must release composition work even if disposed before settlement. Production growth is boundary presentation and native-host handoff code replacing the loader registry; the generic loader helper remains for callers outside this application cutover.

Measured branch guard census remains `onCleanup` 86, manual imports 66, `getOwner` 7, `runWithOwner` 12, and `flush` 3. The removed registration-descriptor callbacks were outside that syntactic counter; these are semantic loader removals, not claimed guard reductions. `check:control-ui-controllers --prune` passed without baseline edits.

Before/after screenshots below use synthetic fixtures at 1440×1000. They cover the retained sidebar, a cold command-palette import with a typed draft, and the ready palette. The browser capture verifies the full draft survives the handoff and Escape closes the palette.

prs.title: fix(android): avoid chat catalog reloads for unrelated metadata
prs.body:
Related: #179075

## What Problem This Solves

Android reloads chat commands and model choices when the Gateway reports only usage changes or a different agent's catalog changes.

## User Impact

The open chat keeps its existing choices without unnecessary catalog requests for unrelated events. Relevant catalog, authentication, command, selection, and refresh-status changes still refresh normally. No settings, stored data, or protocol changes; no user action required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settings catalogs already filter metadata events, but the chat controller still refreshed unconditionally. Apply the existing event flags at that remaining owner, including catalog-status recovery so a successful refresh can clear its warning. Unflagged events retain their existing full refresh behavior. This adds no cache, retry policy, or alternate refresh owner.

This is a focused repair for the demonstrated event-triggered traffic. A new diagnostic using the reported Android source and official Gateway 2026.9.6 reproduces a transient startup request-timeout warning that clears naturally, but not the sustained fast-response idle loop or Gateway memory pressure in #179075. That Gateway emits legacy unflagged notifications, whose refresh behavior this change preserves. The full reported incident remains unresolved; this PR does not close it.

## Evidence

- Baseline `a8ead196291935d24c44a4f40b67397d88c70256`: the new catalog regression fails on unwanted requests; both existing catalog tests pass (3 tests, 1 failure). The initial candidate run exposed a missing required model-name field in the new fixture; that fixture was corrected before the passing run.
- Candidate: all **99 tests pass** across catalog, model selection, and command controls; production and test Kotlin compile cleanly (focused Gradle run 134 seconds).
- Scoped Kotlin formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass; only the chat event handler and its existing catalog test suite change.
- **Exact-head native Android proof passes:** [immutable evidence bundle](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/635ffc07421b00da109df44528a053fc013e873d/README.md), [wire trace](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/635ffc07421b00da109df44528a053fc013e873d/native-wire.jsonl), [phase results](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/635ffc07421b00da109df44528a053fc013e873d/native-results.json), and [terminal receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/635ffc07421b00da109df44528a053fc013e873d/native-receipt.json). The installed production APK hash matches the build from `5fb773cb7daba27233488e8384471273d52fbb78`; Android instrumentation and the host scenario both pass across 12 phases on Android 36 with a real isolated Gateway and two synthetic catalog models.
- Ten usage-only events and three other-agent events produce **zero chat.metadata and zero session-catalog models.list requests**, retaining both accepted rows. Catalog, authentication, commands, selection, and legacy events each preserve the chat refresh (one metadata request and one session-catalog request). Injecting `refreshFailed` on an otherwise real Gateway response sets the existing warning while retaining both rows; the status-recovery event clears it. The existing ViewModel refresh action also clears a second injected warning.
- The trace retains independent global/provider-settings traffic: the other-agent phase produces six settings-owner model reads on the Overview screen, where no chat agent is selected. This PR suppresses the changed chat owner's reads; it does not claim to suppress those separate settings reads. Observation uses the live native activity's model state; the supplemental manual-refresh phase invokes the existing ViewModel action, not a physical button-tap assertion. Events and the warning fault are explicit proxy injections; catalog responses and app transport are real.
- Earlier 732-model runs hit client deadlines under heavy host contention. The passing two-model run proves the event-filter behavior; it makes no large-catalog performance or broader idle-loop/memory-pressure claim. Raw failed attempts are retained locally, and the public bundle explains the scope and counter correction.
- **Reported-version baseline, separate from the positive filter proof:** [immutable diagnostic evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bbac576892c0ca10f41572ac2ba6637297d584e9/reported-version-baseline/README.md), [wire trace](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bbac576892c0ca10f41572ac2ba6637297d584e9/reported-version-baseline/native-wire.jsonl), and [results](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bbac576892c0ca10f41572ac2ba6637297d584e9/reported-version-baseline/results.json). Android `dbac7730a12c90e95143f23e556199ab642e639e` with two logging-only observations and official Gateway `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b` completed normal pairing/startup plus **120 seconds idle** with **3 models.list, 2 chat.metadata, 1 models.authStatus, and zero metadata-change events**. The default configured response had **729 available and 3 missing-auth** rows; scoped/provider views left those three indeterminate. The first metadata reply took 21.308 seconds, beyond the app's 15-second deadline, producing a captured request-timeout warning. A natural health retry accepted all 732 rows and cleared the warning. These timings differ from the report's successful 85–1296 ms replies; there was no sustained 2 Hz producer and no candidate differential. The synthetic emulator/task-host fixture does not establish the reporter's private catalog, Tailscale route, background catalog churn, or memory-pressure cause. All task processes were cleaned up; no source-head change was made.
- Required exact-head CI and security status contexts pass; there are no failed or pending check conclusions. One duplicate Security Review job was cancelled by GitHub's concurrency queue despite the same-head review completing successfully. That cancelled administrative check remains visible; a supported rerun was refused because it requires base-repository admin rights.

prs.title: fix: recover sessions left processing without an active run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sessions remaining `processing` without an active run after an operation moves or input waits behind retained cleanup; the stuck-session diagnostic previously offered `recovery=none` for this state.

## User Impact

Queued input is shown as waiting until the controller admits it. Stale ownerless state can be reconciled automatically, with runnable mailbox work woken through normal admission. Retained cleanup stays visibly waiting: recovery does not discard queued input or release a writer that may still be running. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller already projects idle when a reply ends (#176682), but two producer paths bypassed that protection: message preparation marked processing before admission, and operation rekeying left the old diagnostic key processing while completion cleared only the destination. Admission promotes input already marked waiting, and rekey transitions retire the prior key (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation-admission.ts`). Cron admits before enqueueing, so admission leaves its first message accounting to the message lifecycle; the pre-admission producer is `src/logging/message-lifecycle.ts:57`. Ownerless recovery checks the captured diagnostic generation and current controller state, preserves queue counts and custody, publishes idle/waiting, and wakes the existing mailbox. It cannot adopt or cancel a later operation.

The supplied restart logs distinguish several incidents rather than one recovery failure. In `team-20261023-boot2051.log.gz` (uncompressed line numbers):

| Session | Correlation |
| --- | --- |
| `fa35e3ac` | A parent/requester-settle turn was interrupted by Gateway draining (restart lines 279/291/296/330); this was not the child session itself. Restart recovery started at 1234–1235 and completed at 1632. A later yield-cleanup timeout appears at 3744. Stale reports at 4113/4265 have terminal reply progress; six queued-without-run reports follow at 4542/4635/4928/5435/6569/8395. Operator abort at 12519–12520 released an 8,603,337 ms admission wait; recovery and queued dispatch resumed at 12522–12523 and 12581–12582. |
| `7325551f` | Seven stale reports at 5716/5886/6164/6710/7620/10179/14471, ending at age 9,584 seconds. The transition dates to well after boot; no matching owner, restart-recovery event, or provable subagent-parent relationship is present. |
| `074b4e8e`, `b60fbede` | Reports at 8044/8058 were controller-owned waits; both progressed at 8094/8096 and 8105/8107. |
| `5c6bc88f` | The repeated `failed=1` summaries (1391/1631/1664) retry this separate candidate after “Restart recovery requester has no matching operator authority” (1366/1615/1648). Final retry exhaustion hands it to the operator at 1665. |

The three “authority changed” messages (3389/4656/8078) concern reaction permission or sandbox finalization, not that recovery candidate. The restart excerpt records six sessions marked and 13 runs aborted at `team-20261022-restart2051.log.gz:274–275`.

The logs do not identify which retained in-memory barrier held `fa35e3ac`, nor the initiating event for `7325551f`. This patch fixes reproduced producer/recovery holes; it does not claim to reproduce that exact live barrier or weaken restart authority checks. Existing late-heartbeat PR #142349 covers a different recovery gate; recent child-recovery fix #180728 does not change these owners.

## Evidence

- Owner-boundary regressions failed on the unchanged base: source-key retirement, pre-admission waiting, and ownerless reconciliation with/without queued input.
- Focused controller, diagnostic recovery, message lifecycle, and dispatch lifecycle tests pass. The retained-cleanup regression also exercises reconciliation without releasing custody.
- Core and changed-test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- ClawSweeper identified an admission-before-enqueue counter regression. The real controller/lifecycle/heartbeat regression failed on the first PR revision (one running message falsely reported queued=1). Admission now promotes only existing waiting input; both event orderings retain the second-message backlog control.
- Independent Codex autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings on the committed branch.
- Production: +139/-10 lines (net +129); tests: +185/-62 (net +123); documentation: +1/-1. Growth is the missing safe reconciliation path and explicit admission/rekey projection; no new manager, timer, schema, or cleanup authority.
- Exact-head CI watcher: GREEN for `69f6ce8489be670bb2a1d39270142bf204fb2e97`, run [39892731593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892731593). The native policy excludes 19 superseded same-lane checks. No rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed.
- No live Team Gateway state was changed and no live restart was performed.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/sessions/session-controller.diagnostic-state.test.ts src/logging/message-lifecycle.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-controller-recovery.integration.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.diagnostic-events.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/sessions/session-controller.diagnostic-state.test.ts","src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts","src/logging/message-lifecycle.test.ts","src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.lifecycle-and-bindings.test-utils.ts"]' --concurrency 1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed TypeScript files>
pnpm exec oxfmt --check <changed files>
git diff --check
```

Result: 127 tests passed across six files; core and the affected test type graphs passed; focused lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The rekey regression was red on unchanged main before the owner fix. The added admission-order cases ran in 8 ms and 3 ms; controller regressions took 46 ms total. This run spent about 968 seconds in four Vitest shards (1,108 seconds including wrapper verification), dominated by shared-host compilation and filesystem waits; the unchanged cron consumer took 511 seconds including startup.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): release memory retained across page and session changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated page visits and session switches kept retired Control UI state alive, causing avoidable memory growth during long sessions.

## User Impact

Long sessions release retired geometry listeners and fallback board providers. Existing page, chat, and board behavior is preserved; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two strong-retainer paths explain confirmed growth. Font-ready promise callbacks kept disposed views reachable, including refs created in an inert template document. A module-level fallback-provider map accumulated one entry for every new session identity. Removable font-loading subscriptions now follow the active document, and each pane owns its fallback provider; leased Gateway-provider sharing stays with its existing owner.

The accompanying opt-in census measures the production renderer through ordinary routes, UI actions, and synthetic Gateway events. It records retention without adding a production diagnostics surface or setting speculative memory budgets.

| Confirmed leak, ranked by retained bytes/cycle | Evidence | Owner fix and regression proof |
|---|---|---|
| Font-ready promise chain: **~684,881 B per Custodian visit** | The same `FontFaceSet` retainer grew **3,424,404 B** between visits 5 and 10; promise reactions kept disposed view graphs reachable. | Remove promise callbacks in favor of removable font-loading listeners; bind inert-template refs to the active document. A retired publisher is collectible while fonts remain pending, and active views still remeasure. |
| Global fallback board-provider map: **~614 B per new session** | Map retained size **28,348 → 59,044 B** across 50 additional session identities (**30,696 / 50 B**); 100 real fallback providers at 100 switches on base (excluding one V8 allocation template). | Keep the fallback with its pane and retire replaced providers. Candidate snapshots have 4 real providers at 50 switches and 5 at 100, rather than one per historic identity; the existing retention suite proves replaced providers collect. |

Production LOC across the five changed modules: **1,352 → 1,346**. Across all 24 changed production, test, configuration, and documentation files: **6,285 → 9,501** lines. The 3,061-line opt-in census and parser probe cover the requested 122 production-renderer workloads, reusing existing parity recipes and transport fixtures; this code never loads in the product. Solid refactor checklist: `createEffect` **1 → 1**; `createRenderEffect`, `untrack`, raw `addEventListener`, DOM queries, `onCleanup`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner`, and `flush` each **0 → 0**. The remaining effect belongs to the existing layout-measurement primitive.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| Production renderer core census | **7/7 passed** in `SicV1F`: Custodian, Appearance, New Session, command palette, 100 session switches, 2,000 deltas plus finalization, and 10 reconnects. |
| Baseline inventory | **119/122 workloads complete** from `sDMqRl, SEw64k, ZB6vTF, 35pCVW, 3gE7i2`; incomplete rows below are setup/finalization failures, not passing measurements. |
| Remaining production head scenes | Queued behind the final baseline cases; no claim of a complete before/after pass yet. |
| UI/scripts typechecks and scoped lint | Passed on the final source, using the pinned typechecker. |
| Scroll observer collection regression | `releases retired publishers while fonts load and remeasures active views`: fails on base, passes with the fix; active-document/inert-template proof also passes. |
| Layout measurement tests | 4 passed, covering font settlement, disposal, and frame-batched resize behavior. |
| Existing chat-pane retention suite | 3 passed, including `releases replaced session providers while keeping the current fallback`. |
| Heap parser tests / tooling typecheck | Passed in the recorded checks. |
| Production build + strict performance | Both builds pass; exact startup/route figures below. |
| Isolated review | Final isolated Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The subsequent progress-log-only fix also passed isolated review. |
| Production Knip | One inherited unused file: `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs`. The exact path also fails in scheduled main run **39885503944**, job **120192944836**; no new Knip finding. |
| PR CI | `ci:full` requested for all UI unit, Control UI E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shards. |

### Production size

| Surface | Base gzip B | Head gzip B | Delta B | Requests base → head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Startup JS | 315,877 | 315,906 | +29 | 7 → 7 |
| Startup CSS | 41,124 | 41,124 | 0 | 1 → 1 |
| Chat boot JS | 1,353,087 | 1,353,125 | +38 | 23 → 23 |
| Chat boot CSS | 145,924 | 145,924 | 0 | 8 → 8 |
| New Session boot JS | 826,125 | 826,164 | +39 | 17 → 17 |
| New Session boot CSS | 106,434 | 106,434 | 0 | 6 → 6 |

Each JS difference is within the strict check's **64 B build-variance allowance**; CSS and request counts are unchanged. No lazy boundary changed and no budget was raised.

### Core retention comparison

| Workload | Interval | Raw heap B/cycle, base → head | Detached nodes over interval, base → head |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| route-custodian | 5–10 | 1,038,644 → 403,380 | 4,618 → 8,398; 186 → 186 |
| route-new-session | 5–10 | 1,193,671 → 524,116 | 11,333 → 15,563; 6,505 → 6,505 |
| route-appearance | 5–10 | 1,163,886 → 523,874 | 11,195 → 15,376; 6,335 → 6,335 |
| dialog-command-palette | 5–10 | 305,326 → 319,998 | 854 → 854; 855 → 855 |
| session-switch | 50–100 | 53,818 → 82,132 | 963 → 965; 1,056 → 1,499 |
| reconnect | 5–10 | 391,958 → 387,166 | 614 → 616; 666 → 668 |

On the candidate, Custodian, Appearance, and New Session detached-node counts plateau from visits 5 to 10. Streaming holds **511 detached nodes / 4,502 live owners** from 500 through 2,000 deltas, then settles at **508 detached nodes** after finalization. Session-switch raw heap and detached nodes still grow in the candidate; this table does **not** claim all retention is eliminated. The removed fallback map is established by its owning retainer and collection probe, separately from other heap contents.

A separate bounded dependency issue remains: Solid rc.16 `writeSelectValue` allocates its global `selectInsert` callback inside the first node activation. A sibling microtask captures the node, so the shared closure context retains the first select and an old settings form (~4.09 MiB in this snapshot). Hoisting the handler allocation out of the per-node activation is the upstream fix; this PR does not modify the Solid dependency. The session-switch anomaly is one older pane held through V8 shape metadata and a bridge props getter (~410 KB), rather than one retained provider per session. It is recorded for follow-up owner analysis.

Raw post-GC heap growth is report-only, not a leak estimate or a timing benchmark. JIT code, browser caches, retained templates, synthetic transport, and probe overhead remain included. For example, candidate New Session's visits 5→10 add about **2.68 MB of retained compiled code**; baseline reconnects 5→10 add about **1.84 MB** while live owners and detached DOM stay stable. Constructor retained totals overlap and must not be summed.

All **59 complete extended-baseline workloads** have stable per-event window/document/body listener counts and no interval-count increase from visits 5→10. The high timeout counts were traced to **30-minute router cache retirement** (agent-route keys include selection intent revision), plus bounded pet schedules, approval expiry, and question-refresh retries. These have named lifetimes; the audit did not establish another permanent timer/listener leak.

<details>
<summary>Measurement method, provenance, and coverage limits</summary>

Production bundles, Chromium **156.0.8078.4**, macOS arm64, synthetic data, native clocks, and one retained CDP profiler session per measured context. Samples follow a 4.1-second drain, two animation frames, and two explicit GCs. The mock request history is cleared before each sample. Timer instrumentation stores IDs, not callback references. Live/disposed owners are decoded from the installed production Solid shape; unknown flags fail the measurement rather than count as live. Host load was recorded in each manifest (one-minute load roughly 42–138 across these runs); these are retention observations, not interleaved timing claims.

Base bundle built **2026-10-23 01:21:09 UTC**; patched candidate bundle built **02:15:32 UTC**. Artifact IDs identify immutable observations: baseline `sDMqRl` (catalog/core), `SEw64k` (100 switches), `ZB6vTF` (expanded catalog), and retries `35pCVW` / `3gE7i2`; candidate core `SicV1F`. The candidate was built from the patched tree before its production-fix commit, so its embedded commit label alone does not distinguish the bundles. Full manifests retain the build timestamps and source revision.

Page/dialog workloads warm once and measure ten repeated visits in one document; the MCP App warms separately and opens ten confirmations total to respect its native prompt limit. Browser-auth recovery preserves the real 30-second throttle. File/private recovery reopen one seeded draft/failure rather than accumulating fixture content. Full exec approval uses its documented shell event because no browser UI dispatcher was found. MCP uses the official App SDK and sandbox document, not direct component mounting.

Boot-only Gateway confirmation and standalone approval/question windows use repeated full-document navigation in a retained browser context. Their snapshots cover retired documents; timer/listener counts describe the current document. Native OS pickers, the Linux companion renderer, arbitrary third-party dialogs, and every visual/loading/error variant are outside this core renderer census. Synthetic transport proves renderer lifetime, not real-Gateway behavior; broader proof belongs to PR CI.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full baseline census — 122 inventoried workloads</summary>

Use the last five visits for page/dialog slopes and the named intervals for long workloads. Detached bytes are native nodes' **shallow** bytes, not retained subtree size. Listener columns are window / document / body totals; per-event details remain in each census. A partial row is an observation before a failed setup/finalization and is not a completed proof.
