prs.title: feat: let plugin tools show native views in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Let trusted, operator-installed plugins surface their own interactive controls at the point they are useful in a conversation, without sending the user away to a separate page or asking the agent to generate a one-off UI.

For an internal incident-management plugin, that might be a live incident dashboard with an Acknowledge button and a link to its full panel. The agent decides **when** to show it; the plugin owns **what** it is and does. A tool supplies a data descriptor for a pre-existing component, which appears immediately and can later be reconstructed from history as it approaches the viewport.

**Why not sandboxed widgets?** Sandboxed widgets and MCP Apps remain the right choice for generated or isolated content, including interactive experiences through their supported bridges. This use case is different: the operator has already installed and trusted a native plugin whose browser code can use authenticated host APIs, share application state, and open native panels. Requiring its inline view to be a separate sandboxed integration adds cross-frame communication and state coordination just to change where that UI appears. This feature brings the existing native-plugin model into the transcript instead.

The invariant is unchanged: **the agent selects from registered components and supplies data; it never supplies executable UI code.** All executable code comes from the active installed plugin, under the same trust boundary as its native pages and panels.

## User Impact

User impact: installed plugins can show rich, interactive views directly in the conversation, immediately after a successful tool result. Reopening history reconstructs views only near the viewport, without rerunning the agent or tool.

This uses the existing native-plugin trust boundary and Custom plugin UI setting. The agent supplies data, not UI code. Plugin authors remain responsible for safe rendering, current-viewer resource authorization, and repeatable mount behavior; core adds no sandbox, HTML policing, or per-plugin RPC allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an owner-bound `api.inlineView(viewId, payload, { version, summary })` result helper, a versioned backend declaration, and `host.ui.registerInlineView`. One durable record carries plugin/view identity, the component interface version, payload, and text fallback, associated with the originating invocation. The installed native renderer must explicitly register the same interface version; there is no silent latest-version dispatch or core migration engine.

Payloads are limited to 16 KiB of serialized UTF-8, summaries to 4 KiB of serialized JSON, and interface versions to integers 1–65535. Missing plugins or unsupported versions leave the complete saved record intact and show its summary; a compatible registration can render it when available again. Compatibility/admission is resolved by the current browser catalog, not competing Gateway/browser schema systems.

Data freshness is entirely plugin-owned: a component may render a saved snapshot, fetch current data from a stored resource ID, or combine both. The incident example deliberately hydrates current state and shares it with a panel. Restoration does not rerun the original tool or agent; plugin network reads are allowed.

**Transfer scope:** native Markdown and catalog/Beam mirroring intentionally export the saved summary. Native HTML export retains the complete raw record and invocation metadata, without packaging executable renderer code. Full rich Beam transport and a general rich-session importer are not implemented; external catalog imports remain untrusted text. Text fallback is not claimed as full rich-component transfer.

## Evidence

### UI E2E readiness repair

[CI run 39891193575, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891193575) on `13fb07dc79b6` completed with 102 successful, 20 skipped and three failed jobs. The earlier wrapper/provisioning and hook typecheck jobs passed. The two remaining root failures were WhatsApp confirmation selection and a retained Terminal scenario choosing desktop controls during a mobile transition; the third failure was the aggregate gate. No inherited-failure exception was claimed.

`fdfb3dd991e42688c657426b6b2b59259bea4928` changes seven test/helper files only. Confirmation readiness now selects actual confirmation content while retaining both native prompt and Gateway-switch families and the existing visibility/opacity checks. Panels callers explicitly identify their intended mobile/desktop presentation, so the helper waits for that control rather than choosing a stale opposite control. Production UI/Gateway behavior, assertions, request counts, draft/canvas identity, timeouts and skip policy are unchanged; no sleeps or retries were added.

Both original cases passed their initial bounded replay; that was not treated as a fix. The exact final controlled browser-boundary regressions failed four cases with the original helpers and passed all six after repair. Final integration passed 18 cases across seven files, including both CI cases and representative modal/mobile/light/dark/desktop/Dashboard/side-chat consumers. Both UI E2E typecheck leaves, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Candidate tree: `0d7e28f78d0ad46c13c7420bf6b9617cea26f541`.

**Input limit:** ten of twelve inspected test/helper/owner blobs match this branch and the tested main/merge. CI's main has a lazy confirmation loader while this branch is eager. The controlled helper-boundary proof establishes the readiness defects independently; it does not claim timing equivalence or an exact-base failing run. The unchanged production feature retains the runtime/performance/authority proof below. Current-head CI remains required before landing.

### Extracted-wrapper CI repair

[CI run 39887429248, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887429248) on `bb61622da423` completed with 99 successful, 20 skipped and four failed jobs. Two root jobs exposed a PR-caused omission: the plugin API builder imports the inline-view emitter, but the extracted PR-wrapper inventory did not include `src/plugins/inline-view.ts`.

`13fb07dc79b60af7e0f97aa3e65a1c117a5af483` adds that single inventory entry; its three runtime dependencies were already listed. Both eager-import/extracted-package cases and all three failing cold-provisioning cases reproduced red before the fix and passed afterward. Whole selected files passed 19 eager-closure and 15 provisioning tests; the real unsupported-filesystem case also passed separately on executable tmpfs without altering its guard. Owning types, runtime-file lint, formatting, 958-file script erasability and diff checks passed. No production, UI, budget or assertion changes. Inventory-repair proof tree: `ccda1c7cca662b36b0f16eeadb636d5aa77e207c`.

**Coverage correction:** the earlier 32 scheduling/E2E/inventory passes included three narrowly seeded closures that never reached the plugin API builder. They did not prove complete extracted-wrapper execution; the full inventory and provisioning tests now do. The unchanged runtime inputs reuse the fresh authority/browser/performance proof below.

The other root failure was a hooks API/test mismatch already present in tested main `60e2d4b5ee9d241b9eb9147feeb3fbe0453c783b`: its loader removed `managedHooksDir` while the unchanged test still supplied it. Loader, test and typecheck config are byte-identical between that tested main and CI merge `b94cd2dbd2578573f27dfb18280a71cc2dcf851f`. This is source attribution, not a separately executed failing-main claim; the classifier's “new / selected scope not compared” result is retained. The aggregate CI gate failed downstream. No inherited-failure exception was used while the PR-caused defects remained. Fresh current-head CI is required.

### Refreshed runtime proof and startup budget

The runtime-verified base candidate `bb61622da423e238af4ac417d855a35cfe303a05` incorporates `9c29902212c54ebcfbc73324043af3923aa42f2f`, resolves five conflicts, and preserves current-main lifecycle cancellation, lazy tool rendering, sender-label ownership, native record/export semantics and tighter route budgets. A one-line ClawRouter host-fixture completion fixes the new-main TS2741 compiler error without changing production behavior or weakening assertions.

**Budget decision:** Jacob Tomlinson accepted the +50 B startup allowance on 2026-10-22. The fixed committed ceiling remains 325,131 B, but this refresh preserves main's newer **315,881 B stored baseline**, rather than restoring the older, larger baseline. The existing 512 B growth and 64 B build-variance allowances are unchanged: the effective startup limit is now **316,457 B**. No additional allowance was needed or used.

Canonical `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 9c29902212c54ebcfbc73324043af3923aa42f2f` passed with normalized build inputs:

| Surface | Gzip bytes | Limit | Headroom | Requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,273 | 316,457 | 184 B | 7/9 |
| Chat boot | 1,354,617 | 1,405,102 | 50,485 B | 23/25 |
| New Session boot | 826,254 | 837,725 | 11,471 B | 17/19 |

- **29 final scoped checks passed:** 79 backend, 80 UI, 25 Beam, 37 performance-checker, 32 scheduling/E2E/wrapper, one selected scheduling guard, two mock-browser, one real-Gateway and two ClawRouter fixture tests; current runtime/UI builds, targeted types/lint/format, and SDK exports/current surface checks. The CLI boundary accepts 316,457 B and rejects 316,458 B.
- **Fresh real-Gateway authority proof:** authorized mutation and independent readback; read-only denial without resource mutation; retirement during authentic hydration rejects retained handles with zero new authenticated requests. The served entry hash is `2ae7b48063b64424905f8ef1465d5e80a0d204ccfda45a1f586cdd24fd8f89ac`. This is saved-native-record restoration with **zero model turns**, not a live-provider claim.
- Independent review of the full refreshed candidate, with eleven complete owner contexts, found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The sole later change is the inspected one-line fixture member; its type and behavior checks pass. Runtime/test-fixture proof tree: `b4b3779f87361cbbee448b2ec508056af96e2130`.
- **Measurement distinction:** the ordinary, non-normalized build emitted a 316,486 B startup warning (+29 B). Its successful compilation is not treated as a size-gate pass; the canonical normalized comparison above is the passing performance evidence.
- **Retained local limitation:** the historical two Levanto DNS-fixture failures under trusted proxy selection were not rerun or relabeled green. Their test/transport blobs remain unchanged, with no proxy bypass, deadline change or assertion weakening. No baseline replay established inheritance or the historical CI failure cause.

Earlier publication evidence follows; its CI and measurements belong to the explicitly named older heads, not this refresh. Current-head CI is still required by the native landing workflow.

- Versioned emission/dispatch, durable record round trips, current scope/Labs admission, restoration, and direct/nested invocation identity are covered. The earlier 69 backend/projection/transfer tests passed; storage/catalog/import and HTML preservation proof remains valid. Core storage/import coverage and the 25 passing Beam mirror/parser tests now live in their respective owners. External imports still cannot authorize native mounts.
- On the final repair candidate, 135 transcript/search/input-order/native-view tests passed, plus both built-browser scenarios. Actual bundled Control UI and the compiled example cover immediate display, shared panel action, lazy 30-call history/disposal, version fallback, missing-plugin restoration, and search filtering with synthetic Gateway I/O. Plugin hydration reads are allowed; no original tool/model is rerun.
- All five hosted findings are addressed: scoped example lockfile, search filtering, trusted-wrapper runtime inventory, core/plugin test ownership, and SDK export count. The extension boundary, complete wrapper extraction, SDK surface-report/compiler-join, and affected catalog/Gateway tests pass. Public SDK exports remain 3810/3810 without increasing the budget or removing unrelated shipped exports.
- The exact Gateway-root and extension-test compiler configurations that failed CI now pass, as do UI production types. Touched-file lint has zero warnings/errors after extracting cohesive canvas logic and fixing the companion render; formatting and whitespace checks pass. The census mock retains real exports, its test passes, and the supported mock-factory check passes with no baseline edits.
- Independent full-branch review at `8d7be4e18ef7` and fresh review of the complete repair delta at `43d6e32ba4b1` completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Earlier full `pnpm build` passed (161.8 s), with startup JS at 325,011 bytes gzip below the unchanged 339,379-byte limit. The repair batch regenerated the boot manifest and rebuilt the production UI for browser proof; unchanged full-build inputs reuse earlier evidence. PR CI provides broad current-head coverage.

### Final CI corrections

At `a87add038d66`, the new real-Gateway fixture is included in the independent private-server ownership expectation. The owning guard failed before the one-line repair and passed afterward; all 13 scheduling-contract tests pass.

The separate Levanto batch-conversion test now controls its clock rather than racing a 500 ms wall-clock deadline. The deadline value, production behavior, payload assertions, and dedicated deadline/abort cases are unchanged; 47 registration/guarded-transport tests pass under the pinned Bun runtime. Targeted extension/tooling types, lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and independent delta review pass.

**Attribution limit:** [the previous CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39312262389) did not record Levanto's unavailable reason. Normal replay passed; a deterministic 501 ms expiry control reproduced `unavailable: transport` with the same valid response. This establishes clock sensitivity, not the historical failure's exact cause or proven inheritance. The assertion now includes the outcome if it fails again.

### Real-Gateway authority proof

[The committed production-path test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8ae949331483e70840cd2c4bf6ab0d13491392bc/ui/src/e2e/plugin-inline-view.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts) passed against a disposable real Gateway, the built Control UI, and the actual incident example—not mocked Gateway responses.

| Case | Observed final effect |
| --- | --- |
| Connection granted exactly `operator.read` attempts acknowledgement | Gateway rejects with `missing scope: operator.write`; independent reads show INC-42 unchanged (`acknowledged: false`). |
| Authorized browser restores/reloads the saved inline view and clicks Acknowledge | Exactly one mutation request; independent backend read confirms INC-42 acknowledged. |
| Mount retires while an authentic hydration reply is held | Hydration and retained-host read/write calls reject with `This plugin UI view has ended.`; zero new authenticated requests from the retired host. A live-host read crosses the same socket afterward and confirms INC-43 unchanged. |

The test seeds an already-saved descriptor through the transcript owner while the disposable Gateway is offline. A browser observer retains the genuine scoped mount host; transport instrumentation delays one real reply after the handler produced it, without replacing authorization or response contents. It records zero `chat.send` calls. This demonstrates **mounted-view retirement**, not independent replacement of the whole plugin activation. No production policy or behavior changed to obtain the result.

The scenario passed in 4.19 s (9.25 s including Gateway setup; 39.78 s cold runner). The QA runtime and production UI builds, 37 scheduling/inventory tests, targeted UI-E2E/tooling typechecks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent review of this proof-only delta found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The sanitized trace contains only synthetic incident IDs, scopes, allowed/denied outcomes, request counts, and bundle identity; its SHA-256 is `19fe341e5d25550c124c3bbe38f71fca5e40ee446e5097357cf5aaa9063e025c`.

prs.title: fix(cli): config set writes null holes into arrays when setting a missing index
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set` writes `null` holes into a config array when the path sets an array index beyond the array's current length, corrupting the authored config (e.g. `config set 'agents.list[5].id' 'other'` turns `agents.list` into `[{"id":"main"},null,null,null,null,{"id":"other"}]`).

## User Impact

Users can no longer accidentally corrupt their config with `config set` on an out-of-range array index. Instead they get a clear error telling them the array's current length and that they can append with that index or update a lower one. Existing in-bounds updates and appends (index == length) behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`setAtPath` in `src/cli/config-cli-path.ts` wrote array elements without checking the index against the array length, unlike `getAtPath` and `unsetAtPath` which both bounds-check. An out-of-range write produced sparse array slots that are preserved through `coerceConfig` and written to the config file, silently corrupting user config. The fix rejects `index > current.length` in both the traversal and leaf cases with a message that guides the user to append or pick a valid index.

## Evidence

Reproduction (before fix) — setting an index beyond the current array length:

```text
> openclaw config set 'agents.list[5].id' 'other'
result list: [{"id":"main"},null,null,null,null,{"id":"other"}]
```

After fix:

```text
Error: Cannot set array index 5; array "agents.list" has 1 element(s). Use index 1 to append or a lower index to update.
```

Tests: `pnpm vitest run src/cli/config-cli-path.test.ts` — 26 pass (5 new regression tests covering traversal and leaf out-of-range writes, in-bounds update, append at length, and the exact error message). Also verified `coerceConfig` preserves the sparse holes, confirming the corruption was real and reachable. `tsgo:core` and oxlint clean.

prs.title: fix(tts): stop duplicating captioned final text when separators differ
prs.body:
Fixes #181070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicated reply text in Telegram captioned final TTS when streamed blocks and the final answer use different paragraph separators.

## User Impact

The complete answer appears once across the voice-note caption and overflow text, retaining the final answer's paragraph spacing. Distinct code literals, spaces, tabs, and indentation remain distinct. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the normal and ACP block collectors join deferred text with a single newline. The final payload retains blank lines, so the shared merger's literal equality and prefix checks can fall through to concatenating two complete copies of the same answer.

The maintainer rewrite narrows the contributor's all-whitespace comparison to runs of newlines after the existing end trimming. It returns the original final text on equivalence, without rewriting output bytes. Blank-line-only differences are treated as formatting; meaningful spaces and tabs are never normalized. The comparison fits into an existing return branch, and the redundant exact-equality term is removed. No new helper, state, or transport-specific policy is needed.

Thanks @mushuiyu886 for the original fix and paragraph-separator regression. Their commit remains in the PR history; the regression is retained in its owning test group, with one added regression for ClawSweeper's internal-space example.

## Evidence

- Source confirmation on main `93ba611dc599a87d84435d6e4b35ebcf9a77aae3`: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.block-reply.ts:91` and `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts:280` join blocks with one newline; normal dispatch calls the shared merger at `dispatch-from-config.choose-route.ts:361`; `src/tts/captioned-final.ts:63` concatenates separator-equivalent complete answers.

prs.title: fix(memory): session memory search loses earlier transcripts after a session reset
prs.body:
Closes #137265

Replaces my earlier attempt #156256, which changed which transcript block types get exported and does not address this; I am closing that one.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory search stops finding earlier conversations once a session key rolls over to a new session id (daily or idle `session.reset`), even though the transcript is still stored.

## User Impact

User impact: with `memory.search.sources` including `sessions`, what was said before a reset stays searchable after it. `memory status --index` keeps counting the earlier transcripts and `memory index --force` no longer drops them. Installs that already lost those index rows get them back on the next index pass, which costs one extra transcript read per rolled-over session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session corpus used by the search index only listed the current transcript behind each session key, so after a reset the earlier transcript looked stale and its chunks were removed, while `docs/cli/memory.md` says retained and reset transcripts stay eligible. Retained SQLite transcripts were only requested by dreaming ingestion.

The sync now requests retained transcripts as well and keeps the ones a live session rolled over from, following the recorded `previousSessionId` chain. Transcripts of deleted sessions that are still awaiting cleanup are not in that chain, so they keep dropping out of the index as before. Corpus entries now carry `previousSessionId` from the session window for this. Because a rolled-over transcript shares its session key with the current one, and the sync pipeline addresses SQLite transcripts by that key, each retained transcript gets its own address inside the sync.

## Evidence

- Regression test `manager-session-rollover.test.ts`: seeds a transcript under `agent:main:main`, indexes, rolls the key to a new session id that records the previous one, indexes again. Failed on the base with `files: 1, chunks: 1` (the earlier transcript gone), passes with both transcripts indexed and the earlier one returned by search.
- Existing guard `index.test.ts` "prunes removed sessions without re-embedding unchanged survivors" still passes, which is what keeps deleted sessions out of the index.
- Real entry point, built from this branch, local mock model/embedding server, `session.reset: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 1 }`:
  - base behavior (same on 2026.8.2 and 2026.10.5): after the rollover `memory status --index` reported `sessions · 1/1 files`, `memory search <marker>` returned nothing, `memory index --force` did not bring it back.
  - this branch, after the same rollover (`session_windows.previous_session_id` set, Gateway stopped, CLI offline):

    ```
    $ openclaw memory status --index --agent main
    Indexed: 3/3 files · 12 chunks
    Dirty: no
      sessions · 2/2 files · 2 chunks · 24.1 KiB text + embeddings
    $ openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
    -> sessions/main/797245cd-….jsonl  "User: La parola di controllo memoria è ZAFFIRO927. ..."
    $ openclaw memory index --force --agent main && openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
    -> same hit; the current session (sessions/main/e03a80d4-….jsonl) stays indexed and searchable too
    ```
- Focused suites run locally with `--maxWorkers=1`: memory-core `manager-session-*`, `manager-reads`, `manager-targeted-sync`, startup catch-up, sync control, `index.test.ts`, `tools.real-manager`, `memory-mutation-authority`, `session-backfill`, `dreaming-phases`, and `session-transcript-corpus` in memory-host-sdk; `check-changed` on the touched files.

prs.title: improve(ui): reduce gzip boot transfers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clients negotiating gzip currently download avoidable bytes before the Control UI's first usable view.

## User Impact

Startup transfers 12,527 fewer gzip bytes, Chat 52,342 fewer, and New Session 32,092 fewer, with the same requests and application code. Brotli clients are unchanged. The matched production build takes 2m07s versus 1m20s on this shared host; the extra build work buys smaller gzip transfers and does not add browser work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing build-output owner uses its canonical boot-asset collector to select optimized gzip for Chat, New Session, and login. Other assets retain the existing fast Pako encoder. Brotli, lazy boundaries, asset URLs, and serving behavior stay unchanged. The same collector still supplies offline critical assets.

`@gfx/zopfli` 1.0.15 is a build-only dependency: a portable Wasm wrapper around Google Zopfli, no install hooks, one existing transitive dependency (`base64-js`). Registry integrity and package contents were checked. Its upstream implementation is stable but lightly maintained (last upstream commit in 2021, unarchived; about 246,000 monthly downloads). No dependency reaches the application bundle.

## Evidence

Final head `cc3d6229396d55fc524768d22051b6ed54ba95a9`. Matched production builds use base `3b39800d247e8c6fc17b97ba38b0ba05a4adab3a`, identical fixed build metadata, and 29 hash-pinned generated plugin inputs. The integrated output has the same 2,944 raw artifacts and 2,117 byte-identical Brotli files. All served raw files are byte-identical; 533 sourcemaps differ only in checkout-root paths (including generated worker-import source text), verified after substituting those exact roots. All 2,117 gzip files round-trip to the exact same raw bytes. Across all precompressed assets the encoder saves 70,625 B; the route table below counts each route separately. No rendered output changed, so there is no visual delta to capture.

| Surface | Base gzip B | Head gzip B | Reduction | JS requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup | 316,324 | 303,797 | 12,527 (3.96%) | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,349,072 | 1,296,730 | 52,342 (3.88%) | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 823,291 | 791,199 | 32,092 (3.90%) | 17 → 17 |

Caps preserve the base's relative headroom: startup 312,208 B, Chat 1,346,097 B, New Session 801,833 B. The startup baseline was regenerated with `--update-baseline --reason`. Strict performance checks pass with zero violations. Complete feature-grouped attribution remains in #181052; this change alters compressed transfer bytes, not that source graph.

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| UI typecheck | Pass on final encoder selection |
| Existing precompression contract | 1/1 pass with optimized round-trip/size, unchanged Brotli, and byte-identical optional gzip |
| Vite configuration tests | 41/41 passed during encoder implementation; final default encoder restores the original byte contract |
| Targeted format / lint / diff | Pass on the final selection |
| Production build / strict budgets | Pass; same raw, Brotli and request inventory |
| Production Knip | Integrated head and exact `3b39800` base both exit 1 with the identical sole unused file `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs`; no UI or dependency findings |
| Simplification / isolated review | Existing owner and collector reused; isolated P0–P2 review clean |
| Cold-load benchmark | Failed declared gate after the allowed 20 pairs; see below. PR held. |

Timing acceptance, recorded before measurement: ten alternating cold-cache base/head pairs on one Testbox, using the committed Control UI cold-load workload without tracing. Transcript-visible and enabled-composer median regressions must each be ≤5%, and neither p95 may worsen. One further ten-pair batch may qualify combined twenty-pair evidence. A Vite preview benchmark checks presentation timing; no claim is made that Brotli transfer or JavaScript execution gets faster.

Production/build TypeScript LOC: 1,628 → 1,643 (+15); direct test LOC: 24 → 28 (+4). The growth selects the slower encoder using the existing boot set while keeping optional-asset build cost unchanged.

### Cold-load result: held at the timing gate

Exact base/head above, Testbox run [39894403908](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894403908). Requested 16-class runner supplied 4 CPUs and 16.56 GB RAM; actual resources and load are recorded. Two batches of ten alternating cold-cache pairs used the same source, builds, and host. No third batch.

| Sample set | Milestone | Base median / p95 ms | Head median / p95 ms | Median / p95 change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First 10 pairs | Transcript | 800.40 / 870.80 | 797.00 / 958.70 | -0.42% / +10.09% |
| First 10 pairs | Enabled composer | 797.95 / 869.50 | 795.50 / 956.90 | -0.31% / +10.05% |
| Additional 10 pairs | Transcript | 429.75 / 512.00 | 421.35 / 552.20 | -1.95% / +7.85% |
| Additional 10 pairs | Enabled composer | 428.90 / 510.70 | 420.45 / 551.50 | -1.97% / +7.99% |
| Combined 20 pairs | Transcript | 505.35 / 813.70 | 588.85 / 946.00 | +16.52% / +16.26% |
| Combined 20 pairs | Enabled composer | 503.90 / 811.90 | 587.70 / 944.60 | +16.63% / +16.34% |

The combined twenty-pair result does **not** meet the declared gate. Both batches have a slightly faster candidate median, and both variants move from roughly 800 ms in the first batch to roughly 430 ms in the second, but neither fact waives the combined result or the worse tails. This PR is held; no timing pass or merge authorization beyond the standing gate is claimed. The raw application bytes and Brotli assets remain identical as verified above.

All 136 downloaded timing artifacts passed SHA-256 verification. The final source proof identifies exactly `cc3d6229396d55fc524768d22051b6ed54ba95a9` and base `3b39800d247e8c6fc17b97ba38b0ba05a4adab3a`, verifies all 12 changed source/configuration files, and confirms identical build/plugin inputs. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the hook-loader cache regression test failing the current test type graph after `prepareInternalHooks` intentionally stopped accepting private directory override options. The stale fixture call prevents the compiler from reaching the cache-freshness coverage even though those fields are no longer consumed by the loader.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible or production-runtime change. Maintainers regain type-correct CI coverage for hook import freshness while the existing workspace fixture continues to verify reloads after same-size edits with restored modification times and after metadata lookup failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loader now owns its production discovery roots and accepts only failure-mode and selection options. This change removes the obsolete argument object from the missed test caller and preserves fixture isolation through the existing root owners: the test pins the managed state directory to its temporary workspace, points bundled-hook discovery at an empty temporary root, and restores both in teardown. It does not restore private production inputs, add a test-only seam, change production discovery or selection, or weaken any cache, handler, lifecycle, path-admission, or cleanup assertion.

## Evidence

On exact base `cbd99fa1e3663a57bd292302ff9536d354b7c12f`, the canonical `core-test-config-cli` type graph failed with TS2353 at this call because `managedHooksDir` is not a supported option.

prs.title: fix(macos): skip passive Gateway uninstall without a service
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes passive macOS Gateway stops dispatching an uninstall when the active profile has no LaunchAgent definition. Remote and otherwise inactive profiles can reach this path during normal lifecycle reconciliation; the unnecessary low-level call can consult shared service handoff state and turn an already-stopped profile into a failed state.

## User Impact

A profile with no installed Gateway service now remains cleanly stopped without touching another profile's service state. Installed services still stop normally, including their child-process teardown, lifecycle generation checks, runtime-retention behavior, and service-authority validation. Explicit low-level disable remains able to remove a ghost launchd registration when its plist has disappeared.

## Why This Change Was Made

`GatewayProcessManager.stop()` already captures the current profile's immutable service custody after stopping its owned child and rechecking the active lifecycle. The captured definition therefore provides the caller-level distinction that the low-level API cannot make: an absent definition means a passive stop has no service effect to request, while an explicit `GatewayLaunchAgentManager` disable still means label-based ghost recovery.

The correction stays at that ownership boundary. It adds no service state, retry, timeout, lock, configuration, or compatibility path, and it leaves the low-level uninstall behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

The source-equivalent failure was recovered from macOS CI run `39885503944`, job `120196314067`: the default-profile absent-service case observed an unexpected `uninstall`, and the named-profile case observed that same call followed by a handoff-state failure. The existing direct low-level regression independently requires missing-plist disable to dispatch `uninstall`.

The final exact head will be qualified by the maintained `macos-swift` CI job, including Swift lint and format checks, native test compilation, the default-profile process-manager suite, the named-profile isolation suite, and the direct launch-agent-manager ghost-recovery control. No operator Gateway, preferences, Keychain, credentials, or user state are used for this proof.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep active code-mode run expiry on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A running Code Mode session can be killed early or left parked far past its TTL whenever the system clock is stepped by NTP (a rewind stretches the expiry timer, a forward jump prematurely expires active work). The active-run expiry deadline chain in `src/agents/code-mode-state.ts` scheduled and compared everything against the wall clock `Date.now()`.

- Problem: four call sites used the wall clock: the `setTimeout` remaining-time computation, the `removeExpiredRuns` comparison default, the renewal seed, and the `storeSuspendedRun` seed. A rewind inflated the armed `setTimeout` delay (runs lingered); a forward jump shrank it (active sessions were killed early).
- Solution: switch the whole in-process deadline chain to `performance.now()`.
- What changed: `src/agents/code-mode-state.ts` (4 one-line seed/consume swaps), plus a table-driven regression test.
- What did NOT change: the shared `resolveExpiresAtMsFromDurationSeconds` helper; `live-agent-probes.ts` still uses wall-clock epoch as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The expiry values are purely in-process: `expiresAt` / `agentWaitRetainUntil` live in an in-memory `Map` and are never serialized, persisted, or compared across processes. Every seed and comparison stays inside one process, so the whole chain can (and should) run on the monotonic clock — mirroring the established repo pattern in `request-start.ts`, which already uses `performance.now() + MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_MS`.

- Best fix: switch the full chain (seed, comparison, delay, renewal) to one clock domain. Mixing a `Date.now()`-seeded value with a `performance.now()` comparison is the exact domain mismatch this fix removes.
- Alternative rejected: applying `performance.now()` only at the `setTimeout` site leaves the comparison and renewal seeds on the wall clock.
- Seed points are wrapped in `Math.floor(performance.now())`: the shared `resolveExpiresAtMsFromDurationSeconds` requires a `Number.isSafeInteger` result (`nowMs + durationMs` must be integral), and `performance.now()` returns a float. The `setTimeout` consume site keeps the raw float. This preserves the integer contract without modifying the helper.
- Risk: one existing test ("preserves accepted output when wait expiry exceeds the Date range") was removed because a bounded monotonic clock can no longer overflow the Date range; it can be re-targeted at the `storeSuspendedRun` unit level if reviewers prefer.

## User Impact

Active Code Mode runs now expire on the monotonic clock, so clock adjustments no longer distort them: a rewind no longer leaves a completed run parked far past TTL, and a forward jump no longer prematurely kills a still-active session. Stable-clock behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real subprocess proof driving the shipped chain in `src/agents/code-mode-state.ts`: real `createCodeModeRunOwner` → real `storeSuspendedRun` → real `removeExpiredRuns`, with real `setTimeout` and real monotonic `performance.now`; only the host wall clock (`Date.now`) is skewed after arming (TTL = 5000 ms).

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-expiry-real.mts   # standalone real subprocess, only Date.now monkey-patched
```

Before/after matrix, real monotonic elapsed time to disposal:

| wall-clock skew | base (`Date.now` deadline) | this head (`performance.now` deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ~5010 ms ✓ | ~5008 ms ✓ |
| +120 000 ms | **406 ms ✗ early-kill** | ~5006 ms ✓ |
| −120 000 ms | **>12000 ms ✗ lingered** | ~5001 ms ✓ |

- Base forward: killed at 406 ms of 5000 ms TTL (**early-kill**); Base rewind: still parked past 12 s (**lingering**).
- This head: disposed at ~5 s monotonic TTL under every skew.

**Settlement renewal (Scenario B, +120 000 ms wall step):** a parked run still awaiting an `agentWait` bridge settlement holds an `agentWaitRetainUntil` retention window. When its `expiresAt` elapses, `removeExpiredRuns` renews it. The retain-window seed is epoch-based on the wall-clock implementation, so the forward step pulls it past and the run is disposed; on the monotonic head the window is untouched and the run is renewed.

| scenario | base (`Date.now`) | this head (`performance.now`) |
|---|---|---|
| agentWait renewal, +120 000 ms | **DISPOSED despite pending agentWait** ✗ | **renewed, kept alive** ✓ |

- Base: the forward step pulls the epoch `agentWaitRetainUntil` into the past → run **wrongly disposed**.
- This head: monotonic retain window holds → run **renewed** and kept parked.

This is a real running process (real `setTimeout` delays, real monotonic `performance.now`), only the wall clock stepped — the same technique used by the sibling monotonic-clock PR #178986.

**Shipped Gateway exec/wait proof** (isolated real Gateway + real agent/model + real `exec` tool): the same in-process expiry chain is exercised through the shipped `exec` tool entry. `startGatewayServer` + a real token `connectGatewayClient` + a mock OpenAI-responses model (real SSE transport) drive the real `exec` tool; exec#1 parks cell A via the shipped `yield_control` → `storeSuspendedRun` path, exec#2 sleeps to keep the agent run alive so the cell can expire via the code-mode TTL timer rather than run-end cleanup. Only the host wall clock (`Date.now`) is stepped briefly (±120 000 ms) after parking; `performance.now()` stays real (TTL = 15 000 ms).

```console
$ cd openclaw && VITEST=1 node --import tsx/esm proof-expiry-forward.mts   # forward step
$ cd openclaw && VITEST=1 node --import tsx/esm proof-expiry-backward.mts  # backward step
```

Forward (+120 000 ms wall step):

```text
[provider] exec #1: "await yield_control(); return \"A\";"
cell A parked runId=cm_e8c4aaee-9653-4800-9a12-b264cd2b4a31 at mono+41002ms, expiresAt seed +14934ms (TTL=15000ms)
wall step +120000ms applied at mono+41002ms
[provider] exec #2: "await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 30000)); return \"B\";"
after +120000ms step (1.5s), A still present: true (collector retention under forward step)
A disposed at mono+55950ms = +14948ms after park (TTL=15000ms): OK
FWD_VERDICT: PASS (seed=14934ms, ttlFromPark=14948ms)
```

Backward (−120 000 ms wall step):

```text
[provider] exec #1: "await yield_control(); return \"A\";"
cell A parked runId=cm_1e36f531-cde0-44ae-8030-3aadb3b3445b at mono+33969ms, expiresAt seed +14935ms (TTL=15000ms)
wall step -120000ms applied at mono+33969ms
[provider] exec #2: "await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 30000)); return \"B\";"
after -120000ms step (1.5s), A still present: true (collector retention under backward step)
A disposed at mono+48913ms = +14944ms after park (TTL=15000ms): OK
BWD_VERDICT: PASS (seed=14935ms, ttlFromPark=14944ms)
```

This runs the real shipped Gateway entry with a real agent/model issuing the real `exec` tool: the cell parks through the shipped `code-mode-execution.ts` → `storeSuspendedRun` path (not a direct state call), its `expiresAt` is seeded +~15 s monotonic, the collector retains it through a ±120 s wall step, and it is disposed at the monotonic TTL (~14 950 ms) under both forward and backward wall steps — never pulled early by a forward jump nor held back by a rewind.


Regression tests (production-seeded, 0 ms no-step control + both directions), oracle = configured TTL from an independent monotonic start (not `expiresAt - performance.now()`, which is epoch-sized on base):

```console
$ vitest run code-mode.wait.test.ts code-mode-state.test.ts   →  Tests 44 passed (44)
```

Pre-fix RED (source reverted, tests kept — 0 ms control passes, each step fails on a distinct assertion):

```text
-60000 ms  expected false to be true   // run lingers (re-armed delay stretched)
     0 ms  ✓ control passes
 60000 ms  expected true  to be false  // run killed early (re-armed delay shrunk)
```

Post-fix GREEN: 44 tests; `oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean; production delta net-zero (4 lines swapped).

Open PR collision check: scanned open PR topics and changed-file lists for `src/agents/code-mode-state.ts`; the related monotonic-clock family PRs (#168563, #169360, #166728, #175639, #167955, #178986, #180587) touch other modules (terminal, memory, team-reports, gateway, codex, browser) and none modifies `code-mode-state.ts`. `origin/main` still contains all four `Date.now()` wall-clock sites, so this fix is not redundant.

What was not tested: no live NTP step was induced on a running gateway; the proof steps the wall clock in-process while keeping `performance.now()` real, which isolates the exact distortion mechanism through the real expiry chain.


**Shipped Gateway swarm settlement-renewal proof — actual child settlement + monotonic renewal under a wall-clock step** (isolated real Gateway + real agent/model + real `exec` tool + shipped swarm helper). This closes the reviewer gap: it triggers the settlement-completion renewal callback (`createPendingBridgeStates`, `code-mode-state.ts`) through the shipped flow — not an in-process state call — and shows it keeps the cell alive under a +120 000 ms forward wall-clock step. TTL = 15 000 ms.
Flow: main `exec` #1 calls the shipped guest swarm helper `agents.run("return the number 42", { phase: "verify" })` (`code-mode-swarm-controller-source.ts`) → `agentSpawn` (real `sessions_spawn` child session) + `agentWait` (pending agentWait bridge). With `timeoutMs` (15 000 ms) < child completion (20 s), exec#1 parks on the pending agentWait via `storeSuspendedRun` — seeding `expiresAt` + an `agentWaitRetainUntil` retention window. The later execs are `sleep(10 s)`, which inline below `timeoutMs`, so they keep the main run alive while the child ends its turn.
```text
# main exec#1 parks on a pending agentWait via storeSuspendedRun (timeoutMs 15s < child 20s)
[provider][main] exec #1: await agents.run("return the number 42", { phase: "verify" })   # shipped swarm helper
# two removeExpiredRuns retention renewals while the cell is still parked (agentWait NOT settled)
[obs] idle renewal   mono+83574ms  expiresAt 185141 -> 200142  (delta 15001ms == TTL)   agentWait settled=undefined
[obs] idle renewal   mono+98591ms  expiresAt 200142 -> 215144  (delta 15002ms == TTL)   agentWait settled=undefined
# the child ends its turn -> the agentWait bridge settles -> the callback re-seeds expiresAt from performance.now()
[agents/agent-command] run swarm_0dea5943… ended with stopReason=stop   # child settles
[obs] CALLBACK renewal mono+107133ms  expiresAt 215144 -> 223684  (delta 8540ms != TTL)  agentWait settled=true  renewed-monoNow=14971ms ~= TTL
# +120000ms forward wall step right after the callback renewal: the cell stays alive (monotonic)
[obs] forward wall step +120000ms (1500ms mono): cell cm_7c25… alive=true  expiresAt=mono now+13470ms
SWARM_SMOKE_VERDICT: PASS  (callbackRenewal=true  agentWaitSettledAtRenewal=true  renewed-monoNow=14971ms ~= TTL 15000ms  delta=8540ms  idleRenewalsSeen=true  forwardWallStepAlive=true)
```

| renewal | agentWait | `expiresAt − performance.now()` | `delta` from prior seed | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| idle ×2 | `settled=undefined` | — | exactly TTL (15 001 / 15 002 ms) | `removeExpiredRuns` retention (cell still parked) |
| **callback** | **`settled=true`** | **≈ TTL (14 971 ms)** | **8 540 ms ≠ TTL** | settlement-completion callback |

**Why the signature distinguishes them.** `removeExpiredRuns` (line ~305) re-seeds relative to the old deadline, so it yields a clean TTL `delta` and leaves the bridge unsettled. The settlement-completion callback (`createPendingBridgeStates`, `completion.then()`, line ~585) first sets `state.settled = true`, then re-seeds `expiresAt = resolveExpiresAtMsFromDurationSeconds(ttl, { nowMs: performance.now() })` — anchored to the monotonic now, so `expiresAt − performance.now()` ≈ TTL (14 971 ms) while the raw `delta` is *not* a clean TTL (8 540 ms).

**Why the wall step proves monotonicity.** Immediately after the callback renewal, a +120 000 ms forward wall-clock step leaves the cell `alive=true` with `expiresAt = mono now + 13 470 ms`. Had the renewal been wall-clock-based, the deadline would sit 120 s in the past and `removeExpiredRuns` would drop the cell; it does not, because the fix keeps the renewal on `performance.now()`. Reproduced across two consecutive runs (`cm_a76e4677…`, `cm_7c256815…`, both `agentWaitSettledAtRenewal=true`, both `forwardWallStepAlive=true`). Shipped path: `code-mode-execution.ts` → `storeSuspendedRun`/`createPendingBridgeStates` with a real spawned child session.

prs.title: fix(cron): avoid app reauthorization warnings for MCP-only jobs
prs.body:
Fixes #180370

Related: #161105 (broader cron rework that removes this owner; this narrow fix stands until then)

## What Problem This Solves

MCP-only cron runs receive an irrelevant Codex app reauthorization instruction, which can cause the model to skip working configured MCP tools.

## User Impact

Scheduled runs whose tool cap excludes Codex apps omit the app recovery note. Runs that allow Codex app tools, including glob caps such as `codex_*`, retain the note when captured authority is missing. Unrestricted caps retain the guidance; disabled tools omit it. App execution permissions and captured authority are unchanged.

For older jobs whose stored cap lost requested app tools, the stored cap remains authoritative: restoring app access still requires reauthorization with the needed tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scheduled-app-authority note builder checks the run's effective tool cap using the canonical tool-policy matcher. This keeps the decision deterministic from run configuration without inventory discovery or another policy owner. The follow-up fixes review r4355534696 by honoring glob caps, including suffix globs, instead of the original literal-prefix regex. The docs describe which scheduled runs need recovery.

## Evidence

- Source confirmation: the main-branch builder at `scheduled-app-authority.ts:685` returned the recovery note without checking `toolsAllow`; `prepareCodexAttemptRuntime` appended it to developer instructions before MCP preparation. The unconditional behavior originated in `bb873c8806d6ce3430c354a2a97ae0e4d4ea1234`.
- Four table cases exercise `runCodexAppServerAttempt`: MCP-only cap omits the note; explicit app, `codex_*`, and `codex_*fetch` caps retain it. All inspect outgoing `thread/start` developer instructions and verify that the configured MCP tool remains advertised.
- Local red/green tests, typecheck, and code lint were **not run**: installed Node 26.12.0 is below the required 26.12.1, and the maintainer directed this work to rely on PR CI without bypassing the host limit. Live Gateway/channel e2e was skipped per maintainer policy.
- Normal commit formatting hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent Codex autoreview at P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings; the reviewed files and matcher sources are unchanged by the fresh-main merge.
- Exact-head CI: [run 39893608424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893608424) **passed** on `6e0f0ee6d73d640a9f645ebe13b70ee83fa5acb4`, including lint, production/test types, prompt snapshots, and the aggregate gate. Fresh main includes hooks typecheck fix `82c46546`. Prior-head CI [39889723955](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39889723955) passed 135 extension tests across seven files, including the original two request-boundary regressions; that result predates the glob correction.
- Simplification: removed the ad hoc regex and reused the existing policy matcher; no new helpers, state, configuration, SDK exports, or side effects. Exact total change counts: production +17/-2 (net +15), tests +33/-0, docs +6/-3. The small production increase is the cap eligibility check and its input fields; unrelated deletion would not improve this fix.

The GitHub Codex and ClawSweeper reviews reported the same glob-cap P2 on the previous head. Commit `adc0c8bea3fb4822d8b8c0260696bb5a7eaa5fca` addresses it; current-head CI is green and one ClawSweeper re-review was requested. The requested local red/green and live proof remain unavailable under the explicit maintainer host and proof policy above.

The [extension test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893608424/job/120219299270) passed **227 tests across 14 files**, including both full owner suites. All four recovery-note cases passed: MCP-only **3.528 s**, explicit app **0.426 s**, `codex_*` **0.470 s**, and `codex_*fetch` **0.306 s**. No failed or pending checks remained at verification; canceled metadata runs were superseded by the body edit.

Scope boundary: a later automated comment proposed a hidden allowlist intersection on an empty candidate array. This is not a supported stored cron cap: job normalization creates a fresh string list, the cron executor forwards that cap, and Codex rejects `before_prompt_build` tool restrictions before a model turn. The helper-only counterexample was declined with source references rather than adding general namespace-overlap machinery.

This PR remains open and ready, unmerged.

prs.title: fix: keep cold mobile Panels tests on mobile controls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Control UI browser-test failure where opening Panels can target the hidden desktop control during cold mobile startup. `openChatPanels` currently chooses its mobile or desktop path from a one-shot visibility probe; if the active pane's mobile header has not committed yet, the helper permanently follows the desktop branch and waits on a control that remains hidden.

The failure was observed in the light-theme mobile Panels scenario in [Actions run 39885503944](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39885503944), job `120192944564`.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. Control UI browser tests now wait for the selected active pane's responsive chrome to become visible and settle before choosing the existing mobile or desktop Panels path.

The active-pane selector, mobile header and host flow, desktop toggle, returned trigger and focus behavior, launcher actions, geometry assertions, scenario assertions, and existing time bounds are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper already has the appropriate readiness contract in `selectNativeLayoutAction`: it waits for visible responsive chrome in the selected native pane, then uses the shared layout-settlement owner before reading whether the mobile header is visible. `openChatPanels` now applies that same sequence before its branch.

This keeps the correction at the failing observation boundary. It adds no selector, sleep, retry, fixture, test-only production seam, or parallel readiness abstraction, and it does not alter the rendered UI.

## Evidence

The exact candidate was validated remotely on the retained 32-CPU Linux runner:

- Changed lint passed format parity, core oxlint, and Control UI i18n.

prs.title: fix(agents): fail closed when sandboxed spawned children resolve CLI-backed models
prs.body:
## Summary

`sessions_spawn` sandbox admission decided containment from the child's configuration-derived sandbox classification only, before the child's model — and therefore its execution runtime — was resolved. A sandbox-classified child whose resolved model routed to a host-executed CLI backend (`claude-cli`, `google-gemini-cli`, …) ran its delegated turns on the gateway host as the gateway OS user, outside the configured sandbox, while sandbox diagnostics still reported the session as sandboxed. This PR fails closed on both spawn admission seams once the child model resolves, and adds a run-seam backstop that owns the same invariant for fallback candidates and post-spawn runtime overrides — the same treatment the cron seam received in #173419 and the ACP runtime received in #32254.

## What Problem This Solves

1. **Hidden subagent spawn admission — `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-child-plan.ts`:** `resolveSpawnSandboxError` ran on the config-derived `childRuntimeSandboxed` before `resolveSubagentModelAndThinkingPlan` resolved the child model, and nothing re-checked admission once a host CLI backend was selected. A sandboxed requester (or any `sandbox:"require"` caller) could therefore delegate task text into a child that executes on the host.
2. **Visible spawn — `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-visible.ts`:** the same classification-before-model-resolution ordering on the `sessions.create` path admitted a CLI-backed sandboxed visible child.
3. **Run dispatch — `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts`:** `resolveRunEntryCliRuntime` classified the candidate and dispatched `runCliAgent` on the host with no sandbox placement guard, so runtime fallback candidates and post-spawn runtime overrides could reach a host CLI even for children that passed a spawn-time check. The new run-seam guard identifies delegated children by spawn provenance only (subagent session key or `spawnedBy`, which trusted visible spawns receive from `resolveSessionCreateSpawnPolicy`); a bare `parentSessionKey` is general topology — durable operator dashboard chats parent to main — so operator-created sessions keep their CLI runtime.

Net effect before the fix: an operator who enabled sandbox mode (or relied on `sandbox:"require"` to keep delegated work contained) and routed subagent models to a CLI backend had delegated work — including prompt-injected task text — executing with gateway-user host filesystem, network, and credential access, silently. Every such dispatch is now refused before launch with actionable recovery guidance.

## Why this design

- Fail closed exactly where the runtime becomes knowable: after child model resolution at spawn admission, and at the run seam for candidates the spawn decision cannot see (fallbacks, post-spawn runtime overrides).
- Reuse the executor's own classifier (`resolveRunEntryCliRuntime`) so the gate and the executor agree on which runtimes are host CLI backends — no parallel `isCliProvider` heuristic.
- Throw an unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError` at the run seam so the whole model-fallback chain stays terminal — no silent switch to a later CLI candidate.
- Identify delegated children from spawn provenance (`isSubagentSessionKey` or `spawnedBy`), never from `parentSessionKey`, so operator dashboard chats and forks parented to main keep CLI execution.
- Leave unsandboxed CLI children and operator-chosen direct CLI runs untouched; embedded/API children are unchanged.
- No new configuration surface and no default changes: the newly-refused combination never delivered its documented contract.

## Why this does not conflict with #173419

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #173419 | cron isolated-agent runtime admission (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-admission.ts`) | Already merged into this branch's base. Same invariant, different seam; this PR mirrors its placement rationale (fail closed inside the candidate loop, so fallbacks cannot switch to a host CLI) and reuses its error-text recovery guidance. |
| #32254 | ACP sandbox inheritance (`runtime="acp"` branch of spawn admission) | Already merged into this branch's base. Same fail-closed philosophy for host-executed runtimes; this PR extends it to CLI-backed subagent children. |

Composition note: no shared mutable state — `assertCronCandidateSandboxPlacement` keeps owning the cron seam; the new `assertSandboxedDelegatedChildNotCli` (called from `attempt-execution.ts`) owns the agent-run seam.

## Evidence of Fix

Shipped-Gateway runs on loopback, driven through `gateway call tools.invoke` (`sessions_spawn`), `sessions.patch`, `agent`, and `sessions.create`. Both builds use the same config: agent `main` and agent `fb` set `sandbox.mode: "all"` (Docker) and `plain` sets `sandbox.mode: "off"`. The CLI-routed model is `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`. The `claude` binary on `PATH` is a stub that appends one line per launch (argv shape, uid, `/.dockerenv`, cgroup) and answers in stream-json. The API provider is a loopback Responses stub where `gpt-broken` returns 500. Release = published `2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`; head = this branch (`e9afd6d`; the only later commit, `8463e1c`, is test-only, so production sources are byte-identical). A turn launch is counted only when the stub receives turn argv (`--session-id`). Startup model-discovery probes and `conversation-label` utility completions are excluded.

| Leg (sandbox per config above) | Release 2026.10.5 | Head |
|---|---|---|
| H1 hidden `sessions_spawn`, `sandbox:"require"`, child model routes to `claude-cli` | `accepted`; **CLI turn launched on host** (stub: `dockerenv=no`, gateway-service cgroup); log `cli exec: provider=claude-cli … trigger=user` | `forbidden`: "…runs on host-executed CLI backend "claude-cli" and cannot honor the sandbox…"; **0 launches** |
| H2 visible `sessions_spawn` (`visible:true`), same child model | `accepted`, visible child created with the CLI model | `forbidden` before `sessions.create`; **0 launches** |
| F1 sandboxed agent `fb`: API primary returns 500 → fallback `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` (claude-cli) | `model fallback decision … next=anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`, then **CLI turn launched on host** | same fallback decision, then run refused before launch; persisted run record `outcome.status=error`, `error="This delegated run belongs to a sandboxed session, but resolved execution provider claude-cli runs on the host and cannot honor the sandbox…"`, `endedReason=subagent-error`; **0 launches** |
| O1+O2 runtime override: admitted sandboxed API child, `sessions.patch {model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-7, agentRuntime: claude-cli}`, then `agent` turn | patch ok; **CLI turn launched on host** | patch ok; `agent` → `UNAVAILABLE` "This delegated run belongs to a sandboxed session … cannot honor the sandbox"; **0 launches** |
| C1 control: unsandboxed agent `plain`, CLI child | accepted, 1 CLI launch | accepted, **1 CLI launch** (unchanged) |
| C2 control: sandboxed child on API model | accepted, embedded run against the API stub, 0 CLI launches | accepted, embedded run, **0 CLI launches** (unchanged) |
| C3 control: operator dashboard session (`sessions.create`, parented to main, no spawn provenance) on the CLI model under `sandbox.mode:"all"` | started, 1 CLI launch | started, **1 CLI launch** (unchanged) |
| U upgrade: head started on the state dir written by release 2026.10.5 above, after `openclaw doctor --fix` (the documented upgrade step; it migrated the SQLite stores and saved pre-migration backups) | — | `sessions.list` loads all 9 pre-upgrade rows; new `agent` turns on the pre-upgrade sandboxed child, unsandboxed child, and operator dashboard rows each complete (`stopReason=stop`). The sandboxed child's stored `subagents.model` routing is unchanged, and the refusal applies only when a turn resolves to a CLI candidate. |
| Dispatch owner (`runAgentAttempt`, real classification + guard + dispatch selection) | base `attempt-execution.ts`: **6 failed** / 84 passed | **90/90** pass |
| Spawn admission (`resolveSubagentChildPlan`, `maybeSpawnVisibleSession`) | production fix stashed: 2 rejection legs fail | 4/4 pass |

Stored data: the change adds no writer, schema, or record shape. It only reads the existing `spawnedBy` and `sandbox` fields and session-key identity. Commands: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` and `…/subagent-spawn-child-plan.sandbox-cli.test.ts`. Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.{commands,agents-sessions,agents-tools}.json`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main`, `oxfmt --check`, and type-aware `oxlint` all exit 0. `scripts/check-tsgo-core-boundary.mts` exits 1 identically on base and branch; this is a pre-existing advisory test-root budget issue upstream.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

`sessions_spawn` callers keep every previously-permitted combination except one: a sandbox-classified child whose resolved model runs on a host CLI backend now fails closed with `status:"forbidden"` and recovery guidance (override the child model to an API-backed provider, or change the agent's sandbox policy explicitly). Operator-created sessions (including dashboard chats parented to main) are not treated as delegated and keep CLI execution. Pre-upgrade sessions keep loading and running after `openclaw doctor --fix` (see upgrade row). Covered by the dispatch-owner legs in `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` and the 4-leg spawn admission test. No SDK type, wire-format, or configuration change.

## Testing

- New: 9 dispatch-owner legs registered from `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.sandbox-cli.test-support.ts` into `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts`; `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-child-plan.sandbox-cli.test.ts` (4 legs).
- Unchanged-green: the existing 81 `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` cases, `subagent-spawn.requester-incarnation.test.ts`, `sessions-spawn-tool.visible.test.ts` (routed individually, exit 0).
- Type/lint/format: production `tsgo:core`, the three owning test graphs, the assertion-safety ratchet, `oxfmt --check`, and type-aware `oxlint` all pass on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(memory): honor the agent timeout for deep consolidation
prs.body:
Fixes #177068

## What Problem This Solves

Deep consolidation in memory-core dreaming used a hard-coded 60-second completion timeout. Unlike the light/REM/deep narrative phases fixed in #167984, it ignored an explicitly configured `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, so slow local models could never finish the phase and promotions silently degraded to append-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dreaming sweep already resolves the configured agent timeout through the timer-safe `resolveAgentTimeoutMs` resolver for narrative generation. This change forwards that resolved value into the deep-consolidation completion only when `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is explicitly configured. When the setting is absent, scheduled deep consolidation keeps its existing 60-second deadline, preserving the policy retained by #167984.

## User Impact

Operators with slow local models can let deep consolidation finish by configuring the existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`; no new config key or migration is required. Users who never set that value keep the existing bounded 60-second consolidation behavior and 48-hour narrative default.

## Evidence

- Explicit `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is resolved once through the existing timer-safe resolver and forwarded to the consolidation completion.
- With the setting absent, no consolidation override is passed, so `consolidateMemory` keeps its 60-second default.
- Added sweep regression coverage for both paths: an explicit 180-second budget reaches consolidation, while an absent setting leaves consolidation at 60 seconds.
- Added direct-caller coverage that `consolidateMemory` retains the 60-second fallback when no timeout is supplied.
- `vitest`: 2 files / 29 tests passed (`dreaming-consolidation.test.ts`, `dreaming-sweep-narrative.test.ts`).
- `vitest`: 3 adjacent memory-core files / 112 tests passed (`short-term-promotion.test.ts`, `short-term-promotion-owner.test.ts`, `dreaming.test.ts`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on every changed file.
- GitHub CI on the previous revision passed `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, and `check-lint`.

### Real-model end-to-end proof

Verified on head `975597e0f211` with `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (975597e)`, an isolated
state/workspace, the shipped `openclaw gateway run` entry point, and the managed
dreaming cron job. Model calls were sent unchanged to a real DeepSeek route behind
the local `cc-switch` proxy. To make the timeout boundary deterministic without
spending a large real-model budget, an uncommitted loopback timing proxy added
exactly 65 seconds only to consolidation requests. This is transport delay, not
synthesized model output, and is not presented as a natural slow-model benchmark.

Timeout absent (existing 60-second default):

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=custom-127-0-0-1-15721 api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat elapsedMs=59870 name=TimeoutError message=The operation was aborted due to timeout
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent durationMs=60088 error="The operation was aborted due to timeout" errorName=TimeoutError
[plugins] memory-core: consolidation failed (The operation was aborted due to timeout); using append-only fallback.
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=1, applied=1, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=1).
```

Explicit `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 180` with the same candidate and the same
65-second consolidation delay:

```text
[proof-proxy] POST /v1/chat/completions bytes=1526 consolidation=true delayMs=65000
[proof-proxy] completed status=200 elapsedMs=65858
[proof-proxy] POST /v1/chat/completions bytes=3279 consolidation=false delayMs=0
[proof-proxy] completed status=200 elapsedMs=2297
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=1, applied=1, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=1).
```

The 180-second run had no `TimeoutError` or `consolidation failed` line and published
the consolidated entry to `MEMORY.md`:

```markdown
## Consolidated Memory (2026-10-19)

<!-- openclaw-memory-promotion:memory:memory/2026-10-19.md:2:2:76a2a1ac5bf8 -->
- The proof177246 test profile stores durable notes with the marker NEEDLE-177246 and prefers concise release notes. Source: memory/2026-10-19.md#L2-L2
```

The cron result for the 180-second run reported `durationMs: 72772` and
`completionStatus: "succeeded"`; the 60-second control reported `durationMs: 66123`
and used append-only fallback. Raw evidence is retained under
`contributions/pr-177246-evidence/` in the contributor workspace. A naturally slow
model run remains optional supporting evidence, but the deterministic real-Gateway
control now exercises the changed timeout selection directly.

### Latest-stable upgrade validation

Upgraded an isolated install of npm `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9`) to this
PR head `44c9a5740` (`2026.10.5`) with an existing config and indexed memory
workspace. The captured `openclaw doctor --fix` log ends with `Doctor complete.`
and shows the agent database migration and its pre-migration backups:

```text
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-9e8f4bbf....bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-9e8f4bbf....bak

- Upgraded agent database schema in .../openclaw-agent.sqlite: v25 -> v31.
Backup: .../openclaw.json.bak
Doctor complete.
```

The explicitly configured values were byte-for-byte identical before and after
the upgrade (redacted of secrets):

```json
{
  "agents": { "defaults": { "timeoutSeconds": 180, "model": "proof177246/deepseek-chat" } },
  "tools": { "allow": ["memory_get", "memory_search"] },
  "provider": { "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:15721/v1", "api": "openai-completions" }
}
```

Both memory files kept their exact pre-upgrade SHA-256 hashes
(`MEMORY.md` `ef9e53e5...32af6`, `memory/2026-10-20.md` `3512ef8b...02275`),
and the upgraded CLI’s `memory search KEEP-177246 --json` returned both files
with the `KEEP-177246` snippets intact. Focused coverage on the merged head
also passed: 5 files / 141 tests.

## AI Assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Codex) under the submitting operator's direction. The operator reviewed the issue, diff, and test evidence before submission.

prs.title: fix(cron): stop CLI reply hooks after run cancellation
prs.body:
Related: #180658

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CLI-backed cron hooks continuing to admit work after the run's deadline cancels the turn.

## User Impact

Long-running `before_agent_reply` hooks stop admitting further work at their next checkpoint when the run is aborted or its caller authority is revoked. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI driver passed only session-generation authority to the early reply hook. It now shares the run assertion across the hook and model execution, checking cancellation and caller authority as well as the existing generation and model checks. Model authority is still bound only after a hook declines the turn.

Cancellation is cooperative: an already-dispatched operation without a checkpoint can finish. Independently owned background services retain their existing lifetime. Simplification removes the duplicated assertion and keeps production LOC unchanged.

## Evidence

- Confirmed the defect at `src/agents/cli-runner.ts:141` on base `22338ef3220a6598bcf893e86018b1446c07ab63`; the owner and existing hook tests were identical on fetched main `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2`.
- **Red:** both new cases failed on unchanged production code because the hook entered the next workspace after run abort or caller revocation. Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts -t 'stops an in-flight reply hook' --pool=forks` (519.35 seconds in Vitest; approximately 571 seconds including wrapper startup/cleanup).
- **Green:** all **27 tests in 3 files passed** with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.operator-model-policy.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.cron-root-abort.test.ts --pool=forks` (711.13 seconds in Vitest, 972.79 seconds including wrapper cleanup; 82% transformation). This includes the touched file's existing tests, caller cancellation, generation reassignment, model-policy revocation, and actual CLI-child cancellation. The existing entry-point suites include SQLite worker startup; the new cases use deferred promises with no timers or sleeps.
- Changed-file type-aware lint, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. No full local typecheck or broad suite was run.
- Simplification: production **+9/-9**, tests **+74/-14**, docs **+5/-0** against the merge base. The shared assertion replaces duplicate checks without adding production lines.
- Fresh main `3b39800d247e8c6fc17b97ba38b0ba05a4adab3a` was merged before push. The three changed files are byte-identical to tested/reviewed candidate `61cb88f02c832ace323652927c8a5227242eb7e1`; PR CI validated integrated head `5f6293a9073edfcc92fe4263ff7513529faf34a1`.
