prs.title: fix: streamed replies with a leaked model control token no longer re-scan the whole reply
prs.body:
Fixes #175444

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a streamed reply that contains one leaked model control token (for example `<|assistant|>`) re-scans the entire reply on every later delta, costing seconds of Gateway event-loop CPU per reply and growing quadratically — 5.6 s at 65 KB and 23.4 s at 128 KB on `main` at 51ebf30c8e0. One 128 KB reply made the token scan read 2.05 billion characters to strip a single token. Leaked control tokens are a reported user-visible path (GLM-5 in #44179, the `<|...|>` leaks behind #40020), and any reply that quotes a token — tokenizer help, F#/Elm `<|` examples, documentation — takes the same code path. The sanitizer runs for every streamed reply on the single-threaded Gateway, so the repeated work delays session updates and channel deliveries while the reply streams.

## User Impact

Replies that contain or quote a control token now scan each appended delta once instead of re-running the whole-reply scrub. End to end, the streamed delivery projection drops from 5.6 s to 0.65 s of CPU at 65 KB and from 23.4 s to 2.2 s at 128 KB; the token scan itself drops from 528 M to 65 K characters at 65 KB and from 2.05 G to 128 K at 128 KB. Tilde-dense prose drops from 21.2 s to 0.64 s at 65 KB. Visible output is unchanged: tokens outside code are still removed, code examples are still preserved, and streamed deltas still concatenate to the batch result.

The one-pass bound covers token/backtick-sparse replies, which is the reported case. Inline-code-dense replies still revalidate once per backtick delta, because a backtick can change ownership of an earlier token; the cost is bounded by the number of backtick deltas, not every delta, and output stays exact. A follow-up could skip revalidation inside a settled fence. Other sanitizer stages are unchanged and keep their own pre-existing per-delta costs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stripModelSpecialTokens()` was registered with `activationTokens`, so once any `<|`/`<｜` appeared every delta ran the canonical transform over the whole cumulative reply. The transform cannot settle the input because the leaked token remains in the source, so it also re-ran `findCodeRegions()` and the full match scan each time.

The filter now provides a projector that keeps the stripped output and appends a delta directly only when that delta cannot change the result: no token opener, no token split across the boundary, no pending separator after a token at the end, no surrogate-pair split after it, no backtick, and no 3+ tilde run (two characters are carried so a split fence opener still revalidates). Backtick and tilde-fence deltas are the only ones that can change code ownership, so they re-run the canonical transform and can emit a corrected replacement; everything else appends directly. Token boundaries are found from their pipes rather than the last `<`, so a token body containing `<` is handled too.

`transform` remains the canonical batch path, so history and delivery extraction are untouched.

## Evidence

Minimal repro (through the shipped `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` projection, 4-character deltas, one `<|assistant|>` followed by ordinary prose), measured on Windows 11 / Node 26.11.1:

| Reply | Before: total / token-scan chars | After: total / token-scan chars |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32 KB | 1,295 ms / 128,144,037 | 243 ms / 32,041 |
| 65 KB | 5,616 ms / 528,417,537 | 651 ms / 65,041 |
| 128 KB | 23,384 ms / 2,048,576,037 | 2,176 ms / 128,041 |

Output matched the batch result in every case (`matchesBatch: true`). A tilde-dense 65 KB reply (many `~12 ms`-style numbers) measured 21,223 ms before the tilde narrowing and 639 ms after, with the token scan at 65,041 characters.

Independent review found and this branch fixed four boundary problems across earlier heads:

- A token inside an inline code span whose closing backtick arrived after more text was stripped and never restored when the span closed. A backtick delta now re-runs the canonical transform, so the closing delta emits the corrected replacement.
- The first gate used the raw inline-code scanner, which treats a lone or escaped backtick as an open span forever and disabled the fast path for the rest of the reply (16 KB: 12.1 s). The gate now keys on the deltas that can change ownership: stray and escaped backticks cost one revalidation (16 KB: 58–76 ms) instead of disabling the fast path.
- The ownership gate matched any tilde delta, so tilde-dense prose paid a full scan per tilde. It now matches only 3+ tilde runs.
- A token that batch sanitization stripped inside a reference definition stayed stripped after a later suffix invalidated the definition (the image became unresolved and its code span became code-owned again), and the mirror case left a standalone definition label's token kept where batch strips it. The projector now keeps the token decision unsettled while a definition has no blank-line boundary after it - the same boundary the canonical parser uses for its stable-prefix rule - for tokens currently stripped and for kept tokens in a line-start label whose `]` is missing, is the last character, or is followed by `:`. Appends re-run the canonical transform until the definition settles.

Regression coverage in `src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts`:

- 37 fixtures × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 64 vs `stripModelSpecialTokens()` and delta accounting
- per-prefix parity: every 1-character prefix equals the batch transform of that prefix
- split opener, token at the end with a pending separator, replacement replay, inline-code ownership change, closer-run revocation, escaped backticks, tilde fences, token body containing `<`, astral and combining-mark boundaries, image-label revocation, and reference-definition settlement (strip, restore, and standalone-definition label cases)
- three bounded-work assertions (plain, stray backtick, tilde-dense prose): fewer than 4× the source length scanned by the token pattern, versus about 32 M characters on the pre-fix path for the 16 KB fixture

Checks run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts` — 49 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` on the filter consumers (`assistant-visible-text*`, `text-projection`, `strip-markdown`, `embedded-agent-utils.strip-model-special-tokens`) — all passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0
- cross-check fuzz: 4,000 randomly assembled markup sources × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 16 (24,000 streamed runs) vs the batch transform — zero divergences
- `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` — 14 passed, 5 skipped
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the three touched files — clean
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --config .oxlintrc.json` on the three touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` reports the three inherited `ui/` suppressions already present on the base commit; no `ui/` file is touched by this PR.

Only one problem is addressed. No configuration, migration, or dependency changes.

## AI disclosure

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review. I set the scope (bounded incremental work with batch parity), required the before/after reproduction, and reviewed the code and evidence before opening this PR.

## Shipped Gateway behavior proof (2026-10-19)

Added after review. The streaming path is now exercised through a real `gateway run` process, not only the shared module, and the image-ownership finding has a base-failing / repaired-head-passing regression.

**65 KB reply that starts with a leaked `<|assistant|>` token, provider streaming four-character deltas** (16,254 SSE events in 3,332 ms from a local OpenAI-compatible fixture provider). Run against this head (`d0cf858d45a0`) through `gateway run`; Gateway process CPU sampled, control round subtracted.

```json
{
  "providerEvents": 16254, "providerEmitMs": 3332, "chunkChars": 4,
  "deliveredChars": 65000,
  "deliveredSha256": "28570f36dc0a15ff736fc4845448d73daccd4e8eb8e59a247fef4fe76483ce72",
  "deliveredDeltas": 51, "chatDeltas": 51,
  "deliveredHasRawToken": false, "deliveredDeltasHaveRawToken": false,
  "streamWindowMs": 3970, "firstDeltaMs": 553, "lastDeltaMs": 4523,
  "terminalStatus": "ok", "terminalMs": 4698,
  "gatewayCpuSec": 6.02, "controlCpuSec": 0.83, "streamingCpuSec": 5.19
}
```

The delivered 65,000 characters are byte-identical to the canonical batch transform of the source (`stripModelSpecialTokens()`), so streamed delivery and batch delivery agree exactly (stream sha and delivered sha verified against the source in-process).

<details><summary>Raw client transcript (redacted)</summary>

```text
[client] warm-up turn completed in 13867ms
[client] control turn completed in 652ms (gateway cpu delta 0.83s)
[client] terminal=ok deltas=51 streamedChars=65013 streamedHasRawToken=true   # raw agent stream, pass-through
[client] gateway cpu delta during measured turn: 6.02s
[client] streamWindowMs=3970 firstDeltaMs=553 terminalMs=4698
[client] delivered final: chars=65000 rawToken=false sha256=28570f36dc0a15ff…
[client] delivered head: "The gateway keeps the session transcript and streams the rep"
[client] chat stream: deltas=51 chars=129516 rawToken=false
```

</details>

**Ownership revocation (P2) regression now has a base-failing / head-passing pair.** Same test file, same command:

```text
base 2a53f78dda0 (without d0cf858d45a0)
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
  Tests  8 failed | 28 passed (36)
    token inside an image label resolved by a late definition at 1 chars:
      expected '![a `<|assistant|>`][id]\n\n[id]: /ur…' to be '![a ``][id]\n\n[id]: /url\n'
    token inside an image label with an inline destination at 1 chars:
      expected '![a `<|assistant|>`](/img.png)\n' to be '![a ``](/img.png)\n'
    (plus inline title, shortcut label, definition-continuation, prefix-33, and the two dedicated revocation tests)

head d0cf858d45a0
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  36 passed (36)   (exit 0)
```

Also re-run on this head: cross-check fuzz (24,000 streamed variants vs the batch transform, including the image late-definition and inline-destination prefixes) with zero divergences, plus tsgo, type-aware lint, and format checks clean.

**Definition settlement (P2) regression now has a base-failing / head-passing pair.** Same test file, same command:

```text
base d0cf858d45a (without 17b1de11ebe)
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
  Tests  10 failed | 39 passed (49)
    token restored when a reference definition is invalidated at 1 chars:
      expected '![a ``][id]\n\n[id]: /url x' to be '![a `<|assistant|>`][id]\n\n[id]: /ur…'
    token stripped when a standalone definition settles at 1 chars:
      expected '[a `<|assistant|>`]: /url' to be '[a ``]: /url'
    (plus the definition-title, next-line-destination, collapsed, shortcut, settled-paragraph, every-prefix, and two dedicated definition tests)

head 17b1de11ebe
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.streaming.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  49 passed (49)   (exit 0)
```

Redactions: the run used a local `127.0.0.1` fixture provider on a random port; no keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints appear.


<!-- special-token-escape-maintainer-follow-up -->
## Maintainer follow-up (2026-10-22)

Fixes the escaped-opening-bracket finding and the additional ownership transitions uncovered by a deterministic split-point sweep. Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the incremental projector, the earlier repairs, and the accepted Gateway proof; all contributor commits are preserved.

The projector now consumes canonical Markdown text spans, retained-block bounds, and reference definitions instead of maintaining private reference/image walkers. An escaped inner `[` cannot hide the enclosing label. Link destinations/titles, tables, image references, and backticks inside token bodies can all revoke or restore code ownership, so those transitions revalidate through the batch owner. Ordinary quoted-token prose remains incremental; a later line boundary rechecks possible table ownership.

Evidence on this follow-up:

- Seven independent expected-output transition cases fail on the contributor implementation (`7 failed / 55 passed`), then pass with the repair. The final owner file has 63 passing tests, including the original three bounded-work cases plus ordinary quoted-token prose. Its final run used 1.406 seconds of test execution and 58.08 seconds command wall time on the contended macOS host; runner/worker startup dominates. Owner and consumer suites total 227 passing tests across nine files; the combined run took 42.78 seconds before the final test-counter cleanup, and the owner file was rerun afterward.
- A deterministic corpus of 1,495 synthetic Markdown sources exercises every nonempty two-chunk split and 1-/4-character chunkings. It checks both projected text and delta replay against batch output at every supplied prefix. Before: 2,399 divergences across 256 sources. After: **58,682 chunkings, 366,860 equality checks, zero divergences in 28.231 seconds**. The exhaustive generator stays lane-only; the bounded transition/work-count table is committed.
- Through the real `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` entry point, an 8,013-character leaked-token reply drops from 8,036,037 token-pattern characters scanned on main to 8,041, with identical output. An ordinary 4,336-character quoted-token example scans 4,364 characters on both the prior PR and this repair. Five interleaved warm owner-level samples reproduced the same counts; shared-host timing spread is too high to claim a latency improvement over the prior PR.
- Scoped typed lint, production/shared-test typechecks, formatting, and max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-exports, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks pass. Initial local lint attempts failed during unrelated SDK declaration preparation / missing lint-tool dependencies; the canonical core lint config passes after installing the existing locked lint-tool workspace, with no package or lockfile changes.
- Independent Codex autoreview on `3f5650e9d1d16d78f1a5465d34643639553b47e8`: scoped-clean; no actionable P0–P2 findings.

This supersedes the earlier backtick-only fast-path description: unresolved bracket syntax, multiline code-bearing blocks, and mutable reference definitions can still require conservative reparsing until canonical ownership settles. Ordinary leaked-token and quoted-token prose retain bounded scan work. Literal code preservation is unchanged.

Whole PR against the merged main revision: production +210/-24 (net +186); tests +285/-0. This maintainer follow-up removes 248 net production lines and two net test lines. No configuration, dependency declaration, or migration changes.

The existing 65 KB fixture-provider run through a real Gateway remains the accepted delivery proof. No additional Qwen smoke was run; new execution proof is macOS source-boundary proof. Initial gateway setup installed dependencies and compiled main/plugin outputs, but its optional local runtime-postbuild packaging was stopped; no new completed full build is claimed. Exact-head [CI run 39888918217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888918217) completed: all selected checks passed except `check-test-types-core-1` and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. The failed leaf reports TS2353 at `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57`: main PR #181122 removed `managedHooksDir` from `prepareInternalHooks` but left that test caller. The API, caller, and leaf config are byte-identical between the exact CI base `16920345c878` and merge commit `3f72f6be5699`; a minimal local typecheck extracted from that base reproduces the same error. CI calls it new because its scheduled comparison run predates #181122. This is an inherited main failure; the gate remains red and no rerun was requested.


[ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175448#issuecomment-6233307572) on `3f5650e9d1d16d78f1a5465d34643639553b47e8`: no findings, no before-merge items, proof sufficient, ready for maintainer review. Its remaining CI-attribution note is addressed above.

## What problem this solves

Chat loaded the detailed person activity card before anyone opened a person mention. This change keeps the synchronous portal and its loading/error, live-input, resize, focus, and cleanup ownership, and defers only the card body with Solid `lazy()`. The loaded card and focused controls survive presence updates.

## Performance

Same-machine production builds compare main `82c46546765f97edea22f0d9fea65f97ed7d67b2` with runtime candidate `e4f793e64191fe79d0f1d5c63cfb450bfb9cb6e7`. Both use identical fixed metadata and all 29 canonical generated plugin inputs; emitted proof files match, and the helper verified every plugin input again after building. The final cap-only delta changes no bundle input.

| Surface | Base gzip | Head gzip | Change | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,324 B | 316,304 B | −20 B (variance) | 7 → 7 |
| Chat boot | 1,349,072 B | 1,346,928 B | **−2,144 B** | 23 → 23 |
| New Session boot | 823,291 B | 823,213 B | −78 B (hash/compression variance) | 17 → 17 |

Chat's cap decreases from 1,400,431 to 1,398,206 B: `ceil(1400431 * 1346928 / 1349072)`, preserving existing relative headroom. Startup and New Session caps stay unchanged.

The detailed card renderer is absent from requests before opening a mention and loads exactly once after interaction. No restored-open card state exists.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Integrated `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |

## What Problem This Solves

Session-event fanout repeats row-delta preparation and row encoding for viewers whose sockets hold identical histories. This change moves that work into publication-scoped plans owned by the existing connection-row owner.

**Recommendation: do not merge this version on the available performance evidence.** The first two swapped pairs reduce recipient-callback allocation by 8.49%, against the requested 60% target. Runtime source grows by 81 lines, while this workload attributes less than 5% of allocation to the full projection owner. That does not justify the growth under the campaign's simplification-only rule for small owners. The ready PR remains open for the lead's decision; this lane does not merge it.

All three pairs completed. **Eligible aggregate and percentile gates hold, but pair 3 exceeds the major-GC maximum-pause bound.** Its maximum is 70.782 → 174.841 ms (+104.059 ms; 2.47×), above the 141.563 ms bound, with 142 / 148 collections. The analyzer's overall ADVERSE label is solely this maximum signal. Major-GC p95 and p99 remain context under the sample-count rule; this is not a claimed statistically established percentile regression. The resolving pair is included in the absolute-mean decisions below. Target attainment, regression gates, and the complexity tradeoff are separate conclusions.

## User Impact

Session messages and roster updates preserve existing wire bytes, permissions, capability negotiation, and failure recovery. There are no schema, configuration, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection-row owner prepares a delivery plan once per publication and complete history revision. Recipient handoff updates each socket's own bounded maps. Empty wire histories retain their monotonic version; ancestor invalidation preserves equivalent histories across recipients. Revision tokens retain no payloads or prepared plans.

This removes serialized baseline keys and per-recipient plan/result closures. The row plan shares its encoded session bytes across ordinary, field-reference, and bodyless envelopes. Live authorization, Control UI filtering, and bodyless selection remain per recipient. The only broadcaster cutover passes the actual recipient to the shared handoff callback; serialized-json and compression owners are unchanged.

Runtime source grows by 81 lines to preserve independent socket histories, LRU/capacity limits, and monotonic versions while sharing plans through explicit history identities. The old baseline-key machinery is removed. Benchmark tooling adds 55 lines and documentation adds 14; the requested non-test diff calculation totals +150 lines. No cross-publication prepared-object cache is introduced.

## Evidence

The owner work-count regression covers interleaved equal-version/different-content sockets and capability variants. Row JSON encodings fall from **16 to at most 6** per publication. The test fails on excess encoding on the baseline, and the candidate preserves payload equality and negotiated envelopes.

Baseline Node 26.12.1, with TurboFan and Maglev inlining disabled through the wrapper entry: 64 measured turns, 30 viewers, 30,840 continuous deliveries. This identifies work; it is separate from the normal-inlining acceptance measurements.

### Acceptance workload

Node 26.12.1; synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-run fixture; 30 viewers split equally among legacy, row-delta, and row-delta-plus-field-reference capabilities, with five exact and five roster viewers per cohort. Each arm has five minutes of warmup, twenty minutes of normal-inlining measurement, 80 measured cohorts, eight turns per cohort, and a reset every 20 cohorts. All six arms completed 640 measured turns and 40 resets. Sampling includes collected objects at a 512 KiB interval.

Each concurrent pair used interleaved CPU sides under the shared slot helper and unchanged production guard; pair 2 swapped sides. Guard-interrupted pairs are discarded. The target is -60% recipient-subtree bytes/delivery. Whole-Gateway allocation/turn, promotion/turn, total GC/work, and eligible tails must hold: reject a >=20% adverse paired mean or >=10% adverse in both swapped pairs. Opposite signs or >5x baseline spread require a third pair, decided on the absolute mean. A p95 needs 200 samples/side; a p99 needs 1,000. The GC count/total-time exemption and maximum-pause condition are applied below.

All accepted pairs preserved their input hashes. There were no diagnostic drops, attribution gaps, missing metrics, or guard interruptions. The synthetic workload is 32 agent turns/minute with frequent roster polling; its allocation shares should not be extrapolated to a different production load.

### Why sharing is limited

Each sessions.list response clears that socket's ancestor certification before roster admission. Staggered polling then produces different full-parent/reference envelopes and wire versions. Complete-history tokens remain distinct afterward, fragmenting reuse. Row planning was only about 27% of the first-pair callback allocation, and its subtree fell about 37%; live recipient preparation, audience-key construction, and variant payloads remain significant. The work-count test proves sharing for matching histories; the longer workload shows how normal polling limits that opportunity. Removing the admission reset or weakening history identity would violate the preserved reconstruction contract.

A further design should separate encoding for relevant row baselines from socket-specific retention without weakening live authority or recovery. That is a distinct implementation, not an unmeasured amendment to this result.

## Validation

- Final unchanged source: 48 tests across session-row-delta-audiences, session-row-publication-authority, session-row-event-trees, session-row-event-parity, server-broadcast.serialization, server-broadcast.transport, and server-connection-state (77.97 s Vitest / 86.68 s wrapper). Includes nine unchanged wire goldens and committed-policy changes between recipients.
- Initial owner cutover: 15 tests across delta audiences, delta retention, delta delivery failures, ancestor references, and publication authority (50.68 s Vitest); these overlap the final run.
- Coherent source-overlay subprocess test passed (197 ms test / 2.61 s runner). Changed-file formatting/lint and pnpm tsgo:core passed. No Testbox lease was used.
- Independent autoreview was clean through P2. GitHub code review and ClawSweeper reported no actionable findings.
- Exact head e0c343982ecd14d3c76a702604f113d340cec117: required openclaw/ci-gate passes and the CI run succeeded, without reruns. The rollup also contains a historical canceled Auto response automation and a neutral CodeQL result; neither is a failed test gate. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39884194417).

## Limits and Production Signal

Main-isolate figures exclude workers and external buffers. Measurements use coherent eight-file source overlays on frozen runtime base 9f89542dafed5af10322f0a4d3b5eb58b48f3eed, not independently rebuilt candidate artifacts. The branch was rebased before push; all eight measured owner files remained byte-identical, and PR CI validates the exact pushed head. Background RPC counts vary with cohort completion and are reported above. The manually stopped initial setup never entered measurement and was excluded.

For any revised candidate or separately approved deployment, compare recipient and full projection-owner bytes per delivered session event at comparable viewer capability mix and turn rate, with ordinary roster polling active. Confirm promotion, total GC per unit of work, event-loop p99, and maximum pauses hold. The lead owns production profiling and deployment; this lane changed neither production runtime nor state.

prs.title: fix: keep oversized streamed table continuations renderable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An oversized streamed Markdown table renders correctly only at the start of the first delivered message. Later chunks lack the header/delimiter needed by channel table conversion, so recipients see raw Markdown rows. Fixes #160668.

## Changes

Split oversized standalone tables at complete row boundaries and repeat their header only as delivery framing. Preserve original-source accounting through streamed deltas, cumulative replacements, and reconciled delivery boundaries. Keep the existing hard-break fallback for oversized headers/rows and container-dependent tables; fitting tables and fenced code retain their existing behavior.

Thanks to @McgAtom for the fix; contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

Built main `cbd99fa1e3663a57bd292302ff9536d354b7c12f` and candidate `d27481aa3dab454fc601a628435e2b6b76dbb7aa` with `pnpm build` in isolated Linux Docker on Node 24.22.1. Proof uses the shipped Matrix channel against an owned Synapse server and a scripted OpenAI-compatible SSE service, not the contributor's temporary RPC. OpenClaw state was created through shipped config commands and ordinary inbound Matrix messages.

With normal block delivery, a 1200-character budget, and table-to-bullets conversion:

| Case | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 240 rows, fragmented SSE, first turn | 11 messages contain raw continuation rows | All 240 rows converted, exactly once in order |
| 240 rows, fragmented SSE, second turn | 12 messages contain raw continuation rows | All 240 rows converted, exactly once in order |
| Fitting 3-row control | Fully converted | Fully converted |
| 80 rows, CRLF source | 3 messages contain raw continuation rows | All rows converted, exactly once in order |
| 240 rows in one SSE text delta | 10 messages contain raw continuation rows | Same ordered converted rows as fragmented SSE |

Every candidate message stays within the configured limit (largest observed body: 1171 characters). Full `chat.history` requests return the exact original assistant source for all five replies, including CRLF bytes, without synthetic repeated headers.

The three focused chunker suites passed: 45 tests covering tables, existing fences, and mutable previews. Changed-file formatting/lint passed. The simplified table suite also passes independently. A real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` smoke through the shipped embedded-agent CLI returned `TABLE_STREAM_LIVE_OK`; the task-scoped credential was deleted afterward.

The same 240-row reply also passed the maintained Telegram Test Server userbot gate: 10 received bot messages, rows 001–240 exactly once in order, zero raw table continuations, and maximum received text length 1030. The runner completed recording, removed delegated credential state, and the host confirmed broker lease release. The final table regression has nine intended failures on main and all 13 cases pass on the candidate.

Simplification removed a redundant assertion against the private table-span representation; the remaining fallback case verifies delivered chunks, row conservation, original-source bytes, and the character cap. No second parser, loader, cache, public config, or plugin-SDK surface was added. The remaining continuation state is needed across append, replace, force/replay, and reset boundaries. Whole diff: production +145/-27 (net +118), tests +232/-0, documentation +4/-1. Subsequent main integration and the test-only simplification leave the proved production files unchanged.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully undoes the change; no stored-state or config migration. Blast radius is streamed Markdown block chunking across channels, especially oversized tables and adjacent fence/replay boundaries.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): honor WAL checkpoint warning policy
prs.body:
Closes #172118

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes noisy SQLite maintenance warnings when normal reader contention blocks one checkpoint, or a competing writer denies best-effort incremental vacuum admission.

## User Impact

Operators receive warnings for sustained or oversized blocked WALs and genuine errors. A single blocked checkpoint remains recorded as incomplete, while a zero-timeout vacuum admission failure quietly skips that pass and reclamation resumes after contention clears. There are no configuration, schema, durability, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner computes a warning threshold but independently reported every native BUSY result (`src/infra/sqlite-wal-checkpoint.ts:257`). Reporting now follows `observation.warning`. The reclamation owner already catches and skips lock contention before transaction entry (`src/infra/sqlite-wal-reclamation.ts:136`); it now supplies the existing begin-only suppression option so the transaction logger does not warn before that owner handles the skip. Entered-operation and commit failures still throw and retain their diagnostics.

Maintainer policy acceptance: the warning threshold also governs non-quiet explicit and final-close checkpoints. Their incomplete return value and health remain observable; SQLite, parsing, and file-observation errors still report immediately. Quiet checkpoint-only ticks remain quiet. Every later qualifying non-quiet blocked observation can warn; this does not introduce deduplication or change the maintenance cadence.

The contributor's production changes are unchanged. Current main was merged without rebasing their commit; tests use the current fixture and extend the existing native-reader regression instead of duplicating it. The obsolete mock test deleted on main stays deleted. Documentation now states the accepted reporting policy. Thanks @mike1122real-hub.

## Evidence

Sanitized operator evidence: two state-database worker observations at approximately 21:22 and 21:52 UTC on 2026-10-22, release `cf2558f5639e`, journal lines 2784 and 3907, reported `SQLite transaction lock wait failed`, `operation=incremental-vacuum`, `step=begin`, `busyTimeoutMs=0`, `elapsedMs=0`, `failureKind=lock-contention`, `isMainThread=false`. This is expected opportunistic admission loss, already skipped by the reclamation owner. No message content, account identifiers, or live database data is included.

Current-main negative control at `b4031b2954c7984754a2c375ab528162b795654b`, with the final regression tests and unpatched production owners: exit 1, two intended failures (first blocked TRUNCATE callback and vacuum admission diagnostic), two guard cases passed. The oversized retained-WAL case still warns immediately. All fixtures are synthetic SQLite databases.

The contributor's earlier comments additionally record source-built CLI and maintenance-owner checks, plus a 124-minute isolated Gateway run observing natural full-maintenance warnings, reader release/recovery, contention skipping, and later reclamation. Those are supporting contributor evidence on the original head, not fresh proof of the merged head. This takeover does not touch a live Gateway or Team deployment.

Production delta against integrated main: +10/-4 (net +6); test delta: +118/-5 (net +113); docs: +6/-0. The additional production lines name an existing diagnostic option and explain its owner; no new policy machinery is introduced.

Takeover validation on the merged branch (macOS arm64, Node 24.22.1):

- `pnpm test src/infra/sqlite-wal-checkpoint.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal-reclamation.diagnostics.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal-reclamation.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-diagnostics.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 61 passed, seven existing platform skips. The native-reader regression covers first-pass silence, second-pass warning, complete recovery, and a fresh quiet first pass; the vacuum regression proves skip and next-pass page reclamation. The lease regression verifies commit contention still warns and throws. Changed-file test time was 4.657 s for checkpoint coverage and 1.104 s for vacuum diagnostics; cold worker preparation dominates wall time.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/infra/sqlite-wal-checkpoint.test.ts","src/infra/sqlite-wal-reclamation.diagnostics.test.ts"]'`: affected `state-logging` graph passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the four changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all five changed files and scoped `git diff --check`: passed.

The initial integrated test run exposed one stale first-BUSY warning assertion on current main; it was updated at the existing owning test rather than skipped or weakened. The old head's failing `openclaw/ci-gate` status reported missing completed CI; no failed Actions test job was attached. Final-head CI and independent review are recorded below.

Independent Codex autoreview of committed head `c0624d4240db6599d23cbdd30a1c6c9b9b35706d`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The transaction owner, WAL caller, current fixture, and commit-contention regression were supplied as source context. The validated report confirms incomplete results/health remain intact and suppression is limited to BEGIN reporting. Exact-head [CI run 39886076741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39886076741) completed successfully, and [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888154151) passed. The exact-head watcher returned GREEN. GitHub required one fork-workflow approval before jobs could run; no test job was rerun and no inherited-failure exception was needed.

prs.body:
Chat eagerly loaded English for unopened session panels, composer menus, Labs, organization, account inventories, and usage details. A named code fence also loaded every highlighting grammar. Keep visible transcript/composer copy eager, register optional catalogs at their existing lazy consumers, and load only the named grammar dependency group. Unlabeled fences retain all 14 original autodetection languages and order; existing escaped markup stays visible while imports load or fail.

Catalog registration extends retained objects in place so previous translations survive later parent registration. Host catalog reconstruction preserves source-key ordering. No dependency, route, tag, or selector changes.

Both use identical explicit metadata and 29 checksum-verified plugin inputs. CSS is unchanged; strict performance has zero violations. Chat/New Session caps lower to 1,389,363 / 829,482 B with the same relative headroom. The existing 315,881 B startup baseline is already stricter and stays unchanged.

Cold-load acceptance is fixed before the run: use the baseline's committed 240-message workload,20 ABAB cold-HTTP-cache samples (10 pairs), untraced; transcript/composer median regression ≤5%, p95 no worse. **Fresh integrated-head timing is pending the shared exclusive slot; this PR will not land until it passes.** Historical 60e/d96 timing passed, but is not current-head proof.

## Named and unlabeled code tradeoff

These original-source resource captures use the same synthetic 240-message fixture and wait for visible transcript/composer and highlighted fences. They are resource and screenshot proof, not timing samples.

| Code workload | JS requests | HTTP encoded bodies | Total JS wire bytes including headers |

The opt-in `--transcript-code named|auto` fixture adds TS/JSON fences only to the last assistant message. Without the option the default fixture is unchanged. Timing used the unchanged baseline benchmark without this option, so the candidate cannot tailor the measured input.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve literal download and trace output paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser download and trace output paths silently lose surrounding whitespace when `.trim()` is applied across the CLI, route, capture, and file-writer layers. A path like `" report.pdf "` is shortened to `report.pdf`, writing to the wrong file. The route containment gate (`pathScope().writable()`) trims its requestedPath input, validating the trimmed neighbor rather than the literal destination — if `report.pdf` is a directory or symlink, the route returns 400 even though ` report.pdf ` is a safe ordinary filename (GHSA-XWJM-J929-XQ7C containment gate).

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces `.trim()` with `readNonBlankString` (preserves whitespace, rejects blank) at all nine trim points in the browser output path flow, including the node transfer consumer (`collectBrowserProxyPaths`). The route containment gate stops passing the literal path into `pathScope().writable()`'s trimming input branch and instead routes it through the shared fs-safe empty-request branch as `defaultName`, which is never trimmed: `pathScope(root, { label }).writable("", { defaultName: literalPath })`. This preserves the operator's exact spelling while reusing the shared canonical-parent containment, regular-file requirement, and Windows namespace-alias rejection — the same admission the downstream `writeExternalFileWithinRoot` writer uses, so the gate and the writer agree on the same destination. `"~/name"` stays a literal scoped filename (never expanded to home).

## User Impact

`openclaw browser download`, `openclaw browser waitfordownload`, and `openclaw browser trace stop` preserve the exact output path supplied by the operator. Whitespace-only paths still fail. Paths with no surrounding whitespace are unaffected. The output root, existing non-regular destinations, and symlink escapes are rejected before Playwright dispatch, and Windows namespace-alias rejection is retained by the shared admission. When a browser node transfers files, the literal path is preserved through `collectBrowserProxyPaths` → `readBrowserProxyFiles` so the saved file is read, not the trimmed neighbor.

## Evidence

Product head: `d751edc32c69` (rebased onto main `58992a473bd`).

Route regression in `server.agent-contract-core.test.ts`: output root rejected, existing child-directory target rejected, `"~/report.pdf"` treated as a literal scoped filename, parent symlink escaping the canonical root rejected, existing regular-file overwrite accepted, and an existing FIFO destination rejected. Writer regression in `output-files.test.ts` writes to `" report.pdf "` and verifies the literal file receives the bytes. Node-transfer regression in `invoke-browser.test.ts` creates `" report.pdf "` and verifies `collectBrowserProxyPaths` reads the literal file, not the trimmed neighbor.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/output-files.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 82 passed (3 files)
```

Real patched CLI + real Playwright chromium (isolated dev Gateway, loopback HTTP server, `browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork=true` for the harness):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 " report.pdf "
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf        # literal trailing space preserved
$ ls -la "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf "        # literal file exists, content correct
-rw-rw-r-- ... /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf
$ ls "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/report.pdf"              # trimmed neighbor absent
ls: cannot access .../report.pdf: No such file or directory

$ openclaw browser waitfordownload " wait.pdf "        # waitfordownload literal preserved
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ wait.pdf
$ openclaw browser trace stop --out " trace.zip "      # trace output literal preserved
TRACE:/tmp/openclaw/ trace.zip     (Zip archive; trimmed neighbor trace.zip absent)
```

Admission regressions (real CLI, rejected before dispatch — route 400, no download event):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 "escape-link/existing/report.pdf"   # parent symlink escapes root
GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory
$ openclaw browser download e2 "report.fifo"                       # FIFO is not a regular file
GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory
```

Base-failing / head-passing regression (current main trims; this PR preserves the literal name).

| Scenario | Base (current main) | Head (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download " report.pdf "` | trimmed to `report.pdf` (wrong file) | literal ` report.pdf ` written, trimmed neighbor absent |
| `download e2 "."` | dispatches, then writer rejects (UNAVAILABLE) | rejected before dispatch (route 400) |
| `waitfordownload " wait.pdf "` | trimmed to `wait.pdf` | literal ` wait.pdf ` written |
| `trace stop --out " trace.zip "` | trimmed to `trace.zip` | literal ` trace.zip ` written |
| node-transfer `" report.pdf "` | `collectBrowserProxyPaths` trims → reads `report.pdf` → "file not found" | literal path preserved → file read successfully |

Validation: 82 passed (3 files), `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, assertion-safety, line-cap, timeout-race and mock-exports ratchets all clean. `tsgo` extensions shard blocked by worktree symlink (environment, not code).

Scope: 4 source files and 3 test files changed. The route hunk now lives in `browser/routes/index.ts`, where current main registers `/trace/stop` (`agent.debug.ts` was folded into it); the admission validator reuses shared fs-safe `writable()`. No config, protocol, schema, permission, dependency or upgrade changes.

Not tested: Windows trailing-space filenames; complete repository suite.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat selection including transcript chrome and media/layout regions instead of only the message text.

## User Impact

The muted-blue family from the reference is lightened to preserve selection visibility: white selected text is 4.77:1, and the fill stays at least 3:1 against page/card/panel surfaces across composed palettes. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript currently opts its entire container into native selection. Make the container nonselectable and opt the existing message and reasoning text owners back in, including the WebKit-prefixed declarations. This uses the browser's existing selection and clipboard behavior; no new handlers or state.

The shared selection color token changes from saturated blue to the requested muted blue. Simplification pass retained only the two CSS changes and their regression coverage (production +11/−4 lines; tests +237/−7).

## Evidence

- Four built-UI browser cases pass: native drag/select-all, unchanged image and turn-gap pixels, visible text highlight, excluded metadata, and reasoning selection in ordinary/expanded bubble layouts. Both reasoning cases failed with empty native selection before the correction.
- Seven focused browser checks passed across selection, app-chrome interaction, and content/context copying. The production Control UI build used by that lane passed.
- Command: pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-text-selection.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 — 32.66s command wall, 6.14s test time for four real-browser cases (the command includes the production UI build). Contrast suite: 11 passed, 2.66s command wall / 1.01s Vitest wall. Highlight-to-surface relationships failed at 2.13:1 before the fix. Final-head CI run 39893399225 passed: the four selection E2E cases took 10.77s; the form-controls file took 10.47s and the contrast file 0.81s (reported test execution durations, not whole-job wall times).
- Targeted stylelint, oxlint, UI typecheck, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Limitation: Chromium proof covers selection scope and preserved media pixels, but does not reproduce the broad Safari-style gap rectangles from the report. WebKit fixture navigation was refused by the host proxy, so Safari execution remains unverified.

- CI follow-up: initial CI run 39887989805 found the older form-controls browser test expecting the whole transcript to be selectable. The exact assertion failed locally, then passed after updating the fixture to separately verify nonselectable layout and selectable message text. All 21 tests in that file pass (5.84s command wall; 4.27s test time), with targeted lint/format and an independent delta review clean. That fixture-only correction did not change production CSS or visual proof; final-head required CI subsequently passed.

- Preview-fixture follow-up: CI run 39889040117 passed the selection checks but failed the first lazy HTML-preview ownership assertion. prs.title: refactor(ui): lazy-load chat panels and widgets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional chat panels and widgets still carry manual component-loading and registration state that duplicates Solid’s lazy boundaries.

## User Impact

This refactor preserves panel tags, cold activation, retained previews, and local loading/error actions. Queued panel commands reach the current mounted recipient.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat sidebar panels and transcript widgets now use Solid's lazy component boundary instead of a global custom-element registration/loading registry. Saved Files and Dashboard panels stay cold until first shown, then retain their controls while hidden. Terminal, browser, desktop, portal, companion, processes, subagents, discussion, file/detail previews, Canvas, and MCP content keep their existing tags and lazy import points.

Queued panel commands wait for the actual mounted recipient and recheck the owning session before delivery. Canvas parking and one-second retention remain in their existing owner, which now creates the registered bridge’s native element directly. Detached MCP hosts retain native context admission. Loading and retry errors remain local to the optional panel, preserving the conversation and composer. Ordinary render and load failures offer local Retry; stale assets retain the guarded Reload action.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Passed (`pnpm tsgo:ui`) |
| Controller guard / prune | Passed; syntactic baselines unchanged |
| Focused sidebar lazy suite | 4 passed |
| Focused panel-toggle suite | 17 passed |
| Focused widget-card suite | 25 passed |
| CI-discovered board/widget consumer tests | 50 passed |
| Files, Review and Desktop retention | 17 tests passed across the focused repair runs |
| Production Knip | Same 11 pre-existing findings on exact base and head; no new findings |
| Matched production builds + strict performance comparison | Passed; startup −13 B, chat −1,514 B, New Session +10 B gzip |
| Independent autoreview | Scoped clean, P0–P2 |
| Full UI/browser-extension/real-Gateway CI | Required via `ci:full` |

The first full CI run found that creating ref registrations inside a loading boundary made it depend on freshly produced callback props. A normal pane update then replaced the region or board and discarded retained controls. Ref registration now belongs to the stable component lifetime. The widget loading placeholder also uses the saved height to avoid a first-frame jump. Tests await component readiness and supply the existing application context where they previously relied on native-only context transport.

The first local sidebar attempt could not start a Bun thread worker. Focused proof uses the same pinned Bun runtime with one fork worker. The lazy-error fixture was corrected to inspect Vitest’s wrapped cause and await the surviving lazy boundary after closing a panel; the final run passes all four cases. No Node runtime override or broad local E2E run.

The production Knip reports are byte-identical on base `29a9a96427159c6ced8471453a031331ceff2440` and this head: one Telegram test-support file, five exports (`decodeSessionArchiveBytes`, `MAX_PLUGIN_COMMAND_SCHEDULE_BYTES`, `createGatewayCronAgentJobRunner`, `buildPluginToolMetadataKey`, `ProjectCrumb`), and five types (`XRefreshClaim`, `SessionCleanupSummary`, `ScheduledOccurrenceRun`, `ModelsListCatalogSource`, `PluginHookMessageSendingResult`). The base run used the same checkout with only this patch reversed, then restored and verified byte for byte.

## Size and ownership

Fifteen manual component loader callbacks become lazy components (13 sidebar/board/detail loaders and two widget loaders). These callback registrations were not counted by the current AST guard, so no baseline allowance can be removed for them. No new owner API or effect is introduced. Touched files: production 9,053 → 9,017 lines; tests/helpers 4,537 → 4,714 lines. The wider test footprint keeps existing behavior assertions across the new asynchronous boundary and supplies explicit context to renderer fixtures.

Matched startup: 315,686 → 315,673 B gzip JavaScript, 7 JS requests, 41,124 B gzip CSS, 1 CSS request. Chat: 1,352,159 → 1,350,645 B gzip, 23 JS + 8 CSS requests. New Session: 825,460 → 825,470 B gzip, 17 JS + 6 CSS requests; +10 B is within the 64 B build variance. Strict comparison reports no warnings or violations.

prs.title: fix(workspace): exclude generated build caches without losing tracked inputs
prs.body:
Closes #177057

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace capture treated generated build caches under `.artifacts/build-all-cache/` and `.artifacts/build-cache-inputs/` as authored workspace content. An unreadable generated cache could block local or remote workspace capture with `EACCES`, even when source changes and ordinary `.artifacts/` reports were readable.

A blanket exclusion would also drop legitimate files tracked or admitted under those roots. This revision therefore applies the cache policy only when capture has a trusted source inventory.

## Fix

- Keep the shared workspace-path predicate as the single policy point, with build-cache exclusion enabled by an explicit trusted-input context.
- Preserve exact tracked or admitted inputs under both cache roots while excluding new generated descendants.
- Supply trusted inventories from:
  - local managed workspace source admission and its Git index;
  - remote Git capture from `requestedBaseCommit` (falling back to the worker index when the shallow copy lacks that object);
  - native-node transfer from the Git index plus every path admitted by the host transfer list (including `.worktreeinclude` selections);
  - initial SSH capture from the host transfer-list admission inventory;
  - managed base refresh from the selected before/after commit trees.
- Keep the prior behavior when no trusted inventory is available.
- Restore prior archive inputs without trusting newly appearing guest cache files.
- Update the workspace access documentation.

No schema changes are introduced.

## Evidence

### Base-red

On the pre-fix predicate both cache roots were selected. With mode `000` on a generated cached file:

```text
localCapture: EACCES
remoteCapture: EACCES
```

### After-fix behavior

The regressions exercise the shared predicate and shipped capture paths with authored and generated files under both roots:

```text
workspace-generated-paths.test.ts
workspace-manifest.test.ts
workspace-managed-skills.test.ts
workspace-reconcile-fs.test.ts
26 passed / 26

node-workspace-transfer-service.test.ts
12 passed / 12

github-publication-base-refresh-actions.test.ts
1 passed / 1

node-worker-workspace-manifest.test.ts
6 passed / 6

local-workspace-projection.test.ts (targeted cache/archive cases)
2 passed / 2
```

`pnpm format:check` passes across 52,683 files. `git diff --check` passes.

The native-node regression starts with tracked `.artifacts/build-all-cache/authored.txt`, generates an untracked unreadable cache output, and confirms that the authored file remains in the transfer manifest while the generated file and its directory are excluded. The base-refresh integration uses upstream tracked files under both cache roots and confirms both survive refresh.

## Operational note

This does not unconditionally exclude the two roots for older or inventory-less captures. That compatibility choice avoids changing saved workspace semantics where the producer cannot prove which cache paths were authored inputs.

## Latest repair

The worker inventory now unions the requested base tree with the current Git index, so a cache-root file staged after the accepted base remains an admitted input.

```text
workspace-generated-paths.test.ts
6 passed / 6
```

That run includes the new valid-base + newly-staged-input regression and the typed Set fixtures.

## Shipped worker-path proof

The focused worker regression downloads the prepared snapshot through a real `NodeWorkerWorkspaceRuntime` subprocess. The worker snapshot starts with a tracked `.artifacts/build-all-cache/authored.txt`, contains an unreadable untracked `.artifacts/build-all-cache/generated/output.js`, and includes a newly staged cache-root input plus an ordinary report. The transfer completes and verifies the tracked input, newly staged input, and report all survive while the unreadable generated output is absent.

`node-workspace-transfer-service.test.ts` — 12 passed. Focused worker proof — 1 passed.

### Gateway execution evidence (CI, head `0e8780e05`)

Job `checks-node-changed-compact-large-29` executed the Gateway workspace-sync path end to end: real Git pack/`read-tree` setup, rsync transfer, and remote manifest capture through the test SSH transport.

```text
workspace-sync-tunnel.test.ts > retains host-staged cache inputs through initial SSH setup and later captures   ✓ 517ms
node-workspace-transfer-service.test.ts > retains explicitly included ignored cache inputs in node transfers    ✓ 39ms
```

Full log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39557174144/job/119080261754

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cleared replayed memory or reset diary entries reappearing when an older refresh finishes after the successful action.

## User Impact

The Memory panel now shows the post-action data instead of restoring removed entries. Failed actions still preserve the pending read. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A pre-action read cannot satisfy the required post-action refresh. Successful writes retire the affected reads, and retired responses cannot publish over their replacements. Normal concurrent-read deduplication and actions that intentionally do not refresh the diary are preserved.

## Evidence

- Actual operation regressions: baseline **2 failures / 26 passes**; fixed operation suite **29 passes**, including failed-action continuity.
- Real Chromium mounts the actual Memory owner/view, clicks Refresh and then the enabled Clear Replayed action while that read is pending, and releases the old response last. Baseline retains the removed entry/count 1 despite the success receipt; fixed source removes the entry/count 0.
- Focused verification: **65 passed, 1 existing opt-in full-owner test skipped** across operation, panel retirement, and Chromium tests. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Canonical independent P0╬ô├ç├┤P2 review: scoped-clean, no findings in the three changed files. The reviewer did not independently execute tests or inspect unchanged server/owner context.

They prove the rendered action/data behavior, not full Gateway/chat-shell E2E or production appearance. No production style changes are included. Broad standalone typechecking and full suites are left to exact-head PR CI.

Head `3bd6c5809e6cb8d434e1eda4e7a7a06885216d96` attaches the same identity guard through the existing request promise's completion callback, so the read is initialized before that callback. The production request path delegates to an async request implementation; its promise/rejection contract is preserved. No type suppression or behavioral workaround was added.

After the correction, **30 operation/Chromium tests pass**, targeted type-aware lint has zero findings, and formatting/whitespace checks pass. The original independent review covers the bug logic; this follow-up is a mechanical compiler-initialization correction. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid workspace skills being skipped as "resolved path escapes skill root" when the configured workspace path uses different letter casing from the directory on a case-insensitive macOS filesystem.

## User Impact

Workspace skills load without requiring users to change the spelling of their configured workspace path. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skill discovery used JS realpath while guarded file admission uses native realpath. They can return different case spellings for the same directory. Use fs-safe's existing native resolver for skill roots, candidates, and configured symlink targets so they agree at admission while retaining its Windows AppContainer and Bun handling. The shared general-purpose realpath helper and fs-safe version are unchanged, and all existing containment, symlink, hardlink, and descriptor-identity checks remain in place.

## Evidence

The defect is visible at [main’s canonical-root override](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2/src/skills/loading/local-loader.ts#L42), which forwards a JS-realpath spelling into native final admission.

- On macOS with Node 26.12.1, the new regression through `loadWorkspaceSkills` failed on main `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2` with the exact reported warning; all 17 existing containment tests passed. The symlink-free case-alias regression took 611 ms. It explicitly skips on case-sensitive filesystems.
- Baseline command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/skill-path-containment.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Vitest took 495.06 seconds including cold worker compilation/imports; the complete wrapper took 582.35 seconds.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Green on `31685ce698f833ad2b37c9aae67bd15f6f6e4822`: **59 tests passed** across `skill-path-containment.test.ts`, `workspace-skill-prompt.test.ts`, and `src/node-host/skills.test.ts`. The regression took 208 ms; Vitest took 380.38 seconds including preparation, and the complete wrapper passed in 662.50 seconds.
- Green command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/skill-path-containment.test.ts src/skills/loading/workspace-skill-prompt.test.ts src/node-host/skills.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Merged fresh main `153f09ee3f67be06c2721cd46419efbcd1a88e32` before pushing. It introduced no changes to the skill/filesystem inputs or dependency lockfile used by the focused proof; the reviewed patch is unchanged. PR CI validates the merged head.
- Codex autoreview through P2: **scoped-clean**, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891723136) passed on `5850b1b0ed2f2181ac94959d6b4840baf0c358b5`. At 03:01 UTC on October 23, 66 checks passed, 64 were skipped, and none were pending or failed. GitHub Codex review also completed on that head with no findings.

Live Gateway/channel e2e, broad local suites, and full local typechecks were skipped per maintainer policy; PR CI is the broad gate.

Simplification kept the fix at the existing skill-path owner and preserved nullable resolution failures. Exact diff: production +12/-4 (net +8), tests +19/-0, docs +0/-0. The production increase is the small wrapper needed to preserve null-on-error behavior and existing native platform support without changing the shared helper or weakening admission checks; no unrelated cleanup was added to meet the LOC target.

A supplemental backup-helper run was interrupted during module imports to address review feedback; it produced no test result. The final focused run above completed successfully.

prs.title: fix(database): avoid writer stalls during initial host admission
prs.body:
Related: #169260, #169283

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: personal account, operator approval, and auth usage writes can block other SQLite writers while a busy Gateway host decides their initial admission.

## User Impact

Account connect/link/unlink, approval decisions, and credential usage recording no longer reserve the shared SQLite writer before their first host authorization. This reduces avoidable contention without changing credentials, permissions, schemas, retention, or timeout budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seven initial admission calls ran after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`: four account mutations in `src/state/user-model-accounts.ts:392`, two auth handlers in `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.worker.ts:108`, and the shared approval transaction helper in `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.ts:47`. They now obtain that grant before beginning the transaction. Authoritative rows are still read inside the transaction; final host authorization, rollback, and committed receipt publication remain intact.

The tests pause at real worker admission and attempt a zero-timeout `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` from an independent SQLite connection. Initial admission must leave the writer free; final commit admission must retain it. This deterministically proves the lock boundary without sleeps, extra worker startup races, or altered production timeout settings. Enrollment now uses a populated shared auth row and verifies persisted authorization metadata.

## Evidence

Sanitized Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 around 23:30:29 UTC, line 9463: `pluginState.register` failed at `BEGIN` after 5,013 ms with SQLite busy/lock contention. This proves a competing state-DB writer exceeded its budget; it does **not** identify these account/approval/auth writers as that incident's holder.

Another visible state-DB writer nearby was `localWorkspace.mutate` (line 9382): 1,553 ms transaction hold, including 1,525 ms of host-admission wait. The `trajectory.runtime.append` and `sessions.transcript-maintenance` diagnostics at lines 9448 and 9453 refer to the separate agent database.

Local proof:

- A standalone Node 26.12.1 control called the four real account mutation APIs against an isolated SQLite database and probed the writer at each admission. With production modules from main `b4031b2954c7984754a2c375ab528162b795654b`, all four assertions failed: initial admission observed `transaction:held`. Restoring this candidate made all four pass with `transaction:free`, while final admission remained `commit:held` in both cases. No host timing or sleeps are involved.
- `pnpm test src/state/user-model-accounts-contention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed (Bun; about 1 second of tests).
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-personal.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 32 passed, including persisted authorization enrollment and existing revocation/receipt cases. Total wall time was 243.5 seconds on a loaded host, primarily transformation/worker setup; the new enrollment case took 1.653 seconds.
- Targeted `run-tsgo.mjs` check: passed for the nine changed TypeScript files using a temporary config extending `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.shard.json`.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on those nine files: passed. `oxfmt --check` on all ten changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

Local limitation: the combined usage/account-connect/approval worker shard was stopped during Vite source-map transformation before reporting test results. A separate Vitest baseline attempt likewise spent 328 seconds preparing 16,820 worker inputs; the standalone real-owner control above supplied the negative proof. Exact-head CI run [39887110150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887110150) passed, providing the remaining broad verification; these interrupted local runs are not claimed as passes.

Compared with current main: production +14/-10 (net +4), tests/support +227, docs +6. This removes 263 test lines from the contributor version, principally the repeated extra-worker/timed-stall scaffolding. The production fix is unchanged apart from merging current main's usage-receipt shape.

Original-head CI classification: CI run 39382949804 passed. The two red commit statuses, `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, came from Security Review run 39383995622 awaiting maintainer approval. They were not test failures or inherited-main failures. No changed path matches the restricted CODEOWNERS rules; the supported maintainer security clearance is still required.

Codex committed-branch autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings.

Accepted scope: final commit admission still holds transaction custody to preserve current authority. Other writer families are unchanged. No live Gateway was modified.

Contributor: @xialonglee; original commits retained, with maintainer conflict resolution and deterministic test simplification.

Verified head: `54f03650d71ad85b3106a5966d66935878aa4982`. Exact-head CI [39887110150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887110150) is green, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Maintainer security clearance passed in [39887297739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887297739). The exact-head watcher reports GREEN; older superseded check runs remain visible in the raw GitHub rollup. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private runtime helpers still advertise arguments no serving caller selects, and reply rotation exposes an unused preparation snapshot left behind by a completed cutover.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration, or operator action. Config keys, CLI flags, protocol and persisted shapes, effective Plugin SDK parameters, security boundaries, normal concurrency, and standalone session memory remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing canonical environment, clock, discovery, logger, process supervisor, and OAuth dependencies instead of private test-only alternatives. Remove the unread reply-rotation preparation method and its orphan map; keep the live controller's physical-store, lineage, completion, cancellation, and admission checks. Tests use existing dependency boundaries and scoped cleanup rather than production injection options.

Whole-tree caller checks include extensions, packages, UI, and SDK barrels. Against the rebased merge base, this removes **123 net production lines across 19 production files**, plus **3 net test/support lines across 20 files**. The author simplification pass retains only complete argument/return-member cuts and their minimal fixture migrations. Eight additional production lines from the original candidate are already on main and are not counted here. A Windows adoption argument newly consumed by main is retained unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A caller cannot supply an invalid private backup timestamp anymore. The original optional Date and its check came from the completed backup feature #122485; no caller supplied it. The canonical clock is trusted, with ISO formatting sampled after the email lookup. An invalid system clock now fails through `toISOString()` instead of the deleted custom error. Backup ownership, staging, durability, integrity, and restore behavior stay.
- The unused rotation snapshot checked hypothetical changes to a delayed preparation observation. #163997 explicitly removed this exact unused machinery; the completed controller cutover #175837 recreated it without a production consumer. Removing it accepts no new serving-path race: live physical-owner and lineage checks remain. The direct fixture keeps its actual cross-store observation and completion assertions.
- Private alternate environments, clocks, UID selectors, DNS/HTTP factories, loaders, loggers, and supervisor arguments cease to be supported test entry points. All serving callers already selected the retained path. Actual OAuth loopback/PKCE/CSP/abort guards, plugin ownership validation, current effect authority, bounded retries/timeouts, and persisted migration semantics remain intact.

## Evidence

Focused single-worker proof includes 57 OAuth/caller cases, 53 backup/privacy/ownership/cold-storage cases (one existing Windows-only skip), 46 Web Push cases, and 44 reply preparation/rotation cases. Earlier per-cut owner proofs cover discovery/Doctor, groups, image configuration, enrollment, transcript reads, process supervision, and update adoption. Kept-behavior assertions and test budgets are preserved; only calls/assertions for the removed snapshot method disappear. Conflict-only rebase keeps main's already-landed UI cuts; the sole conflict is the placement of the existing isolated-child clock stub in the calendar fixture.

Sparse native typechecks, scoped typed lint, formatting, SDK export validation, and independent per-cut and complete-candidate reviews through P2 pass. Suppression checks pass all 14 cases; runtime value and Madge cycle checks both report zero cycles. A local unbound cleanup callback lint finding was corrected in a separate follow-up before publication; no suppression was added. No local build, E2E, broad suite, whole-graph typecheck, or full SDK declaration build/API diff is claimed. Hosted CI on the exact PR head is the broad proof.

Initial exact-head CI caught two attributable omissions: a rebased PostgreSQL fixture still supplied `gitEnv`, and the deleted OAuth override cast left an obsolete assertion-safety baseline row. The fixture now installs the same synthetic Git identity through its existing environment owner; the single baseline row is removed. Focused native PostgreSQL types, lint, formatting, and independent review pass; the local suite has its existing two skips without a PostgreSQL service, so hosted PostgreSQL conformance remains the runtime gate.

The initial head also exposed a hook-fixture type error already on main, repaired directly in `82c46546765f97edea22f0d9fea65f97ed7d67b2` with red/green targeted types and both original freshness cases passing. An unchanged `state-migrations.test.ts` case expects six schema hints but receives eight after independent Heartbeat/workspace additions; the exact same assertion reproduces on a fresh main-derived checkout. This inherited failure will use the authorized native exception if it remains on the final head; no schema, audit behavior, or expectation is changed here.

Only the viewport, highlighted option, and digit-shortcut rows mount. The panel keeps its existing lazy boundary. E2E helpers now reveal options through their explicit model reference instead of waiting for offscreen DOM nodes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep service credentials referenced only by auth profiles
prs.body:
Related: #162675.

## What Problem This Solves

A systemd Gateway discards inherited managed credentials referenced only by saved auth profiles during startup.

## User Impact

Saved API-key/token references preserve the inherited service values needed for resolution; unrelated stale values are still removed. Unreadable rows preserve uncertain values with a credential-safe Doctor warning. Admission, native-close and snapshot-cleanup failures remain errors. Whole-database inspection retains its startup I/O and temporary-storage cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read reference names through the existing auth owner after final configuration/state selection, before stale-value cleanup. The selected SQLite/PostgreSQL backend remains authoritative. Shared generic readers, async display paths and snapshot/pool custody are reused. No new identity/cache/reader owner, global engine installation or credential activation is added.

Current head: `e9e5d4459beb54a2a3a0b54175fa6daa7ce0598f`. Normally merged official main `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2` into prior author head `8e425f77de78311617bbd87550ecca5713e3b79c` for one actual adjacent-import conflict. Both the author’s `detectRespawnSupervisor` and main’s shared `applyProcessEnvKeys` are retained; the retired duplicate environment-restore helper stays removed. Fifteen other complete proposal-file blobs match the prior reviewed head. The authored diff remains 16 files, with no authored dependency, schema/version, protocol, persisted-format, service-file or permission-rule change. Normal merge ancestry preserves existing contributor credit.

## Evidence

Current local runtime results are **82 passing cases and one unresolved Doctor timeout across seven complete files**. No case was skipped, weakened or assigned a longer timeout to turn that failure green.

- **Reported startup defect, before:** the complete pinned-main pre-bootstrap owner, with current support/fixtures fixed, produces **one intended failure / 22 unselected**, **269.001 s** native wrapper. The auth-profile-only inherited key is removed and reference resolution returns `SECRET_REF_NOT_FOUND`; the unrelated stale key is removed as expected. This is a source-runtime child through actual startup selection/reference resolution, not a pristine-main deployment or installed Gateway.
- **After:** all credential-preservation controls pass, including the auth-profile-only key, unreadable secondary stores, reset, final-config replacement, and ownership/credential snapshot-cleanup refusal. The first five-target native command runs two files before stopping on the Doctor failure: **10 pool cases pass; 22 startup cases pass and one fails**, **829.011 s** wrapper. The three remaining files are then run explicitly: **32 cases pass / 287.274 s**, covering reference collection, pooled reader custody and merged auth-list/order behavior. These are 64 passes and one failure, not 65 passes.

It covers cold registered `models auth` CLI text/JSON/list/order, all four SQLite/PostgreSQL family combinations, committed reads/reopen, identity/source/anchor retention and transcript/participant readers. A new task-only PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster uses a private 0700 Unix socket with TCP disabled and synthetic data; unaccent/pgcrypto prerequisites are qualified. All test schemas are removed, normal shutdown completes and the postmaster PID file is absent. Initial setup carried an old cluster’s test-role DSN and failed before any test; binding the DSN explicitly to this cluster’s initialization user corrected the fixture environment.
