prs.title: fix(memory): memory search misses session turns stored as input_text/output_text blocks
prs.body:
Related: #137265, #137937

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory search` never returns a conversation turn from the `sessions` source when the turn is stored as an `input_text` or `output_text` block, even after `memory status --index`.

## User Impact

User impact: with the `sessions` source enabled, those turns can be found through `memory_search` and `openclaw memory search` again. Before this change such a session indexed as one file with 0 chunks.

No schema or stored-format change, so no migration. Sessions indexed before this fix get the skipped turns on a full reindex with `openclaw memory index --force`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session text extractor for memory only kept `text` blocks. The other readers of the same transcripts already accept `text`, `input_text` and `output_text` (`session-transcript-projection-append.ts`, `session-transcript-derived-readers.ts`, `chat-display-projection.helpers.ts`). In my repro the same turn was already in `session_transcript_fts`, but memory search indexed nothing for it. The extractor now accepts the same three types.

The guard is the one @Finn763 proposed in #137937, which was closed because of the author's PR limit, not because of review. This PR adds the regression test and the before/after run that review asked for.

Since the first version of this branch, #157278 moved the extractor into `session-entry-projection.ts`, where `collectRawSessionText` now serves both the saved session files and the SQLite snapshot path (`projectSessionEntryRecord`). After merging main the change lives there, so both paths get it, and the earlier `session-message-text.ts` split is gone. The net diff is the predicate in `session-entry-projection.ts` plus the test.

## Evidence

Regression test in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`: `keeps persisted input_text and output_text blocks in the export`. It runs `buildSessionEntry` on a saved transcript with an `input_text` user turn and an `output_text` assistant turn, which covers the session-file path. With current main's extractor it fails with `expected '' to be 'User: Remember the control word ZAFFI…'`; with the fix the file passes 36/36. The new test takes 12 ms. The whole file takes 42–65 s wall here with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`; the test adds no new setup.

Before/after with the real CLI on an isolated state dir (`memory.search.provider: "none"`, sources `memory` and `sessions`), re-run on the merged head (main at fb2487a903) to cover the SQLite path. The session was written with `persistSessionTranscriptTurn`, and the stored user event is:

```json
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"The memory control word is ZAFFIRO927."}]}}
```

Before (current main's `collectRawSessionText`, same build otherwise):

```
$ openclaw memory status --index --agent main
Memory index updated (main): 1 file indexed.
  sessions · 1/1 files · 0 chunks · 0.0 B text + embeddings

$ openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
{
  "results": []
}
```

After:

```
$ openclaw memory status --index --agent main
Memory index updated (main): 1 file indexed.
  sessions · 1/1 files · 1 chunks · 91.0 B text + embeddings

$ openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "sessions/main/proof-provider-text-blocks.jsonl",
      "startLine": 2,
      "endLine": 3,
      "snippet": "User: The memory control word is ZAFFIRO927.\nAssistant: Stored the control word ZAFFIRO927.",
      "source": "sessions",
      "provenance": { "originClass": "untrusted", "sessionKind": "interactive" }
    }
  ]
}
```

I used `provider: "none"` so the run needs no embedding key. The extractor runs before chunking and embedding, so the provider does not change this path. I don't have the reporter's session, so this covers the `input_text`/`output_text` case from the issue review, not their exact transcript.

Checks: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the two changed files selected the `core` and `coreTests` lanes and passed all 34 steps (format, oxlint, the line-cap and assertion ratchets, plugin boundaries, core and core-test typecheck, unused-export scans, state schema guards). `git diff --check` against main is clean.

CI on this head: every selected check passed except `check-additional-extension-package-boundary`, which hit the job's 20-minute limit while building the last of the 125 extension packages (`The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 20m0s`). The same job passed on a sibling PR run at 19m36s, so it is running at the edge of its budget on hosted runners. This PR does not touch any extension package.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep the reader's place when history loads, refreshes or streams
prs.body:
Related: #163121, #124759
Companion: #163146

## What Problem This Solves

Loading older messages, refreshing history, or receiving streamed content can move an iOS reader away from the message they were reading. On real history the jump can be a whole page: the reader lands on rows they never scrolled to. The first history page also waits on optional metadata.

## User Impact

Readers keep their place when older history loads, including while they are still flinging at the top, while a landing stalls the main thread, while a live row below keeps changing height, and when rows above finish sizing after the page lands. Newly sent questions stay anchored with the keyboard hidden; the visible keyboard follows the live reply. Cached conversations reopen at the latest reply without shifting when fresh history arrives. A completed-work disclosure the reader opened stays open as new turns arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Session-scoped history paging validates route, branch, cursor, and generation before accepting older messages.
- **Row-following landing.** A UIKit marker on the reader's row lets `ChatNativePrependViewport` correct the offset in the page's own layout pass and then follow that row frame by frame until it settles. It ignores a same-pass read of the row's pre-page position, re-acquires the marker when SwiftUI rebuilds the row, counts only observed frames as stable (a main-thread stall cannot end it early), finishes a top-edge rubber band instead of keeping it, undoes a first size change that turns out not to be the page, and starts no new page while one is landing. A page that projects no rows, or only adds work above an unchanged first message, continues to the next page once the landing settles.
- **Measured history.** All history groups render in one eager `VStack` under one `ForEach`, so every row has a measured height and a stable identity (see Rendering choices).
- Completed-work folds are owned by the chat view, keyed by the work's anchor message, so a group rebuilt under a new identity keeps a fold the reader opened.
- Only live user admission starts a reader turn; cache and history hydration do not.
- The first history page appears before optional metadata completes.

## Rendering choices

**Measured rows instead of `LazyVStack`.** The precedent cited for lazy history, deb168691b2, is #147770, a CI SimSlim/release-qualification change; its `ChatView` edit fixed a scroll-target starvation and states that lazy rendering "remain[s] intact". It records no design rationale for lazy history. A lazy stack estimates the heights of rows it has not built and re-estimates them when a page lands. On real history with tall tool output and code, the size change for one page of about 125 messages was 134,442 pt, the reader's row left the built window and was torn down, and the landing could only guess. This reproduced on device (test builds of this branch with a lazy list) and in the simulator: `testPrependWithUnevenOlderRowsPreservesReader` fails 2/2 with `LazyVStack` and passes with the measured list. Measured rows make the correction exact.

**Response frame.** Removing the outer single-response frame is part of this reader-position repair, not a separate cosmetic cleanup. The repair renders response parts through one message renderer and attaches a stable row ID and native geometry marker to each transcript row; the viewport follows the actual reading row through prepends and subsequent layout changes. Logical run/input ownership remains intact without selecting a different enclosing response renderer. This replaces #156944's single-frame presentation so narration and the final answer are rendered as individual messages. The contributor explicitly approves this presentation direction as part of the fix.

**ClawSweeper P2 (fold reset).** Fixed two ways: the redundant eager prefix/suffix partition is gone (one `ForEach`, so a new turn no longer moves a group between partitions), and the open state lives in the chat view rather than the row. `testOpenedCompletedWorkStaysOpenAcrossNewTurns` opens a fold and sends five turns: it fails with the previous partition and row-local state ("Five new turns must not collapse the work the reader opened") and passes on this head.

## Evidence

Head `776b11e50db`, rebased on main `17416f83ecf` (after #168919). Simulator: iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, built from the exact commit with the repository's pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1, XcodeGen 2.46.0 and Node 26.12.1. The Watch app dependency was removed from the generated simulator project only, because the Watch WebRTC prebuild needs Rust nightly-2026-10-02, which the test host does not have; every Swift file under test is this commit's. The table is from the pre-rebase head `888851564620` (the landing code is byte-identical on this head); the full suite was rerun on `776b11e50db`, with the results below the table.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `testPrependWhileDeceleratingAtTopPreservesReader` (flings at the top while the page loads) | pass, drift 0 pt |
| `testPrependLandingDuringStallWithTouchPreservesReader` (2.5 s main-thread stall, touch queued) ×2 | pass ×2, drift 0 pt |
| `testPrependWithTickingRowBelowPreservesReader` (live row below changes height) | pass, drift 0 pt |
| `testPrependWithUnevenOlderRowsPreservesReader` (older pages much taller) ×2 | pass ×2, drift 0 pt |
| `testPrependWithLateGrowingRowsAbovePreservesReader` (rows grow 0.4 s after landing) | pass, drift 0 pt |
| `testLoadingEarlierHistoryPreservesReadingPosition` | pass |
| `testLongHistoryPrependPreservesReaderAndTrueLatest` (two 101-row pages, return to latest) | pass |
| `testDisclosurePrependPreservesReaderWithMoreHistory` ×4 / `…WhenHistoryExhausted` | pass ×4 / pass |
| `testEarlierHistoryContinuesPastEmptyProjectedPage` | pass |
| `testPagedHistoryCanBeReadBackToOldestAndReturnToLatest` | pass |
| `testOpenedCompletedWorkStaysOpenAcrossNewTurns` (P2) | pass; fails on the negative control |
| `testCompletedWorkDisclosureKeepsFinalReplyVisible` | pass |
| `testT299RichTranscriptFirstHistorySwipeRemainsResponsive` / `testT299RichHistoryWindowCrossingRemainsResponsive` | pass / pass |
| `testManualReturnThroughRichHistoryDoesNotTeleportBack` | pass |
| `testNewlySentTurnWithCompletedReplyKeepsQuestionAnchor` / `testStreamingReplyKeepsQuestionAnchorAfterKeyboardDismissedSend` | pass / pass |
| `testManualReaderDoesNotJumpDuringToolStream` / `testLongTranscriptFlingScrolling` ×2 | pass / pass ×2 |
| `ChatNativePrependViewportTests` (app unit tests) | 6/6 |
| `swift test --filter Chat` (OpenClawKit) | 18 XCTest + 1779 Swift Testing passed |

**On `776b11e50db`.** The full rerun passed 22 of 27. The decelerating and both stall+touch probes failed with the same ~711 pt drift (711/739/711), and long-history and one fling run failed. That run was the first on a freshly built tree and simulator, with the probes run first. Repeat runs of the exact head then passed everything: decel 3/3, stall+touch 3/3, long-history 3/3 and fling 2/2 untraced, plus decel 6/6 and stall+touch 6/6 with landing traces compiled in (0 failures in 21 probe runs). Viewport unit tests 6/6 and `Chat` kit tests again passed. The first-run failure is not reproduced and its root cause is not identified; it is recorded here, not claimed fixed.

The probes measure the reader's row on screen before the request and after the page settles; a pass is the row still on screen within 4 pt. The gesture probes touch only while the page is pending.

**Pre-existing failures, not addressed here.** `testEarlierHistoryButtonWorksBeforeMetadataCompletes` and `testHistoryFirstPageAppearsBeforeOptionalMetadataCompletes` time out on this head and also on the previous head of this PR, c107976544 (same assertion, same waiter). The first-page-before-metadata behavior was shown earlier on d4df452 with a temporary proof fixture and harness that were not kept ([validation record](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/75b65870c9497385e554540dbb7e21753571f38a/reader/validation.md)); it is not re-proven on this head.

**Device.** iPhone test build 102465 carries this landing and measured list on the author's device build (not this exact commit). Real history, 8 landings: no lost row and no size-only guess; the tester reported small glitches and no jump. Landings freeze the main thread for 100–300 ms on long histories. Test build 102464 with a lazy list jumped: 7 of 9 landings lost the row or fell back to a size-only guess.

Native i18n verification, repository SwiftLint (strict) and pinned SwiftFormat passed on the changed files and in the Xcode build phases.

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep forwarded cron history readable after provider changes
prs.body:
Fixes #180920

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat history failing to load when a session retains a Claude CLI binding, switches to another provider, and contains a forwarded cron message.

## User Impact

History remains readable after a provider switch, with current automation names on forwarded messages. There are no configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preliminary CLI-history eligibility read projected messages without a cron-name resolver, so it threw before the ordinary history worker could prepare the final labels. Supply the existing deferred resolver at that read; preserve the projector's preparation guard and worker-owned final name lookup.

The maintainer rewrite follows ClawSweeper's recommendation: remove the three defensive live-broadcast, reply-selection, and inject changes and their synthetic broadcast test. No current production producer was identified for those forwarded inputs. The regression instead exercises the real `chat.history` handler with canonical transcript storage and a retained CLI binding after a provider switch. Thanks @ywjanewer for the initial investigation; the contributor commit remains in the branch history. Related existing repair: #166980; #175550 already fixed the separate process-held paging path.

## Evidence

- Source-confirmed on main `153f09ee3f67be06c2721cd46419efbcd1a88e32`: `prepareCliSessionHistoryReader` calls `readIncrementalChatHistoryTail` without a resolver at `src/gateway/cli-session-history.ts:101`. That reaches the deliberate throw at `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.history.ts:660` before the RPC response worker prepares labels.
- Regression: `reads forwarded cron history after switching away from Claude CLI` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.cli-import.test.ts` calls the real history handler/native storage with a retained binding, canonical forwarded cron input, and an unrelated native Claude message. It requires exactly the canonical message with `Daily report` as its label. On the base, this case reaches the missing-resolver exception before the response. That base failure is source-confirmed, not a claimed local execution; exact-head runtime results are below.
- Local install was attempted once on trusted main and refused: this Mac has Node 26.12.0; the repository requires >=26.12.1 for Node 26. No engine bypass or runtime download was used. Local tests, lint, formatting, and typechecks are skipped per maintainer host policy; contributor code was not executed locally.
- Live Gateway/channel e2e and remote compute were skipped per maintainer proof policy. PR CI is the broad test and lint gate.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Simplification removed all speculative live-caller handling. Exact diff versus main: production +2/-0, tests +30/-0, docs +1/-0. The two production lines are the existing deferred callback plus its ownership comment; no unrelated cleanup was added to manufacture a net-negative count.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings. The introduced patch remains byte-identical after merging fresh main. Static review only; runtime validation remains for CI.
- [Latest exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892711536) passed on `3aa4c39e9c52d3003f7706b5178af65685c0637e`, including changed-file lint/format and typechecks, without failures or retries. [The handler/native-storage job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891537642/job/120212591346) passed all 19 tests; the new regression took 769 ms. The file took 42.62 seconds (58% transformation; reported test durations total 16.403 seconds); the containing CI job took 142 seconds. The existing native integration fixture exercises the real response/worker boundary and accounts for the file cost; no new Gateway boots, timers, or polling were added.
- The [GitHub Actions CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892711536/job/120218348274) and [combined Security Review status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39893479239) succeeded. The [initial exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891537642) also passed; reopening this maintainer rewrite after the author closed the superseded defensive scope automatically triggered the latest run. No manual rerun was requested.

prs.title: fix(compaction): explain empty summary budget failures
prs.body:
Related: #178805

## What Problem This Solves

An empty, length-stopped compaction summary reports generic advice, leaving operators to find the compaction thinking setting and the selected model's output limit themselves.

## User Impact

The error now identifies the selected model, the actual summary allowance, and its `maxTokens`, and points to `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel: "off"` when supported or `agents.defaults.compaction.model`. The docs explain why increasing a model limit alone may leave the reserve-derived summary allowance unchanged. Failed compaction still preserves history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing summary-completion owner already classifies this failure. Improving its diagnostic keeps the repair small: production +1/-1 lines (net zero), tests +3/-1 (net +2), docs +2. The existing regression still requires one summary request and now protects the concrete operator guidance. No prompt/tool text changes (token delta zero).

Automatic retry remains a separate decision. Logical off, advertised capabilities, and actual local wire behavior are not interchangeable; a shared retry would also affect hosted routes. This PR changes no thinking defaults, retries, configuration surface, or hosted-route policy.

Thanks to @crabanagent for the report and @ericcurtin for confirming the local-model workaround.

## Evidence

Real `sessions.compact` through an isolated Gateway on macOS, Node 26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.8. Histories were seeded with three genuine `chat.send` turns against a deterministic provider; compaction used the real local model below. Baseline is `4039ebd5df375f02a4b576dbb70fa3e8d9593cca`.

| Probe | Wire request | Result | Provider / RPC time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline native Qwen3:4b | `think: true`, `num_predict: 512` | `length`, 512 output tokens, 2,378 reasoning characters, zero visible text; generic error | 26.085 / 26.575 s |
| Baseline custom Qwen3:4b at Ollama `/v1` | `reasoning_effort: low`, `max_tokens: 512` | `length`, 512 output tokens, 2,514 reasoning characters, zero visible text; generic error | 16.157 / 16.383 s |
| Candidate custom Qwen3:4b, same session | `reasoning_effort: low`, `max_tokens: 512` | `length`, 512 output tokens, 2,485 reasoning characters, zero visible text; new actionable error | 9.861 / 9.968 s |
| Candidate native Qwen3:4b, explicit low, safeguard mode | `think: low`, `num_predict: 409` | `length`, 409 output tokens, 1,879 reasoning characters, zero visible text; new error survives safeguard wrapper | 14.472 / 14.551 s |
| Candidate native Qwen3.5:4b control | `think: false`, `num_predict: 512` | `stop`, 309 output tokens, zero reasoning, complete summary | 10.193 / 17.254 s |

Every failed probe above made one summary request and preserved all six history messages with an identical hash. The deterministic candidate replay also exposed the new error with one request and unchanged history (9.237 s RPC including cold setup; baseline 236 ms). Ollama reports output tokens but no separate reasoning-token count. These are functional probes, not a latency benchmark.

Native default behavior varied across startup runs: the candidate default Qwen3 request sent `think:false` and produced visible but truncated text, although `/api/show` still advertised only `true`. That path retained the existing truncated-summary error and preserved history. The explicit-low safeguard probe establishes the native empty-summary behavior without treating capability metadata as proof of wire-off support. A custom `/v1` probe with logical off omitted `reasoning_effort`; Ollama still spent all 512 output tokens on reasoning (2,348 characters), returned no visible text, and preserved history (10.510 s provider / 10.592 s RPC). The reported hosted MiniMax route has not been live-tested; proof is local macOS only.

The extended regression fails on original production source at the missing model/setting diagnostic: 1 failed, 26 passed, 23.00 s wall time. Candidate core suite: 27 passed, 253.47 s (225.51 s Vitest, mostly cold worker/transform preparation). Baseline suite: 27 passed, 12.37 s. Core typecheck, formatting, all seven affected ratchets, and independent Codex review through P2 passed. Full candidate build passed in 48m02s on the busy shared host.

Scoped type-aware lint passed in 23.53 s after installing the existing locked Solid lint-tool dependencies. The initial lint attempt stopped before rules ran because Gateway-only setup omits that tool package. Extra broader test attempts were cancelled during worker preparation and are not counted as passing evidence.

CI run [39892868465](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39892868465) found an inherited `check-test-types-core-1` failure: `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57` passes removed `managedHooksDir` / `bundledHooksDir` options. The failed config-CLI typecheck leaf reproduces the identical TS2353 error on the run's exact base `936b57750cf99dbef410e224412a99a91f0d3f46` locally (7.89 s). prs.title: fix: show running native agents in the Subagents panel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: running Codex-native subagents are absent from the Control UI Subagents panel even while their parent can receive their progress and results.

## User Impact

Users can see current native child labels and running/completed/failed/interrupted status in a separate “Live native agents” section. Existing Open/Stop controls continue to apply to managed OpenClaw child sessions. This first stage covers the full Subagents panel; saved native history, transcript navigation, and Details/header counts remain outside its scope. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native monitor already owns child observations, but the panel reads only child session rows. The retired Tasks mirror no longer supplies those rows. This change adds an optional, read-only harness observation hook to an opt-in parent description and renders its bounded result separately from sessions.

The host rechecks the real parent's physical identity, current plugin owner, and sharing authorization after awaited work. Codex reads its existing binding, retained client, and monitor without starting or adopting work. Opaque native IDs never become session keys or cancellation handles. Visible panels refresh with one non-overlapping read every five seconds; retired, hidden, disconnected, or denied owners clear the observations.

Related: #168162, #175041, and #176442 improve managed child presentation and are already included in the affected build. #166350 concerns durable native activity across reconnects; this proposal exposes live observations only.

## Evidence

### Latest-stable upgrade preservation (2026-10-23)

A stopped-state upgrade check from official stable **2026.10.6** passed using isolated, task-created state and synthetic session content. The published core archive matched npm SHA-512/SHA-1 metadata (SHA-256 `b13fc9f1221e185451573a435ff31bdeb8c5875f569e6f41008198708ca2359f`). Stable source/build: `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`.

Stable public `sessions.create` RPCs created a parent and linked child; `chat.inject` persisted one synthetic assistant history row in each. After shutting stable down, candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0, migrating agent schema 25→31 and state schema 20→30. The candidate retained both physical session IDs, labels, parent/child linkage and every original history row exactly. Selected agent/tool/plugin/session/update and Gateway settings matched. Stable rejected the new `includeNativeSubagents` field; the candidate accepted it for both existing sessions and returned the same identities without inventing native observations. A subsequent parent history write persisted.

**Revision qualification:** execution used the retained integrated local build `583f9cf88fb6a6e478aba10d4946bc1d7581a6da`, not a whole-head build of reviewed `6af87ba50c9feb7f68a389afb0b8b597843caa76`. All seven changed core RPC/harness/protocol files match the reviewed head byte-for-byte; UI/native-monitor and other migration source differ. This supplies bounded RPC/session-preservation evidence, not new native-child, external-model, browser, installed-updater or deployment proof. The stable package used a task-owned dependency overlay reusing retained exact-version production packages, plus the verified matching official AI package; unused Chrome DevTools MCP was absent. The shipped launcher completed its own pending package lifecycle; no marker was manually removed. The 13,995 remaining core files and 127 AI files match their verified archives.

Doctor's successful exit retains warnings: the disabled memory-core health surface was unavailable, synthetic inference-account/model context was absent, the existing native database owner was still requested by one inspection, the tool allowlist was narrow, synthetic plaintext tokens and absent recorded backup were noted, and the retained build was older than its checkout source. This is not a warning-free health result. Two preliminary fixture attempts failed before upgrade (runtime selection missing its required model, then an incorrect lineage-field assertion); both remain recorded and are not credited as passes.

Both successful-run Gateways exited 0 with null signal, their observed PIDs are absent, all three attempt state roots were removed, and the selected candidate artifact hashes stayed unchanged. The reviewed checkout remains clean. The optional public observation-hook/live-only presentation decision still requires maintainer acceptance.

All **31 focused tests across three UI suites pass**, covering polling/retirement, panel readiness and Stop behavior, scope replacement, and retained details. The existing owner tests read `nativeSnapshot?.children` directly, distinguishing a retired/absent snapshot from a valid empty roster. Redundant getter assertions are removed where the test already asserts that the snapshot itself is absent. The repair adds no replacement API, helper, or fallback and removes four production lines.

All **18 existing owner and retained-panel tests** pass across two suites (2.29s Vitest duration). UI types, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and a repository reference search pass. Fresh independent helper review is scoped-clean for P0–P3 with no actionable findings (one complete source-review pass; no project execution was claimed by the reviewer).

Desktop/mobile renderers, native/Gateway contracts, snapshot publication, authorization, and polling paths are unchanged. The inspected synthetic captures remain evidence at `1080de986ce145c7b7d9a6322909479889b52851`; the prior actual-native capture keeps its recorded revision and collector limitations. No new browser, native, external-model, or deployment capture is claimed. The recorded CI classification below remains tied to its actual tested revision; new-head hosted CI remains the broad gate. Public observation-hook and live-panel acceptance remain an owner decision.

## Integration repair (2026-10-22)

Integration revision `1080de986ce145c7b7d9a6322909479889b52851` integrates pinned upstream `52df852cd5be3b3691ef27d0942a4db7b2258eb1` to resolve actual merge conflicts. GitHub reported the previous head unmergeable; all 14 Actions runs at that head used `pull_request_target`, with no broad CI run. GitHub suppresses `pull_request` workflows while a branch conflicts. This repairs the integration rather than rerunning an old job or pushing an empty change.

The native observations now render through one shared read-only component in the current desktop, mobile, and classic panel paths. The current managed-session navigation, grouping, Stop confirmation, focus/scroll retention, and visibility owners are preserved. English native labels, including the P3 automatic-retry guidance, live in the existing lazy chat-session catalog; the startup catalog remains empty at that subtree. The native-completion contention test retains upstream's existing receipt/readiness order exactly. No new observation API, state, timer, permission rule, or execution control is introduced by this repair.

The corrected production-browser baseline fails at the missing native-row assertion while retaining the managed child. After integration, the same scenario passes desktop Running → Completed, mobile Completed → access denied, and a return to desktop with the denied contents cleared. Native rows remain separate and have no Open/Stop controls or session identity; the existing managed Open/Stop controls remain available. The scenario takes 6.71s (36.43s wrapper including its isolated production build). An initial baseline capture failed because the older fixture did not account for the new hover-only Stop presentation; that fixture problem was corrected before the meaningful red/green comparison.

Validation: all 20 native/Gateway authorization, physical-identity, continuation, observation and completion-settlement tests across five files pass (124.53s wrapper including cold worker preparation). All 18 panel-owner and retained-detail tests pass across two files (6.35s). UI types, scoped typed lint, keyless English baseline/verification, formatting and whitespace pass. The earlier direct package-boundary and external scoped-config typecheck attempts failed during declaration/root-directory setup. The supported canonical source graphs then passed without dependency, source, type-rule, or configuration changes.

The final candidate against pinned upstream changes 29 files: source +668/−123, tests/support +769/−0, and docs +17/−0. One shared native renderer serves all three presentation paths; no effect, untrack, DOM-listener/query, or flush machinery was added.

All **40 tests across three native-observation/inventory/settlement files** pass. The canonical runtime build records this exact commit; the existing UI gzip-size advisory remains and no budget was changed. The native/browser capture below remains at `235dce3165c6866d53fff24b0b3d05d658ef6332`, including its failed-collector qualification. This merge incorporates other upstream production changes and is not a new native/browser execution or deployment. The public observation-hook and live-panel decision remains maintainer-owned.

SDK-surface evidence revision: `99a13e230a9`.

### SDK surface repair

The new named `AgentHarnessNativeSubagents` SDK re-export was unnecessary for this feature. Codex now derives its plugin-local snapshot type from the existing `AgentHarness["readNativeSubagents"]` method, and the roster uses that same alias. The optional observation hook and protocol snapshot shape remain unchanged. The removed named export was introduced by this PR; no previously shipped API is removed.

- The real surface check fails before the repair at **3,811 public exports against a 3,810 budget**, then passes at **3,810**. The budget is unchanged and the shipped-API check reports no unauthorized removals.
- Core and Codex extension types, scoped lint and formatting pass.
- **Eight existing consumer tests pass across three files:** four Gateway authorization/lifetime cases, one composed native-observation case and three native-inventory/settlement cases. These consume synthetic observations; they do not execute a real native child.
- Independent review of the three-file type-only repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings. No runtime behavior change is claimed from this repair.

### Prior feature evidence at `d0ac9504f2e030cff4afa2364bd2d3678dc1a057`

- The new Gateway opt-in test failed before the API change. The production-browser scenario failed to find the native row before the UI change despite receiving the same synthetic native observation.
- The earlier feature candidate passed 78 focused checks across Gateway authorization, native monitor/protocol, composed attempt/binding/reader, UI lifecycle and eight production-browser scenarios. Its production build passed in 3m12.5s; selected production/test types, typed lint, styles, i18n, Swift/Kotlin generation, import-cycle and unchanged line/mock/assertion ratchets passed. These are prior-head results; the SDK surface failure and its current repair are stated separately above.
- The existing synthetic before/after screenshots below demonstrate presentation. The browser supplies the roster response, so they are not native-to-Gateway runtime proof.

### Actual native → Gateway → production panel at `235dce3165c6`

[Redacted runtime trace and collector qualifications](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177414#issuecomment-6285730236).

**The full collector exited 1, not a passing full run.** The requested native-panel boundary succeeded: a genuine native `spawn_agent`/`list_agents` child appeared through the shipped, authorized `sessions.describe` hook and actual production browser as **Running → Completed**, with the same prefixed child identity. The browser used real canonical device pairing and natural five-second refresh; no roster, native notification, Gateway response or browser clock was replaced. Private screenshots and raw native/Gateway/browser receipts are retained with an offline audit script for review.

This isolated proof used synthetic content and a scripted loopback Responses provider, with the installed official native **0.163.0** binary explicitly overriding the source dependency **0.162.0**. It is actual native/runtime/browser integration, not external model inference. The owned synthetic model catalog enabled V2 multi-agent metadata; native RPC bytes were forwarded unchanged. No compiled-owner instrumentation was used in this post-fix capture.

The native child and original parent both recorded their expected normal finals. Afterward, an additional completion continuation used another native thread and hit the scripted provider fixture's overly strict original-parent assertion. That later failure remains recorded; no successful later continuation or full-run pass is claimed. All native processes exited 0 without a signal; browser, Gateway and provider were joined and task state removed.

This proof found and repaired a real producer mismatch: native-monitor registration retained the logical `sessions.json` selector while the authorized Gateway reader supplied the canonical physical store. Registration now uses its existing captured `entryCurrent.source.path`; the exact store/currentness/identity guard is unchanged. The owning regression fails before the fix and all seven parent-continuation cases pass after it. Canonical Codex production-entry types, scoped lint/format and fresh P0–P2 review pass; the broad extension test-type graph remains an exact-head CI gate.

### Recorded CI fixture repairs

Recorded head `a80a17cf2d5e9594acfade7b2a47ca6d47cadd39` changes only two tests after the `235dce3165c6866d53fff24b0b3d05d658ef6332` native/browser capture; all production and UI source remains unchanged. The composed observation fixture now supplies its actual captured physical store, matching the repaired production registration. Its old logical-selector query reproduces the hosted failure before this test correction. The contention fixture receives the already-existing native receipt while its deliberate write is held, then releases retirement before awaiting observer readiness; this removes a fixture deadlock without starting new execution before readiness or weakening receipt, transcript, currentness or exactly-once assertions.

All **13 tests across the three affected observation/continuation/contention suites pass**. Scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The full all-plugin test-type graph was not rerun locally; exact-head CI remains the broad gate. The earlier native capture retains its original revision and failed-collector qualification.

The remaining Swift failure at `235dce3165c6` is the repository-wide **iOS ∩ macOS Periphery intersection**, not a base-versus-PR comparison. [Job118512145573](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39386209828/job/118512145573) reports `replaceSocketCredentials(_:expectedToken:)` and `bindNull(at:)`. Its actual tested merge is `9ee3107b2d93` over upstream `3a0253f25470`. Both reported Swift owner files and the intersection script in that tested merge are byte-identical to that upstream base (blobs `174edee9b397`, `0088c6e57cfe`, and `8a74c1a3bd14`). The PR's older Swift owners differ from the incoming base; the failing merge retained upstream's complete versions. This is source-based attribution of an unrelated shared-Swift gate; no separate base Swift build/scan was executed, and no unrelated methods or gate exclusions were changed.

### Remaining scope and maintainer decision

The bounded native-to-Gateway-to-panel observation above is now demonstrated, with the full-collector qualification preserved. It does not prove external-model behavior, a successful later completion continuation, saved native history or production deployment. Completed observations can disappear when their existing monitor owner retires; a Completed row alone does not assert parent consumption.

Maintainer direction is still requested for the optional public observation hook, opt-in session-description roster and separate live-only presentation. Removing the redundant named type export does not resolve that product/API decision. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

All fixtures and images are synthetic; no live conversation data, private identifiers, credentials or endpoints are published.

After:

![After: native child running separately from managed sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e57a978-0343-4d87-b132-07f85c7a9d4b)


### Hosted CI qualification at `1080de986ce145c7b7d9a6322909479889b52851`

[Hosted job119627628309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39718804203/job/119627628309), `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3`, fails the existing `session-catalog-index-recovery.test.ts` case “retries a failed rollout read after access recovers without a fingerprint change.” The line207 assertion reports that the mocked `fs.open` was never called for the changed rollout. This remains a recorded hosted CI failure.

The job checkout receipt identifies tested merge `c27d4e5f4c82dfffdd8b55dd0ca5cf5805904330` over upstream `afecea855376287edd92621852067e6c9154f1e8`. All **97 `session-catalog*` files** in the tested merge are byte-identical to that base. The determining test, catalog index/files/scanner/rollout owners and rollout fixture also match this PR head: test blob `4d51f4ad15d6537216fb0b7fce6a01531adefa37`, index `a66c52a73bda168b88b2f80063d6237614dc3dda`, files `367d12dcd0f7f6197952bbdfb5f559687409a051`, scanner `587a2e11dd563ac5482c1efc66d25ed7481d202d`, rollouts `81c51afb21ec7ddad3bb7d03d2d9a4bd8fad49aa`, fixture `2a7b5b877a599408ac6735230745c5fa1ae4ca3a`.

The failing catalog code is inherited unchanged from the actual base. This rules out a direct edit to those files; it does not establish that the failure is independent of every other PR change. No base execution comparison was run, and the hosted trigger remains unproven. The canonical `test:ci-failed` helper, invoked through its exact declared Node24 entry after the local pnpm frontdoor failed to start, classified the job **unknown** because it found no matching main job and could not consume its log. Its available output selected no test rerun. The actual failed job log was separately inspected as cited above.

One bounded replay of the exact-head owning file through the canonical test wrapper passes **all 12 tests**, including the failing named case (12ms), in **64.99s wrapper wall time** including cold worker preparation. No unrelated catalog source, exclusion, timeout, baseline, or CI workflow was changed. The source and UI/browser evidence remain at `1080de986ce145c7b7d9a6322909479889b52851`; this qualification adds no runtime/native/model claim or new review request. prs.title: refactor: localize private channel handoff frames
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three channel operations carry private argument/result frames between modules with one production consumer, obscuring the existing operation owner.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or operator action changes. Public contracts, validation, errors, fallback order and lazy imports remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the ACP health probe in the Discord provider callback, Matrix transcription context at ingress, and Slack identity fallback in the delivery owner. Move Matrix's private context proof to the room handler. Retain the serialized OpenRouter suite's migration to the real installed application host and remove two retired options from the stale hook freshness caller; no behavior assertions are weakened.

Remaining net production reduction: **63 lines** (Discord27 + Matrix27 + Slack9). Moved implementation bodies, tests/support/generated/declarations are excluded. This is a rule8 attribution-sized slice of the original161-line family, not a new tiny cleanup batch.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No guard or supported edge case is removed. This retires private DTOs, callback shuttles and single-consumer exports; security authority, validation, errors, timeouts, fallback order and realistic concurrency remain.
- Discord retains the lazy provider-session import, pre-await snapshots and every probe classification. Matrix retains pre-await metadata capture and mention/history/FIFO semantics. Slack retains payload identity from #127678 and all ordered identity downgrades.
- The original MCP HTTP, strict-tool host and Anthropic naming folds are **not in this PR anymore**. CI's unchanged Claude diagnostic-drainage test received two EPIPE events instead of one. Serial exact-head and base replays both passed, so rule8 restored all six changed files in the failing test's head/base import-graph union to freshly fetched main. No timeout, retry, skip, suppression or expectation was changed. Original reviewed candidate is preserved on `deslop/z25-parked-cli-drainage-20261015` without a PR, pending qualified Linux attribution. Only those reachable hunks were dropped.

Public SDK/protocol/config/CLI/persisted contracts and Phase E standalone session memory remain untouched. No dependency or schema change.

## Evidence

- Unchanged Discord provider32, Matrix public audio/classifier12, Slack payload/blocks/Enterprise34 and hook freshness2 cases passed. Matrix public baseline10 passed before the production fold.

prs.title: fix(macos): stop trusting the stale /etc/ssl/cert.pem bundle in services
prs.body:
## Summary

macOS gateway and node services defaulted `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. Apple no longer updates that bundle, and Node treats the extra file as additive trust, so the default added roots that the macOS trust store distrusts. This PR removes that additional trust source (the existing `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` darwin default stays), treats the exact legacy value as unset when service environments are built, and makes `openclaw gateway install` refresh a service that still stores it. It complements the already-merged compromised-chain fixes in the Rust TLS build (#179246) and the secret egress proxy (#179249) by closing the Node service-environment path they do not touch.

## What Problem This Solves

**What this Problem Solves** — Fixes: macOS gateway and node services trust the stale `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` bundle on top of the macOS trust store, so a certificate chain the system distrusts is accepted for the service's own HTTPS traffic (model providers, channels, plugin downloads, `web_fetch`).

1. `src/bootstrap/node-startup-env.ts`: the darwin branch of `resolveNodeStartupTlsEnvironment` defaulted `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
2. `src/daemon/service-env.ts`: `buildCommonServiceEnvironment` copied that value into the generated gateway and node service environments, so it was frozen into launchd definitions.
3. `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.ts`: reinstall preserved the stored value and the drift check had no leg for it, so an existing install was never refreshed.

Net effect: OpenClaw's own default added a stale trust source on top of the service's other roots.

## User Impact

Operators of macOS services no longer get the stale bundle added to their service's trust. Node's own bundled roots and the system store remain in effect as before, so this removes one additional trust source and does not make the service trust identical to the macOS trust store: a root that macOS distrusts but Node still bundles can stay trusted until the Node runtime itself is updated. After `openclaw gateway install` (or the automatic refresh on update) and a service restart, the stale bundle is gone from the service definition.

Compatibility: an operator whose HTTPS relies on a root present only in the stale bundle will see certificate errors after the refresh. Migration: copy the bundle to any other path and set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to it; every non-legacy path is preserved byte for byte. An operator who deliberately set the exact string `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` cannot be told apart from the value OpenClaw wrote, so that setting is treated as unset.

Scope of the repair: it applies to service definitions OpenClaw generates and refreshes. A CLI respawn (`src/entry.respawn.ts`) or node-worker snapshot (`src/node-host/node-worker-environment.ts`) that inherits an environment already carrying the legacy value keeps it until its source service definition is rebuilt. This PR does not rewrite those inherited maps.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` as the darwin default: it reads the macOS trust store, so the launchd TLS behavior that motivated the original default still works without the stale bundle.
- Strip only the exact legacy value, in the resolver that owns the default, so service builders and the drift check agree on one rule. No new configuration surface and no exported symbols.
- The drift check asks the same resolver whether a stored value resolves to nothing; only the exact legacy darwin value can, so operator-chosen paths are never flagged.

## Evidence

| Path | Mode | Before (base `14530ae62b5`) | After (this branch) | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Generated darwin service env, gateway and node | no inherited value | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` unset, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | real `buildServiceEnvironment` / `buildNodeServiceEnvironment`, `platform: "darwin"`, output below; `service-env.test.ts` |
| Generated darwin service env | inherited legacy `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` | value kept | unset, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | same run; `service-env.test.ts` |
| Generated darwin service env | inherited `/opt/corporate-ca.pem` | kept | kept | same run |
| Gateway install drift check | stored legacy value | no refresh | refresh warning, reinstall | `install.test.ts` with the real resolver forced to `darwin` |
| Gateway install drift check | stored `/opt/corporate-ca.pem` | n/a | not flagged | `install.test.ts` |
| Node TLS under each env (stand-in root, Linux host) | peer cert signed by a root only present in the extra bundle | trusted, 1 HTTP request reached the server | `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, 0 HTTP requests reached the server | trace below |

Generated service environments (real functions, `scripts/tsx`):

```
BEFORE (base)                                          AFTER (branch)
inherited=(unset)         gateway: EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1     EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=(unset)         node:    EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1     EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/etc/ssl/cert.pem gateway: EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1   EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/etc/ssl/cert.pem node:    EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1   EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/opt/corporate-ca.pem gateway: EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem       EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem
inherited=/opt/corporate-ca.pem node:    EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem       EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem
```

Handshake trace. A local HTTPS server presents a leaf signed by a throwaway root that stands in for a distrusted root. A child Node runs under each env; the server counts requests that reach its handler:

```
BEFORE env (base): NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<stale bundle>
    client: TRUSTED status 200
    HTTP requests that reached the application: 1
AFTER env (branch): NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS unset
    client: rejected UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
    server saw TLS handshake failure: ECONNRESET
    HTTP requests that reached the application: 0
```

Gaps, stated plainly: the trace ran on Linux with a stand-in root. It shows that an extra bundle adds trust and that removing it rejects the chain before any HTTP data is sent. It does not exercise macOS `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` or the real incident chains. I have not run a launchd service handshake on macOS.

## Boundary decisions requested

None. No CODEOWNERS owner is needed for a resolver default; the default change is the one compatibility item listed under User Impact.

## Testing

- New and changed: `node-startup-env.test.ts` (legacy value dropped under both `includeDarwinDefaults` modes), `service-env.test.ts` (gateway and node service env, fresh and legacy-inherited), `install.test.ts` (legacy value triggers refresh and an operator-chosen path does not, both through the real resolver forced to `darwin`).
- Red on base: the new and changed expectations fail on the unpatched code; green on this branch (32/32 in `install.test.ts`).
- Existing `entry.respawn.test.ts` (2 cases) and `daemon-install-helpers.test.ts` (1 case) fail on this Linux host identically with and without this branch, and are unrelated to the diff.
- `scripts/check-changed.mjs`: typecheck core and core tests, format, changed-file lint and import cycles pass. The max-lines suppression ratchet, tsgo graph boundary, and dead export scan fail on files this diff does not touch.

prs.title: fix(android): refuse embedded Control UI auth on pinned gateway connections
prs.body:
## Summary

The Android app's embedded Control UI WebView never enforced the native Gateway TLS certificate pin: its pin check lived only in the SSL-error callback, which Android invokes exclusively for recoverable certificate errors, so a successful platform-CA-trusted handshake bypassed the pin entirely and the page's own WebSocket transport was outside it too. This change refuses embedded Control UI auth admission — before credential evaluation, bridge registration, or remote loading — whenever the admitted native connection actually enforces a pin, and sources that decision from the admitted connection's TLS parameters instead of the saved fingerprint preference.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/ControlUiWebView.kt` — `installAuth` installed the native-auth bridge and the document-start credential script with no pin gate, and the page then loaded unconditionally on success. The only pin comparison was `onReceivedSslError`, unreachable for CA-trusted handshakes per the Android `WebViewClient` contract. A network attacker holding a different system-CA-trusted certificate and key for the exact Gateway hostname could serve an allowed-origin document that the startup auth and native-connect bridge would provision with the current native credential while the native connection stayed pinned. Now `installAuth` fails closed when `page.tlsFingerprintSha256` is set: no bridge, no credential script, no remote load; the superseded SSL-error proceed-exception and its helpers are removed.
2. `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt` — the control page's fingerprint was read from the saved preference store even when the active connection had not enforced it. `GatewayConnectionContext` now carries the `GatewayTlsParams` resolved for the connection, and `refreshGatewayControlPage` reflects the admitted transport: an actively enforced pin gates the embedded page, while an intentionally admitted local-cleartext connection with an inactive saved pin keeps working.

3. `ControlUiWebView.kt` — the refusal reused the generic "Reconnect the app to reopen this gateway page." message, which is wrong for a pinned connection because reconnecting with the same pin repeats the refusal. A pinned refusal now shows a localized explanation that embedded pages are unavailable on certificate-pinned gateways and native screens remain usable.

Net effect: a document admitted through a transport that cannot enforce the native pin can no longer receive native authentication material or connect proofs, and the local-cleartext workflow is preserved rather than broken by a naive saved-preference refusal.

## Why this design

- Fail closed at the owning boundary: Android WebView exposes no pre-document certificate hook for successful CA-trusted handshakes and cannot pin the page's own WebSocket networking, so the only sound admission decision for a pinned connection is refusal.
- The refusal keys off the admitted connection's TLS params, never the saved preference: a stored fingerprint that the current transport does not enforce must not lock users out, and the admitted transport must not inherit trust it did not verify.
- No new configuration surface: behavior is keyed entirely off existing per-connection pin state; unpinned CA-trusted workflows are unchanged.
- Embedded terminal, desktop, dashboard, and browser views are unavailable on actively pinned connections; native Gateway operation and native app screens retain the pin. This mirrors the Linux native-auth fail-closed approach and is documented in `apps/android/README.md`. A future feature-preserving transport that carries the pin across documents and credential-bearing WebSockets remains a separate design option.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path | Mode | Before | After | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `installAuth` admission, pinned connection (`ControlUiWebView.kt:341`) | Active native pin, no SSL-error callback (successful CA-trusted handshake simulated via feature-supported WebView mounts) | Bridge registered, credential script injected, remote URL loaded, credential callbacks reachable — pin never consulted | No remote load, no bridge registration, no document-start script, no auth-port transfer, zero credential evaluations and zero signings, across https and loopback origins and both modern and legacy auth feature paths | New regression `pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` (passes in 0.159 s) |
| Control page fingerprint source (`NodeRuntime.kt` `refreshGatewayControlPage`) | Manual local cleartext admitted with a saved-but-inactive pin | Page carried the saved fingerprint (wrong source; a naive refusal would break cleartext) | Page fingerprint is null — reflects the admitted transport, not the preference | `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest.controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` extended with a saved pin + cleartext connect |
| Superseded SSL-error proceed-exception (`onReceivedSslError`) | Pinned self-signed certificate, recoverable SSL error | Proceeded only on exact leaf-hash + origin match (the only path consulting the pin) | Removed; helper-only test coverage removed with it; pinned connections now refuse by default instead of exceptioning through | `ControlUiWebViewTest` trimmed; remaining 6 tests green |
| Refusal message on a pinned connection (`ControlUiWebView.kt`) | Opening an embedded page while the pin is enforced | Generic "Reconnect the app…" text (reconnecting never clears it) | Localized message that embedded pages are unavailable on pinned gateways and native screens remain usable; asserted not to say "Reconnect" | Same regression, extended; `native:i18n:verify` and `check` for the new string |
| Normal native auth / navigation / lifecycle | Unpinned CA-trusted gateway | Working | Unchanged — gate is a no-op when no pin is enforced | ControlUiWebViewAuthTest 13, GatewayBootstrapAuthTest 86, ConnectionManagerTest 37, GatewayTlsTest 15 all green |
| Native connection pin itself (`GatewayTls.kt`) | Fingerprint mismatch on native transport | Rejected | Unchanged (file untouched) | GatewayTlsTest 15/15 green |

Limits of this proof: the regression mounts the production composable under Robolectric with the AndroidX WebView shadows, so it proves the admission decision and the absence of credential/signature delivery, not Android network delivery. Not demonstrated: a live device/emulator certificate-interception PoC — the attack prerequisite (a distinct system-CA-trusted certificate and key for the exact Gateway hostname plus active MITM) is not reproducible in a unit-test harness, and the refusal is proven at the admission boundary instead.

Local gate runs (Ubuntu x86_64, Node 24.22.1, Temurin JDK 21.0.13+9, pinned Gradle 9.7.1, Android platform 37.0 rev 2): `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` focused suites — 157 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:lintPlayDebug` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL; `scripts/android-app-i18n.ts check` — no inventory diff; `git diff --check` — clean.

Red on base: with the production files (`ControlUiWebView.kt`, `NodeRuntime.kt`) restored to the base revision and the new tests kept, `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` fails both regressions. `pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` fails with `expected null, but was:<https://gateway.example:8443/openclaw/dashboard>` (the remote page loads under an active pin). `controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` fails with `expected null, but was:<abab…>` (the saved-but-inactive pin leaks into the page). The existing `mountedBridgeSignsNativeIdentityAndCurrentTokenWithoutExportingStartupSecrets` control passes on base. With the fix, all three pass.

Stored data and upgrade: this change reads no new stored data and writes none. `SecurePrefs.kt`, `ConnectionManager.kt`, the `gateway.tls.*` and `gateway.manual.tls` keys, device auth storage, and the native TLS trust manager are untouched, so saved pins and local-cleartext settings from an earlier release are interpreted exactly as before by the native connection. The only new input is the per-connection `GatewayTlsParams` that the existing `resolveTlsParams` already produces for the native sessions. A device or emulator upgrade run was not performed.

## Testing

- New: `ControlUiWebViewAuthTest.pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` (refusal contract, no SSL-error callback involved, both origins, both auth feature paths).
- Extended: `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest.controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` (admitted-transport fingerprint semantics).
- Removed: helper-only `ControlUiWebViewTest.pinnedSslError_proceedsOnlyForExactCertificateAtGatewayOrigin` testing the deleted SSL-error exception logic.
- Unchanged-green suites: `ControlUiWebViewAuthTest` (13), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` (86), `ControlUiWebViewTest` (6), `ConnectionManagerTest` (37), `GatewayTlsTest` (15).
- Docs: `apps/android/README.md` documents the pinned-connection behavior for users.

prs.title: fix(gateway): restore remote access after Tailscale restarts
prs.body:
Closes #148308.

Based on @Nachx639’s #137454 ([original commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/988cf4b25abd93965a9fee46a21935d46863780b)), adapted to current upstream by @enki. Both contributor commits are preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes remote access staying unavailable after a Tailscale daemon restart terminates the Gateway’s foreground Serve/Funnel claim while the local Gateway remains healthy.

## User Impact

Managed remote access recovers after Tailscale returns, without restarting the Gateway. Another application’s HTTPS route remains untouched. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing exposure owner now waits for claim loss, withdraws the expired origin, and reacquires the same dedicated backend with abortable backoff from about one second to one minute. A successful replacement republishes the origin. One recovery loop replaces the recursive watcher and its pending-promise bookkeeping.

Startup retains its original cancellation signal; resident recovery belongs to the returned shutdown handle because the CLI retires startup operations after handoff. Shutdown cancels and joins recovery and releases the replacement claim. Ownership conflicts stop recovery, and unconfirmed cleanup remains an error.

The change preserves disabled-Serve local fallback, hostname diagnostics, and existing route-ownership checks. Against main: production +109/-59 (net +50), tests/fixtures +232/-31 (net +201), documentation +1. This is 76 fewer net lines than the previous revision. The remaining production growth implements retry, cancellation, and cleanup handling within the existing owner.

## Evidence

- The recovery regression fails on unchanged main: the published origin remains absent after claim loss and retry intervals. It passes with this change, including transient failures and retirement of the startup signal.
- All 75 exposure, WebSocket consumer, and real worker/CLI fixture tests pass after integrating current main. The Serve and Funnel process cases terminate the original claimant, observe a replacement on the same backend without restarting its Gateway owner, then verify replacement-process cleanup. The post-integration process cases took 2.22s and 2.15s locally; CI timing remains available in the attached checks.
- Typed lint, formatting, whitespace checks, core typecheck, and all core test-graph typechecks pass. Independent P0–P2 review is clean.
- The broader changed-file check passed its typechecks and ratchets through deprecated-API scanning; its optional repository-wide Knip phase was stopped after prolonged local execution. Exact-head CI remains the broad gate.
- The unchanged startup-handoff test timed out once under heavy local load, then passed standalone with the same 120-second limit (97.8s). Its exposure function is mocked; no timeout or assertion was changed. The exposure/process run passed 28 tests, and the standalone retry passed the remaining test.

The current revision was not tested against a real Tailscale daemon or an external HTTPS client on this shared Mac; process fixtures avoid changing the operator’s tailnet configuration. The contributor’s [prior-revision real Serve proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180081#issuecomment-6330764938) remains supporting evidence, not a new-revision live claim.

ClawSweeper found no actionable code defects in this revision; its remaining request is a fresh real-daemon/HTTPS trace. That proof needs a separate isolated tailnet environment; the current-head red/green and real-process evidence above avoids modifying shared tailnet state.

prs.title: fix: allow model fallback after unexecuted tool calls
prs.body:
Closes #179396

## What Problem This Solves

Configured model fallback stops after an unknown tool is rejected without executing and a subsequent provider request fails. The terminal tool metadata treats that rejected call as unsafe to replay even though execution never started.

## User Impact

Agent runs can use their configured fallback after unknown-tool or argument-validation rejection. Calls that actually executed retain their replay protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor the existing authoritative execution-started fact when recording replay safety. No fallback policy, dispatch, configuration, or plugin SDK changes are needed.

## Evidence

[Captured Gateway/CLI outputs and safety controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179450#issuecomment-6356325545).

Built Gateway and CLI artifacts, Node 24.22.1 in isolated Linux Docker, with owned local primary and fallback provider fixtures. Configuration and session state were created through shipped config commands and sessions.create; real agent turns and chat.history supplied the observed results.

- Main: two independent unknown-tool turns both recorded `Tool definitely_missing_tool not found`, then a primary HTTP 404 `model_not_found`; neither called the configured backup or produced its final response. A no-tool control called the backup once and recorded its final response once.
- Candidate: the same two unknown-tool turns and an argument-validation rejection each called the backup once and recorded its final response once, with no side effects.
- Safety controls: policy-denied exec did not call the backup; a successfully executed write created exactly one marker and did not call the backup. The no-tool fallback control still passed.
- Focused replay-safety regression passed for explicit false, true, and absent execution-started metadata.

Simplification: one expression changes at the metadata owner; no new state or abstraction. Production delta: one replacement line. Test delta: 34 lines protecting the three execution-started states. No production machinery is added.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the old behavior; no migration or persisted-schema change. Blast radius is configured fallback after a tool result. Executed and uncertain calls retain existing replay safeguards.

prs.title: fix(process): stdout.pause() is ignored on a spawn broker command after ready()
prs.body:
Closes #162135

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `stdout.pause()` is ignored on a broker-launched command when it is called right after `await child.ready()`.

## User Impact

User impact: a caller that pauses a command's output gets it paused, so it can apply backpressure instead of receiving data it asked to hold.

## Why This Change Was Made

While the pipe is held, the broker now records the caller's last `pause()` or `resume()` and replays it after Node's own release-time resume. Before, it replayed only a past `resume` event and Node then resumed the stream anyway.

## Evidence

Real broker (`createSpawnBrokerHost`, real child process, Linux, Node 24): pause right after `ready()`, child writes `held`, then `resume()`.

- before: paused stream still delivers `held` (`received while paused = "held"`)
- after: `isPaused = true`, `received while paused = ""`, then `received = "held"` after `resume()`

A readable listener's own `resume()` now wins over an older held `pause()` (regression test in `pipe.test.ts`).

Test from the issue, on current `main`: `2 failed | 10 passed`. With the fix: `12 passed`. Both cases fail on `isPaused()`.

`pipe.test.ts` covers a `pause` or `resume` made right after release, which a first version of this fix got wrong (found in review, fails if the wrappers are restored early).

`src/process/spawn-broker`: 25 files, 118 tests pass. `oxlint`, `oxfmt` and `tsgo:core` clean. `check:changed` passed every gate and all core test graphs except `ui-components`, which my shell timeout killed at 25s (this change does not touch UI).

Test wall (`--maxWorkers=1`): `handoff.test.ts` 12s (2 cases added), `pipe.test.ts` 2s.

autoreview could not run (Codex and Claude not logged in). An independent read-only review found the post-release gap above; fixed.

prs.title: fix(update): keep verified updates successful after maintenance errors
prs.body:
Fixes #181020

## What Problem This Solves

An update can verify the target Gateway successfully, then report failure or enter rollback because later optional maintenance fails. Thanks @najef1979-code for the report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The finalizer retains the health owner's verification fact for the same invocation. The terminal-result owner converts only these recognized maintenance failures to a successful result with a warning:

| Existing failure classification | Eligible after verified activation |
| --- | --- |
| `GatewayRestartHealthError` | A late restart-health report |
| `UpdateCommandFailure` with `wrapper-retirement-failed` | Inspection/removal failure from retiring the old CLI wrapper |

Every collected nested error must also qualify. Authority refusals, deferred admission, data-at-risk failures, unknown errors, and unverified activation remain failures. Wrapper retirement propagates package-ownership and live-finalizer refusals before deletion instead of flattening them into optional-maintenance text. No configuration, schema, dependencies, or failure taxonomy is added.

Historical failed attempts remain unchanged when a later status probe finds the target healthy. This does not claim to fix the reported Linux readiness timeout or change the service-definition safeguard.

## User Impact

A 2026.10.5 to 2026.10.6 (or later) update whose new Gateway is verified healthy no longer reports failure or enters rollback because of a late, optional maintenance error (late restart-health report, old CLI wrapper retirement). Those are recorded as warnings on a succeeded update. Authority, data-at-risk, and unknown failures still fail exactly as before.

## Evidence

Validated revision: `388e4c2685cd2cde3876f0253354d0994155d535`.

- Regression on `4ca97d3a`: authority refusal, unknown error, health error wrapping an authority refusal, and unavailable admission incorrectly resolve successfully (four failing assertions); the data-at-risk control remains a failure. The original issue regression also failed on base `7a23014fd6ec231ded210a602e8266577c6ac29e`.
- Final Node focused selection: 19 passed in 48.89 seconds total; the finalization file took 29.84 seconds (45% tests), wrapper-retirement file 11.42 seconds (1% tests). Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-wrapper-retirement.test.ts -t 'classifies post-activation|recovers and retains the package|keeps a verified target|retireStandaloneGitWrapper' --maxWorkers=1`.
- Pinned Bun: all 105 tests in those two files passed in 111.28 seconds including preparation; file durations 62.30 seconds (75% tests) and 10.13 seconds (1% tests). Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-wrapper-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- All 47 original caller files completed under Node in their original input order: 1,365 passed, one inherited host failure, and one existing platform skip. Total wrapper time: 2,184.59 seconds. The inherited failure is detailed below.
- All 11 additionally affected caller files passed: 150 tests, 123.07 seconds including preparation. These cover Git admission/execution, dry-run, package ownership, snapshot, cleanup, timeout, and wrapper retirement.
- Core and CLI-update test type checks, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and dependency-cycle check pass (0 cycles). File limits are preserved by keeping the expanded regression table in the existing finalization test-support owner.
- Fresh independent P1 review: no accepted/actionable P0 or P1 findings.
- All proof ran locally with isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under the worktree. No remote lease was created. Full `check:changed`/SQLite inventory omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Prior live smoke on `4ca97d3a`: an isolated Gateway on a free loopback port returned `ready: true`, `coreReady: true`, and no failing components twice; it was stopped and its listener closed. The separate CLI probe hit the source-build publication guard and is not counted as successful. The Linux 2026.10.5-to-2026.10.6 upgrade was not reproduced; the P1 correction is proven at the finalization boundary above.

Inherited host failure: `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` / `keeps every tracked repository skill visible to Git-aware syncs` expects `git check-ignore` to exit 1. The shared `.git/info/exclude` already ignores `.agents/`, so Git exits 0. The test and repository `.gitignore` are byte-identical to the merge base; direct `git check-ignore --no-index -v` identifies the existing exclusion. No shared Git configuration was changed.

The packaging shard took 644.59 seconds. Its existing default-parent admission test took 30.174 seconds, and its 256-group case took 88.403 seconds (257 evaluations, 241,792 emitted bytes). These execute the real frozen-admission source graph repeatedly. The existing database rollback cases also start real candidate workers. No timeouts, retries, assertions, or baselines were weakened.

Production delta against the merge base: +100/-43; tests/support: +148/-12; documentation: +7/-0. This P1 revision adds +33/-10 production, +102/-52 tests/support, and +3/-2 documentation. It reuses existing error classifications and moves authority checks out of optional cleanup catches; no second health or authority owner is introduced.
