prs.title: fix(agents): describe sessions_spawn agentId allowed targets in the tool description
prs.body:
Fixes #149550

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` never said which `agentId` targets are allowed, so models only learned by being rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: the tool description lists the targets the spawn path accepts, for native subagents and ACP. Text only. Lists are capped at 20 ids, so a large roster cannot bloat every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text is built from the real admission rules: ACP ids go through the ACP resolver and `acp.allowedAgents`, and `requireAgentId` is honored. Callers pass the requester's already-resolved subagent status, so building the tool reads no session store. One helper resolves `allowAgents` and `requireAgentId` for all four callers.

Native and ACP lists share one renderer (`describeTargetIdList`, built on `summarizeStringEntries`). It lists the first 20 sorted ids, then `(+N). Only the first 20 ids are listed.` Agent ids are at most 64 chars, so the count cap also bounds bytes (about 1.4 KB per list). The overflow text does not assume `agents_list` exists.

It lives in the tool description, not the `agentId` schema property. Codex drops every schema description once a tool schema passes 5,000 bytes (first pass of `compact_large_tool_schema`), and `sessions_spawn` is already at 5,045 on `main`. The schema is unchanged; the tool description is kept.

Tests: the metadata-only suite that imported the full spawn runtime is deleted. Policy and cap cases live in the target-policy and ACP target tests. One registration assertion and the prepared-requester regression (never a store read) sit in the existing `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Shipped entry point: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message hi` against an isolated state dir and a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the model request. Agents `main` and `planner`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. `sessions_spawn.description` in the captured request:

| Config | `main` (base) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No allowlist | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |
| `agents.entries.main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]` | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |

The schema `agentId` stays `{"type":"string"}` in both.

ACP, through the Gateway with a backend enabled: an isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` (own state dir, loopback port) with `acp.enabled`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.defaultAgent: "codex"`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["codex","claude"]`, agents `main` and `planner`, and `main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]`. The Gateway logs `embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily`. `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message hi` then sent this `sessions_spawn.description` fragment (head `02c4032`) to the local OpenAI-compatible mock (full text, nothing truncated, no secrets):

```
`agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id from: claude, codex. Omit to use the configured ACP default ("codex").
```

The captured `agentId` schema is still `{"type":"string"}`.

Real output, config with `main`, `planner`, `acp.defaultAgent: codex`:

```
description: `agentId` targets a configured agent; ... `sandbox` inherit|require. `agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id, for exam...
schema agentId: {"type":"string"}
acp agentId=codex:     accepted
acp agentId=main:      rejected: agentId "main" is an OpenClaw config agent, not an ACP harness
acp agentId=(omitted): accepted
requireAgentId=true:   ... agentId is required; the requester agent is "main".
```

Codex fixture, `sessions_spawn`: schema 5,045 bytes on both `main` and this branch (byte-identical); tool description 2,805 to 2,884. Checked against `openai/codex` at `064c6b8c`, `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`. A local Codex checkout was not available, and Codex's own normalized byte count was not measured.

The existing `agents_list` rewrite of `configured agent;` still applies (`agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`).

Cap regressions: exactly 20 ids has no overflow text, 21 ids does, and 5,000 allowed ids render under 1,000 chars (native); 25 ACP ids are capped for both the allowlist and example forms.

Main merged; prompt snapshots regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo:core`, changed `tsgo:core:test` graphs and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass.

Test wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured on this head):

| File | Wall |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent-target-policy.test.ts` (16 tests) | 3.4s |
| `acp-spawn-target.test.ts` (22 tests) | 20s |
| `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` (74 tests, existing suite) | 31s warm; the 2 added cases take 5ms and 51ms |
| removed `sessions-spawn-tool.agent-target-description.test.ts` | was ~74s cold |

CI on `02c4032` (main at `12a91e0919` when it ran), all in files this PR does not touch:

| Red | Same on base? |
| --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (wrapper inventory) | Yes. Fails on pure `main` `12a91e0919` and `08005517c4` locally, and on unrelated PRs in the same window. |
| `src/gateway/server.visible-spawn-fallback.product-proof.test.ts` (session storage) | Yes. Fails 2 cases on pure `main` `12a91e0919` locally (`Session patch failed unexpectedly`). |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-mention-search.e2e.test.ts` (UI) | Not reproduced locally (no browser here). No UI file is touched; unrelated PRs fail other UI e2e cases in the same window. |

Touched tests, `tsgo:core` and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass on this head.

The full `chat-state.test.ts` file was not claimed as passed because a separate baseline harness case hung; the modified invalidation cases were run explicitly.

prs.title: fix(ui): show configured active budgets in the model picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model picker displays a configured model's maximum context window but omits its active context budget. For example, a model configured for 96k active tokens out of a 128k maximum appears as only **128k**.

Thanks to @ceckert for the original fix. Credit also to #173005 by @zyz619963502zyz as an earlier report and implementation of the same picker fix.

## User Impact

Picker rows show the configured active budget alongside the maximum when the active budget is smaller: **96k active · 128k max**. Equal active/maximum and missing-active controls continue showing just the maximum. A selected session's own budget remains scoped to its row.

## Why This Change Was Made

Always project the existing effective `contextTokens` field in ordinary model catalog rows, not only detailed queries. Carry that existing value through the picker option builders and format it alongside the maximum. No new configuration, schema, plugin SDK, or storage contract.

## Scope

This is now picker-only. The stale context-widget budget did not reproduce on main with a correct native retry: an installed prior release created the retained session, the current shipped Doctor migrated it, and real Codex 0.162.1 completed a turn through an owned Responses endpoint. Switching models cleared the previous prompt budget. That widget change and its associated snapshot/provenance tests and documentation were therefore removed in a separate commit, preserving ceckert's original commits. A separate PR with a reproduction of the stale-widget behavior is welcome.

## Evidence

Real built Gateway and Control UI in isolated Docker; configuration, session creation and chat state came only from shipped commands/RPCs. No mocked Gateway or injected session/catalog rows.

- Main twice: ordinary `models.list` omits the configured active budget and the picker shows **Capped budget 128k**.
- Candidate twice: the same ordinary catalog includes the active value and the picker shows **Capped budget 96k active · 128k max**.
- Equal active/maximum and missing-active controls remain **128k** on both arms. The separate selected model also shows its own configured active/max values on the candidate.
- Added picker regressions fail on main (3 failures); the candidate passes 51 model projection tests and 3 picker tests. Changed TypeScript passed Oxfmt and Oxlint.
- The real-provider built agent smoke returned `MODEL_PICKER_LIVE_OK`.

[Inspected before/after screenshots and actual accessibility/DOM evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180870#issuecomment-6355986825). Both uploaded image URLs were checked after publication.

## Simplification

Removed the unproven widget invalidation path rather than adding another state owner or retaining unused tests. The remaining change reuses the catalog projection and existing picker formatter. Production delta: +7/-5 lines; tests +90/-1; documentation +6/-3.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the old catalog projection and picker display; no persistent state changes. Blast radius is model-catalog budget metadata and model picker labels. Session context budgeting and the context widget are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: resume peer updates with session-scoped authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved peer updates failing after restart when the original requester has session-only write access, and permission failures appearing as generic delivery failures.

## User Impact

Authorized `sessions_send` updates can resume with `operator.sessions.write`. Read-only requesters remain blocked with a permission-specific resend notice; revoked authority is still rejected by the existing restoration and admission checks. Saved-input retention is unchanged; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope capture and restoration preserve the original scope set. Live peer sends bind their prepared session request through `bindInProcessSessionRun`, allowing the existing session-write authorization alternative. Recovery reconstructed an unbound request (`src/gateway/session-send-recovery.ts:400`), so method authorization incorrectly required broader `operator.write`. Reuse the same binding after source/communication validation, preserving current-authority checks. Classify typed Gateway `FORBIDDEN` errors as `permission-denied` (`src/gateway/session-send-recovery.ts:115`).

The boot log does not record original scope arrays, so it cannot distinguish narrow-write requesters from genuinely read-only requesters. Both cases are covered without widening authority. Existing unavailable-requester and endpoint replacement behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

The 2026-10-22 20:51:48 UTC Team boot on `cf2558f5639e` recorded four `missing scope: operator.write | FORBIDDEN` failures followed by peer replay `waitReason: "unknown"` (boot-log lines 443–446, 479–480, 489–490). Line 1028 reports five blocked inputs, zero cancelled, five retained; the fifth was a separate unavailable-requester failure. No message content or session identifiers are included here.

The regression exercises the real recovery owner, scope snapshot serialization/restoration, method authorization, and typed error conversion, with storage discovery and turn execution substituted. On the unchanged production base, session-write delivery was rejected and read-only denial was classified `unknown` (both regression cases failed). No live Team mutation or model invocation was used.

Validation passed on the final branch:

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/gateway/session-send-recovery.authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2/2 passed. Cold-run wall time 652 seconds, 89% module transformation.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` and gateway-root test typecheck: passed.
- Targeted `run-oxlint.mjs` for both TypeScript files, formatting for all three files, `check-docs-mdx.mjs`, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Independent Codex committed-branch review: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings. A separate local run of the existing recovery suite stalled before test execution and was interrupted after more than ten minutes without a test result; it is not counted as a pass. Exact-head CI provides the broader suite proof.

Production delta: +27/-18 lines (net +9); tests: +157; documentation: +5.

Exact-head [CI run 39888629397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888629397) completed with one inherited root failure: `check-test-types-core-1`, TS2353 in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57` (`managedHooksDir` is not accepted by `prepareInternalHooks`). The fixture and API source are byte-identical in the tested main parent, tested merge, and current main `f00f6a56a83a`; neither is touched here. The older scheduled-main comparison called it new without comparing selected scope. All other selected CI jobs, including `security-fast`, passed. The native inherited-failure exception is being used; CI is not claimed green.

Independent current-main proof on `f00f6a56a83a`: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --incremental` reproduced the same sole TS2353 at `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57` (exit 2), using a separate checkout and frozen dependency install.

prs.title: perf(infra): avoid async frames for synchronous stall phases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stall attribution copies the async-context frame while labeling synchronous session-row and agent-roster work, adding allocation to the work it measures.

## User Impact

Keeps stall task names, phases, longest-segment accounting, and asynchronous task inheritance while reducing the allocation cost of synchronous phase scopes. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observer now runs the callback and restores its previous segment in `finally`, removing its per-call exit closure. Phase scopes use the existing synchronous observer; task boundaries continue to establish the async label. `withAgentRosterFactsBatch` and `withPreparedRows` are the only production task-name readers and phase callers. Roster callbacks are synchronous; placement captures the originating task before awaits, requires synchronous consumption, and explicitly enters its stored owner context for asynchronous preparation. The observer-first name lookup still works inside an older owner snapshot. Node already avoids copying an unchanged async store; this change preserves that behavior.

Runtime production delta (`src/`, excluding tests): **−3 lines**, no cache or retained prepared context. The regression adds 37 test lines; the committed measurement adds 90 script lines and 16 documentation lines. The broader non-test diff is positive only because it includes this rerunnable proof.

## Evidence

Owner benchmark on Linux, Node 26.12.1, with 21 live async stores; five alternating baseline/candidate process pairs, each with 20,000 warmup calls and 50,000 measured calls. Allocation sampling includes objects collected by both GC generations at a 512-byte interval. Throughput is measured separately without allocation sampling. Values below are arithmetic means; 250,000 allocation and 250,000 timing calls per side per row. Allocation sample counts (baseline/candidate): task entry 3,266,572/3,212,519; same-name reentry 88,689/49,598; phase 3,262,606/31,011.

| Scope | Baseline bytes/call | Candidate bytes/call | Baseline calls/s | Candidate calls/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Async task entry | 8,092.30 | 7,971.36 | 723,541 | 748,385 |
| Same-name task reentry | 195.30 | 107.00 | 6,207,674 | 9,902,110 |
| Synchronous phase without inherited name | 8,082.75 | 66.35 | 748,728 | 10,397,038 |

The copy-heavy phase case reduces allocation by 99.18%. Literal zero allocation is not achieved: timing/caller bookkeeping remains. These mechanism results do not establish whole-Gateway gains or production call frequency.

Reproduce each row with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/main-thread-stall-measure.mjs <entry|same-name|phase> 21 50000` on both revisions. The benchmark verifies the task name inside every callback.

A separate instrumented baseline Gateway completed 12 measured rounds / 96 turns with 5,000 synthetic sessions and 12 clients. Six counter snapshots wholly inside its 90-second measured window span 75.052 seconds: 35,806 observed scope calls (**477.08/s**), including 27,331 phase calls (**364.16/s**). Of those phases, 25,478 already had the same inherited name (93.22%); 1,853 did not (**24.69/s**). Task boundaries account for the remaining 8,475 calls (**112.92/s**). These are windowed call rates, not per-turn counts. No production Gateway or production profile was used.

The first counter setup lacked the retained transcript required by the mixed-history workload and was discarded. The corrected run completed; a post-window cron cleanup request timed out, after which its Gateway process and both ports were verified stopped. Acceptance pairs use independent fresh fixtures.

- Focused monitor tests: 7 passed, including same-name nested phase restoration after a throw.
- Session-row placement lifecycle tests: 8 passed, including RPC/scheduler attribution after readiness waits. Combined focused command: 76.74 seconds, including cold compiler preparation; actual tests took under one second.
- Changed-file format and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Automated PR review and ClawSweeper also report no actionable findings on `490cbc14a6d824375bb4468228861378865b4004`.
- Changed-file lint passed (initial missing-brace findings in the benchmark fixed); export-name collision guard passed; both script-closure files passed all 22 tests in 62.04 seconds.

## Paired Gateway result

**Neutral whole-Gateway result; qualifies as a simplification.** Three accepted concurrent pairs on Node 26.12.1 compare baseline `6ada8b0211b848fa10a8c13a3dfc4b421c42a360` with candidate `490cbc14a6d824375bb4468228861378865b4004`. All used the same slot with interleaved CPUs: baseline even/candidate odd in pairs 1 and 3, reversed in pair 2. The shared admission and production guard were unchanged; none of the accepted pairs was interrupted. Each side completed 320 measured turns, 40 measured rounds (52 including warmup), and 24 reset calls including warmup. Each measured window lasted about 400 seconds after a 120-second warmup.

The workload used 12 clients, 8 concurrent agent runs, streaming and tool stress, mixed RPC reads, and fresh synthetic fixtures with 5,000 sessions, 15,000 participants, 32 retained runs, and 1 MiB of transcript text. These compact fixtures do not reproduce production's retained-heap size. Allocation and GC figures below cover the main isolate, not worker heaps. Both revisions use identical instrumentation; collected-object heap sampling runs continuously through the measured window.

The gate is a ≥20% adverse paired mean or ≥10% adverse in both initial pairs. Opposite signs or a >5× baseline spread require a third pair and an absolute-mean decision. The first two valid pairs disagreed on allocation and several latency metrics, so a third pair was required. No qualified metric exceeds the rejection gates after the required absolute-mean assessment. Allocation changes by −1.646 MB/turn (−0.855% of mean baseline), total GC by −0.577 ms/turn (−1.687%), promotion by −1.375 MB/turn (−3.503%; mean paired relative delta −3.527%), and event-loop p99 by −0.863 ms (−1.777%; baseline/candidate n = 18,067/18,199, 18,630/18,630, 18,605/18,615). These small deltas are not claimed as a demonstrated system-wide speedup.

The large pair-1 observed GC-entry maximum (169.604 → 525.959 ms) belongs to incremental entries, not the native `pause` field. The native maxima are reported separately above. The long candidate entry co-occurs in the same round as a 940.048 ms event-loop maximum (n = 298; baseline round: 351.535 ms, n = 282), so it is not dismissed as harmless. Individual entry timestamps were not retained; exact causation cannot be established. The overall pair-1 loop maxima were 935.330 → 940.048 ms. Pairs 2 and 3 did not repeat that large incremental-entry spike. Native maximum pauses in all three pairs remain below max(50 ms, twice baseline).

The stall owner's self/native allocation share is below 5% in every Gateway sample, so this is accepted only as the net-deletion/no-new-cache simplification. Owner allocation samples / all allocation samples, baseline → candidate:

| Pair | Owner share | Owner samples / all samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.1848% → 0.1659% | 218/117,022 → 192/114,795 |
| 2 | 0.1760% → 0.1639% | 206/116,096 → 193/116,771 |
| 3 | 0.1699% → 0.1670% | 200/116,757 → 194/115,280 |

Profile byte totals exactly match the driver allocation totals. These coarse owner samples establish workload share, not a precise owner improvement percentage. In the separate counter run, most phases already inherited the same task name, explaining why the copy-heavy microbenchmark is not representative of every phase call.

After deployment, inspect allocation under the stall scope for fewer async-context frame/Map copies and exit closures while task names, phases, and longest-segment attribution remain unchanged. Watch total GC time per unit of work, promotion, connection p95, and event-loop p99. Production profiling remains the deployment owner's responsibility.

## Benchmark recovery

The initial second-pair setup hit a busy loopback port before measurement and was discarded. Its replacement completed the timed workload but exposed a post-window benchmark cleanup race: disabling the synthetic cron job cancelled a newly started run, and the subsequent all-history assertion rejected that intentional cancellation. Both sides had 22 successful cron runs; their only errors began 873 ms and 1,510 ms after profiling ended. That pair is also discarded because the failed driver did not persist its exact whole-window event-loop histogram.

The replacement measurement uses the same task-private harness correction on both revisions: validate cron history before disabling the job, preserving every assertion, and save whole-window diagnostics after allocation profiling stops. The measured path is unchanged; this correction is not part of the PR diff. The original successful first pair remains valid. The correction's SHA-256 is `006486555b1b1ee7405f4ffdbf9454a23f6b610e8a485a0d5f721c1104f22c44` (original harness: `a9f332d274d8d87c0ee0e8db8954836c1769411c4981a6cd6d12f0763e591642`).

## CI and handoff

The current exact-head check rollup has 68 successful checks. The red browser check is `checks-ui-e2e (4/9)` in [run 39882050600](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39882050600/job/120181894759): the active and note-only progress-card tests in `session-progress-live-placement.e2e.test.ts` fail at line 698, expecting zero pills after keyboard hide plus a viewport change and receiving one. The aggregate gates are red as a consequence.

This scenario serves bundled browser UI with an injected mock WebSocket; it does not execute the changed Node stall owner. Scheduled [main run 39885503944, browser shard 6/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39885503944/job/120192944479), at `6676ef1fc9fea35a1031e647c1cdec3d3eb97797`, independently fails the **same active-progress test at line 698 with the same expected-0/received-1 assertion**. The note-only parameter variant passes on that main run; both variants fail at the shared assertion on this PR. This is inherited browser-test failure evidence, not a green check. No CI rerun was requested, and no UI source or test was changed.

Subsequent scheduled [main run 39890895258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890895258), at `b8d8c220af0b6bbee84b8768ab7378a394c0c910`, passed all nine bundled UI E2E shards. The failing test, menu machine/runtime, progress-card presentation, and E2E harness/config are unchanged between the failing and passing main heads. Surrounding lazy-loading/boot work did change, so this supports intermittent or timing-sensitive behavior rather than proving a repair. The earlier run is the newest **matching failure** evidence; the latest scheduled run passes this suite. The PR's red check remains red, and no rerun or rebase was used to chase green.

The performance gates support this simplification. This PR remains open and ready for the lead's review; the lead owns merging. The browser CI caveat above remains explicit, and this lane has not merged the PR.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer workspace preview content until it is opened
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat downloads file-preview preparation, editing, and artifact-decoding code before a workspace item is opened.

## User Impact

Chat boot loads 2,032 fewer gzip bytes with the same 23 JavaScript requests. The content runtime loads when a file, artifact, or file download is requested. Workspace selection, temporary tabs, navigation, and preview settlement retain their existing owner. No layout, schema, configuration, or migration changes are intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move content preparation and its exclusive dependencies behind the existing admitted workspace operations. Preview admission stays synchronous; after loading the runtime, the original connection and workspace must still own the operation before any read starts. File editing, source-conflict recovery, and download cancellation keep their existing behavior.

The source move leaves no parallel implementation: the retained file helper contains only path resolution and text decoding required by the synchronous diff owner. The generated boot manifest drops three stale header/mobile entries.

## Evidence

Current candidate `e231cd8b1412a8b4b2a170dc1a103b3dd4f0b414` merges main `4f44cc7d7899cc924e7ce17cb0e399db8a72b6f7`. The only conflict was the asset-budget file; the resolution retains main's stricter Chat and New Session caps unchanged. The Workspace implementation and its regression tests are byte-identical to the previously reviewed candidate `c216f27fcdd6`.

Matched production builds compare the exact merged-main baseline with the integrated candidate, using identical pinned metadata, dependencies, and 29 canonical plugin inputs. Build-proof files are byte-identical. Measurements use `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --json --base-dist <baseline-dist>` and shipped compression sidecars.

| Boot surface | Base gzip JS | Candidate gzip JS | Change | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat | 1,349,072 B | 1,347,040 B | −2,032 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 823,291 B | 823,253 B | −38 B | 17 → 17 |
| Startup | 316,324 B | 316,296 B | −28 B | 7 → 7 |

CSS is identical. Across all emitted JavaScript, gzip output grows by 217 bytes and three assets. This relocates optional work rather than deleting capability. Strict performance checks pass with no warnings or violations. The supported boot-manifest regeneration produced exactly the merged manifest; both production builds and current production UI typechecking pass. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings.

The reconnect regression fails on the original base because a file read starts before the deferred boundary can revalidate ownership, and passes with the extraction while also checking synchronous admission and selection. The original 31-test Workspace suite and the previous 72 focused file-panel/embedded-panel/retained-pane tests passed. On the integrated candidate, all 103 focused tests passed: 81 in the shared UI shard and 22 retained-presentation cases. The wrapper took 1,177.74 seconds, with 97% and 94% of the shard durations spent in cold transformation. The CI repair preserves synchronous selection checks while waiting for concrete read-start before resolving or retiring a held request.

Earlier production Knip checks on exact base `7a23014` and candidate `d4210326` both exited 1 with byte-identical inherited findings. No ignores or unrelated repairs were added; this is prior-head evidence, not a current-head Knip claim.

Refreshed cold-load timing on this exact candidate against `4f44cc7d789` passed ten alternating baseline/candidate cold-cache pairs (`--runs 20`), using production Vite preview HTTP, synthetic fixtures, persisted UI state, identical metadata/plugins, and no tracing/profiling.

| Presentation metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Transcript median | 460.00 ms | 444.30 ms | −3.41% |
| Transcript p95 | 815.50 ms | 769.40 ms | −5.65% |
| Composer median | 459.25 ms | 443.55 ms | −3.42% |
| Composer p95 | 814.30 ms | 768.00 ms | −5.69% |

The transcript gate requires median regression ≤5% and p95 no worse; both pass without an extra batch. The runner actually supplied four AMD EPYC CPUs, 16.56 GB RAM, affinity 0–3, and sample one-minute load 2.42–3.03. Command time was 242.613 seconds, exit 0. All 72 collected files were verified, including 46 parsed JSON files, the 20 alternating runs, the exact pinned manifest, and identical baseline/candidate build proofs. [Timing allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891689079). The lease is stopped and remote settlement is complete; workflow cancellation records cleanup after the successful command.

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891596879) is in progress on `e231cd8b1412`. Prior-head CI passed on `c216f27fcdd6`; it is not used as current-head evidence.

prs.title: fix(providers): typed Ollama, LM Studio, oMLX, llama.cpp or Copilot Proxy URL is appended to default
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Ollama, LM Studio, oMLX, llama.cpp and Copilot Proxy setup, a base URL the user types is appended to the prefilled default (for example `http://127.0.0.1:11434http://gpu-box:11434`), so setup fails or uses a broken URL.

## User Impact

User impact: typing a remote base URL in these setup prompts now uses exactly that URL, and pressing Enter on the empty field still uses the default (or, for oMLX and llama.cpp, the saved URL). The default stays visible as a hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompts passed the default as `initialValue`, so the field starts filled and typed text lands after it. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175855 fixed the same thing for SGLang and vLLM (issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175736), and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173164 for LiteLLM: the default goes in `placeholder`, only a saved URL is prefilled, and blank input resolves to the saved URL or the default. This PR applies that shape in each plugin's own setup prompt:

- Ollama and LM Studio: the default moves to `placeholder`, blank input uses it, and the "Required" check for blank input is gone. Neither prompt prefilled a saved URL before, and this PR does not start doing so.
- oMLX: prefills only the saved URL; blank input keeps the saved URL or the default.
- llama.cpp: prefills only the saved URL (the default was already the placeholder); blank input keeps the saved URL or the default instead of failing "Required".
- Copilot Proxy: the default moves to `placeholder`; its URL normalizer already maps blank input to the default.

The Control UI shows the same steps through the Gateway wizard, which already forwards `placeholder` and accepts an empty answer, so it gets the same behavior.

## Evidence

Tested at `bd3e832ff7b` (the CLI runs were made at `6472068ad08`, the same tree with a longer commit subject; base `upstream/main` `a5e54e44960`).

Built CLI (`pnpm build`, then `node openclaw.mjs models auth login --provider <id>`) on Ubuntu 22.04 with Node 24. Each run had a fresh, empty home and state directory, no network and no provider keys. A script wrote each step's text to the prompt in a pseudo-terminal in one write, without clearing the field first; the prompt handled each character as a keystroke, as with typing.

Before (base `a5e54e44960`):

```text
ollama, typed http://gpu-box:11434:
  field: http://127.0.0.1:11434http://gpu-box:11434
  note:  Ollama could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:11434http://gpu-box:11434.
lmstudio, typed http://gpu-box:1234:
  field: http://localhost:1234http://gpu-box:1234
  error: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL without embedded credentials (e.g. http://localhost:1234).
omlx, typed http://gpu-box:8000/v1:
  field: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1http://gpu-box:8000/v1 (accepted)
  then:  No oMLX chat models were found. ...
llama-cpp, "Existing llama-server", typed http://gpu-box:8080:
  field: http://127.0.0.1:8080http://gpu-box:8080
  error: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL without embedded credentials (e.g. http://localhost:8080).
copilot-proxy, typed http://gpu-box:3000/v1, model list kept:
  field: http://localhost:3000/v1http://gpu-box:3000/v1
  openclaw.json: "baseUrl": "http://localhost:3000/v1http://gpu-box:3000/v1"
```

After (this PR, same steps):

```text
ollama, typed http://gpu-box:11434:
  field: http://gpu-box:11434 (the default http://127.0.0.1:11434 is shown dimmed as a hint before typing)
  note:  Ollama could not be reached at http://gpu-box:11434.
ollama, Enter on the empty field:
  note:  Ollama could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:11434.
lmstudio, typed http://gpu-box:1234, then Enter at the API key:
  field: http://gpu-box:1234
  note:  LM Studio could not be reached at http://gpu-box:1234/v1.
omlx, typed http://gpu-box:8000/v1:
  field: http://gpu-box:8000/v1
  then:  No oMLX chat models were found. ...
llama-cpp, "Existing llama-server", typed http://gpu-box:8080, then No at the API key:
  field: http://gpu-box:8080
  note:  llama-server could not be reached at http://gpu-box:8080.
llama-cpp, Enter on the empty field:
  note:  llama-server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:8080.
copilot-proxy, typed http://gpu-box:3000/v1, model list kept:
  field: http://gpu-box:3000/v1
  openclaw.json: "baseUrl": "http://gpu-box:3000/v1"
```

Observed result: on the base every prompt appends the typed URL to the default; with this PR the typed URL replaces it, and blank input keeps the default.

Saved URL and upgrade from the latest stable, same isolation (the network namespace brings up loopback only). A small mock OpenAI-compatible server on loopback (`127.0.0.2`, ports 18000 and 18080) answered model listing and logged each request; no real provider server was used.

```text
saved URL, this PR's build, two runs on the same state:
  omlx run 1, typed http://127.0.0.2:18000/v1:  mock: GET /v1/models; openclaw.json baseUrl http://127.0.0.2:18000/v1
  omlx run 2, field prefilled with http://127.0.0.2:18000/v1, Enter:
                                                 mock: GET /v1/models; openclaw.json unchanged
  llama-cpp run 1, typed http://127.0.0.2:18080: mock: GET /health, /models, /props; baseUrl http://127.0.0.2:18080/v1
  llama-cpp run 2, field prefilled with http://127.0.0.2:18080, Enter:
                                                 mock: GET /health, /models, /props; openclaw.json unchanged

upgrade, openclaw 2026.10.5 from npm, then this PR's build on the same state:
  2026.10.5 copilot-proxy, field cleared, typed http://127.0.0.2:3000/v1: baseUrl http://127.0.0.2:3000/v1
  2026.10.5 models set copilot-proxy/claude-sonnet-4.6
  this PR: config get models.providers.copilot-proxy.baseUrl -> http://127.0.0.2:3000/v1
           config get agents.defaults.model.primary          -> copilot-proxy/claude-sonnet-4.6
  this PR: doctor --fix --non-interactive (main's own state migration from 2026.10.5; baseUrl and primary model kept)
  this PR copilot-proxy, typed http://127.0.0.2:3001/v1 (no clearing):
           openclaw.json diff: only baseUrl, http://127.0.0.2:3000/v1 -> http://127.0.0.2:3001/v1
```

Stored data: this PR changes no config key, shape or reader. It changes only the prompt's initial value and what a blank answer resolves to, and the URLs it saves are written by the same code as before. 2026.10.5 bundles Ollama, LM Studio and Copilot Proxy; oMLX and llama.cpp are not in it, so their saved-URL path is shown with this PR's build above.

How blank input was checked: Ollama and llama.cpp by the CLI runs above; LM Studio and oMLX by the regression tests below; Copilot Proxy by its URL normalizer (`normalizeBaseUrl` in `extensions/copilot-proxy/index.ts` maps an empty answer to the default), not by a run.

Regression tests (fail on the base, pass here):
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` "Docker setup hints the host Ollama endpoint and uses it for blank input" (base: the prompt still has `initialValue`);
- `extensions/lmstudio/src/setup.test.ts` "interactive Docker setup hints the host LM Studio endpoint and uses it for blank input" (base: `expected 'http://host.docker.internal:1234' to deeply equal undefined`);
- `extensions/omlx/setup.test.ts` "blank input uses the default" and "blank input keeps the saved URL, prefilled for editing" (base: blank input reaches discovery as an empty URL and setup fails);
- `extensions/llama-cpp/src/external-server/setup.test.ts` "blank input uses the default" and "blank input keeps the saved URL, prefilled for editing" (base: the default is prefilled, and blank input with a saved URL discovers the default instead).

The first two replace the old Docker-default tests, which asserted the prefilled `initialValue`.

Checks: the four touched test files and the other tests of these prompts (`extensions/lmstudio/src/setup-url.test.ts`, `extensions/ollama/index.test.ts`, `extensions/ollama/lazy-import.test.ts`, `extensions/ollama/src/setup-model-selection.test.ts`, `extensions/ollama/src/setup.cancellation.test.ts`, `extensions/llama-cpp/lazy-import.test.ts`) pass; `pnpm check:changed` typecheck and lint pass, and oxfmt is clean on the changed files.

| Test file | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local | CI seconds (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` at `bd3e832ff7b`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` | 2.34 s for the Vitest shard (Vitest duration 1.51 s) | results over 0.91 s, in a 26-file shard of 62.17 s |
| `extensions/lmstudio/src/setup.test.ts` | first run 25.64 s for the Vitest shard (Vitest duration 24.02 s); second run with a warm cache 7.94 s (6.45 s) | results over 1.01 s, in the same 26-file shard |
| `extensions/omlx/setup.test.ts` | 11.02 s for the Vitest shard (Vitest duration 9.56 s; the two new cases take 73 ms and 90 ms) | its own shard: 18.97 s (Vitest duration 17.38 s) |
| `extensions/llama-cpp/src/external-server/setup.test.ts` | 6.72 s for the Vitest shard (Vitest duration 5.20 s) | results over 0.53 s, in a 10-file shard of 20.29 s |

Simplify pass: each fix stays in its plugin's setup prompt, with no shared helper and no caller changes. What disappeared: the blank-input "Required" rejection in Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp, and the default as the prefilled value in oMLX and llama.cpp. Saved-URL prefill was not added to Ollama, LM Studio or Copilot Proxy, which never had it. Behavior still protected: Ollama still rejects an `ollama.com` URL, LM Studio and llama.cpp still reject invalid or credential-bearing URLs, and oMLX still rejects non-HTTP URLs. Delta against the merge base: production +24/−19 in 6 files, tests +50/−7 in 4 files.

Not covered: the Control UI path was not run (it renders the same wizard steps through the Gateway; the UI e2e tests build those steps themselves and do not run plugin code, so they are unchanged). Copilot Proxy has no test file; its change is the one prompt field, covered by the run above. The upgrade from 2026.10.5 was run for Copilot Proxy only (oMLX and llama.cpp are not in that release; Ollama and LM Studio never prefilled a saved URL, before or after). No real Ollama, LM Studio, oMLX, llama.cpp or Copilot Proxy server was running: the fresh-state After runs stop at the reachability check, and the saved-URL runs used the mock server.

prs.title: fix(markdown): inline backticks swallow following prose in chunking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inline triple-backtick code at the start of a line incorrectly making subsequent prose look like an unclosed code block to message chunkers.

## User Impact

Prose following inline code can be split normally. Actual fenced blocks, including tilde fences, keep their existing protection. No configuration changes or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the CommonMark restriction on backticks in a backtick-fence openerΓÇÖs info string at the existing scanner owner. Four production lines; no new parser or state.

## Evidence

- Owner regression fails on the base and passes with the repair.
- Fence/code-span suites: 32 tests pass (5.05s Vitest; 14.76s wrapper). Outbound chunking consumer suite also passes.
- Targeted type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors; formatting and diff checks pass.
- Independent structured review: scoped-clean at P0ΓÇôP2. Review used a source-only linked checkout on the same host; both changed files match by SHA256 and the base is identical. Review does not independently attest test execution.
- Broad proof belongs to PR CI. No live gateway/channel was modified.


## Shipped-channel HTTP red-before / green-after proof

Exact head0b18f1aad38cf67d8a742a8a629795908f3b5fe6;comparable source base9827935108e185e3f290d622dcccec07ff3814ae. Executed exported production sendMessageSlack() plus production createSlackWriteClient()/real Slack WebClient against a temporary synthetic HTTP server receiving actual chat.postMessage requests. No chunker,formatter,send-method,fetch mocks or Vitest. Per-process temporary state/config,synthetic token/recipient,no live service/account/Gateway changes. Node24.22.1,same locked dependencies.

Config: channels.slack.streaming.chunkMode=newline,textChunkLimit=32. Single-newline input stays one paragraph and exceeds cap, reaching scanner-backed Markdown chunking before actual Slack formatting and HTTP I/O.

Before: replaced only production fences.ts with exact-base content; it is the sole changed runtime file (other PR file is tests). Actual five HTTP payloads have repeated inline labels and invented empty code blocks; literal payload assertion exits1:

~~~~json
{"entry":"sendMessageSlack","fixture":"inline-opener","input":"```literal```\nParagraph outside code with ordinary words.","actual":["`literal`\nParagraph outs\n\n","```\n\n```","`literal`\nide code with\n\n","```\n\n```","`literal`\nordinary words."],"methods":["/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage"]}
~~~~

After: restored exact committed head and verified clean git diff. Same fixture assertion exits0; actual three payloads preserve one inline label and ordinary prose, with no invented code fence. Real-fence and ordinary-prose controls also pass:

~~~~json
{"entry":"sendMessageSlack","fixture":"inline-opener","input":"```literal```\nParagraph outside code with ordinary words.","actual":["`literal`","Paragraph outside code with","ordinary words."],"methods":["/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage"]}
{"entry":"sendMessageSlack","fixture":"real-fence-control","input":"```text\ninside\n\ncode\n```","actual":["```\ninside\n\ncode\n```"],"methods":["/api/chat.postMessage"]}
{"entry":"sendMessageSlack","fixture":"prose-control","input":"First paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.","actual":["First paragraph.","Second paragraph."],"methods":["/api/chat.postMessage","/api/chat.postMessage"]}
~~~~

Fixture dynamically imports the shipped sender/client,creates the real client with slackApiUrl pointing only to its ephemeral loopback HTTP server,and asserts received POST text arrays against literal expected values. Server returns synthetic successful Slack acknowledgments. This proves real shipped-channel sender/HTTP behavior,not live Slack UI receipt or a full model/Gateway session. Ports and local paths omitted.

prs.title: improve: roomier automation hover rows without underlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The automation row in session hovercards gains an underline and has a cramped hover highlight.

## User Impact

Automation rows stay undecorated on hover and keyboard focus, with 4 px of vertical padding on each side. Existing navigation and inspection behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the row’s existing background highlight instead of underlining its label, and expand its normal hit area without changing layout on hover. The production change is one added and one removed CSS declaration; no new components or state.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the original production bundle: the regression received `underline` instead of `none`.
- Production-bundle browser suite: 7/7 passed, covering desktop (1440 px), mobile (390 px), keyboard focus, flyout inspection, and navigation.

prs.title: fix(exec): require approval for test/[ -v operands in allowlist mode
prs.body:
## Summary

The exec allowlist classifier trusted `test` and `[` as "safe builtins" without inspecting their operands, and bash >= 4.2 evaluates the array subscript of a `test -v` operand even inside single quotes — running command substitution. A single-quoted operand like `'a[$(cmd)]'` therefore executed `cmd` with no allowlist match and no approval prompt in `allowlist` + `on-miss` mode. This PR requires approval for any `test`/`[` segment carrying a `-v` operand (mirroring the existing `system.run` guard), and stops classifying case-variant heads (`TEST`, `Cd`) as builtins since POSIX builtin lookup is case-sensitive.

## What Problem This Solves

In gateway exec with `tools.exec.mode` `ask` or `auto` (both resolve to `security: "allowlist"`, `ask: "on-miss"`), the command `test -v 'a[$(touch /tmp/marker)]'` was classified as `safeBuiltins` by `isSafeBuiltinSegment` (`src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts`) with zero operand inspection, satisfied the allowlist, skipped the on-miss approval (`requiresExecApproval` in `src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.ts`), and was rendered unchanged in enforced mode (`buildAuthorizedShellCommandFromPlan` in `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts`, since builtin segments are deliberately never rewritten). The tool-facing model is an untrusted principal, so this silently executed attacker-chosen commands with the gateway user's privileges on hosts whose exec shell is bash 4.2+. A prompt-injected model could run any command despite the operator's allowlist, which is exactly what the approval boundary exists to prevent. After this change, those commands trigger the normal on-miss approval instead of executing silently.

## What was wrong

1. `isSafeBuiltinSegment` (`src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts`) matched only the command name: `test` was in the closed safe set and `[` was accepted whenever the segment ended with `]`, with no operand checks. Bash evaluates `test -v VAR` operands by expanding array subscripts — including `$(...)` and backtick substitution inside them — so an operand the classifier treated as an inert single-quoted literal executed instead.
2. The enforced-render argument gate (`hasUnquotedShellExpansionSource`, `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts`) intentionally skips single-quoted content, so the payload never tripped the "shell expansion in enforced arguments" refusal that already blocks the double-quoted and unquoted variants.
3. `isSafeBuiltinSegment` lowercased `argv[0]`, so `TEST`/`Cd` classified as safe builtins while POSIX shells resolve them as external binaries (latent mismatch; defense-in-depth fix included here). The `system.run` path already treated `test`/`[` with `-v` as needing a stable approval binding (`src/infra/system-run-mutable-file-operand.ts`); the gateway allowlist path now applies the equivalent rule.

## Why this design

- Gate every `test`/`[` segment containing a `-v` token (any argv position, negation forms, both heads) rather than trying to detect malicious subscripts: subscript-shaped heuristics invite regex-bypass games and false positives, while `-v`-gating mirrors the established `system.run` guard and only routes these rare commands to the operator.
- Fail-safe only: nothing becomes newly executable; affected commands fall back to the existing on-miss approval flow (operator can approve once, allow-always, or allowlist), and the approval path's enforced render rewrites the segment through the external `test` binary, which treats the operand as a literal.
- Match builtin heads case-sensitively: shell builtin lookup is case-sensitive, so the old lowercase match trusted tokens the shell never treats as builtins.
- No new config surface or default change: the repair tightens classification of a bypass form; the file's documented contract ("builtins cannot execute external code on their own") is restored rather than changed.
- Ordinary predicates (`test -f`, `-d`, `-n`, `[ -d ]`, `cd`, `:`, `true`, `false`, `pwd`) keep their existing auto-approval, verified by the pre-existing regression tests.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path | Mode | Before | After (this PR, head `1595e9a2a01`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway agent turn → `exec` `test -v 'a[$(touch M)]'`, no approver connected | released 2026.10.5 Gateway, `tools.exec.mode: ask`, host `allowlist`/`on-miss`/`askFallback: deny` | no approval requested; tool result `exit 1`; **marker created** (payload ran) | not run on the release-only row; see the next rows for the head |
| Same payload, approver denies | head Gateway, same policy | — | approval requested (`exec.approval.requested` shows the command); `deny` → `Exec denied (… user-denied)`; no marker |
| Same payload, approver `allow-once` | head Gateway | — | approved command runs through the rewritten external `/usr/bin/test`; operand stays literal (`'-v': unary operator expected`, exit 2); no marker |
| Same payload, no approval route (headless) | head Gateway, `askFallback: deny` and `askFallback: allowlist` | — | `exec denied: Headless runs cannot wait for interactive exec approval`; no marker in either fallback mode |
| Approval invalidated while waiting: host policy tightened to `security: deny`, then `allow-once` | head Gateway | — | `Exec approval changed before execution`; no marker |
| Approved control `touch M2` (`allow-once`) | head Gateway | — | runs; marker `M2` created |
| Ordinary predicate `test -f /etc/hostname`, no approver | released Gateway and head Gateway | auto-approved, runs | unchanged: auto-approved, runs, no approval request |
| Production chain `evaluateShellAllowlistWithAuthorization` → `requiresExecApproval` → `buildAuthorizedShellCommandFromPlan` → bash 5.2.21; payload in `test -v`, backtick, and `[ -v … ]` forms | in-process, allowlist + on-miss | `satisfiedBy=["safeBuiltins"]`, `ask=false`, rendered unchanged, marker created | `satisfiedBy=[null]`, `ask=true`, rendered via external `test`, no marker |

Gateway rows used isolated loopback Gateways, the released 2026.10.5 package versus a local build of this head, driven by `openclaw agent` turns against a loopback Responses stub that emits one `exec` call per turn. Approvals were resolved by a loopback `exec-approvals` operator client through `exec.approval.resolve`, and tool results were read back from the stub. Markers are inert `touch` files in a scratch directory. The 30-minute wall-clock approval timer was not waited out. The headless no-route rows use the same timed-out `askFallback` resolution (`resolveTimedOut`) that applies on expiry.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

`isSafeBuiltinSegment` and the SDK-exposed `evaluateShellAllowlistWithAuthorization` / `requiresExecApproval` keep their signatures. Callers can only observe stricter results: `test`/`[` `-v` segments now report unsatisfied and may raise approval requests that previously auto-passed. No caller fails closed in a new way; the covering tests below pin both sides.

## Testing

- New regression tests in `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts`: the three bypass forms are rejected from the safe set; position/negation variants rejected; case-variant heads rejected; the ordinary-predicate case stays covered by the existing allowlist integration tests (helper-level duplicate removed).
- Unchanged-green suites touching the path: `src/infra/exec-approvals.test.ts`, `exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts`, `exec-authorization-render.test.ts`, `exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts`, `exec-approvals-authorization.worker.test.ts`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec.security-floor.test.ts`, `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.shell-literals.test.ts`, `invoke-system-run-allowlist.test.ts` — 138 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed` (base `upstream/main`): typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, and format lanes green for this change.

prs.title: fix(apple): a two-second Gateway stall ends realtime Talk
prs.body:
Related: #180426 (#180571 covers the failure close) Related: #155839, #173388 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: on iOS and macOS, Gateway-relay realtime Talk ends with "Realtime audio input fell behind. Reconnecting…" once about two seconds of microphone appends are waiting (48 requests), and it also ends when any single append takes longer than 8 seconds. ## User Impact User impact: a Gateway or network stall now costs the microphone audio sent during the stall, plus a "repeat the last part" notice on iOS, instead of the call. Talk still ends when an append fails or stays unanswered for 30 seconds. macOS drops audio the same way but has no surface for relay status notices. ## Why This Change Was Made This applies the browser relay contract (#155839, #173490) to the shared Apple kit: - in-flight microphone audio is bounded by time (3 s), not by request count; - frames are admitted before their send task starts, so a stall no longer queues one task per callback; - frames over the budget are dropped, with one notice per loss episode and one recovery notice; - the relay ends only on an explicit append error or an append unanswered for 30 s. The Gateway answers appends in order (one handler; appends during an output cancellation wait on one drain), so a per-request deadline equal to the 30 s liveness window acts like the browser's renewable watchdog without a separate timer. Like the other relay statuses, the kit sends the two notices as status keys and iOS localizes them, mapping both to the listening phase; otherwise the generic status path would show an active call as idle and freeze the input meter. Tradeoff: a Gateway that stops answering while keeping the socket open is now detected after 30 s instead of about 2 s, as in browser Talk. A lost connection still ends the call immediately. If a notice arrives while the assistant is speaking, iOS shows listening until the next speaking change. ## Evidence - Kit: `microphone saturation terminates once without sending the frame past the cap` became `input past the audio budget is dropped without ending the call`, and `a one second gateway stall does not saturate microphone input` became `audio appends give a stalled Gateway thirty seconds to answer`, which pins the deadline each append hands the transport (the transport owns the timer). iOS: `realtime input loss notices keep the call listening`. `swift test --filter RealtimeTalkRelaySession` on macOS (Swift 6.4, Xcode 27): 62 tests in 7 suites passed. With only the new kit tests applied to the base, both fail: the over-budget frames are still admitted, and appends get the old 8 s deadline. iOS 27 simulator: `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, `TalkModeManagerTests`, `TalkRealtimeConsultCancellationTests`, and `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests` pass, and the app build includes the project's SwiftFormat lint and strict SwiftLint phases. - `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes. Locale strings follow through the native locale refresh workflow. - End to end against a 2026.10.5 Gateway that we froze with `docker pause` (the way #155839 was proven): - macOS, 5 s freeze: the same relay session continued (a later consult ran in it) and no close was sent; up to 3 s of audio arrived late, then latency returned to normal. - macOS, 35 s freeze: the client ended the relay at 30.3 s with "gateway request timed out after 30000ms" and reconnected after the Gateway resumed. - iOS simulator, 5 s freeze: the status line showed the notice below about 3.4 s into the stall and the call continued. The recovery notice was replaced by "Thinking…" within a second, so it is easy to miss; unlike browser Talk, iOS has no persistent notice surface. - Baseline: an iPhone on App Store build 2026.10.50 (without this change) dropped the call on the same 5 s freeze.
Trace of the macOS runs (Gateway log and macOS unified log, ids removed, all times UTC+8) ```text 17:55:17.114 gateway res ✓ talk.session.create # relay session for this run 17:58:11.405 gateway lane enqueue: lane=talk # consult before the freeze 17:59:03.548 docker pause (5 s) 17:59:08.875 docker unpause 18:00:57.219 gateway lane enqueue: lane=talk # consult in the same relay session 18:01:00.504 gateway lane task done: lane=talk durationMs=3285 # no talk.session.close or talk.session.create between 17:55:17 and 18:12:22 18:11:46.943 docker pause (35 s) 18:12:17.295 client talk realtime microphone failed: Realtime audio failed: gateway request timed out after 30000ms 18:12:17.530 client talk realtime terminated=audioInputFailed 18:12:22.270 docker unpause 18:12:22.534 gateway res ✗ talk.session.appendAudio UNAVAILABLE Unknown Talk session # x31, queued during the freeze 18:12:22.562 gateway res ✗ talk.session.close UNAVAILABLE Unknown Talk session 18:12:22.915 gateway res ✓ talk.session.create # client reconnects ``` The Gateway logs failed relay requests and lifecycle calls, not successful appends, so the 5 s run shows up as the absence of a close or a new session around a consult that still ran. The 35 s freeze also outlived the session on the Gateway side, so its queued appends were answered with `Unknown Talk session` once it resumed.
- The macOS app builds; `pnpm format:docs:check` and `git diff --check` pass. - The macOS end-to-end run used the debug binary with the microphone and speech usage strings embedded at link time (plain `swift build` output has no Info.plist) and a local one-word workaround for an unrelated crash when Speech Recognition permission is first requested; that crash will be reported separately. AI-assisted (Claude Code). The change and the evidence above were run and reviewed as described.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native catalog and completion continuity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reply or a returning child result can fail with “claimed by active work” while a Codex child is still running. Per-turn tool descriptions or conversation context can make OpenClaw try to replace a native thread that the child still needs.

## User Impact

An owner can continue using the tools already offered to that busy thread while its native work finishes. Genuinely new tools wait until the thread is idle. Every call still uses the current caller's permissions and executable tools; a saved tool list grants no authority. If a tool's prepared definition changes, including a narrower schema after a policy change, that tool stays unavailable until its new definition can publish while idle.

Connections using the parent-local inference relay receive current conversation context on each request. Other connections keep the existing protections against changing conversation policy during active work. The optional SDK declaration reader and idle-publication behavior still require maintainer acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the tool list accepted by Codex with the existing native binding, instead of rebuilding thread identity from each caller's current tool availability. Core producers supply stable declarations, and the existing idle lifecycle publishes additions. Related completion fixes let results return without prematurely retiring the shared client or holding a completed child's execution pin.

## Relationship to the other continuity fixes

[#175246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175246) has landed as `4caee42f65317c1e853db523b55be4046cfe0770` and is already an ancestor of this branch. Its terminal-child parent-pin release is upstream baseline, with completion custody and retry retained; this PR does not need a second implementation of that repair. Credit belongs to quqi1599 and the adapted contention work from Stronggenetics.

[#176177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176177) remains a useful narrower proposal for overlapping protected-catalog, current-executor and completion-lifecycle repairs. Its relevant changes are selectively integrated here with contributor credit. The additional catalog contract here supplies stable declarations from the core producers through an exact-host, data-only reader; validates persisted accepted-catalog receipts before reuse; and matches prepared current executors against accepted definitions, including in-place schema mutations. Those differences need their own regressions and native/upgrade evidence.

The current-inference conversation cutover is limited to actual relay-backed requests. This revision implements the review recommendation to defer the nonrelay cutover: those connections retain their existing native creation-policy and active-work behavior. If the narrower overlapping repairs land first, their implementations should become baseline and the remaining proposal should retain only the uncovered guarantees.

## Maintainer decision requested

Approve optional `hostCapabilities.readCoreToolDeclarations(tools)` and the existing binding’s accepted-catalog receipt, including deferring genuinely new declarations until native work is idle. The method is optional for existing harness consumers and is used for registration, not execution authority. Unknown remote catalogs remain preserved with an actionable refusal rather than guessed declarations. SDK/publication-policy acceptance is still required; no approving owner decision is claimed.

## Compatibility

No SQL schema migration or configuration option is added. Validated catalog receipt versions 1, 2 and 3 remain readable without rewriting existing receipts. Missing older receipts use the existing native read owner; corrupt/incompatible receipts preserve the thread. Native-owned supervision catalogs and current permission/authority guards remain authoritative. Existing receipt/fingerprint guards are retained at both admission and writer reuse.

**Nonrelay cutover deferred:** native compaction can discard injected developer history before a host callback runs. The current revision therefore keeps the exact producer-annotated section in creation policy whenever no actual relay is selected, including its existing policy-change/refusal behavior. The default builder also retains the full prompt when callers omit explicit developer instructions. This does not promise relay-like protected context changes for unsupported connections. Earlier native captures of the proposed nonrelay cutover remain historical evidence of the gap that motivated deferral.

## Behavior decision

The [review's SDK/publication question](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174900#issuecomment-6227772583) remains the requested owner decision. I recommend the data-only SDK reader and binding-owned accepted catalog. The [reader](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/68b340061d1cde7a06927e75014986b1d99285fc/src/agents/harness/host-tool-declarations.ts#L68) accepts only the exact surface built by that admitted host, checks its lifetime, and returns cloned declarations without executors. Core remains the declaration owner; the native binding remains the owner of what Codex accepted.

This preserves the native ownership established by [#134660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5f44faeca4e68b178712152e059436f98888e50). [Protected selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/68b340061d1cde7a06927e75014986b1d99285fc/extensions/codex/src/app-server/protected-thread-tool-catalog.ts#L19) retains that catalog while native work protects it. Current executors still enforce permissions and declaration compatibility; catalog receipts grant no execution authority. Changed declarations can publish when the existing idle owner permits it.

The nonrelay recommendation is now implemented rather than left as an accept/defer checkbox. The actual route owner retains the exact annotated section in creation policy when uncovered, recomputes from the original input on retries, and keeps transient executable-tool availability outside immutable identity. The pre-inference compaction regression is red on the preceding candidate and green after the repair; the default-policy consumer and incognito rejection/recovery controls also pass. No maintainer acceptance of a context-loss gap is requested.

## Evidence

### Hosted CI investigation (2026-10-23)

CI remains unclassified at unchanged head cb69b03e. The hosted failure rejects SQLite snapshot-token ownership during cleanup, then repeats the same staging-directory failure across 31 cases and native-worker teardown. The decoded manifest selects only server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts in the failed inner Vitest process; four preceding compact groups run as separately supervised processes. A replay of that same 107-case file/order using the repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de passes on macOS/arm64 (40.80s wrapper). It does not reproduce CI's Linux/x64, Node24, tested merge or shared compact host/cache state. Cleanup-owner source is unchanged, but inherited versus PR-caused attribution remains unresolved. Inspection found no demonstrated catalog-to-token-retirement mechanism; no speculative SQLite repair or weakened check is bundled. Hosted CI remains red, and the Codex/SDK API and idle-publication owner decision remains open.

[Failed hosted job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39847556511/job/120066036118). The actual tested merge is `8bbfe7170201a27396edee317e45c5cc1244c1ee` over `2f1a28f9eec60beb09c5a8bb6a3a366611df5bbd`. The exact-version local control uses Node 26.12.1 on macOS/arm64; hosted orchestration uses Node 24.22.1 on Ubuntu24/Linux x64. The original mismatched-Bun replay is superseded by the pinned-Bun replay for version comparison only. No CI rerun, source edit, or speculative cleanup repair was made.


### Current upstream integration

Head `cb69b03e9c4699e2c0fde5ccec936314b8a0b3c5` integrates the prior public head `2aa12dba752cb824141e3c1c1677cf3afdbd2bad` with pinned main `3e0475a199e5877f1b5e0c086437ef1fedd3b693`, preserving both histories. The repair keeps upstream's canonical tool finalizers, conversation-tool factory, Gateway policy, descendant allowlists, and nested-completion settlement. Native completion still joins its existing assignment-publication owner before delivery. Upstream's retired heartbeat fallback and its dead tests remain deleted; current executors are checked against the saved accepted declarations without that fallback route.

Validation covers **336 distinct focused tests**: 97 core checks and 239 extension checks across 13 extension files. After the final two fixture edits, both coupled run-attempt files were rerun and all 136 tests passed. Coverage includes declaration/execution boundaries, stable prompt prefixes, current Gateway policy, protected catalogs, native inventory and nested completion, skill delivery, and startup refusal.

Canonical core and all-extension production types, core agents-tools and full extension test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 reviews are complete and scoped-clean for the full 19-path integration resolution and the subsequent four-file and two-file test-only deltas. The integration removes retired fallback machinery and obsolete duplicate fixture code, preserving upstream's existing owners; the complete manual resolution covers 23 paths, including the two retired deletions.

The incoming Gateway-policy regression now checks the existing strict-definition contract: a saved read/write declaration remains unchanged when current policy narrows the executable schema; both calls are unavailable through the old catalog, with no execution. A freshly accepted narrowed declaration permits read and still denies write. This bridge test models the successor's accepted catalog; it does not itself prove native idle publication. Other fixture repairs follow the current timing-tracker interface and shared test owner, removing retired arguments rather than restoring retired production paths.

The canonical runtime build passes on the resolved production source. It was built before the final merge commit, so its pre-commit Git metadata is not an exact-new-commit binary receipt. It reports an advisory UI startup gzip overrun of five bytes; no separate main build was used to attribute that warning, and no threshold was changed.

The source-declared Codex **0.162.1** contract was checked at [`092d3acd6bec`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L145): dynamic tools are offered at thread start; turn start/resume do not replace that catalog. This integration adds no native API or queue policy.

Earlier actual-native, private-parent denial, idle-publication, and stable-upgrade captures remain qualified by their recorded source and transport. This integration is not a new native execution, external-provider, upgrade, or deployment capture, and does not establish whole-binary equivalence. Genuine active protected receiptless upgrade and the separate #176311 HTTP-startup repair remain outside the demonstrated scope. SDK/publication-owner acceptance and new-head hosted CI remain separate gates.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation, native captures, and upgrade evidence, each with its original revision and limitations</summary>

Previous candidate source: `2aa12dba752cb824141e3c1c1677cf3afdbd2bad`. [Revision-qualified native traces, regression evidence and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174900#issuecomment-6285896499). Historical captures below retain their explicit source revisions.

### Previous upstream conflict repair at `2aa12dba752`

Integrated pinned upstream `e99ca016a45fcd503de91eea9e992374fa3a1039` with both parent histories preserved. The sole manual conflict was the upstream helper refactor in `dynamic-tool-availability.test.ts`; the resolution retains every authored active/fallback/split reader, in-place schema, and final-preparation case. Accepted-declaration mismatch still asserts unavailable execution and an unchanged native catalog; it does not use the broader invalid-argument helper in place of that guard.

Validation on the resolved source: **51 tests across four owning files pass**, including dynamic availability, heartbeat fallback, final tool preparation and prompt-prefix stability. Canonical core and extension production TypeScript checks, scoped typed lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 conflict-resolution review is clean. The earlier local package-boundary type attempt used stale generated SDK declarations/an unsuitable producer configuration; it is not counted as a passing check or a product defect. Canonical declaration preparation and the supported production checks subsequently passed. Broad extension-test types remain for hosted CI.

This merge brings in upstream production changes, including the inline tool-schema finalizer and other tool-assembly changes. Earlier native and upgrade captures remain evidence only for their recorded revisions and named unchanged-source scopes; no blanket whole-head byte equality, new native execution, deployment or owner approval is claimed. The optional SDK declaration reader and idle-publication policy still require the stated maintainer decision. New-head hosted CI and mergeability remain gates.

### Documentation correction after review

Candidate `0efba79a122c1d3ec217d1d3d42343e6cf3c991e` corrects the remaining P3 documentation finding: only a selected parent-local inference relay carries annotated context outside native creation policy. Nonrelay connections retain that context and their existing policy-change protections; developer handoffs supplement it. The reference now agrees with the implemented deferral and core-ownership guide. Scoped Markdown lint, formatting, whitespace and independent source agreement review pass. This commit changes one documentation file only; production source is identical to `697b3b5b460c986a8c02b1d57e5cc4516c5035f1`. Its runtime build and earlier native evidence retain their recorded revisions; no new build or runtime execution is claimed. SDK/publication-policy acceptance remains a maintainer decision.

### Recorded recovery-safety integration at `697b3b5`

Candidate `697b3b5b460c986a8c02b1d57e5cc4516c5035f1` additionally integrates upstream `5c5bd2eaf0b3aa753a9adda0d634d091f0e9150c`. prs.title: experiment(control-ui): isolate literal dashboard mount scheduling [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a literal dashboard deep link admits cached pane construction before the initial WebSocket connect. The campaign's original reload evidence recorded 14 visible states across roughly 15 seconds; this experiment targets the remaining client-side mount work in the handshake window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the shipped short-name snapshot/first-frame behavior exactly as main. Only literal full-UUID dashboards wait for the existing first-connect milestone and split cached rows through the existing hydration owner. No second cache or admission rule.

## User Impact

**Experiment rejected; do not merge.** The short-name first-frame regression is fixed, and dashboard connect, hello, painted transcript, final rows, and blocking improve. Chart pixels regress beyond the pre-declared stop rule, so this PR is closed rather than promoted.

## Evidence

# L181 round 2 — stop: chart pixels regress

Candidate `85f38ad2ec2362c9f03c1fef55faf6790d9303d0`; baseline `1720d2a430f08687fa807960844a94a263ddfb32`. AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_1dcc41fce747` (eu-west-1), 16 vCPUs. Same lease, bundles, Chromium, and live-like latency throughout. 15 interleaved pairs for each route and 15 clean filmstrip-only chart pairs. No CPU profiler in gate runs. All values below are milliseconds unless named counts/bytes.

The short-name path is restored exactly to main. Literal full-UUID dashboard routes alone wait for `initialConnectSent`, then use a presentation-only input to split cached rows in the existing hydration owner. No cache, admission rule, Gateway contract, or stored shape was added. Runtime delta: **+18** (21 insertions, 3 deletions), six production files; test delta +28. The growth preserves the shipped short-name first-frame contract without coupling presentation to the send/outbox authority flag.

## Gate results

**STOP.** Chart pixels: 1657.0 [1633.7–1729.4] → 1772.6 [1731.3–1838.9]; paired median +83.5; 11/15 later. Both the separated-IQR regression rule and the explicit >+30 ms / ≥10-of-15 stop rule fail. The primary handshake and painted-row gates improve.

## Clean chart-pixel pairs and attribution milestones

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
