**Equal-count analysis:** zero of 15 chart pairs have matching MCP counts; none of the observed candidate counts occur in the baseline chart series. The timing series also has no equal-count pairs. A causal estimate holding setup count fixed is unavailable; do not describe the chart regression as pure row-commit cost.

Initial cached DOM rows are intentionally later (400.9 → 533.0), while their first paint improves (804 → 764). The connect-to-hello interval grows 259.5 → 282.1 (paired +22.6); absolute hello remains 97.3 ms earlier per pair. No standard chat metric regresses under the declared rule.

## Validation and limitations

- Local focused tests: route-warm-boot 8, route-snapshot 16, snapshot-hydration 7, board-loading 6 = 37 passed. The literal-route regression failed on pre-fix code in round 1 and still passes after the round-2 rebase. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/route-warm-boot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: runner wall 1.30 s.
- Native bundled UI e2e: 17/17 passed in three files, 107.22 s. Includes both cached-dashboard first-frame cases (3.91 s and 4.11 s) plus snapshot routing and reconnect. The prior short-name failure is fixed with the original assertion intact.
- Production build and both UI builds passed on the lease. Autoreview clean through P2 before commit. No source changes after review except clean rebase.
- Full UI suite, changed-file gate, ready promotion, and broad exact-head CI are intentionally not pursued after the performance stop. Exact-head CI run 39890556568 is skipped (draft); Workflow Sanity passed. There are no attributed CI reds to classify.
- The initial chart series was declared diagnostic-only before reading its results because completed-timing artifact compression overlapped it. The gate uses a complete replacement 15-pair series with no concurrent compression, builds, or tests; both series are retained.

## Files

`ui/src/pages/chat/{route-loader.ts,session-route-data.ts,chat-page-pane-render.tsx,chat-pane-inputs.ts,chat-pane-state-owner.ts,chat-pane-snapshot-hydration.ts,route-warm-boot.test.ts}`. Short-cache helper has no diff against main.

## Profile attribution

Unprofiled milestones place baseline cached rows at 400.9 ms, before connect at 482.2; candidate rows move to 533.0, after connect at 357.5. Chat rows remain around 913 ms, after connect around 360. The real-loader regression proves literal route presentation cannot be returned while initial connect is held. This identifies the literal route's early pane mount as the work admitted into the connect window.

Three source-mapped profiles per revision confirm the task split:

| Profile run | Baseline combined mount + rows, ms | Candidate mount, ms | Candidate row commit, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 308.0 | 150.6 | 179.3 |
| 2 | 233.4 | 111.4 | 124.6 |
| 3 | 227.7 | 119.5 | 124.6 |

The dominant source frames are `chat-pane-runtime-view.tsx` (`MountedPane`), `chat-pane-layout-view.tsx` (`PaneLayout`), and `components/chat-transcript-layout-solid.tsx` (virtual row construction). The split row tasks end at 930.0/892.0/905.5 ms; the first MCP requests occur at 1876.4/1801.6/1891.0 ms in those same profiles. Thus these profiles do **not** show the initial row task landing directly on MCP setup or iframe insertion. They also move the baseline mount after connect and reduce MCP calls to 1/1/1 (baseline) and 6/3/1 (candidate), so do not use them to estimate unprofiled chart cost.

The clean unprofiled chart series localizes the regression more precisely:

| Milestone | Baseline median | Candidate median | Paired median Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Widget grant request (`board.widget.appView`) | 745.2 | 691.5 | −47.7 |
| Widget grant response | 919.4 | 904.0 | −12.0 |
| First `mcp.app.view` request | 920.4 | 1052.6 | +130.4 |
| Last `mcp.app.view` response | 1227.3 | 1425.9 | +175.2 |
| First iframe insertion | 1231.6 | 1430.3 | +175.0 |
| First visible chart pixels | 1657.0 | 1772.6 | +83.5 |

Grant-response → first-MCP-request grows 0.9 → 143.3 ms (paired +142.4). Last-MCP-response → first-iframe insertion stays 4.3 → 4.4 ms (paired +0.2). First-iframe → visible-pixels decreases 422.0 → 351.0 ms (paired −76.4), but does not offset the earlier delay. There are two replacement-frame outliers: chart pair 3 candidate and pair 15 baseline. The table always uses actual first visible pixels, not the surviving child document's FCP; first insertion and last reply are not the same generation in those two runs.

The grant starts earlier, but setup begins later and restarts more often (MCP medians 14 → 24). This is an observed scheduling/churn interaction, not evidence that the row task directly blocks iframe insertion. With zero equal-count pairs and changed races under profiling, the portion caused by L180's setup churn cannot be separated here. The pre-declared pixel failure still requires stopping. A future retry can measure this same narrow patch on a baseline with independently proven stable MCP setup; that is a lead decision, not additional work in this lane.

## Disposition

Performance gate failed; do not merge. Draft PR #181192 is closed with this report. The candidate remains on the lane branch for inspection. Lease is released; final AWS inspect confirms `hasHost: false`, `ready: false`. No local Gateway was started.

prs.title: fix(daemon): empty quoted argument dropped from service command lines
prs.body:
Closes #176472

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an empty `""` argument is dropped when a Scheduled Task script or systemd `ExecStart` is read back, so later arguments shift.

## User Impact

Inspected service commands match what was installed. No other change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared splitter now treats a quote pair as a word even when empty.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI on Linux, Node 24, built `dist`, before then after. A user unit with `ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --label "" --port 18789` (isolated `HOME`, `--profile proof176`), then `openclaw --profile proof176 gateway status --json --no-probe`, `service.command.programArguments`:

- before: `["/usr/bin/node","/opt/openclaw/dist/index.js","gateway","--label","--port","18789"]`
- after: `["/usr/bin/node","/opt/openclaw/dist/index.js","gateway","--label","","--port","18789"]`

The Windows launcher has no CLI path on Linux, so its reader was called directly: `readScheduledTaskCommand` on a `gateway.cmd` written by the installer's `buildTaskScript` and `encodeWindowsLauncherScript`.

- before: `["C:\\openclaw\\node.exe","gateway","--label","--port","18789"]`
- after: `["C:\\openclaw\\node.exe","gateway","--label","","--port","18789"]`

New tests fail before and pass after. `src/daemon` and `src/infra/ports` suites, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt pass.

Not covered: a registered Windows Scheduled Task (the launcher file is read, not the task). Accepted: `Environment=""` in a drop-in is now rejected like `Environment=foo`.

prs.title: fix(daemon): preserve empty arguments in service inspection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes service inspection dropping empty quoted arguments from Windows batch launchers and systemd ExecStart commands. For example, `--label "" --port 18789` was read back as `--label --port 18789`, shifting later arguments and misrepresenting the installed command.

Related: #176472. Supersedes #181187, thanks @aniruddhaadak80. Related existing proposal: #176494.

## User Impact

Service status, inspection, and repair retain explicitly empty arguments and the positions of subsequent arguments. No new options, dependencies, or state migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared daemon argument splitter used an empty string for both “no argument started” and “an explicitly empty argument.” A nullable accumulator represents those states separately, without another tracking flag. The existing systemd and Windows writers already quote empty values; their readers now preserve them.

Production: +8/-8 (net 0). Tests: +13/-2 (net +11). Documentation: +2/-0. The single-use quote-opening predicate was inlined; no additional owner, fallback, or compatibility path was introduced.

## Evidence

- On base `cbd99fa1e3663a57bd292302ff9536d354b7c12f`, seven regression cases fail because empty arguments disappear. The actual systemd service-file reader also loses empty arguments in both its returned command and managed-definition snapshot.
- Node 26.12.1 and the pinned Bun fork: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/systemd-unit.test.ts src/daemon/cmd-argv.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `bun`: 27/27 pass on each. Final wall times: 1.54s / 1.42s; Vitest durations: 308ms / 132ms.
- Consumer tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports-format.test.ts src/daemon/systemd.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks-runtime-definition.test.ts src/daemon/service-command-read.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 233/233 pass. Total wall time 38.60s, including 18.85s shared worker compilation; actual test time remains below two seconds per shard.
- Live file-boundary proof: `HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/state" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/service-argv-proof.ts`. The probe generates a systemd unit with `buildSystemdUnit`, writes it, and reads it with `readSystemdServiceExecStart`; it generates/encodes a Windows launcher and reads it with `readScheduledTaskCommand`. Output: `PASS: real systemd service-file read preserves empty argv in command and managed definition` and `PASS: real Windows batch-file writer/reader preserves empty argv`. No native service was installed or started; native Linux/systemd and Windows Task Scheduler startup were not exercised on this Mac.
- Scoped services typecheck, typed oxlint, oxfmt, MDX validation, documentation links (15,835 checked; zero broken), `git diff --check`, and madge (zero cycles) pass.
- Full `check:changed` / SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies the broad proof. No Testbox lease used.
- Independent Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automation validation-summary links leave invalid Advanced fields hidden when that section is collapsed.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can activate an error-summary link and reach the visible field to correct it. No configuration, migration, or scheduling behavior changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron's existing field-navigation helper now opens the enclosing Advanced disclosure before scrolling and focusing the field. This keeps the repair page-local, with no new state or shared focus/modal changes.

## Evidence

- [CI run 39890056134](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890056134) completed successfully on head `993b7430b1e2a718e7ff1da8d4653fccb01988b6`; the CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review gates are green.
- The owning regression fails against base 87aada17522b9146cf5e26df3352b81d8cc0669b: Advanced remains closed, the field is hidden, and focus stays on the summary button. The same bundled Chromium scenario passes with the fix: the disclosure opens and the invalid field is visible and focused.
- Seven bundled Chromium scenarios pass, including six existing desktop/narrow create/edit keyboard and select scenarios. The new regression took 1.34 seconds locally and 2.855 seconds in [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890056134/job/120207830730); the combined local invocation, including production build, took 48.57 seconds.
- Bundled WebKit 27.2 proof also passes field reveal/focus, correction, and ordinary Name-summary navigation. No scheduling writes were made.
- 48 focused Cron owner/view tests pass. UI production and E2E typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, controller guards, English/keyless i18n baseline and verification, and diff checks pass.
- Author simplification retains one existing navigation owner: +5 production lines and one 63-line browser regression. Independent Auto Review accepted the patch with no P0 findings.
- Inspected, synthetic Before/After screenshots below show the same keyboard action. Proof covers browser semantics, not screen-reader speech or physical-device Safari.

### Before

prs.title: fix(agents): restore full plugin tool inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Enabled tool-only plugins disappear from the session's effective-tools preview when a dynamic selected-model lease narrows the plugin registry. Valid `coding` plus `alsoAllow` grants can consequently look misconfigured even though the tool remains executable. Fixes #167365.

## Changes

Assemble tools inside the matching complete Gateway registry and metadata snapshot, then restore the selected provider's narrow generation for normalization. Existing registry ownership, workspace/config fingerprint checks, and retained-work custody prevent borrowing stale or mismatched registrations during asynchronous assembly. Policy filtering is unchanged.

Thanks to @TUARAN for the fix and @Chisalita for the report; contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

Built main `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2` and candidate `0a40c45a375` with `pnpm build` in isolated Linux Docker on Node 24.22.1. Created state using shipped plugin-install/config commands and authenticated Gateway RPCs; no temporary RPC or private state injection.

Current head `de74862a260def5fc492cd474af8aab1fbbc2af3` integrates main's unrelated hooks-fixture typecheck repair. Neither changed inventory file changed during that merge, so the built-artifact proof remains applicable.

- Main: two `tools.effective` calls for a dynamic-provider session omit `workboard_list`.
- Discriminating control: selecting a configured static model includes that same tool with plugin provenance. The real `tools.invoke` command also executes it successfully with the dynamic model selected.
- Candidate: two identical dynamic-provider inventory calls include `workboard_list`, `source: plugin`, `pluginId: inventory-workboard`; real invocation succeeds. Disabling the plugin with `config.patch` removes it from inventory.
- The real-loader regression fails on main at the missing-tool assertion and passes on the candidate. It also protects selected-provider isolation, config mismatch, and close-time custody. Changed-file formatting and lint passed.
- Built-artifact real-provider smoke through the shipped `agent --local` CLI returned `INVENTORY_LIVE_OK` from OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` (7.8s); the task-scoped key was deleted immediately afterward.

Simplification pass retained the single scoped assembly path: there is no second loader, cache, public API, or SDK surface. The added scope composes existing metadata, registry and custody owners; deleting its guards would lose mismatch/lifecycle protection. Whole diff: production +70/-23 (net +47), tests +265/-0. The remaining growth protects those distinct boundaries rather than widening the selected model generation.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting fully removes the behavior change; no stored-state or config migration. Blast radius is Gateway effective-tool previews for dynamic-model sessions using plugin tools. Agent execution and policy grants are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: recover missing local credentials for PostgreSQL state
prs.body:
Closes #180344

Supersedes #180345 (thanks @ceckert).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing recovery path when a replacement Gateway host retains PostgreSQL state but loses `client/credentials.sqlite` and has no matching credential backup.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly create a fresh local credential store with:

```sh
openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive --rebind-missing-credentials
```

**Security trade:** clients on this host get new identities and must re-pair. Paired remote devices that retain their credentials stay paired; their pairing records remain in PostgreSQL. Ordinary startup never rebinds. SQLite and existing unsafe, incomplete, mismatched, or corrupt store refusals remain unchanged. A healthy present store is preserved.

**DRAFT — awaiting approval of this public CLI flag and recovery policy. Do not mark ready or merge.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing credential recovery owner admits this operation only for a missing local store on PostgreSQL. It writes the complete first-bootstrap receipt with the existing PG store identity and current anchor, and seals all six legacy import claims so retained JSON cannot revive retired identities or tokens. The existing post-port receipt repair (#178005) and once-per-process credential admission (#177962) keep their ownership. No receipt format, schema, or identity protocol changes are needed.

This is a trusted-main rewrite informed by the contributor's diff. Release-note context: explicit Doctor recovery after loss of host-local credentials, with local re-pairing and retired-import protection.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `6e17838c5cfd`:** real compiled Doctor CLI + PostgreSQL 17.11, with `client/` removed. Ordinary Doctor emitted the exact missing-backup refusal; the proposed flag exited 1 as an unknown option.
- **Green locally:** all five real PG CLI cases passed, plus 74 focused CLI/startup/lifecycle/budget tests. The CLI cases cover explicit recovery, exact refusal preservation, SQLite, complete receipts, sealed identity/token imports, later anchor replacement, and retained remote pairing records. The five-case run took 317.32 seconds in Vitest, 434.01 seconds including runner setup/cleanup.
- **Final head `5d7b9f9e545e71af73a0e095e7d1a109496d9186`:** all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed: [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890618009/job/120209679099), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890618009/job/120209678874), [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890618009/job/120209678845). Completed logs show **1,121 passed tests**, with 37 Workboard skips reported by the existing suite. All five new real-CLI cases executed and passed in shard 1. The only change after the local green run adds required braces to the test; production code is identical.
- `pr-simplify`, formatting, `git diff --check`, scoped type-aware lint, and isolated Codex review through P3 are clean. Final-head CI passed production and all test types, all five core lint shards, source contracts, and runtime topology/architecture.
- The dependency/dead-code check reports the same 16 findings as [clean-main scheduled CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39885503944), with zero added or removed findings. The earlier test brace lint failure is fixed. Additional broad CI jobs are still running; this is not an all-green CI claim.

Local PG catalog, schema, migration, and trigger parity checks passed. Full conformance is assigned to CI: the campaign's dependency layout blocked local declaration checking and full asset-build setup. The retained Testbox expired before its payload and was stopped; no remote-test result is claimed. An initial manual CI dispatch rejected an incompatible validation-tier input before analysis; the corrected dispatch passed preflight. Its superseded run was canceled after the brace repair.

Diff: 8 files, +422/-17 lines; production and conformance registration +78/-8, tests +328/-9, documentation +16.

prs.title: feat(update): show recovery disk use and retire selected untracked copies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recovery copies can consume substantial disk space without appearing in status, and old unregistered migration originals or orphan update captures have no supported retirement command. A space-rejected original-state capture also needs an unmistakable warning when the update continues.

**Stacked on #181033** (`fix/auto-update-recovery-cleanup`, `1a65852c3ab6ae4252c321ad6fcbc2390f6307b4`). This PR targets `main` for review/CI, but must not merge ahead of that dependency. The PR-3-only delta starts at that SHA; rebase onto `main` after #181033 lands. PR #181025 and Doctor capture reuse remain separately owned.

Related: #174253 #162622 #179789.

## User Impact

- `openclaw status` / `--json`, normal read-only Doctor, and `doctor --lint` report local logical bytes and counts by recovery-copy kind and eligibility.
- `openclaw update cleanup --include-unmanifested <path>` explicitly selects one known unregistered migration original or orphan update capture. Repeat it for additional exact paths. Preview shows bytes, modification age, and irreversible consequences; applying still requires offline ownership and separate consent.
- Insufficient measured capture space produces a prominent **NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT** warning with needed/available bytes in stderr, final text/JSON, and durable run steps. The update can still succeed.

**No total-size cap and no byte-budget-driven deletion.** Unmanifested/orphan originals are never automatically selected. Retirement permanently loses those selected originals; maintain an independent backup when that recovery history is still needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing recovery inventory and retirement custody rather than introduce another retention owner. Status bounds directory entries, metadata reads, and elapsed scan time; limits only return an incomplete observed-byte estimate. A large shared history database is not copied just to render status, and unknown eligibility stays protected. Logical bytes are not physical allocation or a promise of reclaimed space.

Explicit retirement refuses pending/retained recovery references (including aliases), configured live databases and sidecars, symlinks/hardlinks/nonregular files, changed identities, and paths outside the existing recovery inventory. Current config, references, and custody are checked again before removal; files are unlinked individually instead of recursively removing an uninspected tree. Existing automatic eligibility rules are unchanged.

Space measurements survive the existing worker diagnostic transport; they do not create an update failure gate or remove old copies to make room. Installed-updater behavior requires an updater containing this change; staging a candidate cannot retrofit an older running driver's initial capture warning.

Simplification: shared inventory/projection serves both status forms and Doctor; no new cache, database schema, persistent inventory, or retention policy. The necessary growth is the exact-path safety/identity checks, bounded diagnostic scan, and behavioral refusal/transport coverage across the three requested outcomes.

## Evidence

Candidate: `d1de1771abbe7842a0e0d8906c7d6cc910b67191`.

- **200 tests passed in 17 focused/affected files** on `118e343ec161f201f728a6eaeaaa01fab2f74f7e`, four Vitest shards, **148.06 s wrapper wall time**. The final two-file assertion-safety repair was then covered by **34 affected tests in 2 files, all passed in 33.07 s**, with unchanged evidence reused for the other paths. Coverage includes status text/JSON and Doctor lint bytes/counts, entry/metadata/time incomplete scans, explicit CLI selection/consent, pending recovery and alias references, running Gateway custody, live database/sidecar/link/outside-path refusals, confirmation/effect-time mutations, automatic cleanup, and successful updates after both payload and subprocess database-space rejection.
- The status JSON regression fails without the output projection (`recoveryCopies` is absent), then passes with it. Both capacity-warning regressions failed before their fix; an aliased pending-recovery refusal regression also failed before correction.
- Production `tsgo:core` and affected CLI-update, commands, and Doctor test typecheck leaves passed.
- Scoped type-aware lint: **0 warnings / 0 errors**. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Docs audit: **15,836 links, 0 broken**.
- Full touched-test audit completed: real temporary filesystem/state fixtures; mocks constrain external disk measurement/service I/O, not retirement or warning decisions. No source-text mirrors.
- Every test invocation used an explicitly verified task-private handoff store. No live Gateway stop, restart, update, or live-state mutation.
- Local harness issues resolved: use the installed supported Node; clear an inherited profile that changed an existing CLI-text expectation; serialize source writes and compiled-worker checks. Declaration validation rejects external global-graph compiler paths, so this worktree alone used a local virtual graph while reusing the shared pnpm package store.

Independent API-only review found and prompted two fixes:

1. **P1 resolved:** explicit retirement now requires successfully resolved source configuration/includes initially and at subsequent authority checks. Real missing-include regressions at selection and effect time fail before the fix and pass afterward, preserving the selected original.
2. **P2 resolved:** incomplete migration dependency discovery now protects previously observed candidates rather than calling them retirable. A completed manifest plus an oversized unfinished manifest sharing one original reproduces the incorrect count before the fix and passes after it.

A fresh, independent, full pinned-file API-only review of `118e343ec161f201f728a6eaeaaa01fab2f74f7e` found **no remaining actionable P0–P2 issues**. It read the production delta and all six touched test files in full (1,689 lines), confirmed both repairs, and did not execute code or rely on a local checkout. Author-run checks above remain separate execution evidence.

CI caught two unchecked production type assertions; the final commit replaces them with array-element validation and the existing errno predicate. The assertion-safety ratchet, production typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, and affected tests pass locally. Fresh API-only review of final commit `d1de1771abbe7842a0e0d8906c7d6cc910b67191` also found no P0–P2 issues, after reading both complete changed files and the pinned errno dependency implementation. Exact-head CI has completed; the remaining blocker and per-check results are below.

## Remaining blockers and final CI

**Not ready to merge; no merge attempted.** #181033 remains open at `1a65852c3ab6ae4252c321ad6fcbc2390f6307b4`. Its owner must land it before this PR can be rebased onto `main` and requalified. ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no correctness findings and retains that same dependency/rebase action. The new scenarios have in-process/worker integration proof, not an installed-CLI upgrade run of this head.

Required `openclaw/ci-gate` completed **failure** on the exact candidate. Its only underlying failed check is [`check-test-types-core-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39890249600/job/120209204909): unrelated upstream `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57` passes the removed `managedHooksDir` loader option (`TS2353`). The failed CI checkout merges this head into upstream `27ae5f7ecb89b13ffb6384b624ecbe41623c66a1`; both the offending test (`fb9cc064c8795ebc259afb9e66ac90d8edf809fd`) and loader (`f020a23e71d89eaaab6501c55a33fc9c783636c0`) blobs are identical between that upstream commit and merge `42c372bc000f40544d652211f4e5fe2f5db42e64`. They are outside this stacked delta. The upstream hooks/test owner must reconcile that test with the loader API; this PR does not waive the failure or expand into unrelated hook work.

All other selected CI lanes completed successfully, including the repaired assertion/baseline ratchet, production lint/types, changed Node tests, UI E2E, docs, Android/native-access, and PostgreSQL conformance. The aggregate gate fails because of the upstream test type error. Skipped and neutral checks are listed as such, not counted as passes.

prs.title: refactor: keep private runtime handoffs with their consumers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private one-consumer modules and argument/result handoffs obscure the operation owners without providing a reusable boundary.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change or migration. Public SDK, configuration, CLI, protocol and persisted contracts, lazy imports and the standalone session-memory backend remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep timeout classification with the system-agent planner; config recovery and GitHub authentication-path hints with Doctor; Discord reactions and progress options with their dispatchers; Teams welcome payloads with the member event; and WhatsApp conversation prompt selection with inbound preparation. Remove the unused private DTOs, forwarding frames and exports, not their behavior.

Private-helper tests now exercise the existing public planner, Doctor and channel handlers. Existing authorization, recovery, queued cleanup, prompt precedence and transport behavior remain protected. A retired QA source reference and native-Bun qualification entry are removed with their files; Doctor's obsolete one-cast allowance also shrinks to zero.

Net production reduction: **209 lines** (+393/-602), excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files and declarations. Moved bodies receive no deletion credit. This coherent internal-surface batch uses the coordinator's 150-line floor waiver.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No runtime guard is removed. The private unsupported-reaction fallthrough no longer adds an empty asynchronous handoff; actual reaction authorization and effects retain their original order. Doctor's non-mismatch statuses were never consumed and now directly produce the same intentional absence of a hint.

The redirected-HOME diagnosis from #78063, WhatsApp empty-specific-prompt suppression from #70381, Teams PascalCase card enums from #96290 and late queued Discord cleanup from #156186 are retained. No security, durability, concurrency or update behavior is relaxed. An open agent-filter policy proposal is deliberately not incorporated.

## Evidence

Focused public proof passed: 13 configured planner cases, 11 recovery cases, 18 Doctor skills/hint cases, 123 Discord action/reaction cases, 57 Discord progress/ack cases, 16 Teams event/presentation cases and 61 WhatsApp inbound/audio/context cases. Planner, Doctor hint and channel test migrations passed against unchanged production before their helper folds. The redundant older group-prompt smoke is covered by the migrated specific-prompt row. No skips, retries or longer timeouts were added.

Targeted native imported-graph typechecks, formatting and source caps passed. Seven typed-lint SDK-resolution diagnostics reproduce serially on actual preimages: two Discord error-type constituents, three Teams error-union/consistent-return diagnostics and two WhatsApp error-type constituents. Candidate files were restored and byte-compared; no casts or suppressions were added and those local failures are not labeled green. Exact-head hosted CI supplies broad lint/type/build proof.

Fresh cumulative independent review and final structural checks are recorded before publication. Local proof is isolated and serial with one worker; no local whole-graph typecheck, broad suite, build or live external integration proof is claimed. CI timings are pending.

prs.title: fix(telegram): resolve mixed-case account config keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram normalizes runtime account IDs before routing them. When an account was configured with a mixed-case key such as `Work`, several group and mention-policy readers later indexed `channels.telegram.accounts` with the normalized key `work`. The lookup missed the configured account and silently fell back to root Telegram settings, so account-specific `groups` and `mentionPatterns` were ignored.

## Changes

- Resolve account groups through `resolveTelegramAccountConfig` for group mention policy, account inspection, and status membership audits.
- Resolve per-account `mentionPatterns` through the same normalized lookup for text and media inbound paths.
- Add regressions for mixed-case group keys and unmentioned-group status.

Closes #180066

## Evidence

- Targeted regression command: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/group-policy.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/account-inspect.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Result: 2 test files passed; 9 tests passed and 1 platform-specific test skipped.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `oxfmt` passed on all changed files.
- The two new tests distinguish account-specific configuration from the root fallback: `Work` uses `work` at runtime, and the expected group/topic settings are selected from the mixed-case account entry.
- The PR changes no dependencies, credentials, network behavior, or external schemas.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the change and its affected call sites.

prs.title: fix(compaction): name whole missing identifiers in corrective feedback and count the rest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction's corrective request lists only the first three missing opaque identifiers. If one is long, the 4,000-character untrusted-data wrapper can cut that identifier in half. The provider then receives neither the exact value nor a count explaining that other missing identifiers were omitted.

Thanks to @amittell for the report and original fix.

## User Impact

Corrective feedback now names only complete identifiers that fit and explicitly counts the remainder. An oversized identifier does not hide shorter values that follow it. This improves the truthfulness of the retry request; it does not promise that every identifier can fit into a bounded summary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Budget the existing missing-identifier audit reason before wrapping it. Reserve space for the other bounded audit reasons and the corrective sentence. Keep the existing untrusted-data wrapper and its limit unchanged. No new configuration, plugin SDK, storage, or public API surface.

## Evidence

Built baseline main `a542a596af43400d5dfad10d572d7615cfecfe95` and this candidate in isolated Docker. A real built Gateway received ordinary configuration, session creation, chat turns, and `/compact`. Conversation state was created only through those shipped commands/RPCs. The owned inference endpoint returned legal streamed summaries with missing headings/identifiers, exercising the actual safeguard audit and corrective provider request.

- Main twice: the actual outbound corrective block contains a partial first URL, no complete identifier, and no omitted count.
- Candidate twice: the outbound block contains the four shorter URLs in full, skips the oversized first URL, and includes `missing_identifiers_omitted:1`.
- Valid-summary control: one summarization request and no corrective retry on both arms. The ordinary wrapper's 4,000-character cap remains covered separately.
- Focused audit regressions: baseline 4 failed / 2 passed; candidate all 6 passed. Changed TypeScript passed Oxfmt and Oxlint.
- Real-provider built agent smoke returned `COMPACTION_FEEDBACK_LIVE_OK`.

[Exact transmitted corrective request text](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138415#issuecomment-6355688999): these are captured provider requests, not a helper replay or a reconstructed prompt.

## Simplification

Retained the existing audit owner and a single bounded list builder. Removed 12 lines of explanatory production comments and the new test's copied session-manager/model/hook stubs and mocked summarizer orchestration. Focused regressions still cover whole values, omitted counts, reserve overhead, all short identifiers, the unchanged untrusted cap, and skipping an oversized value. The built-Gateway proof exercises the actual corrective dispatch. Production delta: +23/-3; tests +133/-0 (down from +305); documentation +2/-0. Contributor commits and credit are preserved.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: a revert fully restores the previous feedback text; no persisted state changes. Blast radius is the private compaction quality-audit reason text sent to built-in corrective summarization requests. It does not change provider-owned compaction policy or summary acceptance limits.

prs.title: fix: GitHub identity setup failures report no cause in Gateway logs
prs.body:
Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub identity setup recordings contain no cause in the Gateway log when `tools.github.configure` fails; the operator sees only a generic `GitHub identity setup failed` error.

## User Impact

Operators can read the actual failure cause from the Gateway log (for example a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use setup handoff, or a store error) instead of reproducing the failure and guessing across the several fallible setup steps covered by the single try block.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler's catch block discarded the caught error completely, so nothing about the failure reached anywhere. This change binds the error and logs it using the established gateway logging convention (`logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage`, matching the sibling `mcp-app.ts` catch paths) before responding with the unchanged generic error. There is no behavior change: same error code, same message, same response shape.

## Evidence

- Before (observed in production logs): 10 failed `tools.github.configure` calls on 2026.10.5 (Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 01:44–02:00 UTC), each logging only the `res ✗ … errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed"` response envelope, with no cause-bearing log line anywhere near them. Method and context: #181165 (full journal slices inspected, not just grep hits).
- Regression test (per the review's next-step ask), run locally on this change: `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts` — *"logs the unavailable-handoff cause while retaining the generic response"* — handoff consumption throws; the test asserts `logWarn` carries the thrown cause (`tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: setup handoff expired before use`) while `respond` keeps the byte-identical generic UNAVAILABLE error shape. **Red on the base** (fix stashed): `1 failed | 12 passed` — only the new test fails, at the `logWarn` expectation. **Green with the fix**: 13/13 (`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest 5.0.3 on Node v24.22.1).
- Runtime note, stated plainly: local runs used Node v24.22.1 (sha256-verified from `nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt`); this host does not have the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork, so vitest fell back to Node (printed by the harness). PR CI runs the standard lane.
- Scope check: 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) — production: `catch (error)` binding, one `logWarn` line, two convention imports (+4/−1 vs base); the rest is the regression test and its spy setup.
- Known upstream-main statuses observed while running the local check graph (all empty-diff, none from this change): the max-lines suppression ratchet reports three `ui/` files (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`) that are identical to base `d5ce64b7` — inherited `main` state, zero hunks from this patch.

prs.title: fix(setup): preserve the current model when activating saved auth
prs.body:
Related to #167381

## What Problem This Solves

Activating a previously saved auth profile failed with `The candidate route does not match the selected model` when the saved credential's starter model differed from the current agent model. The activation path staged the stored starter model instead of the model the agent was already using, so route verification rejected the candidate. If the models happened to match, activation could also overwrite the user's current model with the starter model. Discovery had the same mismatch: Model Setup forwards the discovered candidate model explicitly, so fixing activation alone was bypassed by the normal UI flow. Provider-qualified aliases such as `openai/Fast` must also be resolved to their canonical model identity or the same route check rejects a valid current model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved-auth discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now share the same model-selection decision:

1. An explicitly supplied `modelRef`.
2. The canonical current agent route model, when it belongs to the same provider as the saved credential.
3. The saved credential's stored model, preserving the existing cross-provider fallback.

Both paths call `resolveCurrentModelRefForSavedAuth`, which uses the existing setup route resolver. Configured aliases therefore resolve to the same concrete model identity used by the model-selection updater, and discovery advertises that canonical current model to Model Setup. The trailing auth-profile suffix is removed before comparing providers. API-key header configuration is applied to the provider of the resolved model rather than always using the saved starter model's provider. Credential and auth-profile binding behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can switch back to a saved sign-in without a spurious route mismatch, and activation no longer resets their current model to the provider's starter model. Cross-provider saved credentials retain the previous fallback behavior.

## Evidence

- Full target test file: `42 passed` on the final head, including both `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and the configured `openai/Fast` alias.
- Discovery-to-activation regression: both cases call `setup.detect()`, assert the saved-auth candidate advertises the canonical current model, activate that candidate as Model Setup does, and verify the persisted model and inference call.
- Discovery base-red: with the previous discovery selection restored, both cases advertise `openai/starter-model` and fail before activation.
- Discovery unit suite: `19 passed` in `setup-inference-detect.test.ts`.
- Type-safety hardening: the API-key header target uses the resolved model provider when a model is present and otherwise falls back to the saved provider, so `parseInferenceRef` never receives an optional model reference. The final-head model regressions pass (`2 passed | 40 skipped`).
- Formatting: `oxfmt --check` passed for all changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Logs: `167381-vitest.log`, `167381-base-red.log`, `180832-full-vitest.log`, `180832-alias-base-red.log`, `180832-p2-typefix-vitest.log`, `180832-discovery-vitest.log`, `180832-discovery-base-red.log`, `180832-detect-vitest.log`, and `180832-full-vitest-final2.log` under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/` in the contributor workspace. Upgrade readback logs: `stable-doctor.log`, `stable-baseline.json`, `candidate-doctor.log`, `candidate-activation.log`, `candidate-followup.json`, `requests.jsonl`, `schema-before-after.json`, and `upgrade-verification.json` under `180832-live-proof/upgrade-20261023e/`.

### Real CLI behavior proof

On 2026-10-23 I exercised the shipped `openclaw` CLI in an isolated state directory against a local loopback OpenAI Responses provider. The state had an active `openai:baseline` credential and a saved replacement `openai:saved-proof` credential whose recorded model was `openai/starter-model`; the current agent model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.

- A baseline `openclaw agent --local` turn authenticated with the baseline credential and returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1` on `gpt-5.4-mini`.
- `openclaw models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` It authenticated the probe with the saved credential, not the baseline credential.
- A subsequent `openclaw agent --local` turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` from `gpt-5.4-mini` and used the saved credential.
- Persisted config after activation: `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, while `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.
- The saved profile remained present in the migrated auth store with its original key; only its consumed setup marker was cleared.

Provider-side request sequence, with keys redacted:

```text
baseline warmup   Bearer <baseline>  gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1
activation probe  Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_2
follow-up turn    Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3
```

The discriminating latest-stable run used the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` package with the same fixture. It activated the saved credential as `openai/starter-model` and persisted `agents.entries.main.model = openai/starter-model@openai:saved-proof`, reproducing the reported drift. The head above instead persisted `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

### Existing-state compatibility

The fixture initially used the legacy `auth-profiles.json` layout. The reviewed head's `doctor --fix` migrated it to the current state SQLite database, retained both profile IDs and credentials, and the CLI listed and activated both afterwards. This PR adds no persisted-format change.

### Latest-stable upgrade readback

The readback was verified on `a8b7787e`, rebased onto current `main` (reports `2026.10.6`). The branch was then rebased once more to `e3d624de` solely to pick up upstream `82c46546`, a test-fixture typecheck fix; the source diff is unchanged. I seeded an isolated state with the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` (fe06181) package: its `doctor --fix` migrated the legacy store and stamped `meta.lastTouchedVersion=2026.10.6` with schema v20, and one baseline turn ran against that state (`LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1`, baseline credential, `gpt-5.4-mini`).

The candidate head then opened the same state. Its `doctor --fix` advanced schema v20 -> v31 and retained pre-migration SQLite backups. `models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` with no downgrade-guard warning. The follow-up turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` on `gpt-5.4-mini` using the saved credential. After the upgrade, `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, and only `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

Machine-checkable result: `upgrade-20261023e/upgrade-verification.json` (13/13 checks), with logs in `upgrade-20261023e/` under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/`.

Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \
  src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

`tsgo` could not be run on this host because the available glibc is older than the installed TypeScript native binary requires, so this PR does not claim a local typecheck result.

## CI note

`check-test-types-core-1` failed only in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts` (`managedHooksDir`), which this PR does not touch; it is a pre-existing failure on `main` already fixed by upstream `82c46546`. The final rebase includes that fix.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and test preparation. The contributor reviewed the diff, ran both the focused regression and base-red checks, and verified the final patch.

prs.title: fix(ui): Settings search loses keyboard focus in forced colors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings search has no visible keyboard-focus indicator when forced-colors mode suppresses its shadow-only focus ring.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard users can see when the Settings search input is focused in high-contrast mode. Normal-color styling and navigation behavior are unchanged; no migration or action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a system-color outline only to the Settings search input's forced-colors `:focus-visible` state. The fix stays page-local and does not alter shared navigation, command-palette, or composer focus handling.

The simplification pass retained seven production lines and one 49-line bundled regression, with no new state, helper, configuration, or duplicated focus owner.

## Evidence

**Before** — the keyboard-focused search input has no focus outline.

![Settings search before: no keyboard-focus outline in forced colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20e2b2c7-7f9d-4121-96a8-16465b5cf31d)

**After** — the same input has a visible system-color outline.

![Settings search after: visible keyboard-focus outline in forced colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58290e4f-aada-4935-a879-35c04ca74702)

- Reproduced on canonical main base `87aada17522b9146cf5e26df3352b81d8cc0669b`: the actual bundled input was keyboard-focused with `outline-style: none` and `box-shadow: none`. The owning regression recorded that expected failure; its tool finalization was interrupted afterward.
- The unchanged regression passes with the repair: **1/1**, 1.20 seconds for the scenario, 30.17 seconds including the production bundle and harness. The fixed input has a solid 2px outline while forced colors suppress shadows.
- **36/36** existing Settings-sidebar/search tests pass. UI production and E2E-consumer typechecks, scoped lint/style/format, controller guards, keyless i18n verification, and whitespace checks pass.

Fixes cron history failing to load when a session retains a Claude CLI binding but selects another provider, or when private CLI history contains a forwarded cron input.

## User Impact

Users can read the scheduled conversation through native history without dropping cron inputs. There are no schema, public RPC, permission, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker-owned cron-label preparation refactor left two preliminary CLI-history reads without the prepared resolver. They now use the same placeholder contract as the existing history page paths; the native history worker or host still resolves current automation names for the returned page.

## Evidence

On Node 24.20.0 / pnpm 12.5.1 in isolated Linux compute, both new cases fail on unchanged 2026.10.1-beta.2 with `Cron job names must be prepared before projecting forwarded messages`. The corrected source passes both complete affected test files: 12 tests.

`pnpm test src/gateway/cli-session-history.paging.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.cli-import.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 190.92 seconds including 80.65 seconds of native worker compilation. The focused original-code run took 81.03 seconds with cached worker artifacts. The new cases extend existing native SQLite/CLI-history fixtures and add no Gateway boots, timers or polling.

Current-head Linux qualification at `06e876fb934e8cead4afdff4d7e55ab725bba691` on Node 24.20.0 / pnpm 12.5.1: both affected native test files passed 20/20; production core and both affected Gateway test type graphs passed; focused formatting and native type-aware core lint passed (four files, zero warnings/errors). Source freeze passed. No release has been published from this branch.

Evidence limits: the first sandbox was destroyed before its complete raw 20-test/core logs were exported; their terminal pass results remain in the tool transcript. The original Gateway-root type pass is likewise a retained terminal observation; its raw log was overwritten by an aborted duplicate. Current scoped lint, formatter, Gateway-method type and source-freeze outputs were exported. An initial default lint invocation timed out in unrelated extension declaration preparation; the native changed-file planner's explicit core lint configuration passed without that preparation.


### Additional installed Gateway evidence (October 10)

The retained Claude CLI binding / selected OpenAI provider case passed through the actual published-fork Gateway and native CLI `chat.history`; [redacted response and assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166980#issuecomment-6096168487). prs.title: fix(memory): restore memory search on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #178771
Related: #93199

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `memory_search` failures on multi-agent gateways when the request has
`runSessionKey=global` but already carries the valid scoped key
`agentSessionKey=agent:<agent>:<session>`.

## User Impact

Authorized non-default agents retain working memory retrieval without changing
existing agent-scoped visibility restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The execution owner is now resolved once at the shared outer tool-construction
boundary, before either synchronous or asynchronous preparation, and the
prepared result is propagated to downstream consumers.

- `runSessionKey=global` with a valid scoped `agentSessionKey` preserves the
  known scoped owner.
- A valid scoped `runSessionKey` remains authoritative, preserving the nested
  session behavior introduced by PR #126221.
- Explicit execution-agent overrides remain subject to the existing resolver
  validation.
- Two different scoped keys can represent legitimate delegation; execution
  ownership remains distinct from requester/policy identity.
- Malformed or genuinely unresolved ownership fails closed.

The relevant implementation is in [`resolveOpenClawToolSession`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38c5491af44ac0fe7d56cfaeb37e7c11237f44e7/src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.ts#L79-L93), outer preparation in [`prepareOpenClawTools`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38c5491af44ac0fe7d56cfaeb37e7c11237f44e7/src/agents/openclaw-tools.preparation.ts#L24-L41), and synchronous/async propagation in [`openclaw-tools.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38c5491af44ac0fe7d56cfaeb37e7c11237f44e7/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts#L151-L224).

Memory visibility continues to use strict owner resolution with the trusted
scoped owner as fallback. Conflicting or ambiguous aliases are excluded rather
than assigned to the requester.

The final reconciliation also moved the type-only `ResolvedOpenClawToolSession`
contract into `openclaw-tools.types.ts`. This removes the direct type-import
circular dependency between the plugin-context and shared types modules without
changing runtime behavior.

## Evidence

### Construction-path reproduction

The unmodified baseline reproduced the original failure for:

```text
runSessionKey=global
agentSessionKey=agent:research:dashboard:control
```

The baseline raised:

```text
Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner.
```

At the published head, the synchronous regression uses the real
`createOpenClawTools` factory, returns a non-empty tool array, executes
`sessions_search`, and verifies that the constructed request carries
`agentId: research`:

[`openclaw-tools.session-context.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38c5491af44ac0fe7d56cfaeb37e7c11237f44e7/src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-context.test.ts#L236-L275)

The corresponding asynchronous construction path also resolves successfully.

### Installed 2026.10.5 bundle reproduction

A separate isolated probe against the installed OpenClaw `2026.10.5` bundle
reproduced the same construction-boundary failure. The synthetic fixture was:

```text
runSessionKey=global
agentSessionKey=agent:research:dashboard:control
agents.ownership=explicit
```

The **captured baseline output** was:

```text
error AgentSelectionRequiredError Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
```

In the unmodified bundle, both outer construction paths used the following
expressions before plugin-context resolution:

```js
sessionKey: captured.runSessionKey ?? captured.agentSessionKey
sessionKey: options?.runSessionKey ?? options?.agentSessionKey
```

The disposable copy replaced those two expressions with calls to the existing
`resolvePluginSessionKey` helper:

```js
sessionKey: resolvePluginSessionKey(captured)
sessionKey: resolvePluginSessionKey(options ?? {})
```

**Captured disposable results** were:

```text
scoped-agent-with-global-run PASS 36
scoped-run-with-global-agent PASS 36
explicit-owner-override PASS 36
malformed-agent-key REJECTED Error Malformed agent session key; refusing default-agent resolution.
ambiguous-global-only REJECTED AgentSelectionRequiredError Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
```

This confirms the relevant 10.5 failure is at the outer construction boundary:
the unscoped `global` run key displaced a known scoped owner before the
existing selector could resolve it. The 10.5 installation already contained
the earlier scoped plugin-context selection and the three Memory Core
`fallbackAgentId: scopedAgentId` sites. This was an **isolated
bundle-construction reproduction**, not a live Gateway test, actual memory
retrieval, or complete authorization proof. The probe's commands are
reconstructed in the retained local evidence record; the output above is the
captured result.

Sanitized earlier candidate-validation output:

```text
Baseline: AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured...
Patched:  Test Files  5 passed (5)
          Tests       55 passed (55)
Patched:  Test Files  3 passed (3)
          Tests       32 passed (32)
```

### Authorization and visibility evidence

At PR head `38c5491af44ac0fe7d56cfaeb37e7c11237f44e7`, the isolated synthetic
tests exercise the actual synchronous and asynchronous tool factories plus
Memory Core's real-manager query path. Construction preserves the scoped
execution owner, while requester/policy identity remains a separate context.

The Memory Core real-manager fixture performs local provider-backed search and
then applies the canonical session-visibility filter to four **same-agent**
`agent:main` session candidates: two authorized Telegram-private results are
returned and two Discord-group results are withheld (`candidateHits: 4`,
`hits: 2`, `withheldHits: 2`, `embedQueryCalls: 1`). This is not
cross-agent-provider evidence. Separate cross-agent visibility tests use
mocked session-store fixtures to reject foreign-agent results and conflicting
persisted ownership. The tool-construction and Memory Core suites passed; the
architecture guard reported `Madge import cycle check: 0 cycle(s)`.

The construction tests cover scoped run/agent-key precedence, legitimate
delegation shapes, malformed/unresolved ownership, nested lookup behavior, and
live revocation for retained session lookup tools. A retained
`memory_search`-specific revocation-after-construction test was not available
in this bounded run and is not claimed.

This is isolated synthetic/runtime evidence, not a live Gateway request or a
production two-agent trace. It does not establish fresh Ollama embedding
health, complete authorization coverage, or that every denied candidate avoids
provider I/O; the provider search precedes result-disclosure filtering in the
tested path.

### Checks

- Earlier candidate validation: construction, delegation, and authorization
  tests **55/55**; memory visibility tests **32/32**; focused validation
  **69/69**.
- Final reconciliation: construction, delegation, and policy tests **45/45**.
- Final Memory Core visibility and real-manager tests: **44/44**.
- Madge import-cycle check: **0 cycles**.
- Pinned core TypeScript checking: **passed**.
- Formatting and whitespace/diff checks: **passed**.
- The cumulative PR diff contains **8 intended files**.

Fresh Ollama embedding health was not established, and the second agent's live
session did not expose the same memory tool surface. These tests do not claim
that every denied request performs zero provider I/O. No cross-agent memory
leak is claimed; the evidence confirms preservation of the existing ownership
and visibility restrictions through the tested paths.

Full extension-wide typechecking and linting were not run in the bounded
filtered checkout because of unrelated dependency and host limitations.

prs.title: fix: per-account thread-binding and Discord guild settings ignored for mixed-case account keys
prs.body: Related: #180066 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: per-account thread-binding settings (`enabled`, `spawnSessions`, `defaultSpawnContext`, `idleHours`, `maxAgeHours`) and Discord per-account `guilds` policy (`requireMention`, `tools`, `toolsBySender`) are silently ignored when the account is configured under a mixed-case key such as `channels.discord.accounts.Work`. ## User Impact Accounts configured with mixed-case keys now get their own thread-bound spawn policy and lifetimes, and their own Discord guild tool and mention policy, instead of silently falling back to the root channel settings. This also closes a permissions gap: today an account-level guild `tools.deny` under a mixed-case key is ignored, so tools the operator denied for that account stay available. ## Why This Change Was Made Account ids are normalized at routing time (`Work` → `work`), but these readers indexed the stored `accounts` map with the normalized id as a raw key, so the lookup missed and fell back to root config. #180066 reported this for Telegram and noted the Discord thread-binding readers as a sibling; #180654 fixes the Telegram readers. This PR covers the remaining sites: - The shared core thread-binding resolver (subagent spawn, ACP bindings, account-scoped conversation bindings, for every channel) now resolves the account entry through `resolveChannelAccountEntry`, the same lookup other core per-channel account readers use. - Discord's idle/max-age helpers duplicated that core logic; they now delegate to the core `...ForChannel` helpers (exported names unchanged). - Discord guild policy (`resolveDiscordPolicyScope`, which serves both `requireMention` and `tools`) resolves the account through `resolveDiscordAccountConfig`. Existing fallback order (account → channel root → session defaults) is unchanged. No config shape, defaults, migration, or stored state changes. ## Evidence ### Live Gateway + real Discord bot (before/after) Isolated Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/config), real Discord bot in a private test channel, real model (`google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`). Only my user and that one channel are allowlisted. Root and `accounts.Work` deliberately conflict: ```json5 channels.discord: { threadBindings: { spawnSessions: false, idleHours: 24, maxAgeHours: 48 }, guilds: { "": { requireMention: true, users: [""], channels: { "": { enabled: true } } } }, accounts: { Work: { token: { source: "env", id: "DISCORD_WORK_BOT_TOKEN" }, threadBindings: { spawnSessions: true, idleHours: 1, maxAgeHours: 2 }, guilds: { "": { requireMention: false, users: [""], tools: { deny: ["exec"] }, channels: { "": { enabled: true } } } }, }, }, } ``` "Before" = this PR's head with the three source files reverted locally; "after" = PR head `6811a767`. Same config, state, bot, and messages. **1. Account guild tool policy is applied before any tool I/O.** Message: `@bot Please run the shell command: echo hello`. - Before: no account group policy is applied; the shell `exec` tool stays in the agent's tool catalog despite `accounts.Work…tools.deny: ["exec"]`. - After, on every turn in the channel (including the spawned subagent): ``` [agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 1 tool(s) via group tools.deny: exec; matched exec ``` The agent searched its tool catalog for a shell (`catalog.search("terminal")`, `catalog.search("process")`); the 65-tool catalog returned no shell `exec`, and code-mode telemetry reported `callCount: 0`. No command ran; the model replied with plain text. **2. Thread-bound spawn policy honors the account.** Message: `@bot Call sessions_spawn with thread: true, mode: "session", label: "proof-check" …` - Before (root `spawnSessions: false` wins): the `sessions_spawn` schema only offers `mode: "run"`: - After (`accounts.Work.spawnSessions: true` wins): `"status": "accepted", "mode": "session"` and a bound `proof-check` thread is created: **3. Allowed tool executes; revocation applies on the next external turn of the retained session.** Same Gateway process, same Discord channel session, identical message both turns: `In one exec code block run exactly: return await exec({ command: "echo allowed-turn" })`. | | Turn 1: `accounts.Work` guild has no tool deny | Turn 2: `tools.deny: ["exec"]` added to `accounts.Work` (config hot-reloaded, no restart) | |---|---|---| | Policy log | (none) | `tool policy removed 1 tool(s) via group tools.deny: exec; matched exec` | | Tool catalog | 66 tools (shell `exec` present) | 65 tools (shell `exec` absent) | | Code-mode result | `exitCode: 0`, output `allowed-turn`, `callCount: 1` | `ReferenceError: exec is not defined`, `callCount: 0` | The tool was removed before any I/O on the first external turn after revocation. (On turn 2 the model's chat reply re-pasted turn 1's JSON from history; the transcript tool result above is the authoritative outcome.) **4. Upgrade from latest stable with config and data intact.** Fresh isolated state, same config, same bot: 1. `openclaw@2026.10.6` (latest stable) + `@openclaw/discord@2026.10.6` installed via `openclaw plugins install`: Gateway starts, Discord account `work` connects. `sessions_spawn` only offers `mode: "run"` (bug present); the account's `tools.deny` is never applied (0 `group tools.deny` log lines). 2. Same state dir and config, this PR's build (head `dcfef29`, includes current `main`): the upgraded Gateway asks for `openclaw doctor --fix` (main's agent DB schema v25 → v26, unrelated to this PR). Doctor saved pre-migration backups, migrated, and preserved every user config value (it only added defaults). Gateway starts, loads the PR's Discord plugin, and the existing channel session continues. 3. After upgrade: `tool policy removed 1 tool(s) via group tools.deny: exec` applies, and `sessions_spawn({ thread: true, mode: "session", label: "upgrade-check-2" })` returns `"status": "accepted", "mode": "session"` with a bound thread created; the child subagent ran in that thread. ### Regression tests Tests use an account stored under `Work` with conflicting root config; they fail on `main` and pass with this change (exact-key `work` cases pass on both): - `src/channels/thread-bindings-policy.test.ts`: spawn policy, idle timeout, and max age for `accounts.Work`. - `extensions/discord/src/group-policy.test.ts`: account guild policy for `accounts.Work` (base: `{ allow: ["message.root"] }`; fix: `{ allow: ["message.account"] }`). - `extensions/discord/src/group-policy.test.ts`: isolation across accounts: `Work` denies `exec`, `Ops` allows it, and an account with no guild overrides falls back to root; each account resolves only its own policy. Consumer suites green: Discord `monitor/thread-bindings*`, `subagent-spawn.thread-binding`, `sessions-spawn-tool`, `spawn-plan.admission`, `runtime-capabilities`, `account-scoped-conversation-bindings`, `commands-acp`. Format, lint, and typecheck (`tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`) clean; CI green on `dcfef29`. ### Not covered - A second human sender in the same channel: the live runs used one Discord user. This PR only changes which stored account entry is selected for the current account id; sender-specific `toolsBySender` matching runs afterwards inside the same unchanged resolver. Follow-up (not in this PR): `extensions/discord/src/setup-core.ts` reads `accounts[accountId].guilds` raw in a setup write path; it needs its own look at key resolution on write.

prs.title: fix(gateway): let workers message non-default global families
prs.body:
Fixes #138234

## What Problem This Solves

Workers reject valid sends to a non-default agent's global parent or sibling because raw family-key lookup loses the sending agent's owner.

## User Impact

Workers can message their exact live parent and siblings under the existing messaging policy. Fixed-store ownership, qualified targets, source authority, and incarnation checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both target lookup and shared-parent lookup now carry the source agent for unqualified keys without a configured fixed-store owner. The existing Gateway resolver still owns storage access and fixed-store routing; the core send path still owns messaging policy. No worker-side storage access, configuration, schema, or protocol change is introduced.

Current main already passes the shared-store core handoff case, so that path needs no production change. The production delta is 14 added and 2 removed lines; the other changes are the boundary regression, shared fixture support, test-lane registration, and documentation.

## Evidence

Both regression runs used `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-session-tool-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Baseline: `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2`. Removing only the production fix makes both per-agent parent/sibling sends fail with `session key "global" has no explicit owner`; the shared-store control passes.

| Check | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Worker-owner regression with baseline lookup | Expected failure: 1 failed / 1 passed | 31.527 s |
| Worker-owner regression with fixed lookup | 2 passed, both destinations in both store layouts | 30.886 s |
| Scoped type-aware lint through `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` | Passed | 95.52 s |
| `pnpm run tsgo:core` | Passed | 14.54 s |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all five files; `git diff --check` | Passed | — |
| Independent Codex review, P0–P2 | No actionable findings | — |
| Final combined local worker-suite rerun (58 cases) | Stopped during runtime preparation; no case result emitted | 682.03 s |

prs.title: fix(crabbox): shorten new Windows worker workspace paths
prs.body:
Fixes #166198

## What Problem This Solves

Native Windows Crabbox commands inherit deep workspace paths, leaving little room below MAX_PATH for installers, dependencies, and nested build outputs.

## User Impact

New Windows workers use a short, deterministic state root on the profile's drive. Existing leases keep their current paths and recovery behavior; reprovision an existing worker to use the shorter layout. Linux and macOS paths stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and diagnostics now share one path selector. It reuses an existing legacy directory, otherwise deriving a Windows drive-root directory from a 128-bit hash of the canonical home and full lease ID. This bounds path length while separating accounts and leases. The new directory receives private account/SYSTEM/administrator permissions before state is written. Node-host workspace naming and ownership checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on base `6e17838c5cfd9a7ca700091b98e4d86666dfebe4`: composed path length 503 exceeds the 180-character budget; 27 existing Windows cases pass. Wall time: 279.75s.
- With the fix, the maximum composed path is 168 characters, including maximum-length lease IDs and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` generation. The regression also checks account and lease separation and legacy enrollment replay.
- Focused replay/diagnostic suite: **71 tests passed in 3 files**, wall time **315.82s** (Vitest duration 259.49s). Shared worker compilation/verification accounts for most wall time; the new regression took 16ms.

```sh
pnpm test \
  extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment-windows.test.ts \
  extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment-replay.test.ts \
  extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment-diagnostics.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

- `pnpm run tsgo:core`: passed, 17.80s.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all five changed files: passed, 0.33s; `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification pass retained one shared selector, with no new configuration, state store, or workspace migration (production +29/-4 lines; tests +67/-5).
- **Local validation gap:** CI-style type-aware lint through `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json` scoped to the four changed TypeScript files could not reach linting: plugin SDK declaration preparation timed out after 300s (353.31s command wall time). PR CI must cover this check; it is not recorded as passing. Native Windows ACL execution and the reported installer comparison were not run. CI timing is pending.
