prs.title: fix: configure, classic onboarding and agents add save new channel tokens as plaintext in openclaw.json
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel token entered in `openclaw configure`, classic onboarding (and the Gateway's default `wizard.start` flow, which runs the same setup), `openclaw agents add` or the chat's channel setup in Control UI is saved as plaintext in `openclaw.json`. The same token entered through `openclaw channels add` goes to the protected secret store since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169732. Doctor then warns about plaintext secret-bearing fields, and the prompt's plaintext option says "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config".

## User Impact

User impact: a new or changed channel credential entered through any of these setup paths is saved as a protected entry in the shared secret store, and `openclaw.json` keeps a `store` SecretRef, as with `openclaw channels add`. The plaintext entry option now reads "Saves the credential in the protected secret store". Existing config is not rewritten: only credentials that differ from the config the setup started from are moved, so plaintext tokens, SecretRefs and env references saved by earlier releases stay as they are.

`--secret-input-mode plaintext` (the onboarding default) still means typing the value in. Channel credentials entered that way now go to the store as well, as they already do in `channels add`.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169732 put the protected-store step inside `persistChannelPluginConfig`, the save path of `channels add` and the Gateway's channels wizard. The other setup paths run the same `setupChannels` prompts but commit config through their own writers, so they never reached it.

What changes:
- The store loop moves unchanged out of `persistChannelPluginConfig` into `storeChannelSetupCredentials` in the same module. `persistChannelPluginConfig` calls it as before, so `channels add` keeps its retained-entry notice and its authority checks.
- `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and `runHostedChannelSetup` call it at their config commit point, comparing against the config the channel step started from. The hosted chat setup passes its existing `beforePersistentApply` and live-owner assertion, so a stale chat session still cannot write.
- The Gateway's `wizard.start` setup flow passes the wizard session's cancellation lock and liveness check into that store write, as its channels flow already does: if the client cancels after the token prompt and before the store write, the write throws and nothing is saved; once the write has begun, cancellation is refused until the next prompt. Because setup keeps prompting after the channel step, it takes that preparation lock rather than the permanent one. A setup session cannot be replaced mid-flow: setup admission rejects a second setup session as busy.
- `wizard.ts` composes that liveness check with the live authority of the client that answered last: `wizard.next` already records the answering request's `hasCurrentClientAuthority` (the callback `secrets.store.set` checks through `readGatewayRequestMutationAuthority`), so a revoked device, a lost operator scope or a rotated shared credential now fails the check. Both `wizard.start` flows use it, so this also closes the same window in the existing channels flow.
- The check runs at the store writer's admission and inside the config writer's `assertBeforePublish`, the synchronous hook `config.patch` uses. Before, both flows checked once before awaiting the config commit, and an isolated Gateway showed the commit publishing after a device removal while it waited on locks. A store write already admitted settles; its entry then stays unreferenced (see the first accepted limit).
- The Control UI chat follows the same rule. `SystemAgentChatEngine` hands each turn's Gateway request `hasCurrentClientAuthority` to `ChatWizardHost`, whose persistent-effect check, already used at the hosted store write, now also fails once that authority is gone. `runHostedSetup` runs the channel setup's check in the same `assertBeforePublish` hook. CLI chat has no request scope and passes no authority, as before.
- The plaintext option's hint and `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md` describe where the credential goes.

The store step runs where each path commits config, not inside `setupChannels`: a later prompt, a cancel or a failed check before the commit then leaves no store entries behind.

Accepted limits:
- If the config write fails after the store write (including a requester whose authority ends between the two), `configure`, onboarding, `agents add`, the Gateway setup flow and the hosted chat leave unreferenced store entries without the "retained" notice that `channels add` prints. The entries are unused and the config keeps its previous value; a retry stores the credential under a new name.
- Like `channels add`, the store step covers credential paths registered as channel secret-input targets. A plugin credential outside that registry is still saved as entered, under the same option hint.
- While the store write holds the preparation lock, `wizard.cancel` is refused and returns `status: "running"`; the cancel is not queued, so the client cancels again at the next prompt.

<details><summary>Writers and overlapping PRs</summary>

Writers that skipped the store step: `writeWizardConfigFile` in `configure` and the hosted chat setup, `commitSetupConfigFile` in onboarding and Gateway `wizard.start` setup, `createAgent` and `commitConfigWithPendingPluginInstalls` in `agents add`.

Open PRs touching the same files (none changes the channel save step):
- `src/wizard/setup.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127083, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163527, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573
- `src/commands/configure.wizard.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131153
- `src/commands/agents.commands.add.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174857, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175069, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168268
- Draft https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121563 adds a shared credential-mode hint in `src/channels/plugins/setup-wizard-credential-mode.ts` that still says "Stores the credentials directly in OpenClaw config"; whichever lands second should use this PR's wording.

</details>

## Evidence

The CLI built from this branch and from the base `19c5e58c2e8`, each run in a fresh `HOME` and state directory under `env -i`, with synthetic tokens. The prompts were driven in a pseudo-terminal by the same step file on both sides. Runs that start the Gateway or the bundled Codex app-server were in a network namespace with only loopback.

Re-run on 2026-10-23 after merging `main` `f125cb714f3`, with the same scripts on Node 24.22.1:
- `configure` built at `f125cb714f3` still writes the token into `openclaw.json`, with the "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config" hint, and `secrets audit --check` exits 1 with `plaintext=1`.
- `configure` built at the merge writes a `store` SecretRef, and the audit is clean.
- Gateway `wizard.start` built at the head `7b1c2db75d5`: the forbidden, cancel and complete scenarios match the first table below. With the answering device removed after its last answer, 0 of 5 runs stored the token.
- Hosted chat built at the merge: the forbidden and complete steps match the hosted chat table below. With the answering device removed at its last answer, 0 of 5 runs published config or stored an entry.
- The hosted chat table no longer lists a second `operator.admin` device answering the admin's step. Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176587, shared-token operator connections share the Gateway owner profile, so a second shared-token admin device is the same chat owner on `main` too. This PR does not change session ownership.

The tables below keep the commits they were first measured at.

`openclaw configure --section channels`, Telegram, "Enter Telegram bot token":

| Check | Before (`19c5e58c2e8`) | After (`dd48b4790aa`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| entry option hint | "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config" | "Saves the credential in the protected secret store" |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` in `openclaw.json` | **the token** | `{"source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_…"}` |
| `doctor --lint` `core/doctor/security` plaintext warning (`Paths: channels.telegram.botToken`) | **present** | absent; the other five findings are unchanged |
| `secrets audit --check` | **exit 1, plaintext=1** | exit 0, clean, unresolved=0 |

`openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-…`, Telegram at "Select channel (QuickStart)", After at `6719dd19adc`:
- Before: exit 0; the token is in `openclaw.json` and `openclaw.json.bak`.
- After: exit 0; `botToken` is a `store` SecretRef and only the state database holds the token. `secrets audit --check` lists only `gateway.auth.token`, which onboarding generates and which this PR does not touch.

`openclaw agents add helper` on the onboarded state (After only, `6719dd19adc`), Discord at "Set up a chat channel now?": exit 0, "Agent "helper" ready.", `channels.discord.token` is a `store` SecretRef, resolves, and only the state database holds the token.

Gateway `wizard.start` setup, built at `786f6bc8daf` (the production code of the then-head `080097ce070`, which added one test-only commit): an isolated Gateway with token auth and a driver on the real `callGateway` client, answering each `wizard.next` step and reading the config file and `secrets.store.list` after each scenario.

| Scenario | Result | `channels.telegram.botToken` | Store entries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| client with `[operator.write]` calls `wizard.start` | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| admin client enters the token, cancels at the next prompt | `cancelled` | absent | none |
| admin client completes QuickStart setup | `done` | `store` SecretRef | exactly the referenced entry |

The cancel above stops at a prompt, which the flow already honored. The new guard covers a cancel that lands after the last prompt and before the store write; the `wizard.test.ts` case below shows that window.

Device revoked after the last prompt, same Gateway setup: a client with its own paired device answers every step. At "Set up administration from your own chat account?", the last prompt before the store write, it sends its answer, and an admin client removes that device with `device.pair.remove` at once. Each run used a fresh state.

| Gateway build | Runs | Token stored after the removal | `wizard.status` after the answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `6719dd19adc` (session hooks only) | 5 | **5** (config published 154–173 ms after the removal) | `running` |
| `fcc798f1332` (client check before the awaited commit) | 5 | **1** (config published 167 ms after the removal, after a lock wait) | `running` in the stored run, once `error` "Gateway caller authority is no longer active.", otherwise already ended |
| `3e378f75424`, a local build of `70078921176`'s production code before a test-only amend; it differs from `080097ce070` only in `src/system-agent` and `setup.test.ts` (check at publication) | 10 | 0 | already ended and collected |

Hosted chat in Control UI (`openclaw.chat`), the same isolated Gateway setup, built at `786f6bc8daf`, the production code of the then-head `080097ce070`. A chat session needs a verified model before it starts, so a loopback stand-in for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint answering "OK" was the default model; it was called once, for that check. The admin, a client with its own paired device, sent "connect telegram" and answered each hosted wizard step with `wizardAnswer`, as Control UI does.

| Step | Result | Config field | Store entries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[operator.write]` client sends "connect telegram" | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| at the admin's token step, an `[operator.write]` client answers it | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| the admin answers through the last step | "Done — telegram is configured." | `store` SecretRef | exactly the referenced entry |

Hosted chat, answering device removed at its last chat answer ("Set up administration from your own chat account?"), a fresh state per run. Counted runs are those where the removal closed the answering request (4001); two `786f6bc8daf` runs where the request completed instead are listed in the proof file and excluded. In one, the answer's connection was silently re-paired on loopback after the removal. In the other, its handshake finished as the removal ran. `device.pair.remove` closes only registered connections, so a connection whose handshake completes during the removal keeps its capture, and loopback silent pairing can approve the device again; that is an existing Gateway race outside this PR.

| Gateway build | Removal | Counted runs | Config published after the removal | Store entry left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before the hosted fix (`wizard.start` fixes only) | at once | 5 | **3** | 3 |
| `786f6bc8daf` | at once | 13 | 0 | 0 |
| `786f6bc8daf` | after 30 ms | 10 | 0 | 10, admitted before the removal; unreferenced (first accepted limit) |

Upgrade from v2026.10.4: the release (`383c124`) wrote a state with a plaintext Telegram token, a Discord `env` SecretRef, a Slack `store` SecretRef and `env` SecretRef, a store entry, and gateway/model settings. `configure` built at `6719dd19adc` then added Zalo:
- Entered token: only `channels.zalo.*` and `plugins.entries.zalo.enabled` change; the other 21 config values, including the plaintext Telegram token, are identical. The store keeps the release entry and gains one `CHANNEL_SETUP_…` entry.
- "Use external secret provider" → Environment variable: an `env` SecretRef, no store entry.
- `secrets audit --check`: `unresolved=0`; `plaintext=1` for the pre-existing Telegram token, as the release reports it.

Tests:
- `src/cli/program/register.configure.persistence.test.ts` (new case): runs the registered `configure --section channels` command with a fixture channel plugin and checks that the file holds a `store` SecretRef and the store returns the token.
- `src/system-agent/hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` "rejects stale hosted channel authority at config revision" now expects the `store` SecretRef in the hosted write, reads the token back from the store, and checks that a stale write phase leaves the store empty. Two new cases run the chat engine's turns in a Gateway request scope whose authority ends after the last answer, before the store write or while the config commit waits: the reply names "Gateway caller authority is no longer active.", nothing is published, and the store is empty or keeps only the admitted entry.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts` (new, four cases): the real `wizard.*` handlers and `WizardSession`, each request in a Gateway request scope whose authority is a real device-revocation capture. The setup flow running, cancelled after the token prompt, and with the answering device revoked before the store write; the channels flow with the device revoked. Running: the store holds the token. Cancelled: `cancelled`. Revoked: `error` "Gateway caller authority is no longer active.". In the last three, no store entry and no config write.
- `src/wizard/setup.test.ts` (two new cases): a rejecting `beforePersistentEffect` stops `runSetupWizard` before it saves the channel token; authority that ends once the channel config commit has started stops its publication.
- `src/commands/channels/plugin-config-persistence.test.ts` (new case): with the real config writer and store, authority that ends at the commit's last await before publication leaves no channel config. It fails on the base, whose channels flow checked before the commit.
- The new and changed cases fail on the base with this branch's test files and pass on this branch. At the head `7b1c2db75d5`, a fail-to-pass run of the six changed test files against `main` `f125cb714f3` gives 11 cases that fail on `main` and pass here, and 98 tests that pass on both. At `080097ce070`, eight wrong fixes were caught:

| Variant (`080097ce070` minus one guard) | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| `no-client-authority`: the session check without the answering client's authority | both revoked-device cases in `wizard.test.ts` |
| `gateway-no-session-hooks`: setup flow without the `wizard.ts` hooks | the setup-flow revoked case; it also breaks the cancelled-session case |
| `setup-ignores-hooks`: `setup.ts` not passing them to the store write | `setup.test.ts` "checks the hosted session before saving a classic channel credential" |
| `setup-precheck-only`: setup checks before the awaited config commit (`fcc798f1332`) | `setup.test.ts` "checks the hosted session when the channel step config publishes" |
| `channels-precheck-only`: channels flow checks before the awaited commit (the base) | the new `plugin-config-persistence.test.ts` case |
| `chat-host-no-authority-check`: `ChatWizardHost` ignores the turn's authority | both new hosted cases in `hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` |
| `chat-engine-no-carry`: the engine does not hand the turn's authority to the host | both new hosted cases |
| `chat-no-publish-check`: the hosted config commit has no publication check | the hosted config-publication case |

Each changed test file, timed with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file> --maxWorkers=1` (what `pnpm test` runs) and a warm transform cache, at the merge:

| Test file | Tests | Vitest duration | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cli/program/register.configure.persistence.test.ts` | 2 (1 new, 531 ms) | 4.88 s | 9.28 s |
| `src/system-agent/hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` | 19 (2 new, 81 + 387 ms; 2 changed) | 6.58 s | 11.02 s |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts` | 26 (4 new, 471 + 28 + 25 + 24 ms) | 6.77 s | 9.80 s |
| `src/wizard/setup.test.ts` | 34 (2 new, 44 + 34 ms) | 8.78 s | 13.17 s |
| `src/commands/channels/plugin-config-persistence.test.ts` | 3 (1 new, 496 ms) | 6.77 s | 8.67 s |

Merging `main`: conflicts were in `src/system-agent/chat-wizard-host.ts` (both sides added fields; both kept) and in test imports and fixtures. `main`'s `hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` no longer imports the `configSnapshot` helper and verifies the hosted chat's inference route against a real config snapshot, so the two hosted authority cases build their config with `createInferenceConfigFixture`, as `main`'s neighboring cases do. With `main`'s additions, `src/wizard/setup.ts` reached 707 of its 700 counted lines. `7b1c2db75d5` moves `SetupWizardOptions` to `setup.types.ts` and passes the channel step's result straight to the store step. It changes no behavior.

Related suites pass at the head `7b1c2db75d5`: the changed test files and every test file that imports a changed production module (38 files, 499 tests), including `src/commands/channels.add.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.authority.test.ts`, the `system-agent` Gateway suites, the chat engine and turn router suites, and the onboarding and setup suites.

Checks at `7b1c2db75d5`:
- `tsgo` passes on the core project and on every `src` test shard.
- Type-aware `oxlint` (`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, as CI runs it) and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files.
- `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet` passes.

These ran through the repo scripts directly.

Not covered:
- The other hosted setups (skills, Gateway, memory import) and the classic setup's non-channel config commits (model auth and the rest) still do not recheck the answering client when config is published. That is pre-existing, and they write config only, not the team secret store, so it is outside this PR.
- `agents add` was run on this branch only.

<details><summary>Simplify pass</summary>

- Invariant: a channel credential typed into any interactive channel setup reaches config only as a `store` SecretRef, and a Gateway setup or Control UI chat setup whose session or answering client is no longer current writes no credential and publishes no config.
- One owner: the store step stays in `plugin-config-persistence.ts`; the four other save paths call it instead of copying it. `persistChannelPluginConfig` keeps its retained-entry notice and authority checks. Session liveness stays with `WizardSession` and caller authority with the Gateway request scope; `wizard.ts` composes the two in one function both flows use; the chat engine hands the same request callback to `ChatWizardHost`, which composes it into its existing check. Publication-time admission stays with the config writer's `assertBeforePublish`.
- Against `main` `f125cb714f3`: production +182/−79 in ten files (44 of the removed lines return unchanged in `storeChannelSetupCredentials`, and the channel step's nine options in `setup.ts` return re-indented inside the store call), tests +334/−4 in six files, docs +1.
- The helper returns at once when the channel section is the same object as before: onboarding, `agents add` and the hosted chat skip secret-target discovery when the channel step changed nothing. `configure` always scans, because it compares against a clone of the base config.
- No new tests for onboarding and `agents add` beyond the CLI runs above: they call the same helper at their commit point.

</details>

prs.title: fix: activate context engines with distinct plugin and engine IDs
prs.body:
Related: #126972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes context-engine plugins selecting or loading the wrong owner when their plugin and engine IDs differ, including mixed-case runtime IDs. Ownership must remain consistent through install, activation, update, Doctor and removal.

## User Impact

A plugin's declared engine can be selected without rewriting explicit custom selections or `none`. Deny, disable and independent trust requirements remain enforced; ambiguous approved owners fail before runtime import. Existing plugin settings and installation metadata remain under their original owner.

Older hosts do not implement this declared-owner activation contract. Downgrade requires compatible config/install state and, when necessary, a matching verified backup. Automatic failed-update rollback is not claimed. Human maintainer review of configuration compatibility is still required before merge.

**Upgrade migration:** released hosts stored the plugin ID (for example `upgrade-proof-plugin`) in `plugins.slots.contextEngine` when a context-engine plugin was installed. With declared engine IDs that selector no longer resolves, so turns would silently use `legacy`. `openclaw doctor` now warns about it, and `openclaw doctor --fix` replaces it with the plugin's single declared engine (`replaced plugin ID "upgrade-proof-plugin" with its declared engine "MiXeD-upgrade-proof"`). It only rewrites when that plugin is independently enabled or allowlisted and no other eligible plugin declares the same engine; plugins with several engines, unapproved owners and collisions get a warning naming the exact value to set, and config is left unchanged. Engine-ID, `legacy` and `none` selectors are never touched.

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugins.slots.contextEngine` remains an exact **engine ID**, not a plugin ID. Optional manifest `contextEngineIds` resolves its eligible plugin owner; existing installation records retain ownership metadata for lifecycle cleanup, without a new table, dependency or sidecar store. Runtime owners remain exact while allow/deny/config-entry policy remains canonical.

[Josh's documented contract acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146018#issuecomment-5705710381) covers selector semantics, manifest metadata, persistence and recovery. This repair preserves contributor history and main's loader, custody and consent owners. It also fixes Doctor's canonical-key/exact-owner join, preserving authored settings paths and matching deferred migration receipts to their actual owner.

Doctor owns the upgrade repair (`src/commands/doctor/shared/context-engine-plugin-id-selector.ts`), run before the host-compatibility check, which now inspects the selected engine's declared owner instead of treating the engine ID as a plugin ID.

## Evidence

Final head **c5e1c4658a75473fc9621bbdb94d864378bcbf81**: main `eabadc409a03` merged, config baseline regenerated, plus a test-mock fix found by hosted CI. The upgrade matrix ran on `ee56eaf`; `c5e1c46` only changes `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing-mocks.test-support.ts`. All runs were secretless Crabbox boxes: public network, Tailscale off, fresh PR checkout pinned to the SHA, no hydration. No production state or services changed.

- **Upgrade matrix, all 4 cells pass** (published npm baseline → candidate built from `ee56eaf`, real CLI, scripted loopback model provider):
  - `2026.10.6`, `2026.10.4`, `2026.9.33` → **plugin-id-selector**: the baseline CLI installs a context-engine plugin and stores its plugin ID `upgrade-proof-plugin` in `plugins.slots.contextEngine`; a baseline turn runs on `legacy`. After the package switch, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exits 0, replaces the selector with the declared engine `MiXeD-upgrade-proof` and reports the change; a rerun is idempotent; the plugin entry/settings, models and gateway port are unchanged. With the selector restored, `doctor` without `--fix` warns and leaves config unchanged, and `--fix` repairs it again. The installed plugin payload and plugin-created data are unchanged after Doctor and after the candidate turn, which runs the engine's assembly and carries the retained baseline history.
  - `2026.10.6` → **retained-legacy**: an explicit `legacy` selector is left untouched by Doctor; data and history are retained, and selecting the engine afterwards runs it.
  - Doctor output after the fix includes main's existing informational notice that offline host-compatibility inspection is unavailable for the runtime-registered engine; the earlier "could not inspect … not registered" warning now appears only in the preview, while the selector still names the plugin.

- **Checks on `c5e1c46`** (scoped to this PR's 94 changed TS files vs main `eabadc4`): `config:docs:check`, oxfmt, oxlint, core and core-test type checks and the full `check:baseline-ratchets` suite pass; all 39 changed test files, all 114 Doctor test files (`src/commands/doctor`, `doctor-config-flow`) and `repair-sequencing.test.ts` (27 tests) pass. The mock-exports ratchet caught the selector-migration mock on `ee56eaf`; it now spreads the real module.
- Repository lint has one error outside this PR: `ui/src/pages/config/view.tsx` is 704 lines against the 700 `max-lines` limit. That file is byte-identical to main `eabadc4`.
- Two UI browser tests, `multi-select.browser.test.ts` ("does not commit a disabled choice…") and `provider-picker.browser.test.ts` ("focuses the selected provider…"), failed in a broader run. Both are byte-identical to main and this PR changes no `ui/` or `packages/` files. In 6 alternating runs on the same box, unmodified main `eabadc4` failed 5/6 (both tests) and `ee56eaf` failed 6/6 (provider-picker) and 1/6 (multi-select). They are main's own instability, not from this PR.

- Hosted CI on `c5e1c46`: `check-test-types-core-1` fails in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts` (`managedHooksDir`), which main broke in `9cc4450` and fixed in `82c4654`; `checks-ui-e2e (6/9)` failed 1 of 467 tests (`session-progress-live-placement`, a UI-only mocked-Gateway test). Both shards passed on `ee56eaf`, and this PR changes no `src/hooks` or `ui/` files.
- Earlier broad run (head `a606850`, ~1,350 test files): two failing files, `bundled-plugin-icons` and `marketplace.download.native`, also fail on unmodified main (twice each); not from this PR.
- Scope: Crabbox proof of this PR's contract, not a substitute for full hosted CI. Upgrade proof is external package replacement, not in-process self-update, rollback or production service recovery.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse malformed UTF-8 before claiming node state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Current main validates retired node-host text at domain parsing, after shared claim recovery has already run. A malformed `node.json.doctor-importing` can therefore be moved away from its original path before encoding refusal; correcting that retained path and retrying then fails. Recovery can also compare/remove distinct malformed source and claim bytes that replacement-decode identically. Admit text before those recovery decisions.

Merged #180861 already fixes malformed ordinary-file import. This refresh retains the independent pre-recovery invariant; it does not claim that main still inserts corrupted ordinary-file node state. The fresh main comparison and current-head proof are first under Evidence; original acceptance and prior-head installation results are labeled as historical.

This follows the accepted strict text-intake family (#172953, #172742), at the node-host migration owner. It is independent of the meeting transcript importer: different input, source-claim lifecycle, canonical table and runtime consumer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode the retained bytes with the existing fatal UTF-8 helper in the node-host owner's snapshot callback. Checking only JSON parsing would be too late: shared claim recovery can compare and remove a retained claim before domain parsing. Every read/recovery/verification therefore sees admitted text before making a destructive decision.

Existing-solutions preflight: reuse decodeUtf8Input and the existing bounded, identity-checked snapshot/claim helpers. No new reader, library, config/default, schema, protocol, token handling, authorization choice or runtime fallback. Generic raw archive readers remain unchanged.

Against refreshed main, production **+16/-5, net +11** moves its existing fatal decode from parsing into snapshot admission and supplies the affected path plus backup/correct-copy/retry guidance; tests **+49/-10** replace the overlapping single-file case with source/claim/recovery coverage; docs **+5/-0**; **3 files**, no generated/lockfile changes. The existing 64 KiB bound remains intact. Use the existing `Utf8InputError` class so main's recoverable-warning contract remains intact. The shared decoder's other callers are unchanged.

## User Impact

Malformed node.json and node.json.doctor-importing files stay byte-identical at their original path, with a valid-UTF-8 diagnostic and no canonical node row inserted. Operators can preserve a backup, correct the encoding in a copy, replace the affected source and rerun Doctor. Valid Unicode and literal U+FFFD characters remain valid; corrected imports preserve node identity/Gateway metadata and retain existing retired-token discard behavior. Current main's encoding refusal is a recoverable warning and the tested Doctor commands exit 0; this patch preserves that contract instead of introducing a new fatal outcome.

## Evidence

### Current-main recovery gap and exact refreshed head

Current head **`6554e11735cfe3b2da62f792d65d36a24109b337`**, tree `4450fd6141ef4f6f1d3e4a70f3c0ea1e23e0fea0`, normal merge of main `4039ebd5df375f02a4b576dbb70fa3e8d9593cca`. Linux, Node 24.22.1, source version 2026.10.6. The conflicting test was reconciled without keeping duplicate malformed-file cases. Main's existing parse-time decode is moved earlier, so the snapshot owner admits text once before recover/read/verify/claim decisions. Source lock and SQLite owners are unchanged.

Same unchanged real-driver command for the current-main comparison and refreshed candidate:

```sh
node ../node-import-utf8-proof-20261023.mjs
```

The comparison runtime is `5534bea3152285db1a85b39750e7f5f0db7b5c5d` (main bb41 plus an independent Prometheus-only delta); the relevant node-host, source-snapshot, lock and decoder sources match main4039. The comparison is scoped to those owners, not claimed as a pristine full-main build. It produces RED specifically on interrupted-claim path preservation/corrected retry. Main's ordinary-file refusal is already a working control.

| Independent native Doctor / SQLite readback | Main owner before repair | Current committed candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary malformed source | source preserved, 0 canonical rows; corrected retry creates 1 exact row | same working control |
| Malformed interrupted claim | original claim path no longer exists after recoverable warning | same original claim path and exact bytes preserved |
| Correct only the retained claim and retry | 0 canonical rows; import/cleanup fails | 1 exact Unicode node config; both retired names cleaned up |
| Recoverable warning / Doctor exit | exit 0 | exit 0, same warning disposition |

Candidate native run began `2026-10-23T02:04:38.593Z`: PASS, failures=[], no timeout/signal. Both bad inputs retain SHA-256 `9840928332d9d89beafa7ea44c1cb760ccd6981077350bbcc2178fcdf5b96338`; canonical queries before retry return `[]`. Both corrected retries independently read back:

```json
{"version":1,"nodeId":"synthetic-node","displayName":"Café 会议 �","gateway":{"host":"127.0.0.1","port":18443,"tls":false,"contextPath":"/proof"},"installedAppsSharing":false}
```

The retired token is absent. Driver SHA-256 `cf067bf9c3b719fdd9599059de5957f25231e8cf88a67f308d4755b378437185`; main-comparison receipt `372e762f3e0587b6f4005aad403d884ddf4f5f7a16a68275f097aaadd60e7da1`; exact-head GREEN receipt `581f9aa4f28adcba983d6e1b766616bc44f8c922f4653932d16c8c2384fa5f33`. The driver still uses the unchanged v2026.7.1 writer and pinned fs-safe dependency described below. No production state or external Gateway is involved.

**Additional native claim-collision readback:** the same separate paired-file driver was run on the main-owner comparison build `e54532c6deeeba1678e4d80c3dd34a288aa6d32a` and candidate6554. Its relevant migration owners match current main `4f44cc7d7899cc924e7ce17cb0e399db8a72b6f7`; the comparison build includes only an unrelated Prometheus delta. Both inputs come from the unchanged released writer, then receive different invalid bytes (`e9` versus `ea`) with equal byte length and equal replacement-decoded text. The real compiled Doctor is invoked twice, and source bytes plus canonical SQLite are independently read back.

```sh
node ../node-import-utf8-claim-pair-proof-20261023.mjs
```

| Paired malformed files, before corrected retry | Main-owner comparison | Exact6554 candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source SHA-256 `9840928332d9d89beafa7ea44c1cb760ccd6981077350bbcc2178fcdf5b96338` | preserved | preserved |
| Distinct claim SHA-256 `7765d1ef8ac3cc35bb06db4614b71a63e60f79dc4d3485477ca1f4e05a6575b8` | deleted | preserved at original path |
| Canonical node rows | 0 | 0 |
| After replacing both inputs with the valid original and retrying | 1 exact Unicode row; cleanup completes | 1 exact Unicode row; cleanup completes |

The comparison returns RED because the distinct claim disappears, not because of the already-fixed ordinary-file import. Candidate returns PASS, failures=[], original source/claim preservation **2/2** versus **1/2** before, and the same valid retry succeeds. Both Doctor refusals retain main's recoverable exit0 contract. Paired driver SHA-256 `4b32fd823902aa989be25272ae99e9a48cfb1812c4a939da608ec40b0677f56e`; RED receipt `0e03f5df9462a44e99f204316a6f7a8ea74d6186b463701ca890198a1c24098a`; GREEN receipt `0d79d7b2f2496e12eae7dbb3f544edd435d2b3219168174f3c8efac812080120`. This supplements the unchanged original driver; it does not replace or rewrite earlier evidence.

**Current installed-stable upgrade:** PASS in local Linux container `leon-node-recovery-installed-upgrade-20261023`, Node 24.22.1 / npm 11.19.0 / glibc 2.35; run began `2026-10-23T02:04:38.678Z`.

```sh
node /harness/probe.mjs node /candidate/openclaw.tgz 6554e11735cfe3b2da62f792d65d36a24109b337
```

- A fresh copy of the actual official OpenClaw 2026.10.6 installation (build `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`) first creates canonical node state through its installed Doctor. The installed node CLI consumes the saved context path through an independent loopback HTTP recorder.
- Back up the isolated config/state, add malformed legacy input, then perform normal npm installation of the private candidate runtime over the same prefix. Installed build-info identifies the exact6554 commit, package version 2026.10.6.
- The candidate reports a recoverable UTF-8 warning, preserves the exact malformed-source hash and the existing canonical node identity/Gateway settings. Corrected-copy retry succeeds; independent canonical rows before/refusal/retry are byte-equivalent in value. Existing workspace setting is also unchanged.
- Actual stable and candidate node CLI each request `/proof` from the recorder. It deliberately returns HTTP503, after which owned foreground processes are stopped through parent stdin (SIGTERM observed). This proves saved-endpoint consumption, not completed pairing/authentication/WebSocket transport.
- Every operator setting is deep-compared except the existing Doctor-owned provenance fields and queue default explicitly checked by the driver: `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, `wizard.lastRunVersion`, `wizard.lastRunAt`, `messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering=false`. No new config/default owner is introduced. The current fixture uses canonical explicit agent ownership and preserves main's recoverable exit contract; the original prior-head driver remains unchanged.

Private runtime archive SHA-256 `c889aa556a57b4af31691cd38647e3aa7848cc62b2673a2745c1bfaffbb3712c`; installed driver `3868f5e99c5108c81d2d77c99f76757e3f2fa4e3f565cac24359ff74b4a4969d`; receipt `3dcdedae0f528c5468bc04952f914d46c6318b8eda1900e067b0830904364c2a`. This is a local isolated installed-runtime upgrade, not remote Testbox or release/SDK certification. Backups and raw artifacts stay outside the product branch; the redacted readbacks above are the published evidence.

Current checks:

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.node-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **24/24 PASS**, 117.58s Vitest / 126.55s wrapper including cold compilation, local container `leon-node-recovery-merge-tests-20261023`. Covers source/claim correction, distinct invalid-byte claim collision, recoverable warning disposition, Unicode/U+FFFD and existing identity/race/cleanup cases.
- Supported focused Go typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, `pnpm docs:list`, changed MDX check (86ms): PASS.
- Exact committed `pnpm build sourcePerformance`: PASS, 242.1s; build-info matches6554. UI build and canonical private runtime package integrity/import-graph check: PASS, package check101s.

**Hosted CI exception:** [check-test-types-core-1, run39888492231/job120203205034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39888492231/job/120203205034) reports TS2353 at `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts:57`: `managedHooksDir` no longer belongs to `prepareInternalHooks` options. The job checks synthetic merge `fc8f207f55a5fe2dbab1e726242b1f01eaf5ed45` (candidate6554 into main936b577). Upstream [9cc4450e9d79 / #181122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9cc4450e9d79a993a51dc6fa362468f46c6f1819) removed `managedHooksDir` and `bundledHooksDir` from the loader, while current main4f44 still passes both from that test. Neither hooks file is changed by this PR; the test is byte-identical to current main. The focused migration checks above pass, but this separate main regression leaves hosted CI red. No unrelated hooks change or baseline relaxation has been added to this migration patch.

Not tested at the current head: completed node pairing/handshake, real credentials or external Gateway, service installation, production operator data, Windows/macOS or repair of already corrupted canonical state. No independent-review pass is claimed.

### Historical original acceptance and prior-head evidence

- Scenario: refuse malformed node state before claim recovery/import/cleanup; corrected inputs still migrate with exact values.

Closes #180657

## What Problem This Solves

Dreaming performs an unnecessary content-revision read for each SQLite transcript before scanning it.

## User Impact

Dreaming sweeps avoid this redundant inventory work. Transcript selection and detection of later changes remain intact. No migration or user action is required.

## Evidence

The new regression failed on the original source because the discovered SQLite entry contained a revision. With the fix, an isolated SQLite-backed Dreaming sweep discovers the entry without a revision, ingests its first message, and ingests a message appended before the next sweep.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Markdown links in Synology Chat attachment captions being sent as raw `[label](url)` syntax even though ordinary text messages already use Synology's native `<url|label>` form.

## User Impact

An attachment caption such as `[Read docs](https://example.com/docs)` becomes the same native link as a text-only reply. Markdown inside inline code remains literal. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the existing code-aware text-link formatter with the media-caption path and apply it before caption chunking. This preserves the existing escape/code protections rather than adding a second formatter. It is a concrete caption behavior repair, not a standalone refactor.

Caption transmission from merged #128555 is already in the tested base. The independent overflow-receipt repair is #180676; neither PR depends on the other. - Actual `synologyChatPlugin.message.send.media` + HTTP-loopback regression fails on the original code because the webhook caption contains raw Markdown. With the fix it contains `<https://example.com/docs|Read docs>` and preserves the inline-code literal.

## What Problem This Solves

Live board updates cause unrelated, settled chat rows to prepare their contents again. With two mounted rows, one snapshot-only revision currently triggers two preparations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the global board snapshot revision from the shared row dependency vector. The widget pin button already subscribes directly to board membership; board-provider identity and pin capabilities remain dependencies. The virtualizer, anchor placement, row sizing, and rendered layout are unchanged.

## User Impact

Board-backed chats avoid redundant transcript work during board updates. Widget pin state still follows authoritative board membership.

## Evidence

The pre-declared gate is zero row preparations for an unrelated board revision, retaining row identity/text, plus 11 interleaved steady-state CPU pairs on ~240 history / six visible rows. Timing must improve in ≥9/11 pairs, or the explicitly authorized count-only gate applies if overlapping IQR and mixed signs put the update below timing noise.

- Real ChatThread regression: **N=2; 2 → 0** `prepareMessageGroupFrame` calls. Baseline fails; candidate passes. Both exact row nodes and the rendered answer remain. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-board-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2.74 s** wall time.

The per-update timing difference is below noise: overlapping IQRs and mixed pair signs (4/11 faster), so this does **not** claim a measured CPU latency win. prs.title: fix: retry temporary database capacity failures during agent startup
prs.body:
Related: #162497

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents remaining degraded after startup when a temporarily full SQLite worker broker rejects their database open, even if capacity becomes available shortly afterward.

## User Impact

Agents can finish preparation during the same startup once temporary capacity pressure subsides. The existing store limit remains unchanged; persistent saturation or genuine database failures still leave the affected agent degraded. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the startup owner's existing bounded, abortable retry policy for canonical SQLite overload errors during opening. Release the opening permit before backoff so other agents can progress, and keep migration and publication outside the retry. Shutdown and replacement still prevent further opening or publication.

## Evidence

**Runtime proof added on October 16 (head `205f57ea4c060048db89691e1033f6c28114d6c4`).** Ran the built Gateway through the shipped launcher on Node 26.8.2 with isolated synthetic state. A temporary load plugin opens 64 real worker-backed SQLite stores through the public SQLite SDK, observes canonical `overloaded`, then releases them after 1.8 seconds. Gateway inspection, opening, migration and publication use their actual production implementations; none of those callbacks is replaced.

The same Gateway startup recovered the deferred agent after release. A subsequent normal `agent` RPC completed successfully through the actual ACP manager/runtime and a controlled stdio peer, and history retained both its pre-restart input and the new completed turn. This trace covers an unclean restart of the isolated Gateway, with its normal stale-lease integrity gate.

```text
2026-10-16T21:58:52.682+08:00 PROOF_CAPACITY_SATURATED canonical=overloaded held=64
2026-10-16T21:58:54.503+08:00 PROOF_CAPACITY_RELEASED stores=64
2026-10-16T21:58:57.093+08:00 agent database recovered after background inspection and preparation
Opening phase: 3963ms; migration: 692ms; secrets: 127ms; models: 28ms; publication: 1ms
agent(PROOF_CAPACITY_RECOVERED) -> status=ok, summary=completed
history -> PROOF_EXISTING_STATE + reply, PROOF_CAPACITY_RECOVERED + reply
PASS: successful agent use after capacity release, without another restart
```

The load is controlled fault injection using separate synthetic native database files, not a production fleet benchmark. Pressure also causes expected background-maintenance errors while capacity is held; the claim here is recovery of the deferred opening path only.

**Published-version upgrade restart also passed.** Installed the actual npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` release in a separate prefix; its CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)`. That released Gateway reached ready and returned the seeded `PROOF_UPGRADE_PRESERVED` user message. After stopping it, ran the candidate's normal Doctor repair and Gateway against the same isolated settings/data. The candidate returned HTTP 200 from `/readyz` (`ready: true`, `failing: []`) and returned the same session ID and message. Workspace bytes (SHA-256), configured workspace/session-store paths, Gateway mode/bind/port, and plugin enablement were unchanged. This is a CLI/Gateway upgrade smoke, with channels and Control UI disabled; it does not claim a native-app or authenticated-provider upgrade.

- Exact-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38871257001), including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

- Reproduced with the actual SQLite broker at its 64-store capacity: freeing one busy store still left the agent unprepared before the fix; the same regression now reaches prepared admission and publishes once.
- At the original published head, all 17 tests in `src/state/agent-database-startup.journal-bound.test.ts` passed. Boundaries include retry exhaustion, terminal/aggregate errors, permit release, shutdown/replacement, and no migration/publication replay. That run: 6.14s Vitest / 8.01s wrapper; the real broker case took about 0.7s.
- At that original head, targeted typecheck through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- This addresses temporary opening pressure only; it does not claim to resolve every capacity condition reported in the issue.


## Upstream integration and current validation

Merged main `f5a4d6157d858e668afd9bcc7c655d0c5c76001b` into the original PR branch. Resolved only the journal-bound test conflict, retaining upstream schema-admission publication retries and this PR's opening-capacity retries. Added a composition regression: an overloaded open followed by changed schema admission must recover without repeating migration.

The regression fails on that main source because agent-0 remains degraded, and passes on the merged candidate. Four affected startup/admission/Gateway-activation files pass **65 tests** across four files (46.98s wrapper); targeted canonical types, typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. These consumer suites control selected callbacks; the retained busy-broker case uses real SQLite stores. The original published Gateway/upgrade traces remain evidence for205f57ea, not a fresh boot of this merged tree.

A separate read-only P0–P3 source review covered the complete merged patch and its owning/calling paths, with no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected supplied evidence without executing the project. Current validation is pinned to merged tree `790d22f4ec8e3ddb7953d0c7a87acedb13567a2f`; new-head remote CI is tracked separately and is not inferred from prior-head results.

prs.title: fix(snapshot): honor verified Windows volume-root ACLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Windows Doctor can reject original-state capture when an otherwise trusted local volume-root ancestor grants Authenticated Users Modify (`0x1301bf`). That mask intersects the ancestor replacement policy only at DELETE-self, which cannot delete or rename a volume root.

## User Impact

This is the OpenClaw consumer half of https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1023, related to #180892. The current published dependency omits this new fact and therefore retains the existing safe refusal. A later authorized fs-safe release and OpenClaw dependency update are required to deliver the exception to installed users; this PR does not publish or change the dependency pin. Thanks @WG-Mojo for the detailed ACL report and local Windows observations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the optional `isVolumeRoot` fact from fs-safe and remove only DELETE-self from the ancestor mask when that fact is exactly true. Ordinary ancestors, private repository roots, untrusted owners, remote filesystems, incomplete ACLs, DELETE_CHILD, DACL/owner changes, generic-all/maximum-allowed and unknown rights retain their existing checks. The policy never infers volume identity from a drive letter or pathname.

## Evidence

The new regression failed before the fix at the reported mask. The expanded policy table proves the positive case and ordinary/unverified/private-root, unsafe-rights and remote negative controls. Platform identity comes from fs-safe's same-handle native observation and is tested upstream; the local policy test uses synthetic ACL facts and does not claim a Windows Doctor run.

`pnpm test src/snapshot/local-repository.windows-acl-probe.test.ts src/snapshot/local-repository.windows.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 25 passed, 2 Windows-only cases skipped on macOS. The single-file pre-fix run took 4.54s overall (2.68s Vitest); the combined post-fix run took 257.41s including first-use worker and package-boundary builds. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Local typechecking was stopped while preparing unrelated plugin declarations on this heavily loaded host; exact-head PR CI supplies broad typechecking. Isolated autoreview is clean at P0–P2 for this policy diff; native metadata is reviewed in the companion fs-safe PR. The change adds 13 production lines and 30 regression lines, with no new process or policy owner.

Windows Crabbox was requested once but not granted immediately; its create was durably cancelled and provider cleanup was verified complete. No remote test ran. [Exact-head CI 39884135392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39884135392) passed, including production/test types, lint, focused policy tests, security-fast and the CI gate. The OpenClaw Windows matrix was skipped by the CI planner; native Windows metadata proof is tracked in the companion fs-safe PR, and no Windows Doctor run is claimed here.

### Native authority proof

The companion fs-safe head `1045bfd7770c914037e1fae96c29bd895ad54962` passes [Windows native and packaged .NET batch validation](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/39887829313/job/120200398176), [Windows 2022](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/39887829313/job/120200398386), [installed Windows package smoke](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/39887829313/job/120201140148), and [ARM64 native-host coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/39887829313/job/120200398208). The real API test distinguishes a volume root from ordinary directories and root-targeting junctions, including trailing slash/dot spellings. The native owner binds the normalized GUID-root property to the ACL handle and a matching non-reparse namespace entry. Batch tests preserve true/false/missing facts and reject malformed facts.

Combined with this PR's reported-mask positive case and unsafe-rights/private-root negative controls, this proves the two component contracts. The existing snapshot owner awaits this admission before payload copying; that ordering is unchanged. This is not a Windows Doctor end-to-end or upgrade-success claim. The fs-safe PR merged as `cdbfafe73fe10de6238c7d47348e21108dcab8e6` from that exact reviewed head after 52 successful and 5 skipped checks, with no failed or pending checks; FreeBSD ARM64 also passed. No dependency release or bump is included here.

## Release-note context

Allow original-state capture under a verified local Windows volume-root ancestor whose only relevant untrusted replacement right is DELETE-self, while preserving every other admission check. Requires the corresponding fs-safe metadata release/dependency update.

prs.title: fix(cli): complete zsh long-option values after equals
prs.body:
Closes #180674

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Zsh Tab completion leaving long-option values unchanged when entered after `=`, for example `openclaw completion --shell=f`.

## User Impact

Newly generated Zsh completion scripts complete `--shell=f` to `--shell=fish`. Separated values, short-option clusters, and subcommand completion retain their existing behavior. Regenerate cached completions with `openclaw completion --shell zsh --write-state` to pick up the change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commander accepts long-option equals values. Mark value-taking long options with Zsh's existing `_arguments` `=` form so completion follows that same contract. Short-option spellings and alias exclusion names stay unchanged. Other shell generators are untouched.

## Evidence

Real Zsh 5.9 Tab completion on Debian 13 with Node v24.22.1, using the production generator and actual completion command registration:

| Input before Tab | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw completion --shell=f` | unchanged | `openclaw completion --shell=fish` |
| `openclaw completion --shell=z` | unchanged | `openclaw completion --shell=zsh` |
| `openclaw completion --shell f` | `openclaw completion --shell fish` | same |

- The existing native Zsh PTY regression gains one equals-value case. On the unmodified generator that case fails while all four pre-existing controls pass. The repaired generator passes all five cases without mocking completion results.
- The complete completion test file passes through the canonical repository runner: 14 passed, 20 environment-dependent skips because Fish and PowerShell are unavailable. The native Zsh test takes under three seconds in the isolated worktree run.
- An independent review found no actionable issues; an external native-shell matrix passed 22 cases covering optional/required values, long aliases and exclusions, hidden-option traversal, booleans, and short-option controls.
- Two-file formatting, scoped owner lint, canonical core and CLI-test typechecks, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full built-CLI proof now passes at exact PR head `200053948e4e227b9cdb4cf85ed1ea0aafec897e`. In a clean checkout, `pnpm --silent openclaw completion --shell zsh` exited 0 after 384 seconds and emitted 540,302 bytes. Its stdout was sourced unedited in fresh native Zsh 5.9; actual Tab completion passed all five cases: `--shell=f`, `--shell=z`, `--shell f`, `-s f`, and `-ys f`. Zsh exited 0 with empty stderr; the source checkout remained clean.
- This run used Node v24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, isolated home/config/state, plugins disabled, and the supported 5120 MB build heap. Generated script SHA-256: `94389238d8f31d2c2976e4813be1d0fa08460e5a24237429c7861e51456b80e9`. The earlier 180-second build attempt was incomplete; this completed run supersedes that limitation. No source-level generator imports or script edits were used for this end-to-end proof.

The before/after comparison above remains source-level red/green evidence. The added end-to-end proof exercises the normal built CLI at the repaired head, not a packaged-release installation. AI-assisted change; local execution and independent review were performed.

prs.title: fix(synology-chat): attachment receipts omit caption overflow posts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful Synology Chat attachment sends dropping the platform post IDs of caption-overflow messages. A 4,001-character caption is delivered as three posts, but only the attachment post was returned in the receipt.

## User Impact

Downstream delivery bookkeeping receives every accepted platform post ID rather than an incomplete receipt. The attachment remains the primary message. No configuration or delivery-order changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the existing delivery accumulator's completed result instead of discarding it after it has tracked the attachment and overflow sends. This reuses the same owner already used for partial-delivery errors.

This is a follow-up to merged #128555: its caption delivery is already on the tested main base; this fix addresses the remaining successful-return receipt loss, not caption transmission itself. The independent caption-link formatting fix is intentionally separate.

## Evidence

- Actual adapter + HTTP-loopback regression sends a 4,001-character caption and returns recipient-matched post IDs `701`, `702`, `703`. The original code fails the assertion, returning only `701`; the corrected code returns all three and preserves primary `701`.
- All **18 tests** in `extensions/synology-chat/src/client.loopback.test.ts` pass with `--maxWorkers=1`, including existing caption custody/partial-delivery coverage.
- Focused type-aware lint: 0 warnings/errors on both changed files. Format and `git diff --check` pass. Lint used the supported skip-prepare mode after broad artifact preparation exceeded the local budget.
- Canonical isolated Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted P0–P2 findings.

No live NAS was used. The existing test fixture supplies a synthetic hosted-media capability; outbound adapter, HTTP transport, recipient-matched IDs, and receipt aggregation execute as production code. Broad/package-boundary proof is left to PR CI.

## Exact-head CI follow-up

For head `3f8d03b94af49fc353fba2175e7c3b2af5cd6bda`, CI run `39792138171` / job `119872396581` (`check-test-types`) failed with TS2304 only in the untouched `extensions/twitch/src/outbound.test.ts`: missing `expectTarget` and `expectTargetError` (lines 141/147). The log shows checkout of merge `884dad7c` into upstream parent `51a117fa54a72d59e565f3543e7a9ac49a4e3cec`. The Twitch file has identical blob `81830063aed26f1cd0005e51a70999222ec2e3c0` in that upstream parent and the tested merge; both contain the two calls without definitions. Thus this failure is inherited from the newer merge base, not introduced by this Synology patch. The failed CI gate remains red; no reruns or unrelated Twitch edits were made.

## Captured adapter behavior output

Windows / Node v24.19.0, published head `3f8d03b94af49fc353fba2175e7c3b2af5cd6bda`; actual `synologyChatPlugin.message.send.media`, webhook HTTP transport, and delivery accumulator, with only hosted-media capability preparation supplied by a synthetic fixture:

```text
{"payloadTextLengths":[2000,2000,1],"messageId":"701","ids":["701","702","703"]}
exit 0
```

The synthetic server returns one recipient-matched post ID per request; the capture asserts the chunk sizes, complete receipt, and primary ID. This is inspectable **adapter/HTTP boundary proof**, not a shipped CLI/Gateway or live-NAS capture. The requested shipped-entry-point proof remains unclaimed: this host has Node v24.19.0, below the repository entry guard's `>=24.22.1 <25` or `>=26.12.1` requirement. No runtime guard or host installation was changed.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): agents in a group acknowledge each other forever when bot-sender silence is allowed
prs.body:
Related: #164946
Related: #159230

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where two agents in the same group acknowledge each other indefinitely when `silentReply.group` is `"allow"` and replies go through the `message` tool. An unaddressed bot message is admitted as a turn that may stay silent, but the per-turn hint still tells the model to "send the final user-visible answer". The agent then posts a reply it does not need, and the other agent receives that post as a new request. For example, a deploy bot's status report gets an acknowledgement from the agent, and the deploy bot receives that acknowledgement as a new message to answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

For a `message_tool_only` user request whose sender is a bot and whose admitted reply expectation is `optional`, the per-turn hint becomes `BOT_SENDER_DELIVERY_HINT`: "If a visible reply is warranted, use the `message` tool to send it; none is required." Every other turn keeps the standard hint, byte for byte.

- `source-reply-delivery-mode.ts → resolveUserRequestDeliveryHint` picks the hint next to `resolveSourceReplyExpectation`, which owns admission. `get-reply-run-context.ts → resolvePerTurnDeliveryDirective` calls it.
- The new hint is listed in `MESSAGE_TOOL_DELIVERY_HINTS`, so transcript and memory sanitizers strip it like the others.
- Admission and stranded-reply recovery are `main`'s, unchanged; `main` already skips recovery for optional turns.

| Turn (`message_tool_only` user request) | Hint |
| --- | --- |
| Bot sender, admitted `optional` (unaddressed group turn under `allow`) | Optional-reply hint |
| Bot sender, admitted `required` (explicit mention, authorized command, `disallow`, direct chat) | Standard, unchanged |
| Human sender | Standard, unchanged |

No config option, schema, admission rule or recovery behavior changes.

## User Impact

Agents in a shared group no longer feel obliged to answer every message from another bot when the operator has allowed silence there. They still reply when mentioned, when the operator sets `disallow`, and in direct chats. Human senders see no change.

## Evidence

Exact head `43fa0035391` (a clean merge of `main` at `4686ed4c431`; the PR's diff is unchanged by it).

| Check | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source-reply-delivery-mode.test.ts → resolveUserRequestDeliveryHint`, using real `resolveSourceReplyExpectation` admission | Bot + `allow` gets the standard "send the final answer" hint | Only bot + `allow` gets the optional hint; bot + `disallow`, a bot's explicit mention, human + `allow` and unknown sender + `allow` keep the standard hint |
| Discord channel proof: bundled Discord plugin, local Crabline server, `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` | — | Under `allow`, three bot status reports got the optional hint and ended with private finals of 371–503 chars, with no post, warning, retry or notice. One arrived while another turn was running. Under surface `disallow`, the same report got the standard hint and a reply. |

The channel proof ran on `227dda864ff`, which behaves the same as this head; later commits only format code and move hint selection into a helper. Transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166380#issuecomment-6258351902.

On this head, these suites pass (221 tests): `source-reply-delivery-mode.test.ts`, `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `heartbeat-filter.test.ts` and `memory-capture-sanitization.test.ts`. The last two iterate `MESSAGE_TOOL_DELIVERY_HINTS`. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `pnpm tsgo:core` are clean on the changed files.

```sh
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/heartbeat-filter.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-capture-sanitization.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): tools.github.configure failures now log the real cause before the generic response
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators running the GitHub identity setup flow (Control UI / CLI save path) would only ever see the generic "GitHub identity setup failed" response: every failure inside `tools.github.configure` — a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use handoff, an installer failure — collapsed into the same opaque message with zero cause-bearing log lines on the Gateway host, forcing reproduce-and-guess triage (10/10 failures in the reporter's session left no cause in the journal).
- **Related:** #135028 (its fix surfaced `GitHubCliUnavailableError` on the sibling `tools.github.authorize.start` path but left the `configure` catch unchanged); #140576 (different defect on the same UI surface). Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** bind the caught error and log it server-side (`logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage`, matching the existing `mcp-app.ts` catch-path precedent) so Gateway diagnostics record the real cause; the client-facing response stays byte-identical.
- **Out of scope:** mapping `GitHubIdentityError` to more specific client error codes (explicitly named a possible follow-up in the issue); no change to the credential lifecycle or response shape.
- **Highest-risk area:** accidental credential material in the new log line. **How is that risk mitigated?** `formatErrorMessage` redacts sensitive text, and a regression test asserts the logged cause contains no token material.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** any `tools.github.configure` failure now produces a `tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: <cause>` warn line in Gateway diagnostics while the client response remains `UNAVAILABLE "GitHub identity setup failed"`, letting operators distinguish a missing `gh` CLI, an expired handoff, and hard failures by reading one log line.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts` (the configure catch block); regression tests `logs the setup failure cause while responding with the generic error` and `keeps the failure cause log free of credential material` in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — the real `tools.github.configure` handler was exercised in-process (real modules imported directly, no test doubles or `vi.mock`) with an isolated `HOME` state directory, before and after the patch.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # before: handler reverted to origin/main, invoke the real handler with a missing one-use handoff
  git checkout origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  HOME=/tmp/oc-proof-181165 NO_COLOR=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence-dir>/proof-configure-failure.mts
  # after: identical invocation with the patch applied
  git checkout HEAD -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  HOME=/tmp/oc-proof-181165 NO_COLOR=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence-dir>/proof-configure-failure.mts
  # regression tests (gateway project)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts    # 14/14 passed
  # type checks
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental                     # passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --builders 1   # passed
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  [tools-github] GitHub identity setup failed: temporary GitHub credential is unavailable
  RESPOND:[{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"GitHub identity setup failed"}}]
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the missing-handoff failure cause now appears in Gateway console diagnostics, and the client response is byte-identical to before (`UNAVAILABLE "GitHub identity setup failed"` envelope).
- **Before evidence (optional):** the identical invocation against unpatched `origin/main` produced only `RESPOND:[{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"GitHub identity setup failed"}}]` — no cause-bearing line anywhere, matching the journal behavior reported in the issue.
- **What was not tested:** a full Gateway process round-trip over WebSocket (the handler was exercised in-process with its real dependencies rather than against a live systemd Gateway), and the Control UI save flow end to end. CI lanes pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2 — deterministic real-module runtime output captured before/after; not a shipped-path capture from a live Gateway journal.
- **Proof limitations:** the harness invokes the handler directly instead of through a booted Gateway WS transport; the log call and response envelope exercised are the same code paths a live Gateway uses.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review.

prs.title: feat(sandbox): add lightweight local SRT backend
prs.body:
Related: #163540

## What Problem This Solves

Adds an optional Docker-free sandbox backend that confines local command and file writes to admitted writable roots while keeping managed skills and readonly resources protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SRT plugin uses the existing sandbox SDK and one filesystem policy for command and file tools. Host-owned custody contains command descendants; the backend retains the host authority callback and checks it before new effects. Cleanup remains available after revocation. Windows execution stays disabled before provisioning because the pinned runtime cannot establish safe shared-account ownership and rollback.

This update replaces an argv-shape assertion with launched exec-spec effects, adds a regression for a failed exec-spec build releasing its own custody lease, and makes qualified live runs fail when SRT is unavailable. It also records representative installed macOS workflow results. No host runtime logic changed in this update; installed proof therefore uses a compatible released host rather than a locally built host.

## User Impact

Operators can select the optional `srt` backend on macOS or Linux. This is write-focused confinement: host reads remain broad except explicitly hidden workspace paths. External npm/ClawHub distribution is configured, but sponsorship/distribution and security-owner acceptance remain maintainer decisions.

macOS custody necessarily denies `setsid`, `setpgid`, and `posix_spawn`. In the installed qualification, shell pipelines, an existing Git repository's status/diff/empty commit, Node itself, ripgrep and tar/gzip worked. Node child-process APIs failed with `EPERM`; npm/pnpm scripts, the system Python launcher, a make/cc build, and Git initialization with default hook templates failed. A successful version command does not qualify a build workflow. Maintainers still need to accept these restrictions or narrow initial platform support. Windows execution is not qualified or enabled. No merge, platform-acceptance, or product-direction decision is made here.

## Evidence

Candidate: `0c0704c303ede0a8f4ca97c9f2fd4ba659ae2ed3` (proposal3 delta above `119c99b81b9974c6c297d1f130c96fd5ecd4474c`).

Real installed proof ran on macOS 15.3.1 arm64 / Node 26.5.0 with released **OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447)** and the final **@openclaw/srt-sandbox 2026.10.3**, packed through `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`. The host was installed into an isolated prefix, the plugin through the installed CLI, and real Gateway `/v1/responses` turns selected real exec/write tools. A scripted model fixture supplied tool requests; it did not replace admission, sandboxing, execution, filesystem operations, or cancellation.

| Installed check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed exec and file writes | Both exact contents landed in the workspace |
| Exec and file writes to managed skills / outside writable roots | Denied; files absent; existing outside file unchanged |
| Deny-policy network | Connection to a host-reachable fixture endpoint rejected |
| Allow-policy network | Same final artifact returned HTTP 200 through SRT's proxy with ambient `NO_PROXY` bypass cleared |
| Real Gateway-owned HTTP disconnect during a running deferred command | Two processes existed before cancellation; none remained after 21 ms; releasing the flag produced neither main nor descendant write |
| Disconnect after sandbox preparation while model response was held | Held request included sandbox context; after release, neither requested exec nor file write occurred and no corresponding tool result was emitted |
| Shutdown | No retained pin-owner or proof-root processes remained |

The HTTP request's owner abort signal cancels the admitted run. An exploratory `chat.abort` returned `aborted:false` for this HTTP flow and is **not** claimed as revocation proof. This evidence does not claim a direct replay of an exported retained bridge after owner retirement.

Artifact SHA256:

```text
openclaw-2026.10.3.tgz
761685d010d96645d1deabe19299ecde263eac3f2489a17322f48c461a1130a5
openclaw-srt-sandbox-2026.10.3.tgz
90bd5ba600a61b80a2d49767987afebc9c1b0fd780a932e7867eea92d28a43bf
```

Focused validation:

- macOS exec-spec file: 3 passed, zero skipped, 11.78 s wall; authority file: 9 passed, zero skipped, 8.64 s wall. CI timing is not yet available.
- Removing only `custody.release()` made exactly the new lease-directory assertion fail (8 other tests passed); restoring the production bytes returned all 9 tests to green. No mutation remains.
- Native Linux 6.19.13 arm64, Node 26.8.2, Bubblewrap/socat/ripgrep present: `OPENCLAW_SRT_SANDBOX_REQUIRE_LIVE=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/srt-sandbox/src/backend.network.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed deny-all, strict allowlist and open with zero skips (48.24 s wall; test body 903 ms). The availability helper and network test bytes match this candidate. The historical 168-pass/15-skip suite is not installed-artifact evidence.
- Plugin runtime packaging, targeted production typecheck, type-aware lint, format and whitespace checks passed. Focused test typecheck: passed with the repository test declarations preserved.
- Fresh independent review of the complete proposal3 delta through P2 completed `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Incidental `@pnpm/exe` lockfile pollution was backed up and removed. HEAD already excludes its umbrella importer/package/snapshot entries, matching upstream's cleanup; required platform packages and intended SRT dependencies were preserved.

Hosted CI, current mergeability/conflicts, security-owner acceptance, distribution ownership and macOS platform acceptance remain landing considerations. No rebase or merge was performed; no all-green repository-wide CI claim is made.

prs.title: docs: explain plugin-owned database client error recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A plugin-owned PostgreSQL client can emit an error while idle, outside the promise returned by a tool or service. Without a client error listener, that native in-process failure can terminate the Gateway.

Related: #146290

## User Impact

Plugin authors get explicit guidance for handling native client errors, reporting unavailability, recovering connections, and testing idle disconnects. This is documentation only: Gateway crash policy and runtime behavior are unchanged, and #146290 remains open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing managed-call boundary covers returned work, and service health belongs to registered services. It does not automatically own a plugin's arbitrary native socket. The documentation keeps listeners, recovery, cached initialization, and cleanup with the client owner, and links this guidance from the native-plugin execution model. No SDK contract, dependency, or runtime code changes are introduced.

## Evidence

- A loopback PostgreSQL wire-protocol probe using the current `pg` driver emitted `57P01` followed by an uncoded `Connection terminated unexpectedly` error. Suppressing only the first error still exited 1; attaching the client's error listener before connecting handled both and exited 0. These are real-driver boundary probes, not Gateway survival or reconnection proof.
- Targeted documentation formatting, `git diff --check`, and the repository's Markdown parser checks for both linked anchors passed.
- Simplification and independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P3 findings. The patch adds 31 documentation lines across two files; production/test changes are zero.
- Final-head PostgreSQL conformance is pending before merge.
