prs.title: fix(gateway): show interruptions for unrecoverable requesters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated restart-recovery failures with `Restart recovery requester has no matching operator authority.` when an interrupted turn retains requester identity but has no matching restorable operator authority.

## User Impact

Recovery now records the existing visible interruption notice instead of retrying a definitive refusal. The transcript and session identity remain intact. With no other recovery or delivery custody owed, a new authenticated message can continue the conversation. Existing pending custody retains its normal explicit recovery behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatch boundary already denied missing, mismatched, and stale requester sources, but threw generic errors. The recovery owner only settles typed authorization/ownership refusals. Use those existing error types; keep the original authority checks and messages unchanged. No authority is reconstructed from a profile ID, session creator, transcript, or another operator.

A current matching operator source still resumes. Profileless channel sources use their existing owner; mapped channel requesters without a retained operator source fail closed. Cron remains scheduler-owned. Device/credential revocation and profile merges fail earlier during source restoration; changing a display name does not change the profile ID. These source distinctions explain which states can produce the reported error, but the original affected sessions were not inspected, so their specific missing/mismatched source cannot be attributed from the log alone.

Current main also fixes one concrete producer: authenticated Goal Resume input now retains its operator source despite internal-system transcript provenance (#181102, 784d9ce1b556). This patch handles definitive refusals, including existing saved claims without that source.

Related: #179579, #179689, #180090, #180227.

## Evidence

- Restart integration regression uses real SQLite claims, shutdown marking, lifecycle rotation, operator restoration, dispatch rejection, and transcript settlement. Model execution is stubbed.
- Before: missing operator authority, different operator profile, and stale requester source each return `failed=1, settled=0`; matching authority starts normally.
- After: each definitive refusal returns `settled=1, failed=0`, writes one actionable interruption, preserves the session, and cannot retry or duplicate the notice. Matching authority still starts.
- Focused proof: `server-instance-runtime.operator-recovery.test.ts` (24 tests), plus `operator-run-recovery.requester.test.ts`, `operator-run-recovery.test.ts`, and `server-instance-runtime.native-restart-recovery.test.ts` (60 adjacent tests).
- Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:core` (tsrs), and independent Codex autoreview through P2 passed. The initial integration fixture retained a separate unfinished run; correcting its active source ID exercised single-turn retirement. Existing adjacent tests cover retained custody.
- No production changes or recovery RPCs; no performance claim or benchmark. The patch was rebased without changes onto current main; PR CI owns exact-head broad validation.
- Simplification: reuse the existing settlement owner; no new state, retry loop, fallback, or schema. Production delta: +8 lines for typed imports/throws; test delta: +69 lines.

prs.title: refactor: keep private presentation and profile APIs at their owners
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Private one-consumer exports, DTO handoffs and re-export modules obscure the existing operation owners without providing a reusable boundary.

## What changed

Keep Discord voice routing and retained progress in their consuming operations; keep widget presenter selection in tool construction; call canonical OpenAI hosted-search and Google thinking wrappers directly. Place Telegram schema construction and reasoning defaults at their existing consumers. Make pairing operation types private to the worker client, and OpenResponses continuity types/constants private to its store. Fold the model auth-profile handoff into the existing public directive selection operation.

Tests that imported private profile/store surfaces now exercise public operations with independent expectations. Personal-pin proof still observes real account preparation and live identity validation, including zero caller-thread SQL. No new production test seam.

Net production reduction: **150 lines**, excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files and declarations. Moved bodies are not counted as removed code. This coherent internal-surface batch uses the coordinator's 150-line floor waiver. No user-visible behavior change, migration or action required. Public SDK/config/CLI/protocol/persisted contracts, lazy imports and the standalone Phase E memory backend remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None affecting runtime behavior. Only private handoff packaging disappears. Credential/identity authority, Discord transport authority and FIFO retirement, voice teardown, widget delivery precedence, Telegram schema allocation and session overrides, Incognito noncreation, existing store bounds and realistic concurrency remain intact.

## Evidence

Focused public proof passed: 48 Discord voice/retained-progress cases; 16 widget registration/scheduled/prompt-prefix cases; five OpenAI native-search and six token-sharing cases; 16 pairing worker cases; nine Telegram progress/reasoning cases; two OpenResponses continuity cases; two personal-pin authority cases plus three existing profile-command cases; and 32 Google/sampling cases. Unrelated name-filtered cases were not run; no skips were added.

The existing Telegram discovery suite plus a temporary recursive schema descriptor/symbol/allocation comparison passed 13 cases against a captured preimage. The temporary comparison test was removed before publication. Public test migrations passed against unchanged production before their folds. Initial raw model-route fixture preparation performed unrelated metadata SQL inside the observer; canonical model policy/alias preparation now happens before observing the real pin operation. No authority/SQL assertion was weakened.

Targeted native typechecks, formatting and line caps passed. Typed lint passed except for three unchanged SDK-resolution `no-redundant-type-constituents` diagnostics (Discord two, OpenAI one), reproduced serially against actual preimages and recorded without suppressions or casts. Exact-head hosted CI supplies broad lint/type/build proof.

Fresh cumulative independent review through P2 is scoped-clean. Final structural proof covers suppression tests, assertion/mock-export ratchets, protected wrapper/import closure, runtime/static cycles and source caps. No baseline growth, retry, longer timeout or new suppression. No broad local build or live external integration proof is claimed.

prs.title: fix(config): accept web search provider ids that differ only in case
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation rejects an existing web-search provider ID when only its case differs, such as `SearXNG` instead of `searxng`. Runtime provider lookup already trims and case-folds that same ID, so the writer rejects a value the configured provider can resolve.

## Changes

Case-fold the already-trimmed ID for active-provider and install-catalog lookup. Preserve the supplied spelling for stored config and diagnostics. This aligns validation with the existing runtime lookup; it does not add a provider, schema option, default, or credential route.

Thanks to @wangmiao0668000666 for the fix and case/padding regressions; their commit is retained. The existing unavailable-provider table now also covers a mixed-case catalog lookup and preserves its original spelling in the diagnostic.

## Evidence

Built main `22338ef3220a6598bcf893e86018b1446c07ab63` and candidate independently in isolated Node 24.22.1 Linux Docker with a per-PR proof mount. Enabled the existing SearXNG plugin and configured its owned local endpoint using shipped CLI commands. No invalid config file was manually written.

| Shipped operation | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config set tools.web.search.provider '"SearXNG"' --strict-json`, twice | Exits 1: unknown provider; no settings saved | Exits 0 both times |
| Lowercase `searxng` | Accepted; validates | Same |
| Unknown provider ID | Rejected | Same |
| Padded lowercase ` searxng ` | Accepted; JSON readback preserves spaces | Same |
| Final config validation | Valid with lowercase control | Valid with stored spelling `SearXNG` |

Started the built Gateway and ran a real agent turn through its documented HTTP chat endpoint with a local OpenAI-compatible model fixture. The fixture follows the actual shipped `tool_search` → `tool_describe` → `dispatch_action` flow instead of calling a private provider helper. On both arms, the existing SearXNG client makes one real HTTP search request to the owned service and the agent returns/stores `SEARXNG_RUNTIME_OK`. Main uses the valid lowercase control; candidate runs with `SearXNG` still stored. Public `chat.history` readback retains the tool results and final answer.

All 9 focused config tests pass, including unavailable-provider diagnostics; changed-file formatting and lint pass.

Simplification uses one lowercase operation after the existing string/trim/empty checks, avoiding a duplicate normalization pass and shortening the redundant comment. Whole PR production +4/-2 (net +2), tests +16/-0, plus documentation. Provider IDs, credentials, and defaults remain owned by their existing registries.

Merge danger: two-way validation repair, no migration or credential rewrite. Blast radius is web-search provider-ID matching during config validation; unknown IDs and existing availability checks retain their behavior.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse lossy meeting transcript imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Current-main status, 2026-10-23:** the original meeting-transcript import behavior is now implemented by merged [#180861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180861), commit `bb41c47d7736fa04592a80c5e59826623ede2046`. A fresh run of the unchanged real Doctor/SQLite/CLI driver passes using those main owners; details are first under Evidence. This PR's head remains `458ed8e20d44b6c01c3293178f233777d39fb472`. The implementation and original before/after below are retained as history, not a claim that current main still imports corrupted transcript text.

Doctor can import malformed UTF-8 meeting transcript files as if their replacement-decoded text were original content. The corrupted title, utterance or summary then becomes canonical SQLite state, and Doctor archives the source tree. Correcting the archived metadata and rerunning does not replace an already imported corrupted title.

This extends the accepted strict-text intake fixes in #172953 and #172742 at a different owner: the one-time meeting transcript importer. Original archive bytes are preserved by the existing implementation; this PR prevents corruption of the canonical representation, rather than claiming those archive bytes were lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the four textual source files during the initial streaming hash pass, before parsing, staging or insertion. A fatal streaming decoder handles sequences across chunks and rejects a truncated sequence at EOF without buffering an entire recording transcript. Existing imported-receipt recovery and archive verification continue hashing original bytes without retroactively rejecting old imports.

Existing-solutions preflight: Node's built-in fatal TextDecoder fits the existing bounded streaming hash owner; no new library, alternate importer, config/default, schema, protocol or runtime fallback is needed. Production **+29/-6, net +23** implements streaming validation and actionable recovery; tests **+53/-0**; docs **+6/-0**; **3 files**, no generated/lockfile changes.

Competition check: #167061 changes line splitting for valid U+2028/U+2029 in transcript/backup files. Its relevant source and diff were inspected: that reader still replacement-decodes malformed bytes, and it does not validate metadata or summaries. The two fixes address distinct root causes; this PR leaves stageUtterances and line-splitting policy unchanged.

## User Impact

Malformed metadata.json, transcript.jsonl, summary.json or summary.md blocks import with the offending path and instructions to preserve the bytes, convert a copy and retry. The source remains in place and no partial transcript batch is committed. Valid Unicode, literal U+FFFD characters and corrected inputs still import. Existing imported receipts can finish their original archive lifecycle.

## Evidence

### Fresh main-owner comparison

The maintained implementation decodes metadata and both summary forms with the shared fatal decoder, and streams utterances through `decodeUtf8Chunks`, including EOF validation. The existing transaction/staging owner keeps invalid text out of canonical tables. This covers the original four-file import outcome through a shared owner rather than this PR's additional preflight pass.

```sh
node ../transcript-utf8-proof-20261023.mjs
```

At `2026-10-23T01:44:52.766Z` the unchanged driver ran on Linux / Node 24.22.1, built source commit `5534bea3152285db1a85b39750e7f5f0db7b5c5d`. That checkout is main `bb41c47d7736fa04592a80c5e59826623ede2046` plus the independent Prometheus-only delta; its Doctor sources are identical to the merged implementation. Targeted owner/snapshot/decoder files also match main `4039ebd5df375f02a4b576dbb70fa3e8d9593cca`. This is a scoped main-owner comparison, not an installed release or a runtime built from the original transcript PR head.

| Actual Doctor readback | Merged main implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Malformed metadata, utterances, JSON summary, Markdown summary | all four refused import; 0 canonical transcript rows, 0 import receipts, 0 archives |
| Original source bytes | preserved in all four cases |
| Valid Unicode and literal U+FFFD control | exact title/content imported; fresh native list succeeds |
| Corrected-source retry | one exact Unicode session; existing archive receipt completes; fresh native list succeeds |

PASS, failures=[]; current-main Doctor exit is **0 with a recoverable warning**, which permits independent repairs to continue. This differs from the historical candidate's exit 1 and is explicitly not represented as that candidate's execution. Unchanged driver SHA-256 `39de496f2ebb158752ad4637e4663ee4fd394511f8516229ef89522dbd84533a`; comparison receipt SHA-256 `9e03161e17496e90c86bea636dad79ab5b8793e84feac0819778f112cf8a0445`. No production state, channel, provider or recipient was used; artifacts remain outside the branch and the redacted readbacks are published here.

### Historical candidate acceptance and installed-upgrade evidence

- Scenario: Doctor refuses malformed source bytes before canonical import/archive and accepts a corrected retry without changing valid Unicode.
- Entry: actual compiled `node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive`, independent SQLite/source inspection, then a fresh `node openclaw.mjs transcripts list --json`.
- Same command on base **068c4d87be12fa47353ce2e015c7516fad1fac9b** and head **458ed8e20d44b6c01c3293178f233777d39fb472**: `node ../transcript-utf8-proof-20261023.mjs`.
  - Before: all four malformed-source cases exit 0, insert 1 canonical session with replacement-decoded content, record 1 archived receipt and move the original tree. A corrected metadata retry still reads the corrupted title.
  - After: all four exit 1 with an encoding diagnostic, 0 transcript rows, 0 import receipts, 0 archives and unchanged source bytes. Valid-source and corrected-retry controls each import 1 exact Unicode session.
- Readback: independent SQLite queries cover session, utterance, summary and receipt tables; exact source byte equality is checked before retry; a fresh native CLI process reads the corrected title.
- Proof harness SHA256: `39de496f2ebb158752ad4637e4663ee4fd394511f8516229ef89522dbd84533a`. The identical final driver ran both native builds and asserts build-info commit equals HEAD.
- Other callers checked: complete snapshot/staging/transaction/archive owner, receipt-resume and cleanup paths, canonical TranscriptsStore, transcript list CLI and valid-text line-splitting sibling work.
- Tests: 34/34 in 2 explicit files, one worker; baseline main-file result 5 intended new failures / 26 passes. Includes all four sources, truncated EOF, multibyte chunk boundaries, literal U+FFFD, atomic batch refusal, corrected retry, imported receipts and cleanup.
- Measured test cost: 170.46 seconds Vitest / 180.98 seconds including cold preparation. Exact committed native sourcePerformance build: 229.9 seconds. Focused types, typed lint, formatting, MDX and diff checks passed. No broad suite.
- Additional installed-state upgrade: latest stable npm v2026.10.6 → the exact-head candidate package passed with existing canonical sessions, utterances, summaries, exports and operator settings preserved; see below.
- Not tested: active meeting provider, external APIs, cross-OS behavior, production operator data or repair of previously corrupted canonical rows. No independent-review pass or unrun upstream CI result is claimed.

### Released-source setup and actual commands

Source files were created by unchanged **v2026.7.1** TranscriptsStore and summary writer code, not handwritten JSON approximations. The [release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.7.1) points to **2d2ddc43d0dcf71f31283d780f9fe9ff4cc04fe4**. The writer and its exact release normalization sources were bundled without edits; every input was checked byte-for-byte against that tag. Bundle SHA256: `d4e09669a4ff5092d7718542cfa1486b5c5053f50af4eceea996b5ac3e6d02d3`.

One valid `é` byte sequence is then replaced with Latin-1 byte `e9` in one of the four files. This is a released-owner upgrade unit with controlled encoding fault injection, **not** an installed-release package-upgrade claim.

~~~sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive
node openclaw.mjs transcripts list --json
~~~

Linux, Node **24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**, isolated synthetic home/config/state, no real provider/channel configuration. Candidate proof began **2026-10-22 17:26:43 UTC** at exact build/head **458ed8e20d44b6c01c3293178f233777d39fb472**.

### Captured readback

Baseline, malformed metadata: Doctor exits **0**; independent SQLite and fresh native list both read:

~~~json
{"session_id":"utf8-proof","title":"Caf� 会议 �"}
~~~

Candidate: Doctor exits **1** with these captured diagnostic lines; the intervening local path identifies metadata.json in the isolated transcript source:

~~~text
- Failed migrating meeting transcripts: Error: Legacy meeting
  transcript file must be valid UTF-8:
  .../transcripts/2026-07-01/utf8-proof/metadata.json.
  Preserve its bytes and convert a copy before rerunning doctor --fix.
~~~

Independent SQLite observations before retry:

~~~json
{"sessions":[],"utterances":[],"summaries":[],"sources":[]}
~~~

All four original files remain byte-identical. For this metadata case, the unchanged malformed metadata SHA256 is `c69d33ef8b3dbf6fc1514bd5506c2e853b0fc05a9a581cde641482bde935fdff`; the other three source hashes are also checked, not merely file existence.

| Malformed source | Doctor exit before / after | Canonical sessions before / after | Import receipts before / after | Archives before / after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| metadata.json | 0 / 1 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| transcript.jsonl | 0 / 1 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| summary.json | 0 / 1 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| summary.md | 0 / 1 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 |

After replacing the preserved source with its valid UTF-8 copy, Doctor exits **0**. Independent SQLite reads:

~~~json
{"sessions":[{"session_id":"utf8-proof","title":"Café 会议 �"}],"utterances":[{"text":"Café transcript 会议 �"}],"sources":[{"status":"archived","removed_source":1}]}
~~~

The complete fresh native list contains one session with `sessionId: "utf8-proof"`, `title: "Café 会议 �"` and `hasSummary: true`; both summary JSON and Markdown match their released-writer originals. The separate valid-source control gives the same exact Unicode result, including the intentional literal replacement character.

### Latest-stable installed-state upgrade

PASS, **2026-10-22 18:38 UTC**, provider **local-container**, id **leon-transcript-installed-upgrade-final-20261023**, Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35, Node **24.22.1**, npm **11.19.0**. Installed the actual [v2026.10.6 release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.6) from the official npm registry with lifecycle scripts enabled. Its installed build is **fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc**; registry integrity:

~~~text
sha512-jSpQPa2Jw5rG0J2GC07j9+qHtVYIuoHjgccU88JeS+p7188sBCnvIJeuaiNPHj1zsWkuHcBv443QiEUh7qrxwA==
~~~

The stable installation was copied to an isolated prefix. Its actual Doctor imported valid legacy writer output into canonical state, then its installed `transcripts list`, `show`, and `path --transcript` commands read the existing data. A second source with malformed metadata was added before replacing that **same prefix** with the candidate. The candidate's installed build-info commit was asserted equal to **458ed8e20d44b6c01c3293178f233777d39fb472**.

~~~sh
npm install --prefix "$PREFIX" "$STABLE_SPEC" --registry https://registry.npmjs.org --no-audit --no-fund
# Copy the installation into the isolated proof prefix; retain the original.
npm install --prefix "$PROOF/prefix" /candidate/openclaw.tgz --no-audit --no-fund
node "$PROOF/prefix/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs" doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive
node "$PROOF/prefix/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs" transcripts list --json
node "$PROOF/prefix/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs" transcripts show existing-stable --json
node "$PROOF/prefix/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs" transcripts path existing-stable --transcript --json
~~~

`STABLE_SPEC` pins the published openclaw package to version 2026.10.6. The complete installed-upgrade driver ran as `node /harness/probe.mjs transcript /candidate/openclaw.tgz 458ed8e20d44b6c01c3293178f233777d39fb472`.

Captured independent canonical session readback:

~~~json
{
  "stable": [{"session_id":"existing-stable","title":"Café installed 会议 �"}],
  "candidateRefusal": [{"session_id":"existing-stable","title":"Café installed 会议 �"}],
  "candidateCorrectedRetry": [
    {"session_id":"existing-stable","title":"Café installed 会议 �"},
    {"session_id":"new-source","title":"Café installed 会议 �"}
  ]
}
~~~

The malformed-source candidate Doctor exits **1** and preserves its exact bytes; the original session, utterance, summary JSON and summary Markdown remain exactly equal. After correcting that input copy, Doctor exits **0** and adds precisely one new session. Fresh installed CLI list/show/export processes exit **0**. Existing transcript export SHA256 is identical before and after:

~~~text
d2a39665578a35adae122182499949735e419e2976312f32e1c618179998c1f5
~~~

The existing summary and workspace readbacks also match exactly. Config bytes legitimately change: existing Doctor owners update `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, `wizard.lastRunVersion`, `wizard.lastRunAt`, and persist the absent `messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering=false` default. The driver explicitly checks those four source-verified changes and deep-compares **every other setting**, including migration pins and operator values. Contracts inspected: `src/config/io.meta.ts:75`, `src/commands/onboard-helpers.ts:147`, `src/commands/doctor-config-flow.ts:307`, `src/config/defaults.ts:124`. These owners are unchanged by this PR.

The source-main candidate retains package version **2026.10.5**, so the expected newer-config version warning is recorded; neither version nor product code was edited for the proof. This is exact-build compatibility evidence from latest-stable stored state. The canonical self-contained packer produced a private runtime archive, and its package-integrity checker passed; this does not claim SDK declaration or release qualification.

Candidate archive SHA256: `7f218419861fa1b17e4e4dcda926ce66c20adc94da1cea6a6f7fe76061735f5d`. Installed-upgrade driver SHA256: `e7fe11e81250c72625f0e2caa5d7c54e0f7e43d23f8f21168dceebe19a83df0d`. Complete receipt SHA256: `2ec759988b9f29848cb221a986bd70855cb23132db0dd4b63392461b2e98ded7`.

A first run exposed the driver's overly strict byte-identical-config assumption. After reading the existing Doctor contracts, the whole upgrade was rerun from pristine stable state with the explicit comparison above; the failed receipt was retained. The original stable installation, copied pre-upgrade state and config backup remain available for rollback. All data is synthetic; no production service, provider, channel or credentials were used.

### Focused test results

~~~text
Baseline main file: 5 failed | 26 passed (31), all failures new encoding cases
Candidate:         2 files | 34 passed (34), exit 0
~~~

The host's old glibc cannot load the native proc-safe identity binding. Tests therefore ran with the real binding in an isolated local Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35 container: provider **local-container**, id **leon-transcript-utf8-tests-green-20261023**, Node **24.22.1**, one worker. This is local validation, not a remote Testbox claim.

~~~sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.meeting-transcripts.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.meeting-transcripts-stage-cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <focused-config>
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig <focused-config> src/infra/state-migrations.meeting-transcripts-files.ts src/infra/state-migrations.meeting-transcripts.test.ts
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/cli/doctor/state-migrations.md
pnpm build sourcePerformance
~~~

Author simplification checked the complete diff and lifecycle: validation shares the initial streaming hash pass, adds no whole-transcript buffer or extra file pass, and leaves raw archival/receipt recovery alone. Recovery guidance is included in the migration docs.

<details>
<summary>Redacted agent transcript — this task only</summary>

- User: Extend already accepted bug families with independent, proved fixes.
- Assistant: Inspected current import, staging, transaction, archive and receipt owners plus all-state competing work. Generated legacy files using unchanged released writers and reproduced replacement-decoded canonical content through the real compiled Doctor.
- Implementation: Added fatal streaming UTF-8 admission to initial snapshots, preserving raw receipt verification and existing SQLite ownership.
- Validation: Five new regression cases failed before production edits; all 34 focused tests passed afterward. Identical native drivers demonstrated four refusals and corrected-source fresh-process readback. A separate actual latest-stable installed-state upgrade then preserved the existing canonical data, summary/export bytes and source-verified operator settings at the same exact head.

Credentials, private paths and unrelated conversation are omitted.

</details>

prs.title: perf: harden embedded bootstrap-context event loop and add substage timing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The embedded bootstrap-context prep path (the work `runEmbeddedAttempt` does before the
first model turn) reported bootstrap-context time as a single opaque total with no
per-substage breakdown. That makes any future "the agent hung during bootstrap" report hard to attribute.

This PR does two things:

1. **Hardens the extra-bootstrap file-read path**:
   - **Keeps the remote workspace bridge as the sole owner of remote discovery and
     guarded reads.** Extra-bootstrap resolution now gates on `getAgentWorkspaceAccess`:
     with an access registered, discovery runs through `bridge.readDirectory` and reads
     through `bridge.readFileWithSource` with `assertCurrent` revalidation, never through
     local filesystem APIs (even when the gateway host itself lacks `fs.glob`); with no
     access registered, the hardened local path applies, including a realpath-aware
     containment pre-gate. The remote containment pre-gate stays lexical (the gateway
     host cannot canonicalize remote paths) and is backed by the guarded bridge read as
     the authoritative second line: a symlink that slips past the lexical gate still
     cannot deliver out-of-workspace bytes (remote tests + discriminating runs in
     Evidence).
   - The `**/AGENTS.md`-style extra-bootstrap glob resolver
     (`resolveExtraBootstrapPatternPaths`) keeps `main`'s recovery contract for a failing
     native `fs.glob`, but no longer recovers silently. ENOENT (a missing cwd) still means
     "no matches". Any other native `fs.glob` failure (including a synchronous throw)
     discards partial native results and re-resolves the pattern through the guarded
     fallback directory walk, so readable configured files still load; the resolver
     reports the original error as `nativeGlobError`, and the loader logs it as an
     operator-visible structured warning (pattern + original reason). No diagnostic entry
     is added, because the pattern was recovered.
   - The same silent-swallow existed one level deeper: the per-match containment check
     (`fs.realpath` on each glob result) caught *every* failure and `continue`d, so a
     matched file that failed `realpath` with EACCES/ELOOP/etc. simply vanished from the
     match set with no diagnostic at all — the outer error handling never saw it. It now treats
     only ENOENT as a benign delete-race (the entry vanished between `fs.glob` yielding it
     and the `realpath`) and records every other failure as a per-match diagnostic keyed to
     that specific matched path, then continues the walk. The resolver returns its readable
     matches alongside a list of per-match canonicalization failures; the loader loads every
     readable match and turns each recorded failure into its own operator-visible `io`
     diagnostic (deduped across patterns). So one unreadable match no longer discards its
     whole pattern — readable siblings under the same pattern still load, and the fault is
     attributed to the exact path that could not be canonicalized. A top-level native
     `fs.glob` failure is recovered through the fallback walk with an operator warning
     (previous bullet), so it no longer drops the pattern. The native `fs.glob` path and the
     `fs.glob`-absent fallback feed the same shared realpath-containment filter, so both
     isolate per-match failures identically.
   - Fixes a correctness bug (false-reject) in the security pre-gate for mixed-bracket
     globs. `pkg[ab]/*/AGENTS.md` is routed to `fs.glob`, where `[ab]` is a character
     class — but the pre-gate derived its literal walk-root prefix with brackets-literal
     grammar and realpath'd the literal directory `pkg[ab]`. If a stray `pkg[ab]` entry was
     an external symlink, the whole pattern was rejected with a misleading `security`
     diagnostic even though `fs.glob` walks `pkga`/`pkgb`, not that symlink. The prefix is
     now derived with the same grammar the pattern is actually resolved under.
   - Fixes the same false-reject class in the security pre-gate for routed extglob
     globs. A pattern whose leading segment is an extglob (`@(a|b)/*/AGENTS.md`)
     carries none of `? * { } [ ]`, so the pre-gate's literal-prefix scanner treated
     the extglob segment as a literal directory and realpath'd it. When that segment
     is a directory symlink escaping the workspace, the whole pattern was falsely
     rejected with a misleading `security` diagnostic — even though `fs.glob` roots
     its walk at the workspace over the alternatives and never traverses the
     literally-named symlink. The routed magic-segment grammar now treats an extglob
     open (`@(`, `+(`, `!(`, `?(`, `*(`) as magic, collapsing the prefix to where
     `fs.glob` actually roots the walk. `hasGlobPattern` and the non-routed branch
     are unchanged, preserving the literal-path contract for `@(a|b)/AGENTS.md`.
   - Restores `main`'s recovery contract for native glob failures, now with an
     operator warning instead of silent recovery: on a non-ENOENT `fs.glob` failure the resolver recovers via the
     guarded fallback walk and the loader emits a structured `workspaceLogger.warn`
     (pattern + original reason) with no diagnostic entry; ENOENT stays silent. The shared
     embedded-runner test fixture also aliases `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` to
     the same controlled mock, so the timing-aware resolver production calls are covered.
   - Corrects a misleading comment on the guarded workspace read that claimed the read
     "never blocks the event loop." The bounded read and fd close are async, but the
     identity-pinned *open* is a deliberate synchronous TOCTOU-atomic primitive owned by
     `@openclaw/fs-safe` (`openPinnedFileSync`: `lstat -> open -> fstat`). The comment now
     states that accurately.
   - Preserves literal backslash bytes in `fs.glob` match paths. The match-result side of
     the resolver previously folded every backslash to `/`; on POSIX a backslash is a legal
     filename byte, so a configured extra bootstrap file under such a path was opened at a
     different (missing) path and silently skipped. Match results now fold only the platform
     separator (`toPortableMatchPath`): a no-op on POSIX that preserves literal backslash
     bytes, and lossless on Windows where filenames cannot contain a backslash. Pattern-side
     normalization and the realpath containment check (run on the raw pre-rewrite path) are
     unchanged.

   - On runtimes without `fs.glob`, the local fallback walk now follows contained literal
     directory symlinks. The fallback read each entry with `readdir(withFileTypes)`, whose
     Dirent reports `isDirectory() === false` for a symlink to a directory, so a link reached
     mid-walk by a pattern (e.g. `**/pkg/linked/**`) was never descended and the configured
     bootstrap file behind it was dropped silently — while `fs.glob` follows such links. The
     fallback now resolves each link and descends it only when the target is a directory
     inside the workspace, gated by the same partial-match alignment as real directories; a
     link whose target escapes the workspace is never listed, and the shared
     realpath-containment filter still drops any escaped match. Cycle termination is structural (each followed link consumes
     a distinct literal pattern position; `**` never re-crosses a recorded descent depth), not
     identity-based, so two aliases to the same target are both walked, matching `fs.glob`.
     The `fs.glob` happy path is unchanged.
   - On runtimes without `fs.glob`, the fallback walk root is now selected with the same
     routed matcher grammar the security pre-gate uses. The fallback previously derived its
     walk root by scanning for `? * { }` magic characters and missed `[` `]`; since the
     fallback matcher treats `[ab]` as a character class, a pattern like
     `packages/[ab]/*/AGENTS.md` rooted the walk at the non-existent literal directory
     `packages/[ab]` and silently dropped every match. Root selection now delegates to the
     shared `literalPatternPrefix` helper (constant `true`: the fallback matcher always
     treats brackets as classes, and only glob-routed patterns reach the fallback), so the
     two derivations can no longer drift. The `fs.glob` happy path is unchanged.
   - On runtimes without `fs.glob`, the fallback's directory-symlink descent no longer
     depends on `path.matchesGlob`. The descent alignment called `path.matchesGlob` with no
     capability check; that API ships later than `fs.glob` (Node 22.5 vs 22.0) and is not
     guaranteed on the opt-in Bun runtime surface, so on a runtime missing it the alignment
     threw mid-walk and the loader dropped the configured bootstrap file as an `io` failure.
     Segment matching now goes through the same Minimatch grammar and options the rest of
     the fallback already uses, so descent alignment can no longer disagree with the full
     matcher. The `fs.glob` happy path is unchanged.
   - On runtimes without `fs.glob`, the fallback walk now yields fully-matching
     directories. The fallback descended into matching directories but never yielded the
     directory itself, so a configured pattern that `fs.glob` would satisfy with a
     directory match resolved to a strictly smaller set on a no-`fs.glob` runtime and
     dropped the directory match silently. Both the plain-directory branch and the
     descended literal-directory-symlink branch now yield a fully-matching directory,
     including the trailing-slash directory-only form (`pkg/*/`, which Minimatch
     full-matches only against the slash-terminated key); the terminal non-descended
     symlink branch deliberately keeps the non-slash form only, matching `fs.glob`,
     which does not follow such links for slash patterns. The `fs.glob` happy path is
     unchanged.

2. **Adds and exercises bootstrap substage instrumentation** so a slow bootstrap-context
   window reports where it spent time (`workspace-setup-state`, `workspace-file-load`,
   `hook-overrides`, `bootstrap-routing`, `continuation-scan`, `context-build`) instead of one opaque number.
   The breakdown (the substages plus a parent `bootstrap-context` stage) is routed through the
   embedded-run timing owner (`logEmbeddedRunStageSummary` in `attempt-stage-timing.ts`)
   instead of a separate bootstrap-only threshold: it is emitted at **warning level** when any
   stage takes >=5s or the total reaches >=10s, and at trace level below that, so the
   attribution is visible at the default console level during the exact slow-start incident it
   is meant to diagnose (it was previously `debug`-only, i.e. invisible on a default install).
   Genuine fault warnings are untouched. Includes proof harnesses that show both warn paths
   operator-visible at the default console level.

## Why This Change Was Made

This branch started as a candidate fix for the profiled ~14–22s bootstrap-context stall in
#87509. Root-cause analysis concluded it is **not** the right fix for that specific stall:

- The `agent:bootstrap` extra-files glob path is **off by default** (no
  `bootstrap-extra-files` patterns configured), so a default install never runs it.
- On `main` that path is already async (`fs.glob` + async reads); the harness here confirms
  it keeps the event loop live (sub-10ms timer gaps across a cold 20k-directory walk).
- A ~40KB reported workspace cannot produce a 22s glob/read stall; the isolated `fs.glob`
  and guarded-open measurements are three to four orders of magnitude below 22s.

One compatibility note: the backslash-folding of glob *match results* above was
introduced by this PR's own consolidation onto `fs.glob` (pattern normalization is
unchanged), so it is corrected in-PR here, covered by a POSIX regression test that fails
on the pre-fix code plus a runtime proof (Evidence).

One runtime-contract note: the consolidated resolver calls `fs.glob`, which exists on every
currently-admitted runtime but not on every runtime the repository documents as
experimental. The prior no-`fs.glob` compatibility path is therefore preserved as a narrow
capability-gated fallback: only when `fs.glob` is absent does resolution fall back to the
local matcher walk (the same matching behavior `main` uses). When `fs.glob` is present, the
happy path is unchanged byte-for-byte. The fallback keeps the PR's realpath-containment
filter and is covered by discriminating tests (absent-API resolution, loader-boundary
behavior, walk-root semantics, containment, and strictPatternRead sibling-directory
semantics). A follow-up parity gap in that fallback is also closed here: a directory symlink
reached mid-walk was never descended (Dirent reports `isDirectory()` false for links), so on
`fs.glob`-less runtimes a configured bootstrap file behind such a link was dropped silently
while `fs.glob` runtimes loaded it. The fallback now follows contained literal directory
symlinks under the same alignment and containment rules, with an identity-free cycle guard
(two aliases to one target both walk), covered by discriminating tests and an exact-head
runtime proof (Evidence). A second fallback parity gap is closed alongside it: the fallback
walk root was derived with a brackets-literal magic scan while the fallback matcher treats
brackets as character classes, so bracket-class patterns rooted the walk at a non-existent
literal directory and silently dropped their matches; root selection now shares the
routed-grammar helper with the security pre-gate (Evidence). A third gap in the same
fallback is closed here: the directory-symlink descent alignment called `path.matchesGlob`
unguarded. Node added `fs.glob` (22.0) and `path.matchesGlob` (22.5) as separate
capabilities, and the repository advertises Bun as an opt-in runtime surface where that
pairing is not guaranteed; with `fs.glob` absent (so the fallback is selected) and
`path.matchesGlob` also absent, the alignment threw mid-walk and the loader dropped the
configured file as an `io` diagnostic. Segment matching now uses the fallback's own
Minimatch grammar, covered by seams that hide BOTH native glob APIs together (Evidence). A fourth
pre-gate gap is closed alongside them: the routed literal-prefix scanner did not
recognize extended-glob operators, so a routed extglob pattern could be falsely
rejected with a `security` diagnostic when an unrelated external symlink carried
the extglob segment's literal name; the scanner now treats extglob opens as magic,
and a loader regression pins both the routed fix and the unchanged non-routed
literal-path contract (Evidence).

**Integration with current main.** While this branch was in review, main introduced the
remote workspace bridge (workspace access selection in `workspace.ts` plus guarded reads
in `workspace-file-read.ts`), which rewrote the same function family this branch hardens.
The branch has been re-integrated on top of current main so the bridge remains the owner
of discovery and reads for remote workspaces, and this PR's hardening applies to the
local (no registered access) path: per-match failure isolation with `io` diagnostics, the
realpath-aware containment pre-gate, the capability-gated `fs.glob`-absent fallback walk
(reachable only through the no-access gate), the operator warn / benign-skip diagnostic
split, and the substage timing instrumentation. The earlier event-loop scheduling
experiments on this branch (async fd close, overlapping phase reads, hook-yield split)
were dropped as outside the accepted narrowed scope; main's plain hook dispatch and
guarded-read structure are preserved unchanged.

So this PR does **not** claim to fix the 22s stall. What it keeps is the durable value: the
file-read hardening (no silently-dropped bootstrap files, no false security rejects) and the
per-substage timing needed to *attribute* a future incident. The real suspects for #87509
are untouched synchronous-SQLite paths that run inside the same bootstrap-context window;
they are filed as follow-ups (synchronous transcript-projection reconcile, and the
synchronous workspace-state snapshot / unmigrated-state assertion in bootstrap-routing), to
be re-attributed using the new substage breakdown.

## User Impact

- No behavior change for configured extra bootstrap files on the happy path.
- A non-ENOENT native `fs.glob` failure still recovers through the fallback directory
  walk (readable configured files keep loading, as on `main`), and now also logs an
  operator-visible warning naming the pattern and the original error instead of
  recovering silently.
- A matched bootstrap file whose final `realpath` check fails with anything other than
  ENOENT (e.g. EACCES) now surfaces its OWN `io` diagnostic keyed to that specific matched
  path instead of disappearing silently, and the readable sibling matches under the same
  pattern still load (per-match isolation); an ENOENT race still skips just that one match.
- Mixed-bracket globs (`pkg[ab]/*/AGENTS.md`) that were falsely rejected with a `security`
  diagnostic when an external bracket-named symlink existed now resolve their real,
  workspace-contained matches. Fully-literal bracket paths (`pkg[ab]/AGENTS.md`) still open
  the real bracket-named file (the `main` compatibility contract).
- New per-substage timing in embedded bootstrap-context prep, reported through the shared
  embedded-run timing owner: when any stage takes >=5s or the total reaches >=10s, a
  `bootstrap-context substages: ... stages=<name>:<ms>@<elapsed>` breakdown is logged **at warn
  level, visible at the default console level**; below that the breakdown is trace-only, so
  fast preps print nothing extra at the default level. Genuine fault warnings are unchanged.
- Extra-bootstrap matches whose directory or file name contains a literal backslash
  (legal on POSIX) are now preserved and loaded instead of being silently dropped;
  ordinary paths are unaffected.
- On runtimes without `fs.glob`, configured extra-bootstrap patterns still resolve via the
  local matcher fallback instead of surfacing an `io` diagnostic with an empty bootstrap
  set (the `main` compatibility contract); runtimes with `fs.glob` are unaffected.
- On runtimes without `fs.glob`, a configured extra-bootstrap pattern that reaches a
  workspace-contained directory symlink mid-walk (e.g. `**/pkg/linked/**`) now loads the file
  behind the link instead of dropping it silently; symlinks escaping the workspace are still
  discarded, and runtimes with `fs.glob` are unaffected.
- On runtimes without `fs.glob`, a configured extra-bootstrap pattern whose magic segments
  use bracket character classes (e.g. `packages/[ab]/*/AGENTS.md`) now resolves its real
  matches instead of silently dropping them; runtimes with `fs.glob` are unaffected.
- On runtimes without `fs.glob` AND without `path.matchesGlob` (separate Node capabilities;
  also possible on the opt-in Bun surface), a configured extra-bootstrap pattern that
  reaches a directory symlink mid-walk now loads the file instead of surfacing an `io`
  diagnostic that drops the configured file; outcomes on runtimes that have
  `path.matchesGlob` are unchanged.
- Remote workspaces: no behavior change — extra-bootstrap discovery and reads stay
  bridge-owned with access revalidation; a symlink that escapes the workspace is still
  blocked past the lexical pre-gate by the guarded bridge read, and the attempt surfaces
  as an operator-visible `io` diagnostic instead of leaking out-of-workspace content.
- Local workspaces with no registered remote access gain the hardened discovery path
  described above (per-match isolation, realpath containment, capability-gated fallback).
- No default-path behavior change: the extra-bootstrap hook is off by default.


**Supported-runtime contract for the no-`fs.glob` fallback.** The local fallback matcher
is strictly capability-gated: it runs only where `fs.glob` is absent
(`typeof fs.glob !== "function"`), and the native `fs.glob` path remains preferred and
byte-for-byte unchanged everywhere it exists. The contract the fallback honors is that
every configured extra-bootstrap pattern resolves to exactly the same set native
`fs.glob` produces on the same workspace, except the documented `**/..` edge case listed
under Known boundaries. Parity is enforced by the oracle-backed unit
suite (every fallback case asserts byte-equality against live `fs.glob` results) and by
the exact-head runtime proofs below; any discovered divergence is closed by adding the
case to the oracle suite first. Maintainers accepting this PR accept this contract as the
supported behavior for no-`fs.glob` runtimes.

## Evidence

This PR links no videos.

**Integration verification at head `dfb8f1e599076bfdccd9eb311ec02b4715965c5e`** (base: `upstream/main`
`7d0c0531888de48d6b9baee1e287da7a8a89433c`, reached by a clean catch-up rebase).

- Focused tests (latest verification round on this head): 8 suites, 136/136 tests green —
  `attempt-bootstrap-prepare`, `attempt-stage-timing`, walker, loader,
  `bootstrap-read-diagnostics`, `bootstrap-context`, `spawn-workspace` context-injection, and
  `system-prompt`.
- Fresh `$autoreview`, pass 1: one finding, accepted and folded into the branch (into the
  brace-alternative commit). The `fs.glob`-absent fallback followed a literal directory
  symlink and listed its target before the realpath filter ran, even when the target was
  outside the workspace. The fallback now resolves the link and descends only when the
  target is a directory inside the workspace. A discriminating test asserts that neither the
  link path nor the external directory is ever listed; it fails against the old walker and
  passes with the fix. The symlink-fallback proof harness was updated alongside it (§2 below,
  still `VERDICT: PASS`). The native `fs.glob` half of the same finding was rejected as out of
  scope: upstream already calls `fs.glob(pattern, { cwd })` unpruned, and every match is still
  realpath-filtered before any content is read.
- Fresh `$autoreview`, pass 2: two P2s, both rejected with reproduced evidence.
  (a) `**/../AGENTS.md` never yields on the downward-only fallback walk while native `fs.glob`
  finds it. Reproduced (native `["AGENTS.md"]`, fallback `[]`), and it matches upstream's
  pre-existing behavior: upstream's fallback used the same downward Minimatch walk and never
  matched `..` either. Native `fs.glob` behavior is unchanged. It is documented below as an
  accepted edge case.
  (b) "Bootstrap timing excludes an initial awaited state check" is false: nothing is awaited
  before `bootstrapContextStartedAt` (`resolveContextInjectionMode` and `makeBootstrapWarn` are
  synchronous), and `isWorkspaceBootstrapPending` runs as a callback inside
  `resolveWorkspaceBootstrapRouting`, i.e. inside the measured `bootstrap-routing` substage.
- Remote defense-in-depth (QA focus): three remote tests prove that a symlink escaping the workspace cannot deliver out-of-workspace bytes past the lexical pre-gate — the real remote-shell bridge refuses the escaped read (per-path `io` diagnostics, operator warn, escaped bytes absent from the hook context), and a mid-await access replacement rejects with "Workspace access changed". Discriminating runs: neutering `assertCurrent`, or the post-await guard, or the remote-host containment each flips specific tests RED (escaped bytes delivered / leak without warn); restoring returns GREEN.

**CI status.** The only remaining red checks are
`checks-node-changed-compact-large-13` (`run-orchestrator.rooted-proof.test.ts`, "reuses
configured plugins for runs outside the canonical workspace") and
`checks-node-compact-small-5` (`ci-workflow-planning.test.ts`, "packs flat manual Node rows
without losing timing identity", x2). Both reproduce identically at merge-base
`7d0c0531888de48d6b9baee1e287da7a8a89433c` WITHOUT any commit of this PR (both trees:
3 failed | 603 passed, same assertions), so they are inherited from the base, not caused by
this diff.

**Known boundaries (not covered by this evidence):**
- No live ACP / runtime-managed remote workspace was exercised end to end; the remote tests drive the real remote-shell bridge with a local script runner standing in for the remote host.
- The fallback walk keeps one documented, accepted divergence for exotic `**/..` patterns (e.g. `**/../AGENTS.md`): the fallback walks downward only and yields nothing, while native `fs.glob` can find a contained match. This matches upstream's pre-existing fallback, which never matched `..` either; native `fs.glob` behavior is unchanged. It needs both the fallback path (no `fs.glob`, or `fs.glob` failing) and an unusual `..` pattern.
- On the remote branch, when `path.matchesGlob` is absent the capability guard yields the pattern itself as a single candidate (mirroring the local capability branch); not reachable on supported engines.

### 0. Shipped-flow proof - real CLI agent turns through a Gateway built from the exact head

**Environment.** Head `dfb8f1e599076bfdccd9eb311ec02b4715965c5e` (clean tree). The dist was
rebuilt from this tree, and `dist/build-info.json` records
`"commit": "dfb8f1e599076bfdccd9eb311ec02b4715965c5e"` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (dfb8f1e)`).
Node v26.5.0, Darwin arm64. Every proof process ran under `proof-env.sh`, a hermetic `env -i`
environment holding only PATH, HOME, TERM, NO_COLOR, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH
and OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT, with a throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and config. The proof Gateway
is a throwaway instance on loopback ports 19089/19090 with a throwaway token; the operator's
live Gateway and `~/.openclaw` were never touched. Model: provider `stub`
(`api: "openai-completions"` on loopback), which records each request and streams
`PROXY-ECHO-OK`. Hook config: `hooks.internal.enabled: true`,
`bootstrap-extra-files` paths
`["**/AGENTS.md","pkg[1]/AGENTS.md","pkg[ab]/*/AGENTS.md","back\\slash/AGENTS.md","escape/AGENTS.md"]`.

**Commands.**

```
proof-env.sh <proof> 19089 pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 19089
proof-env.sh <proof> 19089 pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message "hello" --model stub/echo --json        # exit 0
proof-env.sh <proof>/slow 19090 pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 19090
proof-env.sh <proof>/slow 19090 pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message "hello" --model stub/echo --json --timeout 600   # exit 0
```

A `--local` agent turn CANNOT exercise this hook: internal hooks are only registered by
Gateway startup/reload (`prepareInternalHooks` in `src/hooks/loader.ts`, called from
`src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.ts`), so a `--local` turn injects only the root
bootstrap files. The shipped proof therefore routes a normal `openclaw agent` turn through an
isolated `openclaw gateway run`.

**CASE 1: context loading and fault visibility (fast workspace)**

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| a) all five sentinels reach the model request | PASS | Each of `SENTINEL-{ROOT,ALPHA,BRACKET,MIXED,BACKSLASH}-6CB2D52E` occurs once in the captured `/v1/chat/completions` request. The system prompt has `## <proof>/ws/pkg[1]/AGENTS.md`, `## <proof>/ws/pkga/x/AGENTS.md`, and `## <proof>/ws/back\slash/AGENTS.md` sections (excerpt below). |
| b) escaped file never reaches the model | PASS | `OUTSIDE-MUST-NOT-APPEAR` occurs 0 times in the full request JSON. |
| c) default-level security warning naming the escape path | PASS | `[bootstrap-extra-files] bootstrap extra-file resolution failed for 1 path(s) failed=1 reasons={"io":0,"security":1} paths=["<proof>/ws/escape/AGENTS.md"] hint="check hook bootstrap paths, workspace containment, and file permissions"`. The JSON file log records it as `level=WARN logLevelId=4`. |
| d) no timing warning for the fast workspace | PASS | 0 lines that mention `substages` or `bootstrap-context` in the Gateway console or the CLI output. |

**Case 1b (discriminating supplement).** In case 1, `**/AGENTS.md` also matches the bracket,
mixed and backslash files, so criterion (a) alone can't tell which pattern loaded each one.
Case 1b reruns the same workspace with paths
`["pkg[1]/AGENTS.md","pkg[ab]/*/AGENTS.md","back\\slash/AGENTS.md","escape/AGENTS.md"]`
(no `**/AGENTS.md`): ALPHA drops to 0 occurrences (no pattern matches it now);
BRACKET, MIXED and BACKSLASH stay at 1 occurrence each, so each literal/bracket pattern
resolves on its own, with `pkg[ab]/*/AGENTS.md` resolving through the real `pkga` directory;
OUTSIDE stays at 0 with the same security warning. Agent exit 0.

prs.title: fix(ui): stabilize the cold multi-select selection test
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The disabled-choice multi-select browser test asserts its selection callback as soon as the browser finishes delivering Enter. On the first menu open, navigation can still be loading, so the valid queued selection arrives after that assertion. This caused [the checks-ui failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39882502299/job/120183807104) even though the interaction completes correctly.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The browser check reliably covers disabled choices and cold keyboard replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test still clicks the disabled choice and presses Enter before waiting. It now waits for the existing callback assertion instead of assuming synchronous completion, preserving coverage of the queued interaction.

## Evidence

A focused diagnostic held the real menu runtime import: clicking the disabled choice emitted no callback; Enter while the import was held emitted no callback; releasing it produced exactly the enabled `fixture/ready` selection. The temporary diagnostic was removed after verification. The original case passed once locally; the CI failure remains the evidence of the premature assertion.

The complete multi-select browser suite passes 15/15. Vitest reports 10.57 seconds (about 1.6 seconds in assertions); the wrapper took 269.89 seconds, including about four minutes of cold startup before Vitest began. CI timing remains pending. Focused component typechecking, lint, and format checks pass. The reused checkout has external dependency links, so the typecheck ran with the identical test temporarily in the dependency-qualified checkout; the MultiSelect/menu production sources are identical, and the temporary file was restored. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. No timing or bundle change is introduced by this test-only repair.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer Online sidebar rendering until opened
prs.body:
## Outcome: closed — restored Online boot grows

This experiment removes the Online sidebar renderer from ordinary Chat and New Session boot. The plain ordering/snapshot helper remains eager; Solid loads the renderer inside the existing Online branch. Loading and error states retain the header and collapse control.

The ordinary routes shrink, but the supported cold-reload path with Online already selected adds **923 B gzip and one JavaScript request**. This exceeds the campaign's 64 B variance allowance, so this head will not land or consume another timing lease.

## Matched production bytes

Baseline main: `a568b793472027417a820a0be63d35db5930fce9`. The retained Menu build at `6cdc426ae6b` has equivalent production/build inputs: intervening UI changes are the cap scalar and media-test readiness. Candidate: `5b15500f206dea340b156d593544a90e7de00499` (production build source `a2115bd90294ffa1024859f4e42f5d48b6ba6d04`; subsequent change is only the cap scalar/comment). Both use identical fixed build metadata and all 29 canonical generated plugin inputs.

| Surface | Base gzip | Head gzip | Change | Product JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,327 B | 316,324 B | −3 B | 7 → 7 |
| Ordinary Chat | 1,353,266 B | 1,351,649 B | −1,617 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 826,422 B | 824,777 B | −1,645 B | 17 → 17 |
| Chat reload with Online restored | 1,366,899 B | 1,367,822 B | **+923 B** | **28 → 29** |

Startup CSS stays 41,124 B in one request. Ordinary route CSS changes by one hash byte. The candidate's deferred `app-sidebar-online` chunk is 2,539 B gzip; loading it again for the restored pane outweighs the shared-graph saving.

The restored-path capture uses the existing synthetic Team cold-load fixture with one plain-text transcript and 120 people. It waits for the actual Online IndexedDB write, performs a direct reload with HTTP cache disabled, and waits for the restored selected Online pane, final person row and visible transcript. Live roster replies are delayed 500 ms on reload so the stored pane paints before the live result settles. Unique production JavaScript requests are mapped to shipped `.gz` sidecars; the seven identical synthetic plugin scripts are recorded separately and excluded from product bytes/requests. Both sides restore successfully, with zero page errors. No new production build was needed for this check.

## Other proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Exact-head full CI [39882286698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39882286698) | All 71 jobs passed or skipped, including all nine UI E2E shards, UI units, browser extension and both real-Gateway shards |
| UI typecheck; controller/lifecycle guards; targeted format; diff check | Passed |
| Directly affected Online/people units | 111/111 passed; earlier session-row suite 20/20 passed |
| Independent complete-diff and integration reviews | Scoped clean |
| Production Chromium delayed/rejected import, collapse/reopen, current presence, native-header geometry | Passed; loading and loaded headers both 44 px, no zero-height frame in 14 samples |
| Production Knip | Sole inherited unused Telegram test-support file; reproduced on exact main, no ignore added |
| Fresh paired timing on this integrated graph | Intentionally not run: restored-path byte gate failed |

Earlier timing belongs to earlier graphs and is not current-head proof. Earlier CI exposed two test readiness assumptions at the new lazy boundary; those now await the visible Online state while retaining their assertions. A real-Gateway shutdown failure passed its exact focused replay; the later full CI above passed.

Production UI LOC: **968 → 1,014 (+46)**. No new effects, listeners, DOM queries or owner API calls. The added source mainly supplies the local loading/error header.

## Synthetic before/after screenshots

Full frames were inspected. Loaded/reopened Online views are pixel-identical; the restored-path captures also show the same pane and transcript. Existing public images remain below.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Online loaded | ![Before: Online loaded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb4c3372-1fbb-4b2d-a45a-160061807464) | ![After: Online loaded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9402dfd-9680-4040-9905-5e8557e64e8b) |
| Online reopened after presence update | ![Before: Online reopened after presence update](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bea2c55e-59b0-41df-bffa-53fd744c9768) | ![After: Online reopened after presence update](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d92ea9e-ba37-4e4a-8bd9-8c1db96e7f86) |

prs.title: feat(release): validate Windows-node releases and main
prs.body:
## Summary

Add Windows-node compatibility coverage to Full Release Validation: the same immutable OpenClaw candidate is tested against the current stable Windows-node release, production alpha release, and an exact `main` source commit. Main does not currently provide these three lanes.

**Status: refreshed, but not merge-ready.** The missing-alpha claim in the previous description was stale. The live resolver now selects `v2026.9.8-1` and `v2026.10.5-alpha.4`; remaining blockers are concrete defects in the external Windows-node workflow/harness, listed below. No release was published or full release workflow dispatched for this refresh.

## Architecture and conflict repair

- Preserve the current phased release architecture. The shared planner owns selection; Windows-node runs in the candidate phase only, with canonical candidate acquisition, candidate-child routing, and child evidence sealing. It never runs in the independent phase.
- Keep three distinct consumers of one immutable package. Stable allows only a structured `PROTOCOL_MISMATCH`; prerelease and main must pass. A selected skipped lane fails the verifier.
- Keep Windows-node implementation in its repository. The immutable reusable workflow remains `d3ed6c78bf1448444d0e8618b24848bb88121b40`, whose workflow bytes match inspected Windows-node main `f5978f0f47aa021aa732dafc86e76044c4a3b622`.
- Accept documented stable correction tags (`vX.Y.Z-N`), fixing selection of the obsolete unsuffixed stable release. Keep latest-by-publication selection, exact tag/source/asset/digest binding, and rejection of superseded or artifact-less alpha releases.
- Integrate `windows-node` into the CLI, both input validators, execution plan, package demand, and focused rerun handling. Move documentation into the current split reference pages; do not restore retired shell scheduling or the old summary routing map.
- Retain package metadata in the shared package artifact for the external consumer. No runtime, config, database, migration, or installed-update behavior changes.

## Review disposition and remaining external blockers

The old request for caller-identity rejection proof does not establish a privilege escalation here. Direct callee inspection shows caller-scoped `actions: read`/`contents: read`, GitHub-hosted Windows, no inherited secrets, and no publication operation. OIDC binds the called YAML revision; it is provenance, not caller authorization. Do not add speculative caller-auth machinery without a concrete protected effect.

The callee does have actionable defects:

1. **Evidence name collision:** all three invocations upload `windows-node-release-candidate-e2e-${run_id}-${run_attempt}` without a lane discriminator. The later uploads collide. [External upload owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/d3ed6c78bf1448444d0e8618b24848bb88121b40/.github/workflows/release-candidate-e2e.yml#L441).
2. **Prerelease candidate rejection:** validation-package setup calls the stable-only exact-version validator, rejecting an OpenClaw beta candidate before compatibility testing. Use the existing package-version owner without weakening normal stable-install policy. [External setup owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/f5978f0f47aa021aa732dafc86e76044c4a3b622/src/OpenClaw.SetupEngine/GatewayInstallPolicy.cs#L182).
3. **Unimplemented mismatch exception:** the workflow reads `OPENCLAW_E2E_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH_RESULT`, but inspected current/stable test sources do not produce it. Expected stable protocol incompatibility therefore fails instead of yielding the declared structured outcome. [Consumer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/d3ed6c78bf1448444d0e8618b24848bb88121b40/.github/workflows/release-candidate-e2e.yml#L418).

The YAML pin is also not a test-harness pin: tests/setup are built from the selected app source SHA. Repairs only on Windows-node main cannot repair historical release-source harnesses. The external owner should separate maintained harness identity from released app identity, then publish a reviewed immutable workflow revision and prove the three lanes. Merely refreshing this PR's pin changes nothing because current workflow bytes are identical.

## Validation

Refreshed head: `81247dd12cdcc6a813d297e60f680f0268eeab6b`.

- Integrated main commit `718bd3d69d293d992212bf1c4cc685d9551ddfc2`; retained the original PR history in a merge refresh rather than force-pushing rewritten ancestry.
- Focused production-path/workflow/planner/summary proof: **357 passed, 670 outside the selected scope, across six files**; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <six affected files> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot -t '<affected release contracts>'`, **103.73 seconds wall time**. The unfiltered run was interrupted during unchanged admission-scale tests; it is not claimed passing. CI seconds are pending on the refreshed head.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mts`: passed (pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated CI ownership, composite interpolation, conflict markers).
- Tooling test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json`), targeted lint, formatting, docs index, and diff check against integrated main: passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview through P2: no new actionable caller findings; documented external defects remain unresolved. Subsequent changes were test-only lint fixes (braces and shadowed variable names).
- Simplification: retained current planner/summary owners instead of restoring obsolete shell/group-map implementations, moved docs to their current owners, and removed incidental resolver source-string assertions while retaining executable resolver and skipped-lane regressions.

Prior August green CI is not current-head release proof. No current-head full Windows E2E pass is claimed.

Live read-only resolver proof selected:

- stable `v2026.9.8-1`, source `2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114`, canonical hashed x64 Tray ZIP;
- prerelease `v2026.10.5-alpha.4`, source `f81edef9a06222e4eea5a93dd21ecfb7e3002c10`, canonical hashed x64 Tray ZIP.

The prerequisite release artifacts exist. Full Windows execution remains unverified on the refreshed PR head and must not be inferred from resolver/unit tests.

prs.title: fix: reject channel names without message destinations
prs.body:
Related: #91372

## What Problem This Solves

An inferred outbound channel can mistake its own bare name for a destination, producing misleading provider errors or selecting an unintended native recipient.

## User Impact

Ambiguous channel-only targets fail closed with destination guidance. Exact directory matches, explicit handles, numeric/chat IDs, conversation references, provider-qualified targets, and native destinations with an explicit or contextual channel remain supported.

Compatibility decision: an implicit same-name native recipient must select the channel explicitly or use a provider-qualified or exact-directory destination.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared outbound resolver owns namespace recognition and recipient policy. Cron, proactive delivery, and message actions use the same boundary; restrictive channel-selection provenance survives ordinary and scheduled Gateway delegation. The optional false-only wire field can restrict native namespace acceptance, never grant it.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(config): redact authored credential fallbacks in public snapshots
prs.body:
Closes #168147
Related: #168109 (closed by its author, unmerged).

## What Problem This Solves

Credential fields containing `${VAR:-fallback}` were treated as secret-free environment references. Even when `VAR` supplied a different active credential, authenticated `config.get` could expose the authored fallback through its parsed and raw views. The shared redaction owner also serves `/config show` and configuration response previews.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing environment-template parser to distinguish a bare or empty-fallback reference from a literal credential. Redact nonempty fallbacks using the existing sentinel. Withhold the raw view when an authored sensitive fallback is present: resolved-value replacement cannot safely redact a different, possibly JSON5-escaped fallback. This uses the existing `raw: null` contract; the UI already reconstructs its editable view from the structured snapshot.

Existing-solutions preflight: SecretRefs avoid embedding credentials and remain the recommended authoring option, but they do not repair redaction of existing supported fallback templates. This repair belongs in `src/config/redact-snapshot.ts`; no plugin, library, or additional redaction system is needed. The unmerged previous proposal is closed; a fresh issue/timeline and semantic PR search found no active implementation or human rejection.

## User Impact

Fallback credential material stays hidden in public configuration projections. Bare `${VAR}`, empty `${VAR:-}`, blank strings, and nonsensitive fallbacks stay editable. Actual sentinel-based configuration writes continue to preserve the authored template and its environment binding. Configurations with sensitive fallbacks receive the existing structured-editor representation instead of raw text; comments/formatting are not exposed through that raw view.

No configuration/default, protocol, schema, dependency, migration, authorization, or provider-routing change. This is redaction hardening within the existing authenticated operator surface, not a claim of unauthenticated access. Security-owner review before merge remains appropriate.

## Evidence

### CI attribution check — October 18, 2026

The contributor head remains `a1176b96f21666576d2fdd7f02bf48bdde63c530`; no code or head update was made.
