prs.title: fix(doctor): complete legacy heartbeat migration without blocking startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor leaving an upgraded Gateway unable to start when legacy heartbeat configuration meets a retained plugin migration or existing heartbeat scratch.

Fixes #181110, Fixes #181013. Thanks @jalehman and @hartmark for the reproductions and source traces.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` completes the heartbeat-to-Automations cutover without deleting existing scratch or requiring manual SQLite edits. When scratch differs from `HEARTBEAT.md`, or was explicitly unset, Doctor preserves both originals and prints a notice. The automation keeps its existing scratch; operators can review the retained file and copy wanted instructions later. Repeated Doctor runs preserve that choice.

Unreadable sources, failed writes, and conflicting migration ownership still stop unsafe changes. No configuration, CLI, dependency, or schema additions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin settlement required a fully schema-valid config before the later heartbeat repair could remove the retired key. Settlement now checks source readability and unchanged source inputs under the existing source/lifecycle locks, allowing Doctor's subsequent config repair to run.

The scratch migration already preserved differing content safely, but classified that preservation as a fatal warning. It now reports a nonfatal notice. Candidate admission retains source-safety and monitor-ownership checks while dropping its duplicate scratch veto. Four scratch helpers return to private scope. Production delta: +26/-65 (net -39); tests: +119/-17 (net +102); docs: +16/-6.

## Evidence

- Follow-up CI repair: the update-admission consumer now expects exit 0 for conflicting operator scratch, verifies every input file remains byte-identical before activation, then runs the real Doctor migration and checks the complete scratch row, retained `HEARTBEAT.md`, ordinary automation, and nonfatal notice. No other old scratch-refusal assertions remain in update-admission or Doctor heartbeat tests. All 11 tests in `update-command-admit.heartbeat.test.ts` pass on Node (30.53 s wall) and Bun (30.94 s wall); scoped CLI-update test types, oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review is clean. This follow-up changes tests only (+43/-8).

- Both regressions fail on base `7a23014fd6ec`: retained stateless plugin settlement throws `Plugin migration source config changed or could not be read`; differing hashless scratch throws during candidate admission and Doctor retirement.
- The plugin regression setup now seeds the pending receipt through the canonical persistence API instead of running Doctor twice: 32.0 s → 8.82 s on the failing base, with the same failure.
- Isolated real CLI: base Doctor exits 1 with the reported settlement error. Fixed Doctor exits 0, removes legacy heartbeat config, completes the plugin migration, and leaves one ordinary `agentTurn` automation. Read-only database comparison confirms scratch content, revision, source hash and timestamp are unchanged; `HEARTBEAT.md` remains byte-identical.

- Node 26.12.1: **203 tests passed across 10 files**, including every direct/one-barrel consumer selected from the changed owners. Pinned Bun: **32 tests passed across both touched suites**. The new plugin regression takes 18.0 s on Node / 14.8 s on Bun; the two new scratch cases take 148/419 ms on Node and 150/386 ms on Bun.
- The second isolated `doctor --fix` also exits 0. Read-only comparison again confirms one automation, retired heartbeat config, byte-identical source, and an unchanged complete scratch row.
- Core and Doctor-test TypeScript checks, scoped oxlint/oxfmt, Madge (0 cycles), and `git diff --check` pass. Isolated P0–P2 diff review is clean.
- Existing multi-pass integration cases are slow: plugin deferral's broken-contract case takes 47.2 s Node / 56.3 s Bun; its unavailable/replacement-owner recovery case takes 90.1 s Node / 62.5 s Bun; the newer-obligation case takes 36.4 s Bun, and stale-candidate recovery takes 56.3 s Bun. The unavailable-owner repeated Doctor/startup case takes 63.2 s Node. These cases intentionally invoke real Doctor preparation repeatedly across distinct package/config states; their behavior and timeouts are unchanged. The full Node command takes 825.4 s, including shared runtime preparation; the two-suite Bun command takes 450.8 s.

The synthetic fixture disables bundled plugins and has no provider credentials; its unrelated plugin/model readiness notices are expected. The host volume also prevents automatic recovery-copy staging because of a writable ancestor; a separate byte-verified copy of the synthetic database and source file was retained before repair. No operator state or existing Gateway was used.

The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof. No remote leases were used.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and verification commands</summary>

The CLI used isolated synthetic state and a free port under the worktree. The failing baseline combined a retained stateless plugin with legacy heartbeat config. The fixed and repeat runs additionally contained differing hashless scratch and the original `HEARTBEAT.md`.

```sh
HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/live/home" \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live/state" \
OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 \
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external \
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PARENT_ALLOWS_GATEWAY_SERVICE_REPAIR=0 \
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PARENT_ALLOWS_GATEWAY_ACTIVATION=0 \
pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
```

Local test/check commands used an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `.artifacts/`:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent.heartbeat-migration.test.ts \
  src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-source-archive.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-cadence-migration.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.unavailable-owner.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-write-ownership.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-model.test.ts \
  src/config/config-startup-corpus.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun \
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH="$PWD/.artifacts/bun-fs-module-cache" \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-admit.heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-admit.heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --incremental
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts
```

Scoped oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` also passed. Isolated P0–P2 diff review reported no actionable findings.

</details>

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing FRV decision, diagnostic-drain, verifier, and manifest owners evaluate policy from admitted release tooling while candidate tests remain frozen. Publication accepts only successful authenticated FRV evidence, never a runtime waiver or a publisher-side override.

The current-main repair preserves recovery and changelog-reuse changes, shared admission fixtures, and original sealed coverage-plan digest ordering. It also removes a retired Telegram-waiver reference from main's new plan-sealing step.

prs.title: fix(browser): isolate executable detection fixtures from host files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser executable-discovery tests consult the host filesystem instead of their access-permission fixture, rejecting synthetic browser paths and blocking otherwise unrelated repairs.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176119

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Browser CI can validate executable filtering and cache precedence independently of browsers installed on the runner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connect the native `fs.accessSync` object to the existing fixture mock, alongside the existing `statSync` bridge. Keep all assertions and cleanup unchanged.

This is the browser-only contribution from @yinx65588-boop in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176119, independently reproduced on current-main source and credited in the commit. That broad PR includes unrelated changes and has non-green CI; it stays open for its original scope. This standalone prerequisite avoids importing those changes into blocked repairs.

## Evidence

- Base `9395f44dccb97c38cec985c0a480daabc43878d9`: the default-browser fixture failed 25 tests and passed 3. Synthetic Linux/Windows paths were rejected, and the macOS Edge case fell back to host Chrome.
- With this one-line change: the default-browser fixture and Playwright cache sibling passed all 50 tests across two files, sequentially with one worker.
- Both runs used the normal repository Vitest wrapper and browser config, Vitest 5.0.3, verified pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`, and an independent frozen-lock installation on macOS ARM64.
- Targeted native typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh independent full-context review reported no actionable findings.
- Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: +1 line. Existing access-denial, directory rejection, cache layout and precedence assertions remain intact.
- Historical contributor proof: https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39726999713. Current proof above is separate; Linux runner coverage and broad required checks belong to this PR's CI.

prs.title: feat(tools): per-turn per-target send budget guard for message tools
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-turn, per-target outbound send guard shared by the `message` and `conversations_send` tools to curb within-turn duplicate-answer storms.

The existing loop detector hashes full tool params, so a model that re-sends the same answer with slightly reworded text produces a distinct hash every time and stays invisible to it — a single healthy `200` run can emit six reworded variants of one reply. This adds a lightweight ledger, independent of the loop detector and its default-off switch, that counts *successful* deliveries per (turn, target).

Closes #119992

## What Problem This Solves

A model can emit many reworded copies of the same reply within one turn. The existing tool-loop detector hashes the full stable tool-parameter object, so each reworded body is a distinct call and evades it entirely — a single healthy run can fan out six variants of one answer to the same recipient. Nothing in the ordinary send path accounts for repeated deliveries per turn.

This change adds a shared per-agent-turn, per-destination ledger observed by both the `message` tool and `conversations_send`, giving the model a default-on nudge to finalize after the first repeat and an opt-in hard cap that blocks further sends before dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The loop detector cannot catch reworded duplicates (it is content-hash based and default-off), so the guard must be independent of it and count *successful* deliveries, not param hashes.
- The two send tools reach the same recipients, so the ledger has to be shared and keyed on one canonical destination identity, or alternating the tools would evade it.
- The ledger must run on the ordinary Gateway execution path (not just embedded/subagent paths), which requires the active run ID to reach the tools that gate on it.

Seven runtime-path defects surfaced in review are fixed here so the guard actually protects the claimed workflow:

- **Gateway path dropped the run ID.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwarded `runId` to the mediated coding tools but not to `createOpenClawTools`, so the `message` tool and `conversations_send` received `runId=undefined` and their ledger contexts declined to activate — the nudge and cap were silently inert for every Gateway-scoped turn. `params.runId` is now forwarded to `createOpenClawTools`; it stays `undefined` on the single-shot HTTP `tools.invoke` path, which correctly leaves the ledger off there.
- **Current-source key split.** `resolveOutboundActionRoute` keyed current-source sends on a literal `<current-source>` sentinel, while `conversations_send` keys on the resolved concrete target. The two never matched, so alternating a no-target source reply with `conversations_send` to the same peer split the count across two ledger slots and bypassed both the nudge and the cap. The current source is now resolved to its concrete target (`currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId`), failing open when it cannot be resolved (mirroring the existing multi-target bail), so both tools share one slot for the same recipient.
- **Routable target not threaded through the Gateway/CLI-loopback chain.** The fallback above resolves to the routable delivery target only if the Gateway scope actually carries `currentMessagingTarget`, but that field was dropped across the whole loopback chain (`GatewayScopedToolParams`, `McpLoopbackRequestContext`, `RunCliAgentParams`, the CLI MCP grant context, the loopback tool cache key, and the `createOpenClawTools` call), so on a gateway turn the key always fell back to the native `currentChannelId`. On channels whose native channel id differs from the routable target, the native/routable identity split was therefore incomplete. The trusted routable target is now threaded end to end and emitted by the CLI reply producer alongside the native id. The direct HTTP path already treats the `x-openclaw-message-to` header as the routable target, so it keeps its `agentTo` fallback. Security: the routable target is trusted only from the server-minted bound grant context — the grant-authenticated header branch fails closed and a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header can never override the bound value.
- **Ledger key was not canonicalized before admission.** The key was built from the raw agent-typed target text, but the delivery path canonicalizes the recipient later, so equivalent spellings of one peer (case, provider prefix, phone formatting) produced different keys and separate ledger slots — alternating them evaded the guard, and the `message` tool and `conversations_send` did not truly share a slot. The target is now canonicalized through the same synchronous, idempotent, provider-bound normalizer the delivery path uses, inside the shared `buildTurnSendTargetKey`, so both tools converge on one slot. Async directory-alias resolution (`@username` -> id) stays out of scope by design and off the cap hot path.
- **Queued was counted as a delivery.** `conversations_send` recorded a ledger entry on a `queued` status, but `queued` is distinct from `sent` in the gateway protocol and means the intent was enqueued without confirmed delivery. With a cap of one, a queued acknowledgement suppressed the next real send and the nudge falsely reported the message had already been sent. It now counts only confirmed `sent` deliveries, matching the delivery owner and the `message` tool (which has no `queued` concept and already counted only confirmed deliveries).

- **Overlapping same-session runs evicted each other's counts.** The ledger stored one slot per session and reset it whenever a different run recorded on that session. Concurrent foreground turns can share one session key with distinct run ids (see `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`, which starts run A, completes run B on the same session, then resumes A), so an A -> B -> A interleave let run B evict run A's slot; when run A resumed, its per-target count read zero and both the nudge and the opt-in cap were silently bypassed — exactly under the concurrency the cap exists to protect. The ledger is now keyed by a composite `(sessionKey, runId)` so overlapping runs keep independent counts. Each slot stays authoritative for the whole run lifetime (no idle expiry) and is deleted by the run owner at its terminal boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun`, wired into the embedded runner's fallback-chain `finally`); terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — there is deliberately no size-based eviction, because evicting a slot while its run is still live (an idle run while many turns execute concurrently) would silently zero that run's committed counts and release the opt-in cap mid-turn. Retained slots are bounded by the number of concurrently live runs.
- **An idempotent message replay was blocked by the cap.** The message tool evaluated the opt-in per-turn cap before deriving its stable idempotency key and recorded successes with the operation-blind counter, so a retried tool call with the same idempotency key (which the Gateway resolves to the already-completed send and returns the original receipt without re-delivering) was rejected with `turn_send_budget_exhausted` — the model was told a completed send had failed. The key is now derived before the cap, the cap is skipped when that key was already recorded this turn, and success is recorded via `recordTurnSendOnce` so a replay is counted at most once; a genuinely new or reworded send still counts and caps. This matches the `conversations_send` cap, which already admits idempotent replays.
## User Impact

- **Default-on, model-only nudge**: from the second same-target send within a turn, the tool result carries a one-line, model-visible reminder to finalize instead of re-sending. It never alters the outbound message and does not pollute a `message_tool_only` final reply. Opt out via `tools.message.turnSendNudge: false` (per-agent override inherits the global).
- **Opt-in hard cap (default off)**: `tools.message.maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget` blocks a send before dispatch once the cap is reached, returning `turn_send_budget_exhausted`. Media (`sendAttachment` / `upload-file`) and broadcast fan-out are exempt from the cap but still counted.
- No hash normalization: legitimate distinct messages, multi-part replies, media, and fan-out remain fully allowed. Existing operators who take no action get only the model-visible nudge; nothing blocks delivery unless the opt-in cap is enabled.

## Design notes

- A "turn" is one agent run (`runId`). A slot is authoritative for the entire run lifetime — including long tool waits and provider-fallback candidates that reuse the `runId` — so the opted-in cap holds for the whole turn; the run owner deletes the slot at the terminal run boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` from the embedded runner fallback-chain `finally`), and that terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — retained slots are bounded by concurrently live runs, and no size-based eviction ever removes a live run's counts. Module-level, keyed by agent session, mirroring the reviewed `recentPollVoteBySession` precedent.
- Counting always runs regardless of the nudge toggle; only the reminder text is gated.
- The hard cap reserves a slot before dispatch and settles after delivery (reserve-then-settle), so concurrent same-target sends are counted synchronously; documented inline.

## Evidence

Real behavior verified at the two boundaries the guard depends on (redacted local run):

- **Gateway boundary — ledger activates only when the run ID flows through.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ runId, surface: "loopback" })` produces a `message` tool whose per-turn cap engages; reverting the `runId` forward makes this fail. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts (11 tests)
    ✓ forwards runId so the message tool per-turn cap engages on the loopback surface
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  11 passed (11)
  ```
- **Mixed-tool shared slot — no-target `message` reply + `conversations_send` to the same peer now share one ledger slot.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` the second tool is capped; reverting to the `<current-source>` sentinel makes it deliver (`status: "sent"`) instead of `suppressed`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts (15 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)
  ```
- **Routable-target threading boundary — native id != routable target still share one ledger slot.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `currentChannelId: "D123"` (native) and `currentMessagingTarget: "user:U123"` (routable) differing: a pre-seeded routable slot and a no-target source send resolve to the same key and hit the cap. Reverting the routable-param forward makes this fail (verified). The header fail-closed invariant is covered: a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header leaves the bound routable target undefined. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts / mcp-http.request.test.ts / mcp-grant-context.test.ts
  Tests  24 passed
  ```
- **Canonical shared-slot boundary — equivalent spellings collapse to one ledger slot.** `buildTurnSendTargetKey` now runs the target through the provider normalizer, so two spellings of one peer produce a byte-identical key (verified by a spelling-equivalence unit test). Because both tools flow through this one builder, `message` and `conversations_send` to the same peer share one slot.
- **Queued does not consume a slot.** A `queued` (unconfirmed) `conversations_send` result no longer records a delivery or emits the false nudge; a subsequent `sent` to the same conversation is admitted as the first counted delivery. Verified by a queued-then-sent regression under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` plus a table over `suppressed`/`queued`/`unknown`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts / conversation-tools.test.ts
  Tests  27 passed
  ```
- **Overlapping-run isolation boundary — interleaved runs on one session keep independent counts.** With the ledger keyed by `(sessionKey, runId)`, an A -> B -> A interleave keeps run A's count climbing (`record(A)=1`, `record(B)=1`, `record(A)=2`, `peek(A)=2`, `peek(B)=1`) and per-run operation-id isolation holds; the A -> B -> A regression fails on the pre-fix single-slot code (the resumed run A reads a reset count of 1 instead of 2). The new tests are anchored to the concurrent-same-session behavior proven in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (16 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)
  ```
- **Idempotent-replay-past-cap boundary — a retried send at the cap reaches delivery dedup.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, a first send is admitted and counted, a replay of the same tool call (same idempotency key) is not cap-blocked and returns the completed receipt without double-counting or a false nudge, and a genuinely different send is still capped. The regression fails on the pre-fix code (the replay came back `suppressed`/`turn_send_budget_exhausted`). Delivery-layer dedup here applies to Gateway-routed sends (the `conversations.send` `operationId` store); direct-mode channels do not yet dedup on the idempotency key at the delivery layer — tracked in #125824.
- Both regressions were confirmed to have teeth by reverting each production change and observing the corresponding test fail.
- Full suite for the feature: `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint --type-aware`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.




- **Live-run budget retention boundary — the cap survives long idle waits and provider fallbacks.** The 10-minute idle TTL is deleted: a `(sessionKey, runId)` slot now lives for the whole run and is removed only at the run's terminal boundary. Regressions (fake timers): a capped run stays `exhausted` after an idle interval far past the old TTL (this fails on the pre-fix TTL code — verified by temporarily restoring the prune), a committed operation is still admitted as a `replay` across the same idle wait, and `clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` deletes only the exact `(session, run)` slot (siblings on the same session and same-runId slots on other sessions stay intact; missing scope/slot is a no-op). Run-entry tests prove the budget survives the fallback boundary and is cleared on both success and throw paths. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  embedded-agent-runner  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.test.ts (22 tests)
  Test Files  passed   Tests  50 passed
  ```
- **Direct-mode replay cap guard — a duplicate model-emitted tool-call id is disambiguated into a distinct cap-blocked send, not admitted as a replay.** The discriminating regression drives the real streaming normalization (`wrapStreamFnTrimToolCallNames` -> `normalizeToolCallIdsInMessage`): a model response emitting the same `message` tool-call id twice with byte-identical arguments is rewritten to two distinct ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys and the second is cap-blocked with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result while the runner is invoked exactly once. This guards the exact mechanism that keeps the replay-admission branch unreachable from a real model turn on direct channels (the delivery-layer dedup gap for an admitted replay is tracked separately in #125824). Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (253 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  253 passed (253)
  ```

- **Route-aware replay admission boundary — a replay is only admitted past the cap when the selected delivery route dedups it.** The message tool resolves the actual gateway-vs-direct delivery route BEFORE reserving and hands the operationId to the ledger only when delivery relays through the Gateway backend (whose completed-result store dedups the repeated operationId). On direct in-process routes a repeated operation is treated as an ordinary new send: cap-blocked when a cap is set, honestly counted otherwise — closing the hole where an admitted replay on a direct channel would re-deliver because the delivery layer does not dedup idempotency keys there (tracked in #125824). Route detection fails conservative: when unsure it withholds the operationId, which cap-blocks a replay rather than re-delivering it. Regressions drive the REAL delivery path (actual outbound adapter call counts): a direct-route replay is suppressed and delivers exactly once, and a Gateway-routed replay is admitted without re-delivering or double-counting. Both fail on the pre-fix unconditional replay admission. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (254 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  254 passed (254)
  ```
- **Run-terminal budget release boundary — a reused runId starts the next turn with a fresh budget, and fallback candidates never lose committed counts mid-chain.** `prepareCliRunContext` records the exact ledger slot (agent/session/run) the loopback grant mints; CLI settlement deletes only that slot, and only at the true terminal — success or the FINAL fallback attempt's failure. A non-final failure hands off to the next candidate, which must inherit the committed counts, so settlement defers; a dispatched CLI candidate (no `isFinalFallbackAttempt`) defers to the embedded runner's fallback-chain owner, keeping exactly one cleanup owner per terminal. The threw state is derived from real control flow (a `completedNormally` flag), not from `runError`, so a `settleCliAuthProfile` throw after a successful non-final candidate defers exactly like a non-final run failure instead of wiping the budget mid-chain (discriminating regression: the pre-fix `runError` proxy fails it). Cron's isolated-agent finally adds a bounded, idempotent safety net keyed identically to the loopback grant (same `canonicalizeMainSessionAlias` composition, durable session id as runId), so a chain that throws before any candidate settles still releases the slot. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts (18 tests)
  cron            src/cron/isolated-agent/run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts (1 test)
  agents-tools    src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  47 passed (47)
  ```

### Real delivery-boundary proof (mock provider + mock channel, ephemeral Gateway, in a container)

Added `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: a real-behavior proof that boots an ephemeral Gateway child with the mock-openai provider and the `qa-channel` synthetic transport, then exercises the shared per-turn send ledger at the real delivery boundary (Gateway + qa-channel outbound bus), not by stubbing `callGateway`. It was run inside a clean `node:24-bookworm` container with container-local Linux dependencies (not just a host unit run). All scenarios pass and the run emits a machine-readable verdict:

```
test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts (8 tests)
  ✓ sanity: a plain qa-channel DM turn delivers one outbound reply
  ✓ scenario 1: second confirmed message send in one turn nudges and both deliveries land
  ✓ scenario 2: hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed conversations_send result
  ✓ scenario 3: a suppressed message send does not charge the per-turn budget
  ✓ scenario 4: idempotent conversations_send replay does not re-deliver or double count
  ✓ scenario 5: two concurrent distinct-op sends to one target admit exactly one under the cap
  ✓ scenario 6: a model-repeated direct message send under the cap is disambiguated and cap-blocked (exactly-once delivery) — proves the cap-block path, NOT idempotent admission
  ✓ scenario 7: a spoofed attach-grant principal is refused before any delivery I/O (authority chain)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Verdict (`pass: true`), summarized per scenario:

- **Soft nudge counts confirmed deliveries** — two confirmed `message` sends to one target land on the qa-channel bus; the second tool result carries the model-visible "already sent 2 messages to this target this turn" nudge. `deliveriesRecorded: 2`, ledger `{ "qa-channel:qa-operator": 2 }`.
- **Hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed result** — with `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, only one delivery reaches the bus; the second `conversations_send` returns `status: "suppressed"` with details that pass `Value.Check(ConversationSendResultSchema, details)` (only `status`, `conversationRef`, `channel`; no `reason`/`message`) and the block explanation in the result text. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`.
- **Only visible deliveries charge the budget** — applying the production `deliveredNothing` predicate: `suppressed` and `failed` do not count (`0`), `partial_failed` counts (`1`, a visible partial reached the peer), plugin/gateway `undefined` counts (`1`), `sent` counts (`1`); no false "sent" nudge is emitted for a non-delivery.
- **Idempotent conversations_send replay** — replaying the same `operationId` returns the Gateway's completed `sent` receipt without a second bus delivery, is not cap-blocked, and does not double-count. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`, ledger stays at `1`.
- **Concurrent distinct-op sends under the cap (reserve-then-settle)** — two parallel `conversations_send` calls with distinct operationIds (NOT a replay) to the same conversation under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`: the first in-flight reservation counts toward the cap synchronously, so the second call is exhausted before it reaches the Gateway — exactly one delivery lands on the bus and the ledger commits exactly one send. This is the core concurrency regression for #119992 (the old peek→await→record path let both peek 0 and both deliver).
- **Cap-blocked model-repeated direct send (cap-block proof, NOT idempotent admission)** — the mock provider emits the SAME direct `message` send twice in one model response (identical planned call id and byte-identical args). The runtime disambiguates the duplicate model-emitted ids into two distinct tool-call ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys: the first delivers, and the second is cap-blocked before dispatch with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result fed back to the model. Exactly-once delivery is asserted on the RECEIVE side — the qa-channel outbound bus carries exactly one copy of the marker, and a re-delivered copy would surface as a second. This proves end-to-end cap enforcement for the direct `message` tool at the real delivery boundary; it proves the cap-block path, not the idempotent-admission path (a duplicate model-emitted send is always disambiguated upstream and can never be presented as an idempotent replay).
- **Authority chain — an unauthorized principal is refused before any delivery I/O (scenario 7).** The harness's own `attach.grant` method mints a real non-owner grant; the test then drives the REAL MCP loopback HTTP entry with that grant plus spoofed delivery-authority headers (`x-session-key`, message channel, account id, current channel id, and `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` pointed at a registered conversation) — every hop is the genuine defense, with no mocked resolver output: `validateMcpLoopbackRequest` → `resolveAttachGrant` → `resolveMcpRequestContext` (grant branch forces every spoofable header, including the routable target, to undefined) → owner-only tool deny. Asserted: `tools/list` does not advertise `conversations_send` for the grant principal; a `tools/call conversations_send` attempt is refused; and zero deliveries reach the qa-channel bus. Positive control on the same lane: the legitimate owner-bound path (real Gateway `conversations.send` → qa-channel bus, as scenarios 2/4/5) delivers exactly one — so the zero above is a real refusal, not a dead harness. Verdict entries carry no tokens.

Full unit suite for the feature (`turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` + `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` + cron `run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts`) passes; `tsgo:core`/`tsgo:extensions`/`tsgo:test:root` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.

### Final-head validation (HEAD `782540cd69f`)

Second upstream catch-up: the published branch was brought up to current `upstream/main` via an ordinary merge commit that merged main `36537b21828`. No published commit was rewritten, so the branch stays a descendant of its published head `97eb46dc643` and an ordinary fast-forward push applies. This second merge only resolved the generated config-documentation baseline conflicts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` / `.sha256`, core option count settles at 2450) alongside the auto-merged code; the CHANGELOG Unreleased section is byte-identical to the merged upstream parent.

Re-verified on this final head `782540cd69f`:

- **Real qa-lab per-turn-send-budget E2E: 8/8 passing.** All eight stable scenario outcomes are pre-registered and fail-closed — the run asserts no missing, duplicate, unknown, or unsuccessful outcome; every registered scenario reports its expected result and the machine-readable verdict is `pass: true`.
- **Typecheck green:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, and `tsgo:test:root` all exit 0.
- **Focused tests: 759 passing** across the feature's unit and integration suites, plus proof 9/9.
- **Config docs / lint / format / diff check green:** config docs generation, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- **Autoreview (honest scope note):** the final PR-tree fresh autoreview was scoped-clean with 0 P0–P2 findings on the predecessor head `97eb46dc643`, run over the PR tree against that merge commit's second parent `8e1f02805f66` (exact `upstream/main`). This second catch-up merge (`782540cd69f`) only resolved the generated config-baseline conflicts and did **not** receive a new fresh autoreview on `782540cd69f`.

Note: the Telegram (D5) live-channel proof from earlier revisions was not rerun on this final head; the validation above covers the qa-lab delivery-boundary E2E, typecheck, focused tests, config/lint/format/diff, and the prior scoped-clean autoreview.



### CI line-cap ratchet remediation (HEAD `4bcae80db14`)

CI job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed at `782540cd69f`: the send-budget work pushed eight grandfathered files past their `check:line-cap-ratchet` baseline (deterministic against the merge base `36537b21828`). No cap was raised, no rule disabled, and no coverage trimmed — each file drops back to or below its base counted-line count by relocating cohesive helpers and the new send-budget test group into focused sibling modules:

- `message-tool-execution.ts` → `message-tool-turn-send-budget.ts` (turn-send-budget resolve/reserve/settle/nudge orchestration).
- `message-tool.test.ts` → `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` for the per-turn-send-budget group; `createChannelPlugin` and the runner-input type shared via `message-tool.test-support.ts`. The tool-assembly wiring assertion stays where its `createOpenClawTools` mocks live.
- `command/attempt-execution.ts` → `attempt-execution-auth-profile.ts` (harness auth-profile selection).
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `auth-profile-resolution.ts` (CLI auth-profile resolution).

prs.title: fix(ui): announce Models provider read failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Models inserts provider-access and provider-usage read failures as ordinary text, so screen-reader users receive no alert when Refresh fails.

## User Impact

User impact: assistive technology can identify the existing read-error feedback as an alert. Provider filtering, retry behavior, visible text, layout, and saved settings are unchanged. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `renderProviderNoticeRow` is the shared owner for both failures. Give that row `role="alert"`, consistent with the neighboring model-discovery and installed-app errors, without moving focus or changing request ownership. This is independent of provider-card button naming (#178848).

## Evidence

- Real bundled Control UI, synthetic Gateway only, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, English/dark, 1440 × 1000. Both regression cases fail on base `d5ecc7da0ba84072600ddd046fef58fb8c8b58bb`: the failure text is visible but the alert count is 0 instead of 1. Both pass with the repair, including filter/clear and Retry/Refresh recovery. Each case confirms no credential save/logout request.
- Candidate: 2 E2E cases passed, 2.632s test-file runtime (35.41s invocation including production build). Base invocation: 61.30s including its cold build.
- Relevant render/catalog/load siblings: 56 tests across 3 files passed (11.25s Vitest duration; 15.05s wrapper wall).
- Production and UI-E2E TypeScript, targeted lint/format, controller guard, keyless English/i18n verification, and `git diff --check`: all passed (terminal exit 0).
- Simplification: one attribute at the existing owner, no new state, handlers, effects, DOM queries, styles, copy, or API contracts; production LOC unchanged. The focused regression uses the real bundled route because async owner-to-render delivery is the protected boundary.
- Independent Auto Review: accepted `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`). Full view/caller context limitation was resolved; unchanged layout wrappers were also inspected and add no live-region ancestry. Hosted CI will be reported separately; pending is not passing. This is Chromium accessibility-tree proof, not manual NVDA/VoiceOver certification. No overlay/focus behavior changed; the current E2E workflow selects Chromium for this suite.

### Actual accessibility snapshots

Before:
```yaml
- text: Provider access could not be refreshed. Try again.
- button "Retry"
```

After:
```yaml
- alert: Provider access could not be refreshed. Try again.
- button "Retry"
```

The supplemental usage case likewise changes from ordinary `text` to:
```yaml
- alert: Provider usage is unavailable; the last request failed. Refresh to retry.
```

### Inspected before/after screenshots

The images are intentionally pixel-identical: only the accessibility role changes. Both independent captures have SHA-256 `d16e6a7269882c6fb21b6c0efb0829af5d48fba1469c9f5872359443fec7d3fe` (129,119 bytes, 1440 × 1000).

| ![Before: provider read failure as ordinary text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9256edf3-27e0-4718-b935-8bcbc82ff22c) | ![After: provider read failure exposed as an alert](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c0768cb-9e66-4e6c-8ae7-1785264a5c95) |

prs.body:
Related: #111796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway model connection checks can test the wrong model when an agent overrides the default model or uses aliases.

## User Impact

User impact: Connection checks use the selected agent's configured model routes and aliases. No configuration migration is required. The probe output cap stays at 8 tokens; per review, raising it was split out of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing native model, fallback, utility-model, and alias resolvers instead of reading only the global default model. Preserve explicit empty fallback lists, disabled utility routing, model version suffixes, and catalog selection when no native default is configured.

## Evidence

- Before the production fix (new tests against `origin/main` `fbc99b8c03f` source): **4 failed / 14 passed** — agent primary and fallback overrides, explicit empty fallbacks with disabled utility routing, agent primary suppressing default fallbacks, and agent aliases overriding default aliases.
- After the fix (head `44f6ae52e63`): **18 passed** in `models-probe.test.ts` (Vitest shard 37.7 s), including an ACP-only case that must not invent a native default.
- Mock-export ratchet: **OK** (7913 grandfathered factories) after pruning the stale `models-probe.test.ts` entry.
- Gateway-method typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, two-file format check, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Review follow-up: the 8 → 64 output-cap change is removed and the duplicate inherited-defaults test row is dropped.
- `autoreview` in branch mode against `origin/main` (P0–P1, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`) was **scoped-clean** on the earlier head `d32ced30f73`; the follow-up commits only restore the output cap, drop one duplicate test row, and prune one baseline entry.

The regression tests exercise the real Gateway handler and model-selection resolvers with probe execution mocked. They verify the candidates passed to the probe runner, not live provider responses. The full suite was not run locally.

### Live Gateway proof

Run locally on 2026-10-21 (Node v24.19.0) at HEAD `44f6ae52e63`. "Before" swapped in only `src/gateway/server-methods/models-probe.ts` from `origin/main` (`fbc99b8c03f`); each version was rebuilt, then a real Gateway (`gateway run --port 20031 --bind custom --auth none`) was probed with `gateway call models.probe --params '{"provider":"proof-local","agentId":"<agent>"}'` against a local OpenAI-compatible fixture. prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

Ollama users whose prompt evaluation jumps after sub-agent or announce turns have no documented alternative.

They can try llmman as the local server.

llmman 0.1.562, CPU only, 5.4k-token prompts alternating between two system prompts (A, B, A, B) on `/v1/chat/completions` with `qwen3.5:0.8b`: each prompt took about 19 s on its first pass, then 0.1 to 0.2 s with 5397 and 5399 tokens cached. `llama3.2:1B-Q8_0` behaved the same (about 0.3 s). prs.title: docs(llmman): embedding server uses 1.8 GiB on a small host unless limited to one slot
prs.body:
Related: #164390

## What Problem This Solves

The documented llmman fix for an OOM-killed managed embedding server starts four slots by default, so it can use as much memory.

## User Impact

Small-host users get the setting that keeps llmman embeddings small.

## Why This Change Was Made

Names `LLMMAN_NUM_PARALLEL=1` in the llmman embeddings entry, which the llama.cpp troubleshooting bullet already links. The default itself is tracked in llmmanorg/llmman#686.

## Evidence

llmman 0.1.564, EmbeddingGemma, CPU, docker runtime. Default: `n_slots = 4`, 1.77 GiB. `LLMMAN_NUM_PARALLEL=1`: `n_slots = 1`, 501 MiB. A 16-chunk batch took 5.4 s vs 5.2 s. `format:docs:check`, `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-links`, `lint:docs` and `git diff --check` pass. `autoreview` is not installed here, so it was not run. This does not change OpenClaw's own managed server (#168020).
