prs.title: fix: recover sessions blocked by oversized workspace artifacts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local managed sandbox session has no supported recovery path when a newly generated file exceeds the reconciliation limit and blocks every later workspace preparation.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw sandbox recover --session <key> --path <relative-path>` to preserve one selected oversized file outside synchronization, then retry the session without losing its remaining source edits. Recovery is explicit and administrator-authorized. Recovered artifacts are retained outside automatic worktree cleanup; the operator owns their subsequent storage and cleanup.

Already-admitted source files, staged receipts, remote-worker workspaces, Git metadata, symlinks, and hardlinks remain unsupported/refused. File-size limits and ignore rules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed oversized checkpoint remains pending, and the next preparation retries it before the agent can run. The recovery command reuses the local workspace owner, reconciliation lease, sandbox quiescence, canonical source inventory, and no-overwrite filesystem move. It relocates only the explicitly selected new oversized retained file; ordinary preparation still owns settlement. A caller-supplied recovery ID permits a safe retry after a lost response.

No new database state, automatic deletion, or blanket cache exclusion is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through real sandbox preparation, Git staging, and SQLite projection state: a 64 MiB + 1 byte retained file rejects checkpoint and repeated later preparations while preserving the pending reference.
- Regression verifies explicit relocation, recovery-ID retry, source-edit settlement on the next preparation, preserved file size/content marker, and refusal of admitted source paths, traversal, symlinks, and hardlinks.
- Seven affected suites passed (119 tests, one existing skip); the final owner/schema and metadata-policy replay passed 104 tests.
- Core production typecheck and the four owning test typecheck graphs passed; scoped lint, formatting, documentation lint, protocol registry, and Swift/Kotlin protocol contract/determinism checks passed.
- Simplification reuses existing state/lease owners and removes duplicate metadata-read configuration. Independent autoreview through P2 found no actionable P0–P2 findings on production head `20ecebdd957b12fb3cd3d7672c8eb2d6af7119d9`. A fresh bounded review of the subsequent tests-only authority delta also found no actionable P0–P2 findings; its reviewed tree `7820431920e840ad321968797ef03eff3332a8db` matches published head `4a92573c7c0ea5d8d0426d526fad3a67cefb4828`. prs.title: fix: recover chat sends automatically after lost acknowledgements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a lost send acknowledgement can leave chat messages and their successors blocked, asking the user to work out whether delivery happened.

## User Impact

User impact: ordinary sends recover automatically with their original submission ID and physical conversation, without executing accepted input again. Confirmed delivery cannot be downgraded by a late timeout. Cases that genuinely need a decision show a neutral **Delivery unconfirmed** label and local Retry/Discard controls, not a warning paragraph.

Automatic replay excludes steering, interrupts, unknown/replaced physical targets, and copied-tab ownership holds. Discard affects only the browser's pending copy. No configuration, schema, storage-version, dependency, or protocol-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing outbox now retains the physical target before dispatch and uses durable transcript consumption to reconcile an uncertain ordinary send. The Gateway's ordinary ingress recognizes an already-committed submission as consumed instead of granting new execution custody, even after its transient acknowledgement cache and terminal-run hints are gone. Private completion replay keeps its existing contract. Recovery rechecks live authority, preserves FIFO, and reuses the existing receipt owner and retry scheduling.

## Evidence

- Copy-only follow-up: replaced “Paused” with “Delivery unconfirmed” in the shared English label. No recovery logic changed. All 28 queue-rendering tests and the 2 selected Chromium scenarios (retry/discard recovery and 320px keyboard-accessible controls, including enlarged text) passed. i18n verification, formatting, and diff checks passed.

- Regressions fail without the repairs: receipt-before-ACK timeout loses confirmed custody; ordinary committed replay executes again after transient dedupe expires; reconnect requires a manual click; expired admission acknowledges a replay; steering/interrupt actions are automatically retried.
- **196/196 focused UI tests**, **38/38 server admission tests**, **15/15 withdrawal tests**, and **46/46 selected storage-contract tests** passed (24 other storage cases were not selected). The authority changes were additionally checked with 12 selected admission cases.
- **28 GUI scenarios passed** across recovery, attachment payloads, migration, and System outbox notices. A 25-case full run plus the 3-case migration suite cover automatic reconnect/reload, exact Blob bytes and same ID, physical replacement, copied tabs, narrow layouts, receipt retirement, and explicit recovery. Six changed startup fixtures were rechecked using valid missing-target responses. This is isolated mock-Gateway boundary proof; no live Gateway was changed.
- Fresh independent review is clean. The complete required changed-file plan passed. Updated-test lint/type checks, formatting, line caps, i18n, and docs lint/MDX sanity passed.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and incident limitation</summary>

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-pending-inputs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 147.96 seconds wall time; the added ordinary consumed-replay case took 2.04 seconds locally.

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-pending-input-withdrawal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 156.64 seconds wall time, including cold compiler preparation; the new authority-boundary case took 8.15 seconds. It exercises real worker-backed durable staging and handler continuation, not a fabricated receipt.

The combined five-file focused UI command (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`) took 18.49 seconds wall time. The ACK-deadline file alone was previously measured at 3.57 seconds; its added virtual-time regression took 5 ms. Existing GUI fixtures/tables were extended rather than adding a new boot configuration. Actual hosted CI seconds for this revision are not yet measured.

The original browser's exact event ordering was not recoverable. This fixes independently reproduced delivery/replay defects without claiming to reconstruct that incident.

</details>

prs.title: fix(prometheus): preserve worker heap and GC metrics at scale
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker heap-space and GC duration metrics still lose label sets at their per-family ceilings after #180261. The reported deployment needs approximately 390 heap-space sets and 250 GC sets, exceeding the old 256 and 128 limits.

## User Impact

Preserves worker heap-space attribution and main/worker GC distributions without changing metric labels, the 16,384-entry total, other core reservations, or drop reporting.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Family | Old reserve/ceiling | New reserve/ceiling | Headroom over reported population |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `openclaw_worker_heap_space_used_bytes` | 256 | 640 | 64% over 390 |
| `openclaw_gc_duration_seconds` | 128 | 384 | 54% over 250 |

Total reserved capacity becomes 15,380, leaving 1,004 shared entries. The change only updates two catalog values; production LOC delta is zero.

Heap-space labels multiply script by space. GC slot labels correlate Code Mode isolates with their memory gauges, while bounded reason labels preserve SDK callback attribution. Native GC already reports reason `other`, so removing that label would not reduce native cardinality. Both labels remain. Drop counters count rejected observations rather than unique rejected sets; the supplied populations are conservative sizing inputs, not a reconstruction of unique drops.

## Evidence

Extended the existing exporter scrape regression with 39 worker scripts × 10 heap spaces and 250 GC label sets (244 slotted worker sets, four native main sets, two SDK reason sets). It still includes 170 RPC methods, worker/WebSocket startup traffic, and core run/model/tool populations.

Before the fix, the regression failed specifically at 256/390 heap-space sets and 128/250 GC sets. After the fix all populations export with zero drops, including late `sessions.list` and slot 61 GC. The existing all-family saturation test still retains exactly 16,384 entries and protects every RPC reservation; repeated memory samples and main/worker GC tests pass.

Focused validation: 30 tests passed across `service.subscription.test.ts`, `prometheus-metric-store.test.ts`, and `service.event-loop.test.ts`, with one worker, on Node 26.12.1. Runner wall time was 11.19 seconds (Vitest 9.09 seconds). Changed-file formatting and lint passed, as did the targeted plugin native typecheck. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The simplification pass retained only the two catalog changes, expanded existing regression, and corresponding documentation; no new production machinery or test files.

All required PR checks passed on `7d792f7aa8f28ad3032bcad723450b932f108e1e` in [CI run 39884997295](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39884997295). The final changed-file test job took 7m45s; no CI retry was needed.

The existing 16,384-entry capacity measurement is in #180261; this fix redistributes reservations without increasing the total. No new benchmark claim. Production recovery requires deployment.

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve operator continuations across edits and restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scheduled operator continuations (the "finish this after CI" turns agents schedule while landing PRs) fail closed and silently stop the task when the owner refreshes a queued continuation, or when a recurring trigger fires with context.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that schedules a same-conversation continuation from an authenticated owner turn can refresh it while it waits, and a CI-watch trigger can hand back context, without the continuation losing the owner's authority. A continuation whose stored source is unusable now stops after one failure with its error kept, instead of retrying with backoff for hours. Non-owner edits still strip the owner's authority, and model-facing names and schedules stay part of the bound definition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two production incidents on a shared Gateway, both observed during PR landings:

- **Queued owner edit.** The owner turn created a one-shot continuation, which became due while that turn was still running. The turn then refreshed the continuation's payload text. That edit revoked the waiting occurrence, so it failed 8 ms after dispatch with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active". The one-shot job was auto-disabled, and the landing stopped for two days. Separately, `cron.update` never recaptured `operatorSource`, so even an owner edit stripped the owner's own authority.
- **Trigger context.** A recurring CI-watch continuation's trigger returned `{fire:true, message:"Continue the existing authorized PR… Exact-head CI signal: …"}`. `appendCronPayloadText` appends that message to the execution copy, and restoration hashed the copy instead of the stored definition. Every fire therefore failed with "Scheduled operator continuation definition changed" and retried with backoff. The journal shows 40 such failures in a week.

The repair:

- **Launch-time check.** A queued continuation waits for its target session to become idle, then admits the current stored job. Its source is checked once, at launch, against that stored definition, not against the trigger-augmented copy. A turn that has already been admitted keeps its definition. Disable, remove and cancellation still revoke it through their existing owners.
- **Owner update capture.** Owner-authenticated `cron.update` captures the source through the same owner that `add` uses. The capture is applied only if its definition revision matches the definition committed under the mutation lock, so a concurrent manager edit cannot borrow it.
- **Hash.** `resolveCronRequesterExecutionRevision` is unchanged, so Discord/local requester and message-action consumers are untouched. Only the operator-source binding normalizes `enabled`, the one field the runtime row writer puts into `job_json`. Every existing stored source was captured while enabled, so stored data validates without a migration or a fallback hash.
- **Terminal failures.** Failures while restoring the source before admission become a typed `CronOperatorSourceError`, which both run callers classify as permanent, so the job retires after one failure. Aborts (restarts, cancellation) are rethrown unchanged and stay retryable.

Accepted edges:

- A source originally captured while its job was paused does not validate after upgrade; the owner recreates it. Operator sources (#176422) are in no release yet, stable or beta, and all stored rows on the one main-tracking deployment that has them were captured while enabled.
- A transient authority race during restore retires a recurring continuation after one visible failure.
- The idle wait has no deadline of its own; stalled sessions are owned by the session watchdog.

## Evidence

- Real cron queue, Gateway automation handlers, session admission and guarded publication owners, with synthetic model and GitHub execution (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.operator-continuation.test.ts`, 17 passed). Covered: queued owner payload edit, recurring trigger message across disable/re-enable, reschedule and restart, manager rename (no owner authority, no guarded effect), manager payload replacement racing an owner metadata capture, `next_check` leaving the hash unchanged, a pre-upgrade row built with main's hash and runtime-disabled through the real row writer, and one terminal failure for definition mismatch, malformed source and oversized source.
- `src/gateway/cron-operator-source.test.ts`: an aborted restore stays retryable, while an unusable source is typed (red on the previous head, green now).
- Red on base: the queued-edit and recurring-trigger cases fail on `main`. The rename, concurrent-capture and malformed-source cases fail on the previous PR head `420854d100a4`.
- Consumer suites: requester, run-receipt, timer outcomes, tool policy, mutation authority, active jobs, plugin-command scheduling, requester Gateway integration, session run and run queue. 223 tests across 13 files passed with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`.
- `pnpm tsgo`, cron and gateway test typechecks, changed-file oxlint and format checks, and `git diff --check` all passed.
- No live Gateway was touched. Production is +85 net lines: owner-update wiring, the typed failure, and the launch-time read.

prs.title: fix(media): allow CP932 CSV attachments without transcoding
prs.body:
Closes #178619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid Japanese CP932 CSV attachments being rejected by host-read text validation before channel upload.

## User Impact

Users can attach structured CP932/Windows-31J CSV exports while retaining their original bytes and line endings for downstream importers. This does not transcode the file or expand filesystem permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the existing UTF-8/Latin-1 text candidates fail validation, a CSV-only fallback strictly decodes Shift JIS and requires printable, rectangular records with quoted-field handling. It preserves the existing MIME-sniffing, root, size, and generated-HTML checks.

Current main now owns host-read admission in `src/media/host-read-media-policy.ts`. The conflict resolution places the CP932 fallback in that owner and preserves its generated-HTML provenance and explicit-publication checks. No dependency, setting, transport, or runtime patch is added.

## Evidence

- Fixed synthetic Japanese-heavy and quoted CSV tests both fail on base `79262d0571694dbf083b7d1bf5a206cc8fb93936` with the reported `LocalMediaAccessError`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts`: **53 passed**, including exact original-byte comparisons, mostly-ASCII CP932, malformed/control-byte cases, renamed binary media, and existing root/size/HTML protections.
- Direct model-free `loadWebMedia` reproduction returns `document`, `text/csv`, and `exactBytes: true` on the fix.
- Core typecheck, all `tsgo:test:src` shards, touched-file type-aware oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Focused current-main Auto Review completed scoped-clean for P0/P1 after the policy-owner conflict resolution.

- Merged current main normally at exact head `129d62349970790218cba13e328168d0394cb8b8`; the PR diff against current main remains the policy owner plus its focused test.
- This authored problem statement and evidence apply to exact head `129d62349970790218cba13e328168d0394cb8b8`.

### Shipped Slack channel proof (2026-10-21)

Exact-head isolated Slack upload proof passed through the shipped `sendMessageSlack` entry point and real shared media loader/write client. The received raw upload body exactly matched the synthetic CP932 source and retained both CRLF pairs. Fixes: every iMessage reply fails with `Delivery failed before dispatch` when the imsg private bridge inside Messages.app dies (for example after the Messages Mac reboots), and OpenClaw never re-injects it on its own.

## User Impact

User impact: a stalled imsg bridge now triggers the existing automatic `imsg launch` recovery for normal sends, so the next reply goes through instead of every reply failing until an operator re-injects Messages.app by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic bridge recovery (#134572, #137029) only recognized imsg's legacy wait error, `Timed out waiting for response to '<action>'`. imsg 0.14+ (steipete/imsg#216) reports bridge_v2 mutation stalls, which includes every `send-message`, as structured delivery data instead:

```json
{"transport": "bridge_v2", "operation": "send-message", "disposition": "not_started",
 "retry_safe": true, "detail": "The bridge response deadline expired. The client reclaimed and removed the unclaimed request."}
```

The legacy text still appears only for non-mutation bridge calls, so for sends the detector never matched and recovery never ran. The existing regression test fed a send failure with the legacy wording, a shape imsg does not emit, which is why it stayed green.

The detector now also accepts the structured `bridge_v2` deadline detail. Recovery behavior is unchanged: the failed mutation is still never retried, so there is no duplicate-send risk.

## Evidence

- Production: from Oct 20 to Oct 22, five replies on a personal Gateway failed with exactly the payload above. `imsg status` on the Messages Mac reported `v2_ready: false` ("The IMCore bridge is not responding"), with the bridge files untouched since the host rebooted on Oct 9. A manual `imsg launch` restored `v2_ready: true` immediately, which is the step this fix automates.
- `extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts` now uses real imsg payloads: a legacy non-mutation wait and the bridge_v2 send deadline. The send case is red on `main` (no `imsg launch`, cache not invalidated) and green with the fix; 19/19 pass.
- `run-oxlint-shards --only=extensions` passes on the changed files; oxfmt is clean.

An earlier `sessions_send` message loses its source warning in the active model request, then regains it when a later turn reconstructs history. That changes previously submitted user text.

prs.title: fix(release): refuse forbidden changelog thanks before FRV dispatch
prs.body:
Related: #180084

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a publish-purpose Full Release Validation dispatch is accepted when the candidate's release notes contain a forbidden changelog thanks (for example `Thanks @steipete`), and the run fails roughly two hours later in the "Check npm release source" job's `pnpm check`. This happened during 2026.10.6.

## User Impact

Release operators get the refusal at dispatch time, before any GitHub write, with the offending `file:line` and the next step, instead of losing a full FRV run. There is no change for candidates with clean changelogs.

## Why This Change Was Made

#180084 moved the release-candidate changelog gates (render/row count and record provenance) to dispatch time, but the changelog lint in `pnpm check` still ran only inside the FRV. That lint, `check:changelog-attributions`, is the only changelog-scoped check in `pnpm check`: oxfmt ignores `CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG/**`, and `changelog:check` belongs to `check:docs`, not `pnpm check`. It is cheap, deterministic, and changelog-only.

- `scripts/check-changelog-attributions.mts` now exports `findChangelogAttributionViolations(files)`, a pure function that keeps the docs-mirror exemption. Its CLI uses that function, so the rule still has one owner.
- `scripts/lib/release-changelog.mjs`, which already owns working-tree and immutable-Git changelog reads, adds `readReleaseChangelogFiles({ rootDir, ref })`. It reads `CHANGELOG.md` and the `CHANGELOG/` release artifacts from the resolved candidate commit through the existing `sourceReader`, not from the working tree.
- `validateCandidateChangelog` runs this lint first, so the FRV dispatch gate and `pnpm release:candidate` both enforce it at the candidate SHA. The error looks like this: `Forbidden changelog thanks attribution (pnpm check:changelog-attributions): CHANGELOG.md:3 uses Thanks @steipete. Use verified human GitHub credits; ...`. The dispatch wrapper then adds "Fix the release notes ... on the release branch ..., then validate the new candidate SHA."

## Evidence

- Regression test at the dispatch helper boundary: `test/scripts/full-release-validation-at-sha.candidate.test.ts` › "refuses publish qualification when the candidate changelog thanks an internal handle". A candidate-owned publish dispatch whose candidate changelog has `Thanks @steipete` exits 1 with the `CHANGELOG.md:3` error, makes no non-GET `gh api` calls, and sends no workflow dispatch. Before the fix it **failed**: the dispatch exited 0. After the fix it passes. The clean publish case is the existing "retains publication and lane inputs ..." test, which still dispatches successfully.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/full-release-validation-at-sha.candidate.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20/20 passed, 68.4 s wall for the whole file. The new case takes about 2.2 s, most of it building one git fixture template, the same cost as the sibling unreachable-record case. It adds roughly 2 s of CI time.
- Also passing: `test/scripts/check-changelog-attributions.test.ts`, `test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts`, `test/scripts/full-release-validation-at-sha.test.ts` (247 tests), and `eager-import-closure.test.ts -t "PR wrapper inventory"`.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, tsgo on `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json` and `tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`, targeted oxlint, `run-format.mts --check` on the changed files, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- `scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`: no new findings. Its output is byte-identical to `origin/main` at the base, which already exits 1 on pre-existing unrelated exports.
- Real-repo check: reading the 157 changelog artifacts at `HEAD` through the new reader finds 0 violations, the same result as `pnpm check:changelog-attributions`, in about 1.9 s.

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve scheduled accounts and restart retry deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron inference capture could bind a scheduled job to the creator's interactive account even when scheduled execution selected a different configured model or account. Recurring jobs interrupted by a Gateway restart could also record a retry deadline earlier than their enforced error backoff, then shift an `every` schedule after the retry succeeded.

## User Impact

Scheduled jobs retain the account selected by their scheduled model policy, including Gmail hook and explicitly bound execution-session selection. Restarted recurring jobs expose the deadline the scheduler can actually honor and resume their authored interval afterward. One-shot retries, cancellation semantics, failure limits, and explicit model overrides remain unchanged. No new configuration or automatic repair of existing stored account bindings is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inference capture now uses the scheduled-model owner, including model overrides from a persistent execution target; creator auth inheritance remains separate. Restart scheduling reuses the canonical failure backoff and interval-anchor calculation. A real failed retry normalizes malformed persisted failure counts before incrementing them; interrupted or cancelled attempts do not count as new failures.

The native tooling dependency resolver also keeps repository-local hook Git variables out of explicit donor metadata probes, without changing the commit environment or qualification guards. The prepared-runtime test fixture includes its required catalog and uses the canonical runtime directory resolver. Existing fixture setup lives in coherent sibling test-support modules to satisfy required line caps without removing assertions.

## Evidence

- Complete 23-path candidate passed fresh independent full-delta source review through P2. Signed commit `38a58056ecef1f06cba2d5787d7a575bfbddb792` has exactly the reviewed tree; required hooks, staged line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed.
- Exact-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39883214714 completed success:53 successful jobs,26 nonselected/skipped jobs (not passes), no failures. Required owning/affected proof is178 passing tests across13 files, including13 operator-continuation cases, both original scheduled-recipe archive identity assertions, the22-case tooling suite and all38 Gateway inference-binding cases.
- Focused bootstrap regression is red on the original resolver and green after the fix under inherited hook Git directory/worktree/temporary index context. Genuine sparse and different-origin donors reject; parent environment/index remain unchanged.
- Prior-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39880599593 failed9 operator-continuation cases because the shared catalog fixture supplied a different credential-owner directory for capture than execution. This revision corrects that fixture owner without weakening the real authorization guard; the formerly failing13-case suite now passes. That failed run is neither passing nor inherited evidence.
- Four new Gateway cases actually passed: isolated/current exclusion of creator model overrides, persistent target capture, and explicit payload precedence. All three requested type leaves (services-cron, commands-doctor, gateway-methods), tooling test types, lint, exact23-file oxfmt/Bun parity and baseline/line-cap ratchets passed on this exact head.
- Earlier CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39877412156 failed on fixture/catalog, invalid public-RPC fixture and Number.NaN lint issues. Those corrections remain included; that run is not reported as passing.
- No production restart/deployment, local project dependency install/relink or replacement test resource. The formatter staged the unchanged checksum-pinned Bun binary in its tool cache.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw skills list` prints each skill's `description` and `source` verbatim, so a workspace skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter carries ESC/BEL sequences changes the operator's terminal while they list skills.

## User Impact

User impact: the skills table renders skill text as text and no longer interprets escapes embedded in a workspace `SKILL.md`; `skills list --json` keeps the raw values for scripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The single-skill report in the same module already sanitizes the same fields (`skills info` passes `name`, `description`, `source`, and `homepage` through `sanitizeForLog`), while the list row builder handed them to the table raw. The row builder now sanitizes description, source, and the verbose missing-requirements summary before theming.

One existing case changes meaning: `skills-cli.formatting.test.ts` previously asserted that a C1 sequence stayed in the description cell (`"left right"`, i.e. the escape was still delivered and only its layout effect was measured). The cell now carries only printable text, so the case asserts `"leftright"` and that the report contains no C1 byte — same fixture, escape removed instead of forwarded.

## Evidence

- Base `711eb843136`, head `97d9379f732`; secretless Linux container, Node 24.18.0, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- Fixture: a workspace skill at `<state>/workspace/skills/evil/SKILL.md` whose frontmatter description is `Evil \x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m \x1b[2Kbell\x07 cr\r end`.

| | base | this head |

| description cell | `Evil ^[[31mRED^[[0m ^[[2Kbell^G cr end` | `Evil RED bell cr end` |
| ESC / BEL / CSI bytes in the report | 3 / 1 / 3 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

      → expected 'left right' to be 'leftright'

prs.title: fix(update): allow unchanged dist files with extra execute bits
prs.body:
Fixes #181050

## What Problem This Solves

npm updates can fail at `package-verify` when a filesystem adds execute bits to otherwise unchanged packaged dist files, as reported on UGREEN UGOS.

## User Impact

An inventoried non-executable file may gain execute bits without blocking an update, provided the actual file has neither group/world write bits (`mode & 0o022`) nor setuid/setgid/sticky bits (`mode & 0o7000`). The update report records one warning with the affected file count. Permissions are left unchanged.

All other mode handling retains main's existing semantics: non-execute permission differences are not a new integrity gate, and an inventory-executable file must remain executable. This preserves owner-only modes such as `0644` → `0600` produced by retained-package recovery. Hash, size, path, symlink, and file-type checks remain intact.

The issue's independent reproduction uses `0755`. The exact numeric mode on the actual UGOS installation is undocumented in the issue and comments; they do not establish `0777`. The installed updater must contain this fix; staging a newer candidate cannot repair an older updater's verifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared comparator conflated extra executability with changed content. It now checks the safety of newly executable files while retaining the existing comparison for other mode changes. Runtime and tarball collection preserve special bits so `4755` cannot be mistaken for `0755`. Package verification forwards the bounded warning through existing update-report fields; candidate verification and activation settlement share the comparator.

Thanks @hannesrudolph for the report and four-case reproduction.

## Behavior

| Inventory | Actual | Bytes | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0644` | `0644` | unchanged | Pass |
| `0644` | `0755` | unchanged | Pass, one bounded warning |
| `0644` | `0777` | unchanged | Fail |
| `0644` | `0775` | unchanged | Fail |
| `0644` | `4755` | unchanged | Fail |
| `0755` | `0644` | unchanged | Fail |
| `0644` | `0600` | unchanged | Pass, existing recovery behavior |
| `0644` | `0664` | unchanged | Pass, existing non-exec behavior |
| `0644` | `0644` | changed | Fail |

## Evidence

- Original regression: unchanged `0755` failed on the unchanged base; original/restored `0644` and changed-byte control behaved as expected. Review regression: the prior PR head incorrectly accepted newly executable `0777` and `4755`; the final staged-update tests reject those modes and `0775` while preserving the previous installation.
- Recovery coverage includes the three previously failing settlement cases in `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-package-activation.test.ts`. They require recovery's intentional `0644` → `0600` normalization; the final rule preserves that contract.
- Node: all 121 tests in six files passed (52 focused tests plus 69 recovery/activation/publication tests). Commands used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1` with isolated HOME/state and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. The four-file run took 69.76s wall and the two adjacent consumer files took 52.91s.
- Pinned Bun: the same 121 tests in six files passed, 80.99s wall (46.26s infra and 25.60s CLI Vitest shards). The three consumer files were `update-repair-package-activation.test.ts`, `package-update-activation-lifetime.test.ts`, and `package-update-publication-boundary.test.ts`; the focused files were `package-update-steps.test.ts`, `package-dist-content-inventory.test.ts`, and `package-dist-inventory.test.ts`.
- Scoped TypeScript check, core/script oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (zero cycles). Fresh independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign local gate budget.
- Real npm proof: `npm pack` and `npm install --global` used a fresh prefix and HOME under TMPDIR, with `npm_config_prefix` and `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG=/dev/null`. Before every global install, `npm prefix -g` was asserted equal to the explicit temporary prefix. Every global path and resolved updater target was constrained to that root. Actual file modes were checked after chmod, and all temporary installations were removed.

```text
0644 → 0755: package-verify=0, activated 2.0.0, warnings=1
0644 → 0777: package-verify=1, preserved 1.0.0, warnings=0
0644 → 0775: package-verify=1, preserved 1.0.0, warnings=0
0644 → 4755: package-verify=1, preserved 1.0.0, warnings=0
0755 → 0644: package-verify=1, preserved 1.0.0, warnings=0
0644 → 0600: activated 2.0.0, warnings=0
0644 → 0664: activated 2.0.0, warnings=0
changed bytes: package-verify=1, preserved 1.0.0, warnings=0
```

Live command: `env HOME=$PWD/.artifacts/home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$PWD/.artifacts/state TMPDIR=$PWD/.artifacts/l1834-tmp node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/l1834-r3-live.ts`. This proves real npm staging, verification, and swap with synthetic packages on macOS. It does not emulate UGOS ACLs or prove a complete NAS Gateway update.

Production delta against the PR base: +51/-11 lines; regression tests: +50; documentation: +9. The correction itself is production +10/-4, tests +12/-5, documentation +8/-6. The comparison and warning remain with their existing owners; no configuration, dependency, or state-format change was added.

Earlier broad consumer proof measured the unchanged `src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts` cases at 183.8s in total; their per-case isolated state/native lifecycle setup remains a separate test-cost follow-up. No timeout, retry, skip, or assertion was weakened.

prs.title: fix(doctor): settle missing retained originals onto verified survivors
prs.body:
Closes #179957

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `doctor --session-sqlite recover` defers duplicate-archive settlement forever when the historical original path is already missing, even though a byte-verified surviving archive exists.

## User Impact
Offline recovery can now reconcile historical archive references whose originals vanished, instead of reporting `restored=0 ... reason: doctor recover completed with remaining issues` on every run. In the linked report, 6,420 missing references all had surviving archives matching the receipt size and SHA-256, yet none were settled.

## Why This Change Was Made
The settlement loop asserted that every non-disposed original still exists on disk before recording a replacement, so a retained original whose file had already vanished failed with "artifact is unexpectedly missing" and its references were never repointed. The replacement-retention check likewise required every reference to be disposed before keeping the repoint.

A missing retained original has nothing left to retire: settlement now skips the existence assert and disposal selection for it (the survivor was already byte-verified in the same loop) and still records the replacement, and a replacement survives when every reference is disposed or its original file is absent. The "Archive was recreated after disposal" guard and the identity-mismatch deferral for changed originals are unchanged.

## Evidence
- Regression in `doctor-session-sqlite.duplicate-lookup.test.ts`: two byte-identical retained archives, the original's file removed, settlement now reports `historical_duplicate_settled` (previously `historical_transcript_deferred` with "artifact is unexpectedly missing") and the survivor's bytes stay intact. Red on base, green with this change.
- Neighbors stay green: the remaining 3 settlement cases in `doctor-session-sqlite.duplicate-lookup.test.ts` and all 18 cases in `doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-mutations.test.ts` (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Not run locally: full commands suite and typecheck (CI covers).

Fixes: `web_fetch` joins definition-list terms and values together when its basic extractor reads minified HTML.

## User Impact

Field/value pairs remain distinguishable in both Markdown and text output instead of becoming strings such as `RegionEMEAUnits120`. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing renderer inserts block boundaries for paragraphs and lists, but omits `dl`, `dt`, and `dd`. Include those tags in the same owner rather than introduce another renderer. The regression goes through the actual basic-extraction entrypoint, including HTML sanitization, in both modes. Production delta: +3 lines; test delta: +11 lines.

## Evidence

Reproduced against upstream `9827935108e185e3f290d622dcccec07ff3814ae` on Windows 11, isolated Node 24.22.1 and locked dependencies:

```html
<dl><dt>Region</dt><dd>EMEA</dd><dt>Units</dt><dd>120</dd></dl>
```

Before: `RegionEMEAUnits120`. After, in both modes:

```text
Region
EMEA
Units
120
```

- Red/green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-fetch-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t definition-list` fails both new cases against the original production file, on the merged-text assertion.

- Targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Simplification: retained the existing block-tag owner and one owner-level regression, with no new helpers or state. A broader real-tool test was deliberately not retained: its cold import exceeded the local 180s budget, while the changed extraction boundary is directly exercised above.

Independent structured review of the committed diff completed scoped-clean at P0-P2. Review was limited to the supplied diff and did not independently rerun local checks. prs.title: fix: keep resumed Goals running after Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Goal explicitly resumed by an operator can stop after a Gateway restart instead of continuing automatically.

## User Impact

Resumed Goals retain their authorized restart continuation. Pressing Stop still prevents recovery. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal Resume is an authenticated operator action, but its hidden transcript message is marked as internal. That marker inadvertently excluded the action from restart-authority capture. Classify only the validated Resume operation as operator input for this capture, without changing its transcript provenance. Existing live-authority, scope, execution-lineage, and incognito checks remain in place.

## Evidence

- Strengthened the existing public Goal Resume boundary regression: it fails on the base because the acknowledged Resume has no recovery source, then passes with this fix. The existing hidden-input and idempotency assertions remain intact.
- 83 focused tests pass across Goal chat admission, Goal RPC operations, restart recovery, and requester recovery.
- A real isolated Gateway and production agent, using a synthetic loopback HTTP model, survive two actual process crashes after Resume. Each replacement process automatically makes a new model request; the final response reaches public chat history. A stopped sibling remains killed across both restarts. No manually seeded recovery state or recovery RPC.
- Gateway and root-E2E test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks pass. Independent autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 issues, including a complete-context authority-boundary pass.

### Live model and recovered-effect verification

- A separately isolated, compiled Gateway using real OpenAI inference passed public authenticated Goal Resume across process replacement. The recovered model executed its barrier command again and delivered the expected result to public chat history; a stopped sibling did not restart. The live case passed in 39.14 seconds.
- The committed cold-process test now also verifies a real recovered exec write exactly once, plus a separately authenticated operator revoked through public `device.token.revoke` while its recovered model response is held. Releasing that stale tool response produces no filesystem effect, no follow-up provider request, and no success reply; neither stopped nor revoked control resurrects on the next restart. This run passed in 29.54 seconds.
- Revocation occurs during an already-admitted provider request, before subsequent tool/provider effects—not before the initial recovery provider call. The revocation fixture uses a synthetic HTTP model; the separate restart smoke uses a real provider. Gateway and command processes and disposable state were verified removed. Hosting Gateway state was untouched.
- This follow-up changes tests only. Its typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and fresh P0–P2 independent review passed. The published Git tree matches the tested tree.

The revoked count of two is its original request plus the recovered request already in flight when revoked; it does not increase after the held response is released. prs.title: fix(gateway): reject FIFO TLS material without blocking validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured Gateway TLS certificate, private key or CA path that is a FIFO without a writer blocks startup before TLS validation can report the invalid input. Public certificate inspection has the same admission gap. The existing byte-limited cert/key reader cannot help while `open()` is waiting for a writer.

This is a malformed local material path, not a claim that OpenClaw normally creates FIFO certificates or that an untrusted remote user can configure these paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit configured material nonblockingly on POSIX, check the opened descriptor is a regular file, then use the existing read policy. Both server startup and read-only public certificate inspection use this owner. Keep configured symlinks, current 64 KiB cert/key limits and the existing uncapped CA-bundle contract. Windows retains its current open mode.

Read the full TLS owner, startup preparation/kernel caller, local HTTPS probe, certificate inspection, renewal consumer and adjacent tests. Renewal retains previously accepted material on reload failure. The installed fs-safe bounded descriptor implementation was inspected: its limit applies after opening; the generic regular-file API rejects symlinks, so substituting it would change supported configured paths. No new package, timer, fallback or config option is needed.

All-state semantic/symbol searches and open TLS PR changed-file checks found no active implementation of this fix. Historical #110046 proposed new fixed input caps and was closed for inactivity with unresolved compatibility concerns. This patch does not adopt that policy or replace certificate-generation code: it preserves today's cert/key bounds, uncapped CA reads and staged generation/publication safeguards. #171105 fixes SSH probe endpoint selection in a different owner.

## User Impact

Invalid nonregular material now reaches the normal required-TLS startup failure path and produces an actionable diagnostic instead of blocking inside the reader. Regular material and symlinks still start an actual HTTPS listener with the configured certificate. Invalid TLS never falls back to an unencrypted listener.

Three existing path inputs now explicitly reject nonregular descriptors; this validation change matters for compatibility. The reproduced no-writer FIFOs block unattended startup. A finite writer can make some FIFO PEM inputs work today: rejecting that use is a compatibility choice requiring owner acceptance, not established by the no-writer reproduction. This refresh does not claim that acceptance. No config/default addition, protocol/schema, dependency, trust policy, certificate generation or migration change. CA bundles gain no size cap; ordinary files and their configured symlinks retain the observed behavior.

## Evidence

**Current-head refresh, 2026-10-23:** `6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59`, after a normal merge of main `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`. Linux, Node 24.22.1, source OpenClaw 2026.10.6. Main's flattened TLS tests and newer coverage were retained; only the FIFO regression was carried into that structure. Production remains +19/-8 and tests +48/-0 against this main; two files.

Current source-runtime command:

```sh
node ../gateway-tls-fifo-live-proof-20261023.mjs "$PWD" ../maintenance-172741-proof-v2-20261023-run green
```

At `2026-10-23T01:07:04.063Z`, all six real Gateway startup scenarios passed on the exact rebuilt head:

| Scenario | Current result | Observation time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular cert/key/CA | actual HTTPS readiness and matching peer fingerprint | 23.156s |
| Symlinked cert/key/CA | same HTTPS identity; links retained | 20.086s |
| Ordinary invalid PEM | real startup-failure artifact, no TCP listener | 15.028s |
| Writerless certificate FIFO | regular-file failure artifact, no TCP listener | 14.488s |
| Writerless private-key FIFO | same rejection | 13.981s |
| Writerless CA FIFO | same rejection | 14.070s |

Waiting FIFO reads 3/3 on the historical base become 0/3 on the current head. Configuration/material preservation 6/6; no FIFO writers or watchdog timeouts. Invalid runs still needed explicit cleanup of the harness-owned process groups: no natural CLI exit guarantee is claimed. The current driver only removes a retired heartbeat field from its synthetic configuration; the original driver and historical RED remain unchanged. One failed obsolete-config attempt is retained as a fixture failure. Current driver SHA-256 `dacd6ec63a1a3cdff9151aa95cbd48d916357da1a61894bbd2e9efdd0e603693`; receipt SHA-256 `fb5ed121e5098c03385b180a3853005a3abfc8a2e7549ad68c062969aaa074fd`.

**Installed stable → exact-head upgrade proof:** PASS in isolated local Linux container `leon-tls-installed-upgrade-20261023`, Node 24.22.1 / glibc 2.35, starting `2026-10-23T01:17:19.716Z`.

- Start from a fresh copy of the official OpenClaw 2026.10.6 installation, shipped build `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`. Read installed TLS settings and establish actual CA-verified HTTPS through configured certificate/key/CA symlinks; fingerprint matches.
- Back up the isolated config, state and workspace. Perform a normal npm 11.19.0 install of the private exact-head runtime package over the same prefix (exit 0, 46.309s). Installed build-info now identifies `6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59`, package version 2026.10.6. This is not a published release or SDK certification.
- Read back the same TLS settings and actual HTTPS certificate identity. Stable HTTPS readiness 16.063s, candidate 24.391s; these include startup and are not performance claims.
- Replace only the isolated certificate link with a writerless FIFO. The installed candidate reports the existing regular-file startup error in 13.572s, creates no TCP listener, and retains the FIFO. Restore the original link.
- Original config, certificate, private key, CA and workspace artifact are byte-identical after the upgrade and controls; all three symlinks remain symlinks. Config SHA-256 `daa2106d727620d8f970614b950495aaccf9d9eb1b8d7b4b70b9f148418e6600`; workspace artifact SHA-256 `3452af9dd340934ffae02a6d2a4a67adf45a13067211dd37dbe84c7eb98ce4f8`; zero FIFO writers. No production configuration, channels, credentials or recipients were used.

Installed-proof invocation inside that container:

```sh
node /harness/probe.mjs /candidate/openclaw.tgz 6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59
```

Harness SHA-256 `5991d8b7246755d6b669038daa0ade06b8d714b748bc7c92f3e1925010a17a75`; package SHA-256 `38c61dc095c2d7e646d7b73f8aa125028c521464db6834f994d8a0fa54c866c1`; receipt SHA-256 `f5087287fdee9b2a148eba87480ff20338fe17384c8b810052922fde9004cfbb`. Raw receipts/logs/backups are outside the product branch; the redacted readbacks above are the published evidence. This is a local container, not remote Crabbox/Testbox.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): bundle the Knowledge memory plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge, the evidence-backed memory plugin, ships separately from OpenClaw, so it can drift from core and users have to install and load it themselves.

## User Impact

User impact: Knowledge ships with OpenClaw as a bundled plugin, off by default. Setting `plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge"` turns it on. Existing stores keep working: the bundled build opened a copy of a real standalone-Knowledge store without a migration step.

People who installed the standalone plugin need a manual switch, because an installed copy takes precedence over the bundled one. `openclaw plugins uninstall knowledge` also clears `plugins.entries.knowledge.config`, including `stores`. The [Knowledge guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/openclaw-ef3/bundle-knowledge/docs/plugins/knowledge.md) lists a safe save, uninstall, enable and restore order. No vault data is touched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin moves into `extensions/knowledge` and now follows the repository rules for bundled plugins:
- Its tests run under vitest.
- It passes repo lint, type and file-size gates. Large files are split; assertions are justified or removed.
- Workers, the default ontology and the sample vault load from the runtime entry and ship as static assets.
- SQLite access uses the plugin SDK's worker helpers, Kysely builders and immediate transactions.
- A new `knowledge_attach_file` tool attaches a file from the agent's workspace by path, reusing the durable chunked-upload path, so the model no longer copies attachment bytes through its context.

**One part needs maintainer review:** keyword search keeps its SQLite FTS5 index. `scripts/database-dialect-inventory.mts` now excludes `fts5`, `temp-schema` and `rowid` in `extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.ts` only, through the same mechanism as the existing SQLite-only exclusions. The reasons:
- The index is a cache rebuilt from the vault.
- It lives only in each store's private `state.sqlite` and is never opened through the PostgreSQL-capable database layer.
- Moving it behind a shared SDK text-index API would need core to own plugin database files, which it doesn't today.

`docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` documents the exclusion. Tests prove that other constructs in that file, and `fts5` anywhere else, still fail the ratchet. If this exclusion isn't acceptable, the fallback is scoring search in TypeScript inside Knowledge.

The config-surface baseline grows by 28 entries. They are Knowledge's own config schema (`stores`, write and read policy, maintenance), now part of the bundled inventory.

## Evidence

- **Upgrade on real data.** I took a consistent copy (SQLite online backup) of a live standalone-Knowledge state directory: 487 MB, 2 stores, about 76k state pages. An isolated Gateway built from this branch opened it on port 19390 with Knowledge as the memory slot:
  - `status`: the store is `ready` and live watching is on.
  - Keyword search: the FTS index is `ready` and returns ranked hits.
  - Record read, exact lookup, `records`, `timeline`, `history` (git `committed`) and `connections` all succeed.
  - A temporary, uncommitted test opened the same copied store through `createKnowledgeService` and saved a claim with `remember`. The receipt came back `published`, the claim count went from 1,097 to 1,098, and keyword search found the new claim.
- **Build.** `pnpm build` passes, and Knowledge loads from `dist` with origin `bundled`.
- **Rebased onto current `main`** (`0843b940a56`, which includes #180466). Two real conflicts: `main` added a v31 `rowid` exclusion to `scripts/database-dialect-inventory.mts` and its test in the same spots as this PR's FTS5 exclusion, so both exclusions are kept and the test covers both files. The config baseline and worker inventory were regenerated with their generators. On head `64a8959f4cb`: the dialect ratchet (against `0843b940a56`), its 39 tests, the worker-inventory, config-baseline, plugin-inventory and skill-reference checks, `tsgo:extensions`, Knowledge oxlint, the import-cycle check and `pnpm build` all pass.
- **Tests.** Under Node (the CI runtime), `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test:extension knowledge` passed on `3a28571f0ae` (the rebase before the attachment commits): 48 files, 385 tests, in 13m7s. On head `64a8959f4cb` (49 files, 391 tests), 390 passed. The one failure was `publication.test.ts > cross-process publishers fence competing edits and never lose the winner`, which saw revision 4 instead of 2 while the winner's hash was correct. It passed 3 of 3 runs alone, and passed in the earlier full run. The attachment commits don't touch publication, so I'm treating it as a rare timing-sensitive failure under load, tracked as a follow-up, not a regression from this head.
  - `fix(knowledge): bound Markdown block runs before link lexing` fixes the Bun-only slowness in `record-capacity.test.ts > near-limit records…`: JavaScriptCore gave up on `marked`'s paragraph regexp after ~49K lines and fell back to line-by-line lexing. CI runs Node, so CI wasn't affected.
- **Control UI.** Screenshots from an isolated Gateway on this build (origin `bundled`), seeded with the synthetic sample vault. Knowledge is a new page, so there's no "before".

  ![Knowledge Recent view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff1e59e3-07f9-48c7-b121-6e6e89dc4ee3)
  ![Knowledge Browse view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1dfee30-839d-4fcd-80ba-13bee055fa1a)
  ![Knowledge record view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39a802af-b106-4bfd-bf3b-e478e1be373c)
- **Gates.** `pnpm check:changed` passes every gate that covers Knowledge, including typecheck, the dialect, worker and assertion ratchets, and import cycles. The dead-export scan flagged two of this PR's re-exports. I removed them, and the scan is now clean. Three gates fail only on files this PR doesn't touch:
  - lint, for line caps in `ui/`, `src/` and `extensions/{telegram,crabbox}`
  - the `max-lines` suppression ratchet, for `ui/` files
  - the core test-shard root budget
- **Review.** Autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, P0 threshold) returned `scoped-clean` across 5 passes.
- **Simplify.** `pr-simplify` removed a test-only `Publisher` rename alias and two unused `MAX_ENTRIES` re-exports. Two things remain by design:
  - The `includeMetadata` tool input stays, because agents already use it with the published plugin.
  - Raw prepared statements stay where the SDK database rules allow them.

Diff against the merge base: about 53.7k lines added. Roughly 26.5k is production TypeScript and 3.3k CSS. The rest is tests (14.7k), docs (8.1k) and fixtures, ontology and skills.

prs.title: fix(pr): review-init fails with a client credential custody error on pre-cutover PR registries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr review-init` (and every other provisioning `scripts/pr` command) fails in `[pr-worktree-provision]` with "Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix." when the wrapper's private PR registry (`<canonical>/.local/pr-state`) predates the client-credential cutover.

## User Impact

Maintainers can provision PR worktrees again from a pre-cutover PR registry. The first run migrates the private registry under Doctor-style custody, with a scoped pre-migration backup. The operator's own Gateway database is never involved, and no action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration custody contract was fine. The guarded migration simply never ran when `scripts/pr` executes wrapper code materialized from the trusted anchor. That tree contains only `scripts/pr`, `scripts/pr-lib` and the files listed in `wrapper-components.txt`. The state preflight forks `src/state/openclaw-agent-schema-inspection.worker.ts`, which was not listed, so the child exited 1 and the preflight reported the registry as `indeterminate` rather than as a pending migration. `preparePrStateSchema` only looked at `pendingMigrations`, treated the store as current and returned. The allocation lease's ordinary open then hit the v28→v29 cutover with no maintenance scope or backup capture, and the custody check refused it.

This change makes three adjustments:

- **Inventory:** lists the forked runtime children that wrapper code can launch (11 files). The PostgreSQL bridge is deliberately left out: wrapper processes never install a PostgreSQL engine selection, and `pg` is not a pinned wrapper dependency.
- **Inventory check:** the "PR wrapper inventory" check now follows `resolveRuntimeProcessEntrypointUrl("…")` references, so a forked child missing from the extracted closure fails CI instead of failing at runtime. This gap dates from #171984 (online preflight in a forked child) and became fatal with #174599, which added the preflight-gated migration.
- **Routing:** `preparePrStateSchema` no longer treats a store the preflight could not classify as current. An `indeterminate` state store goes through the same guarded doctor-preparation as a pending migration, and that path re-inspects the store under custody (a current store passes its integrity check and needs no repair). Without this, any future gap of this kind degrades into a misleading custody error that recommends `openclaw doctor --fix` for a private wrapper registry.

Accepted edge case: if two provisioners race the one-time migration of the same registry, the second one fails fast with a visible, retryable `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError` while the first holds the migration owner. Pending migrations already behaved this way. Live lease holders do not make the preflight indeterminate (its inspection is a plain WAL read), so ordinary concurrent provisioning is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Real reproduction and fix through `scripts/pr review-init 178648`.** I used a disposable canonical clone holding a copy of the real pre-cutover registry (v28, clean-close seal re-bound to the copy), with the anchor materialized exactly as `scripts/pr` does it.
  - With the anchor at unfixed `main` (`fbc99b8`), the run logs `[state/db] state database schema migration pending; verifying integrity first` and then the custody refusal, identical to the incident.
  - With the anchor at this change, `review-init` completes. The registry is at `user_version` 29 with the legacy credential tables dropped, `client/credentials.sqlite` has phase `complete`, a `.pre-startup-migration-*.scoped.bak` exists, and the operation lock is released.
  - The live shared registry was never touched; all runs used copies.
- **Controls.** The same copied registry migrates cleanly when the provisioner runs from a full checkout, with or without the seal. So the store bytes and seal are not causal; only the extracted-tree composition is.
- **`test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts -t "PR wrapper inventory"`.** Red on base, naming 7 unlisted forked children. Green with this change.
- **`test/scripts/pr-worktree-state.test.ts`.** New case `v28 from unclassified extract` runs the real provisioner from extracted wrapper sources with the inspection child removed. On base it fails with the custody refusal (~17 s); with the fix it passes and keeps the existing assertions: migration, preserved rows, credential move and backup restore. The existing checkout cases still pass.
- **Other checks.** The full `pr-worktree-state` file passes (15 tests). Also passing: the `eager-import-closure` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure` suites in full (22/22), `pr-worktree-interruption` (the other consumer of the owner fixture), `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root`.
- **`pr-worktree-provision`.** 14 of its cases pass. Three cold-provisioning cases hit the 120 s timeout on this host (load average around 90), and they time out identically with this PR's production files reverted to base, so PR CI is the judge for those.
- **Review.** Codex autoreview (P0–P1) found nothing actionable.
- **Cost.** The new state case copies the wrapper inventory and runs a real provisioner. Locally it took 73 s, but under a load average around 90; CI records about 40 s for the whole file. No cheaper layer exercises the extracted-tree route that failed.
- **Current head on current `main`.** I merged `main` into the branch, because one inventory entry (`src/process/spawn-broker/resource-port.ts`) had been deleted there and `git archive` would refuse it, so that entry is dropped. On the merged tree (Node 26.12.1) the inventory check reports nothing missing or stale. The closure suites pass 22/22, `pr-worktree-state` passes 14/14 (the extracted-source case takes 21 s), and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` pass.
- **Lint.** CI's first run caught a `no-map-spread` error in the new inventory check; it is fixed with `Array.from`. The same changed-file oxlint command now passes locally. The `ui/**`-only Solid plugin override was stripped from a temporary config because that worktree has no `eslint-plugin-solid`.

prs.title: refactor: keep single-consumer internals with their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal APIs with one consumer leave unnecessary modules, parameter bags, and forwarding layers between operations and their owners.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change, migration, or required action. Public SDK/CLI/config/protocol contracts, lazy imports, authorization, and durable delivery/maintenance settlement stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private implementation details with their actual owners: portal dispatch, channel hints/catalog policy, agent selection and continuation, request transport, hook loading, worker-bundle staging, and Doctor completion. Tests that previously reached a retired helper now exercise the existing public operation instead; no replacement production test seams are introduced.

This is one single-consumer-surface cleanup batch, explicitly requested for publication at this size. Net production reduction is **206 lines** (+1,130/-1,336 across 56 production paths), excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, and declarations. The complete diff spans 82 paths, including test migrations and shrink-only inventories. Moved implementation bodies are not counted as deleted code. No feature or standalone memory backend is removed.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No runtime guard is removed or weakened. Security-effect checks, ordinary concurrency, bounded work, crash/restart durability, and uncertain-delivery reconciliation remain.
- The Doctor migration registry calls its lazy imports directly instead of through a generic asynchronous loader factory introduced by #166982. An extra private promise/microtask hop is not preserved as a contract; each operation still imports lazily and reads the same arguments after that import settles. Mutation of the internal registry context specifically between redundant forwarding microtasks is not a supported coordination mechanism.

## Evidence

- Each cut received a fresh isolated review through P2; all accepted/actionable findings were resolved. Final simplify passes retain named algorithms, remove only redundant internal surfaces, and preserve the real adapters and public entry points.
- Focused public-operation tests, targeted native typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and line-cap checks passed for each cut. Test-only helper access was migrated and proved against unchanged production before its corresponding fold. No new lint suppressions, baseline growth, retries, skips, or timeout increases.
- Representative proof includes dashboard socket/Gateway-auth paths (39 cases), worker-bundle production plus real worker adapter (24), public spawn failures (13), maintenance release/publication ordering (18), Gateway dispatch/reattachment and outbound contracts (98), compaction boundaries (13), and Feishu retry/concurrent sends (6). Continuation proof includes the prompt-prefix contract. Name-filtered unrelated cases were not run; no new skips were added.
- Full branch structural proof: lint-suppression tests, assertion/mock-export ratchets, protected wrapper/import closure, runtime/static cycle checks, and line caps. Exact-head PR CI is the broad/build/platform proof; no full local build, broad suite, or live-provider/channel verification is claimed.

The source-only plugin-shape test import migration is deferred to hosted CI because its automatic private-QA build prerequisite exceeds the local proof budget. No generated artifact was hand-edited. The scripts inventory changes only remove retired paths; PR-tool implementation is unchanged.

prs.title: perf(diagnostics-prometheus): avoid duplicating scrape bodies for HTTP
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prometheus scrapes allocate a second full copy of the rendered metrics body when Node concatenates the HTTP headers and first string chunk, then flattens that combined string for the socket. On a synthetic fixture matching observed family cardinalities, that unnecessary copy is approximately 5.28 MB per scrape.

## User Impact

Large scrapes generate less main-thread garbage. Metric identity, values, ordering, cardinality limits, authorization, and GET/HEAD metadata stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Call `res.flushHeaders()` before ending the response, preserving the existing immutable string renderer. GET and HEAD now share the final response path. Production code is **+4/-5 lines, net -1**, with no new cache or retained objects. The larger diff extends the existing benchmark and adds a synthetic cardinality fixture.

The benchmark measures the store plus real Node HTTP transport with a separate child-process client, excluding client CPU and heap from server measurements. The fixture has **4,628 stored entries, 60,154 rows, and a 5,278,020-byte body**. It preserves observed family counts and bucket bounds; labels, help text, and values are synthetic. Three historical exporter-drop rows are omitted from the observed 60,157-row shape. The 16,384-entry budget counts stored entries, not rendered histogram rows.

## Evidence and Decision

Measured on Node **26.12.1**, with baseline and candidate concurrent on separate interleaved CPU sets under an exclusive measurement slot, swapping placement in successive pairs. Pair 2 used slot B and the others used slot A; baseline ran on the even CPUs for pairs 1/3/5 and the odd CPUs for 2/4/6. The shared production guard remained in place; none of these pairs was interrupted. Each side used the identical store/fixture and one render per request. Only the candidate enabled the benchmark's `--flush-headers` option, matching the production change. The renderer source is unchanged between the measured baseline and this PR.

Each pair has **200 unprofiled HTTP requests per side** for CPU, latency, GC and promotion, followed by **100 sampled requests per side** at a 4 KiB heap-sampling interval, including objects collected by minor and major GC. Totals: **1,200 unprofiled and 600 sampled requests per side**. The reported latency means average per-pair percentiles; they are not pooled percentiles. Promotion comes from GC trace events inside the unprofiled phase only.

Admission: byte-identical output and reduced allocation; stop on a >=20% adverse mean or >=10% adverse result in both swapped pairs. Tail gates require >=200 samples for p95 and >=1,000 for p99; major GC is context below 50 collections per side. Mixed-sign paired deltas are inconclusive, require extra pairs for a gating decision, and are assessed by their absolute mean rather than a relative mean dominated by a small baseline.

**Allocation is consistently lower in all six pairs: -41.65%, saving 5,276,501 bytes/scrape. Total GC time also fell in all six pairs.** CPU, latency, and promotion have mixed-sign deltas and are **inconclusive as improvement claims**. Their six-pair absolute means are non-adverse: CPU -0.153 ms/scrape, p95 -0.770 ms, promotion -195,527 bytes/scrape. No metric meets an adverse gate. prs.title: feat(browser): save rendered pages as offline MHTML archives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #180472.

Operators cannot save an already-interacted browser tab as a reopenable offline page archive through OpenClaw. `openclaw browser archive --target-id <id>` captures the selected Chromium CDP tab as MHTML; JSON output reports the artifact path, target ID and URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Chromium's existing `Page.captureSnapshot` serializer in the browser plugin, with existing selected-tab, navigation-policy, CDP-session and media-publication owners. The node caller supplies the current node/profile policy at final media publication, including when policy changes during asynchronous preparation.

Existing-solutions preflight: current-document downloads fetch the original URL, while screenshot/PDF/text produce different artifacts. The inspected SingleFile CLI CDP implementation creates a new target and navigates it, so it does not preserve this selected tab's already-interacted state. No new dependency or archive engine is needed. Related merged direction: browser-owned download artifacts in #101369; that merge is not approval of this proposal. The linked issue has a bot advisory requesting maintainer consideration; no human acceptance is claimed.

Main deleted the former debug route module. This refresh keeps it deleted and registers the bounded archive route in `agent.archive.ts` through the canonical route index. The large snapshot module stays identical to main; no alternate dispatch or compatibility route is added. The route uses the public media SDK and the existing admission/publication guards.

## User Impact

The already-rendered tab can be reopened offline with its serialized DOM and resources. Browser media is temporary: copy archives that need durable retention. Archives can contain private page content, are not sanitized, and are not backups of application/server state. Capture retains the existing 5 MiB media limit. Existing-session Chrome MCP and Lightpanda profiles remain unsupported.

Twelve changed files against refreshed main: production **+135/-4**, tests **+64/-0**, docs **+11/-1**; no generated, lock or proof assets. Production growth supplies native capture, route/CLI discovery and the final node authority guard. The separate route owns one bounded operation and avoids growing the existing snapshot module beyond its lint limit. No new config/default, dependency, database, channel or protocol-version surface.

## Evidence

Exact current head: `1486f83bf553bd282f5acd347745216ff845bdda`, normal merge of main `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`. Linux, Node 24.22.1, Google Chrome 152.0.7977.64, pinned Playwright 1.64.0. Current proof ran on 2026-10-23; the committed source runtime's build-info matches this head. This is local Linux source-runtime proof, not installed-package or remote Testbox certification.

**Real public CLI → real Gateway → real Chromium → offline file readback**, rerun on this exact head:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../mhtml-live-proof-20261022.mts ../maintenance-180486-native-cli-20261023-run green --native-cli
```

The compiled public browser CLI calls an isolated token-authenticated Gateway and the production browser plugin. It captures an interacted DOM with CSS, image and iframe resources. The origin is then stopped and Chromium put offline before independently reopening the saved artifact. This is not a mocked Gateway or browser.

Redacted readback at `2026-10-23T01:09:37.581Z`:

```json
{
  "head": "1486f83bf553bd282f5acd347745216ff845bdda",
  "buildCommit": "1486f83bf553bd282f5acd347745216ff845bdda",
  "cliExit": 0,
  "realGateway": true,
  "authenticatedRpc": true,
  "artifact": {
    "bytes": 2101,
    "extension": ".mhtml",
    "sha256": "e1d5c5f996063b679200b3e97db8e1cf5fc4782373b957104204766d10debd53"
  },
  "offlineReadback": {
    "renderedText": true,
    "css": true,
    "image": true,
    "iframe": true,
    "originStopped": true,
    "browserOffline": true,
    "ordinaryHttpNavigationRejected": true
  },

```

Existing text inspection succeeded 1/1 before capture. Offline ordinary HTTP navigation succeeded 0/1, while the archive preserved all four content checks, 4/4. Logical MHTML resource-request events are not claimed as network egress. Receipt SHA-256 `232ce7e31a44a8440af2751b6802f7d0001584b645cd8db94729632bf9b12404`; unchanged driver SHA-256 `33439a1996f03ffd28e76baf64912ac94ce69ba9b3229580e275f2f73114e53e`.

**Real node owner / media-publication authority**, also rerun on this head:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../mhtml-authority-proof-20261022.mts <isolated-output-dir>
```

At `2026-10-23T01:09:18.136Z`, the production node command, registered archive route, native Chromium and actual media store yielded:

| Scenario | Current result |

| Allowed profile | saved 1, transferred 1; artifact independently reopened in Chromium |
| Initially forbidden profile | rejected 1; new archives 0 |
| Profile revoked when the actual temporary file appears | watcher observed revocation; request rejected; retained archives 0 |

Revocation uses public runtime config-snapshot publication and a native filesystem watcher during asynchronous media preparation. This is source-mode production node-owner proof, not paired-node WebSocket transport or a model turn. Receipt SHA-256 `46771cc28a5e522e929c77de8d41780b19981a41a780116ae3d4c58865760b45`; unchanged driver SHA-256 `5f7af1ab0c03151723748e00d3a089d47d7eacca85e98cd25f5999e0951d6b48`.

The paired dispatcher acceptance command is `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../mhtml-live-proof-20261022.mts "$MHTML_PROOF_OUTPUT" green`. The initial capability passed at c90e; the authority repair then passed at `17a966ab4708fb27aea20df5d887394cf86357a9`. Those historical receipts remain unchanged. Both relevant production paths above were rerun after this main merge; no ancestor proof is represented as current-head execution.

Current-head validation:

- `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CONTENT_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-observe.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.admission.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.content.chromium.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **57 passed, 1 skipped**, 136.48s Vitest / 146.51s wrapper. Native Chromium cases enabled.
- Repository-supported Go typecheck, focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: PASS. The final route layout was rechecked after moving it out of the snapshot module.
- `pnpm docs:list` and `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/cli/browser.md docs/tools/browser-control.md`: PASS, two MDX pages / 190ms.
- `pnpm build sourcePerformance`: PASS on the exact committed head, 229.1s; source runtime/plugin build. This profile omits UI and declaration generation.

Raw receipts, logs and MHTML artifacts remain outside the product branch; the redacted readbacks above are published here. All state, browser profiles and fixture pages were isolated; no production channels, model calls or external recipients were used.

Not tested: installed/release packages, full suites, full UI/declaration builds, paired-node WebSocket transport, existing-session Chrome MCP, Lightpanda, Windows/macOS, hostile-page or complete stale-caller race matrices. No hosted-CI success, independent review pass or maintainer product approval is claimed. Independent AI review was explicitly waived by the requester.

<details>
<summary>AI assistance and sanitized task transcript excerpt</summary>

Implementation and validation were AI-assisted. Task-only excerpts; unrelated discussion, paths and credentials omitted:

- User: prefer genuine new capabilities in directions demonstrated by merged Feature PRs; subsequently fix actionable open-PR issues and publicly request bot re-review.
- Assistant: distinguish saving the already-rendered tab from downloading the original document or printing PDF; inspect the pinned Playwright CDP contract and SingleFile's fresh-target behavior.
- Acceptance: existing text/native serialization controls worked; production archive dispatch on the base returned 404.
- Implementation: reuse browser-owned CDP capture, navigation policy and media store; fix lazy CLI discovery after exercising the built CLI.
- Review repair: reproduce a profile revocation that still publishes an archive; supply the existing synchronous requester guard from the node owner. The unchanged authority scenario then rejects publication.
- Current maintenance: preserve main's deleted debug module, register a focused archive route, rebuild the exact commit, run 57 focused tests and rerun real public CLI/offline readback plus node publication proof.

</details>
