prs.title: fix(ui): Settings Prefs shows an unlabeled empty Locale text box
prs.body:
Closes #172817

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Appearance → UI → Prefs shows an unlabeled, empty "Locale" text box that people mistake for a region or timezone setting.

## User Impact

User impact: the UI language is set in one place, the Appearance → Language picker. The generic Prefs form no longer offers a free-text box for it, which could save an invalid locale string. Existing `ui.prefs.locale` values are kept and still apply. `openclaw config schema` and the config docs now describe the field as the Control UI language, unrelated to `agents.defaults.userTimezone`. No migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Appearance → Language already owns `ui.prefs.locale`, so the generic form now leaves that one field out. This uses the same pattern as the `wizard` section, which the generic form leaves out because Setup owns it. The schema keeps `string`, max 20, rather than adding an enum, so configs that already hold a locale stay valid. The field gets a title and description (`Interface Language`) for every schema-driven surface. The UI labels move into `schema.labels.ui.ts`, because `schema.labels.ts` is already over the line cap.

## Evidence

Before and after: Control UI Settings → Appearance → UI, rendered in Chromium by the repo's mocked-Gateway e2e harness. The mocked `config.schema` is the real `ui` schema and hints from `computeBaseConfigSchemaResponse()`, on `upstream/main` 55147a0e6 for "before" and on this branch for "after".

**Before (main):** the Prefs group has an empty "Locale" text box between Chat Show Tool Calls and Theme.

![Before: Prefs form with empty Locale text box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae93a684-6c09-4fe5-9a3f-9dcdc232482b)

**After:** the Prefs group no longer shows Locale. Every other pref is unchanged.

![After: Prefs form without Locale](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d2f9dbf-fc51-4a57-a9ed-a9d3e08e389c)

**After:** the owned Language picker on Appearance is unchanged.

![After: Appearance Language picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2816983a-bbe7-466b-a3e3-601a53ca2336)

Schema output for `ui.prefs.locale`:
- Before: `{"type":"string","maxLength":20}`
- After: `{"type":"string","maxLength":20,"title":"Interface Language","description":"Language for the Control UI, as a supported locale id such as en, de or zh-CN. Leave it unset to follow the browser or system language. Set it from Settings → Appearance → Language. Not related to the assistant's timezone (agents.defaults.userTimezone)."}`

Checks run locally (ClawSweeper's acceptance list):
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/config/view.browser.test.tsx src/pages/config/view-appearance.browser.test.tsx`: 37 passed. The new regression test covers both an unset locale and a set one (`de`). It fails on main, where the form still renders "Locale", and passes here.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/config-form-guidance.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/appearance-settings-defaults.e2e.test.ts`: 10 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: the line-cap, format, schema, docs-baseline, typecheck and plugin-boundary checks pass for this change. The remaining failures happen the same way on `upstream/main` 55147a0e6 and involve none of the files changed here: the `OPENCLAW_*` env-var budget (455 > 454), knip unused exports in `chat-picker-overlay.ts` and other files, and `max-lines` lint errors in 43 existing files. The SQLite worker ratchet needs `rg`, which is not installed on this machine, and this change has no SQLite code.

Merge danger: **two-way door**. Reverting brings the text box back. The change touches no persisted state, schema validation or Gateway behavior. Blast radius: the generic UI Prefs form and the schema metadata for one field.

prs.title: feat(cron): read retained run transcripts from the CLI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #167242.

Operators inspecting a completed automation can list its run summary, but the native cron CLI cannot read the retained transcript for a selected job/run. Today they must manually construct `gateway call cron.history` JSON. A truncated summary can be mistaken for truncated output and lead to unnecessary reruns; [#69678](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69678) describes duplicated digest delivery during that diagnosis.

Add `openclaw cron history <id> --run-id <runId> [--cursor <opaque>] [--limit <n>]`, with JSON output and the existing `automations` alias. This reads whatever the existing transcript owner retains. It does not recover absent output or change summary limits, retention, delivery, UI navigation, or conversation continuation. The broader #69678 and #155588 requests are not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI is the missing owner surface. The Gateway already implements `cron.history`, and the Control UI already uses recorded job/run identity and opaque pagination. The implementation reuses existing cron registration, option inheritance, integer/string validation, error handling, and JSON output. Limits, authorization, run binding, visibility, pagination and storage remain owned by the existing Gateway method.

Existing-solutions preflight: the generic public RPC is a functional alternative, but it requires hand-authored parameters rather than a discoverable native command. No plugin, dependency or new integration is necessary. The retained owner work merged in [#158776](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158776) establishes the existing owner contract; that merge is not endorsement of this new CLI proposal. This is an I1 Feature issue created by this contributor, not a claim of prior human approval.

## User Impact

Operators can select and page a retained transcript without rerunning the automation or manually assembling RPC JSON. Missing/blank selectors, blank cursors and invalid integer limits fail before a request; opaque cursor bytes pass through unchanged. The server retains its default/max limit decisions.

Four files against the refreshed main: production +30/-0, tests +112/-0, documentation +27/-1; no generated or lock files. The production additions register one command and include it in existing JSON output routing. No config/default, protocol/schema, permission, dependency, migration, scheduling or storage changes. For custom/shared-session jobs, the existing owner can return shared conversation messages, including later messages; this command does not promise run-exclusive content.

## Evidence

**Current-head refresh, 2026-10-23:** `51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b`, tree `7ef1e5d99c2f15a424bac12e4ee41482aa856349`, after a normal merge of main `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`. Linux, Node 24.22.1; source build version 2026.10.6. The upstream-deleted broad test file remains deleted. The eleven retained-history command cases now live in the focused `register.cron-history.test.ts`; a redundant oversized-output mock assertion was removed. The production command contract is unchanged. This supplies updated code/proof, not human acceptance of the proposed CLI surface.

The exact committed runtime was rebuilt with `pnpm build sourcePerformance` (PASS, 279.7s); `dist/build-info.json` matches the current head. Both public-entry scenarios were rerun:

```sh
node ../cron-history-cli-proof-20261008.mjs --root "$PWD" --phase green --expected-head 51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b
node ../cron-history-gateway-proof-20261023.mjs --root "$PWD" --phase green --expected-head 51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b
```

- Public CLI/WebSocket transport: **11/11 PASS**, 40.485s, `2026-10-23T00:58:40.471Z` to `00:59:20.956Z`. prs.title: fix(ios): authenticate embedded Settings behind Basic proxies
prs.body:
Related to #175522

## What Problem This Solves

Embedded iOS Settings receives HTTP 401 behind an HTTPS Basic-auth proxy while native Gateway/chat already works with configured proxy credentials.

## User Impact

Embedded Settings and the Dashboard pages sharing `EmbeddedDashboardContent` can authenticate their document, resources and Dashboard WebSocket with existing per-Gateway Basic credentials. This intentionally extends the original custom-header feature's WebView exclusion. Colin (@Solvely-Colin) explicitly approved this narrow embedded credential scope and landing on October 23, 2026, after reviewing its iOS and Mac impact. This decision does not waive enforced GitHub review or security gates. Desktop, Terminal and session-dashboard callers retain their existing behavior.

HTTP-error classification and retry remain separate work in #174957.

## Why This Change Was Made

Answer WebKit's native Basic authentication challenge after checking HTTPS, exact host/port, non-proxy origin and first attempt, then reread the existing Keychain owner. Credentials use `URLCredential.Persistence.none` and never enter URLs, page scripts or logs. The real bridge retains its reply-capable `addScriptMessageHandler` registration.

Credential lifetime is the next authentication challenge: every eligible challenge rereads Keychain, including deletion and replacement. The retained-WebView transport regression proves no obsolete credential is transmitted on subsequent HTTP or WebSocket requests. This does not revoke credentials at the proxy, recall requests already sent, or terminate an already-authenticated WebSocket.

## Evidence

Complete-app simulator validation now passes on unchanged production head `b06898491aa26b9f429e348ea5883ecf580277c3`, using Xcode 27.1, Swift 6.3 and iOS 27.0:

- **3/3 authentication tests passed in 4.623s** in the ordinary complete OpenClaw app host. The cold build/test command completed successfully in 443.273s. This includes actual document/resource/WebSocket authentication, a second HTTPS origin receiving its Basic 401 challenge without Authorization, and real Keychain deletion/replacement on the retained WebView.
- **1/1 actual Settings/Gateway flow test passed in 10.459s**; the full command completed successfully in 96.264s. Real `NodeAppModel`, `GatewayConnectionController`, `SettingsHubScreen`, its WKWebView and production-built Dashboard assets ran behind an isolated synthetic HTTPS Basic-auth proxy. Native operator/admin connected normally. The actual browser connection received successful `connect`, `config.get` and `config.schema` responses on that same connection, with 133 authorized HTTP 200 responses and zero model-send RPCs. The test also required the actual `/settings/advanced` config panel DOM to be present, have visible dimensions and finish loading its schema.
- Both runs retained the standard OpenClaw scheme, real reply-capable Settings bridge, all 10 resolved Swift packages, real Watch WebRTC and the share/widget/Watch target graph. No production stubs, source/target exclusions, fake connected/admin state, auth-disabled mode or fake Dashboard responses were used. The additional flow harness and isolated server fixture were test-only inputs outside the PR branch.
- The genuine unmodified upstream baseline previously failed the Settings integration regression in 1.216s on all four expected authentication assertions. The earlier bounded component runs also passed, but the complete-app runs above supersede the earlier full-app disk-capacity limitation.
- Hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` and iOS screenshot checks pass on this head. Pinned SwiftFormat, targeted production SwiftLint, whitespace checks and the independent scoped P2 review previously passed; no production changes were made for this validation.

Sanitized excerpts from the successful app-hosted runs and captured transport trace:

```text
SettingsProxyAuthenticationTests: 3 tests passed, 4.623 seconds
** TEST SUCCEEDED **

SettingsFullAppGatewayProofTests:
  Settings hub uses its real operator and browser connection behind the Basic proxy
  passed after 10.459 seconds
** TEST SUCCEEDED **

Native operator/admin: connected
Settings document/assets: HTTP 200, Basic authenticated
Browser connection 5: Origin matched, openclaw-control-ui / webchat
Browser connection 5: connect OK, config.get OK, config.schema OK
Advanced config panel: visible DOM, schema loading complete
Authorized HTTP 200 responses: 133
Foreign HTTPS origin: HTTP 401, Authorization absent
Keychain removed: HTTP 401 / WebSocket rejected, Authorization absent
Keychain replaced: HTTP 200 / WebSocket authenticated, replacement observed, old absent
Model-send RPCs: 0
Owned Gateway/proxy listeners closed: true
Isolated fixture state removed: true
```

The suites ran separately in the complete app scheme with `xcodebuild test`, selectors `OpenClawTests/SettingsProxyAuthenticationTests` and `OpenClawTests/SettingsFullAppGatewayProofTests`, and `ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES COMPILER_INDEX_STORE_ENABLE=NO -jobs 2 -parallel-testing-enabled NO`. The real native scene lifecycle and normal approval/retry of only the fixture's own observed synthetic devices were exercised. The isolated Gateway retained token authentication; the proxy used synthetic Basic credentials. Only the public synthetic fixture certificate was trusted in a task-exclusive simulator, and native fixture observation/approval used the production exact certificate-pin evaluator. Live Gateway/user configuration was untouched, and owned fixture state and listeners were cleaned up.

## Complete-app Settings capture

Actual embedded Settings root rendered in the complete app during the isolated simulator validation behind the synthetic HTTPS Basic-auth proxy. This image shows the Settings root list; the Advanced configuration route is established by the separate DOM assertion and transport evidence above.

![Actual embedded iOS Settings root in the complete-app simulator validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68da6d83-48ae-426d-b32d-eb71621755de)

## Scope Decision and Limits

Colin (@Solvely-Colin) approved reusing existing saved Basic proxy credentials for embedded Settings and the Dashboard pages sharing its host, restricted to the configured HTTPS authority. Desktop, Terminal, session dashboards and the Mac app are unchanged. The original implementation remains credited to @brianmcguire.

The complete-app results above are contributor-supplied validation on the exact reviewed head, not a new native execution by the landing reviewer. Simulator proof does not establish physical-device behavior, manual onboarding, or every proxy deployment. Clearing a saved credential does not revoke open authenticated sockets, in-flight requests or server-side sessions. Enforced review and security gates remain applicable.

Named wording follow-up: align the iOS custom-header footer's next-reconnect wording with this handler's next-eligible-challenge behavior, and describe the shared Dashboard scope consistently with Settings. This PR does not change that UI wording.

prs.title: improve: load About and Dashboard copy when each view opens
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI startup and Chat load English copy for About and the Dashboard gallery before either view opens.

## User Impact

Those views keep their text and behavior while their optional copy follows the existing lazy view boundaries. Shared build details and dashboard-document controls remain available immediately. Changes-panel copy remains with its existing owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split only the optional About and Dashboard English fragments into the existing synchronous registrar pattern. Each view registers its fragment when its module loads. The build-time catalog preserves all 11,299 flattened keys, values, and ordering; registration keeps the shared namespace objects and non-English fallback intact. No generated locale output or boot-manifest change is needed.

## Evidence

Matched production builds compare the shared `6ada8b0211b` UI baseline with this candidate after merging current main `bb41c47d7736`. The intervening main changes do not touch UI, build scripts, package manifests, or the lockfile. Builds use identical metadata, 29 plugin inputs, and dependencies. Measurements use `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --json --report-only --base-dist <baseline-dist>` and shipped compression sidecars.

| Surface | Baseline gzip JS | Candidate gzip JS | Change | Requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Startup | 316,344 B | 315,878 B | −466 B | 7 → 7 |
| New Session | 826,448 B | 825,998 B | −450 B | 17 → 17 |
| Chat | 1,353,278 B | 1,352,854 B | −424 B | 23 → 23 |

CSS is unchanged. Across all emitted JavaScript, output grows 16,444 gzip bytes and 42 deferred locale fragments. This is a boot-path reduction that relocates optional work, not a total-size reduction. Strict performance budgets pass with no warnings or violations.

The actual About/Dashboard module-loading regression passes under a partial German locale; restoring the base's eager catalog makes it fail. Shared labels remain eager and complete English fallback appears on view import. All 11,299 host-catalog entries match the original keys, values, and order exactly. The 38 host-catalog tests, production UI and script typechecks, targeted lint/format, and keyless i18n verification pass. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

**Cold-load timing is pending and is a landing gate.** Before the first timing run, acceptance is fixed as 10 alternating baseline/candidate cold-cache pairs using the committed Control UI benchmark (`--runs 20`), with transcript-visible median regression ≤5% and p95 no worse. Report composer median/p95 separately, use identical metadata/plugins, record host CPU/RAM/cgroup/load, and keep profiling separate. One additional batch may extend the comparison to 20 pairs. This PR makes no wall-clock speedup claim yet.

prs.title: fix(workspace): prevent baseline preparation from blocking the gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recurring multi-second Gateway stalls when preparing a full local workspace baseline. Follow-up to #180149 (`7ef85325b7c718f7ec27ecf496fe09a92a080d94`). Production profiles identified 19 baseline-replacement stalls over one second, totaling 73.4 seconds in about 3.5 hours; this is not limited to first use after migration.

## User Impact

Workspace baseline preparation no longer constructs and serializes the complete digest tree on the Gateway main thread. **No schema change; schema 31 and its existing migration/recovery contract are preserved.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement path ran the synchronous tree builder after returning to the Gateway. Legacy conversion is one-time per persisted baseline, but new workspace creation, base refresh, full-document acceptance and archive/recovery operations also use the same path. Ordinary checkpoints remain incremental.

Build full sibling trees in one pass after sorting, then compute each node and subtree digest once. Full construction and incremental updates share the same record/digest owner. Prepare and compress the replacement in the existing workspace manifest read worker, then forward the opaque bytes to the existing writer. The host retains only the root and patch needed to publish the committed row. Scan metadata for unchanged files also stays encoded between workers, instead of returning a full object graph to the host for cloning and serialization. Its prepared acceptance combines fresh host-path admission with metadata persistence while preserving the separate pending content delta. The existing atomic acceptance, revision/previous-root checks, live lease and registry authority, rollback and lost-reply handling remain in place. Replacement reads skip the old node rows they will replace.

The simplification pass removes the main-thread tree-construction path and reuses the existing worker, wire encoding and writer transaction. Production code grows by 155 lines to carry the prepared mutation across that boundary without cloning the complete tree back onto the main thread and construct full trees without repeated ancestor hashing. The shared leaf mutation contract avoids importing the writer implementation from its read worker. This introduces no new cache, configuration or stored format.

## Evidence

- Final observation-change store/projection tests: 47 passed, 2 existing skips; 172.69s Vitest wall time (178.36s wrapper), including worker compilation. The six unchanged tree tests passed earlier. The new observation regression fails on the prior head (37 expanded records cross the worker boundary, over the bound of fewer than 32) and passes after the fix; it covers fresh host Git admission, stale prepared-update rejection, retained pending edits and eventual content acceptance. Proof covers interrupted prepared replacement, atomic rollback, lost commit reply and materialized data afterward, plus edits/deletions/renames/modes/symlinks after restart. The new digest-work regression fails on the old builder (12,146 hashes for 576 paths, exceeding the 2,308 bound), and passes with the bulk builder. Serialized records and roots match incremental construction; an independent sandbox comparison also matches the original builder across flat/nested/order variants and subsequent edits.
- Changed-file formatting and focused type-aware lint passed. Final-head PR CI is green on `88cbe7082060b38928ba6ca80f5ba3ae99be2689`, including `openclaw/ci-gate` (CI run `39879438460`, aggregate run `39880382630`). Earlier CI found a type-only dependency cycle and a test-only heterogeneous-array inference error; both are corrected. The final test-only correction leaves runtime and measurement driver bytes unchanged. CI run `39879438460` finished with 51 passed jobs and 27 skipped, zero failures; its exact-head logs include store 14 passed, tree 6 passed, projection 34 passed/1 skipped and closure checks 22 passed.
- Source review verified all full-replacement callers use the worker path and bulk construction preserves the stored digest format. Autoreview is scoped-clean through P2, including the final prepared-observation change. All final measurements pass independent review under v5.2, including the absolute 50 ms natural baseline limit. Final-head CI and autoreview are clean; the required evidence is complete.

### Measurement contract (recorded before runs)


The committed reproducer is `scripts/bench-workspace-computation.ts`, run separately for each pinned side under the guard, scope and placement described below:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-workspace-computation.ts \
  --candidate "$SOURCE_ROOT" --scenarios baseline-build --sizes 20000 \
  --concurrency 1 --file-bytes 1024 --changed-files 0 --runs 10 --warmup 1 \
  --sampling-interval 0 --reuse-root "$FIXTURE_ROOT" \
  --start-barrier "$BARRIER" --output "$RESULT"
```

Checkpoint runs use `--scenarios checkpoint --changed-files 100 --runs 200`. Separate allocation runs use `--runs 10 --sampling-interval 32768`; sampled latency is not substituted for natural latency. Fixtures are prepared sequentially with the same driver and `--prepare-root` before pairing.

Synthetic 20,000-file workspace. Time the real owner baseline migration (including preparation and acceptance), separately from steady-state checkpoints and restart reuse. Measure maximum synchronous main-thread callback/Promise-job duration, wall time, main allocation, and natural checkpoint p95 (200 checkpoints per side per swapped pair); do not treat an averaged percentile as pooled. Two concurrent A/B pairs under one quiet lock each, interleaved physical cores, swapped placements. Shared production guard as-is (2,500 ms, three consecutive bad minutes). Prep uses CPUs0–63, nice19, CPUWeight10, IOWeight10, bounded memory, small sequential writes.

Apply v5/v5.1/v5.2: sample minima, absolute and paired-relative deltas, inconclusive opposite signs or >5x baseline spread, third pair for an inconclusive gate, and GC pause-percentile exception with baseline/candidate maxima. Require every measured baseline-build main-thread callback/Promise-job slice to remain at or below 50 ms. The initial bulk-build candidate failed this limit: one natural pair reached 158.001 ms (baseline 622.486 ms). Profiling identified full unchanged-file observation records returning to the main thread for cloning and serialization. The final candidate prepares that mutation in the read worker as well. The failed earlier candidate is not used as final-head proof. Keep allocation sampling separate from natural latency/GC.


### Baseline build: final runtime, natural timing and GC

Frozen baseline `d535d274183d19e2e838c7a7fc96063df676b368` versus final head `88cbe7082060b38928ba6ca80f5ba3ae99be2689` (runtime identical to `95a3b021`). All eight production overlay files were hash-verified. A later main fetch at `f492d369d69b` showed no changes in the owned runtime or benchmark paths since pre-push qualification. Each side has 10 measured warm baseline builds plus one cold build and one warmup per pair. **All 36 actual candidate builds stayed below 50 ms: maximum 34.388 ms, versus 596.810 ms before.**

Each cell is baseline → candidate. GC values sum isolate work, not elapsed stop time. MB is decimal.

| Pair | Maximum main callback, ms | Wall mean, ms/build | CPU mean, ms/build | Main GC, ms/build | All-isolate GC, ms/build | All-isolate promotion, MB/build |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 474.236 → 29.024 | 3355.143 → 2917.936 | 5064.001 → 4673.632 | 81.753 → 2.020 | 266.776 → 179.287 | 274.690 → 145.322 |
| 2 (swapped) | 596.810 → 34.388 | 3241.762 → 3421.387 | 5066.026 → 5192.812 | 93.660 → 4.113 | 258.427 → 236.456 | 213.772 → 203.256 |
| 3 (v5.2 resolution) | 479.495 → 31.276 | 3430.015 → 2716.659 | 5218.174 → 4301.480 | 84.288 → 2.507 | 266.634 → 190.270 | 270.491 → 145.460 |

Wall and CPU signs differed in the first two pairs; the required third pair resolves them using absolute means: wall **−323.646 ms/build (−9.683%)**, CPU **−393.426 ms/build (−7.690%)**. Stable metrics retain the original swapped-pair basis: main callback −94.06%, main GC −96.57%, main promotion −91.77%, all-isolate GC −20.65%, all-isolate promotion −26.01%. Ten warm samples per pair do not qualify a build-latency p95 gate.

| Pair | Minor GC p95, ms (collection counts) | Minor maximum, ms | Major GC p95, ms (collection counts; context) | Maximum GC pause, ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 1 | 5.012 (n=1044) → 4.761 (n=822) | 10.864 → 12.037 | 16.499 (n=72) → 15.153 (n=67) | 28.823 → 18.537 |
| 2 | 6.308 (n=919) → 4.463 (n=940) | 23.043 → 16.733 | 17.215 (n=63) → 25.331 (n=83) | 57.799 → 68.616 |
| 3 | 5.199 (n=1087) → 5.338 (n=809) | 9.151 → 12.685 | 17.219 (n=79) → 13.213 (n=62) | 32.496 → 15.698 |

GC includes all isolates. The 68.616 ms pause is in a worker, not a main-thread slice. No maximum exceeds the v5.1 override. Minor tails in pairs 1 and 3 are context under the count-reduction/total-GC exception; major tails are under the 200-collection p95 minimum in all pairs. Independent review reparsed raw GC traces and verified counts, all measured build callbacks, placement and decisions.

Fresh-process reuse retained the converted root and reconciled a subsequent real edit. Its separate source-mode startup profile attributed a roughly 118 ms callback to dynamic ESM/tsx/esbuild loading (104/109 samples), not baseline tree construction. The callback probe measures individual callbacks/Promise jobs; adjacent microtasks are separate.

### Baseline allocation: final runtime, separate sampled runs

Two swapped pairs, 10 warm builds per side per pair; main-isolate allocation sampling interval 32,768 bytes. Both metrics improve in both pairs and pass independent raw-sample review under v5.2; no third pair is required.

prs.title: fix(ui): prune the live cli-assistant segment when its row persists mid-run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #180927. In a Control UI webchat session on a CLI backend with block streaming off, the assistant reply appeared twice: the live stream bubble kept the partial text while the durable row, persisted mid-run, was admitted beside it. The reporter measured the corresponding gateway failure 360 times in one day.

The pane already clears the live stream when a persisted row owns the active run — but that ownership check requires an explicit envelope run id (`event.runId` / row metadata), and the mid-run transcript publish can omit it. CLI assistant rows are self-proving: the Gateway stamps the run id into the persisted idempotency key (`cli-assistant:<runId>`), which the projection layer already canonicalizes into the row's run id.

## What Changed

`ui/src/pages/chat/session-message-apply.ts` only:

- A persisted CLI assistant row (`role: assistant`, `api: "cli"`) whose canonical idempotency-key run id is present now qualifies as producer-owned for the matching active run, even when the envelope omits the run id.
- That ownership feeds the existing persistence path, which clears the live stream so the durable row replaces the bubble instead of duplicating it.

The first revision of this PR keyed a different stream owner (`chatStreamSegments`) that the CLI assistant flow does not write; that path is gone. No other surface changes: rows without CLI provenance keep the terminal-stream behavior, and no delivery path gains or loses a send.

## Evidence

**Red/green regression** (`session-message-apply.test.ts`, real pane event path: live `chatStream` filled, then the persisted `session.message` row):

```
fix applied (9caa2aab):  ✓ 10 passed (10)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (without an envelope run id)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (with a matching envelope run id)
  - keeps the live stream for mid-run persisted rows without cli provenance

fix reverted, same tests:  × clears the live stream ... (without an envelope run id)
  Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
```

**Adjacent suites after the change:**

```
session-message-apply + chat-pane-{session,snapshot}-hydration + tool-stream-fallback: 57 passed (57)
```

prs.title: fix(ui): Shift+Tab accepts composer suggestions instead of moving backward
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Shift+Tab accepts a composer suggestion instead of moving focus backward, unexpectedly changing the draft and potentially selecting a notification recipient.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard users can move backward from slash-command, skill-reference, and person suggestions without accepting them. Unmodified Tab still completes the selected suggestion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the suggestion keyboard owner’s existing modifier guard for Tab, rather than adding consumer-specific handlers or focus management. No new state, listeners, ARIA, or configuration.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway data: Shift+Tab changed `@Casey` to `@Casey Vale `, selected a recipient, and retained composer focus. With the fix, the draft and recipients remain unchanged and focus moves to the same preceding native control as without the popup. No message was sent.
- Regression red on base `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`, green on candidate: shared modifier contract (empty/populated suggestions), bundled mention flow, and native slash navigation in both Chat and New Session.
- Local passing proof: 86 focused unit/consumer/IME/emoji/prediction tests; 8 Chromium composer browser tests; 1 bundled Chromium E2E. New test runtimes: owner file <1 ms test time; bundled flow 1.25 s test time / 30.48 s including production build; browser file 4.19 s total. Per-file CI timings were not separately extracted.
- Passing checks: UI and ui-components/ui-chat/ui-e2e-chat test types, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, controller guard, keyless English i18n verification, and diff whitespace.
- Independent Auto Review: scoped-clean through P2 on all four changed files; no findings. Simplification: one additional guarded key, no new production machinery; tests cover modifier policy, native browser behavior, and bundled recipient selection at distinct boundaries.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39881729697) on `594fc099edc1455990ef44065cd8fe248f3a5575`: 39 checks passed, including the existing Chromium and WebKit composer-focus job. The WebKit installation and test steps both completed successfully. Local WebKit could not qualify this rootless host, so this required engine proof came from normal CI without a validation skip or host change.

Before: Shift+Tab accepts Casey Vale and adds a notification recipient.

![Before: Shift+Tab selects Casey Vale and retains composer focus](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ecc4377-2ebf-4ad6-9625-b53d12beb086)

After: the draft remains `@Casey`, no recipient is selected, and focus moves backward to the preceding native control.

![After: unchanged draft and backward native focus without selecting a recipient](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ce5371b-38d7-4fc0-9605-56999157100c)

Requested by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fa35e3ac-f155-4285-962e-e966642f64c8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/455dbc29-cb81-45de-a84e-ed977f77a954)

prs.title: improve: load optional chat panels when needed
prs.body:
**Closed after failing the declared cold-load timing criterion.** The byte saving is real, but neither sampling batch established p95 non-regression. The source branch is retained; this change is not being landed.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat downloads optional panel renderers just to display their small header controls and the subagent avatar.

## User Impact

Chat boot transfers 5,957 fewer gzip bytes with the same 23 JavaScript requests. Header controls and subagent avatars keep their existing appearance and behavior. Startup and New Session remain unchanged within build variance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing panel-header controls and avatar into small shared modules. Eager header consumers can then use them without importing the optional embedded-panel and desktop-subagent renderers. The existing panel loaders still own when those renderers load; this adds no loader, loading state, state owner, or runtime dependency. Both avatar stylesheets remain available to its header and mobile consumers.

The official boot-manifest generator records the resulting graph. The full initial module attribution is in #180852; standalone module gzip figures are diagnostic and non-additive.

## Evidence

Same-machine production comparison: base source `69740ceee5847e56fd6e8b2a73629821549bb27d` (retained runtime build `6cdc426ae6b`, with only scalar budget differences), candidate runtime source `119b9da1067`, Node 26.12.1, with identical fixed build metadata and the same 29 packaged-plugin files. Both use build ID `solid2-boot-comparison`; these controlled metadata inputs are distinct from the actual source identities above.

| Surface | Base JS gzip | Head JS gzip | Change | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,327 B | 316,316 B | −11 B (variance; raw unchanged) | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,353,266 B | 1,347,309 B | −5,957 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 826,422 B | 826,397 B | −25 B (variance) | 17 → 17 |

Startup CSS stays 41,124 B gzip / one request. Strict performance comparison has zero violations and warnings. Chat's cap falls from 1,405,102 to 1,398,917 B: `ceil(1347309 × 1405102 / 1353266)` preserves the existing relative headroom. Other byte/request caps and the startup baseline are unchanged.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Official boot capture and production build | Passed |
| UI typecheck | Passed after Menu/main integration |
| Sidebar lazy-loading, mobile header actions, desktop/mobile subagents | 28/28 across three focused files after Menu/main integration |
| Strict base/head byte comparison | Passed, zero violations/warnings |
| Independent P0–P2 review of the extraction | Scoped-clean |
| Production Knip | One inherited unused file: `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.context.test-support.mjs`; same finding reproduced on exact main `9f89542dafe` before Menu, with unchanged Telegram/config inputs |
| Targeted lint/format and final budget review | Passed; isolated budget review scoped-clean |
| Full UI CI | Prior head `ecab317861909b690e157835aed413b36bfc762b` passed [run 39876684350](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39876684350); fresh integration-head CI pending |
| Reload-to-transcript/composer timing | Failed the declared p95 gate in the initial and combined samples; auto-merge was never armed |

Timing acceptance was declared before sampling: at least ten serial alternating cold-cache base/head pairs with the committed comparison driver; median may not regress more than 5%, and p95 may not worsen. The initial ten pairs failed the p95 rule. The coordinator authorized exactly one additional ten-pair batch on the same lease; the combined twenty pairs still failed. No samples were discarded, no third batch was run, and no tolerance was added after measurement.

| Samples per side | Metric | Median base → head (ms) | Median change | p95 base → head (ms) | p95 change | Verdict |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Initial: 10 pairs | Transcript visible | 465.20 → 443.00 | -4.77% | 549.30 → 566.30 | +3.09% | Failed |
| Initial: 10 pairs | Composer enabled | 464.30 → 442.20 | -4.76% | 548.40 → 565.40 | +3.10% | Failed |
| Combined: 20 pairs | Transcript visible | 511.40 → 528.25 | +3.29% | 835.70 → 838.80 | +0.37% | Failed |
| Combined: 20 pairs | Composer enabled | 510.40 → 526.85 | +3.22% | 834.50 → 837.30 | +0.34% | Failed |

Timing used exact base `69740ceee5847e56fd6e8b2a73629821549bb27d` and candidate `a1d262a6a4acc8804e58a2dc2f6e6a06a9ba18f1` (the runtime above plus its cap-only commit) on one Blacksmith Testbox, with identical build proof and plugin inputs. Observed resources were four AMD EPYC CPUs (affinity 0–3), 16.55 GB total RAM, Node 24.22.1; the requested runner label advertised 16 vCPUs but did not describe the allocation. The production Vite-preview benchmark used synthetic bootstrap, WebSocket RPC and media fixtures, persisted UI warm state with cold HTTP cache, no tracing or profiling, and a fixed fixture clock. It measured reload-to-first-nonempty-transcript and first-enabled-composer. Load averages and every raw sample remain in the retained evidence; both batches reported valid measurements.

The benchmark ran on [Testbox workflow 39883063449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39883063449). The local evidence archive includes both raw summaries, all 40 sample artifacts, resource records, install/build logs, matching base/head build proofs, and a 133-file SHA-256 manifest. Archive SHA-256: `cc15e07e9958214fc74b97ead1c78899b0a7142942d565b289bd8a68301e8ef3`. The 5,957 B Chat saving does not justify claiming the timing gate passed; this PR is closed without merging.


Production TypeScript/TSX in the changed scope: 2,594 → 2,608 lines (+14). The added lines are module imports and the shared prop type; existing renderers are moved, not copied. Effects, render effects, `untrack`, direct listeners, DOM queries, `flush`, owner APIs and component cleanup remain zero in the touched files. Existing dynamic imports remain 4 → 4. Simplification review found no additional state or abstraction to remove.

This is a module-boundary change with identical JSX and existing lazy-panel loading states, so it introduces no visual state to capture. No local E2E suite was run. One task-owned Testbox lease ran the two authorized timing batches and was stopped after evidence collection.

prs.title: fix: recover queued follow-ups after missed completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a queued follow-up stays stuck behind stale Working/Waiting state when the original browser misses the previous run's completion.

## User Impact

Queued follow-ups can resume after the Gateway reports the previous run idle, without refreshing the browser. Existing queue ordering, edit holds, and steer/interrupt behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

A new queued follow-up now asks the existing serialized outbox owner to reconcile activity from authoritative history. Passive event-driven wakes keep their known-active shortcut, avoiding a large history read on every streaming event. Each foreground reconciliation request is consumed before awaiting history, so a passive rerun cannot reuse it; a new foreground request arriving during the await remains pending. No new timer, persisted state, or Gateway policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the production-built Control UI: the original browser stayed busy with a local queued follow-up after 65 seconds of virtual time; a fresh browser was idle; refreshing the original released the follow-up exactly once.
- Initial stale-busy reproduction fails on base `d0931ba3d436f91d5793868d51954193e74e9207`. The current two-case work-count regression fails on previous PR head `7bfb0fa86f3aec80cfa13e7059a4ecfa60c6abc6` and passes after the passive-rerun repair.
- Original production browser regression passes: with terminal events withheld and authoritative snapshots idle, Queue sends exactly once without a refresh and removes the stale run display.
- 372 focused outbox/send tests pass on the repaired candidate. UI production and test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. The exact candidate was built with `pnpm build` and `pnpm ui:build`.
- Independent autoreview of the follow-up repair: scoped-clean for P0–P2. The reported passive-rerun finding is covered by active-history tests with an interleaved passive wake and an additional foreground request.

### Before

The original browser still shows the previous run as active, with the follow-up retained in the local queue.

![Before: stale active run and queued follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d649fb1a-2b44-4ace-8eff-4038814dfffb)

### After

Without refreshing, the follow-up has been sent and the stale previous run is gone. The waiting indicator now belongs to the newly submitted request.

![After: follow-up sent without refreshing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f10d29e6-d60e-48b3-b17e-f2ad9b901a86)

### Isolated live Gateway and model

The screenshots above show the original synthetic-Gateway reproduction. An additional run used the production-built UI, a disposable real Gateway, and the real OpenAI model `gpt-4.1-mini`. No Gateway history or send responses were replaced. At the browser transport, the proof withheld terminal notifications and matching session-row updates; provider responses and RPC traffic were not replaced.

- The original run completed while its follow-up remained queued in the stale browser.
- A new foreground follow-up triggered real authoritative history before the first queued send, on the original connection.
- All three real assistant replies arrived in order: `INITIAL_LIVE_DONE`, `FIRST_FOLLOWUP_LIVE_DONE`, `SECOND_FOLLOWUP_LIVE_DONE`. Exactly three unique sends occurred, with no browser document reload.
- The owned Gateway, synchronization gate, and temporary state were cleaned up.

![Real assistant replies after queued recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/750d70b5-745f-49a3-9811-3437633caacd)

**Retained live-harness failure:** the extra no-WebSocket-reconnect assertion failed (expected 3 sockets, observed 4). The fourth socket was opened with two sends already recorded: the initial request and first recovered follow-up. Thus authoritative reconciliation and first recovery dispatch happened on the original connection. Browser document identity remained unchanged; FIFO and exactly-once send checks passed. This is not a fully passing live-harness run.

**Failure classification after bounded source/artifact inspection:** the injector also withheld matching `sessions.changed` / `session.message` updates until recovery dispatch. Browser connections negotiate session-row deltas; suppressing those updates can leave their connection-owned baseline stale even though transport sequence numbers are preserved. The unchanged [row decoder and reconnect owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a7b188e241b9b22eabaa1bf516805c0927131a5c/ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.ts#L69-L76) intentionally reconnect on a missing baseline, with [existing regression coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a7b188e241b9b22eabaa1bf516805c0927131a5c/ui/src/api/gateway-session-row-events.node.test.ts#L193-L221). This provides a concrete injection-induced explanation, not evidence of an outbox regression or a no-reconnect product requirement. The retained run lacks close code/reason and per-frame timestamps, so the exact trigger remains unconfirmed. No live replay, weaker assertion, or production-guard change was used to claim green; the original failure and this uncertainty are retained under the test-failure policy. The original cause of missed terminal delivery and a live rate-limit trigger remain unproven.

Thanks to @steipete for initiating and directing this reliability audit.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a31b883-0124-4d45-8df4-9f83973e9f4a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/914884fa-b8ca-454c-9dd2-aa33aacbe7ee)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix(ui): announce agent file save failures and conflicts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: screen readers can miss a failed agent-file save or workspace conflict while the editable draft remains on screen.

## User Impact

User impact: the existing failure and conflict messages are exposed as alerts, including their existing Reload and Overwrite recovery controls. Normal file information stays nonassertive. No file permissions, write ordering, draft handling, focus behavior, or visual layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled operator continuation loses its final reply when it removes its own follow-up automation.

## User Impact

Automations can clean up their own schedule and finish replying. Removing or disabling a job from another turn, or pressing Stop, still cancels its active run. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion retired the job's source row before the post-commit ownership check, so the legitimate removing run was treated as an operator cancellation. Keep full caller/source validation before the mutation, then recognize only the exact still-live admitted run after commit. Its continuation keeps the existing live operator, session, and delivery checks without requiring the deleted definition to remain present.

This reuses the existing occurrence marker, removal guard, and delivery fence; no new scheduler mode or state owner. The admission assertion's type now preserves its existing scope-only check. Net production growth is 18 lines; the regression coverage adds 76 lines.

## Evidence

- The real scheduled shared-session/Gateway-tool regression fails on base `d0931ba3d436f` with `Cron job removed by operator.`, then passes with this repair and a successful completion summary.
- Fresh disposable Gateway built at exact head `88c03ac0a835a7387239b8b475e10b571222937d`, real OpenAI `gpt-4.1`: the agent created a disabled same-conversation automation; a forced run removed it; the final assistant reply was readable through public `chat.history`; the job was absent from `cron.list`. Separate live streaming runs proved both Control UI's session-owned Stop RPC (`sessions.abort` with the exact run) and external `cron.remove` produce failed completion receipts, with no final reply. The three-scenario fixture passed in 26.73 seconds of test execution (84.77 seconds total); the owned Gateway and disposable state were verified removed. This exercises public RPCs, not browser clicks. No live operator state was changed.
- Post-removal authority proof uses real scheduler, admission, source-restoration, session-state, and publication-action owners with synthetic model/GitHub I/O. Self-removal precedes inspect/merge: current authority permits the expected merge PUT; committing operator-role revocation or source-session replacement during awaited preflight rejects with zero PUTs. This follow-up changes tests only.
- All 16 continuation cases passed on the updated tree (70.57 seconds wall time, 33.16 seconds test execution). This owner composition is needed to check final I/O. The earlier 90-test run covers companion self-removal/admission boundaries, including closed, aborted, copied, stale, and other-run guards.
- Core types plus cron, agent-root, and Gateway-method test type graphs passed. Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreviews of the implementation and the post-removal proof found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Credit: @steipete for requesting the reliability audit and repair.

prs.title: fix(sessions): parent follow-ups fail after native child runs age out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a parent cannot continue a kept native child after its completed run falls outside the 30-minute recent-run window, even though the child and its stored lineage still exist.

## User Impact

Parents can list, recall, inspect, and continue their retained native children under the existing session-tool scope. This does not grant global visibility or let a parent take over a child occupied by another active controller, including cancellation-in-progress.

Incognito, self-only, sandbox/A2A, sharing revocation, and exact agent/session identity checks remain in force. Archiving keeps its existing behavior rather than erasing lineage. No configuration option, schema migration, dependency, lease, or authorization store is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway relationship owner now separates durable native parent facts from run recency and from the actual current executor/reservation. Lists, exact ownership resolution, history, search, and status consume that canonical relationship projection; terminal and unowned controller snapshots do not confer control.

Send admission distinguishes durable parent access, temporary live-controller access, and independently authorized peer access. Temporary control cannot mint persistent completion/watch rights and is rechecked at the final effect. An explicit stored parent remains readable during foreign execution; legacy spawnedBy-only lineage yields to the verified active controller. The released history-only fallback for older Gateways is preserved without extending it to send/search/status.

The existing endpoint owner also absorbs the unchanged ancestry walk, keeping one identity-continuity implementation and the delivery owner bounded. The oversized status test's existing lookup assertion moves into its shared fixture module; no coverage or line-limit gate is relaxed.

## Evidence

- **Real baseline, pinned to cba956feca63b163119f81a704c1f99f84077344:** an isolated Gateway and OpenAI agent actually spawn and complete a native child. Aging only the real terminal timestamps by 31 minutes reproduces the sessions_send tree-visibility denial.
- **Real repaired flow:** the same tool entry point returns the child's reply with the same session ID. A second zero-wait follow-up delivers its completion to the parent and registers a state watch. Final live run: **84.63 s wall / 46.28 s test time**, using openai/gpt-5.4 and the native OpenClaw runtime.
- **Real negative authority trace:** a retained-child send reaches the product's pending receive-approval boundary. Reassigning control to a real, held child-model execution, or revoking the parent run through `chat.abort`, makes the attempted `Allow once` resolution fail. Both cases leave **no child transcript input, no pending input, and no watch cursor**, with the child session ID unchanged. An unrevoked approval control then succeeds and produces the reply and watch. This uses no authorization, registry-lookup, or dispatch mocks; it exercises the existing Gateway question, execution, revocation, transcript, pending-input, and watch owners.
- Focused Gateway/tool tests cover durable navigation, legacy and explicit lineage, active and canceling foreign controllers, terminal/unowned snapshots, agent-qualified lookup, current-policy peer access, temporary-controller admission retirement, incarnation replacement, archive/deletion, sharing/caller revocation, history/search/status/list, and paused-task completion behavior.
- Targeted core and agent-tool/Gateway test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, whitespace checks, and normal commit hooks are used. Independent autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**; it is static review, separate from the runtime proof.
- Three wire golden fixtures changed only for durable childSessions and removal of fabricated historical spawnedBy/controlOwnerSessionKey fields. Restoring just those old fields reproduces every original hash; other wire values remain pinned.

- **CI follow-up:** complete failed-shard inventories on `59208af` and `1edab1` identified 15 assertions across seven files. All were reproduced and repaired; the final replay passes **79 tests across nine focused files**. The existing 128-row, two-viewer compact/sidebar warm-encoding gate is unchanged: the 128-row count must equal the two-row-page count (the failed head measured 136 versus 10). A private process-local index key no longer JSON-encodes on every lookup; no authority cache, persisted format, or budget waiver is added. Controller fixtures now hold actual execution claims and settle terminal state; describe/event/presentation expectations distinguish durable lineage from stale control. Fresh independent repair reviews are scoped-clean through P2, and scoped type/lint/format checks pass. Hosted CI for the final updated head is pending.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, focused validation, and test cost</summary>

Real Gateway/agent/model proof (requires the existing authorized OpenAI test credential):

```bash
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_RETAINED_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_SUBAGENT_E2E_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.4 pnpm test:live -- src/agents/tools/sessions-send-retained-child.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Focused action-right boundary batch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-communication.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-policy.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The CI repair replay runs session-list-viewers.perf, session-row-event-parity, session-row-presentation, session-row-projection.subagent-index, session-row-selection, session-utils.single-row-cache, session-utils.navigation-lineage, sessions-describe-worker, and subagent-registry-memory tests.

The affected Gateway/status batch additionally runs session-utils.navigation-lineage, session-utils.filters, session-utils.subagent, session-utils-row.materialize, and openclaw-tools.session-status tests. Consumer proof also includes sessions-list, sessions-search, sessions-resolution, sessions-send-followup, real sessions.resolve RPC, and session-subagent-resume tests.

Typechecks use scripts/run-tsgo.mjs with tsconfig.core.json and the agents-tools, agents-root, gateway-root, gateway-methods, and agents-sessions test leaves. Lint uses scripts/run-oxlint.mjs with the touched TypeScript paths; formatting uses the repository's pinned formatter. Autoreview compares the complete candidate with the pinned base at P0–P2.

Observed changed-test body time is approximately 0.03–4.1 s per ordinary tool/filter/navigation fixture; the existing SQLite/worker subagent fixture is approximately 9.3 s. The opt-in live test takes 46.3 s because it must exercise a real Gateway and model through spawn, completion, retained-child follow-up, and watch custody; it is not added to ordinary PR CI. Hosted CI seconds are pending.

One intermediate compiler-preparation attempt aborted in Node before collecting tests (exit 133) and was not counted as proof. A stable-input supported-wrapper rerun and the final source-bound gates passed.

prs.title: fix: restore plugin host links after external reinstalls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #180903. Reinstalling OpenClaw into a new global root after a Node upgrade leaves managed plugin host links pointing at the previous installation. Gateway startup verifies those stale links and drops otherwise valid plugins.

Thanks @rybing7 for the report and published-package reproduction.

## User Impact

Gateway startup repairs stale or dangling OpenClaw host links in managed npm projects and registered plugin installations before checking plugin availability. Repairs report the old and new targets. Developer-owned path installations remain untouched; unsuccessful filesystem repairs retain the existing warning and plugin-quarantine behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

External reinstalls bypass the updater's post-core convergence. Startup now reuses Doctor's host-link repair owner with its already-read install records, before payload verification. It preserves the startup effect guard and leaves update rehearsals and deferred-repair passes read-only. Successful repair notices do not mark the Gateway degraded. There are no config, schema, or install-record changes.

## Evidence

- The regression fails on the base for both an existing old installation and a dangling old target: real managed-plugin links remain stale. It exercises the Gateway startup preflight, then checks owned-link repair, developer-link preservation, unchanged config and install records, and a no-op second startup.
- Node: 277 passing tests across 31 passing consumer files selected by imports of the changed owners. Seven tests in two PostgreSQL-only files were skipped by their existing environment guards. Pinned Bun: 53 passing focused tests across four files. The two new regression cases passed on both runtimes after correcting the assertion to require an absent startup warning. Their test time was 7.33s on Node (63.44s wall) and 4.92s on Bun (23.68s wall); CI timings are pending.
- Separate source-level startup probe from a synthetic global installation: asserted `npm prefix -g` equals the temporary prefix before `npm install -g --ignore-scripts --offline --no-audit --no-fund "$TMPDIR/new-install-source"`. With unchanged main, startup reported `degraded: ["managed", "registered"]` and retained the old target. With the patch, both links pointed to the new root, `degraded: []`, and `idempotent: true`. The developer link and config bytes remained unchanged. This uses synthetic packages and real filesystem links, not a published-package upgrade.
- Probe command from that installation: `node --import "$npm_config_prefix/lib/node_modules/openclaw/scripts/tsx.mjs" "$npm_config_prefix/lib/node_modules/openclaw/probe.ts" before` / `after`, with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `TMPDIR`.
- Scoped oxlint, the command-test tsgo project, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Madge reported zero import cycles. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was not run locally; PR CI supplies the broad checks. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The first consumer run was rejected during compilation because the warning fix changed a captured source file. No tests ran in that attempt; the final run uses the frozen patch.
- Existing slow integration cases observed: Gateway quarantine readiness (31.00s), divergent auxiliary database migration (34.80s), and repeated unavailable-owner Doctor/startup settlement (49.61s). These exercise cold boot or repeated migration/readiness passes; no timeouts, retries, or skips were changed.
- Diff: production +76/-9 lines; tests +112/-0; docs +10/-0.

prs.title: fix: restore beta webhooks and preserve runtime lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On `release/2026.10.10`, immediate webhooks can be refused before inference, scheduled scripts can retain disposed plugin hooks, and account removal adopted during config reload can leave model and reply dispatch unavailable until restart.

## User Impact

Webhooks and channel introductions use their ordinary configured account. Scheduled scripts refresh replaced hooks before execution. Removing a login during reload preserves a usable runtime with the login removed. Stored jobs still require their recorded inference account, event turns carrying a job ID keep their current-job automations scope, and completed tool effects are never replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backports three merged repairs:

- #172775, `5f604ddd809518b8d0ce4ad9142584b90ebb12d3`, originally implemented by Dallin Romney: classify trusted immediate producers as events while stored jobs remain cron executions.
- #177825, `1e56117f00f5858e025bdc7f4f396c7567ab32ee`: refresh disposed script hooks while preserving admission, deadlines and the setup-only single retry.
- `5650e59bfdf4cb2e3745e8b94fb76ac3d720d831`, Peter Steinberger: retain the captured Gateway metadata snapshot during adopted auth replay rather than binding the replacement to a temporary config-operation cache.

Beta adaptations retain its CLI binding facts and runtime invalidation. Tool assembly preserves the owning scope condition used in @jalehman's #178904. The auth drain receives the existing refresh-options object and forwards only its metadata snapshot, satisfying the beta file limit without unrelated refactoring.

There is no configuration/schema migration or new account grant. Model routing, tool policy and delivery restrictions stay in force. The separate catalog-budget backport #180299 is outside this diff.

## Evidence

Source verification: 208 focused cases across ten files, 74 tool-scope cases, and 45 supersession/reload-auth/auth-recovery cases pass. The actual assembled automations tool rejects sibling removal for event turns with a current job ID; the old condition reaches a Gateway spy. Keeping the auth-replay regression while restoring the old owner fails at the first post-retirement reply-dispatch consumer. The script replacement regression also fails with the old owner. Restoring each repair passes. Production types, selected agents-other test types, formatting, typed lint for the auth owner and assertion-safety checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review of the final auth adaptation is scoped-clean.

The complete native package build and tarball integrity check passed (35m24s, 11.7 GiB peak, zero swap). Exact combined source: `7f95fdb924bad11deef7305c81f46342111a1a62`; archive SHA-256: `82a7d8e916cc93dfe3bc82690a0edf53b3859bde2fa48d44efa4c55112a1772f`. The qualified combined tree differs from reviewed head `d72667846551c9cf1f148c8a977d73ef5f488982` only in the five catalog-budget files belonging to #180299. Following the review, current head `b6fc0b43bf2805d01f1e21db39057f0014ce5e11` removes only the private-helper classification table from `run-fallback-policy.test.ts`, restoring that file byte-for-byte to the pinned beta. Its remaining nine cases and formatting pass. All production files changed by this PR remain byte-identical to the qualified package; no runtime code changed after acceptance.

The sealed acceptance program ran against that actual installed package using authenticated native Gateway calls and an owned loopback HTTP provider. No external model or real account was used.

| Behavior | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing beta.1 install, native update to candidate | Succeeded; finished; package activation complete; no active update; exact candidate build ID |
| Existing beta/default-model settings and disabled stored job | Preserved through update; sentinel removed afterward |
| Immediate event / unbound stored job / bound stored job / revoked account | Actual inference POST deltas `[1,0,1,0]`, independently with plugins disabled and an enabled startup plugin registered in the same Gateway |
| Queued account revocation | Actual shared-session lane observed with one active request and one queued request; logout occurred while the first HTTP response was held; second request ended with authorization-retired error and zero additional HTTP POSTs |
| Native logout and adopted auth replay | No warning; profile and provider key reference removed; nonforced catalog reads succeeded after both ordinary and queued logout; applied config revision matched |
| Recurring native scheduled exec across supported plugin replacement A → B | Both runs succeeded on Gateway PID 6982 / start ticks 15779029; old instance disposed and absent afterward; exactly two actual exec effects, no replay |
| Delayed catalog provider and unavailable sibling behavior | Three forced six-second HTTP refreshes succeeded after update; baseline beta.1 aborted at five seconds; later HTTP 503 remained truthfully unavailable while the healthy sibling stayed usable |
| Cleanup and identity | Candidate source remained exact; jobs removed; owned Gateways and HTTP fixtures stopped; container exited 0 without OOM and was removed |

The immutable package program and both authority programs passed. The outer receipt checker initially indexed `nativeQueue.idle` as an object, while the native API returned `null`. The pinned [diagnostics owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d72667846551c9cf1f148c8a977d73ef5f488982/src/process/command-lane-diagnostics.ts#L96) defines null as zero dynamic lanes. prs.title: fix(ui): refresh an open Tool access view when the session run settles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An already-open composer **Tool access** view keeps saying that MCP tools appear after an agent run even after the run discovers and uses those tools. #168668 fixes reopening the view, but not keeping it open while a run finishes.

## User Impact

The open view now shows the discovered tools and their toggles after the selected session's run settles, without closing the view or reloading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The effective-tools cache key does not change when a run discovers tools. Track completed direct runs in the existing capability host and include that revision in cache/request ownership. The open view rereads once after settlement; closed views do not fetch in the background. A late response from the earlier read cannot overwrite the settled result. No Gateway, plugin SDK, configuration, or storage contract changes.

## Evidence

Built current main `25dde259d84a365859b4ceceb63feb9cfbac3e0e` (including #168668) and the candidate in isolated Docker. State was created through shipped configuration, sessions and chat commands. A functional stdio MCP server handled real initialize, tools/list and tools/call requests; the inference endpoint supplied ordinary protocol responses.

- Main twice: the selected session discovered and invoked `proof__proof_echo`, then finished. `tools.effective` returned the tool, but the still-open view retained the discovery notice.
- Candidate twice: the same still-open view changed to **1 of 1 tool on** and exposed the `proof_echo` toggle.
- Direct `tools.effective` queries confirm the server inventory was populated independently of the UI cache.
- Focused capability-host suite: 20 tests passed, including settlement, closed-view and stale-response ordering coverage. Changed TypeScript passed Oxfmt and Oxlint.
- Real-provider built agent smoke returned `TOOL_ACCESS_LIVE_OK`.

[Inspected before/after screenshots and accessibility/DOM evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180865#issuecomment-6354880272). Both uploaded images were checked after publication.

The simplification pass retained one existing cache owner rather than introducing a new discovery subscription or polling path. Production delta: +27/-8 lines; tests +116/-0; documentation +2/-0. The additional private state is needed to distinguish the current session's completed run from a same-key cached result. Contributor commits and credit are preserved.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous UI cache behavior; no persisted state or public contract changes. Blast radius is the composer Tool access cache and its refresh after direct session runs.

prs.title: fix: recovered child sessions fail after their parent finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes running child sessions failing after their recovered parent finishes when the child was started through an in-process `agent` request, including `sessions_send` continuations.

## User Impact

A child that has retained its own admitted operator authority can continue after the parent replies. Revoking the operator still blocks child effects, and an expired caller cannot authorize a new execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The child admission already selected the independent policy authority introduced in #176769 and generalized in #178693. However, the in-process agent facade also retained the incoming parent's work assertion as its Gateway-context assertion. Execution checked that redundant assertion before the child's valid authority, so a completed parent could still stop its child.

Separate the existing Gateway-instance assertion from source authorization. Check the incoming source during admission; let accepted execution use the authority retained by its admission owner. Scope intersection, canonical child-lineage selection, revocation, session ownership, and cancellation remain with their existing owners. No new policy, configuration, or stored format is introduced.

This is a narrow follow-up to the merged authority fixes #176769, #178186, and #178693, within the lifecycle ownership consolidated in #177698. Those changes correctly retain child execution authority; this closes the separate in-process facade assertion that still checked parent work after admission.

Related #180704 fixes a different restart symptom: obsolete child-completion reservations parking later input before execution starts. Neither PR depends on the other, and neither replaces the merged consolidation or the outstanding policy proposals. This PR does not change model timeouts, peer-message delivery policy, selected-requester policy, or reply obligations.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway authority controls

The missing authority controls now pass through the real built Gateway, with an added positive control under the same role-governed synthetic authentication:

| Case | Actual owner boundary | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Allowed | Real `sessions_spawn` → fixture restart → recovered-parent `sessions_send`; parent finishes before child release | Exact child terminal `ok`; one real `exec` HTTP receiver request after parent done; child final persisted |
| Role revoked | Same role/tool configuration; canonical `users.setRole` sets the identified operator's role to denied after child admission, before its queued exec response is released | Exact child terminal `error` / `rpc`; zero receiver I/O |
| Parent expired before admission | Actual `sessions_send` enters a real pending communication approval; canonical `chat.abort` ends the recovered parent while approval is awaited | Late canonical approval rejected as cancelled; zero new child model requests, no forbidden child input in canonical transcript, zero receiver I/O |

Each case used isolated state and a scripted loopback provider on Node 24.22.1, started/joined two owned Gateway processes, and closed both clients and provider. No turn service or authority owner was mocked. No live operator state, external inference or native Codex behavior is claimed.

```text
SAME-AUTH ALLOWED: parent done -> child release -> receiver=1 -> child final persisted; terminal=ok
ROLE REVOKED: child admitted -> parent done -> users.setRole denied -> receiver=0; terminal=error/rpc
PARENT EXPIRED: sessions_send approval pending -> chat.abort -> late approval cancelled; child requests=0 receiver=0
CLEANUP EACH: Gateway started=2 joined=2; clients closed; provider closed
```

Existing build metadata identifies `271329fd32df15f9347099872d1c35e756597cad`; the working-tree build contains the production patch unchanged at reviewed head `b9bf4f98121f226906990933610568c7a69ae403`. Captured source hashes match that head, and compiled dispatch retains the source assertion at admission while using the Gateway lifetime assertion during execution. This is source-qualified reuse of that built candidate, not a new clean-head build.

The negative captures used driver SHA-256 `0cdc9d0dbf7ee8d5685e5d5f9238d007de0cee3366d1d88db23c42fd100f183d`. Adding only the allowed case/branch produced driver SHA-256 `bd4cef65d6cac8dd210c2a88d788e0293dbb9710b99bfe2faf5d1795e5d4efc0`; its common authentication, provider, tool preparation and negative paths are unchanged. Both driver revisions, their exact diff, full sanitized terminal captures and source/compiled hashes are retained for inspection. Earlier authentication setup failures remain qualified as setup failures with joined cleanup.

### Original regression and allowed-path evidence

- Regression on upstream base `271329fd32df`: **1 failed, 15 passed**. The child retains valid independent authority, but the real in-process facade rejects its synthetic effect with `Recovery claim retired` after the parent's work claim closes. The retirement-before-acceptance control passes.
- Fixed candidate: **102 focused tests pass**: 15 continuation tests plus 87 adjacent tests covering requester continuation, authorization, commit guards, compaction, recovered operator admission, and cancellation.
- Changed test file (maintainer remeasure, `--maxWorkers=1`, warm cache): 15 tests, about 7.7 seconds of test time; the two new cases take about 2.1 and 0.8 seconds.
- Production build, targeted Gateway typechecking, lint, and formatting pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Built-Gateway recovery flow passes:** a fresh authenticated operator creates a canonical child through actual `sessions_spawn`; its next parent turn is interrupted by deliberately killing only the isolated fixture Gateway. The same private profile restarts and recovers the parent. Actual `sessions_send` admits the existing child; the child's model response is held until public history contains the parent's final reply and public status is done. Releasing the child then produces exactly one real `exec` effect against the synthetic fixture receiver and a persisted child final, with both session incarnations unchanged. Both Gateway processes and the fixture server are joined afterward.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized process-proof sequence and limits</summary>

```text
canonical sessions_spawn -> retained child incarnation and spawnedBy verified
parent model request held -> fixture Gateway SIGKILL -> same-profile restart
actual recovered-parent prompt -> sessions_send -> child model request held
parent final persisted + status done + no active run; child effect count 0
release child -> exec receiver count 1 after parent done -> child final persisted
cleanup: 2 Gateway processes started, 2 joined; client and receiver closed
```

This is the real built Gateway and agent/tool path, using Node 24 and a scripted loopback Chat Completions provider, synthetic inputs, and a fresh private state/config/credential directory. It is not evidence of live-provider transport behavior or native Codex behavior. The build contains the reviewed patch on `271329fd32df`; source hashes were recorded and the patch is unchanged in head `b9bf4f98121f`. Earlier collector attempts failed fixture setup, request classification, or tool-parameter assertions and are not credited as product proof. Raw requests, configuration, and logs remain private; no production conversation data is included here. That original allowed-path process trace did not exercise revocation or pre-admission rejection. The additional real-Gateway controls above now cover both boundaries; the committed regression controls remain supporting evidence.

</details>

All committed fixtures are synthetic. The live report included both a model-idle timeout and a later recovery-authority failure; the regression proves this reachable authority defect, but does not establish that it caused every observed delay. The later human-started model turn completed, so no transport-timeout change is claimed.


### Maintainer follow-up commit

- Dropped the committed `operator role revoked` case. Its mocked turn service enforced revocation itself, so it would still pass if execution stopped checking `prepared.operatorAuthority`. The built-Gateway `users.setRole` control above is the real revocation proof.
- Renamed the execution-side slot from `assertContextCurrent` to `assertGatewayLifetimeCurrent` (`createAgentTurnService`, `StartAgentRunExecutionParams`) and documented on the facade option that agent dispatch carries it into accepted execution, so it must not carry caller authority.
- `captureOperatorToolGatewayContinuationContext` now reuses `resolved.assertGatewayCurrent` instead of an inlined copy of the Gateway-binding check.

### Local integration qualification

The patch cherry-picks cleanly onto the existing customized local build. Its continuation suite reports 15 passing cases, including all three new authority cases, and one existing failure in `preserves GitHub identity access after subagent_announce admits a write-only continuation`: expected `[operator.write]`, observed `[operator.read, operator.write]`. A determining-owner rollback of the three changed production files to the incumbent local commit `7281cfa5c56b` reproduces the same assertion failure; the candidate files were restored afterward. The local completion path explicitly retains its source scope ceiling. This local integration difference is not introduced or repaired by this PR; the upstream-based PR candidate still passes all 103 focused tests.


The unchanged production patch is now deployed locally as `583f9cf88fb6` on the existing customized build. The native service was stopped, the production build passed in 2m 20.2s, and the same Node 24 service started successfully. Authenticated health, core readiness, remote UI access, active plugin registrations, and both affected conversation incarnations were verified. Service definition, configuration, and private environment bytes are unchanged. This verifies activation and preservation, not a claim that every previously observed model delay has been resolved.
