prs.title: fix(media): refuse to rewrite transcript archives that are not valid UTF-8
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #181125

`openclaw doctor --fix` migrates legacy top-level media fields in archived transcripts (`*.jsonl.deleted.*` / `*.jsonl.reset.*`) and **rewrites the archive file in place** when content changes. The archive reader decodes bytes lossily (`Buffer.toString("utf8")`), so an archive containing invalid UTF-8 (crash-truncated write, external tooling) is decoded with U+FFFD replacement characters — and the rewritten archive then **permanently carries those replacement characters**, destroying the original bytes of a long-term retention artifact.

Example: an archive line whose `content` is `"café"` with the first byte of `é` replaced by `0xff` stays valid JSON after lossy decoding, so the migration "succeeds" and burns `caf` into the archive forever.

## Fix

Decode fatally on the **rewrite** path only:

- `decodeSessionArchiveBytes` gains an opt-in `{ fatal: true }` mode that reuses the existing `decodeUtf8Input` helper (default behavior unchanged — read-only viewers keep the lossy decode).
- `migrateTranscriptArchive` uses it; invalid UTF-8 now throws into the **existing** per-archive skip path, producing the recoverable warning `Skipped archived transcript media migration for <path>: … must be valid UTF-8.` and leaving the archive byte-identical for manual recovery.

Production: +12/-6 across 2 files. Regression test: +23 (real SQLite + real filesystem, asserts warning, no rewrite, byte-identical archive).

## Evidence (real behavior proof, 2026-10-23 UTC)

Regression test `rejects and preserves an archive whose bytes are not valid UTF-8` in `src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts`:

- **RED on main code** (exact base of this branch, `0e0563a5f9`): test fails — main migrates the corrupt archive (no skip warning; the archive gets rewritten).
- **GREEN on this branch**: 20/20 pass in `state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts` (bare vitest, `vitest.infra.config.ts`).

Shipped-CLI upgrade cell (server Docker, Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real `dist/` builds; state lineage authored by the published **openclaw 2026.10.6** CLI; the corrupt fixture is one invalid byte `0xff` inside a JSON string, so it stays parseable under lossy decoding):

| Cell | Driver → runner | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Corrupt archive, **current main** build (RED) | main `doctor --fix` | `Migrated archived transcript media in …` — archive **rewritten**: md5 `b72c65bc…` → `9f504f58…`, 157 → 183 bytes, U+FFFD burned in, original `0xff` byte gone |
| Corrupt archive, this head (GREEN) | head `doctor --fix` | `Skipped archived transcript media migration for …: Session transcript archive must be valid UTF-8.` — md5 `b72c65bc…` **unchanged**, 157 bytes, original byte intact |
| Upgrade preservation | stable 2026.10.6 `doctor --fix` → head custody pass → corrupt archive appears → head `doctor --fix` | Same GREEN result on stable-lineage state: preserved byte-identical with the warning |
| Valid legacy archive (control) | head `doctor --fix` | `Migrated archived transcript media in …` — normal migration unaffected, no U+FFFD |

Raw cell output:

```
# base (current main) — RED
fixture ready: …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z bytes: 157
b72c65bc2fc99f9220396c431cec92a7  …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z
- Migrated archived transcript media in …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z.
== snap base ==
9f504f58d7411244a937b30ff9ef5be1  …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z
HAS-FFFD=true
HAS-ORIGINAL-CORRUPT-BYTE=false
SIZE=183

# head (this PR) — GREEN
fixture ready: …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z bytes: 157
b72c65bc2fc99f9220396c431cec92a7  …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z
- Skipped archived transcript media migration for …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z: Error: Session transcript archive must be valid UTF-8.
== snap head ==
b72c65bc2fc99f9220396c431cec92a7  …/corrupt-encoding.jsonl.deleted.2026-07-24T01-02-03.000Z
HAS-FFFD=false
HAS-ORIGINAL-CORRUPT-BYTE=true
SIZE=157
```

## Notes

- Read-only archive viewers (`readSessionArchiveContentSync`, the materialized read cache) intentionally keep lossy decoding; only the doctor-owned rewrite path becomes strict.
- The skip path is pre-existing design (same handling as blank-record / all-NUL archives), so a corrupt archive surfaces as a recoverable Doctor warning instead of silent data loss.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse malformed UTF-8 in retired runtime state imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #180795

Doctor's retired-runtime import (added in #174489 for the pre-July upgrade dead-end) decodes four legacy sources — `settings/voicewake.json`, `settings/voicewake-routing.json`, `bindings/current-conversations.json`, and `plugin-binding-approvals.json` — with lossy UTF-8 (`bytes.toString("utf8")`). When one of these files contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (a crash-truncated write, or bytes left by an older editor encoding), the JSON still parses, but every invalid sequence is silently replaced with U+FFFD, and the rewritten values are then committed to config machine state and shared SQLite state while the original source file is removed. A damaged legacy trigger phrase such as `wãke up` becomes `wke up` in the live config, and conversation bindings / plugin binding approvals are persisted with rewritten bytes.

This applies the same strict-decoding principle as #180281 (config health and auth profiles) to the retired-runtime readers: decode with `fatal: true` via the existing `decodeUtf8Input` helper, reject damaged sources through the existing warning + recovery-instructions pathway, and preserve the original bytes in the migration backup instead of importing replaced characters.

Behavior for valid files is unchanged; sibling readers (`exec-approvals`, `workspace-setup-files`) already decode with a fatal decoder.

## Evidence (real behavior proof, 2026-10-22 UTC)

All runs use the shipped CLI (`dist/index.js doctor --fix`, Node v24.22.1) on isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. The malformed fixture is `{"triggers":["wãke up"]}` with the first byte of `ã` replaced by `0xff` (still parseable JSON).

**RED — main dist (`5ee11829a6` base):** the damaged file is imported and the rewritten value lands in live state:

```
Doctor: retired state repair
│  - Migrated settings/voicewake.json → shared SQLite state (existing values retained)
...
config_machine_state row: {"state_key":"voicewake.triggers","value_json":"[\"wke up\"]"}
```

**GREEN — this PR's dist:** the same file is refused, nothing is committed, and the original bytes stay in the migration archive:

```
│  - Could not import settings/voicewake.json: Legacy retired state
│    settings/voicewake.json must be valid UTF-8. | The encoded data was
│    not valid for encoding utf-8 ... Restore the listed trigger phrases
│    through Voice Wake settings.
config_machine_state: no voicewake.triggers row
settings/voicewake.json.migrated bytes: 7b 22 74 72 69 67 67 65 72 73 22 3a 5b 22 77 ff a3 6b 65 20 75 70 22 5d 7d (intact)
```

**Valid-Unicode control — this PR's dist:** a legitimate `{"triggers":["wãke up"]}` (bytes `c3 a3`) still imports, and the stored value keeps the original character (codepoints `U+77 U+E3 U+6B U+65 U+20 U+75 U+70`).

**Upgrade cell — published 2026.10.6 → this PR:** a state dir carrying all four valid legacy sources (with `wãke up` / `wörk` / `agent:main:tést` / `exámple`) is first left untouched by the published 2026.10.6 CLI, then migrated by this PR's `doctor --fix`. Every value lands intact:

```
triggers:  [{"value_json":"[\"wãke up\"]"}]
routing:   [{"value_json":"{\"version\":1,\"defaultTarget\":{\"agentId\":\"wörk\"},\"routes\":[]}"}]
bindings:  [{"binding_key":"discord␟default␟␟123","target_session_key":"agent:main:tést"}]
approvals: [{"plugin_root":"/plugins/example","plugin_id":"example","plugin_name":"exámple"}]
```

**Regression fails on base, passes on the fix:** the four new parameterized cases in `src/infra/state-migrations.retired-runtime.test.ts` fail against the base source (4 failed) and the full file suite passes with the fix (12/12, `vitest.infra.config.ts`, Node v24.18.0).

Closes #180782

## What Problem This Solves

When Doctor retires pre-SQLite Skill Workshop proposal sidecars, it decodes `proposal.json` and `rollback.json` with a lossy UTF-8 conversion. A legacy bundle with one damaged byte still parses as JSON, so the recorded pre-apply contents arrive carrying U+FFFD replacement characters — and the unfinished-apply recovery then restores those replacement characters into the user's workspace skill files. Once nothing else blocks, the legacy bundle (the only intact copy) is removed, making the corruption permanent.

## Fix

Decode both sidecars with the existing strict `decodeUtf8Input` helper (fatal `TextDecoder`). A malformed bundle now throws into the existing recoverable-failures path (`Could not read Skill Workshop proposal …`): nothing is restored, exported, or removed, so the operator can recover the bundle by hand and rerun `openclaw doctor --fix`. Valid bundles behave exactly as before. Production diff: +9/-2, one file.

## Evidence

All runs are the shipped Doctor CLI entry point (`doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-color`) against packaged builds, on Node v24.22.1 (2026-10-22, UTC).

**Fixture.** A legacy bundle `skill-workshop/proposals/deploy-procedure-1/` whose `rollback.json` carries one invalid UTF-8 byte (the first byte of `é` in a recorded support file's `previousContent`; the JSON still parses under lossy decoding). The workspace is left mid-apply: `SKILL.md` at its pre-apply content, the support file at the proposed bytes.

**RED — main-behavior build** (same tree with the one-file fix reverted to `aa52e91bf9`):

```
- Restored /cell/ops-workspace/skills/deploy from the unfinished apply of Skill Workshop proposal deploy-procedure-1.
support-bytes: 6e6f74efbfbdefbfbd730a     → "not��s\n" — replacement characters written into the user's skill file
```

**GREEN — this PR head `860798606a` (proof build: `1e96c01845`; the delta is the format-only test commit)**, same fixture:

```
- Could not read Skill Workshop proposal deploy-procedure-1: Error: Skill Workshop proposal deploy-procedure-1 rollback must be valid UTF-8.
support-bytes: 70726f706f7365640a     → "proposed\n" — workspace untouched
bundle-rollback: PRESERVED (md5 identical to the RED fixture)
```

**Data-model compatibility — published-stable upgrade cell** (`openclaw@2026.10.6` from npm as the old install, then this PR head on the same state directory):

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| stable + valid bundle | `Restored …`, `Exported 1 pending Skill Workshop proposal draft`, legacy files retired; workspace support file `6e6f74c3a9730a` = `"notés\n"` with the é intact |
| PR head re-run on stable-written state | exit 0, no changes, no warnings; archive and workspace bytes unchanged |
| PR head + new malformed bundle after upgrade | refused with `must be valid UTF-8`; workspace untouched; bundle preserved |
| PR head + new valid bundle after upgrade | `Restored …` with the é intact (`6e6f74c3a9730a`), bundle retired — identical to stable behavior |

**Regression.** New case `keeps a legacy bundle whose rollback bytes are not valid UTF-8 out of the workspace` in `src/commands/doctor-skill-workshop-retire-proposals.test.ts` fails against the main-side code (the run reports the restore) and passes here; the full file is 10/10 green under `test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts`.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse malformed UTF-8 in the legacy cron import
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` imports a pre-July legacy cron store (`cron/jobs.json` plus the optional
`cron/jobs-state.json` runtime state) into the canonical SQLite rows. Both files were decoded with a
lossy `Buffer.toString("utf8")`, so invalid bytes *inside* a job definition became U+FFFD while the
JSON still parsed: the import reported success and wrote the replacement characters into `cron_jobs`
(job name, `payload.text`, schedule identity). The repair is one-shot and the source is retired, so
the corrupted definition is what the user sees afterwards.

The failing input is data, not an internal state: these are user-owned JSON files in the state
directory, produced by the pre-`#174343` cron writer and re-writable by any editor, backup restore,
or truncated write. The entry is the ordinary upgrade path: `openclaw doctor --fix` →
`migrateRetiredCronState` (`src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-repair.ts:494`) → the
`importRetiredStateSource` parse callback at `legacy-repair.ts:518`.

Precedent: #180281 (Doctor refuses a legacy source instead of re-decoding it), #180264, #180268.

No linked issue: this is the follow-up in the same family, with no open issue describing it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseLegacyCronJobs` (`src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-json-shapes.ts:121`) now decodes the retained
source bytes through the existing strict owner `decodeUtf8Input` (`src/infra/utf8-input.ts:1`)
before JSON5 parsing. Malformed bytes throw `Legacy cron job store must be valid UTF-8.` from the
existing parse callback, so `importRetiredStateSource`
(`src/infra/state-migrations.retired-archive.ts:29`) takes its documented parse-failure path: no rows
are written, the warning names the archived path, and the existing `openclaw automations add`
recovery instruction is preserved. The source is archived byte-identically, so the original bytes are
never destroyed.

The optional runtime-state file is decoded strictly too, but a failure keeps its pre-existing
`Unrecognized legacy cron runtime state remains available in the archive` path, so valid job
definitions still import.

Valid UTF-8 — including a literal replacement character — still imports byte-identically, and
ordinary malformed JSON takes the same path as before. No new validator, option, config key,
schema, dependency, or archive policy.

Production LOC is `+6/-4` in one file; the regression is `+31` in the existing
`legacy-json-migration.test.ts`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A user whose legacy cron file was damaged now gets an explicit Doctor warning naming the
byte-identical archive (`cron/jobs.json.migrated`) instead of silently receiving automation prompts
full of ``. Restoring valid UTF-8 and rerunning `openclaw doctor --fix` performs the same import.
Files that are already valid behave exactly as before, and valid non-ASCII text keeps its exact
bytes.

## Evidence (real behavior proof, 2026-10-22 UTC)

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `b89e1d7f7f87ec2ff7a3cdf5c79e5ede5d842d2a`
- Current-main RED baseline: `5b8a35f45e4a8aa7a696079770029b7f6a3c5526` (`upstream/main`)
- Production entry: packaged `node dist/index.js doctor --fix --non-interactive` (the shipped CLI)
  → `migrateRetiredCronState` → the `importRetiredStateSource` parse callback
- Canonical owner exercised: `parseLegacyCronJobs` in
  `src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-json-shapes.ts:121`
- Decision surface: the bytes of `cron/jobs.json` and `cron/jobs-state.json` handed to the one-shot
  import
- Recorder/readback boundary: the canonical `cron_jobs` rows read back from the real state SQLite
  (`node:sqlite` read-only), the `.migrated` archive bytes (md5), and the Doctor warning text
- Acceptance RED: the unpatched build imports the malformed store and the job name read back from
  SQLite is `R��sumé`
- Acceptance GREEN: the exact head imports nothing (`cron_jobs` stays empty), warns
  `Legacy cron job store must be valid UTF-8`, and archives the source byte-identically
- Legal control: the same build imports a well-formed legacy store with the non-ASCII name intact
- Cleanup: every run used a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`HOME` in a container. No production
  Gateway, session, agent, token, or config was touched.

### Build provenance

Both builds ran `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts` on Node v24.22.1 (inside the
`>=24.22.1 <25` requirement) in a Debian 12 container. The head build is the exact head tree. The
RED build is the same tree with only `legacy-json-shapes.ts` at its base content (production file
md5 `7b88084aa0d4dde47edd40159891aa03` base vs `043caf5d64d859e2ef87a2ff810064b1` head); the fixture
is identical in every run (malformed md5 `bf5252ef8d7de3abe0ed56f9ae87ec15`, valid md5
`0d16a73c37f25506190bff86e7df0b0a`).

### RED -> GREEN terminal trace (packaged CLI, fresh state each)

Fixture: legacy `cron/jobs.json` whose `Résumé` job name carries one invalid byte (first byte of
`é` replaced by `0xff`), still parseable as JSON.

```text
# base (current main, no patch)
$ node dist/index.js doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-color
Doctor: retired state repair
 - Migrated legacy cron jobs → shared SQLite state (existing values retained)
 - legacy cron jobs: original bytes are preserved at /cell/state/cron/jobs.json.migrated. ...
CAND-EXIT=0
CRON-ROWS=[{"job_id":"legacy","name":"R��sumé", ... "text":"keep me" ...}]
```

The `R��sumé` above is literal U+FFFD bytes (`ef bf bd`) in the captured log — the damaged
definition was silently rewritten into shared state.

```text
# exact head, same fixture
$ node dist/index.js doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-color
Doctor: retired state repair
 - Could not import legacy cron jobs: Legacy cron job store must be valid UTF-8. | The encoded
   data was not valid for encoding utf-8 | ... Recover job definitions from
   /cell/state/cron/jobs.json.migrated with openclaw automations add.
CAND-EXIT=0
== snap ==
-rw-------. 1 1000 1000 248 ... jobs.json.migrated
bf5252ef8d7de3abe0ed56f9ae87ec15  jobs.json.migrated   # == source md5: byte-identical archive
CRON-ROWS=[]                                          # nothing imported
```

Control on the same head build with a well-formed store: the job imports with the name intact
(`CRON-HAS-RESUME=true`, no U+FFFD), and `jobs.json.migrated` matches the source md5.

### Latest-stable upgrade cell (published `openclaw@2026.10.6` from npm × exact head)

```text
# 1) stableinit: latest stable doctor --fix on a fresh state dir authors the SQLite cron state
$ node /stable/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
STABLE-EXIT=0
CRON-ROWS=[{"job_id":"75748a89-...","name":"heartbeat-main", ...}]   # stable-written state

# 2) candidate1: exact-head doctor on the stable-written state (upgrade preservation)
$ node dist/index.js doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-color
CAND-EXIT=0
CRON-ROWS=[{"job_id":"75748a89-...","name":"heartbeat-main", ...}]   # preserved, no FFFD
# (the heartbeat row also picks up main's standard Automations-delivery migration, as designed)

# 3) candidate2: a malformed legacy store appears after the upgrade
CAND-EXIT=0
 - Could not import legacy cron jobs: Legacy cron job store must be valid UTF-8. ...
CRON-ROWS=[heartbeat-main only]   # stable-written state intact, no U+FFFD, no partial import
jobs.json.migrated md5 == source md5   # original bytes preserved

# 4) candidate3: a well-formed legacy store after the upgrade imports alongside existing rows
CAND-EXIT=0
CRON-ROWS=[heartbeat-main, {"job_id":"legacy","name":"Résumé", ...}]   # name intact
```

Note: on published stable this exact legacy shape is hard-gated earlier
(`retired files whose last writer predates July 1, 2026 ... upgrade through 2026.9.7`), because
stable predates the `migrateRetiredCronState` import path entirely; the lossy decode exists only on
the main-line import path this PR fixes, which is why the RED build above uses current main.

### Verification

- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-json-migration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  — exact head 5 passed / 5
- Packaged-CLI RED/GREEN and the `2026.10.6` upgrade cell above (same container, Node v24.22.1)
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both touched files
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+6/-4` (one file)
- Test LOC: `+31` (existing test file)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `decodeUtf8Input` and the existing
  `importRetiredStateSource` parse-failure/archive path; no new error handling, validator, or option
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. The only
  behavior change is that a lossy decode is refused before any row is written; upgrades with valid
  sources are unaffected.

prs.title: fix(cli): strip terminal controls from Claw project reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw claws create|validate|build|dev` write values taken from the project being inspected straight into the human report. In particular, `openclaw claws validate <project>` prints every entry it excludes:

```text
Excluded: <path>
```

A checked-out Claw project can contain file and directory names with terminal control bytes, so validating a third-party project can clear the screen (`ESC [2J`), ring the terminal (`BEL`), or forge an extra report line with an embedded newline. The requested project root, the `Package: <name>@<version>` / `Built Claw: <name>@<version>` lines, and the `Claw dev preview` agent/workspace lines are written through the same boundary.

Precedent: #174989 (same module, same `sanitizeTerminalText` helper).

## Why This Change Was Made

The human report in `src/cli/claws-cli.project.ts` is a terminal rendering boundary, and `sanitizeTerminalText` in `packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts` is the canonical filter for it. `src/cli/claws-cli-output.ts` already imports that helper for diagnostics, so this reuses the owner that is already in place instead of adding a validator, option, or output format.

The interpolated report lines now pass their value through the helper: the project root (`create`, `validate`), the package name and version (`create`, `validate`, `build`, `dev`), each excluded path (`validate`), and the dev preview's agent id and workspace path. The `--json` branches are untouched.

`Package` name/version are additionally constrained by the canonical ClawHub-name and exact-semver checks in `src/claws/reader.ts`, so the control bytes reachable today come from the project root, excluded file names, and the preview workspace path; the identity lines are wrapped at the same boundary so the report does not depend on an upstream validator staying control-free.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Operators can validate, build, or preview a Claw project without its directory or file names driving the terminal: ESC/BEL are removed and a newline renders as the two characters `\n`, so each report line stays on one line. Values without control bytes, including the package identity and ordinary excluded paths, print exactly as before. `--json` callers receive the original bytes.

## Evidence (real behavior proof, 2026-10-22 UTC)

Packaged-CLI RED→GREEN on the supported runtime: both builds produced with the repo's own `scripts/tsdown-build.mts` + `runtime-postbuild` chain on Node **24.22.1** (satisfies `engines.node >=24.22.1 <25`), run as `node dist/index.js claws …` subprocesses in an isolated Linux container with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` pointed at throwaway dirs. No Gateway, session, token, or real config touched.

- GREEN head: `d672ae35b7ae8dc1c377eab85e744aa2765cebaf` (exact PR head)
- RED baseline: `ae40e1864ba6ea2a8d0f37362933c6bbf59b2cff` (current `main`, the rebase target)

The fixture: project directory `author<ESC>[2J<BEL>` plus an excluded file named `payload<ESC>[2J<BEL>.bin`. `<ESC>` is the raw byte `0x1b`, `<BEL>` is `0x07`; output below is shown through `cat -v` (`^[` = ESC, `^G` = BEL).

RED — `main` dist, human reports:

```text
Created Claw project: /tmp/proof-out/author^[[2J^G
Valid Claw project: /tmp/proof-out/author^[[2J^G
Excluded: payload^[[2J^G.bin
Claw dev preview: author-flow@0.1.0
Workspace: /tmp/proof-out/author^[[2J^G/preview-workspace
control-byte scan: create-human HAS RAW CONTROL BYTES; validate-human HAS RAW CONTROL BYTES; dev-human HAS RAW CONTROL BYTES
```

GREEN — exact-head dist, same commands:

```text
Created Claw project: /tmp/proof-out/author
Valid Claw project: /tmp/proof-out/author
Excluded: payload.bin
Claw dev preview: author-flow@0.1.0
Workspace: /tmp/proof-out/author/preview-workspace
control-byte scan: create-human clean; validate-human clean; dev-human clean
```

JSON preservation (both revisions, `--json`): `root` and `excludedPaths` carry the original bytes (4 `\u001b` escapes present in the payload), so machine consumers are unaffected. Legal control: `Package: author-flow@0.1.0` and the artifact integrity `sha256:5f2af05a…` are byte-identical across revisions.

### Regression test

`src/cli/claws-cli.project.test.ts` drives `runClawsCreateCommand` / `runClawsValidateCommand` / `runClawsDevCommand` against real files on disk and asserts the human report contains no control characters while the JSON payload preserves them. The control-character filesystem fixture is guarded to POSIX (`it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`), because Windows rejects those bytes in file names and would fail in fixture setup instead of exercising the sanitizer.

```text
exact head d672ae35b7 — vitest.cli.config.ts shard, bare vitest, --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ Claw project CLI (4 tests, incl. keeps terminal controls out of the human Claw project report)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Revision 2 changes

- Rebased onto current `main` (`ae40e1864b`), which also clears the inherited `check-test-types-core-4` red (that failure was main's own `sessions-patch.test.ts`/`PatchFixture` skew, fixed upstream in #180628).
- The control-char filesystem regression is now POSIX-only (review finding).
- The same sanitization now also covers the `Claw dev preview` human report (`build.claw.name/version`, `plan.agent.finalId`, `plan.agent.workspace`), and the regression exercises it.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+19/-6` net across create/validate/build/dev human-report lines; 2 files, no new files
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `sanitizeTerminalText`, the helper already imported by `src/cli/claws-cli-output.ts` per #174989; no new validator, option, config, or output format
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

prs.title: fix(control-ui): keep sidebar rows steady through reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the late sidebar flicker Peter reported when reloading a signed-in chat or dashboard deep link. The r183 filmstrip showed one shrink-then-grow at the cached-to-live handoff: a partial live roster was published before the remaining boot queries answered. The two changes were about 80 ms apart; the earlier blank-sidebar issue was already fixed.

## User Impact

Cached sidebar rows stay in place until the complete live roster is available. The handoff happens once, retaining the existing rows. On exceptionally slow loads, the three-second cap publishes the available live data and can permit a later change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing foreground/idle handoff and check the current scope's canonical roster, selected roster/owner queries, counts, and visible children before releasing the cache. Reconnect resets the deadline; account/owner changes still replace the scope. There is no partial-merge path. The disposable sidebar cache records the child-query keys and retires incompatible entries individually.

This is the original minimal gate, rebased without product edits. Runtime delta: **+42 lines** (63 added, 21 removed across seven owners). The requested broad diff-stat filter reports **+98** (157 added, 59 removed across 12 files), including benchmark/fixture/test-support changes. The added runtime state is required to carry roster completeness and the bounded deadline; it replaces the old handoff timer rather than adding another handoff mechanism.

## Accepted tradeoff

Peter explicitly accepted the dashboard reload cost on 2026-10-22. The prior 15-pair comparison measured dashboard-reload LoAF **+24 ms paired median, IQR −9..+45**, against an A/A paired noise distribution of **−27 ms median, IQR −47..+21**. Those results originally parked this gate; the maintainer has now accepted the cost to remove the reported flicker.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop replies after their parent is deleted
prs.body:
Related: #96692; complements #119737. Compared with merged backport #180878, this draft retains observed-deletion lifecycle and per-physical-write/retry coverage; neither check and publication are atomic.

## What Problem This Solves

A threaded reply can outlive its parent. An observed parent deletion currently becomes only an informational event, so queued output, native buffered output, and files can continue publishing to a destination that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact active publishing address after an authorized deletion, without cancelling the underlying agent work. Carry that publication-only signal through deferred replies, previews, native streaming, and ordinary delivery. At the ordinary sender boundary, verify the live parent before each physical text/card send and file completion, including known-safe transport retries. Native retries and preview/final edit retries honor observed parent retirement too. Managed writers and deletion signals reach partial updates, both finalization paths, explicit rate-limit retries, and invalid-block replacement; ambiguous final-edit readback keeps the original reader. Keep earlier accepted parts and do not turn a later failure into permission to replay them.

This complements the confirmed-placement receipt work in #119737. It does not replace that PR or claim to repair every existing receipt/reconciliation inference. A parent read and Slack write are not atomic. Native streams without an observed deletion remain a separate limitation.

## User Impact

After OpenClaw observes deletion of an active reply parent, it stops publishing further output to that parent, including buffered native output. Child deletions and another workspace's matching timestamp leave unrelated publishers intact; explicit top-level sends remain supported. Ordinary threaded sends now require a readable live parent, adding bounded read requests and failing without publication when that evidence is unavailable. Workspace/listener and direct-handoff authority stay scoped to the existing delivery owner.

## Evidence

- Independent review found a native HTTP429 replay gap, and hosted review found a preview/final edit replay gap. Both are corrected in this candidate. A fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its confidence is limited by unavailable surrounding source and unrun tests, types, lint and formatting; live behavior remains unverified.
- Candidate base: `7dcc40f7addb9e45ce3e36768c505ff9cb005209`.
- Regression cases cover deletion before pending final text/file output, deferred delivery, native buffered append/stop, workspace/child isolation, queued sender release, multipart acceptance, upload completion, and identity/transport retry boundaries.
- All 23 original changed TypeScript files and the seven follow-up files passed Node syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. These do not establish type or runtime correctness.
- Local dependency setup is blocked: Corepack's fetch of the repository-pinned pnpm version received HTTP 403 from the managed package registry before installation. No alternate registry, package-manager version, or credentials were used.
- The focused repository test wrapper exits before collection because `node_modules` is unavailable. Tests, typecheck, lint, formatting and CI are pending; syntax-only checks and source review are not substitutes.
- No live Slack test messages, service changes, deployment or release performed. The incident's original raw Slack response is unavailable, so this is boundary repair rather than proof of the provider's exact fallback behavior.

Draft: validation and independent review must be resolved before readiness.

Production growth is needed to propagate exact-parent retirement across existing ordinary, preview, deferred and native publishing owners and to verify queued writes at the transport boundary. No configuration, schema, dependency or persistent-state changes.

Known readiness blocker from the #180878 comparison: the published head can drop the configured account reader when a monitor supplies its writer, and Enterprise parent reads can inherit the listener lookup policy. A six-file correction with credential-isolation and transport-deadline regressions is staged locally. Syntax and whitespace checks pass; fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings, with unavailable unchanged source context and unrun checks as limits. The configured signing agent refused the normal commit signature, so the correction is not yet committed or pushed. No signing configuration or security hooks were bypassed. Runtime/type/lint/format validation remains pending.

prs.title: docs(codex): RFC for recovering pending provider-review linkage
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178923

Builds on merged prevention PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179054.

## What Problem This Solves

An earlier failed acknowledgment can leave an existing conversation bound to a replacement native thread while its pending provider review still identifies the original; the normal review UI then rejects continuation with `Provider review no longer matches the native thread`.

## User Impact

**RFC/design only, not a working recovery fix.** This draft does not restore affected conversations or change runtime behavior. It proposes verifying current authority, restoring the original link through canonical ownership, and then requiring a separate normal acknowledgment with all existing safety checks intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #179054 prevents new replacements but explicitly does not repair an already-mismatched binding. This draft records the recovery contract, a data-only native policy comparator, and an already-mismatched regression specification. It implements no recovery endpoint, authority issuer, binding/review mutation, or acknowledgment path.

The OpenClaw coordinator and native broker remain unimplemented. Confirmation of the provider's ownership/configuration guarantees remains a dependency: Codex 0.160.0 exposes useful policy fields, but matching those fields does not establish exclusive native ownership or a configuration generation valid through canonical commit. If existing native semantics cannot supply that guarantee, provider support is required. Unknown evidence must refuse recovery.

Consistency repair must preserve the pending review and cannot approve continuation, fabricate ownership, spoof a channel sender, bypass catalog/current-policy checks, or replay held input.

## Evidence

- **23 supporting offline checks passed** for the data comparator and scenario fixture (22 data-comparison checks and one fixture consistency check).
- **31 actual recovery acceptance scenarios are specified but unexecuted**, including recovery of an already-mismatched state, authorization failures, changed policy/catalog/review, concurrency, idempotence, partial/uncertain recovery, rollback/crash disposition, and separate normal acknowledgment.
- No successful recovery, live provider acceptance, full Gateway/native integration, repository Vitest/build/typecheck or CI result is claimed.
- Local proposal diff syntax and full-content privacy scans passed. Only generic fixture identities and public source references are included.

Before this can become a recovery fix, implement and validate the coordinator/native broker and catalog preparation, resolve the provider-guarantee dependency, and prove the already-mismatched regression fails on prevention-only #179054 and passes on the implementation. This RFC should not close an existing-mismatch recovery report.

prs.body:
**Rejected experiment — not landing.** The fixed-input byte reduction is real, but the required reload-to-transcript timing gate failed in both batches. Full PR CI passed; no auto-merge was armed.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat boot loads PNG preparation and image-gallery networking before either is needed.

## User Impact

Chat loads 4,691 fewer gzip JavaScript bytes, with the same 23 requests. New Session saves 616 bytes; startup stays effectively unchanged. There are no markup, layout, permission, schema, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load oversized-PNG preparation only after the existing synchronous attachment admission and read-lifecycle setup. Keep its serialized queue, cancellation, worker lifetime, and 15-second read timeout intact. Move the pure image-title, resolved-image, and outgoing-URL helpers into existing lightweight owners, so their eager callers no longer import gallery, fetch, or retry code. Image titles retain reactive translations.

Regenerate the boot-module manifest through `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`. This also refreshes stale membership left by earlier emoji/header deferrals; it adds no manual chunk rule. The module-level top-30 tables and complete attribution are in #181052.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: reduce chat bytes; add no boot requests; keep startup and New Session within the 64-byte build-variance allowance; preserve reload-to-visible timing. Same-machine builds use fixed metadata and the same 29 plugin inputs. Reference: `4f8cf06b1892`; source base: `fb824384939f` (the only intervening commit repairs QA image-generation checks outside Control UI build inputs).

Timing workload before the first run: committed `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts` against production Vite builds, `--runs 20 --face chat --untraced --cold-http-cache --fixture-now-ms 1792712700000`, alternating frozen reference `4f8cf06b1892` and candidate `4302cf42c1e9` (10 pairs). Record transcript-visible and composer-enabled median, p95, all sample values, and host load. The required transcript gate is median no more than 5% above base and p95 no worse than base; report composer values alongside it. This measures synthetic bootstrap/WebSocket fixture transport and persisted UI warm state, not a live model round trip.

| Surface | Before gzip JS | After gzip JS | Delta | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,336 B | 316,324 B | −12 B | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,386,742 B | 1,382,051 B | −4,691 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 859,888 B | 859,272 B | −616 B | 17 → 17 |

CSS: startup 41,124 B unchanged; chat 146,208 → 145,906 B; New Session 106,409 → 106,416 B (+7 B build variance). CSS requests remain 1/8/6. Strict performance check has no violations.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Controller guard | Passed; no baseline increase |
| Targeted lint and formatting | Passed; three existing renderer warnings on unchanged lines |
| Focused attachment-import, gallery, attachment tests | 42/42 assertions passed; uncaught inherited runtime error described below |
| Production Knip | Same 10 finding groups as a recorded base run; no new unused exports |
| Isolated autoreview | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Synthetic production-build capture | Transcript and opened gallery are byte-identical before/after at 1280×900 |
| Reload-to-transcript-visible | Failed in the first 10 pairs and combined 20 pairs per side; results below |
| Full PR CI | Passed on head 4302cf42c1e9, run 39880137022 |

The three-file test command exits 1 despite all assertions passing: `chat-attachments.test.tsx` emits `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')` at `abortFetch` (`node:internal/deps/undici/undici:13142:20`). Running that file on exact base `fb824384939f` also passes all 27 assertions and exits 1 with the identical uncaught error and stack. The new regression holds the actual preparation module, aborts the admitted PNG, then releases it: no Worker, FileReader read, or attachment publication occurs, and pending counts settle exactly once.

Production Knip's output exactly matches the recorded `7a23014fd6ec` run. All ten reported source files are unchanged between that base and this source base. Existing findings: cron schedule constant, cron runner, plugin tool-metadata key, four approval-presentation exports, ProjectCrumb; XRefreshClaim, SessionCleanupSummary, ScheduledOccurrenceRun, ModelsListCatalogSource, and PluginHookMessageSendingResult.

Changed production source: 4,901 → 4,908 lines (+7); generated manifest: +16/−31. The small net growth is the direct async import/error block and import formatting; no new state or ownership layer.

Inspected captures below contain only synthetic names, text, and geometric PNGs. The corresponding before/after PNGs have identical SHA-256 hashes per state.

## Rejected timing result

Both source revisions were built on the same Blacksmith Testbox with the pinned 29 plugin inputs and build metadata. The requested 16-vCPU profile yielded 4 available AMD EPYC CPUs, 16.6 GB RAM, and affinity 0–3; runtime was Node 24.22.1. Samples were serial ABAB cold-HTTP runs of the committed benchmark with no tracing.

prs.title: fix(ci): local checks fail on clean main while CI stays green
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` fail locally for every branch, including pristine `main` (observed at 81ad214a7ab3 and fbc99b8c03f5), while `main` CI stays green.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible product change. Contributors and agents get the same verdict locally and in CI again: unrelated branches pass the baseline ratchets and the core tsgo boundary locally, and CI now stops the drift that caused the local failures instead of only annotating it.

The env-var budget moves from 452 to 461 to record names that already landed on `main` (each listed with its PR in the file); owner-approved with the land instruction.

## Why This Change Was Made

CI runs the same ratchet script with the same base shape; it does not skip it. The difference is `scripts/lib/check-limits.mts`: since 9ed5a04a6551 every limit violation is a warning under `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` and an error locally. The max-lines suppression inventory and the env-var budget were routed through that policy, so `main` absorbed drift with green CI (the main-push job for dc029d8c02 annotated these exact warnings): files moved with suppressions but without their baseline entries (#173575, #173811, #173802), dozens of baseline entries went stale, and `OPENCLAW_*` names landed without budget updates. Every later local run then failed on debt the branch did not create.

The fix separates two things the policy had merged. Whether an inventory describes the tree (unlisted suppression, stale entry, name count different from the budget) is bookkeeping with no legitimate growth path, so it now blocks in CI and locally, matching the sibling shrink ratchets (assertion safety, timeout race, mock exports) that already block. Growth of an inventory relative to the merge base keeps the limit policy, so owner-approved growth still lands with a CI warning.

The core tsgo shard root budget is the opposite case: its own contract (4a93b5e5c8ea) says oversized shards warn and never block, because no single change owns shard size. Routing it through the limit reporter made it locally fatal for every branch touching core TypeScript. It now warns everywhere. Over-limit shards were rebalanced by moving whole test globs (`src/media` to messaging, `src/acp` to gateway-other, `src/security` to config-cli, root `src/gateway/github*` to gateway-methods, root `src/agents/cli-*` to commands); the largest shard is now agents-sessions at 701 roots.

The drift is cleared at its owners rather than grandfathered. `main`'s #180868 has since split the Settings and Sessions page state files, so this branch only splits `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx` (2,640 lines) into five subject suites plus two support files, all well under the test cap, with its suppression removed. The baseline is pruned (508 to 438), and an internal constant that the env counter misread as an environment name is renamed.

## Evidence

- Before, pristine `main` (fbc99b8c03f5) plus one unrelated exported constant: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` fails `max-lines suppression ratchet` and `core tsgo graph boundary` (`Core test shard root budget exceeded`). After, the branch plus the same line with the branch head as base: both lanes pass. In both runs the dead-export scan flags only the proof constant itself.
- Rebuilt head on current `main`: `check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base HEAD` → `max-lines ratchet OK: 438`, `OPENCLAW_* count 461/461`; with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true --base origin/main` exit 0 with the single budget-growth warning; locally against `origin/main` the only failure is that growth, by design.
- `check-tsgo-core-boundary.mts`: on the old shard layout with this script, exit 0 with advisory warnings (previously exit 1); on the rebuilt head, exit 0 and silent; exactly-once ownership test passes.
- Regression tests red on the base scripts, green with the fix: `check-max-lines-ratchet.test.ts` (moved suppression and stale entry block under GitHub Actions) and `check-env-var-count.test.ts` (unrecorded names block under GitHub Actions; recorded growth warns).
- Chat split: 67 declarations / 79 executed tests before and after with identical names and assertions; one moved test now awaits `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` because it had relied on an earlier test loading the lazy image renderer (the file already uses that idiom elsewhere). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:root`, scoped lint and format pass. No visual change, so no screenshots.
- The earlier PR CI failure in `lint-suppressions.test.ts` came from `main`'s own `scripts/perf/*` suppressions on that merge ref, not from this branch; the test passes on this head.
- Codex autoreview (P2) of the branch and of the rebuild: scoped-clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the unnamed chat transcript log that screen-reader users encounter when tabbing through a conversation.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind the existing translation to the transcript's accessible name. No new translation catalog entries are needed.

## Evidence

The existing chat-view fixture renders the production transcript component. Its name assertion fails on the base with `expected null to be 'Chat'`; both existing cases pass with the fix (2 tests, 37.06 s suite / 40.25 s wrapper). Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent review found no actionable issue.

The canonical UI typecheck (`scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui.tsbuildinfo`) passed locally. Local targeted lint stopped during SDK declaration preparation (300-second timeout); the exact-head [hosted lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39828356099/job/119999343783) and [production typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39828356099/job/119999343855) both pass. prs.title: fix(agents): reject FIFO native-hook credentials without blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native remote-hook relay opens its credential before checking that it is a regular file. A FIFO with no writer blocks that open, so the relay cannot reach the existing denial response, even with `--timeout 1000`. This is malformed local credential input, not a remote privilege-escalation claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `O_NONBLOCK` at the existing no-follow open. The existing descriptor `isFile()` check can then reject the FIFO and the existing `finally` closes the handle. The HTTPS request AbortSignal cannot cancel a filesystem open; adding another timer would leave the blocked worker behind. No new helper, fallback or transport path is needed.

Existing-solutions preflight: native open flags already solve this admission problem. The shared database recovery reader and archive walker own different synchronous/traversal contracts; importing them here would create the wrong ownership relationship. The remote credential reader is shared by Codex and Claude relay invocations, so the repair belongs here. Fresh all-state semantic and symbol searches found no active implementation of this repair.

The native relay entry, command generator, denial mapping, descriptor cleanup and HTTPS close settlement were inspected. Upstream Codex was checked directly at `2df67054232090af8d2fa197c46b994bc2b0dda1`: [command_runner.rs, timeout and process-tree ownership](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2df67054232090af8d2fa197c46b994bc2b0dda1/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs#L205), including lines 284–370. An outer harness timeout does not make this inner credential read cancellable. No Codex protocol or runtime behavior is changed.

## User Impact

An invalid FIFO promptly produces the relay's existing deny output instead of hanging until an outer process timeout. Regular credential files still use the existing size/JSON checks and trusted HTTPS transport. No config/default, dependency, protocol/schema, migration, URL/TLS policy or capability-authority changes.

## Evidence

### Current-head verification after main synchronization — 2026-10-23

Head **f23329781c9bb89ecb78fdc6f1c86aa1321d28dc**, normal merge of main **7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92**. Retained main's consolidated real-TLS/response-close coverage and removed imports made unused by that upstream reorganization.

- Complete current owner file: **2/2 PASS**, local-container `leon-nativehook-merge-tests-20261023`, one worker, Vitest **8.82s**, wrapper **13.22s**. Focused `tsgo`, typed lint, formatting and diff checks PASS. Current production **+6/-1**, tests **+42/-0**.
- `pnpm build sourcePerformance`: PASS in **276.1s**, build-info commit **f23329781c9bb89ecb78fdc6f1c86aa1321d28dc**, version **2026.10.6**, Node **24.22.1**.
- Same proof command: `node native-hook-fifo-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new-output-directory> green`; exact build commit asserted, checked **2026-10-23T00:57:28.163Z**.
- Ordinary credential: **381.8ms**, one real authenticated loopback HTTPS request and exact response stdout. Malformed credential: **356.0ms**, existing deny output, **0 requests**. Writerless FIFO: **358.8ms**, existing credential error and deny output, **0 requests**, no timeout or writer.
- Receipt `maintenance-172271-proof-20261023-run/receipt.json`; unchanged harness SHA256 **a914f9dd3492291887f6f21ec085d2c488bf0b7c55427cac9c1d617b754ef595**. Real receiver and cold packaged relay entry; no credential-reader/transport replacement.
- Personally rechecked sibling Codex at **2df67054232090af8d2fa197c46b994bc2b0dda1**: `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs:205`, `:284`, `:334`; `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs:1`; `codex-rs/hooks/src/registry.rs:200`. No upstream protocol/timeout semantics change.

### Original acceptance RED/GREEN (historical commits)

Built OpenClaw 2026.10.3 on Linux/Node 24.16.0, using the actual cold `dist/native-hook-relay/entry.js` executable, synthetic credentials and a real loopback HTTPS receiver with a temporary trusted CA. The receiver validates the capability header and payload and records accepted requests. Filesystem and relay owner are unmocked; the receiver stands in for the remote endpoint, so this does not prove the remote Gateway's authorization/backend.

Same native entry on both versions:

```text
node dist/native-hook-relay/entry.js hooks relay --provider codex --relay-id proof-relay --event pre_tool_use --remote-credential <credential> --timeout 1000
node native-hook-fifo-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new-output-directory> green
```

The harness uses the `red` expectation on the unmodified base and sends the same synthetic PreToolUse input on stdin.

| Credential | Before | Committed fix |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary JSON, trusted HTTPS | 1 authenticated request; exact response stdout; exit 0 in 0.364 s | Same request/response; exit 0 in 0.385 s |
| Malformed JSON `{` | Existing credential error and `permissionDecision: deny`; 0 requests in 0.336 s | Same denial; 0 requests in 0.331 s |
| FIFO, no writer | No response after 5.03 s despite the 1 s CLI timeout; owned-process watchdog required; 0 requests | Existing credential error and deny response in 0.331 s; 0 requests |

**1/1 blocked FIFO processes becomes 0/1**. Both invalid inputs issue **0/2 HTTPS requests**; the ordinary control issues **1/1** and reproduces the exact receiver response. The deny response intentionally exits 0 under the existing hook contract; it is not an allow. The new regression runs the FIFO probe in a bounded child so a regression cannot strand a libuv worker in Vitest.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.test.ts src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  4 passed, exit 0; Vitest 3.57 s / wrapper 7.97 s
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.ts src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.test.ts
  passed, exit 0
oxfmt --check src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.ts src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-remote-client.test.ts
  passed
git diff --check
  passed
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  passed on exact committed head
```

The existing real-TLS test covers untrusted certificates, trusted capability delivery, redirects, response size, abort, invalid URL and malformed credentials. Two lifecycle tests cover joining the socket after response/error delivery.

RED base `3d9637ef6301e6823f621cf7ed419dd2a75e8c61`; GREEN head **`98e0345ad909dac2b2326558824ee570fb497fc6`**, tree `08f7f180e02dbf1dd2548ee5d397df341308116a`; clean worktree, matching build commit, built `2026-10-14T15:22:49.479Z`, GREEN completed `2026-10-14T15:26:17.659Z`. Harness SHA256 `a914f9dd3492291887f6f21ec085d2c488bf0b7c55427cac9c1d617b754ef595`; RED receipt `ae7201821172e6e08abb064cfdb67e6f078af6c7f7437529255828e3a5105dce`; GREEN receipt `c8f6d483b62c41a1f14e78fd14436d6107974f369b79a98e24b5630fa8273c83`. Sanitized output is published above; raw receipts remain local.

Production: **1 file +6/-1, net +5**. Current tests: **1 file +42/-0**. No generated/lockfile changes. Production growth explains the cancellation boundary and formats the existing open with one additional flag.

Not tested: native macOS/Windows, an actual Codex/Claude model turn, remote Gateway authorization/backend behavior, or full suites. The reproduction uses the native OpenClaw relay executable, not a model session. Independent automated autoreview was not run at the contributor's request.

<details>
<summary>AI disclosure</summary>

Implemented with AI assistance for Leon-SK668. Inspected the owner, callers/siblings and direct upstream Codex contract; reproduced native blocking before edits; added the admission flag; ran focused checks; rebuilt and replayed the exact committed head. No maintainer acceptance, rating or merge is claimed. No raw session logs or secrets are included.

prs.title: fix: allow retry after Side chat times out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a timed-out Side chat question offers no Retry action and can release its source context before the canceled run finishes cleanup.

## User Impact

User impact: timed-out questions can be retried after cleanup, without losing earlier answers or appending a late answer. The 60-second execution deadline and 1,200-character answer budget are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return a typed, retryable timeout and keep the request's source facts and busy slot alive until internal-session execution and cleanup settle. Ordinary requests still time out promptly while waiting only for context. This matches the existing incognito lifetime rule without adding another cleanup owner.

A provider that ignores cancellation can still delay settlement; this change does not increase the execution budget or diagnose the original slow answer.

## Evidence

- Red on the base, green with the fix: typed timeout recovery and the real RPC/native-session path retaining source authority through cancellation, cleanup, late-answer suppression, and successful retry.
- Five Side chat suites: 64 tests passed, plus the incognito source-lifetime sibling test. Final changed-file runs: 25/25 and 18/18 passed (51.69s and 19.82s wrapper wall time). The one new regression took 1.32s; no new fixture or suite.
- Production and Gateway-test typechecks; targeted lint/format; documentation MDX/Markdown checks; diff sanity passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- The broad changed-test graph selector hit pre-existing graph-size limits (725/729 roots vs. 720); the matching Gateway test graph passed directly instead.
- The initial production-path regression uses a controlled model loop; the real-provider confirmation below covers the production execution path. The original slow-answer cause remains unknown. No UI layout changes.

### Rendered timeout recovery

Production Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses: the old timeout has no Retry action; the new typed timeout exposes Retry. The browser test also clicks Retry, verifies the recovered answer stays in place, preserves earlier Side chat and main-chat content, and observes no main-chat sends or resets. One focused browser test passed (3.07s; production build plus test 31.28s). This proves rendered recovery behavior, not the cause of the original live-provider timeout.

Screenshots embedded below: **Before** (first image, no Retry action) and **After** (second image, Retry available).

### Real-provider deadline and recovery

A newly created, isolated Gateway and its actual production Control UI ran against OpenAI GPT-4.1 mini on head `1e5f238116932acde951cb1a2796abf965c90860`. All six provider requests completed upstream with HTTP 200. A local relay deliberately withheld one genuine provider response; neither Gateway RPC responses nor model output were synthesized.

The unchanged deadline returned the typed, retryable timeout after **60.254 seconds**. The Gateway canceled the held request and completed cleanup before exposing Retry. Releasing the held response afterward could not deliver a late answer. Clicking the actual UI Retry button made a new real-provider request and answered the contextual question correctly (Thursday), in place. The earlier Side chat answer (Friday) and main-chat transcript were preserved; no reset or extra main-chat send occurred.

The focused live browser test passed (74.39s; runner 153.80s). Process exit, isolated state deletion, relay closure, and a clean source worktree were verified. Only the disposable Gateway was started/stopped; the hosting Gateway was not modified. The third image below shows the actual recovered live-provider result.

**Limit:** latency was deliberately induced. This verifies deadline, cancellation, cleanup, and Retry behavior—not the cause of the original slow answer.

Credit: @steipete for requesting the reliability audit and repair.

prs.title: fix(doctor): reject malformed UTF-8 across legacy imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor could decode malformed UTF-8 as replacement characters and persist the changed text into SQLite, config, or workspace skill files. Audit all legacy import boundaries, including the retired runtime state and Skill Workshop reports.

Fixes #180795, Fixes #180782.

Supersedes #180794 and #180781, thanks @wangmiao0668000666.

## User Impact

Damaged legacy text is refused with a warning while independent migrations continue. Original bytes stay in the source or its existing byte-for-byte archive. Invalid Skill Workshop rollback text never reaches workspace files. Valid input and existing database, permission, and malformed-JSON failure handling retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `decodeUtf8Input` and add bounded streaming decoding to the same owner. A distinct encoding error lets existing migration owners report recoverable refusals without relaxing unrelated failures. Keep opaque backup reads separate from semantic text import; do not reject arbitrary bytes before they can be backed up.

Coverage includes ACPX history/owner records; Codex binding sidecars and external owner indexes; Teams delegated tokens; Matrix credentials and sync cache (Doctor and startup); Zalo Personal credentials; Reef identity, registration, audit, replay, reviews, and delivery state; retired Voice Wake/routing/bindings/approvals; Skill Workshop proposals and rollbacks; legacy session indexes and key repair; plugin JSON state; model catalogs and credential imports; OAuth key files and decrypted sidecars; pairing requests and allowlists; cron definitions, runtime state, and quarantine; Phone Control; node-host state; Web Push; TUI last-session pointers; managed image metadata; audit records; meeting metadata, summaries, and streamed utterances; and plain/zstd transcript archives.

The simplification removes the unused cron-state version wrapper. The pre-commit line-cap gate required two bounded extractions: shared session-key classification now lives with session-surface helpers, and Codex binding ownership inspection lives in its own migration module. Their function bodies and behavior are unchanged; callers use the new owners, and the obsolete Codex max-lines suppression is removed. Production: +702/-329 (**+373**); tests: +841/-18 (**+823**). Remaining growth is shared streaming/error handling and encoding-specific warning propagation; no new state owner, schema, dependency, or configuration option.

## Evidence

- **Assertion-safety follow-up:** replaced the extracted binding-owner error assertion with the existing `isRecord` runtime guard before inspecting `code`. This preserves the expected agent-selection fallback and rethrows other values unchanged. The original `session-binding-owners.ts: 1 > 0` failure is gone. Shrank only the obsolete `session-binding-sidecars.ts` assertion baseline from 4 to 3 to record the removed violation. The full `pnpm check:assertion-safety` run now passes with exit 0 (2,464 files, 5,643 grandfathered assertions). All 143 tests across nine Codex Doctor/migration files passed on Node (303.80 seconds) and Bun (124.40 seconds). Scoped lint, formatting, diff-check, and independent review pass. The unrelated update-CLI recovery failure is tracked separately.

- **Red on the original readers:** 55 new regression cases reproduced imported replacement characters or rewritten source/workspace bytes. Source-preservation and independent-migration assertions pass with the fix.
- **Bun:** 23 focused files, 344 passed / 1 skipped, 181.22 seconds wall time. Includes late stream corruption after prior records have been staged, plain/zstd archives, and valid multibyte chunk boundaries.
- **Node core/siblings:** 100 files selected; 1,334 passed, 21 skipped, and 3 fixture-environment failures in the original invocation (1,362.41 seconds). The three failures were in `doctor-health.fleet-preflight.test.ts` (2) and `doctor-migration-preservation.test.ts` (1): the shared volume is group-writable, which the unchanged recovery-copy guard rejects. All three passed with `TMPDIR="$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)"`, keeping HOME and state isolated in the worktree. The preservation case takes 40.131 seconds of test time because it performs repeated full recovery captures and integrity checks; no timeout or assertion was weakened.

prs.title: fix: public conversation links show raw embed shortcodes for YouTube and external pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: public conversation links show a raw `[embed url="…" /]` line when the assistant embedded a YouTube video or another external page.

## User Impact

User impact: signed-out readers of a publicly shared conversation now see YouTube and other external embeds as ordinary links, labeled with the embed's title. The public page still loads no third-party pages, players, or thumbnails, and its content security policy is unchanged. Hosted inline widgets keep rendering in their sandboxed frames.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to #178648, which taught the public reader to render Gateway-hosted inline widgets but deliberately left every other `[embed]` shortcode as text.

The public reader now strips every valid embed shortcode outside Markdown code:

- Gateway-hosted canvas documents keep the existing sandboxed widget frame.
- Absolute `https`/`http` URLs without embedded credentials become a plain link after the message text, using the same link policy and `rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow"` as Markdown links (the policy is now one shared helper).
- Anything else, such as other Gateway pages or `javascript:` URLs, is omitted, the same way the reader already omits hosted widgets it cannot serve.
- Shortcodes inside code fences and inline code stay literal.

Framing YouTube (even through `youtube-nocookie.com`) or loading its thumbnail would be a new third-party load from an anonymous page, so that stays out of scope pending a separate product decision. Widgets and links share one ordered list, so a message's embeds appear after its text and images in shortcode order, matching the Control UI. Malformed shortcodes with no `url` or `ref` keep today's literal text, as in the Control UI.

Docs: `web/urls` describes the public behavior, the Control UI YouTube section notes it, and `concepts/multi-user` no longer claims public links exclude images and widgets (stale since #178648).

Release note: Public conversation links show YouTube and other external `[embed]` content as plain links instead of raw shortcode text.

## Evidence

- New render regression test (YouTube with title, untitled block form, a private Gateway path, `javascript:` and credentialed URLs, an embed-only message, code literals): fails on `main`, passes here.
- Mixed-order regression (link, hosted widget, link in one message renders in that order): fails on the first revision of this PR (flagged by the Codex connector and ClawSweeper), passes here.
- Focused suites pass: 8 files / 130 tests (public reader render, HTTP, chat route, refresh, entry, media, card render, canvas render). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, and format pass for the changed files.
- Codex autoreview (P0–P2): scoped-clean on the first revision and on the ordering fix.

### Live proof (isolated Gateway, real model turn)

Isolated state and port, built from this branch, `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`. The agent replied with `[embed url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw" title="Me at the zoo" /]`, a Wikipedia URL embed, and the same YouTube shortcode inside a fenced code block. Public access was enabled with `session.publicShare.set`, then `/chat/main` was opened in a fresh, signed-out headless Chromium context (empty storage, no cookies, **Log in** shown):

- Two plain links (`Me at the zoo`, `YouTube — Wikipedia`) with `rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow"`; no literal shortcode outside code.
- 0 iframes, 0 transcript images, and **no requests to any non-loopback host** during the page load.
- The fenced shortcode stays literal.
- Response CSP unchanged (`frame-src 'self'`, `img-src 'self'`).

Before (`main` renderer, same Gateway state and transcript):

![before: literal embed shortcodes on the public page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dfbaf6a-468d-474c-aefc-ba017da64a03)

After, dark and light:

![after: embeds shown as plain links, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaeb0703-40ea-48e1-9d23-8a2549d75c59)
![after: embeds shown as plain links, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b972142c-dec3-4b41-8f46-2e3ae56283b1)

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

- Production change: about +45/-25 lines across the public projection, renderer, and widget-token minting; no config, schema, protocol, or copy-key changes, and no locale refresh needed.
- Local `check:changed`: the max-lines suppression ratchet flags the same three untouched UI files reported on #178648 (pre-existing on `main`). The SQLite worker ratchet did not finish locally (it hit a local timeout while a build ran alongside it), so PR CI covers it; this change touches no database code.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): composer shows no keyboard focus in forced-colors mode
prs.body:
Closes #180134

## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session composer focus is visually indistinguishable under forced colors: normal border/shadow cues disappear, leaving keyboard users without a surviving focus indicator.

## User Impact

The focused native editor gets a visible 2px system `Highlight` outline with a 2px offset around its composer. It clears when the editor no longer matches `:focus-visible`. Normal light/dark styling and focus ownership remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a forced-colors-only CSS fallback at the existing shared composer surface. No JavaScript handlers, tab stops, options, permissions, or schema changes.

The separate media rule is intentional: the neighboring background rule also covers enhanced contrast and reduced transparency. Combining them would broaden this focus change beyond forced colors.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and Control UI together in isolated Docker. Created real session/model metadata through shipped commands, then used native Tab navigation to the actual enabled Chat and New Session editors in Linux Chromium.

Exercised both routes with forced colors active/off and light/dark schemes, twice on main and twice on the candidate. Captured unfocused, keyboard-focused, Tab-away, and pointer phases with computed wrapper/editor styles, DOM/accessibility snapshots, Tab traces and screenshots.

- Main under forced colors: native editor `:focus-visible` is true, but wrapper `outline-style` remains `none`, box-shadow is `none`, and the system border is unchanged. The unused computed outline width is not painted.
- Candidate under forced colors: `solid` / `2px` outline, `2px` offset, using the resolved system Highlight color in light and dark schemes.
- Before focus and after Tab away: the wrapper outline is unpainted again.
- Forced-colors-off light/dark border/shadow controls are unchanged. Pointer text-field focus follows Chromium's native `:focus-visible` heuristic; no custom modality logic is introduced.
- Both new browser regressions fail on main and pass on the candidate; the existing normal-theme focus control passes on both. All three focused checks pass on the candidate.
- Targeted formatting, Oxlint and Stylelint pass.
- Exact-head built CLI smoke with real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` returns `UI smoke ready`.

[Inspected Chat/New Session before-and-after screenshots and computed-style/keyboard evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180135#issuecomment-6354586762).

This proves Chromium forced-colors emulation, not a native Windows app run.

Whole-diff simplification retains the minimal shared CSS rule and paired route regressions, with no new state or focus implementation. Production +8/-0, tests +38/-0, documentation +1/-0. Contributor commit and credit are preserved.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores prior styling without changing state. Blast radius is native editor focus outlines on shared composer surfaces while forced colors are active.

prs.title: fix(backup): reject raced FIFO sources without waiting for writers
prs.body:
Closes #171986

## What Problem This Solves

A regular backup source can become a FIFO between its pathname check and native open. The current no-follow open waits for a writer, preventing the existing descriptor-type check from rejecting the change. Related: #159229; its separate SQLite snapshot stall is outside this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add O_NONBLOCK at the archive walker's POSIX admission boundary. Its existing descriptor check then rejects the FIFO before emitting a header, and existing cleanup closes the handle. Windows retains its flags. This keeps one traversal and introduces no timeout/fallback path.

Existing-solutions preflight: inspected the installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` read-admission contract, which already uses nonblocking open before classification. The specialized walker owns tar traversal, progress and descriptor lifecycle; this invariant fits its existing open. No new dependency/helper is needed. At selection, all-state issue/PR, timeline and semantic searches found no active repair for this race. The merged #164161 covers a different configuration-input owner.

## User Impact

Backups over changing workspaces fail promptly if a checked source becomes a special file; correct the source and retry. Regular bytes, verification, stable special-file omission, symlink/identity safeguards and partial-output cleanup are preserved. No config/default, protocol, schema, migration, dependency or authorization change. Same-user pathname mutation is host mutation, not a privilege exploit. The CLI's existing generic failure/Doctor guidance is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Current-head verification after main synchronization — 2026-10-23

Head **3c3632a2e9cf8030417ba57071afcd74e52c9ddb**, normal merge of main **7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92**. Retained upstream large-inode, Windows tar/PAX link and symlink/identity cases while resolving the test-import conflict.

- Complete walker file **9/9 PASS**, local-container `leon-backup-merge-tests-20261023`, one worker, Vitest **6.67s**, wrapper **11.18s**. Focused `tsgo`, typed lint, formatting and diff checks PASS.
- `pnpm build sourcePerformance`: PASS in **286.2s**, build-info commit **3c3632a2e9cf8030417ba57071afcd74e52c9ddb**, version **2026.10.6**, Node **24.22.1**.
- Same actual public CLI harness: `node backup-fifo-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new-output-directory> green`; clean source, checked **2026-10-23T00:49:17.372Z**.
- Ordinary backup **3.356s**, pre-existing-FIFO control **3.343s**: exit **0**, verified archives; independent system tar readback matches all **86,041 bytes** and excludes the pre-existing FIFO.
- Native source replacement at the real open: **3.186s**, exit **1**, no timeout, no writer and **no published archive**. The preload records real flags **133120** and confirms that the replacement is a FIFO. The zero-header owner regression also passes.
- Receipt `maintenance-171989-proof-20261023-run/receipt.json`. Harness SHA256 **6d235fdd07f38160766aac7af0e852dc1f4384d4c6bcf2221301e840873368fb**; unchanged race preload SHA256 **601f9daf6c58de2fbd6b6fcb5d0c850019c4276329953b898ae58f342aa01634**. No lockfile/generated/proof-asset changes.

### Original acceptance RED/GREEN (historical commits)

Normal built OpenClaw 2026.10.3 CLI on Linux/Node 24.16.0, isolated homes/state/workspaces; no model, channel or external recipient.

| Scenario | Unmodified walker | Committed fix |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary source | Verified archive; exact 86,041-byte system-tar readback | Same verified payload |
| Pre-existing FIFO beside regular source | FIFO omitted; regular payload verifies | Same omission and exact payload |
| Regular source replaced by native FIFO immediately before open | Blocked five seconds after observed open; owned process killed; no published archive | Exit 1 in 2.77 s total CLI time; no writer needed, no published archive |

The fixture controls mutation timing only: native rename/mkfifo followed by the real Node open and production archive pipeline. It does not fabricate filesystem returns or replace the CLI with an owner helper. The regression also checks zero emitted header chunks. An initial green assertion incorrectly expected the owner's detailed error at the CLI; the complete replay was corrected to check the actual generic public failure banner.

Before production edits, the real-FIFO regression fails because its backstop writer is required. Afterward the complete walker file passes **9/9**, including exact large inode identity, Windows header/PAX link rendering, symlink/parent replacement, unlinked-leaf identity and root disappearance controls.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer menu navigation until first open
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closed menus loaded Zag navigation during Chat and New Session boot. Defer that runtime until a menu opens. The existing native overlay keeps admission, dismissal, initial focus, item DOM and pointer activation synchronous; one Zag implementation takes over keyboard navigation after loading. Queued input preserves order, retained-focus listboxes and embedded controls remain actionable, and a failed import has a visible retry.

The cold facade also preserves native item selectors, initial-row scrolling, and Zag pointerdown focus prevention. Without the last behavior, focusing a trigger settled its ancestor animation and moved it 24 px before pointerup, causing a real click to miss. The shared/personal rejected-publication recovery cases and a focused pointerdown regression verify the repair. Right-click and macOS Control-click retain their native behavior.

## Performance

Matched same-machine production builds: base source `4f8cf06b18925ff494a305ac364cdbb8271227fe`, candidate runtime source `6cdc426ae6b`, Node 26.12.1. Candidate includes current main `fb824384939`; that revision has no UI/shared-source or budget difference from the measured base. Both builds have exactly identical fixed build metadata, including `dirty: false`, and the same 29 verified packaged-plugin files. Both use build ID `solid2-boot-comparison`; these controlled metadata inputs are distinct from actual source identity.

| Surface | Main gzip | Candidate gzip | Savings | JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,336 B | 316,327 B | 9 B | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,386,742 B | 1,353,266 B | 33,476 B | 23 → 23 |
| New Session | 859,888 B | 826,422 B | 33,466 B | 17 → 17 |

Startup CSS is unchanged: 41,124 B gzip / one request. The strict matched comparison has zero violations and warnings. Caps fall from 1,439,860/871,648 B to **1,405,102/837,725 B**, using `ceil(candidate × main cap / measured main)` to preserve relative headroom. Route request caps remain 25/19, two above observed use. No startup baseline is raised. The original split reduced one route request; current main's additional chunk changes make final request counts equal while retaining the byte reduction.

Production LOC across seven affected modules: **2,252 → 2,627 (+375)**. Growth is the synchronous facade, loading/error handling and ordered replay around the deferred runtime; there is no second navigation implementation. Refactor census: one effect, four `untrack`, zero render effects/direct DOM listeners/queries/`flush`/Solid owner APIs.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck after current-main integration | Passed on `fb824384939` integration |
| Matched production build + strict performance | Passed, zero violations/warnings |
| Production Knip | Passed after current-main integration |
| Independent isolated P0–P2 review | Final integrated review scoped-clean, zero actionable findings |
| Loading browser tests | 16/16 Chromium + WebKit; latest pointerdown/loading Chromium run 9/9 |
