prs.title: fix(update): preserve JSON errors for invalid repair channels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An invalid channel passed to the public update repair command exits with an actionable diagnostic but leaves redirected JSON stdout empty. Automation cannot parse that failure despite requesting JSON. The internal finalize entry has the same guard.

This follows the accepted CLI refusal-output repairs in #176018, #176013 and #172281. It is separate from #131411, which kept Doctor panels out of successful repair JSON output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The finalizer now throws the existing expected CLI error instead of printing and exiting inside the channel guard. The shared root renderer can produce its canonical JSON failure while preserving the existing human diagnostic. Public repair and internal finalization share this owner; ordinary update already propagates its invalid-channel error.

Existing-solutions preflight: reuse throwExpectedCliError and the existing root renderer. No new formatter, dependency, configuration/default, protocol, schema, migration or repair lifecycle is introduced. Production LOC **+2/-3, net -1**; tests **+32/-8**; **3 files**, no generated or lockfile changes. The existing admission-ledger consumer now expects the propagated finalization error while retaining its zero-mutation assertions.

## User Impact

Invalid repair channel options still exit 1 and leave the requested update channel unchanged. JSON consumers receive one complete error object on stdout. Human mode and the actionable stderr message remain intact; stderr is diagnostic output, not the JSON document.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Invalid repair/finalize channel options produce parseable JSON stdout; human diagnostics and existing update state remain intact.
- Entry: node openclaw.mjs update repair --channel unrecognized-channel --json; node openclaw.mjs update --json repair --channel unrecognized-channel; corresponding internal finalize paths. The real finalizer and root renderer run unmocked.
- Same command on base 19f6fa1851d83415299ab24154c0194b449c8de3 and head 0fcebf3c30f49c782b13342777d4f7130da5a1f1: node ../update-channel-json-proof-20261022.mjs
  - Before: all four command/flag combinations exit 1 with 0 stdout bytes and the 93-byte channel diagnostic on stderr.
  - After: all four exit 1 with one complete 181-byte JSON error on stdout, preserving the same 93-byte stderr diagnostic.
- Readback: independent child-process JSON parsing, unchanged config/package byte hashes after all refusals, and an explicit valid config-write control followed by fresh-process readback.
- Proof harness: SHA256 6d2ef76984f14f16c8067d8e2dc8505273207b205367bdf3fec42f7bea63c41a; identical final driver on fresh main and candidate. Both native builds assert build-info commit equals HEAD.
- Control: refusal fixture records zero repair runs and retains pending migrations; cleanup dry-run remains successful JSON; existing timeout refusal remains parseable; a separate valid config write changes the file and a fresh command reads beta.
- Other callers checked: public updateRepairCommand, updateMaintenanceError, internal finalize/resume, ordinary update channel validation, runCommandWithRuntime, and root failure rendering.
- Tests: complete refusal and admission-ledger files, one worker, 22/22 PASS; original qualified baseline 1 intended new failure / 11 existing passes. Focused tsgo, typed oxlint, oxfmt and git diff --check passed.
- Measured follow-up test cost: 311.78 seconds Vitest duration; 415.52 seconds including cold worker preparation. No broad suite. Exact-head native build passed in 232.3 seconds; the unchanged native proof driver passed again afterward.
- Not tested: successful repair lifecycle, installed-release upgrade, package swap, daemon restart, plugin migration, external API or macOS/Windows. This is an early CLI validation repair, before entering that lifecycle.

Exact product/build head: **0fcebf3c30f49c782b13342777d4f7130da5a1f1**. Fresh-main RED/build: **19f6fa1851d83415299ab24154c0194b449c8de3**, with unchanged relevant owners from the original ce54bc8 baseline. The original native proof was captured on **2026-10-22 around 16:14 UTC** and rerun after the consumer-test fix, Node **24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**, isolated synthetic home/config/state and no provider credentials.

### Captured native output

The same command runs on both builds:

~~~sh
node openclaw.mjs update repair --channel unrecognized-channel --json
~~~

Before: exit **1**, stdout **empty**. Stderr:

~~~text
--channel must be "stable", "extended-stable", "beta", or "dev" (got "unrecognized-channel")
~~~

After: exit **1**, complete stdout:

~~~json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--channel must be \"stable\", \"extended-stable\", \"beta\", or \"dev\" (got \"unrecognized-channel\")"
  }
}
~~~

Stderr retains the exact diagnostic above. Human mode retains empty stdout and that same one-line stderr. The final driver checks those actual contracts; it does not require empty stderr in JSON mode.

| Native command / JSON placement | Before stdout | After stdout | Exit before / after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| update repair ... --json | empty | complete JSON error | 1 / 1 |
| update --json repair ... | empty | complete JSON error | 1 / 1 |
| update finalize ... --json | empty | complete JSON error | 1 / 1 |
| update --json finalize ... | empty | complete JSON error | 1 / 1 |

After these refusals the config and installation manifest hashes equal their initial values. A separate positive write control then runs:

~~~sh
node openclaw.mjs config set update.channel beta
node openclaw.mjs config get update.channel --json
~~~

The config file changes and the fresh read process exits **0** with complete stdout:

~~~json
"beta"
~~~

The successful read-only update cleanup control exits **0** and reports an empty artifact inventory, zero removed files, status preview and dryRun true. No repair/update installation was performed to produce this evidence.

### Focused verification

~~~text
Qualified baseline: Tests 1 failed | 11 passed (12)
Candidate follow-up: 2 files, Tests 22 passed (22), exit 0
~~~

The host's old glibc cannot load the proc-safe native identity binding. The two complete files ran in a local Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35 container with native identity available: provider **local-container**, id **leon-update-json-tests-fixed-20261023**, Node **24.22.1**. This is local validation, not remote proof.

~~~sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize-refusal.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.admission-ledger.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <focused-config>
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig <focused-config> src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize-refusal.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.admission-ledger.test.ts
pnpm build sourcePerformance
~~~

Author simplification checked the complete change, caller chain and sibling validation paths. No independent-review pass or unrun upstream CI result is claimed.

CI follow-up: the initial admission-ledger failure was an existing consumer assertion missed in the first patch; the new commit fixes that assertion and the complete file passes. The initial CI also reported two resume-completion failures. A local Node parent control hit a different process-cleanup failure, so it does not establish those CI failures as inherited; fresh exact-head CI is still required before merge. No process-cleanup behavior, timeouts or unrelated assertions were changed.

<details>
<summary>Redacted agent transcript — this task only</summary>

- User: Extend recently accepted bug families using complete, independently verified probes.
- Assistant: Checked current source, shared error contracts and all-state competing work. Reproduced empty JSON stdout through public repair before changing production.
- Implementation: Reused the root expected-error path at the shared finalizer guard; removed the local print-and-exit branch.
- Validation: Qualified baseline had only the new regression fail. After CI exposed a missed consumer assertion, the complete refusal/admission-ledger files passed 22 tests and the rebuilt exact committed native CLI again produced structured failures at both flag positions, preserving human diagnostics and byte-level state controls.

Credentials, private paths and unrelated conversation are omitted.

</details>

`openclaw update repair --channel unrecognized-channel --json` exits with empty stdout, so automation cannot parse the failure. Internal `update finalize` has the same issue, including an explicitly empty channel.

The shared `updateFinalizeCommand` printed and exited inside its channel guard, bypassing the root CLI failure renderer. Route that guard through the existing expected-error helper. These three files and `update-command-runtime-recovery.test-support.ts` are restored byte-for-byte from `origin/main`; this PR does not change their expectations. prs.title: fix(migrate-hermes): reject FIFO text inputs without blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hermes migration can wait indefinitely for a writer when a text input or an existing memory append target is a named pipe. This affects required `config.yaml`/`.env` reads, optional profile selection and the memory dedupe read before the existing safe append.

This continues the accepted nonblocking file-admission direction in #164161 (CLI configuration input). It addresses a separate migration owner; #172742 fixed malformed UTF-8 in Hermes memory, which does not prevent waiting for a FIFO writer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing public `security-runtime` regular-file reader for both required and optional text reads, including memory dedupe. Resolve source symlinks first to retain supported symlinks to ordinary files. The reader uses nonblocking open and descriptor/identity checks; the existing safe append still rejects a special-file destination. Required read failures include the original path and a recovery instruction. Optional unreadable selectors still return `undefined`.

Existing-solutions preflight: reuse `readRegularFile`/`appendRegularFile`, rather than adding a timeout, custom filesystem primitive, dependency or configuration. Directly checked fs-safe **0.26.8** implementation/types and the public SDK exports. Its default read has no new size cap; this patch retains strict UTF-8/BOM handling and changes no credential fields, protocol, schema, default or persistence owner.

Three files: production **+24/-5 (net +19)**, tests **+73**, docs **+6**. The added production code centralizes regular-file admission and path/recovery diagnostics for the two existing read policies. No generated files, lockfiles or proof assets.

## User Impact

Preview/import returns instead of hanging on a pipe or device. Required input failures name the file and tell the operator to use an ordinary readable file and retry. Optional unreadable selectors retain their existing behavior. Ordinary source files, their symlinks, exact Unicode text and memory import dedupe remain functional. Original source bytes and special-file nodes remain intact.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Hermes text intake and memory dedupe do not wait for FIFO writers; regular-file source symlinks, exact Unicode and repeat-import dedupe retain their behavior.
- Entry: actual compiled `node openclaw.mjs migrate hermes --dry-run --json --no-auth-credentials` and `node openclaw.mjs migrate apply hermes --json --yes --no-auth-credentials --no-backup --force --item memory:MEMORY.md`, using isolated synthetic home/config/state/workspace.
- Owner: `extensions/migrate-hermes/helpers.ts`; required/optional readers and `appendItem` dedupe ran unmocked through the shipped CLI entry.
- Same command on compiled base **e1f4e11918cda015da76ab57b29e59a7c5455d33** and exact final head **c336a0ed26e9b19d2a46c8b00b0a2107a9715caf**: `node ../hermes-file-proof-20261023.mjs`.
- Harness SHA256: **97f36399ee9f9ab68d233f8e51e7a2449a337508bdab1462bea3f6b86d195bd6**. Both runs assert `dist/build-info.json.commit` equals the checked-out commit. Node **24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**. Final run **2026-10-22 18:50 UTC**.

| Actual CLI case, no FIFO writer | Base | Final head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config.yaml` FIFO | blocked at 40.064s; stopped by harness | exit 1, 6.819s, path/recovery diagnostic |
| `.env` FIFO | blocked at 40.055s; stopped by harness | exit 1, 7.148s, path/recovery diagnostic |
| optional `active_profile` FIFO | blocked at 40.060s; stopped by harness | exit 0, 6.820s, existing unreadable-selector behavior |
| existing `MEMORY.md` append target FIFO | blocked at 40.060s; stopped by harness | exit 1, 7.184s, one memory item error |

The baseline backstop stops only the harness-owned process group. **Zero FIFO writers** run in either native proof. Independent `lstat` confirms all four FIFO nodes remain present. Source/config hashes remain unchanged on refusal. These timings include CLI startup, not just file reading.

### Captured output and independent readback

Required `.env` refusal, exit **1** (only the synthetic root replaced with `$PROOF`):

~~~json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Failed reading text file $PROOF/-env-fifo/hermes/.env: path must be a regular file. Use an ordinary readable file and retry migration."
  }
}
~~~

The memory target refusal reports item `memory:MEMORY.md`, status `error`, reason `Refusing to append to non-file: $PROOF/memory-target-fifo/workspace/MEMORY.md`; summary errors **1**, migrated **0**.

Positive control: rename the synthetic target FIFO aside, create an ordinary target with existing operator text, then rerun the same native apply command. Summary: **migrated 1, skipped 2, errors 0**. Independent disk readback is exactly:

~~~text
Existing operator memory


<!-- Imported from Hermes: MEMORY.md -->

Café project memory 会议 �
~~~

A fresh native CLI apply then reports that exact memory item **skipped: already imported from Hermes**, with **migrated 0, skipped 3, errors 0** overall (the other two config items were deliberately unselected). The independently read target remains SHA256 **166cd271f4cd114bae55d490b952ed7d635e3143eeebf266a67a0050678b9d6f**. Original Hermes memory bytes remain unchanged. A symlinked ordinary `config.yaml` also previews `openai/gpt-5.5` successfully on both versions, and valid literal U+FFFD/Unicode is preserved.

`--no-backup` is used only in the synthetic fixture; no real operator data or service is touched.

### Installed stable → exact-head upgrade (2026-10-23)

Provider **local-container**, id **leon-hermes-installed-upgrade-v2-20261023**, Node **24.22.1**, npm **11.19.0**. The official registry's latest stable was **2026.10.6**, build commit **fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc**. This run used that actually installed release, then installed the private runtime package built from **c336a0ed26e9b19d2a46c8b00b0a2107a9715caf** over the same prefix, with normal npm lifecycle handling. It reused the same isolated config/state/workspace and invoked fresh installed CLI processes before and after activation.

~~~sh
node /harness/probe.mjs /candidate/openclaw.tgz c336a0ed26e9b19d2a46c8b00b0a2107a9715caf
~~~

- **PASS**: stable CLI imported an ordinary Hermes memory source and a fresh stable CLI skipped its repeat. Candidate activation retained the exact existing memory bytes; a fresh candidate CLI also skipped that old import.
- **PASS**: `config get agents.defaults --json` returned identical model, workspace, concurrency, subagent and compaction settings across the upgrade. Config bytes remained SHA256 **8a3596c0ee1e7894047d6a0d9a753e1ca38f1a5f2b763c41791aa7d683b6d0ee** throughout; no doctor/config rewrite was needed.
- **PASS**: installed candidate preview accepted a regular-file config symlink. An `.env` FIFO with **zero writers** returned exit 1 with the regular-file/recovery diagnostic, preserving the pipe, config and existing memory.
- **PASS**: after moving only the synthetic pipe aside and creating an ordinary `.env`, candidate import appended the new Unicode source once. Independent disk readback retained the entire old memory prefix. A fresh CLI skipped the new import and left the resulting bytes unchanged.
- Existing-memory SHA256 before activation: **397d3a57a7b4c37361a5ae04d305d137eb47aeb750a5b9b4108d3a1382e7197a**. Final memory after one new import: **a6899a06075d45fbc9421844382616135048a0972655a62ced8bc2f3234d4188**. Both original Hermes source files remained byte-identical.
- Harness SHA256 **4c18d8e46bcebf0ffe6f84c3b688b9945723a4a99c3869282e4dc1e22bf68dfa**; package SHA256 **832a71f380730e3b016efceee1c1cf50e0c371f1ec2b4253731b412bef51a124**. Receipt `hermes-installed-upgrade-cYNe5Z/receipt.json` records install output and each actual CLI result. Build-info commit was checked after activation.

This is a private exact-head **runtime** upgrade proof, not SDK/release-package certification. The checkout's package version is 2026.10.5 while its build commit is the PR head; the stable package is 2026.10.6. The version string was not altered to conceal that difference. Config/state/workspace backups and a pristine stable prefix were retained inside the isolated proof root; rollback means restoring that test prefix and those synthetic backups. No production installation or channel was touched. An initial observer-only newline mismatch was corrected to match the existing `trimEnd` append contract, then this complete run started from a fresh stable copy.

### Focused verification and contract checks

~~~sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/migrate-hermes/files-and-skills.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/config.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/secrets.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build sourcePerformance
~~~

- Baseline file: **3 intended FIFO regression failures / 19 passes**, including the symlink/Unicode control. Unit-test backstop writers exist only to release a broken baseline test; the green tests assert they were never needed. Native proof above uses no writers.

prs.title: fix: Linux non-ASCII mount points are decoded as the wrong path
prs.body:
Related: #181101

This empty draft stays open. It will be closed only if it is still unresolved on 2026-11-06. It does not change OpenClaw.

## What Problem This Solves

The report claimed that Linux writes a non-ASCII mount point as octal escapes, and that `decodeMountInfoPath` then turns those escapes into a different path.

A live `/proc/self/mountinfo` read does not support that claim. Linux writes the UTF-8 bytes literally. It octal-escapes only space, tab, newline, and backslash. The current decoder restores those live fields to the original path.

## Why This Change Was Made

No decoder change is included. The kernel leaves non-ASCII bytes unchanged, and the current function already preserves them. Callers stay unchanged. No config, schema, or changelog change.

## User Impact

None. This draft does not change runtime behavior.

## Evidence

Head: `e9cacc64cbbbc05538589024545e0f393df94787` (empty claim commit; no source files changed).

Live producer read on `ubuntu-ai`, Linux `6.8.0-139-generic`, at 2026-10-23T00:24:50Z. Command: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=6 ubuntu-ai`, then inside `unshare --user --mount --map-root-user --propagation private`, `mount --bind` a temporary directory onto these mount points and read each mount-point field from `/proc/self/mountinfo`. The temporary directory was removed afterward. Exit code 0.

The host's existing mount table had no non-ASCII mount point, so this read used a private bind mount rather than a pre-existing system mount.

- `/tmp/oc-181101-mountinfo-proof/用户` was emitted as literal UTF-8 bytes `e7 94 a8 e6 88 b7`. The field contains no `\347`, `\224`, `\250`, or `\346` sequence.
- `space dir` was emitted as `space\040dir`.
- `back\slash` was emitted as `back\134slash`.
- `用户 data` was emitted as literal UTF-8 `用户` plus `\040` for the space. Field hex: `2f746d702f6f632d3138313130312d6d6f756e74696e666f2d70726f6f662fe794a8e688b75c30343064617461`.

Decoder check at the same head, Node `v26.7.0`: `decodeMountInfoPath` from `packages/normalization-core/src/mountinfo-path.ts` on those four captured fields. Each decoded string equaled the original path. The UTF-8-only field was already equal before decoding. Exit code 0.

No repair is warranted, so there is no after-fix output from a shipped flow.

prs.title: fix(agents): retry ready context-engine turns behind old admissions
prs.body:
Refs #135628 — repairs cross-session retry starvation; historical admission retirement remains outside this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Sixteen older unresolved session heads consume the bounded context-engine retry list. A later `ready` turn is not selected even when an independent session finishes successfully. Protecting the current accepted turn and disposing new admissions does not make the existing retry slots available to other ready sessions.

## User Impact

Ready context-engine commits can progress despite unresolved admissions in other sessions. Same-session FIFO, blocked audit evidence, engine/plugin isolation, idempotent commit, and current admissions remain intact. No historical cleanup, TTL, new queue, config/default, schema, protocol, dependency, provider-authentication, or permission change. This is a bounded part of #135628, not a claim to resolve its broader recovery request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identify each session's oldest non-blocked row **before** filtering for readiness and limiting the retry list. Keep ownership filters on both queries and apply the same invariant to the memory-store sibling. An unresolved head still blocks later work in its own session, without consuming another session's retry slot.

The canonical owners are the existing outbox kernel and memory session store; the finalizer/drainer continues to own commit, retry accounting and acknowledgment. Existing-solutions preflight: this is a missing invariant in the current queue owner; neither an external queue nor a new plugin/library is needed. Installed Kysely aggregate/subquery types and source, database schema and executor, callers and memory sibling were inspected.

October 18 maintenance normally merges `9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c`. The query now uses main's canonical explicit `enqueue_sequence` and typed `fn.min`; it does not restore deleted rowid helpers or alter schema. The accepted-turn regression uses main's consolidated fixture and places 16 unresolved rows ahead of the ready retry. The other stale type-check failure was in unrelated `memory-core` Worker/MessagePort test code; no contributor workaround was added there.

## Evidence

Current contributor head **`1c4293e5c87f389f7e1e634859c414465da67968`**, tree `0d1f835de572ef70426d49346ea3228277c57085`; clean checkout. Built OpenClaw **2026.10.4**, Linux, Node **24.16.0**. Build metadata records this exact head and `2026-10-18T03:08:46.938Z`.

The original acceptance RED was captured before production edits on `d4256984ac0435d8f5225e0d1706235b798f1e9e`: an independent successful CLI turn left the ready backlog behind 16 unresolved admissions. The October 18 exact-head GREEN replays the same immutable native harness after integrating main:

```text
node context-outbox-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new output directory> green
```

Three real `openclaw.mjs agent --local --agent main --session-key ... --message ... --thinking off --timeout 60 --json` processes use isolated state, a normally registered context-engine fixture and a loopback HTTP/SSE model endpoint. Every invocation returns the expected current answer and exits 0.

| Native scenario | Authoritative SQLite/engine-ledger readback |
| --- | --- |
| Warm control | 1 real engine commit; 0 outbox rows |
| A new turn's genuine engine commit fails once | 16 historical admitted rows + 1 ready row; recorded attempt count 1 |
| Independent successful turn triggers normal drain | 3 engine commits; ready row acknowledged; 16 historical rows retained byte-for-byte |

The recovered ledger contains the exact closed-turn user/assistant payload. **1/1 ready backlogs drain**, compared with **0/1** on historical RED. **16/16 historical admission hashes remain identical**. Fixture initialization represents reported persisted state; it does not claim to recreate the original crash. No external model account, channel recipient, production state or Mac environment is used.

GREEN completed `2026-10-18T03:16:14.687Z`; three CLI invocations took 30.60 / 31.45 / 29.58 seconds. Harness SHA-256 `c217e70233acdfc99d10341774048fc4c549f91ac5b5e62459673376dc261a3b`; current receipt SHA-256 `d5f2e9e303906f3fe41cbd2635a7a9f1e108542959c3c6f872b836f68cd04ac0`. Local logs/databases/receipts retained; the table supplies sanitized observations, without claiming a hosted artifact.

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox-selection.test.ts \
```

prs.title: fix(cron): native completion waits on its own session cleanup
prs.body:
Related: #180758

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes isolated Agents API cron runs waiting on their own active turn during continuation-session cleanup after native inference has completed.

## User Impact

Completed scheduled runs can finish cleanup and publish their outcome without cancelling their own turn or spending the native cleanup drain budget waiting for it. Existing pending-background-work safeguards remain in place. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact-run continuation was deleted inside the admitted cron turn. Native deletion waits for that turn's owner to settle, but the owner cannot settle until deletion returns. Defer deletion until admission has unwound, retaining the selected runtime through cleanup and releasing it afterwards through the existing resource stack.

## Evidence

- On pinned upstream `4f39309c731d181adbabe9db8043997d9866a299`, a regression through the actual cron runner and session-controller drain reproduces `aborted: true, drained: false`. [Baseline reproduction](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39826526178).
- The same service-level regression fails for both successful and failed provider outcomes on baseline, then passes with the repair. It reads the real CronService terminal event and persisted run history; provider execution and the native deletion entry are controlled fixtures, while the controller drain is real. [Before/after service proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39827416708). Test bodies took 2.42 s and 1.16 s; the focused test command took 65.10 s including transforms.
- The initial repair passed all 33 selected tests across cron session identity, continuation cleanup, and execution diagnostics. Its core and cron test type graphs and changed-file lint passed. [Owner validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39827512940). That run correctly remains failed because it caught a test import-order formatting issue, corrected afterwards.
- Final source uses the existing resource stack to express the same cleanup ordering without a separate mutable context/finalizer. Core types, cron test types, changed-file lint, and both formatter implementations pass on that source. [Final static validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39829524183).
- Independent complete-source Codex review found no actionable P0-P2 findings.

All 33 owner tests pass on the final resource-stack implementation. Its validation run also passes core types, cron test types and lint, and retains the same test-import format failure subsequently corrected by the final static run above. [Final owner validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39829056530). The subsequent test-only import reorder is formatting-only.

Remaining proof: shipped `cron add/run/runs` through an isolated Gateway and controlled TLS Agents API endpoint has not passed. The first environment attempt needed the existing Corepack cache carried into the private network namespace. A subsequent run reached the real SDK and Gateway, but the fixture held subscription headers until input arrived, deadlocking before the SDK could submit input; neither failure is presented as a product reproduction. The fixture now sends headers before input, and that HTTP handshake was independently checked. Repository Actions currently refuses dispatch with HTTP 422, `Actions has been disabled for this repository`, despite enabled repository permissions and an active workflow. The corrected [readable fixture](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/blob/proof/agentsapi-cron-cli-stream-20261023/.proof/agentsapi-cron-cli-proof.py) and manually dispatchable workflow are retained for resumption. No paid provider calls or live user state are used.

The baseline service regression proves self-drain; it does not independently reproduce the report's persistent empty-history symptom after the full 95-second wait. This PR stays draft until the missing product proof is resolved.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat downloads detailed tool-argument parsing and formatting before it can show a transcript, even when the first visible messages contain no tools.

## User Impact

The current integrated build transfers 12,013 fewer Chat gzip bytes (0.85%) with the same 24 critical requests. Startup shrinks by103 bytes; New Session changes by−15 bytes, within build variance. Tool rows preserve their existing layout while their detailed summary loads; import failures offer Reload without disabling the composer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the detailed tool-row renderer and standalone tool-message summary behind the existing `ChatImportBoundary`. The eager facade still owns plugin replacements, permissions, progress receipts, approvals, browser previews, and expanded-body selection. Shared chrome stays in a leaf module, so the lazy row does not import back into its facade. Fourteen expanded-tool English strings load with the existing output/expanded views.

The resolved label/icon identity is now a small shared leaf; full tool-display parsing no longer runs during every message's eager preparation. Ten modules leave the chat boot graph: `tool-call-view`, `tool-call-patch`, `tool-display`, `tool-display-common`, `tool-display-exec`, `tool-display-exec-shell`, `chat-command-highlight` (component and helper), `chat-diff-stat`, and `dedupe-by-key`. Three lightweight leaves enter: `chat-tool-card-chrome`, `tool-display-identity`, and `tool-display-name`. The original top-30 and full feature attribution is recorded in #180852; module-level gzip is diagnostic and non-additive.

## Evidence

Current integrated comparison: baseline source `87a94c4b4236ccaded2cd75790032122037d5a66`, integrated source `18fce985d1c926824cd163c325c081ddce8fbd79` (merges current main `cba956feca63b163119f81a704c1f99f84077344`). The intervening main commit changes no UI inputs. Both builds use identical explicit build identity, timestamp, and prepared native plugin distributions; all four previously missing native packages were copied from the baseline before the candidate build. The fixed build stamp is intentionally shared for comparison and is not source provenance. Full module attribution is retained for both bundles.

| Surface | Base JS gzip | Head JS gzip | Change | Critical requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,274 B | 316,171 B | −103 B | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,415,894 B | 1,403,881 B | −12,013 B | 24 → 24 |
| New Session | 916,192 B | 916,177 B | −15 B (variance) | 18 → 18 |

Strict performance comparison passed with no violations. The Chat cap is ratcheted from main's1,469,628 to1,457,159 B (`floor(1469628*1403881/1415894)`, the same relative headroom). The earlier canonical `--update-baseline --reason` startup reduction to315,881 B is retained; the integrated fixed-stamp measurement does not raise that budget. Main's tighter New Session929,032 B and request caps are retained. The cap-only follow-up changes no bundle input. Cold HTTP-cache reloads used the same exact base/head bundles, an untraced production preview, and the committed comparison driver `66ac6866a2d` (SHA-256 `cc7ad23fdfdd76451c59a0e5dd3a5b31bd34f7afe820b7956e8fcc95ce19d991`). Observed Testbox hardware was 4 usable CPUs and 16.6 GB RAM. [Owned Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39865212801).

| Transcript visible | 607.50 ms | 595.00 ms | −2.06% | 884.50 ms | 852.40 ms | −3.63% |
| Composer enabled | 606.10 ms | 593.55 ms | −2.07% | 882.80 ms | 851.00 ms | −3.60% |

Current integrated validation passes UI typecheck and the strict byte comparison; production Knip has the same nine findings as the matched base, as detailed below. | Chat / Sharing and annotations | 20,973 / 0 | **mixed** — Persisted annotations/reactions may appear initially; export/share dialogs, new comments and selection popups are interaction-only. | Keep visible annotation data and placement, defer mutation/dialog entry bodies. Preserve selected range and focus while loading. |
| Shared domain / Text and session normalization | 20,922 / 19,517 | **first-paint** — Visible-text filtering, reasoning/tool-markup stripping and canonical session references define the transcript shown on reload. | Keep current filters on the first visible transcript. Any narrower parser change requires behavior proof across imported/provider transcript forms, not timing-based omission. |
| Shared domain / Chat normalization and commands | 20,219 / 13,008 | **mixed** — Imported transcript normalization and sender/content interpretation are first-paint. Slash command lookup and some editing helpers are interaction-dependent. | Preserve byte/visibility semantics of old transcripts. Split editing command help/suggestions at input use, keeping command admission available before send. |
| Chat / Model and permission controls | 19,799 / 14,586 | **mixed** — Selected model, effort, permission labels and enabled state are first-composer data. Search results, picker options and provider-review bodies follow interaction. | Model picker bodies and provider-review are lazy. Preserve selected labels, focus and permissions while assessing any remaining option-building leaf. |
| App / Platform, updates and background integrations | 18,247 / 18,015 | **mixed/background** — Connection/auth recovery and native listeners may be prerequisites for a usable first render; explicit push subscription, update details and some platform actions occur later. Both routes retain this shared owner. | Recovery dialog, update-run report and some native operations already load dynamically. Inspect still-eager action implementations individually, preserving listeners and authority/recovery state rather than delaying the whole platform owner. |
| Claw and Workboard | 18,207 / 3,971 | **mixed** — A normal conversation does not need board widget/render actions. Persisted board face or a selected board route can need them immediately. | Keep selected surface detection and lightweight state; load board presentation/actions only when that surface is chosen, including restored state. |
| Shared domain / Config | 17,156 / 17,156 | **mixed** — The runtime config capability is created at bootstrap and supplies accepted values/reload protection. Editor drafts, schema operations and write coordination are not ordinary text transcript rendering. | Potential owner-level split: retain accepted snapshot/subscription and reload protection, lazily acquire editor/write implementation when requested. This is more invasive than a leaf-view split and must preserve pending writes. |
| Gateway / Client transport | 16,635 / 14,757 | **first-paint** — WebSocket connection, pending request correlation, retries and session projection are required for first transcript and ongoing streaming. | Keep. No optional whole-transport deferral. |
| Chat / Voice and realtime | 16,497 / 10,885 | **interaction** — Voice/dictation capture and device selection are unnecessary for an ordinary text draft; status and stop/cleanup may be needed for an already active capture. Both composers retain dictation support. | The full talk session is already imported on activation. Remaining dictation/audio helpers must be separated behind the existing capture owner, preserving permission feedback, active-capture status, and cleanup; this is not a claim that the full realtime stack is eager. |
| Other routes / Lazy route entry stubs and shared helpers | 16,351 / 16,351 | **first-paint** — Route descriptors and matching must know all destinations. Their emitted presence does not imply page bodies are loaded. | Do not count this as eager page code. The inspected Config route explicitly imports its page dynamically; only genuinely heavy helper imports behind route descriptors merit splitting. |
| Chat / Tool cards and streaming | 16,267 / 0 | **content-type** — A visible tool message needs its collapsed card and current streaming status. Ordinary text does not. No tool-card renderer is required by the empty New Session composer. | Detailed tool body rendering is already lazy. The small eager tool-content wrapper remains for loading and expansion; do not count the removed detailed body again. |
| App / Gateway connection and authority | 15,082 / 15,082 | **first-paint** — Connection snapshots, auth scope, selected gateway and live authority are required for correct initial rendering and actions. | Keep lightweight connection/authority owner. Optional method or surface adapters may be isolated without delaying authority publication. |
| App / Settings and preferences | 14,902 / 14,902 | **first-paint** — Restored layout, theme, locale and per-session choices determine the first render. Mutation/reconciliation is also used outside settings pages. | Keep canonical accepted settings. Separate rare editing UI or migrations only with an explicit owner contract; do not introduce a second settings reader. |
| Icons / SVG data and presentation | 14,769 / 13,475 | **mixed** — Icons on visible controls are required, but a combined name-indexed registry includes tool/provider/brand paths unrelated to a plain transcript. | Split icon data only at stable feature boundaries and migrate every dynamic consumer; a catch-all fallback or common registry import can retain all data. |
| Shared domain / Agent and capability catalogs | 13,991 / 13,991 | **mixed** — Current agent identity and advertised capabilities may be first-paint. Full channel/configuration catalogs need not be presented immediately. | Keep current selection and capability receipt; acquire browse/configure-only operations on their UI boundary. |
| Shared domain / Session presentation | 13,772 / 9,113 | **content-type** — Progress cards, pull requests, presence and display summaries can be visible in sidebar or transcript, depending on session data. | Keep cheap summary projection; separate fetching/detail interaction implementation from initial summary display where ownership already distinguishes them. |
| App / Theme and environment presentation | 13,066 / 12,864 | **first-paint** — Theme, typography and shell branding must be ready before first paint; delaying them creates visual and geometry changes. | Keep initial theme. Optional artwork/favicon updates may be scheduled later through the same owner without delaying initial colors or fonts. |
| Chat / Sidebar and split layout | 12,856 / 2,870 | **mixed** — Restored split placement and mobile shell affect transcript geometry immediately. Closed side-panel bodies are conditional. | Keep layout facts/size ownership; existing lazy sidebar bodies should remain lazy. Do not move geometry restoration after transcript paint. |
| App / Overlay and action owners | 12,648 / 12,648 | **mixed** — Pending approvals or questions can be present on reload; update and confirmation bodies are conditional. Current owners hold live authority. | Keep state/authority/admission and lightweight visible pending status; lazy leaf dialog contents only. |
| Boot / Entrypoints and generated glue | 12,282 / 12,282 | **first-paint** — Main entry, route paths, navigation and build identity are needed to locate and mount the selected UI. | Keep route contracts; avoid importing page bodies into this graph. Small route metadata is not a useful standalone lazy target. |
| Vendor / DOM sanitization | 11,547 / 0 | **content-type** — Sanitization is required before inserting generated Markdown/HTML from the transcript. | Do not bypass or delay sanitization after insertion. It may follow a content-specific renderer only if the renderer itself is safely deferred. |
| Shared domain / Tool presentation | 11,218 / 6,571 | **content-type** — Exec titles, tool-call repairs and argument formatting are needed only for tool-bearing visible messages, though message normalization may invoke shared parts. | Split exec/browser/diff details at the tool-kind renderer; leave minimal collapsed summaries available. A shared tool module still referenced by normalization will remain in boot. |
| Chat / Questions and goals | 10,643 / 0 | **content-type** — A pending interactive question or restored goal can appear with the first visible messages; inactive editing UI is optional. | Keep pending-question/goal receipt and send semantics; split inactive editor and history detail views if a measured leaf dependency remains. |

prs.title: fix: prevent duplicate optional-question answers across viewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate optional-question answer popups and submissions when several viewers share a conversation, including when the first answer is queued.

## User Impact

The first accepted answer is shared across panes and reloads as **Answer queued** or **Answer sent**. A stale second submit does not send another message. Normal typed corrections remain ordinary messages. Explicitly withdrawing a queued answer makes the question answerable again; interrupted custody does not release it. There are no new configuration options or database migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the canonical question reference with the existing input and enforce uniqueness through its authoritative actor state before queued or direct custody. Incognito public staging applies the same guard at its storage-command effect. Shared presentation derives from accepted inputs, and confirmed withdrawal releases the submitting pane’s retained hint even when cancellation redacts the message. There is no separate question registry. The follow-up simplifies the SQL guard and consolidates repeated fixtures and scenarios.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original duplicate popup, retained-pane withdrawal, and previously missed public incognito staging path before fixing them. Two consolidated shared-state Chromium scenarios plus 15 existing scenarios passed: **17 total**, covering mounted viewers, confirmed queue removal, stale-submit reconciliation, outbox retirement, reload, and canonical confirmation.
- **65 focused backend/storage tests across five files passed.** Public durable/incognito active/idle cases race two answers, retry the actual winner, reject same or contradictory stale submits, distinguish cancellation from interruption, and preserve invalid-source rejection, ordinary corrections, and new same-worded questions. Existing authorization/replacement and memory-owner consumers passed.
- Reused real data produced by published `openclaw@2026.10.6` at commit `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`. On the simplified kernel, an isolated copy again passed existing Doctor migration **schema 25→31**, cold SQLite reopening, legacy queued/saved duplicate rejection, explicit withdrawal, interrupted retention, and original transcript/message integrity. This is a storage compatibility rehearsal, **not** a full service install-over.
- Wrapper extraction/materialized-context checks passed **2 tests**. The worker inventory check and SQLite ratchet passed at **170→170**, compatibility **15→15**, without raising baselines. Affected production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, controller guards, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent **P0–P2** review and originating-session review found no actionable issues.
- Browser proof uses the actual compiled Control UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures; two browser contexts simulate viewers. No live Codex/model execution or actual signed-in multi-profile browser run is claimed. Existing before/after images remain representative; this simplification changes no production rendering.

**Before**

![Duplicate optional-question popup alongside an accepted queued answer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e26922d-4435-42ed-a887-8d4839a637fc)

**After**

![Shared queued answer shown without a duplicate optional-question popup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9152c36-ff12-496f-94ee-bf50c8288d1e)

Thanks to @shakkernerd for reporting the issue and guiding the fix.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @shakkernerd](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4e09645f-1d37-4a76-91fe-3d140524daca)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/dc4426e5-85e5-4470-84a8-68011ac84720)

## Worked on by

- @shakkernerd

prs.title: fix(config): report write-safety refusals during dry runs
prs.body:
Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.
- Conflict-resolved candidate: original seven-file shard, all 87 tests passed; the named test took 12.338 s. Config CLI and writer suites passed 202 tests (34 integration, 65 CLI, 103 writer), 67.86 s combined runner wall time; integration file 27.12 s Vitest wall time.

The original CI timeout remains unattributed. These passing replays are not presented as a timeout fix; no retry logic, longer deadlines, weakened assertions, or speculative production changes were added. The subsequent CI run [38082056748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082056748) passed all 86 jobs on `64e6949e85a3`; this is prior-head evidence.

Final local validation on `64e6949e85a3`: types, targeted lint, formatting, and all remaining selected guards pass. The aggregate check stops at 17 Knip findings; the same canonical scan on a separately installed, clean `0c94b6966078` worktree reproduces the identical set (15 authentication/runtime exports, one Solid lint export, one UI test-helper export). They are inherited rather than introduced by this PR.



### Review guidance and async conflict follow-up

Commit `3687439fae0` reuses `createConfigWriteSafetyRejectionError` for actionable recovery guidance in both JSON and text previews, retaining the size-drop reason. The existing registered-command case failed before the message repair and now verifies both output formats and unchanged config/files. No new test fixture or production abstraction was added.

Integrated main `c6d71fae0ed` to resolve the writer conflict from #168481: topology preparation is now asynchronous, so the preview and writer await it and the shared payload type consumes its resolved value.

Validation: 202 tests passed across config CLI integration (34), CLI (65), and writer (103); 101.20 s runner wall time. Integration-file Vitest wall time: 46.38 s. No hosted CI timing for this new head yet.

Final local checks: production types, all core-test type groups, scoped lint, formatting, and the selected ratchets passed. The aggregate changed check stops at four Knip unused exports outside the PR diff: `stripClaudeCliGeneratedUserPrefixes`, `createChannelApprovalHandlerAsync`, `GitHubConnectionsContent`, and `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files match the integrated base; no clean-base Knip replay was run for this head. These findings remain recorded, not suppressed.



### Conflict refresh (2026-10-11)

Integrated main `0ff0202128f` for the new writer conflict. Preserved upstream's agent-deletion authority check before publication and awaited metadata recording. Applied upstream's payload cleanup in the extracted shared preparation function; audit metadata remains computed by the writer. No new behavior, tests, or dependencies were introduced by this conflict repair. The prior head `3687439fae09` had a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109291576); that remains prior-head evidence.

Conflict-resolved head `963d92c985b`: 137 tests passed (34 CLI integration, 103 config writer), 121.12 s runner wall time; CLI integration 61.12 s and writer 42.78 s Vitest wall time. Core types, scoped lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. New-head CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(qa): image generation checks reject valid completion replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native image-generation QA rejects a successfully delivered image and its separate completion reply. The mock misses current completion carriers, and the scenario compares persisted completion text with the earlier image-only caption.

## User Impact

This repairs private QA; production image-generation behavior is unchanged. The check retains exactly one PNG with exact saved bytes and one successful generation, then correlates the public task receipt with a distinct persisted completion run and exactly one matching text delivery after the image.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mock reads current user and protected runtime context and respects confirmed host delivery without replaying media. The scenario uses the canonical text reader through the existing flow API; public history intentionally omits private tool-result details, so task correlation reads the public background-task receipt.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original native failure and preserved its chronology: the distinct completion had persisted and delivered before the failing caption comparison.
- Canonical queued/V4 producer regressions are red on base and green with the mock repair; the public-history fixture with details omitted is independently red before the task-receipt repair and green afterward. Negative controls reject acknowledgement-only, wrong-run and mismatched completions, duplicate media, and failed turns.
- Final source head `1650db820d1fd93b366ea0426aa909c806cfa327`: 38 affected image/flow/runtime tests, targeted types, type-aware lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P2 review pass. The existing mock/server and core public-facade proof is retained with unchanged inputs. Parsed comparison confirms all six authored image assertions and eight budget bindings are unchanged by the final owner simplification.
- The final image scenario passes against unmodified native upstream source `be1ffced8df6a2d8affbc5569fce1b877f703ec1` on Node 26.12.1, with fresh synthetic state/providers and its original deadlines. Native source/build/entry/Node identities remain unchanged before and after; all 113 observed owned processes settled.
- Inherited CI remains red: final head [QA4/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39875681647/job/120161247451) and newest completed [scheduled main QA4/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39872214487/job/120149514603) fail the same `memory-dreaming-sweep` assertion after 90 seconds: embedding fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for captured `errors-DlnpgPcN.mjs` imported by `manager-search.worker`. Full artifacts match the concrete signature; failing scenario/staging/capture inputs have identical Git blobs. The 67-job PR attempt has 38 successes and 27 skips; only QA4 and its downstream CI aggregate fail, and `security-fast` passes. This image repair does not fix the separate worker-closure defect; its original acquisition path remains a distinct investigation. No current-head CI green result is claimed.
- Additional diagnostic limits remain: the prior `7c42` capture failure is retained. One installed memory check stopped in Doctor after 120 seconds without phase progress, before memory behavior ran; retained temp-root cleanup also reported `ENOTEMPTY`. It supplies no native memory product verdict. Full local all-graph checking still stops on unchanged base shard budgets (725 gateway / 730 infra roots, all already in base); no threshold or exemption changed.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer emoji catalogs until composer or reaction intent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session load the full emoji shortcode catalog before the first transcript or composer needs it. New Session also retains MarkdownIt and its entity tables through the old shared boot grouping after the emoji consumer becomes lazy.

## User Impact

Chat boot transfers 16,667 fewer gzip bytes; New Session transfers 56,593 fewer bytes. Each removes one critical JavaScript request. Quick reactions remain immediately available. Shortcode suggestions load on shortcode-shaped input, and complete reaction search loads when **More…** opens.

A complete shortcode typed before its first catalog load stays literal, with no retroactive edit; the next eligible edit uses the loaded resolver. Native typing, Tab, Enter, and undo remain with the browser while optional data is pending; the loader never replays input. Once ready, closing-colon conversion works synchronously. Restored focused drafts discover suggestions, and late loads read only the current connected, focused draft and caret.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer uses the existing optional-import owner for its synchronous editing library; the reaction panel uses Solid `lazy` with local loading/error UI and usable Back/Retry controls. Explicit chunk ownership prevents stale boot captures from keeping these now-deferred modules eager. MarkdownIt and its actual vendor closure (`entities`, `linkify-it`, `mdurl`, `punycode.js`, `uc.micro`) join the existing `markdown-runtime` chunk at priority 20. The retained consumers are transcript parsing, lazy emoji input/search, command-palette snippets and the Meetings page; none needs MarkdownIt for the first empty New Session composer.

New Session's final module attribution contains **zero MarkdownIt, entities, or Markdown parser modules**, and its preload graph contains no Markdown asset. Chat keeps its first-paint Markdown parser. No schema, dependency, shared state owner, or new chunk abstraction is added. The original top-30 module attribution and first-paint assessment is in #180852; the detailed tool-row cut is #181052. This focused PR does not claim the full campaign target.

## Evidence

Source base: `2c5b726de0e978c4c05ec5fc06dcce422f3ef21b` (landed #181052). Both production builds used Node 26.12.1 on the same Mac, the same fixed version/build metadata, and byte-identical 29 prepared plugin inputs (SHA256 map `f65321679903ed6c67e33f5ff7c2cd1de84191549466f909fbefc71a9c1aade4`). Integration used a normal merge of `origin/main`. Current head: `d7b29411baf`.

| Surface | Base JS gzip | Head JS gzip | Change | Critical JS requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,173 B | 316,105 B | −68 B | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 1,403,921 B | 1,387,254 B | −16,667 B (−1.19%) | 24 → 23 |
| New Session | 916,218 B | 859,625 B | −56,593 B (−6.18%) | 18 → 17 |
| Largest ordinary chunk | 208,159 B | 208,182 B | +23 B (within 64 B build variance) | — |

Strict `ui:check-performance --base-dist` passes after ratcheting. Route caps preserve the base's relative headroom: Chat 1,457,159 → 1,439,860 B; New Session 929,032 → 871,648 B. Request caps retain two requests' headroom: 26 → 25 and 20 → 19. Startup CSS stays one request. The existing startup baseline is already tighter than this build; it is preserved, rather than raised through `--update-baseline`.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Passed after final chunk closure change |
| Composer/reaction tests | 42 passed across three directly changed files; repaired composer disposal covered |
| Chunk boundary fixture | 6/6 passed, including MarkdownIt/entity lazy import closure |
| Cold/warm editing | Delayed catalog preserves native keys/text, reads current caret, ignores blur/detach, discovers restored Chat and New Session drafts |
| Visual proof | Inspected synthetic before/after at 1280×900; loaded layout preserved; cold More Back control verified |
| Controller census | Zero effects, untrack, direct listeners/queries, cleanup hooks or owner APIs added; one Solid lazy boundary |
| Production Knip | Passed on final head (`pnpm deadcode:knip`) |
| Independent review | Complete final diff: scoped-clean at P0–P2 |
| Full exact-head CI | [39876918333](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39876918333) passed on `d7b29411baf0db9a7af86809c4f7ba191ae31070` |
| Reload timing | Passed: 20 alternating cold-cache runs (10 pairs), transcript and composer median/p95 improved |

Timing acceptance was fixed before running: committed `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`, cold HTTP cache, 20 alternating runs (10 pairs), same Testbox; transcript-visible and composer-enabled medians no more than +5%, p95 no worse. The exact-head run passed both limits:

| Timing metric | Base median | Head median | Base p95 | Head p95 |

prs.title: fix(codex): unblock parents after native follow-up completion
prs.body:
Related: #172837. Follow-up to #175246.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent requests being refused with `Codex thread <id> is claimed by active work; stop it first.` after a native follow-up finishes while its result is still awaiting acknowledgement.

## User Impact

A parent can cold-resume to receive a completed follow-up result. Active child execution stays protected, and pending results and persisted submission receipts remain available until their normal acknowledgement.

## Why This Change Was Made

#175246 releases the monitor-owned parent pin after all children finish. A follow-up accepted and admitted while its foreground parent is still registered also holds a separate submission-owned pin. That pin survived until result acknowledgement, keeping the same refusal alive.

Release that redundant execution retention only after successful monitor admission. The monitor retains active execution; completion custody and receipt settlement keep their existing owners. No dependency, schema, retry-policy or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Baseline: `b8f91cb249b8c702cfc02befd6d2fb11215928f3`. Both new cases fail at the actual `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread` guard after the follow-up ends; the other 20 tests in the custody file pass. The cases cover predecessor acknowledgement before and after successor admission.
- Fixed: 87 distinct tests pass across seven lifecycle/receipt suites, including parent retention, release retry, completion contention, submission storage and `sessions_yield` follow-up custody. The changed custody file passes all 22 tests; its standalone command took 9.11 s wall time (7.48 s Vitest duration, approximately 70 ms test execution).
- Real Codex 0.162.1 stdio protocol replay: a synthetic Responses backend drives actual native spawn and `send_input`. On the baseline, terminal execution plus pending delivery retains one extra parent/client/child hold and the guard rejects. With this fix, active execution still rejects release; after completion, the guard allows unsubscribe and actual `thread/resume` succeeds while the receipt remains in the fixture binding store. Acknowledgement then consumes the receipt once. This is a real app-server/production-owner protocol proof with a controlled provider and delivery callback, not a live-model Gateway reproduction.
- Independent lifecycle source assessment and `autoreview` completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Isolated real Gateway + authenticated V1-capable model + Codex 0.162.1: the same native child completes A, accepts and completes `send_input` B, and the next ordinary user request succeeds (`LIVE_A_OK`, `LIVE_B_OK`, `LIVE_NEXT_OK`). Native persisted output contains the accepted submission ID matching B's completed turn. This is a healthy live-flow smoke; the pending-acknowledgement interval is tested separately by the controlled protocol replay above.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39301606325) passed on `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`; required `openclaw/ci-gate` reports that CI and applicable security review requirements passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, targeted type-aware Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

This PR fixes the separate submission-owned execution pin. Durable retirement after retry exhaustion or blocked recovery is already handled by merged #173018. These are distinct fixes related to #172837; this PR does not change delivery retry or abandonment policy.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, environment, commands and scope</summary>

### Reproduction

1. Complete native child turn A, then accept and persist a `send_input` receipt for B while the foreground parent is still registered.
2. Start/admit B before unregistering that parent. Check that cold resume is refused while B executes.
3. Complete B while result delivery remains pending or returns undelivered. Call `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread` for the parent. Baseline: the claimed-by-active-work error remains. Fixed: unsubscribe/cold resume is allowed and the submission receipt is unchanged.
4. Acknowledge delivery: the receipt is consumed once. The parameterized regression runs with A acknowledgement before and after B admission, and checks parent protection inside every release callback.

Apply the regression-test change to the base without the production change to reproduce the two failures. Run the same command on this PR for the passing result.

### Environment

OpenClaw and bundled Codex plugin source at the base/head SHAs above; Codex app-server 0.162.1; macOS arm64; Node 24.19.0; pnpm 12.12.1; repository-pinned Bun; Vitest 5.0.3. Synthetic thread/result fixtures for regression and protocol replay; fresh isolated Gateway state and a supported authenticated V1-capable model for the live smoke.

### Commands

```sh
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.release-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-completion-delivery.contention.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-followup-custody.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-owner.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts
pnpm format:check -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-owner.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts
git diff --check
```

macOS arm64; Node 24.19.0; pnpm 12.12.1; repository-pinned Bun; Vitest 5.0.3. PR CI supplies broad coverage; the successful CI run took 681 s elapsed including setup, parallel checks and gate publication (not per-file execution time).

Live-proof accounting: the initial observer counted only `function_call_output`, so it incorrectly reported no submission receipt when the real model used CodeMode's `custom_tool_call_output`. The original failure is retained; independent native-rollout and Gateway-terminal readback verified the matching submission/child turn and all three visible replies without rerunning the successful workload. Earlier V2/model-unavailable attempts are not counted as V1 proof. The separate GitHub Codex review integration failed without publishing findings; local independent review completed.

`pr-simplify`: existing lifecycle owners suffice; no new owner or production seam. Production delta +3/-2 (one release plus ownership comment); tests +84/-36, reusing the existing submission binding-store fixture. Tests keep the actual client identity, explicitly retire pending delivery custody during cleanup, and inspect protection at release callbacks during the active handoff.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inspectable redacted execution capture: real Codex pending-ack replay and live Gateway</summary>

These are excerpts from captured execution output, not expected-value examples. Only relevant fields are shown. Synthetic UUIDs are consistently aliased as `P` (parent), `C` (child), `A`/`B` (child turns), and `P_B` (parent follow-up turn); local paths/endpoints are omitted. No production data or credentials were used in this replay.

Runtime: `codex-cli 0.162.1`, real stdio app-server and native spawn/`send_input`; synthetic Responses output and a deliberately held completion-delivery callback. The guard calls below are the production `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread`. This replay is distinct from the live-model Gateway smoke at the end. Receipt writes/consumption use the production binding mutation API with its existing in-memory test-store backend; this replay does not prove disk durability or restart recovery. Native app-server execution, completion notifications, unsubscribe/resume, and the separately captured native rollout files are real.

### Baseline — `b8f91cb249b8c702cfc02befd6d2fb11215928f3`

```jsonl
{"at":1792432690644,"event":"receipt-record","receipt":{"parentTurnId":"P_B","callId":"SEND_B","childThreadId":"C","submissionId":"B","predecessorRunId":"codex-thread:C","predecessorNativeTurnId":"A"}}
{"at":1792432690681,"event":"active","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":2,"parent":2,"child":1},"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."},"receiptCount":1}
{"method":"turn/completed","params":{"threadId":"C","turn":{"id":"B","status":"completed","items":[{"type":"agentMessage","text":"B_RESULT"}]}}}
{"at":1792432690687,"event":"delivery-pending","params":{"childSessionId":"C","childSessionKey":"codex-thread:C:turn:B","result":"B_RESULT"}}
{"at":1792432690886,"event":"terminal-pending-ack","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":1},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."}}
{"event":"result","pending":{"claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":1},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."}},"ack":{"receiptCount":0,"deliveryCount":1,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0}},"outcome":"RED"}
```

Captured `receipt-consume` calls after releasing the acknowledgement gate: **1**.

### Fixed source — later committed unchanged as `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`

Submission-owner SHA-256: `69fea86a827910ecb12536e52b77e73a79b69b8e5454130f558a6936738acd9d` (matches the committed file).

```jsonl
{"at":1792433382642,"event":"receipt-record","receipt":{"parentTurnId":"P_B","callId":"SEND_B","childThreadId":"C","submissionId":"B","predecessorRunId":"codex-thread:C","predecessorNativeTurnId":"A"}}
{"at":1792433382672,"event":"active","claimed":false,"protected":true,"holds":{"client":1,"parent":1,"child":0},"guard":{"error":"Error: Codex thread P is claimed by active work; stop it first."},"receiptCount":1}
{"method":"turn/completed","params":{"threadId":"C","turn":{"id":"B","status":"completed","items":[{"type":"agentMessage","text":"B_RESULT"}]}}}
{"at":1792433382677,"event":"delivery-pending","params":{"childSessionId":"C","childSessionKey":"codex-thread:C:turn:B","result":"B_RESULT"}}
{"at":1792433382882,"event":"terminal-pending-ack","claimed":false,"protected":false,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"released":true}}
{"event":"result","pending":{"claimed":false,"protected":false,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0},"receiptCount":1,"guard":{"released":true},"coldResume":{"threadId":"P","status":{"type":"idle"}}},"ack":{"receiptCount":0,"deliveryCount":1,"holds":{"client":0,"parent":0,"child":0}},"outcome":"GREEN"}
```

Captured `receipt-consume` calls: **1**. In the fixed run, the `coldResume` fields are the actual awaited `thread/resume` response, obtained **before** releasing the acknowledgement gate.

### Isolated live Gateway — committed head `1cb15871a7f99b0f7af6346f2a04581344dd1928`

Real authenticated V1-capable model, real Codex 0.162.1 and fresh isolated Gateway state. No delivery fault injection in this healthy-flow smoke. The following fields were read back from actual Gateway terminal receipts, native lifecycle notifications and the persisted native rollout:
