prs.title: fix(codex): unblock replies after interrupted native children
prs.body:
Related: #172837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new replies being rejected with “Codex thread is claimed by active work; stop it first” after an interrupted native worker is restored, even though that worker is no longer running.

## User Impact

Users can continue the conversation without restarting the Gateway or deleting saved worker assignments. Interrupted work remains resumable, and genuinely running work stays protected. No configuration, permission, or storage migration is required.

This fixes the stale ownership left after interruption; it does not prevent upstream connection outages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor already distinguishes interrupted, resumable children from active execution, but parent subscription retention treated both as running. Release the parent pin when all children are terminal or interrupted, and reacquire it when execution resumes—including model admission before a delayed `turn/started` notification.

The existing cold-resume guard, assignment persistence, cancellation selection, and completion delivery remain in place. This complements the terminal-child fix in #175246; it does not duplicate the promoted-submission custody change proposed in #177577.

## Evidence

- The three new regression cases fail on the base with the real cold-resume ownership error and pass with the fix. They cover restored interrupted assignments, preservation of saved work, and resumed inference followed by either completion or interruption.
- **97 focused tests passed** across the parent-retention, direct-authority, custody, cancellation, monitor, completion-delivery, and release-retry suites (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`).
- Production and test typechecks passed: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review identified a timing-dependent pre-Stop assertion; the running-work assertion now happens before interruption, and the affected tests were rerun.
- **Exact-candidate live validation passed on October 22:** restored interrupted work survives same-parent cold resume, resumed native work remains protected, and the guard clears after completion. Redacted terminal proof and the procedure are below.
- Exact-head CI remains green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review. The head SHA is unchanged.


<details>
<summary>Exact-candidate live proof — October 22, 2026</summary>

**Candidate:** `30e7861a765f8cbf71fe5b96723499c4c2971b1b`. `pnpm build` exited 0; `dist/build-info.json` identifies this commit (built at `2026-10-22T05:19:25.410Z`). No production source edits were made for this proof.

**Setup:** A real built Gateway, native Codex CLI 0.162.1/app-server, and authenticated model calls, in temporary state/workspace/Codex home on a free loopback port. No fake native transport, mocked model, edited assignment rows, or disabled ownership guard. The installed production Gateway and Discord channels were not restarted or modified.

A one-off, uncommitted live driver composed the existing `createCodexHarnessLiveInstance`, Gateway client, native history reader, and `createExternalGates` helpers. It ran with the supported live-test wrapper:

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$ISOLATED_AUTH_SOURCE" OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  pnpm test:live --codex-harness -- src/gateway/pr179099-proof.live.test.ts
```

The scratch driver is not a new permanent test target. The reproducible scenario was:

1. Through the public `agent` RPC, have the native parent spawn one child executing a shell request held by a test-owned HTTP gate. Wait for actual execution, then use native `interrupt_agent`—not close or Gateway Stop.
2. Read the saved assignment and interrupted native turn; stop/restart only the fixture Gateway with the same state. Send two ordinary replies and assert the complete saved assignment is unchanged.
3. **Exercise the actual cold-resume boundary, not just warm replies:** send another ordinary reply with a new benign `extraSystemPrompt`: “Synthetic continuity proof: preserve this conversation and its existing worker.” This changes the immutable developer-instruction fingerprint, causing warm reuse to fall through to same-thread cold resume and `releaseRetainedThread`. Require `RESTORED_COLD_REPLY_OK`, the **original native parent ID**, and exact equality of the full saved assignment. Keep that prompt unchanged for the next step.
4. Resume the **same child** with `followup_task`, holding a new native shell request at another gate. Require a new native turn ID, Gateway execution state `running`, and one outstanding gate request. Assert the parent did not execute that request.
5. Change `extraSystemPrompt` again to exercise the same cold-resume boundary while the child is running. Require the real “claimed by active work; stop it first” error, unchanged assignments, and continued running execution/held I/O.
6. Release the child's I/O gate and wait for its persisted native turn to complete. Repeat a reply with the same previously blocked prompt configuration; require `RELEASE_AFTER_COMPLETION_OK`.

Live running state comes from Gateway execution events plus held native I/O—not from a separate app-server's `thread/read` status. Native history reads establish persisted turn identity and completion.

**Result:** 1 live test passed; command exit 0. Selected terminal output below; synthetic IDs are consistently aliased, and paths/endpoints/credentials are omitted:

```text
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"candidate-restarted-same-state","details":{}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"agent-response","details":{"runId":"<request-id>","status":"ok","text":"RESTORED_REPLY_ONE"}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"agent-response","details":{"runId":"<request-id>","status":"ok","text":"RESTORED_REPLY_TWO"}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"assignment-preserved-after-two-restored-replies","details":{"childId":"<child-A>","assignmentsUnchanged":true}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"agent-response","details":{"runId":"<request-id>","status":"ok","text":"RESTORED_COLD_REPLY_OK"}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"same-parent-cold-resume-after-restoration","details":{"parentId":"<parent-A>","assignmentsUnchanged":true,"extraSystemPromptChanged":true}}
PR179099_PROOF {"step":"agent-response","details":{"runId":"<request-id>","status":"ok","text":"CHILD_RESUMED"}}
```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mobile session headers spend scarce width on a workspace eyebrow, avatar strip, and a separate panel button, truncating the session title.

## User Impact

A compact 48px single-row header gives the title more room. Tap the title for the full name and Details; open the overflow menu for Panels, People, or the session Dashboard. Desktop controls, public/incognito indicators, and offline notices remain available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep session identity primary on small screens without introducing another tab row or another panel owner. A single retained native menu and the mobile host preserve navigation, keyboard focus while session metadata arrives or connectivity changes, and mounted panel state. The retired header-only people grid and styles are removed (net-negative production code).

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a7c1302f-5ec3-495f-bb01-22d05d24d2c9)

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced on the base: header was 54px; new 48px assertion failed before the fix.
- 16 browser tests pass: 320px phone, 390px phone, 760px tablet, 852px landscape, desktop, light/dark, offline/reconnect, full-title Details, menu-to-Files navigation, and retained panels across viewport changes.
- 50 original affected component tests pass, including People navigation/lookup retention. The follow-up adds a deterministic trigger-identity/focus regression (red before, green after); both affected component suites pass 44/44.
- CI caught remaining E2E consumers of the retired header buttons. Those now navigate through the real overflow menu. All 94 selected browser scenarios are verified across 11 affected files (93 in the full run, then the remaining Dashboard-label correction in a targeted rerun).
- Production UI build, UI typecheck, all UI test typecheck shards, scoped lint (zero errors; two pre-existing Solid warnings), CSS lint, and formatting pass. Independent reviews are clean after fixing offline navigation and retaining menu identity; local navigation remains available while remote session commands are hidden. Follow-up scoped lint has zero warnings/errors.
- Screenshot fixtures are synthetic; no private session content.

### Before

![Before: workspace eyebrow and extra controls truncate the session title](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3937a13a-06da-4a41-b5e2-fd27e06f17cf)

### After

![After: compact one-row mobile session header with more title room](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fec54c8e-d8b6-4e99-bba1-d7c504c0f912)
### Current-main integration

Resolved the mobile-header contract conflict against `c64eaf54ad0b6`, retaining required presentation inputs and the compact layout. After integration: 44 component tests, 23 browser scenarios (mobile header/sharing/native navigation), UI typecheck and all eight UI-test typecheck shards passed. Scoped lint/format and fresh independent review passed.

Final browser-consumer audit found one obsolete Panels readiness wait in the Details/progress test. It reproduced on the production UI; removing the redundant wait leaves the native Details helper responsible for readiness. Both Details/progress scenarios pass, with all layout, focus, draft and scrolling assertions retained. No production change from the independently reviewed conflict resolution.

prs.title: feat(agents): preserve stores during controlled Gateway handoff
prs.body:
Related: #178748

## What Problem This Solves

An agent's identity and history should survive a change in where it runs. An operator may start an agent on a shared Gateway, then move it to a dedicated Gateway for capacity or isolation. Today there is no supported per-agent removal operation for that handoff: `agents.delete({ agentId, deleteFiles: false })` still requests session-store purging. Keeping files does not preserve sessions.

With PostgreSQL, the durable agent data can already stay in the same database. The missing operation releases the source Gateway's use of that store without deleting its contents.

## User Impact

An administrator can:

1. Stop routing new work to the source and wait for `agents.detach({ agentId })` to succeed.
2. Transfer the closed original anchor and required workspace files, keeping the agent ID and PostgreSQL namespace.
3. Use existing `agents.create` on the destination, verify retained identity/history, restore destination settings, then switch routing.

This enables planned capacity changes and maintenance without resetting the agent's history or copying its PostgreSQL rows. The prototype moved shared → dedicated → shared carrying an 8 KiB anchor; workspace files remain a separate transfer responsibility. This is a new operator capability, with no claim of a current outage or regression.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing `agents.delete` would weaken its cleanup contract. Editing the roster or copying an anchor alone bypasses admission closure, draining and restart recovery. Detach makes retention explicit while reusing those lifecycle owners.

The implementation records durable detach intent, drains work, closes database owners and retains the store/files. Recovery and destructive retries cannot convert a pending detach into deletion; offline CLI deletion refuses a pending detach.

Core supplies the local lifecycle primitive; a controller or plugin orchestrates placement and routing. There is no database schema-version change, new adoption RPC or distributed ownership manager. Three unchanged session-policy constants move out of the method table to meet the repository's file limit.

## Scope and Compatibility

This is administrator-controlled sequential handoff. The controller owns exclusive assignment, routing, database permissions and file transfer. Source tombstones refuse ordinary writes after restart, but cannot prevent explicit source recreation or duplicate adoption.

Detach removes Gateway-local bindings, execution approvals and provenance; restore required destination settings explicitly. It retains cron jobs and, where the downstream scheduler-custody prerequisite is installed, their migration hold. The detached agent cannot execute them. Octogee's downstream `cron.migration` owner exports/stages jobs, retires source jobs after cutover, or resumes them after source adoption on rollback. That scheduler owner is absent from this upstream source; the held-handoff regression therefore has an unshipped prerequisite and is not ready, as detailed below. Existing restrictions on the sole configured agent and shared/inherited credential owners remain. Local shared state and anchors can remain SQLite.

The new journal phases are a compatibility commitment: older binaries reject retained detach journals, including completed records. Keep a compatible runtime while those records remain.

## Evidence

Current head: `5038c65b0dce7a55270e0100fa13f09a89e12cf5`.

- A downstream held-scheduler handoff reproduced `Agent roster committed, but cron cleanup did not complete` because cron pruning rejected the migration hold after roster removal. An unheld detach also erased cron rows. The follow-up retains cron state during detach and leaves ordinary delete's transactional pruning intact.
- The identical follow-up on common base `122c7e65` passed the real Gateway RPC regression for both held and unheld jobs plus the pending-destructive-deletion refusal: **3/3** cases. It verifies denied cron execution before/after source restart, job and history retention, same-ID adoption, held mutation refusal until explicit resume, post-adoption writes and ordinary delete pruning. Core types, targeted lint, formatting and a fresh independent P0/P1 review passed. Review was static; tests ran separately. These proofs do not claim a final-head deployed PostgreSQL handoff or broad upstream CI.

- Recorded local validation: 74 distinct focused tests covering journal persistence/fencing, detach/restart/adopt, destructive-retry refusal, authority/discovery, offline deletion, deletion recovery and published-stable phase-less journal upgrades.
- The added public-RPC integration test retains session ID/transcript, refuses source writes before and after restart, keeps a neighbor usable and permits re-adoption and another write. It uses one local state directory.
- An isolated PostgreSQL 16 prototype experiment used separate Gateway processes and retained store UUID, namespace, session ID, transcripts, synthetic credentials and keyword memory through a round trip. Interrupted detach completed safely after lease expiry. This ran on the prototype base, not the exact PR head; no live inference or active-active ownership was exercised.
- Recorded lint, core typecheck, protocol/schema and native-contract checks, formatting, documentation checks and CLI startup build passed after the final mechanical extraction. Isolated autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Required PR CI remains a landing gate.

## Maintainer Decision and Remaining Proof

**Decision requested:** should OpenClaw support `agents.detach` through the existing lifecycle owner, including durable retention intent and older-binary refusal? If an SDK lifecycle hook is preferred, guidance on that interface would help settle the implementation direction.

The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178755#issuecomment-6301090114) requests:

- [ ] Redacted, inspectable exact-head proof: two independent Gateways/state directories, retained PostgreSQL identity/history, source refusal after restart and interrupted-detach recovery.
- [ ] Administrator success, `operator.write`-only rejection before mutation, and replaced deletion-lease rejection before configuration/database effects.
- [ ] Upgrade proof from v2026.10.5 preserving settings, sessions and deletion-journal behavior; older phase-less fixtures alone do not cover this.
- [ ] Maintainer acceptance of the API and retention contract, plus security approval for the final head.

Prototype results establish feasibility; these remaining items are not claimed satisfied by the local test count.

## Offline CLI follow-up and current qualification

The separately published [offline detach candidate](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/compare/524d54b44d5a2f297e1ec6c93e4a7b7551b07159...3315652339ddffb060e59f861294aa5efd501251) adds `openclaw agents detach <id> --force --json` through the existing exclusive local-state owner and preserve-store coordinator. It refuses a running Gateway, missing journals and pending destructive deletion; it does not fabricate recovery history. This is a narrow offline adapter, not a whole-Gateway migration: detach removes roster entries, bindings and execution approvals.

At downstream pin `524d54b44d5a`, Node 24.22.1 qualification passed the real executable/Gateway SQLite round trip and a mixed SQLite-global/PostgreSQL-agent round trip. The PostgreSQL case retained the original store UUID/namespace, full history, immutable job definition and migration hold across detach, reattachment and restart, with live-owner and detached-write/scheduler refusal. It passed in 95.104 seconds within its unchanged 120-second budget; fixture cleanup was verified. Five CLI process cases, 21 policy/registration cases, core types, targeted lint/format and a strict-smoke build also passed. The wider PostgreSQL harness separately failed `42501` on `SET LOCAL track_functions='all'`; it is not claimed green.

Independent review for this narrow follow-up was unavailable because of network access and was explicitly waived by the operator. No independent review is claimed. The normal commit content/format checks passed; docs tooling could not prepare its cache on the host, so the documented targeted-validation local commit path was used after equivalent cached markdownlint validation passed.

The narrow CLI adapter was integrated at `66051efff294d7457d0828b4f88878c5a45abcc2`, followed by fixture-only isolation repair `5038c65b0dce7a55270e0100fa13f09a89e12cf5`. Both are fast-forwards from the previous PR head. Its default PostgreSQL conformance inventory includes the new mixed-backend integration target; the inventory regression failed before that wiring and all eight catalog cases passed afterward. Core typecheck, targeted source/script/test lint, ten-file formatting, docs lint and diff checks passed. A canonical process-fixture helper is included because the older PR head predates that refactor. No unrelated source history or dependency changes were imported.

Full frozen local dependency reconciliation remains blocked by uncached packages/network access (latest missing snapshot: `baileys@7.0.0-rc14`). Matching cached tools provide the limited source/catalog results above, not a complete frozen-install or final-head live behavioral claim. The first [fork dispatch](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/actions/runs/39875446247) failed preflight because the selected main validation tier is restricted to the canonical upstream repository. A corrected [full fork dispatch](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/actions/runs/39875661291) passed preflight and security-fast, but expanded into unrelated native-app and release-proof lanes. Its remaining queued allocation was cancelled after the local exact-head run established the prerequisite failures below. No broad CI pass is claimed. This PR remains draft and retains its preexisting conflict with upstream main. These results do not close the broader maintainer/security, two-independent-Gateway, replaced-lease or stable-upgrade requirements above. Maintainer edits are enabled.



### Exact submitted-head behavioral result

The normal Node 24.22.1 runner on submitted adapter head `66051efff` reached real Gateway startup, then failed before invoking the new offline adapter: the held SQLite case returned `unknown method: cron.migration`; the subsequent mixed-backend case still selected SQLite. Relevant installed tools/modules match this head's lock, but the full frozen graph remains unresolved as noted above.

Source inspection separates two issues. The process-wide database engine selection survived sequential fixtures. Fixture-only repair `5038c65b0` uses the existing completed-fixture reset owner and explicitly asserts the selected backend, without relaxing hold or backend assertions. The identical repair on downstream pin candidate `3315652339d` passed the normal Node 24.22.1 runner with both offline cases consecutively in one process: SQLite 36.918 seconds and mixed SQLite-global/PostgreSQL-agent 81.882 seconds, total shard 158.13 seconds. The PostgreSQL case retained exact UUID/namespace, complete history, immutable job and migration hold; live-owner refusal, detached write/scheduler refusal, reattachment/restart, subsequent write and destructive-delete control all passed. Its exact synthetic namespace was cleaned up in 522 ms. This establishes the fixture repair on the qualified downstream runtime, not a new upstream-head behavioral pass. Separately, the previous PR head already called `cron.migration` in its held test, but has no production handler for it. An exact-SHA GitHub contents lookup for that handler on upstream main `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd` returned 404; full current-main catalog inspection was unavailable, so a complete refreshed upstream analysis is not claimed. It exists in the downstream Octogee scheduler overlay `266170e1aa8`; that is an unshipped prerequisite, not a missing method registration to paper over. The complete overlay is not being imported into this PR. Hold assertions remain intact, and no submitted-head behavioral pass or readiness is claimed.

The prerequisite extraction inventory separates 25 scheduler/RPC/fencing production paths from seven legacy Doctor bridge paths. Runtime custody uses retained plugin-state KV and adds no runtime table/schema-version bump, but introduces a public scheduler custody and durable retention contract. It needs separate acceptance and proof; the narrow CLI review waiver does not cover it. Related #178768 supplies offline configuration-import effects and explicitly refuses held-store restoration; it does not supply this scheduler state machine. No whole-overlay import, fake method registration or relaxed hold assertion was applied.

prs.title: fix: keep onboarding pending after starter template updates
prs.body:
Closes #149768

## What Problem This Solves

An untouched profile created by an earlier release can be mistaken for a user edit after bundled templates change. Running setup then completes pending onboarding, removes BOOTSTRAP.md, and drops the original starter-file receipts before the user has finished the identity conversation.

## Solution and User Impact

Use the workspace's existing generated-file hashes as well as current and retired bundled-template recognition. Preserve a historical hash only while the file still matches it. A real edit continues to complete onboarding; workspaces without recorded hashes retain existing detection rules. No schema, migration, state version, configuration, or plugin-SDK surface changes.

The contributor's fix is integrated with current workspace preparation and typed state guards. The existing preparation owner passes its already-read attestation to the hash collector; no parallel writer or extra state read was added. The retired survival-test file stays deleted, and its three historical-profile cases now use the canonical workspace suite and shared fixtures. Production +44/-15; tests +29/-0; docs +2/-0.

## Evidence

Fresh Linux Docker proof uses Node 24.22.1 and installed built CLI packages, with independent profiles created by published `openclaw@2026.9.2` (`3928bad`). Main source: `ee174d73efbcbe51d705b484c53d799877721a39`. Candidate source: `3e235c6dc9ec767c698d92ae23bc85fa3e74dd7b`.

Each arm runs the released `setup --baseline --workspace ...`, the current shipped `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migration, then two separate current `setup --baseline --workspace ...` processes. Setup and Doctor create all application state. The observer only reads SQLite and hashes files.

- Main reproduced twice independently: Doctor preserves pending onboarding, but the first current setup removes BOOTSTRAP.md and writes `setup_completed_at`. All three profile bytes remain untouched, yet all three historical receipts disappear. The second setup remains incorrectly complete.
- Candidate repeated the same upgrade twice independently: both setup processes retain BOOTSTRAP.md, the original seed timestamp, pending state, unchanged profile bytes, and all three historical hashes.
- Fresh main/candidate controls both remain pending through two setup processes.
- An ordinary `agents.files.set` Gateway RPC edits USER.md in the upgraded candidate. The next setup completes onboarding and removes BOOTSTRAP.md; a second setup stays complete.
- Released-CLI skip-bootstrap workspaces start with no generated-hash rows. A USER.md edit through the shipped Gateway RPC still completes setup on both main and candidate; the second setup stays complete. This preserves no-receipt fallback behavior.
- The three profile regressions fail on main with `bootstrapPending: false` instead of true. Candidate workspace and setup suites pass: 53 + 14 tests. Targeted formatting and lint pass.

Captured commands, output, and read-only observations follow below. Paths, profile names, and Gateway tokens are synthetic. No model conversation or package replacement via `openclaw update` is claimed.

prs.title: fix(automations): limit webhook-triggered turns to their own automation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: webhook (`/hooks/agent`) turns get the full automations tool instead of the current-job scope scheduled runs get, although both run through the same automation runner.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent turn started by an inbound webhook or a channel join introduction now gets the same automations tool scope as a scheduled run. Within that turn it can only inspect or remove its own run, not list or change other automations. Scheduled runs and ordinary conversation turns are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is consistency and defense-in-depth hardening. The Gateway already limits agent-runtime callers to automations their own session can see. Before this change, a hook turn's request for another automation passed the tool and was rejected only by the Gateway. The current-job scope was derived only from the `cron` trigger, so turns with trigger `event` that the cron runner starts were left out. They now share it. The condition still requires a job id, so other `event` turns that don't come from the cron runner stay as they were.

Channel join introductions already run with an empty tool allowlist. This change keeps that behavior and adds a test for it.

## Evidence

- **Crabbox real behavior proof (direct AWS, lease `cbx_a903c769bf38`, clean `--fresh-pr` checkout at `048267bca94`):** see the proof comment below, which includes the redacted run output.
  - The QA scenario `hook-turn-automations-scope` runs a real Gateway child and sends an HTTP `POST /hooks/agent` to it, with mock-openai inference. It passes on the PR head:
    - The hook turn's `remove` of a sibling automation is rejected by the tool scope (`Automations tool is restricted to the current automation.`) before any Gateway call.
    - The allowed control, `list` with `includeDisabled: true`, succeeds and doesn't expose the sibling.
    - The sibling is still in `cron.list` afterward.
  - Negative control: the same scenario with only `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` reverted to `main` **fails**. The sibling `remove` gets past the tool and reaches the Gateway, which rejects it as `cron job not found`.
- **Closed-run authority:** hook jobs are built in memory and never stored, so no stored current job exists that a leftover claim could remove after the run. The scope is applied when each attempt constructs its tools. Gateway `cron.remove` keeps its existing live-run check (`bindCronSelfRemovalCommitGuard`), which this PR doesn't change.
- **Unit tests:** a new cron-runner suite drives a hook-shaped job, and the results match scheduled runs. Event-triggered sibling `remove` is rejected, and the turn gets the self-scoped schema (no `add`). The test doesn't pin the exact self action list, which `cron-tool-schema.ts` owns and which grew on `main` (`scratch_get`, `scratch_set`, `record_result`). Join introductions still get no automations tool. 3/3 and 13/13 pass on Crabbox. I removed the mocked option-forwarding construction asserts, since ClawSweeper flagged them as low-value.
- **CI attribution:** `checks-node-changed-10` (`gateway-mcp-app-grant-revalidation.e2e.test.ts`) and `checks-node-changed-18` (`gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts`) fail the same way on the merge base `50dfbacf1ab`, which doesn't include this PR. Neither failure comes from this PR.
- **Regression QA (mock-openai):**
  - `cron-send-then-continue` and `cron-blocked-outcome` pass.
  - `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` fails the same way on unmodified `main`.
  - `cron-explicit-authority-execution` needs the live-frontier lane and wasn't run.
- **Refresh onto `main` `8021f987ed4` (head `ca10df7c2c4`, includes #178043):** rebased cleanly. Locally the unit suite passes 3/3, and reverting only `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` makes the hook-turn case fail. `gateway-mcp-app-grant-revalidation.e2e.test.ts` and `gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts` now pass 10/10, and the `hook-turn-automations-scope` QA scenario passes.

prs.title: fix(doctor): reuse verified captures across healthy repair runs
prs.body:
Refs #173564 #174253
Related: #173564, #174253

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated standalone `doctor --fix` runs on healthy, unchanged state retained another full original-state capture each time. Avoiding a copy was not enough: Doctor itself dirtied schema metadata and plugin lease/index pages, and WAL-mode source headers differ from the retained single-file images.

This PR is scoped to **reuse a verified capture when state is unchanged**. Deferring the first capture until the first actual mutation is a separate follow-up below. The existing eager pre-repair safety boundary stays intact.

## User Impact

Three consecutive healthy standalone repair runs now retain **one** original capture. A real config, database, filesystem, or declared-resource change still requires a fresh capture. No equivalence checks are replaced with timestamps or logical-row comparisons.

Update-associated originals, Docker activation markers, retention, pending-recovery protection, full-integrity capture semantics, and free-space checks remain intact. No live deployment or release is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Verify the newest eligible sealed standalone original, every retained payload, and the complete rediscovered config/includes, database owners, plugin declarations, files, directories, missing paths, symlinks, permissions and SHA-256 content.
- Use the existing fresh-capture database owner for discovery and canonical SQLite images rather than a parallel discovery path. WAL-mode normalization changes header bytes even without data changes; compare **complete canonical-image digests**, preserving source fingerprints across preparation, not masked headers or selected rows. Nonempty WAL/journal data still refuses reuse.
- Keep healthy schema version/header metadata idempotent. Full repair still runs and performs real recognized repairs.
- Plan plugin registry and configured-install repair against fresh read-only metadata before acquiring a durable lease. Empty work must not insert/delete lease rows: deleted-cell bytes alone break exact reuse. Actual work is replanned under the original lease and effect guards. Bundled-record planning is shared with the existing repair owner rather than duplicated.

Reuse still streams retained payloads and prepares temporary SQLite images, then removes those images. This avoids additional **retained** full originals, not all I/O or temporary space. Incomplete or unprovable comparison, PostgreSQL, and unknown plugin coverage fall back to fresh capture. Verification limits are cache misses, never update failure policy.

## Evidence

Candidate: `9b02f8104463aadcd118319736787e6d8ec3bbfc`; merge base `a39dd6d4968891599257cca778d2530ceba5d037`. No relevant owner drift or merge conflict required a rebase at preparation.

- **Permanent real-Doctor regression, red then green:** after first-install initialization, run actual `doctorCommand(..., {repair:true, nonInteractive:true})` three times with real maintenance, repair, snapshot, comparison and retention. Prior published `0bb1d49b` produced capture counts **1, 2, 3** and changed SQLite bytes each run. The final implementation produces **1, 1, 1**, with the entire healthy shared SQLite file byte-identical after every run. A subsequent real config change produces a second capture and preserves the first. No repair or capture owner is mocked; only installation-root selection is redirected to a disposable fixture. Private HOME/config/state/TMPDIR and external service-repair policy are enforced.
- Repeat suite: **1 test passed, 52.763s test time / 55.68s wall time**. It intentionally performs six real Doctor invocations (two first-install preparation runs, three healthy runs, one changed run). A helper-only test missed the original incident, so this composition is retained despite its cost.
- Capture suite: **9 tests passed, 68.28s wall time** including compiler preparation. Covers exact inventory/content, retained seals, WAL/journal refusal, 257 MiB payloads, verification-bound fallback, successful 65 MiB WAL-mode reuse, and cancellation/settled cleanup during selection, discovery, and canonical-image preparation.
- **Production-identical `f40c9526` aggregate: 250 tests passed across 14 files, 179.65s wall time** (89 unit, 123 infra, 38 commands). Includes all affected schema/snapshot suites, missing-plugin repair, registry, original capture, rehearsal capture, retention, repeat-Doctor and reuse tests. One earlier registry-test failure was inherited `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=odin` leaking into expected CLI wording; rerunning with that profile unset passed, without changing production or test expectations.
- Core, commands-test and infra-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint: **0 warnings/errors**. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation audit: **15,831 links, 0 broken**.
- Full-file audit of both touched/new test suites completed. Tests assert observable captures, exact bytes, preserved originals and settled work; no source-text mirrors or fake repair results.
- **Final-head CI repair proof:** `f40c9526` CI found a fixture lifetime bug: per-case cleanup removed a cached native broker's Unix socket. Reproduced locally with a short private TMPDIR (same two initial-capture failures), then joined retained readers and the broker before fixture removal. The complete capture suite and complete migration suite pass in order: **70 tests, 2 files, 111.10s wall time**. The second CI failure was a pre-existing hardcoded migration-preview inventory omitting v30/v31; the test now asserts its specific audit migration and first completed schema receipt while preserving exact event/owner/version data checks. Full 3,126-line test audit also removed an optional-call non-test and strengthened seeded ingress and no-refusal assertions. No test cases or production guards were skipped.
- **Published-stable compatibility:** installed npm `openclaw@2026.10.6` (published CLI commit `fe06181`, registry SHA-512 `jSpQPa2Jw5rG0J2GC07j9+qHtVYIuoHjgccU88JeS+p7188sBCnvIJeuaiNPHj1zsWkuHcBv443QiEUh7qrxwA==`) into task-private dependencies. Its real CLI initialized schema **20** and original captures. Three candidate Doctor owner invocations upgraded to schema **31**, passed SQLite quick-check, preserved gateway port/auth settings, an existing user file, a persisted sentinel row, and every digest of the newest stable original's manifest/payloads. **1 proof passed, 60.34s wall time.** This is published-stable data through the real candidate Doctor owner, not live deployment or package-publication proof. The source CLI bootstrap's artifact-publication guard could not inspect the task profile's LaunchAgent; that separate CLI bootstrap was left unrun rather than bypassing the guard or touching a live service. The migration proof redirects only install-root selection to disposable fixtures, as the permanent repeat test does.
- Source simplification removed the reuse-specific database discovery branch in favor of the existing backup owner and shared bundled-record planning between inspection and repair. No schema, persistent cache or retention policy added.
- Test-only dependency layout: local physical pnpm graph with the shared package store, required by the compiler's checkout-containment check. No guards bypassed. Private handoff-store resolution was asserted before Doctor execution; no live Odin state or lifecycle operations.

### Independent review and CI

Earlier API-only reviews found two large-database cancellation defects; both were repaired. This head additionally removes parallel discovery, and proves canonical-image work cancellation and successful large reuse. **Fresh API-only review of production head `f40c9526` found no substantiated P0–P2 findings.** ClawSweeper subsequently identified the CI fixture lifetime defect and requested published-stable compatibility evidence; both are addressed above. Fresh final-head API-only review of `9b02f8104463aadcd118319736787e6d8ec3bbfc` found **no substantiated P0–P2 findings** after all 12 diffs and all three touched test files. It confirmed the broker fix joins the actual retained owner and the migration assertions preserve behavior. ClawSweeper’s exact-head re-review also reports **no findings / Before merge: None**. Required exact-head CI is **green**: [run 39874891637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39874891637), **69 successful jobs, 27 intentionally unselected/skipped**; `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review and security-sensitive review are all successful. The skipped jobs are not claimed as passed. No merge is requested from this task; stop at ready-to-merge.

## Follow-up: capture at first mutation

Prior isolated production-path probes established why empty repair reports are not safe admission to defer capture:

- Current shared schema v31 can return `needsOpenClawStateDatabaseSchemaRepair(..., "doctor") === false` and `{changes: [], warnings: []}`, while full Doctor repair updates `schema_meta.updated_at`. With a recognized retired `database_verifications` table, the same signals occur while that table is actually dropped.
- A real on-disk channel plugin with only `doctor.runConfigSequence` returns no config-repair preview, yet its first sequence call repairs a file and its second is genuinely a no-op. That callback has no complete planning contract.

This PR fixes recurring healthy schema/index bookkeeping and needless plugin leases. It does not skip full schema repair based on version detectors or empty reports: actual retired-table removal, opaque plugin callbacks, and post-scope service changes remain reasons to retain eager capture.

prs.title: fix(msteams): streamed reply is sent again when Teams rejects the formatted final
prs.body:
Closes #158103

## What Problem This Solves

Teams personal chats in progress streaming mode can reject a formatted final because it replaces Markdown that Teams already accepted. A late acknowledgement can then be ignored, leaving the entire answer eligible for duplicate fallback delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render the progress final before its first emission and reuse the existing `queueFinalReplacement` owner. The stream update and close now use the same rendered activity, while acknowledgements retain the logical Markdown for fallback accounting. Partial mode is unchanged.

This incorporates @rdbartram's root-cause repair and preserves Ryan Bartram as its commit author. The October 23 refresh adapts the three files to current main without restoring removed defensive branches or superseded tests. The earlier event-wait maintenance is retained in the adapted transport regression.

## User Impact

Progress-mode replies avoid the raw-to-rendered prefix violation. Existing cancellation, media, presentation-card settlement, and later reply payloads retain their current behavior. Table rendering follows the existing Teams formatter; this does not introduce a new table format or change partial-mode mentions.

## Evidence

Candidate: `ee8371eaf544330bfb2821d0161955c6b4fe5d5d`. Base: `471bdafdfdb0e0666c595334e2523b9a4b6cb50a`.

- **Discriminating baseline:** on the unchanged base controller with the adapted regressions, both new cases fail. The real Teams `HttpStream` / HTTP loopback receives `[201, 201, 403, 403]`; the delayed original-text acknowledgement leaves `visibleReplySent: false` and the full `# Status` fallback. The transport case now waits for the first actual streamed-answer acknowledgement before finalizing, rather than merely waiting for an informative progress acknowledgement. This makes the failure deterministic with the current SDK batching behavior.
- **Candidate behavior:** the two complete controller files pass, 19 unit cases and 16 SDK/HTTP cases. The actual caller's `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` passes all 26 cases, including cancellation, cards, multiple progress finals, joined close/fallback, and later payload ordering.
- **Static verification:** Teams package production types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent P0–P2 autoreview is `scoped-clean`; no actionable findings remain.
- **Test cost:** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` measured 32.41 s command wall / 27.90 s Vitest duration for the unit file and 11.95 s command wall / 9.52 s Vitest duration for the SDK file. The latter includes 16 real SDK/HTTP lifecycle cases; its 4.607 s summed case time exercises batching and acknowledgements without adding a timer or polling wait. On this exact head, CI summed controller case times are 0.138 s (19 unit cases) and 5.180 s (16 SDK/HTTP cases). The [extension CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39874972449/job/120158748604) passed 4 files / 64 tests; these summed case times are distinct from isolated command wall time and shard setup/transform time. The complete [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39874972449) passed. The PR rollup has 34 passing checks, zero failed or pending checks, 58 skipped checks, and one canceled auto-response automation check.

Reproduction command on the base controller with the adapted tests:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/reply-stream-controller.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/reply-stream-controller.sdk.test.ts -t 'progress final acknowledgement|progress table reply'
```

Observed baseline output (exit 1):

```text
expected [ 201, 201, 403, 403 ] to not include 403
Tests  2 failed | 33 skipped (35)
```

**Remaining live acceptance:** the affected tenant verified the reporter's earlier progress-mode patch ([result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158103#issuecomment-5898840580)), but has not yet confirmed this exact refreshed candidate. The HTTP loopback is a simulated provider and does not establish live tenant acceptance. Before merge, obtain that result or an explicit maintainer decision accepting the remaining provider uncertainty.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved chat and agent updates remaining stranded after a crash-loop quarantine clears and their interrupted predecessor resumes.

## User Impact

Accepted inputs resume in order after the existing boot owner clears quarantine. Shutdown or another restart cancels the wait without replaying or discarding those inputs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup replay previously finished when predecessor recovery was temporarily paused. The later predecessor recovery did not restart saved-input replay.

Keep the existing replay owner waiting on the boot owner's quarantine deadline, with the existing shutdown and restart signals. This preserves predecessor ordering and current requester-authority checks without adding a scheduler, persistent state, configuration, or another recovery owner.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent review of the complete integrated five-file delta and relevant lifecycle contracts: no actionable findings.

prs.title: improve(ui): offer native video capture in Android composers
prs.body:
Part of #180298. ## What Problem This Solves The composer’s native Camera path only requests photos, and a delayed native return can begin attaching to a replacement draft. ## User Impact On the existing recognized Android browser route, Chat and New Session offer **Record video** alongside **Take photo**. A returned clip becomes a draft attachment and is sent only after an explicit send. Cancelled, detached, and replaced-draft camera returns are rejected. **This is a draft proposal for review, not accepted picker policy or authorization to merge.** Desktop photo preview/capture/retake, other iOS photo routes, Safari’s combined **Attach…** picker, image-only restrictions, upload safeguards, and unrestricted File selection remain unchanged. No custom recorder or microphone request is added by OpenClaw. Native browser/OS recording and permissions remain platform-owned. ## Why This Change Was Made A dedicated single-video capture input reuses the existing native-browser policy and attachment admission, preparation, preview and send owners. Explicit photo/video labels avoid implying that every platform has a video recorder. The native-return guard binds selection to the opening draft before asynchronous attachment reading starts. This is independent of the existing-media proposal #180723 and menu-heading proposal #180579. Their shared-file integration may need reconciliation when choosing landing order; neither is incorporated here. Files separation, broader iOS capture policy, and a desktop recorder remain outside this contribution. Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**. AI-assisted implementation. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfd1f162-7d1d-4dc0-a7e0-0a65c7817bd8) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/074b4e8e-6f15-40c7-9a31-e18ac3ab0f85) ## Evidence - **Published/tested-source head:** `f36269109b8dbe32def219b35afd7828b5b5eb05`, published by `roboclaw-bot`. All nine published files match the tested/reviewed source byte-for-byte; all three PR commits, including the managed base integrations, have the required TheAngryPit co-author trailer. - Prepared official-main base: `a6c561f954c41209124f7add70a13c59e883eda3`. Tested/reviewed candidate tree: `74ade09e50c17aaa58bc9968aeb76e4985ac10cb`; nine source/test/documentation files. - **25 focused unit cases passed** across native return, input ownership and existing photo capture. The two principal regressions fail on the exact prepared base: missing video action and native photo admission into a replacement draft. The corrected connected fixture was used for that base-red proof. - **27 production-browser scenarios passed across the initial run and focused correction.** Existing 25-case platform suite passed (Chat/New Session, native photo return, preview/retake, denied/unavailable preview, picker geometry, keyboard, Safari and embedded-host exclusions). The two new cases verify pointer/keyboard gesture admission, native video return, cancellation/reselection, no browser preview request, and exact attachment bytes at explicit `chat.send`/`sessions.create`. These run the actual built Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses, not a separate mock UI or live provider delivery. - Initial new-video browser attempt failed its test-only gesture probe: desktop Chromium does not expose the `input.capture` property used by the probe. Reading the actual capture attribute fixed the probe; no assertion was dropped, timeout raised, retry added or product safeguard weakened. Both cases then passed. Early unit-fixture connection/disposal mistakes and an unsupported icon choice were corrected before the final passing checks. - UI types, affected Chat and browser-test typecheck leaves, scoped typed lint, stylesheet lint, controller ratchets, i18n baseline/verification, format, changed-document MDX and whitespace checks passed. Production builds passed as part of browser verification. - Fresh independent Auto Review: **scoped-clean through P0–P3**, no actionable findings; OpenClaw engine, effective model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. It reviewed the complete base-relative candidate and supplied owners, did not independently rerun tests, and is not product acceptance. - Test cost: final focused unit run 1.14 s total; new browser file 7.888 s test time (two flows), combined video/capture run 44.71 s including setup. Initial 27-case run took 144.92 s with the two probe failures described above. Hosted draft checks: 7 passed and 70 skipped/neutral on this head at verification; the broad CI gate and UI lanes are skipped while draft. These are not passing full-suite results. - Simplification: no new state store, recorder, policy owner or effect/listener ratchet allowance. Net production growth is 49 lines for the explicit input and opening-draft guard; regression coverage adds 248 lines net. Temporary capture code and generated media are excluded. ### Actual Before / After Inspected screenshots from the actual built Control UI: identical 390 × 844 light-theme synthetic Chat content, with an emulated Android Chrome identity. Before restores the exact prepared-base production modules; candidate bytes were restored and hash-verified afterward. No private conversation or photo-library content is used.
Before — prepared baseAfter — Camera proposal
New Session — returned synthetic video, dark theme ![A synthetic camera clip staged in the actual New Session composer before explicit send](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac2c7d4b-cef6-44f1-a991-8cc645b76909) 1024 × 800 viewport. This is returned-file browser proof, not physical Android camera certification.
The same actual pair is hosted in the work session’s inline preview. Structured chat attachment delivery is unavailable on this source surface, and that preview’s chat-frame rendering is unverified. All three PR assets returned HTTP 200 anonymously with SHA-256 hashes matching the inspected originals. A public browser readback decoded all three embedded images, verified the Before/After pair on one row at equal 300px display widths, and verified both exact Work sessions links. The rendered PR comparison was inspected. ### Remaining qualification Physical Android camera/OS behavior, OEM differences, native permission prompts and actual video recording are **not certified by Chromium browser-identity emulation**. The browser tests prove returned-file handling and the UI-to-Gateway boundary, not physical-device recording or model ingestion. The proposed Android exposure and unchanged platform exceptions need human product review. Broad ready-PR CI and required maintainer approvals are not claimed; this PR stays draft and is not merged or deployed. ## Worked on by - @TheAngryPit

prs.title: feat(auth): allow write access without personal credential enrollment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared Gateway operators need ordinary write access without letting teammates enroll personal credentials outside their managed credential system.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/3049

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `operator.write.no-credential-enrollment`. It blocks personal model-provider API-key/token/OAuth enrollment and personal GitHub publication OAuth enrollment, including reconnects and pending credential installation after permission is withdrawn. Ordinary writes, saved-account use, account status, and disconnection remain available. Shared credential setup remains admin-only.

**GitHub identity/co-authorship is not a publication credential.** Verified GitHub identity from supported sign-in, profile editing, and the Git co-author credit preference remain available. This does not add a manual identity-linking/OAuth feature or make an arbitrary proxy username a verified GitHub account; OCE’s ingress must use an already-supported verified identity path.

Existing `operator.read`, `operator.write`, admin, and default grants retain their behavior. Legacy read permits personal GitHub enrollment, so restricted roles must not also grant it. Grant only the non-enrolling scope, and review unioned device grants or apply a role ceiling. Adding legacy read restores GitHub enrollment; adding full write/admin restores all enrollment. Already-saved credentials, their refresh, and existing session selections are not revoked. This is an API guardrail, not isolation from unrestricted host execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared scope owner keeps grant containment separate from action eligibility. Full write includes restricted write, never the reverse. Because legacy read includes GitHub enrollment, the `operator.read.no-credential-enrollment` subset represents ordinary reads when read authority is capped by restricted write. Without that representable subset, intersection, cookies, or synthetic calls could restore enrollment or lose ordinary read capabilities.

Enrollment retains its original full-write (model providers) or legacy-read (GitHub) authority through provider I/O and credential persistence. Existing Gateway, tool, UI/native, and bundled-plugin adapters consume ordinary action requirements without manufacturing broader grants. No new policy store, database migration, config switch, dependency, or protocol-version change. Simplification keeps one action/grant owner rather than a deny flag or parallel policy; ordinary-read adapters are necessary because legacy read itself enrolls GitHub credentials.

## Evidence

- **2026-10-22 review refresh — a7d517ce8456b9df0feaed8a817a21083745e3bb:** rebased onto `a68d0eb252586b11412bced0ef41e41e5fc6e798`, preserving the scope lattice and upstream self-profile/UI owner behavior. Addressed the production-effect proof request by reproducing four unwanted GitHub HTTP dispatches after authority withdrawal, then carrying the transport’s existing live-authority callback through personal and System/agent device flows. Existing credential-install/store guards remain intact.
- **New execution proof:** 10 GitHub final-effect cases pass through real lifecycle/parser/profile/SQLite owners using a synthetic loopback issuer; 3 shipped-provider/private-store cases pass, including successful real-WebSocket API-key enrollment and withdrawal at transaction/commit admission. This is not genuine external GitHub OAuth, remote provider key validity, or model inference. The final effect/lifecycle rerun passes 54 tests (108.24s); the profile cleanup rerun passes 31 tests (8.67s). The earlier 295-test focused run (162.32s) is separate, not an additional distinct-test count. Six conflict-resolution consumer files also pass 109 tests (48.20s).
- **Current local gates:** core and Control UI production types, Gateway root/server and profile-page test types, targeted typed lint, formatting, and whitespace pass. Independent canonical Auto Review of the complete integration and final repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings; review was static and limited to supplied source/delta, not reviewer execution. [Detailed review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6353908519).
- **Still unverified:** genuine external OAuth, native builds/device execution, and the stable 2026.10.6 account/selection upgrade lane. The maintained upgrade runner requires Docker, unavailable here; a Podman substitution awaits Sally’s decision. No feature-owned schema migration is introduced, but an upgrade result is not inferred from that fact. Existing screenshots and the live recording below remain historical evidence, not captures of this refresh.

- [Live Gateway recording and result matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6346078709) on `3150e352715d`: real browser/WebSocket requests, profile/co-author preference API readback, and four direct enrollment denials under restricted write. Synthetic trusted-proxy principals; legacy controls intentionally stop at schema validation. This supplements screenshots, not external OAuth or OCE/OpenShell qualification.

- 2026-10-22 conflict rebase onto `c5650f3a5e59d6523c913a8ebfff2b787cf58435`: preserved upstream profile/GitHub owner refactors and web-push inlining. The 27-file focused matrix passes (577 tests), four additional profile/GitHub lifecycle files pass (35 tests), and both production-built browser grant scenarios pass. Core/UI/extension production types, affected UI/Gateway and extension test types, targeted lint, i18n, formatting, and whitespace pass. Fresh canonical independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 across the supplied candidate delta; no reviewer test execution or unchanged-context qualification is claimed. Earlier evidence below remains historical.

- A red probe against the previous provider-only implementation showed restricted write reaching GitHub device authorization. The retained router, real-Gateway, and lifecycle regressions now cover start/poll denial, ordinary status/profile reads, legacy-grant compatibility, and in-flight role withdrawal before credential installation.
- Real Gateway coverage verifies broader grants attenuate to restricted write, ordinary profile changes succeed, and provider enrollment is denied. A GitHub-backed sign-in fixture verifies identity and co-author consent remain available while GitHub credential enrollment is forbidden.
- Grant intersection/projection and plugin-cookie/relay checks protect against restoring legacy read. Device normalization does not synthesize that enrollment-bearing grant.
- Production-built UI scenarios compare legacy full write with restricted write: provider and GitHub credential setup are disabled only for restricted access; verified identity, co-author preference edits, and saved-account selection/unlink remain available. Captures use synthetic profiles and compare grants on the same implementation, not two source revisions.
- Focused backend, UI, and plugin tests pass after correcting a profile fixture; the two affected files were rerun successfully. The two production-built browser scenarios also pass. The initial 37-file batch took 206s, the final two-file repair run 36s, and browser proof 30s (2 tests; 5.2s test execution), excluding its 23s production build. These timings include cold compilation; no CI-seconds claim is made.
- Core/UI/extension production types and focused Gateway/UI test types pass. Targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. A direct lattice probe passed 4,648 implication/intersection checks. Canonical independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2; review was static and limited to the supplied delta/context, with no reviewer test execution claimed.
- Main integration was needed for one Workboard fixture conflict. The resolution keeps both write-scope cases and the current fixture owner. All four overlapping test files pass after integration (95 tests, 128s); extension test types, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Earlier broad focused checks and browser captures are pre-integration evidence; the integration changes no feature UI or scope semantics.
- Retained qualification gaps: native Swift/Kotlin builds/device execution and real external OAuth were not run. Existing voice-call startup failures (21 cases) were reproduced on the original unchanged base `afa9bfdcf82a7e1bdc4f8baf1bd4cbaf3200a936`; the suite is not claimed green. Broad CI is not yet qualification of this draft.

### UI comparison

Actual production-built Control UI with a synthetic profile, light theme, 1280×1400 viewport; tight crops make the changed controls visible. These compare grants on the same implementation, not two source revisions.

**Before — existing operator.write**

![Full write permits personal GitHub credential enrollment](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89ce5af8-30e1-427d-857a-5fb5acee1405)

**After — operator.write.no-credential-enrollment**

![Restricted write disables personal GitHub credential enrollment and explains that identity and co-author credit remain available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90ceccd7-15da-4f7a-a57e-7693a0e03088)

**Preserved — verified identity and editable co-author credit under restricted write**

![Verified octocat identity and enabled co-author preference under restricted write](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/030b3c4e-84f9-4fb2-89c4-072efb797aea)

## Contributor credit

Co-designed with @sallyom.

## Worked on by

- @sallyom

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c93cdcb7-363c-4c89-8a15-d23aab46d811)

prs.title: fix: prevent background summarization from delaying replies to new messages
prs.body:
Closes #176944

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new message waits for background summarization to finish when a context engine's host LLM request is still in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: new messages can interrupt a context engine's background summary preparation instead of waiting for the model request to finish. In an isolated Gateway the second turn was admitted after 0.235 to 0.315 s instead of 40.8 to 42.3 s, and the held request was aborted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deferred maintenance is optional work, so a foreground turn cancels it. The host combines maintenance cancellation with the request's existing abort signal, including for engines that do not wire cancellation themselves. Foreground admission waits for disposal to finish; aborted cleanup retains predecessor ordering but cannot publish transcript rewrites or start another host LLM call. Coalesced reruns are discarded, and requests that arrive during cleanup are refused for retry on the next turn.

## Evidence

Regression tests, run with the source changes reverted and with them:

| Test | Without the change | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| host LLM request carries maintenance and request cancellation (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | `expected false to be true` | passes |
| foreground turn preempts a held host LLM request, joins disposal, discards the coalesced rerun (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | times out after 120 s | passes |
| aborted cleanup re-enters ownership without publication authority (`coordinator.test.ts`) | times out after 120 s | passes |
| maintenance and cleanup run without the launching turn's caller or operator authority (`coordinator.test.ts`) | `owner.runCleanup is not a function` | passes |
| new deferred request is refused while preempted cleanup waits for an earlier writer (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | the failure callback is never called | passes |

The host-cancellation assertion was also replayed with only `context-engine-capabilities.ts` restored to unpatched source: `expected false to be true` at `expect(passed.aborted).toBe(true)`. Restoring the fix makes the same assertion pass. The full suites check that foreground admission waits for actual disposal, coalesced work never runs, canceled cleanup cannot publish, and a later maintenance run still succeeds.

Test environment: macOS 26.6.1 (arm64), Node 26.12.1, repository-managed Bun 1.4.4 test runner. The Gateway reproduction uses the supplied background-maintenance context-engine plugin and a loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture model server.

Focused validation passes: 31 tests in the coordinator and context-engine maintenance resource suites, the eager-import closure and PR-worktree provisioning guards, formatting, type-aware lint, and type checks scoped to the changed source and test files.

Isolated Gateway run from source (own state directory, loopback fixture model server, a context-engine plugin whose `maintain()` calls `runtimeContext.llm.complete` with no abort handling; the server holds that request open and the script releases it after 40 s on the unpatched tree):

| Tree | Run | Second turn admitted after | Reply received after | Held request aborted |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| unpatched | 1 | 40.806 s | 40.894 s | no |
| unpatched | 2 | 42.263 s | 42.521 s | no |
| patched | 1 | 0.315 s | 0.376 s | yes, engine disposed before admission |
| patched | 2 | 0.235 s | 0.287 s | yes, engine disposed before admission |

The driver sends both turns through the Gateway's HTTP chat-completions endpoint, into the same session. The fixture deliberately supplies no maintenance abort listener or request signal. Both patched runs record the request disconnect and engine disposal before the second provider request; neither reaches the 40-second release cap.

[Gateway driver, source attribution and current traces](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/bdafbbfa3d70a9969d75750b408b5705) · [Unpatched run 1](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9395532733ad5c05106a937ecc1990093710e84b/maintenance-preemption/runs/red-1-summary.json) · [Unpatched run 2](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9395532733ad5c05106a937ecc1990093710e84b/maintenance-preemption/runs/red-2-summary.json)

## What Problem This Solves

Chat boot loads image retrieval and browser operation code before either feature is used.

## User Impact

Chat boot downloads 9,324 fewer gzip JavaScript bytes, with unchanged image opening, media rendering, and browser annotation behavior. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing synchronous image-open helpers and browser annotation event contract into lightweight modules. Load browser screenshot operations inside the existing serialized thumbnail capture operation. The existing owners still publish pending work and admit annotations synchronously; no new cache, loading state, renderer, or compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

Production builds compared against `722ad802bc2801eadd83c8b484cd9715480b1f97`: Chat JavaScript gzip 1,417,590 → 1,408,266 bytes (−9,324); Shell 315,959 → 315,985 (+26); New Session 953,504 → 953,516 (+12). Shell/New differences meet the campaign's ≤64-byte build-variance allowance. JavaScript request counts remain 7/24/18. Chat CSS gzip increases 204 bytes without a new first-paint request.

130 focused test cases passed across thumbnail serialization, image gallery/custody/handoff, annotation admission/lifecycle, browser panel suites, and caught lazy-chunk recovery. UI typecheck, scoped lint, production build, and generated boot manifest checks passed. Independent review found no actionable defects. Production Knip reports the same out-of-scope cron/gateway, approval presentation, X OAuth, and session cleanup findings already confirmed on the campaign baseline; no finding involves these changes.

Timing acceptance, recorded before the run: compare this exact candidate and the pinned base on one focused Blacksmith Testbox, recording observed CPU/RAM and load. Run ten alternating samples per variant for signed-in Chat reload and New Session first load, with cold HTTP cache. Chat first nonempty transcript and enabled composer, and New Session enabled composer, must each have median ≤ base × 1.05 and p95 ≤ base. Four allocations entered capacity queues and were stopped without running samples; all four are reconciled. The second reached hydration while its stop was in flight. Timing remains a required, unproven gate before landing; results will be added when capacity is available.

Exact-head [CI run 39869744663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39869744663) completed with one inherited native-plugin UI failure (plus its aggregate CI gate): all 48 footer assertion signatures match [scheduled main run 39865398397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39865398397). The obsolete pseudo-element expectations are repaired on main by [a68d0eb2525](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a68d0eb252586b11412bced0ef41e41e5fc6e798); none of those assertions or production paths is changed here.

prs.title: fix(ui): pinned sessions cannot be reordered and guest drags fail
prs.body:
Related: #178066, #143909, #179023

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: guests cannot drag sessions onto the navigation rail, and dropping a session inside Pinned never changes its order.

## User Impact

User impact: users, including guests, can drag eligible sessions onto the rail and reorder personal pins above or below another row. The order survives reload, including for saved pins outside the loaded session list; rail shortcuts remain independent. Shared-group moves and section reordering retain their existing access checks. No migration or permission upgrade is required. Read-only connections retain the existing browser-local persistence behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows incorrectly required shared-group write access to start any drag. Permit pin-eligible rows to start dragging while retaining destination authorization.

Pinned accepted only section-level drops, which called “pin this session” again and did nothing for an existing pin. Top-level Pinned rows now supply a before/after insertion target to the existing organizer and canonical personal-preference writer. This reuses the rail's drop indicator and insertion logic without adding state, storage, permissions, or a second ordering owner. Self-drops are consumed without moving the pin; nested child rows are not reorder targets. A personal-pin drop can also resolve its source through the current pin projection when the session is absent from the loaded roster. Shared-group drops keep their original loaded-row lookup and pin eligibility is still checked.

#178066 is the reported UX context, not a proven introduction point. #143909 identified the older drag-permission gate; #179023 proposes a broader alternative pin-placement implementation. This PR repairs the current Solid sidebar's rail dragging and within-Pinned ordering. Personal groups remain separate work.

## Visual evidence

Same mouse gesture with `operator.sessions.read`: drag Research notes above Reliability Tracker.

### Before

Research notes remains last.

![Before: dragging does not reorder personal pins](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfadc021-4ab3-4524-93d6-3c398a7fb43d)

### After

Research notes moves first; the existing rail shortcut is unchanged.

![After: the dropped pin occupies its chosen position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dedf7d6f-d3e7-4aaf-aaa5-3c2523d2079f)

<details>
<summary>Original rail-drag evidence</summary>

Before: no shortcut appears with `operator.read`.

![Before: dragging to the rail has no effect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df1a0da9-67f4-42c2-a64f-5e4178cdeb91)

After: the shortcut appears while the full Pinned row remains.

- 244 affected component tests pass: sidebar interactions, sessions, rail, and row rendering. The new regression covers before/after placement, self-drop, inserting an unpinned session, preserving unrelated/unknown navigation entries, and no shared-group/session mutations.
- All 5 Chromium flows pass: admin and `operator.sessions.read` reorder in both directions, self-drop, reload persistence, and independent rail shortcuts; an additional `operator.sessions.read` case exercises three visible descriptor-only pins excluded from `sessions.list`; admin and `operator.read` retain the original rail-drag/add/remove behavior. - Follow-up regression on `21ddd965b8718271ee8175b64910e1afe0140437`: a descriptor-only pin was visible and draggable but retained its old order. prs.title: test(e2e): prove the session input lifecycle through a real Gateway
prs.body:
Stacked on #177698. The base branch `stack/pr-177698` mirrors that PR's head (`6f5fca7d891`), so this diff contains only the new tests. Retarget to `main` after #177698 lands.

## What Problem This Solves

#177698 reworks how a session admits, steers, queues, recovers and settles input. Its proof today is mostly unit tests over internals, plus captures the author ran privately. There is no committed test that drives the public Gateway surface and checks what a user would actually see: whether a correction reached the running turn, whether anything ran twice, and whether any input was left waiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

These tests drive real public RPCs (`chat.send`, `chat.abort`, `agent.wait`, `chat.history`, `device.pair.*`) and the `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` tools, against a real Gateway. Only the model is scripted, as a loopback OpenAI Responses server. Assertions read only observable outcomes:

- what each model request received;
- which runs executed;
- the persisted transcript;
- `pendingInputs`.

They never read internal state.

- **`gateway-session-steering.e2e.test.ts`:** one out-of-process QA Gateway child for the whole suite.
  - The requester's correction joins the active run exactly once.
  - `/followup` runs as its own turn after the active run.
  - Stop on the run keeps queued work; Stop on the session cancels it visibly.
  - `sessions_send` to a busy peer: `followup` runs as a separate turn and its reply returns to the requester exactly once; `steer` joins the active run.
  - A subagent result returns to its requester in exactly one announcement.
  - A message sent during an announcement is answered exactly once.
  - A correction sent during recovery compaction reaches the same run exactly once.
- **`gateway-session-steering-people.e2e.test.ts`:** two people (Alice and Bob) signed in through a trusted proxy.
  - Bob's steering is refused without queueing and never reaches the model.
  - With collaborative steering enabled, Bob joins Alice's run and stays the author of his message.
  - After Bob's device is revoked, his queued followup is cancelled before it reaches the model.

  This file boots one in-process Gateway per test. A shared-token Gateway has a single owner identity, and the e2e setup resets in-process runtime state after every test, so these scenarios can't share an in-process Gateway.

The scripted model never sleeps. Where the runtime accepts input asynchronously, the model keeps the run working through real tool boundaries until the input actually arrives, with a hard cap. Every wait is on produced state: model requests, chat and lifecycle events, or `agent.wait`.

## User Impact

None at runtime. The steering and queue contracts in `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md` and `docs/concepts/session-tool.md` now have boundary-level regression coverage.

## Evidence

- On #177698's head (`6f5fca7d891`): 12 of 12 pass, in two consecutive runs.
  - Test time: about 34s for the main file (including about 20s of one-time Gateway startup) and about 45s for the people file (three Gateway boots).
  - Wall time including the build: 139–174s.
  - Both files exceed the 30s target because each scenario needs a real Gateway, and that is the contract under test; no cheaper layer proves cross-process admission, recovery and delivery together.
- On `main` at the PR's merge base (`bd2dbfdeb49`): **the recovery-compaction scenario fails.** The original run works through 200 boundaries and ends `Never received: Correction sent during compaction.`, so the correction was downgraded to a separate later turn. That is exactly the defect #177698 fixes. The other scenarios pass on both versions; they pin behavior #177698 must preserve.
- `oxlint` passes on the three files, and they typecheck under `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.e2e.json`.

### Findings from building these tests

- **Behavior change for review.** A message sent during a subagent announcement in a Control UI conversation runs as a separate turn on `main`; with #177698 it joins the announcement run. Control UI announcements are `result-required`, so this matches #177698's "compatible required-to-required steering", but neither version documents it. The test asserts only what must hold either way: answered once, one announcement, nothing pending.
- **Pre-existing bug, not from #177698 (reproduces on `main`).** If a Gateway restart interrupts a turn and a new message arrives before restart recovery starts (about 5 seconds), both the recovery continuation and the new message stay `queued` indefinitely. The model receives nothing for 180+ seconds, and the Gateway logs `stuck session ... reason=stale_session_state`. Without the new message, recovery runs normally. It is not included here as an expected failure; I'll track it separately.
- **Not covered:** the exact restored state behind the yielded-cohort fix in #177698 (a retired child whose owed wake was never dispatched before restart) can't be reached through public APIs. Its restore-level regressions in #177698 remain the proof.

prs.body:
Closes #176268

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway and node-host `stop` and `uninstall` failures report the error but omit the next step that neighboring lifecycle commands provide. Operators are left without guidance when the service manager refuses an operation.

## Solution

Pass service-specific recovery hints through the existing shared lifecycle failure output. Gateway failures suggest `openclaw gateway status --deep`; Gateway uninstall also links to manual service removal. Node-host failures suggest `openclaw node status`. Human output prints the tips and JSON uses the existing `hints` field. Failure status and the original error remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Built and installed main (`3412694c1977a5e4d31757cb305c0c63a98c98fb`) and the integrated candidate in secretless Linux Docker using Node 24.22.1, with a real systemd user manager. Both Gateway and node services were created by the shipped install commands, not hand-written unit files.

- Real D-Bus refusal of `StopUnit`: main exits 1 without recovery guidance; candidate exits 1 with the original error and the appropriate inspection command. Exercised both human and JSON output for both services.
- Read-only mount of the unchanged CLI-generated unit directory: real uninstall fails at `systemctl disable`. Main omits guidance; candidate retains the failure and supplies inspection guidance (plus the Gateway manual-removal link). Exercised both human and JSON output for both services; unit-content hashes remain unchanged.
- Writable stop and uninstall controls succeed on main and candidate for both services.
- Focused lifecycle-core, config-guard, Gateway lifecycle, and node daemon suites: 4 files, 135 tests passed before removal of one callback-only test. The modified Gateway lifecycle file was rerun afterward: 44 tests passed. Formatting check passed on all seven changed files; targeted lint reported no warnings or errors.

The four core regressions retain managed-stop, unloaded-service recovery, uninstall-error, and still-loaded postcheck coverage.
