prs.title: fix(daemon): clarify launchd inspection failures over SSH
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS service-inspection error currently asserts that the launchd GUI domain is unavailable and directs operators to manage the Gateway from a desktop session. The classifier uses that reason for native launchctl exits 1, 13, and 125, so this wording overstates the cause and can be read as an SSH-management restriction.

## User Impact

The error now says OpenClaw could not inspect the GUI domain and that it may be missing or inaccessible. It explicitly distinguishes this observation from SSH management being disabled, gives read-only account/domain checks, and makes desktop-login guidance conditional on a missing domain. For externally supervised Gateways, it retains a concise conditional link to the supported owner-managed recovery procedure.

No service-control, admission, ownership, error-classification, configuration, or database behavior changes. Existing detailed external-supervisor guidance remains unchanged for the other inspection reasons. This does not diagnose why a particular Mac's launchctl behavior changed or claim all SSH environments work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is observed at the native service-inspection boundary; the message should describe that boundary rather than prescribe local-only management. Keep the existing safe refusal and offer diagnostics before recovery advice.

## Evidence

Original reviewed candidate: `45dc0ee76c54014b2402fc94aae80811791555d9`. The evidence below belongs to that revision; follow-up evidence is recorded separately below.

- Baseline: the new start/stop/restart CLI-boundary regressions fail on the old wording (3 failures; 34 existing tests pass).
- Candidate: lifecycle/status/launchd-membership suites report 94 passed and 16 skipped on Linux. These tests feed native exit fixtures through the real launchd probe/classifier/formatter and CLI lifecycle owners, and assert that service start/stop/restart mutations are not called.
- Independent review identified a Windows portability issue in the macOS fixture; explicitly pinning the fixture to Darwin fixed it. The affected lifecycle suite then passed 37/37. No production change was needed for that correction.
- Targeted lint, formatting, core and relevant test typechecks, and whitespace checks pass. Full supported build passed in 4m16s.
- Shared independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean for P0–P2; supplemental review verified the fixture correction. No remaining actionable findings.

## Original native macOS observation

An isolated-state, task-label, read-only invocation of the installed CLI reproduced the original service-inspection message. Native `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)` returned exit 125, `Domain does not support specified action`; the user-domain query succeeded. This proves the inspection failure, not the machine's historical root cause.

The exact candidate was built with the supported full build, then its complete build outputs were copied into a separate Mac checkout with Mac-installed dependencies. The normal built launcher ran successfully (exit 0) using isolated state, a task-specific service label, and `--no-probe`. The artifact checksum and production source hash were verified before execution. No live service was stopped, restarted, installed, or repaired.

Sanitized candidate output from `node openclaw.mjs gateway status --deep --no-probe --json`:

```json
{
  "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable",
  "loadState": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "ServiceInspectionError: OpenClaw could not inspect the macOS launchd GUI domain for this account; it may be missing or inaccessible. This does not mean SSH management is disabled. From the account that owns the Gateway, run id -un and launchctl print gui/$(id -u) to check the account and domain. If the domain is missing, log that account into the macOS desktop, then retry; you can still use SSH. Otherwise, check launchctl output for access errors.",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "Could not print domain: 125: Domain does not support specified action",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "targetRole": "diagnostic-only"
}
```

The installed CLI and candidate both report the same native exit-125 detail and `unknown` load state. Only the explanatory guidance changes. The old output directs management from the desktop and appends `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`; the candidate offers account/domain diagnostics and does neither.

**Limits:** This is an actual non-GUI macOS CLI/native-launchctl observation, not an SSH transport end-to-end test or a successful service start/stop/restart. The lifecycle refusals and no-mutation behavior for all three actions are covered by deterministic CLI-boundary regressions. Linux skips are not counted as native Mac test passes. No claim is made about what originally changed on the reporting machine.

## Review follow-up: preserve recovery discoverability

The recovery route introduced in #145023 was intentional and reporter-confirmed. The GUI-domain diagnostic now retains a conditional documentation pointer: "If an external supervisor owns this Gateway, see https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway#existing-system-launchdaemons for owner-managed recovery." This follows the reviewer recommendation without prescribing Doctor repair merely because inspection failed. The documented recovery policy, state-owning account requirement, coordinator/lease checks, and owner-controlled shutdown/restart are unchanged.

Follow-up head: `60b9a0c815efdf6a9dffd7b356362e1076c387cc`.

- The three existing start/stop/restart cases now require the conditional recovery link. They fail on the previous head (3 failures, 34 passes) and pass after this change. All existing no-service-mutation checks remain.
- Lifecycle, status-gather and launchd-membership suites: 121 passed, 16 platform skips. CLI shard wall time 7.89s; daemon shard 30.69s, primarily cold compilation; fresh CI timing pending.
- Formatting, targeted lint, core typecheck and diff checks passed. Supported runtime build passed in 84.5s. Independent Auto Review: scoped-clean P0–P2 on the complete follow-up delta.
- Rebuilt runtime transferred to the Mac with SHA-256 verification. The normal built launcher again ran `gateway status --deep --no-probe --json` with isolated state and a task-specific label, exit 0. The native exit-125/unknown state is unchanged and the conditional recovery pointer is present. No live service mutation. This remains a non-GUI local macOS observation, not SSH service-control proof.

Current built CLI output:

```json
{
  "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable",
  "loadState": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "ServiceInspectionError: OpenClaw could not inspect the macOS launchd GUI domain for this account; it may be missing or inaccessible. This does not mean SSH management is disabled. From the account that owns the Gateway, run id -un and launchctl print gui/$(id -u) to check the account and domain. If the domain is missing, log that account into the macOS desktop, then retry; you can still use SSH. Otherwise, check launchctl output for access errors. If an external supervisor owns this Gateway, see https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway#existing-system-launchdaemons for owner-managed recovery.",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "Could not print domain: 125: Domain does not support specified action",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  }
}
```

prs.title: fix(agents): remove leaked temp dir when the bundle MCP json write fails
prs.body:
## Summary
- Problem: `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson()` creates its temp directory with `fs.mkdtemp` but only constructs and returns the cleanup closure after the write succeeds. On the non-atomic path used to hand a Claude MCP config to the CLI backend (`src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.ts:282`, `atomic = false`, file name `mcp.json`), any write failure propagates out of the helper, so the caller never receives a cleanup handle and the directory stays behind in the OS temp directory, which has no TTL sweep. The value written there has already passed through `resolveOpenClawMcpEnvTemplates`, so what ends up on disk is the resolved header credential rather than a template placeholder. The atomic path (used for Gemini settings) has the same leak shape on failure.
- Solution: Wrap the write in try/catch inside `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson`; on failure remove the freshly created temp directory before re-throwing, so the caller never needs a cleanup handle for a failed call.
- What changed: `src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.ts` (cleanup-on-failure in `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson`), plus a focused regression test file `src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: No other components were affected. Both callers (`bundle-mcp.ts`, `bundle-mcp-gemini.ts`) keep their existing success-path cleanup contract unchanged; the atomic/non-atomic write behavior and returned `filePath` are unchanged.

Fixes #179555

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A failed write inside `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson` leaves an orphaned `openclaw-cli-mcp-*` directory in the OS temp directory containing the resolved MCP header credential; every exceptional run leaks one directory with no TTL sweep.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Windows checkout of `main` @ `80ae18c1` (task worktree for this fix). The real helper was exercised directly against the real OS temp directory (`fs.mkdtemp` / `fs.writeFile` / `fs.rm` — no fs mocks), covering both the non-atomic `mcp.json` path from the issue and the atomic `settings.json` path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm exec vitest run --configLoader runner src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts
  ```
  The test sweeps the real OS temp root for `openclaw-mcp-leak-regression-*` entries created during each call. Before the patch, the two failure-path tests failed with a leaked directory (`openclaw-mcp-leak-regression-uLcLLa` captured on the atomic path and on the non-atomic path); after the patch all three pass.
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts > writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson > removes the temp directory when the non-atomic write fails 203ms
  ✓ agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts > writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson > removes the temp directory when the atomic write fails 7ms
  ✓ agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts > writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson > removes the directory via cleanup after a successful write 12ms

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  3 passed (3)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** When the write step fails (non-serializable value hitting both the non-atomic `fs.writeFile` path and the atomic `writeJson` path), the temp directory is removed before the error re-propagates and no `openclaw-mcp-leak-regression-*` entry remains in the OS temp root. The success-path `cleanup()` still removes the directory.
- **What was not tested:** No live OpenClaw gateway session was started for this proof: the bug lives in a temp-file helper with no external services involved, and the real function was exercised against the real filesystem on both failure paths. A full `pnpm check` typecheck was not run locally; `oxlint --deny=warn` on the changed files passes with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test (real filesystem, no fs mocks)
- Target test file: `src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: When the write step fails (non-serializable value on the non-atomic `fs.writeFile` path and on the atomic `writeJson` path), the temp directory created moments earlier is removed before the error re-propagates, leaving no `openclaw-mcp-leak-regression-*` entry in the OS temp root; the success-path `cleanup()` still removes the directory.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The test exercises the exact public helper from the issue with a real OS temp directory and a real failing write, so it fails if the cleanup-on-failure invariant is ever regressed, without mocking fs internals.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson` allocates the temp directory before the write and transfers ownership to the caller only through its return value; a throwing write skips the return, so nothing owns or removes the directory.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No try/catch around the write step, and no test asserted that a failed call leaves no temp directory behind.

prs.title: fix(cli-runner): clean failed temporary skills plugin trees
prs.body:
Fixes #179557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failure while building the temporary Claude CLI skills plugin leaves a partially created `openclaw-claude-skills-*` directory behind because cleanup is only returned after a successful build.

## User Impact

Failed plugin preparation no longer accumulates empty or partially populated skill trees in the OpenClaw temporary directory. The original filesystem error is still propagated to the caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareClaudeCliSkillsPlugin` now owns the temporary tree for its entire lifetime. If directory creation, manifest creation, or skill linking throws, it recursively removes the tree before rethrowing the original error. The successful return path and the existing zero-linked-skills cleanup remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression tests mock `EACCES` during directory creation and `ENOSPC` during the manifest write, assert that the original error is preserved, and verify the temporary root is empty afterward.
- Without the fix, both tests fail with a leaked `openclaw-claude-skills-*` directory.
- Focused test: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-runner/claude-skills-plugin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 2 passed.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, core `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.


## Runtime Proof

The regression tests mock the filesystem; this capture exercises the shipped `openclaw.mjs` launcher and the real `claude-cli` preparation path in an isolated workspace and state directory.

**Failure setup:** a private temp root whose path length lets `mkdtemp` and both `mkdir` calls succeed, while the manifest write path (`.../openclaw-skills/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) exceeds `PATH_MAX` and returns `ENAMETOOLONG`. No application code, `fs`, or Claude CLI behavior is mocked.

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs agent exec --isolated --cwd <workspace-with-one-skill> \
    --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6 --json hi

# Before: main 502a942ca53
exit=1
ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, open '[...]/openclaw-claude-skills-0FZnJo/openclaw-skills/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'
leftover openclaw-claude-skills-* trees: openclaw-claude-skills-0FZnJo

# After: PR head a26825e4974 source, built to dist with scripts/tsdown-build.mts

ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, open '[...]/openclaw-claude-skills-Kzm1WQ/openclaw-skills/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'
leftover openclaw-claude-skills-* trees: 0
```

Both runs preserve the original `ENAMETOOLONG` error. The patched build removes the allocated `openclaw-claude-skills-*` tree before rethrowing. Paths are sanitized; the full captures stayed in local temp storage.

prs.title: docs: make release index consistent and scannable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The release index leaves the eight newest releases without summaries and mixes bare links with long paragraphs, making it difficult to scan what changed.

## User Impact

Readers can compare all 19 releases using summarized cards grouped by month, with the newest release clearly marked and a single-column layout on mobile. Existing release destinations, ordering, published section anchors, historical version guidance, and changelog links are preserved. No release-note bodies or runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Card and CardGroup components in the canonical English source rather than adding a renderer or editing generated docs. The change replaces the inconsistent list without introducing scripts, styles, dependencies, or new configuration.

## Evidence

- Built a bounded preview with the current `openclaw/docs` renderer and inspected desktop dark, desktop light, and mobile screenshots.
- Browser checks verified all 19 summarized cards, their original order and destinations, the `#releases` and `#changelog` anchors, and no horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768, and 1440px.
- Docs MDX check, oxfmt, whitespace check, and changelog integrity passed. The internal link audit checked 15,832 links with zero broken links.
- Completed the required local ClawSweeper review of `ec3e103076825dfdf19127adaf25e037e63bbcdd..0ddd7e7399ddb9fcf4ce529efa5be049b3977a4f`: no actionable correctness or security findings. The reviewer did not receive screenshot evidence; that evidence is included below and was delivered in the originating chat.
- Scope/simplification: one source file, +73/-19 lines; existing shared components supply all rendering and responsive behavior. No new runtime code or test scaffolding.

### Before

![Before: bare version links and inconsistent release summaries](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c553195-7ad3-464c-8c09-0ca1887c9ec5)

### After

![After: release cards grouped by month with a summary for every release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0976112-be97-4f10-8ff3-956306498dd3)

### Mobile

![After: single-column release cards on mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a0dd68b-8149-47ed-bf8c-34493b9e39b3)

prs.title: perf(ui): defer New Session picker bodies and obsolete preload code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

New Session loaded the closed Where, Project, and Checkout menu bodies before its composer was usable. The generated boot capture also promoted an idle pet decoration into the New Session preload. Startup additionally included Vite's modulepreload compatibility probe despite every documented supported browser implementing native modulepreload.

## User Impact

New Session transfers less code before its composer is usable. Picker labels, search, focus, and retained content remain unchanged; the detailed picker content loads on first open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing state owners, tags, classes, visible triggers, and routes. Load each New Session picker body on first open and retain it across closes. Preserve Where search autofocus after its first import; Project and Checkout preserve their existing trigger focus. Keep the pet's existing idle loader. Share the picker error boundary; its Reload action uses the existing guarded recovery owner for stale chunks, checks that the picker remains open, and retains ordinary retry for other errors. Disable only the modulepreload polyfill; retain native preload links, dependency hints, and Vite's CSS waits. Safari 26.2+, Chrome 147+, and Firefox 150+ are the documented browser floor.

Conflict integration (`66ac6866a2d`): `main` now owns bundle identity switching in the existing comparison helper; this PR retains that implementation and adds only cold-load comparison, readiness sampling, host-load recording, and compact timed-run output. The benchmark scripts typecheck after the merge.

The performance checker now reports emitted, source-mapped module gzip attribution. The existing reload benchmark alternates production bundles using their actual embedded build identities and records visible transcript/composer readiness. Full diagnostic records are written after the timed run, rather than serialized twice by the preview-server process. Its pinned-session setup now uses the existing pinned sidebar section rather than an obsolete rail selector.

## Evidence

The final integration merges `da8b252a70aca34d141bf26ae7c550095a143b72` without replaying main. A stale side-effect import in `chat-pasted-text.ts` pulled its optional renderer into boot; the renderer has no registration side effect, and its actual consumers already import it. Removing that import keeps the picker savings without adding Chat bytes. All six pasted-text component tests and the UI typecheck pass; the final P0–P2 independent review is clean.

Both builds use the same Node 26.12.1/Vite 8.3.4/Pako 3.0.2 toolchain, fixed embedded build identity, and all 29 byte-identical consumed packaged-plugin artifacts across seven plugins. An unmatched initial base omitted extra packaged plugins and was rejected as comparison evidence.

| Surface | Matched base gzip / requests | Integrated candidate gzip / requests | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 316,202 B / 7 | 316,040 B / 7 | −162 B |
| Chat boot | 1,416,831 B / 24 | 1,414,864 B / 24 | −1,967 B |
| New Session boot | 953,052 B / 18 | 915,265 B / 18 | −37,787 B |

The strict matched-base performance check has no violations or warnings. Chat's cap ratchets to 1,469,628 B with the same relative headroom; New Session retains its already-stricter 929,032 B cap. The existing stricter startup baseline remains unchanged. The approved timing below remains the checkpoint's ten-pair evidence; this integration adds no renderer behavior change. Fresh full CI is required on the integrated head.

Production Knip was run on the final head and pinned base. Both report the identical unused exports `MAX_PLUGIN_COMMAND_SCHEDULE_BYTES`, `createGatewayCronAgentJobRunner`, and the four approval-presentation functions, plus types `XRefreshClaim`, `SessionCleanupSummary`, and `ScheduledOccurrenceRun`; the base has additional unused dependencies and `PluginHookReplyDispatchResult`. This PR introduces no new Knip finding. No ignores were added.

Current complete-file LOC versus the pinned base: production UI 1,625 → 1,768; tests/support 3,038 → 3,288; measurement/tooling/docs 4,263 → 4,493; generated config 1,966 → 1,941. The small production increase is the shared retry/loading boundary and retained focus handoff around moved picker bodies. Refactor checklist: effect, untrack, direct listener, query, owner APIs and component cleanup remain zero; onSettled 2 → 4 and lazy 0 → 3.

Exact-head full CI run [39869745484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39869745484) is complete. All jobs pass except the inherited `Native plugin UI ownership > loads without asset grants for auth:none and preserves canonical chat admission and view recovery` footer expectations and the downstream gate. Its 72 normalized assertion log lines match the latest completed scheduled-main run [39865398397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39865398397), with no additional failure signature. The entire styles tree and test/support files are unchanged between the CI baseline and tested merge. This uses the native inherited-failure route; failed CI is not relabeled green.

## Earlier checkpoint evidence

Same machine, identical packaged-plugin inputs. Baseline `c4fd27d76ca`; candidate runtime sources `82135bc170d` (all 3,056 consumed local input files match byte-for-byte; embedded build commit `c4fd27d76ca` plus the candidate source overlay).

| Surface | Base gzip / requests | Candidate gzip / requests | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 315,930 B / 7 | 315,775 B / 7 | −155 B |
| Chat boot | 1,417,315 B / 24 | 1,417,243 B / 24 | −72 B |
| New Session boot | 953,843 B / 19 | 915,613 B / 18 | −38,230 B; −1 request |

Strict performance checks pass without violations or warnings. Chat/New Session caps become 1,471,597 B / 928,864 B, preserving each surface's relative headroom over the measured base. The already-stricter startup baseline is retained. All ten packaged-plugin input files match; unrelated extra plugin artifacts in the primary checkout are excluded by using the matched proof checkout.

Local timing remains **unqualified**. The last ten alternating pairs on updated main measured transcript median 864.1 → 527.5 ms, p95 3,128.4 → 5,532.1 ms; one-minute host load reached 27.4. The pre-integration candidate `82135bc170d` was measured once on Blacksmith Testbox, allocated in 4.0 s without queueing: 4 available CPUs, 16 GB RAM, initial load 0.73. Across ten alternating cold-cache pairs, transcript median **572.65 → 593.40 ms (+3.62%)**, p95 **899.90 → 729.20 ms (−18.97%)**; composer median **571.50 → 592.10 ms**, p95 **898.20 → 727.50 ms**. The coordinator explicitly accepted this result: No measured rerun was performed. Setup-only attempts corrected the native sync identity check and fetched the missing exact base; all 26 changed source files were verified by hash before building.

> “I accept the timing result as coordinator. A +3.62% transcript median over ten cold-cache pairs, with p95 −18.97%, is within noise for n=10 and inside the performance skill's 20% rule. My order's ‘no regression’ meant no real regression, not zero movement at n=10.”

Acceptance: no startup growth beyond the 64 B build-variance allowance, seven startup requests, reduced New Session transfer, no Chat growth, and no real readiness regression in ten alternating cold-HTTP-cache Chat pairs. The coordinator accepted this checkpoint and set the future rule to median regression ≤5% with p95 no worse, or ten additional pairs bringing the result within that band. The committed 240-message workload uses persisted state per build, no profiler, and records host load. Readiness means visible-DOM animation-frame observation, not a compositor paint timestamp.

Earlier candidates that also deferred optional Chat/Claw content did not satisfy the timing rule. Their measurements are retained as failed experiment evidence; those production and test changes are fully removed. This checkpoint makes no claim to meet the campaign's 15% Chat target. The original top-30 attribution below identifies the remaining required Markdown/runtime/composer costs and the New Session imports removed by separate focused wins.

Commands: `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`; `pnpm ui:build`; `pnpm ui:check-performance --module-attribution --base-dist <base> --json`; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --runs 20 --face chat --untraced --cold-http-cache --output <evidence>`.

Local proof: shared picker recovery plus Where 20/20; Project/Checkout picker files 30 tests with two focused fixture-wait repairs; performance checker 36/36 and attribution fixture 1/1; production Vite build tests 13/13; UI typecheck, targeted formatting/lint, and production `pnpm deadcode:knip` pass. Exact-head broad UI unit/E2E/real-Gateway proof runs with `ci:full`.

The stale-chunk review finding is fixed for all three pickers through the shared boundary and existing manual reload owner. The original CI repair opens the picker before inspecting its lazy content, gives the stylesheet fixture explicit membership, and retains a spy rather than an unbound method. The earlier catalog failure was fixed on main by #180742 and is incorporated. No inherited-failure exception is claimed without matching test-name evidence.

Scoped complete-file LOC: production UI **1,604 → 1,748 (+144)**; tests/support **2,772 → 3,012 (+240)**; measurement tooling/config/docs **4,231 → 4,474 (+243)**; generated manifest **1,972 → 1,951 (−21)**. Renderer changes mostly move existing bodies. The remaining growth supplies lazy loading/error boundaries, the delayed Where focus handoff, emitted-module attribution, and actual-bundle benchmark identity.

Refactor checklist across touched production UI: effects, untrack, direct listeners, DOM queries, owner APIs, and component cleanup remain **0 → 0**; `onSettled` **2 → 4**, `lazy` **0 → 3**. Domain owners remain plain TypeScript; the final integration only removes the stale Chat pasted-text renderer side-effect import.

Inspected synthetic captures preserve Where search autofocus and all six Project/Checkout focus checkpoints. Project is pixel-identical; Checkout differs only in glyph rasterization within the same text bounds. These captures use the same New Session renderer source as the final candidate; the later polyfill and Chat rollback do not change their rendering inputs. The original module tables and Chat/Where captures remain below.

Every mapped module appears once in these 93 groups. This uses the same measured `82135bc170d` runtime-source build as the table above. **Standalone gzip is non-additive**: group sums are diagnostics, not transfer savings. Source inspection includes the subsequently merged main changes.

Coverage reconciles exactly: 4,336,425 mapped + 78,277 unmapped = 4,414,702 raw JS bytes (98.23% mapped). prs.title: feat(sandbox): allow named host roots for sandbox bind sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- External sandbox binds currently require disabling the source-root check. Named `allowedBindSources` grants permit specific host roots while preserving canonical-path and reserved-target checks.

## User Impact

- Configure permitted host roots globally or per agent. Global grants are additive for every agent; an empty per-agent list does not revoke inherited roots.
- Changed permissions are checked before agent or browser container reuse. Revocation refuses reuse while preserving existing containers and data.
- Restricted plugin dispatch rejects writable external binds, including affected browser and managed-worktree binds and read-only or absent workspace modes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep bind admission in the existing sandbox security and container-allocation owners, with one workspace-confinement contract for plugin callers.
- Existing configs retain their validation behavior. The new key requires this version; older versions reject it. No database schema or stored-state format changes are introduced.
- Upgrades using restricted plugin dispatch require removing external writable binds or using an appropriately confined workspace.
- Merge requires maintainer acceptance of additive grants and stricter plugin confinement, plus security approval for this head.

## Evidence

- Head: `e0a682c737568b839234360014352d79cbfb1f2e`.

prs.title: fix: isolate sidebar pin E2E source server
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar pin-placement E2E test starts its own source Vite server, but its path was missing from the canonical private-server inventory. That mismatch routed the test through the bundled parallel project and caused the source-derived CI ownership guard to fail when it detected the undeclared server owner.

## User Impact

There is no product-visible behavior change. The existing sidebar scenario, assertions, timeouts, synthetic IndexedDB fixture, and source-server setup remain unchanged. CI now runs that scenario through the existing serial standalone project so its optimizer cache and private server stay isolated under one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

`uiE2ePrivateServerTestFiles` is the existing owner for tests that start private UI servers. Adding the already-existing sidebar test path to that list makes the derived project selection agree with the server lifecycle the test already uses: it is excluded from the bundled parallel project and included exactly once in `ui-e2e-serial-standalone`. No new registry, project, worker policy, or test case is introduced.

## Evidence

- GitHub Actions run `39849675545`, job `120072729531`, failed on exact head `7492ad6400de448be6e1e9bc29c551c3ec2e5ee1` because the existing ownership scanner found this one private-server path missing from the declaration.
- On the exact candidate tree, the maintained remote recipe passed changed formatting/lint, both affected type graphs, and 181/181 tooling owner tests across `ci-workflow-guards` and the UI E2E config contract.
- The unchanged sidebar scenario passed 1/1 through the natively selected `ui-e2e-serial-standalone` project. The result confirmed phase 1, one worker, no shared-server lease, and one private source server; no project or config override was used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: internal scheduled prompts fill the conversation when an automation continues work in an existing session.

## User Impact

Automation prompts stay collapsed while normal replies and human messages remain visible. Existing recorded prompts are fixed on display without modifying transcript history. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-admission migration in #178764 stopped carrying the cron job/run/session identity needed by the existing compact activity renderer. Restore those facts at the event producer, using the canonical execution ID for run navigation. Older incomplete envelopes use the existing collapsed system-notice presentation instead of exposing the raw prompt.

Reuses the existing projection and disclosure owners: no new component, parser, setting, or state. Production delta: +17/-2 lines; regression tests: +111 lines.

## Evidence

- Producer-to-history regression fails on the base and passes with the fix.
- Production-bundle mobile browser regression fails on the base and passes with the fix; verifies collapsed initial state, expand/collapse, reload, visible replies, and literal human cron-like text.
- Focused session-event, scheduler, activity, and notice tests pass. Production core/UI typechecks, targeted lint and format checks pass.
- CI caught a widened string type in the new regression fixture (TS2322). Replaced concatenation with a contextually typed template literal; the owning core-test messaging typecheck, producer regression, lint, and format checks now pass locally. No production behavior changed in this correction.
- Independent Codex review and ClawSweeper re-review of `4a4dd08081fea`: no remaining actionable findings.
- Browser test: 1.48s execution, 28.60s including production build. Producer test: 5ms execution, 39.12s cold compiler/import startup. Current-head hosted CI passed ([run 39871179961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39871179961)), including core test types, UI, and browser E2E.

prs.title: fix: catch lint inventory drift in pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a pull-request CI gap where changes inside the production lint-suppression inventory's source roots could skip the inventory test. That allowed a new suppression to reach the branch without the existing explicit allowlist being checked.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Contributors now get the existing lint-suppression inventory check when a pull request changes a supported file under `src`, `extensions`, `scripts`, or `ui`, while unsupported roots and extensions retain their current selection behavior.

The scanner, allowlist assertions, Vitest owner, shard limits, workers, and CI jobs remain unchanged. The watch intentionally includes JavaScript-family test suffixes and tracked dot-prefixed paths because the inventory scans them; this accepts bounded selection of one existing test for some scanner-filtered paths rather than narrowing valid inventory inputs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory reads source files from the filesystem, so normal import analysis cannot discover every dependency. OpenClaw already centralizes these dependencies in the policy-watch map, but that map included the type-suppression inventory and omitted the lint-suppression inventory.

This adds one dedicated watch using the inventory's exact roots and extensions. Its existing matcher opts this watch into dot-prefixed path segments, including nested hidden directories, without changing other policy watches. It does not use the broader existing source-inventory watch, which also covers `packages`, `.mts`, and `.cts`, and it does not add a dependency or CI job.

Existing planner-consumer contracts now explicitly retain the added lint-inventory target while keeping their original embedded-owner, QA, boundary, packing, and startup-corpus budget assertions scoped to the same subjects as before.

## Evidence

The production escape was traced through the actual changed-node planner and confirmed in an earlier successful CI run: the mapped type inventory ran for the changed `.mjs` producer while the lint inventory did not.

On the exact committed trees, focused remote validation showed:

- changed formatting and lint passed;
- the affected scripts and test-root type graphs passed;
- changed-target selection passed 15/15 cases;
- the actual planner retained the PR-exempt lint inventory for the original `.mjs` shape, a JavaScript test suffix, a direct dot file, the current `.boundary-stubs` path shape, and nested dot-prefixed directories; it preserved ordinary importer selection and rejected `.mts`, `.cts`, `packages`, and docs controls;
- the unchanged lint-suppression inventory passed 14/14 cases with one worker;
- the two directly affected planner-consumer suites passed 77/77 and 147/147 with one worker.

The broader source-owner test file also contains one pre-existing scheduled-turn expectation failure observed on the prerequisite parent. That assertion and its owner paths are unchanged by this pull request; all candidate-owned source-owner cases passed, and the current target already contains its separate correction. Full pull-request CI and exact-head hosted review remain pending after this update.

Channel-authored message IDs, errors, and action payload text can reach human `message` CLI output as active terminal escape sequences. A server response can clear/recolor the terminal or install an OSC 8 hyperlink instead of merely displaying its text.

Reuse the existing terminal-safe table renderer for broadcast and generic payload tables, and sanitize the scalar fallback. Provider results and the JSON output path are untouched.

Current main already inlined the old outbound-summary helper into `src/commands/message-format.ts`. This repair ports the behavior there; it does not restore the deleted helper or add a shim/SDK surface. Thanks to @wangmiao0668000666 for the original fix and regressions; their commit is retained.

## Evidence

Built main `3412694c1977a5e4d31757cb305c0c63a98c98fb` and candidate independently with Node 24.22.1 in isolated Linux Docker. Configured the shipped Mattermost plugin/account through CLI commands against a local HTTP API fixture. Ordinary lookups succeed; post responses contain either an actual control-bearing post ID or an HTTP 400 JSON message. Ran the built shipped `message send`, `broadcast`, `read`, and `react` commands, capturing raw stdout/stderr bytes with trusted color disabled.

The fixture uses real ESC clear-screen/color sequences and an OSC 8 hyperlink terminated by BEL—not literal backslash text.

| Successful send with hostile ID, twice | 5 each time | 0 each time |
| Failed send with hostile API error | 7 | 0 |
| Broadcast error table | 2 | 0 |
| Normal send, supported read and reaction controls | 0 | 0 |

Readable ID/error markers and report rows remain present. Decoded failed-send, read, and reaction JSON receipts are exactly equal across arms. Successful-send receipts are equal apart from their naturally different `receipt.sentAt` timestamps; the exact original control-bearing ID remains intact. Human-only filtering does not rewrite channel data.

All 36 focused private formatter tests pass, including the migrated direct/Gateway summary cases. Changed-file formatting and lint pass.

Simplification removes redundant per-field filters in favor of existing style boundaries and shared terminal-core helpers. Whole PR production +12/-6 (net +6), tests +116/-0, plus documentation. Removed-helper direct/Gateway regressions now live with the active private CLI owner; no obsolete path remains.

Merge danger: two-way presentation change, no persisted-state migration or authorization change. Blast radius is human message CLI summaries/tables; JSON receipts and channel delivery identities retain their semantics.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support pre-storage ingress sanitization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Policy plugins cannot remove sensitive content from Discord events before the raw durable ingress queue stores it.

## User Impact

Discord can await a permission-gated sanitizer before storing an event, without modifying the channel bundle. Plugins must check `channel-ingress-transform-v1`, obtain the existing conversation-access grant, and verify handler registration. This does not sanitize rows already stored; other channel integrations must opt in explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the narrow `before_channel_ingress` transform to the existing hook and ordered admission owners. Each handler sees the preceding replacement; errors, timeouts, cancellation, or retired authority reject intake with neutral diagnostics. Provider event identity and lane remain fixed. Native singleton and atomic batch writes reuse current-authority transaction/commit checks; older external queues remain supported without policies and must implement authorized admission before using this hook.

The capability ladder reaches a missing generic plugin contract: observation, agent, and transcript hooks all run after raw ingress storage. Provider-specific privacy rules remain in the policy plugin. The restart chat-hook safety list stays unchanged because claims replay the already-prepared payload rather than rerunning this pre-queue hook. SDK/security review is requested for the new raw-event boundary.

## Evidence

- Real Discord ingress to native SQLite regression is red on the base: content is stored before policy completion, and policy failure does not reject admission. It passes with this change; original private markers are absent from the test state files, including SQLite/WAL.
- 71 focused tests pass, covering FIFO admission, identity/lane refusal, hook permission and instance retirement, timeout/error handling, native transaction/commit revocation, atomic batches, legacy queue compatibility, replay and Discord siblings.
- The canonical full build passes. Core, extension, and three canonical test type graphs pass. Typed lint, formatting, scoped MDX, glossary, internal links and SDK export synchronization pass. Independent P0–P2 Autoreview is scoped-clean.
- Committed SDK API report (`2b33e823`): four exports added; no public subpaths added/removed, existing exports removed, or direct signatures changed. Reachable declaration updates reflect the additive hook, optional queue/monitor contracts, and shared type extraction.
- Personal native Gateway canary passed at the exact PR head before and after actual browser model/exec use: each phase observed two hook calls, one sanitized accepted row, no rejected row, and zero raw markers across the full state/SQLite/WAL and both actual log files. Core source/build identity stayed unchanged.
- The affected Discord entrypoint profile passed against that same installed native build: 254 ms import CPU and 113 MiB peak RSS; no build or runtime overlay. Deployment follows the normal upstream origin/main update workflow after merge.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep node cwd off gateway workspace
prs.body:
Closes #161028

## What Problem This Solves

An adopted Claude session can retain a node-owned working directory in `spawnedCwd`. Gateway preparation can interpret that remote path as a local workspace and fail before inference.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared ingress workspace decision excludes the saved cwd for node-hosted Claude execution while retaining local worktrees and explicit spawned workspace inheritance. Model provider and execution runtime are separate: standard `anthropic/*` models can run through `claude-cli`. Callers now pass the selected execution runtime rather than the model provider; compaction uses its selected native transcript owner. The node execution cwd and persisted formats remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Continuing an adopted node-hosted Claude session selects the configured Gateway workspace. Shell-only node routing preserves the saved local worktree. This repair covers workspace preparation; it does not claim successful remote inference or globally eliminate every remote-path metadata probe.

## Evidence

### Conflict integration update

- Current head: `8c285f2aa80b68fb023ade38e31706518401a42d`; merged main `471bdafdfdb0e0666c595334e2523b9a4b6cb50a` without rewriting published commits. Resolved four conflicts while preserving main's refactored reply pipeline, cron ownership checks, and prepared-session compaction lifecycle.
- Independent P0-P2 review found two integration issues; both are fixed: media staging resolves its policy session key through the existing workspace module, and scheduled ownership checks retain the persisted remote cwd as a workspace binding. Incremental independent reviews are scoped-clean. The normal commit hook and line-cap ratchet passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/spawned-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9 tests passed. Changed production/test file formatting and PR diff whitespace check passed.
- Local compaction, cron workspace, and sandbox diagnostics suites could not start their tests: stale TypeScript dependencies do not export `typescript/fs`. Targeted lint hit the same `typescript/fs` preparation failure. Core typecheck could not start because `tsrs/package.json` is absent.
- Frozen dependency installation was attempted in this task worktree and rejected by main's Node requirement: installed Node 26.7.0; required >=24.22.1 <25 or >=26.12.1. No dependency or lockfile changes are included. New-head CI remains pending.
- The shipped-Gateway capture below and its earlier review acceptance apply to `e9ad176970e645d5dfe42064162ee688615f5d36`; they have not been rerun on this merge head.

### Historical shipped-Gateway proof

- Exact head: `e9ad176970e645d5dfe42064162ee688615f5d36`. Built with the repository's supported `runtime` profile: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime` (exit 0, 49.4s). `dist/build-info.json` and `.buildstamp` match this commit; source inputs are clean.
- Started the real `node openclaw.mjs gateway run` entry in a fresh isolated macOS state directory. A previously persisted fixture contains the existing adopted-session shape, standard Anthropic provider, Claude execution policy, `execHost=node`, and a unique Linux-only cwd. Waited until the stored row was visible through public `sessions.list`, then sent real `chat.send` and `agent.wait` RPCs.
- Passive Node Inspector breakpoints recorded the actual reply-preparation provider, execution runtime, workspace override, and selected workspace. A filesystem observer delegated every original call unchanged, including native function properties. It logged paths and call stacks without returning synthetic results. The final node transport was not replaced.
- The observed selected workspace is local; actual `ensureAgentWorkspaceOwned` materializes that local directory. No workspace/bootstrap read or write touches the remote cwd, which remains absent before and after the turn.
- **Explicit scope limit:** one real `stat` of `<remote-node-cwd>/.git` remains in system-prompt repository-hint discovery. This is reported separately from workspace preparation, so this evidence does not claim zero filesystem probes across the entire turn.
- The actual downstream path returns `Gateway node runtime unavailable`. The proof establishes the changed Gateway workspace boundary, not node connectivity, successful remote inference, or `PONG` output. No real credentials, user data, or production Gateway was used.
- Shell-only control: an OpenAI/Codex turn with `execHost=node` selects its saved local worktree. It later stops on model availability; only workspace selection is claimed for that control.

prs.title: fix: restore compaction status when reopening a running chat
prs.body:
Related: #100388

## What Problem This Solves

Reopening or reconnecting to a running chat can hide active compaction and replay an earlier failed-attempt finishing status instead. Live compaction events already exist, but the bounded in-flight snapshot omitted them.

## User Impact

Users retain the existing compaction status across reconnects, including during context-overflow recovery. Compaction execution, message admission, duration, and stored transcript behavior are unchanged. This does not repair permanently stuck queues or identify every provider abort cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the latest compaction start/end in the existing full and summary progress snapshots. A start replaces stale attempt status; completion replaces its start, using the same run sequence and existing byte/count bounds. No new state, scheduling policy, protocol surface, configuration, or migration.

## Evidence

Built the shipped Gateway and Control UI together in isolated Docker, without private QA support or direct state writes. A normal seed agent exchange creates history. The actual browser composer then exercises three recovery requests against a local Responses fixture: ordinary context-overflow error → real summarizer request held pending at HTTP → final model retry held pending at HTTP.

- Main twice: live compaction start is received at sequence 8, but history/startup replay omits it and retains failed-attempt finishing sequence 7. The active indicator is absent after reload during the stable pending summary phase.
- Candidate twice: the same run/start sequence 8 is replayed and `Compacting context...` remains visible after a full browser reload.
- Releasing the summary replaces start with completed end sequence 9. Completion is retained through another reload while the final retry is still pending.
- Releasing the retry renders the final answer; `agent.wait` reports success and final history has no `inFlightRun`.
- Independent-session control: a second chat completes normally while the primary summary remains held. This is one extra control request, separate from the three recovery requests and one seed request.
- All 92 focused Gateway-state/UI-recovery tests pass, including full/summary retention, delayed older completion, and existing byte/count bounds. The three new regression cases fail on main. Touched-file formatting passes.
- Exact-head built CLI smoke with real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` returns `UI smoke ready`; no real-provider latency or overflow claim is made.

[Inspected before/after screenshots, real provider/RPC sequence, completion and final-answer evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180303#issuecomment-6353076169).

Whole-diff simplification reuses the existing snapshot owner and UI consumer: production +4/-0; tests +74/-1. The growth is the missing event admission/replacement and distinct Gateway-policy/UI-recovery regressions. Contributor commit and credit are preserved.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores previous replay behavior without changing stored messages or compaction execution. Blast radius is in-flight progress replay for clients reopening a chat during compaction.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): subagent completions reset the Claude session and lose context
prs.body:
Closes #178953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `claude-cli` session started from the Control UI loses its native session, and most of its context, whenever a subagent completion or a channel turn runs in it.

## User Impact

Agents that delegate to subagents keep their Claude session across completion announcements and the client turns that follow, instead of being reseeded from saved history each time. Other tool-name changes still start a fresh session, as before.

Upgrade caveat: an existing binding can reset once when its tool fingerprint changes. The latest-stable-to-development-head test below preserved saved messages and settings, but native context was not transferred automatically; the original conversation remained readable through the history tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

`screen`, `show_widget`, `suggest_task` and `dismiss_task` exist only when the turn's client provides them (Control UI caps, gateway task delivery). Turns with no client drop them, and since #176577 that changes `promptToolNamesHash` and invalidates session reuse with `prompt-tools`. These four names are now left out of that hash.

The stale-catalog problem #176577 guards against does not return for these tools. They are still listed in the system prompt, so a change restarts a warm process through the live fingerprint's system prompt hash. A resumed Claude CLI process then lists the current MCP tools (see Evidence). A call to one of them on a turn that doesn't serve it gets `Tool not available` from the loopback bridge, because each turn's grant still filters `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

The docs for `prompt-tools` resets now name the excluded tools.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway + Claude CLI flow (stock versus this head)

[Redacted native stdout, reset events, upgrade transcript, and test setup](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/fca5ca0aaa94e34912564dfce6a775fb). Real Anthropic calls through Claude Code 2.1.305; no mocked provider. A signed Control UI WebSocket client supplied `ui-commands,inline-widgets`, native `sessions_spawn` created real children, and real child settlement delivered completion turns. This validates the server/runtime flow, not browser rendering.

| Build | Control UI → real child completion → Control UI | Actual current catalog |
|---|---|---|
| Stock parent `fd8cd75f96d` | `e68f6fd9…` → `47e65689…` → `e68f6fd9…` | 48 → 46 → 48 tools |
| PR head `6cb5f16fe18` | `84306e78…` → `84306e78…` → `84306e78…` | 48 → 46 → 48 tools |

- Stock logs `cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=prompt-tools` on completion. Its returning UI turn remembers the initial nonce but explicitly cannot see the child completion: native context is split across the two sessions.
- Patched: the real completion recalls the original `SATURN-CEDAR-178955`; the final UI turn recalls it without tools/history. All three phases retain the exact same native session UUID.
- Actual Claude initialization records show `screen` and `show_widget` present on UI turns, absent on completion, and restored afterward. Thus the resumed process receives the current catalog; this is not just a model self-report.
- Separate fresh scratch states, canonical temporary paths, distinct port, `env -i`, and launchd label `ai.openclaw.scratchproof`. Production launchd PID remained unchanged before/after. Both runtime builds exited 0.

### Latest-stable persisted-data compatibility

- Installed exact latest-stable npm package `openclaw@2026.10.6` (`fe06181`), created a real Claude conversation and assistant reply, and saved a session label and `low` thinking setting.
- Stopped stable and upgraded the **same state directory** to this PR head. Standard `doctor --fix` performed the intervening upstream migrations (state schema 20→29; agent schema 25→31), with automatic pre-migration backups. This patch adds no schema migration.
- The original session ID, both pre-upgrade messages, label, and thinking setting loaded. A real Claude `sessions_history` call retrieved the pre-upgrade nonce and returned `QUARTZ-ORBIT-178955`.
- **Limit:** this proves persisted-data loading and use, not uninterrupted native identity across upgrade. The first upgraded turn reset with `prompt-tools`; automatic old-nonce recall failed when native-auth history reseeding was unavailable. Saved history remained intact and tool-readable. The attached transcript includes the failed automatic-recall turn as well as successful history recovery.

### Focused regression and existing checks

- `keeps the Claude session across Control UI turns and caller-less completion turns` in `prepare.completion-tools.test.ts` fails on main with `prompt-tools` and passes patched. It also asserts that exactly the four excluded caller-surface tools differ and that the system prompt still changes.
- Touched suites: `prepare.completion-tools`, `prepare.existing-session`, `prepare`, `cli-session`, and `prepare.configured-mcp`: 187 passed in 5 files.
- Previously recorded targeted production typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed; exact-head CI is green.
- Earlier separate stdio MCP resume checks also observed new tools after resume, including deferred `ToolSearch`. The Gateway trace above now exercises the actual changed flow.

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and adversarially reviewed by two models (Claude and Codex) before filing.

prs.title: fix(mcp): keep the capacity cleanup wait on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Once a Gateway has used MCP in 256 sessions, every new turn evicts the least recently used idle runtime to make room. If the host clock moves during that eviction (NTP correction, VM migration, sleep resume), it goes wrong both ways:

- **Clock steps back:** the cleanup wait stretches far past its 5-second budget. A 60-second rewind turned the wait into 64,999ms, so a turn that should have evicted an idle runtime and continued instead sat in cleanup.
- **Clock steps forward:** the budget is already spent before the first eviction attempt, so admission refuses immediately. The turn continues without MCP tools - reported as *"all 256 Gateway MCP runtimes are in use"* - even though idle runtimes were available to evict.

## Why This Change Was Made

`reserveRuntimeSlot` seeded `cleanupDeadline` with `Date.now()` and computed `remainingMs` from the same wall clock, then handed those milliseconds to `raceWithTimeout`. That helper arms a **relative** `setTimeout`, which runs on the monotonic clock. Seeding and spending across two clock domains is what let a wall-clock step resize the wait.

The fix keeps the whole budget on the clock the timer already uses:

```ts
const cleanupDeadline = performance.now() + CAPACITY_CLEANUP_WAIT_MS;
...
const remainingMs = Math.ceil(cleanupDeadline - performance.now());
```

`Math.ceil` is deliberate: `performance.now()` is fractional, so rounding down can expire before the deadline, matching `oauth-refresh-fence.ts` and `code-mode-headless.ts`.

What did *not* change: `lastUsedAt` stays on `Date.now()` because it is real wall time used for LRU ordering and idle-TTL comparisons against `store.scheduler.now()`. No new configuration, policy branch, or storage.

## User Impact

- A Gateway at the MCP cap keeps evicting idle runtimes across clock corrections instead of refusing.
- The cleanup wait honors its 5-second budget instead of stretching to the skew.
- No config or data migration; behavior without clock skew is unchanged.

## Evidence

Head `f3ab1fe0d27b` on base `25b0983502d3` (rebase onto current main; only the two mcp-manager files are touched and main did not change them). Production delta: `+4/-2`. Test delta: `+43/-2`.

**Regression test, red on base, green with fix.** New `it.each([-60_000, 60_000])` case in the existing `agent-bundle-mcp-manager.capacity.test.ts`, failing with the source reverted:

```
BASE  × keeps the capacity cleanup wait within its budget across a -60000 ms wall-clock step
        → expected 65000 to be less than or equal to 5000
      × keeps the capacity cleanup wait within its budget across a 60000 ms wall-clock step
        → expected +0 to be 1
FIX   ✓ -60000 ms step (159ms)   ✓ 60000 ms step (103ms)
```

Those two failures are the two user-visible symptoms (13x-inflated budget; timer never armed).

**Two lifecycle tests moved onto the faked clock.** `agent-bundle-mcp-manager.lifecycle.test.ts` faked `Date` only, so its `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` no longer spent the `performance.now()` budget and admission hung. Both scopes now also fake `performance`; reverting that line reproduces the hang:

```
× MCP manager creation ownership > bounds capacity cleanup waiting across consecutive idle owners
  → admission must not wait for a second full cleanup deadline: expected undefined to be defined
```

With `performance` faked: 40/40 in that file, 36/36 in the capacity file.

**Real-process probe** (real lifecycle owner, real timers; only the wall clock steps): base `wallReads=2` vs fixed `wallReads=0`; base rewind budget 64,999ms, fixed 5,000ms.

**Real MCP transport cleanup across a wall-clock correction.** The evicted runtime holds a **real streamable-HTTP MCP client transport** to a real HTTP MCP server (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`), acquired through the shipped `acquireSessionMcpRuntime` path. Its physical cleanup (a real `DELETE`, observed as `server.terminationCount 0->1`) hangs via the server's `holdTermination`, so the wait is bounded purely by the cleanup budget under `raceWithTimeout`. Capacity store filled to 256 (255 busy + 1 idle real client transport); a wall-clock (`Date.now`) step lands after the seed read; `performance.now` stays monotonic.

```
# PROBE_MODE=<normal|rewind|forward> vitest run -c vitest.tmpfinal.config.mts
FIX  (performance.now budget)   # real client transport, hanging physical cleanup
  normal   outcome=admitted elapsedMs=5007 term=0->1
  rewind   outcome=admitted elapsedMs=5009 term=0->1
  forward  outcome=admitted elapsedMs=5009 term=0->1
BASE (Date.now budget, source reverted; real-DELETE transport matrix)
  rewind   outcome=still-waiting-after-8s elapsedMs=8004 realDeleteFired=true  serverTerminations=0->1 timedOut=true
  forward  outcome=refused              elapsedMs=21   realDeleteFired=false serverTerminations=0->0 timedOut=false
```

With the real client transport and a hanging physical cleanup, FIX keeps the wait at ~5.01s across no-step, -60s rewind, and +60s forward, retiring the transport (`term 0->1`) in every mode. BASE rewinds the remaining to ~65s (cleanup still pending after 8s) and forwards it negative (refuses in ~21ms and **never retires the transport** even though an idle runtime was available) - the two user-visible symptoms.


**Suites and gates.** Capacity 36/36, lifecycle 40/40, production typecheck 0 errors, strict test typecheck clean for touched files, `oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean.

**CI.** After rebasing onto current main the full check set is green (`mergeState: CLEAN`); an earlier `check-test-types-core-4` failure was a main-side `sessions-patch.test.ts` issue that main has since fixed.

**Remaining gap.** The matrix exercises the shipped capacity-evict path with a real MCP client transport and real monotonic clock; it does not replay a full Gateway with 256 live model turns. Mid-run `libfaketime` is unavailable, so the wall clock steps in-process while timers, the real MCP server, and the monotonic clock stay real.

Related: #176880 and #177268 introduced this loop.

prs.title: fix: clarify pending agent startup admission messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading repair advice when a Gateway listener is available but an agent is still completing normal startup preparation.

## User Impact

Operators see that startup preparation is pending, its current phase and elapsed background-preparation time, and a request to retry when preparation finishes. Actual failures retain their repair guidance.

This does not speed up startup or change readiness, queueing, retry policy, configuration, or database schemas. It does not claim that rejected input was queued. No migration or operator configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending admission currently suggests stopping the Gateway and running `doctor --fix`, even when no failure has occurred. The existing startup owner already tracks phase and elapsed time; this change reuses its phase transitions and progress timer to update the pending refusal instead of introducing another state owner or timer. Elapsed time is refreshed at those existing progress points, not continuously.

## Evidence

- Regression on the base: 23 tests passed; the new pending-message assertion failed against the old startup reason.
- Patched focused suites: **51/51 tests passed**, covering pending retry metadata, phase/elapsed updates, successful admission, and actual failure repair guidance.
- Targeted format, lint (0 warnings/errors), and whitespace checks passed.
- Core plus Gateway-server and state-logging test typechecks passed.
- Independent supplied-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; source-owner context was inspected separately.
- Gateway preparation suite: 24 tests in 2.93s. Combined focused run: 117.14s including compilation and existing native SQLite integration suites. CI timing is not yet available.

The focused tests exercise the production admission/startup owners with controlled external preparation and native database integration. Separately, an installed-runtime backport was activated and verified through a clean Gateway start. That runtime check is separate from the exact-head isolated RPC proof below; it does not claim that pending or genuine failure responses were captured on the live Gateway.

## Additional real Gateway operator-facing proof

Exact head: `80ddc37d056e5939341bbdcbc22c779502188254`. Full `pnpm build` passed (4m4.5s); previous focused tests were not rerun.

Ran the built Gateway in isolated synthetic state with channels, cron and providers disabled. A supported index-repair fixture (40 queued agents plus the probe) kept real background preparation pending; a separate agent had a required table deliberately removed. No production admission hooks, fabricated refusals, or copied helper implementation were used.

**Authenticated `sessions.create` WebSocket response while pending:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "Agent probe is still preparing (phase: open-wait; background preparation elapsed: 4s).\nStartup inspection and preparation are still running. Retry the request after preparation finishes; no repair action is needed while it is pending.",
  "details": {
    "reason": "startup-sidecars",
    "method": "sessions.create"
  },
  "retryable": true,
  "retryAfterMs": 250
}
```

**Genuine schema failure through the same RPC:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <isolated-state>/agents/broken/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table session_key_contract; missing or drifted index idx_agent_session_nodes_active; run openclaw doctor --fix to repair it.\nSessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.",
  "retryable": false
}
```

Captured 35 pending error frames across phases `open-wait`, `open`, `migration`. Every pending frame retained `retryable: true`, `retryAfterMs: 250`, phase/elapsed text, and no Doctor/stop/restart advice. Genuine failure frames retained `retryable: false`, no retry delay, and Doctor repair guidance. The real GatewayClient retried the pending request and `sessions.create` succeeded after admission (`runStarted: false`; no model call).

Capture used an unchanged-byte loopback WebSocket forwarder because GatewayClient intentionally hides retryable startup refusals behind automatic retry. Raw responses were inspected before sanitization; only isolated filesystem roots were replaced in the failure excerpt. Gateway runtime: Bun1.4.4/Linux; observer: Node24.22.1.

**Limits:** This adds current-head RPC/operator-message proof, not a base-runtime before/after recording, channel/UI screenshot proof, or a restart-performance claim. The large synthetic queue is a fixture, not a proposed production configuration.

## Consumer-test correction after CI review

Correction head: `e0b67835fc9d11643c8241c5d0f1ef138839a0c9`.

Updated six stale pending-error expectations across `server-request-context.test.ts` and `session-row-prepared-read.test.ts`. They now assert the preparation phase, numeric elapsed seconds and retry guidance. The copied-context test explicitly checks the transition from `inspection` to `readiness`. Existing handler-wait, eventual success, authority, cancellation and genuine-failure checks remain intact.

Exact-head CI on `80ddc37d` reproduced the obsolete-message failures in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-8` and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-11` (run 39864296549). After the test correction, this focused command passed **85/85 tests** across all four files:


## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's managed GitHub OAuth credential expires, `github_identity_status` can diagnose the state but cannot get the operator into the masked reconnect flow from the active session. Long-running release work must stop and wait for the operator to find the agent's Tools settings manually.

## Why This Change

- Adds a capability-negotiated `screen` action, `github_identity_settings`, that routes only the requesting Control UI to the current agent's Tools panel.
- Keeps the OAuth flow entirely inside the existing masked Control UI; no token, code, or callback data enters model context.
- Makes `github_identity_status` direct the model to open that flow and re-check identity health afterward.
- Requires an action-specific client capability in both tool construction and Gateway routing, so older or cross-origin Control UIs fail closed instead of silently ignoring the command.
- Computes reconnect guidance after effective deployment tool/action policy, preserving manual Settings guidance when `screen` or `github_identity_settings` is filtered out.

## User Impact

An active release session can diagnose an expired GitHub identity, open the correct reconnect surface for the requesting operator, and verify recovery without losing the session or exposing credentials.

## Evidence

- 50 focused tests passed across registration, identity status, and Gateway tool policy, including tool-denied, action-denied, and action-allowed reconnect guidance.
- Focused `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Earlier branch evidence: 91 targeted tests across Gateway routing, screen/status tools, tool registration, Control UI capability negotiation, and UI navigation; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `pnpm tsgo:ui`; `pnpm protocol:check`; `pnpm format`; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`.

## Limits

This opens the existing operator-owned reconnect flow; it does not move OAuth handling into the model or auto-authorize GitHub access.

prs.title: fix(browser): bound Chrome MCP permit wait on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A queued Chrome MCP operation could wait longer than its configured `timeoutMs` when the system wall clock steps backwards, or be expired early when it steps forwards.

`withChromeMcpLease` queued its operation-permit wait behind an absolute wall-clock deadline:

```ts
deadlineAtMs: timeoutMs !== undefined && timeoutMs > 0 ? Date.now() + timeoutMs : undefined
```

The shared permit pool then consumed that wall-clock deadline through `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`, which re-arms a relative `setTimeout` on the remaining wall-clock time. The seed (wall-clock) and the consumer (monotonic timer) live in different clock domains, so an NTP-style step breaks the budget:

- **Clock steps back by Δ**: the computed remaining time grows by Δ, so a queued operation waits past its configured `timeoutMs` before it is cancelled.
- **Clock steps forward by Δ**: the remaining time shrinks (or goes negative), so a healthy queued operation is cancelled early as "timed out".

## Why This Change Was Made

A queued-wait budget is fundamentally an *elapsed-time* bound, so it must be seeded and consumed on the same clock. The permit pool already owns the wait boundary, so the fix lives there: `createPermitPool.acquire` now accepts a relative `timeoutMs` budget that is seeded and checked on `performance.now()`, and the Chrome MCP lease passes `timeoutMs` instead of computing an absolute `Date.now()` deadline.

The absolute `deadlineAtMs` parameter is retained for callers (notably the codex inference relay) that share one wall-clock deadline across an entire request — that is a different contract and is out of scope here.

## User Impact

- **Clock step back**: browser MCP operations no longer hang past their configured timeout while queued behind another operation.
- **Clock step forward**: a healthy queued browser operation is no longer spuriously cancelled as timed out.
- No change for codex inference relay callers, which continue to use the absolute `deadlineAtMs` contract.

## Evidence

**Real-browser before/after proof** (shipped Chrome MCP entry point, real Chromium 138): two concurrent `withChromeMcpLease` operations on one profile share the session permit pool. The first holds the permit ~5000 ms; the second queues with `timeoutMs=3000`. While the second is queued, the wall clock (`Date.now`) is stepped **back 2000 ms** via `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake:["Date"] })` — this moves only `Date.now`; `performance.now` and `setTimeout` stay **real**, so elapsed timers are real. Only the deadline clock source differs between the runs.

| queued op (timeout 3000ms behind ~5000ms hold, wall clock −2000ms) | **pre-fix** `deadlineAtMs` (wall clock) | **post-fix** `timeoutMs` (elapsed) |
|---|---|---|
| expiry after real elapsed | **~5000ms** (3000 budget + 2000 step) | **3030ms** (on the 3000ms budget) |

The large 2000 ms step makes FIX and BASE unambiguous (3030 ms vs ~5000 ms — a ~2000 ms separation, far beyond timer noise). The FIX queued op expires at 3030 ms real elapsed with the shipped error `Chrome MCP operation timed out after 3000ms while waiting for another operation.` A wall-clock `deadlineAtMs` implementation (the pre-fix behavior) instead extends the wait by the step to ~5000 ms.

**Fake-clock matrix** (production `createPermitPool`, the exact `operationPermits.acquire` Chrome MCP calls). `setSystemTime` rewinds only the wall clock; `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` advances the monotonic clock:

```
[A] fix  timeoutMs:300, Date.now()-200 -> at 299ms elapsed pending=true, at 300ms expired=true
[B] base deadlineAtMs:Date.now()+300, Date.now()-200 -> at 300ms elapsed pending=true, at 500ms expired=true
```

- **[A] fix**: the relative `timeoutMs` budget expires at the configured 300 ms elapsed budget even after the wall clock steps back 200 ms — the wait is not extended by the step.
- **[B] base**: the old wall-clock `deadlineAtMs` path extends to ~500 ms after the same step (the defect this PR removes from Chrome MCP). This path is unchanged for codex's shared-deadline callers.

**Regression tests** (all RED on the base, GREEN with the fix):
- `bounds a queued wait by elapsed time, not wall-clock steps` — asserts pending just before the 300 ms budget and expiry exactly at it (wall clock stepped back).
- `does not expire a healthy waiter when the wall clock steps forward` — a forward wall-clock step must not cancel a healthy queued waiter on release; RED under a wall-clock consumption, GREEN on the monotonic budget.
- `rechecks deadlines on release...` — `timeoutMs: 0` now means no deadline (immediate admission), matching how callers treat explicit timeouts; `deadlineAtMs: Date.now()` still expires immediately (base behavior retained).
- The deadlineAtMs backward-clock-step and native-timer-overflow regression cases (protecting the #165359 fix) are restored unchanged.

Test results with the fix:

```
src/shared/permit-pool.test.ts       8 passed
extensions/browser/chrome-mcp.test.ts       47 passed
extensions/browser/chrome-mcp-connect.test.ts + chrome-mcp.ownership.test.ts + collector.deadline.test.ts  24 passed
extensions/codex/inference-proxy.deadline.test.ts + capacity.test.ts   27 passed, 1 main-inherited failure
```

The gateway health collector and codex inference relay (both `createPermitPool` consumers) keep their deadline behavior. The single codex `inference-proxy.capacity` failure reproduces identically on `main` (an unrelated socket-close timing test, not touched by this PR).
