prs.title: refactor(plugins): consolidate plugin-local owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins repeat stream finalization, document-emission arguments, ingress binding, numeric validation, and preparation of facts already owned by their existing implementations.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Existing provider output, channel routing, error messages, authorization, media limits, and accepted-work settlement remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Complete the cutovers inside each plugin's existing owner: one OpenRouter music finisher, document-local Telegram emission, prepared Slack lookup names, the existing LINE numeric validator and context finalizer, existing SDK media encoding for Fal, the already-resolved Mattermost account, one Zalo route fallback, and one PixVerse poll-status validator.

This is a plugin-area split of the maintainer-requested measured-clone cleanup. No plugin imports core internals or another plugin's private files; the Fal reuse is through an existing public SDK export, with no SDK surface expansion. Against publication base `013240515205573248c27ab6b8eec7303f0da1a8`, this removes 70 net production lines across 10 production files; six test files add 140 net lines. The wider measured packet is split by area to keep CI attribution bounded.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Mattermost button callback settings use the account snapshot already selected for the send. Reinterpreting an in-place-mutated config or environment while target lookup awaits is not supported within one send; a subsequent send takes the new configuration. The duplicate lookup originally supplied an account hidden inside a helper (#38767); inlining that helper (#179782) made the prepared account available. Strict credential preparation and the client's live request-authority checks remain.
- LINE's ordinary owned argument fields are prepared before entering the shared finalizer, rather than after the ingress callback settles. Production callbacks do not depend on a receiver or mutate those argument bags. Final-route binding still precedes profile/envelope reads, and rejection still prevents subsequent work.
- Other cuts consolidate existing behavior without removing a failure guard. Native/provider transport, authorization, body/deadline bounds, data durability, and public text/contracts are unchanged.

No config, schema, protocol, dependency, or public SDK changes. The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Evidence

Publication head: `37d3570d410cfc1a888c42e71d4849ddb9f962fc`.

Focused proof passed: 335 cases across 27 files, serially with one worker (160.1 seconds); targeted native typechecking; formatting; 14 lint-suppression cases; zero runtime and static import cycles; and all plugin SDK/import-boundary checks. The proof driver verified all 121 named inputs, exact HEAD, and the clean tracked diff before and after execution. All runtime proof used task-owned isolated state, which was cleaned afterward.

The complete production and test diff received an author simplification/test-audit pass and an independent P0–P2 review with no actionable findings. These are preservation tests, not live vendor/channel claims. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad proof.

Local typed plugin lint has a named setup gap: Oxlint discovers plugin projects that consume generated SDK declarations, which are absent here; sparse native typechecking resolves concrete source types instead. Canonical preparation emits the full SDK declaration graph and is outside the campaign's local build budget. No unions, casts, suppressions, or project topology are changed to conceal the gap. Hosted CI's canonical preparation and exact-head lint are required before landing; local source-backed types and focused tests are separate evidence, not substitutes.

prs.title: fix(path): keep frontmatter values the strings they were written as
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Markdown frontmatter values are documented as literal string leaves. `openclaw path set` nevertheless writes values such as `1.10`, `true`, and `null` bare, so YAML readers see a number, boolean, or null instead. Writing `- draft` produces invalid YAML.

## Changes

Before leaving a frontmatter value unquoted, check that the existing YAML parser reads it as the identical string. Otherwise use the existing quoting path. Ordinary strings retain their existing formatting. The shared formatter covers both replacement and insertion; no plugin SDK surface changes.

Thanks to @wangmiao0668000666 for the report and fix; their commit is retained.

## Evidence

Built main `287b38a78d2fa6c7171f4bb16e26754278db6241` and the candidate in isolated Node 24.22.1 Docker. Enabled the bundled plugin through `plugins enable oc-path`, then invoked the shipped `openclaw path set` entry point with isolated profiles and state.

- Main twice: writing literal `1.10` produced YAML number `1.1` both times.
- Control: `plain value` remained an unquoted string.
- Main also coerced `true` and `null`; `- draft` produced a YAML parse error.
- Candidate: the same six calls all produced the exact requested strings, including valid YAML for `- draft`; the control stayed unquoted.
- Focused edit suite: 20 tests passed, covering replacement, insertion, and ordinary strings.

Simplification: reused the YAML dependency and existing quoting owner; no new state or serialization abstraction. Whole PR delta: production +20/-1, tests +26/-1. The parser-backed type check is necessary growth. The existing mutation documentation already states the corrected contract.

Merge danger: two-way code change, but reverting cannot repair frontmatter already corrupted by older builds. Blast radius is Markdown frontmatter replacement/insertion through the optional oc-path plugin; ordinary strings keep their formatting.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): selected 200K context window runs on the full 1M window after model discovery fails
prs.body:
Closes #177701

## What Problem This Solves

A direct Anthropic session can retain its selected `200k` window while the runner budgets against 1M after live model discovery fails. The hand-built fallback model carries the maximum window and compatibility metadata, but drops the manifest's existing window choices and default. The runner therefore cannot apply the smaller selection.

## What Changed

Preserve the provider-owned manifest's `contextWindows` and `contextWindowDefault` on the fallback row. Registry compatibility overrides keep their existing precedence. Claude CLI rows and models without declared choices gain no new choices.

Preserves @nxmxbbd's contributor commits. This forwards existing metadata through the existing resolver; no model registry seeding, SDK surface, configuration option, default, or stored format is added.

## Evidence

Built main `e875ec9c918c523373f37d66a53468667faf58bd` and candidate `017ac7d76ea01c0a42c9fad2c319f965b82257a6` each ran twice through ordinary shipped `agent --json` and `chat.send` entry points.

The isolated namespace had no external egress interface. `api.anthropic.com` resolved to a public-address alias on its own loopback, served by a local TLS fixture with a per-process trusted CA. Normal TLS and SSRF checks remained enabled. The fixture synchronously returned **401** to every real `GET /v1/models` discovery request and valid synthetic Messages inference responses.

The model configuration contained only a bundled model primary and a synthetic environment API key: the source config had **no `models` block or custom model rows**. Each failed-discovery arm refreshed to **zero models**, with Anthropic outcome `auth-rejected`, and had no earlier successful discovery.

One session selected `200k` through `sessions.create`; another selected it through `sessions.patch`. Their stored selections remained `200k` throughout:

| Observed selected-session behavior | Main, twice | Candidate, twice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent-reported budget | 1,000,000 | 200,000 |
| Persisted `contextTokens` | 1,000,000 | 200,000 |
| Actual native compaction trigger | 700,000 | 140,000 |
| Actual native tool-clearing trigger | 300,000 | 60,000 |

Persisted budgets were read from the task-owned closed stores with read-only SQLite access; no state was seeded or edited. Request triggers came from the actual primary-model request bodies, excluding auxiliary recap calls.

- Unselected controls remain at 1M and 700,000/300,000 triggers in both arms.
- Independent successful local-discovery controls publish models normally, honor 200K selections, and retain the unselected 1M default in both arms.
- Public session admission and inference succeeded; no credential or choice-admission bypass was needed.
- Focused provider suite: candidate 9 passed; baseline 1 failed/8 passed. Changed source/test lint and formatting pass; provider documentation formatting passes.
- A separate bounded real-provider smoke through the built agent CLI returned `P177702_LIVE_OK`.

Two-way door for the resolver code: no schema/config migration. Normal compaction or tool clearing already performed under the selected smaller budget is not undone by reverting. Blast radius is direct Anthropic fallback-model context budgeting after unavailable discovery; declared defaults and other provider routes retain their existing policy.

prs.title: improve: make agent credential requests opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent credential requests were available by default and presented a raw handoff URL; operators need deliberate opt-in and a clearer secure-entry flow.

## User Impact

**The entire agent-facing `secrets` tool—request, list, and delete—is now disabled by default.** An operator can add the exact name `secrets` to `tools.alsoAllow` or an existing `tools.allow` list, globally or per agent. Existing restrictive profiles, provider policies, and denials still apply; wildcards and broad groups do not opt in.

The Settings secret store, masked CLI, existing credentials, and config SecretRefs remain available. No new config key, schema, storage, or authentication change is introduced.

When enabled, supported channels offer **Open secure form** with the credential name, reason, destination hostname, and sign-in guidance. The shared web form remains masked and uses **Save credential** / **Credential saved**. Text-only channels retain the full working URL. Normal Gateway sign-in and session access are unchanged; this does not make an unreachable private hostname reachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing effective-policy owner records exact opt-in without rewriting ordinary allow/deny policies; tool construction and protected Gateway question creation consume that decision, including a check after awaited preparation. This prevents alternate harness/RPC paths from creating a protected question without opt-in, without introducing another policy system.

The existing shared credential-safety prompt tells every harness to suggest enabling only when the user **already has public HTTPS or Tailscale configured**. It forbids automatic enablement, setting up exposure merely to collect a key, or asking for the value in chat. A configured address is not proof of reachability. Missing-link guidance points to existing trusted clients or local Settings/CLI instead of inviting new exposure.

Portable URL actions and existing question lifecycle correlation implement the handoff. Navigating does not answer the question; terminal resolution retires its controls. Protected-store wording does not apply to arbitrary secret questions or agent-readable environment entries.

Requested by Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc); the explicit opt-in default was requested by Ayaan (@obviyus).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7113a88a-142d-45d1-b8be-60bba5c4b463)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1ce0f32b-ba5e-4265-a973-ad86f878f611)

## Evidence

### Opt-in update, conflict repair, and reviewed security fixes — head `8edcbc04c1fd119a6a0e282f9677e7dcc5b2e116`

The opt-in source is commit `62d7ce51fcb7288af4feacc7b0d622c2fc17b719` (the identical tree originally tested as `080bd1b`). The exact GitHub API reported a real merge conflict; main `d4b913d4689aafffa4f30d370ef7145d734f4917` was integrated. Five conflict resolutions preserve its policy/error and Solid focus/loading/action owners. The two new commits’ coauthor blocks were subsequently normalized without changing their trees, authors, or merge topology; original UX commit `2730e0c` is untouched. Earlier evidence below names the actual tested object.

- **Red → green through the actual coding-tool constructor:** the new regression failed on the previous production code in four cases (default, full profile, wildcard, broad group), 47.84s wrapper wall time. Those cases pass with this update. Pre-integration registration suite at `080bd1b`: **45 passed**, 56.24s wall time, including opt-in, deny, restrictive-profile and per-agent behavior; it was also rerun in the final integrated batch below.
- **Protected-question admission and real store, pre-integration `080bd1b`:** focused policy/prompt/Gateway suites passed **99 tests**, 67.32s. The production question handlers wrote a synthetic credential to a real isolated SQLite secret store and returned/fanned out only the stored marker. Default/no-origin, HTTP, HTTPS, Tailscale, explicit opt-in and deny are covered. This is production-handler/store boundary proof, not a new full network/model end-to-end run.
- **Affected consumers, pre-integration `080bd1b`:** **221 tests passed**, 126.88s, covering ordinary/shared/hosted question authority, embedded tool delivery, core configured prompts, and the Codex/Copilot/AgentsAPI shared-guidance callers. The separately run own-run/hosted question tests also passed. A pre-existing fixture was updated to opt in explicitly; an unsupported test-only option was removed after test typechecking identified it.
- **Initial integrated-head proof at `2bf6f57`:** **163 tests passed** across seven focused policy/prompt, Gateway admission/store/session-access, and shared UI/page suites (132.77s wrapper wall time). The full browser question-flow suite passed **17 tests**, including desktop and 390 px mobile submission (59.50s Vitest wall time).
- At `2bf6f57`, core/UI typechecks, touched-file lint (**0 warnings/errors**, 53.8s), i18n verification, and the PR diff whitespace check passed. The earlier 719/720-line inherited lint finding on the old base no longer applies after integrating current main’s existing simplification; this PR did not introduce a suppression or unrelated quota-driven extraction.
- **Concrete CI/review repairs:** the earlier generic default-deny rewrite dropped non-enumerable additive-grant provenance and unnecessarily restricted native runtimes. It is removed, not patched with another marker or native exception. Exact opt-in is one fact consumed by credential admission; ordinary policy objects and their provenance remain untouched. Registration also carries the already-resolved agent owner, fixing explicit multi-agent global sessions without guessing an owner.
- **Production plugin authority chain:** the committed synthetic-plugin regression uses the real capability resolver, registry registration, plugin admission, and execution wrapper. Replaying the prior policy owner from `2bf6f57` admitted an ungranted optional tool (**1 failed / 1 passed**, 63s); the repaired owner blocks its factory before execution and executes the explicitly granted case (**2 passed**, 10s). The replay restored the fixed source byte-for-byte; no product gate or loader guard was bypassed.
- **Affected contracts:** 162 existing policy/prompt, native-runtime, constructor, and Gateway/question/store tests pass on the final production source. Their combined 154s wrapper run also exposed a synthetic-plugin fixture setup error; normal contract/artifact declarations fixed that fixture, which then passed separately as above. Stale delivery assertions preserve URL navigation, lifecycle correlation, cancellation, and no-chat-input behavior. Only the protected-question lifecycle case opts in explicitly; the other store/SecretRef cases keep their empty tool config. The original sandbox additive-policy expectation remains unchanged. Final global-session and required prefix-stability checks: **12 passed** (81s).
- Canonical `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` updates only the universal opt-in sentence and derived counts/hashes; **six generated artifacts check current**. The three new literal wording pins were removed; availability branches, credential-boundary assertions, and the canonical prompt artifact retain the meaningful coverage. Targeted lint/format and agent, messaging, Gateway, and plugin test typechecks pass. Fresh scoped P0/P1 autoreview with unchanged policy/native/plugin owner context found no actionable finding; it inspected source, not executed behavior.
- **Hosted CI:** [run 39849659077](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39849659077) passed on `8edcbc04c1fd119a6a0e282f9677e7dcc5b2e116`: **59 CI jobs passed, 24 skipped**. Workflow start to last check: **1,912s**; summed parallel CI-job elapsed time: **16,363s** (not billing). This includes the previously failing consumer, native-policy, and prompt-snapshot checks. [ClawSweeper’s completed exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174109#issuecomment-6213818509) reports **no code findings and no security findings**, with all three prior findings addressed. Its one remaining pre-merge request is fresh-install/latest-stable compatibility proof; that request is not represented as completed. Installed fresh/default/opt-in proof and a published-driver upgrade were subsequently attempted on the exact unchanged head; the partial results and remaining failures are recorded below.

### Installed package compatibility — partial, exact unchanged head

[Package Acceptance run 39858112581](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39858112581) built source `8edcbc04c1fd119a6a0e282f9677e7dcc5b2e116` once using separately pinned trusted workflow `e875ec9c918c523373f37d66a53468667faf58bd`. Candidate tarball SHA-256: `81b56246e934af9491a8035ab11971c072329da3abce3cfa3d0bbcb26fac57ac` ([artifact 12461785271](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39858112581/artifacts/12461785271)). Package integrity and npm 12 `install.sh` acceptance passed; no package/image publication occurred.

- **Fresh installed candidate passed:** a task-owned rootless container ran the packaged CLI and actual Gateway with authenticated `tools.effective` RPC, not source helpers. With no tool configuration, `secrets` was absent (53 other available tools); exact `tools.alsoAllow: ["secrets"]` made it present (54 tools). Installation took 25.01s. No model/channel turn was requested.
- **Pinned published baseline:** live npm `latest` resolved to `2026.10.6`, build `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`. Its registry payload was verified against `sha512-jSpQPa2Jw5rG0J2GC07j9+qHtVYIuoHjgccU88JeS+p7188sBCnvIJeuaiNPHj1zsWkuHcBv443QiEUh7qrxwA==`. Its installed CLI seeded a synthetic protected credential, and the original stored SecretRef authenticated a real baseline Gateway. Candidate and baseline both retain their real version `2026.10.6`; no relabeling or admission override was used.
- **Generic installed upgrade proof:** the maintained published-upgrade **base** survivor passed in **887s**. This proves that scenario's assertions, not the credential-specific preservation matrix.
- **Credential-specific upgrade remains blocked:** the published baseline's real `openclaw update --tag <same-candidate.tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` failed after **1,044.06s**, with `runtime-verification-failed / candidate-gateway-startup / candidate-startup-failed`. The candidate logged ready, but the updater timed out awaiting `startupz` after `runtime.post-attach`. It left the baseline package installed; no manual replacement bypassed the failed check. The retained timeout does not preserve the last HTTP response, so it does not establish a credential regression, auth failure, or fixture correction. Normal candidate startup and fresh inventory passed separately; they do not turn this update into a pass.
- **Additional failed lane:** the same hosted run's **sqlite-volume** survivor passed migration/survival and its first Gateway history RPC, then timed out at `gateway-restart-volume-history` after **2,290s**. Overall Package Acceptance is **failed**, not green. It is not labeled inherited without a comparison.

**Remaining gap:** protected-store contents, original SecretRefs, and tool settings have not yet been verified after a successful credential-specific installed-driver upgrade. The earlier isolated handler/store proof remains valid, but does not fill this gap. All task Gateways/containers stopped; no production state was touched. No new ClawSweeper request was sent for this partial result.

### Reused enabled-flow visual and channel proof — captured at prior head `2730e0ca8f6e87932420fedb8339f2aae8665b45`

- [Actual Telegram Web Test Server before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174109#issuecomment-6217098403). The enabled, configured-origin payload and web UI are unchanged by the opt-in update, so these inspected captures remain representative. Synthetic fixture values only.
- Official Test Bot API acceptance and the leased QA user's TDLib stream confirmed **Open secure form** as a native URL button. Actual official Telegram Web K screenshots show both states; messages were deleted, temporary browser authorization terminated, browser closed, and QA lease released.
- Discord link-button, Slack Block Kit URL-button, and plaintext-fallback assertions passed on that prior source. They are payload-boundary proof, **not** actual Discord/Slack client screenshots; those client visuals remain unverified.
- Desktop/mobile images below show the actual built UI with deterministic mock Gateway data. Prior-head proof: 102 Gateway/tool tests (47.80s), 30 Telegram presentation/finalization tests (33.00s), 16 browser-flow tests (49.26s), desktop/mobile standalone scenarios (15.36s), and full build passed.
- Limits remain explicit: Telegram visuals are Web K, not iOS/Android/Desktop. The synthetic form URL was not opened. The full isolated Telegram Gateway attempt encountered a local Test Bot API proxy `UND_ERR_SOCKET` failure; direct transport/client proof does not substitute for Gateway/model admission.

### Requested pr-simplify pass

Audited every hunk against the merge base and reused the existing policy, prompt, presentation, and question owners. No new state, config schema, cache, relay, transport adapter, or independent exposure detector. Factory gating was narrowed so ordinary ask_user behavior is untouched; all harnesses consume one bounded universal prerequisite rather than new per-harness flags.

Final whole-PR deltas against integrated merge base `d4b913d4689aafffa4f30d370ef7145d734f4917`: production **+186/−37**, tests **+340/−65**, generated fixtures **+28/−27**, docs **+28/−9** (net +444 across 25 files). The later repair removes the generic denial rewrite instead of adding metadata-copy or native-harness exception machinery, removes three repeated wording pins, and simplifies the existing error assertion without growing its over-cap file. Necessary remaining test growth is a fully typed synthetic registry exercising denied versus granted optional-plugin execution, plus two distinct global-owner cases. During conflict repair, main’s retired ad-hoc screenshot capture helper stayed removed; mobile coverage uses its current suite helpers, and the moved host field retains its current native ref. Growth is necessary opt-in enforcement and distinct constructor/RPC regression boundaries; no net-reduction claim against a different base is made.

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A configured primary account can be mistaken for an explicit conversation pin when fallback changes CLI provider, rejecting a usable destination account. A second defect lets an earlier account candidate launch after placement installs a different explicit pin for the same provider.

## User Impact

Configured Chat and event fallbacks can select the destination runtime's account. Host dispatch and the migrated Anthropic transport recheck user/user-link pins after preparation waits and before effects. Selecting the same account remains allowed. Scheduled inference retains main's shared preparation owner, recorded-account forwarding and current-credential checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth owner carries configuration provenance as a runtime-only fact. Chat/Cron preparation constructs it once and consumers carry it through execution. The final session gate compares current explicit intent with the account actually selected; comparing only with the pin captured after placement can miss a stale selection.

Public V1 preparation/context declarations are retained. Additive V2 requires awaited account admission and the current-owner assertion. Native private-input checks, interruption, iterator cleanup, task ownership and protocol fixtures retain main's owners. No authored option, public SDK subpath, dependency, schema or protocol version is introduced against main.

The prior `c3f403b0` normal merge integrates official main `98818f034e3cbeb4a17373d4487c7d2754f4df44`, preserving both histories and contributor credit. That integration’s added/removed author-source sequences match independently reviewed `62181050` in all 62 files; the later conflicts were resolved around main's task/protocol cutover without changing that patch.

## Evidence

Current head: `5ccbd1caf5856e44370fff977a2d8c381bb48654`. The follow-up changes only two existing test files (+9/-6); all production bytes remain identical to `c3f403b0`.

Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 match this branch's manifest. Installed dependency/lock inputs remain qualified; upstream's release version and pnpm age exemptions required no install or authored dependency update.

- **Current fixture-cutover repair:** natural CI [39856115472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39856115472) on `c3f403b0` exposed three failures in two jobs. The native helper classified both jobs as unknown versus main, not inherited. The same two complete files reproduce **3 failures / 8 passes** locally in **263.542 s**. The Claude upgrade fixture overrode only V1 while the spread backend retained higher-priority V2, so it accidentally entered the native runtime and rejected its synthetic MCP grant. It now wraps real V2 preparation and replaces only final provider I/O. The two Chat assertions now read the same expected profile from `runtimeAuthSelection`, matching the producer and execution consumer; the shared-session isolation assertion is unchanged. **All 11 existing cases pass**, with no added cases, changed inputs, retries, skips, timers or weaker assertions. Wrapper: **149.925 s**; complete-file Vitest durations: Chat **61.24 s**, CLI **66.80 s** (including imports/transforms). These existing storage/upgrade compositions retain their production owners; no cheaper helper would prove their contracts. Per-file CI durations were not collected; planner job duration is not test-only time. Targeted consumer types, typed lint, format, line-cap, assertion-safety and diff checks pass. A fresh independent P0–P2 pass on the two-file repair is scoped-clean; it executed no project code.
- **141 production-path cases on `c3f403b0` (reused, not rerun on this test-only head):** five complete files cover real process account controls 12, two Cron files 27, CLI preparation 31 and Anthropic native stdio 66; five selected Chat admission/provenance/cleanup cases also pass. Wrappers: 419.815 s and 70.289 s. Other Chat cases were filtered, not claimed as passing. These exercise isolated SQLite workers, placement, owned child effects and synthetic native protocol I/O, without a vendor or listening Gateway.
- Before the final-pin repair, two same-provider user/user-link pin-change cases fail while the existing unpinned cross-provider control passes. This negative control uses the integrated pre-repair candidate, not pristine main. The explicit matching-pin positive case was added afterward and passes in the final 12-case matrix. Child receipts distinguish version probes from inference launch.
- On `c3f403b0`, production/core-consumer/Anthropic production and test types, core/native typed lint, format, line-cap and diff checks pass. Full native build passes in **480.436 s**, including declarations/exports, CLI/bootstrap checks and packaged assets. Its non-failing startup-gzip budget notice remains recorded (309.0 versus 308.9 KiB); no baseline adjustment or performance attribution is claimed.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the prior matching 62-file author patch completed three passes with no actionable findings within its supplied scope. Reviewers did not execute project tests. That integration was revalidated with the build, four type groups and its runtime cases above. This follow-up reuses that unchanged production/build evidence and adds the focused fixture checks above.
- Assertion, mock-export, timeout, database-worker/dialect and MDX checks passed on the prior `759015dc` integration. That is explicitly reused safety evidence for the identical author delta, not a claim those broad commands all reran on `98818f03`. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

Failed attempts are retained. The initial complete 20-file run has 550 passes and one fixture copying a V1 preparer from a backend migrated to V2; that fixture now uses V2 without changing assertions. Scheduled occurrence setup forwards the real owner-issued occurrence and started-state callback. Main's retired false heartbeat field was removed, and an existing auth-cleanup case moved to the existing auth helper with assertions and registration order preserved, rather than growing an oversized test file. The entire original 551-case set was not rerun after cleanup.

A local SDK declaration preparation exceeded its unchanged 300 s budget before lint started; subsequent canonical serialized lint passed with the same budget. One grouped replay hit the native 900 s no-output watchdog before an agents-support result; serialized scoped replays passed, but the unique stall cause remains unproven. No timeout, assertion, skip or baseline was relaxed, and a passing replay is not presented as a root-cause repair for that stall.

Prior head `375937d1` had successful [CI 39205414842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39205414842). That is historical proof, not CI for this new commit. The later `c3f403b0` failure and verified repair are recorded above. Exact-head natural [CI 39861269921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39861269921) completed **SUCCESS** on `5ccbd1caf5856e44370fff977a2d8c381bb48654` (completed 2026-10-22 22:19 UTC). This is the ci.yml result; the separate dependency/security-sensitive classic guards still require maintainer approvals. Earlier green runs remain prior-head evidence.

## Remaining Proof and Review

The latest durable ClawSweeper review of `c3f403b0` (2026-10-22 21:26 UTC) reports no concrete code findings and still requires integrated cold/warm account-change/closed-callback proof, installation/upgrade evidence and SDK/security direction. SDK/security and fixture-owner acceptance remain required. Legacy declarations are source-equal to main and representative consumers compile, but the native exhaustive API-diff helper creates worktrees prohibited for this task and was not run. SDK/security owners still need to settle V1 deferred-I/O guarantees and coexistence. The older unconditional bound-CLI refusal rationale is superseded by current main's supported exact-account forwarding, which this patch retains.

Live persisted-account edits through a real cold/warm vendor runtime, retained-settings installation/upgrade and shipped-Gateway captures remain unverified. Mocked stdio/request tests do not establish those outcomes. The actual Gateway watchdog file was typechecked, not executed. Earlier unrelated/head-specific Gateway permission or evidence is not proof for this head.

This author maintenance performed no operator Gateway operation, vendor/model call, paid test allocation, release, CI rerun, maintainer-only approval or upstream merge.

prs.title: refactor: simplify CLI output test fixtures
prs.body:
Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

CLI output regression tests duplicate usage-expectation construction and an existing message-start fixture.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All 72 existing tests and their assertions remain; production code, defaults, configuration, dependencies, and parser contracts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the eight original numeric usage literals directly and reuse the identical message-start helper from the module these tests already import. This removes 31 net test lines without adding a helper or another module dependency.

The existing non-strict `toEqual` matcher already treats absent and explicitly undefined object fields alike. Unexpected defined fields and incorrect numeric values still fail; these are not subset assertions.

## Evidence

- Both complete suites: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts src/agents/cli-output-records.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 72/72 pass before and after. Fresh baseline wall time: 3.93s; candidate wall time: 4.64s. No performance claim or new test cases.
- All 29 core-test typecheck graphs pass; targeted typed lint reports 0 warnings/errors; formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Whole-test AST comparison preserves every other statement, assertion, case, input frame, and numeric value. A supplemental probe of the installed matcher’s plain-record equality branch produced identical results for 616 comparisons (83 accepted, 533 rejected). The full suites remain the integration proof.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 review with complete tests and relevant owner context: no actionable findings.
- Original [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39864622141), attempt 1: success; all 49 jobs finished (18 successful, 31 skipped), 2,447 cumulative job-seconds. No reruns.

The selected repository check remains **failed**, not all-green. Its unrelated failures are documented below.

<details>
<summary>Baseline guard failures and attribution</summary>

At exact baseline `1a82e93a5d6190829b72655fba8a626d6d4221fe`:

- The max-lines guard fails on the existing suppression in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`. The supported staged-snapshot scan reproduced the identical failure against the untouched baseline index.
- The core-test root-budget guard reports gateway-root 725 and infra 730 against a 720 limit. All 44 controlling source/config files and the source path inventory are unchanged; this edit changes neither test roots nor module requests. This is source-qualified attribution, not a claimed separate full baseline graph execution.
- All three mandatory dead-code commands were run on baseline and candidate: dependencies, unused files, and exports (the candidate export scan ran inside the selected check). Each fails with identical findings: unrelated cron/gateway/config/X/approval exports, the runtime-recovery and dashboard support exports, and three benchmark-script files. No findings were suppressed or baselines changed.

The complete selected check ran through its remaining gates, including all 29 typecheck graphs and targeted lint. Its baseline-only failures remain recorded despite the successful original CI run.

</details>

Requested by @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix: session usage logs exceed the cap with fractional limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.usage.logs` caps requests at 1000 entries, but a positive fractional limit passes the shared loader's finite-number check and disables its bounded retention. For `limit: 0.5`, slicing effectively starts at zero and can return the entire session log.

## Changes

Use the existing invalid-limit empty-list result for fractional values by requiring an integer. Remove the now-unreachable unbounded-retention flag; accepted limits always use the bounded sorted window. Document the RPC default, cap, and invalid numeric limit behavior.

Thanks to @ericcaiwx-star for the fix and fractional regression inputs; their commit is retained. After integration, those inputs extend the current invalid-limit table instead of restoring its old duplicate fixture.

## Evidence

Built main `f7e64b22e307dcac9039d7c80ec806e8f218f56f` and candidate independently with Node 24.22.1 in isolated Linux Docker. Started the shipped Gateway and created the session through `sessions.create`. Each arm then completed **503 real chat turns** through the Gateway's documented `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint, with explicit session routing and a local OpenAI-compatible provider fixture. Every HTTP response contains that turn's acknowledgement. The resulting canonical transcript contains 1006 user/assistant usage-log entries—not a seeded JSONL or SQLite fixture.

Queried the real `sessions.usage.logs` RPC through the shipped CLI:

| Request | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit: 0.5` after 3 turns, twice | 6 entries both times | Empty both times |
| `limit: 0.5` after 503 turns | **1006 entries**, exceeding the cap | Empty |
| `limit: 1` | 1 newest entry | Same |
| Omitted limit on large session | 200 entries | Same |
| Zero or negative limit | Empty | Same |
| Above-cap integer `1001` | 1000 entries | Same |

Retained raw RPC responses include first/last turn markers. Public `chat.history` readback confirms the same session identity and recent conversation; no internal log records were manually created or edited.

Focused reporting and Gateway receiver suites pass all 54 tests; changed-file formatting and lint pass.

Simplification deletes the dead unbounded branch. Whole PR production **+2/-3 (net -1)**; tests +1/-1, plus two documentation lines. No cap, wire schema, authentication, configuration, or SDK change.

Merge danger: two-way code change, no persisted-state migration. Blast radius is malformed fractional log limits in the shared reporting loader; positive integer controls retain their behavior.

prs.title: fix: accept intentionally empty bundled provider catalogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the bundled provider-catalog validator failing when an owned refreshable provider intentionally declares an empty model list without credential ownership metadata. Vercel's bundled catalog has this supported shape, so the validator rejected the same normalization behavior that production and the model-catalog contract tests already preserve.

## User Impact

There is no runtime behavior change. CI can validate intentionally empty refreshable catalogs without weakening checks for malformed model arrays, dropped nonempty rows, explicitly owned empty providers, decision-only rows, or populated static provider configurations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production normalizer omits a provider only when normalization produces no model rows and the raw provider has no `authScope`. The test previously treated every missing normalized provider as data loss.

The validator now checks the raw model field first, recognizes only that exact intentional-absence contract, and otherwise still requires a present normalized model array with identical cardinality. The existing discovery filtering and static provider builder remain on the unchanged path for normalized providers.

## Evidence

- The original failure is the completed `checks-node-compact-small-6` job from CI run `39849675545`. The validator, normalizer, normalizer controls, and Vercel manifest are unchanged between that run, the repair base, and the current target source used for supersession checking.
- Exact-candidate remote proof passed changed formatting/core lint with zero errors and the maintained `core-test-other` type graph.
- The corrected bundled-catalog validator passed `1/1` with one worker (2.31s Vitest time, 4.69s wall time). The unchanged model-catalog normalizer controls passed `11/11` through their canonical owner route.
- Production and manifest files are unchanged; the complete diff is one test-owner file (`+16/-3`). Exact-head hosted CI is green, the fresh calibrated review and separate canonical autoreview are clean, and ClawSweeper returned Gold with no findings.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): reject invalid UTF-8 when reading workspace text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a daily memory file (e.g. `memory/2026-04-05.md`) contains non-UTF-8 bytes (edited by a user or external tool), the next inline dreaming report lossily decodes those bytes to `U+FFFD` and rewrites the whole file, permanently corrupting it. The malformed byte is silently replaced with `�` and can never be recovered. This change makes the read side reject the file instead of rewriting it.

- Problem: `readWorkspaceText` decoded the file buffer with a lossy `.toString("utf8")`, so invalid bytes became `U+FFFD`; the dreaming inline path then wrote the mangled content back over the original file, destroying the data irreversibly.
- Solution: gate the read with `isUtf8` before decoding. A non-UTF-8 memory file now throws `not valid UTF-8` and is left unchanged.
- What changed: `readWorkspaceText` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-workspace-files.ts` now validates the buffer with `isUtf8` before `.toString("utf8")`; a regression test was folded into `dreaming-dreams-file.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: valid UTF-8 files, the write path, and all other `readWorkspaceText` callers keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix lives in the canonical owner for reading workspace text (`readWorkspaceText`), which is the single place that performs the lossy UTF-8 decode. Adding the `isUtf8` guard there means every caller — the dreaming inline path and the other six read sites — inherits the protection, matching the existing `readMemoryContent` guard in `short-term-promotion-memory-write.ts`. No new parser or policy branch was introduced; only the existing decode point was hardened.

All seven callers propagate non-ENOENT errors correctly (they either let the error bubble up or rethrow after the ENOENT special-case), so the new error surfaces as a failed write rather than being swallowed. This is fail-closed behavior consistent with the wider malformed-UTF-8 family (`reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting`).

## User Impact

Users who have a memory file with invalid UTF-8 bytes (from manual edits or external tooling) will no longer have that file silently corrupted by a dreaming report. Instead, the write is rejected with a clear `not valid UTF-8` message, and the file is left byte-for-byte unchanged so the content can be recovered.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway dreaming proof — a real OpenClaw Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`) with memory-core dreaming inline storage, seeded with two daily notes in `workspace/memory/`: one valid UTF-8 (`2026-10-20.md`) and one malformed containing `0xff` (`2026-10-21.md`). Dreaming triggered via shipped `openclaw cron run` (agent turn short-circuits in `before_agent_reply` — no model call needed).

**Post-fix** (with `isUtf8` guard): Gateway rejects the malformed file; bytes preserved.

```console
$ openclaw gateway run --port 18923 --allow-unforced --log-level trace
$ openclaw cron run 94de547a --wait --wait-timeout 90s --json
status: ok  completion: succeeded  summary: NO_REPLY  duration: 3595ms

$ sha256sum memory/2026-10-21.md   # before run
7ceb1f4efe8b...  (contains 0xff at offset 0x1f)
$ sha256sum memory/2026-10-21.md   # after run
7ceb1f4efe8b...  ← UNCHANGED
$ xxd memory/2026-10-21.md | grep ff
00000010: 496e 7661 6c69 6420 6279 7465 20ff 2068  Invalid byte . h
```

Raw Gateway log (post-fix dreaming sweep):

```text
[hooks] running before_agent_reply (1 handlers, first-claim wins)
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming verbose enabled (cron=0 3 * * *, limit=10, workspaces=1).
[plugins] memory-core: light dreaming failed: Memory file is not valid UTF-8: .../workspace/memory/2026-10-21.md. The file was left unchanged; convert a copy to UTF-8 before retrying.
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=1, degraded=0, narrativesPending=0).
```

**Pre-fix** (source reverted to `origin/main`, same dist rebuilt): Gateway lossy-decodes `0xff` → `U+FFFD`, rewrites file with inline dreaming phase — irreversible corruption.

```console
$ openclaw cron run 77035dd2 --wait --wait-timeout 90s --json
status: ok  completion: succeeded  summary: NO_REPLY  duration: 5329ms

$ sha256sum memory/2026-10-21.md   # before run
7ceb1f4efe8b...
$ sha256sum memory/2026-10-21.md   # after run
5253f257aef0...  ← CHANGED (0xff corrupted to ef bf bd)
$ xxd memory/2026-10-21.md | head -2
00000000: 2320 3230 3236 2d31 302d 3231 0a0a 2d20  # 2026-10-21..- 
00000010: 496e 7661 6c69 6420 6279 7465 20ef bfbd 20  Invalid byte ... 
```

Raw Gateway log (pre-fix dreaming sweep — no error, silent corruption):

```text
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming verbose enabled (cron=0 3 * * *, limit=10, workspaces=1).
[plugins] memory-core: light dreaming staged 4 candidate(s) [workspace=...].
[plugins] memory-core: REM dreaming wrote reflections from 4 recent memory trace(s) [workspace=...].
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=1).
```

Behavior matrix (same shipped Gateway entry, same daily note, only variable = PR fix):

```text
                     pre-fix (lossy)              post-fix (isUtf8 guard)
0xff byte             0xff → ef bf bd (U+FFFD)     0xff preserved
SHA-256               changed                       unchanged
dreaming sweep        succeeded (failed=0)          rejected (failed=1)
file after run        rewritten with inline phase   byte-for-byte original
```

Focused regression test (folded into `dreaming markdown storage` describe block):

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-dreams-file.test.ts
 ✓ dreaming markdown storage > leaves an inline daily file unchanged when it contains invalid UTF-8
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

prs.title: improve(ui): make composer actions easier to scan
prs.body:
Part of #180298.

## What Problem This Solves

The composer's **+** menu mixes attachment actions and session capabilities without labels that distinguish the sections.

## User Impact

This proposed UX contribution adds quiet **Attach** and **Capabilities** headings in the existing root menu across Chat and New Session. **Manage plugins** remains visible as a secondary action at the bottom; session overrides can still be reset immediately above it.

Existing attachment labels, image-only restrictions, Safari's single-picker path, direct Skills and Connectors selectors, selection state, and permission checks are unchanged. There is no new submenu, picker policy, capture behavior, preference, or overlay-placement repair. This is a UX proposal for maintainer review, not maintainer-approved design.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared menu already owns all affected composers, including the attachment-only session rail. Its existing non-interactive content rows supply the headings, and unavailable sections produce no heading or extra separator. The existing reset action stays with the capability controls above the management footer.

This section-labeling proposal was requested by Vitor Cepeda Lopes.

## Evidence

- Published head: `b4804673df6c20d4a91957075bebe5bba3d3ab92`, verified to match the tested tree exactly.
- Verified official main base: `698a6f83b46beae08b9e63dc06138c5fccfb66b1`. Tested candidate tree: `22967b96522e4d81516c4e0d8af1043f876e71ae`.
- Focused shared-menu suites: **24 passed**. The three populated-section regressions failed on the original production component specifically because the headings were absent; the empty-menu case already passed.
- Production Control UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures: **48 selected scenarios passed across the initial run and bounded replay**, covering Chat/New Session, attachment picker identities, capability/reset behavior, restricted controls, keyboard activation, Escape/focus return, and desktop/mobile light/dark captures. Initial run: 39 passed/9 failed in 247.30 seconds; four capture-harness expectations incorrectly assumed Draft was enabled and were corrected. The other five initial browser timeouts passed unchanged in focused replay; their cause remains unproven. Replay: 9 passed in 24.68 seconds. This is not a claim of a clean uninterrupted full run.
- Real-component browser regression: longer localized headings wrap at **320px**, stay outside the keyboard order, and retain Escape/focus return (**1 passed**, 1.24 seconds total).
- UI types, changed UI test typecheck leaves, scoped typed lint, CSS lint, controller guards, i18n baseline/verification, formatting, whitespace, and the changed document's MDX check passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review through the repository-configured **P0** threshold: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0 findings. It did not independently rerun tests and is not product acceptance.

### Before

![Before: actual Chat root menu without section headings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50a7a39f-51ae-4736-8033-18030e8254a6)

### After

![After: Attach and Capabilities headings with a secondary Manage plugins footer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffe2856d-bf05-42f6-9354-59df2abfa671)

<details>
<summary>New Session — narrow dark viewport</summary>

![New Session: the same shared menu sections in a 390px dark viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41e9c54f-6405-4177-9b6b-864946f7d6e2)

</details>

These inspected screenshots use synthetic content and the actual production Control UI. The Before capture is from the verified base; After is from the exact tree published above. Anonymous access to all three images returned HTTP 200 with SHA-256 hashes matching the inspected originals. A public GitHub browser readback decoded all three embedded images at their native dimensions and verified both Work sessions links. The earlier sandbox-tool timeout is resolved; screenshot delivery verification is complete.

Limits: browser/device identities and mobile viewports are emulated Chromium, not physical iOS/Android or WebKit certification. Picker/capture policy and anchoring workstreams remain separate. Before marking this PR ready for review, available checks for the published head were passing while most lanes were skipped/neutral due to draft status. Those draft-stage checks do not establish that the broad ready-for-review CI matrix passed.

The production change reuses the existing menu owner, introduces no state or lifecycle owner, and adds 33 net production lines for labels, footer ordering, and typography. Regression tests add 116 lines; documentation has a small wording update.

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

prs.title: fix(ui): remove the shadow strip above the chat composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the rectangular shadow-like strip painted immediately above the chat composer, especially visible on phones in light mode.

## User Impact

The conversation canvas now meets the composer cleanly. The composer outline, focus treatment, and independent scrolling indicators are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removes the footer gradient, its unused spacing token, and obsolete mobile/short-pane overrides. Production CSS is 32 lines smaller; a focused raster regression protects the visible boundary.

## Evidence

- Reproduced against the original production build: the mobile light-mode pixel regression fails on the painted strip (10-channel-level deviation).
- Fixed production build: both light/dark mobile raster cases pass. Test invocation wall time: 47.08 seconds including the shared production build; CI duration pending.
- Existing footer/reachability and mobile latest-clearance suites: four cases pass, including desktop, phone, long drafts, and short viewports.
- UI and chat E2E typechecks, targeted lint, CSS lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings.
- CI follow-up: updated seven stale footer-fade assertions to require no generated shadow, retaining autosizing, notice layout, and menu hit-test coverage. The focused footer file reproduced all seven failures before the assertion update and now passes all nine tests (2.21 seconds test duration, about 5 seconds invocation wall time).

After

![After: clear canvas above the mobile composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/630b6401-79bb-48e9-a35f-9a8bbff06bd5)

prs.title: fix(irc): SecretRef IRC passwords fail validation and service-only NickServ overrides skip the inherited ref
prs.body:
Closes #176238

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IRC config validation rejects a SecretRef on `password` / `nickserv.password` (even though the secret contract and docs support it), and an account whose `nickserv` block only sets other fields (e.g. `service`) never gets the inherited top-level `nickserv.password` ref resolved.

## User Impact

User impact: IRC server and NickServ passwords can be supplied as SecretRefs at the channel or account level, and service-only NickServ overrides keep identifying with the inherited password instead of an unresolved ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The IRC config schema and `IrcAccountConfig` types now use the shared secret-input schema/type for `password` and `nickserv.password`.
- The top-level NickServ inheritance predicate in `secret-contract.ts` now follows the same field-by-field merge that `resolveIrcAccount` uses: the top-level ref is active unless the account sets its own `nickserv.password`, and `enabled` is read from the merged block.
- Regenerated the bundled channel config metadata and config baseline.

## Evidence

- New tests: `extensions/irc/src/config-schema.test.ts` (SecretRef accepted at all four password paths) and `extensions/irc/src/secret-contract.test.ts` (service-only override resolves the inherited ref end to end through `resolveIrcAccount`; an account-owned password keeps the top-level ref inactive; inherited `enabled: false` stays inactive).
- `vitest` on `extensions/irc`: on `main` 5 of the new tests fail (2 files); with this change 21 files / 144 tests pass.
- `scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` passes.
- Gap: I couldn't finish a local tsgo run (my machine ran out of memory), so I'm relying on CI for the typecheck.

## Real behavior proof (branch CLI, head f457bd72b)

Run from this branch with `node scripts/run-node.mjs`, each scenario in a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Secret values are throwaway env vars and are redacted; IRC points at `127.0.0.1:16667` with nothing listening, and `channels status` runs without `--probe`, so it reports config-only status.

| Scenario | `config validate` | `secrets audit` | `channels status --channel irc` |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 channel `password` ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 | default enabled, configured |
| S2 `accounts.work.password` ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 | default + work enabled, configured |
| S3 `accounts.work.nickserv = { service }` only, top-level nickserv password ref | valid | clean, unresolved=0 (inherited ref resolved) | default + work enabled, configured, no secret warning |
| S4 top-level `nickserv.enabled=false`, account nickserv password ref to an unset env var | valid | unresolved=2 (see note) | both refs reported inactive ("NickServ is disabled for this account"), no resolve failure |
| S5 same as S4 plus `accounts.work.nickserv.enabled=true` | valid | unresolved=2 | account ref is active, so the missing env var is reported |
| main, S1 config | `channels.irc.password: must be string`, exit 1 | config invalid | config invalid |

Note on S4: `secrets audit` statically resolves every configured SecretRef regardless of whether its owner is active (`collectConfigSecrets` in `src/secrets/audit.ts` doesn't consult activity), so it flags the unset env var for every channel, not just IRC. The runtime path, shown by `channels status`, honors the inherited disablement.

Upgrade / existing data: I installed the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` into an isolated prefix and created a state dir with an existing IRC setup using plain string passwords (channel, NickServ, and one account). 2026.10.5 validates it, then this branch's CLI validates the same state dir and `channels status` lists both IRC accounts as enabled and configured. The config file's sha256 is identical before and after both runs and `diff` is empty, so existing string credentials keep loading unchanged. One caveat: the npm 2026.10.5 build reports the IRC plugin as a missing external plugin, so on that version the IRC fields are only schema-validated, not exercised.

prs.title: refactor(ui): route shell navigation directly to its owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shell navigation passed through eight forwarding methods even though an existing navigation owner already implements every operation.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Routes, shortcuts, recovery, focus, tags, and lazy imports retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing navigation owner as a readonly capability and let its callers use it directly. Remove the forwarding methods and duplicate interface signatures. Native/readiness consumers still use their existing application-context contract; callbacks retain the correct receiver, including not-found recovery. Chrome and command-palette ownership is unchanged.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| `app-host`, `app-host-navigation-focus`, and `app-shell-command-palette-loading` tests | 53 passed, one worker |
| Targeted type-aware lint and formatting | Passed |
| Independent P2 review with affected source and readiness context | Clean, no findings |
| Full CI on final head `5e1d3b3d646` | [39861984186](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39861984186): success |
| Same-machine startup/route comparison | Pass: startup 315,746 B gzip / 7 JS requests / 1 CSS request; Chat −98 B and New Session −94 B versus base; request counts and CSS unchanged |
| Production Knip | Same pre-existing export/type findings as campaign baseline; no new findings |

Production LOC across touched modules: **4,066 → 4,045 (−21)**. Changed test/support LOC: **3,615 → 3,616 (+1)**. No new tests or runtime abstractions. The Solid refactor checklist's effects, lifecycle, async state, manual loading and owner-API counts are unchanged. No rendered markup or CSS changes, so there is no visual difference to capture. Full UI CI is requested for this shared shell change.

## CI repair

The first full CI run (39857768757) found two test fixtures still supplying the deleted forwarding fields: the keyboard-shortcut New Session fixture and the Gateway retained-pane lifecycle fixture. Both now supply the existing navigation owner. The New Session and Gateway consumers require only the methods they use through `Pick`; full shell consumers retain the full owner. There is no runtime fallback.

The nine keyboard-shortcut cases, the exact Gateway lifecycle test, both failed core test-type configurations, UI typecheck, and targeted lint/format checks pass. A fresh isolated P2 review is clean. All four repaired production modules have identical emitted runtime ASTs to the previous head, so the existing startup/route measurements remain applicable.

prs.title: fix: avoid false failures during node session discovery
prs.body:
Related: #172473

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading discovery failures and disappearing previously loaded conversations when native session discovery is slow or temporarily fails.

## User Impact

Slow conversation discovery no longer looks like a failure or removes conversations and pages that are already visible. Confirmed successful responses remain authoritative, including empty results and removed hosts.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use `catalog.pending` for normal waiting; retain a previous real error until recovery.
- Keep the original caller's authorization until admitted native work settles. Revoked callers remain rejected; later requests cannot lend authority to older work.
- Preserve loaded rows on host/catalog failures. The explicit native `node:registry` / `NODE_LIST_FAILED` marker preserves omitted paired nodes while fresh local results remain authoritative.
- Preserve expanded pages and cursors through pending/failed reads without adding polling or repeated-cursor loops.
- Reuse the existing error indicator for a failure before any rows load. Successful empty and owner-filtered catalogs stay hidden.

This also covers #172508's pending-warning behavior, including pagination. That alternative remains open.

## Evidence

### Before / after

Same synthetic catalog failure after loading a conversation. Before is main `3cd9bdd`; after is this PR's validated production tree.

| Before: loaded conversation disappears | After: conversation retained, real error indicated |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main: catalog disappears after discovery failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c477d056-90c2-4e47-946b-d7cff5f897df) | ![PR: loaded conversation retained with existing error indicator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32c7ea55-fc27-4be3-afc6-fb047a4567b2) |

### Integrated caller-authority verification at `baa4fe2f`

[Inspectable reproduction patch and results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171870#issuecomment-6352601854) now cover the real authenticated dispatcher, catalog handler, plugin node runtime and `NodeRegistry`, with synthetic node transport.

- The same positive-case test passes on this head and fails on actual main base `cd982fce` because the original caller's authority expires before delayed node dispatch.
- Revoking A before dispatch blocks its request even while its signal remains un-aborted; B, with the same profile/device/query on a separate connection, keeps its own authority.
- Revocation after dispatch prevents late catalog publication. Delivery expiry sends a matching cancellation, rejects a late reply, and releases retained work.
- Three cases passed in the expanded run; the expiry case passed in a focused retest after correcting its expected cancellation frame. No production code changed. This verification overlay is not added to ordinary CI; command cost was 40–54 seconds, mostly transformation/import overhead.

### Maintainer-supplied validation at `b89b8d2`

- Six Chromium scenarios passed through the actual UI and synthetic Gateway boundary: loaded host/catalog failures, pending recovery, replacement/empty results, cached discovery, expanded-page replay/Load More, and the real native producer's inventory-failure result. A long error did not widen the sidebar.
- 115 focused Gateway/protocol/UI cases passed across the initial run and affected-file retest. They cover identity/scope replacement, revocation, late work, hidden-panel delivery and cursor cycles. Five performance/lifecycle cases passed.
- Five old assertions expected an empty failed catalog to stay hidden. Three assertion sites now require the error indicator and zero rows; request counts, cursors and recovery checks remain. The 22-test file passed in 6.93s wall time.
- Final format, targeted Oxlint, and core/core-test/UI type checks passed. Independent source review found no unresolved defect.

### Revision-bound performance

Same isolated Linux instance class and toolchain, 3,000 synthetic stored conversations, 100 warm reads:

| Measurement | Main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| p50 / p95 | 3.26 / 4.65 ms | 3.06 / 3.78 ms |
| Worker reads | 100 | 100 |
| Native RPC / file reads during warm reads | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Standalone heap after 1,000 settled operations | 20.02 MB | 20.03 MB |
| Retained roots / subscriptions after settlement | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

### Current integrated revision

prs.title: refactor(clients): remove unserved private inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Client and channel internals expose arguments, alternate forms and result metadata that no production caller selects or consumes.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or required action. Config, CLI, Gateway protocol, SDK and persisted contracts stay unchanged. Phase E is untouched.

## What Changed

Use the serving values directly for UI completion/publication, private Beam requests, Mattermost draft cadence, Nostr/Zalouser ingress, Telegram question resolution/webhook registration, browser Doctor and the private QA tool report. Remove their unserved argument forms and orphan plumbing. Keep real authorization, retry, receipt, delivery, resource bounds and ordinary concurrency/durability behavior. Tests use scoped module spies only where cheaper than the retired seam.

This is an area split under campaign rule 11. The surviving cut removes **88 production lines and 19 test/support lines across 47 files**. The already-landed runtime and host areas removed 258 and 115 production lines; the retained family totals 461. A separate 45-line portion is parked for proof, not counted as landed or included in this PR's surviving cleanup.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. Only unsupported private argument forms and permanently unselected branches retire; supported serving behavior remains. Whole-tree callers, runtime export surfaces and provenance were checked before each cut. Completed features are preserved, not treated as dormant preparation.

Public QA heartbeat options, command environment and discovery phase arguments were excluded after checking actual JavaScript/DSL reachability. Narrow TypeScript facades are not treated as runtime stripping. Beam's distinct sender/receiver clocks also remain because a shared clock mock would change the test's real clock domains.

## CI Repair and Scope Reduction

Original head `5a485662695a375727d2d9428f0a35f19c5b26b5`, CI run `39858498437`, job `120103518653` failed the unchanged `otel-gateway-runtime.e2e.test.ts` linked success/failed-read telemetry test at its 120-second deadline. The other two invocations in that job passed. This is **not claimed as inherited**. The coordinator flake registry and the last six completed scheduled main runs did not establish a matching signature; one full-log download failed, and individual job evidence was used where available. The local proof budget excludes this E2E baseline replay.

Following rule 8, all 13 changed production files in the failing test's conservative static/literal-dynamic/type/export import closure were returned byte-for-byte to current main. Its one affected capability fixture also restores the existing explicit reconciliation input, preserving every assertion. The closure's 45 production lines are retained on `deslop/z28-parked-otel-reachable-20261015`, an original-head recovery snapshot, with no PR. Only those reachable hunks were dropped; the other client areas remain here. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, ignore or baseline was relaxed. No CI rerun was requested; the repaired exact head receives its normal CI run.

## Evidence

Original assembly replayed without conflicts onto main `a1df0148036bc63e98605e40b1b1b82d66c44b80`. The surviving owners retain the same-input per-cut focused proof and independent aggregate review. Fresh Beam projection/mirror/real-receiver and private-report proof passed 50 cases across four files/three shards in 67.15s. Earlier aggregate native no-emit types, canonical-root lint, formatting, runtime/Madge zero cycles and all 33 suppression/wrapper guards passed. The initial explicit hidden-JavaScript lint selector error and its correction remain recorded: maintained Node assets are outside the canonical TS-root lint policy; both syntax checks and their 28-case fixture proof pass, without policy/source/suppression changes.

Fresh repair native no-emit types pass. All ten affected owner/consumer files pass 81 cases across five shards in 50.76s; two existing Linux-only process-boundary cases are unrun on macOS and remain assigned to CI. All fourteen restored source/fixture paths pass typed lint and formatting; runtime/Madge cycles are zero. Suppression and wrapper import-closure guards pass all 33 cases across two files in 21.93s. Fresh independent repair P0-P2 review is scoped-clean. No source changed after review.

All local commands use isolated state, `nice -n 10`, one worker and serial heavy commands. Hosted exact-head `ci:full` supplies broad UI/overlay and E2E proof. No broad local suite, whole-graph typecheck, build, E2E, live deployment or performance gain is claimed.

prs.title: fix: open the keyboard when tapping the mobile composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: tapping the compact mobile chat composer can expand it without opening the keyboard.

## User Impact

User impact: a first tap focuses the existing text field before the composer moves. Drafts, selection, accessory menus, and desktop pointer behavior are preserved. No layout, configuration, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mobile pointer handler expanded the composer before native focus. Focus the retained, editable textarea synchronously in that same primary-pointer gesture, before changing presentation. Keep the existing disabled/read-only checks and native selection behavior.

The early expansion was introduced by the mobile-composer hunk of #175291 (commit 413d2fc66983d), which removed the already-focused condition added in #176498. This repair retains that drawer-recovery behavior rather than reverting it.

## Evidence

- Production-bundle touch regression is red on the original implementation (textarea not focused during pointerdown) and green with the fix; typing after the first tap works without sending.
- Composer pointer E2E: **5/5 pass**, covering touch, narrow/wide desktop, keyboard activation, send/stop, and canceled pointer activation. File test time 5.24 s; complete invocation including build 32.24 s.
- Focused Chromium/mobile unit coverage: **16/16 pass**. The existing mobile composer browser suite is now included in the WebKit lane. Local WebKit could not connect to its test session; physical iPhone/software-keyboard display remains unverified on this Linux host. CI must run the WebKit coverage.
- Production UI TypeScript, touched-file lint/format, controller ratchets, documentation glossary check, and whitespace checks pass.
- The wider editor/test TypeScript graph separately reported errors in untouched native-desktop and quota-reset fixtures; it is not claimed green.
- Independent GPT-6.1 Sol review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification: one focus call at the existing interaction owner; no new state, effects, listeners, or rendering owners. Production delta +1 line; test/runner delta +34 lines.

Reported by @steipete.
