prs.title: fix(compaction): hydrate the bounded model-context view for compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction on a long-lived session fails every time with `worker task timed out waiting for host callback transcript-hydration-chunk`, and the recovery notice sends users to `/compact` and `/new`, which hit the same failure. Daily reset and `/new` keep the session id, so the archive behind every reset stays in one transcript; the reporter's Telegram DM session held about 130k events (~530 MB) after 17 days and 19 resets.

Fixes #180514.

## User Impact

Compaction no longer loads the entire saved conversation before starting; in the runs below that removed the history-loading timeout. It now loads the same limited history window a normal turn uses. The previous summary gets priority over older messages in the recent history, provided it fits within the loading limit; a saved summary larger than the whole limit (possible only after switching to a model whose window is far smaller than the one that wrote it) stays out, as it already does for turns. Older messages, including previously retained context, can fall outside that window and therefore outside the new summary; they remain saved on disk and reachable through session history. The summary-priority rule lives in the two history readers that turns and compaction share, so an ordinary turn whose recent history alone fills its window now also keeps the latest boundary and drops its oldest loaded message instead; the turn's own context selection already reserved that boundary when it was present. When all relevant history fits within the loading limits, the summary input is unchanged. Overflow recovery has worked on this window since #147202. A larger bounded cap for compaction (the loader's ceilings, 10,000 events / 64 MiB) would fold older stretches more often without changing the shape of the change; it still could not promise that everything fits, so this PR keeps the attempt limits and leaves the choice to the owners.

Measured at 20k events the manual path is slower end to end (3.6 s to 4.4 s); larger sessions improve, and the CPU-limited cases complete instead of timing out (table below). On the bounded view the compaction session can append a `thinking_level_change` control entry when the latest selection sits outside the loaded window, as an attempt already does.

Stored data, schemas, reset semantics and retention are unchanged. No config option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three compaction entry points opened an unbounded `SessionManager`: preflight and byte-guard compaction (`executePreparedCompactionSession`), manual Gateway compaction (`sessionManagerOpenCompaction` behind `sessions.compact`), and the CLI-harness pre-turn compaction (`runCliTurnCompactionLifecycle`). A full read streams every stored row through the history worker under the request runner's default 60 s budget; `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` only arms the compaction watchdog and never reaches that read.

Ordinary attempts and overflow recovery (#147202) hydrate the bounded model-context view instead: `resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits(contextTokenBudget)`, a byte-capped tail that keeps reset-retained entries and injects the latest boundary when they fit. Compaction does not need the entire archive; this change loads that same window.

<details>
<summary>What changed in the code</summary>

- All three compaction opens pass the attempt limits, derived from the foreground session budget, never from the summarizer model's ceiling, so a smaller summarization model cannot shrink the window the next turn sees. The budget comes from the caller's `contextTokenBudget` (preflight passes the session's window), else the session entry's recorded `contextTokens`, else the foreground model's catalog projection (`resolveModelContextTokenProjection`, the same owner the session row uses), so a catalog-only large-context model keeps its window. The queued path resolves that before `resolveCompactionRuntimeSelection` replaces provider and model with the configured summarizer, and carries it as the caller budget; the prepared runtime, which may already hold the summarizer, falls back only to the recorded window, then the queued `tokenBudget`. Manual compaction requires the limits; the Gateway runner resolves them the same way.
- The worker reads the compaction session facts (`entry`, `runtimeEntry`, `primaryConversation`) inside the bounded read's snapshot (`readSessionCompactionPreparation`), and no longer on the full stream path. The bounded `PreparedSessionTranscriptHydration` variant carries `compaction`.
- `sessionManagerOpenCompaction` builds a bounded manager and reports `eventCount` as the session's active event count.
- Both bounded readers (`session-accessor.sqlite-active-context.ts`, `session-actor-bounded-history.ts`), which turns and compaction share, reserve the latest boundary ahead of the tail: when the newest turns alone fill the byte cap, the oldest of them give way so the previous compaction summary is loaded. This changes what an ordinary turn's raw view holds in that one case as well; its canonical selection already expected the boundary first. #168157 (c16bff1978ba) made the canonical replay (`selectBoundedModelRequests`) reserve that summary and left the raw resident view, which `getBranch()` serves to `prepareCompaction`, injecting the boundary only when it still fit. For an attempt that was harmless (replay re-selects from the view); for compaction it meant a cap-filling tail dropped `previousSummary`. A saved summary larger than the whole cap (possible only after switching to a model whose window is far smaller than the one that wrote it) still stays out of the bounded view, as it already does for every turn on main; compaction then summarizes the tail without it, where the base's full read folded it in. This is an accepted edge case rather than a cap that follows the boundary's size: the cap is what keeps the read bounded, that summary has already fallen out of every turn the session makes, and the stored entry is untouched. Follow-up: let `/compact` take the latest boundary's size as the floor of its read so a model switch can shrink an oversized summary.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/compaction.md` says what compaction loads and that older context the cap omits is not folded into the summary.

</details>

## Evidence

Regression (`compact.delegate.test.ts`): a session with 40 archived turns behind a reset; queued manual compaction with a 200k foreground budget and a 128k summarizer model makes one `transcript-hydration` request carrying the 200k attempt limits (not the summarizer's), kind `bounded`, loads fewer than half the events while `totalEvents` counts the archive, commits one compaction entry, leaves the archive on disk, and keeps archived text out of the model context. A second row passes no caller budget and records a 1,000,000-token window on the session entry: the request carries the 1,000,000-token limits, not the queued budget the summarizer model produced. A third row records nothing and configures `compaction.model` to a 32k summarizer while the foreground model's catalog entry says 1,000,000: the request still carries the 1,000,000-token limits (red when the projection runs after the summarizer swap: 256 KiB). Second case: `prepareGatewaySessionCompaction` on an entry whose recorded context window is 1,000,000 tokens opens the bounded view with the 1,000,000-token limits (8 MB), not a default, reports the whole active count and the session facts from that snapshot, and keeps the archive out of the model context. All fail on the base (full read, no limits).

Summary reservation: reader-level cases for the SQLite reader (`session-accessor.sqlite-bounded-context.test.ts`) and the in-memory reader (`session-actor-bounded-history.test.ts`) put a compaction summary behind a tail that exactly fills the cap and expect the summary in the window with the oldest tail entry dropped and `truncated` set; both fail without the reservation (`[session, middle, new]`). End to end (`compact.delegate.test.ts`): a session with a ~320 KB earlier summary and three ~500 KB live turns under a 200k budget (1.6 MB view) compacts on the bounded view and the summarizer request carries that earlier summary; without the reservation the view holds the three turns and no summary, and the request lacks it.

Consumer suites on `d1f61e5769e`: compact.delegate, compact.queued-successor, compact.hooks, compaction-session-execution, the session reader suites (bounded context, actor kernel, replica, residency, memory transcript, projection facts, byte size, message rewrite), session-manager-async-entries, session-manager-hydration-stream, session-manager-model-context, session-manager-model-context-prefix, session-model-context-window, session-transcript-worker-readers, cli-compaction, run.compaction-runtime, chat-send-compaction-handoff, session-boundary-prompt-cache-key: 19 files, 248 tests green. `tsgo` core, extensions, `core.test.agents-other`, `core.test.agents-sessions` and `test:root` lanes green on the head (`aa792278ab3`); type-aware oxlint on the changed files, 0 warnings.

### Real behavior proof (isolated shipped Gateway, stub model, no credentials)

Base: `8eb23c34e440674900802e19e7336a0cf254f88b` (main). This branch: `d1f61e5769e`, built and run after the last code change; the head commit on top of it (`aa792278ab3`) changes one test file only. Config: `agents.defaults.compaction: { mode: "safeguard", timeoutSeconds: 300, maxActiveTranscriptBytes: "2mb" }`, model `contextWindow: 200000`, everything else default. A session grown through the real transcript writer with reset boundaries every ~6,800 events, the way daily reset keeps one session id: 130,000 events, 19 resets, 1,013 MB store. Each variant ran against a copy of the same state in a no-network container on an 8-vCPU VM: `openclaw sessions compact` through the Gateway, then a turn through a fresh Gateway on another copy so the byte guard compacts before the model call. Every row is a single run. Phases are the Gateway's own `[sessions/lifecycle]` diagnostic (prepare = transcript open, run = guard size read + summarizer + persistence).

| 130k events, 1 GB store | base | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| manual compact, 8 CPUs: prepare / run | 4,826 / 2,505 ms (RPC 7.9 s) | 796 / 4,309 ms (RPC 5.8 s) |
| byte-guard turn, 8 CPUs: wall time | 17 s, 2 summary requests | 14 s, 2 summary requests |
| Gateway peak RSS (manual / turn) | 2,825 / 3,489 MB | 2,331 / 3,046 MB |
| manual compact, 0.3 CPU | `worker task timed out` (prepare 60,102 ms, RPC 70.8 s) | compacted (prepare 7,004 / run 76,303 ms, RPC 92.4 s) |
| byte-guard turn, 0.3 CPU | preflight compaction fails, reply after 280 s | compacts, reply after 185 s |

The 0.3 CPU rows reproduce the report on the base and not on this branch:

```
# base, manual /compact
[sessions/lifecycle] ... operation=compaction ... phaseDurationsMs={"prepare":60102,"run":0,"finalize":0}
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.compact 70811ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=worker task timed out
# base, byte-guard turn
[agent/embedded] [compaction-diag] end ... trigger=budget provider=stub/stub-compaction attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=timeout
[auto-reply/preflight-compaction] preflight compaction failed: worker task timed out
# this branch, same state, same 0.3 CPU
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.compact 92400ms   (compact.json: "compacted": true)
byte-guard turn: two summary requests, no failure lines, reply delivered
```

Differing foreground and summarizer budgets, same state, 8 CPUs, manual compaction with `agents.defaults.compaction.model` set to a second stub model (every summary request in the stub log went to that model):

| foreground window | summarizer window | base prepare / run | this branch prepare / run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2,000,000 tokens (16 MiB cap) | 32,000 tokens | 8,485 / 2,968 ms | 345 / 6,093 ms |
| 32,000 tokens (256 KiB cap) | 2,000,000 tokens | 8,556 / 2,885 ms | 273 / 6,127 ms |

The open phase is the bounded read sized from the foreground window in both rows; the summarizer's window does not change it, and the base reads everything either way.

<details>
<summary>Where the remaining time goes, and smaller sessions</summary>

An earlier local revision of this branch with the same bounded-view change, before the summary reservation and the foreground-budget derivation, measured the size curve (prepare / run ms): 20k events (160 MB) base 1,052 / 2,555 vs 347 / 4,069; 60k (475 MB) base 2,234 / 2,192 vs 264 / 3,737; 130k on 1 CPU base 25,306 / 7,201 vs 1,279 / 20,110; the base at 0.4 CPU failed the same way as at 0.3 CPU. The open phase grows with stored history on the base and stays flat on this branch.

The run phase is larger on this branch at every size. The likely cause, inferred from the timing split before the summarizer is called: the guard's size read (`maxActiveTranscriptBytes`) scans the stored rows and now runs on a cold cache the full read used to warm. Measured separately on the same store, that read takes 13.6 s cold and 16 ms warm. It already runs before every guarded turn on the base and is unchanged here (follow-up: maintain the active size incrementally). Direct reads of the same store: full hydration 130,026 events, +600 MB heap, 6–10 s; bounded view 363 events, +5 MB, 96 ms once the database is open.

The archive stays on disk after compaction (`totalEvents` unchanged, rows intact), and the following turn delivers normally.

</details>

### Real-model compact-and-continue (`d1f61e5769e`, Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5`, isolated Gateway on a laptop)

The same flow with a real provider, so the summaries and the answer come from the model (`real-model.sh` in the gist; key from the environment only):

1. A real turn creates the session; the archive grows through the real writer: 2,400 events, 3 resets (the daily-reset shape).
2. A real turn plants a fact ("the launch code word is PERIWINKLE"), a filler turn follows, then 60 ordinary events so the fact sits behind the kept-recent turns. Manual `/compact` through the Gateway writes summary 1 in 16 s; it contains the code word.
3. 600 more events (about 2.4 MB) are appended after summary 1, so the recent tail alone fills the 1.6 MB window of a 200k model. Manual `/compact` writes summary 2 in 11 s from summary 1 plus that tail; it still contains the code word, which only summary 1 held.
4. A real turn asks "What is the launch code word? Answer with the word only." The reply is `PERIWINKLE`.

Measured on the saved state after step 4: the full read is 3,092 events in 3.2 s; the bounded read at the model's window is 334 events in 47 ms, with the same 23 context messages (summary 2, the kept turns, the question). The tail that compaction 2 had to summarize was larger than its window, and the previous summary survived it.

Not exercised: a real Telegram client. Reproduction scripts (generator, stub model, run script, real-model script, hydration measurement): https://gist.github.com/sukhdeepjohar/44aeb2dedc4851fe9e269c2aa8e1e742

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve steered turns after final replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up submitted while native Codex delivers an earlier final reply can be cancelled before consumption. Preserving the native turn alone is insufficient: the earlier reply can also suppress the follow-up answer, and discarding its terminal optimization can lose a successful sibling `sessions_yield`.

Related: #147759 (same warning, different reported lifecycle). This does not claim to fix #176028 or stale native-thread ownership.

## Repair

- Preserve native ownership after steering submission, including when its consumption receipt precedes the release check.
- Reset current-input final-reply suppression on confirmed steering consumption. Remember suppressed assistant item identities so terminal snapshots cannot resurrect A's redundant coda; identical text in a later answer remains valid.
- Project current-input delivery state in normal attempt finalization, independently of runtime-refresh transcript options. Historical send receipts remain available for side-effect accounting.
- Preserve independent successful terminal actions beside a final reply, including nested Code Mode yields and both sibling completion orders.

No configuration, schema, migration, dependency, or public SDK changes. Ordinary non-steered final replies retain their existing behavior.

Current head: `ddf42e31bd57b1dd365e5ff61e3a8db6b46cc1ce`. Production repair: `8f47d9275520a09101a65c35adebd4ca13c4eb81`; the follow-up adds only the missing full-suite test registration.

## Evidence

### Actual Gateway evidence

An isolated Gateway built from this candidate ran native Codex 0.160.0 against a real model, with the repository's QA HTTP channel transport and synthetic messages. Model responses were not mocked. Automatic reply visibility was explicitly configured because the continuation deliberately uses ordinary assistant text.

The fixture holds A's successful delivery receipt, submits B through the Gateway, verifies native `turn/steer` acceptance, then releases A's receipt and checks actual outbound messages. Conversation history alone is not treated as delivery proof.

Sanitized observed sequence:

```text
PROOF gateway-agent-ready
PROOF first-answer-delivered-receipt-held
PROOF steer-ack {"runId":"proof-steer-b","status":"started","messageSeq":3}
PROOF native-steer-accepted-before-release
PROOF outbound-on-settlement [{"text":"PROOF_ANSWER_A"},{"text":"PROOF_ANSWER_B"}]
PROOF outbound [{"text":"PROOF_ANSWER_A","direction":"outbound"},{"text":"PROOF_ANSWER_B","direction":"outbound"}]
Test Files 1 passed
Tests 1 passed
```

The prior repair candidate, with the same automatic-visibility fixture, delivered only A and failed the B outbound assertion. This exposed a real finalizer integration gap: a delivery-state override was incorrectly gated on a refresh-only transcript option. The revised candidate above passed in 20.262 seconds of test execution (58.81 seconds total).

This is actual Gateway/native/model/channel-transport proof, not a Telegram-service deployment test. No live Gateway was modified or restarted for these runs.

## Regression and review evidence

- Four regressions fail on published head `1138b4424ffa0ea4aba72752b0def5b41d540dcb`: two P1 consumption/release orderings and two P2 sibling completion orderings.
- The repaired candidate passed 91 scoped lifecycle/projector/steering/finalization tests. Direct and nested terminal-sibling controls are included.
- A further normal-finalizer regression failed on the initial repair (`sourceReplyDeliveryState` absent) and passed after the propagation fix. The affected nine-case suite and seven generation-finalization consumer tests pass.
- Targeted lint/type checks pass. Production runtime rebuild passes.
- Independent shared Auto Review completed on the revised candidate. Its machine result was `findings`, not `scoped-clean`: an INDEX-only finding was repaired in the working tree and that reviewed content was staged; a later-final-send early-release finding was declined as the existing, explicit native-completion tradeoff below. An earlier admission-versus-consumption finding was rejected after inspecting the pinned native tool-drain contract.

### CI registration correction

Exact-head CI exposed an omitted full-suite inventory entry for the new steering regression. The ownership assertion was reproduced red, then the suite was registered beside the existing lifecycle-controller suite. All 32 configuration tests and all 6 steering tests under their assigned database-worker lane now pass locally; format and diff checks pass. Fresh hosted CI is pending on the corrected head. Production code and the Gateway-proven artifact are unchanged.

## Native contract and tradeoff

Pinned Codex `rust-v0.160.0`: `a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc`.

- [Native pending-input drain](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L430).
- [Tools are drained before sampling returns](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L3145).
- [Native follow-up decision includes pending input](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L551).
- [Interrupt clears pending input](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs#L536).

ClawSweeper revision 2 accepted the main delivery proof and confirmed both original findings addressed. Its remaining test-registration finding is repaired above. Upstream lifecycle-owner acceptance of the following tradeoff is still required; the bot recommends accepting it.

Once steering is submitted, a final message send does not use the host's early-terminal optimization; the turn finishes through the existing native loop. This also applies to a later final send answering the steer. Independent explicit yield remains authoritative. No retry loop or new persisted owner is introduced. Consumption acknowledgement is not treated as proof of an answer. No exactly-once guarantee or fix for unrelated late-finalization races is claimed.

## Remaining coverage limits

The live two-answer run exercises native admission before A's held tool receipt. Receipt-before/after release-check permutations and final-reply-plus-yield sibling orders have deterministic regression coverage; two additional bounded real-model yield-control attempts delivered A and B but omitted the requested `sessions_yield` call. Therefore successful final-send-plus-yield is proven by the direct/nested regression controls, not by the live Gateway run. Those attempts do not establish a dropped successful yield; this remains an explicit live-proof gap.

The earlier runtime deployment attempt rolled back; this PR is not deployed to the live installation.

prs.title: fix: preserve assistant answers when media delivery reuses response indexes
prs.body:
Closes #166536

## What Problem This Solves

Earlier assistant responses can lose media, or later responses can be suppressed, when retries reuse content indexes or distinct responses repeat the same text/image. Each physical response must retain its own delivery and transcript identity; provider content and signatures must remain intact.

## Evidence

Current hosted head is `336ccde048234e74a873980e03fe788ff18ec76b`. Hosted checks apply to that tree and do **not** cover the unpublished current-main correction below. Current check status is visible on the PR’s Checks tab.

Upstream #177049 (`0d7df3fc2cf6bc9c53b04f7857b7cbca61b3c927`) now supplies the canonical `AgentAssistantSourceReceipt` and exact transcript anchor. The hosted branch needs reconciliation with that owner. A local ancestry-preserving correction integrates main `cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de`, removes the competing receipt pipeline, and retains the residual occurrence-aware dedupe, aggregate coverage, streamed-media and timeout-recovery fixes. It also keeps TTS supplements from replacing source images. **Local commit `3e57cec961f9821b985b5775cb75a1361c54f7f3` is not published or available from this PR branch.**

Local correction validation: full affected gateway suites 149/149 passed with no skips; commentary media 18/18 passed; focused agent/autoreply and recovery suites passed; type-aware lint and production core typecheck passed. Fresh independent committed-candidate review completed scoped-clean at P2 after real transcript regressions reproduced and repaired TTS selection, append-key and owned-rewrite losses. These are local boundary results, not hosted CI or live Telegram proof.

Publication is held at the native workflow: this merge needs a verified commit signer, which is unavailable on the checked authoring hosts. The correction review retains `NEEDS DISCUSSION`; no signing override, raw push or merge was attempted. Once published, exact-candidate hosted CI and the mandatory Telegram Test Server proof must be established.

The [existing live-QA handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#issuecomment-6087119969) remains outstanding. No broker credential pair or ready launcher is available on either checked host, and no live lease was allocated. Earlier real local model/media/compaction observations and historical CI describe their recorded earlier heads; they do not certify this correction or replace the required reused-index Telegram scenario.

prs.title: fix(tooling): run line-cap hooks in code-only worktrees
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes commit-hook failures in code-only worktrees when the line-cap check cannot load TypeScript dependencies or selects a stale oxlint executable from the canonical checkout.

## User Impact

Developers can commit from code-only worktrees using an already-qualified tooling checkout without installing or linking dependencies into the worktree. Line-cap enforcement still checks staged contents. There is no Gateway runtime change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ratchet now uses the existing qualified tooling loader and runs the admitted oxlint package's own CLI with the same Node executable. Package identity, exact-version admission, physical containment, and hook freshness checks remain enforced.

This PR contains only the tooling fix, its regressions, and one documentation clarification.

## Evidence

- Fixed focused proof covers 92 distinct cases across the affected tooling and hook suites, including staged growth despite an under-cap working file, stale versions, foreign repositories, and escaping CLI paths.

prs.title: fix(infra): stop shadowing real session-work counters in safe-restart preflight
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createSafeGatewayRestartPreflight()` shadowed six of the snapshot's inspectors with literal zeros placed **after** the caller spread:

```ts
const snapshot = createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot({
  ...inspectors,
  getSessionAdmissions: () => 0,
  getSessionMutations: () => 0,
  getChatRuns: () => 0,
  getQueuedTurns: () => 0,
  getTerminalPersistence: () => 0,
  getTerminalSessions: () => 0,
});
```

`createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot` already defaults `getSessionAdmissions` to the live `getSessionControllerWorkCount()` and `getSessionMutations` to `getSessionMutationCount()`. The post-spread zeros clobbered those defaults (and would clobber any caller-supplied inspectors for those keys), so the safe-restart preflight was blind to in-flight session admissions and lifecycle mutations.

## Fix

- Pass caller inspectors through untouched: `createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot(inspectors)`. The snapshot defaults provide the live session counters; `getChatRuns` / `getQueuedTurns` / `getTerminalPersistence` / `getTerminalSessions` keep their zero defaults.
- Project `sessionAdmissions` and `sessionMutations` into the returned `counts` and include them in `totalActive`, so `safe` now respects session work.
- Derive `summary` from `safe`: a session-only deferral previously produced an empty `blockers` list together with a "safe to restart now" summary; it now reports `restart deferred: active session work`.
- Extend `SafeRestartInspectors` with the six session keys so callers/tests can pass them.

## Evidence

**Production timeline (observed before the fix):** `gateway.restart.safe` reported "safe to restart now" and scheduled the restart immediately while session work was active, returning an empty `blockers` list. After the fix, the same session-work conditions produce `safe: false`, a populated `counts` entry for `sessionAdmissions`/`sessionMutations`, `totalActive > 0`, and the summary `restart deferred: active session work`.

**Regression repro (fails before, passes after):**

- Active session admissions: `getSessionAdmissions: () => 3` → `safe: false`, with `counts.sessionAdmissions` respected and `totalActive` including it. On the previous code the literal-zero stub clobbered the override, so the preflight stayed safe.
- Active session lifecycle mutations: `getSessionMutations: () => 2` → same shape (`safe: false`, count projected, `totalActive` includes it). Also fails on the previous code for the same reason.
- Existing assertions updated for the two newly projected counts.

**Suites run:**

- `src/infra/restart-coordinator.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/restart.test.ts`

Result: 24/24 passing, two consecutive clean runs. No code changes accompany this body update.

prs.title: feat(cli): show plugin trust status in plugins list output
prs.body:
Closes #178411

## What Problem This Solves

Installing a third-party plugin grants it access to tools, hooks, channels and providers inside the gateway, so whether a plugin is officially trusted or not is a security-relevant signal. But `openclaw plugins list` never showed trust status in either the table or verbose output — a user scanning their plugin list could not tell official/trusted plugins from third-party ones without running `openclaw plugins inspect <id>` on each one individually.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PluginRecord.trust` (with a `reason`) is already recorded and canonical, but the list renderer omitted it. This adds a compact trust label to `openclaw plugins list`: a `Trust` column in the table and a `trust:` line in verbose output, both derived from `plugin.trust.reason`. This follows the project's existing `skills search` convention of showing a trust label in list output. Rendering-only change; trust evaluation and install policy are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users reviewing their installed plugins can now see at a glance whether each plugin is `bundled`, `trusted-official`, or untrusted (`provenance-missing`, `install-path-mismatch`, etc.) directly in `openclaw plugins list` — no need to inspect each plugin individually.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI run from an isolated state directory with a bundled plugin (`amazon-bedrock`) and a third-party config-sourced plugin (`community-tool`, no install record):

Table output (default view, `FORCE_COLOR=1`):

```
│ Name              │ ID                 │ Format   │ Status  │ Source                   │ Version   │ Trust          │
│ Community Tool    │ community-tool     │ openclaw │ enabled │ /tmp/…/community-tool/.. │ 0.4.1     │ record-missing │
│ Amazon Bedrock    │ amazon-bedrock     │ openclaw │ enabled │ …/amazon-bedrock/index.. │ 2026.10.5 │ bundled        │
```

Verbose output (`--verbose`, `FORCE_COLOR=1`):

```
Community Tool (community-tool) enabled
  format: openclaw
  source: /tmp/oc-proof-178483/plugins/community-tool/index.ts
  origin: config
  version: 0.4.1
  trust: record-missing          ← yellow (theme.warn)

Amazon Bedrock (amazon-bedrock) enabled
  format: openclaw
  source: …/amazon-bedrock/index.ts
  origin: bundled
  version: 2026.10.5
  trust: bundled                 ← green (theme.success)
  providers: amazon-bedrock
```

Trust label coloring follows `formatPluginTrustLabel`: `bundled` and `trusted-official` route through `theme.success` (green `\x1b[32m`); all other reasons route through `theme.warn` (yellow `\x1b[33m`). When no trust record exists the cell/line is omitted.

Reproduction:

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-178483 node openclaw.mjs plugins list
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-178483 node openclaw.mjs plugins list --verbose
```

Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-list-format.test.ts src/cli/plugins-list-command.test.ts` — 15 passed (10 format + 5 command). The format suite verifies each trust reason renders in verbose output and that trusted vs untrusted styling emit distinct ANSI sequences under forced color; the command suite verifies the table includes a `Trust` column with the recorded reasons.

Regression proof (red-on-base → green-on-fix): removing the `Trust` column from `plugins-list-command.ts` causes the table test to fail — `expected '┌───┬───┐' to contain 'trusted-official'` (column header and values absent from real rendered output). Restoring the column passes. The table test uses the real `renderTable` (only `getTerminalTableWidth` is stubbed to 120), covering column layout, width, and wrapping behavior.

prs.title: fix(gateway): cron wake prompts show as user messages in imported Claude CLI history
prs.body:
Related: #151962

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a cron reminder wakes a Claude CLI session, the internal "A scheduled reminder has been triggered..." (or "A scheduled cron event was triggered, but no event content was found...") prompt shows up as a user message in the chat history.

## User Impact

User impact: cron wake prompts no longer appear as user bubbles in Control UI/WebChat for sessions that import Claude CLI history. Real user messages, including ones that quote this text, stay visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat runner records cron wakes as internal system input (`sourceTool: "cron"`), the same as exec completions. The Claude CLI importer already hides the exec-completion and heartbeat prompts but not the cron ones, so Claude's native user row for a cron wake was kept as a human turn. The importer now matches the complete `buildCronEventPrompt` frames: the reminder form (fixed opening plus one of the two fixed closing instructions) and the no-content form (fixed opening sentence). Only prompts that start with the producer's opening sentence are hidden.

This is the cron sibling of the exec-completion prompts in #151962; the broader phantom-turn reports there are not addressed here.

## Evidence

- Added the cron prompt variants (delivered, silent, no content, no content with the heartbeat response tool) to the existing `internalInputs` table in `cli-session-history.claude-input.test.ts`, which checks that the imported copy is hidden, that the turn is not counted as human, that quoted text inside a real message stays visible, and that a matching human row wins in the history merge.
- Without the source change, 5 tests fail (the four new cases and the file-based projection test that reuses the table). With it, `cli-session-history.claude-input`, `cli-session-history` and `cli-session-history.merge` pass (88/88) on Linux.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean on the two touched files.

### Runtime proof (running Gateway)

A real Gateway process (`openclaw gateway run`, isolated state dir, loopback port, token auth) with a session bound to Claude CLI whose project file (`~/.claude/projects/.../<id>.jsonl`) holds the rows below. History is read through the shipped CLI entry point: `openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"..."}'`. Output shows role and the first characters of each returned message.

Rows in the Claude project file: a real question and answer; the silent exec prompt; the silent exec prompt with heartbeat scratch; a cron reminder; a cron wake with no content; a periodic-task prompt; and two real user messages that quote a silent exec / cron prompt.

Before (upstream `main` b582963, Gateway 2026.10.4), 10 messages:
```
user      (local anchor)
user      What is the status of the deploy?
assistant The deploy finished.
user      An async command completion event was triggered, but user delivery is disabled
user      An async command completion event was triggered, but user delivery is disabled
user      A scheduled reminder has been triggered. The reminder content is: Stand-up rem
user      A scheduled cron event was triggered, but no event content was found. Reply wi
user      Run the following periodic tasks (only those due based on their intervals): -
user      Please explain this: An async command completion event was triggered, but user
user      What does this mean? A scheduled reminder has been triggered. The reminder con
```

After (same session data, Gateway rebuilt with #174780, #174798 and #174815 applied together), 5 messages:
```
user      (local anchor)
user      What is the status of the deploy?
assistant The deploy finished.
user      Please explain this: An async command completion event was triggered, but user
user      What does this mean? A scheduled reminder has been triggered. The reminder con
```

| Row | Hidden by |
|---|---|
| silent exec, silent exec + scratch | #174780 |
| cron reminder, cron without content | #174798 |
| periodic-task prompt | #174815 |

The two real user messages that quote an internal prompt stay visible. Nothing in this output is private; the session, transcript and Claude project file are synthetic.

prs.title: feat(openai): accept Codex v3 GPT-Live voices
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: choosing one of the newer Codex GPT-Live voices (for example `himari`) for `gpt-live-1-codex` silently falls back to `cove`.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk, Discord voice, and Voice Call on the Codex route can use the 16 voices Codex added to its realtime v3 list. The public `gpt-live-1` route and its voice list are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex expanded the realtime v3 (`gpt-live-1-codex`) voice list in openai/codex#52363 (`RealtimeVoicesList::builtin().v3` in `codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`, checked at openai/codex@6ae8b8aa7c60). It adds `aube`, `bubbie`, `haetsal`, `hanul`, `himari`, `leher`, `miko`, `neer`, `porto`, `rindo`, `rio`, `rivage`, `selva`, `sonna`, `tinta`, and `viola`. `OPENAI_GPT_LIVE_VOICES` still listed only the original nine, so `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoice` replaced the new names with the default.

GPT-Live-1.1 (announced 2026-10-15) does not introduce a new Codex model id: Codex main still sets `DEFAULT_FRAMELESS_REALTIME_MODEL = "gpt-live-1-codex"` in `codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs`. So this PR changes no model ids. The public API `gpt-live-1` 1.1 is not out yet, so nothing is added for it.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-wire-profile.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver.test.ts` (rebased on main after #179894 moved the catalog voice-profile case into `realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts`): 3 files, 37 tests passed. The new case checks that `himari` is kept on `gpt-live-1-codex` and still falls back to `marin` on `gpt-live-1`.
- Applied the same list change to a local 2026.10.2 install: `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceCapabilities("gpt-live-1-codex")` now returns all 25 voices, and `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoice("gpt-live-1-codex", "himari")` returns `himari`.
- Base-fail / head-pass: with the same tests and the pre-PR `realtime-quicksilver.ts`, 2 of 37 fail (`keeps Codex v3 voices on the Codex route only`: expected `himari`, received `cove`; `publishes gpt-live-1-codex with its own catalog voice profile`). With this PR: 3 files, 37 tests pass.
- Live Discord call, 2026-10-22, on a 2026.10.2 install with the same 16 voices added to its dist (`gpt-live-1-codex`, ChatGPT sign-in route, `agent-proxy`). The speaker asked to switch to `himari` mid-call; on the second request (the first was cancelled when a new utterance superseded the delegating turn, which ends its voice-control authority as documented), the realtime session reconnected with `voice=himari` and replied in that voice. The speaker confirmed the voice changed. Gateway log, IDs redacted:

      17:53:08.138 [discord] voice: realtime bridge starting mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1-codex voice=himari ...
      17:53:10.608 [discord] voice: realtime bridge ready mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1-codex voice=himari
      17:53:10.613 [discord] voice: voice changed guild=<G> voice=himari
      17:53:10.614 [ws] res ✓ talk.voice.set 2488ms
      17:53:10.858 [discord] voice: realtime lifecycle server:session.started
      17:53:19.487 [discord] voice: realtime assistant transcript (14 chars): <"switched to himari" in Japanese>
      17:53:28.396 [discord] voice: realtime assistant transcript (13 chars): <reply to a greeting>
      17:53:30.598 [discord] voice: participant left event queued ...

  No provider error or relay failure in that session. A recorder bot in the same channel captured about 5 s of bot speech after the switch (`silencedetect` at -45 dB: 55.3–57.3 s, 60.5–60.8 s, 64.8–66.5 s, 68.2–69.3 s of an 80 s recording; the switch completed at 50.1 s).
- Separately, `OpenAI GPT-Live gateway relay failed` occurred on this host on 2026-10-20/21 with the original `arbor` voice as well as `himari`, so it does not appear specific to the new voices. It is being investigated separately and is not addressed here.

prs.title: feat: configure custom model endpoints in Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings → Models can manage provider credentials but cannot define or edit an independent custom inference endpoint.

## User Impact

Administrators connected locally to the Gateway can add, edit, and delete independent endpoints, configure multiple models, discover compatible model IDs, and manage saved keys separately. Adding an endpoint does not change the default model.

The first stage supports Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages. Remote endpoint changes remain unsupported; the server preserves the existing verified-local-client boundary. Anonymous authentication remains limited to effective Chat Completions routes. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor separates endpoint definitions from credential-only provider sign-in. It uses the existing configuration writer, revision checks, secret restoration, and credential owners rather than another configuration store.

Existing models submit explicit field edits, preserving omitted metadata, advanced settings, SecretRefs, pricing, and model-level API/base-URL overrides. Configured references must be resolved before removing models/endpoints; endpoint deletion does not remove stored credentials. Official provider and OAuth setup flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused configuration/Gateway/method tests passed: 54 tests in 13.29s wrapper wall time after the structural extraction; the input-default regression run passed 30 tests in 31.79s wrapper time. These are measured local times, not measured CI execution seconds.
- Four production-bundled Control UI E2E scenarios passed, including authored versus materialized metadata, create/edit/delete, discovery multi-selection, partial key failures, and remote refusal without fallback. Final affected run: 98.20s including build/artifact-lock waits.
- Core/UI/scripts and targeted test typechecks, protocol-vintage negative regressions and exact protocol generation checks, scoped lint (including method-table max-lines), stylesheet lint, formatting, i18n, Solid guards, assertion safety, and UI builds passed. The descriptor split preserves all 551 preceding descriptors in the same order with identical policies/function references.
- Independent Codex review through the shared autoreview workflow covered P0–P2 across implementation and structural changes. All three actionable P2 findings were repaired with focused regressions; the final complete-candidate review returned scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. No findings were suppressed.
- Genuine isolated Gateway proof passed through authenticated public WebSocket RPC: create/edit/delete hot-application and file persistence, matching revision hashes, stale CAS and reader-scope rejection, actual Gateway-side HTTP model discovery, and canonical shared-store key persistence. One Gateway was reused; final post-extraction wall time 37.39s (6.769s test time). The initial application failure reproduced on ordinary config.patch and was traced to the fixture lacking its required recovery owner; the corrected fail-on-unexpected-recovery fixture completed without a restart. External provider accounts, inference, and WebKit proof were not run.

Screenshots use synthetic fixture data; the before/after page pair uses the same light-theme fixture.

### Before

![Settings Models before custom endpoint editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2e79e30-6edd-423e-8411-1ee9af8a9715)

### After

![Settings Models with Custom endpoints section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de5986bb-680c-4107-b9ee-fd7442a7165f)

### Endpoint editor

![Custom endpoint editor with explicit models and adapter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0beb1fa0-f74a-407f-90c7-623d09a377e9)

Contributor: @jacobtomlinson supplied the use case and scoped the work; the implementation commit preserves verified co-author credit.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9b69b6e9-897a-42df-9d84-465d90a5aa1b)

prs.title: fix(ui): align startup ratchet with measured bundle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The startup ratchet introduced in #180890 records 315,696 B although its reason records a measured 315,926 B. This corrects the baseline to an actual same-machine measurement rather than keeping it below the shipped bundle.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Runtime source, lazy boundaries, request counts, the 325,081 B hard cap, and the 512 B growth / 64 B build-variance allowances remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported ~316,380 B startup / ~454 B growth did not reproduce. Building `c4fd27d76ca` and current main `cd982fce7e5` on the same Mac measured **315,930 B → 315,967 B (+37 B)**. Both pass the old 316,272 B enforcement limit. The corrected baseline is exactly **315,967 B**, generated using `pnpm ui:check-performance --update-baseline --reason`; its enforcement limit is 316,543 B.

All **468 startup source-map sources** are retained, with none added or removed. The only changed startup source is `src/shared/session-method-scopes-base.ts`: `df72d285c4e` adds `users.setAvatar` and `users.setDisplayName` to read-scoped admission. This shared method policy belongs on the startup path. Chat interaction/model-catalog changes and provider/profile renderers remain behind their existing lazy boundaries; the stylesheet cleanup and Brotli-quality increase introduce no eager module.

## Evidence

Acceptance: compare canonical shipped gzip sidecars on the same machine, preserve startup sources and one CSS request, and pass the strict checker. This is a bundle-size correction; no runtime timing change is claimed.

| Startup asset | c4fd27d76ca gzip B | cd982fce7e5 gzip B | Delta B | Raw delta B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| control-ui-core | 157,614 | 157,641 | +27 | 0 |
| control-ui-lib | 74,147 | 74,150 | +3 | 0 |
| index | 61 | 61 | 0 | 0 |
| rolldown-runtime | 478 | 478 | 0 | 0 |
| session-snapshot-database | 1,360 | 1,355 | -5 | 0 |
| solid-runtime | 40,127 | 40,126 | -1 | 0 |
| ui | 42,143 | 42,156 | +13 | +37 |
| **Total** | **315,930** | **315,967** | **+37** | **+37** |

The shared `ui` chunk contains the two added admission method names. Every other startup chunk is byte-identical after asset-filename hashes are normalized: their net +24 B gzip is hash/compression churn, not newly eager code. Per-chunk gzip deltas are additive here; they do not claim independent per-module compression costs. This revision has no `--module-attribution` option, so attribution uses emitted source maps and normalized emitted chunks alongside the strict checker.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm ui:build` on c4fd27d76ca and cd982fce7e5, Node 26.12.1, unchanged lockfile | Passed |
| `pnpm ui:check-performance --base-dist <c4fd27d76ca dist> --json` | Passed before and after update; zero violations |
| Startup JS requests / CSS requests | 7 / 1 on both |
| Startup CSS | 41,145 B gzip on both |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 36 passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Independent autoreview | Clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings |

Configuration LOC: **5 → 5** (+2/-2). Production/test source delta: **0/0**. No visual change, so screenshots are not applicable. No remote lease used. Release notes/changelog are not applicable to this internal measurement correction.

prs.title: fix(plugins): channel plugin commands never receive native subagents or scheduled turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin commands typed in Slack, Discord or another channel never receive `ctx.runtimeContext.subagents` or `scheduledTurns`. This happens even for an authorized sender who has operator authority, although the docs describe channel senders as eligible. The S6 follow-up proof (#180282) found the gap in the command capability added by #180173.

## User Impact

User impact: some channel senders can now use a plugin command's declared native helpers and scheduled continuations from channel text, as Gateway chat clients already can. The sender must have a verified identity linked to a person whose current role grants `operator.admin`, and the channel must authorize them for the command.

- Unlinked, unverified, demoted or unauthorized senders still see `undefined`.
- No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a product gap, not a documentation bug.

- **The authority model already covers channel senders.** Channel ingress binds the verified sender's operator authority. It is the same admitted-run authority type Gateway clients use, with the same live identity and role rechecks. It also carries a channel recovery source that scheduled turns can restore.
- **#180173 already expected channel ingress.** It labels the admission `channel` and tests with real channel admin ingress. However, those tests injected the two pieces only Gateway `chat.send` creates: a run id and a user-turn recorder. Real channel dispatch never creates them, so the gate always declined.

**What changes:**

- **Run id and recorder.** For channel ingress only, the host now creates them. It does so only when the reply's operator authority is exactly the one ingress bound to the message's verified sender, so a caller cannot lend a message someone else's authority.
- **Gate unchanged.** Command authorization, the command's declaration, the requester's native tool policy, run admission and per-call authority rechecks still decide, as on the Gateway.
- **One transcript entry per message.** The committed input uses the message's source turn id (a stable id per channel message). A continuing agent turn and restart recovery join that entry instead of adding a duplicate.
- **Redaction preserved.** The committed input uses the same redacted form the delivered-command transcript mirror records. That mirror now records only the reply once a native command has committed the input.

**Docs:** The previous "authorized non-owner" wording now applies only to Gateway chat. On channels, operator authority requires a [channel identity link](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model#channel-identity-links) to an `operator.admin` person.

## Evidence

**Verified on `main` first (`d535d27`).** An authorized, admin-linked Discord sender ran `/review-panel` through real channel dispatch, and the handler saw `subagents === undefined`. An instrumented gate showed `operatorAuthority: true`, `runId: false`, `recorder: false`, which matches the S6 Slack trace.

**New test `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-plugin.channel-native.test.ts`.** It sends text through the real path: host channel ingress, `dispatchInboundMessage`, `getReplyFromConfig`, then a plugin command loaded from disk. Channel dispatch runs inside the same Gateway context resolver scope that `server-channels` uses for channel accounts. The test does not inject a run id, recorder or request scope.

| Case | Before (production code from `main`) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discord with role authority: live runtime (`list`), scheduled turns only when declared, redacted input committed once per message | ❌ | ✅ |
| Slack with identity-grant authority: same checks | ❌ | ✅ |
| `continueAgent`: one committed input, agent run admitted | ❌ | ✅ |
| Demotion during the handler: `spawn` rejects with "Channel operator authority changed" | ❌ | ✅ |
| Channel-unauthorized command: refused, handler not called | ✅ | ✅ |
| Unlinked, unverified, borrowed-authority and demoted senders: `undefined`, nothing committed | ✅ | ✅ |

**End-to-end proof through signed Slack HTTP ingress.** This is a proof-only QA Lab run and is not committed. It used Crabline's local Slack provider, the real Slack plugin, an ephemeral Gateway built from this head, `mock-openai`, and a third-party plugin loaded from disk. The config set `tools.swarm.maxConcurrent: 1` and `commands.allowFrom: { slack: ["*"] }`. A personal profile with an `operator.admin` role was linked to Slack sender `U0123456789`. All 6 scenario steps passed.

| Step | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Linked operator sends `/chanproof` | The handler gets `subagents: true` and `scheduledTurns: true`. Its child finishes `done` with `CHAN-AUTHORIZED-CHILD-OK`; the provider received an `agent-initial` request carrying that child's marker. The schedule is enrolled (`survivesRestart: true`). |
| `cron.run` forces an occurrence | The restored channel requester's child finishes `done` with `CHAN-SCHEDULED-CHILD-OK` and reaches the provider (`agent-initial`). |
| Unlinked sender `U9876543210` sends `/chanproof` (the channel authorizes it) | `subagents: false`, `scheduledTurns: false`, 0 child provider requests. |
| Linked operator starts a capacity holder plus a queued child, then is demoted with `users.setRole` | The holder, released after the demotion, ends `error`: "source execution authority is no longer active \| Channel operator authority changed; send a new request." The queued child never starts. There were 0 provider requests for either child after the demotion. |
| `cron.run` after the demotion | The run ends `error`: "Queued channel operator authority changed; submit a new request." The plugin is not invoked and there are 0 provider requests. |

A control run without the demotion launches the queued child as soon as its holder finishes, and that child reaches the provider. So the demotion is what stops the queued child.

**Known gap, not introduced here.** After the demotion, the queued child does not settle as failed. `agent.wait` still reported `timeout` after about 90 s, including after `sessions.abort` on the finished holder. Gateway operator authority aborts its revocation signal when a role changes, so its queued children settle immediately. Channel operator authority has no such signal for role-based links. This is pre-existing for every channel-origin swarm child, including `sessions_spawn` from a channel agent turn, and it never allowed an effect. I'll propose giving channel operator authority a revocation signal as a separate follow-up rather than widening this PR.

**Mutation checks** (each reverted afterwards):

- Dropping the source-keyed id fails three cases.
- Dropping the mirror's committed-input flag fails three cases.
- Dropping the authority-identity check fails the denial case.
- Dropping the redaction fails both positive cases.

**Affected suites at head (rebased on `60c92913`):** 14 files, 305 tests, all passing. They cover the #180173 native-subagent tests, the #180282 and #180844 scheduled-turn and restart tests, plugin command and owner tests, command and inline-command transcripts, session transcripts, channel operator authority, command refusal, the subagent production boundary, and the ACP and allowlist owner tests.

**CI changed-plan owner test.** `ci-changed-node-test-plan.source-owners.test.ts` passes, with two edits:

- It lists the new test as a direct importer of the operator-authority test support.
- It drops `commands-plugin.scheduled-turns.test.ts`. Since #180844 moved that file's ingress import into `commands-plugin.scheduled-turns.test-support.ts`, the planner no longer selects it, and this expectation already fails on `main` (`60c92913`).

**Cost** (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): about 19 s of test time and 37 s wall; the first case includes about 5 s of cold imports. This end-to-end path through channel ingress is the contract under test. The earlier unit-level injection in #180173 hid exactly this gap.

**Local checks:**

- Type-aware oxlint and oxfmt pass on the changed files.
- tsgo core plus the messaging and config test graphs report only the existing `packages/ai` TS2353 diagnostic from `main`.
- `check:changed` has no failures from this diff. The remaining ones also fail on `main`:
  - max-lines suppressions in `ui/`;
  - the advisory test-root budget, which reports the same counts with this test removed;
  - that TS2353 diagnostic;
  - existing dead exports.
- Local `autoreview` (Codex, branch mode against `origin/main`): scoped-clean, patch correct (0.88). Its sandbox saw only the diff, not the full repository.

prs.title: feat(naming): opt-in one-time refinement of automatic session and topic names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first automatic session or Telegram DM topic name is based on the opening message, so it can become misleading as the conversation develops. This adds an **opt-in, one-time** refinement after a configurable number of later task messages (1–100, default 6). It remains off by default, never renames a manual title, and consumes at most one additional naming attempt per session or topic. This deliberately avoids the continuous renaming proposed in #99583 and #81781.

## Resulting Behavior

For dashboard sessions, generated-name provenance and bounded recent task context are tied to the session ID. The ordinary title-producing turn is excluded by the chat-send scheduler; a title prepared before an opening turn (including worktree and public `sessions.create` titles) carries an explicit skip marker. Later concurrent turns count toward refinement without losing the first follow-up. Private `titleRefinement` state, which can contain task excerpts, is removed from public and plugin session-entry projections.

For Telegram DM topics, the bot arms the refinement when initial naming starts. Later task turns retain their bounded context while the first label is pending; attaching that label resumes a reached threshold through the same serialized owner. The one-shot edit rechecks the current topic name after inference so a manual rename wins, then revalidates the owning account immediately before the Bot API edit. Per-DM `autoTopicLabel: true` overrides account-level `false`; an absent direct setting still inherits the account policy and prompt. Existing boolean/object configurations remain valid.

## Evidence

Current published head: `254aef058c40a0b97492e4d357bb8e9dc2e27aae`.

[Current-head reproduction packet](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/998740dd74233419f17d9a4cd2f0f83e98240fb8/runtime-proof/pr174317/254aef0/README.md) · [actual replies and persisted state](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/998740dd74233419f17d9a4cd2f0f83e98240fb8/runtime-proof/pr174317/254aef0/dashboard-gateway.json) · [validation and log hashes](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/998740dd74233419f17d9a4cd2f0f83e98240fb8/runtime-proof/pr174317/254aef0/validation.json) · [successful CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39854253550).

### Current-head shipped Gateway / real model

A fresh run used the shipped Gateway and CLI `gateway call` entry point with actual `local/gemma4:12b` as **both primary and utility** through the existing durable Ollama queue. No completion was stubbed and no title was patched manually. Normal model selection preceded the opening task.

| Gateway snapshot UTC, 22 October | Observed title |
| --- | --- |
| 21:25:09.027 — opening meeting task | Planning a team meeting |
| 21:25:14.060 — first PostgreSQL restore follow-up | Planning a team meeting |
| 21:28:10.903 — second follow-up after restart, threshold 2 | PostgreSQL backup and recovery rehearsal |
| 21:28:16.106 — additional ordinary turn | PostgreSQL backup and recovery rehearsal |

All four actual model replies match captured `chat.history`. After the first follow-up, normal shutdown returned 0 and offline SQLite inspection confirmed count 1 / done false / original generated title / one bounded excerpt. Restart preserved the same session identity, model and title. Final normal shutdown returned 0; reopened SQLite confirmed count 2 / done true / matching refined names / **no retained excerpts**. Both core and agent databases passed integrity and foreign-key checks before and after restart.

The existing stopped QA checkout/profile was updated in place and verified against 58,621 source files and 40,760 runtime files across 26 roots, including modes, membership and deletions: zero mismatches. Affected originals were backed up and rollback validated before testing. No new checkout, dependency installation, model or environment was created. Original configuration/catalogs were restored, registry refresh returned 0, and our processes/listeners were released. The delivery archive was removed after verification; the checked original and bounded rollback backup remain.

### Repairs, merge and checks

The dashboard P2 regression observes actual generation/routing and real SQLite for utility=primary, no utility, and failed distinct utility. It replaces a flag-only test and checks a persisted refined name and no second attempt; completion output is stubbed only in that regression. The separate current-head runtime above uses an actual model.

The accepted [lifecycle rotation repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174317#discussion_r4350507344) clears private refinement state on replacement, and the [interrupted label attachment repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174317#discussion_r4350507352) serializes pending label/cache recovery through the existing Telegram owner. Their regressions failed before repair and pass afterward.

Main `cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de` introduced a real generated config-baseline checksum conflict. An ordinary two-parent merge preserved that main commit and predecessor `4044e1ff4caf1e54f49082f942294eac9d1b4971`; the normal generator resolved the checksum. Native checked merge `25977f791fb40899cf04aed444b40b8268767c6c` and published head share tree `b5574da8989e9f5f5f08873778070740b2b1119c`. Parents, modes, deletions, resulting tree and ordinary expected-head ref update were verified; no history was rewritten.

Post-merge **76 existing naming tests and 46 existing new-session UI tests pass**, as do core/UI types, config generation/check, diff check and normal commit hooks. Normal `pnpm build` on the exact published SHA passes and build-info identifies that SHA. No new test was added for this merge; independent read-only integration review found no concrete lost repair or incompatibility.

Full hosted pagination at 21:30:59 UTC verified **175 terminal CheckRuns: 129 success, 45 skipped, 1 neutral**, no failures, cancellations or pending checks. All three separate commit statuses, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, were success. These are current-head results. Automatic Codex sampling failure is not represented as a completed code review or rejection.

### Previously accepted Telegram and upgrade evidence

The [4044 shipped Gateway packet](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/407926a3a8d400bde2a18f86828096f7d97d7423/runtime-proof/pr174317/4044e1ff/README.md) and [F35 Telegram/upgrade packet](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/edb1ff7cdaa0e58b83bb0a07d93cce8cd82abf72/runtime-proof/pr174317/f35cd67/README.md) retain their original SHA qualifications. The [completed revision 7 assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174317#issuecomment-6218304774) accepted them with proof confidence 5/6 and no actionable findings.

F35 covers real Telegram transport: threshold 2 / restart / no repeat, actual manual rename during held inference, captionless media, and a separate account-service stop before the edit. Those synchronized cases use controlled completion output. A separate real-model Telegram case through the existing Ollama queue received four replies, refined once after restart and retained no excerpts. The official stable `2026.10.6` → candidate upgrade preserved session identity, history and existing topic-cache fields.

The current merge preserves the Telegram-specific collector/cache/account guards and ordinary mode-absent utility routing. The new current-head Gateway restart case exercises main's updated shared session infrastructure. **No Telegram or stable-upgrade run is relabelled as a 254aef0 execution**, and the accepted matrix was not repeated without cause.

## Remaining Review Boundaries

The [completed revision 8 assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174317#issuecomment-6218304774) reviews exact head `254aef058c40a0b97492e4d357bb8e9dc2e27aae`, accepts the current shipped-Gateway/restart packet and qualified F35 Telegram/upgrade reuse, and finds no actionable correctness issue. It confirms that the prior conflict request no longer applies and proof is sufficient (confidence 5/6). Only explicit maintainer decisions remain; its status is waiting on maintainer. Optional duplicate helper-test consolidation is not a merge blocker.

The external maintainer decision is whether to adopt bounded opt-in message-count-triggered generated-name refinement and its settings, creation-provenance RPC parameter and concurrency SDK export. That product/API-contract decision and final acceptance belong to maintainers. The author has not assigned labels or approval, merged to main or deployed to production.

## What Problem This Solves

Internal agent and Gateway helpers still advertise alternate inputs that no production caller supplies.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration or configuration action. Public config, CLI, Gateway protocol, Plugin SDK and persisted shapes stay unchanged. Phase E is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unserved arguments and their alternate paths, using the values and dependencies already selected by every serving caller. This includes unused truncation variants, the single-string diagnostic join wrapper, private scheduling/cleanup switches, fixed worker launch policies and fixture-only dependency inputs. Keep actual authorization, transcript recording, cancellation, settlement, ordinary durability and realistic concurrency checks.

This is the runtime area of one 506-net-production-line cleanup family. It removes **258 production lines and 179 test/support lines across 61 files**. The other two areas are separate branches, keeping each PR below 80 files and failures attributable. Counts exclude tests, fixtures, generated files and declarations from production. Final assembly retained the QA heartbeat options exposed by the SDK runtime loader, plus command environment and discovery phase options reachable through public scenario definitions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. No live security, durability or concurrency guard is removed. Whole-tree caller and export checks show only one live production value for each retired argument. The removed alternate truncation forms and multipart diagnostic helper have no remaining production consumer; their mechanism-only tests go with them. Real head-page Unicode/cursor/byte limits, redaction-before-bounding, restart/backoff and physical queue settlement proofs remain.

Relevant provenance: truncation helpers are private package implementation, not Plugin SDK; diagnostic capture #156603 is a completed feature; its live opt-in/privacy/redaction gates stay. Snapshot `trackProducer` lost its production supplier in completed retirement #154776; snapshot coalescing and retained cleanup remain. Delivery inputs were orphaned by completed consolidation #177698, which explicitly disclaims dormant machinery. Disk monitoring #123177 remains fully active. Setup retains live route, config-revision and internally captured newly-created-agent checks; only unsupplied outer inputs retire. No in-flight foundation is deleted.

## Evidence

All changes applied without conflict to main `cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de`. None of the 60 changed files changed between either census base and that main; same-input focused proof is reused. Every constituent cut passed an independent scoped P0–P2 review. The complete assembled area also receives a fresh review.

Focused repository Vitest runs used isolated state, `nice -n 10`, one worker and serial heavy commands. Retained proof includes:

- Diagnostic capture/redaction: 36 cases across four files; independent wrong-order negative control caught the secret-boundary regression.

- Setup/live-target concurrency: 89 cases across five files in 47.92s.
- Session delivery/admission/custody: 67 cases across six files in 88.63s.
- Disk monitor/real worker read cache and projection: 38 cases across three files in 35.91s.

Targeted native no-emit typecheck of the touched graph passed, including the 61st fan-out consumer after CI exposed its stale call. Exact-path typed lint, formatting and whitespace passed. Fresh aggregate review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Both runtime and Madge cycle checks report zero cycles; the test-only repair adds no runtime imports. The suppression and PR wrapper source-closure guards pass. Broad proof belongs to PR CI on the exact head. No broad local suite, whole-graph typecheck, build, E2E or live deployment is claimed.

One serial candidate-versus-base replay reproduced the same two failures (22 other cases passed on each). ## What Problem This Solves

Adds regression coverage for pasted text attachments disappearing from model context on follow-up turns, as reported in [this X thread](https://x.com/steipete/status/2112989437110227423).

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The existing durable-context fix in #167938 is already present in v2026.10.5 and current main. This PR protects that behavior; it does not reconstruct context previously discarded by an older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The former prompt path temporarily substituted enriched text while retaining only the original caption and attachment reference for replay. The existing fix records the first model-facing text on the canonical user turn and reuses it on later requests.

Existing projection tests use prepared prompt strings. This regression starts with a >1,000-character base64 pasted-text attachment, runs the real parser and text extractor, persists the user turn before dispatch, and checks complete provider-bound text on the first request, a follow-up, and a reopened session. The assistant deliberately does not echo the supplied fact. The visible transcript keeps its caption and attachment metadata.

Simplification: reuse the existing attachment, transcript, session, and prompt owners; no new runtime state or compatibility path. Production delta: **0 lines**. Test/routing delta: **162 added lines**. A separate test file keeps the existing projection suite within its lint limit.

prs.title: fix(security): backport compromised CA distrust to extended stable
prs.body:
The September maintenance line still exports the affected emSign ECC G3 root to secret-egress children and selects pre-fix Rust WebPKI/root data. Backport the already-merged main repairs from [#179249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179249) (`b617d97`) and [#179246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179246) (`01eef92`) onto `extended-stable/2026.9.33` at `5873f817`.

One filtered CA array feeds the existing exported PEM and upstream TLS context. Keep the maintenance branch's existing connection owner. Update only the three selected version/checksum entries across its two Rust lockfiles. The local proxy CA and other roots remain usable; legitimate chains depending exclusively on the distrusted root lose trust. Restart the Gateway after installation. Existing binaries, independent trust stores and blind tunnels need their own updates.

Validation in an isolated Linux arm64 UTM guest:

- The real Worker/exported-PEM regression is red on the pre-fix branch and green with the backport under Node26.12.0; **99** Worker, proxy, lifecycle and WebSocket tests pass. Touched lint, formatting and infra-test typecheck pass.
- Actual old Cargo locks accept **12/12** incident chains with affected CA roots; precise Cargo regeneration matches both fixed locks, which reject **12/12** as `CertDistrusted`. All **148 Rust workspace tests** and locked Linux manifest metadata pass.
- Qualified nativepnpm12.15 installs the unchanged **186-workspace** frozen graph with supported `--pm-on-fail=ignore`. No maintenance packageManager selection changes; this is not historical-tool replay proof.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. Public fixtures/docs were separately compared with the exact merged source. Real Worker-exported trust also rejects all12 chains under current supported stable/fork Bun with legitimate localCA and ordinarypublicTLS controls; the suspected AAA-root export gap does not reproduce.

Initial dependency/tool-selection/offline/disk setup failures and an already-fixed-runtime baseline are retained in the audit evidence. Actual native desktop execution, full published package upgrade, and full release validation remain unqualified here.

This is an incident-only source backport. No release version, SDK/config/schema contract, tag, publication or deployment changes are included. Linux desktop locks are repository source remediation; the extended-stable Gateway track does not publish native app artifacts. Current Node and native pnpm fixes require their main PR to merge before a separate branch adaptation. Upstream Bun/native consumer and OS-CA obligations remain separately tracked. No full release-set qualification or release publication is claimed.

The maintained branch’s E2E musl stage now upgrades the normal Alpine CA bundle to `20261020-r0` before installing build dependencies. Both architectures of its immutable selected Node image use Alpine 3.24.2 and the same base-layer identities as the independently qualified Alpine package transaction. The replacement default trust data rejects all twelve incident chains; existing non-Alpine package behavior is unchanged. The complete Dockerfile received a fresh scoped P0–P2 review. This is a default OS trust repair, not a complete runtime cutover: this maintenance branch still selects Node 24.21.0 and its Node/pnpm adaptation remains an internal follow-up after the main remediation is merged. No image build, publication or deployment is claimed.
