## 2026.10.6

### Highlights

- **Patched Node runtime required:** OpenClaw now requires Node 24.22.1+ on the 24 line or 26.12.1+ on the 26 line, which reject TLS chains signed with the compromised certificate keys addressed in the October 2026 Node.js security releases. Docker images ship Node 24.22.1, installers select the patched runtimes, and `openclaw update` refuses with recovery guidance before installing on an older Node instead of breaking the running install. Source builds now pin pnpm 12.15.0. (#179992) Thanks @joshavant.
- **Safer updates and recovery:** package swaps now refuse unsafe service states, Windows and macOS package-manager updates recover from platform-specific failures, and frozen Gateway startup owners can be retired cleanly. (#171101, #170940, #171936, #171678) Thanks @RomneyDa, @homeworld520, @Yolo521-bot, @stop-time, @AntaresGG, and @TommyLei666.
- **Data-preserving migrations and backups:** Doctor and migration paths now refuse malformed or lossy workspace imports, preserve malformed Notes bytes, reject unsafe non-UTF-8 wiki rewrites, keep deeply nested SQLite backups, and retain staging evidence when restore inspection fails. (#172293, #172953, #172742, #174573, #168583, #170867, #172028) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666, @RomneyDa, @Leon-SK668, @ericcurtin, @Yolo521-bot, @obviyus, and @altaywtf.
- **Reliable delivery across restarts:** queued turns, watched child results, dead-lettered deliveries, and streamed replies now survive recovery without disappearing, duplicating, or producing false missing-answer notices. (#170384, #169489, #169932, #173798) Thanks @RomneyDa, @huyengiang101086-spec, and @Yolo521-bot.
- **Provider and model resilience:** GPT-5.6 tool turns, OpenRouter DeepSeek tool calls, LM Studio overflow recovery, parallel OpenAI reasoning settings, and model retry/fallback budgets now behave consistently. (#176709, #175058, #169189, #169322, #164808) Thanks @RomneyDa, @Linux2010, @ZhimingQ, @xpeng5278-web, and @anyech.
- **Windows and mobile stability:** fresh Windows state stores, Proxy-backed environments, and stored Anthropic credentials no longer block startup, while iOS Talk and chat connectivity recover from first-reply and timeout failures. (#176174, #176194, #174571, #168416, #169912) Thanks @RomneyDa, @tjarrau-dev, @skyzhao1223, @easyteacher, @scalesmart, @masatohoshino, @Takhoffman, and @Solvely-Colin.
- **Agent and tool-call recovery:** unfinished tools now time out visibly, context overflow compacts after steered tool results, malformed calls continue after earlier refusals, large patch hunks avoid argument-limit crashes, and stopped yielded tasks stay stopped. (#172983, #172019, #170615, #174477, #169453) Thanks @RomneyDa, @budzation, @mirasrael, @r3n3x, @freeqaz-openai, and @obviyus.
- **Channel delivery correctness:** WhatsApp retries and stickers, Telegram albums and dual-stack replies, Slack relay recovery, and Discord voice-call replies no longer lose or duplicate messages. (#142434, #164210, #163926, #171564, #173407, #172380) Thanks @ashawwal, @RomneyDa, @andrewwbuilds, @abacha, @Dat1GUI, @brainmonger, @obviyus, and @vincentkoc.
- **Worker and worktree recovery:** hosts reclaim worker capacity after reboot, partial-clone worktrees repair missing objects, and child-result and exec-wake evidence survives Gateway restarts. (#168863, #168864, #169489, #169645) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- This patch release contains focused reliability fixes only; it does not introduce new user-facing features.

### Fixes

- **State and system-agent recovery:** restore access to agents held by affected upgrades, recover held system-agent databases after schema changes, and preserve live configuration when forensic snapshots fail. (#175007, #176783, #171217) Thanks @RomneyDa, @PennyVibe, and @Yolo521-bot.
- **Windows state and updates:** canonicalize schema ownership across path aliases, serialize Proxy-backed environments before inspection IPC, hide SQLite helper windows during update work, and recognize native Scheduled Task permission failures in every locale. (#176174, #176194, #174969, #178624) Thanks @RomneyDa, @tjarrau-dev, @skyzhao1223, @easyteacher, and @throwingbones.
- **macOS companion execution:** honor long command and approval deadlines across the companion socket, classify late or lost replies without replaying submitted commands, and preserve native permission details. (#172117) Thanks @holgergruenhagen, @RomneyDa, @ylcn91, and @Colton-Harris.
- **Doctor and managed plugins:** repair empty retired-plugin metadata, clear resolved migration warnings, and converge app-managed plugins onto the installed core version. (#173851, #177096, #174257) Thanks @RomneyDa, @fengfan201314-eng, @ScientificProgrammer, @yinx65588-boop, @jj5638521, and @kazuyuki-eguchi.
- **Update diagnostics:** preserve FRV blockers, explain package-journal identity and runtime-retention failures, and avoid cleanup stalls on shared recovery manifests. (#171186, #170385, #169280, #174249) Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @astapenkoav, @council10-kera, and @shoaibulhaque.
- **SQLite correctness:** preserve transaction outcomes when warning handlers throw, settle peer closes after shared-worker refusal, and prevent retired cache generations from taking worker ownership. (#157151, #173813, #172798) Thanks @vincentkoc and @RomneyDa.
- **Reply recovery:** preserve side-question and immediate fallback ordering, avoid repeated or missing answers after streamed delivery, and keep stopped yielded tasks from restarting. (#174869, #169305, #173798, #169453) Thanks @RomneyDa and @freeqaz-openai.
- **Codex and native sessions:** release stalled startup waits and completed subagents after cancellation or cleanup failures, preserve conversations across runtime restarts, keep workspace bindings across reply resets, and settle recovered child binding writes before session readiness. (#168347, #173547, #166368, #160549, #177564) Thanks @RomneyDa, @Kimiyu-186, @alkor2000, @jhgaylor, @vincentkoc, @jjjhenriksen, and @obviyus.
- **Gateway lifecycle:** retain restart custody, avoid stop-time lease deadlocks, recover worker capacity after reboot, and preserve suppressed-channel configuration across reloads. (#172852, #171308, #168863) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **CLI and process diagnostics:** preserve JSON output on Gateway command exits, report resource-disposal and PTY EOF failures, and surface failed diagnostic writes without crashing. (#176795, #173566, #176362, #174622) Thanks @vincentkoc and @RomneyDa.
- **Scheduled follow-ups:** same-conversation follow-ups scheduled from an authorized operator turn keep that operator's current authority when they run, and one-shot continuations can call `next_check` to check back later. (#176422)
- **Media and TTS:** time out slow hosted speech synthesis and report playback cache, probe, and quota failures rather than silently dropping cleanup errors. (#175614, #175634, #174668) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.5..bba7238a1be3a0d4e92c371988f94e81011a06b2 history: 293 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 293 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: web_search (ddgs): ambiguous failures look like empty results

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With the default search provider (DuckDuckGo, no API key), consecutive web_search calls in the same turn fail with an error that reads like an empty result set:
  Error: DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)

The original report observed that spacing the same distinct queries correlated with recovery. Follow-up diagnostics on the original host observed an explicit Mojeek HTTP 403 refusal, then intentionally stopped the remaining requests. These observations do not establish that every `No results found` exception is rate limiting, or that retry/backoff is the root-cause fix. ddgs can hide upstream refusal, empty parsing and aggregation failures behind that generic exception. The agreed nanobot-side resolution is to report search unavailability and uncertainty honestly, rather than interpret the exception as a completed search with zero matches.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep the default provider (tools.web.search.provider = "duckduckgo", empty api_key), no proxy.
2. In one turn, issue several distinct web_search calls with no pause between them (a normal multi-query research turn does this).
3. Observe that a subset of the calls fail with the "No results found" error; repeating the same queries with a pause succeeds.

Isolated library repro (no nanobot involved), same host:
  from ddgs import DDGS
  qs = ["capa galaxy a12 preco", "fone bluetooth barato", "notebook i5 usado", "cadeira gamer preco",
        "tenis corrida promocao", "panela eletrica preco", "mochila escolar", "lampada led preco"]
  d = DDGS(timeout=15)
  # no pause -> 0/8 results, all DDGSException: No results found
  # 3 s pause between queries -> 8/8 results

### Agreed acceptance criteria

- Return ambiguous ddgs failures as tool errors that explicitly say no usable search result was obtained and the cause is unknown. Do not present them as confirmed zero matches or infer rate limiting from `No results found`.
- Distinguish the tool's waiting deadline from a timeout reported by ddgs.
- Preserve successful result formatting, the configured network route, cancellation and existing diagnostic privacy behavior.
- Verify through a normal public entrypoint with a real model: live search succeeds and uses returned sources; controlled refusal and timeout cases report the failed lookup without claiming that matching pages do not exist or inventing sources.

### Outside this issue

- Removing upstream rate limits, IP restrictions or anti-automation blocks.
- Adding automatic retry, backoff or pacing configuration. These are not required for this issue's resolution.
- Recovering HTTP refusal/rate-limit facts already discarded by ddgs. Upstream error preservation and any later nanobot integration are separate follow-up work. Related upstream report: https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs/issues/478.

### Resolution

PR #6409 resolves the agreed nanobot-side scope when merged. This scope supersedes the original retry-based proposal; the original reproduction steps, measurements and environment are retained in this issue as reported evidence, not proof that every failure has the same cause.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Two calls issued in the same second, then the failure (Telegram turn, 17/10/2026):
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:44 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:32:50 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:32:54 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:33:40 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:33:51 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.

Additional measurements
- 8 distinct queries with no pause: 0/8 returned results (all DDGSException: No results found).
- The same 8 queries with a 3 s pause: 8/8 succeeded.
- The host recovers after idling, and a second host on a different IP served results while the first was failing — transient and rate/IP dependent, not a permanent block.
- exclusive=True only keeps DuckDuckGo out of the parallel batch; it does not pace calls, so consecutive searches still go out immediately.
- The per-turn guard in utils/runtime.py (_MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2) only blocks repeating the same query or URL, so it does not help with distinct queries.
- ddgs 9.16.0 itself has no retry/backoff (checked its sources).
- Checked todays `main`: _search_duckduckgo is unchanged there.
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.5

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, aarch64 (Oracle Cloud VM, kernel 7.0.0-1013-oracle)

### Channel / Platform

Telegram (headless, systemd service)

### LLM Provider

opencode

### Model

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Browser

N/A — headless VPS, no browser involved

### Connection

Direct outbound HTTPS from the host, no proxy (tools.web.proxy unset), datacenter IP

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml

```

### Additional Context

issues.title: Feature Request: Persist API usage in messages for better compression estimation
issues.body:
# Feature Request: Persist API usage in messages for better compression estimation

## Background

### Limitations of current compression logic

- Compression relies on `estimate_prompt_tokens_chain`, which uses **tiktoken** (cl100k_base) to estimate token counts
- Different models use different tokenizers; tiktoken diverges significantly from actual encoding, **[especially for Chinese](https://github.com/Zhaobudaoyuema/prompt-token-counter/blob/master/README.md)**
- Estimation errors affect when compression triggers and how boundaries are chosen

### Provider-side capability status

- The design expects each Provider to implement `estimate_prompt_tokens` for model-specific accuracy, but **no Provider implements it yet**
- Most models also lack public APIs for token usage queries, making pre-call precise calculation difficult

### When and what gets estimated

- 4 estimation calls in total: 2 **before** the current turn, 2 **after**
- Pre-turn: only history + `"[token-probe]"`, excluding current-turn input—risk of underestimation
- Post-turn: history + current turn's all_msgs—complete content

---

## Proposal

After each model request, persist `response.usage` on the corresponding assistant message; use these usage values to compute total tokens when compressing.

Current compression only updates `last_consolidated` and does not physically delete messages; `get_history()` still reads from `messages[last_consolidated:]`. For estimation, usage is only applied to the unarchived portion—no extra handling needed.

---

If this approach looks good, I can implement a first version soon.

---


# Feature Request: 将 API usage 写入 messages 以优化压缩估算

### 背景

**当前压缩逻辑的局限**

- 压缩依赖 `estimate_prompt_tokens_chain`，使用 **tiktoken**（cl100k_base）估算 token 数
- 不同模型 tokenizer 不同，tiktoken 与真实编码差异较大，**[中文场景尤其明显](https://github.com/Zhaobudaoyuema/prompt-token-counter/blob/master/README.md)**
- 估算误差会影响压缩触发时机和边界选择

**Provider 侧能力现状**

- 设计上希望由各 Provider 实现 `estimate_prompt_tokens` 以适配不同模型，但**目前没有任何 Provider 实现**
- 大部分模型也没有公开的 token 消耗查询接口，调用前难以精确计算

**压缩触发的时机与内容**

- 共 4 次估算：2 次在**当前轮之前**，2 次在**当前轮之后**
- 前置估算：只包含 history + `"[token-probe]"`，不含当前轮输入，存在低估风险
- 后置估算：包含 history + 本轮 all_msgs，内容完整

### 方案

每次请求模型后，将 `response.usage` 写入对应 assistant 消息；压缩时基于这些 usage 计算总 token 数。

当前压缩只更新 `last_consolidated`，不物理删除消息，`get_history()` 仍从 `messages[last_consolidated:]` 取值。估算时只对未归档部分使用 usage，无需额外处理。

如确认方案可行，我可以尽快实现一版。

issues.title: [WebUI] Top of the viewport renders washed out in iOS PWA standalone mode
issues.body:
## Bug Description

In iOS PWA standalone mode, the top of the viewport renders washed out. The strip holding the
sidebar toggle and the right-hand controls, plus the message content immediately below it,
appear semi-transparent or blurred compared with the rest of the page.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the WebUI to the iOS home screen (Safari: Share, then Add to Home Screen).
2. Launch it from the home screen icon so it runs standalone with no browser chrome.
3. Observe the top strip and the content directly beneath it.
4. Scroll and compare the affected region against the rest of the page.

## Expected Behavior

The top of the viewport should render at full contrast and match the rest of the UI surface.
The status bar treatment should follow the iOS PWA conventions rather than compositing the
page behind a translucent band.

## Additional Context

Client: iPhone Air, iOS 27. A screenshot is available and can be attached on request. It would
also help to know whether this happens in the chat view or in the drawer.

Surfaces to audit, all verified to exist in the current tree:

- `webui/index.html` sets `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` to `default` and uses
  `viewport-fit=auto`. `env(safe-area-inset-*)` only resolves to non-zero values with
  `viewport-fit=cover`, while several components rely on `env(safe-area-inset-top)` and
  `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.
- The chat view draws a fade gradient over the top of the scrolled content:
  `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx` renders `pointer-events-none absolute
  inset-x-0 top-0 h-3 bg-gradient-to-b from-background to-transparent`, and
  `webui/src/components/thread/activity/ThinkingReasoningShell.tsx` does the same inside
  reasoning blocks.
- The chrome layer is `bg-transparent` and absolutely positioned over the content:
  `webui/src/App.tsx`, the `HostChrome` header (`host-drag-region pointer-events-none absolute
  inset-x-0 top-0 z-40 h-11 bg-transparent`).
- `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadComposer.tsx` uses `backdrop-blur-md` on a surface that can
  sit near the viewport edge.

Possibly related: #4479 removed `backdrop-blur` from the sheet overlay for smoother mobile
animation, which is the same family of issue.

issues.title: Feature Request: Simple usage logging for token/cost tracking

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: Good for newcomers

issues.body:
## Problem

Users running Nanobot with custom gateways or paid API providers currently have no visibility into token usage or costs. The session files store conversations but don't capture usage metadata that many API responses include.

## Proposed Solution

Add a simple usage logging mechanism that:

1. **Captures usage data from API responses** - Many LLM APIs return usage data (prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens). Store this in a structured format.

2. **Logs to a dedicated file** - Create a usage log (e.g., `logs/usage.jsonl` or `logs/usage.csv`) with entries containing:
   - Timestamp
   - Model used
   - Prompt tokens
   - Completion tokens
   - Total tokens
   - Estimated cost (optional, based on configured rates)

3. **Minimal overhead** - Implementation should be lightweight and not slow down conversations.

## Benefits

- **Cost visibility**: Users can track spending over time
- **Model comparison**: See which models are used most frequently
- **Budget management**: Set alerts or limits based on actual usage
- **Analytics**: Understand usage patterns (peak times, common tasks)

## Implementation Ideas

```python
# Example log entry format (JSONL)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-14T13:25:00Z",
  "model": "glm-5:cloud",
  "prompt_tokens": 1500,
  "completion_tokens": 320,
  "total_tokens": 1820,
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "provider": "custom-gateway"
}
```

## Considerations

- Should be optional/configurable (some users may not want logging)
- Cost calculation would require per-model rate configuration
- Could integrate with existing OpenClaw `cacheRetention` patterns for Anthropic caching

## Alternative Approaches

- Add a `usage` field to existing session files
- Create a separate usage stats skill that aggregates and reports
- Expose via API for external dashboards

---

Thanks for considering this feature! It would be valuable for users managing costs across multiple models and providers.

issues.title: Control plane MVP for subagents: list/kill commands (bus-first)
issues.body:
## Background

Subagent support currently focuses on `spawn` + completion callback. There is no first-class control plane for operators/users to inspect and stop running subagents.

This creates an operational gap for cases where a task is wrong, runaway, or no longer needed.

## Proposal (MVP)

Add a minimal **control plane MVP** for subagents with:

1. `subagent list` (or equivalent command/tool)
2. `subagent kill <id>`

Scope is intentionally small and aligned with the current architecture direction:

- **bus-first compatible**
- no new direct-call-only execution path
- no behavior change to existing `spawn` flow

## Out of scope (for this issue)

- steer/intervene with natural-language guidance
- human-in-the-loop approval workflow
- persistence/replay/history UI

These can be follow-up issues after MVP lands.

## Suggested behavior

### list

- show active subagent IDs and labels
- include status (`running` at minimum)
- include start time (if available)

### kill

- stop target subagent by ID
- return explicit result:
  - success: subagent stopped
  - failure: not found / already finished / cannot stop

## Acceptance criteria

- Users can reliably list currently running subagents.
- Users can stop a running subagent by ID.
- Existing subagent spawn/completion flow continues to work.
- Unit/integration tests cover:
  - list with zero tasks
  - list with N running tasks
  - kill success
  - kill non-existent ID
  - race case: task finishes right before kill

## Why this matters

This is the minimal control-plane primitive needed for safe operation, and it creates a clean base for later steer/HiL capabilities.

issues.title: [Security] Session history should not live inside the agent workspace
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #713 ("scope sessions to workspace with migration and tool metadata",
commit `8f49b520` / `27a13183`) moved session storage from the global
`~/.nanobot/sessions/` directory to `<workspace>/sessions/`. The stated goal of
that PR is a good one: **per-workspace session isolation** so that different
projects/workspaces (e.g. via the WebUI multi-project support and
`WorkspaceScope` / `project_path`) keep independent session stores instead of
sharing one global pool.

This issue is **not** about reverting that isolation goal. It is about a side
effect of the chosen storage location: because the agent's filesystem tools
(read / list / glob) operate **inside the workspace**, putting `sessions/`
*inside* the workspace makes every session's full conversation history readable
by any agent that has read access to its workspace — including sessions that
belong to other users/channels on a shared deployment.

## The tension

The `workspace` directory has two roles, and PR #713 only considered the first:

| Role | What it means |
|---|---|
| Data-home root | `sessions/`, `memory/`, `skills/` hang off it → satisfies per-project isolation |
| Agent filesystem sandbox | read/list/glob default scope is the workspace → sessions become reachable |

PR #713 achieved logical per-workspace isolation, but as a side effect it placed
all conversation history inside the agent's own readable filesystem.

## Impact

Regardless of `restrict_to_workspace`, an agent with filesystem read tools can:

1. `list_files` / glob `sessions/*.jsonl` to discover every session, and
2. `read_file` each one to recover full message history.

`restrict_to_workspace` does not help: even with it set to `true`, the sessions
directory is still reachable because it sits **under** the allowed root. Session
histories routinely contain sensitive data — user prompts, secrets/API keys pasted
into chat, tool outputs, PII — so on any deployment where more than one
conversation/user shares a workspace (the common case for chat channels:
Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, …), one agent can read everyone else's
transcripts.

## Where it comes from today

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — default `workspace = "~/.nanobot/workspace"`
- `nanobot/session/manager.py`:

  ```python
  class JsonlSessionStore:
      def __init__(self, workspace: Path):
          self.sessions_dir = ensure_dir(workspace / "sessions")   # inside workspace
          self.legacy_sessions_dir = get_legacy_sessions_dir()     # ~/.nanobot/sessions (global, outside)
  ```

- `nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py` — read/list are allowed within
  `agent_workspace` (and `restrict_to_workspace` defaults to `False`, so the
  blast radius is actually wider than the workspace).

## Suggested fix

Keep PR #713's per-workspace isolation, but move the storage location **outside**
the tool-reachable workspace — namespace the global data dir by workspace, e.g.:

```
~/.nanobot/sessions/<workspace-hash>/
```

The path still varies per workspace (isolation preserved), but lives outside the
agent's filesystem sandbox. As defense in depth, the `sessions/` path could also
be explicitly excluded from filesystem-tool access (similar to how `memory/` is
partially treated today), but relocating it is the cleaner fix since it removes
the directory from the tool surface entirely rather than relying on a per-tool
allowlist.

Happy to open a PR if the maintainers agree on the target path.

## Environment

- Default configuration (no `restrict_to_workspace`).
- Affected since `8f49b520` (PR #713).

issues.title: webui: "Context compacted" divider never says why — background idle compaction looks identical to context-window pressure
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Every compaction in the WebUI transcript renders the same two-line divider: `Compressing context…` → `Context compacted`. It carries no information about *why* compaction ran: `ContextCompactionEvent` only has `compaction_id` + `phase` (`nanobot/events.py:37-42`), and the WebUI wire payload forwards exactly those two fields (`nanobot/webui/outbound_wire.py:101-105`).

That matters because two very different mechanisms produce that divider:

1. **Context-window pressure** inside a turn — the request no longer fits the model budget.
2. **Background idle compaction** — `idleCompactAfterMinutes` (default 15) — which rewrites the transcript into a summary checkpoint purely because the session sat idle, with no relation to the model's context window (`nanobot/agent/autocompact.py` → `Consolidator.compact_idle_session`).

On my install the second case dominates: 15 `context_compaction` records in `~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl`, **13 of them without a `turn_id`** (background idle path), only 2 emitted inside a turn. So the transcript keeps announcing "context compacted" on sessions that were nowhere near the 200k budget, which reads as "your model's context is exhausted" — confusing for users on large-window models.

The idle trigger is also undiscoverable from the UI: `idleCompactAfterMinutes` is config-file only (`grep -r idleCompact webui/src` → 0 hits), so there is no in-app way to learn that idleness, not window pressure, caused it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. nanobot 0.3.5, WebUI over local WebSocket; provider `opencode_go`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, preset `contextWindowTokens: 200000`.
2. Leave `idleCompactAfterMinutes` at its default (15).
3. Open a topic, send one short message, leave it idle for more than 15 minutes, come back.
4. The transcript shows `Context compacted` — indistinguishable from a real window-pressure compaction.
5. Confirm which path ran:
   ```
   grep -h context_compaction ~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl | grep -vc turn_id   # 13
   grep -h context_compaction ~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl | wc -l              # 15
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The divider should state the trigger and, ideally, the reclaim:

- `Idle compaction after 15 min idle · 12k → 3k tokens`
- `Context limit reached (182k / 200k) · summarized 140 messages`
- `Manual /compact`

and link (or at least hint) at how to turn the idle scan off, since it is not exposed in WebUI settings.

Minimally: do not render background idle compaction as a full transcript divider, or mark it explicitly as a background/maintenance compaction.

Note the inconsistency with the earlier "silent compaction" work: #5780 / #6029 made background compaction quiet on chat channels (`notify=False`), but the WebUI still renders a full divider for it, so the user-facing result of "quiet" is not visible in the WebUI.

### Relevant Logs

```
# idle/background path: no turn_id
{"event": "context_compaction", "chat_id": "301140c1-…", "compaction_id": "a86a35b533404b65b30f74a131f17b8a", "phase": "succeeded", "created_at_ms": 1792574155881}

# in-turn path: turn fields present
{"event": "context_compaction", "chat_id": "246876b4-…", "compaction_id": "4b48e89c3878411f9fcf13fd28b6e020", "phase": "succeeded", "turn_id": "8d49719a-…", "turn_phase": "activity", "turn_seq": 5053, "created_at_ms": 1792550978538}
```

LLM usage for the same install (from `~/.nanobot/llm_usage.sqlite3`, `llm_calls`): peak `input_tokens` 181,794, mean 76,794 — i.e. real window pressure does happen too, which is exactly why the two cases need to be distinguishable.

### nanobot Version

0.3.5

### Python Version

3.12.4

### Operating System

Windows 11 (10.0.26100)

### Channel / Platform

WebSocket (WebUI)

### LLM Provider

opencode_go

### Model

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Browser

Microsoft Edge (Chromium)

### Connection

Local host

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml
agents:
  defaults:
    idleCompactAfterMinutes: 15
modelPresets:
  opencodeGo:
    model: deepseek-v4.1-flash
    provider: opencode_go
    maxTokens: 8192
    contextWindowTokens: 200000
```

### Additional Context

Related but distinct:

- #5885 — server-side proposal to gate *idle transcript replacement* on a token threshold. This issue is the UI half: even with that gate in place, the divider still cannot tell the triggers apart.
- #6029 / #5780 — silenced background compaction notices on chat channels; the WebUI transcript was not covered.

Code pointers (main): `nanobot/events.py:37-42`, `nanobot/webui/outbound_wire.py:101-105`, `webui/src/lib/thread-event-projection.ts:887-908`, `webui/src/components/thread/ContextCompactionNotice.tsx` (0.3.5 renders the same strings from the bundled `ThreadShell` chunk), `nanobot/agent/autocompact.py` (`_is_expired` / `_archive`).

Happy to be told this should be labeled `enhancement` instead of `bug`, or to split the "expose `idleCompactAfterMinutes` in WebUI settings" part out.

prs.title: fix(web): report ambiguous ddgs failures as unavailable
prs.body:
## Why

Resolves #6285. ddgs can collapse upstream refusal, empty parsing and aggregation failures into `DDGSException("No results found.")`. That exception does not establish that a search completed with zero matches. This PR implements the agreed nanobot-side resolution: report the uncertainty accurately to the model without guessing a cause or retrying the search.

## What changed

- Report generic ddgs failures as search unavailable with an unknown cause, explicitly preserving uncertainty about matching pages.
- Distinguish the tool's waiting deadline from a timeout reported by ddgs. Keep the existing error status, cancellation behavior, diagnostic logging and unexpected-exception path.
- Exercise the released Wikipedia parser and ddgs aggregator with offline responses, checking the next model request's actual tool message and error event for empty parsing, HTTP 403, HTTP 429 and library timeout. Strengthen the existing outer-timeout check.

## Scope

This PR resolves the agreed nanobot-side scope of #6285: report ambiguous ddgs failures honestly as search unavailable with an unknown cause. Preserving precise underlying HTTP refusal/rate-limit facts requires an upstream public contract and is tracked independently (related upstream report: https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs/issues/478). This PR does not claim to recover HTTP 403/429 from `No results found`.

No automatic retry, pacing configuration, dependency/backend changes, production hooks into ddgs internals, Agent core changes or frontend changes. Existing successful search formatting and proxy routing remain unchanged.

## Verification

- Red/green: the four model-input cases and existing tool-deadline case fail against the frozen parent because of the misleading or empty error message, then pass with the fix.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/agent/test_runner_web_search_errors.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/tools/test_private_tool_logging.py tests/agent/test_runner_errors.py -q --tb=short` — 149 passed with ddgs 9.11.4.
- The same search/model-input/privacy scope under `uv run --no-sync --with ddgs==9.16.0` — 134 passed. These are controlled offline library/runner checks, not a new VPS or live-model acceptance run.
- Full-project Ruff and Python import boundaries — passed.
- `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` — **FAIL**, four `BaseFileLock`/`FileLock` return-type diagnostics in unchanged `mcp_oauth.py`, `gateway/runtime.py`, `process_runtime.py` and `xai_oauth.py`. The identical environment against the frozen parent `06f398196` reproduces the same four diagnostics; they remain failures and are outside this change.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -n 3 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short` — **FAIL**, 1 failed, 11,020 passed, 186 skipped in 23m12s. The failure is `tests/gateway/test_runtime.py::test_competing_foreground_claim_preserves_the_live_gateway`: its first child did not publish the claim marker within the existing deadline. The isolated case passes on both this candidate and the frozen parent; the original full-suite failure remains unattributed, not cleared by those isolated passes.

Subsequent published-head CI and real-model black-box acceptance have passed. The original local failures remain documented above; no unrelated gateway tests, timeouts or type annotations were changed to make checks pass.


## Black-box acceptance

Completed through the normal CLI entrypoint in separate processes with isolated homes/configs/workspaces, a real DeepSeek `deepseek-v4-flash` model and ddgs 9.16.0. No scripted model responses or production hooks. All four cases used the same one-search request; persisted tool messages and the real final assistant responses were inspected.

| Case | Network condition | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Live search | Real search through the existing configured Web proxy | ddgs returned the official Python asyncio documentation; the model explained asyncio and cited the returned official URL. PASS (13.0s). |
| Refused connection | Task-owned proxy returned HTTP 403 to CONNECT; it did not contact search engines | Tool reported unavailable / cause unknown; the model reported the failed lookup and explicitly distinguished it from no matching pages, without inventing source links or a rate-limit diagnosis. PASS (7.2s). |
| Tool deadline | Controlled proxy held the connection beyond the configured one-second tool waiting deadline | Tool and real model reported the waiting timeout; no fabricated search-based answer or source. PASS (7.9s). |
| Library timeout | Controlled proxy held the connection; the tool's 100-second waiting budget allowed ddgs's existing request timeout to finish first | Tool identified a timeout reported by ddgs; the model reported the failed lookup and declined to invent a source link. PASS (47.1s). |

Each case made exactly one `web_search` tool call. The refusal and timeout conditions are synthetic network faults, not a claim to reproduce the original VPS rejection. Task processes and fixture listeners exited, fixture ports were released, the source instance's configuration was unchanged, and no provider keys were persisted in the verification files.

[CI run 39893174211](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39893174211) completed successfully for this published head, including the required gate, Python 3.11, Python 3.14 + coverage, Windows, Windows process compatibility and Docker. Path-unrelated checks were skipped. The original local failures above remain recorded; they were not reclassified as passing.

prs.title: feat(matrix): add "listen" group policy (observe room, reply on mention)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a third Matrix group policy value — **`"listen"`** — for rooms where the bot should read the whole conversation but reply only when mentioned (#6288).

Under `mention`, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright (`_on_message`), so the bot has no knowledge of the conversation when it's finally mentioned. Under `open` it replies to everything. `listen` closes that gap:

- Every message from an **allowed sender** in a listen room is ingested into a bounded per-room buffer.
- The bot replies **only when mentioned** — same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `mention`.
- On a mention-triggered turn, the buffered chatter rides along as **trusted runtime context** so the answer reflects the intervening conversation.

## How context is attached

Uses the existing trusted channel seam `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`) — this is the first channel producer of `_runtime_context_blocks`, whose docstring describes exactly this: *"trusted, channel-produced context blocks"* read from inbound metadata. Blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, so the LLM retains the context in subsequent turns while users never see the injected block as chat output.

Bounds per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's requirement ("callers must bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources"): 30 messages / 6,000 chars per room, 500 chars per line, header-delimited block, buffer cleared once consumed. No LLM calls for unheard messages; no agent-core changes.

## Behavior details

- Deny-listed senders are never buffered.
- Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass the policy entirely, as today.
- Media messages buffer a caption or `[attachment]` note — downloads/transcription are not triggered for unheard messages.
- Composes with per-room `groupPolicyOverrides` from #6287 once that lands (a trivial rebase in `_should_process_message`).

## Fixes #6288

## Tests

Seven new tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. `"listen"` accepted via attribute and camelCase config; unknown policy values still rejected.
2. Buffer bounds: oldest-dropped at 30 entries, 6,000-char budget, 500-char line truncation.
3. Unmentioned messages buffered with no reply/typing; the next mention triggers one turn carrying a bounded `matrix_room_transcript` block containing the buffered line; buffer cleared (subsequent mention carries no block).
4. Denied senders neither replied to nor buffered.
5. Direct rooms unaffected (no buffering, normal DM path).
6. `open` policy rooms never buffer (regression guard).
7. Media captions buffered as notes.

Verified locally: 127 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, import-boundary check passes, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on touched files. WebUI locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW).

> Note: this branch is based on current `main` without #6287. If #6287 merges first, expect small conflicts in `_should_process_message` (adjacent lines) and the docs table — happy to rebase.

prs.title: refactor(webui): replace idle polling with gateway invalidations
prs.body:
Related: [NAN-339](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-339)

## Why

Keeping WebUI tabs open repeatedly reads unchanged pairing requests, channel status, automations, usage, and remote connections. Replace those browser polling loops with gateway-owned invalidations so real changes appear promptly without multiplying work across idle tabs; retain the existing visible polling behavior when connecting to an older host.

## What changed

- Add optional `webui.state-events.v1` over the existing trusted WebSocket, with fixed resource-only notifications. Gateway-owned file watches, expiration deadlines, committed usage observation, and lightweight runtime sampling invalidate existing authoritative reads; remote-directory notifications retain their local-only audience.
- Share the browser refresh lifecycle across the six consumers: initial reads, changes during pending reads, hidden/visible return, reconnect, cancellation, and bounded transient retries. Move remote health probing to one manager-owned loop, preserve remote drafts/iframes, and apply health changes received during pending host switches.
- Keep time-dependent UI correct without restoring network polling: pairing countdowns follow the server deadline locally, and usage snapshots carry their grouping timezone so an externally changed timezone cannot make a mounted chart falsely display zero. Add regression coverage and a concise [developer contract](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/c906d4e3daefe47dd37d434e8f00b08769798533/docs/webui-state-events.md) for event/access boundaries, client refresh/compatibility, and gateway ownership/lifecycle.

## Scope

Covers pairing, Channels, the global automation list/calendar, session automation panels, Overview usage, and the local remote-instance directory. Keeps WebUI core protocol 1 and existing authoritative HTTP/mutation validation. Does not change agent execution ownership, authorization policy, session storage, OAuth/QR/update-job tracking, or automatically reconnect a remote host.

Documentation-only follow-up `c906d4e3d` reduces the contract from 925 to 448 words, removes per-feature implementation narration and verification checklists, and updates the development, WebSocket, and frontend README references. The event payload, trust/local-only policy, recovery/legacy behavior, watch readiness/failure handling, and joined shutdown requirements remain documented. Local link/anchor, JSON example, scope, and whitespace checks passed; runtime checks retain their recorded implementation revisions.

## Tradeoffs

- Persistent changes rely on native filesystem notifications, including atomic replacement and writes from another process. Source registration failure prevents the WebSocket/WebUI listener from starting rather than advertising an incomplete capability; unusual/network-mounted filesystems need deployment validation.
- A shared lightweight channel-runtime sample and shared remote health probes remain. This removes repeated browser snapshot polling, not every backend timer.
- Hosts with a confirmed compatible WebUI core contract that lack the new optional capability retain their supported polling schedules. Missing or malformed core metadata remains compatibility-unconfirmed and does not authorize mutations. Duration-only pairing responses are anchored at receipt; the host remains authoritative for expiration and approval.

## Blast Radius

The affected surfaces are trusted WebUI event delivery, lifecycle/cleanup of the six refresh consumers, and local remote-connection health. Tests cover stale/pending reads, visibility, reconnect/restart, multi-client propagation, secret-free invalidations, local-only directory access, and independent old-host compatibility.

## Follow-up convergence (`6ca51a1c2`, test-only correction `1e58a8d7d`)

Remote-directory manual, wake, and event reads now use one awaitable `useStateRefresh` scheduler, removing the second read queue and linked-signal bridge. Callers still await coalesced reads and receive the final failure/cancellation; mutation/connection isolation, deferred health, cached iframes/drafts, and legacy behavior remain. No backend or wire contract changed.

Fresh checks on the exact follow-up contents:

Windows CI also exposed a test-only portability error: Python `print` produces CRLF there, while the two cross-process usage readiness markers required LF. The test now removes only trailing CR/LF; uncommitted-WAL silence, post-commit notification and persisted-count assertions are unchanged. The corrected related Python suite freshly passed **1715 tests**; no production or asset bytes changed in this correction.

- Full frontend/channel suite: **3315 passed** (188 files); full controlled-browser suite: **230 passed**. TypeScript (app/browser), lint, import checks, production build and whitespace checks passed.
- The mixed manual/online/pageshow + state-invalidation regression first reproduced **3 GETs instead of 2**; it now makes exactly **2** and awaits the follow-up. Final-error propagation, hidden/unmount cancellation, and explicit legacy refresh without a live frame are covered. A separate real-network production-UI manual refresh + WS invalidation also coalesced to one follow-up.
- Fresh CLI gateways + production Chromium + public HTTP/WS: **12 current-host scenarios passed** and **203 effective remote/auth/real-old-host assertions passed**, without double-counting superseded usage reads. All six legacy consumers exercised visible polling, native hidden zero reads, return reads and supported manual actions. Shutdown with a real in-flight probe released owned listeners while the target remained up.
- Initial attempts included one renderer crash, one 40.554 s old-host activation/read observation, and one controlled-browser load timeout. Raw failures remain recorded. Bounded unchanged-source repeats passed; the old-host repeat retained both original and native-visibility 3 s deadlines (usage 32 ms, the other return reads 36–172 ms). **The earlier stalls remain unattributed warnings, not claimed product fixes or proven OOM causes.**
- GitHub CI on implementation head `1e58a8d7d` passed all selected checks, including Windows Python/installer/native-package acceptance and the required gates ([run 39820278944](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39820278944)). The first browser job exhausted its 15-minute job budget after browser provisioning took 8m37s; a single accepted same-head job rerun completed successfully. No browser assertions or time limits were changed.
- All test-owned processes/displays were stopped; an independent final check found all **43** recorded owned ports refusing connections. No daily instance was operated.

## Earlier broader verification (`75a28b62e`, followed by docs-only `b096069b4`)

The following evidence retains its original revision identity. The unchanged Python/backend checks remain applicable; the changed browser lifecycle was freshly rechecked above rather than counting these older executions as new runs:

- `python -m pytest -q tests/pairing tests/llm_usage tests/cron tests/triggers tests/webui nanobot/channels/websocket/tests`: **1715 passed**.
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1`: **3312 passed** across 188 frontend/channel test files, with Bun available for its runtime check.
- Full Playwright browser fixture suite: **230 passed**. This is controlled-browser coverage, not the real-host black-box evidence below.
- WebUI/browser TypeScript, frontend lint, changed-Python Ruff, affected-production BasedPyright, Python/client import boundaries, production build, and `git diff --check`: passed. The import-boundary suite's Windows-only casing check was skipped on Linux.
- Fresh CLI gateways + production Chromium + public HTTP/WS/CLI: **23 effective core black-box scenarios passed**; remote/auth/legacy integration: **195 effective assertions passed**. Invalid harness attempts were retained and classified, not silently removed or counted as product passes.

High-signal black-box observations:

- All browser API requests were **0** during measured idle chat (60 s), two automation views (65 s), Channels (60 s), and usage (60 s) windows. Pairing countdowns continued to update without reads; a real ten-minute request expired naturally and the old code was rejected.
- Actual channel/model/tool/automation/usage writes propagated, including an independent CLI task writer and a second CLI gateway committing usage. Changing UTC to a next-day timezone and back preserved **192 tokens** without reloading.
- Hidden consumers performed **0** relevant reads, then converged on return. A notification during a real 1500 ms delayed HTTP read caused a follow-up; real TCP disconnection and owned-gateway restart both converged on the latest state.
- Single/two-tab remote idle windows each issued **0** repeated directory GETs and the same **3** health probes per 16 s. An 80-GET burst added **0** probes. Actual identity changes/401s failed closed; pending single-offline delivery, preserved drafts/iframes, explicit disconnect, and shutdown with an in-flight health read passed.
- Current production assets served by an actual archived `eceea7b5` Python host naturally negotiated no state-events capability. All six consumers exercised real visible polling, native hidden zero reads, and return reads; no capability/event fabrication.

Boundaries: external model/chat endpoints and the SSH server were explicitly labeled loopback protocol peers (real OpenSSH authentication/forwarding to another real gateway), not real vendor accounts or WAN acceptance. Windows, unusual filesystems, natural midnight rollover, and deployment-level networking remain unverified. All test-owned processes/listeners were cleaned up; no daily instance was operated.

Local verification used the tested base `6ace6068d`; current `main` has two newer, non-overlapping WebUI changes. This PR preserves the verified candidate instead of silently rebasing it. Remote CI and review remain separate checks.

prs.title: fix(webui): make task state backend-authoritative
prs.body:
## Why

After reload, reconnect or switching topics, the sidebar and Composer can disagree about whether work is still running. Local sends, uploads and transcript history are not authoritative evidence that an execution is alive or that its final reply has arrived.

Related: [NAN-263](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-263).

## What changed

- Publish gateway-owned execution snapshots for real admitted owners, including work targeting a WebUI session from outside its WebSocket. Track queued, running and stopping independently from input delivery, transcript recovery and final-result settlement.
- Keep one FIFO worker/inbox per scheduled session and await a separate task for each root. Targeted Stop cancels only that root, waits for settlement and continues the original FIFO; it does not cancel/recreate the worker or re-admit later roots. Session discard/shutdown retain their worker-level cancellation boundary.
- Put early reservations, immutable admission identities and Stop intent in `ExecutionLifecycle`. The gateway receives its narrow control port explicitly; `RunStateAuthority` only projects facts and the event publisher no longer creates owners. Internal continuations enter the ordinary enqueue boundary rather than writing the raw inbox.
- Add optional `webui.runs.v1` snapshots with instance identity, monotonic revisions and live owners only; no execution-completion cache or public receipt history. State-only sidebar subscriptions do not attach every topic's transcript. Disconnect means unknown; replaced sockets and stale HTTP responses cannot restore freshness.
- Use the same confirmed per-topic state for sidebar, Composer and Stop. Accepting Stop is not proof of exit. Preserve early cancellation before persistence/FIFO admission, retire provisional unified-session steering reservations and rejected journal admissions without affecting another owner, acknowledge only explicitly owned follow-ups, and do not block the global inbound consumer while awaiting a scoped Stop.
- Commit the final reply before releasing result fences or automatically sending queued input. Require confirmed idle state and preserve recovery authorization; never automatically resend an unconfirmed input. Keep invalid no-argument command errors outside the agent lifecycle.

## Scope

Execution lifecycle/admission, WebUI transport and client state consumers, with regression tests and user/developer documentation. No persistence-schema, dependency, provider-API or core protocol-floor change. Older protocol-1 hosts retain basic chat; confirmed execution indicators, scoped Stop and automatic queued sending require the optional capability. This does not unify direct-call and scheduled entrypoints or introduce another scheduler/general hook framework.

## Tradeoffs

Execution authority is process-local and versioned, not inferred from history or elapsed time. Execution exit does not certify result delivery; message receipts, canonical completion and result fences remain separate, and missing evidence remains unknown. Reconnection converges on confirmed state rather than promising instantaneous equality across a disconnected network. Existing bounded subagent cancellation remains unchanged: resistant child work stays tracked, not certified physically terminated. Older clients may still leave a local candidate for malformed inline commands; this is not an active backend owner and is not claimed fixed universally.

## Blast Radius

Agent admission/cancellation, root-task context and continuation lifecycle, WebUI HTTP/WebSocket projection, reconnect, sidebar, Composer/Stop and queued input. Channel transports forward only an optional trusted frozen admission identity. Gateway composition explicitly shares the agent's execution control; its fixture updates do not introduce an adapter-owned fallback. Tests protect early/queued Stop, unchanged worker/FIFO identity, cleanup barriers, non-overlap, unified-session steering/rejection, in-flight journal handoff, cancellation during recovery admission, concurrent owners, stale epochs/revisions, lost acknowledgements and final-text ordering.

## Verification

### CI repair and main sync — `1a282c94718e714d6137f01e00c15593e7b6a179`

- Rebased without conflicts onto main `06f3981962ccfa37e9d8edda583cad4b651a6054`; the seven existing patches compare equal across the final rebase. The additional supervisor-test commit is scoped below.
- Restrict the channel CSS regression to the actual channel globs and every exclusion from the loaded production Tailwind configuration. It still generates the real channel CSS and fails when the channel glob is removed or excluded, without repeating the whole application/test-source scan.
- Enumerate existing PowerShell session/PATH commands without importing unrelated modules while probing missing managers. Keep session functions/aliases and the persistent uv/pipx installation policy. Native Windows checks cover the missing-manager module trap and existing session function.
- Keep the stale-supervisor regression at its authorization boundary: real frozen supervisor/worker/installed preflight, all stale-A no-side-effect assertions, current-B journal/claim/admission, controlled preflight refusal, unchanged environment/approval, no mutation/fence and released lease. Complete managed installation/restart/recovery remains in the existing native packaged acceptance, not this focused authorization case. No failed-case timeout or production safety check was relaxed.
- Local supervisor/confirmation/retry/budget selection: **11 passed**; omitting only the disposable frozen supervisor's first-journal identity gate makes the original no-stale-journal assertion fail. Local portable-Python verification used an external symlink-venv bootstrap, not a repository fixture change; Windows CI uses the ordinary fixture.
- Exact-head [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39827769996): **all 15 checks passed**, including `CI required`, Windows Python/process/installer compatibility and Linux/Windows native packaged installation, upgrade and automatic recovery. WebUI coverage ran **3,317 unit tests**; browser/type/lint/build checks passed. Windows isolated jobs: **81 passed / 5 skipped**; Windows installer: **80 passed / 1 skipped**. The formerly failed cases and the new PowerShell regression are explicitly PASSED, not skipped.
- Causality limit: the unwanted command-discovery module-import mechanism and the authorization test's full-install coupling are confirmed; the exact actors consuming the historical Windows 90s/40s limits are not established by the old logs. A later green run is not claimed as proof of those historical timings.

### Cleanup snapshot — `954247489c3fc79fa6230a4dc46265b3af679b5c`

- Remove unused metadata Stop/wait APIs, duplicated execution identity, completion/outcome receipt plumbing, three latest-turn caches and ingress dual registration. Net reduction from `efd102bd`: 240 production lines and 361 lines overall; this is subtraction, not a file move.
- Derive workspace busy decisions and legacy live hints from execution facts. Pending transcripts retain only display owner/generation and write-failure protection; a reset cannot inherit an old generation's unfinished guard, including when storage rejects the old write at capacity before validating generation.

prs.title: fix(agent): budget oversized tool-result delta after compaction so large read_file rounds no longer abort the turn
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5879: a tool round of large `read_file` results can abort the turn even when history summarization succeeds. `read_file` is exempt from the ingest-time tool-result budget (deliberately — the exemption prevents persist→read→persist loops, #4155), so its results enter the post-acceptance delta unbounded. Compaction preserves the delta unchanged, so when the delta alone exceeds the input budget, `ensure_request_fits` raises `ContextWindowExceededError` after a successful summary and the turn ends `started -> failed`.

## Change (`nanobot/agent/context_governance.py`)

- In `_compact_request_history`, if the post-compaction request still doesn't fit, the delta's tool results are admitted under the standard budget on the model-facing copy as a last resort, and the fit check runs again. The context guard is unchanged: a request that still doesn't fit after budgeting is refused exactly as before.
- The budgeting reuses the existing machinery — `apply_tool_result_budget` / `normalize_tool_result` gain an `include_exempt` flag that lifts the offload exemption for this pass only. With a workspace, oversized results are persisted in full and replaced by the usual reference + preview, so the model can read the persisted result back in slices; the raw transcript is never modified. The ingest-time exemption itself is untouched, so the #4155 loop cannot return.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py`, using the issue's scenario (three 80,000-char `read_file` results, `max_tool_result_chars=16000`, byte-fallback estimator forced for determinism):

- `test_oversized_read_file_delta_is_budgeted_after_summarization` — compaction emits `started -> succeeded`, the prepared tool results are shrunk, and the raw transcript keeps its full contents. Fails on the unpatched code with the issue's exact error (`240507/190784 via heuristic`).
- `test_oversized_delta_still_rejected_when_budgeted_delta_cannot_fit` — 30 oversized reads still raise `ContextWindowExceededError` after budgeting, locking the guard in place.

## Verification

- The issue's own reproduction probe: unpatched aborts with `ContextWindowExceededError` and `['started', 'failed']`; patched completes with `['started', 'succeeded']`.
- Repo test suite: full `tests/agent` run passes — 1980 tests (1978 pre-existing + the 2 new ones); the pre-existing oversized-delta refusal tests pass unchanged.
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files.

prs.title: ci: isolate Test Suite runs by revision
prs.body:
## Why
The Test Suite used only workflow name and ref for concurrency. A re-run retains the original SHA and ref, so re-running an older `main` commit could cancel a newer commit's checks; [run 39797323916](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39797323916) lost its WebUI and Docker jobs this way, leaving the latest revision unverified while aggregate checks reported failure. The validation identity should be the ref **and the code revision**, not the time a run was requested.

## What changed
- Include `github.sha` in the workflow concurrency group. Different revisions on the same ref no longer cancel one another; retries of the same revision can still supersede each other.
- Add a regression check for the workflow's revision-scoped concurrency contract. Leave `CI required` strict: cancellation must not masquerade as a passing test.

## Scope
This changes scheduling for Test Suite runs on `main`, pull requests, and manual dispatch. It does not change test selection, job definitions, branch protection, or runtime code.

## Tradeoffs
A PR update no longer cancels checks for earlier commits on the same PR, so rapid pushes can consume more runner minutes. This also avoids the same stale-re-run cancellation defect on PRs; the existing ref-only group cannot distinguish a genuinely newer revision from an older run requested later. Checks for the same ref/SHA can still supersede one another. Only existing standard GitHub-hosted runners are used.

## Blast Radius
CI concurrency grouping only. Distinct SHAs may run concurrently, but their required checks still report against their respective revisions.

## Verification
- Before the workflow change, the new regression test failed against the ref-only concurrency key; after the change, `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py tests/scripts/test_ci_gate.py tests/scripts/test_ci_scope.py -q` passed (81 tests).
- `python -m ruff check tests/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` and `git diff --check` passed. Parsed the workflow with the existing PyYAML BaseLoader.
- GitHub's real scheduler race cannot be reproduced locally; this PR's remote checks remain the integration validation.

prs.title: perf(webui): animate segmented indicator without layout
prs.body:
## Why
Switching between differently sized segments currently interpolates the indicator's `width`, performing layout on animation frames. This is a small rendering-cost improvement, not a demonstrated user-visible speedup.

## What changed
- Hold the indicator's box width steady during selection changes and animate its `translate` and `scale` independently with the existing 220 ms / 160 ms timing curves.
- Rebase the width without motion when a measured option actually changes size; ignore no-op resize notifications.
- Update the existing unit test to cover selection and a genuine size change; no dedicated browser test is retained.

## Scope
Only the shared WebUI segmented-control indicator changes. Tab semantics, focus behavior, data flow, and the gateway are untouched.

## Tradeoffs
Horizontal scaling can subtly reshape the indicator's rounded ends, ring, and shadow **during** travel. Its final position and dimensions match the selected option. This is not a blanket rule to replace intentional layout transitions elsewhere.

## Blast Radius
Shared controls in settings and file preview use the indicator. Locale, size changes, and reduced motion were checked in a one-off Chromium gallery run; Firefox/WebKit were not verified with the current Playwright release because their matching browser binaries are not installed locally.

## Verification
- Production-built A/B fixture using the baseline from `main` and this branch in Chromium 156, five interleaved runs per side, 12 Day/Week/Month switches per run: **median layout time 7.17 ms → 0.57 ms per 12 switches** (132 → 12 layout events). No alignment failures, console errors, or >22 ms frames in either variant; style/script time was not meaningfully reduced, and the animation still takes 220 ms.
- Existing focused Vitest suite: 4 passed after the test cleanup; TypeScript check, targeted ESLint, and `git diff --check` passed. The production Vite build and two one-off Playwright gallery checks passed before the standalone browser spec was removed (it is not part of this PR).

prs.title: feat(exec): enforce user deny patterns in full access with case-insensitive matching
prs.body:
@'
## Summary

When users configure 	ools.exec.denyPatterns (e.g. [\Remove-Item\]), commands were previously still executed without restriction if the workspace permission was set to Full Access. This occurred because commit 09d3bd76 bypassed _guard_command in Full Access mode under the rationale that Full Access is an explicit trust decision.

However, user-configured denyPatterns represent an explicit, intentional safety boundary (e.g. blocking destructive commands like Remove-Item) that users expect to be enforced even when granting filesystem freedom via Full Access. Furthermore, pattern matching was previously case-sensitive against lowercased command strings, which prevented uppercase or mixed-case patterns like Remove-Item from matching.

This PR:
1. Treats user-configured deny_patterns as an explicit safety policy enforced across all access modes (including Full Access mode).
2. Uses case-insensitive regex matching (e.IGNORECASE) for both allow and deny patterns.
3. Preserves llow_patterns priority so users can explicitly exempt commands.
4. Keeps workspace path boundaries and network/URL safety guards restricted to estrict_to_workspace=True mode, maintaining Full Access filesystem freedom.
5. Adds explanatory comments and comprehensive unit test coverage.

## Changes

- **
anobot/agent/tools/shell.py**:
  - Store self.user_deny_patterns = list(deny_patterns or []) in ExecTool.__init__.
  - Add helper _check_deny_patterns with case-insensitive matching and llow_patterns precedence.
  - In _prepare_command, enforce self.user_deny_patterns before the workspace restriction check, with clear code comments.
  - Refactor _guard_command to reuse _check_deny_patterns.
- **	ests/tools/test_exec_security.py**:
  - Update 	est_exec_full_access_skips_command_guard to test metadata URL guard skipping without conflicting with user deny rules.
  - Add 	est_exec_full_access_enforces_user_deny_patterns to assert user deny patterns block execution in Full Access.
  - Add 	est_exec_deny_patterns_case_insensitive to verify case-insensitive pattern matching (e.g. Remove-Item).
  - Add 	est_exec_user_deny_patterns_allow_priority to assert allowlist exemptions function in Full Access.

## Verification

- uv run ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py tests/tools/test_exec_security.py: All checks passed.
- uv run pytest tests/tools/test_exec_security.py: 79 passed, 9 skipped.
- uv run pytest tests/tools/test_exec_allow_patterns.py tests/tools/test_exec_session_tools.py: 59 passed.
'@

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
## Why

Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What changed

- Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the same native user-message bubble, preserving its background, typography and natural sizing. The focused editor has its own draft, Cancel and Resend controls, actionable errors, and concise translations in all 10 locales; Composer drafts, attachments and waiting input stay separate.
- Route replacement through gateway idle admission and the session-state owner. Revision-bound anchors, an SQLite transaction, a recoverable display-transcript journal and persisted retry receipts preserve session identity and accept the new input exactly once.
- Fence discarded history by generation across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results. Invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation and reuse the shared history-prefix boundary while preserving the existing **New conversation** fork behavior.
- Settle interrupted edit journals under the transcript deletion lock. Restore old display files only while the original canonical generation still exists; deletion or recreation retires the journal instead of resurrecting removed messages. Close the recovery SQLite connection explicitly on Windows.

## Scope

The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together: message editing has no per-feature compatibility gate or gateway-unsupported fallback.

Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, branch picker or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back.

## Tradeoffs

Canonical history lives in SQLite while the display transcript remains file-backed. A temporary rollback journal coordinates their commit and crash recovery; it is removed after settlement and is not a retained conversation version. Pre-acceptance failures preserve the previous effective history. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix.

## Blast Radius

This touches session admission/persistence, WebUI transcript reads and WebSocket delivery, frontend history reconciliation, and subagent result ownership. The main risks are cross-client races, stale events restoring a removed suffix, and retry/crash behavior around the two persistence projections. Existing new-fork behavior is covered separately; this does not redesign subagent cancellation or external-effect rollback.

## Verification

Published source: `6fc74f88896877b2b8c8b3010546d95cef63cc75`, based on `909b277e7a5a7ecd2aebdba9611e5febe86988d9`. The latest follow-up fixes interrupted-edit recovery after deletion/recreation, removes the new edit capability gate, and replaces the misleading conversation/gateway-unavailable error with the actual shared-history restriction in all 10 locales. Missing required edit services are composition errors, not optional older-gateway behavior. The earlier native-bubble integration, helper-line removal, strict typing/task-context fixes and test-only CLI fixture fix remain intact.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh related Python tests | **110 passed** across message editing, pre/post-commit crash recovery and delete/recreate regressions, forking, client contract, agent admission and transcript/thread helpers |
| Fresh full ThreadShell and editor component files | **123 passed**, including saved-message edit/Resend through the full shell without an edit capability flag |
| Fresh i18n tests and 10-locale content audit | **29 passed**; only the obsolete unavailable error key is replaced with the shared-history error in each locale |
| Fresh Ruff; strict BasedPyright; Python import boundaries | **PASS**; BasedPyright reports 0 errors/warnings/notes, import boundaries cover 10 rules / 166 files |
| Fresh WebUI lint; `git diff --check` | **PASS** |
| Fresh `bun run build` | **PASS**, with the existing Vite >500 kB chunk warning; output is isolated outside the retained preview |
| Fresh `bun x tsc --noEmit` | **FAIL**, exit 2, **473 diagnostics**. Normalized `(file, TS code, message)` diagnostics exactly match committed head `723e670f62ea4df73611702f086acdfdae943be0`, with none added or removed. |
| Fresh authenticated public-wire crash/delete probe | **PASS**: real child exits after SQL commit, journal survives startup scan, WebSocket `session.delete` succeeds before first replay, history returns HTTP 404, the topic is absent from the complete session list, and canonical/display/journal/stage data remain absent. Owned listener closes and temporary data is removed. |
| CI for the newly pushed head | Not yet verified; the earlier green run below belongs to `723e670f`, not this new head. |

The earlier deletion-fix broad backend command had **882 passed, 18 skipped, 2 failed**. Both failures are Windows remote-discovery tests whose `getpass.getuser()` cannot find username environment variables in this execution sandbox; the exact committed tests and owning modules reproduced the same failures. No environment/config workaround or unrelated remote-discovery change was made. The 110-test final-snapshot run is focused verification, not a replacement claim that this broader command passed. The previous 11 session-delete HTTP route cases also passed; their owning behavior is unchanged by removing the edit capability gate.

Earlier [Test Suite CI at 723e670f](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39382896974) passed the applicable Python 3.11/3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI checks/build/browser regressions, Docker and change-detection jobs; the unchanged TUI matrix was skipped. GitHub tested synthetic integration snapshot `aeb1a671f3c80eb48eeb297ed734244ff5d02032` against main `a1bca7dc50c993a30e3730d8bc63baea457991a9`. This is historical evidence, not CI for the latest commit. The local branch was not rebased or merged.

At `723e670f`, task-owned Chrome for the helper removal checked English and Chinese at desktop and 390×844 touch-emulated widths against the retained production-build preview. All four cases passed: the editor stays inside the same native bubble, only Cancel/Resend controls appear beneath its text, and cancelling preserves the original input without sending a replacement. There were no page errors. The served index was checked against the new build; no gateway restart or history reset was needed.

The earlier full native-bubble browser pass exercised an isolated gateway, SQLite/display storage and a deterministic OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider fixture: desktop mouse/keyboard and focus/cancel, first/middle/paginated edits, Composer draft/quote/mention/attachment/waiting-input isolation, busy/stale rejection, refresh, real socket disconnect/retry, same-turn retry with a different request ID, post-acceptance provider failure, and stable identity/topic count. Seven core groups and the independent **New conversation** regression passed with no page errors. That browser run remains evidence for the unchanged native editor, input/admission and replacement behavior; the newer deletion/recovery change is covered by the fresh crash/delete probe and focused tests above. No fresh browser or model E2E run is claimed for this follow-up.

Earlier contract evidence remains scoped to the unchanged owning behavior: the original candidate's related Python scope had **1885 passed, 21 skipped** and the earlier local full frontend run had **2968 passed / 169 files**; the previous head's local CLI run had **163 passed, 1 skipped**, with strict BasedPyright and backend checks passing; canonical history, authenticated display history and complete provider prompts matched; SQL/display fault injection and real subprocess exits before/after commit covered journal recovery; native subagent tests covered old children returning during and after the replacement reply. These earlier runs are inherited evidence, not freshly rerun final-head local full-suite results.

Physical touch hardware, external-model acceptance and user visual acceptance remain unverified. The separate browser-verification runtime has been cleaned; a user-requested local preview remains available. No production configuration/history was used. Maintainer review is still required.

## Summary

Replace the JEV-specific client and configuration with a reusable structured-decision client. The client exposes typed questions and results through a provider/protocol abstraction; OpenRouter with the System One protocol is the initial registered backend.

The default model remains `typesafe/jev-1.13`. JEV is now a model choice behind the shared interface rather than a JEV-specific client API.

- Replace the top-level `jev` config with opt-in `structuredDecision` settings.
- Document the configuration and current provider limitations.
- Add client and configuration tests.

## Scope and limitations

- OpenRouter is the only registered provider, and System One is the only supported protocol.
- The client is infrastructure only; no heartbeat, routing, policy, or other caller is integrated.
- Custom decision endpoints and endpoint URL overrides are not supported.
- Provider fallback, telemetry, and caller-specific confidence thresholds are out of scope.

## Verification

- The latest PR checks report success for Python 3.11, Python 3.14 with coverage, Windows 3.14, and the matrix job.
- Tests cover structured-decision client behavior and configuration parsing.

prs.title: fix(webui): refine sidebar icon consistency and spacing
prs.body:
## Why

The sidebar's detailed navigation icons looked visually heavier than their labels. Refine their silhouettes and scale while keeping navigation compact and conversation handles recognizable.

## What changed

- Simplify Skills, Automations, and Channels icons into a rounded puzzle piece, square clock, and single speech bubble; keep the Apps grid unchanged.
- Render expanded sidebar action icons at 16px rather than 18px, keeping the existing label typography, row height, and 8px icon–label gap.
- Use an 8px handle–title gap consistently across conversation rows without imposing a shared navigation/conversation grid or fixed handle column.

## Scope

Presentation only. Preserve handle fonts and colors, navigation behavior, running indicators, touch targets, accessibility labels, and client/host contracts. No gateway, configuration, dependency, or persistence changes.

## Blast Radius

These are shared product icons: the Skills silhouette also appears in command suggestions, and the Automations silhouette appears on cron tool cards. Their callers, sizing contracts, and behavior are unchanged.

## Verification

- Frontend unit suite: 3,281 passed, 1 skipped across 184 passing test files and one skipped file.
- TypeScript typecheck and production build passed; Vite reports a non-fatal large-chunk advisory.
- ESLint on changed TSX files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused read-only source review found no blocking regression, including shared icon consumers, collapsed navigation, touch hit areas, and accessibility labels.
- The user accepted the rendered rounded icon style and 16px icon scale in the isolated Vite instance.
- Chromium black-box acceptance covered navigation through all four entries and return to chat, desktop and 390px narrow layouts, expanded/collapsed sidebar, Simplified Chinese and English, light/dark themes, long-title truncation, stable row geometry on hover, keyboard focus, and skill command suggestions. Inspected screenshots and geometry show left-aligned icons/handles, 16px icons, and 8px icon–label gaps; no page script error or narrow-page horizontal overflow was observed.
- Browser-run caveat: Chromium reported two renderer `Target crashed` failures during automation. The browser/pages were recovered and the scoped scenarios completed, but the cause is unresolved; this does not establish long-running stability or rule out an application contribution.
- Limits: no model execution, real message sends, real channel integration, physical touch device, screen reader, or cross-browser matrix. The test instance has no cron history, so cron icon rendering was reviewed in source rather than exercised with a new tool run. Remote CI remains a separate check.
