prs.title: fix(webui): check for updates only after opening About
prs.body:
## Why

Normal chatting should not trigger background release discovery or produce slow version-check requests. Wait until the user opens Settings → About instead of checking when the client connects.

Closes https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-337

## What changed

- Remove the connection-check effect and its `autoCheck` / `checkUpdatesOnConnect` props, including the application caller; do not retain a disabled or unused path.
- Keep About-entry automatic checks, manual check/retry, channel-change refresh, shared results, in-flight deduplication, and late-host-response isolation.
- Update the existing About-entry and update-flow tests and add a short user-guide section explaining when checks run. No interface strings or locale keys change.
- Add an `AGENTS.md` rule against tests that merely assert nonexistent behavior or removed symbols are absent; require negative assertions to protect concrete reachable risks.

## Scope

Frontend check triggers only. No HTTP/WebSocket contract, capability, authentication, persistence, release discovery, timeout, installation, or restart behavior changes. Existing clients keep their own check-trigger behavior; hosts do not need a protocol change. The sidebar notice remains usable after About discovers an update.

## Blast Radius

Startup and connection changes no longer discover updates, so a new update notice appears only after a user-initiated discovery (including entering About). Shared version state and the existing update consent flow remain intact. The screenshot's repeated ~20-second requests are not a proven network root cause, and this PR does not claim to fix network latency.

## Verification

- Extend the existing About-entry scenario to assert no request before entry, then check the visible loading/result states, shared in-flight request, re-entry, and retry. Remove the separate absence-only lifecycle test; no source-text or removed-symbol absence tests.
- `bun run --cwd webui test`: 185 files, 3282 tests passed, including About re-entry, manual retry, channel refresh, in-flight deduplication, draft preservation, and late-host-response isolation.
- `bun run --cwd webui typecheck`: passed.
- `bun run --cwd webui lint`: passed.
- `bun run --cwd webui check:imports`: passed (396 files).
- `bun run --cwd webui build`: passed (bundle-size warnings only).
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Verification used frontend component tests, not a live gateway/browser acceptance session. No daily instance was changed or restarted. Remote CI is separate from these local results.

## Summary

The OAuth callback input showed a sample localhost URL. Users could mistake that placeholder for a generated URL that they should copy. This change makes the next action clear.

- Replace the sample URL with a short instruction to paste the full callback URL.
- Explain where to copy the URL, including when the localhost page cannot load, and how to finish sign-in.
- Use a sign-in waiting message that does not imply the callback listener stays active.
- Update all ten supported languages and the existing test assertions. The shared MCP placeholder stays provider-neutral.

## Verification

- 145 related localization, provider, model and MCP OAuth tests passed. After the final wording edits, all 28 affected provider tests passed again.
- Targeted ESLint, production build and diff checks passed.
- Locale comparison confirmed that only four existing values changed per language. Keys, interpolation variables and prompts are unchanged.
- An isolated Chrome check rendered the production dialog in 16 language, viewport and local/remote combinations. It checked empty input, paste, button enablement and fixture submission. Chinese and French screenshots were checked for wrapping.

## Compatibility and limits

No breaking change. OAuth execution, timeouts, credentials, storage, startup and update contracts are unchanged. The browser checks used a fake authorization flow, not a live account. This fixes misleading guidance; it does not repair a stopped localhost callback listener or publish a release.

prs.title: ci: reuse isolated pip seeds and parallelize native acceptance
prs.body:
## Summary

Reduce repeated integration preparation and the native serial critical path while retaining per-test isolation and the complete acceptance workload. This is an experimental Draft: the final matched-source full run is green, but current-main PR integration still exposes two timing-sensitive Windows failures.

## Changes

- Keep stdlib venv responsible for creating each independent test prefix. Reuse the current interpreter's exact ensurepip wheels through virtualenv's offline app-data seeder only; copy packages and regenerate prefix-specific console scripts without virtualenv creation/import hooks. Real pip installation, updates and recovery remain exercised.
- Split native acceptance into two independent controller lanes, retaining all nine scenarios and fifteen journeys per OS. Each lane installs its own dependencies once and owns its venv, HOME/config/data/cache/temp, locks and processes. Recovery and the following upgrade stay ordered within the same lane; target wheel identity and complete report coverage are checked before merging results.
- Try doubled workers: Linux pytest 2→4, ordinary Windows pytest 3→6, browser 1→2 and native 1→2. The heavy Windows update6/installer8 trials failed, so these lanes retain their original 3/4 budgets. Serial CLI/process checks, platform/Python matrix, coverage gates, original test assertions/parameterization, retries and existing deadlines are unchanged.
- Retain controller-tree ownership after the controller exits: reuse the existing suspended-spawn Windows Job Object owner; unconditionally clear the owned POSIX process group before private-config gateway cleanup. Public native artifacts remain restricted to explicit safe result/report JSON paths, excluding credential-bearing raw logs.

The dev extra adds virtualenv rather than hand-building pip or copying a live relocatable venv. Its current dependency constraints resolve dev filelock to 3.32.7 instead of 4.2.4; production dependency constraints and the application version are unchanged. Native parallelism pays for a second independent dependency installation.

## Snapshot-bound measurement

Frozen product baseline: `bc5c58d23941b1bcca8980c4a0ebfc4d1d783bf2`. Final head: `d8a1fbd0b8402273c57d39f7126893f8eb9aeeb5`. Ancestry and unchanged production/browser workload were checked. Main advanced by five commits during the experiment; PR synthetic-merge timings are excluded from this performance comparison.

Two frozen-source control runs: [39748961300](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39748961300) and [39765369473](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765369473). Final matched-source candidate: [39765207434](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765207434), **SUCCESS, 21m28s total**. The following ranges use only successful, equivalent stages; the browser has one completed control.

| Stage, excluding job queue | Frozen baseline | Final candidate | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Windows native upgrade/recovery | 16:32–22:23 | 10:03 | 39–55% |
| Linux native upgrade/recovery | 9:28–11:13 | 5:07 | 46–54% |
| Linux coverage main tests | 8:33–8:41 | 5:19 | 38–39% |
| Linux minimum main tests | 8:29–10:16 | 7:32 | 11–27% |
| Windows isolated update tests, still 3 workers | 6:11–7:08 | 5:23 | 13–25% |
| Windows ordinary main tests, successful control only | 9:15 | 8:20 | 10% |
| Browser test step, same 223 cases | 8:13 | 6:28 | 21% |

Whole Windows native job: 23:29–28:52→20:59 (11–27%); build, clean installation and other setup limit the end-to-end benefit. Whole Linux native job: 11:42–13:47→7:03 (40–49%). Installer4 has **no established gain**: its successful test steps ranged 13:28–16:44 in controls and took 16:39 in the final candidate.

Original Python node IDs were retained with unchanged outcomes against the successful repeat-control stages: Linux main 10,937→10,952 and Windows main 10,696→10,711 add fifteen infrastructure regression cases; update86, installer80, serialCLI253, process59 and coordination25 are unchanged. Both native reports retain exactly 9 scenarios/15 journeys with identical outcome facts. Browser223 passed in the completed control and candidate, with zero retries.

The first control overall failed with a Settings API `httpx.ReadTimeout`. The repeat control's Python/native/installer jobs passed, but browser installation took 577s and the browser job hit its unchanged 15-minute limit before completing tests. Queueing reached 364s in that repeat and is reported separately from execution. Thus there is no all-green-before/all-green-after whole-workflow comparison. Observed runner-seconds were 7,299/6,847 for the incomplete controls and 5,656 for the successful candidate; these are recorded, not presented as a proven full-workflow cost reduction.

## Verification and remaining blockers

- [Final current-main PR integration 39765214057](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765214057) tested merge `284a936ed60f174a581da8920c1a21bd0e34d84e` with target `254f94b068bd0338396b71ac6ec244812b79e1c8`. Native, Linux, installer, browser228 and the isolated Windows update suite passed. Windows main had two failures, so the required gate remains red:
  - `test_graphql_rate_limit_error_is_retryable`: its live-clock 60-second reset was created before setup; the test took 12.68s and then asserted at least 50s remained, observing 47.32s. This is an existing wall-clock-sensitive test exposed in the six-worker run; the effect of worker count has not been isolated.
  - `test_settings_api_returns_safe_subset_and_updates_whitelist`: `httpx.ReadTimeout`, the same failure observed in the first frozen control at three workers. The endpoint root cause remains outside this optimization's verified results.
- Initial six-update/eight-installer worker trials failed in two independent runs ([matched](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39753831920), [PR](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39753834636)). Restoring update3 did not immediately eliminate an intermittent supervisor timeout in a matched run, while that head's PR run passed it. Final stdlib-created environments passed update86 in both matched and PR runs; this does not establish the cause of the earlier timeout. No deadline or retry was increased.
- Real exited-controller descendant-listener regression demonstrated red→green; verifier/seed/lifecycle selection: 31 passed with two workers. Final direct seed/supervisor selection: 2 passed; exact seed isolation also passed under Python 3.11.12. Original 83 installation/update test function ASTs, including decorators and parameterization, are unchanged.
- Hosted final Linux lint, import boundaries, BasedPyright and coverage passed. Local Windows BasedPyright still reports two optional setproctitle diagnostics, reproduced on the exact archived baseline under the same interpreter/dependencies.
- Full local WebUI typecheck/lint/import scan passed; browser223 passed with two workers. Import-checker tests initially had 39 pass/3 timeout; one unchanged-command rerun passed42 without increasing deadlines. Initial prototype-only local covered timing (291.19→170.79s, identical4,411 executed production lines) is retained as earlier evidence, not attributed to final source.

Keep Draft pending Windows stability work. No formal review, merge, tracker change or shared-runtime modification was performed.

prs.title: feat(attachments): support local files and video attachments
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI rejects videos before they reach the existing upload backend, and native TUI path pastes remain plain text. Add video attachment entry points and let both clients reference files the gateway can already read, without uploading or copying their contents.

Related to [NAN-284](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-284).

## What changed

- Revoke borrowed-media access when its draft/persisted session is deleted or Temporary Chat is discarded. Resolve live session authority for every signed request; a missing session returns unavailable instead of inheriting a broader default workspace.
- Preserve prompt typing before/after a pasted path while its asynchronous inspection completes in WebUI and TUI. Invalidate only an edited path, retain IME composition and cursor position, and do not steal focus from another Composer control. Accept apostrophes in otherwise valid standalone paths.
- Offer an explicit local Retry after video loading fails, so a recovered connection can restore playback without refreshing the conversation. No automatic retry, timer, or new player/source replacement is added to the healthy path.
- Keep each usable image path as an explicit text reference beside its native vision block, so the model can both see the image and use the same file with tools. Persist that reference once; keep upload storage paths distinct from borrowed original paths and preserve provider continuation.
- Preserve mixed local/upload attachment order through one ordered Composer draft sequence, including navigation/remount, draft identity tracking and first-send recovery. Browser File bodies remain memory-only; local references retain their relative order after reload and existing v1 records remain readable.
- Share lightweight `attachment.inspect` checks and send-time permission/readability/nonempty/format/count validation in the gateway. Local path references have no per-file or combined byte cap and never upload or copy the original. Messages still allow one MP4/WebM/MOV video plus four non-video attachments. Browser File/clipboard uploads retain the existing 20 MiB video limit and 6 MiB per non-video / 24 MiB combined non-video budget; local references do not spend those upload budgets, including in mixed or restored queued messages.
- Add WebUI video picker/drop support and standalone-path conversion in WebUI/TUI, with removable attachments and retained text/drafts on failure. Preserve browser `File` and clipboard-image uploads, including first-message rejection/retry. Oversized uploads now report the actual size and upload maximum in all ten locales; the backend also returns a specific size/limit error instead of `Invalid attachment size`.
- Serve borrowed local references in place through session-scoped signed media URLs; recheck permissions, support byte ranges, reflect source changes, and keep borrowed originals out of upload/temporary-chat cleanup. Persist attachment origin so immutable uploads retain their original signed URLs and private immutable HTTP cache policy, including after canonical history replay.
- Start uploaded-video playback from the durable URL returned by `message_accepted` and preserve that player/source through canonical history hydration. Pending user bubbles do not retain the encoded video body; fresh history/reloads use the same signed URL. Local path references keep reading their original file.
- Skip upload-store inspection/pruning for text-only and local-only sends. Remove the redundant preliminary upload resolution while retaining batch validation before commit; uploaded sends return from three staging scans to the original two.
- Resolve the previously failing verification: make Windows fixtures independent of symlink privileges, copied Scoop shims, and optional username environment variables; include the process-naming type dependency in the dev environment; fix stale typed WebUI fixtures/mocks and load Vite declarations in the full-project typecheck. Make the stream idle-renewal test independent of host scheduling while retaining real timeout/cleanup checks. No tests or type checks are disabled.

## Scope

WebUI, native TUI, and their shared gateway attachment ingress/media replay are covered. The frontend and gateway ship together and use the matching release's attachment contract; no independent-upgrade compatibility layer is added. Other channels' receive/download/storage behavior is unchanged. Videos still enter the agent context as `[Attachment: path]`; native provider video input, transcoding, frame extraction, and transcription belong to NAN-190.

## Tradeoffs

Borrowed references intentionally follow the current original file rather than a snapshot. Removing a draft, discarding uploads, or deleting a session must not delete that file. Only borrowed references use `Cache-Control: no-store` to reflect changes and current permissions; managed uploads retain `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Assistant outbound staging remains unchanged. Browser files still use the existing upload pipeline, but an uploaded video no longer pins an encoded preview in its message/player state.

## Blast Radius

The shared upload batch policy, WebSocket message admission, user-media signing/replay, and both composers are affected. Signed borrowed-media URLs recheck the session workspace instead of staging a copy; managed-upload signing keeps its original ownership and cache behavior. Test/config-only follow-up commits repair the existing full-project verification failures separately from the attachment behavior changes.

## Performance follow-up

Five alternating same-machine runs compare `4e908b1` with the performance candidate `f38412977`; the original feature base (`909b277`) is also included in the send-path comparison. These measurements were not repeated after the rebases, test-only CI repair, or local-reference byte-policy follow-up. Workloads and failures are preserved in the local evidence bundle.

| Measurement | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| Staging scans per text / uploaded send | 1 / 3 → 0 / 2 (original base: 0 / 2) |
| 20 MiB video, settled CDP backing-storage delta after GC, median | 28,637,774 → 674,746 bytes (26.67 MiB less; not browser RSS) |
| 49,701-byte upload, second normal HTTP fetch | 50,001 → 0 transferred bytes, with identical decoded body |

The real WebSocket test completes 300 accepted/answered turns per source (50 measured + 10 warmups per run). Admission p50/p95/p99 medians are 9.13/16.04/18.97 → 9.56/15.37/17.52 ms; the original base is 9.41/14.12/17.68 ms. Completion p95/p99 medians are 128.40/173.09 → 129.42/180.89 ms, with overlapping run ranges. These results establish removal of the extra scans and the measured cache/encoded-storage costs, not blanket latency or total-memory parity. JS used-heap delta medians are 5,815,068 → 6,044,652 bytes; concurrency and other machines are not covered.

## Current UX/security fixes and verification

Current head: `cdcbe6921e9ff47c25f26bc6f04f12b538210ebc`, two ordinary follow-up commits on top of `1b18467f0c520bb017316ad0f8a142e02b629054` (rebased main snapshot `f11ea5f9e03c502303f5097e35a1646178d5472e`). The four confirmed review findings are repaired: deleted-session borrowed URLs fail closed; typing during inspection preserves attachment conversion; valid apostrophe filenames work; and transient video failures have a local Retry. The follow-up also preserves IME composition and toolbar focus during passive confirmation. NAN-329's failure-feedback redesign remains separate.

| Current-head check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Related Python/WebUI gateway/WebSocket/transcript/attachment/provider selection | PASS: 1,564 passed, 17 skipped, with isolated per-test config paths |
| Full Python BasedPyright; touched Ruff; Python import scan | PASS: 443 files, zero diagnostics; both scans passed |
| Full WebUI unit suite | PASS: 3,247 tests / 182 files |
| Full WebUI typecheck/lint and production import scan | PASS |
| Production WebUI build | PASS with repository-pinned Bun 1.3.13; output isolated from the running user preview |
| Full TUI tests; typecheck/import scan | PASS: 293 tests / 33 files; both scans passed |
| Shared client import-boundary CLI self-tests | PASS: 42 tests, pinned Bun also used by child processes; original timeout/assertion settings retained |
| Real Chromium + isolated built gateway/provider | PASS: eight scenarios covering mixed local/upload order and image/path pairs through remount/replay, controlled typing-during-inspect, toolbar focus, apostrophe paths, first-send missing-source recovery, actual video playback after Retry without reload, queued-source revalidation/retry, and permission denial with draft retention |
| Real borrowed-media HTTP authority | PASS: 200 while authorized, 403 after narrowing access, 404 after session deletion; live Temporary Chat 200 then discard 404; original files preserved |
| Real WezTerm + native TUI | PASS: normal local image, controlled typing during inspection, and apostrophe path each reach the provider as one native image; originals unchanged and owned pane closed |
| Final-head GitHub CI | NO RESULTS YET at 2026-10-22 08:20 UTC: the one bounded read returned an empty statusCheckRollup; required review remains pending |

Each repaired regression has failing-before/passing-after evidence. Real-client acceptance uses synthetic local files and a deterministic localhost provider. An initial native harness used the wrong fixture response marker, and its fresh native-only retry initially assumed a request log already existed; corrected harnesses passed without product changes, and both failed attempts remain archived. The historical boundary self-test timeout at `0b1cd7536` remains recorded below; this final head's fresh 42-test run passed. Full local Python coverage, the full repository browser suite, performance, mobile browsers, terminal drag/drop and arbitrary codecs were not rerun for this repair.

## Previous image-path and ordered-draft verification

Source: `0b1cd75363f587de38fafffdb9a01e26f74f0a69`, ordinary follow-up to `6d6ebed76`. The two confirmed review findings are repaired: provider-visible image/file correspondence and restored mixed-attachment order. Permissions, original-file ownership, upload limits and backend scheduling are unchanged. Failure-feedback refinement remains the separately recorded UX follow-up.

| Previous-source check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Agent/provider/WebSocket/transcript related Python suite | PASS: 4,006 passed, 1 skipped |
| Full Python BasedPyright; touched Ruff; Python import scan | PASS: 443 files, zero diagnostics; both scans passed |
| Full WebUI unit suite | PASS: 3,198 tests / 180 files |
| Full WebUI typecheck/lint and production import scan | PASS |
| Production WebUI build | PASS with repository-pinned Bun 1.3.13; output isolated from the user's running preview |
| TUI check/import scan and affected attachment/composer tests | PASS: 27 tests; affected tests also passed with pinned Bun 1.3.13 |
| Real Chromium + isolated gateway/provider | PASS: local A / uploaded B / local C retain chip and send order across SPA navigation; provider receives three native image blocks with the correctly paired actual file paths; refresh/followup retains each reference once; persisted local-only draft order is retained |
| Real WezTerm + native TUI | PASS: two local images arrive at the provider with native image data plus the corresponding original paths; originals unchanged and no additional managed files; owned pane closed |
| Local client boundary CLI self-tests | FAIL: latest pinned-runtime control was 40 passed / 2 default-5s subprocess timeouts; checker scripts and dependencies are unchanged, while the frozen-parent checker snapshot passed all 42. Attribution remains unresolved; no timeout, assertion or product behavior was changed to hide it |
| CI observed at that previous source | IN PROGRESS at 2026-10-22 06:06 UTC: Detect changes passed and 12 checks were running in [run 39731813580](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39731813580); required review is pending |

The real-client checks use synthetic PNG fixtures and a local deterministic provider; they establish native-image/path transport and draft/replay behavior, not a new external-model semantic evaluation. The previous original-video, upload-budget and performance evidence retains its original source identity below. Full local Python coverage and performance were not rerun for this follow-up.

## Previous local-reference byte-policy verification

Source: `6d6ebed76db45b09ef18c32482501791025043a4`, rebased onto main `421bd6b593d5ace856dcfb9f2e66236e907195f1` before this ordinary follow-up. The final change separates borrowed local references from upload byte accounting; it does not increase upload budgets, timeouts, or staging capacity.

| Previous-source check | Result |

| Gateway/WebSocket attachment, transcript and agent-reference selection | PASS: 577 tests, with isolated per-test config paths |

| English/Chinese rendered upload rejection | PASS: actual 26.7 MiB versus 20.0 MiB upload maximum, draft retained; all ten locale strings retain both placeholders |
| Real WezTerm + native TUI | PASS: two large synthetic local files sent as path references, no upload request or copied media, originals unchanged |

prs.title: fix(webui): keep restored waiting messages manual (NAN-275)
prs.body:
## Why

Restoring a waiting message also restored its automatic execution eligibility. Loading an old completed turn could therefore start a new agent run without fresh user confirmation.

Related: [NAN-275](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-275).

## What changed

- Scope automatic sending to the live page that queued the message. Legacy drafts and drafts from another page restore as manual input without losing text, attachments, quotes or session targets.
- Revoke eligibility on `pagehide` and document `freeze`; retain it across topic/component remounts and short reconnects. Keep Stop and failed sends manual.
- Add regression coverage, five browser cases, and document the changed restore behavior.

## Scope

Frontend waiting-message authorization only. Backend scheduling, admission, recovery, protocol and the existing merged-message behavior are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Reloading, reopening or leaving the page now requires **Send now** or editing and sending the restored content. A live hidden tab or a disconnected socket alone retains eligibility; no elapsed-time cutoff is introduced. Browser suspension is handled when the browser reports `freeze` or creates a new document.

## Blast Radius

All Composer variants and their waiting messages. The existing localStorage key and v1 array shape remain; an optional page identifier cannot authorize execution in a different document.

## Verification

### After resolving the main conflict (`79c37cdcb`)

Merged `main@169062be1` with an ordinary merge commit. The only conflict was in `docs/webui.md`; this keeps main's concise guide and the restored-draft safety guidance. The queued-send implementation and its regression fixtures are unchanged.

- Current merge: **333 focused tests**, **5 Chromium browser regressions**, full typecheck, lint, import-boundary check and production build passed.
- Full-suite and gateway figures below remain bound to the original implementation snapshot.

### Initial implementation (`c5716534`)

- New component regressions: **5 failed / 16 passed before the fix**, then **21 passed**. Composer/shell/navigation focused suite: **334 passed**.
- `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`: **3,233 passed** across 182 files, unchanged coverage thresholds.
- Full typecheck, lint, import-boundary check, **42 import-rule tests**, and production build passed. Build retains its large-chunk warnings.
- Chromium browser regressions: **5 passed**, one worker and zero retries; includes desktop/narrow reload, live topic switching, browser back navigation and complete legacy payload preservation.
- Real isolated gateway with production assets and a deterministic loopback provider: frozen-base build reproduced an unsolicited admission, model request and real file write after restoring the old queue shape. The candidate produced **zero admissions/model calls/tool effects from the restored draft**; explicit Send now admitted it once and executed the file tool. Live topic navigation and a byte-preserving WebSocket outage each released fresh waiting input exactly once. Stop retained the queue for manual delivery, which then completed once.

The first default-worker coverage run timed out in the unchanged Tailwind-scan test; the initial import-rule run had six child-process timeouts. The final runs above passed without changing assertions, timeouts, coverage or dependencies. Native browser freeze could not be induced in this headless setup; its revocation handler is covered by the document-event regression, not claimed as native freeze acceptance. The original incident trace and Safari/device acceptance remain unavailable. Shared instances, real browser profiles and user histories were untouched.

prs.body:
## Why

After installing channel dependencies, Channels currently disables the switches and puts the required next step in a small notice above the catalog. The installed channel should offer **Restart** directly in its existing action position.

Addresses [NAN-334](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-334).

## What changed

- Track successful install-only actions that require a restart in the gateway's channel settings owner, and return a per-channel `restart_pending` fact on catalog reads and updates. It survives browser refreshes and clears with the gateway runtime.
- Replace the affected channel's switch with a restart icon action matching the existing install control. Keep a localized accessible name and shared `HoverHint`, wire it to the existing restart flow, and retain progress/errors without the duplicate catalog notice.
- Cover the install → restart → normal-switch transition, refresh, unrelated channels, and failed-install retry; update the Channels usage guide.

## Scope

No dependency installer, restart mechanism, configuration, or channel activation changes. Installation never automatically restarts nanobot or enables a channel. Other settings restart notices keep their existing behavior.

## Verification

- Related Python suites: **326 passed** (`test_websocket_http_routes.py`, `test_restart_control.py`, `test_settings_system.py`, `test_settings_routes.py`, `test_channel_plugins.py`), with an isolated test HOME.
- Related WebUI suites: **88 passed** (`settings-channels`, `channel-toggles`, `settings-system`, `catalog-loading`).
- WebUI full-project `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` (**42 passed**), and production `bun run build`: passed.
- Python Ruff on changed files, Python import boundaries, and BasedPyright on `nanobot/webui/settings_system.py`: passed. Full-project Python typechecking and the full unit/browser suites were not run for this focused change.
- Real built WebUI + isolated Windows gateway: installed Telegram dependencies through the UI; verified the immediate in-row action, no automatic activation, browser-refresh retention, all ten locales at 390px, disabled/busy restart control, actual gateway restart with a new run ID, and the restored normal switch after reconnect/refresh. **16 checks passed**, no browser page errors.
- The new frontend regression and backend pending-state contract were observed failing before the implementation and passing afterward.

### UI feedback follow-up

The restart action now matches the existing 38×22 icon control and uses shared HoverHint for pointer hover and keyboard focus. Repeated the 88 related WebUI tests, full-project typecheck/lint, client import checks, and production build; all passed. Fifteen real-browser checks passed, covering icon geometry, pointer/focus hints, all ten locales at 390px, and light/dark rendering. The existing Slack pending state remains available in the isolated preview.

The real installation/restart journey and backend checks above were run on parent 5b9d06123; this follow-up changes only action presentation, its hint test, and matching usage wording. Backend state and restart callback semantics are unchanged.

### Disabled installation hints

Install actions blocked by a pending restart now expose a shared `HoverHint`: “Restart nanobot before installing another channel.” The disabled native button is retained; a matching focusable hint target supports pointer and keyboard discovery without enabling installation. During a restart, the hint uses the existing restarting status. This reason is not reused for unrelated installation-in-progress or unsupported states. The copy is complete in all ten locales.

Verification at `c64c3cd39165a730a6ef195aff7ae736285d4bff`: 114 related WebUI/i18n tests, full-project typecheck/lint, client import checks and production build passed. prs.title: refactor(plugins): bind approval and activation to an instance owner
prs.body:
Plugin approval storage used the process-global config selector during discovery, authorization, and activation. `AgentPlugins` now binds the instance home H and agent workspace W, and owns approval markers, fingerprints, plugin data, MCP activation, and the shared skill cache.

Skills, filesystem tools, Dream, subagents, CLI installation, and WebUI call the bound owner. The old free operation functions are removed. Owners with the same canonical H/W share invalidation. Different homes keep separate approvals. Runtime MCP retains launch-effective W while the settings catalog uses persisted W. Existing standalone constructors capture their selection once.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1["Skills / files / MCP / CLI / WebUI"] --> B2["Free plugin operations"]
    B2 --> B3["Read global config selector on each operation"]
    B2 --> B4["Approval markers and package fingerprints"]
    B2 --> B5["Cache keyed by workspace and config file"]
  end
  subgraph After
    A1["Runtime and WebUI construction"] -->|"H and agent W once"| A2["AgentPlugins"]
    A3["Skills / files / Dream / MCP / CLI / WebUI"] -->|"domain operations"| A2
    A2 --> A4["Approval, fingerprint and plugin data"]
    A2 --> A5["Shared cache and invalidation by H/W"]
  end
```

This is PR 1 of the four refactors preceding #6261, based on main `508cedff3`. Related to [NAN-264](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-264/). CLI flags, disk layout, and WebUI wire contracts remain unchanged. This closes plugin ownership; standalone construction still selects default paths at its existing entrypoints.

Validation passed on Linux with Python 3.12.

- Full Python suite excluding the serial CLI file, 9,778 passed and 49 skipped. Serial CLI suite, 163 passed and 1 skipped.
- Ruff, BasedPyright, and all ten Python import-boundary rules passed. `bun run build` passed.
- Real isolated gateway HTTP/WebSocket checks covered enable, fingerprint persistence, replacement revocation, disable, and settings persistence. Built WebUI enable survived a browser reload.
- Real stdio MCP connected and executed a tool, kept launch W on reload, and removed its connection and tool after another same-H/W owner disabled the plugin.

Native Windows and macOS were not run locally. [CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39016850769) passed on Linux 3.11/3.14 and Windows 3.14, including Windows process compatibility and Docker.

prs.title: feat(webui): add configurable local trusted extension surface
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a configurable local WebUI extensions surface for trusted browser-side add-ons.

Extensions are discovered from a local directory, validated as folders with an `extension.json` manifest, and served through the gateway under scoped `/extensions/...` and `/api/extensions/...` routes. The host bridge authenticates requests and keeps API tokens out of the iframe.

## Why

This lets nanobot host small local browser apps without exposing credentials or creating a generic third-party app sandbox. The extension directory remains local to the gateway and can be configured per deployment.

## Changes

- add configurable extension root via `tools.webui_extensions_path`
- discover and validate extension manifests
- serve static extension assets from the gateway
- expose authenticated extension APIs through the WebUI host bridge
- add extension catalog / settings integration in the WebUI
- keep invalid or broken extensions from breaking the whole catalog

## Testing

- `cd webui && npm test -- --run src/tests/extension-client.test.ts src/tests/extensions-catalog.test.tsx`

## Notes

- The feature is local and trusted, not a sandboxed remote app model.
- The UI remains empty unless the configured extension root contains valid extensions.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore existing macOS WebUI windows from Dock and Command-Tab
prs.body:
## Summary

Restore the existing local WebUI window when the macOS Dock cat is clicked or selected with Command-Tab, instead of opening another page or activating an empty helper.

- Reuse the matching Chrome/Safari tab, restore minimized windows and raise the captured window ID without navigating or reloading it. Open a new window only after a successful lookup finds no matching tab.
- Coalesce activation/reopen actions, suppress startup focus, and show actionable errors for denied Automation permission or an unresponsive browser instead of creating duplicates.
- Keep the helper's per-installation identity stable across code/icon updates and use the actual interpreter image for framework Python so the generated app retains its bundle identity.

## Boundaries and compatibility

This changes only the macOS Dock adapter, its launcher, focused tests and WebUI documentation. The browser continues to own the live page, profile and drafts; the gateway owns chats, authentication and execution. No gateway, update-worker, persistence, configuration or frontend protocol changes.

Dock window reuse currently supports Chrome and Safari as the default browser and may require browser-wide macOS Automation permission. The helper reads URL properties only, not page contents, and does not run page JavaScript. Other browsers still work via the WebUI link, but the Dock action explains the limitation instead of blindly opening duplicates. Closing a page retains the browser's existing saved-draft semantics; temporary-chat drafts and unsubmitted attachments are not made durable by this change. Python/install-path relocation can still require authorization again.

Foreground/background ownership, `--no-open`, `--no-dock`, SSH/headless behavior and non-macOS behavior remain unchanged. Starts, restarts and updates do not request browser control.

## Verification

- Focused CLI/Dock tests: **208 passed, 1 skipped**; touched-file Ruff, basedpyright, import-boundary checks and diff checks passed.
- Real Mac system events: exact Dock accessibility activation and global Command-Tab, including verification of the system switcher's selected application. Chrome and Safari restored minimized matching windows; repeated activation did not create another window. The Safari backend was selected by a private test-only resolver override, without changing the machine's default browser.
- Real testing found and fixed a window-order bug: AppleScript loop references were live list indices. Capturing the stable window ID before activation prevents restoring or raising the wrong window.
- Installed the exact final private macOS ARM64 candidate `0.3.7.dev2026102108` from source `ddb5be40bdac3f05fbfdd8a7cf3c09ccdd4ee44d`. In the actual authenticated WebUI, both Dock and Command-Tab preserved the original window, conversation route, historical messages and unsent draft. After closing, only one new page opened and the saved chat draft remained available.
- Earlier private real-package acceptance covered upgrade from the retained `2106` package, post-shutdown backup failure with automatic service restoration, and a separately confirmed subsequent successful upgrade. Data/auth/chat continuity and native Dock lifetime passed. That report retains its original `2107` package identity; the later browser-focus changes do not alter those updater/lifetime contracts.

First-time permission-prompt UI was not exercised because this machine already permits Automation; denied-permission and timeout behavior have focused test coverage. Initial Safari cold startup exceeded the former five-second limit and safely reported an error; the bounded timeout is now fifteen seconds, while native Safari acceptance covers the running-browser path. This PR does not publish packages, change signing settings or modify user data.

prs.title: fix(retry): prevent replay amplification and isolate backoff (NAN-313)
prs.body:
## Why

Nested retry owners multiply physical requests, replay already-delivered Telegram prefixes, and let failing destinations hold every outbound send slot while sleeping. Keep replay decisions with the domain owner, release resources before backoff, and remove duplicated recovery mechanics without adding a retry framework or dependency.

Fixes [NAN-313](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-313)

## What changed

- Hold outbound permits only for an adapter invocation, retaining bounded admission, destination FIFO, scheduled claim ordering, and pre-submission deadlines; add equal jitter to local manager/LLM backoff without changing server-hint rules.
- Prevent Telegram whole-message replay after per-part failures, disable nested SDK retries for internally created Bedrock clients, and close StepFun SSE response contexts before retry waits.
- Share request-only recovery across MCP wrappers and keep LLM stream/image/persistent recovery in an explicit domain loop; consolidate regression coverage into existing fixtures. No Tenacity dependency remains.

## Scope

Python outbound delivery, model-request retries, MCP wrapper recovery, and StepFun transcription resource lifetime. Preserve configured admission, scheduled unknown-result handling, provider continuation, cancellation, and public return shapes. Persistent-task recovery, other adapters' delivery policies, UI, configuration schemas, and dependency versions are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Removing nested retry budgets intentionally reaches exhaustion sooner; it does not promise equal success probability for every external fault sequence. Adapter-internal waits still occupy one invocation permit, and Telegram transport retries do not provide exactly-once delivery. Local jitter uses `[base / 2, base]`; provider/server Retry-After buffer and cap rules remain intact.

The final diff is production -77 lines and tests +668 lines, net +591. The proposed library adaptation was withdrawn because it added callbacks/state and maintenance cost without sufficient simplification.

## Blast Radius

ChannelManager scheduling affects ordinary outbound sends; Telegram and internally created Bedrock clients have intentional retry-policy changes. MCP tools/resources/prompts share one recovery owner, while rendering remains outside the replay boundary. Review focus: partial delivery, independent recovery budgets, active-permit release, cancellation, and response closure before sleep.

## Verification

Local checks ran on the exact published source delta against base `73a55e0b2fac17ae70641f028448201c4a0cb710`; commit preparation changes no source content. The current target branch is newer, so these local results are not merge-result CI results.

- **FAIL:** CI-scope Windows Python suite, isolated HOME, `-n 2 --dist loadfile`, the existing three CLI/native/WSL files excluded for serial execution, and `--cov=nanobot`: **9989 passed, 130 skipped, 5 failed; coverage 85.43%** (75% threshold unchanged). Four failures reproduce on the baseline environment: copied Scoop rg shim companion, Windows symlink permission, and two missing-USERNAME cases. The fifth is an unchanged shell-test marker-write race: normal focused runs pass on both snapshots; exposing the existing non-atomic marker window reproduces the same empty-content assertion on both. The full run remains FAIL.
- **PASS:** excluded serial CLI/native/WSL files: **222 passed, 1 skipped**. Ruff, import boundaries, dependency consistency, `git diff --check HEAD`, and strict typechecking of affected production files pass.
- **FAIL:** full-project BasedPyright retains the same two baseline `setproctitle` diagnostics; no affected-production diagnostics.
- **PASS:** real FastMCP stdio/connect/registry/reconnect/timeout/cancel/aclose comparison; five balanced fresh-process loopback SDK/MessageBus pairs preserve work/error/result counts; real unread-response SSE closure and cancellation regressions. These use deterministic local services, not production accounts or public models.

Performance evidence distinguishes the policy comparison from the final simplification rerun: before/after retry-policy probes measured Telegram 9→3 HTTP requests, successful-prefix submissions 3→1, and Bedrock continuous-503 requests 20→4. Final-source reruns preserve the reduced counts. An equal-work public-MessageBus fixture (65 sends, 33 completed destinations) reduces healthy-destination queueing under 32 sleeping retries from about 1009ms to 0.1ms. These are fault-isolation/request-count results, not general model throughput claims.

Seven new original-base/final bookkeeping pairs show transient→success p50 16.4→16.1µs, p99 31.7→33.5µs, and worst-run p99 37.7→43.1µs; provider-import medians are 101.7→107.5ms with overlapping ranges. No general speedup or zero-tail-regression claim. The issue records scope, acceptance criteria, measurements, and local evidence identifiers; raw local logs remain outside tracked source.

prs.title: fix(slack): replace compaction outcome notices in place with chat.update
prs.body:
Fixes #6084 (option 2 only)

**Scope note (please read before closing as stale/duplicate):** option 1 — automatic
compaction notices silenced by default — already landed on `main` via #5780
(`0b402d0`, `ab6d5f1`, unreleased as of v0.3.5). This PR deliberately does **not**
touch that behavior or `SlackConfig`; it implements only option 2 from the issue:
when compaction notices are shown, the outcome phase now edits the start notice in
place instead of posting a second permanent message.

### Root cause

`SlackChannel.send()` (`nanobot/channels/slack/runtime.py`) treated every
`ContextCompactionEvent` phase as an ordinary message and discarded the
`chat.postMessage` response, so the `ts` needed to edit the message was lost and
there was no `chat.update` path. With notices enabled, one compaction produced two
permanent messages ("compressing…" + outcome).

### Change (mirrors the Discord channel's #5720 behavior)

- `_compaction_notices: dict[(chat_id, compaction_id) -> (message_ts, thread_ts)]`
  on the channel; `stop()` clears it on reset (same as Discord's `_reset_runtime_state`).
- `started` phase: after a normal post, remember the returned `ts` — only when the
  notice fits in a single chunk (a split notice must not be half-edited).
- Outcome phases (`succeeded`/`failed`/`cancelled`): pop the stored notice and call
  `chat.update(channel, ts, text)`; on success return, so the lifecycle stays one
  message. No stored notice (e.g. after a restart) or a refused update falls through
  to the ordinary post — identical semantics to Discord's `_edit_compaction_notice`
  fallback.
- `chat_update` added to the local `_SlackWebAPI` protocol. No new scopes needed:
  Socket Mode bot tokens cover `chat.update` with the existing `chat:write`.
- Notice map entries lost across restart simply re-post the outcome (same as
  Discord); enterprise workspaces that disable message editing degrade to the old
  two-message behavior via the same fallback.

### Tests

7 new tests in `nanobot/channels/slack/tests/test_slack_channel.py` using the fake
web client (added a `chat_update` stub with a fail switch, and `chat_postMessage`
now returns a `{"ok", "ts"}` response like the real SDK):

- automatic compaction stays silent by default (regression coverage for option 1)
- `notify=True` still posts
- outcome edits the start notice in place — exactly one post, one `chat_update`
  carrying the remembered `ts`, map empty afterwards
- `chat_update` failure falls back to a second post (and is attempted exactly once)
- outcome without a stored start notice is posted as usual
- multi-chunk start notices are never remembered for editing
- `stop()` clears in-flight notices

Red → green (tests written first):

```
$ pytest nanobot/channels/slack/tests/ -q
FAILED ...::test_compaction_outcome_edits_the_start_notice_in_place
FAILED ...::test_compaction_outcome_falls_back_to_send_when_edit_fails
FAILED ...::test_stop_clears_in_flight_compaction_notices
3 failed, 39 passed in 0.60s

# after the runtime change
$ pytest nanobot/channels/slack/tests/ -q
42 passed in 0.51s
```

Commands (offline, venv):

```bash
pytest nanobot/channels/slack/tests/ -q        # 42 passed
pytest nanobot/channels/ -q                    # 1288 passed, 15 skipped (pre-existing optional-dep skips)
ruff check nanobot tests                       # All checks passed! (E/F/I/N/W, line-length 100)
basedpyright nanobot/channels/slack/runtime.py # 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

### Environment notes

- Developed/tested locally on macOS arm64 (Python 3.14 homebrew venv, slack-sdk
  3.45.0), no network; CI's ubuntu-latest/windows-latest not exercised locally.
- `basedpyright` was run against the changed file (config is strict, tests excluded
  by `[tool.basedpyright]`); the full CI sequence (`uv sync --all-extras --dev` +
  `install_channel_dependencies --all-channels` + project-wide `basedpyright`)
  needs network and was not run offline. Diff sticks to the file's existing typing
  style (Any-narrowing at the SDK boundary).
- Diff is limited to the Slack channel runtime + its tests; no formatting churn
  (files are not ruff-format-canonical on `main` either — left untouched).

prs.title: feat(webui): distinguish context compaction reasons (NAN-324)
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI currently labels idle maintenance, context-pressure compaction, and manual `/compact` identically. Record the actual trigger at its owning entrypoint so the notice explains what happened without hiding idle compaction or guessing from turn metadata.

NAN-324 · Refs #6370

## What changed

- Carry optional `idle`, `context_pressure`, `manual`, and `provider_native` reasons through the existing compaction lifecycle, WebSocket projection, and SQLite display-history replay.
- Keep the existing inline divider and update its wording for each reason and lifecycle phase in all ten languages. Historical records without a reason keep the generic wording.
- Cover real trigger paths, stable row updates, SQLite reopen/pagination, shared client decoding, and browser refresh/topic re-entry.

## Scope

No changes to compaction timing, thresholds, summarization, model context, channel notification policy, or TUI rendering. No token estimates or additional settings. Provider-native wording identifies the mechanism without asserting that the context limit was reached.

## Blast Radius

The shared notification contract gains an optional field. Existing reasonless events remain valid; the WebUI history allowlist and projection retain the reason. TUI decoding/type checks are covered while its presentation stays unchanged.

## Verification

- Python affected tests: **511 passed**, including actual idle scheduling, manual command dispatch/cancellation, runner context-pressure/provider-native paths, SQLite reopen/older-page projection, and WebSocket persistence.
- Full WebUI unit suite: **3235 passed** on the final run.
- Browser regression: **10 passed** across all ten languages; checks live phase replacement, topic re-entry, refresh, light/dark rendering, and 390/1280px widths using synthetic HTTP/WS fixtures.
- TUI shared-consumer checks: **72 passed**, plus full TUI typecheck and import-boundary checks.
- WebUI typecheck, lint, import checks, import-checker tests (**42 passed**), and production build passed. Python Ruff and import boundaries passed.
- Isolated built gateway: real idle compaction and `/compact` with DeepSeek V4 Flash produced distinct persisted notices and retained them after refresh. Other cause/state combinations are explicitly labelled synthetic display examples; live provider-native compaction is not claimed.
- **Known baseline failure:** full BasedPyright reports two Windows `setproctitle` diagnostics in unchanged `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py`; the exact base `f11ea5f9e` reproduces the same two diagnostics with the same dependencies. This check remains FAIL.

Detailed local evidence, including earlier failed verification attempts, is retained under `webui/.verify-evidence-nan324/`. Remote CI results are pending publication; no merge or automatic CI monitoring is requested.

prs.title: feat(linear): manage member access and simplify workspace connections
prs.body:
## Summary

Let an administrator choose who can use the Linear agent directly from the WebUI, without asking every teammate to exchange a pairing code.

- Add workspace-scoped member search, avatars and access switches. Only active human members in the app-visible teams are eligible; explicit off overrides pairing and allowlists, and request admission rechecks membership.
- Clarify the workspace/member hierarchy, show workspace logos, and keep existing content visible while directory refreshes run. Permissions remain server-confirmed; uncertain saves require a refresh.
- Simplify authorization to **Continue in Linear** without a QR step. Keep pairing as an alternative and retain the shared component's QR default for other channels.
- Present stored secrets as **Saved** with explicit **Replace / Save / Cancel**, without returning existing secrets to the browser.
- Add workspace reauthorization/removal and a clearly scoped connection reset, including partial-failure handling. Recover inspection after gateway reconnects and prevent delayed revocation events from deleting a newer authorization.
- Update all ten channel locales and the setup guide, including networking, multi-workspace installation, member access, and removal/reset semantics.

No agent-loop/core changes. The shared production change is the QR presentation opt-out; the rest is channel-local.

## Compatibility and operational notes

- SQLite changes are additive: existing installations/tokens are retained, and existing pairing/allowlist approvals still apply unless explicitly overridden. No new admin OAuth scope is requested.
- Reauthorizing the same installation keeps member choices. Removing a workspace clears its choices but preserves pairing approvals and chat history; reconnecting can therefore reuse an existing pairing approval. Reset is not an authorization-history wipe.
- Turning access off blocks new requests, not already running tasks. API/directory failures do not authorize new work.
- Older versions ignore member overrides. Before downgrading, disable the channel and reconcile legacy pairing/allowlists so an older version cannot restore a deliberately revoked grant.
- A private Linear app is limited to its own workspace. Installing the same app in another workspace requires the corresponding distribution setting in Linear.

## Validation

- `pytest nanobot/channels/linear/tests -q` — 105 passed, including old-database upgrade, restart, legacy approval precedence, pagination, failed admission and delayed revocation coverage.
- Focused Linear, settings, locale and shared-QR WebUI tests — 134 passed across 9 files.
- Strict Python type check for the Linear package — 0 errors; targeted Ruff and ESLint passed.
- TypeScript + Vite production build and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Prior live server/browser tests on this feature implementation verified real mentions/replies, pairing approval, member on/off behavior, restart persistence, one distributable app in two workspaces, workspace isolation, remove/reconnect, and reset using a disposable installation.

Real token-expiry/refresh, rate-limit/outage behavior, and attachment/Stop delivery were not separately exercised end-to-end in this pass; do not interpret mocked coverage as live validation. The latest base was incorporated before the local regression run. This PR does not publish a release.

prs.title: feat(webui): unify session file and website previews
prs.body:
## Summary

Consolidates the file actions from #5850 and website previews from #5852 into one conversation-side preview workflow.

- Keep files and websites in session-owned tabs within one stable, resizable preview pane. Restore tabs when returning to a conversation, with compact shared header styling, keyboard navigation and a contained overlay on narrow panes.
- Preview PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP alongside existing text previews; keep HTML and SVG files as source. Image links provide a small hover/focus preview, while explicit inline images and attachments share a bounded gallery and zoomable viewer without duplicating the same displayed image.
- Keep file references uncluttered: click to preview; right-click or Shift+F10 on a reference/tab to copy its absolute or project-relative path.
- Use one monochrome file-icon family across reply references, preview tabs and attachment tiles, with shared strokes and inherited colors; retain distinct image, code, JSON and text symbols without tiny letter badges or mixed brand logos.
- Keep HTTP(S) links uncluttered too: right-click or Shift+F10 opens a compact shared-style menu. Touch retains the native browser menu, while Message actions → View links provides a tap-only route to preview, copy and external opening. Only rendered reply links are listed and deduplicated; no per-link ellipsis or nested popup.
- Reuse bounded, short-lived file preview requests and snapshots without resetting an open preview or image zoom when credentials renew. Subsequent requests use the current credential.
- Keep tab clicks responsive for large text previews: avoid redundant cache-hit renders, paint the full plain source first, and limit detailed syntax spans to nearby visible chunks. Selection changes cannot bypass the initial paint opportunity. A single scroll container owns both axes before and after highlighting. Offscreen text remains present for selection and browser search; very large or minified previews remain plain text. Existing permission revalidation is unchanged.
- On phones, place Copy and More below the message with touch-sized controls and a shared-style bottom sheet, leaving the reply its full width. On desktop, show a quiet timestamp below the hover control: today's local time, otherwise a numeric date, with the full local date/time available on hover or keyboard focus.

## Boundaries and compatibility

- Existing authentication and workspace containment remain authoritative. Raster responses are signature-checked and bounded to 8 MiB. HTTP preview/metadata reads are no-store; temporary-chat responses require their owning connection and bypass replay caching.
- Preview state is memory-only and cleared on session deletion/disconnect. No new durable store, session migration, agent-loop behavior or tool permission.
- Website previews require credentialless support and an opaque sandbox with scripts only. Same-origin embedding, credential forwarding, mixed-content downgrades, proxying around frame policies and native browser privileges are not enabled. Unsupported or blocked sites retain an external-open link.
- Older text payloads remain readable; metadata failure degrades to copying the original reference. New image payloads require the matching bundled WebUI. File links do not automatically insert images into a reply.
- No native Finder/editor/terminal launcher or full embedded browser. Third-party page DOM, navigation and forms are not preserved across session navigation. Physical touchscreen pinch and long-press behavior have not been hardware-verified.

## Validation

- All 1,886 WebUI tests passed, including shared file-icon identity across surfaces, real-App session navigation, bootstrap credential renewal, keyboard/outside dismissal, clipboard failure/stale completion, native touch event preservation, hybrid input, mobile sheet transitions and local-calendar timestamp boundaries. File-copy callbacks cannot dismiss a reopened menu or report feedback for a different reference.
- 255 focused Python file-preview, WebSocket and turn-owner tests passed on the updated base, including workspace/owner restrictions, temporary-chat cleanup, no-store behavior and local-handshake requirements.
- WebUI lint, TypeScript, production build, scoped Ruff and diff checks passed.
- Actual-browser validation used production components with synthetic conversation data: tabbed previews, image viewer/quick look, compact context-only link actions, keyboard/outside dismissal, and the tap-only message menu flow in light/dark mode at 390px. Preview opening, copy feedback and back navigation were checked. A real interactive cross-origin page loaded; a separate page with CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` was visibly blocked in the pane and rendered normally under direct navigation. Copying was verified by pasting into an unsent synthetic composer.
- The mobile reply/footer was also checked at 320px, including the dark bottom sheet. Desktop today/date/full-time labels and keyboard tooltips were checked without shifting the message body. These responsive browser checks do not replace physical iOS/Android gesture testing.
- The shared file icons were additionally checked in the actual app at desktop and 390px widths, in light/dark themes, including file opening, tab switching and neutral attachment styling. Only synthetic fixtures were used.
- Large-preview regression checks cover bounded token DOM, complete source text, multiline syntax across chunk boundaries, active selection preservation, delayed-render cancellation, and oversized/minified plain-text fallback. Actual-browser checks used a 602-line synthetic HTML file in both development and production builds, including repeated HTML/JSON/image switching and keyboard scrolling to the final line. The synthetic production case reached its first animation frame in 7–9 ms on cache-hit switches; later highlighting still produced a roughly 120 ms longest frame gap, so this is not a claim of zero jank or a general benchmark.
- Follow-up review reproduced and fixed premature enhancement on `selectionchange` and split horizontal/vertical scroll ownership. Regression tests cover selection events before both initial frames. Actual-browser checks confirmed horizontal keyboard scrolling and the complete final line at desktop and 390px widths, plus image zoom and light/dark layouts.
- External-open URL/target/rel behavior is unit-tested; a one-click handoff was not observable in the in-app browser, so it is not claimed as end-to-end verified there.
- See the PR checks for CI results on the current head.

prs.title: fix(agent): report current workspace access before tool use
prs.body:
## Problem

The file tools use the project selected for the current chat. But `my(action="check", key="workspace")` shows the agent directory, and `workspace_sandbox` returns a missing-field error. The model also has to infer the access restriction before it calls a tool. These gaps can lead it to report that a selected project is inaccessible.

## Changes

- Add a short model-only context block to each new user request. It reports the current project and file-access restriction before the first model call, even when the `my` tool is disabled.
- Restore the read-only `workspace_sandbox` result for detailed inspection. Both views use the same workspace resolver as the file tools, including the restriction from a configured exec sandbox.
- Keep the new context with its message. Do not rewrite earlier messages, the system prompt, or tool definitions. New requests refresh the context without a separate tracking cache.
- Pass the validated execution scope through the existing runtime-context provider interface. Injected follow-ups report the active run's policy, not a requested scope that the tools have not adopted.
- Preserve permissions, the legacy `workspace` display command, and the tool action schema. Shell binds do not grant file-tool access. OS permissions still apply.

The loop change only registers the provider and passes the typed scope. The runner is unchanged. Most test updates distinguish stored model-only context from user-visible history.

## Validation

- On the final integration head `2f2688f34`, 2,269 local tests pass across agents, security, sessions, commands, prompt-cache markers and accounting, model API selection, and instance-home selection. Ruff and changed-production-file type checks pass. This head includes main at `9261e731c`.
- Earlier revisions passed 2,425 local tests, including scheduled tasks, API/SDK streaming, the facade, and tool loading. That is historical evidence, not a new full run on the integration head.
- Backend tests use scripted providers and real message/tool execution. They cover selected projects, restricted/full access, configured shell restrictions, concurrent chats, read-only protection, and injected follow-ups.
- Cache-focused follow-up: 175 local checks pass. Tests use the real Chat Completions and Responses request builders for consecutive requests, access-mode changes, tool continuations, idle compaction, `/new` archiving, and capacity-triggered compaction with structured tool history. A transient 503 goes through the production retry policy and produces the same serialized request on retry. Network/model responses are simulated.
- Public history excludes the added context, including after persistence, restart, and compaction. Tool definitions stay stable across scope changes.
- [CI passes on `2f2688f34`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38126802583), including Python 3.11/3.14, full-repository lint and strict types, Windows compatibility, and Docker. Unaffected WebUI/TUI jobs were skipped by the workflow.

## Cache boundaries

The context is appended only to new user messages. Tool iterations and transient retries do not add another copy. Prior message values and order, system content, and tool definitions stay unchanged when only the access mode changes. Provider conversion is checked, not only the agent's raw messages. Tests normalize JSON object key order; message order, text, tool arguments, and tool schemas remain exact.

This is not zero-cost context. For `/workspace/project`, the block including its separator uses 40 tokens in Full Access, 44 when restricted, or 57 with a configured shell sandbox, measured with `cl100k_base` (down from 43, 48, and 64). Other paths and model tokenizers differ. Each new user request pays for its new suffix and retains it in history. This can affect the hit ratio and when compaction occurs. Changing the project or compacting history can start a new prefix. The fixed `my` description change can also require a cache refresh at upgrade. No live provider cache-hit percentage is claimed.

The design follows stable-prefix guidance from [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) and [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching). Provider expiry, routing, and model-specific policies still apply.

This fixes a confirmed inspection gap. It does not prove the cause of every model refusal or override OS permissions. No live-model evaluation is claimed.

## Problem

Models on one connection can need different request headers or parameters. Connection-wide settings force users to duplicate a connection or change all its models.

## Change

- Add optional headers, query parameters and body parameters to model presets and inline fallbacks.

- Use the effective parameters when reusing a provider. Keep inherited values within the same connection, including automatic routing and SDK model overrides. Different connections can share an endpoint without sharing preset credentials.
- Reuse the existing parameter editor and styles. Mask saved secrets, clear overrides when the provider changes, and keep failed input available for correction. Translate the known missing-secret error in all ten locales.
- Hide the controls on hosts without this feature. Document inheritance, supported adapters and downgrade limits.

The shared request validation is also used by #6160. This PR does not change image generation, provider removal or the agent loop.

## Compatibility

Existing configurations keep their behavior. Omitted and empty override maps inherit connection defaults. New override fields require a version that supports them; older versions ignore them. A fallback uses its own settings. No prompt or tool-schema changes are introduced.

## Verification

- After merging main `bdfc8f7bd`: 320 focused Python tests and 107 WebUI tests passed. The tests cover routing, cross-connection isolation, settings, secret handling, saved input and translations.

prs.body:
## Problem

The settings Restart button sends a silent `/restart` command. Without a current chat, it uses the connection's default routing ID. Saving that command, workspace scope or reply could create an empty topic.

## Change

Treat this authenticated settings request as a transient control. Keep the existing allowlist and workspace checks, correlated reply, ACK and retry deduplication. Do not save a chat, change its workspace, append display history or broadcast a user message for this request.

The gateway sets the internal marker only for an exact silent restart from a trusted WebUI connection. A turn-ID prefix alone is not sufficient. No new endpoint, client capability or agent-loop branch is needed.

Keep restart progress in each participating browser tab. Another tab can consume the shared reload marker without leaving the initiating tab stuck on “Restarting...”.

## Compatibility

Keep the existing wire protocol. Typed `/restart` and session commands keep their behavior. Existing canonical records and display transcripts are not migrated, deleted or hidden. Users can inspect and remove old empty topics. Prompts and tool schemas do not change.

## Verification

- After merging main `1e5ab8e95`, 418 backend tests passed across restart controls, command dispatch, workspace permissions, WebSocket ingress and HTTP routes. They cover repeated default IDs, unchanged history, canonical-only and display-only history, fresh-manager sidebar discovery, ACK retry, allowlist rejection and untrusted clients.
- 363 UI tests passed across App layout, composer, workspace selection and the WebSocket client. They include another tab clearing the restart marker before or after disconnect and integration with the permission-switching change in #6175.
- Earlier real gateway/browser checks restarted twice with multiple tabs connected. Both initiating tabs recovered without a page reload. No canonical record or display transcript was created.
- Current-head CI covers the Python matrix, WebUI and Docker build.

No live model or messaging channel was called. Physical mobile/PWA testing was not performed. This fixes the settings Restart action, not every possible cause of a new topic.

prs.title: fix(webui): make full chat navigation scrollable and efficient
prs.body:
## Summary

The message rail currently grows only when older chat pages load. Long rails can exceed the viewport, and users cannot select prompts that have not loaded yet.

This change gives the rail a complete prompt directory, independent scrolling, and fading edges. Long and short rails stay centered against the complete chat frame, including the shared composer. Clicking a prompt loads the nearby history page instead of every preceding answer.

## Implementation

- Build bounded prompt summaries from the existing WebUI display transcript. Cache summaries by segment identity. Do not change SQLite, agent context, configuration, or chat storage.
- Reuse the transcript reader for forward and backward cursor pages. Keep at most three navigation pages. Keep the canonical live conversation separate, and provide a return-to-latest action.
- Window both the rail and the searchable message navigator. Preserve Markdown previews, keyboard navigation, and reduced-motion behavior.
- Revalidate unchanged directories with HTTP 304. When a previous snapshot is cached, transfer only the changed suffix. Send a complete directory after cache eviction or restart. Cache keys include the instance data path.
- Keep the current page on a failed read. Cancel superseded requests, reject stale jump targets, and hydrate deferred activity details in the correct browsing window. Return to the live conversation when selecting a new prompt that has not yet acquired a saved cursor.
- Avoid rebuilding the complete directory or its position observers for each streamed answer token.
- Cancel an in-flight history read when the user selects an already-rendered prompt or returns to the latest messages. A late response cannot replace the newer selection.

## Compatibility

WebUI protocol 1 and `webui.core.v1` remain unchanged. The new read path uses optional capability `webui.prompt-navigation.v1`. Older compatible hosts keep navigation within loaded messages; older clients keep the existing latest/before reads. Authentication still runs before conditional responses.

No data migration, new persistent index, dependency, installer, or startup requirement is added. The update and recovery paths are unchanged. Navigation caches are derived and memory-only; they do not replace either session storage or display transcripts.

## Verification

- Rebased onto `main` at `5f6e8a6baab8487ff5249993cb54a2c05bf0f587`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39113793736) passed for `b1e898155d369e2a3e9c3d8c7018569e877aa7d9`: seven successful jobs, including Linux, Windows, WebUI and Docker, with one conditional matrix placeholder skipped.
- After rebase, 361 focused frontend tests and 65 backend prompt-index, transcript and client-contract tests passed. After the final cancellation fix, the affected hook/viewport suites passed 76 tests, including two new regressions. The two regressions fail without the fix: a delayed request replaces the later local selection in both live and historical views.
- All four real-browser regression tests passed after the final repair. Geometry assertions use the real workbench and its portalled composer. They cover long and short rails, a taller composer in a shorter window, and narrow-to-wide resizing.
- Full ESLint, production TypeScript/build, affected-file Ruff, Python/client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed locally. Exact-head CI also passed strict BasedPyright, the full configured suites, and the browser regression job.
- Tests cover a complete 2,000-prompt rail, virtualized controls, centering, independent scroll, unloaded-message jumps, bounded forward/backward browsing, retry, rapid switches, old-host fallback, deferred trace details, directory truncation/replacement, and cache eviction.
- The browser performance harness also used the production components and a real authenticated local HTTP handler with 10,000 synthetic conversation rounds. No personal configuration or chats were used. It does not exercise a model or an installed release package.

## Local performance evidence

Comparison is against the first implementation of this fix (`affe68db1`), not against an equivalent complete-directory feature on `main`, which did not have one. Measurements used macOS ARM64, Python 3.11.4, and headless Chrome. Backend source data was about 55 MiB; the OS filesystem cache was warm.

| Measurement | First implementation | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Uncached summary build, median / P95 (7 runs) | 271 / 335 ms | 136 / 158 ms |
| One new round, uncompressed directory JSON | 4,166,649 bytes | 503 bytes |
| Revalidation, browser click-to-response P95 (30 operations) | 111 ms, HTTP 200 | 59 ms, HTTP 304 |
| Old-message jump, click-to-visible P95 (20 operations) | 179 ms | 102 ms |
| Position observer constructions, 120 simulated token updates | 120 | 1 |
| Prompt geometry reads during those updates | 3,510 | 300 |
| Sampled browser JS heap high-water mark | 98 MiB | 53 MiB |

The optimized browser run recorded no tasks over 50 ms during those jumps or simulated token updates. These are local development-harness observations, not latency or memory guarantees for every browser and conversation. The first uncached visit still reads transcript segments. The build retains the existing large-chunk advisory.

## Documentation and release

`docs/webui.md` describes the navigation behavior and cache boundaries. Include the user-facing improvement in the release notes when this change ships; do not advertise it as released before then. No release or running-gateway restart is part of this change.
