prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Provide one Stable / Preview update flow with installation-owner-aware guidance and bounded service recovery. The gateway owns policy, durable state, shutdown and execution. WebUI presents the reviewed target, explicit consent and authenticated reconnection. This PR does not publish a release or activate the public update channel.

## Integration status — 2026-10-21

Merged into main by the explicitly authorized **admin squash merge** at `fbb61a373f47769734a0d47d8f61935ffca84b84`. The reviewed head was `9c4a52c6d751b7c3e4929c61006c365f050a8c0a`, containing base `76da55994b55bf0e8c0bb634dbd674a990417964`. [All 11 pre-merge CI checks passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39586263340). The squash commit has that base as its only parent and exactly matches the reviewed file tree. GitHub recognizes both @Re-bin and @chengyongru as authors. All three review threads are resolved; formal approval was explicitly waived, not fabricated. #6355, #6356 and #6280 are included. No release, tag, signing, public-feed or main-rule change was made.

Both current Linux and Windows native reports pass **9 scenarios / 15 operations**, including configuration, authenticated canonical/display history, SQLite/outbox, continued writes, second start, recovery followed by another update and final process stop. Reports bind to tested merge `03c0f945c7e262be845e1170af21f5dc8301290f`, whose verified parents are the base and reviewed head above; its tree also equals the squash commit. Linux wheel SHA-256: `8e50124ee279af216b680a35da45d5b7ecc4c2bee433c30f9c1f425ef615f626`. Windows wheel SHA-256: `1ba79ce1bf9c61f1248e94bc651373c83da1101f8393762e16eaab02a25405b2`. Windows actually ran with `LongPathsEnabled=0`. Both installation probes pass 379 assets, native protocol 1 and readiness without frontend build tools or native downloads; Windows' separate probe uses forced cleanup and is not graceful-shutdown proof. The macOS evidence below retains its original source identity and documented unchanged-contract scope. Main's push CI is a separate post-merge run; the successful checks above are pre-merge evidence.

The latest main integration changes stream-segment closure, optional transcript projection metadata and memory-only frontend checkpoints. It does not change persisted records, installation identity, update/recovery protocols, startup or native dependencies. Focused Python checks: **65 passed**. Frontend integration checks: **261 passed**, with full typecheck. Actual Chromium checks for About layout, current/legacy stream replay and cached return at wide/narrow widths: **15 passed**. Earlier macOS lifecycle proof retains its exact source and wheel identity and covers unchanged update/recovery/data/Dock contracts; these new checks cover the changed projection contract. It is not a newly built macOS UI artifact.

- Integrated the Windows extended-path fix at atomic record and lease I/O boundaries, including its frozen planning-child dependency. Stored path identities and installation policy do not change. Native package CI now tests recovery with `LongPathsEnabled=0` on the disposable Windows runner, without changing users' machines.
- Integrated the compact About version/update row, automatic checking on entry and the visible Preview toggle. Added explicit lazy-view synchronization to two existing tests without increasing their deadlines. A delayed-image reproduction exposed an About layout shift; the original wordmark now reserves its intrinsic aspect ratio before download.
- Retained main's SQLite schema-v2 display-history migration. Package acceptance permits its deliberate empty display-only session owner, but still requires every existing canonical record and message to survive. This does not relax the program-only recovery boundary or restore old user data over a migrated database.

- Integrated @chengyongru's #6280 with both original commits and authorship preserved. That PR is incorporated into this branch, not independently into main.
- Addressed all three maintainer findings: pre-stop revalidation shares rollback-protected catalogue history; the supervisor validates the exact confirmation before its first journal write and retains that identity during recovery after launch expiry; interrupted preparation offers explicit lease-checked settlement without granting new installation consent. The review threads are resolved. No approval was submitted on the maintainer's behalf.
- Resolved the new About gallery conflict without dropping either localized controls or Preview/update feedback. Feedback follows language changes without resetting the selected preference. All ten gallery locales include the new messages.
- Fixed a demonstrated integration failure in main's new QQ connector. A live QR session now participates in update admission; cancelled, closed or expired sessions cannot save a late portal result. Credential-writing threads remain owned after request cancellation, and cleanup waits for them before the runtime can become idle. Gateway admission remains strict for unknown connector types.
- Retained main's TUI packaging, typography, gallery localization and history changes. Update protocol 1, worker request schema 4, installation/data identities and recovery policy are unchanged.
- Preserved the previous CI repair: real terminal-pipe tests run first in a fresh serial CLI process on all three Python platforms. This avoids the reproduced `select()` descriptor limit without deleting tests or weakening coverage. Windows full-suite budget remains 30 minutes; per-test assertions remain unchanged.
- Fixed the new Windows CI failure in the existing late-theme animation test. A renderer flush can finish before the timer repaints styled status chunks. Controlled timing reproduced one old color before the tick and five theme colors afterward. The test now waits for the painted frame using its existing two-second limit and retains the color assertion; production animation code is unchanged.
- Integrated the subsequent main change for model-error recovery and chat controls. Its optional recovery metadata does not change storage identity, update protocols or the frozen recovery program. Focused tests cover saved-context continuation, restart, duplicate-action refusal and update interaction together.
- Integrated main's graceful Windows CLI shutdown and history/composer fixes without conflict-resolution edits. The updater retains its consent-bound cooperative mailbox; it does not use the CLI's forced-stop fallback. Runtime publication adds an optional process-bound shutdown token, not a data-root or update-protocol migration. Windows-specific lifecycle proof remains required from the new CI.
- Integrated the subsequent listener-shutdown and test-support changes. Each listener owns its binary bridge and closes it before waiting for its server; the bridge still wraps upload activity in update admission. Resolved four conflicts without dropping update-specific isolation, architecture checks or native acceptance. Applied the merged #6362 browser regression correction; no duplicate implementation was added.
- Retained main's three-worker Windows budget for the broad suite and used three workers for isolated update jobs. Added phase/JUnit reports. Restored the separate installer group to its previously passing four workers after three workers exhausted its 20-minute job budget. All per-test timeouts, assertions and native package/recovery checks remain. The previous supervisor timeout did not recur: its Windows test call passed in 25 seconds, within the unchanged 40-second subprocess limit. The original timeout's root cause remains unconfirmed.

## Product and installation scope

| Installation owner | Supported update experience |
| --- | --- |
| Official managed install | Review the exact target, prepare verified files, stop idle reviewed gateways, back up, install offline, restart and verify the running version; bounded automatic service recovery. |
| Compatible POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry tool | Reviewed inline transaction retaining the recorded manager policy; no claim of managed-venv program restoration. |
| Other uv, pipx, ordinary pip, source, containers, OS services and Desktop | Version discovery and owner-specific instructions: the correct machine/account, applicable copyable commands and running-version/data verification. No silent adoption or fallback to another manager. |

Preview is visible but opt-in. Changing the subscription never installs, restarts or downgrades. Returning to Stable keeps an installed newer Preview until a newer stable release exists. Stable patches need not wait for a monthly feature release. Maintainers trigger packaging manually; this PR does not schedule daily publication.

macOS WebUI uses the approved original cat on a white tile. The gateway owns the optional Dock helper for managed background launches, recreates it after protected activation/recovery and removes it on stop. Closing the icon hides the shortcut, not the service. `--no-dock` preserves the instance preference. The helper owns no installation/data lease and is not loaded by the frozen updater.

## Safety and compatibility

- Exact plans, confirmation generations, installation/data leases and capability negotiation remain gateway-owned.
- Both channels require release metadata bound to the fixed official release-approval identity before download. Bytes are verified, and the reviewed release is revalidated before shutdown. Verification failure does not permit an unsigned fallback. Signing remains disabled.
- Recovery can retry the admitted exact target once, then restore only the original **program**, before activation and while protected data remains unchanged. It never overwrites current configuration or conversations with an old backup.
- Restored service is not reported as update success. Changed data, ownership changes, persistent disk faults, missing base Python or loss of both recovery processes can require operator repair. This PR makes no absolute reliability or supply-chain security claim.
- Scheduled delivery participates in maintenance and current backups. Old protocol-1 startup grants are not widened: the lazy delivery store takes its own ordinary lease and cannot write before activation.
- No new breaking change is intended by this integration. User guidance, implementation contracts and release procedures remain in `docs/updating.md`, `docs/update-protocol.md` and `docs/releasing.md`.

## Verification

Latest local integration: update/storage boundary selection **128 passed**; acceptance-oracle regression **12 passed**; atomic/lease/shutdown and real offline job selection **151 passed / 11 Windows-only skips**. After the frontend-only base update, planning-bootstrap/helpers **35 passed**. These selections overlap and must not be added together. The Windows patch was unchanged by both rebases. The original child also has attributed native `LongPathsEnabled=0` parent/fix controls and deep-home WebUI acceptance from @chengyongru; that is not a new native execution of this combined head.

Six frontend interaction suites: **190 passed**, plus full typecheck, lint and client import-boundary checks. The delayed-image test reproduced and fixes a 32.796875-pixel shift. CI then identified a separate About mismatch: current-version feedback wraps under wider system fonts. A controlled monospace case reproduced the exact **18px** shift. The row now reuses the existing six-column wide-control layout, retaining accessible feedback and narrow-screen wrapping. All **7** image/font/locale/viewport browser cases pass, plus browser typecheck and touched-file lint.

Private macOS arm64 candidate `0.3.7.dev2026102105` was built from `83350603b` (version-only candidate `5154a4bb8723e9d9896d9355dc2c43d7c331b50a`, wheel SHA-256 `7a92828bdb68a76c46bb235973f2f78c5417a59ebb28a02bed9e5ece404092ae`). Fresh installation/startup passes **379 assets**, native protocol 1, readiness and graceful stop without frontend build tools or TUI downloads. Both genuine retained SQLite-v1 packages pass the direct upgrade, including data/continuation/restart/Dock assertions. Their backup-failure restoration followed by another upgrade reached a healthy target service but failed Dock presence; these recovery journeys are not accepted as passed. The older 1902 package contains SQLite and must not be represented as a pre-SQLite baseline.

The Dock handshake inherited a **2s** connection timeout even though the child loads AppKit before acknowledging readiness. A native cold start measured **1.928s**; a controlled real-child **2.5s** start reproduces the premature timeout. Commit `3ca334cc9` separates short connection setup from a bounded **10s** readiness/start-lock wait on the existing background thread, preserving cleanup and user-hidden intent. **27 Dock/restart tests pass**, plus Ruff/diff checks. Logs expose only an exception category, never credentials or the URL. The original warning did not preserve its exception type; that historical cause is not asserted with certainty. Installed startup passes 379 assets, native protocol 1, readiness and graceful stop. Private feed/fault fixtures do not establish official-signed public-download compatibility. Windows' separate installed-startup probe uses forced cleanup and is not evidence of graceful shutdown.

## Remaining gates

- [x] Complete current-head CI and applicable native package acceptance, then perform the authorized admin squash merge with verified contributor attribution. Formal independent approval was explicitly waived by the user.
- [x] Integrate the separately owned Windows long-path fix #6356 and About refinement #6355 through their reviewed stack, preserving authorship. Their integration does not waive the combined-head checks above.
- [ ] Select the final immutable version/source and obtain separate publication authorization. Public baselines without this updater need an original-owner first upgrade.
- [ ] Review runtime dependency trust and release-protection settings. Enable signing only with separate authorization, then verify official-signed public old → candidate → next-version and failure-recovery paths.
- [ ] Build and retain the same-batch five-platform wheels, sdist, native archives, manifest, checksums and proof. Bind native and supported-old-version/owner-bootstrap acceptance to those bytes. Three native platforms do not prove macOS x64/Linux arm64; container replacement and volume preservation remain separate.
- [ ] Confirm corresponding-source/relinking offers, retention responsibility, licenses/notices and source availability.
- [ ] Separately approve GitHub/PyPI publication and protected catalogue advancement; verify public bytes and installation before advertising availability.

Daily configuration, conversations and the user's active worktree are untouched. CI retains small reports. The optional candidate handoff is bounded to one day; no paid macOS runner is added.

prs.title: ci: scope native acceptance and bind release candidate artifacts
prs.body:
## Why

Small frontend changes currently inherit native installation and upgrade/recovery acceptance on both Linux and Windows. In the inspected main run, the Windows packaged-recovery step alone took 21m30s and its enclosing job about 31 minutes. Separate code validation from release-package acceptance, without deleting recovery scenarios or reducing the Python compatibility matrix.

## What changed

- Centralize affected-path selection with per-path explanations and a stable `CI required` check. Keep shared client consumers covered; retain full selection for unknown paths, unavailable diffs and manual runs. Windows isolated installer/update journeys and reusable native acceptance run for relevant PRs/manual checks, not ordinary main pushes.
- Keep ordinary TUI checks separate from native packaging/install/update acceptance. Preserve the complete nine-scenario recovery suite and add incrementally persisted phase timings, including failure evidence, without uploading raw credential-bearing logs.
- Build release candidates once, transfer the exact Linux/Windows wheels by immutable producer artifact IDs, verify manifest/package/commit identity before execution, and require both native consumers before promoting an explicitly requested installable handoff. Producer IDs also support failed-jobs-only retries without rebuilding or looking for a nonexistent new-attempt artifact.

## Scope

No automatic release, signing, catalogue advancement, scheduling, branch-protection changes or production-service changes. Python platform/version coverage, frontend/browser/terminal checks and Docker safety checks remain. Candidate fixture acceptance does not replace real historical baselines, remaining native-platform coverage or public-download acceptance. Requiring the stable aggregate check in repository rules remains an administrator-owned action.

## Tradeoffs

The path policy is deliberately conservative and requires maintenance when shared contracts or installed-lifecycle inputs move. Regression coverage includes the actual frozen update-worker archive inputs, Docker pytest files and the TUI fork-chat backend. Native scenarios still run serially inside their shared private installation; this change removes unrelated scheduling, not a measured acceleration of the specialized recovery flow. No speedup percentage is claimed.

## Blast Radius

CI selection, conditional job execution, candidate artifact handoff and diagnostic evidence only; production update/recovery behavior is unchanged. Key risks are missing a consumer or installation input, treating an unexpected skip as success, and testing different bytes from those handed off. Tests cover these boundaries, producer-ID wiring, commit/hash mismatch rejection, diff ranges, renames, failure/timeout timing evidence and cleanup.

## Verification

- Focused Python contract tests: **102 passed** on Python 3.12.10: `tests/scripts/test_ci_scope.py`, `test_ci_gate.py`, `test_ci_workflows.py`, `test_native_acceptance_input.py`, plus `tests/test_packaged_update_probe.py`, `tests/test_release_candidate.py`, and `tests/test_installed_release_probe.py`.
- Actionlint **1.7.12**: all repository workflows passed. Its current action metadata recognizes `download-artifact@v4` producer artifact-ID downloads; the actual upstream action definition was also checked.
- Ruff **0.17.1**: all changed/new Python scripts and associated tests passed; `git diff --check` passed. No formatter was run.
- Regression-first review fixes: five focused policy cases failed before fixing Docker pytest selection, frozen-worker `data_access`, shared fork-chat selection and the installed WebUI launcher; all now pass.
- Selection-only replay used complete paginated file lists from eight merged PRs. Pure frontend PRs #6369 and #6335 select WebUI/Docker without native recovery; actual installation/update changes retain native acceptance. This is selection proof, not execution-time measurement.
- Native GitHub runner execution and the manual release-candidate transfer path were not executed locally. The signature-only suite was not validated in the local interpreter, which lacks `sigstore`; signing code and its workflow are unchanged. CI results on this PR provide separate runtime evidence, not a claim of release approval.


### CI follow-up

Run `39614121240` passed Linux and Windows native acceptance, Linux Python, both clients and Docker. Windows Python exposed two test fixtures that tried to create Unix-only filenames; the injection test now constructs actual Git trees without materializing invalid Windows paths, preserving newline/output-escaping coverage. Windows process/installer tests all passed (78 installer cases), but the combined job exceeded its 20-minute job deadline during teardown. Installer compatibility now has an independently gated job (25-minute bound based on the observed 18m06s installer step), retaining all cases and the existing four-worker budget. Aggregate-gate and workflow-wiring regressions cover the split. Local follow-up: 102 tests, Actionlint 1.7.12 and Ruff passed; latest pushed-head CI is pending.


### Installer timeout diagnostics

Run `39618051766` passed both native acceptance jobs, clients, Docker and Linux Python; Windows Python logs also reached passing main/serial suites. Its independent Windows installer job failed the uv persistent-owner case at the unchanged 90-second command deadline. The pipe-based harness provided no partial command output, so the exact slow phase is not yet established. Commit `d74ff2d04` captures installer output in temporary files, preserving the same deadline/assertions and reporting both partial streams on timeout. This also waits for command completion rather than inherited-pipe EOF; inherited handles are a possible mechanism, not a confirmed diagnosis. Local verification: 104 tests passed, including a real timeout-diagnostic test and Linux uv owner-preserving install/upgrade; Ruff and Actionlint passed. Windows behavior and latest-head CI remain pending. No timeout increase or automatic retry was added.

prs.title: fix(agent): finalize stopped turns without checkpoints (NAN-211)
prs.body:
## Why

Stopping a request before its first runtime checkpoint leaves `pending_user_turn` persisted. `/stop` reports success, but the next gateway startup treats that marker as an interrupted request and shows an unnecessary recovery decision.

Linear: [NAN-211](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-211)

## What changed

- Materialize any available checkpoint, then finalize the cancelled turn through the existing session owner's `finish_turn()` operation regardless of whether a checkpoint exists.
- Preserve completed tool results and the existing shutdown/discard guards.
- Add a persisted 2×2 regression covering explicit stop versus gateway shutdown, both before a model response and after completed tools. Update the existing checkpoint-preservation test to observe the owner operation used for finalization.

## Scope

This fixes newly stopped turns. It does not migrate or clear pre-existing recovery metadata, change the frontend, alter recovery classification, or change storage schemas. Gateway shutdown continues to preserve interrupted work for confirmation.

## Blast Radius

The change is confined to the AgentLoop cancellation finalizer and its tests. Explicit stop must clear pending state without losing completed work; lifecycle shutdown must still retain recovery state. Both contracts are covered by the regression and real-process checks.

## Verification

- Regression first: **1 failed / 3 passed** on the unmodified base; the failure was the stopped request without a checkpoint. All four cases pass after the fix.
- `uv run --no-sync python -B -m pytest tests/agent tests/session tests/command -q -n 3 --dist loadfile`: **2284 passed, 4 skipped**.
- CI's repository-wide `ruff check` scope: **passed**.
- `uv run --no-sync python -B -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: **passed** (13 rules, 216 files).
- Real gateway processes and WebSockets with an isolated loopback OpenAI-compatible SSE fixture: reproduced the erroneous recovery on the base; verified stop-before-response and stop-after-tools remain recovery-free after graceful process shutdown/restart, completed tool results remain saved, and genuine gateway shutdown still requires recovery confirmation. Restart did not issue another model request. All owned processes, listeners and temporary runtime data were cleaned up.
- Full-project BasedPyright: **FAIL**, with two Windows `setproctitle` import/type diagnostics in `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py`. The frozen base, checked with the same interpreter/dependencies, produces the identical two diagnostics. No type-check success is claimed.

The provider fixture is local and deterministic; live-provider and browser visual acceptance were not performed. There are no frontend changes.

prs.title: fix(webui): parse CJK emphasis at delimiter boundaries
prs.body:
## Why
Chinese replies can expose literal `**` when punctuation touches an emphasis delimiter and the next sentence starts immediately. The previous text-node repair cannot recognize emphasis spanning inline code or links. Resolve CJK emphasis boundaries during parsing instead of repairing the parsed text with regular expressions.

Tracks [NAN-320](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-320).

## What changed
- Register the parse-only entrypoint of `remark-cjk-friendly` 2.3.3 and remove the old CJK strong-boundary AST rewrite and its obsolete position shape.
- Cover the original long reply, nested code/links/emphasis, Chinese opening and closing punctuation, Japanese and Korean boundaries, standard Markdown, escapes/entities, code isolation, and streaming-to-complete rendering.
- Add isolated browser regressions through the real lazy `MarkdownText` entrypoint at 390px and 1440px, including an incomplete streaming prefix followed by completion.

## Scope
Client-side emphasis parsing only. No history rewriting, server protocol changes, new HTML permissions, URL-policy changes, or daily-instance deployment. This is a CJK emphasis extension to CommonMark, not a claim that the triggering source is recognized as emphasis by strict CommonMark or that every Markdown ambiguity is solved. It does not add a CJK strikethrough extension.

## Tradeoffs
The old repair also accepted a space immediately inside a closing delimiter, such as `**边界说明： **issue`. With the explicitly agreed compatibility boundary, invalid internal-whitespace emphasis remains literal after completion rather than being silently rewritten. The former positive test is replaced with explicit literal-output coverage, not deleted. Valid alternatives include `**边界说明：** issue` and `**中文**。继续`.

Use the maintained tokenizer extension rather than expanding the local regular expression across AST siblings or replacing the entire renderer. The parse-only import avoids loading its Markdown serialization path into the renderer; both npm and Bun locks record the dependency chain.

## Blast Radius
All consumers of the shared Markdown renderer, including replies and document previews, receive the CJK emphasis rules. Existing math, code, HTML-subset and link handling remain on their existing paths. Streaming may temporarily complete unfinished Markdown as before; final rendering uses the unmodified source and the same grammar. No host capability or persistence changes are needed.

## Verification
- Red first: both new nested code/link regression cases failed against the old text-node repair.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: passed; actual loaded `remark-cjk-friendly` 2.3.3 / `micromark-extension-cjk-friendly` 2.0.2.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`: passed.
- `bun run test`: 176 files, 3123 tests passed, including 134 renderer cases.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint`: passed.
- `bun run check:imports`: passed; `bun run test:imports`: 41 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- `NANOBOT_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=4293 bun run test:browser -- markdown-emphasis.spec.ts`: 2 Chromium cases passed; isolated Vite fixture server exited and port released.
- `bun run build` and `git diff --check`: passed. Build retains a large-chunk warning; renderer tests emit KaTeX warnings.

The browser checks use synthetic content, not a live gateway or real conversation. Windows/macOS runtime acceptance and remote CI are not established by these local Linux checks. A separate scoped candidate check found no blocking issue; no formal GitHub approval or merge is implied.

prs.title: fix(compaction): align native lifecycle and reconcile replay notices
prs.body:
## Why

Idle compaction notices can appear twice when live delivery is reconciled with saved history. Codex also reports native compaction only after streaming the answer, because its notification was attached to subsequent checkpoint materialization.

Fixes https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-326
Fixes https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-327

## What changed

- Reconcile compaction units by their existing `compaction_id`, preserving sequence receipts and distinct operations.
- Emit Codex native lifecycle events around the actual validated trigger request, before generation. Carry an internal response receipt to avoid notifying again during checkpoint work.
- Report server-observed inline completion as succeeded without inventing its start time. Keep completed native facts independent of later checkpoint failure or cancellation, and retain the latest compaction boundary.

## Scope

Preserves H/Δ checkpoint boundaries, native/local/idle/manual compaction policy, retry budgets, and the public event payload. No settings, dependency, UI-copy, or timeout changes.

## Tradeoffs

Portable checkpoint materialization still follows the model response; it no longer masquerades as native compression. Existing whole-call retries can perform distinct physical compactions, each with its own identity; this change adds no retry cache or lifecycle manager.

## Blast Radius

Codex pre-request notices, response-observed native compaction notices in the governor, and WebUI transcript reconciliation. Existing channel notification policy and local/idle/manual lifecycle ownership remain intact.

## Verification

Passed on `421bd6b5` + this change:
- Focused provider/runner/Responses/context-pressure suites: **271 passed**.
- Transcript/projection/stream-hook tests: **145 passed**; browser history-hydration scenarios: **7 passed**.
- WebUI full-project typecheck, lint, import checks, and production build; touched Python Ruff and import-boundary checks.
- Real Codex HTTP verification: two generation requests and one actual native trigger; succeeded precedes generation/answer deltas, and a synthetic marker survives compression.
- Built production App with an isolated gateway and real SQLite-backed HTTP history: one live idle operation stays singular after history acceptance and reload; two distinct operations remain in native → answer → idle order. Live frames in this browser scenario are controlled synthetic replay. Both owned runtimes were cleaned up.

Outstanding full-project results (hence Draft):
- Broader Python run: **4760 passed, 21 skipped, 2 failed** in Windows remote-discovery username handling. The same two failures reproduce on the frozen base.
- Full BasedPyright: **2 `setproctitle` diagnostics**, identical on the frozen base.
- Default-worker WebUI coverage: candidate **108 failed / 3080 passed**; frozen base **33 failed / 3112 passed / 39 skipped**. These differing sets are not claimed as failure parity.
- A complete single-worker candidate run hit its declared 600-second budget; the following baseline control was cancelled. No full-suite success is claimed, and assertions/coverage thresholds/CI configuration are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(network): centralize proxy settings and add MCP routing (NAN-315)
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements [NAN-315](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-315).

- Configure one ordinary, visible shared proxy address in **Settings → Advanced**, with **Use proxy** switches for supported providers, Web access, Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix/WhatsApp, and HTTP/SSE MCP connections. Includes all ten locales.
- Select the route before the first MCP OAuth attempt. Discovery, registration, token exchange/refresh, transport, tool calls, reconnect, and selective hot reload share the same instance-scoped route. Explicit proxy failures do not fall back to direct connections; target and redirect SSRF checks remain enforced.
- Migrate legacy single-address file/environment settings after source merging; preserve saved opt-outs and unresolved credential references. Existing two-argument channel plugins retain their construction API through explicit shared-proxy opt-in.
- Follow-up review repairs register the public MCP proxy mutation, retire consumed proxy drafts without overriding later saved opt-outs, preserve OAuth-provider false flags across saves, handle combined-userinfo/Discord scheme environment templates correctly, and keep proxy credentials out of connection traceback diagnostics while retaining useful error details.
- Update usage and upgrade documentation. MCP error classification/copy remains in [NAN-316](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-316).

## Upgrade notes

`network.proxy` replaces per-feature addresses; features store `useProxy` flags. One old address is promoted automatically on load and written on the next normal save. Different old addresses require explicitly choosing one shared address; no multi-proxy compatibility is retained.

For an old Discord configuration using an entire URL environment reference plus separate credentials, first combine them into one full-URL environment variable and set `network.proxy` to it. Literal URLs and scheme templates with credential references migrate without writing resolved secrets.

## Verification

Tested source: `7aa0515c1a92b2f8e65756cf5ebc328b507eab20`; frozen comparison base: `b32b1327ceb0e7fb9ecbb3ad9f0e7bf04fccb8a6`. Tracked dependencies and lockfiles are unchanged. Three independent first-pass review areas and a fresh repair cross-boundary review were completed; source review is separate from runtime evidence below.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Config + Docker configuration + complete settings routes | 237 passed, 1 existing platform skip |
| Full Python, `pytest tests nanobot/channels -n 3 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short` | **FAIL:** 10,278 passed, 130 skipped, 4 failed. The same four signatures reproduce in the exact frozen-base attribution subset: configured ripgrep shim, Windows symlink privilege, and two remote-discovery username/environment cases |
| Full Vitest, `bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` | 3,045 passed across 172 files |
| Complete local Playwright suite, one worker, zero retries | 176 passed; own Chrome contexts |
| Full BasedPyright | **FAIL:** the same two unresolved/unknown `setproctitle` diagnostics as the exact frozen base |
| Ruff, Python/client import boundaries, WebUI typecheck/lint, production build, diff check | Passed; build retains the existing chunk-size advisory |
| Isolated built gateway + real Chrome, desktop/narrow | Visible-address save/refresh/clear, first-OAuth proxy setup, missing-address refusal, unavailable-proxy failure, public WebSocket proxy mutation, and saved disabled state after refresh passed |
| Real recording proxy + MCP SDK | Discovery, registration, token exchange/refresh, activation, tool calls, and terminated-session recovery use the selected route |
| Diagnostic safety regressions | Real HTTPX constructor and setup/cleanup chain/group failures retain useful type/stack/stage text without raw or decoded selected-proxy credentials; short credentials do not corrupt diagnostic words |

The new worktree initially lacked the ignored environment `uv.lock`, causing one additional benchmark prerequisite failure. Copying the unchanged provisioned lock after verifying identical pyproject bytes fixed that setup; the benchmark and full Python rerun above include it, with no dependency sync or test weakening.

## Figma authorization limitation

The shared proxy reaches the real Figma MCP 401 challenge and OAuth discovery metadata 200. The actual first-authorization attempt then receives **403 Forbidden during client registration** at `https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/mcp/register`. User-Agent, minimal-metadata, and callback-host controls did not change that refusal.

[Figma's official remote-server instructions](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) require approved MCP clients and direct new clients to request access. This is a service-side prerequisite consistent with the observed registration refusal; full Figma account authorization remains blocked, not passed. No client-name impersonation or speculative transport workaround was added.

Production configuration and shared gateways were not changed. The user's earlier preview is preserved, and the repaired preview uses separate synthetic data. Final-head CI is reported separately from local verification.

At the bounded final-head status check, [CI run 39588557900](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39588557900) was still running. Python 3.11, Windows process compatibility, and Docker had passed; remaining jobs were pending/in progress. No continuous CI monitoring was started.

prs.title: fix(webui): restore messages after batched visibility changes
prs.body:
## Why

Historical messages can remain as large blank placeholders after scrolling back into view. `ThreadDisplayUnit` consumed only the first `IntersectionObserver` record, so a coalesced leave/enter batch could apply an obsolete offscreen state and discard the newer enter notification.

Linear: [NAN-333](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-333).

## What changed

- Apply the latest record from each single-target observer batch, preserving the existing height measurement and offscreen recycling policy.
- Extend the existing component regression to cover batched leave/enter and enter/leave notifications, placeholder removal, and subsequent re-entry.

## Scope

Frontend-only, two files. No new timers, polling, fallback behavior, dependency changes, backend changes, or history-data changes.

## Blast Radius

Completed historical message/activity units managed by `ThreadDisplayUnit`. The observer still watches one element; its root margin, lifetime, interaction retention, and measured-height placeholders are unchanged.

## Verification

- Regression first: the updated component test failed on the base implementation because the historical answer stayed unmounted after a leave/enter batch.
- `bun run test src/tests/thread-messages.test.tsx`: **58 passed**.
- `bun run test`: **3229 passed**, 182 files.
- `bun run test:browser history-boundary.spec.ts`: **19 passed**, zero retries; includes scrolling, prepend anchoring, delayed layout, cached windows, and navigation.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, and `bun run build`: **passed**.
- Native Chromium reproduction using the real `ThreadMessages` component with synthetic content and controlled task pressure: the same 12-record leave/enter batch left a **2020.25px empty placeholder in 2/2 base runs**; the fix retained the text and cleared the inline placeholder height in **2/2 candidate runs**, without another scroll or click. prs.title: fix(webui): preserve file edit stats and left-truncate long paths
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes [NAN-332](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-332).

- Keep file-edit addition/deletion statistics visible independently of the path width. Short paths keep their statistics immediately adjacent.
- Truncate overflowing file-edit paths from the left, preserving the filename/extension and trailing directories without changing text direction or rewriting the underlying path.
- Reuse the existing delayed hover/focus tooltip for the complete absolute path: left-aligned, selectable, viewport-bounded, and wrapping at directory separators with an emergency break for long names.
- Preserve preview, keyboard activation, context menus, diff disclosure, and active-text sheen. Other file references retain their existing truncation behavior.
- Remove the ambiguous total diff-line count beside “View changes”, including its unused translations. Keep addition/deletion statistics, large-diff truncation notices, and show-more/show-fewer controls.
- Image file-edit hints show the complete path above the existing image preview, including an accessible full-path label. Ordinary image references keep their existing preview-only hint. The explicit accessible label avoids mounting a second preview in Radix's hidden tooltip description.

## Cause and scope

The file-edit label has placed the path and statistics side by side since `aa8387fb4`. Later, `05bee21b1` wrapped file references in `FileActions`, adding an inline-flex minimum-width boundary outside the caller's `min-w-0`. The label's overflow clipping can then hide the statistics even though the statistics themselves are non-shrinking. This change restores the shrink boundary for the file-edit caller and opts that caller into start truncation.

Start truncation keeps the complete text in normal order and right-aligns it inside a clipping viewport. A component-local ResizeObserver only determines whether a leading ellipsis is needed; it does not slice the path or impose a fixed statistics width. It is installed only for the opt-in file-edit reference and disconnected on unmount.

## Verification

- Browser regression against the unchanged `130f4edef` baseline reproduces hidden statistics; the same desktop/narrow fixture passes on the candidate.
- Chromium browser cases at 360px and 1024px cover long Windows paths, Unicode/spaces, oversized filenames, short paths, multi-digit counts, suffix visibility, complete hover/focus hints, keyboard preview, diff expansion, and resize back to an untruncated path.
- Full-project WebUI typecheck, browser-fixture typecheck, lint, import-boundary check, and production build.
- Initial implementation: 96 related unit tests covering file-edit activity, file actions, file references, and activity rows; full-project checks above passed on `4bed67a3d`.
- Line-count removal follow-up: 72 activity/localization unit tests and both browser regression cases passed again. Rendered screenshots confirm the disclosure row now contains only its action label; show-more/show-fewer coverage is retained.

- Image-hint review fix: the two browser cases first failed on the missing image path, then passed with visible full-path text, hover/focus access, viewport wrapping, and a single mounted image preview. Full-project and browser typechecks, lint, and 96 related unit tests passed after the fix. The preview fixture uses a synthetic one-pixel PNG.

Browser checks use the real components with synthetic file-edit data; no production sessions or running gateway were modified. No full-suite or real-gateway end-to-end claim is made.

## Why

A typing pause is not an editing boundary. The previous 600 ms autosave could admit intermediate context-window values, and older save responses could replace newer drafts. Save completed edits without losing the automatic-save experience.

Refs https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-323

## What changed

- Replace debounce with completion-driven, revision-deduplicated saves across model presets, capabilities, safety and channel/Linear settings. Blur, close and navigation complete text/numeric edits; discrete controls still submit immediately.
- Serialize captured draft/target versions, preserve newer edits through responses and native reconnect refresh, validate queued renames against the latest catalog, and keep failed/invalid editors open with visible errors.
- Guard standalone Channels and browser-history section changes. Prevent stale picker focus restoration and changing error-feedback geometry from causing premature saves or losing a Close click. Remove the redundant advanced-channel blur drain.
- Keep one controller-owned model completion owner and one grouped settings-owner registry; share repeated Email fixture data without removing test cases or assertions. The final focused cleanup is three files, +43/-72, net -29 lines.

## Scope

No backend production changes, dependency changes, configuration migration or increased debounce. Existing explicit creation/credential flows remain explicit. Application UI close waits for saving; browser/process shutdown cannot guarantee asynchronous persistence. Production config, sessions and shared services were not modified.

prs.title: fix(exec): yield long-running commands by default (NAN-328)
prs.body:
## Why

An `exec` call that omitted `yield_time_ms` waited for process exit, potentially keeping the agent blocked for the entire configured runtime. A command can already have printed an error while leaked browser resources keep its process alive. The agent needs to regain control to inspect output and decide what to do next.

Tracks [NAN-328](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-328), including the agreed design and acceptance criteria.

## What changed

- Default model-facing `exec` observation to 1000 ms. If the command is still running, return its session ID, current output and runtime facts; continue through `exec_session` without launching it again.
- Preserve implicit closed stdin, explicit interactive stdin, independent hard/inactivity budgets and cancellation ownership. Clarify that `exec_session(until_exit=true)` is still bounded by its observation timeout.
- Preserve completed results for trusted direct `!command` through an explicit internal completion method; update output-focused tests to request or observe completion rather than assume every default call has finished.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Agent calls exec] --> B[Start managed execution]
    B --> C[Observe for at most 1000 ms by default]
    C --> D{Execution finished?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Return output and exit status]
    D -->|No| F[Return running and session ID]
    F --> G[Agent regains control]
    G -->|Observe again| H[Bounded exec_session wait]
    H --> D
    G -->|Investigate| I[Inspect logs or process state]
    G -->|Stop| J[Terminate and reap execution tree]
```

## Scope

No new scheduler, automatic stall verdict, command replay, UI changes, completion push, production configuration changes or shared-runtime restart. The temporary browser script that exposed the issue is outside this product change.

## Tradeoffs

A long command can require another tool call to observe completion. This intentionally favors returning control over holding the agent inside a tool call. Trusted direct `!` commands have no agent observer, so their existing complete-result behavior remains explicit and separate.

## Blast Radius

The shared shell execution path also serves `rg`; its schema and default observation follow the same contract. Existing runtime limits, process-tree cleanup and tool activity projection are unchanged. Consumers must treat a running result as a handle to the existing execution, not a reason to rerun it.

## Verification

- Final CI run [39726483091](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39726483091) passed on head `0c46afda4`: Python 3.11, Linux Python 3.14 + coverage, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, Docker and the required CI gate. Other jobs were skipped by the existing path filters.
- Linux 3.11 and 3.14 each: **10693 passed, 78 skipped**, plus serial CLI **252 passed, 1 skipped**. Windows 3.14: **10395 passed, 135 skipped**, plus serial CLI **244 passed, 9 skipped**.
- CI strict full-project BasedPyright: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**. Ruff and import boundaries passed. The earlier local full-project attempt timed out; CI now supplies the complete result.
- Regression-first real-process default-observation tests failed on the old completion-only behavior and pass with the fix, including error output followed by a live process, implicit stdin EOF, later output and nonzero exit.
- Test-only follow-ups avoid waiting for markers already returned (focused cases 11.16/11.15 s → 1.32/1.31 s) and explicitly observe hard-timeout cleanup before asserting completion. A controlled 200 ms cleanup overlap reproduced all three locally executable CI failures before the latter fix; all three pass afterward. Relevant local suite: **276 passed, 5 skipped**. Hard runtime budgets and exit/cleanup assertions are unchanged.
- Earlier public black-box acceptance on `08d6b8498` covered four real DeepSeek CLI/tool scenarios and the trusted WebSocket shell path: **5 PASS**. Production code is identical across the later test-only CI repair.

The previous Windows goal-test failure was in its initial provider-start readiness wait, before the goal command was published. Its cause remains unconfirmed; goal code, timeouts and retry policy were left unchanged. The final Windows CI run passed it.

Local tests used the installed real ripgrep binary first on the test process PATH. An unchanged executable-copy test fails with the default Scoop shim because its adjacent metadata is missing; the same failure was reproduced on the exact base. No product configuration, assertion or skip was changed for that environment issue.

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping executions of the same job
prs.body:
## Problem

`CronService.run_job()` can enter the callback for a job that is already suspended in another manual run or in the scheduler. The WebUI's Run action creates a new `run_job()` task on each request, and a manual run can also overlap a due timer. Both invocations execute the agent callback and append a successful run record. This can duplicate model/tool work for one automation.

This was found by source inspection and reproduced offline on `main` at `fbb61a373f47769734a0d47d8f61935ffca84b84`; it is not a claimed production incident.

## Change

- Claim the job ID before awaiting its callback, shared by manual and timer entry points; release it in `finally`, including cancellation.
- Return `False` from an overlapping manual run, including `force=True`. Other jobs remain concurrent, and a later intentional run of the same job still works.
- Add event-coordinated regressions for manual/manual, timer/manual, manual/timer, cancellation, and persisted run history.

The guard is local to one `CronService` instance. It does not provide distributed locking or crash-safe exactly-once execution. Related #3245 proposes a persisted cross-instance claim; this patch does not implement that. Historical #961 was closed by its author in February; the current manual-run paths still reproduce the problem.

## Verification

- New regression file against unchanged main: **3 failed, 1 passed**. All three overlapping cases execute the callback twice; the cancellation control already passes.
- `python -m pytest tests/cron -q`: **181 passed** after the fix.
- `ruff check nanobot/cron/service.py tests/cron/test_cron_single_flight.py`: passed.
- `basedpyright nanobot/cron/service.py`: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed (13 rules, 216 files).
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.

Tests ran on Windows with Python 3.12.14 and workspace-local temporary directories. The restricted sandbox initially blocked Windows asyncio's local socketpair during event-loop creation; rerunning the offline checks with local socket access allowed produced the results above. No real model/provider requests, channel delivery, full-repository suite, or browser end-to-end run were performed.

## AI assistance and review status

Codex inspected the source and related contributions, wrote and ran the before/after tests, implemented the fix, and reviewed the complete diff under LJK-ikun's direction. This PR is ready for maintainer review. The validation above is automated local validation; independent human testing or approval is not asserted.

issues.title: Turn-end verification nudges are gated on file edits (`_edited`) — an answer that states unverified numbers can still finish unchallenged

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

issues.body:
Hermes already has the right shape for "verify before you finish" (`agent/verification_stop.py` verify-on-stop #65919, and the `pre_verify` plugin hook), but both are gated on the same condition (v0.21.1):

```python
# agent/turn_stop_gates.py:52-76
_edited = sorted(getattr(agent, "_turn_file_mutation_paths", set()) or [])
if _edited and has_hook("pre_verify") and attempt < max_verify_nudges():
```

So the mechanism is unreachable for a turn that **did not edit files** — the common case in practice: the assistant states numbers/versions/paths without looking anything up, and nothing before finalization asks it to check. Plugins cannot compensate from the output side either: `transform_llm_output` (`agent/turn_finalizer.py:400-420`, contract at `hermes_cli/plugins.py:109`) receives only `response_text`/`session_id`/`model`/`platform` — no tool-call history for the turn.

**Measured on my machine** (618 turns / 3 days): 78% of final answers contain "hard facts". Judging them by "was any verification-ish tool called in the last 30 min?" fails both ways — wide whitelist: 2 hits/3 days (dead); narrow whitelist: 208 hits (≈60/day), 71% ordinary discussion turns, including turns that *did* verify via `terminal`. Root cause: tool usage has no reliable mapping to "that specific claim was looked up".

External: pre-answer verification is the shape with measured effect (Chain-of-Verification: Wikidata precision 0.17→0.36, F1 +23%); passive after-the-fact warnings are ignored (clinical alert override 93%, "Alert fatigue does not seem to contribute" — low specificity is the driver).

**Proposal (default-preserving):** allow a `pre_verify` hook to request a verification continuation for turns without file edits, e.g. `if has_hook("pre_verify") and attempt < max_verify_nudges() and (_edited or hook_requests_continue(...))`. With no hook registered, behavior is byte-identical; `max_verify_nudges` already bounds the loop; synthetic nudge rows are already handled (`_pre_verify_synthetic`). Optionally, include a compact summary of the turn's tool activity in the `transform_llm_output` kwargs so an output-side plugin does not need a parallel ledger to know what happened.

(Full write-up with additional evidence was prepared locally; happy to paste any section.)
