prs.title: feat(memory): let MEMORY.md anchor a chain of documents
prs.body:
Refs #116564.

## What this does

Lets `MEMORY.md` anchor a chain of documents, in the smallest slice that is actually usable end to end.

**Gap confirmed on `main` first**: `tools/memory_tool_store.py:191 _path_for` maps only `memory|user` → `memories/MEMORY.md|USER.md`, `:202` applies one scalar `_char_limit` to the whole file, `tools/memory_tool.py:293` has no `read` action, and `git grep -ni 'chain_doc|memory_docs|doc chain'` returns nothing — the feature does not exist under another name.

**Precedent reused, no new subsystem**: the existing target abstraction (`_path_for` / `_entries_for` / `_set_entries` / `_char_limit` / `_render_block`) gains a third named store, and store-level support is reachable as `"doc:<name>"`. Addressing stays schema-safe (`tests/tools/test_memory_tool_schema.py` enforces the `target` enum): a chain doc is addressed with an **additive `doc` parameter** (`target="memory"`, `doc="conventions-2026-09"`) rather than by widening the enum, so strict-provider schema validation is untouched.

**Behaviour**: `memories/docs/<name>.md`, bare filename only (no separators, so a name cannot escape the directory); `@doc:<name>` inside any MEMORY.md entry is the anchor reference; writes are refused until the anchor references the doc, with an error that names the fix; `action="read"` returns entries, plus the anchor's `chain_docs` with sizes; the character cap applies to the **anchor only** (`_char_limit` → `None` for docs), and the anchor block gains exactly one line naming its chain docs — contents stay out of the prompt.

3 files, +263/−15: `tools/memory_tool.py`, `tools/memory_tool_store.py`, and a new 98-line test module.

## Evidence (red/green)

Committed first, mutated after, reverted with `git checkout --` (no stash); reproduced by the author and independently by the reviewer:

- mutation: chain resolution off (`MemoryStore._doc` → `return None`) → **4 failed / 6 passed**, e.g. `assert result["success"] is False` → `assert True is False` (`test_unreferenced_chain_doc_write_is_refused`), `At index 0 diff: 'Dated memory chain: @doc:conventions-2026-09' != 'First note'` (`test_read_returns_doc_entries_and_anchor_chain_list`), and `assert 'secret detail' not in '═══…secret detail'` (doc contents must not leak into the prompt)
- restored → new module **10 passed**; with neighbours, 9 files → **123 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped**

Baseline: the same 8 neighbouring files on clean `main` → **113 passed / the same 2 failed / 1 skipped** — the two are pre-existing Windows chmod semantics (`test_memory_tool.py::TestMemoryFileLockPermissions::*`, `assert 438 == 384`), and the +10 is this PR's new tests. Also smoke-verified through the real registry handler and the staged-approval replay (`apply_memory_pending` on a `doc:` payload). `ruff check` clean on all three files.

## Not done (deliberately outside this slice)

- The desktop/web memory view (`hermes_cli/web_routers/ops.py:431,482`) still lists only MEMORY.md / USER.md, so chain docs are not visible there.
- `/memory reset` (`hermes_cli/subcommands/memory.py`) and profile clone (`hermes_cli/profiles.py:36`) do not cover `memories/docs`.
- No reviewer-prompt change (the reviewer can now use the tool, but nothing nudges it toward chain appends) and no website docs update.

## Uncertainties

- `doc=` vs `target="doc:<name>"`: the store already accepts the latter, but the `target` enum is schema-enforced and widening it would drop a strict-provider guard — happy to switch if maintainers prefer target addressing.
- The anchor-reference gate is my reading of "let the anchor reference them". It is one branch (`_anchor_gate`) and trivially removable if it is stricter than intended.

prs.title: feat(gateway): answer vault prompts on messaging surfaces
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the vault prompts (master-password unlock, save-login, one-time code) answerable from a messaging surface.

The gateway wires `agent.clarify_callback` but never registered the three vault prompt callbacks — only `tui_gateway` and `hermes_cli` do that. On top of that, `can_prompt_here()` only asked whether the *unlock* callback existed. So every vault tool called from Telegram/Discord/etc. returned `prompt_unavailable`, and the only way to save or fill a login was to open a remote desktop and type it there.

This reuses the clarify primitive the gateway already has rather than adding a second transport: the reply is intercepted on the inbound path and handed straight to the caller, so a secret never becomes a conversation message, a memory, or part of the next request.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/vault_prompts.py` (new) — builds the unlock / save_login / code callbacks over a single blocking `ask`. `save_login` asks the identifier and then the password; both cards are numbered `(1/2)` / `(2/2)`, and only the final one holds the stream re-arm, matching `_clarify_batch_sync`.
- `agent/vault_backends/unlock.py` — adds `any_prompt_callback_registered()`; `can_prompt_here()` now answers for any vault prompt instead of only unlock.
- `tools/clarify_gateway.py` — `secret` flag on a clarify entry.
- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` — `_vault_ask_sync` bridge, installed per turn next to `agent.clarify_callback` and cleared in the turn's `finally`. It logs both the dispatch and the outcome of each prompt, which is what separates "the card never posted" from "the user never answered" — without it the caller just sits in `wait_for_response` until the clarify timeout.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` — a secret answer is no longer echoed into the retired card's summary line, and the user's own message is deleted once the value has been read (best-effort; the value has already been consumed without entering history either way).
- `tests/gateway/test_vault_prompts.py` (new) — callback contract, prompt sequencing, and the rearm/blank-answer behaviour of the runner seam.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_vault_prompts.py tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py -q` → **64 passed**
2. `pytest tests/gateway/ -q -k "clarify or approval or inbound or vault"` → **438 passed, 4 skipped**
3. Live over a real Telegram gateway, against a live signup page with two password fields:
   - `browser_vault_save_login` dispatched card 1/2, the typed reply was intercepted, card 2/2 was dispatched, that reply was intercepted, and the password was typed into both password fields on the page (`len=20` each).
   - The adapter deleted the password message from the chat immediately after the value was consumed.

Reproducing the old behaviour: on `main`, calling `browser_vault_save_login` from the Telegram gateway returns `{"error_type": "prompt_unavailable"}` without ever sending a card, because no vault callback is registered for that surface.


prs.title: fix(slack): render mentions as rich_text elements in rich_blocks
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`rich_text` does not interpret mrkdwn, so a mention inside a rich_text block was emitted as a `text` element and Slack rendered the raw token. A reply written as `- It posts one message in <#C0C6N2RF5HS>.` displayed `<#C0C6N2RF5HS>` literally in `rich_blocks` mode.

`_inline_elements` now parses mention tokens into rich_text mention elements, the same way the existing `<url|label>` autolink path handles links:

- `<@U…>` / `<@U…|label>` -> `{"type": "user", "user_id": "U…"}`
- `<#C…>` / `<#C…|name>` -> `{"type": "channel", "channel_id": "C…"}`
- `<!here>` / `<!channel>` / `<!everyone>` -> `{"type": "broadcast", "range": "here"}`

Unmatched angle-bracket runs (`- a <b> c`) still fall through verbatim as text. Mentions are emitted without a `style` key, since Slack rejects styled `user`/`channel`/`broadcast` elements.

## Related Issue

Fixes #133315

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/slack/block_kit.py`: add `_SLACK_MENTION_RE` + `_mention_element()` and a `_walk_mentions()` stage between the Slack autolink and emphasis walkers, so sections, list items, quotes and table cells all route through it.
- `tests/gateway/test_slack_block_kit.py`: the old `test_slack_mentions_in_bullet_are_not_links` asserted the buggy output (token present as text); it now asserts the mention elements and that no literal token remains. New `TestSlackMentions` class covers the labelled forms, broadcast ranges, a quote, a table cell and a non-mention angle token.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_slack_block_kit.py -q` -> 22 passed.
2. Before/after on main vs this branch (standalone script, no installs):

```
$ PYTHONPATH=. python3 repro.py
before: elements: [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'It posts one message in <#C0C6N2RF5HS>.'}, ...]
        REPRO:BUG (exit 1)
after:  elements: [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'It posts one message in '},
                   {'type': 'channel', 'channel_id': 'C0C6N2RF5HS'}, {'type': 'text', 'text': '.'}, ...]
        exit 0
```

3. `scripts/check` -> 11 checks, ok; `tests/gateway/test_slack*.py` -> 276 passed, 1 skipped.

prs.title: Sessions can stop at a spend cap and resume on "continue" (usage_limits, salvage #90191)
prs.body:
A session can now carry a spend cap: once its estimated cost passes `usage_limits.session_cost_usd`, the agent stops before the next model call, says which limit stopped it, and picks up where it left off when you raise the limit and send "continue".

Salvages #90191 by @enzo-adami (token and wall-clock belts on the loop boundary, commit kept as-is with authorship) and adds the cost dimension plus the resume flow on top.

## Source: GitHub Copilot CLI AI-credit session limits

- Docs: [Setting an AI credit session limit in GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/set-session-limit), [Optimizing your AI usage § 5](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/optimize-ai-usage#5-set-ai-credit-session-limits)
- Their mechanism: `/limits set max-ai-credits N` (interactive) or `--max-ai-credits N` (with `-p`). It is a soft limit: a response already in flight finishes, then the session stops, and you raise the limit to continue from the stopping point.

| | Copilot CLI | Hermes before | Hermes with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend cap per session | yes (AI credits) | none | `usage_limits.session_cost_usd` (estimated USD, same estimate as `/usage`, finished subagents included) |
| Token / time caps | no | none (#90191 open) | `session_total_tokens`, `turn_total_tokens`, `turn_wall_clock_seconds` |
| Where it stops | before the next model call | n/a | before the next model call (loop boundary, no extra summary call) |
| Raise and continue | `/limits set` | n/a | `hermes config set usage_limits.session_cost_usd 10`, then "continue" (limits are re-read every turn) |
| Shown on | their CLI | n/a | every surface: the notice is the turn's reply (CLI, TUI, Desktop, gateway, cron, `-z`) |

Not ported: a `/limits` slash command. Config-driven limits already reach every surface; a session-only override command would need a CLI, TUI, Desktop and gateway handler each and can follow if wanted.

## Changes

- `agent/usage_limits.py`: `session_cost_usd` field (bool/inf/nan/text/negative disable the field instead of tripping at once); `current_usage_limits()` reads config.yaml at turn start (mtime-cached); the breach message names the key, the command to raise it, and "continue".
- `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`: the check also reads `session_estimated_cost_usd`; the message is handed to the finalizer instead of a CLI-only print.
- `agent/turn_finalizer.py`: the stop reply is that message. `partial=True`, `completed=False`; a verification-held answer still wins (#90191's contract).
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: `usage_limits` registered, so `hermes config set usage_limits.*` no longer warns "not a recognized config key". The `loop_caps` comment above it is one line shorter to keep the file at its line cap.
- `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`: new "Usage limits" section (soft-limit semantics, the resume flow, counters reset on `/new`, unpriced models never reach the cost limit).
- Tests: #90191's three files (25 cases) trimmed to `tests/agent/test_usage_limits.py`, three invariants: each limit trips at its ceiling and junk disables it; a session already over the cost limit ends the turn with 0 API calls through the real `run_conversation`; a pending verification answer survives a limit stop.

## Live verification

Real provider (OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.7-flash`), scratch `HERMES_HOME`, limit `0.000001` USD so the first priced call crosses it. Prompt: run `echo step-one`, then `echo step-two` as a separate tool call, then reply DONE. Numbers read back from the run's own `state.db`.

| Run | origin/main `bf0203a` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes -z` | `DONE`, 3 API calls, $0.0098 | `⏹️ Session cost limit reached (~$0.0035 of $0.000001) … send "continue"`, 1 API call, $0.0035 |
| `hermes chat` (tmux), turn 1 | n/a | ran `echo step-one`, then the stop notice |
| turn 2 "continue", limit unchanged | n/a | stop notice again, 0 API calls (cost unchanged at $0.008660) |
| `hermes config set usage_limits.session_cost_usd 1`, turn 3 "continue" | n/a | ran `echo step-two`, replied `DONE` |

Session transcript from that state.db: `user` → `tool step-one` → `assistant ⏹️ …` → `user continue` → `assistant ⏹️ …` → `user continue` → `tool step-two` → `assistant DONE`. Total billed across all probes: about $0.11.

A probe pitfall turned up on the way: `hermes -z` and `hermes chat` now start a `gateway run --idle-exit` for their HERMES_HOME and later invocations attach to it, so a main-then-head A/B in one scratch home runs main's code twice. Each leg above killed its own spawned gateway (by PID) before the next one ran.

Local: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_usage_limits.py tests/agent/test_turn_iteration_prep.py tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_*.py tests/agent/test_conversation_loop*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_config*.py` green; `scripts/check --only health` 0 blocking.

Supersedes #90191 (salvaged here with authorship; close it with credit once this lands).

## Infographic

![Session cost limit](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf7b7c/bOGHJnpJF2FBwTLpKd0aD_ONu7bOTy.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): let browser_vault ask for codes and logins in Desktop chats
prs.body:
## Summary

`browser_vault` can now ask the user for a sign-in code, a login to save or a password-manager unlock in Desktop chats. Before, it answered `prompt_unavailable` ("this session cannot ask the user") in every Desktop chat.

Desktop chats run on the session authority (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py`), which installs the sudo and skill-secret prompts for a local viewer's turn (`session_sudo_prompt.py`, `session_secret_prompt.py`) but never the three vault callbacks the TUI sidecar registered in `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py`. With no callback on the agent thread, `can_prompt_here()` was false, so an emailed code (Epic Games, in the report) could not be entered at all. The owner now sends the sidecar's `vault.unlock_prompt`, `vault.save_login` and `vault.code` requests to the attached viewers through `session_server_requests.ask_viewer`, the same path sudo and secret use. The Desktop (`server-requests.ts`, `prompt-overlays.tsx`) and Ink renderers already handle these frames, so nothing changes on the client. Values travel only in the viewer's response frame and are never published, journaled or logged.

## Changes

- `gateway/session_vault_prompt.py` (new): `vault_prompt_scope` installs the three callbacks and the unlock owner (`set_current_session_id`) for a local viewer's turn and restores the previous ones after; tool workers inherit them through `propagate_context_to_thread`. `release_unlocks` locks the password managers a session unlocked.
- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`: enter the scope beside the sudo and secret scopes.
- `gateway/session_viewer_close.py`: release the session's unlocks when its last viewer closes it, as the sidecar's session end does (`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py` `_lock_vault_managers`). Without this, a manager unlocked from a Desktop chat would stay unlocked until its 30-minute idle timeout.
- `gateway/session_mutations.py`: `retire_live_sessions` (delete, the owner-run prune, onboarding cleanup) releases each retired session's unlocks too. Those paths pop the live session, so the viewer-close settle never runs for them. The hook follows #141260 by @levinkin, credited as co-author.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: the classic CLI viewer answers `vault.*` requests through the panels HermesCLI registers for the turn, instead of ignoring them and leaving the agent to wait out the timeout.

Not in this PR: the Desktop draws these prompts as dialogs rather than inline chat cards; that is the existing renderer design and unchanged here.

## Validation

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop chat, Epic sign-in, `browser_vault enter_code` (live, Windows) | `prompt_unavailable` | code card opened, code reached the page, signed in |
| `tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_vault_prompt.py` (15 new) | — | 15 passed |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_agent.py` (new cases) | — | 63 passed |
| viewer-close, delete, delegation-end and route-recovery suites (6 files) | pass | 95 passed |
| `tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py` | 48 passed, 2 failed | 48 passed, 2 failed |
| `scripts/check --base origin/main` | | 12 checks ok |

The new end-to-end test drives `browser_vault_enter_code` against a fake page: without the scope it returns `prompt_unavailable`; with it the code card is requested, the typed code is filled into the page, and it appears in neither the tool result nor the event stream.

The two `test_browser_vault.py` failures (`TestVaultStore::test_file_permissions_0600`, `TestVaultHardening::test_vault_dir_is_owner_only`) are POSIX file-mode checks that fail the same way on main on Windows.

Deleting a chat now locks what it unlocked: `test_deleting_a_chat_locks_the_managers_it_unlocked` unlocks a manager inside the scope, calls the real `retire_live_sessions` and checks the manager is locked while another chat's stays unlocked (red on `80d92daceba`).

## Infographic

![vault-prompts-desktop-chats](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf7b4c/FVKLs5OOQ8LYYRtLz9E88_AZ9EGT8J.png)

prs.title: fix(cli): warn when provider config entries shadow a built-in provider
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes a silent config trap loud. `providers.<id>` / `custom_providers` entries named after a canonical built-in provider are deliberately ignored when referenced by raw name (`_select_named_custom_provider` — the shared resolver behind `_get_named_custom_provider` and `named_custom_provider_config_path` — defers to the built-in so user config can't hijack it). That behaviour is today neither announced nor tested: the pin that used to cover it, `test_named_custom_provider_does_not_shadow_builtin_provider`, was removed in the upstream test-prune wave. The ignore is also completely silent: in #43026 a `providers.gemini` entry pointing at the OpenAI-compatible endpoint was dropped, requests went to the **native** Gemini API with env-var credentials instead, and the user saw a baffling `Gemini HTTP 400 (INVALID_ARGUMENT): API key not valid` even though the same key + endpoint worked via curl.

This PR keeps the shadowing semantics exactly as designed and adds diagnostics in the two places that can catch it:

1. **Resolve time** — `_select_named_custom_provider` (used by `_get_named_custom_provider` and `named_custom_provider_config_path`) logs a warning (once per provider per process) when the built-in guard drops a user-defined entry, with rename / env-var guidance.
2. **Config validation** — `validate_config_structure` flags shadowed entries, so `hermes doctor`, the model-switch flow, and auth flows all surface it. Only entries the config actually routes to by raw name (`model.provider` / `fallback_model` providers) are flagged — entries selected via an explicit `custom:<name>` menu key are still honored by the runtime and stay unflagged. Per-provider timeout tuning under a built-in id (the documented `providers:` schema in `cli-config.yaml.example`) is not routing config and is never flagged.

**Known scope limit:** the validation check harvests raw-name references from `model.provider` and `fallback_model` only; other routing surfaces (e.g. `model_aliases`, auxiliary model chains) aren't scanned there. Those cases are still covered by the resolve-time warning — they degrade from "silent" to "loud at first request" rather than "flagged by doctor", which is the intended split for a focused diagnostics fix.

## Related Issue

Fixes #43026

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/config_provider_shadow.py` (new sibling) — `find_shadowed_builtin_provider_entries()` (shared by both call sites; skips timeout-only entries via a routing-fields check) + `validate_shadowed_builtin_providers()`, the referenced-only shadow check. `hermes_cli/config.py` only late-imports it from `validate_config_structure` (net +0 lines, for the code-health FILE_LINES ratchet)
- `hermes_cli/runtime_provider_custom.py` — `_warn_once_if_user_entry_shadowed()` called from the `True` path of the built-in guard `_shadowed_by_builtin` inside `_select_named_custom_provider`, the single choke point shared by `_get_named_custom_provider` and `named_custom_provider_config_path`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_validation.py` — new `TestShadowedBuiltinProviderEntries` (6 cases: the exact #43026 scenario, timeout-only entry, non-built-in name, custom_providers shadow, picker-selected `custom:<name>` entry not flagged, alias name like `kimi` not flagged per #15743) + `TestShadowCheckDoesNotReenterProviderResolution`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_shadow.py` (new) — warn-once test + no-entry-no-warning test

## How to Test

1. Put the #43026 config in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`: `providers.gemini` with `base_url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` + an `api_key`, and `model.provider: gemini`.
2. Run `hermes doctor` → the config section now shows the shadow warning with rename/`hermes auth add gemini` guidance (previously: nothing).
3. Run any chat command → the log shows one `runtime_provider` warning explaining the entry is ignored (previously: silent, then `Gemini HTTP 400` from the native API).
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_config_validation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_shadow.py tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py` → all pass.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (targeted: `test_config_validation.py`, `test_runtime_provider_shadow.py`, `test_runtime_provider_resolution.py` + related config tests — targeted 22 passed; related runtime-provider/config tests 536 passed (50 files); every test file touching the changed resolvers/validator 1132 passed with 1 failure (`test_delegate.py::test_child_dedicated_db_follows_parents_db_path`) that fails identically on clean `main`; `python scripts/check` 12 checks ok (code health 0 blocking); plus `pytest tests/hermes_cli/ -k "config or provider or auth"`, which shows the same failure set as clean `main` and +10 passing new tests)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (Darwin 25)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — docstrings on the new helper; no user-facing docs describe the shadowing behavior to update
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no new keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure-Python logic, no platform APIs; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean on the 5 changed files (run as part of `scripts/check`)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

With the exact config from #43026:

```
--- hermes doctor (validate_config_structure) ---
[warning] providers/custom_providers entry 'gemini' shadows the built-in 'gemini' provider — its base_url/api_key are ignored and the built-in's default endpoint + environment credentials are used instead
  hint: Rename the entry to a non-built-in name (e.g. 'gemini-custom') and set model.provider to that name, or configure the built-in provider through its environment variables / 'hermes auth add gemini' and remove the entry

--- runtime resolution (once per provider per process) ---
WARNING hermes_cli.runtime_provider: config.yaml defines a providers/custom_providers entry named 'gemini', but 'gemini' is a built-in provider — the entry's base_url/api_key are ignored and the built-in's default endpoint + environment credentials are used instead. Rename the entry to a non-built-in name (and set model.provider to it), or configure the built-in via its env vars. Run 'hermes doctor' for details.
```

prs.title: feat(agent): opt-in wall-clock and token usage limits per turn/session
prs.body:
IterationBudget bounds how many loop passes a turn may take, but nothing bounds elapsed TIME (slow local generations make 90 iterations an hours-long turn) or TOKENS (a runaway cloud session silently burns prepaid balance). Both matter for unattended 24/7 agents.

Adds pure module agent/usage_limits.py + one check at the loop boundary next to the iteration-budget gate, exiting the turn budget_exhausted-style. Token accounting taps the existing monotonic session_total_tokens aggregate, so limits inherit its retry-surviving property; failed attempts that never reported usage are covered by the wall-clock ceiling. Everything defaults to disabled; config.yaml opts in via usage_limits: {turn_wall_clock_seconds, turn_total_tokens, session_total_tokens}. Inspired by pydantic-ai's UsageLimits, with the wall-clock dimension it lacks. 9 new tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Rebased (2026-10-15)

Re-applied onto `main` at `046094df28` as the PR's net change (the branch was ~4,200 commits behind and conflicting). The only conflict was two adjacent imports in `agent/conversation_loop.py` (`turn_scripted_prelude`, new on `main`, and `usage_limits`); both are kept. No equivalent exists upstream: nothing named `usage_limits`, `turn_wall_clock` or `turn_total_tokens` under `agent/` or in the config defaults, and no competing PR found.

8 files, +368 / -1. Still disabled by default; `config.yaml` opts in via `usage_limits: {turn_wall_clock_seconds, turn_total_tokens, session_total_tokens}`. The test count is now 25 (`test_usage_limits.py`, `test_usage_limits_integration.py`, `test_usage_limits_review_contracts.py`), up from 9.

Measured on macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.14, and re-run independently by a second reviewer:

- `tests/agent/test_usage_limits*.py`: 25 passed on this branch (the module does not exist on `main`)
- non-regression around the turn loop (`tests/agent/test_turn_*`, `test_conversation_loop*`, `test_meta_agent_init`): 29 files, 226 passed on `main` / 226 passed on this branch; the second reviewer's own 26-file selection, 213 / 213

prs.title: fix(update): refresh the release tag the checkout already sits on
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes update` fetches with `--no-tags`, so a checkout whose `HEAD` already contains the release can still be missing the release tag. `version_info()` derives the displayed version from the local tags (`git tag --merged HEAD`), so it reports the previous release — `0.22.2+3030.g4d04303` instead of `0.22.4`.

The post-build refresh (`_run_post_update_maintenance`) already tries to fix this, but it calls `fetch_full_commit_graph`, which fetches `refs/tags/v*:refs/tags/v*` — every published tag — under a **30 s** bound (`_TAG_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). On a slow link that fetch times out and the naming tag stays missing:

```
⚠ Could not refresh release history (... 'refs/tags/v*:refs/tags/v*' timed out after 30 seconds)
```

Fixes #143361

## Fix

- `SourceTarget` carries the published release tag (`tag`); `_resolve_stable` sets it.
- `select_apply_target()` records it on the update request as `release_tag`.
- `_run_post_update_maintenance()` forwards it to `fetch_full_commit_graph(...)`, which now takes an optional `release_tag`. When present it fetches that **one ref** (`refs/tags/vX.Y.Z:refs/tags/vX.Y.Z`) instead of the wildcard. Without it (canary, branch targets) the wildcard path is unchanged.
- The unshallow / partial-clone handling in `fetch_full_commit_graph` is untouched, and the existing 30 s bound now fits one ref easily. Failures keep the existing `⚠` line and never fail an update that already moved the tree.

Earlier revisions of this branch added a separate fetch in the apply path; that was redundant with this refresh and doubled the wait, so it has been removed.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_release_tag_refresh.py` (5 tests):

- the forward-only target records `release_tag`;
- a target without a published tag does not invent one;
- a known release tag pins one refspec instead of `refs/tags/v*`;
- no release tag keeps the wildcard (previous behaviour);
- against a real git repo, a `--no-tags` clone already on the release commit reports `unknown` before the refresh; afterwards **exactly one** fetch ran (`refs/tags/v0.21.6:refs/tags/v0.21.6`) and `version_info()` reports `0.21.6`.

Red/green verified: forcing the wildcard back fails the third test.

Verified against real git as well: a `--no-tags` clone has no tag; `git fetch --no-tags origin refs/tags/v1.0.0:refs/tags/v1.0.0` restores it and it points at `HEAD`.

```
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_release_tag_refresh.py tests/hermes_cli/test_tag_fetch_partial_clone.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_update_version_report.py tests/hermes_cli/test_version_info.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_update_stage.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt_scope.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_source_completion_stamp.py -q
```

48 passed. `test_update_post_commit_followups.py` fails locally at import (`hermes_bootstrap` reads the real `~/.hermes/manifest.json`, blocked by the suite's `home_io_guard`), unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(providers): keep Token Plan Team editions in the Qwen picker group
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Qwen picker group lists the two Personal Alibaba Token Plan slugs, so those fold into the `Qwen ▸` row. The Team editions (`alibaba-token-plan-team`, `alibaba-token-plan-cn-team`) are registered by the standalone Token Plan provider plugin and were never added to the group, so with the plugin installed the picker splits one product family: Personal under `Qwen ▸`, the two Team editions as ungrouped top-level rows.

This adds the two Team slugs to the `qwen` member list so all four editions fold into the same row.

It costs nothing when the plugin is not installed: `group_providers()` restricts a group's members to the slugs actually present in the picker input, so the extra names are inert until a registration exists. One edge to name honestly: the reverse index `_SLUG_TO_GROUP` maps the Team slugs unconditionally, so a leftover `model.provider: alibaba-token-plan-team` on a box where the plugin has since been uninstalled now highlights the Qwen row as "currently active" with no Team option present, instead of showing nothing. That is the pre-existing behaviour of every grouped slug, flagged here only because these slugs come and go with a plugin. Grouping is display-only; `--provider` and `/model <provider>:<model>` addressing are untouched, and no model catalogue, credential, or base URL changes.

Fixes #101218

prs.title: fix(status): show live sessions when no concurrency cap is set
prs.body:
Closes #46303 (partially — the concurrent-session *awareness* half).

### What changed since this PR was opened

This PR originally added a `record_presence` flag so uncapped surfaces would write to the active-session registry at all. **#94595 has since made that unnecessary**: per-session exclusivity is now enforced unconditionally, and `try_acquire_active_session` records an entry for any session with a stored id, capped or not (`hermes_cli/active_sessions.py:529` is the only no-op branch: no stored id). Verified locally: empty `HERMES_HOME` + `config {}` + no flags → `runtime/active_sessions.json` gets the entry.

So I've dropped that half entirely. `record_presence` and all of its plumbing (`cli.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `tui_gateway/server.py`) are gone — those three files are now untouched by this PR. Credit to #94595; this PR is now strictly the residue it left behind.

### What's left

**1. `hermes status` still gates its readout on the cap.** `status.py` wrapped the whole active-session block in `if _cap:`. That was right when the registry was only written under a cap. Now the entries exist for everyone and only this readout is still asking about `max_concurrent_sessions` — an operator who never set one sees nothing, while the data sits in `runtime/active_sessions.json`.

With a cap set, output is unchanged (`Slots: 1/2 in use`). Without one, there are no slots to report, so it prints `Live: 1 session(s)` plus the same per-session lines.

Note that since the `hermes status` rework (`a3149156ec`), the default command prints only the one-screen summary; the Sessions section — and so this `Slots:` / `Live:` readout — appears under `hermes status --full` (or `--deep`). The tests call `show_status` with `full=True` for that reason. Whether the summary should grow a one-line `Live:` count is a separate question I'm happy to follow up on if wanted.

**2. Entries carry no checkout attribution.** #46303 is about two sessions colliding in one git worktree; surface and session id don't say *where* a session is working, and nothing in `hermes_cli/` records it. `_lease_entry` now stores the enclosing checkout as `metadata["repo_root"]` — walked up by looking for `.git` rather than shelling out to `git` (this runs on every session start), testing `exists()` rather than `is_dir()` because `.git` is a *file* inside a linked worktree, which is exactly the two-worktrees-of-one-repo case the issue is about. Status lines then mark each entry `← this repo` or name the other checkout.

It's advisory throughout: a session started outside any checkout records no field at all (not a null one), and `transfer_active_session` carries existing attribution forward instead of dropping it when a caller rewrites identity metadata — that path replaces `metadata` wholesale, so without this the attribution silently vanishes the moment a draft session gets an id.

### Tests

- `test_show_status_lists_live_sessions_without_a_cap` — fails on `main` (verified by reverting `status.py` only), passes here.
- `test_show_status_still_reports_slots_when_a_cap_is_set` — the uncapped listing must not displace capped slot accounting.
- repo attribution across two checkouts, omission outside a checkout, survival across a session-id transfer.

`pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_active_sessions.py tests/hermes_cli/test_status.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_active_session_limit.py tests/hermes_cli/test_active_session_exclusivity.py tests/tui_gateway/test_cross_process_orphan_ownership.py tests/gateway/test_max_concurrent_sessions.py` → 64 passed (on the branch merged with current `main`). `scripts/check` passes.

### Not in scope

#46303's memory cross-bleed half, and advisory worktree locking. This is the "expose a lightweight *other live sessions* signal (count + what repo they're attached to)" item from the issue's suggested directions.

prs.title: fix(desktop): stop queued clarify locks after expiry
prs.body:
## Summary

Stop a Desktop typed-answer chain when the gateway reports that the clarify request has expired. A later queued answer is no longer sent to the same closed request.

## Issue

Fixes #137561

## Root cause

`lockTypedAnswer()` uses the previous lock's boolean result to decide whether the next answer may be sent. Transport failures returned `false`, but the explicit terminal reply `{ status: "expired" }` cleaned local settled state and then fell through to `return true`. The next promise therefore sent another `clarify.lock` RPC for a request the server had already rejected as expired.

## Changes made

- Return `false` immediately after handling an expired lock reply.
- Add a producer-level regression that queues two composer answers, expires the first lock, and asserts the second RPC is never sent.

## Verification

```text
npm exec --workspace apps/desktop -- vitest run src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx --project ui
# 49 passed

npm exec --workspace apps/desktop -- eslint src/store/clarify.ts src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx
# passed

npm run typecheck --workspace apps/desktop
# passed

git diff --no-index --check <main file> <updated file>
# passed for both touched files
```

## Before / after

Before the fix, the new regression failed with:

```text
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times
```

After the fix, the same focused file passes all 49 tests and the request mock is called once.

## Risk and scope

Low and localized. The change affects only the terminal `expired` result in Desktop's composer-entered clarify lock chain. Successful locks, exceptions, card Confirm, setup cards, and gateway/server behavior are unchanged.

## Not tested

- No packaged Desktop build or live gateway session.
- No full repository test suite or `python scripts/check`; the focused UI test, touched-file lint, and complete Desktop typecheck were run.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep hidden tabs awake in Chrome that Hermes launches
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With several named `browser_exec` sessions on one shared headed Chrome, each session works on a tab that is not the window's selected tab. Chrome judges "in use" by visibility and input, not CDP traffic, so it throttles those tabs' timers, freezes their renderers and, with Memory Saver on, discards them: `Page.captureScreenshot` / `Runtime.evaluate` time out and the daemon re-attaches to a blank tab. The reporter verified that relaunching Chrome with the three standard anti-backgrounding flags (the ones Puppeteer and Playwright pass by default) plus Memory Saver off makes hidden tabs answer at normal speed.

This passes those flags on every Chrome launch path Hermes owns for this use and documents them for user-started Chrome.

## Related Issue

Fixes #135435

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `hermes_cli/browser_connect.py`: new `CHROME_ANTI_BACKGROUNDING_ARGS` (`--disable-background-timer-throttling`, `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`, `--disable-renderer-backgrounding`), appended in `_chrome_debug_args()` (the Chrome `/browser connect` launches, and the manual command it prints) and in the macOS `open -a` fallback command.

- `website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md`: under "Concurrent sessions", note that on a shared headed Chrome named sessions are tab-isolated, not window-isolated, and that a user-started Chrome needs these flags and Memory Saver off. Memory Saver has no reliable command-line switch, so it is documented rather than forced.

prs.title: fix(cron): resolve .sh job scripts through Git Bash, not the WSL stub
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the remaining bare `shutil.which("bash")` lookup on the cron script path.

A cron job whose `script:` is a `.sh`/`.bash` file was launched with a bare `shutil.which("bash")`. On a Windows host whose native PATH carries only `Git\cmd` — which ships `git.exe` and no `bash.exe`, because Git's bash lives in `Git\bin` / `Git\usr\bin` that only a Git-Bash/MSYS parent adds — that lookup resolves to `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`, the **WSL stub launcher**. The stub runs bash inside WSL's *default* distro, so a host whose default is a minimal one (`docker-desktop`) dies with:

```
<3>WSL (11 - Relay) ERROR: CreateProcessCommon:640: execvpe(/bin/bash) failed: No such file or directory
```

…even though Git Bash is installed and healthy. The failure is delivered as the job result, so it reads like a delivery bug. Git Bash is never consulted, although `HERMES_GIT_BASH_PATH` may already point at it.

This is the same root cause `gateway/platforms/webhook_filters.py:184` fixed for #116818: `tools/environments/local.py::_find_bash()` is the canonical resolver — it skips the known `System32`/`WindowsApps` stubs and probes that the candidate actually starts.

## Related Issue

Fixes #120504

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/scheduler_script.py` — new `_resolve_script_bash()`: on `win32` it late-imports and calls `tools.environments.local._find_bash()` (late import keeps cron import-light, as in `agent/shell_hooks.py`, `agent/skill_preprocessing.py`, `hermes_constants.py`); its `RuntimeError` is converted into the module's existing `(argv, env_overlay, error)` contract instead of raising into the ticker. POSIX keeps the previous `which` / `/bin/bash` expression unchanged.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_script.py` — two `windows_only` regression tests (see below).
- `tests/fixtures/resolution_allowlist.json` — the bare-`which` row follows the call to its new home (`_script_argv` → `_resolve_script_bash`), so `test_resolution_allowlist_has_no_stale_rows` stays green.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce on unpatched code (from a shell that is NOT a child of Git Bash — Task Scheduler, a service, or a native launcher):
   ```
   mkdir -p ~/.hermes/scripts
   printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho hello from cron\n' > ~/.hermes/scripts/repro.sh
   hermes cron create 1m --name repro-bash --script repro.sh --no-agent --deliver origin
   ```
   The job lands in `last_status: error` with the `execvpe(/bin/bash) failed` stderr above.
2. Same resolution, before/after, on the reporting host (native PATH from the registry, no `Git\usr\bin`):
   ```
   shutil.which("bash")  -> C:\Windows\system32\bash.EXE     (rc=1, WSL error)
   _find_bash()          -> C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe (rc=0)
   ```
   With the patch, `cron.scheduler_script._script_argv()` returns the Git Bash path on that same PATH.
3. Tests: the two new cases are red on base (both fail: the stub path is returned / no error reported) and green with the patch. The first pins that a `.sh` script never comes back as `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`; the second that a host without usable Git Bash gets the actionable message instead of a traceback in the ticker.

prs.title: fix(discord): suppress link-preview embeds and keep it across streaming edits
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Discord expands URLs in bot messages into link-preview embed cards. Streamed answers that cite links — documentation lookups, search results, PR links — end up wrapped in unwanted preview cards, which is exactly the clutter the bot should avoid.

The dependable lever for hiding these cards is Discord's per-message `SUPPRESS_EMBEDS` flag, which has to be set at send time. The Discord adapter never set it, so there was no supported way to stop preview-card clutter.

This adds a `suppress_link_previews` config key (default **on**) and sets `suppress_embeds` on the adapter's outgoing conversational messages. Because the flag is applied at send time and the streaming edit path edits through `PartialMessage.edit(content=...)` — which sends no `flags` field — the suppression survives every mid-stream edit the bot makes while a reply streams in (Discord only regenerates the embed when an edit actively clears the flag). Operators who want previews can set `suppress_link_previews: false`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #91657

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`: read `extra.suppress_link_previews` (default `True`) into `self._suppress_link_previews` via a new `_coerce_suppress_link_previews` helper (accepts bool or string spellings); pass `suppress_embeds=self._suppress_link_previews` on the conversational send paths (main chunked send + reply-reference retry, and the overflow-split continuation sends + their retry). The streaming edit path stays a content-only `PartialMessage.edit`, with a comment noting it must stay that way so it never clears the flag.
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_suppress_link_previews.py` (new): regression tests for config defaulting on, explicit off, string coercion, the flag riding on `channel.send`, overflow continuations carrying the flag, and the streaming edit passing no `suppress`/`flags` kwarg that could clear suppression.

1. Leave Discord defaults (or set `discord.suppress_link_previews: true`). Have the bot stream a reply that contains a URL. The message arrives with no link-preview card, and the card does not appear as streaming continues to edit the message. Set `discord.suppress_link_previews: false` and repeat — the preview card is kept.

prs.title: feat(kanban): model-callable kanban_archive tool over the CLI archive path
prs.body:
feat(kanban): model-callable kanban_archive tool over the CLI archive path

## Why

Archiving a kanban card is CLI-only. `hermes kanban archive` routes through a proven single code path (`kanban_db.archive_task()`, including the #76196 worker-termination handling), but there is no model-callable equivalent: a profile restricted to the `kanban` toolset can create, comment, block, and complete cards from inside a session, yet cannot archive a finished card without a terminal. For deployments that deliberately run such profiles without terminal access, in-session board cleanup is impossible and completed cards pile up in the active list. This PR adds `kanban_archive(task_id, board?)` as a thin wrapper over the exact `archive_task()` the CLI uses — zero new DB logic, zero behavior divergence. The access model follows the open question in #143206: a lifecycle gate — visible to any profile holding the kanban toolset and to dispatcher workers, using the same registration pattern as `kanban_block`/`kanban_complete`; `kanban_list`/`kanban_unblock` stay orchestrator-only.

Linked issue: #143206, the anchor for the access-model decision. Intentionally not `Closes` — settling the access model is the maintainers' call, and this PR is one concrete answer on the table.

## What changes

Minimum footprint: 4 files, +319/−1, of which 277 lines are new tests. The implementation surface is 43 lines across three existing files, and the only touch to an existing line is the toolset registration in `toolsets.py`.

```
tests/tools/test_kanban_archive_tool.py | 277 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tools/kanban_tools.py                   |  24 ++
 tools/kanban_tools_schemas.py           |  17 ++
 toolsets.py                             |   2 +-
 4 files changed, 319 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

## No behavior change to existing paths

- No new DB write logic — the tool delegates to the same `archive_task()` the CLI calls, including worker termination on archiving a running task and child-promote/workspace-reap side effects.
- `_ORCHESTRATOR_TOOLS`, board resolution, and the CLI archive path are untouched. Board pinning reuses the shared `_board()` helper; unknown and already-archived ids report the sibling not-found/CAS error shape.
- The tool is deliberately not stricter than the CLI on running+claimed cards; CLI archive regression receipts are byte-identical main vs branch across 9 scenarios, including `--rm` purge and the both-args / no-args error paths.
- Profiles without the kanban toolset see zero `kanban_*` tools — config-gated, flip-verified before and after the change.

## Test plan and results

- New unit tests `tests/tools/test_kanban_archive_tool.py`: 15/15 pass on the rebased branch.
- Real behavior through the tool registry on throwaway scratch boards (no shared state): create→archive, re-archive CAS error, unknown-id error byte-identical to sibling tools, archiving blocked/todo/running+claimed cards, parent-archive freeing a child, unknown arguments refused before any write — 20/20.
- Guardrail parity: scoped worker refused on a running+claimed sibling; delegate child refused outright; authorized caller archives running+claimed exactly as the CLI does — 7/7.
- `scripts/check`: 12 checks ok; code health vs the merge base: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
- Full suite vs a main baseline on the same host: the set of failing files is identical to the baseline; the single branch-only failing file was proven flaky — 756/756 green in an isolated re-run on both bases.

prs.title: fix(discord): explain auto-thread rate limits
prs.body:
Summary

- Detect Discord HTTP 429 responses during automatic thread creation.
- Configure discord.py to surface REST cooldowns longer than 30 seconds instead of silently sleeping for minutes.
- Show an actionable parent-channel notice containing Discord’s retry delay.
- State explicitly that the original message was not processed and suggest using an existing thread.
- Skip futile seed-message fallback and short retry attempts while Discord’s rate-limit bucket is active.
- Remove a misleading fallback seed message if its thread creation is rate-limited.
- Preserve the existing generic failure notice for non-rate-limit errors.

Motivation

Discord can apply dynamic per-route limits to thread creation. The existing adapter could let discord.py sleep for the full cooldown, retry after 0.75 seconds once an error surfaced, emit misleading duplicate “Thread created by Hermes” seed messages, and finally ask the user to retry without saying when. This change does not queue or process the failed request.

Trade-off

`max_ratelimit_timeout` is a discord.py client-wide setting. Cooldowns longer than 30 seconds on any Discord REST endpoint will now fail fast rather than silently block the gateway; normal short send/global rate limits continue to wait and retry. In practice, thread creation is the endpoint observed returning multi-minute cooldowns. The adapter already contains delivery failures without crashing the gateway.

Test plan

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/gateway/test_discord_channel_controls.py tests/gateway/test_discord_connect.py tests/gateway/test_discord_slash_commands.py tests/gateway/test_discord_double_dispatch.py`
- 42 tests passed.
- `ruff check plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py tests/gateway/test_discord_channel_controls.py tests/gateway/test_discord_connect.py`
- Real discord.py 2.7.1 smoke check confirmed `RateLimited(286.02)` is detected and its retry delay is extracted.

prs.title: fix(discord): a bot's voice-channel speech follows the Discord bot policy
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A bot account speaking in a Discord voice channel ran as a person's turn.

The voice turn's source is either the `/voice join` copy, or a fresh source for a programmatic join. `_voice_input_source` resolves the speaker's `Member` for the display name but never copied `Member.bot`, so the source always had `is_bot=False`. Two things followed:

- **The Discord bot policy did not apply.** The same bot's typed messages are dropped under the default `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS=none`. Under `mentions` or `all` they need a literal inline @mention by default (`discord.bots_require_inline_mention`, see the `author.bot` branch of admission in `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`). Its speech skipped that branch: the voice listen loop checks every speaker against the user allowlist only.
- **The gateway's bot loop guard and inbound bot budget never counted it.** `_admit_bot_message` and the cooldown veto in `_is_user_authorized` return early for a non-bot source. Another agent with TTS in the same voice channel (another Hermes, say) could therefore trade turns with this one with no limit.

**The fix,** in `gateway/run_voice.py` only:
- `_voice_input_source` sets `is_bot` from the speaker's `Member` in both branches. A member-cache miss still reads as a person, as before.
- An utterance carries no @mention, so `_handle_voice_channel_input` hears bot speech only where a typed message from the same bot would need none: `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS=all` with `discord.bots_require_inline_mention: false`. Under the defaults, bot speech is ignored. Admitted bot speech reaches the gateway as a bot, so the `ALLOW_BOTS` grant and the loop guard apply as they do to typed bot messages.

People's speech is unchanged.

## Related Issue

Found while working on #143260, which adds `turn_origin` to the LLM-call hooks and documents that a bot reads `peer` only where the adapter flags bots. Related: #92496, where `SessionSource.to_dict()` drops `is_bot`. The `/voice join` copy goes through that round trip, which is one reason the bound branch never had the flag. #130302 was the same copy losing `role_authorized`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_voice.py`:
  - `_voice_input_source` sets `is_bot` from `Member.bot`, both on the bound join copy and in the programmatic `build_source` call.
  - `_handle_voice_channel_input` returns early for bot speech unless `adapter._get_allow_bots()` is `all` and `adapter._discord_bots_require_inline_mention()` is false.
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_voice_bot_speaker.py` (new). It runs a real `DiscordAdapter` and the real gateway authorization and bot loop guard, through bound and programmatic joins:
  - a bot speaker is ignored under `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS` unset, under `mentions`, and under `all` with the default inline-mention rule;
  - under `all` with the rule off, it is dispatched with `is_bot=True`;
  - a person, and a speaker missing from the member cache, are dispatched as before;
  - once the conversation's bot budget trips, the bot's speech is refused while a person's speech in the same chat still goes through.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/voice-mode.md`: one paragraph under Access Control.

## How to Test

Test interpreter: `python -m pm.build_env --source . --out <test-env> --group dev --group test`, then `HERMES_PYTHON=<test-env>/bin/python`.

1. **Red on base.** Run the new test with `gateway/run_voice.py` at base `3ba2b0787e`:
   ```bash
   HERMES_TEST_WORKERS=1 HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_discord_voice_bot_speaker.py
   ```
   Result: **10 failed, 4 passed**. Every bot-speaker case fails; the 4 passing are the person and cache-miss controls.
2. **Green on head**, same command. Result: **14 passed**.
3. **Touched modules.** Every test file that references the voice mixin, Discord voice, `voice_mode`, the bot loop guard or `ALLOW_BOTS`, plus all `tests/gateway/test_discord*` and `test_voice*` files (179 files). Result: **2625 passed, 14 failed, 56 skipped**. I re-ran the failing files with the source at base `3ba2b0787e`, and the failures are identical there, with one exception. `test_session_hygiene_turnhold_adoption.py` passed in that re-run, but it is flaky on base as well: 1 of 6 base runs failed it, timing out the same way. The other failures come from the local test env, which lacks `aiohttp`.
4. `python scripts/check --base 3ba2b0787e`: **12 checks OK**. `git diff --check` is clean.

Platform: macOS 27.0.1. No full-suite or remote CI result is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (none for voice bot speakers; #130302 is the related role-grant fix).
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix.
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. The full suite is deferred to CI; the focused runs above use the canonical runner.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes.
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27.0.1.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation: the voice-mode guide.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A, no config keys.

prs.body:
## Add `codex-theme` (desktop theme plugin) — v1.0.0

**Plugin:** https://github.com/ethanz-code/hermes-codex-theme @ `5a96907a63c1d83b801c0e754123f1bf2bc5b09f` (tag `v1.0.0`)

Reworked v1.0.0 submission replacing #143006 (closed with notes). The plugin repo history has been rebuilt as a clean 7-commit linear story so this first public version is `1.0.0` end to end — entry, manifest and runtime log string all agree, no re-pin chain to review.

A graphite-on-paper theme for the Hermes Desktop chat, after the design language of the OpenAI Codex app and ChatGPT: dual light/dark palettes that follow the system appearance, a 10px radius system, hairline borders instead of shadows, the 6/10/16/24 spacing rhythm, 1.7 root line height, and an 880px reading column with 768/880/992px presets.

### Surfaces used

Desktop plugin SDK only (`desktop/plugin.js`, `plugin.yaml` manifest):

- `THEMES_AREA` — one theme (`colors` + `darkColors` + `typography` + `customCSS`, the same theming surface user skins use)
- `PALETTE_AREA` — two quiet rows (reapply theme / open settings)
- `ctx.registerSettingsPage` — appearance mode (follow system / dark / light) + reading-column width (Narrow 768px / Standard 880px / Wide 992px)
- `ctx.i18n` — en + zh strings for the settings page

### Validation

`hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` at the pinned commit is green (real output):

```text
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.22.0' parses
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ requires_env — all entries UPPER_SNAKE
✓ oauth — not declared
✓ loadable — entry: desktop/plugin.js
✓ python dependencies — none declared
✓ capability probe — skipped (no __init__.py)
✓ built-in tool collisions — no tools to check
✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
⚠ no __init__.py — capability probe skipped (manifest-only plugin)
◆ Isolation — portable plugin (no Python): runs anywhere

Validation passed.
```

### Disclosure (rule 13)

- No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes.
- One plugin-scoped `ctx.storage` record for settings-page choices (appearance mode + reading-column width); a first-install flag in the same store is written once to decide whether the theme takes over on first load.
- `customCSS` is injected by the app's own theme engine from the theme object, like user skins — visual only, no behavior changes.
- No core patching: everything registers through the Desktop plugin SDK only (`THEMES_AREA`, `PALETTE_AREA`, `ctx.registerSettingsPage`, `ctx.i18n`).
- The theme deliberately does **not** write user-configurable settings (e.g. `--chat-text-scale` stays owned by Settings → Appearance) and applies itself only on first install, never overriding a later manual theme choice.

### Screenshots

`assets/cover.png` (2:1 banner) and `assets/theme-{light,dark}.png` (rendered specimens, referenced by `image:` / `screenshots:` at the pinned sha). The README renders from the pinned tree.

> Note on rule 15: this is a community-tier theme *inspired by* the Codex/ChatGPT design language, not a vendor-lookalike shipped under Nous branding — the README carries an explicit "independent community theme, not affiliated with OpenAI" note. Happy to rename if maintainers prefer a non-vendor name.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `kanban.auto_decompose_excluded_profiles` so contract-bound or specialist profiles can be kept out of generic Kanban decomposition. The prompt roster and accepted-assignee set share the same eligible profiles, while explicitly assigned cards continue to dispatch under the existing `dispatch_profiles` rules.

Configuration errors fail closed: decomposition leaves the root in Triage and records one durable `decompose_config_error` event per distinct reason. The option defaults to `[]`, preserving current behavior. The issue remains labeled `needs-decision`; this PR requests maintainer direction on the implementation.

## Related Issue

Fixes #83046

Related prior attempt: #91944 was closed by its author during open-queue triage and was not merged. This revision includes strict exclusion validation and deduplicated configuration-error events.

Adds `plugin-catalog/adkit.yaml`: AdKit, submitted by the owner of [adkit/ads-mcp](https://github.com/adkit/ads-mcp).

## What it does

Connects Hermes to the hosted AdKit MCP server (`mcp.adkit.so`) to manage ads on Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Reddit and X Ads: launch campaigns as drafts, pull performance reports, browse competitor ads in the Meta, Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, and generate ad creatives.

## Hermes surfaces used

- Agent Plugins v1 package in `hermes/` (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json`), configuration only. No Python, no Desktop code, no skills.
- One stdio MCP server: `npx -y mcp-remote@0.1.49 https://mcp.adkit.so`. Plugin `mcp.json` remote entries cannot set `auth: oauth`, so sign-in goes through pinned mcp-remote, like the adspirer and adwhispr entries.
- `extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.servers.adkit.trust: untrusted`.

## Risky behaviour (rule 13)

- **Changes real ad accounts.** Tools can create, edit and publish campaigns that spend the user's ad budget. Creates are drafts until the user approves publishing. The server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that is not `readOnlyHint: true` and refuses those in unattended runs.
- **Network calls.** Every tool call goes to `mcp.adkit.so`. `npx` downloads `mcp-remote@0.1.49` from the npm registry.
- **Stored credentials.** mcp-remote stores its OAuth tokens in `~/.mcp-auth`. Hermes never sees them.
- **No telemetry.** The package sends nothing by itself. `adkit_feedback` and `adkit_checkin` send data to AdKit only when the agent calls them.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

Requires Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm (mcp-remote depends on `undici@^7`).

prs.title: fix(slack): restart Socket Mode sessions Slack never registered
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Slack Socket Mode session can stay "connected" — websocket ping/pong answered by Slack's edge, `is_connected()` true — while Slack routes no events to it. The watchdog only checks the task, the transport and ping/pong, so such a session stays deaf until the process restarts.

We hit this in production during Slack's "Slack Real-Time Connection Disruption" incident ([slack-status.com](https://slack-status.com)) on 2026-10-22 (16:08–16:26 UTC, "a large number of active connections closed at once and then reconnected"). On a multiplexed gateway serving many Slack apps:

- apps whose sockets reconnected at 16:08–16:09 UTC (some through the SDK's own reconnect, some through the watchdog) answered pings for 7h49m, received **no** events, and never got Slack's periodic connection refresh;
- an app that reconnected at 16:19 received events normally, and Slack refreshed it at 21:19, about five hours later, in line with `hello.debug_info.approximate_connection_time` (18060 s);
- a gateway restart fixed every app at once.

The same symptom is reported in #135714, and below us in slackapi/python-slack-sdk#1940 (Slack's connection registry drifting from the sockets actually held; fixed server-side 2026-10-21) and slackapi/node-slack-sdk#2791 (same incident window).

Slack sends `hello` once it registers a session for event routing, and every event is a text frame. This PR tracks both per Socket Mode client through the SDK's `on_message_listeners` hook, which `receive_messages()` calls for every text frame:

- **Unregistered session → restart.** A session with no `hello` within 60 s of the watchdog first seeing it is restarted (`SLACK_SOCKET_HELLO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `0` disables). Sessions the SDK opens on its own (Slack refresh, CLOSE frame) are checked the same way.
- **Silent session → make-before-break renewal.** After 30 min without any Slack frame (`SLACK_SOCKET_SILENCE_RENEW_SECONDS`, `0` disables), a second session is opened, swapped in only once Slack registers it, and then the old one is closed, so renewing an idle-but-healthy socket never opens a delivery gap. If Slack does not register the new session, the current one is kept and renewal backs off for 5 min. Busy apps never renew: their events reset the clock.
- **Dead dispatch task → restart.** The SDK creates `message_processor` once per client and never restarts it. If it ends, frames (and pongs) keep arriving but nothing dispatches them.
- **Diagnostics.** `hello` is logged once per session (connection count, applink host, refresh interval). `disconnect` reasons are logged; `link_disabled` and `too_many_websockets` are warnings that name the fix. A `num_connections` above what this process holds warns that another process using the same app token is taking a share of the events. During a renewal, Slack counting only the new connection is logged as evidence that the replaced session was deaf.

Restart hygiene on the same path:

- One `is_connected() == False` sample no longer restarts; two in a row do. A single sample can land inside the SDK's own refresh, and restarting then only races it (same idea as #96478).
- `close_async()` is bounded (10 s), so a close hung on a dead network cannot strand the watchdog under the reconnect lock (#91630, #75855).
- A restart skips a handler that was already replaced while it waited for the lock (watchdog vs. task done-callback).

The Socket Mode lifecycle moves out of `adapter.py` into `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter_socket.py` (`SlackSocketModeMixin`), so `adapter.py` shrinks by about 200 lines instead of growing. The moved methods are unchanged except that the watchdog loop body becomes `_socket_watchdog_tick()`.

**How this differs from #135714.** That PR renews every socket every 10 minutes by tearing down before reconnecting (a short delivery gap per app every 10 min) and adds worker-death checks. This PR detects the unregistered session directly from `hello` (within about 75 s rather than up to 10 min), renews only silent sockets, and swaps make-before-break so a renewal never drops events. It keeps the dispatch-task check from #135714.

**Not in scope:** replaying messages sent to a deaf session (#44178, #76818). Slack does not deliver them to any connection, so they are lost; the troubleshooting docs now say to ask users to resend.

## Related Issue

No issue filed. Related: #135714 (same symptom), #25476 and #32574 (zombie connections), #111178 (Discord event-silence liveness), #96478, #91630, #75855.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter_socket.py` (new): `SlackSocketModeMixin` holds the moved teardown and watchdog code plus the `hello`/frame tracking, unregistered-session restart, make-before-break renewal, dispatch-task check, bounded close, two-sample transport check, restart generation check and the two env knobs.
- `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`: `SlackAdapter` mixes it in; `_new_socket_mode_handler()` attaches the frame hook; the socket lifecycle code is removed.
- `tests/gateway/test_slack_socket_app_liveness.py` (new): 20 tests with a fake clock, driving the watchdog one tick at a time.
- Docs (en and zh-Hans): the two env vars in `reference/environment-variables.md`, and a troubleshooting row in `user-guide/messaging/slack.md`.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_slack_socket_app_liveness.py tests/gateway/test_slack_socket_reconnect_heal.py` → 23 passed.
2. With the `messaging` extra (real slack-bolt 1.30.0 / slack-sdk 3.44.1): `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/e2e/core/platforms/test_slack_contract.py tests/gateway/test_slack*.py tests/gateway/test_platform_reconnect*.py tests/website/test_generate_llms_txt.py tests/gateway/test_config.py` → all passed (the e2e stand-in sends `hello`, as Slack does).
3. Reproduction with the real Bolt handler and SDK (script below). A local server implements `apps.connections.open` and a websocket that answers pings but never sends `hello`. With `SLACK_SOCKET_HELLO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2`, after 8 s:
   - `main`: one socket opened, `is_connected=True`, nothing logged; it stays deaf forever.
   - this branch: `Socket Mode unhealthy (no hello from Slack within 2s, session not registered); reconnecting` about every 2 s.

   When the server sends `hello` from the third socket on, the adapter settles on that socket. A forced renewal then opens socket #4, receives its `hello`, and closes #3; the number of open sockets never drops to 0.
4. `python scripts/check` → 12 checks ok (code health: 0 blocking).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (deaf socket)</summary>

```python
"""python repro.py <hermes-agent checkout> — the server answers pings but never sends hello."""
import asyncio, logging, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from aiohttp import web
from slack_bolt.async_app import AsyncApp
from slack_sdk.web.async_client import AsyncWebClient
import plugins.platforms.slack.adapter as slack_mod
from gateway.config import PlatformConfig

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)
opened = {"n": 0}

async def main():
    async def connections_open(request):
        opened["n"] += 1
        return web.json_response({"ok": True, "url": f"ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/ws"})

    async def ws_handler(request):
        ws = web.WebSocketResponse(autoping=True)  # pings answered; no hello, no events
        await ws.prepare(request)
        async for _ in ws:
            pass
        return ws

    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post("/api/apps.connections.open", connections_open)
    app.router.add_get("/ws", ws_handler)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    await site.start()
    port = site._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]

    adapter = slack_mod.SlackAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, token="xoxb-local"))
    adapter._app = AsyncApp(token="xoxb-local", client=AsyncWebClient(
        token="xoxb-local", base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/"))
    adapter._app_token, adapter._proxy_url, adapter._running = "xapp-local", None, True
    adapter._socket_watchdog_interval_s = 0.25
    adapter._start_socket_mode_handler()
    adapter._ensure_socket_watchdog()
    await asyncio.sleep(8)
    client = adapter._handler.client
    print(f"after 8s: sockets opened={opened['n']} is_connected={await client.is_connected()}")
    adapter._running = False
    await adapter._cancel_socket_watchdog("teardown")
    await adapter._stop_socket_mode_handler()
    await runner.cleanup()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```
$ SLACK_SOCKET_HELLO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2 python repro.py <main checkout>
after 8s: sockets opened=1 is_connected=True
$ SLACK_SOCKET_HELLO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2 python repro.py <this branch>
WARNING ...adapter_socket: [Slack] Socket Mode unhealthy (no hello from Slack within 2s, session not registered); reconnecting
WARNING ...adapter_socket: [Slack] Socket Mode unhealthy (no hello from Slack within 2s, session not registered); reconnecting
WARNING ...adapter_socket: [Slack] Socket Mode unhealthy (no hello from Slack within 2s, session not registered); reconnecting
after 8s: sockets opened=4 is_connected=True
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): persist @image: refs for unified-runtime inbound image turns
prs.body:
…on prose

Symptom: since the unified gateway runtime, image turns submitted from the Desktop app persist the vision-enrichment prose as the user row. The desktop renderer rebuilds attachment thumbnails from @image:<path> directive lines only, so after the turn is persisted (or on reload / restart) the user bubble shows the model-only description prose and the image is gone (#142500).

Root cause: _enrich_inbound_images replaces message_text with the enrichment prose before the turn runs, and _hmwa_apply_message_timestamp (building the durable user row) cleans that already-replaced text — the enrichment rides straight into the store. The tui_gateway submit path keeps the two forms apart (persist_user_message = caption + @image refs via _build_persist_message_with_image_refs); the unified inbound path lost that split.

Change: the split is restored where the enrichment happens. A text-mode image turn buffers (caption, image_paths) beside the existing native_image_paths buffer — same lifecycle: set in _enrich_inbound_images, cleared at the next inbound prepare, consumed one-shot at the persist seam. _hmwa_apply_message_timestamp consumes it and persists caption + @image:<path> directives (after the same timestamp/note cleaning the plain path applies); the queued follow-up path in run_turn.py goes through the same swap via _durable_turn_persist_text, keeping that file under its FILE_LINES ratchet. The enrichment keeps riding the model-facing text. Also fixes a latent missing import this exposed: tui_gateway/session_history.py used Path in two module-level builders without importing it — _build_persist_message_with_image_refs NameError'd in any process that called it directly, silently swallowed by the timestamp path's broad except.

Measurements: three new contract tests — an enriched turn persists caption + @image refs while the model text keeps the prose; a plain turn's persist is unchanged; a stale buffer is cleared by the next inbound prepare so a dead turn cannot leak its caption into the next turn's row. All three red on main (no buffer machinery). Six-file seam surface (the new tests, the discord-note contract, session-history canonical, local session recovery, two tui lease/heartbeat suites): 22 passed, 0 failed. python scripts/check --base upstream/main: 12 checks ok.

Restores the persist split the tui_gateway submit path always had: unified-runtime inbound
image turns now persist `<caption> + @image:<path>` refs (what the Desktop renders back as
thumbnails) instead of the vision-enrichment prose.

#142500, since their account is at the repo's open-PR ceiling. Root-cause analysis and the
regression window are documented in the issue.

prs.title: fix(discord): diff slash commands against the raw registry
prs.body:
## Problem

`_safe_sync_slash_commands` re-creates almost every global command on every gateway start. On a 64-command app this burns Discord's 200-creates/day budget within a few restarts. Every later sync then hits 429 with a long `retry_after`, and commands that were deleted mid-recreate stay missing (#104399).

## Root causes

1. **Lossy flag parsing in discord.py.** `ArrayFlags._from_value` assumes 1-based values, but `integration_types` and `contexts` are 0-based. `AppCommand` parses Discord's `[0, 1]` as `[0]` and `[0, 1, 2]` as `[0, 1]` (reproduced on discord.py 2.7.1, still present on `master`). Comparing against `tree.fetch_commands()` therefore never matches.
2. **Server-filled defaults read as diffs.** Hermes leaves `integration_types`/`contexts` unset. Discord fills in its defaults (`[0, 1]`). The canonical comparison sees `None != [0, 1]`, and since only those fields differ, the command is deleted and re-created. Discord fills the defaults again, so the loop never converges.

## Fix

- Diff against the raw registry from `http.get_global_commands(app_id)` instead of the parsed `AppCommand` objects. This also makes `_existing_command_to_payload` and its attribute workaround unnecessary, because the raw JSON already carries `nsfw`, `dm_permission` and `default_member_permissions`.
- Ignore `contexts`/`integration_types` in the comparison when the desired payload leaves them unset. They are still compared, and still trigger a recreate, when Hermes manages them.

## Evidence

- Dry run against a live 64-command registry: the old logic flagged 64/64 commands as changed; the new logic flags 0. Only the 6 commands genuinely missing from the registry are created.
- Live gateway after the fix: `Safely reconciled 70 slash command(s): unchanged=64 updated=0 recreated=0 created=6 deleted=0`. That was the first recorded `last_success_at` after days of 429s. The next restart skipped the sync on the fingerprint.
- Tests: new regression tests for server-filled defaults, zero-based flags round-tripping, and managed-flag changes still recreating. `tests/gateway/test_discord*.py`: 297 passed. The 14 failures also fail on a clean `main` checkout in the same location: they come from the home I/O guard when the checkout lives under `~/.hermes` and are unrelated to this change. `ruff check` is clean.

Fixes #104399. Complements #117299, which hardens the mid-sync failure path; this removes the reason syncs mutate in the first place.
