prs.title: Browser automation runs on browser_exec only; agent-browser and the built-in browser tools are gone (Camofox moves to a plugin)
prs.body:
Browser automation now runs on `browser_exec` only. agent-browser and the ten built-in `browser_*` tools are gone, and Camofox moves to the `camofox` catalog plugin, which installs automatically for homes that use it.

## Why

agent-browser stayed in Hermes for two reasons. It launched the bundled Chromium for `browser_exec`, and it drove the older built-in `browser_navigate`/`browser_click`/... tools. Those tools survived mainly because Camofox implements them: Camofox is Firefox behind a custom HTTP API with no CDP, so `browser_exec` can't drive it. Moving Camofox to a plugin (NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#161) removes the last thing that needed the old tool surface. A small Python launcher replaces agent-browser's Chromium launch.

## Changes

- **Launcher** (`tools/browser_launcher.py`, new): starts the pm-packaged Chromium (Chrome for Testing, unchanged) with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and reads `DevToolsActivePort`.
  - One browser per (profile home, cache key). Throwaway profiles live under `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/browser/chromium/` (0700), one dir per owning process, so two processes on one profile never share or wipe each other's dir. The dir name carries the owner's pid and start time, and the reaper removes the dirs of owners that are gone, including one that died mid-launch before writing its record.
  - Headless by default; `browser.headed` is honoured. The Windows headless default is preserved. The sandbox-bypass args apply under the same host policy as main, and never to the user's real Chrome/Edge/Brave (real-profile launches).
  - Every launched browser is stopped parent-first. A throwaway browser's launcher state lives in a private per-profile dir, `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/browser/chromium-records`. A persistent profile's state (launch record, holder leases and lock) lives in one dir per profile, keyed by the realpath of `user_data_dir` under the OS user's host lock dir, so every home that pins the same profile shares one lease set and lock, and the last holder across homes stops it. Every state dir is created 0700 and used only when it is a real directory of this user closed to other writers. A later process serving that profile reaps a crashed owner's browser after checking pid, start time and its `--user-data-dir` argv, and removes only dirs inside that profile's throwaway root. The reaper walks every profile the process serves. A browser attached after its owner crashed takes over the record, so it is not reaped while in use. The record is written right after the spawn, so a launcher killed during the readiness wait leaves its Chromium to the reaper; a failed or interrupted wait stops it. A stop holds the key's launch lock, so a concurrent relaunch of that key is never forgotten or wiped. Across processes, a shared-profile browser is stopped only by its last holder: attachers leave a lease beside the record (under a lock on that dir), the launcher hands the record to a live holder instead of killing the browser, and crashed holders are dropped by pid + start time. Checking for a running browser, launching or attaching, and writing the lease are one step under the profile's lock, so two processes starting one profile end with one Chromium. The reaper skips a profile that is mid-launch. A throwaway dir is never deleted while a Chromium still runs on it.
  - Records, leases and throwaway-dir names carry the writer's PID-namespace identity (Linux: the pid-namespace inode plus `boot_id`). A `HERMES_HOME` can be shared between a container gateway and a host CLI, and a pid only means something in the namespace that wrote it. So state from another namespace or boot, or state without the identity, is never judged dead: it is never reaped, deleted, lease-dropped or handed over. A process that attaches to a shared browser leases it under the launch record of that same launch, whichever namespace wrote the record. Records, leases and the in-process key registry match on the full launch identity: profile realpath, pid, start time, and the record name, which carries namespace + boot. They never match on a pid number alone. A browser of another environment is bound to the record holding the DevTools browser id its live endpoint serves; every record stores that id once its browser is up. Only the holder part of the lease name carries the attacher's tag, so the launcher sees holders from every namespace. A shared profile whose `SingletonLock` names a browser of another environment (written under another hostname, or by a launch record from another namespace, and not a live local process naming the dir) is attached through its DevTools endpoint and leased, never adopted, stopped or reaped from here. When that endpoint does not answer, the launch fails with an error naming the profile dir; it never starts a second Chromium on it.
  - Binary resolution: `browser.executable_path`, then pm, then the Docker baked path (`/etc/hermes/chromium-executable-path`), then a system Chromium where pm builds none (Termux).
- **Session layer** (`tools/browser_session*.py`): one resolver, `get_session_info(cache_key)`. Shared browsers (Bot Desktop profile, `browser.user_data_dir`, real profile, terminal-sandbox Chromium) are stopped only when their last session goes, and a session whose shared browser was relaunched on a new endpoint is rebuilt. The terminal-sandbox Chromium is keyed by its container, so profiles sharing a container share one refcount and a per-session container's browser stops with that session. Its liveness is cached for up to 30 s, and re-probed sooner if a connection through the port forward fails. A 404 on the cached `/devtools/browser/<id>` path counts as a failure, which catches a browser relaunched on the same port. Only the sandbox's own "not running" answer counts as dead, never a failed or timed-out exec. A sandbox Chromium is owned from the moment it spawns, and stopped if its port wait or forward fails. Its start time is read inside the sandbox at launch, and a stop signals it only after re-checking that start time and its `--user-data-dir` argv token there (a pid reused by another job is left alone and logged). A per-container lock spans check, start and claim, so sessions racing onto one container launch one browser. The real-profile snapshot (the copy of the user's profile) runs inside the copy dir's cross-process launch step, so two processes of one profile never copy at once or over a running copy-browser; the later one attaches. The real-profile browser and its launch lock are per profile home, so under multiplex a profile without consent never stops another profile's browser, and one profile's launch never makes another wait. With `browser.headed` and `bot_desktop.auto_start`, the screen comes up before the profile is chosen, so the first launch uses the Bot Desktop profile. The `browser_cdp` private-page guard fails closed for worker, iframe, unknown and target-less calls while any page is private (as main did). The exceptions are `Target.createTarget` (a blank tab is allowed; any other `url` is checked like `Page.navigate`'s), `Target.activateTarget` and `Target.closeTarget`. It covers CDP override, the hybrid `::local` sidecar, cloud providers (with `fallback_from_cloud` going to the launcher), real profile, Lightpanda and the packaged Chromium. `browser_exec`, `browser_cdp`, `browser_dialog`, `browser_vault`, the supervisor and the Bot Desktop browser all resolve through it. Every `browser.*` setting (`user_data_dir`, `chromium_args`, `cloud_provider`, `real_profile_pin`, `cdp_url`, …) is read through `load_user_config_effective` (managed overlay, `${VAR}` expansion). Shutdown (`cleanup_all_browsers`) tears each session down under its owning profile's scope, like the janitor, so a routed profile's cloud session is closed by its own provider.
- **Deleted:**
  - all built-in `browser_*` tools and the `browser_tool*.py` modules that served only them;
  - `tools/browser_camofox*.py`, the agent-browser pm package and its lock entry, and the npm warm-cache helpers;
  - the `/browser use` command and the `browser.manage use` action;
  - the harness-missing downgrade notice;
  - agent-browser post-setup, doctor and status rows.
  - `browser_tool.py` and `browser_tool_install.py` stay as frozen stubs for old updaters (see their docstrings).
- **Config v52:** `browser.backend` is dropped. Homes with `backend: off` land on `browser_exec`, with a one-time notice that disabling the `browser` toolset is how to turn browsing off. `hermes update` prints it, and when the boot path runs the migration, the first agent's startup warnings show it. Every other removed value is named in the migration report with the reason (e.g. `removed browser.backend: camofox — Camofox is now the camofox plugin`). Unquoted `off` (YAML false) counts as off, and sibling profiles print their own notices. The `AGENT_BROWSER_*` settings move to `browser.*` keys and keep the value they resolved to on main: a set env var wins over a default in config.yaml, and a relative `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE` is pinned against the cwd agent-browser inherited. The note then shows the absolute path it pinned. `browser.extension_control` is dropped. The step lives in `hermes_cli/config_migrations_browser.py`; the registry stays in `config_migrations.py`.
- **Left core:** a new `LEFT_CORE` row gives homes that used Camofox the `camofox` catalog plugin, and that home's `browser` toolset becomes `camofox`. Detection is main's `is_camofox_mode`: a CDP override means not Camofox. Otherwise the stored `cloud_provider`/`use_gateway` selection decides, else `CAMOFOX_URL` from the owning profile's `.env`. A leftover `browser.camofox` block alone never counts. A home that had disabled `browser` everywhere (`agent.disabled_toolsets`) gets `camofox` disabled too. The row fires only for homes from before the split, so a new user who installs the plugin later keeps `browser_exec`. A missing or unstamped config.yaml counts as before the split, and the first save that stamps one records the feature in use. This is intended for a home with no config.yaml whose `.env` sets `CAMOFOX_URL`: main's `is_camofox_mode` would have run Camofox for it. Its conversion writes a config.yaml stamped with the current version and the feature in use. A stamped home that uses Camofox without the plugin (a Nix-managed config is stamped at activation) gets the "moved out of core" notice, without conversion or install. The catalog entry ships as its own data-only PR (see Merge order).
- **Packaging:** Chromium is a default pm package in its own right. `install.sh --skip-browser` and `install.ps1 -SkipBrowser` now skip Chromium, and homes that recorded `--without agent-browser` still skip it. The Dockerfile drops agent-browser staging. A stale agent-browser store entry is ignored by `pm doctor`/`pm install` and removed by `pm gc`. pm also re-records a reused entry's env when the package code changed it (Chromium no longer exports `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`), including when `ensure()` finds the package already installed (under the install lock). The desktop eval probes rely on `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Without that, stores built before this PR, including the Desktop bundle job's restored cache, fail build admission with "binary or environment". Covered by `tests/pm/test_recorded_env_refresh.py`, which fails without the fix.
- **Desktop:** the toolset panel loses the Camofox and agent-browser options, and the Browser Use mode status and bundle exemption are removed. `check:lint` is clean and `i18n:keys` is unchanged.
- **Docs and skills:** every page and every bundled or optional skill now describes `browser_exec` as the only path, and Camofox users are pointed at `hermes plugins install camofox`. `browser_cdp` and `browser_dialog` are documented as needing a configured CDP endpoint (their gate is unchanged). Locale keys for removed surfaces are pruned in all 17 locales.
- **Removed: browser-extension control** (owner decision). Its broker allowlisted only the deleted `browser_*` tools, so it no longer did anything. Removed: `gateway/browser_control_broker.py`, `gateway/browser_control_artifacts.py`, `tools/browser_extension_router.py`, `tui_gateway/methods_browser_control.py`, the `/v1/browser-control/*` and `/v1/artifacts/*` API routes, the `browser.controller.*` contract methods/events (`gateway-contract.*` regenerated), and `browser.extension_control` (dropped from defaults; v52 strips it from user config). The two identity helpers bot relay uses moved to `gateway/session_identity.py` unchanged. Persisted API turns that carry a `browser_control` field still load and run (`test_api_cutover_contract.py`). Integrators drive a browser through `browser.cdp_url` / `/browser connect`. The api-server docs now carry a removal note.
- **Metrics:** `browser_exec` now reports to the existing opt-in browser metric (it would otherwise go silent). A call that ran on a local browser (hybrid `::local`, `fallback_from_cloud`, real profile) is labelled `local`. `extension` stays accepted as a legacy label. `check_shipped_schema_values.py` shows no new removals, so the removed `browser_*` names stay accepted as legacy values.

## Live verification

Real Nous model, scratch homes, tool calls read back from each run's `state.db`.

| Leg | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| (a) fresh install | pm installs agent-browser + Chromium; `browser_exec` works | pm installs Chromium only; `browser_exec` returns "Example Domain" |
| (b) headless, no orphans | — | `--headless=new`, pm binary, per-key profile dir; no Chrome left after `hermes chat -q` exits (ps listing) |
| (c) `browser.backend: off` home | `browser_navigate` via agent-browser | migrated to v52 with the notice, then `browser_exec` |
| gateway SIGTERM | Chromium tree + harness daemon killed | same |
| (d) Camofox homes A → B → A | — | A: plugin auto-installed by the LEFT_CORE row, `browser_navigate` served by a real camofox-browser 1.18.1 on :9377; B: no plugin, `browser_exec`; A again: no reinstall |
| (e) real profile (fixture Chrome profile) | — | fixture cookie visible through the snapshot; a pin naming a missing dir gives a fresh browser + note; `hermes browser close-profile` releases the lock; gateway shutdown kills it |
| (f) Docker image | — | built from head: no agent-browser, `/etc/hermes/chromium-executable-path`, one `browser_exec` turn returns the title |

**Fix round** (review comment 6347781122; per-finding map in comment 6349678902). The legs below ran at `c7b376a996a`, with (a) re-run on the final head `256fed4e408`:
- (a) one `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home: 0 Chromium left after exit; `chromium-records` is mode 700 and empty.
- (c) v51 homes with unquoted `backend: off`, quoted `"off"`, and `.env AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE` with `engine: auto`: all migrate correctly (the env value wins), and `browser_exec` works in each.
- (d) Camofox A/B/A plus a leftover-block-only home and a fresh v52 home: the row fires only for A.
- (e) one multiplex gateway, real-profile profile R plus a no-consent profile N: R's real google-chrome had no `--no-sandbox` and survived N's session (the `7635cbcd2b6` code killed it).
- The `browser_cdp` worker-target bypass is blocked live.

**Re-review round** (comment 6350427176; per-finding map in the follow-up comment), at the final head:
- N5, two Hermes processes on one persistent profile with a real google-chrome, each exiting through the normal teardown: before, the launcher's exit killed the browser the attacher was driving (`C still sees its browser alive: False`); after, the browser survives the launcher's exit and the attacher's exit stops it (`after both exited: alive = False`, no record, no process on the profile).
- One `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home: `Example Domain`; no Chromium after `hermes chat -q` exits, nothing of the home left after the probe gateway's TERM, and the throwaway root and `chromium-records` are empty.

**Round 3** (Greptile inline threads; per-thread replies on each), rebased on main `6e8adc7a462`: one `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home returns `Example Domain` (read back from `state.db`); no Chromium after `hermes chat -q` exits, the throwaway root and `chromium-records` are empty, and nothing of the home is left after the probe gateway's TERM.

**Round 4** (human review by @unsupportedpastels plus 4 Greptile threads; per-item map in the round-4 comment), at the final head:
- Two homes pin one `browser.user_data_dir`, with real Chrome. Before: `B after A's normal exit (other home): alive False`. After: `alive True`, then after B exits the Chrome is gone, with no leases and no records left.
- Two homes race a first launch of one profile. Before: a SingletonLock exit, or a 60 s DevTools timeout. After: one Chrome, the same ws URL in both processes, nothing left.
- SIGINT or SIGKILL to the owner during the readiness wait: no untracked Chromium after the next reap. A throwaway dir with a live Chromium on it survives the reclaim.
- One `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home: `Example Domain`, read back from `state.db`. No Chromium after `hermes chat -q` exits; the throwaway root and `chromium-records` are empty, and nothing of the home is left after the probe gateway's TERM.

**Round 5** (2 Greptile threads plus the real-profile copy race; replies on each thread), rebased on main `7b0f11fc7b2`: one `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home returns `Example Domain` (read back from `state.db`). No Chromium is left after `hermes chat -q` exits, and nothing of the home is left after the probe gateway's TERM.

**Round 6** (4 Greptile threads plus a self-review; replies on each thread): foreign-namespace shared browser attached or refused (`c337cae878a`), `browser.*` through the effective loader (`ba612857020`), sandbox stop re-verifies start time + argv (`ded998aaae7`), v52 tests compare with `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`39efaac8216`), shutdown teardown under the owning profile (`c3565d0d393`). Each is red-first against `ecc1f0edc4f`. 165 targeted test files pass (2924 tests). One `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home returns `Example Domain` from `state.db`; no Chromium after `hermes chat -q` exits, nothing of the home after the probe gateway's TERM.

**Round 7** (3 Greptile threads; replies on each): launch records, leases and the key registry match one browser launch, never a pid number (`59eb771c0ed`). An earlier container's record on the same pid no longer hides an attacher from the live browser's owner, and stopping one of two same-pid foreign browsers drops only its own lease. The new tests are red-first against `c3565d0d393` (`tests/tools/test_browser_launcher_identity.py`, 4 tests). 71 targeted test files pass (989 tests), and `scripts/check --only health` is ok. One `browser_exec` turn on a fresh home returns `Example Domain` from `state.db`; no Chromium after `hermes chat -q` exits, nothing of the home after the probe gateway's TERM. The size thread was answered without a split: the ratchet caps files at 2,000 lines, and the launcher is at 1,108.

The plugin's `hermes plugins validate` passes against this tree (it fails on main with `built-in tool collisions`, which is the plugin PR's only red check):

```
✓ built-in tool collisions — no collisions
✓ security scan — safe
Validation passed.
```

## Prompt surface

Default sessions: **0 token change**. main already sends only `browser_exec` by default, and its schema is byte-identical. Homes on `backend: off`: about −834 tokens per API call (10,875 → 10,041, chars/4 estimate). The CI review bot's 33 → 23 tool table counts every tool as available. With real availability checks, a stock home sends only `browser_exec` on both trees.

## Plugin-used core internals (kept as-is)

The `camofox` plugin imports `tools.url_safety.is_always_blocked_url` and `normalize_url_for_request`, `tools.website_policy.check_website_access`, `agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text` and `_PREFIX_RE`, `tools.credential_files.to_agent_visible_cache_path`, and `import tools` (old-core detection). This PR leaves them untouched. Promoting them to a documented plugin surface is a follow-up.

## Changed test assertions

- **Shared metrics:** browser-call tests no longer go through the extension-controller callable (feature removed). `test_shared_metrics_loop.py` drives the real `_handle_browser_exec` and asserts the backend label for cloud, hybrid-local and fallback calls (`local` when the call ran locally).
- **Camofox detection:** case C of `test_left_core_camofox.py`, where a non-default `browser.camofox` block without `CAMOFOX_URL` counted as in use, now expects **not** in use. That is main's `is_camofox_mode` semantics, and the old expectation encoded the bug.
- **Tool Gateway offer:** `test_nous_subscription.py` again asserts main's `direct["browser"] is True` for a `CAMOFOX_URL` home.
- **Served-profile env:** `test_served_profile_child_env{,_authority}.py` assert again that the routed profile B's browser credential reaches the harness (`b-bu`, through `browser_use_cli._harness_credentials`) and the launch profile's (`a-bu`) never does. A mutation that reads `os.environ` fails 2 tests.
- **Strengthened, each against a mutation the previous version passed:**
  - `test_browser_windows_headless`: real config.yaml, no mocks; flipping the default to headed fails.
  - `test_browser_use_session_expiry`: asserts teardown runs before the replacement.
  - `test_browser_pm`: doctor `--fix` and Termux guard coverage restored.
  - `test_browser_real_profile`: the `--user-data-dir` argv scan now runs on every host, plus a Windows-only reattach test (never run here).
- **Seams:** six test files patched `browser_session.browser_in_sandbox` (never called in production, so the patch did nothing). They now pin the real `bot_desktop.runtime.tool_placement`. `test_managed_browserbase_and_modal` asserts `get_cloud_provider() is None` and `is_local_backend()` in place of the deleted `is_local_mode`. `test_bot_desktop_placement`'s exec stub answers the sandbox liveness probe.
- **Real profile:** tests use `real_profile_key()` (`hermes-real-profile@<home>`) in place of the process-global constant.
- **Launcher records:** `test_browser_orphan_reaper.py` reads records from the profile's `chromium-records` dir.
- **Profiles:** the clone/live-browser test uses `browser_launcher.running_instance` against a stub `/json/version` server. Its assertions are unchanged.
- **Extension removal:** `tests/gateway/test_browser_control_*.py`, `tests/tools/test_browser_extension_router*.py` and `test_api_server_artifact_store_async.py` (it tested only the browser-control artifact store) are deleted. `test_api_canonical_projection`, `test_peer_dm_into_open_bot_chat`, `test_multi_client_fanout` and `contracts/test_generated` lose only their extension parts. `test_authenticated_session_identity` keeps its issuer-separation assert, pointed at the moved helper.
- Tests that only exercised deleted code are deleted. Session-layer, routing, real-profile, Bot Desktop, multiplex, SSRF, CDP and vault tests are ported to `browser_session` and the launcher.

## Merge order

1. **This PR.** It adds the `camofox` LEFT_CORE row but not the catalog entry: catalog PRs must be data-only (`pinned-source-validate`), so the entry ships separately.
2. NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#161: its CI goes green once this lands, since it only fails on the collision with today's built-in tools.
3. A data-only catalog PR adding `plugin-catalog/camofox.yaml`, pinned to the merged plugin sha, then a docs deploy.

Between steps 1 and 3, a Camofox home's automatic install reports "not in catalog yet, run `hermes plugins install camofox`" and retries on the next start. The release channel never sees that gap if all three land before the next release.

## Not covered

- Windows and macOS live legs, including the Windows-only `real_profile_autoclose` lock path. Termux live leg. Headed-mode live run. A full `hermes update` run over a store holding agent-browser.
- Vault fill through a Camofox tab needs a core seam (the vault tool running its fill script through the active backend's tab); follow-up.
- A terminal-sandbox Chromium (per-container refcount, liveness and its cache) is component-tested with stubbed exec streams; its launch/stop identity scripts run against real processes through a local exec prefix, not a docker/ssh sandbox. Its ownership is per Hermes process: two processes reusing one persistent container each see the other's browser as not theirs, so one process's last teardown stops a browser the other still drives (that one relaunches on its next call); the port forward's failure count is tested with a real local relay, not a docker/ssh sandbox. The cross-process holder lock's Windows (`msvcrt`) branch has not run; its retry policy (contention errnos only, 30 s bound) is unit-tested, and a real-`msvcrt` test runs only on the Windows lane. No real Nix activation: the stamped-home notice is tested with a v52 config. Windows-only tests have never run here. The 16 translated startup tips are machine-written and unreviewed.
- A boot-path migration's notices wait for the first agent in that process. A process that never starts an agent (e.g. `hermes doctor`) only logs them.
- By design (PID-namespace rule), launcher state from another namespace or an earlier boot is kept, never cleaned. A shared-profile browser whose holder crashed in another namespace is never stopped from this one. macOS and Windows have no namespace identity, so their behaviour is unchanged.
- Shared-profile state is keyed under the OS user's host lock dir, so homes run with different `HOME`/`XDG_STATE_HOME` values don't share it.
- Pre-existing on main: under multiplex, the CDP supervisor (registered under the bare task id) is not stopped by the `task@home` session teardown and logs about 5 `connect failed` warnings before removing itself.
- The LEFT_CORE conversion turns `browser` off even when the plugin install fails (existing left-core design), so such a home has no browser plus an install notice until the retry succeeds.

## Open PRs this obsoletes

20 campaign PRs plus 137 from the sweep that target the removed stack. 6 more only touch a deleted test and need a rebase. Full list below; closes happen after merge.

prs.title: fix(desktop): name the gateway supplier on model rows
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A **gateway** provider — magpie, or any router behind one OpenAI-compatible
endpoint — serves several vendors from a single provider row. Core labels rows
with `modelBaseId()`, which drops everything before the **last** `/` because
"the vendor lives on the provider group row":

```ts
const slash = trimmed.lastIndexOf('/')
return slash >= 0 ? trimmed.slice(slash + 1) : trimmed
```

That holds for a vendor endpoint (`openai/gpt-5.5`). For a router it is exactly
backwards — the prefix *is* the supplier:

```
workbuddy/hy3     -> "Hy3"
workbuddy-ai/hy3  -> "Hy3"      <- two suppliers, one indistinguishable row
qoder/qfmodel     -> "Qfmodel"
qoder-cn/qfmodel  -> "Qfmodel"  <- same
```

Picking the wrong row means spending the wrong account's quota. The gateway's
`/v1/models` `display_name` cannot help: the picker payload never carries it,
so a gateway-side rename does not reach this UI.

This PR detects a gateway catalog and labels its rows with the supplier in
full, plus the supplier's mark in the leading slot:

```
Hy3 · WorkBuddy AI
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash · Trae CN
Qfmodel · Qoder CN
```

## How the gateway is detected

`isGatewayCatalog()` requires **≥2 distinct *known* supplier prefixes**. A bare
slash is deliberately not the signal: every aggregator id is `vendor/model`
(OpenRouter's `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, Nous Portal, …) and there the
provider row already answers "whose model is this?". Promoting `anthropic` to a
supplier would put a "· Anthropic" on every row of every aggregator. An
existing test caught exactly that regression while developing this.

Non-gateway providers return `null` from every seam, so their labels are
byte-identical to today.

## Design notes

- **The variant suffix stays in the name.** `deepseek-v4.1-flash` renders
  `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash · WorkBuddy`, not "DeepSeek V4.1" + a `FLASH` chip. On a
  router the suffix is part of what the vendor calls the model, and the row is
  ~340px wide with the variant tag, effort chip and checkmark already on it.
- **Gateway rows don't truncate.** Their label is longer by design; truncating
  produced `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash · W…` — losing precisely the half that tells two
  suppliers apart.
- **Surfaces without provider context** (composer pill, sidebar session row)
  use a namer that answers only for known suppliers, so a normal provider keeps
  its own label.
- The search index includes the supplier, so typing `workbuddy` finds its rows.

## Related Issue

Fixes #39878 (same user-visible symptom: a router's same-named models collapse
into duplicate rows in the desktop picker).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-suppliers.ts` *(new)* — supplier table (icon,
  monogram, display name), `isGatewayCatalog()`, `supplierOf()`, the namers,
  and the small helpers the row and the popup need (`modelRowLabel`,
  `supplierMark`, `modelRowNameClass`).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-suppliers.test.ts` *(new)* — 13 cases: gateway
  detection (including the aggregator false-positive), naming, variant folding,
  and "non-gateway providers are untouched".
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-status-label.ts` — `modelDisplayParts` /
  `displayModelName` / `formatModelPillLabel` accept an optional `supplier`
  namer; the namer's answer decides, so a blank answer stays on the ordinary
  path.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.tsx` — rows render the supplier
  mark; gateway rows skip the variant chip and the truncation; search matches
  the supplier name.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/model-visibility-dialog.tsx` — same labeling and
  search, so the two surfaces can't disagree.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/model-pill.tsx`,
  `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-row.tsx` — use the strict namer.

## How to Test

1. Configure a provider whose `/v1/models` returns ids with ≥2 known supplier
   prefixes, e.g. `workbuddy/hy3` + `workbuddy-ai/hy3` + `qoder/qfmodel` +
   `qoder-cn/qfmodel`.
2. Open a new session → ⌘⇧M.
3. Expect `Hy3 · WorkBuddy` and `Hy3 · WorkBuddy AI` as distinct rows, each with
   a supplier mark, and no separate `FLASH`/`PREVIEW` chip.
4. Point a provider at a normal aggregator (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) and
   confirm its rows still read `Sonnet 5` — no spurious supplier suffix.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] `scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation — N/A (no user-facing config or CLI surface changed)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — pure renderer logic, no native code
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A

## Duplicate check

`gh search issues` / `gh search prs` for "modelBaseId", "model label supplier
prefix", "gateway catalog supplier", "modelDisplayParts".

The closest existing PR is **#39892** ("disambiguate provider-prefixed model
names"), which targets the same symptom from the same issue (#39878) with a
different remedy: it keeps the friendly label and only falls back to the raw
`workbuddy/hy3` id for rows whose names collide. This PR instead always names
the supplier on a gateway row and keeps the label human-readable
(`Hy3 · WorkBuddy`), adds the supplier mark, and folds the variant suffix into
the name rather than emitting a second chip.

Both fix #39878. I'm opening this as an alternative for the maintainers to pick
between, and I'm happy to fold any part of it into #39892 instead if that PR is
the preferred direction — the detection helper (`isGatewayCatalog`) and the
supplier table would port over unchanged.

## Screenshots / Logs

Rows on a magpie gateway before/after (4 suppliers, 2 of them sharing model
names with 2 others):

```
before                          after
MAGPIE                          MAGPIE
  Hy3                             Hy3 · WorkBuddy
  Hy3                             Hy3 · WorkBuddy AI
  Qfmodel                         Qfmodel · Qoder
  Qfmodel                         Qfmodel · Qoder CN
  DeepSeek V4.1  FLASH            DeepSeek V4.1 Flash · Trae CN
```

Test output:

```
$ cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/lib/model-suppliers.test.ts \
    src/lib/model-status-label.test.ts src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.test.tsx \
    src/components/model-visibility-dialog.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/model-pill.test.tsx
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  74 passed (74)

$ python scripts/check
scripts/check: 12 checks, ok
```

The 11 pre-existing failures in the `electron`/`scripts` projects
(`Gateway ticket bootstrap failed`, macOS sysroot, native-deps staging) reproduce
identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree and are unrelated to this change.

prs.title: /compress sent mid-reply now runs when the reply finishes instead of being refused (TUI + Desktop; port kimi-code#4276)
prs.body:
`/compress` sent from the TUI or Desktop while Hermes is replying now waits for the reply and runs at the turn boundary, instead of being refused with "session busy — stop the current reply first".

Port of MoonshotAI/kimi-code#4276 ("queue /compact behind the running turn"), adapted to the session authority.

## Changes
- `gateway/session_deferred_compress.py` (new): `defer_compress` keeps an authorized compress that `session.mutate` refused only with `session_busy`; `apply_deferred_compress` runs it through `_mutate_session` (same claim gate, revision/generation fences, receipt, `session.updated` publication and agent eviction as an idle `/compress`) and announces it on a `status.update` edge.
- `gateway/session_mutations.py::_owned_mutation`: the compress branch defers on `session_busy` and answers `{status: "deferred", message, revision, execution_generation}`. `--preview` is never deferred.
- `gateway/session_authority.py::_drain`: runs a deferred compress at the top of each loop, i.e. after the running turn settles and **before the next queued message is claimed**, so that message runs on the compressed transcript.
- Auto-compaction guard (kimi's `autoCompactionSerial`): a bare `/compress` is skipped, with a notice, when the turn auto-compacted while it waited. A second summary right after one throws away more history for nothing. `/compress here N` or a focus topic still runs.
- Desktop (`canonical-protocol.ts::settle`): a `deferred` receipt maps to the `pending` shape the compress action already handles (`markCompressDeferred`, #97948). That path shows the queued toast, then on the `compacted` edge shows the success toast and rehydrates the transcript.
- TUI (`canonicalSessionControls.ts`): prints the queued line. The edge text shows up in the activity line.
- Docs: `/compress` row in `reference/slash-commands.md`.

Same shape as the deferred model pick (RT-12, `session_deferred_pick.py`), but the request is kept in memory on `LiveSession` rather than in `state_meta`. If the owner restarts mid-turn, the queued compress is lost, and the user just runs `/compress` again.

## Live repro (real owner daemon + loopback model, `session.mutate` sent while a turn is `started`)
| | origin/main 3ba2b0787ed | this branch |
|---|---|---|

prs.title: feat(desktop): add complete Korean localization and fix i18n regressions
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a complete Korean (`ko`) desktop locale. `LOCALE_ENDONYMS` already carried `ko` and the backend already lists it in `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` with a `locales/ko.yaml` catalog, so the desktop picker was the remaining gap.

The catalog is at parity with English rather than partial. Measured against the override this branch passes to `defineLocale` — before any English fallback is merged in — and excluding `intro.*` the way the completeness test does, there are no missing keys, no keys left over from an older English catalog, and no drift in value kinds or interpolation arity. `intro` is the documented exception: the English catalog entry is an empty shell because the copy lives in `intro-copy.jsonl`, so the Korean rotation shows up as extra keys against it and is covered by the intro rotation and custom-fallback tests instead. The 37 values that still read as English are audited product and brand names, protocol labels, and URL examples; technical names such as `Mixture of Agents`, MCP and OAuth stay as they are, as do the reasoning effort levels, which are the tokens a provider documents and accepts. `ko` joins `COMPLETE_LOCALES` so the completeness test holds it to the same structural checks as fr/de/es.

`intro-ko.ts` joins the `intro-*` set, keeping the per-personality rotation order and count from `intro-copy.jsonl` and leaving a user-supplied personality name untranslated. The existing intro test now covers Korean; its CJK pattern matches Kana and Han, so Hangul gets a check of its own.

Two smaller things came out of translating the app rather than from the catalog. `t.settings.sections[id] ?? section.label` meant the Browser settings section fell through to its English label in every locale, since `sections` had no `browser` entry. And in the model defaults row the Fast label is a bare text node in its flex container, so its floor is min-content: `Fast` has no break opportunity and holds its width, while a two-syllable CJK label may break between syllables and fold onto two lines. It is now a span that declines to wrap, matching what the Reasoning label next to it already does.

Fixes #71500

Fix a missing cover image on the **Magi** community plugin listing in the Hermes catalog. Magi provides Hermes Desktop interfaces for reviewing pending memory writes and managing stored `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` entries, including user-approved AI compaction.

The pinned Magi release already includes `docs/magi-cover-banner.png`, but `plugin-catalog/magi.yaml` only declares `screenshots`. Those images populate the detail-page gallery; they do **not** supply the catalog card's cover. The catalog needs an explicit `image` field.

prs.title: fix(image_gen): use aspect_ratio auto for OpenRouter edits when the model offers it
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On the OpenRouter Image API, `aspect_ratio` always reaches the payload as a fixed ratio: the semantic value defaults to `landscape` (`resolve_aspect_ratio` coerces a missing or invalid value), so an edit that never mentioned orientation is sent as `16:9`, and one that says `portrait` as `9:16`. The edit path cannot tell a chosen ratio from a defaulted one. The model then fits the reference into that ratio and recomposes the subject instead of editing in place.

When the request carries reference images and the model lists `auto`, send `auto`. A forced ratio (`aspect_ratio_exact` kwarg, `OPENROUTER_IMAGE_API_ASPECT_RATIO`, or config) still wins. Models without `auto` (Gemini, Krea, Qwen) keep the old mapping, and new images (no references) are unchanged.

Measured on a portrait-jacket colour-swap edit (mean absolute error of the pixels outside the jacket, after alignment): models sent a fixed 9:16 changed 13 to 17 levels, versus 1.3 for a model that was sent no ratio.

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests

## Changes Made

- `plugins/image_gen/openrouter/__init__.py`: `_pick_exact_aspect_ratio(..., *, has_references=False)` returns `auto` when `has_references` and the model offers it, with a note in the result; `_build_image_api_payload` passes `has_references=bool(references)`.
- `tests/plugins/image_gen/test_openrouter_compat_provider.py`: edit on a model with `auto` -> `auto` (with note); forced ratio wins; model without `auto` unchanged; no references unchanged.

## How to Test

`pytest tests/plugins/image_gen/test_openrouter_compat_provider.py -q` (the new tests fail on current `main`).

Behaviour change to review: edits on `openai/gpt-image-2`, `openai/gpt-image-1-mini`, `microsoft/mai-image-2.5*` and `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality` now send `auto`. Whether omitting `aspect_ratio` keeps the source shape on models without `auto` (Gemini) was not measured, so they are left alone.

prs.title: fix(openai_compat): handle Gemini thought_signature (echo captured + sentinel for unsigned tool calls)
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Fix the `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error returned by Gemini 3 when continuing a tool-calling conversation through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts.
This is required for tools to work correctly, and missing thought_signature
may lead to degraded model performance. ... https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
```

Gemini 3 requires the `thought_signature` to be **echoed back inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`** on every `functionCall` part of the request history. PicoClaw's OpenAI-compatible provider only sent it under `function.thought_signature`, which Gemini rejects on the follow-up request.

Three distinct bugs are fixed:

1. **Serialization** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go`): resolve the signature from every known location (`Function.ThoughtSignature`, top-level `ThoughtSignature`, `ExtraContent.Google`) and emit it inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`. A signature-less tool call no longer emits an empty `extra_content` block.

2. **Streaming capture** (`pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): `parseStreamResponse` did **not** read the `thought_signature` at all. Since `ChatStream` is the default chat path, any tool call produced in streaming mode lost the signature entirely, so the next request was rejected. The delta parser now captures the signature from both `function.thought_signature` and `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.

3. **Unsigned tool calls on Gemini hosts** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go` + `pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): fixes 1 and 2 only cover the case where the tool call was produced *by Gemini itself*, so a signature is available to echo. They do **not** cover the case that actually breaks the fallback chain: the tool call was produced by another provider (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) and the turn later fell back to Gemini 3. There is no signature to echo, and Gemini rejects the request with the same `400`. Fix: a new `SerializeOptions{GeminiThoughtSignatureFallback}` injects the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` into `extra_content.google.thought_signature` on every unsigned `functionCall` part. The option is enabled only for Gemini hosts (`isGeminiHost`), so every other endpoint keeps omitting `extra_content` exactly as before, and a real captured signature is never overridden.

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [ ] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [x] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

## 🔗 Related Issue

Refs #3230, Refs #3111 — same `400` on OpenAI-compat Gemini 3 tool loops.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
- **Reasoning:**
  - Gemini 3 (via both `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` and gateways such as Cloudflare AI Gateway) mandatory-signature contract. The signature must be resent on the assistant tool-call message of the following request, and Google specifically looks for `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.
  - `extra_content` is a Google-only extension. Providers that don't support it ignore unknown fields on the assistant tool-call object, so emitting it is additive; the `google` key is what only Gemini accepts. This mirrors upstream's existing `serializeToolCalls` behavior of preserving signatures, ordering the resolution so a top-level `ThoughtSignature` (set by the streaming path) still wins.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (linux/amd64)
- **OS:** Linux
- **Model/Provider:** `gemini-3.8-flash` via Google AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`)
- **Channels:** Telegram / web

## 📸 Evidence (Optional)
<details>
<summary>Click to view Logs/Screenshots</summary>

Reproduced failure mode (provider fallback from a DeepSeek primary to Gemini):

```
failover(format): provider=openai model=gemini-3.8-flash status=400
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts...
```

Live reproduction against `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (OpenAI-compat endpoint) confirms the fix for bug 3: an unsigned `functionCall` part fails with `400`, while the same part carrying the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` is accepted; a real captured signature is preserved and never replaced.

Local verification:
```
$ go test ./pkg/providers/...
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/common        0.032s
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/openai_compat 0.121s
(... all pkg/providers packages pass)

$ golangci-lint run --build-tags goolm,stdjson ./pkg/providers/...
0 issues.
```

New tests cover: wire payload contains `"extra_content":{"google":{"thought_signature":"..."}}` when the signature is only on `Function`, only top-level, or only on `ExtraContent`; no `extra_content` when there is no signature; a streaming `ChatStream` round that captures the signature from the delta; the sentinel is injected for unsigned parts on Gemini hosts and omitted on non-Gemini hosts; and a real signature is never overridden by the sentinel.

</details>

## ☑️ Checklist
- [x] My code/docs follow the style of this project.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own changes.

issues.title: Resend channel can't send: null thread id falls back to a platform id the adapter rejects

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

`015a7fe9` (main), with `/add-resend` on adapter 0.1.1 and 0.3.0 (pin bumped in #4042)

### Host platform

All (macOS and Linux)

### What happened?

The Resend (email) channel receives mail but can't send. Agent replies and the hello from "Connect yourself" never go out.

Email is a non-threaded channel, so `deliver()` gets a null thread id. The bridge then falls back to the platform id (`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts:821`, `const tid = threadId ?? platformId;`), which for Resend is the two-part `resend:<address>`. The Resend adapter's `decodeThreadId` rejects that with `Invalid thread ID format`, so the send throws.

Found by @amit-shafnir while reviewing #4042. It is reproduced at code level on both adapter versions, not yet on a live install. The reply changes listed in #4042's release note aren't visible until this is fixed.

### What did you expect?

A reply to an email thread, and the first-contact hello, are sent through Resend.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. On a branch with `/add-resend` applied (adapter 0.1.1 or 0.3.0), call the bridge's `deliver('resend:you@example.com', null, …)` with any text.
2. Observed: it throws `Invalid thread ID format` from the adapter's `decodeThreadId`. Expected: the message is sent.

issues.title: Inbound attachments silently dropped on channels whose message IDs contain a path separator (e.g. Google Chat)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
# Inbound attachments are silently dropped on channels whose message IDs contain a path separator (e.g. Google Chat)

## Summary

`extractAttachmentFiles` in `src/session-manager.ts` gates attachment staging on
`isSafeAttachmentName(messageId)`. That check rejects any value containing `/`
or `\`. Google Chat message IDs are resource paths:

```
spaces/AAAABBBBCCC/messages/AbCdEfGhIjk.AbCdEfGhIjk
```

so the guard rejects every one of them and returns before writing anything to
disk. The result is that **no inbound attachment on Google Chat ever reaches
the container.**

The failure is silent from the user's side. The attachment metadata still
reaches the agent, so it reports the filename it was sent and then correctly
says the file is nowhere on its filesystem. In our case the agent said exactly
that, which is what led us to the code.

Host logs show one of these per affected message:

```
WARN Rejecting unsafe inbound message id messageId="spaces/AAAABBBBCCC/messages/AbCdEfGhIjk.AbCdEfGhIjk:ag-..."
```

## Why it only shows up on some channels

Slack, Discord and WhatsApp IDs are opaque tokens with no separators, so they
pass the check and the path works. Google Chat is the outlier, which is
presumably why this has gone unnoticed.

## Root cause

The check is a *filename* guard (its docstring describes filenames, and it was
added for WhatsApp's client-controlled `msg.key.id`) applied to a field that is
not a filename on every platform. A message ID is an opaque identifier; only
some platforms happen to make it filename-shaped.

## Suggested fix

Sanitize the ID into a single path component rather than rejecting it.
Containment does not come from the rejection — it comes from the result being
one component by construction, plus `ensureContainedInboxDir` (symlink +
realpath containment) and the `wx` exclusive-create flag at the write. Those
three are unchanged.

We're running this locally:

- add a `safeAttachmentDirName(messageId)` helper in `src/attachment-safety.ts`
  that returns the ID unchanged when it is already a safe component, and
  otherwise a sanitized slug plus a short SHA-256 suffix
- use it for the inbox directory name and the `localPath` written back into the
  message

Passing already-safe IDs through verbatim means Slack/Discord/WhatsApp staging
paths are untouched; only IDs that were previously dropped take the derived
form. The hash suffix keeps IDs that differ only in stripped characters from
colliding onto one directory (which, with exclusive-create, would surface as a
second message's attachments being refused).

One existing test in `src/host-core.test.ts`
(`should reject inbound attachments when messageId is unsafe`) asserts the
rejection mechanism rather than the containment property, so it needs to assert
that nothing escapes the inbox instead of that nothing is written.

The outbound side (`readOutboxFiles`, `clearOutbox`) does not need this — those
IDs are container-generated (`msg-<ts>-<rand>`) and always safe.

Happy to open a PR if that would help.

## Reproduction

1. Wire a Google Chat messaging group to an agent group
2. Send the agent an image
3. Agent receives the filename in the message text; no file appears under
   `data/v2-sessions/<agent-group>/<session>/inbox/`
4. `logs/nanoclaw.error.log` shows `Rejecting unsafe inbound message id`

## Note on a second, unrelated bug in the same path

Fixing the above alone is not enough to make Google Chat attachments work.
`@chat-adapter/gchat` also calls the Chat media endpoint without `alt=media`,
so `fetchData()` fails with a 400 and no bytes ever arrive to be staged. That
one is being fixed upstream in `vercel/chat`. Mentioning it so anyone verifying
this fix doesn't conclude it didn't work.

## Environment

- nanoclaw v2.1.54
- Google Chat adapter via `@chat-adapter/gchat` 4.29.0
- Linux host, Docker containers

issues.title: Claude agents can't read PDFs: agent image has no pdftoppm (poppler-utils)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main `a62a8d2f` (local image build). Earlier mains are the same: the Dockerfile has never installed poppler-utils.

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

A user sent a Claude agent a 60-page PDF and asked about page 47. Claude's Read tool returned an error instead of the page:

```
pdftoppm is not installed. Install poppler-utils (e.g. `brew install poppler` or `apt-get install poppler-utils`) to enable PDF page rendering.
```

(Same text when reproduced with Claude Code 2.1.296 inside a fresh main image.)

The agent then looked for `python3`, `mutool`, `gs` and `qpdf`, found none, and replied that it could not read the page. It happened in both runs:

- Run 1: "I can't read page 47 yet. This environment has no PDF renderer: `pdftoppm` is missing, and so are Python, `mutool` and `gs`…"
- Run 2: "I can't read page 47 yet. The PDF page renderer (`poppler-utils`) isn't installed…"

In the same runs Claude read every JPEG and PNG. OpenCode, on the same VM with the same PDF, answered correctly.

### What did you expect?

Claude reads the PDF and answers the question.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Build the agent image from main: `./container/build.sh`
2. `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh nanoclaw-agent-v2-<slug>:latest -c 'command -v pdftoppm || echo missing'` prints `missing`.
3. Send a Claude agent a PDF longer than 10 pages and ask about one page.

### Cause

Claude Code's Read tool turns PDF pages into images with `pdftoppm`, from poppler-utils. `container/Dockerfile` does not install poppler-utils.

### Fix

#4174 adds `poppler-utils` to the agent image (+6.4 MB).

### NanoCo's own images

The hardened image is built by Echo, not from `container/Dockerfile`, so it may lack `pdftoppm` too. Check an image with `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh <image> -c 'command -v pdftoppm || echo missing'`. If it prints `missing`, Echo needs to add poppler-utils.

### Channel or interface

CLI / terminal

### Agent provider

Claude

prs.title: fix(setup/onecli): restrict admin API and postgres to loopback after OneCLI install
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Pins OneCLI's admin API and Postgres to loopback after install, so agent containers can no longer read every agent access token over the Docker bridge.

- **Problem**: OneCLI's installer auto-picks the `docker0` bridge IP as `ONECLI_BIND_HOST` on bare-metal Linux, and its `docker-compose.yml` uses that one variable for all three published ports: the proxy gateway (`:10255`), the admin API (`:10254`) and Postgres (`:5432`). The proxy needs the bridge so agent containers can reach it; the admin API and Postgres do not. On a default install on a Linux host, every agent container can read every agent access token via unauthenticated HTTP at `http://<bridge-ip>:10254/api/agents`, and can connect to Postgres directly with the documented default credentials.
- **Fix**: a post-install step in `setup/onecli.ts`. `hardenOneCliBinds()` does a targeted regex rewrite of the upstream compose, replacing the `${ONECLI_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}` prefix with a literal `127.0.0.1` on just the admin and Postgres port lines; `:10255` keeps whatever bind the installer chose. A marker comment (`# nanoclaw: admin+postgres pinned to loopback (onecli/onecli#268)`) at the top makes a re-run a no-op and the change discoverable. An unrecognized compose layout warns and leaves the file untouched: fail loud but safe.
- **Host admin URLs**: it also rewrites `~/.onecli/config.json` `api-host` and `~/.onecli/.env` `ONECLI_URL` when they point at the bridge IP on `:10254` (never `:10255`), so the host's admin connection survives the pin. Both are best-effort; a missing or unparseable file is logged and skipped. The URL taken from `onecli install` stdout gets the same swap before it reaches `emitStatus`/`writeToEnv`.
- **Reconcile**: `docker compose up -d` runs with `ONECLI_BIND_HOST` resolved from `docker inspect` of the running `:10255` port (fallback `~/.onecli/.env`, then `127.0.0.1`), so the proxy stays on the bridge. Failure is non-fatal; the rewrite has landed and a later compose-up picks it up.
- **`--reuse` mode** does not rewrite (other apps may depend on the existing bind), but detects a non-loopback admin bind (`docker inspect` of `:10254` first, then `~/.onecli/.env`, which also catches shell-set values) and emits a warning plus `UNSAFE_BIND` in the status block. `emitStatus('ONECLI', ...)` gains `HARDENED` and `HARDEN_NOTE`.
- **Why a regex, not a YAML parser**: the upstream compose is small and hand-written, and the lines are exact-match strings. A regex catches drift loudly (warn and no-op), where a YAML parser would round-trip a renamed key and silently do nothing.
- **Out of scope**: the OneCLI auth surface (upstream onecli/onecli#263) and the `--remote-url` path (those installs run no local gateway).

## Related work

Closes #2433. Upstream: [onecli/onecli#268](https://github.com/onecli/onecli/issues/268) (filed with proposed installer and compose-template fixes) and [onecli/onecli#263](https://github.com/onecli/onecli/issues/263); both still open on 2026-09-25. This patch protects NanoClaw users in the meantime and stays useful as defense in depth after upstream lands a fix.

`setup/onecli.ts` no longer exists on `main`: OneCLI setup moved into the `/add-onecli` skill on 2026-09-15 (d5c7cccc), and the skill does not pin these binds (checked 2026-09-25). Landing this means porting the change there and re-checking the compose lines against the current OneCLI release.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

Evidence from 2026-05-12, at b0cdcee4; not re-run since, and the target file has since moved (above).

- `setup/onecli.test.ts`, 19 tests on tempdir copies of the upstream compose shape with an injected `inspectFn` (no docker calls, no real OneCLI install):
  - `hardenOneCliBinds`: vanilla compose rewrite (admin + postgres to `127.0.0.1`, gateway untouched, marker prepended); marker idempotency (`reason: already_patched`); unrecognized layout no-op + warn (`reason: layout_unrecognized`, file untouched); missing file no-op + warn (`reason: compose_missing`); `config.json` `:10254` rewrite, `:10255` preserved, already-loopback no-op; `.env` `ONECLI_URL` `:10254` rewrite, `:10255` preserved; missing config + `.env` no-op.
  - `swapHostInAdminUrl`: admin URL with and without path; loopback unchanged; gateway URL unchanged; non-URL input unchanged.
  - `detectUnsafeOneCliBinds`: non-loopback via inspect; loopback via inspect; inspect fails → `.env` fallback; inspect fails + loopback `.env`; inspect fails + missing `.env`.
- Full suite 342/342, typecheck clean.
- A box patched by hand without the marker gets the marker and any stale URL rewritten on its first setup run; later runs are no-ops.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**On Linux, agents can no longer read other agents' access tokens from OneCLI's admin API.** Setup keeps the admin API and database off the Docker bridge on new installs, and warns when a reused OneCLI install is still exposed.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

This is the trust-boundary fix: agent containers (untrusted) could reach the OneCLI admin API and Postgres on the bridge. After it they reach only the proxy gateway. Setup edits OneCLI's compose file and the host's `~/.onecli/config.json` and `~/.onecli/.env`, and recreates the OneCLI containers with `docker compose up -d`.

prs.title: fix(add-onecli): publish OneCLI's admin API and Postgres on 127.0.0.1
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux, a new local OneCLI gateway now publishes its admin API and Postgres on `127.0.0.1`; only the gateway proxy stays on the Docker bridge.

- **Before**: on bare-metal Linux the OneCLI installer publishes the gateway, admin API and Postgres on the `docker0` address. Agent containers only need the gateway (`host.docker.internal:10255`).
- **Fresh install**: setup rewrites the stock admin and Postgres port entries to `127.0.0.1` and points `ONECLI_URL`, the CLI `api-host` and OneCLI's `APP_URL` at `http://127.0.0.1:10254`, keeping a public `APP_URL`. Non-stock layouts and non-Linux installs are left as installed.
- **Existing install**: binds are left alone; setup reports `ADMIN_NOT_LOOPBACK` (or `ADMIN_BINDINGS_UNKNOWN`), and the upgrade guide gives the manual steps.

## Related work

Supersedes #2434 (closes #2433), which targeted `setup/onecli.ts` before OneCLI setup moved into `/add-onecli` (d5c7cccc). Related: #3302 (thanks @wakqasahmed) saves the bridge bind for the gateway (#2903); main already does that, and this keeps it for `:10255`.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 38 new tests on the 1.42 and 1.45 compose shapes with Docker, installer and CLI doubled; `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/ setup/installer-shell.test.ts scripts/onecli-upgrade-guide.test.ts` -> 220/220; tsc clean.
- Live, on a fresh exe.dev VM (Ubuntu 24.04, Docker Engine, OneCLI 1.45.0), status codes only:
  - Fresh install from this branch: admin and Postgres on `127.0.0.1`, gateway on `172.17.0.1:10255`; from a default-bridge container `admin` 000, `gateway` 400; real agent replies.
  - Gateway installed by main (`b622660c`): setup reports `ADMIN_NOT_LOOPBACK`; after the guide's manual steps the probes give 000 / 400 and the agent replies.
  - `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_LOCKDOWN=true`: the agent replies.
  - Live runs used the first commit; the follow-up (non-Linux skip, shell `APP_URL`, guide) is covered by unit tests.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## Known limits

- An admin port customised at install time (`ONECLI_APP_PORT`) stays on the installer bind; setup reports it with `ADMIN_NOT_LOOPBACK`.
- On OneCLI 1.42 (no `INTERNAL_API_URL`), `APP_URL` is fixed at `http://127.0.0.1:10254`, the container's own port, because 1.42 calls its API through it; a public `APP_URL` applies from 1.45.
- Setup reads `~/.onecli/.env` and the stock compose project; `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` and `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` are not honored.
- An `ONECLI_URL` set in the service's own environment is not changed.
- One failed Docker inspection reports `ADMIN_BINDINGS_UNKNOWN`.
- The guide's probe assumes gateway port `10255` (the container name follows `ONECLI_GATEWAY_CONTAINER`).
- macOS and Windows installs are left as installed.
- `withEnvVar`, shared with NanoClaw's own `.env` writer, now also matches `export NAME=` and indented lines, and collapses duplicate keys into one line.

## User and release impact

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
**On Linux, new OneCLI installs publish the admin API and database on 127.0.0.1; only the gateway proxy stays on the Docker bridge.** Setup reports existing installs that still publish them elsewhere; the OneCLI upgrade guide has the manual steps.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Setup edits `~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml` and `~/.onecli/.env` on a fresh install and recreates the OneCLI containers. Docker is called with argument arrays, no shell.

The scripts run from the skill directory; apply copies only the upgrade guide (`docs/onecli-upgrades.md`).

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup's verify step now says why a Slack install failed, turns green after a good re-run, and reports when no owner can approve new chats.

- **Problem**: a failed background Slack job saved only `install_needs_attention` and dropped the reason. After a successful re-run, the saved job stayed failed, so verify stayed red. With no owner, "Channel registration skipped — no owner" dropped messages, and verify never mentioned it.
- **Fix**:
  - The worker stores the failure reason (one line, tokens removed); verify prints it as `SLACK_INSTALL_REASON`.
  - After a Socket Mode wire with the job's own app token and all companions applied, the job is marked complete.
  - Verify always prints `OWNER: present|missing`, with an `/init-first-agent` hint when a chat channel is set up and nobody can approve.
- **Out of scope**: an expired job that recovers is not re-reported to the portal, by design.

## Related work

No issue; found in an OSS user's WSL setup report (Slack job stuck after a missing jq).

prs.title: fix(onecli): warn when a remote gateway points agents at their own machine
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now warns, with the exact fix, when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send agents to their own machine.

- **Problem**: OneCLI tells agents to use the proxy at `GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, default `host.docker.internal:10255`. With a remote gateway that's the agent's own host, so every model call retries forever and the agent never replies, with no error.
- **Fix**: after setting up or reusing a remote gateway, `check-proxy.ts` reads the proxy address OneCLI hands an existing agent (`/v1/container-config`, which never creates an agent). If it points at the agent's own machine, the wizard shows a note with the `GATEWAY_BASE_URL=<gateway-host>:<port>` line and a recreate command that keeps the running image, bind address and ports. That command refuses an unpinned `latest`. "Is this machine" also counts a Docker bridge that is down, so a local bridge-bound gateway is never called remote.
- **Out of scope**: the docs steps (separate docs PR).

## Related work

No issue; found in the OneCLI 1.45 two-machine test (gateway and NanoClaw on separate LXCs).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/`: 150 pass. The recreate command runs against a stub `docker`: it keeps the published ports, keeps a digest pin, refuses `latest`, and changes nothing on a failed read.
- Live:
  - The two-machine 1.45 setup reproduced the hang.
  - Throwaway 1.42 gateways warned before the fix and stayed quiet after, with no agents created.
  - A Windows WSL install with a bridge-bound local gateway showed no false warning. An earlier run had one, which is the down-bridge fix above.
  - Evidence: `reviews/setup-next-2026-10-21/e2e/RESULTS.md` (local).
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup now warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine (they would never reply), and prints the exact GATEWAY_BASE_URL fix.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Uses the API token setup already holds. The note prints host and port only, never the token or the proxy's credentials, and keeps a non-plain hostname out of the shell command.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup steps no longer need jq, which stock Ubuntu and WSL don't ship.

- **Problem**: these skills pipe `curl` into `jq`, and nothing declares, checks or installs it. On WSL, Slack setup died at "Resolve your DM channel" with `jq: command not found`, which then left a failed install job and no owner.
- **Fix**: simple fields use the engine's `capture:var=.path` (as Mattermost did in #3809). Steps that build a prefix, pick from a list or write a file use a `node -e` one-liner. A good reply gives the same value as before. A bad one now fails where jq let it through: a revoked Slack token, a missing `im:write`, a refused Discord DM.
- **Out of scope**: `add-dial-tool` and `add-dial-number` still use jq. They are optional and run after setup.

## Related work

No issue; found in an OSS user's WSL setup report. The guard test below keeps jq out of every skill setup applies.

prs.title: fix(setup): reach Docker from the user service when the docker group was just added
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

When setup has just added the user to the docker group, the background user service can now reach Docker on the first run.

- **Problem**: the systemd user manager keeps the groups it had at login, and setup's linger keeps it alive, so logging out doesn't help. Setup's `setfacl` workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock Ubuntu and WSL lack. The service crash-loops on `docker.sock`, the first chat is skipped, and the printed fix (`sudo setfacl …`) can't run.
- **Fix**: in the service step, install `acl` non-interactively (`sudo -n`, apt only) when `setfacl` is missing. Then apply the socket ACL and re-check from the user manager before starting the service. When it still can't reach Docker, the wizard prints commands that work: the acl install only when needed, then the setfacl line and `systemctl --user restart <unit>`. It adds that a reboot (on WSL, `wsl --shutdown`) makes the group stick.
- **Out of scope**: the ACL resets when Docker restarts; the reboot note covers the lasting fix.

## Related work

Refs #2006
<!-- Merges cleanly with the sudo up-front PR in either order: this one keeps its platform checks inside setup/lib/docker-access-hint.ts. -->

## Change kind

- Live, with a user whose sudo needs a password and no Docker or acl:

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux and WSL, setup now asks for the sudo password once, in the open, before the progress spinner hides it.

- **Problem**: `nanoclaw.sh` runs the Node bootstrap under a spinner, and the container step installs or starts Docker inside a windowed step. sudo's prompt lands under that output, the user never sees it, and it times out (#2025).
- **Fix**: a pre-flight in `nanoclaw.sh` (`setup/lib/sudo-preflight.sh`) says what it will install, then runs `sudo -v` in the foreground. It asks only when setup will really use sudo: it follows `setup/lib/node-version.sh` (the #4183 minimums, uvx, version-manager Node), so an unpatched apt Node 22 asks and a patched or nvm-managed one doesn't. The container step asks again only if that answer has expired. On WSL, the docker-group hint says to run `wsl --shutdown`, since logging out doesn't refresh groups there.
- **Out of scope**: the service-side docker-group fix (separate PR).

## Related work

Closes #2025
Refs #2006

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/lib/sudo-preflight-shell.test.ts setup/lib/sudo-preflight.test.ts setup/auto.container-sudo.test.ts setup/lib/node-version.test.ts`: all pass. They cover Node missing or below the minimum (apt vs a version manager), patched Node off PATH, uvx, root, passwordless sudo, no TTY, `--skip container`, and refused sudo. prs.title: fix(delivery): one stuck channel send no longer silences a session until restart
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A hung send or channel no longer silences a session until restart, or slows other sessions.

- **Problem**: sends were awaited with no limit. One hung send blocked its session silently, and the shared poll tick waited on it.
- **Fix**: after 60 s a send is parked and logged (`Message delivery passed its deadline`), never re-sent while it might still land. A late failure, or no answer after 60 min, is retried. A tick waits at most 5 s per session. Discord acknowledgements time out after 10 s.
- **Limits**:
  - At most 8 background drains (kept on Ethan's call): more hung sessions slow ticks by about 60 s per 8.
  - A send landing after the 60 min give-up posts twice (3 sends at most).
  - A parked message can arrive after later ones. A session holds at most 3 parked sends.
  - A late landing can't change a row already marked failed; a mailbox error during a give-up can leave a stale attempt row.

## Related work

Refs #2665 (instance A). Overlaps #3059. Not covered: backoff, idempotency keys.

## Summary

The apply phase of an in-place plugin restamp writes to the group folder and the per-group skills overlay, which the agent container can modify while the restamp runs.

- **Problem**: each write did a separate directory check and then wrote to the path, so a directory replaced after the check could redirect the write.

prs.title: fix(db): read legacy container.json without following links
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The startup backfill reads a legacy group's `container.json` with a no-follow open instead of by path. The group folder is a host-owned mount source the container cannot swap, so only the `container.json` leaf is container-controlled.

- **Problem**: the one-time backfill for groups without a `container_configs` row read `container.json` by path, so a symlink or special file at that name was followed, a bad file's text reached the log, and `null` JSON stopped startup.
- **Fix**: open the leaf `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` (regular files only); skip anything else with a warning and create the default row; degrade a read error to defaults instead of aborting startup; log a generic parse reason; treat non-object JSON as invalid.
- **Out of scope**: the spawn-time writer `materializeContainerJson` (it also writes `container.json` by path — tracked as a separate follow-up, see note) and other readers of the group folder.

## Related work

No linked issue. Maintainer hardening; the diff and its tests are the review surface.

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

- Full `vitest run`, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint` (0 errors), `format:check` -> clean apart from load-dependent git-integration timeouts (`scripts/update/*` and similar) that pass in isolation.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The OneCLI upgrade guide now deletes the Dial key only when the upgrade could hand it to agents that were kept away from Dial, not on every upgrade.

- **Problem**: since https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094 and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4095 the guide says "on every upgrade, delete any Dial key". On a gateway that already converted (1.44+), that removes working Dial from every agent on the gateway, other installs included, until each re-runs `/add-dial-tool`. A beta install on rc.2 reported it.
- **Fix**: a read-only `dial-key-check.sh`. It prints `keep` on a converted gateway or with no Dial key. On a verified local 1.42/1.43 gateway it prints `delete` only when the conversion removes a rule on the Dial host or a Dial key, or a `block` default. Where old pre-1.42 rules may decide, it prints `delete`, since those cannot be read in full. That covers older than 1.42 (`unknown` means 1.24 to 1.38), `POLICY_ENFORCE_V2` off, or a container it cannot match to `$GW`. `--delete` repeats the check and reads the version again before each delete.
- **Already converted** with the Dial rule in place: re-run `/add-dial-tool` and detach leftover grants by hand, never delete.

## Related work

Follow-up to https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4095 and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4189. No issue: found from a live install's report. The stable 2026.10.1 notes need the same change; the release PR carries it.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `onecli-upgrade-guide` and `add-dial-tool-scope`: 238/238. Cases cover keep, delete and stop, Dial and non-Dial findings, old and kill-switch gateways, container matching, a version change mid-delete, hostile names and ids, and three shells. Full vitest: 4196 passed; 36 tests in 11 git-heavy files time out at 5 s on this Mac tonight, and the same files time out on `origin/main` too (20 of 308); they pass alone. `tsc` passes; lint has 0 errors.
- Real `onecli` 2.11.0, read-only, against a local 1.42.0 gateway with a fake Dial key injected by a wrapper that refuses deletes: the container is matched, both policies are read, and it prints `keep`, for `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`. A remote `DOCKER_HOST` prints `delete` with its reason.
- Checked against OneCLI source v1.0 to v1.45: which versions report `unknown`, the conversion predicate, the host matcher, the 1.42 cutover and kill switch, and the project-scoped delete.
- Codex, 13 rounds, 31 findings: 28 fixed, 2 refuted, 1 documented limit; the last round was clean. The gambi remote review's 3 points are folded in. Refuted twice: a gateway that converts between the last version read and a delete had the Dial rule in place, so that delete is still the one needed.

prs.title: ci: add Dependabot for Actions, pnpm, bun, docker and skill pins; remove the inert Renovate config
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Turns on Dependabot version updates for every manifest it can read, behind a release-age cooldown, and removes the Renovate config that never ran.

- **Problem**: main has no `dependabot.yml`. Alerts are on but security-update PRs are off, so a fixed version reaches us only when someone bumps it by hand, as with this week's Node.js base image. On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a credential stealer to PyPI and Docker Hub for about two hours ([incident](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-incident-oct-21-2026)); a cooldown keeps a release like that out.
- **Fix**: weekly entries for GitHub Actions, the root pnpm project, `container/agent-runner` (bun), the `container/Dockerfile` base image, and the skill pins. Cooldown is 7 days, 14 for majors and agent-runner minors (its 0.x SDKs break on a minor), 3 for the base image; never below pnpm's 3-day gate. Minor/patch bumps are grouped, except root production and agent-runner runtime deps (one PR each, per CLAUDE.md), so the agent SDK and `claude-code` (skill pins) move in separate PRs. Majors come alone; nothing merges itself. `chat` moves only with its `@chat-adapter/*` pins; Node and `@types/node` majors wait for a deliberate Node move.
- **Out of scope**: turning on security-update PRs (a repo setting); the Dockerfile's `BUN_VERSION`, `PNPM_VERSION` and `NPM_VERSION` args and `# syntax` line; skill Dockerfiles and `go.mod` (listed in `not-covered.json`).

## Related work

No issue. Follows https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3968 (actions pinned by SHA) and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4007 (skill-pins manifest, merged).

- Checked against dependabot-core: it parses this `bun.lock` format, and with `pnpm@10.34.5` it applies the larger of the cooldown and our 4320-minute gate to transitive versions too. Bun has no such transitive gate.
- Renovate: no PRs, `renovate/*` branches or dashboard issue since the file landed 2026-07-29.
- Docker tracks only a pinned `FROM`; a floating `node:22-slim` gets no PRs. https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4183 pinned `node:22.23.4-slim@sha256:…` on main, so the first run moves tag and digest together.
