prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-copilot GitHub Copilot SDK provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an upstream-ready `/add-copilot` provider skill that installs GitHub Copilot as a NanoClaw runtime while keeping the device-login token in the credential gateway.
- **Problem**: Prior Copilot-provider approaches passed the token through environment or container state, which widened the credential boundary.
- **Fix**: The provider sends only a non-secret SDK placeholder; the gateway injects the real token for the licensed Copilot API host (through the gateway-neutral credential store) and for `/copilot_internal/*` on `api.github.com`.
- **Out of scope**: Glob path scoping in the gateway-neutral credential store; the helper keeps a OneCLI call for the one credential that needs it (see Notes).

## Related work

No issue closes. This overlaps with nanocoai/nanoclaw#399, nanocoai/nanoclaw#1351, and nanocoai/nanoclaw#1704: those older approaches passed the token via env/container surfaces, while this provider keeps it in the gateway.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-copilot/SKILL.md` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts --testNamePattern 'add-copilot|provider skill descriptors'` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --all add-copilot` -> passed; applied in a disposable checkout, installed `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.14`, ran provider-contract verification and installed payload tests, and built the local image.
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> passed.
- `pnpm run lint` -> passed with existing warnings only.
- `pnpm run format:check` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> passed.
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` -> passed: 513 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail.
- Live, on a real install (OneCLI gateway, business Copilot plan): a CLI-channel message got a streamed reply; the agent ran a shell tool and the `send_message` MCP tool, and resumed the session on the next message. The container's env, every `/proc/*/environ`, and the Copilot state dir held no real token, only the placeholder.
- `pnpm test` -> failed in unrelated timeout/git-fixture tests; clean `upstream/main` (`c2663b17`) fails the same command in the same environment with unrelated timeouts and `safe.bareRepository` fixture failure.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Adds `/add-copilot`, a GitHub Copilot SDK provider skill that authenticates through the credential gateway instead of container-readable tokens.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- The Copilot device-login token never enters the container; the SDK receives a non-secret placeholder and ambient GitHub token env vars are stripped.
- `api.github.com` is not in `modelDomains`; the OneCLI grant for that host is path-scoped to `/copilot_internal/*`.
- The helper is OneCLI-only and macOS-keychain-only, and fails clearly elsewhere.
- The licensed Copilot API credential goes through `getCredentialStore().connection()` (#4106's seam): host-wide, `Authorization: Bearer {value}`, `proxyValue` = the container's placeholder (`payload/scripts/copilot-login.ts` `copilotApiTarget`, kept in sync with the container by a test).
- Two pieces stay OneCLI-specific because the seam cannot express them. The `api.github.com` secret must cover every path under `/copilot_internal/`: the Copilot CLI calls several undocumented paths there (token exchange, user, entitlement checks), and the set changes between CLI versions. The seam limits a credential to one exact path, so a list of exact paths would break silently on the next CLI bump, and a host-wide grant would expose the token's repo scopes to all of `api.github.com`. The individual-endpoint block rule has no neutral form yet.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves the agent image and CI from Bun 1.4.0 to 1.4.4, which drops the eMudhra intermediates revoked on 18 Oct.

- **Problem**: Bun ships its own root store. On 1.4.0, a fetch of `https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` returns 200. 1.4.4 ([oven-sh/bun#46300](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46300), [oven-sh/bun#46159](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46159)) fails it with `CERT_REVOKED`.
- **Fix**: `BUN_VERSION=1.4.4` in `container/Dockerfile`, plus a build step that fails unless `bun --version` equals the pin. CI, release and registry-skills move to 1.4.4. The three registry-skills jobs on 1.3.12 move too: nothing says they mimic old installs. https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3586 added them on a branch cut before https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3698 moved CI to 1.4.0.
- **Out of scope**: OneCLI intercepts agent HTTPS (the agent sees `OneCLI Local Gateway CA`), so the gateway checks the real chain, not Bun. Gateway 1.45.0, the latest tag, still returns 200 for that site. Hardened installs get Bun from Echo's image. The `channels` branch has the same pins; they follow with the next sync.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Cuts the wait for a pull request's required checks from about 7.5 minutes to about 2.5, without taking anything off the PR path.
- **Problem**: the skills gate ran 22 skill jobs four at a time, and each provider skill built the agent image twice (once per install of its add-remove-add proof); the host suite ran as one 85-second job per Node version.
- **CI workflow**: static checks, host tests and container tests get their own jobs; the host suite runs in four vitest shards per Node version, every file in exactly one shard. Gate: 165 s -> 80 s.
- **Skills gate**: no parallel cap; provider skill jobs build the image through a buildx builder with a layer cache kept by `actions/cache` (written back only on a miss) and never load it, since nothing runs the image there. Gate: 448 s -> 146 s.
- **Skill test**: the second install of the round trip skips its `build` and `test` effects; the byte-for-byte snapshot already proves it identical to the first.
- **Skills gate, continued**: the skill matrix is written into the workflow so every skill job starts with the run; discovery stays as a guard that fails when the matrix and the skill directories differ, and a skill whose registry source is missing skips itself. The legacy-provider refresh runs one job per provider plus one with both in the same tree (the two skills edit the same provider barrels), each with its own image cache key; the payload switch is its own job. The host build is incremental, so the verifier's rebuild takes a second.
- **Cursor probe**: the gateway probe behind the HTTP/2 refusal test asks the SDK not to retry the refused transport (1, 2, 4, 8 s backoffs), which it paid twice per install. Production behaviour unchanged.
- **Trade**: skill jobs now resolve the providers and channels commits themselves instead of taking one pinned pair from discovery, so a push to those branches during a run can reach some jobs and not others; promotion dispatches still pin through their inputs.
- **Out of scope**: the two provider skill jobs sit at about 110 s each (setup, the skill's own build and tests, the contract verifier, a cached image build, remove and re-add), and about 30 s of the gate's wall clock is the chain of two small verdict jobs after them.

prs.title: fix(delivery): carry a mime type on outbound files so Teams accepts them
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What** — adds an optional `mimeType` to `OutboundFile`, derives it from the filename extension where the outbox is read, and stops the chat-sdk bridge dropping it on the way to the adapter.

**Why** — an agent that produces an image can't deliver it on Teams. Every `send_file` with a PNG fails, and the agent is never told: `send_file` reports success as soon as the row is written, and the failure happens later on the host's delivery poll. From the agent's side the file simply never arrives.

`OutboundFile` carried only `{ filename, data }`, and the bridge forwarded exactly those two fields. `@chat-adapter/teams` then does:

```js
const mimeType = file.mimeType || "application/octet-stream";
const dataUri = bufferToDataUri(buffer, mimeType);
```

so a PNG goes out as `contentUrl: "data:application/octet-stream;base64,..."` and Teams rejects the whole activity with `400 Bad Request`.

Worth stating explicitly, because it's the tempting reading for a 133KB image: **this is not the size limit.** Teams answers oversize with `413`/`MessageSizeTooBig`, and base64 image payloads are [explicitly excluded](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/format-your-bot-messages) from its 100KB activity budget. A 400 is the content type.

**How it works** — `mimeForFilename()` in `attachment-naming.ts`, called from `readOutboxFiles()`; the bridge forwards the field in both of its file-upload paths. `EXT_TO_MIME` is derived from the existing `MIME_TO_EXT` rather than written out a second time, with a round-trip test, so the inbound and outbound tables can't drift.

It returns `undefined` for unrecognized extensions rather than guessing `application/octet-stream`. Adapters already have that fallback, and handing them a guess dressed as a fact is what caused this.

**How it was tested** — typecheck clean and 84 tests green on this branch standing alone on `main`. Then on a live install: the same PNG that had failed three times with a 400 delivered on the first retry after the fix — `Message delivered ... channelType="teams" fileCount=1`, outbox cleared, no error.

## Related

- #1988 fixes the same class of bug one adapter down, with an extension→mimetype map inside `src/channels/whatsapp.ts`. This addresses it once at the shared seam instead, which covers Teams and every other adapter that has to declare a content type — and would make that local map redundant. Happy to rebase around whichever you'd rather land first.
- Touches `src/session-manager.ts` and `src/host-core.test.ts`, which #3505 also moves — likely a small conflict depending on merge order.

prs.title: fix(docker-driver): wait out in-flight --rm auto-removal on stop
prs.body:
## Summary

Stops `DockerHandle.stop()` from reporting a failed teardown when Docker's own `--rm` auto-removal is still finishing.

- **Problem**: agent containers are created with `--rm`. `stop()` runs `docker stop`, which starts Docker's auto-removal, then `docker rm --force`, which the daemon rejects while that removal is in flight. `#confirmRemoved` probes `docker ps` once, still sees the container, and throws `session realization failed: unknown`. The container is gone a few milliseconds later.
- **Evidence**: on one Docker Desktop install, 60 of 164 absolute-ceiling kills over several days logged `Failed to stop session`. In one incident the daemon log shows the `ps` probe at `21:31:59.861` and "A container has been removed" at `.876`. A second `stop()` from `finishAndResolve` succeeds, so nothing leaks; the cost is a false error and a teardown marked incomplete.
- **Fix**: `#confirmRemoved` polls the same probe up to 10 times, 200 ms apart, and returns once the container is gone. A failing probe (daemon down) still throws at once, unretried, so auto-removal stays distinguishable from an outage. The original `rm` error is thrown only if the container is still there after about 2 s.
- **Concurrency**: the poll makes `stop()` yield, so concurrent `stop()` calls on one handle now share one teardown promise. Without that, a second kill could finish first, let the session respawn under the same deterministic container name, and the first poll would then see the new container. A failed teardown is not cached, so the retry in `finishAndResolve` still works.
- **Out of scope**: a throw while removing the main container still skips auxiliary container and private network cleanup in `stop()`. That predates this change.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `confirmRemoved`, "removal in progress", "session realization failed"). The change is limited to the Docker driver's stop path and its fake CLI.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/` -> 5 files, 152 tests passed
- `pnpm test` -> 274 files passed, 2 skipped; 3357 tests passed, 15 skipped
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> clean
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed files -> 0 errors, same 18 warnings as before the change
- New tests in `src/drivers/docker-driver.test.ts` (`removal racing Docker auto-removal`): in-flight removal resolves after 2 probes; a container that never goes rejects as `unknown` after 10 probes; a failing probe rejects as `runtime-unavailable` after 1 probe; concurrent stops issue one `stop` and one `rm`; a stop after a failed stop retries. The existing force-remove test now also asserts no probe runs when `rm` succeeds.
- With the `docker-driver.ts` change reverted, 3 of the new tests fail (in-flight removal, never removed, concurrent stops).
- `FakeCli` gains an optional `once` flag on a scripted response, used by the new tests.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)


prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Agent reactions (and edits of inbound messages) reach the platform with the platform's message id, not the session row id.

- **Problem**: the router stores inbound rows as `<platform msg id>:<agent group id>` (`messageIdForAgent`). `add_reaction` hands that row id back as the target, so Telegram gets `<chat>:<msg>:ag-…`, answers `message to react not found`, and the reaction is dropped after 3 retries. The tool already reported success to the agent.
- **Fix**: `deliverMessage` strips a trailing `:<session agent group id>` from `messageId` of any `operation` payload before handing it to the adapter. Plain chat messages pass through byte-identical.
- **Why host-side**: the host knows the session's agent group exactly, so no `:ag-` pattern guessing, and no container image rebuild.

## Summary

Codex agents behind OneCLI can generate images on their ChatGPT subscription, and the images reach the chat.

When Codex reports a saved image mid-turn, the Codex provider steers a one-line note with the path into that same turn, and the agent sends the file with `send_file`. The unused image-directory snapshot and `file` events are removed. No core change.
- **Out of scope**: Iron Proxy's stand-in already claims `plus`, so Iron agents already had the tool; unchanged. A sub-agent's image gets the note in the sub-agent's own turn and reaches the chat only if that agent can `send_file`; sub-agent turn handling is #4165.

## Summary

Keeps keys off `onecli`'s command line and out of its error output.

- **Problem**: setup ran `onecli secrets create --value <key>` and `onecli auth login --api-key <key>`; a failed call's error repeats that command line.
- **Fix**: new `secret-input.ts` passes the value by a 0600 temp file (`--file`) or stdin (`auth login`), and rethrows a failure redacted, even escaped, encoded or line-wrapped. `register-claude-token.sh` now only captures the token; `auth.ts` saves it like a pasted one.
- **Agent steps**: `/add-vercel` and `/migrate-from-openclaw` put the key in a private temp dir by file, never in a command, drop OneCLI's output, and clean up on failure. `/add-vercel`'s save also clears your own token dirs left over 10 minutes by a run that stopped (`find -H`, since macOS `/tmp` is a symlink). Sign-in hints pipe the key into `onecli auth login` and print "sign-in failed" when it fails. The unused `vaultCreateCommand` is gone.
- **Out of scope** (follow-ups): skill-engine `{{secret}}` answers in `bash -c`, and `docker -e` env.

## Related work

Builds on #4094 (merged), which rewrote the same add-onecli scripts. Codex auth, `/add-dial-tool` and `/add-tavily-tool` already use `--file` (onecli CLI 2.2.5+, pinned since June).

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Two fixes to `/add-dial-tool`'s OneCLI grants steps. Both shipped in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4095 (squash `27a0ef7c`, merged today) and are in no release yet.

- **Project mismatch**: `dial-secret.ts` wrote the Dial key in NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID`, while the `onecli` CLI attached the grants in its own project. When the two differed, the write could overwrite another project's Dial key and the grant then failed. It now reads the CLI's effective project (`onecli config get project`, which includes `ONECLI_PROJECT`) and stops before writing when they differ, or when that read answers without a readable value. A CLI without a project setting falls back to `ONECLI_PROJECT`.
- **Group names**: the attach step splits `id<TAB>name` lines, so a group name containing a newline or tab could read as another group's id. Choosing `none` then took the Dial key from another install's agent on the same gateway. Names are flattened before the split, and a group id outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` stops the step. `onecli agents create --name` now gets the flattened name, so a new OneCLI agent's name can differ slightly from its group's.

## Related work

Follow-up to https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4095 and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094.

Each new refusal failed before the fix.
- Real CLI 2.11.0 (on the 1.45 test VM): `onecli config get project` prints `{"hint": …, "key": "project", "value": ""}`, and with `ONECLI_PROJECT=envproj` set it prints `"value": "envproj"`.

prs.title: feat(providers): add pi agent provider (/add-pi payload skill)
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - README, CONTRIBUTING, or docs only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (pi Coding Agent) as an optional agent provider, installable with the `/add-pi` skill. This is the restructured version of #3857, which targeted the `providers` branch. It now ships the way `/add-opencode` does on `main`: the skill carries its provider as a payload and needs no separate branch.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 1.3.0). No `pi serve` process and no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in process (stdio + Streamable HTTP, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, JSON-Schema `pattern` stripped because some model APIs reject the regex dialects MCP servers ship).
- `payload/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (host) + `payload/container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (runtime) — seam version 1. The host contract declares the `AGENTS.md` project document, the group's `.pi-shared` state volume mounted at the agentDir, pi's skill backings/views, and the `auth.json` stub file; the runtime contract declares the permission stance, `textDelivery: 'result'`, and XML slash-command formatting.
- `payload/setup/providers/pi.ts` — the setup picker entry, gateway auth hook, and install check.
- `payload/src/providers/pi.ts` — the host container-config adapter (`PI_AGENT_DIR`, plus optional `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS` / `PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` / `PI_DEFAULT_MODEL`).

**How the review points from #3857 are handled**

1. **Payload skill on `main`.** The whole provider lives under `.claude/skills/add-pi/` (`SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `REMOVE.md`, `apply-fixtures.json`, `payload/`). `SKILL.md` is a parser-applyable set of `nc:` directives: copy the payload, append five barrel imports (host/container providers, host/container contracts, setup), install the pinned runner dependency, build, test. No branch fetch, no `PI_REF`, no per-group overlay propagation. `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` lists the newly offered skill.
2. **Credentials come through the gateway.** No personal `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` is copied anywhere. The container writes fixed `gateway-managed` placeholders into the group's pi agentDir before each session open (`payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi-auth.ts`), and the selected gateway replaces them on the wire by destination host. ChatGPT subscription auth is pi's `openai-codex` provider, which reuses the gateway's Codex/ChatGPT login; because pi decodes the access token for the account id, the placeholder is a syntactically valid JWT carrying the placeholder claim. API-key providers get a placeholder `api_key` entry, and `provider-auth pi` stores the real key through `getCredentialStore().connection(target)` (observing the entry first, as the seam requires), recording the provider ids in `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS`. A real login already in the agentDir is never overwritten.
3. **`bun.lock` / npm registry.** The skill no longer commits `container/agent-runner/package.json` or `bun.lock`; the pinned dependency is installed at apply time by the `nc:dep` directive, and the pin is registered in `.github/skill-pins` so Dependabot tracks it and `skill-pins:sync` writes future bumps back into SKILL.md. Locally regenerating that install against the default npm registry produces a lock with zero `registry.npmmirror.com` URLs (the #3857 lock had 260).

**Model selection follows the SDK, not a hardcoded id.** Model ids change between pi releases (0.85.1 ships `deepseek-v4-flash`; 1.3.0 calls it `deepseek-flash`), so the provider resolves the start provider/model from pi's own runtime catalog (`getAvailableSnapshot` / `getModel`) and writes that into `settings.json`. Operator-authored values are never overwritten. Verified across both versions with no code change.

**Two things a reviewer should know**

- **The secret still has to be granted to the agent.** The credential seam stores secrets but never assigns them, and `/add-opencode` has the same manual step ("follow the selected gateway skill to grant it to agents"). OneCLI's `secretMode` is `selective`, so an ungranted key reaches the provider as `401 access restricted`. SKILL.md documents it.
- **Setup's own ping is not proof the model call worked.** It reports "Your assistant is ready" whenever the chat command exits 0 with any output, and a failed pi turn answers with the generic "The agent run failed" notice. Verify with a real reply and `continuation:pi` instead; SKILL.md says so explicitly.

**How it was tested**

- `scripts/provider-contract-verifier.ts --required-declared pi` — **passed** (host deps, runtime deps, host build, host provider-contract tests, runtime typecheck, runtime provider-contract tests, host/runtime contract inventories, runtime conformance test files).
- Container suite: **673 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**. Host suite: **3613 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**. `skill-pins:check` clean.
- End-to-end on a fresh clone of this branch: `bash nanoclaw.sh` → pick pi → DeepSeek key stored in the gateway → skill applied (14 files, 5 barrels, pin 1.3.0, image SDK 1.3.0) → group switched to pi → real reply, session continuation, and `continuation:pi` in the session's `outbound.db` `session_state`. A WeChat channel was installed onto the same install afterwards, so the channel/provider split was exercised too.
- Testing was done against a OneCLI gateway at 1.45.0 (newer than the 1.42.0 pin in `/add-onecli`), so the grant step used its `PUT /v1/agents/<id>/grants/secrets/<id>` API. This payload itself calls no gateway management API — only the credential seam — so the pinned 1.42.0 gateway is unaffected.

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Configure credentials with `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth pi` (ChatGPT via the gateway's Codex login, or a stored API key), then grant the secret per the gateway's skill. Model selection lives in the group's `data/v2-sessions/<group>/.pi-shared/settings.json`.

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow was stuck in `action_required` on #3857 (first-time contributor). It needs a maintainer approval click to run here too. #3857 is superseded by this PR; it can stay open until this one merges.

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased after #4104 (`/add-codex` payload), #4107 (`/add-cursor` payload), #4105, #4106 and #3980 landed. Two conflicts, both list-append in shared files: `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` now expects `codex, cursor, opencode, pi`, and `.github/skill-pins/package.json` carries this branch's pin alongside upstream's.

Upstream changes that touch this work, checked rather than assumed:

- **#3980 (first-chat ping)** fixed the very problem SKILL.md used to warn about: a failed pi turn's notice is now scored as a failed first chat instead of a green result. The doc now states the post-#3980 behaviour.
- **#4105 (shared exchange archive)** is for providers whose harness keeps no on-disk transcript. pi's session JSONL *is* its transcript — the continuation token is that file's path — so it needs no archiver, unlike Codex.
- **#4106 (credential connection path)** is unnecessary here: pi's provider entry is a key on exactly one host, so host-scoped injection is what we want.
- **#4104 / #4107** moved Codex and Cursor to the same payload-skill shape this PR uses, so the structure now matches three siblings.

Verification on the rebased branch: container `bun run typecheck` clean and the pi suites at 65 pass; host `tsc --noEmit` clean; host `vitest run` has one failure in `setup/gateways/selection.test.ts` ("detects an installed gateway from inside a nested pnpm") that reproduces on a clean `upstream/main` tree with this payload removed — it is a pre-existing flake under parallel load, not a regression here.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (274)
- [x] I tested this skill by applying it onto current `main`, running the provider-contract verifier, and completing a real end-to-end install on a fresh clone

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Ports `/add-dial-tool` to OneCLI agent grants so Dial keeps working after the 1.45 pin move in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094. Merge right after it.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ the project policy API and secret lists the skill used answer `410`, so it stops at its 1.42 gate and `/add-dial`'s tool offer aborts setup. The gateway's upgrade also deletes `Dial: blocked agents` and gives Dial to every agent, so the upgrade guide now deletes the key first and the re-run recreates it.
- **Fix**: `dial-secret.ts` updates the Dial key in place (its id and grants stay), then the skill detaches it from this install's unchosen groups and attaches it to the chosen ones, which also re-narrows an upgraded install. It runs the shared OneCLI grants check (a 1.45 release, no agent still in `all` mode, a CLI with `agents grants`). `dial-policy.ts` is gone.
- **Behavior change**: new groups never get Dial until the skill runs again. With no agents yet, `/add-dial` installs the tool with nobody holding the key and says to run `/add-dial-tool` later.
- **Trade-off**: the key is updated in place so its grants stay. On a gateway shared by two installs, a re-run signed in to a different Dial account moves every agent holding the key to that account; the skill now warns before it. Deleting and recreating the key would avoid that, but drops every grant.

## Related work

Stacked on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094 (base is its branch). Replaces the policy path from https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052 (and #4036's guard). Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `add-dial-tool-scope`, `skill-conformance` and `dial-secret` tests (322) run the skill's real one-liners against stateful `onecli`/`ncl` stubs; the upgrade guide's Dial delete runs under sh, bash and zsh; full vitest passes.
- Covered: chosen-only attach, withhold before attach, agent created only for a chosen group, re-narrowing after the upgrade, other installs' agents untouched, an agent list in either shape (an unreadable list or incomplete entry fails), the gate, removal. Each failed when its rule was broken on purpose.
- VM end to end on 1.45 (no real Dial account): chosen groups get the key, others get the gateway's `403 access_restricted`, and re-running after a 1.42 upgrade re-narrows Dial.

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
`/add-dial-tool` works on OneCLI 1.45: it gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose. If you use it, delete the Dial key before upgrading the gateway (docs/onecli-upgrades.md has the command), then re-run `/add-dial-tool`; Dial is off for those few minutes instead of open to every agent. New groups get Dial only when you add them. Ships in the same release as the OneCLI 1.45 pin move (#4094), which it needs.
```

Dial spends money and reaches real people. The key is now withheld by default and attached per group; agents that are not this install's groups are never touched.

prs.title: fix(security): require Node's October 2026 security releases in setup and the agent image
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes new and rebuilt installs run Node with the [October 21, 2026 security releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases), which fix a Brotli decoder RCE that `fetch()` reaches (CVE-2026-111497) and three TLS hostname-check bypasses.

- **Problem**: the agent image used `FROM node:22-slim`, and `container/build.sh` does not pass `--pull`, so a rebuild can reuse a cached unpatched base. Setup accepted any Node >= 22.
- **Fix**: pin `node:22.23.4-slim` by multi-arch digest (dropping the npm bump the new base already ships). Setup requires 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1: `install-node.sh` upgrades an older one the way it already installs Node, refuses end-of-life 23 / 25 and pre-release builds, and otherwise stops with a plain sentence; on Linux without uvx it leaves a Node from a version manager (nvm, fnm, volta, asdf, n) alone and says which version to install there, instead of running sudo and NodeSource. `nanoclaw.sh` and `migrate-v2.sh` repeat `setup.sh`'s Node choice, since a keg-only `node@22` is not on their PATH and the service is registered with their PATH Node.
- **Out of scope**: the hardened image (Echo rebuilds it), CI runners (cached 22.23.3 / 24.21.0, no version pinned), host webhooks (bodies are never decompressed), `package.json` engines (stays `>=22`; nothing enforces it, setup does).

## Related work

No issue; the public advisory above is the source. #4094 and #4160 narrow what a hijacked agent can reach.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 3,879 passed; one 5 s load timeout in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch, passes alone. `tsc`, `format:check`, `skill-pins:check` clean.
- `setup/lib/node-version.test.ts` runs the real scripts with stub node / brew / apt-get on a sealed PATH, under bash 3.2 locally and bash 5 in CI; `container/base-image.test.ts` keeps the base digest-pinned at or above the minimum.
- Base image read from the registry: the digest is the multi-arch index, and both its amd64 and arm64 layers have Node 22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, tar 7.5.22.
- Fresh install of `a604850a4` on an amd64 exe.dev VM: the image built from that digest runs Node v22.23.4, and setup, service, ping and verify passed; `install-node.sh`'s uvx path and the end-of-life refusal ran there too.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- Maintainers own CHANGELOG.md — do not edit it in this PR. -->
- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Security: Node.js October 2026 security releases.** The agent image now builds on Node 22.23.4 (pinned by digest), and setup requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer; it refuses end-of-life 23 and 25. Existing installs: run `/update-nanoclaw` (it rebuilds the agent image, or pulls it on hardened-image installs once the new image is listed), then `bash setup/install-node.sh` to update the host Node. On Linux that replaces Node in place, so restarting NanoClaw is enough; on a Mac, or whenever `command -v node` now points somewhere new, re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses it. If Node comes from a version manager (nvm, fnm, volta, asdf), update it there. Groups with extra packages: `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild`.
```

prs.title: feat(add-onecli): OneCLI 1.45 grants; new groups get only their model credential
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves NanoClaw to OneCLI gateway 1.45.0 and CLI 2.11.0, the required stop before 2.x, and decides what a new agent group may use now that 1.44+ starts every agent with no grants. Supersedes #4082 and keeps chiptoe-svg's commits.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ a new group's OneCLI agent holds nothing, so it cannot reach its model. Working out a group's secrets from other agents' grants widens or narrows access depending on history nobody can see.
- **Fix**: NanoClaw records the id of each model credential its provider logins save, per install, and on every spawn attaches the ones for the provider the group runs (an older install with nothing recorded is matched once, by the names NanoClaw writes only, and duplicate names are refused; a model key under another name is never adopted, and the host logs an error naming it and the login that records this install's own). Tool secrets and app connections are opt-in: `/add-vercel` now asks which groups and picks its token by host, and Tavily's paid-key upgrade attaches its key to the group. A new `pre-upgrade-check.sh` runs before the pin is saved and stops on anything the conversion deletes or changes.
- **Spawn cost**: each spawn now makes three admin-API calls (agents, grants, secrets) plus one PUT per missing grant. If one fails, that spawn fails and the next spawn retries.
- **Out of scope**: `/add-dial-tool` (stacked PR on `feat/dial-tool-grants`, merges in the same sitting; if this lands without it, the pre-upgrade check still stops an install with Dial on Dial's block rule), per-group model keys (#3205), docs portal pages.

## Related work

Supersedes https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082. Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3205, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4036.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Merged `main` at `ce013d0f` (the setup paste prompt from #4161 now records the saved key). add-onecli payload tests applied to a clean export (SDK 2.2.1), plus `tsc` over the applied files: 84/84; add-onecli setup scripts 73/73. Full vitest and `tsc` pass; files that timed out under parallel load pass when run alone.
- Tests cover each rule (model credential only, the spawn path passing the provider, repair on the next spawn, provider switch, late login, one-time name match only when nothing is recorded, an older key under another name reported with its fix but not adopted, duplicate names refused, `/add-vercel` token choice, the record lock, 1.42 no-op, every upgrade-check exit) and failed when the rule was broken on purpose.
- VM end to end, all pass: fresh 1.45 install, 1.42 to 1.45 upgrade (check stops before the pin is saved, 0 failed conversions), restore rollback, `/add-codex` after groups exist plus a provider switch.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
[BREAKING] The OneCLI gateway pin moves to 1.45.0 (CLI 2.11.0). Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown`. Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs. Fix: follow docs/onecli-upgrades.md before restarting; its check stops if the conversion would delete your rules. Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential. On a 1.42 gateway, new groups still get every key until the gateway is upgraded. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`) so NanoClaw records it. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Credential scope narrows: a new group gets only its own provider's credential. The record holds secret ids only (`data/onecli/provider-credentials.json`, mode 0600); no secret value passes through NanoClaw. Core gains one provider-name field; it names no provider or gateway.

## What

Adds a `WEBHOOK_HOST` environment variable to the webhook server.  Default remains `0.0.0.0`, so existing deployments are byte-for-byte unaffected.

## Why

`webhook-server.ts` hardcodes `server.listen(port, '0.0.0.0')`, so the server is exposed on every interface even for deployments that receive no direct webhooks — e.g. Telegram via long-polling against a local bot-api server, or setups that front the webhook port with a reverse proxy / tunnel.  Operators who want to bind to loopback (or one specific interface) currently cannot.

## Changes

- `src/webhook-server.ts`: read `WEBHOOK_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`), pass to `listen()`, include `host` in the startup log line (+4/-2)
- `src/webhook-server.test.ts`: one new test following the file's existing real-server/fixed-port conventions — sets `WEBHOOK_HOST=127.0.0.1`, asserts the server still serves on loopback, restores env in `finally`

prs.title: fix(webhook-server): default-bind to loopback instead of 0.0.0.0
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code

## Description

The webhook server in `src/webhook-server.ts` currently binds to `0.0.0.0`, exposing the HTTP listener to every interface on the host. Most installs don't actually need this — the Chat-SDK Telegram adapter uses long polling, and operators who genuinely need an externally-reachable webhook are typically fronting it with a reverse proxy on a different port anyway.

This refactor extracts `resolveListenConfig()` so the bind address is environment-driven and unit-testable. Defaults to `127.0.0.1` so the port is not exposed to the LAN; operators who need external exposure can opt in with `WEBHOOK_BIND=0.0.0.0` (or a specific interface IP).

## Diff

```ts
// src/webhook-server.ts
const DEFAULT_BIND = '127.0.0.1';

export function resolveListenConfig(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): { port: number; bind: string } {
  const portRaw = env.WEBHOOK_PORT;
  const port = portRaw ? parseInt(portRaw, 10) : DEFAULT_PORT;
  const bind = env.WEBHOOK_BIND || DEFAULT_BIND;
  return { port, bind };
}

// ensureServer():
const { port, bind } = resolveListenConfig(process.env);
// ...
server.listen(port, bind, () => {
  log.info('Webhook server started', { port, bind, adapters: [...routes.keys()] });
});
```

## Tests

`src/webhook-server.test.ts` (new) — four cases on `resolveListenConfig`:

- Default port + loopback when both env vars unset
- Honors `WEBHOOK_PORT` when set
- Honors `WEBHOOK_BIND` for opt-in external exposure
- Treats empty-string `WEBHOOK_BIND` as unset (so an accidental `WEBHOOK_BIND=` in a dotenv file doesn't silently bind to all interfaces)

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

`pnpm typecheck` is clean.

## Notes

- Companion to #2545 (CSPRNG approval ids). The fork-local commit that PR was cherry-picked from originally included a `webhook-server.test.ts` for this function; the test was dropped in #2545 because the underlying refactor wasn't included. This PR lands the missing refactor + the test.
- Authored by smith-vosburg, applied via cherry-pick from `vosburg-auto/nanoclaw@273da12`.

prs.title: fix(host): stage attachments for message ids that contain '/'
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops attachments being dropped when a channel's message id contains `/`.

- **Problem**: attachments are staged under `inbox/<message id>/`, and `extractAttachmentFiles` refused any id that is not a plain file name. Some channels use resource paths as ids (`spaces/<space>/messages/<id>`), so every attachment on them was dropped and the agent got `[image: name]` with no saved path.
- **Fix**: `inboxFolderName()` in `src/attachment-safety.ts`, used by channel inbound staging. The agent-to-agent forwarder uses it too, for consistency only: its target ids (`a2a-<ts>-<rand>`) are already safe and keep their folder. An id that already passes `isSafeAttachmentName` keeps its folder, so existing paths don't move. Any other id becomes `~<slug>-<16 hex of sha256>`. Safe ids that start with `~` are encoded too, so one id can never name another message's folder. Absolute ids, `.`/`..` segments and NUL are still refused; `isSafeAttachmentName` is unchanged.
- **Behavior change**: a new message whose id starts with `~` now gets an encoded folder instead of `inbox/~…`. Stored rows keep their paths.
- **Out of scope**: outbox ids (container-made); images shared from Google Drive, which arrive without a downloadable reference (#4176); colon-free folder names for read tools and Windows hosts (#3127, #4044). Ids with `:` already pass the check and keep their folder here.

## Related work

Closes #3206

Same approach as #3276 (pass safe ids through, hash the rest). This version adds the reserved `~` prefix so a safe id can't equal another id's encoded folder, keeps `..` and absolute ids refused, and encodes ids over 255 bytes.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests (fail on main, pass here): ids that passed keep their exact folder; a `/` id is staged and its stored `localPath` matches the folder; `..`, absolute and NUL ids are refused by the helper; 13 different ids give 13 different folders; names stay within 255 bytes.
- Regression guards (pass on main too): an absolute-path id stages nothing; the formatter shows the staged path, not one rebuilt from the id.
- `pnpm test`: 3825 pass, 3 timeouts in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` under full-suite load (29/29 alone, same on main). Agent-runner `bun test`: 627 pass. `tsc` clean for host and agent-runner.
- Live Google Chat DM on a test install: a pasted screenshot was saved to `inbox/~spaces-…-<hash>/` and the agent described it. Before the fix the same install logged `Rejecting unsafe inbound message id` for every image.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change

```release-note
Attachments now reach the agent on channels whose message ids contain `/`, such as Google Chat. Before, they were dropped and the agent saw only the file name.
```

Message ids are untrusted input. The folder name is one safe path component by construction and is still opened through `AnchoredDir` (no symlinks) with exclusive create; ids shaped like `..` or absolute paths are still refused.

prs.title: fix(resend): agent replies and the first hello are sent
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the Resend (email) channel send again: agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello.

- **Problem**: email is non-threaded, so `deliver()` gets a null thread id and the bridge falls back to the platform id `resend:<address>`. The adapter's `decodeThreadId` only takes `resend:<address>:<hash>`, so every send throws `Invalid thread ID format`.
- **Fix**: the Resend module, not core, wraps the adapter. A send to `resend:<address>` goes to that person's latest email thread (noted in memory as mail arrives, copied to Chat SDK state for restarts), so a reply keeps its subject and `In-Reply-To`. With no thread yet, the adapter's `openDM` opens one.
- **Out of scope**: the bridge fallback, which is right for the other non-threaded channels, and adding `resend.test.ts` to `/add-resend`'s copy list on main (follow-up).

## Related work

Closes #4142. Found by @amit-shafnir while reviewing #4042.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `resend.test.ts`: base module → 6 failed (`Invalid thread ID format`); fix → 6 passed (hello; in-thread reply to the sender only, CC not copied; held state write; newer of two threads; new thread after 30 days).
- Same tests + `typecheck` on adapter 0.1.1 and 0.3.0 (skill pin) → pass.
- `pnpm test` → only 5 s timeouts in `scripts/update/*`, which time out on the base too.
- Codex adversarial review → no defects on the final diff.
- Live exe.dev VM on `f3b55742`, real Resend → pass: hello delivered, inbound email got an in-thread reply, unsigned webhook 401.
- CI on this branch runs label, template and verify only; the numbers above are local.

<details><summary>Known limits (mail still reaches the right person)</summary>

- Two open threads from one person: the reply lands in the one written to last.
- Two first sends to a new address at once can open two threads.
- A redelivered older webhook can point the next reply at an older thread.
- After 30 days without inbound mail, the next send opens a new thread.
</details>

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Resend email replies are sent.** Agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello failed with `Invalid thread ID format`. They now go out, and a reply lands in the email thread the person last wrote in. Re-run `/add-resend` (or `/update-skills`) to get it.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None new. Inbound still needs Resend's signature; identity is still the email From. A forged From that passes Resend can also steer the next reply's subject and `In-Reply-To`, not its recipient. One thread id per correspondent is kept in memory (max 1000) and in Chat SDK state, 30-day TTL.

prs.title: fix(channels): show long approval cards in full on Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Approval cards on Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud now show the whole request. A card too long for one message posts its full text first, then a short card with the buttons. Slack and Google Chat approval card text shows as typed.

- **Problem**: these channels show a card as one message with a length cap (Telegram 4,096 characters after formatting, a Discord embed 4,096, a WhatsApp Cloud card 1,024 with a 60-character title) and cut or reject text past it.
- **Fix**: each bridge sets `cardFits`, measured with the adapter's own rendering; the bridge overflow from #4147 uses it. Slack and Google Chat set `escapeCardText`; Slack card titles keep link syntax inert, and Discord drops the buttons when a card is edited to its resolved state. The adapters pass the new options through spreads, so they still build on a core without them.
- **Out of scope**: WhatsApp Cloud keeps 3 buttons with 20-character labels; that check needs core changes and follows separately.

## Related work

**MERGE HOLD**: lands together with #4147.

#4147 adds `cardFits` and the overflow on `main`; this branch carries copies of its commits (through 5b4bcfe9, bridge files byte-identical) until the next `main` -> `channels` sync. No issue: found internally; review with #4147.

- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 4,500 passed. 1 `transaction.e2e` test timed out under load; that file passes 29/29 alone.
- New tests run the real adapters (4.41.1; also 4.42.0) with only `fetch` stubbed: each `cardFits` agrees with what the adapter sends at and past its limit, for open, overflow and resolved cards; a long gateway card posts in full across parts plus a short button card on all three channels; nothing posts when a request needs more parts than allowed; Slack and Google Chat card text arrives escaped; a resolved Discord card loses its buttons. Removing `cardFits` fails the end-to-end tests.
- Older cores: each channel skill's files from this branch, installed onto `v2026.10.0` and current `main`, type-check clean and pass their copied tests (154/154); before the spreads, `tsc` failed on both.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, prettier clean, eslint no new errors.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Gives channel adapters the CI they need before any of them moves off the `channels` branch into a skill payload.

- **Problem**: `discover()` keeps a payload-only skill only when it is a provider, so a channel moved into `payload/` would silently lose its matrix job. No job loads all adapters into one tree, and none updates an old host's channels onto a new core.
- **Fix**: `discover()` keeps any skill that copies into `src/channels/`. New job `combined-channels` loads every channel skill into one tree: 19 adapters plus the two Slack companions (`slack-a2a-rooms`, `slack-agent-flow`) = 21, then type checks, vitest, bun test and a refresh. New job `old-channel-refresh` updates a v2026.10.0 host with gchat, slack, telegram and whatsapp to this core, then checks the refresh, every file, the pins and each skill's own tests.
- **Out of scope**: moving a channel (the stacked draft does gchat), gateways, and `registry gate`. The new jobs stay outside its `needs` until they have a green record.

## Related work

Step 0 of moving channel adapters to skill payloads. Both new jobs are green since #3451 (merged 10-21) fixed update-skills reading each barrel import as `add-<name>` (#3529); this branch carries it through a merge from main.

- Every run prints a stderr warning for add-dial-tool, add-iron-proxy and add-onecli: payload-only skills that are neither channels nor providers, still untested and out of scope here.
- Two stand-ins, stricter than a real update: dependency-file merge conflicts take the new core's copy (the updater would stop for a person), and adapters install from today's `channels` tip, with every copy made stale before the refresh.
- `when:` copies, imports and pins are named in a WARN line, not checked: their guards hang on answers the harness does not reproduce (today only add-imessage's two pins).
- The matrix job list is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gchat): tell the agent when a file arrives from Google Drive
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Tells the agent why a file shared from Google Drive never arrived, so it asks for an upload instead of guessing.

- **Problem**: Google Chat sends a file shared from Drive as a Drive id only (`source: DRIVE_FILE`, `driveDataRef.driveFileId`, no `attachmentDataRef`). Chat's [media download](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/api/reference/rest/v1/media/download) refuses Drive files, and the app's service account can't open the sender's Drive. The agent sees only `[image: name]`.
- **Fix**: `gchat.ts` passes `extractRawText: gchatDriveFileNote` to the bridge. For each Drive attachment it adds one line to the message: the file was not downloaded, so ask the sender to paste or drag it into the chat (Docs, Sheets, Slides and Drawings: export first). Uploaded files are unchanged. Core is unchanged too: this uses the existing `extractRawText` hook (v2.4.0+).
- **Out of scope**: downloading Drive files as the sender. That needs add-on `oauthScopes` with the restricted `drive.readonly` scope and per-user consent.

## Related work

No issue. Found during the live test for https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3206, a separate bug. vercel/chat has no Drive issue or PR. The change is two functions and one config line in `gchat.ts`, plus tests, so it carries over when `gchat.ts` moves to `add-gchat/payload/` in the channels move.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/gchat.test.ts`: 9 new tests, written first; the note tests failed before each fix. They cover the note, the export ask for native Google files, quiet output for uploaded/empty/malformed payloads, several files, the Pub/Sub shape, append order, factory wiring, and a hostile name (`"`, `]`, newline, U+2028, U+202E). A guard runs the note on the raw event adapter 4.41.1 returns and pins that Drive files get no `fetchData`, so an adapter change to either fails it.
- Local `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels`: 644 passed, 19 skipped. `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier are clean. CI on this `channels`-based PR runs only label, template-compliance and verify, so these numbers are local. Codex adversarial review: no defects.
- Live (2026-10-21 19:20Z), on an exe.dev test install with a real Workspace add-on Chat app and adapter 4.41.1: an image sent through the Drive button reached the agent as `[Google Drive file "Screenshot 2026-10-21 at 15.47.39.png" was not downloaded: …]`. The agent then asked for a direct upload.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

Untrusted input: the file name comes from the sender. It is JSON-quoted, with control, format, line-separator and bracket characters written as `\uXXXX`, so it stays on one line inside the note. Local helper, since `src/card-text.ts` is not in v2026.10.0. No new scopes or credentials.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets Claude agents read the PDFs users send them.
- **Problem**: Claude Code's Read tool turns PDF pages into images with `pdftoppm`. The agent image has no poppler-utils, so Read fails on any PDF it reads by page, which includes every long one, and the agent answers without it.
- **Fix**: add `poppler-utils` to the base apt list in `container/Dockerfile` (it brings `libpoppler126`; about 6 MB), and a test that keeps it there.
- **Out of scope**: the hardened image. Echo builds it outside this repo, so hardened installs get this only once Echo adds the package.

## Related work

Closes #4175

Found in the #3156 live A/B: OpenCode read the same 60-page PDF, Claude could not.

- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

- `pnpm exec vitest run container/` -> 8 passed. The new test fails when the package line is removed or commented out.
- Local build (arm64): 3,131,371,177 B -> 3,137,786,658 B (+6.4 MB). Package diff: only `libpoppler126` and `poppler-utils` 22.12.0 (bookworm).
- New image: `pdftoppm` renders all 80 pages of an 80-page PDF. Main image: `pdftoppm: not found`.
- Claude Code 2.1.296 inside each image, asked for page 63 of an 80-page PDF. Main: Read -> `pdftoppm is not installed`, no answer. This branch: Read -> page 63 as an image, correct reference.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Egress lockdown now also applies to agents that were running when it was turned on.

- **Problem**: lockdown is read at host start; a container already running then was adopted on its old network and stayed outside lockdown until it exited.
- **Fix**: under lockdown, a surviving container not on the egress network alone (or whose networks cannot be read) is stopped through the ordinary stop path; its next turn starts locked down and an interrupted turn is retried. Covers startup adoption, wake-path and sweep retries of deferred adoptions, and a spawn that finds an existing container. Lockdown also checks its network is internal.
- **Out of scope**: moving a live container between networks (fragile; a restart is simpler). Lockdown off is unchanged.

## Related work

No issue: found in the #4094 e2e matrix (row E1); main behaves the same.

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

- `vitest run src/` → 2074 pass; in the full `pnpm test` only git-heavy `scripts/` tests time out under load (they pass alone, and on main too). `tsc`, prettier, eslint clean.
- e2e on an exe.dev VM (OneCLI 1.45): a container started with lockdown off was stopped when the host restarted with lockdown on; the next turn replied from a new container on `nanoclaw-egress` only, and a second restart kept that container.

prs.title: fix(webhook): listen on 127.0.0.1 by default, add WEBHOOK_HOST
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops the shared webhook server from listening on every network interface.

- **Problem**: `src/webhook-server.ts` bound `0.0.0.0`, so any machine on the network could reach every adapter route. Safety rested on each adapter's own signature check.
- **Fix**: listen on `127.0.0.1`, which is all a tunnel or reverse proxy on the same machine needs. `WEBHOOK_HOST` (process env, then `.env`) takes an IP address to bind wider. A value that is not an IP address throws when the first webhook channel starts, like a bad `WEBHOOK_PORT`; one that cannot be bound logs `Webhook server error`, like a busy port. Unknown routes get the same plain 404 as other unknown paths instead of echoing the name. The `Webhook server started` log line and `ncl status` show the bound host, and the Mattermost setup check probes that host. Nine webhook channel skills tell the operator when to set `WEBHOOK_HOST`, in wizard-visible text and in Troubleshooting, and so does the Mattermost E2E fixture README.
- **Out of scope**: the docs portal pages (follow-up PR in nanoclaw-docs).

## Related work

Same default as #2546 by @smith-vosburg; the `WEBHOOK_HOST` name comes from #3144 by @jonnychesthair-crypto. Both conflict with current main, so this re-applies them. Thank you both.

Companion on `channels`: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4186. `mattermost-live.test.ts` sets `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0`, because the lab's Mattermost calls back through the Linux bridge address. It is harmless before this lands.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/config-webhook-host.test.ts`: default, `.env`, override, empty, invalid values; a real listener refuses a LAN address by default and serves it with `0.0.0.0`. The LAN address is first proven reachable on a throwaway `0.0.0.0` listener, so a firewalled interface cannot fake a pass; with none, those two tests show as skipped. Forcing the old bind makes the LAN test fail.
- `webhook-server-raw.test.ts`: unknown route and non-`/webhook` path both return `Not found`.
- `mattermost-runtime-verification.test.ts`: the setup check probes `127.0.0.1` for `0.0.0.0` and `::`, `[::1]` for `::1`, and a named address as is.
- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 3,876 passed; 2 load timeouts in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`, which passes alone (29/29). Webhook and Mattermost suites also pass with `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` exported. `tsc`, `format:check` and `eslint src/` clean.
- Live on an exe.dev Linux VM with Docker: only `127.0.0.1:3000` listens; the VM's own address, `docker0` and a bridge container via `host.docker.internal` are refused; `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` makes all three answer; `WEBHOOK_HOST=localhost` throws when the webhook channel starts. A request through exe.dev's HTTPS proxy arrives from `127.0.0.1` and is served.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Log files now mask credentials before they are written, so one careless field, error message or tool output no longer puts a key into `logs/`.

- **Problem**: no log sink redacted anything, yet error text can carry a credential (a `fetch` error prints a URL's password, `Command failed:` prints argv), container stderr is copied into `nanoclaw.error.log`, and setup's raw step logs keep child output verbatim.
- **Fix**: one pass in `src/secret-redaction.ts`, driven by a pattern list, runs in the host logger and every setup log writer. Keys with a known issuer prefix keep that prefix and their last 4 characters (`sk-ant-api03-[REDACTED]…WXYZ`) when at least 16 stay hidden; everything else is fully masked.
- **Not masked**: the lines the bash bootstrap writes to `logs/setup.log`, a failed bootstrap's `logs/setup-steps/01-bootstrap.log` (Node is not ready yet), agent transcripts and session DBs.

## Related work

None. Found in an internal audit of log output; no public issue.

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

- Adversarial review, 5 passes: 23 findings, 22 fixed with a red test each, 1 documented in code (the failed-bootstrap log).
- Full suite: 3950 passed; 3 failures are load timeouts that pass alone, or fail the same way on `main`. `tsc` and `format:check` clean.

```release-note
**Logs: credentials are masked.** NanoClaw now replaces API keys, tokens, auth headers and URL passwords with `[REDACTED]` in `logs/nanoclaw.log`, `logs/nanoclaw.error.log`, `logs/setup.log` and `logs/setup-steps/`. Keys with a known prefix keep it and their last 4 characters so you can tell which key failed. Not masked: the lines the shell bootstrap writes to `logs/setup.log`, and `logs/setup-steps/01-bootstrap.log` when the bootstrap itself fails.
```

<details><summary>What is masked</summary>

- Values: `sk-…`, GitHub, Slack, AWS key ids, Google API keys, Telegram and Discord bot tokens, JWTs, PEM private keys, and the token part of Discord and Slack webhook URLs.
- Context: `Authorization` (scheme kept), `Bearer`, `Cookie` headers, URL passwords, and values after names ending in `token`, `secret`, `password`, `api_key`, `secret_key`, `access_key`, `credential(s)`, `authorization` or `cookie`, raw or JSON-escaped. `max_tokens` and `key` stay readable, and so do unquoted placeholder words (`API_KEY=undefined`, `token: not configured`).

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): answer each message in its own thread after /clear
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

After `/clear`, or once a message arrives while the agent is still answering, replies in a threaded chat could land one thread behind for the rest of the query.

- **Problem**: a batch holding `/clear` and the next message took its reply route from the `/clear` row. Also, the Claude CLI folds a message pushed mid-turn into the running turn, and Codex steers it into the running turn. Either way one result answers both, but the turn queue expected one result per push, so it stayed one entry behind until the query ended.
- **Fix**: commands reply on their own route, and a turn routes from the message that woke it. Providers now report a result that answered folded inputs (`answeredInputs`). Claude reads it from `user_message_uuids`; `add-codex` counts its accepted steers. The poll loop then retires the folded turns and sends a failed turn's notice to each folded thread.
- **Out of scope**: OpenCode answers each push with its own result and needs no change.

<details><summary>Behavior notes for reviewers</summary>

- Accumulated (`trigger=0`) rows no longer pick the reply thread when they sort first. This applies to every accumulate batch, not only `/clear`.
- Context rows beside a command never start a turn by themselves. They stay pending and ride along with the next message.
- Codex keeps inputs in push order. It steers only when nothing is queued and no steer is awaiting its reply, and a rejected steer runs ahead of the inputs queued after it. A turn's result waits up to 5 s for its steer replies, or less if the query is aborted. A steer still unanswered then counts as folded. If it is rejected later, it runs as its own turn and one reply is misrouted; an uncounted fold would leave every later reply one behind.
- Claude's `user_message_uuids` keeps only the first 64 entries. Past that, the count falls back to `queued_turn_count`. An input written in the same few ms as the result can then be over-counted: one answer is misrouted, then routing recovers. Undercounting would stay behind for the whole query. A Claude result whose `user_message_uuids` lists none of our inputs retires none of them. If such a result did answer one of ours, `unanswered` keeps that input and a later over-64 count is off by one.

</details>

## Related work

No issue: found by a staging release check (`/clear` in a Slack DM, then answers one thread behind for up to ~30 min). No host, schema, or channel change.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test --isolate` → 645 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. With the `add-codex` container payload copied in and its barrels wired: 702 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail. `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json` is clean both ways. The new tests are red on `main`.
- Real Claude Code CLI 2.1.300 (Haiku) drove the real poll loop and provider against a test session DB. On `main`: q → the `/clear` thread, m4 → m3's thread, m5 → m4's thread. On this branch, each answer landed in its own thread.
- Codex (`CodexProvider` with a fake app-server, real poll loop): a steered follow-up sent the next answer to the previous thread on `main`'s loop, and to its own thread here.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Replies in threaded chats (like Slack DMs) no longer drift one thread behind for the rest of the conversation after `/clear`, or after a message arrives while the agent (Claude or Codex) is still working; a message folded into an answer already in progress is answered in that answer's thread. Unaddressed messages that arrived before `/clear` still reach the fresh session along with the next message.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Routing still uses only the session's own inbound rows.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

`add-codex`: only `codex.ts` and `codex.turns.test.ts` change in place, with no new files, directives, or dependencies. Installed copies pick it up when the payload is next refreshed. On a core without `answeredInputs`, the field is ignored.

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep the turn open on an error Codex will retry
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A transient stream error that Codex retries on its own no longer fails the NanoClaw turn.

- **Problem**: before each automatic retry, Codex sends `error` with `willRetry: true` ([`bespoke_event_handling.rs:1055-1071`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1055-L1071)). Its protocol says such an error does not interrupt the turn. `runOneTurn` ended the turn on every `error`. A network blip therefore failed the turn with "Reconnecting... 1/5" while Codex kept going, and the real reply was dropped.
- **Fix**: an error with `willRetry: true` now yields a `progress` event and leaves the turn open. Any other error still ends the turn. When retries run out, Codex sends a final error with `willRetry: false` ([`core/src/session/turn.rs:817-831`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L817-L831)), so the turn still ends then.
- **Behaviour change**: Codex 0.162.1 retries a lost connection without limit by default. A Codex outage can now hold a session until the existing 10-minute turn limit, which starts with the turn and is never reset (`codex.ts:380`). The reply then fails with "Turn timed out after 600000ms", not at the first retry.

## Related work

Stacked on #4165, which changes the same handler, so review that first. When #4165 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to main.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- add-codex container suites with the payload applied: 186 pass, `tsc -p container/agent-runner` clean. The only 2 failures are the `cli-tools.json` entry tests, which the quick harness does not merge; main fails the same 2.
- New tests in `codex.turns.test.ts`:
  - a `willRetry: true` error keeps the turn open, and the turn still returns its reply (this test fails before the fix);
  - `willRetry: false` and a missing `willRetry` still end the turn.
- Wire shape at the pin: `ServerNotification` is `#[serde(tag = "method", content = "params", rename_all = "camelCase")]` ([`common.rs:1706`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1706)) with `Error => "error" (v2::ErrorNotification)` ([`common.rs:1937`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1937)). `ErrorNotification` is `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` with `pub will_retry: bool` next to `pub error: TurnError` ([`v2/notification.rs:59-69`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/notification.rs#L59-L69)). So the flag arrives as `params.willRetry`, beside `params.error`: what `codex.ts:337` reads and what the test sends.
- CI on this stacked PR runs only `label`, `template-compliance` and `verify`, so the 186-pass result above is local. The full suites run once it targets `main`.
- Not run live: a real network drop needs a ChatGPT-paired VM.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Codex agents no longer fail a reply when Codex briefly loses its connection and reconnects on its own. If the connection stays down, the reply now fails when it hits its 10-minute limit instead of right away.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. The change only affects provider event handling.

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep sub-agent thread events out of the parent turn
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex agents that start sub-agents keep their own turn: a sub-agent's events no longer end, fill or redirect it.

- **Problem**: Codex 0.162.1 streams every sub-agent thread it spawns on the same app-server connection ([`app-server/src/lib.rs:1291-1309`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs#L1291-L1309)). Sub-agents are on by default (`multi_agent` is Stable). `runOneTurn` ignored `threadId`. As a result, a child's `turn/completed` or `error` ended the parent turn early. A child's `turn/started` moved the turn id that steer and interrupt target. The child's message text could also become the parent's reply.
- **Fix**: events from another thread now only yield `activity`, so host-sweep doesn't mark a parent stale while it waits on a sub-agent; they no longer change the parent turn. Codex 0.162.1 always tags these events (`threadId` is a required field, e.g. [`ErrorNotification`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/notification.rs#L62-L69)); untagged events are handled as before.
- **Out of scope**: an `error` that Codex will retry still ends the turn; stacked #4166 fixes that. Unchanged here: the fixed 10-minute turn timeout (`codex.ts:36`) is not reset by activity, so a parent waiting longer on a sub-agent still times out. Images a sub-agent generates land in its own thread's `generated_images/` folder, which the runner doesn't scan, so they don't reach the user.

## Related work

No issue: this bug turned up while working on the Codex image-generation fix. The change is safe to review directly because it touches only the add-codex provider payload.

Draft #4164 (image generation) changes the same handler, so expect a small context conflict next to the new guard. With this guard, a sub-agent's `imageGeneration` item is dropped before #4164's branch runs. If child images should be sent, that branch moves above the guard.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- add-codex container suites with the payload applied: 183 pass, `tsc -p container/agent-runner` clean. The only 2 failures are the `cli-tools.json` entry tests: the quick harness does not merge that file, and main fails the same 2.
- New tests in `codex.turns.test.ts`, all 3 failing on main:
  - a child `error` or `turn/completed` leaves the parent turn running;
  - child text never becomes the result;
  - abort interrupts the parent turn, not the child's.
- Not run live: a real sub-agent run needs a ChatGPT-paired VM.
