releases.name: v2026.10.1-rc.2
releases.body:
NanoClaw 2026.10.1-rc.2 is the second release candidate for 2026.10.1. Installs on the `beta` channel get this candidate; `stable` stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.10.1 is published. Since 2026.10.1-rc.1 it moves OneCLI to 1.45, where new agent groups get only their model key and other keys go to the groups you choose, makes the webhook server listen only on this machine by default, applies egress lockdown to agents that were already running, asks for Node's October 2026 security releases, and lets Claude agents read PDFs; Google Chat now checks that its webhooks come from your app. It also lets agents create other agents from templates, adds Cursor as an agent provider, and moves locally built agent images to Claude Code 2.1.296 with Claude Haiku 5.5. Setup waits for a slow first reply and says when that reply failed, approval cards appear in the thread you are waiting in, and fewer agent runs fail. Six changes need action from some installs, among them the OneCLI upgrade, the webhook address and two new Google Chat settings, so check the section below before you update.

### ⚠️ Before you update

- [BREAKING] **Chat SDK channels move to adapter 4.41.1, which fixes Telegram messages with links that were never delivered.** Affected: installs where `grep -o '"@chat-adapter/[a-z]*"' package.json` prints anything (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, GitHub, Linear). Fix: `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes installed channels; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one. Google Chat: @mentions in spaces now need `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOT_USER_ID=users/<id>` in `.env` (DMs work without it; without it the log says "Google Chat botUserId is not configured" at startup): once the app has replied to you in a DM, list that DM's messages with the Chat API (`spaces.messages.list`), copy the `sender.name` of a message whose sender `type` is `BOT`, and restart the service. Slack agent-to-agent rooms: a sibling bot now arrives as `slack:bot:U…` instead of `slack:bot:B…`, so approve each sibling bot once more. Check: each channel answers a test message. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>` ([rolling back](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading#rolling-back)).
- [BREAKING] **Iron Proxy installs that connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release must sign in to Codex again.** Detect, from the NanoClaw folder (works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. Once running, an affected install's Codex agents answer only with the failure notice ("Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer") and the agent container log shows `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Why: Codex 0.156 and later check the login's workspace id, and older Iron logins never recorded it. Fix: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`, then check that a Codex agent answers. OneCLI installs are affected only when the vault holds several ChatGPT logins or one without a recorded id; the host log then says "OneCLI login stand-in keeps its placeholder account id": delete the extra or stale login (`onecli secrets list`, then `onecli secrets delete --id <id>`), run the same command, and grant the new secret to each agent that had the old one, as `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install describes. Rollback: return to the previous release.
- [BREAKING] **Forks and hand-made templates: the template code moved and `templates/` is now ignored by git.** Affected: fork code that imports `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` (it stops compiling), forks that edit the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line, forks that point setup at their own template library, and anyone who keeps a hand-made template in `templates/`. Why: templates fetched by setup or by an agent are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`, and setup now lists a library from its `index.json`. Fix: import `cloneRegistry` and `listTemplatesFromDir` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `copyTemplate` is gone, so call `ensureTemplateLocal`; a fork that changed `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` edits `LIBRARY_REPO` (`owner/repo`) and `LIBRARY_BRANCH` in `src/templates/library.ts` instead; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines; keep a new hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/<ref>`; give your own library an `index.json` at its root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` (`{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "<category>": [{ "ref": "<folder>", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`). Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and setup's library picker lists your templates ([building templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/building)). Rollback: revert this release; fetched templates then show as untracked in `git status`, so delete them or `git add` the ones to keep.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: upgrade the gateway to 1.45.0 and the `onecli` CLI to 2.11.0, where agents get only the keys you grant them.** Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown` (Iron Proxy installs skip this). Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs, so do not skip past it. Fix: before restarting, follow `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install ([the same guide on GitHub](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/docs/onecli-upgrades.md)); it backs up the gateway database, stops if the conversion would delete your rules, and covers the CLI binary. If you use `/add-dial-tool`, delete the Dial key first (see the Dial item below). Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential, and on a 1.42 gateway new groups still get every key until you upgrade. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. `/add-vercel`, `/add-tavily-tool` and `/add-dial-tool` refuse a gateway that is not 1.45. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex` or `openai`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`). Check: `/api/health` reports 1.45.0 and a new agent group answers. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
- [BREAKING] **The webhook server now listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.** Tunnels and reverse proxies on the same machine keep working. Affected: a proxy on another machine, or anything in Docker on Linux that calls back to the host, such as a Mattermost server; webhooks stop arriving, and the log shows `Webhook server started host="127.0.0.1"`. Fix: set `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or one interface's IP address; a name such as `localhost` stops the host at startup) in `.env` and restart. Check: a message on that channel gets an answer. Rollback: the same setting restores the old behavior.
- [BREAKING] **Google Chat installs need two new settings, or the channel does not start.** Google Chat now verifies that webhooks come from your Workspace add-on Chat app, using `GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL` and `GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER` (digits) in `.env`; `/update-nanoclaw` brings the new adapter but cannot ask for them. Detect: the log says "Google Chat needs GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL and GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER (digits) in .env to verify webhooks". Fix: re-run `/add-gchat`, which keeps your existing values and asks for the endpoint URL, the project number and the bot user id for @mentions in spaces, or set both values by hand and restart. The Chat app must be a Google Workspace add-on, and converting an app to one cannot be undone. Check: a test message gets an answer. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>`.
- **`/add-dial-tool` users: delete the Dial key before upgrading OneCLI, then re-run `/add-dial-tool`.** On OneCLI 1.45 it gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose, and new groups get Dial only when you add them; Dial is off for those few minutes instead of open to every agent. The upgrade guide has the delete command. NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID` and the `onecli` CLI's project (`onecli config set project`, or `ONECLI_PROJECT`) must match or both be unset: when they differ, the re-run stops and writes nothing to OneCLI. An agent group name with a line break no longer changes which groups keep Dial.
- **Update Node to its October 2026 security release.** Setup now requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer and refuses the end-of-life 23 and 25; locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.4, pinned by digest, and hardened installs get it with a later image. NanoClaw keeps running on an older Node, but re-running setup stops. After `/update-nanoclaw`, run `bash setup/install-node.sh`, then re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses the new Node. If Node comes from nvm, fnm, volta or asdf, update it there. Groups with extra packages also need `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild`.
- **Egress lockdown now covers agents that were already running when it was turned on**: they restart on the locked network when the host restarts. If the lockdown network exists but is not internal (only a network made by hand, or a setting that points at an ordinary one), agents no longer start and the host log says "Refusing to spawn with open egress". Fix: list what is attached with `docker network inspect nanoclaw-egress`, detach it (`docker network disconnect nanoclaw-egress <container>`), then `docker network rm nanoclaw-egress`; the next agent start recreates it as internal. Iron Proxy installs name it `nanoclaw-egress-<slug>`, and `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_NETWORK` can set another name.
- **Locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.296 and Agent SDK 0.3.296, where Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5.** On the Anthropic API, Claude Code's background requests and groups set to `haiku` move to Haiku 5.5, which costs a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price for prompts up to 100K tokens. Hardened installs keep Claude Code 2.1.280 and Haiku 4.5 until an image for this release is listed.
- **Hardened installs move to the image built from v2026.10.0.** A pull now takes the image listed in `agent-images.json` on `main` for the newest release in the install's history, so a new hardened image reaches installs without a new release. Release candidates never get an image of their own, so this one uses v2026.10.0's (Claude Code 2.1.280, newer than the old pinned build), and the pull's "agent-runner lock drift" warning is expected. This candidate lists a newer build of that image, made on 2026-10-21, so `/update-nanoclaw` pulls it again. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it ([hardened runtime](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/guides/echo-hardened-runtime)).
- **Codex groups with no model set start new threads on GPT-6.1 Sol.** `/add-codex` now pins `@openai/codex` 0.162.1; existing threads keep their model. To stay on the old one, run `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --model gpt-6-astra`, then `ncl groups restart --id <group-id>`.

### ✨ New

- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask for one in chat, pick from `ncl templates list` or the public library, and the agent builds it. Setup's template library list now shows what each template does ([using templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/using-templates)).
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** The new `/add-cursor` skill runs Cursor's Agent SDK, and setup offers Cursor in the provider picker; it needs a locally built agent image ([providers](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/extend/providers)).
- **Setup waits for a slow first reply instead of failing.** The first-chat check waits 2 minutes, then asks whether to keep waiting, and shows each stage (sandbox, agent runtime, model) with its time, so local models that take minutes to load no longer fail setup. Runs without a terminal now stop after 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds.
- **Agents on slow local models are no longer cut off mid-turn.** Raise `NANOCLAW_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS` (default 30 minutes) or `NANOCLAW_CLAIM_STUCK_MS` (default 60 seconds) in `.env`; the host log names which one fired. Restart the service after a change; installs that set neither are unaffected ([environment variables](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/reference/environment-variables)).

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Setup tells you when your assistant's first reply failed.** Instead of saying the assistant is ready (for example after a bad API key), it shows the agent's error, names the log files and links the troubleshooting docs; `pnpm run chat` exits with code 4 on a failure notice. When an agent has no error of its own to share, every channel's failure notice now reads "Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer" and links the troubleshooting docs.
- **Agents no longer lose or repeat a reply around `send_message`.** An agent that sent something with `send_message` and then left its answer unwrapped is shown what it already sent and asked to finish, and an exact repeat is not sent twice. On streaming providers, a reply sent with `send_message` and followed by plain closing text costs one extra model turn.
- **Fewer failed agent runs.** On Docker Desktop, a message that arrives while an agent is replying no longer fails the run, and "Permission denied" replies to admin-only commands are sent directly to the chat. On every install, `ncl` and agent tools no longer hit intermittent "database is locked" errors.
- **Approval cards appear where you are waiting and are easier to read.** When an agent in a thread of your own DM asks for approval, the card and its "Reject with reason" prompt appear in that thread. Cards show command arguments and agent-to-agent messages in a code block, and names and the install reason quoted on one line. An approval an agent asks for, or an `ask_user_question`, whose title and question together run over 2,000 characters is refused, and the agent is told the limit so it can shorten it; `ask_user_question` also returns an error within seconds of the host giving up on delivering its card, instead of waiting out its 300-second timeout.
- **The background service finds the tools it was installed with.** On macOS it now includes `/opt/homebrew/bin` and the Node.js folder, so Apple Silicon installs using Homebrew or Apple Container no longer crash at start; on Linux it includes the Node.js folder (for example from nvm). Existing installs get it by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops at its validate step on installs with Slack.** The skill refresh now credits each channel import to the skill that adds it, so it stops looking for Slack skills that don't exist. The fix comes with the update itself.
- **Discord: Approve on an approval card now approves.** Button clicks were misread, so approvals were recorded as rejections and answers to questions came back garbled.
- **Claude agents can read long PDFs you send them.** Installs that build their own agent image get it from the image rebuild in `/update-nanoclaw`; groups that installed their own packages also need `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild`. Hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Google Chat attachments reach the agent.** On channels whose message ids contain `/`, such as Google Chat, files were dropped and the agent saw only the file name. When someone shares a file from Google Drive, the agent now says it can't open Drive files and asks for the file to be pasted or dragged into the chat.
- **Resend email replies are sent.** Agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello failed with `Invalid thread ID format`; they now go out, and a reply lands in the email thread the person last wrote in. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`.
- **Smaller fixes.** An agent reads its own replies from other threads of the same chat as its own, not as another agent's; `ncl groups delete` also removes the group's host bookkeeping rows, and agents that could message it stop listing it right away; creating an agent from a template no longer fails when an agent that has not run yet holds that name; a Slack bot set up for channels only no longer sends you an FYI each time it turns away a DM; `ncl messaging-groups delete` also removes the group's wirings, its own sessions and pending approvals instead of failing with a foreign key error, and removing iMessage uses it; creating an agent refuses a name whose group folder would be invalid (too long, or reserved such as "Global") before anything is written, and says why; setup accepts Anthropic's newer API key types (`sk-ant-usr`, `sk-ant-svc`), which must be scoped to one workspace; Linux Signal setup installs signal-cli 0.14.9, which fixes sends to new contacts hanging (rerun `setup/install-signal-cli.sh`, then restart the service); and the `/add-dashboard` dashboard keeps updating when a transcript grows past about 512 MB and no longer re-reads every transcript each minute (rerun `/add-dashboard` to get it).

### 🔒 Security

- **`/add-resend` installs a Resend adapter with no known advisories.** The pin moves from 0.1.1 (4 moderate findings through `uuid`) to 0.3.0, and `/update-nanoclaw` moves existing email installs to it (after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`). The webhook now answers before the message is processed, so a message that fails is not retried, and replies are sent as HTML with a plain-text part that drops link targets.
- **Signal setup checks the signal-cli download's sha256** before installing it.
- **OneCLI setup keeps keys off the command line.** Setup now gives keys to the `onecli` CLI through a private temporary file or stdin, and hides them in error messages. If setup ever failed while saving your Anthropic key or OneCLI API key, rotate that key and delete the old files in `logs/setup-steps/` and `logs/setup.log`.

### 🔧 For custom installations

- **Custom container code that reads `inbound.db`** through `openInboundDb()` or `getInboundDb()` (`mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`) must use `readInbound((db) => ...)`: `openInboundDb()` is gone, and `getInboundDb()` now works only in tests.
- **`/add-codex` ships its provider inside the skill**, so installs and forks no longer need the providers branch; on an older core its instructions tell you to update core first. Codex archives pick up core's header fix (the thread-id line no longer renders as a heading).
- **Provider skills can archive exchanges through core.** Use `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/exchange-archive.ts`; refreshing `/add-codex` deletes the old copy in `providers/exchange-archive.ts`, so a custom provider that imports it must switch.
- **A gateway credential can target one exact path on a host.** The provider credential seam moves to version 2: a custom provider skill that requires exactly version 1 must accept 1 or later, a skill that sets `path` must require 2, and a custom gateway must declare `connectionPaths: true` to accept path-scoped credentials.
- **The agent image no longer installs `cron-parser`** or its `luxon` dependency (about 4.9 MB); scheduling still runs on the host. Custom container code that imported them must add them back.
- **Forks that pointed the `versions.json` agent-image pin at their own mirror** must move that reference to `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF`, because the `agent-images.json` list now comes first.
- **Forks no longer run the agent-image refresh workflow**, which failed every 6 hours outside `nanocoai/nanoclaw`.
- **OpenCode: `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` and `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_COUNT` are gone**; they never took effect.

prs.title: fix(qq): use portable Atomic for gateway timestamps so arm32 nightly builds compile
prs.body:
## Summary

- `gateway_attempt_started_ms` and `last_gateway_activity_ms` in `src/channels/qq.zig` are `std.atomic.Value(i64)`. A 64-bit atomic doesn't compile on 32-bit targets, so the nightly `linux-arm32-gnu`, `linux-arm32-musl` and `android-armv7` builds have failed on every run since the 10-05 merges brought in a87e466c31:

  ```
  lib/std/atomic.zig:21:32: error: expected 32-bit integer type or smaller; found 64-bit integer type
  src/channels/qq.zig:884:64: note: called inline here
  ```

  Because those legs fail, the published `nightly` release is still `nightly-20260927-55907af` on every platform.
- This switches both fields to `Atomic(i64)` from `portable_atomic.zig`. The `sequence` field in the same struct already uses that wrapper (#219).

Upstream nightly runs:
- first failing: https://github.com/nullclaw/nullclaw/actions/runs/37288573019
- latest (10-22): https://github.com/nullclaw/nullclaw/actions/runs/39742438006

## Validation

Fork runs, both on top of main `5f1cade05c`, with the repo's other workflows removed:
- before: https://github.com/glaziermag/nullclaw/actions/runs/39809182720: `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall` for `arm-linux-musleabihf` and `arm-linux-gnueabihf` fails with the two errors above (both attempts)
- after: https://github.com/glaziermag/nullclaw/actions/runs/39809193929: both targets build (both attempts), and the musl binary prints `nullclaw dev` for `--version` under qemu-arm

`zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build test --summary all` on x86_64 Linux pass with and without the change: 13/13 steps, 7493/7507 tests passed, 14 skipped.

## Notes

- PR CI doesn't cross-build arm32 (it moved to the release and nightly builds in 51a834e81b), so this only shows up in the nightly run.
- android-armv7 needs the NDK, so I didn't build it on the fork. It fails upstream with the same two errors at the same lines.

issues.body:
# Daily ironclaw failure taxonomy — 2026-10-22

## Suites analyzed
- [officeqa (64 non-pass)](https://nearai.github.io/benchmarks/#/runs/ironclaw/officeqa/1bebd114-5066-4faf-83ae-c74ec8cd6ae3) — This run's 64 non-pass tasks are overwhelmingly genuine model-quality errors: DeepSeek-V4-Flash navigates the OCR-digitized Treasury Bulletins with healthy, self-recovering trajectories (read_file/grep/shell/result_read all succeed and return the right source text) but reads the wrong cell, picks the wrong table/row/year, or applies a wrong formula/unit, so the final number falls outside the ±1% tolerance while nothing in ironclaw fails. UID0013 is diagnostic: its answer is exactly 1000x the golden, a pure unit error. Every 'Hard' capability signature (host_runtime/OperationFailed 404s, Network drops, auth_required/policy_denied/InputEncode, tool/builtin.http.*) is incidental to a model-error trajectory in which the model attempted an off-document external HTTP fetch (FRED, treasury.gov, measuringworth) it should never make for a document-grounded suite — those fetches correctly fail and the model then falls back to a wrong local computation. The only genuine harness issue is cosmetic and confirmed live: http.rs:492 mislabels a denied HTTP request (request_denied) as InputEncode, which can misdirect model recovery but changes no verdict here. Carried, unconfirmable caveat: a few ratio/duration goldens (UID0240 expected 0.9999 vs 2.54) look methodology-suspect and may deserve a separate bad_eval audit, but cannot be confirmed from this bundle, so they remain model.

_ironclaw rev(s): b0b999d96781516ee05e6ba961d6f3ead900da96_

## 🔧 Harness fix candidates (ranked by blast radius)

| # | Category | Tasks | Suites | Confidence | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Denied HTTP request mislabeled as InputEncode | 1 | officeqa:1 | 0.82 | `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492` |

### 1. Denied HTTP request mislabeled as InputEncode — 1 tasks
**Root cause:** In crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs the error-classification match maps RuntimeHttpEgressReasonCode::RequestDenied to RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::InputEncode (http.rs:492). RequestDenied originates from RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request (host_api/http.rs:551), a request-level denial, and has nothing to do with argument encoding; the sibling reason codes (CredentialUnavailable->Client, PolicyDenied->PolicyDenied, NetworkError->Network, ResponseError->OperationFailed) all map faithfully. InputEncode's model-facing summary (dispatch.rs:471) tells the model to fix its input, steering recovery the wrong way.

**Fix:** Change the RequestDenied arm so a denied request is not surfaced as an argument-encoding fault. Map RuntimeHttpEgressReasonCode::RequestDenied to a kind that reflects a request-level denial/operation failure — RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::PolicyDenied when the denial is policy/egress-based, otherwise RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::OperationFailed — rather than InputEncode. Add a unit test over http_error()/save_error_kind_and_summary that asserts a RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request maps to the denial/operation kind (not InputEncode), mirroring the existing per-reason-code coverage, so the mislabel cannot regress.

_Files:_ `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492`

_officeqa:_ [UID0027](https://nearai.github.io/benchmarks/#/runs/ironclaw/officeqa/1bebd114-5066-4faf-83ae-c74ec8cd6ae3/fail/UID0027)

issues.title: Add arm64/aarch64 platform support for Docker builds
issues.body:
Ironclaw currently only publishes Docker images for linux/amd64. This prevents running the official image on ARM64 machines.
- Cranelift (the WASM JIT compiler used by Ironclaw) already supports aarch64. The only confirmed ARM limitation is armv7 (32-bit), tracked in #1339.
- The Rust toolchain and all dependencies should compile natively on aarch64.

Bumps [dompurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) from 3.4.12 to 3.4.17.
Release notes

Sourced from dompurify's releases.

DOMPurify 3.4.17

  • Fixed an issue with IN_PLACE, SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES and shadow roots, thanks @​manus-pi
  • Fixed IN_PLACE handling of nodes that hooks or custom elements tough during sanitization, thanks @​uttej-badwane
  • Fixed the SMIL attributeName guard in XHTML mode, thanks @​Koukyosyumei
  • Hardened several smaller edge cases (namespaces, literal-text elements, isValidAttribute()), thanks @​artiphishell
  • Added a purify-edge test runner as a compatibility check, thanks @​anzal1
  • Clarified the IN_PLACE documentation in the README about possible risks
  • Updated several dependencies

DOMPurify 3.4.16

  • Fixed a problem with IN_PLACE node removal when working with hooks, thanks @​manus-pi
  • Fixed a problem with IN_PLACE sanitization and raw-text roots, thanks @​h-t-m
  • Fixed a problem with ESM default exports landing in CommonJS declarations, thanks @​ssi02014
  • Migrated from rollup to rolldown because performance, thanks @​ssi02014
  • Bumped several dependencies where possible

DOMPurify 3.4.15

  • Added better clobbering hardening when XML content is involved, thanks @​gnyselcuk
  • Added several smaller hardening and edge-case improvements, thanks @​leechristensen
  • Bumped several dependencies where possible

DOMPurify 3.4.14

  • Fixed an issue with possible bypasses when risky tags are allow-listed, thanks @​AlirezaRouhbakhsh
  • Fixed a couple of edge cases with mixed document contexts, thanks @​fishjojo1
  • Added the SVG pointer-events and vector-effect presentation attributes to the allow-list, thanks @​Jaybhade
  • Conducted another refactoring run, removed dead branches and duplicated logic, flattened attribute validation
  • Updated the documentation in several spots, README, wiki, etc., thanks @​Akokonunes
  • Updated several development dependencies and CI workflow actions

DOMPurify 3.4.13

  • Fixed an issue with hook removal during IN_PLACE sanitization, thanks @​koyokr
  • Fixed an issue with hooks potentially bypassing the clone guard, thanks @​AkshayjainG
  • Fixed an issue with DOM clobbering via ownerDocument during IN_PLACE, thanks @​AkshayjainG
  • Bumped several dependencies where possible

prs.title: fix(auth): show account recovery and model connection states
prs.body:
## Summary
During session restoration, the sidebar hid My Account and the model selector showed a login prompt. If verification then failed temporarily, the selector could incorrectly ask a cached signed-in user to configure a model. Keep the account entry visible and distinguish session restoration, connection failure, model loading, and a confirmed empty model list.

## Related Issue
Reported through local desktop reproduction; no linked issue.

## Changes Made
- Add localized loading and retry notices to account menus and the model selector, preserving the cached account display and access to custom models.
- Track plan-model request status separately from the model list. Prevent late failures from a previous account from replacing the current account's status.
- Cover offline startup, retry recovery, model-load transitions, logged-out behavior, and English/Chinese rendering.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Six focused Vitest files: 120 tests passed.
- [x] Changed-file ESLint and TypeScript checking passed.
- [x] Native development Electron interaction/accessibility checks: restoration state, unavailable state, cached-account menu, and retry transition.
- [x] Recovery to authenticated models covered with mocked IPC responses.
- [x] Full local Vitest suite: 726 files passed, 18 skipped; 7,873 tests passed, 157 skipped. Ran with local socket/watcher access after the sandbox denied loopback listeners with EPERM.
- [x] Production renderer build passed (`npm run build`). Existing dependency/chunking warnings remain.

## Screenshots
Native screenshot capture returned blank app content, so no visual screenshot is attached. Native checks above verify interaction/accessibility state, not pixel layout. Live successful recovery was not verified because the existing network issue remains in place.

Renderer state and presentation only. No main-process, preload, IPC, window-management, persistent-storage, or network-configuration changes.

prs.title: feat(dsh): sync reasoning-effort metadata so thinking strength is configurable for LobsterAI models
prs.body:
## Summary

LobsterAI 内置的 DSH（DeepSeek Harness）工作台同步模型到 `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` 时没有声明 reasoning-effort 元数据，导致 DSH Web UI 中 LobsterAI 提供模型的"思考强度"控件缺失。本 PR 在 `dshConfigSync.ts` 中把 LobsterAI 侧的 thinking 元数据（`supportsThinking` / `thinkingLevelMap` / `thinkingConfig`）映射为 DSH 的 `reasoningEfforts`（模型级）和 `compat`（路由级），使思考强度可配置，且仅在模型明确支持思考时声明，避免 over-claim。

## Related Issue

Fixes #2577

## Changes Made

- `src/main/libs/dshConfigSync.ts`
  - `DshProviderRoute` 增加可选 `compat`（`thinkingFormat` / `supportsReasoningEffort`），模型条目增加可选 `reasoningEfforts`
  - 自定义 provider 模型：`supportsThinking === true` 时渲染默认 OpenAI 档位（`off/low/medium/high/max`），存在 `customParams.thinkingLevelMap` 时按显式映射
  - 套餐（token-proxy）模型：`DshPlanProviderInput` 增加 `supportsThinking` / `thinkingConfig`，从服务端 thinking 元数据渲染 `reasoningEfforts`
  - 仅 `openai-completions` 路由声明 reasoning compat；`anthropic-messages` 路由保持裸模型（pi-ai 该协议无 reasoning-effort 字段）
- `src/main/main.ts`
  - `getPlanProvider` 转发 `supportsThinking` / `thinkingConfig` 到 DSH plan provider 输入
- `src/main/libs/dshConfigSync.test.ts`
  - 新增 5 个测试：默认 efforts、显式 thinkingLevelMap、套餐 thinking config、anthropic 裸路由、无思考能力模型不受影响

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [ ] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

本地验证（fork 上）：

```text
npx vitest run src/main/libs/dshConfigSync.test.ts   # 34 passed (5 new)
npx vitest run src/main/libs/dsh                     # 90 passed
npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 (touched files)  # clean
npm run compile:electron                             # clean
```

端到端渲染验证：同步后 `settings.yaml` 生成：

```yaml
lobsterai-plan:
  api: openai-completions
  compat:
    thinkingFormat: openai
    supportsReasoningEffort: true
  models:
    - id: deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp
      reasoningEfforts:
        'off': null
        high: high
        xhigh: xhigh
```

## Screenshots (if applicable)

无 UI 截图（改动在 main 进程配置同步层；DSH Web UI 由内置 runtime 渲染）。

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

<!-- If your PR includes Electron-specific changes, describe them here -->
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [ ] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [ ] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management

说明：改动在 main 进程的 DSH 配置同步层（`src/main/libs/dshConfigSync.ts` 与 `src/main/main.ts` 的 `getPlanProvider`），不涉及 preload / IPC / 窗口管理。生成的 `settings.yaml` 由内置 DSH runtime（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`）消费，DSH Web UI 的思考强度控件即基于这些字段渲染。

## Additional Notes

- 这是 LobsterAI 侧的集成边界修复，不涉及 OpenClaw patch。
- 保持"不 over-claim"原则：仅当模型明确支持思考（`supportsThinking` / thinking 元数据）时才声明 `reasoningEfforts`；wire 值遵循 DSH 自身 schema（`reasoningEfforts` / `compat`），已对照安装的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` runtime 验证。

prs.title: Add optional keyless Parallel web search
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds Parallel as an explicit engine in the bundled web-search skill. Users can run `WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE=parallel bash "$SKILLS_ROOT/web-search/scripts/search.sh" "query"` without a Parallel account, API key, or browser connection. Anonymous access uses Fast and is rate limited.

Fast scores 80 F1 on [DeepSearchQA](https://artificialanalysis.ai/agents/search-api?search-api-quality-chart=deepsearchqa&search-api-providers=perplexity-medium-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cperplexity-high-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cocten-web-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cperplexity-low-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_advanced-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cbrave-llm-context-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cyou-com-highlights-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa_auto-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cfirecrawl_serp-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_basic-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel-fast-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ctinyfish-web-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa-instant-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa_fast-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cyou_com-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_turbo-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ckeenable_pro-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ckeenable_realtime-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ctavily_basic-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cbrave-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api#search-api-quality-chart-tabs), which tests whether an agent can gather complete, precise answers across many searches. The current [Time per Task chart](https://artificialanalysis.ai/agents/search-api?search-api-quality-chart=deepsearchqa&search-api-providers=perplexity-medium-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cperplexity-high-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cocten-web-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cperplexity-low-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_advanced-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cbrave-llm-context-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cyou-com-highlights-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa_auto-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cfirecrawl_serp-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_basic-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel-fast-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ctinyfish-web-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa-instant-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cexa_fast-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cyou_com-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cparallel_turbo-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ckeenable_pro-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ckeenable_realtime-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Ctavily_basic-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api%2Cbrave-gpt-5-6-luna-medium-search-api#search-api-latency-chart-tabs) shows 15.8 seconds, combining derived model time and measured search time across benchmark tasks. Those are provider benchmarks, not measurements of this LobsterAI integration.

## Related Issue

None. No applicable pre-contribution issue requirement was found.

## Changes Made

- Adds a maintained MCP SDK adapter at `https://search.parallel.ai/mcp`, discovers `web_search`, and maps titles, URLs, and excerpts into the existing search response and Markdown citations.
- Routes an explicit Parallel choice through the normal CLI and bridge without launching or connecting a browser. The existing Google-then-Bing `auto` path stays in place.
- Bounds response reads and output, keeps failures visible, and cleans up the MCP session. Bumps the skill to 1.0.3 so installed copies can upgrade.
- Documents selection and data flow. When selected, queries go to Parallel; browser cookies are not sent. Requests use `LobsterAI-WebSearch/1.0.3` as their User-Agent so Parallel can measure aggregate project usage.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests

prs.title: fix(chat): prevent stale reply targets from duplicating replies
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent a later visible answer from being delivered to stale message anchors left behind by silent completions, streams ending without `Done`, or aborted turns.

For example, in one channel session:

1. Turn A finishes without a visible answer.
2. Turn B produces a visible answer.
3. Before the fix, B's answer can be sent to both A's old anchor and B's current anchor. After the fix, A's unused target has been retired.

Drain pending reply targets at the end of turn cleanup and during abort cleanup while holding the session permit. Queued turns already register their targets only after admission, keeping their destinations out of the previous turn's cleanup. Intentional silence stays silent.

Add five service integration tests with a mock provider and recording outbound handler, covering silent completion, EOF without `Done`, abort cleanup, normal visible replies, and prequeued/new arrivals during abort cleanup.

Forwarder cancellation retains its bounded wait, so already in-flight sends may still complete.

## Implementation context

Reproduced the issue with a mock provider and recording outbound handler, then added reply-target cleanup while holding the session permit. In the earlier red/green run, four regression cases failed on unpatched sources and passed with the fix; the normal-reply control passed in both.

## Validation

### Completed

- [x] `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test --locked -p moltis-chat --all-features --test channel_reply_retirement`: all five tests passed.

<details>
<summary>Feature selection for the workspace Clippy check</summary>

The selected list contains all 367 remaining workspace package features. Its resolved dependency graph was checked to confirm CUDA and Vulkan were disabled and no other workspace feature was omitted.

```bash
selected_features=$(cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1 | python3 -c '
```

## Summary
- Fix the coverage-discovered browser profile lock race: own the lock with a guard that explicitly unlocks on drop, while retaining the guard when container cleanup is unconfirmed. Three deterministic duplicated-descriptor regressions cover release, next-owner exclusion, and quarantine.
- Update both main and desktop lockfiles to `rustls-webpki 0.103.16` and `webpki-roots` / `webpki-root-certs 1.0.10` for the CA distrust incident tracked by Go as CVE-2026-111943. Includes the required main-workspace AWS-LC dependency update.
- Compile the same offline regression against both lockfiles. Reissue all eight upstream public keys under an ephemeral trusted CA, reject them, and accept a benign P-384 key. Fixtures contain only public keys, with upstream provenance, license, and Go SPKI hash checks.
- Document the need to rebuild binaries and update OS/container trust stores. Legacy `rustls-webpki 0.102.8` (Discord/APNs) and native/OpenSSL verification remain separate coverage work tracked in Beads `moltis-p73`; the legacy `webpki-roots 0.26.11` shim now re-exports 1.0.10. issues.title: 📢 [Feature] Coming in v2.3.0: Making QwenPaw Lighter and More Extensible

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Hi everyone! We’re working on making QwenPaw lighter and more modular through a plugin refactor, improving its capabilities while making it easier to extend. This issue shares what we’re working on, our preliminary test results, and what’s next. We’d also love to hear your needs and suggestions. ## Why are we doing this? As QwenPaw supports more features, its codebase, dependencies, and maintenance scope continue to grow. However, different users often need different capabilities. For QwenPaw users, we want to make it possible to choose and enable the features they need, reducing unnecessary runtime overhead. For community contributors, we want to make developing, integrating, and testing code more flexible and convenient, without having to worry about disrupting QwenPaw’s core architecture, so extensions can be developed and maintained independently. Our goals are: + **A lighter core:** Factor out QwenPaw’s core components and shared capabilities while preserving effectiveness, stability, and verifiability. + **On-demand capabilities:** Provide optional capabilities through plugins so users can choose what they need and reduce runtime overhead. + **Easier customization and extension development:** Provide clear extension APIs to reduce the effort required to develop, debug, and maintain plugins. + **More reliable plugin management:** Improve plugin loading, updating, and unloading to reduce their impact on other functionality. ## What are we working on? Our current work focuses on two areas: ### 1. Plugin lifecycle refactor [PR #7565](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7565) improves plugin loading, unloading, updates, and failure recovery. The main improvements include: + **Independent plugin start, stop, and update:** Changing a single plugin no longer rebuilds every workspace, reducing the impact on other functionality. + **Framework-managed resource cleanup:** Disabling a plugin revokes its registered capabilities and stops managed background tasks and connections while preserving user configuration, reducing leftover resources. + **Recovery from failed updates:** New versions are checked before switching. Failed loads can roll back, and interrupted updates have a recovery mechanism. + **Simpler community development:** Existing extension APIs are retained, while the framework handles common cleanup and configuration protection logic so developers can focus on functionality. ### 2. Extracting IM/Channel implementations into plugins Building on this foundation, [PR #8187](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8187) refactors all channels currently supported by QwenPaw into plugins. When a user enables a channel they need, QwenPaw installs the corresponding code and imports the channel SDK in a subprocess. This reduces runtime memory usage caused by importing SDKs for channels that are not in use. We want to make channel loading, operation, and shutdown increasingly independent, align resource usage more closely with the features actually enabled, and make it easier for community developers to integrate and maintain their own channel plugins. ## Preliminary test results We’re comparing runtime resource usage before and after the channel plugin refactor. Here are the preliminary results: | Metric | Before refactor: no channels enabled | After refactor: no channels enabled | After refactor: DingTalk only | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Runtime memory usage | 450.31 MiB | 288.56 MiB (-35.9%) | 389.83 MiB (-13.4%) | | Startup time until the core Agent is ready | 5.24 s | 2.69 s (48.7% reduction) | 3.30 s (37.0% reduction) | Test environment: Python 3.13.10, QwenPaw 2.2.2 beta4. Total memory usage includes both the main process and channel subprocesses. These results reflect our current test environment only. We’ll continue testing different channel combinations and real-world message sending and receiving, focusing on resource usage as well as runtime stability and user experience. ## When will this be available? After completing stability validation and upgrade compatibility testing, we hope to **ship these changes in the next stable release, v2.3.0**. The exact release scope will be adjusted based on test results. ## What’s next? In the near term, we’ll focus on: + Expanding tests for upgrades from older versions, as well as plugin installation, updates, disabling, and uninstallation. + Improving developer documentation, examples, and migration guidance for the new plugin system. + Refactoring more modules, components, and features into plugins, progressively separating out QwenPaw’s core architecture. Longer term, we’re also considering extracting more optional capabilities that can be maintained independently, trimming default dependencies, and improving the plugin management experience. These directions will evolve based on practical results and community feedback. ## Join the discussion We’d love to hear from you: + Which IM/Channels do you typically use? How many do you enable at the same time? + In your deployment environment, which is the biggest concern: memory usage, installation size, or startup time? + Which features would you like to install on demand, and which should remain available out of the box? + If you’ve developed a custom channel or plugin, what was the biggest challenge? Feel free to share your use cases, test results, or suggestions below. Contributions to the related PR discussions, testing, and development are also welcome. We’ll keep this issue updated as the work continues. Thank you for helping make QwenPaw lighter, easier to use, and easier to extend! ------------------- # [Feature] 即将于 v2.3.0 推出：让 QwenPaw 更轻量、更易扩展 大家好！我们正在推进 QwenPaw 的轻量化与插件化重构，希望在优化功能的同时，让 QwenPaw 更轻、更容易扩展。 这篇 issue 想和大家同步目前正在做的事情、初步测试结果，以及接下来的方向，也欢迎大家分享自己的需求和建议。 ## 为什么要做这件事？ 随着支持的功能越来越多，QwenPaw 的代码、依赖和维护范围也在增长。但不同用户真正需要的能力往往不同。 我们希望，对使用 QwenPaw 的用户，能根据自身需求自主选择并启用需要的功能，从而减少不必要的运行负担；对贡献 QwenPaw 的社区开发者，能更灵活、便捷地开发、接入和验证开发代码，不用担心影响qwenpaw核心架构，更方便地独立开发和维护。 因此，这次工作的目标是： + **更轻的核心：** 在保持效果、稳定和可验证性的基础上抽取出 QwenPaw 的核心组件和公共能力。 + **按需使用：** 让可选能力通过插件提供，用户根据自己的需要选择，从而降低用户运行负担。 + **更方便的二次开发：** 提供清晰的扩展接口，降低开发、调试和维护插件的成本。 + **更可靠的插件管理：** 改进插件加载、更新和卸载流程，减少这些操作对其他功能的影响。 ## 目前在做什么？ 当前主要推进两部分工作： ### 1. 插件化重构 [PR #7565](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7565) 完善插件的加载、卸载、更新和失败恢复流程。 这次重构主要带来以下改进： + **插件独立启停和更新：** 不再因单个插件的变更重建所有工作区，减少对其他功能的影响。 + **资源由框架统一清理：** 停用时撤销插件注册的能力、停止托管的后台任务和连接，同时保留用户配置，减少资源残留。 + **更新失败可恢复：** 新版本先检查再切换，加载失败时可回退，更新中断后也有恢复机制。 + **社区开发更省心：** 沿用现有扩展接口，由框架承担通用的清理和配置保护逻辑，让开发者更专注于功能本身。 ### 2. 将 IM/Channel 拆分为插件 [PR #8187](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8187) 在此基础上对 QwenPaw 当前支持的所有 channel 实现了插件化重构，用户根据需求启用所需 channel时，QwenPaw 再安装对应代码并在一个子进程中导入channel sdk，从而降低了日常使用 QwenPaw 的过程中因为导入无需使用的channel sdk带来的运行内存占用。 我们希望逐步让 channel 的加载、运行和停止更加独立，让资源使用更贴近实际启用的功能，也方便社区开发者接入和维护自己的 channel 插件。 ## 初步测试结果 目前，我们正在对比channel插件化重构前后的运行资源占用。下面是阶段性测试结果： | 指标 | 插件化前：不启用channel | 插件化后：不启用channel | 插件化后：只运行钉钉 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 运行内存 | 450.31 MiB | 288.56 MiB
（-35.9%） | 389.83 MiB
（-13.4%） | | 启动到核心 Agent 就绪 | 5.24 秒 | 2.69 秒（减少48.7%） | 3.30 秒（减少37.0%） | 测试环境：Python版本3.13.10，QwenPaw 版本2.2.2 beta4。整体内存统计包含主进程和 channel 子进程。 这些结果仅代表当前测试环境。我们还会继续验证不同 channel 组合和实际消息收发场景，关注资源占用，也关注运行稳定性和使用体验。 ## 什么时候可以使用？ 我们希望在完成稳定性验证和升级兼容测试后，**在下一个正式版本 v2.3.0中推出这部分改动**。具体发布范围会根据测试结果调整。 ## 接下来准备做什么？ 近期，我们会重点推进： + 完善旧版本升级，以及插件安装、更新、停用和卸载的测试。 + 完善新版插件系统开发文档、示例和迁移说明。 + 继续实现更多模块、组件和功能的插件化重构，逐渐抽离出 QwenPaw 核心架构 更长期，我们也在考虑继续拆分适合独立维护的可选能力、精简默认依赖，以及改善插件管理体验。这些方向会结合实际效果和社区反馈逐步确定。 ## 欢迎一起讨论 我们很想了解： + 你通常使用哪些 IM/Channel？会同时启用几个？ + 在你的部署环境中，内存、安装体积、启动速度，哪个问题最明显？ + 你希望哪些功能可以按需安装，哪些功能应该保留开箱即用？ + 如果你开发过自定义 channel 或插件，遇到的最大困难是什么？ 欢迎直接在下面分享使用场景、测试结果或建议，也欢迎参与相关 PR 的讨论、测试和开发。我们会继续在这个 issue 中同步后续更新。 感谢大家一起让 QwenPaw 更轻、更好用，也更容易扩展！

issues.title: [Bug]: 跨会话消息（chat_with_agent）被注册成独立 chat，同一 session 的对话在 UI 中分裂为多个页面
issues.body:
> [AI] **AI 撰写声明**：本 issue 由 QwenPaw 内置 AI 助手协助用户调查、整理并撰写（用户口述需求，AI 完成取证与行文）。所有证据为本地实测记录，欢迎维护者按上述步骤独立复核；如内容有误，责任在使用者与 AI，特此说明。

> 建议标签：`bug` · `Console (frontend web UI)` · `Core / Backend`

## 环境

- QwenPaw 版本：**2.2.2b4**
- OS：Windows 10 (AMD64)
- 安装方式：一键脚本（venv 内 `qwenpaw` 包）
- 渠道：Console（桌面端，同逻辑适用于网页 Console）

## 现象（一句话）

通过 `chat_with_agent` 向**已有会话**注入消息时，消息没有进入用户正在看的那个 chat 页面，而是被 `Auto-registered` 成了一个**同 session、不同 user_id 的新 chat 条目**——用户视角上，"对方的回复显示在了另一个会话里"。

## 预期结果 vs 实际结果（Expected vs Actual）

- **预期结果**：注入消息及其回复显示在用户原对话页面（chat `66e01759-559c-4dcc-8c2b-d2acac70e940`）中，`chats.json` 不新增条目。
- **实际结果**：消息到达时被 `Auto-registered` 新建 chat `83154c71-8f92-4758-8611-66940ac91058`（同 session、`user_id=j9hznn`），原对话页面看不到该消息及其回复。

## 复现步骤

1. 在 Console 正常开一个对话（下称原对话），产生会话 `S`。
2. 从另一个会话调用 `chat_with_agent`，**显式指定 `session_id=S`** 向原对话发一条消息（例如通讯测试）。
3. 观察 UI / `workspaces/<agent>/chats.json`：
   - 新增了一个 chat 条目，`session_id` 与原对话**完全相同**，但 `user_id` 是发送方 agent id；
   - 原对话页面（用户正开着的那个）**看不到这条消息**。

## 本次实测证据（可直接核对）

> [PRIVACY] 隐私说明：下表中的 chat/session 标识与 agent id 均为本地测试环境自动生成的随机 ID，不含任何个人信息、设备路径或凭据；日志片段已去除本机路径。

| chat id | session_id | user_id | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `66e01759-559c-4dcc-8c2b-d2acac70e940` | `1790901923762-h7ojs2k` | `default` | 用户的原对话 |
| `83154c71-8f92-4758-8611-66940ac91058` | **`1790901923762-h7ojs2k`（同上）** | `j9hznn` | 反向消息到达时被新建，名字"测试反向主动消息显示" |

日志（`qwenpaw.log`，08:48:56 恰为消息到达时刻）：

```
2026-10-02 08:48:56 | INFO | qwenpaw\app\chats\manager.py:208 | Auto-registered new chat: 83154c71-8f92-4758-8611-66940ac91058 -> 1790901923762-h7ojs2k
```

（同类现象另有两例：`a0e261ef -> 1c2189d4-...`、`39f10adf -> j9hznn:to:default:...`。）

## 根因（已定位到行）

1. `agents/tools/agent_management.py` · `build_agent_chat_request()`：
   ```python
   request_payload = {
       "session_id": final_session_id,
       "user_id": caller_agent_id,   # ← 病灶：把发送方 agent id 当作 user_id
       ...
   }
   ```
2. `app/routers/console.py:396` · `post_console_chat()`：把 payload 的 `sender_id` 直接传给 `get_or_create_chat(session_id, user_id, channel)`。
3. `app/chats/manager.py` · `get_or_create_chat()`：按 `(session_id, user_id, channel)` 三元组查找——`(同 session, j9hznn, console)` 匹配不到用户原有的 `(同 session, default, console)`，于是 auto-register 新 chat。

即：**跨会话消息在 user_id 层面"冒用"了 agent 身份，导致三元组匹配必然失败**。消息本身带的只有文本前缀 `[Agent xx requesting]`，没有结构化的来源标注可用来归并。

## 影响

- 用户正在看的对话页面收不到注入消息及其回复，误以为"消息发给了别的会话"；
- 同一 session 的对话历史分裂进多个 chat 条目，按 user 过滤/检索时错乱；
- chat 列表被注入消息产生的孤儿条目污染（每次跨会话通讯 +1 条）。

## 建议修法（参考 OpenClaw 的成熟设计，源码可对标）

### 1. `get_or_create_chat` 增加入站守卫 + 归并回退（核心，可独立成 PR）

参考 `openclaw/openclaw` 的 `src/channels/session.ts::recordInboundSession`（`createIfMissing` 参数一路透传，受保护路径**绝不新建会话**）：

```python
async def get_or_create_chat(self, session_id, user_id, channel=...,
                             create_if_missing: bool = True, ...):
    existing = await self._repo.get_chat_by_id(session_id, user_id, channel)
    if existing:
        return existing
    if not create_if_missing:                      # 仅 inter-session 注入路径传 False
        same = await self._repo.list_chats_by_session(session_id, channel)
        if len(same) == 1:
            return same[0]                         # 恰一个 → 并入原对话
        if len(same) > 1:
            raise AmbiguousSessionTarget(...)      # 多候选 → fail-closed，绝不猜（多用户安全）
    # 正常用户消息路径保持现状（auto-register 行为零变化）
    ...
```

调用点：`post_console_chat` 检测到 inter-session 来源时传 `create_if_missing=False`。

### 2. 消息级 provenance（结构化来源，替代"user_id 冒用"）

参考 `src/sessions/input-provenance.ts`：`kind = external_user | inter_session | internal_system` 三分类挂到消息对象上；模型侧注入 `[Inter-session message ... isUser=false]` 信封防混淆，UI 渲染时剥离并显示来源徽标。对应到 QwenPaw：payload 增加 `input_provenance`，**`user_id` 不再用于决定 chat 归属**。

### 3. 注入路径只读复用，不写任何归属字段

吸取 OpenClaw issue #54441 的教训（跨会话消息覆盖 `lastRoute` 导致回复投错频道）：归并复用时 `user_id`/`pinned`/`name` 等归属字段一律只读，不更新。

## 对标源码

- `openclaw/openclaw` · `src/channels/session.ts` — `recordInboundSession` / `createIfMissing` 透传
- `openclaw/openclaw` · `src/sessions/input-provenance.ts` — provenance 模型与 `isUser=false` 信封
- `openclaw/openclaw` · `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` — 所有权校验 + 内部通道投递

## 补充

- 本 issue 的完整调查过程（含 `chats.json` 三页面归属核对、日志取证）可在需要时补充；
- 我认为 PR 规模约 150~400 行（核心守卫 ~65 行 + repo 查询 + 测试 ~150 行），如维护者认可方向，我可跟进提交 PR。

issues.title: Bug: source-group headers overlap their first sidebar conversation
issues.body:
## Description

In the sidebar's source/group mode, moving a normal conversation to **Scheduled
task conversations** or **Conversations with subagents**, expanding the group,
then hovering/selecting its first conversation makes the conversation background
overlap the bottom of the group header.

Reproduced on official main `7cb6234f25798ee8fe1554206942ad87b65fe73d`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Switch the sidebar to source/group mode.
2. Long-press and drag a conversation from an ordinary group to either fixed
   scheduled-task or subagent group.
3. Expand the destination group and hover its first conversation.

Expected: the source header and conversation have separate backgrounds.
Actual: the conversation background starts 4px before the header ends.

## Cause and proposed fix

The virtual list allocates 36px to every group header. An ordinary header uses
32px height + 2px top and bottom margins = 36px. The fixed source headers instead
use an 8px top margin, so need 42px. Reserving 42px only for `cron`/`subagents`
headers restores the intended 2px gap without changing the theme or drag logic.

I have reproduced this with real pointer dragging against fixture HTTP responses
and prepared a small fix with regression tests.

prs.title: fix: prevent stale requests after deleting chat
prs.body:
Fixes #8368
- Introduce a temporary "deleted route" flag within `sessionApi`:
  - Upon successful deletion via the sidebar, record the local ID, backend UUID, and runtime session ID.
  - Ensure `useChatRouteResolution` skips `resolveChat` when encountering a deleted route.
  - Clear these flags during route transitions, agent switches, or test resets.
- When deleting the current session, trigger navigation to a new session before refreshing the sidebar list to prevent race conditions between list updates and route navigation.
- Scope the `session-model-changed` event to include `agentId`, `sessionId`, and `chatId`:
  - Restrict `SessionThinking` and Advisor availability updates to events relevant to the current session.
  - Maintain backward compatibility for existing global events that lack these details.
- Add regression tests covering route deletion, model event isolation, and navigation sequencing.

prs.title: chore(deps): replace GPL-licensed html2text with stdlib converter
prs.body:
## Description Remove the `html2text` dependency. `html2text` is licensed under **GPL-3.0**, which is incompatible with QwenPaw's Apache-2.0 license. It was only used in one place: `web_fetch` (`src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/web_search.py`) to convert fetched HTML into Markdown. This PR replaces it with a small stdlib (`html.parser`) based converter in `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/_html_to_markdown.py` — **no new dependency is added**. The converter mirrors the previous html2text configuration (links kept, images dropped, no line wrapping) and handles headings, paragraphs, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline code and fenced `
` blocks (whitespace preserved, also inside blockquotes), nested ordered/unordered lists, blockquotes, simple tables, `
`/`
` and HTML entities. The `` prepending logic in `_html_to_text` is unchanged.

Design notes:
- Only `script`, `style`, `title` and `iframe` are dropped with their content. `HTMLParser`, like browsers, reads these as raw text, so nothing nests inside them and an unclosed `template`/`svg`/`select`/`noscript` or a missing `</head>` can never hide the rest of the page. Like html2text, the text of those other elements is kept (`select` options go on separate lines).
- Line breaks are written lazily: block elements only *request* breaks, which are flushed before the next text. Empty elements therefore leave no blank lines, empty list items (e.g. icon-only footer links) vanish with contiguous ordered numbering, `<li><p>…</p></li>` stays on the marker line, and no global whitespace tidy pass is needed (so `<pre>` content is never touched).
- Links, emphasis and blockquotes are captured and wrapped on close: emphasis markers hug the text (`A<b> bold </b>text` → `A **bold** text`; italics use `*` so they also work right after a word), inline code containing a backtick uses a double-backtick fence, card-style links wrapping headings/paragraphs are flattened into a single-line link, code blocks are never wrapped in links/emphasis, and mis-nested tags are closed together.
- `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:` and `#...` links are rendered as plain text (case-insensitive, leading whitespace ignored). Parentheses and spaces in link destinations are escaped so the full target survives.
- Code fences (fenced `<pre>` blocks and inline code) are longer than any backtick run in the code, so Markdown examples inside `<pre>` stay intact.
- Paragraphs inside table cells stay on their row, and cells are closed implicitly at the next cell/row/table end (`</td>`/`</th>` are optional in HTML); `<ol start>` is honored.

Known differences from html2text (acceptable for `web_fetch`, whose goal is readable page content for the model):
- Tables are rendered as `| A | B |` rows without the `| --- |` separator row (not strict GFM).
- Complex structures (nested tables, definition lists) degrade to plain text.

Also removes the now-unneeded `html2text` stub module in `tests/unit/agents/test_tool_result_pruning_middleware.py`.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** N/A — pure text transformation, no network/config changes.

prs.title: feat(memory): support PowerContext prepared context and Artifact APIs
prs.body:
## Description

Update the optional PowerContext memory backend to work with PowerContext v1.4.0 and expose its structured context and Artifact APIs. This fixes the old memory request/response assumptions and lets QwenPaw reuse profiles, topic memories, atomic memories, and experiences when preparing a turn.

- Use Atomic Memory writes and preserve exact artifact/source references on recall. Resolve a stable Scope for each installation and agent.
- Make `prepare` the default recall mode, with ordered Profile, Topic Memory, Memory, and Experience sections and a UTF-8 byte budget. Keep explicit `memory` mode for older servers.
- Register `prepare_context` and seven Artifact tools alongside `memory_search` and `memory_remember`: schema discovery, search, list, get, history, create, and conditional replacement. Cover atomic memory, topic memory, experience, skill, profile, prompt, and handoff; search is available for the four searchable families.
- Preserve returned records, pagination cursors, exact revisions, and ETags. Update the bilingual configuration UI and documentation, including old-server migration guidance.

The plugin version is **1.2.0**; the recommended PowerContext server version is **1.4.0**. These are independent version numbers. Existing users of the PowerContext v0.2 server must explicitly select `memory` mode; prepared context and Artifact tools require their corresponding server endpoints.

**Related Issue:** Follow-up to #7080.

**Security Considerations:** Retrieved context remains explicitly marked as untrusted historical data. Network read/write tools retain host governance metadata, and Artifact replacements require the ETag returned by the read path. Deployment credentials, private infrastructure configuration, and acceptance logs are not included in this PR.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor thinking defaults and declared wire controls
prs.body:
## Description

Fix a mismatch between the thinking setting displayed by the Console and the parameters sent by OpenAI-compatible providers.

For a custom Chat Completions model declaring native effort control (`low`, `medium`, `xhigh`, supports off), saving the model default as off (`thinking_enabled=false`) currently has two effects:

1. An inherited request omits the default altogether, although the Console displays off.
2. An explicit off preference is incorrectly routed to compatibility flags because `_uses_compat_thinking_controls()` treats the presence of `thinking_enabled` as a protocol declaration. Changing a default must not change the wire protocol.

An explicit session preference also leaves stale `extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking/reasoning_effort` values behind. A serving engine such as vLLM can give these template arguments precedence over the new request setting.

### Changes

- Apply the existing model-default hook before agent/session preferences.
- Serialize configured OpenAI model defaults through the same declared-control mapper used by explicit preferences.
- Share model-default interpretation between the display and provider construction paths; include configured budgets and nested chat-template settings.
- Honor an explicit model/provider wire declaration before the legacy compatibility fallback.
- Replace conflicting nested template controls when applying a higher-priority preference, preserving unrelated JSON and the original provider/model state.
- Add SDK-boundary regression tests for native and compatibility protocols, inherited defaults, reset/reload, and request isolation.

No model-name matching, global default change, frontend change, or database migration is introduced. Unsupported effort labels are not silently renamed.

**Related Issue:** No matching backend issue identified.

**Security Considerations:** Settings are resolved into request-local dictionaries. Tests verify that shared provider/model configuration is unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Tests

## Testing


## Evidence

Validated on Windows with Python 3.12.3. Tests capture the final SDK Chat Completions arguments before transport; no remote model service is contacted.

Before the fix, the initial regression set reproduced **10 failures / 12 passes**, including missing `reasoning_effort` for an inherited off default and conflicting nested template arguments.

After the fix:


Request-level example:

| Model default | Request preference | Native Chat Completions request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | inherit | `reasoning_effort="none"` |

The full commands were attempted; this PR does not claim that they passed:

- Plain `pytest -q --maxfail=3 --tb=short` stopped during collection because both `tests/integration/test_backup.py` and `tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py` import as `test_backup`. Neither file is changed here.

The native off mapping uses the existing `reasoning_effort="none"` contract, not a vLLM-specific model-name exception. vLLM 0.28.0 documents automatic `enable_thinking=false` for this value: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.28.0/features/reasoning_outputs/#automatic-enable_thinking-activation

prs.title: fix(plugins): do not abort a plugin install when invalidate_caches fails
prs.body:
## Description

`PluginLoader` called `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally at three sites. On Python builds where that stdlib call itself raises (the issue shows `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'` on a distro-patched 3.11), the exception aborted the whole plugin install or hot-update. Refreshing import caches is best effort, so a failure should not be fatal.

The three calls now go through `_invalidate_import_caches()`, which catches the error and logs it at debug level.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8265

prs.title: feat(agents): stop replaying media the model no longer needs
prs.body:
## Description

Every request re-uploaded every image and video block stored in history. A screenshot-heavy WeChat session reached a **48.9 MB** request body; the endpoint rejected it with

```
openai.APIStatusError: Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded
```

and because the block lives in `agent.state.context`, every later turn failed the same way — the session stayed wedged until the file was edited by hand.

### Why the existing guards miss it

- `CappingFormatterMixin` caps **each block** at 2 MB. All 43 blocks in that session were below the cap, so nothing tripped.
- Context compaction triggers on **tokens** (`trigger_ratio * context_size`), and image tokens are cheap while their bytes are not — the log showed `outcome=at_or_below_trigger` at a 48 MB body.
- Prompt caching does not help either: a cache hit lowers the *price* of replaying the prefix (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash bills cached tokens at ~10% of input), but it **never removes the upload**.

### What this changes

Two rules, applied **only to the per-request copy** (stored history and channel delivery are untouched — `_normalize_messages_for_formatter` already deep-copies):

1. **Delivery is not context.** Media returned by `send_file_to_user` is never model input: the channel ships the file, so the model gets a reference instead of the bytes.
2. **Consumed media is not re-sent.** Media belonging to a completed turn (an assistant message with text and no tool calls, followed by something newer) has already been turned into text by the model, so it becomes a reference:

```
[image not re-sent to the model: slide_v_zh_00002_.png (image/png, 0.74 MB)
 at D:\...\slide_v_zh_00002_.png — call view_image again if another look is needed]
```

Only the **current turn's** media stays inline. That keeps the newest message working, including a top-level `view_audio` / `view_image` data block stored in an assistant message. A second look now costs one tool call instead of re-uploading megabytes on every turn.

Properties worth noting:

- **Deterministic** for a given history, and the boundary only moves forward, so prefix-cache churn is confined to the turn boundary rather than rewriting the conversation each request.
- Runs **before** `_prepare_media_sources`, so elided media is never read from disk or base64-encoded.
- **Kill switch:** `QWENPAW_DISABLE_MEDIA_ELISION=1`; extra delivery tools via `QWENPAW_DELIVERY_ONLY_TOOL_RESULTS=a,b`.

## Evidence

- Session in the report: 43 media blocks, 35.4 MB decoded (`view_image` 24 / 17.39 MB, `send_file_to_user` 14 / 11.50 MB, `desktop_screenshot` 5 / 6.51 MB); request dump 48.9 MB.
- With these rules only the current turn's media is inlined (typically 0–3 blocks); everything older becomes a one-line reference. Delivery is unaffected because channels render the tool-result block, not the formatter output.
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/test_media_turn_scoped_elision.py` → 11 passed (including a test that the stored `Msg` list is not mutated, and one that a current-turn `view_audio` block stays inline).
- `pytest tests/unit/{agents,channels,app}` → 9065 passed, 22 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 are the pre-existing `test_offloader.py` retention failures (they fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree on this Windows host as well).
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy` (0 errors) and `pylint` (10.00/10) clean on the changed files.

## Not in this PR (deliberate)

- **No aggregate byte budget.** One turn that views many large images can still exceed an endpoint limit; that case would still need a manual session repair. A byte budget (and a retry on `length limit exceeded` / 413) is the natural follow-up, but it adds config surface and is better discussed separately.
- **No storage-side change.** Media still lives in the session as base64; this PR only stops replaying it. Storing `{path, sha256, dims}` instead is the longer-term direction (see #8335).

## Related

- **#8335** — design discussion: 48 MB bodies, permanent wedges, the two cost bills
  (tokens vs bytes), and the roadmap for media-by-reference.
- This PR implements the **S1 + S2** slice of that design. The aggregate byte
  budget and the oversized-body retry described there are intentionally left
  out, so **#8335 should stay open** to track them.

> Note for reviewers: this PR is intentionally *not* a closing reference. GitHub
> only auto-links an issue when the body says `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n`; this one
> is a partial implementation, so link it manually from the sidebar ("Link an
> issue") if a sidebar link is preferred.

prs.title: feat(deploy): add offline image variant with Office/PDF toolchain
prs.body:
## Description

Adds `deploy/Dockerfile.offline`, a variant of `deploy/Dockerfile` that bakes the
Office/PDF toolchain into the image, plus a short section in `scripts/README.md`
explaining how to build it.

The default image intentionally stays lean: the `docx`, `pptx`, `xlsx`, and `pdf`
skills resolve their prerequisites at task time (`apt-get`/`npm`/`pip`), which
fails in air-gapped or offline deployments and is slow for document-heavy
workloads. This variant preinstalls:

- **System:** `libreoffice-{writer,calc,impress,draw}`, `pandoc`, `poppler-utils`,
  `qpdf`, `tesseract-ocr` (+ `eng`, `chi-sim`, `chi-tra` traineddata)
- **npm (global):** `docx`, `pptxgenjs`, `pdf-lib`, `pdfjs-dist`, `react-icons`,
  `react`, `react-dom`, `sharp`, with `NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules`
- **Python (venv):** `pypdf`, `pdfplumber`, `reportlab`, `openpyxl`, `xlrd`,
  `pandas`, `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `markitdown[docx,pptx,xlsx,xls,pdf]`,
  `pdf2image`, `pytesseract`, `lxml`, `defusedxml`

The Python libraries are installed **before** the app so that the app's own pins
win in the final resolve (`markitdown`'s `magika` pulls `onnxruntime`, and the app
pins `onnxruntime<1.24`). The `uv` binary is therefore copied earlier in the
offline file than in the default one.

`scripts/docker_build.sh` already honours the `DOCKERFILE` env var, so no script
change was needed:

```bash
DOCKERFILE=deploy/Dockerfile.offline bash scripts/docker_build.sh qwenpaw:offline
```

Trade-off: the image grows by roughly 2 GB and duplicates the shared parts of
`deploy/Dockerfile`. The alternative — an opt-in build arg in the default
`Dockerfile` — was avoided so the default image and its build cache are
unaffected. If the duplication becomes a maintenance burden, collapsing to a
build arg is the natural follow-up.

**Related Issue:** N/A

services; the added `tesseract`/`pandoc`/`libreoffice` packages are invoked
headless by the existing skills.

## Description

The Ollama setup flow used by `qwenpaw init`, `qwenpaw models config` and `qwenpaw models set-llm` can prompt for a model name without first discovering the server's models. Even when `/v1/models` returns that model, activation rejects it because it has never been registered locally.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #1453; fixes the CLI initialization failure shown in its attached transcript.

**Security Considerations:** Discovery uses the already-configured Ollama endpoint and credentials. No new external destination or authentication behavior is introduced. Reproduction uses synthetic model metadata on localhost and isolated configuration directories.

- [x] Existing CLI docs already promise Ollama auto-discovery; this restores that documented behavior
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

Not applicable: this change affects CLI provider selection, not a channel implementation.

## Testing

Linux, Python 3.11.15, base `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`, using the existing isolated `.[dev,test,full]` environment with `PYTHONPATH` selecting this worktree.

The reproduction launches the real Click/Questionary terminal command in a PTY. It uses the actual ProviderManager, OllamaProvider and OpenAI client against a localhost HTTP server implementing `/v1/models`. No CLI, provider or manager behavior is mocked. The server advertises synthetic `qwen3:32b` metadata.

## Evidence

Before the fix:

```text
Ollama configured model ids: []
Actual HTTP-discovered models: ['qwen3:32b']
Select provider for LLM: Ollama (ollama)
LLM model name (required): qwen3:32b
Error: Model 'ollama/qwen3:32b' not found
Actual CLI exit: 1
```

The direct production discovery request succeeds, but the CLI issues no discovery request before rejecting the model.

After the fix, the same real terminal flow shows the model picker and succeeds:

```text
Select LLM model: qwen3:32b

Actual CLI exit: 0
Reloaded active: provider_id='ollama' model='qwen3:32b'
Reloaded Ollama model IDs: ['qwen3:32b']
```

An independent PTY run through the complete `qwenpaw models set-llm` Click entry point also succeeds with the same persisted result. Four initial HTTP regression cases failed before the change and passed after it. The final six new cases cover both `config` and `set-llm`, a configured URL prefix and Authorization header, failed/empty discovery preserving an existing active model, existing model metadata, and unchanged noninteractive defaults. prs.title: fix(approvals): deliver approval prompts to the chat channel that raised them
prs.body:
## Description

Approvals raised from a chat turn never reached that chat. The console showed its dialog, WeChat showed nothing, and after five minutes the request resolved to `TIMEOUT` while the tool silently did not run.

Reported before as #6695 and root-caused in #6819. `ApprovalService` only pushes a notification when the pending record carries a channel instance:

```python
if channel and channel != "console" and (
    (extra or {}).get("_channel_instance") or _is_spawn_child_approval(pending)
):
    asyncio.create_task(self._notify_channel(pending, channel_body))
```

`request.channel_instance` was attached in exactly one place — `BaseChannel._stream_with_tracker`, the console/SSE path. Chat channels run their turns through `BaseChannel._run_process_loop`, where it stayed `None`. #6833 fixed the *propagation* through `driver_gate`, but the value it copies was still empty, so the notification could never fire for a chat channel.

### Changes

1. **`_run_process_loop` attaches `request.channel_instance`**, mirroring the console path. This is the line that makes chat approvals reachable at all.
2. **Actionable bodies.** `format_approval_actions()` renders copy-paste commands with the short request id, and driver-policy approvals get the same header/actions block as ToolGuard ones instead of a bare `"Tool 'x' requires approval for call."` sentence.
3. **`no_merge` for approval notices.** `send_approval_notification()` marks its message `no_merge`; WeChat merges text for 30 s by default (`message_merge_enabled`, `message_merge_delay_ms=30000`), so prompts could flush after the approval had already expired.
4. **Expiry is reported.** `wait_for_approval()` pushes an `approval_timeout` notice when the window closes, so the user is told nothing ran instead of being left guessing.

### Behaviour notes

- Console is unchanged: `channel == "console"` still skips push notifications.
- Spawned-child routing keeps its existing channel-manager path.
- `message_type` is keyword-only with the previous default; existing channel subclasses inherit the base implementation unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduction: WeChat session, `Bash` approval. `qwenpaw.log` shows `Approval pending created ... session=wechat:o`, then `decision=timeout` twice (09:53:33 `driver:mcp:blender`, 09:59:20 `Bash`), while every successful approval came from `routers/approval.py` (the console API). `Control command` never appears — nothing ever reached the chat.
- With the fix the same pending carries `_channel_instance`, `_notify_channel()` runs, and the body includes `/approval approve <short id>`.
- `pytest tests/unit/app/approvals tests/unit/channels/test_wechat.py tests/unit/security/tool_guard` → 689 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pytest tests/unit` → 17101 passed, 163 skipped, 45 failed. The failures are pre-existing on this Windows host: 51 of the same files fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree (portability fingerprints, cli lifespan, docker provisioner, openai response provider, offloader retention).
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy`, and `pylint` (10.00/10) are clean on the changed files.

## Related

- #6695 — same symptom, closed.
- #6819 — root-caused the missing notification.
- #6833 — propagated the routing fields, but not their source.
- #6728 / #6804 (unmerged) — Chinese approve/deny replies in WeChat; out of scope here.

## Not in this PR (design notes)

Ideas for follow-ups, deliberately not implemented here:

1. **Channel approval protocol.** Let `BaseChannel` own `send_approval_notification()` + `resolve_approval(action, request_id)`, with a default text implementation (numbered choices) that card channels (Feishu / QQ / Telegram / WeCom) override. WeChat would then only need short-reply parsing (`1/2`, `A/D`, 同意/拒绝 → `/approval …`), which is what #6728 / #6804 were aiming at.
2. **Non-blocking approvals.** `wait_for_approval()` currently parks the tool call — and the turn — for the whole timeout. Moving the wait to a background task and resuming on the decision would keep long chats responsive, but it changes the waiting model in `tool_adapter` / `driver_gate`, so it deserves its own discussion.
3. **Per-channel approval settings.** `approval: {enabled, timeout, default: deny|approve, notify_merge: false}`, so a WeChat-only deployment can decide how long to wait without a process-wide environment variable.
