issues.body:
### Summary

Let an account that signs in to the dashboard with OIDC, without administrator rights, chat with the agents its grants allow, as itself.

### Problem statement

**Dashboard sign-in (#11961) gives non-administrator accounts the dashboard, but not its chat.** The chat runs in the gateway's own process with the shared operator's authority. Offering it as it is would let a scoped account act with the operator's grants, and see conversations that aren't its own. So today the chat is administrator-only. An account that is allowed to use an agent from zerocode can't use that agent from the dashboard.

### Proposed solution

**Serve a scoped account's chat through the daemon's session methods**, on a daemon connection that presents that account's own token. The daemon then runs the conversation as that principal, under its grants, and keeps it as that principal's own.

- **One conversation per chat socket.**
  - It is created when the socket opens. It is closed, never deleted, when the socket closes, at sign-out, shortly before the token expires, when the account loses access, and at a daemon reload.
  - No other socket reopens it, so nothing about a conversation is shared between sockets.
- **Limits:** at most four chats per sign-in and 32 per account. A conversation still being created, or not yet closed, counts. A chat past a limit is told so and closed.
- **The token goes only to the provider that issued it.** Each chat connection is bound to the sign-in's identity provider, so a provider repointed since then never receives the token.
- **Unchanged:** administrators keep today's chat and its history. Paired browsers and installs without dashboard sign-in are unchanged too.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- **History across sockets.** A scoped conversation ends with its socket; restoring a non-live conversation to its owner is #11737.
- Image upload and model switching for scoped accounts.
- Any change to the daemon's session ownership rules.
- Splitting the gateway out of the daemon.
- Identity providers that dashboard sign-in can't use yet (a private CA, extra scopes, resource indicators).

### Alternatives considered

- **One shared daemon connection per sign-in, with the gateway mapping dashboard ids to conversations.** This was tried. It needs cross-socket state, reattachment and cleanup logic that is hard to keep consistent with the daemon on every failure path.
- **Keeping the chat administrator-only:** the status quo.

### Acceptance criteria

- A scoped account chats with an agent it is granted. The daemon runs the turn as that account, under its grants, and nobody else's dashboard lists the conversation.
- Another account cannot read, rename, delete, close, stop or answer approvals for that conversation, even knowing its live id.
- Reloading the page or closing the tab ends the conversation; the next message starts a new one.
- A fifth chat in one sign-in is refused without closing the other four. Signing out and in again frees no slot until the conversations are closed.
- Sign-out, token expiry, revocation and a daemon reload close the account's conversations. The transcripts are kept.
- A provider repointed after sign-in never receives the account's token.
- Administrators, paired browsers and installs without sign-in behave as before.

### Architecture impact

- The daemon gains a provider-bound in-process connection, which needs a runtime placement row: proposed in #11963.
- It builds on the in-process RPC client (#11186), the daemon's retirement of orphaned remote sessions (#11964) and dashboard sign-in (#11965).
- The wire protocol is unchanged.

### Risk and rollback

- **Off by default:** it applies only when dashboard sign-in is configured.
- **To roll back,** revert the change, or remove the providers from `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]`, which also closes every dashboard session.
- **Risk** is concentrated in isolation between accounts and in cleanup when a socket or session ends. Both are covered by tests that attack with real conversation ids.

### Expected routing

Should attach to an existing roadmap/tracker issue

### Next decision surface

Milestone v0.9.0, as the second half of dashboard sign-in (#11961, under #8289). The v0.9.0 tracker #7432 gives scoped dashboard chat a November 3 go/no-go; if it misses, sign-in ships without it.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

prs.title: fix(channels): honor Telegram 429 retry_after via shared per-token flood gate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`) shared **by the clones of one channel instance** (channel fields, spawned typing loop, approval paths) — it is *not* a registry keyed by bot token: separately constructed channels on the same token, including repeated one-off announcement factories, keep independent windows. Gated surface: the channel's text traffic — `sendMessage` (final answers, draft creation, approval prompts), `editMessageText` (draft updates, finalize), and `sendChatAction` in the recurring typing loop. Initial inbound typing hints, model-picker sends and text/markup edits, approval-resolution text edits, acknowledgement reactions, media uploads, `deleteMessage`, and `answerCallbackQuery` still post directly and are not covered by this gate.
  - Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open. Deliver calls wait the window out bounded by a caller-side budget (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs`), **re-check the shared gate after sleeping**, and stop with a distinguishable budget-exhausted outcome if the window is still active — the budget bounds how long the caller waits, never the server deadline, so nothing is sent into an active window. On a fresh 429 a Deliver call retries once; a second 429 contributes its own (possibly longer) `retry_after` to the shared window and stops the formatting/resume/resend fallbacks — a 429 is not a formatting failure.
  - The recorded deadline keeps the later of the active and new values, so out-of-order concurrent 429 responses cannot shorten the window; an unrepresentable delay is rejected rather than clamped into permission to send sooner.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Partial deliveries still suppress the orchestrator's full-answer resend via `FinalizePartialDelivery`, and flood-control exhaustion now stops the chunk-resume path as well instead of burning the wait budget twice. The pending-narration loop in multi-message finalization also stops on the terminal gate outcome: instead of burning three narration retries plus a final-answer wait on fresh budgets, it propagates the gate error, so the outer resend is suppressed without reporting an undelivered final answer as delivered.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60; `0` restores the default — it is not a disable switch) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded). Both resolve from the live config authority at each use, including per-tick in the typing loop, so a published change applies to a running channel without a rebuild.
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and any listener-side changes are explicitly out of scope (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `send_draft`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send) plus one guard in the orchestrator's finalize-fallback arm. No change to inbound/listener logic, other channels, or the agent loop. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per channel instance (shared by its clones) the moment a gated call sees a 429, keeping the longest active deadline. Gated cosmetic traffic (recurring typing indicator, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window up to a bounded caller budget and try again once. When the window clears within budget, the reply is late instead of dropped. When the window outlasts the budget, nothing is sent into it: the answer is held and an error is returned — this slice has no durable delivery queue or automatic later redelivery, so such a reply can go undelivered (WARN-logged) until the sender retries; the gated callers stop retrying inside the recorded window and suppress blind resends of accepted chunks. The direct-call exclusions listed above still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting with escalating deadlines, blocked-window skipping, budget expiry without resend, mid-wait window extension, cancelled waiter, cross-chat window sharing, gated draft creation, live-config resolution, pending-narration finalize stop with zero and nonzero accepted prefixes); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at workspace level shows pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host, Windows-only service code); none originate from this change, and the channels crate itself is `-D warnings` clean. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output (head `fe42c5d30`):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram` → `test result: ok. 429 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize` → `test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed` (including the two new `finalize_stops_on_flood_gate_with_{zero,nonzero}_accepted_narration_prefix` regressions and the retained transient-retry controls).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Author-reported live observation (distinct from CI signals): ran an earlier revision of this change as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h — 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events, every post-429 turn delivered after the gate window. This predates the review-round semantics tightening; the current head's budget/no-resend and pending-narration-stop behavior is covered by the mock-server regressions above, not by live observation.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fe42c5d30` on branch `fix/telegram-429-retry-after`; terminal test output above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` run from the previous round was not repeated at this head; the changed surface (pending-narration finalization, flood gate) is covered by the `telegram` (429 tests) and `finalize` (23 tests) filters above. `cargo test --test integration telegram_` remains un-run locally (link step needs more free disk than this host currently has); the equivalent behavior is covered by the in-crate wiremock tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>` of this PR's merge commit.

prs.title: fix(oidc): form-encode enrollment Basic credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - OIDC enrollment authenticated the client with `basic_auth(client_id, secret)` on the raw values. RFC 6749 §2.3.1 requires both to be form-encoded before they go into the Basic header, and introspection already does this through `form_urlencode_component`. Enrollment now encodes both values the same way, so a client ID or secret containing `:`, `+`, `/`, `%`, a space or similar authenticates against a strict provider.
  - A `:` in the secret was worse than a rejection: it moved the user/password split.
  - `form_urlencode_component` becomes `pub(super)` so enrollment reuses the introspection encoder instead of a second copy.
  - `enrollment_basic_credentials_round_trip_on_every_endpoint` drives device-grant start, device-grant poll and `client_credentials`. For each request it decodes the Basic header and form-decodes the pair back to the configured values. It covers a plain pair, a pair full of reserved characters, and a public client (no secret, `client_id` in the form body) as a control.
- **Scope boundary:** only the enrollment Basic header. Introspection, token storage, config schema and public-client enrollment are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw oidc token` and device-grant enrollment for confidential clients. Credentials made only of unreserved characters (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~`) produce byte-identical headers.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11957. Related #11423, where @Aarlington found and fixed this. Both commits are carried here unchanged, with their original authorship, so the fix can land without waiting for the rest of that draft.

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw enrolls with an OIDC provider as a confidential client, it sends the client ID and secret in an HTTP Basic header. The OAuth spec says to URL-form-encode both first, and ZeroClaw already does that for token introspection, but not for enrollment. Any client ID or secret with a character like `:`, `+`, `/` or `%` therefore reached the provider mangled, and strict providers such as Keycloak rejected it with `unauthorized_client`. This PR encodes the two values the same way introspection does. IDs and secrets made of letters, digits and `-._~` are sent exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw oidc token <profile>`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Keycloak realm with a confidential client whose ID and secret contain reserved characters, for example client ID `zc-basic: +/%` and a secret containing `:`, `+`, `/`, `%` and `%2B`, with the service-account (`client_credentials`) flow enabled; an `[oidc.<profile>]` entry pointing at it.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw oidc token <profile>`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** enrollment succeeds and prints one token line.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `client_credentials enrollment failed: unauthorized_client (Unexpected error when authenticating client)`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` run `zeroclaw-runtime --lib`, which includes the new regression and the existing `security::auth_provider` tests; `Lint` covers clippy with `-D warnings`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no real OIDC provider. The Keycloak run below covers that.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, at ee9a594e30:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `test result: ok. 5807 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`
  - `security::auth_provider::` three runs: `test result: ok. 108 passed; 0 failed` each time
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings`: exit 0, no diagnostics
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - With only the `basic_auth` change reverted, the regression fails: `enrollment_basic_credentials_round_trip_on_every_endpoint` panics with "literal credential separator reached the wire", and passes again with the change restored.
  - Against Keycloak (pinned image, a fresh realm, client ID `zc-basic: +/%`, a secret with `:`, `+`, `/`, `%` and `%2B`):
    - curl with the form-encoded Basic pair: HTTP 200; with the raw pair: HTTP 400, so the provider is strict;
    - `zeroclaw oidc token` on master 96da19523e: `unauthorized_client`;
    - the same two commits on that master: enrolled, one token line.

    That run was on 96da19523e. Master has not touched `security/auth_provider/` since, and the two changed files are identical here.
  - Not verified: device-grant enrollment against a real provider (the regression covers the same header path).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ee9a594e30 for the Rust checks; the Keycloak run used the same two commits on 96da19523e.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the client secret is now form-encoded before Basic encoding, as RFC 6749 §2.3.1 requires and as introspection already does. Nothing new is logged or stored, and the secret still goes only to the configured token and device endpoints.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. IDs and secrets made of unreserved characters send identical bytes. Values with reserved characters now authenticate against RFC-compliant providers; a provider that does not form-decode Basic credentials would see the encoded value, the same as introspection already sends it.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert` of the two commits.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This PR is stacked on #11225 (delegated memory principal scope), which introduces the retained `Agent.delegate_tool` handle and the delegate `principal_scope` cell this change builds on. Until #11225 merges, the branch shows both commits; please review the top commit only (`fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals`).
- **What changed and why:**
  - `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` list, read, and append to other sessions with no principal-ownership check. A non-admin principal that held them (wildcard tool and agent selectors included) could read or append to another principal's transcript on the same agent. Applying a non-admin principal's grants (`apply_principal_grants_to_agent`, which runs at session creation, at rehydration, and before every prompt) now withholds them. `sessions_current` stays: it takes no target and reports only the caller's own session.
  - The tool names live in one place, `zeroclaw_tools::PRINCIPAL_UNAWARE_SESSION_TOOL_NAMES`, with a sync test against the constructed tools. Skill aliases of those tools (a `builtin` or `mcp` skill tool whose `target` is one of them) are withheld with them, because a name-only denylist is bypassed by a renamed wrapper.
  - Nested executors that cannot carry the withholding go too: `spawn_subagent` rebuilds a full registry from config, and `execute_pipeline` runs the tool set captured at construction, which includes the session tools. Both are already marked `requires_unrestricted_principal`; that existing marker is what selects them, so their skill aliases follow as well.
  - The delegate is kept for wildcard principals, but the Agent marks it through the retained handle. The mark is an `Arc<AtomicBool>` shared with background, parallel, and nested bounded delegates exactly like `principal_scope`, and every child registry the delegate builds filters on it: the bounded base (the parent's build list, which still holds what the parent's registry withheld) and the independent target's own registry. An Agent whose registry holds a delegate it has no handle for drops the delegate instead.
  - Source of truth: the principal's resolved grants, re-evaluated by `apply_principal_grants_to_agent` on every prompt. The registry removal and the delegate flag are narrowing-only effects of that evaluation, like the existing selector narrowing; nothing snapshots policy, and nothing is ever restored to a live session. The system prompt is rebuilt only when the withholding actually removed a tool, so later prompts do not rebuild it.
- **Scope boundary:** This is containment: it withholds principal-unaware tools from the sessions of non-admin principals. It does not make the session tools principal-aware (principal-scoped read views and predicates for list, history, and the chat append path); that repair belongs under the session-ownership contract in the #8290 tracker. The agent-ownership scoping in #9746 is related but does not provide principal isolation. This PR does not touch `sessions.rs` or the runtime's session-tool registration. `sessions_reset` and `sessions_delete` are not registered by the runtime; the name list's doc comment now says each must join it if it ever is. Administrators and the unauthenticated shared operator keep every tool.
- **Not covered, and now documented:** runs that execute later under the agent's own identity, with the agent's configured tools, can still call the session-data tools. These are agent jobs created with `cron_add`, or given a new prompt with `cron_update` and started with `cron_run` (the same through RPC cron grants), whose output comes back through `cron_runs`; SOP runs; and the turns `send_message_to_peer` starts in another agent. None of them carries a principal today. The authentication docs now say so and give the interim mitigation: list `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send`, plus any skill tool that targets them, in `excluded_tools` of the risk profile of each agent those runs use. That removes the tools from every run of the agent, administrators' sessions included. Carrying a principal into scheduled, SOP, and peer runs is follow-up work under #8290. `schedule` creates shell jobs only; shell execution as the daemon account is the existing, separately documented limitation.
- **Blast radius:** RPC sessions of authenticated principals without `admin`, including wildcard ones, lose `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, `spawn_subagent`, and `execute_pipeline`, plus skill aliases of any of them and of `delegate` (wildcard principals keep the `delegate` tool itself). Their delegation children lose the same tools. Principals with a constrained selector already lost the nested executors and their aliases. Channel and CLI sessions do not go through this RPC posture and are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11127. Depends on #11225.
- **Labels:** `agent`, `channel`, `channel:core`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `memory`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `tool`, `tool:delegate`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets several people (principals) use the same agent over RPC, each with their own sessions. A few agent tools can look at other sessions: list them, read their history, or post a message into them. Those tools only check which agent a session belongs to, not which person, so one user's agent could read or write another user's conversation on the same agent. Until the tools learn to check the person, this change simply takes them away from every signed-in user who is not an administrator, even users whose permissions say "all tools". It also takes away two helpers that could hand the tools straight back (starting a sub-agent and running a tool pipeline), and it makes delegated helper agents drop the tools too. The tool that reports "which session am I in" stays, and administrators and single-operator installs see no change. When a user is demoted from administrator, their open session loses the tools at its next prompt. This is not complete isolation yet: work that runs later under the agent's own identity, such as a scheduled agent job, a standard operating procedure, or a message to another agent, can still use these tools. The documentation now says so and shows operators how to switch the tools off for those agents until the tools learn to check the person.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the boundary is the RPC dispatcher's session construction and prompt posture, which the new dispatcher tests drive end to end with two roster principals; a manual check needs a second OS user for peer-credential auth or an OIDC provider.

### How I tested

Run on macOS with rustc 1.98.0. New tests:

- `rpc::dispatch::tests::scoped_principals_cannot_reach_session_data_tools_even_with_wildcard_selectors`: two roster principals with `allowed_tools = ["*"]`, `allowed_agents = ["*"]`, and `tools:execute`. Alice's ACP and chat sessions, and her ACP session after rehydration, hold none of the three tools (`execute_tool_for_test` is `None`; production dispatch of `sessions_send` and `sessions_history` against Bob's chat key returns `Unknown tool`), keep `sessions_current` and `delegate`, lose `spawn_subagent`, and their delegate is marked. Bob's transcript is byte-identical afterwards. The shared operator's session keeps all four session tools and `spawn_subagent`, and its delegate is not marked.
- `rpc::dispatch::tests::demoted_principal_loses_session_data_tools_at_its_next_prompt`: an admin principal's session holds the tools; after the profile drops `admin`, the post-admission path (`current_prompt_authority` then `apply_principal_grants_to_agent` with the fresh grants) removes them and `spawn_subagent`, keeps `sessions_current`, `calculator`, and `delegate`, and marks the delegate.
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_delegate_children`: a control delegation offers the child `sessions_history` and a nested `spawn_subagent` probe from the parent build list; after `withhold_session_data_tools()`, the sync, parallel, and background children are offered none of the three tools nor `spawn_subagent`, and still get `sessions_current` (checked on the captured provider requests).
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_independent_targets`: an independent target's own registry holds the three tools, `spawn_subagent`, and a skill alias (`peek__history`, a `builtin` skill tool targeting `sessions_history`) as a control; after withholding it holds none of them and keeps `sessions_current` and `shell`.
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_an_independent_grandchild`: caller, then bounded `middle`, then independent `leaf`. As a control, the leaf's captured request offers `sessions_history` and `spawn_subagent`; after the caller withholds, the leaf is offered none of the three tools nor `spawn_subagent`, and keeps `sessions_current`. This pins the flag the bounded child's target-bound delegate shares.
- `agent::agent::tests::withholding_session_data_tools_removes_aliases_and_nested_executors`: as a control, the raw tool, a skill alias, and an `execute_pipeline` step each reach a `sessions_history` probe; after withholding, all three are unknown tools, the probe is not called again, `sessions_current` and the handle-bound delegate remain, and a delegate without a handle is dropped.
- `session_tool_names_guard::principal_unaware_session_tool_names_match_tools` (zeroclaw-tools): the const matches the constructed tools and excludes `sessions_current`.

Each new runtime test was also checked against a deliberately broken build: removing the dispatcher call, giving the parallel, background, or bounded target-bound delegate a fresh flag, removing the independent filter, dropping alias names, or dropping the nested-executor clause each makes the corresponding tests fail.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test, clippy, and plugin-backend jobs cover the changed runtime and tools code; Docs Style and links cover the doc change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/session_tool|session_data|delegate|withhold|withheld|principal_grants/)'
```

prs.title: fix(security): require administrator authority for SOP execution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require current administrator authority for `sops/run` and every `sops/decide` decision, including when a non-admin has wildcard selectors and `tools:execute`. SOP steps and their descendants do not carry a scoped caller's principal limits.
  - Retain that authority through synchronous start/approval storage effects after decision-model and engine waits; a contended store refuses immediately rather than holding authority while waiting for a writer.
  - Withhold `sop_execute`, `sop_approve`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, and their skill aliases from non-admin RPC sessions. Also withhold `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and delegate aliases that cannot carry the restriction.
  - Keep direct delegation for callers with unrestricted selectors, binding bounded, independent, background, parallel, and nested child builders to the originating credential's live authority resolver. The canonical policy remains `RpcInboundAuth`; no copied grant decision authorizes a child registry.
- **Scope boundary:** This is interim containment, not principal propagation inside SOP steps; RPC SOP authoring and non-RPC triggers retain their existing policies. The cumulative diff includes the session-authority prerequisite from #11234 and current master; unrelated session-data and cron repairs from the supplemental drafts are not imported.
- **Blast radius:** Non-admin SOP execution, approval, workshop use, and unsafe nested tool exposure; administrators and the shared operator retain configured access, and ordinary admitted tools remain usable.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11123. Depends on #11234. Related #11408, #11410, #11230, and #11169.

### What this does, simply

A user could reach a procedure through a tool alias or an allowed agent and then run work outside that user's permissions. Until procedures can carry those permissions into every step, only administrators may start or decide them, and non-admin sessions do not receive tools that bypass that restriction.

```text
RPC run / decision ── current admin authority ── guarded storage effect
                         │ no
                         └───────────────────── FORBIDDEN

non-admin session ── ordinary tools / controlled delegate
                         └─ child registry rechecks live authority
                            └─ SOP entry tools and unsafe builders absent
```

The [current-head review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11220#pullrequestreview-5364022889) identifies the tool-entry and descendant gaps; this carries the SOP-specific repairs from [#11408](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408) and workshop regressions from [#11410](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410), retaining their authorship and adapting their delegate propagation pattern to live resolution.

### Landing and shared-helper reconciliation

Land #11234 before this PR; the supplemental drafts must drop the SOP changes carried here when they refresh. #11169 must rebase onto this admission contract: one `SopAdmissionCheck` returns a held `SopEffectGuard`, and execution must keep the administrator predicate and nonblocking storage boundary rather than restoring its older wildcard predicate or a check returning `()`.

An integration probe against #11169 at `908a035d3f6b3734fcdf471785def4f6c3a1ad00` reports conflicts in `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `sop/dispatch.rs`, `sop/executor.rs`, and `sop/mod.rs`; its new ingress/cancel methods and authenticated approver changes still require that rebase and combined validation before landing.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: compare the same scenarios with the previous head `ec5fc1c28760c63c9da9ea4d74e18379c146a2a8`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Local authenticated JSON-RPC and Chat/ACP tool dispatch used by CLI/TUI clients; model providers in the regressions are synthetic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A non-admin roster principal with `sops:execute`, `tools:execute`, wildcard selectors, and an approval-gated procedure; retain an administrator control.
- **Steps to run:** Request `sops/run` and an approval/denial through `sops/decide`; ask the session to invoke the direct SOP tools and a built-in skill alias, then repeat as administrator. The `sop_principal` tests also exercise a queued admin demotion and workshop persistence.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Non-admin RPC effects return `FORBIDDEN`; withheld tool calls return `Unknown tool` and leave runs/proposals unchanged; administrator controls and ordinary tools succeed.
- **Prior behavior (before):** Wildcard non-admins could pass the RPC guard, and model-facing SOP tools could enter procedures without the caller's principal ceiling.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet for the updated head; fresh CI is required after push.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation is macOS with Rust/Cargo 1.97.1; cross-platform and full-workspace coverage remain with CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc:: sop:: tools::sop_ tools::delegate:: live_config_authority::
  1883 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib live::
  8 passed; 0 failed
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  6 tests OK; no added links
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the registry/factory wiring and the #11169 merge probe; automated controls exercise real run/proposal persistence, SQLite writer contention, queued demotion, credential expiry/revocation, aliases, and all supported delegate construction paths. No external identity-provider or interactive TUI smoke test was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2`, local JSON-RPC/tool regressions; local logs in `tmp/oidc-11220-validation/` in the implementation worktree.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Runtime assertions verify `FORBIDDEN` or `Unknown tool: <name>` and unchanged durable/in-memory SOP state, with successful administrator controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A queued principal demotion prevents SOP/workshop effects; a queued config writer cannot deadlock a nested read; busy SQLite refuses before start/resume mutation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace/all-feature tests were not duplicated locally; the selected suites cover the changed boundaries. The existing two ignored runtime cases remain ignored.

The runtime test linker emits the pre-existing macOS `__eh_frame section too large (max 16MB)` warning; the same diagnostic was reproduced on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` during prerequisite validation, and both builds completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; this restricts existing access.
- New external network calls? **No**.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**; delegate builders retain the originating connection's non-secret authentication evidence in a live resolver, so current revocation/expiry and grants are checked rather than a stored admission decision; no bearer is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**; fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; unsafe tool capabilities are removed from the executable registry and its advertised surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A descendant must not inherit another later caller's authority; each child retains its originating resolver while current policy remains canonical in the auth layer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; non-admin wildcard SOP access is intentionally removed, including deny/amend/revise, and unsafe nested builders/aliases are withheld.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** new setting, flag, or wire method; existing methods have stricter authorization and localized refusal text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**.
- Exact upgrade steps: Use a trusted administrator/shared operator for SOP execution and decisions; adding `tools:execute` alone no longer restores access. Parent session tools narrow at the next prompt admission; recreate a session after promotion to regain removed tools, and retry busy-store requests once contention clears.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge/squash commit while retaining the #11234 prerequisite; no data migration is required, but reverting restores the unsafe non-admin paths.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; the restriction is deliberate and fails closed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `FORBIDDEN` on SOP run/decision, `Unknown tool` for withheld names, localized SOP storage-busy refusals, and matching RPC authorization-denied records.

prs.title: fix(memory): preserve owner in delegation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; refreshed through 6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserve the owned session's full principal scope when a delegate builds target-agent memory. The owner, namespace, and tenant remain fixed; only the target agent changes. The registered delegate and its nested/parallel instances retain that scope, and target construction refuses when it cannot preserve it.
  - Rebuild canonical memory tools and skill aliases over the owned handle, preserving names, schemas, restrictions, and locked arguments. `Tool::builtin_target_name` and `Tool::with_builtin_target` expose this contract through the forwarding wrappers; rebuilding a registry is all-or-nothing.
  - Forward principal-scoped operations through `AgentScopedMemory` and `RetrievalPipeline`. Private recalls bypass the cache whose keys lack an owner dimension. This also restores owned SQLite chat sessions' own memory tools, recall, and configured autosave.
  - Bind factory-built delegates from `Memory::principal_scope` before canonical tools or aliases can execute. Owned sessions, including administrators, refuse background delegation and every result-management action before accessing task rows or result files. Synchronous and parallel delegation remain available under existing policy.
  - Add regressions for owner/target isolation, alias reconstruction, nested factory construction, private-cache separation, and refusal of background creation, foreign results, legacy results, waits, and cancellation. Document the owned-session restriction in the authentication guide.
- **Scope boundary:** No new grants, memory schema, config keys, or RPC plane selection. Shared operator delegation retains its existing behavior. This does not migrate or remove existing result artifacts, nor establish isolation for every other tool: `spawn_subagent` and `execute_pipeline` remain tracked by #11239/#11266. Safe restoration of owned background tasks is tracked by #11995. The routing-order refinement discussed in #11174 remains separate; a routing error currently aborts owned RPC session creation/rehydration.
- **Blast radius:** Owned RPC sessions, including named administrators and restored sessions; direct, bounded, independent, nested, and parallel delegated memory; skill builtin wrappers; memory backend wrappers; runtime tool factories; external Rust consumers of `Tool`, `Memory`, and `AllToolsResult`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11198. Related #11239, #11266, #11174, #11409, #11995.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `agent`, `channel`, `memory`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `priority:p0`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `topic:identity-access`, `release:v0.9.0`.

### Issue and solution in plain terms

A signed-in user's session can ask another agent for help. Previously that helper received fresh memory tools pointing at shared storage, so it could read shared notes and save the user's notes there. The helper now uses that user's private memory for the target agent, including when a skill alias invokes the tool or delegation takes another hop.

Background task results still use an agent-based visibility boundary. The PR therefore refuses that route for owned sessions until task records and output files can enforce principal ownership. The refusal applies to administrators' owned sessions too; their private memory remains private.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: deterministic regressions exercise the actual delegate, factory, memory tools, and SQLite/task stores with synthetic owners. No additional manual browser or terminal rendering claim is made.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** 2595327a0ec8208800dd5c9acd9bfa58b86ce1e5, including the current `master` merge. The merge was conflict-free; the interaction in tool assembly preserves both the owner binding and master's host-name reservations.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39876483288) passed on this revision: 39 successful jobs, no failed jobs, and a successful `CI Required Gate`. `Test` ran the workspace suites, including the new runtime/memory/API regressions. `Parallel Runtime Test` exercised runtime and channels concurrently. `Lint`, `Format`, plugin-runtime checks, platform builds, and `Docs Style` also passed, covering the shared contracts, factory wiring, and documentation.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live authenticated browser/zerocode session or external model-provider acceptance was performed. The affected execution paths are covered with production tools and factories, real SQLite/task stores, and controlled providers; no frontend rendering or transport implementation changes.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The refreshed CI `Test` job reported 19,355 workspace tests passed (42 skipped); the additional test groups passed 189 and 7 tests respectively. Each named regression below appears as `PASS` in that job.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0; no output
  $ git diff --check origin/master...HEAD
  exit 0; no output
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source-traced both RPC owner-routing callers, the factory binding before tool publication, alias reconstruction, and the early background/management refusal. Session construction and rehydration return on routing failure. No production data, external provider, migration, or rollback rehearsal was used. Local Cargo test/clippy runs were not repeated; the refreshed required CI run supplies that coverage.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for visual rendering: no frontend, terminal layout, or rendering code changes. The new localized denial is checked at the production tool-result boundary by the refusal regressions below.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above; the `delegate` tool and skill-wrapper execution interface. The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39876483288/job/120163217120) exercises these regressions:
  - `owned_delegate_child_recalls_and_stores_only_in_owners_target_plane`, `owned_parallel_delegate_stores_only_in_owners_target_plane`, and `independent_delegate_alias_inherits_owner_before_nested_capture` check owner and target selection against shared, caller-agent, and other-owner sentinels.
  - `routing_rebinds_memory_skill_aliases_to_the_owners_private_plane` and `owned_bounded_delegate_memory_aliases_rebind_without_changing_parent` check alias restrictions and private writes.
  - `factory_delegate_inherits_private_memory_owner_before_any_action`, `owned_background_delegate_refuses_before_creating_shared_results`, and `owned_delegate_management_refuses_same_alias_and_legacy_results` check canonical/alias refusal, no provider/task/artifact creation, no foreign-result disclosure, and unchanged task status after denied cancellation. The fixture first proves the same artifacts are readable by the shared operator.
  - `cached_pipeline_keeps_private_recalls_per_owner`, `routed_session_memory_on_the_agent_stack_reaches_the_owners_plane`, and `arc_delegating_tool_forwards_builtin_target_identity` cover the cache, real memory stack, and outer wrapper.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The refusal tests assert `success: false`, empty output, and the English catalogue message: “Background delegation and task management are unavailable in principal-owned sessions until task results enforce principal ownership. Use synchronous delegation instead.” This is tool-result evidence, not a browser screenshot or live-client smoke test.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Owned background and management calls are denied before task or artifact access; synchronous/parallel writes land only in the owner's target plane. Existing shared-operator controls remain supported.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Duplicate local workspace builds were omitted in favor of the required CI matrix on the exact refreshed head. No runtime behavior was changed after that head was pushed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** No. Existing memory access is restricted to the owner, and unsafe owned background actions are refused.
- **New external network calls?** No.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** No.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No; regression data is synthetic.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** Yes. Delegated recall and restored owned-session recall can put the owner's private memory into provider context. Existing memory provenance applies; owner/tenant/namespace/agent predicates and cache bypass keep other scopes out. Owned background results are refused before publication or retrieval.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** No for owned background/task-management calls and external code constructing `AllToolsResult` with a struct literal. Shared operator behavior is preserved.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No config keys, environment variables, or CLI flags. The `delegate` tool now returns the localized refusal above for owned background/management requests; the authentication guide documents it.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Exact upgrade steps:** Use synchronous or parallel delegation for owned sessions; do not remove ownership or elevate permissions to restore background access. External Rust callers must use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools` instead of a struct literal. The new `Memory::principal_scope`, `Tool::builtin_target_name`, and `Tool::with_builtin_target` methods have defaults, but private-memory views and forwarding tool wrappers must preserve the documented scope/rebinding contracts.
- **Other behavior to account for:** On SQLite, owned chat sessions' configured autosave and recall now reach private memory through the wrapper stack; with autosave enabled this persists messages that previously failed to save. Backends without principal support refuse private operations. ACP/rehydrated sessions built with memory excluded retain that exclusion. Existing shared result artifacts are retained and are not migrated.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After landing, `git revert <landed-squash-commit>` restores the prior implementation. Reverting also restores the isolation defect; restrict affected owned-session/delegation access before rollback. Private rows remain stored and are not moved into shared storage.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Existing tool policy can remove delegation while investigating; keep owned background actions denied until #11995 is implemented and reviewed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** The intentional `delegate-owned-background-unavailable` message for owned background/management calls; “owned delegate memory requires target configuration” when a private target cannot be constructed; “memory alias ... cannot rebind its builtin target” for unsupported aliases; RPC session construction/rehydration refusing when memory routing fails.

The background containment and factory-owner changes from @Aarlington's #11409 retain their original commit authorship. This PR incorporates those focused changes and does not supersede that PR's broader prerequisite stack.

prs.title: fix(rpc): judge queued session ownership by current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Current head: `d72bab13cd71f1fa31e0028668a2ee471a88f9fc`, integrating master through `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb`. This adopts the [prepared canonical repair](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/commit/677961e7d73f17c36a7d21742095ea0292d605d8) by fast-forward, preserves the original PR history, and retains the merged #10246 and #11222 behavior.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Session operations that wait (for the session admission permit, the config writer gate, a pending provider binding or the provider-update lock) decided ownership with the administrator bypass stamped on the connection before the wait. `recheck_authority_after_admission` re-resolved the grants afterwards but never updated that stamp, so an administrator demoted while queued still reached another principal's session. A new `scoped_principal_id_from(grants)` derives the ownership scope from a given grant set; `scoped_principal_id()` delegates to it with the stamped grants and remains the pre-wait check. `revalidate_admitted_session`, `authorize_session_owner_for_mode` and `resolve_session_record_for_mode` now take the scope as a parameter instead of reading the stamp, so those post-admission ownership decisions and refusals use freshly resolved grants.
  - `session/close`, `session/kill` and `session/delete` recheck authority right after the permit and revalidate with the scope those grants give. Kill and delete also fall back to the durable record when a hard-cancelled turn removed the live incarnation during the wait; that fallback now requires the record to be the caller's under the same scope. Without it, a demoted administrator whose target's live incarnation disappeared while it waited still tombstoned or deleted another principal's durable row.
  - `session/prompt` derives ownership from fresh grants after admission and provider waits. Final preparation runs inside the execution task after it acquires the canonical Agent lock. It checks the exact Agent and current owner/binding/environment permissions, narrows tools, and authorizes the checkpoint or running-state write under the storage lock before execution. Refused preparation ends the client turn through `refuse_admitted_prompt` without calling the provider. Rehydration uses guarded recovery and seed-trim persistence so a storage-lock wait cannot retain earlier authority.
  - `session/new`: `SessionStore::resume_existing_authorized` hands the session's owner to its authorize closure, and the new `authorize_resumed_incarnation` judges that owner with the same authority it resolves for the agent/workspace binding and the retained environment, under the store lock. A connection whose stamp still carries a revoked bypass therefore cannot rebind another principal's live session. After the permit, authority is re-resolved before anything else and the scope derived from it judges the record found under the permit (so a demoted administrator no longer leaves a cross-principal audit record for a request refused a few lines later, and a principal promoted while waiting is honoured), the post-admission resume, the cross-mode replacement and the ACP restore preload. After the config writer gate wait it is re-derived again: the owner of the session being restored or replaced must match, and whether a failed owner-stamp write aborts creation follows that scope.
  - `session/configure` and the queued (reaped) branch of `session/messages` also act after a wait and call `revalidate_admitted_session`, so they recheck authority and pass the fresh scope as well.
  - Live cancellation, publication and deferred approval-channel installation reauthorize under the live-session boundary. `session/messages` and plan replay reserve outbound capacity before their final ownership/authority check and send synchronously while guarded. The shared plan helper covers live resume, restored `session/new`, and prompt rehydration.
  - `session/append` passes the current ownership scope into its admitted lookup, then resolves authority again after that awaited lookup and before either transcript write. Its regression covers a demoted administrator targeting a foreign session, an owner whose update grant was revoked, and a demoted owner whose update grant remains valid.
- **Scope boundary:** The request gate, durable owner identity (`owner_principal_id`), wire, config and CLI shapes are unchanged. Ownership after the covered waits follows current authority. The guards authorize individual effects; this does not add continuous revocation of an already-admitted running turn or roll back effects authorized before demotion.
- **Blast radius:** RPC dispatch, execution-task preparation, live-session synchronization, outbound frame reservation, and guarded ACP/Chat persistence. New authorization callbacks run after storage locks or transactions are acquired and retain authority through synchronous effects. History helpers acquire the Agent before the session map and recheck incarnation identity. Unsupported guarded backend reads and deletes fail closed. Permitted own-session operations retain positive-control coverage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11126. Related #11222 (merged prerequisite). Related #10412.

### What this does, simply

Named local principals can hold an administrator bypass that lets them act on other principals' sessions. Several session requests wait before they act: behind a turn that holds the session, behind a configuration change, or behind a provider update. The daemon did recheck the caller's permissions after that wait, but it kept deciding who owns what from the administrator flag recorded when the request arrived. If an administrator lost that role while their request waited, the request still went through: it could delete another person's saved session, kill it, send it a prompt, change its settings, read it, or restore it.

After this change, the covered effects decide ownership from the permissions in force after their final wait. A demoted administrator receives the same "not found or not owned" refusal as any other principal before that effect executes, changes saved data, or discloses a foreign transcript or plan. Permitted operations on the caller's own sessions keep working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: reproducing it needs a principal roster and a demotion that lands while a request is queued, which the dispatcher-level regressions below drive deterministically.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No current-head CI result is claimed yet; [Quality Gate for `d72bab13cd71f1fa31e0028668a2ee471a88f9fc`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38948140056) is running. The local checks below cover the changed RPC, storage, live-authority and API crates on macOS arm64; the broader workspace, feature matrix and parallel runtime checks remain pending.
- **Current-head local validation:** `d72bab13cd71f1fa31e0028668a2ee471a88f9fc` (tree `0cb5396b9b114b24801ab91e4a87f00e433c7974`), macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1; default crate features and eight test threads. All 1,094 focused tests passed, with no Clippy diagnostics.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0; no output
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc:: -- --test-threads=8
# 862 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 4919 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session -- --test-threads=8
# 207 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 107 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib live_config_authority:: -- --test-threads=8
# 25 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5756 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 19s
```

- **Linker diagnostic:** The macOS runtime test link emitted `ld: __eh_frame section too large (max 16MB)`; the binary linked and every selected test ran successfully. A clean checkout of pinned master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` reproduces the identical diagnostic with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-run` (exit 0); it comes from the large debug test binary's unwind section and is not introduced by this PR.

- **Historical CI on the previous PR head (not current-head evidence):** On `d5df4214cad96bfc6bfbdea13a64767b116ac1df`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110009962176), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110010144453), Lint, the plugin-backend Check legs, and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110014127332) pass. The Test log explicitly records the admission/provider, final-effect, storage-lock and outbound-backpressure regressions below passing; its main suite reports 19,059 passed and 39 skipped. These results cover only that older revision; the refreshed head has a separate run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current local evidence exercises synthetic principals, in-process RPC handlers, existing local/WSS transport tests and real session stores on macOS; it does not prove a live daemon against a real identity provider. Linux, Windows and feature-matrix coverage for the refreshed head awaits the linked CI run; older CI and local results below are historical evidence only.
- **Regression coverage:**
  - `append_rechecks_authority_after_admitted_lookup` (prepared-repair regression): demotion cannot preserve a foreign-session append, and revoking an owner's update grant prevents both durable and live writes; a demoted owner who retains update authority can still append.
  - `queued_operations_lose_the_admin_bypass_when_the_administrator_is_demoted` (new): alice holds `member` session grants plus an `administrator` profile, and bob owns an ACP session. For each of prompt, close, delete and kill against bob's live session, delete and kill when its live incarnation is reaped during the wait, and prompt (the rehydration path) and messages against the reaped session, alice's request passes its pre-check as administrator and parks on the admission permit; the profile loses `admin` (her `member` grants stay) and the permit is released. Each request gets `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial, each refused prompt ends the client's turn with a failed `TurnComplete` on alice's connection, bob's live generation is unchanged (or the session stays reaped, not revived), and his durable row still exists, is not killed, keeps his owner and gains no messages. Configure parked on the provider-update lock is refused the same way and bob's overrides are unchanged. Positive control: alice, demoted while her delete of her own session waits, deletes it.
  - `queued_prompt_rechecks_ownership_after_its_provider_waits` (new): alice's prompt on bob's live session passes the post-admission ownership check as administrator and then parks, once on the provider-update lock and once on a pending provider binding; she is demoted and the wait is released. Both prompts get `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial and a failed `TurnComplete`, bob's provider receives no call, and his incarnation and durable row are unchanged.
  - `demoted_administrator_cannot_resume_a_foreign_session_with_a_stale_stamp` (new): `handle_session_new_for_test` skips the gate, so alice's connection keeps its administrator stamp after the demotion; `session/new` naming bob's live session is refused and his generation is unchanged, while the same stale connection still rebinds a session of her own. Resumes of bob's reaped ACP and chat sessions queued behind the permit when the demotion lands are refused and nothing is restored; bob's ACP row keeps an interrupted-turn checkpoint unrecovered and his chat row keeps its owner. Positive control: her own reaped ACP session, resumed the same way, is restored.
  - The direct `resume_existing_authorized` tests accept the owner argument and returned authorization guard.
  - `final_prompt_effect_waits_recheck_current_authority`, `removal_effect_waits_preserve_foreign_session_after_demotion`, `restore_effect_waits_preserve_retained_checkpoint_after_demotion`, and `deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait` cover the later execution, mutation and channel-install boundaries.
  - `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_before_disclosure` and `resume_plan_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_and_incarnation` exercise actual dispatcher responses and backpressure. The plan test covers live/restored resume, prompt rehydration, demotion, replacement, own-session and unchanged-administrator controls. Empty-plan and closed-writer cases also pass.
  - `guarded_effects_reauthorize_after_store_lock_without_partial_writes` and `guarded_state_and_delete_recheck_owner_and_authority_after_connection_wait` verify post-lock authorization and preserved durable data on denial. `history_wait_releases_map_and_refuses_replaced_incarnation` covers the changed history lock order.
  - `remote_resume_admission_wait_uses_current_principal` covers remote demotion with an own-session control. `remote_resume_rechecks_channels_at_final_agent_install` checks capability changes during the final Agent wait. The plan-backpressure matrix now includes remote live and cross-mode resume and checks their intended admission-permit lifetimes.
- **Commands run and tail output** (author-reported historical local evidence on b0879527d3, macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0; not a claim of new local runs on the integrated head):
  - `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/admitted|demot|owner|resume|queued/)'`: `114 tests run: 114 passed, 5169 skipped`.
  - `TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/rpc::/)'`: `660 tests run: 660 passed, 4623 skipped`.
  - `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict`: fmt passes; clippy stops on its only error, `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, which unmodified `master` also reports on macOS (the import is used only by Windows and Linux code). The script's provider-dispatch section, run on its own: `provider dispatch gate clean`.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings -A unused_imports`: `Finished`, no diagnostics.
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: `Finished`, no warnings.
  - `./scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
  - `cargo test --no-run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: every test target builds; its only warnings are the two macOS-only ones unmodified `master` emits (the `std::sync::mpsc` import and the `ld: __eh_frame section too large` linker note), so allowing `unused_imports` above hides nothing new.
  - `TMPDIR=/private/tmp ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_RUNS=1 ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`: `zeroclaw-runtime` `5231 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored`, `zeroclaw-channels` `1957 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`.
  - Plugin-backend commands from `check-plugin-backends`, run as written (the change filter reports `true` for this diff). The two `zeroclaw-runtime` legs ran on this commit; the rest ran on the previous revision of it, which differs only in `rpc/dispatch.rs`:
    - `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features` `plugins-wasm-cranelift` / `plugins-wasm-pulley` / `plugins-wasmtime`: all `Finished`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test channel_plugin_e2e --test egress_plugin_e2e --test tool_plugin_timeout_e2e --test reference_plugin --test reference_plugin_e2e --test tool_plugin_e2e`: every binary `ok`, 43 passed, 0 failed.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib`: `260 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib agent::plugin_live_config`: `2 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- plugin_runtime:: tools::tests::shared_ceiling tools::tests::repeated_loader tools::tests::auto_discover tools::tests::colliding_plugin`: `22 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`: `4 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test channel_egress_e2e`: `3 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw`: `551 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test component -- plugin_info_cli`: `4 passed; 0 failed`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical author verification on b0879527d3 and the earlier revisions noted below (not newly repeated on the integrated head): confirmed the regressions fail without the fix by mutating one path at a time and rerunning them. Removing only the ownership check after the prompt's provider waits lets the demoted administrator's prompt complete a turn on bob's session (`"turn finished"` from his provider), once parked on the provider-update lock and once on the pending binding. Judging every scope by the stamp again fails the other two: the queued prompt runs a turn on bob's session (it reaches his provider), and the stale stamp rebinds bob's live session. Removing only the post-lock owner check restores bob's reaped chat session; judging only the ACP restore preload by the stamp recovers bob's interrupted turn into his history before the refusal; removing only the owner check in the resume closure rebinds bob's live session; judging only rehydration by the stamp revives bob's reaped session; removing only the scope from kill's durable fallback tombstones bob's session (`killed: true`), and from delete's fallback deletes it. The delete, kill and rehydration mutations ran on an earlier revision of these tests that lacked only the liveness precondition assertions. At that time, `git merge-tree --write-tree` with #10412 and `master` completed without conflicts; that historical check does not establish their current integration state. Did not run a live daemon against a real principal roster.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface or presentation changed. The existing RPC denial shape is asserted by the handler regressions.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current hosted CI: `d5df4214cad96bfc6bfbdea13a64767b116ac1df` in the linked jobs. Historical local evidence remains `b0879527d3` on #11222's `69532f214e`. The current tests exercise handler and JSON-RPC dispatcher behavior, outbound frames, and storage effects. No live deployment or rendered-interface run is claimed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** a refused request returns `{"code":-32012,"message":"Session not found or not owned by this principal"}` (`FORBIDDEN`), the same uniform denial scoped principals already receive; every regression asserts the code and message.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A demoted administrator's queued prompt, close, delete, kill, configure, messages or resume of another principal's session is refused at the covered waits, with the foreign session's state preserved. Positive controls explicitly cover deletion and live/reaped resume of the caller's own sessions.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** In the historical local runs above, the `zeroclaw-plugins` legs and root-crate plugin tests were not repeated after the final RPC-only revision; the two runtime plugin legs were repeated. The current integrated head is covered by the linked hosted jobs, not a claim of repeated local execution. Docs gates were not run because no docs changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change only narrows access: after a wait, cross-principal access requires the administrator bypass under the policy in force at that moment. Fixtures use the existing fake roster principals (`user:alice`, `user:bob`, uids 4242 and 4343).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Wire/config shapes remain compatible; requests that lose authority while waiting are refused. Rust APIs add guarded `SessionBackend` methods and a generation field to `ResumedRpcSession`. The changed `resume_existing_authorized` callback is crate-private, not a public closure API.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Backend compatibility: the new guarded disclosure and deletion defaults return `Unsupported`; custom persistent backends must implement them to support those RPC operations. The guarded state default has no persistent effect and authorizes the locked live owner; a backend that persists state must override it and read the stored owner under its mutation lock. In-tree SQLite and JSONL behavior is covered by the added tests. No wire or config migration is required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual squash commit; this reopens the reported bypass, so prefer a forward fix.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** session requests from principals whose authority did not change being refused after a wait: `FORBIDDEN` "Session not found or not owned by this principal" on their own sessions, or WARN "RPC authorization denied" for `session/close`, `session/kill`, `session/delete`, `session/configure` or `session/messages`.

prs.title: test(providers): hold the runtime proxy guard in the tool-round wire fixture
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails intermittently in full `zeroclaw-providers` runs. The cause is shared state, not timing. `responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` and `codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction` point the process-wide runtime proxy at a throwaway server for `model_provider.openai`. They serialise on `RuntimeProxyTestGuard`; the tool-round fixture (`wire_body`) did not take that guard. When it overlapped one of them, its OpenAI clients were built through the proxy, and its request went to the proxy fixture instead of its own server.
  - That gives three failure modes, all of which I've seen locally:
    - a decode error, when the proxy answers with its own JSON
    - "Connection refused", once the proxy test has stopped its server
    - the fixture's 5 s timeout, when a stream never sees its final event
  - `wire_body` now holds the guard for its lifetime.
- **Scope boundary:** test-only. No production code changes. I didn't audit other fixtures for the same pattern.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-providers` tests only. The tool-round test now waits for a running proxy test instead of overlapping it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11467 (added the test)

### What this does, simply

Two tests temporarily switch on a global HTTP proxy for the OpenAI provider, and they take a shared lock so nothing else is affected while they do. One newer test didn't take that lock. When it happened to run at the same moment, its requests went through the other test's fake proxy, and it failed for reasons that had nothing to do with what it checks. It now takes the lock too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The loop below reproduces it deterministically.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** the providers test binary run 40 times with only the three tests involved (`native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction`):

```text
master ee2f5f58f7:  40 of 40 runs failed
  panicked at crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai.rs:1951:26:
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: error decoding response body
this branch:        0 of 40 runs failed

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-providers -- --check                          ok
```
