prs.title: fix(build): stop metrics and embedded-web from enabling the gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The two strong edges.** `observability-prometheus` and `embedded-web` forwarded to `zeroclaw-gateway/<feature>`. That is a strong edge: it also turns the optional gateway dependency on.
    - So a build that selected metrics or the embedded dashboard without `gateway` compiled the whole HTTP gateway: axum, the hyper server, tower-http and the dashboard build script.
    - Every root use of the gateway is behind `cfg(feature = "gateway")`, so that code was never reachable.
    - Both now forward with `zeroclaw-gateway?/<feature>`, as every other forward into the gateway already does.
  - **Two unused dependencies.** `zeroclaw-runtime` declared `tower` and `tower-http` as optional dependencies that no feature enables and no runtime code uses. They are removed.
  - **A new architecture gate.** It fails when any root feature other than `gateway` enables the gateway crate, either through `dep:` or through a strong sub-feature edge. Headless builds cannot quietly pick the server up again.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No change to the `gateway` feature, the default feature set, the dist feature sets, or any Rust source outside the new test.
  - This PR does not remove the gateway from any shipped artifact.
  - The existing strong forwards into `zeroclaw-runtime` (`observability-prometheus`, `webauthn`, `plugins-wasm`, `sandbox-*`) are out of scope. This change only adjusts optional gateway activation.
- **Blast radius:** Cargo feature resolution only.
  - Builds that include `gateway` resolve exactly as before: the default build, every dist target and the desktop kernel.
  - Builds without `gateway` that select `observability-prometheus`, `metrics` or `embedded-web` stop compiling `zeroclaw-gateway`. This includes `install.sh --without-gateway`, whose default set carries `observability-prometheus`.
  - `Cargo.lock` loses two unused edges from `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11969. Part of #11971 and #11002.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's web gateway (dashboard, REST API, webhooks) is an optional part of the binary, switched on by the `gateway` build feature. Two unrelated features were wired so that asking for either one also switched the gateway on: Prometheus metrics, and "embed the dashboard files". Someone building a headless agent with metrics got the full web server compiled in, even though nothing could start it.

This PR wires those two features so they only adjust the gateway when it is already included. It also adds a check so no other feature can make the same mistake later. Normal builds, including every release build, are unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It is quick and needs no build, only dependency resolution.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** build (`cargo tree`); no runtime surface.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a checkout of this branch and of `master`.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo tree -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features observability-prometheus -e normal --prefix none | grep -c '^zeroclaw-gateway '`. Repeat with `embedded-web`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `0`
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `1`. The gateway is in the graph although `gateway` was not selected.

### How I tested

The branch merges `master` at 89bd18484b (merge e9f288923f). The merge was clean. The diff against master is still the same five files, so master's current feature and distribution policy is preserved unchanged. On e9f288923f:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              → exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                      → Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw --no-default-features \
  --features agent-runtime,default-channels,acp-bridge,observability-prometheus,schema-export \
  --lib --bins                                                          → exit 0
  (6 pre-existing dead-code warnings in src/main.rs for gateway-off builds; unchanged by this PR)
cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --all-targets -p zeroclaw -- -D warnings          → exit 0
cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --bins -- -D warnings    → exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --test architecture                     → 81 passed, 0 failed (incl. gateway_feature_edges::only_the_gateway_feature_enables_the_gateway_crate
                                                                           and gateway_feature_edges::gateway_edge_classifies_every_entry_form)
```

**Gateway present in the resolved graph.** This is the count of `zeroclaw-gateway` nodes in `cargo tree -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features <F> -e normal`:

| `--features` | master 89bd18484b | this branch e9f288923f |
|---|---|---|
| `observability-prometheus` | 1 | 0 |
| `embedded-web` | 1 | 0 |
| `metrics` | 1 | 0 |
| `agent-runtime,observability-prometheus` | 1 | 0 |
| `gateway,observability-prometheus` | 1 | 1 |
| `gateway,embedded-web` | 1 | 1 |

**Default and release builds are unchanged.** The full package and feature list from `cargo tree -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}'` is identical between master and this branch for each of these:
- the default set;
- the distribution set (`cargo generate features --selection dist`);
- the distribution set plus `embedded-web`, which is the desktop kernel's set, for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-apple-darwin`.

| Set | Target | Lines | master vs this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | 532 | identical |
| dist | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | 914 | identical |
| dist + `embedded-web` | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | 916 | identical |
| dist + `embedded-web` | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | 919 | identical |

The weak edges still apply when the gateway is on. On this branch, `zeroclaw-gateway` still has `observability-prometheus` enabled in the default graph, and both `observability-prometheus` and `embedded-web` in the dist + `embedded-web` graphs.

**Revert check.** With the root `Cargo.toml` put back to master's version (the strong edges) and the new test kept, `cargo test --test architecture gateway_feature_edges` fails (1 passed, 1 failed):

```text
thread 'gateway_feature_edges::only_the_gateway_feature_enables_the_gateway_crate' panicked at tests/architecture/gateway_feature_edges.rs:117:5:
these root features switch on the gateway crate without the `gateway` feature; forward with `zeroclaw-gateway?/<feature>` instead, or select `gateway` explicitly:
  embedded-web = "zeroclaw-gateway/embedded-web"
  observability-prometheus = "zeroclaw-gateway/observability-prometheus"
```

Restoring the change makes it pass (2 passed, 0 failed).

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the workspace tests, which include the `architecture` target with the new gate, plus the lint and build jobs over the changed manifests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not build a headless (`--no-default-features`) configuration with metrics. The headless `cargo check` and the `cargo tree` counts above cover it.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Verified: the headless feature combination compiles, and every root use of the gateway crate is behind `cfg(feature = "gateway")`, so nothing that could run changes.
  - Not verified: a full release build of any target.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** e9f288923f; `cargo tree`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --test architecture`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the tables and tails above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tables.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace `cargo test`. The change is manifest-only apart from the new test, and CI runs the full suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change removes an unreachable HTTP server from headless build graphs and opens nothing new.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Builds with `gateway` are unchanged. Builds without it lose only gateway code that could not be reached.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Cargo feature names are unchanged. `embedded-web` now has no effect unless `gateway` is also selected, and that was already the only case where it did anything observable.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`. The change touches only Cargo feature edges, two unused optional runtime dependencies and one architecture test, so it reverts cleanly.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The change is in feature resolution; there is no runtime switch.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A headless build (`--no-default-features` without `gateway`) that selects `observability-prometheus`, `metrics` or `embedded-web` fails to compile on a missing gateway item. That would mean some root code uses the gateway outside `cfg(feature = "gateway")`. The headless `cargo check` above guards this case.
  - In builds with `gateway`, any difference in `cargo tree` output from master. The identity check above shows none.
  - A revert brings back the unwanted gateway activation. Nothing else changes.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(channels): add configurable XMPP/Prosody channel with optional OMEMO
prs.body:
## Summary



- **Base branch:** `master`.

- Add a first-class, opt-in `channel-xmpp` adapter for direct XMPP conversations, including Prosody. Inbound messages and replies use the existing channel supervisor and agent runtime, rather than an HTTP bridge or a separate agent loop.

- Expose account JID, server, port, Direct TLS or mandatory STARTTLS, masked password, resource, limits, interpreter and optional OMEMO settings through the schema-driven WebUI. The channel page's **Allowed users** tab creates alias-scoped canonical authorization policies and edits allowed/blocked users without a second allowlist.

- Require verified TLS in both transport modes. Optional OMEMO requires manually pinned device fingerprints, persists identity/ratchet state per alias and never downgrades to plaintext.

- **Scope boundary:** direct one-to-one text; no MUC, attachments, MAM, carbons or OMEMO v2. No deployment-specific hosts, ports, accounts, credentials or server provisioning.

- **Blast radius:** additive configuration/attribution metadata, feature-gated channel registration/runtime wiring, and one WebUI tab scoped to XMPP aliases. Existing listeners and the shared agent loop are unchanged.



Closes #9814



### What this does, simply



Operators who already have an XMPP server can bind a ZeroClaw agent to an account and converse with it from authorized accounts. Server address and JID domain are independent: the former selects the TCP destination and the latter remains the TLS service identity. Both STARTTLS and Direct TLS are selectable, and changing protocol does not silently change the configured port.



The Rust adapter owns the normal `Channel` lifecycle and authorization. An embedded, isolated Python transport worker uses Slixmpp for XMPP and an optional slixmpp-omemo backend for legacy OMEMO. It does not call the gateway or run models/tools. Python dependencies must be installed explicitly; Cargo does not install them. Missing dependencies fail closed.



The optional **slixmpp-omemo backend is AGPL-3.0-only**. It is not vendored. This dependency/license tradeoff is explicit in the installation guide and requirements file; TLS-only operation needs only MIT-licensed Slixmpp.



## Testing (required)

### Assembled listener proof requested in review

[Revision, environment and observed results](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/5a0150bdc/.pr-evidence/xmpp-listener.md): built the exact public code revision 37275ff8c and ran zeroclaw channel start against isolated Prosody with certificate-verified Direct TLS. Authorized input reached the real agent dispatcher and returned an XMPP reply. Unauthorized input before and after produced zero model calls and zero replies. Only the external model API was simulated and counted. OMEMO was disabled in this assembled-path proof; the prior transport/OMEMO matrix remains complementary. This evidence-only commit changes no runtime code or production daemon.



### How you can test



- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.

- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; messaging `channel=xmpp`.

- **Setup / preconditions:** build with `channel-xmpp`, install the documented Python requirements in a dedicated venv, and use disposable XMPP accounts with a trusted server certificate. For OMEMO, enable server PEP/pubsub and verify device fingerprints out of band.

- **Steps to run:** follow `docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md`; create an XMPP alias in Config, enter the connection fields, authorize bare JIDs under Allowed users, bind the channel to an enabled agent, enable the listener and reload. Send a direct message from an authorized account and compare with an unauthorized account. Repeat with STARTTLS and Direct TLS. Enable OMEMO and verify that unencrypted/untrusted traffic is refused.

- **Expected on this branch (after):** the channel and settings are available; authorized text reaches the common agent runtime and replies use XMPP. Empty policy denies everyone. Encrypted mode refuses plaintext fallback.

- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no XMPP channel/configuration/transport is available.



### How I tested

Review follow-up (37275ff8c): the adapter now identifies its accepted one-to-one messages as direct chats, avoiding unintended reply-intent classification. Worker frames are explicitly UTF-8 bytes rather than ASCII escapes, keeping maximum-length Unicode bodies within the existing 512 KiB frame bound independently of process locale. The Playwright evidence script uses a literal loopback URL instead of an environment-supplied navigation target.

Focused validation for this revision: three Python bridge tests passed, including 64,000 non-BMP characters, worst-case escaped controls and successful decoding of the following frame; two Rust XMPP adapter tests passed, including direct-message classification after authorization/encryption checks. Rustfmt, Node syntax checking and `git diff --check` passed. New-head CI is pending; no additional live deployment or end-to-end server test is claimed for this follow-up.


OMEMO receive-trust regression (4384a374515f): the real-server integration test reproduces the failure with the previous bridge (cached DISTRUSTED device, then add its fingerprint and receive before any outbound message). The patched bridge passes this regression and inbound pin revocation. Direct TLS, mandatory STARTTLS, certificate rejection, persistent OMEMO identity, bidirectional encryption, plaintext rejection, and outbound trust revocation also pass.

```text
PASS newly pinned cached-distrusted device receives before first outbound
PASS removed pin blocks inbound before first outbound
PASS revoked trust blocks outbound without plaintext fallback
```




- Focused Linux Rust tests: configuration round trips, disabled partial configuration, password secrecy metadata, authorization before dispatch, required encryption, alias attribution and offline/unauthorized sends. Passed on the independent `master` base, including an isolated no-default-features channel build. Registry tests (2) and the channel-migration inventory regression (1) also passed.

- Real isolated Prosody 13 on loopback, disposable accounts and a temporary CA: both TLS modes, rejection of an untrusted certificate, authenticated OMEMO round trips, identity persistence after restart, rejection of plaintext in required-encryption mode, and revocation without downgrade all passed.

- Python helper unit tests: 2 passed. New guide Markdown lint: 0 errors. Frontend TypeScript and Vite production build passed on the independent source, and the final Chrome fixture run includes creating an initially empty authorization policy. Focused Clippy passed with `-D warnings`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the clean generated dashboard contract (`cargo web check`) and Web Permission Tests passed on the initial code revision. The final head reruns the required suite and adds an isolated XMPP feature test lane. No claim is made that every final-head CI job has finished.

- **Known CI coverage gap:** the Python dependencies and real Prosody/OMEMO matrix are opt-in local tests. Native Windows worker execution and an actual model-provider conversation were not verified.

- **Commands run and tail output:**



```text

cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test xmpp

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-xmpp xmpp --lib

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-xmpp --lib -- -D warnings

Finished dev profile

python crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/test_xmpp_bridge.py

Ran 2 tests ... OK

markdownlint-cli2 docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md

Summary: 0 error(s)

```



- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Actual TLS/OMEMO transport against the isolated server. WebUI interactions use a privacy-safe local API fixture with the real page renderer; they are not a live production/gateway or model-provider test.

- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cf9df9215a40e5a0a447df072adf7602b2af9c2d`, `surface=web`, English locale, desktop 1440x1000 and mobile 390x844.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Verification notes, reproducible UI harness and screenshots](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/cf9df9215a40e5a0a447df072adf7602b2af9c2d/.pr-evidence/xmpp.md).

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** protocol saved independently of port; replacement password editor remained blank/masked; OMEMO and enabled controls wrote their schema fields; the page created a scoped `peer_groups.*.channel = "xmpp.<alias>"` policy and allowed-user edits wrote its `external_peers`. Only the authorization fields are edited by that scoped form. No page JavaScript errors or mobile page overflow in the fixture run.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full workspace/all-platform tests are left to repository CI; focused local checks cover the feature and real transport gap. A clean generated-contract check relies on CI because the local Windows generator cache contained missing build-script artifacts. The first CI run identified the migration inventory, expanded all-feature installer lists and one Clippy expression; all three are addressed in the final update.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Enabling a listener launches the configured interpreter and creates private per-alias SQLite state. Interpreter/configuration remains an operator-controlled administrative capability.

- New external network calls? **Yes.** Only the configured XMPP endpoint and XMPP protocol discovery/pubsub operations; TLS certificates are verified and there is no plaintext transport or trust-all option.

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** The account password uses the existing encrypted secret machinery and secret-aware editor, and crosses only private stdin to the worker, not argv/environment/logs. OMEMO keys remain in private per-alias state; confidential backup requirements are documented.

- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Only fictitious reserved-example identities and disposable loopback fixtures.

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** XMPP text is a new untrusted input surface. Canonical peer policy is checked before dispatch to the shared agent runtime; existing tool/approval policies continue to apply. OMEMO protects transport to the bot, not plaintext subsequently sent to a configured model provider.



## Compatibility (required)



- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Additive schema; no configured listener is enabled by default.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New `channels.xmpp.<alias>` settings and Cargo feature; no existing setting is renamed.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

- **Upgrade steps:** no action for existing deployments. XMPP users opt into the build feature, install the documented Python dependencies, configure the alias and canonical authorization/agent binding, then enable it. OMEMO is separately optional and requires verified pins. The transport matrix is validated on Linux; native Windows execution is not claimed.



## Rollback



- **Fast rollback command/path:** disable the alias using its header toggle and reload; or revert this PR. Preserve the private OMEMO database if restoring the same account later.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** omit `channel-xmpp`, set the alias `enabled=false`, or set `omemo_enabled=false` when intentionally choosing TLS-only chat.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** offline channel health, supervisor reconnect/backoff, generic bridge/TLS/authentication failures, or a send error without plaintext fallback. No stanza bodies, passwords or identity keys are logged for diagnosis.




### Master integration follow-up

`8c47216e3` integrates current master and preserves both XMPP and MQTT feature-test lanes. Integrated-tree validation passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --lib xmpp:: (2/2); announcement and one-shot builder inventory tests (1/1 each); Python bridge tests (3/3); YAML parse and git diff --check. The earlier assembled listener proof remains evidence for its explicitly recorded revision; it is not relabeled as a new-head live test. Required new-head CI remains pending.

prs.title: fix(containers): refresh runtime CA stores after emSign distrust
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This branch now merges master at ece3b744e6, which is #11924 as merged. It no longer carries any audit exception.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Refresh the canonical container base pins and their generated recipes, including zerorelay and the separate `Dockerfile.ci` distroless pin used for published images. Rebuilding from the old pins keeps the incident trust anchors.
  - Require the patched native CA packages: bookworm `20250419~deb12u2` (DLA-4845-1), trixie `20250419+deb13u1` (DSA-6572-1) and Alpine `20261020-r0`. A cached or outdated package layer then fails the build instead of shipping the old trust store.
  - Filter the incident roots out of the StageX bundle. Package only the filtered bundle and its aliases, so individual root files cannot restore removed trust. The current StageX input still contains emSign ECC Root CA - G3.
  - Add compromised-issuer regressions, an unaffected-CA control and offline filter tests. Run the filter tests and select the StageX build in Docker PR CI when their inputs change.
  - Give the default ARM64 source-build row the existing bounded-memory helper, with ownership-checked cleanup. Without it, that row ran out of memory on this PR's earlier heads.
  - Update `docs/maintainers/audit-policy.md`: remove the legacy WebPKI inventory that #11924 made stale, and separate audit tool scope from advisory severity.
- **Scope boundary:** Container trust stores, their build checks, and the related policy text. #11924 owns the Rust TLS, MQTT and Wasmtime dependency repair; this branch leaves its lockfile, manifests and code exactly as on master. The earlier MQTT advisory exception, its source guard and its developer audit wiring are gone, and nothing replaces them. Third-party images such as Continuwuity need their own upstream updates.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime CA bundles in every generated image variant, and the native clients that read them (curl, git, OpenSSL-linked tools). Paths through the distrusted issuers stop authenticating, as intended. The StageX filter also lists Sectigo's "AAA Certificate Services" root, which cross-signed the compromised intermediates. Debian's security update removes the same root, and Mozilla had already dropped it. Neither the current nor the previous StageX CA input contains it, so today's filtered bundle differs from its input only by emSign ECC Root CA - G3. Sectigo chains that anchor at USERTrust, COMODO RSA/ECC or Sectigo R46/E46 are unaffected. No application configuration, channel behaviour or production Rust code changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11932. Depends on #11924 (merged as ece3b744e6). Related #11923, Related #11906 (original Wasmtime contribution by @mov-xound-glitch, retained in #11924 and credited as co-author in ece3b744e6), Related #5869 and Related #8519. Public incident references: [Mozilla response](https://blog.mozilla.org/security/2026/10/20/protecting-firefox-users-following-the-compromise-of-emudhra-intermediate-certificates/), [Debian DSA-6572-1](https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00487.html), [incident test chains](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/).

### What this does, simply

The Rust certificate verifier was fixed in #11924. Native tools inside our containers still read the CA files that ship in the image, and the published image still trusts all twelve public incident chains. This change rebuilds those files from patched sources. It also refuses to build if an old CA package slips in, and strips the affected roots from the StageX bundle, which has no patched package yet. Unrelated roots are left untouched. Shipping a corrected image and recreating running containers is release work that follows this source change.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the CA bundle and generated-recipe boundaries.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` test and build commands, and certificate verification beneath TLS consumers.
- **Setup / preconditions:** The repository toolchain and locked dependencies. Python 3 and POSIX tools for the filter tests. Docker or Podman for the optional CA-stage builds. The tests are offline and use public certificates with a fixed verification time.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tls --test emudhra_distrust`; `python3 -m unittest dev/ci/test_filter_emudhra_ca_bundle.py`; `cargo run --release --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- installers dockerfile dockerfile-debian dockerfile-alpine dockerfile-zerorelay containerfile --check`; and `docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f Containerfile --target ca-bundle .` to inspect the filtered StageX output.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Both compromised issuer paths fail with `CertDistrusted` and the unaffected certificate verifies. The five filter tests pass. The filtered StageX bundle has 120 certificates, all identical to the input apart from emSign ECC Root CA - G3. All five generated recipes report `in sync`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The published v0.8.6 image's CA bundle accepts 12/12 incident chains. The StageX CA input accepts 6/12. With `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15, the regression tests return `ServerCertVerified(())` for both compromised paths. These are observations of immutable published images and bundles, not of a container built from unmodified master.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** All runs are on this head, b3006925bc, which includes master's dependency base.
  - [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169861) passed, including [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169861/job/119566597624) and the [Security job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169861/job/119563902967). In the Security job, `cargo deny` reports `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. `cargo audit` scans 1,297 dependencies and finds no vulnerabilities, with six allowed unmaintained warnings and no RUSTSEC-2026-0382 ignore. Lint, Test and the MQTT channel test also pass there.
  - [Docker Image PR Check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169498) passed all 11 jobs. That includes the [Containerfile all-features build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169498/job/119563963187), which exercises the StageX filter stage, and every Dockerfile, Dockerfile.debian and Dockerfile.alpine source build. It also includes the [default ARM64 source build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699169498/job/119563963131), where bounded-memory setup, the build and owned cleanup all succeeded.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The four conditional ARM64 smoke steps (non-root image, Compose port, Alpine binaries, Alpine Compose) are skipped on that row, so there is no ARM64 runtime-smoke result. No rebuilt release digest or deployment is claimed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** These ran on an isolated Linux x86_64 host with Rust 1.98.0 and Python 3.12.3. The merge commit 031c1ce7ac has the same tree as the residual that was validated on top of #11924's tested head. That head's tree is identical to ece3b744e6.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Offline bundle checks reject all 12 incident chains for the refreshed distroless, the rebuilt bookworm and trixie stages, the pinned Alpine stage and the filtered StageX stage.
  - Against the published image, the refreshed Debian bundle drops exactly two certificates, AAA Certificate Services and emSign ECC Root CA - G3. These match the DSA-6572-1 and DLA-4845-1 removals.
  - The previous and current StageX CA inputs (`7773dae6`, `fe24a380`) contain emSign ECC Root CA - G3 but not AAA.
  - The trixie floor accepts `20250419+deb13u1` and rejects the unpatched `20250419`, both with the real `dpkg` comparator and in a container build on the pinned trixie digest.
  - The verifier downgrade, filter guards and native package floors were each mutation-checked and restored.
  - Not verified locally: complete application images for every variant and architecture.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no visual interface state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** merge 031c1ce7ac (tree 699ce9b378) and follow-up b3006925bc (tree 9d9ad6e79e). The source tests are in `crates/zeroclaw-tls/tests/emudhra_distrust.rs` and `dev/ci/test_filter_emudhra_ca_bundle.py`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test output above. The hosted runs on b3006925bc are linked under CI checks.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The corrected CA stages reject the incident corpus. The unaffected certificate and filter controls still pass.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full application-container builds for every variant are left to hosted CI. A full-policy prose check of `audit-policy.md` reports inherited findings on both this branch and master (nine here, twelve on master), with none added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, CI only: the default ARM64 source-build row runs the existing bounded temporary-memory helper. Runtime permissions are unchanged.
- New external network calls? No. Builds use the existing image registries and package repositories.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures are public CA certificates and a neutral `host.invalid` leaf. There are no private keys.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The helper runs only on GitHub Actions Linux and checks disk headroom first. It creates bounded private swap and verifies its ownership receipt before cleanup, and failures propagate. Master's release workflows already use the same helper and step pattern. The CA change narrows trust on purpose; certificate verification stays on.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for valid chains through unaffected roots. Chains through the distrusted issuers fail on purpose.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. The developer-only Python and audit-command additions from earlier heads are gone, and `just audit`, `dev/ci.sh audit` and the editor task match master.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No. The refreshed base digests keep their declared tags.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. After release, pull the new image and recreate containers. Rebuilding old release binaries into new images is not enough.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Stop the rollout and ship a corrected patched build. Restoring the old CA inputs brings the exposure back. If a later StageX input carries the AAA root and a legitimate Sectigo chain that reaches only AAA breaks, there is a narrow option: remove the `d7a7a0fb…` case from `dev/ci/filter-emudhra-ca-bundle.sh`, take `aaa-root.pem` out of the filter test's blocked set, and give the empty-output test another blocked fixture. The Rust verifier still rejects the compromised intermediates; native clients in the StageX image would accept the AAA cross-signed path again.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Keep certificate verification on.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A build stops at a CA package floor, the bundle filter or a memory ownership check. A TLS destination fails with `CertDistrusted` or `UnknownIssuer`. Inspect the server chain and fix issuance or the build inputs; do not disable verification.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A; no PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve completed tool results and reuse bounded recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Reuse #11507's result-aware recovery for channel turns; checkpoint the runtime-owned canonical tool transcript on every terminal path; retain paired prompt-mode results during session reload; allow bounded cooperative cancellation before releasing a timed-out turn.
- **Scope boundary:** No additional tool authority, automatic action replay, background job scheduler, new configuration fields or longer processing budget. Operations without a recorded result remain uncertain.
- **Blast radius:** Shared channel orchestration and the runtime recovery entrypoint. Agent API behavior from #11507 is retained.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11909. Depends on #11507 and #11868. Related #11869 and #11874. The prerequisite commits retain their original history; the follow-up delta is the commit after the integration merge.

### What this does, simply

A channel task can finish an operation and then time out while waiting for the model. Previously its completed results were not saved like those of a successful turn. Prompt-mode results could also be mistaken for a new user request and removed during reload. A follow-up could therefore lack evidence of completed work.

This change saves completed results to the existing session backend before closeout, preserves valid native and textual tool pairs, and tells the next turn to verify uncertain operations before retrying. Repeated identical failures use the existing correction and one-retry policy; successful polling is advisory. Cancellation gets at most five seconds for cooperative executor closeout. A model switch cannot restart the processing deadline.

**Core architecture review requested:** the recorded #11484/#11507 holding-crate exception explicitly excludes a new public API and legacy channel-policy changes. This follow-up requires a bounded extension for the opaque turn-local recovery handle and channel entrypoint in `agent/turn/mod.rs`, re-export in `agent/loop_.rs`, and the receiving channel caller. It introduces no subsystem, persistent guard, grants or config. The intended owner remains the agent-loop owner in the planned kernel extraction. This PR does not self-grant that extension and remains draft pending the recorded decision.

## Testing (required)

### Cancellation regression follow-up

Commit `ffb06c03d` corrects three cancellation assertions to require exactly the runtime-owned interruption marker, while still rejecting provider responses or duplicate markers. Baseline failures were reproduced on the public head. Corrected focused suites passed: message_dispatch_ 21/21, channel_recovery_ 4/4, turn_deadline::tests 6/6, process_channel_message 57/57. Rustfmt and diff checks passed. This is test-only. Fresh CI, dependency audit, architecture approval and integration conflicts remain separate requirements.

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for live messaging: deterministic tests drive the production channel orchestrator, real SQLite backend, tool dispatcher and outbound channel interface with synthetic provider/tool fixtures.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet; fresh upstream CI is requested. Local checks cover the modified runtime and channel boundaries.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live vendor transport or real-model behavior is claimed. External transport behavior is unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Public candidate 3ce4e1102: channel recovery 4/4, deadline 6/6 and existing process_channel_message 57/57 passed. Runtime recovery prerequisite 9/9 passed. cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. cargo fmt --all and git diff --check passed. The separately integrated deployment build also passed runtime turn377/tool execution38/detector28/locales48 and XMPP/progress regressions, plus release compilation.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed cancellation, canonical-buffer ownership, prompt carrier pairing, session hydration and retention opt-out. No production credentials or private incident traces are part of the fixtures.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; this changes execution and session continuity, not presentation. Existing timeout messages remain unchanged.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current candidate; shared channel orchestrator tests `channel_recovery_*` and `turn_deadline::tests`, runtime `agent::agent::safety_net::loop_recovery` from the prerequisite.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** SQLite resume tests clear the cache, reload the session and assert that the completed result is present while the counting tool's execution count remains one. Both native call IDs and prompt-mode carriers are checked. Repeated failures execute three attempts plus one recovery retry and deliver the existing recoverable terminal response.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Tool completes, following provider call stalls, deadline expires, follow-up reloads durable state and reuses the completed result without another operation. Orphan textual results remain stripped. Cancellation cannot be misreported as completion; expired budget never polls a new operation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace-wide tests are left to required upstream CI; focused local regression and Clippy cover the changed crates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No; existing result scrubbing and session access controls remain in force.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes: runtime-owned interruption markers instruct verification of uncertain operations and prohibit blind replay. No remote text is elevated to system authority. Existing tool-context retention controls whether results are persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for config and session schema. Channel recovery intentionally changes from argument-only blocking to completed-result evidence, matching configured Agent APIs.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. There is an additive Rust recovery entrypoint requiring the Core exception extension described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Retention-disabled configurations continue to opt out of saved tool context. Resumption is a new user turn, not an automatic retry.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this follow-up commit; prerequisite PRs remain independent.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing pacing loop-detection and tool-context-retention settings; no new toggle.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing or duplicate tool pairs after reload, repeated operations despite completed results, a conversation lane retained beyond the bounded cleanup allowance, or cancellation reported as success. The SQLite and deadline regressions cover these contracts.


Integration follow-up `1d8980241` merges master `6a99c3dee` and keeps its canonical provider-ready history helper while preserving paired prompt tool results. Local integrated-tree checks passed: rustfmt; process_channel_message 57/57; channel_recovery 4/4; deadline 6/6; message_dispatch 21/21; image 40/40; attachment 61/61; normalization 3/3 (filters overlap). Upstream CI and Core architecture approval remain required.

prs.title: feat(goal): add dormant configuration and command grammar [Goal V1 proposal 2/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

Goal V1 proposal 2/12. This is configuration and command grammar, not an executable Goal Mode prefix. No merge or deployment readiness is claimed.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add transport-neutral Goal command parsing, including multiline resume responses and immediate-pause syntax, without exposing an unwired executable command.
  - Add default-disabled canonical Goal configuration and verifier-alias validation, rename, and deletion handling.
  - Preserve explicitly unlimited budget keys through full and incremental saves alongside ordinary built-in tool selections.
  - Return existing typed configuration error codes and exact field paths instead of internal enum names or pathless errors. Keep the existing English diagnostic payload and presentation-owned localization boundary.
  - Test actual gateway config-save responses, published state, and disk persistence for rejected invalid edits, saved-with-warning edits, and valid enabled settings.
- **Scope boundary:** Slice 02 adds configuration, grammar, persistence safeguards, diagnostics, and tests to slice 01's durable task/control-plane foundation. No Goal executor, provider call, transport admission, scheduler, or usage-ledger integration is added here. The gateway production save policy is unchanged; its new tests cover the consequences of more precise configuration error paths.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/config/command APIs, config introspection and serialization, alias references, full and dirty saves, and gateway error binding. An enable-only edit with a missing/dangling verifier can save with a warning; while that error exists, the unchanged first-error save policy reports only the Goal warning, so an unrelated edit to a field validated after Goal is saved without its own validation. The dashboard does not display these warnings. Direct invalid-verifier edits remain rejected. Execution admission must independently reject an invalid verifier in its owning later slice.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10341; Related #8303; Depends on #11878. Neither tracker nor RFC is closed by this PR.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878

### What this does, simply

This defines how Goal commands and settings are represented, checked, and saved. It does not make Goal commands run. Zero budgets mean unlimited and survive saving. Enabling Goal through the editor without choosing budgets writes both zero defaults; this proposal treats that enablement as consent to unlimited operation, subject to maintainer acceptance. Maintainers may instead require an explicit budget choice before admission. Invalid settings get useful error codes and field locations. The configuration API can save an unrelated repair—or enablement that needs further verifier configuration—and return a warning. The dashboard currently hides successful-save warnings; this PR does not repair that existing limitation. Editing the verifier itself to an invalid value is rejected without changing saved or published state.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — compare the dashboard's configuration surface and error binding with the base.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, dashboard configuration over the ordinary paired gateway. No messaging channel or Goal execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable configuration directory, a loopback-only gateway with pairing enabled, and the ordinary dashboard development server. Do not use an operator configuration or configure a paid provider. Keep both runs isolated. Use the same English locale and browser viewport on base and branch.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and look for Goal under Agent. On this branch, open Goal, enter three spaces in its optional verifier Model field and click Save. Inspect the error and confirm that no whitespace model is written to the disposable config. Do not click Reload daemon or run a Goal. Separately, an Enable click saves immediately; do not follow it with the bottom Save button, because the existing dashboard's stale toggle/draft state can overwrite that write.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Goal settings are discoverable. The invalid model edit shows `required_field_empty`, `goal.verifier.model`, and `must not be empty when provided`; no invalid model is persisted. Enable-only writes retain both zero budget defaults. The API returns a missing-verifier warning (visible only in the PATCH response, e.g. browser developer tools), but the ordinary dashboard does not display successful-save warnings and its enable pill may remain visually disabled despite a successful write.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** At the frozen upstream comparison base `ece3b744e65046a7a528b9e41d7154c04248c2ba`, there is no Goal settings section or these Goal-specific validation errors. The generic dashboard toggle and successful-save warning limitations are unchanged source, not fixes supplied by this PR.

### How I tested

Candidate: `ce72591b32206ade1510646ad7802e85cecb9481`, incorporating frozen upstream `ece3b744e65046a7a528b9e41d7154c04248c2ba`. The incoming merge changes no Goal configuration, command, gateway-save or dashboard implementation.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The completed CI snapshot before this body update recorded 51 successes, five conditional skips and two failures. Subsequent body-update metadata checks also succeeded; they do not replace test coverage. Format, Lint, Security, Test, Parallel Runtime Test, platform compile checks and Windows Service Smoke succeeded. The main Test job reports 19,393 passed and 42 skipped, with two leaky-test warnings retained; its supplementary runs report 189 passed / one skipped and seven passed / five skipped. The gateway Goal config-save and verifier-alias cases were observed passing. All three parallel runtime runs report 5,809 passed / nine ignored each; all three channel runs report 2,015 passed / two ignored each. Security retains six allowed warnings. These results do not erase the failed local workspace runs below.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39872064636
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Test Windows task-owner recovery` failed before compilation because Cargo could not resolve `index.crates.io` while fetching `anyhow`; neither Windows recovery test ran. `CI Required Gate` consequently failed. Windows compile and service-smoke successes do not replace those tests. A scoped rerun request was refused by GitHub CLI (`job 120148911674 cannot be rerun`), and no second attempt started; upstream repository permissions are read-only. A maintainer rerun is needed. No product or workflow change is appropriate for this runner DNS failure. Ignored/live tests, unrestricted feature combinations and later-slice/full-stack execution are not certified.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39872064636/job/120148911674

CI checked GitHub's virtual merge `9792bcbf894eaf48a67a9413686e2c9bd68814ac`, combining this head with upstream `842c71e714dc76c65a374bd75ca050f8f749cc50`, on Rust 1.98.0. Local validation below used this candidate with the frozen upstream base; the two tested trees are distinct. No additional upstream commits were imported into the proposal branch.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Current-head full workspace tests reached two failing targets. The unfiltered no-fail-fast companion reached the remaining packages and doc-tests; the file-backed cases in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/tests/session_goal_control_plane_contract.rs` were observed passing. A supplementary direct log check also confirms the four `goal_patch_*` gateway cases and verifier-alias lifecycle case passed. Those observations are not an aggregate workspace PASS.

Their owning source and the lockfile are unchanged from that base. This supports inherited failures, but does not establish the exact concurrent interleavings of the provider tests. The failed results remain disclosed; no assertions, deadlines, test filters or validation policies were weakened.

The filesystem fixture creates both `nul` and `NUL` in one directory. It fails on a case-insensitive filesystem, not on macOS categorically: macOS volumes can be case-sensitive. Its report and suggested repair remain outside this stack's scope.

Subsequent current-head checks:

prs.title: fix(gateway): admit no new request after the gateway stops, and drain its connections
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11899.

- **The bug.** When the gateway stops, as it does on every daemon reload, the TLS listener only stopped accepting. Every connection it had already accepted went on being served by the stopped gateway's router, with that generation's configuration and authority, for as long as the client kept it alive. Browsers keep TLS connections open, so after a reload they kept talking to the old gateway.
- **The plain listener had a smaller version of the same problem.** It closed idle connections, but it waited without bound for a streaming response such as `/api/events`. The connection tasks it spawned also survived the daemon aborting the gateway.
- **What changes:**
  - **A stopped gateway admits no new request.** Each request first passes an admission check, on every connection the gateway accepted and every HTTP/2 stream.
    - The check is made when the request is first served. It refuses once the gateway is told to stop, or once its tasks were cancelled.
    - A request admitted before the stop is in-flight work: it may finish during the drain.
    - A request the check refuses gets `503` with `Retry-After: 1` and the body `{"error":"The gateway is restarting. Try again.","reason":"gateway_restarting"}`. It never reaches the router.
    - On HTTP/1 the response also carries `Connection: close`. HTTP/2 has no `Connection` header; its connection gets GOAWAY from the graceful shutdown instead.
    - It covers the streams HTTP/2's graceful shutdown still accepts after its GOAWAY.
    - It covers upgrade requests, so no new upgrade is admitted after the stop. One admitted before the stop can still complete afterwards (see below).
    - The response is fixed text. Nothing in it comes from the stopped gateway's configuration, authentication or session state.
  - **Plain and TLS connections share one accept loop, and each connection shuts down gracefully on the stop.** HTTP/1 closes once the response in flight is done; HTTP/2 sends GOAWAY.
  - **The listening port is released as soon as the gateway stops accepting,** as `axum::serve` did for plain HTTP. A connection attempted during the drain is refused, not left in a backlog nothing serves.
  - **In-flight work is cancelled at its next poll, within a bound.**
    - The loop owns every task its serving runs: one per connection, plus the stream tasks hyper's HTTP/2 spawns through its executor.
    - After a stop it waits at most 300 ms for them, then cancels the rest. A cancelled task ends at its next poll, and a task submitted after the cancel never runs.
    - It then waits up to 100 ms for the cancelled tasks to end. After that the gateway stops waiting for its HTTP serving tasks and returns. Daemon replacement still waits for the existing lifecycle owners described below.
  - **Early abort.** If the daemon aborts the gateway first, its tasks are cancelled the same way. The stop was sent before the abort, so no new request is admitted either way.
- **What remains.** A task in code that never yields can outlast the bound. It lingers until its next poll, holding the stopped gateway's state and its socket. It can't admit a request. The gateway logs a WARN with the number of tasks still running.
- **Not changed:**
  - Routes, the services connections run, TLS and mTLS setup.
  - Accept-error handling per listener. Plain HTTP keeps `axum::serve`'s rule: skip a connection that failed before it was accepted, wait out anything else for a second, never stop. TLS keeps its own. The only difference is that a stop now cuts an error backoff short.
  - Which connections can upgrade: native TLS still serves without HTTP/1 upgrades, plain HTTP with them.

## Shutdown budget

- **The cancel happens inside the daemon's 500 ms grace.** 300 ms of drain plus up to 100 ms of waiting for the cancelled tasks stays under it.
- **The 300 ms is a bound on waiting, not on the stop-to-return time.** Scheduling, and the gateway's own teardown after its connections (tunnel, LAN discovery), come on top.
- **No additional barrier for HTTP serving tasks.** The gateway does not wait beyond this retirement budget for those tasks. Daemon replacement still awaits its existing lifecycle drain, including active config writes, agent sessions and turns. An ACP session can therefore delay replacement even after the HTTP listener has retired.

## Upgraded (WebSocket) connections

- **No new upgrade is admitted after the stop.** An upgrade request the check sees after the stop gets the 503, on both listeners. One admitted before the stop can complete its upgrade afterwards; that socket is one of the follow-ups below.
- **Native TLS: no upgraded connections exist.** This path never served HTTP/1 upgrades (`serve_connection`, not `serve_connection_with_upgrades`), and this PR keeps that. Enabling WebSocket over native TLS is a separate change.
- **Plain HTTP: sockets that upgraded before the stop run outside the accept loop.** Once a connection upgrades, axum hands the socket to the route on a task of its own, so this PR neither drains nor cancels it. None of them is fully covered today, and each needs its handler to watch the gateway's stop:
  - **Chat (`/ws/chat`)** watches the stop only between turns; a running turn is awaited first. A socket whose upgrade completes after the stop subscribes after the signal and misses it.
  - **ACP:** its receive loop doesn't watch the stop, so its server and output tasks live until the client leaves.
  - **Canvas, SOP runs and nodes** don't watch it either.

## Testing (required)

- **CI checks relied on:** gateway tests, clippy, rustfmt. [Quality Gate run 39699229693](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39699229693) passed on the refreshed head `7f4fafceae`, including Security.
- **Real gateways** (`run_gateway`), over plain HTTP and TLS:
  - `a_stopped_gateway_admits_no_http2_stream_after_its_goaway`:
    - An HTTP/2 client that never acknowledges the server's PING holds the graceful shutdown in its first phase.
    - After the stop the kept connection gets GOAWAY.
    - A stream sent after the GOAWAY is still accepted by HTTP/2, and never reaches the router: the event stream it asks for never subscribes to the gateway's event bus.
    - Its response, decoded from the wire, is the generic 503 with `Retry-After: 1`, no header beyond `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `Date` (no `Connection`), and the exact body.
    - It covers h2c and h2 over TLS.
  - `a_stopped_gateway_releases_its_port_before_its_drain_ends`: while the drain still holds an event stream, a fresh connection is refused; then the next gateway takes the port.
  - `an_upgrade_racing_the_stop_never_upgrades`: a WebSocket upgrade request written just before the stop, on a kept connection, gets either a closed connection or the generic 503 with `Connection: close`, never `101`.
  - `kept_clients_reach_the_next_generation_on_a_fresh_connection`:
    - A kept HTTP/1.1 connection is closed, and a kept HTTP/2 client's connection ends after GOAWAY, so it can open no stream on it.
    - Each client's next request goes on a fresh connection and is served by the next gateway's router. Its event stream subscribes to the next gateway's bus, not the stopped one's.
  - `a_stopped_tls_gateway_closes_its_connections_and_the_next_one_serves` and `a_stopped_plain_gateway_closes_its_connections_and_the_next_one_serves`:
    - an idle kept-alive connection is closed cleanly;
    - an event stream in flight is cut off within the bound;
    - a pending TLS handshake is closed;
    - the gateway returns promptly;
    - the next gateway serves.
  - `a_stopped_gateway_has_retired_its_http2_streams_when_it_returns`: an h2c event stream's subscription is gone when the gateway returns.
- **The admission check:** `a_stopped_generation_admits_no_request`.
  - It covers HTTP/1.1, an HTTP/1.1 upgrade request, and HTTP/2, after the stop and after a cancel without a stop.
  - It checks: 503, `Retry-After: 1`, `Connection: close` on HTTP/1 only, no other headers but `Content-Type`, the exact body, and that the router never ran.
  - `a_request_taken_before_the_stop_and_served_after_it_is_refused`: the check is made when the request is first served, not when it was read.
- **The task set:**
  - `a_task_spawned_after_the_cancel_never_runs`: sixteen tasks submitted through the executor after the cancel, none of which is ever polled.
  - `a_task_is_counted_until_it_has_been_destroyed`: one task cancelled before its first poll, and one that panics.
  - `spawning_on_a_shut_down_runtime_drops_the_task_without_a_deadlock`: the spawn returns, the task is destroyed before it is uncounted, and the count is zero.
  - `a_task_in_non_yielding_code_ends_at_its_next_poll`: retirement returns within its bound and leaves the task counted, and the task ends once it yields.
  - `dropping_the_serve_loop_cancels_its_tasks`, `retiring_waits_until_the_aborted_tasks_have_ended`, `stream_tasks_hyper_spawns_are_retired_with_the_connections`.
  - `retiring_ends_within_the_daemons_grace`, under paused time.
- **Accept errors:** `each_listener_keeps_its_accept_error_rule` and `a_stop_cuts_an_accept_backoff_short`.
- **Red before each fix (test-only commits over behavior-preserving seams):**
  - **On master's serve code:** the plain and TLS drain tests fail.
  - **Over the admission seam,** five fail:
    - a stopped generation served HTTP/1.1 (200);
    - a stream sent after GOAWAY reached the router;
    - a late task was left running;
    - a task was counted as gone before it was destroyed;
    - spawning on a shut-down runtime deadlocked.
  - **Over the release fix's test commit:** "the stopped gateway still held its port while it drained".
- **Revert-the-fix checks:** each removes one part of the fix and shows a test failing.
  - Admission:
    - A1, refusal after the stop;
    - A2, refusal after a cancel;
    - A3, connections serving through the check;
    - A4, `Connection: close` on HTTP/1.
  - Task set:
    - C1, tasks running under the cancel;
    - C2, the cancel checked first;
    - C3, destruction before uncounting;
    - C4, a dropped serve loop cancelling.
  - Drain:
    - D1, the graceful phase;
    - D2, connections watching the stop;
    - D3, cancelling what the drain leaves;
    - D4, the drain bound;
    - D5, waiting for the cancelled tasks;
    - D6, HTTP/2 stream tasks in the set;
    - D8, the plain accept rule;
    - D9, a stop cutting the backoff short;
    - D10, releasing the port at once.
- **Commands run (head `7f4fafceae`: the earlier head `b49b1b987b` with master `ece3b744e6` merged in):**
  - `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-gateway` (all targets): 690 passed, 7 skipped (the ignored golden-frame tests).
  - The nineteen drain and admission tests: 19 passed in both CI test sets (the workspace set and the opt-in tools set).
  - Revert-the-fix checks: each of the 17 fails its test with its part reverted.
  - `cargo clippy --no-deps -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test architecture`: 78 passed (earlier head `b49b1b987b`).
  - Comment-hygiene gate: pass (earlier head `b49b1b987b`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Authority staleness fixed at the point of admission.** After a reload, the previous generation's router, configuration and authority admit no new request or HTTP/2 stream. That holds on any connection, kept-alive or HTTP/2, TLS or plain. Work admitted before the stop may finish during the 300 ms drain, and is then cancelled.
- **The refusal reveals nothing.** The 503 is fixed text, with no configuration, authentication or session data.
- **No new network calls, secrets or data handling.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible. No route, configuration or CLI changes; it adds the documented reload-time 503 behavior.
- **What a reload now does to clients:**
  - **A request the admission check refuses during a reload gets a retryable 503.** It carries `Retry-After: 1` and `reason: gateway_restarting`, where it used to get an answer from the stopped generation.
    - Not every request racing a reload gets one. A connection can close before its request is read, and a response still in flight when the drain ends is cut off.
    - **The dashboard has no automatic retry for this 503 yet.** A dashboard request racing a reload can show one error. The next request recovers on a new connection.
    - **Webhook deliveries racing a reload get a retryable 503** instead of a stale-generation answer. Senders that retry 5xx deliver them to the next gateway.
  - **Clients reconnect after a reload.** An idle kept-alive connection is closed cleanly and HTTP clients reconnect on their own. An HTTP/2 client gets GOAWAY and opens a new connection. An in-flight event stream ends and EventSource reconnects.
  - **A request still running when the 300 ms drain ends is cut off,** and its client gets no response. For a mutation, the client then can't tell whether it took effect:
    - a config write still completes, because those run as lifecycle jobs the daemon waits for;
    - an upload whose response was lost may have been written.

## Rollback

- `git revert` the fix commits.
- Symptom if it regresses: requests over a kept-alive TLS connection after a reload are served with the old configuration.

## Follow-ups

- **Upgraded sockets on plain HTTP should close when the gateway stops:**
  - chat during a turn, and the late-subscribe race;
  - ACP;
  - canvas, SOP runs and nodes.
- **Tasks that route handlers spawn themselves** are not owned or joined by the accept loop. Their cancellation depends on the handler. For example, dropping an HTTP chat stream cancels its turn token; retained config lifecycle jobs continue and remain part of the daemon lifecycle drain.
- **`spawn_blocking` work** a request started runs to completion after the stop.
- WebSocket over native TLS (no HTTP/1 upgrades on that path).
- **A test for a TLS handshake that completes across the stop.** Today it is covered by the shared admission check, and the tests cover a handshake that never starts.

prs.title: test(runtime): make the receipt-bound late_tool_search tests opt-in
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The 23 `late_tool_search_*` tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs` read two generated fixture components and a fixture receipt from `ZEROCLAW_LATE_TOOL_SEARCH_*` variables. Only the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` prepares those inputs. Any other `cargo test` or `cargo nextest run` that includes the runtime lib tests with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` therefore reported 23 panics ("explicit fixture receipt required") that said nothing about the code under test.
  - Each of the 23 now carries `#[ignore = "requires ZEROCLAW_LATE_TOOL_SEARCH_FIXTURE_RECEIPT, which the runtime plugin admission step in .github/workflows/ci.yml prepares"]`. An unfiltered run reports them as ignored, with that reason.
  - Someone who opts in without the inputs (`--include-ignored`) still gets a panic, but now it names the missing variable and the step: "ZEROCLAW_LATE_TOOL_SEARCH_FIXTURE_RECEIPT is unset; see the runtime plugin admission step in ci.yml". The three `expect` sites for the four variables go through one helper, `late_ci_input`.
  - The admission step changes in two ways:
    - **Listing:** it now runs `--ignored --list` over its whole selection (`selectors_old` plus the prefix) and requires every listed test to be one of exactly the 23. So the "exactly twenty-three" proof stays, and it gains two guards. A `late_tool_search` test that loses its `#[ignore]` (and would panic in local runs again) fails the step. So does any other ignored test in the selection that `--include-ignored` would otherwise sweep in.
    - **Run:** it opts in with `--include-ignored`, as the same single OR'd invocation in the same order. The exit-code, 23-`ok`, summary, case-receipt inventory and binding checks are unchanged.
  - The six `r5_names_*` tests in the same file use the checked-in `namespace.component`, need no receipt, and are unchanged.
- **The other name filters stay, with a comment.** `ci.yml`'s live-config step (`agent::plugin_live_config`) and the Windows job's runtime config and admission selections are positive scope filters: the default-feature workspace Test job runs the rest of the runtime lib. None of them names `late_tool_search`, and none needs to exclude it now. Each gets a comment saying the filter only scopes the step. The Windows comment avoids the `--ignored` spelling that `hardware_feature_test_lane.test.sh` bans in that job.
- **Docs:** one paragraph in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/tests/fixtures/r5-namespace/README.md`. It says the `late_tool_search_*` tests are ignored by default and that the admission step is the reference for building their inputs and running them.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the tests' bodies, their receipt checks, or what the step proves. No change to which tests the default-feature Test job runs.
- **Blast radius:** test attributes and messages in one test module, plus the listing and run argv of one CI step. Local runs and any harness outside CI that runs these 23 must now pass `--include-ignored`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11806. Related #11221.

### What this does, simply

Running the runtime crate's plugin tests on your own machine used to show 23 failures that were not real: those tests need files that only one CI job builds. Now they are skipped by default, with a note saying where they run, and that CI job still runs all 23 and fails if any is missing or fails.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, it takes one command: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- tools::r5_namespace_tests::`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `6 passed; 0 failed; 23 ignored`, each ignored line with the reason above.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `6 passed; 23 failed`, each panicking with "explicit fixture receipt required".

### How I tested

Run on Linux, on master `5162ca01b4` plus this change (`--locked`, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- …`):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `tools::r5_namespace_tests::` on master | 6 passed, 23 failed, all 23 with "explicit fixture receipt required" |
| the same on this branch | 6 passed, 23 ignored, each with the reason |
| `cargo nextest run … --lib -E 'test(/^tools::r5_namespace_tests::/)'` | 6 run, 6 passed; the 23 skipped |
| `tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search --include-ignored`, no inputs | 23 failed, all 23 with the new message naming the variable |
| the step's selection with `--ignored --list` | exactly the 23 listed |
| the step's selection with `--list` | 64 listed, the 23 among them |
| the step's new listing and run with real inputs (below) | 23 listed; 64 passed, the 23 `late_tool_search` among them; 23 case receipts, all passed and cleaned up |

prs.title: fix(plugins): name the sender in plugin_channel_sender_denied records
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a channel plugin delivers a message from a sender outside the instance's peer group, the host drops it and writes a `plugin_channel_sender_denied` record. The record named the plugin, the channel alias and the ingress, but not the sender, so an operator with a wrong or outdated ID in the peer group could not tell which ID to add (#11821). The built-in Discord channel logs `author_id` in the same situation.
  - The record now carries a `sender` attribute with the sender as the plugin reported it. The value comes from the guest, so it goes through `bounded_webhook_detail` (2,048 characters, UTF-8 safe), the bound the webhook diagnostics in the same file already use. Record attributes are JSON-encoded, so quotes, backslashes and control characters are escaped in every sink.
- **Scope boundary:** The denial is unchanged, and so are the record's other fields, level and message. No config path hint is added (the issue's "ideally" part).
- **Blast radius:** One log record in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/wasm_channel.rs`, emitted from both the poll and webhook ingress paths. Anything that parses these records sees one more attribute. The attribute holds whatever ID the remote service uses for the sender (an account ID, a phone number or an address, depending on the plugin); it goes only to the operator's own logs, as the built-in channels' `author_id` does.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11821.

### What this does, simply

A channel plugin (Discord, for example) only passes messages on from people the operator has allowed. When someone else writes, ZeroClaw ignores the message and logs that it did, but the log never said who wrote. If you had put the wrong account ID in the allow list, you had no way to find the right one from the log. Now the log line includes the sender's ID, so you can copy it into the allow list. Very long IDs are cut short so a misbehaving plugin cannot flood the log.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (a plugin channel instance, `plugin.<alias>`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a bound plugin channel instance with a peer group whose `external_peers` does not include your account.
- **Steps to run:** start the daemon and post in the bound channel from that account.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the `Ignoring channel-plugin inbound from an unauthorized sender` record includes `"sender": "<your account ID>"`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the same record has `plugin`, `channel_alias`, `ingress` and `error_key` only.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `zeroclaw-plugins` lib tests (run with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` in CI) include the new `sender_denial_record_names_the_bounded_sender`, which drives `sender_is_authorized` for a poll and a webhook denial and reads both records back from the log stream.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output** (base `c473221313`, toolchain 1.98.0):

```text
# new test only, record unchanged (fails as expected)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- sender_denial_record_names_the_bounded_sender
    assertion `left == right` failed
      left: Null
     right: "1234567890"
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

# with this change
cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- sender_denial_record_names_the_bounded_sender
    test wasm_channel::tests::sender_denial_record_names_the_bounded_sender ... ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]
cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
    test result: ok. 418 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test channel_plugin_e2e
    test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed
cargo fmt --all -- --check
    one diff, in tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs, which this PR does not touch;
    the same check fails on master at c473221313
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reverting only the attribute makes the new test fail. Both callers of `sender_is_authorized` (poll and webhook ingress) only use its return value, which is unchanged. Did not run a live plugin channel.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`: a structured log attribute; the test above reads it from the record.
