prs.title: fix(plugins): record socket and WebSocket egress denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A refused `wasi:http` request logs a WARN `plugin_egress_denied` record naming the instance, host, reason, and the `zeroclaw config set` command that grants reach. A refused socket or WebSocket connect logged nothing: the guest got its typed error (`access-denied`, `destination-denied`) and the operator saw no trace. A channel plugin whose gateway host is not granted therefore retried silently.
  - The remedy builders and the two recorders move out of `wasi_http.rs` into a crate-private module, `egress_report.rs`, and all three adapters call it at the same points: a malformed request, a store with no egress service, and a refusal from the egress service.
  - Records gain a `transport` attribute (`http`, `socket`, `websocket`). `error_key` values (`plugin_egress_denied`, `plugin_egress_connection_limit`) and messages are unchanged, so existing log searches keep working.
  - The requested host and the reason are guest-controlled: the sockets `connect-request.host` and both transports' TLS profile names are unbounded WIT strings, and the reason for a malformed one quotes it `Debug`-escaped (up to 6x its size). Both are escaped and bounded while they are formatted, through a sink that stops the formatter at the budget (host 253 characters, reason 2,048). A guest-sized value is never rendered in full on the host, and control, bidirectional, and zero-width characters in a raw host reach the log escaped.
- **Scope boundary:** Guest-visible errors, the policy decision and its order, WIT, config, and dependencies are unchanged. Only refusals at the egress boundary are recorded. Not recorded, matching `wasi:http` today: timeouts, URL-shape errors, TLS setup failures after authorization (for example a missing profile secret), and dial or handshake failures; recording TLS setup failures under their own key is a follow-up. No deduplication or rate limit: every refused attempt is logged, as `wasi:http` already does, and suppressing repeats per instance and host is a follow-up, tracked in #11626.
- **Blast radius:** The refusal-recording feature lives in `zeroclaw-plugins`. The receiving branch also contains the current public parent’s TLS/config bridge, CI and documentation changes. Log consumers see new WARN records for socket and WebSocket refusals and a new `transport` key on all three. HTTP records' `_file`/`_line` move to the new module. Most of the diff is a move; `git diff --color-moved` shows it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10999 and #7432. Depends on #11228 for the reviewed TLS/authorization parent and required transport selectors. Its source is normally integrated here; its current Core review and actual landing remain separate prerequisites.

### What this does, simply

When a plugin tries to reach a host the operator has not allowed, the plugin only sees an error. For web requests, ZeroClaw also writes a log line that says which plugin was blocked, which host, and the exact command that allows it. Plugins that use raw sockets or WebSockets (IRC, Nostr, Discord) got no such line, so a misconfigured one just kept failing quietly. This PR makes all three kinds of connection write the same log line.

## Testing (required)

### Current public-parent integration

Signed 95dcb66ec318e0dbd0f53dffb0d07d8bed8efab9 normally merges original da06c4f12867464617eb680660138cab9474c494 with current public #11228 ef94475cd46ac6abfc1f8441657ab5eaca614270. Its reviewed tree is dcc53a088451ea55ac9ba839cd7ea55f4ff61f94. Git combined the two documentation additions automatically; no conflicts or manual source edits occurred. Ten whole child-owned source/test blobs, both refusal-record paragraphs and all 35 selected test bodies are unchanged. All 2,166 outside child objects are preserved. Incoming source is the already-reviewed public parent, including actual merged-master content; this creates no new Core exception or authority.

Cargo.lock and both optional probe manifests equal the genuine public parent/master resolver output: 1,293 packages, probe-rs 0.32 and quinn-proto 0.11.19, without ruzstd or espflash. #11715 has landed as b6bad4d41e3db803721fb9c274ce412e25a2a456. The incoming parent carries its exact content; that squash commit is not another merge parent.

[Current Quality Gate 38490446189](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38490446189) attempt 1 is SUCCESS on this receiving head: 41 successful jobs, three conditional skips, no failures or pending jobs. [Required Gate 115616946517](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38490446189/job/115616946517) passes all 35 dependencies (32 successes / three allowed skips). Security, locked compilation, Rust 1.96, generators and Format/Lint/Docs pass.

All 35 named current reporter/socket/WebSocket/witness/coherence controls pass, including both real operator-denial cases. All 24 TLS/private-secret lane observations also pass; the overlapping vectors contain 45 actual result rows for 44 unique methods. Current workspace Nextest passes 19,513 with 39 skips. All three 16-thread parallel repetitions pass: Runtime 5,698/eight ignored and Channels 1,971/two ignored each. Historical da06/ef results are not substituted for this receiving execution; the earlier Telegram wait's cause remains unknown.

Actual CI source 7e3c47025868ba51205c06b2d5ccaebe8b5b6642 combines public master 996355b83c403e8e9b8080dff5f9b75cea188459 with this head. Its complete tree differs in three legitimate master SOP/main imports; all 19 inspected source/manifest/lock/CI/fixture blobs match this head exactly. Forced RNG/serialization/guard controls, non-Linux transport runtime, full archive/platform and live Discord-package acceptance are not claimed.

Current owner/Core re-review, the original draft state, #11228’s actual landing, rate-limit follow-up #11626, platform/live Discord-package and release acceptance remain separate.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the new behavior is asserted end to end by the tests below.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the plugin component and lib steps of `Check (plugins cranelift backend)`. `egress_plugin_e2e` (already in CI) asserts the HTTP record through the shared recorder.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The older da06 official run already executed the selected socket/WebSocket denial suites. Fresh receiving-source results are pending; historical contributor runs below are not new-head evidence.
- **Historical contributor commands and tail output:** The following macOS 26/aarch64, Rust 1.98 report predates this receiving integration. It is retained as author-reported history, with no new execution credit.

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                                  # clean
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings   # clean
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings                     # clean (module absent)
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasmtime   # clean
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-pulley   # clean
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
test result: ok. 274 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift
channel_plugin_e2e 14, egress_plugin_e2e 10, reference_plugin 9, reference_plugin_e2e 1 (+3 filtered),
sequential_egress_e2e 4, socket_plugin_e2e 7, tool_plugin_e2e 2, tool_plugin_timeout_e2e 5,
websocket_plugin_e2e 5: all ok
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ DOCS_FILES=<the two changed docs> bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. ... Summary: 0 error(s)
$ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical contributor-reported mutation checks: each change below was made alone, its target test run, and the file restored. Every one failed its test.

| Injected change | Test that caught it |
|---|---|
| WebSocket: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_websocket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| WebSocket: store with no egress service not recorded | `a_refused_websocket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| Sockets: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_socket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| Sockets: store with no egress service not recorded | `a_refused_socket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| `wasi:http`: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_request_is_recorded_under_the_http_transport` |
| Guest host recorded unbounded | `guest_supplied_text_is_bounded_in_the_record` |
| WebSocket reported under the socket family | `every_transport_is_recorded_under_its_adapter_family` |
| The reason rendered in full before it is kept | `guest_supplied_text_is_bounded_in_the_record` |
| The raw host recorded unescaped | `a_recorded_host_is_escaped` |

  `bounded_formatting_stops_at_the_budget` pins the property the "reason rendered in full" row relies on: a `Display` that would write forever is stopped at the budget, so the cost of a refusal record does not grow with the guest's input.

  Not verified: Linux and Windows locally.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation or interactive interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical da06 official controls in the linked run; current 95dcb66ec318e0dbd0f53dffb0d07d8bed8efab9 source/tree reviewed, current named and gate execution qualified in QG38490446189.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The current run supplies actual named socket/WebSocket operator-denial assertions and reporter records; no predecessor execution is substituted.

Full `cargo test --workspace` was not run: the change is confined to `zeroclaw-plugins`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

They are bounded per record, JSON-encoded, and limited per call by the frame's host-call budget; the writer drops rather than blocks when its queue is full. `remedy` shows the instance's grant lists, which `wasi:http` records already print and which are plaintext in config by design.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(security): read POSIX commands in bash's grammar when bash runs them
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11822 refuses POSIX forms that bash and dash read differently: `<<$'EOF'` delimiters, `<<` inside `((...))`, and a backslash-continued line that joins into a heredoc terminator. That is required when the policy cannot tell which shell runs the command. But the native runtime defaults to the login shell, usually bash on Linux, so it also refused valid bash commands under bash.
  - `SecurityPolicy::for_agent` now records the native shell the runtime factory chooses (`[runtime].shell` or the detected default), or none for other runtimes and Android. Each POSIX check resolves that value the way the runtime does. It reads the command in bash's grammar only when the canonical executable is `bash` **and** the program that will run is bound to be that binary:
    - the configured name is itself `bash`, which also holds inside a container sandbox's image and on another `PATH`; or
    - it is an absolute path (such as `/bin/sh` linked to bash) and the risk profile's sandbox cannot be a container (`auto` may select Docker).
  - Under bash grammar:
    - `$'...'` heredoc delimiters are expanded bytewise, and terminator lines are compared as bytes.
    - A bare `((...))` is arithmetic when its second `(` closes with `)` right after it, the same test #11822 uses for `$((`.
    - A joined continuation line that spells the terminator ends the body, as bash does.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - **Unchanged crates:** no changes to `zeroclaw-runtime` or `zeroclaw-api`. The shell, skill, and cron tools pass the runtime dialect exactly as before, and the policy derives the shell itself. An earlier revision added a `Sandbox` method and tool wiring in the runtime holding crate; that was reverted, because that crate needs a recorded Core Team exception for new functionality.
  - **Other shells:** no dash-, zsh-, or BusyBox-specific grammar. Every other shell keeps #11822's portable rules.
  - **Still refused under bash:** the quoted `"$(cat <<EOF … EOF)"` terminator (bash 4.4, 5.0, and 5.1 each read it differently), and the `\c`, `\u`, and `\U` delimiter escapes (their meaning changed between bash 3.2 and 4.x).
- **Blast radius:** POSIX command validation for policies built by `SecurityPolicy::for_agent` (agent loop, channels, gateway). `SecurityPolicy` gains a public `native_shell: Option<String>` field (`None` by default, so struct literals using `..Default::default()` are unaffected). `schema::parse_sandbox_backend` becomes `pub(crate)` so the policy interprets the profile's backend exactly as sandbox selection does. Workspace `cargo check --all-targets` is clean.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11822. Related #11823.

This is an ordinary PR rather than an RFC under `docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md`. It refines the grammar the existing command checks use, without adding a security layer, changing the security model, or moving ownership across crates.

Until #11822 merges, this PR's diff also shows its commits. The changes here are cd60a7e283 (bash grammar), 5e4c1681e7 (move the decision into the policy), and the bash handling of joined terminators in c0fd095d5e.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw checks every shell command before running it, and to do that it has to know where each command starts and ends. A few shell constructs mean different things in bash and in dash (the usual `/bin/sh` on Debian and Ubuntu). For example, `cat <<$'EOF'` ends at a line `EOF` in bash but at a line `$EOF` in dash. The commands after that line run in one shell while the other treats them as text. #11822 refuses those constructs because it cannot tell which shell will run them. This PR lets the policy work that out from the configured shell. When that shell is definitely bash, the checks read the command exactly as bash does, so valid bash commands are no longer refused. Anything else keeps the safe refusal: dash, zsh, BusyBox, the Docker runtime, or a shell a container sandbox might replace.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `cli` (agent shell tool).
- **Setup / preconditions:** Native runtime, `[runtime] shell = "bash"` (or unset on a host whose login shell is bash), and `allowed_commands = ["*"]`.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to run a three-line command: `cat <<$'EOF'`, then `hello`, then `EOF`. Then set `[runtime] shell` to a dash path, or switch to the Docker runtime, and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Under bash the command runs and prints `hello`. Under dash or Docker it is refused, as on #11822.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** #11822 is not on master yet. On #11822 the command is refused under every shell.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust lint and test jobs for `zeroclaw-config`. The identification tests resolve the host's real bash, and run the spoof case against another installed shell.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI runs one bash version. The cross-version behavior below was checked locally in containers.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (Rust 1.98.0, the CI toolchain)
  ```
  cargo +1.98 fmt --all -- --check                  # clean
  cargo +1.98 check --workspace --all-targets       # clean
  cargo +1.98 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
  cargo +1.98 test -p zeroclaw-config --lib         # test result: ok. 1834 passed; 0 failed
  cargo +1.98 test -p zeroclaw-config --test powershell_policy_probe   # test result: ok. 9 passed
  cargo +1.98 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib        # test result: ok. 5817 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored
  cargo +1.98 test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- --test-threads=1        # test result: ok. 1361 passed; 0 failed
  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                   # Summary: 0 error(s)
  scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh                     # No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Bash rules across versions:** every modeled form was run in the official `bash:3.2`, `4.4`, `5.0`, `5.1`, `5.2`, and `5.3` images, in normal and `--posix` mode. That covers 16 `$'...'` delimiters (hex, octal, `\0` truncation with a suffix, `\0` with an escaped quote, byte sequences, unknown escapes), the bare `((...))` arithmetic, shift, and subshell-fallback cases, and the backslash-continuation terminators. All 12 configurations matched the model. The same harness reports 19 mismatches under dash 0.5.12, so it does tell the shells apart.
  - **Refused escapes:** chosen from a full escape table diffed across those bash versions.
  - **Identification:** the tests confirm that a `sh` symlink to bash gets the bash grammar when given as an absolute path with no container sandbox possible. They also confirm that a bare `sh`, a container-capable profile, a missing binary, and a `bash` symlink to another shell all keep the portable grammar.
  - **Not verified:** zsh, ksh, or BusyBox grammars (deliberately left on the portable rules).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`, no user-visible interface state changed beyond which commands are accepted.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** c0fd095d5e, policy and the shell checks via `cargo test`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the bash matrix above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run full `cargo test` for the whole workspace. I ran the test suites of the crates that consume the policy.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`. The policy resolves and canonicalizes the configured shell path, which the runtime already does before spawning.
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The relevant risk is policy precision: a misidentified shell would apply bash's grammar to another shell. Identification is closed by default. It needs a canonical executable named exactly `bash`, and either a configured name of `bash` or an absolute path with no possible container sandbox. Everything else keeps #11822's refusals. Remaining edge: under a bare `bash`, a TUI-forwarded `PATH` could resolve a different file named `bash` than the ambient `PATH` the policy checks. That's an operator-controlled environment, and the file is still named `bash`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. The public `*_for_shell` signatures are unchanged. `SecurityPolicy` gains one defaulted field.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Behavioral note: under bash, `<<$'...'` heredocs, `((...))` arithmetic commands, and joined continuation terminators that #11822 refuses are accepted again. Under bash, `((cmd))` is arithmetic (bash runs nothing), so it is no longer scanned as a command.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert cd60a7e283 and 5e4c1681e7. Policy falls back to #11822's portable grammar everywhere.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Pointing `[runtime].shell` at a non-bash shell, or using the Docker runtime, already gives the portable grammar.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - (a) Under a bash runtime, a valid bash `$'...'` heredoc, `((...))`, or continuation terminator is refused with `unreadable heredoc delimiter` or `not allowed by security policy`. That's misidentification toward Unknown, a usability regression only.
  - (b) A command that #11822 refuses is accepted under a non-bash shell. That's misidentification toward bash; check `[runtime].shell`, its canonical target, and the profile's sandbox backend.

prs.title: fix(security): split POSIX commands at substitution and subshell boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The shell command scanner split segments only at `;`, newlines, `|`, `||`, and `&&`, and split words only at whitespace. The closing `)` of `$(...)`, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, or a subshell, and the closing backtick of `` `...` ``, stayed glued to the last inner word. `x=$(cmd 2>/dev/null)` therefore produced the redirect target `/dev/null)`. That is not the null device, so with the default forbidden `/dev` the shell tool refused it: `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)`. #11469's exact null-device matching is correct and unchanged; the bad token came from the tokenizer.
  - Under the POSIX dialect, `split_unquoted_segments` now treats command substitution, process substitution, backticks, and subshells as segment boundaries, tracked on a frame stack so nesting and substitution inside double quotes work. The inner command becomes its own segment, and the enclosing word keeps a `$()`-style placeholder.
  - Every character outside heredoc bodies lands in a segment, but that alone does not guarantee the checks see it: if the splitter closes a substitution where the shell does not, it restores the enclosing quote, and commands the shell runs end up inside one quoted argument the checks never look into. The splitter therefore follows the shell where a `)` or backtick is ambiguous: `case` counts after `;`, a lone `&`, `coproc`, `time -p`, and reserved words, an empty `case x in esac` closes, `case` inside arithmetic does not count, and a backtick substitution closes at the next unescaped backtick even inside a comment, quote, heredoc body, or inner `$(` (bash does this; dash does it too or rejects the whole script). As a backstop, when the model ends unbalanced (a frame, quote, `case`, or `${` still open, or a `)` closing nothing), the flat split that ignores substitutions is checked as well. That only adds segments, so it refuses nothing the flat split accepts. It is not a proof: input crafted to rebalance a misparse is only as safe as the specific rules.
  - `$'...'` heredoc delimiters are refused as unproven, like `$"..."`. Dash (the usual `sh`) has no `$'...'` and ends `<<$'EOF'` at a literal `$EOF` line, running commands a bash reading treats as body; bash's expansion is bytewise (NUL truncation, `\xc3`). Either model hides commands from the other shell. Heredocs whose boundary differs between shells, or that no split can bound, are refused the same way: `<<` inside a bare `((` (a shift to bash, a heredoc to dash), and a body that runs to the end inside an open substitution (bash ends it at `EOF)` and runs the rest).
  - `$((...))` text is kept out of the segments only once confirmed: the second `(` closes with `)` right after it, which bash reads as arithmetic and dash always does. Until then it is held, and it becomes segments if bash would read a command substitution instead (`$((cd a && make) 2>&1)`). Substitutions inside the expression are always scanned. A bare `((` is always scanned, because dash runs `((cmd))` as nested subshells. `echo "$(( total / count ))"` and `echo $((10 / 2))` pass.
  - `<<` inside `$((...))` is a shift, not a heredoc. Previously `echo $((8<<1))` opened a heredoc that hid the following lines from the scan, though bash runs them. A command substitution nested inside arithmetic is ordinary shell syntax again, so its heredocs are recognized.
  - A substitution closes only at the `)` bash treats as its closer. A `case` pattern terminator, a `)` inside `${...}`, or a `)` inside a `#` comment no longer ends `$(...)` early. Closing early would restore the enclosing quote state and hide the rest of the inner command inside one quoted argument. Comment text is not syntax until the newline, so an apostrophe in a comment no longer opens a quote that hides the next line (separators inside comments still split, conservatively). This addresses review feedback in 4935b7a82.
  - The strict allowlist keeps rejecting unquoted POSIX grouping parentheses, so `(git status)` is not newly accepted as `git status` as a side effect of the split. Escaped and quoted parentheses (`find . \( ... \)`, `grep -E '(a|b)'`) are still allowed.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change null-device classification (`is_null_device`, `is_safe_device_redirect_target`), the safe-redirect regexes, forbidden-path defaults, allowlists, or sandbox grants. `cmd.exe` and PowerShell splitting are unchanged. Not addressed here: `$(...)` inside an unquoted-delimiter heredoc body (bash runs it; the scanner still skips heredoc bodies by design), and `cmd.exe` parenthesized blocks.
- **Blast radius:** Every consumer of `split_unquoted_segments` under the POSIX dialect: the workspace path scan (`forbidden_path_argument*`) used by the shell, skill shell, and cron paths; `command_risk_level`; `is_command_allowed`; and `is_command_explicitly_allowed`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11469. Related #11823, Related #11824 (follow-ups for the scope this PR leaves out), Related #11825 (`zeroclaw-tools` test flake seen while validating).

### What this does, simply

Before running a shell command, ZeroClaw splits it into the individual commands it contains and checks each file path it mentions. That splitter didn't understand `$(...)`, backticks, or `(...)`, which are how shells run one command inside another. So in `x=$(ls 2>/dev/null)` it read the redirect target as `/dev/null)`, including the closing paren, and refused it as a forbidden path, even though #11469 made `/dev/null` always allowed. This was easy to hit, because `$(something 2>/dev/null)` is a very common shell idiom.

This PR teaches the splitter where those inner commands start and end. The inner command is checked on its own, so `2>/dev/null` inside it works again. As a side effect, commands hidden inside `$(...)` are now actually checked: a forbidden path inside `"$(...)"` is blocked, and `x=$(rm -rf ./build)` is rated high risk instead of low. Commands that the strict allowlist rejected before are still rejected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the `shell` tool, through any surface (`cli`, `tui`, or `web`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Unix host, default `forbidden_paths` (includes `/dev`), `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to run each of these with the shell tool: `x=$(echo a 2>/dev/null); echo "$x"`, then `(echo a 2>/dev/null)`, then ``echo "`echo a 2>/dev/null`"``
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Each command runs and prints `a`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Each is refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)` (or ``/dev/null` `` for the backtick form).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Required Gate (format, lint, Linux workspace tests, MSRV, Windows/macOS compile checks). The change is in `zeroclaw-config` policy parsing, plus one runtime shell-tool test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None specific. The behavior change is gated to `ShellDialect::Posix`, and a new test pins `cmd.exe` splitting as unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `4935b7a82` (base `cdefa0d0a`), with the CI toolchain `1.98.0`:

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
FMT_OK

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 22s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 1799 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

# New end-to-end test against master's policy.rs (fix removed):
test tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED
x=$(echo zc-subst 2>/dev/null); echo "$x" must run, got: ToolResult { success: false, ..., error: Some("Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)") }

# New policy tests against the unmodified tokenizer:
posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries ... FAILED   left: ["x=$(echo a)"]
command_risk_level_sees_commands_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Low  right: High
forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/null)")
forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/nullx)")  right: Some("/dev/nullx")
```

- **Tests added or changed:**
  - `posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries`: segment output for `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, subshells, `<(...)`/`>(...)`, nesting, `$((...))`, unterminated and unbalanced input, quoted and escaped literals, and quotes inside a substitution.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions`: 18 forms with `/dev/null` redirects inside substitutions, subshells, backticks, and process substitution, all allowed.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions`: lookalikes (`/dev/nullx`, `/dev/null/../../etc/passwd`) and forbidden paths inside substitutions stay blocked and are reported without the closing `)`. This includes the double-quoted form, `case` bodies (quoted, unquoted, `(x)` patterns, after `then`, with a subshell in the body), `)` inside `${...}` and inside comments, a nested substitution in `${x:-...}`, a stray `)`, and the arithmetic-heredoc case.
  - `posix_substitution_closers_follow_the_shell`: the review's `&`/`coproc`/`time -p` `case`, arithmetic `case`, backtick comment/quote/subshell closers, empty `case x in esac`, backtick heredoc, and dash `((cmd))` cases stay path-blocked and High; balanced forms such as `case x in esac` are still accepted. Each command was run under bash 5.2 and dash 0.5.12 with a harmless marker to confirm the shell runs the trailing command.
  - `posix_confirmed_arithmetic_is_not_a_command`: confirmed `$((...))` division passes and is Low; substitutions inside it, `$((cmd) )`/`$((true)|cmd)` command substitutions, and bare `((cmd))` stay path-blocked.
  - `ambiguous_heredoc_boundaries_are_refused`: the `EOF)` body inside `$(`, and `<<` inside a bare `((`, are refused, rated High, and rejected under the wildcard opt-out; a heredoc in a spaced `( (...) )` is still modeled.
  - `ansi_c_heredoc_delimiters_are_refused`: `$'...'` delimiters, including the dash `$EOF` terminator and bash NUL/byte-escape forms, are refused by the path check, rated High, and rejected under the wildcard opt-out.
  - `command_risk_level_sees_commands_inside_posix_substitutions`: `rm -rf` inside `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, subshells, and `<(...)` is High; `x=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)` stays Low.
  - `strict_allowlist_still_rejects_posix_grouping_and_substitution`: the default strict policy still rejects `(git status)` and similar, and still allows escaped and quoted parentheses. Passes on both `master` and this branch.
  - `windows_cmd_does_not_split_posix_substitution_syntax`: `cmd.exe` splitting is unchanged.
  - `tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions`: the reported scenario end to end through `RateLimitedTool<ShellTool>` with the default forbidden `/dev`. A forbidden path inside `$(...)` is still refused and named without the `)`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reproduced the original refusal in a live session on a binary that includes #11469. Checked the test fixtures against real `bash` (and `sh`, which is bash on the test host): a quote inside `"$(...)"`; a backtick inside double quotes running a command; `\$\(a\)` being literal while `\$(a\)` is a syntax error; `case` bodies running; and the line after `$((8<<1))` running, not being swallowed as a heredoc. Not verified: Windows execution (`cmd.exe` behavior is unchanged by construction and pinned by a unit test), and dash as `/bin/sh` (no POSIX-only constructs that dash treats differently are interpreted beyond what the tests cover).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed beyond the tool result shown above.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4935b7a82`, `shell` tool via unit test `tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the command output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `x=$(echo zc-subst 2>/dev/null); echo "$x"` returns success with output `zc-subst`. On `master` it is refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - Workspace-wide `cargo test` was not run. The diff is confined to `zeroclaw-config` and one `zeroclaw-runtime` test, and the only other crate calling these policy APIs is `zeroclaw-tools`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` passed (2092 passed with `--test-threads=1`) on the pre-rebase base `329e66f76`, not re-run after the rebase. In parallel it fails intermittently, in a different test on each run (`coding_agent_budget_tests::coding_agent_wrappers_charge_one_action_each`, `browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_fails_closed_on_malformed_screenshot_response`), because a `codex_cli.rs` test sets the process-wide `PATH` to an empty directory. That is unrelated to this change.
  - Clippy on a newer local toolchain (`1.99.0`) reports `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` and `fetch_update` deprecations in untouched files (`zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/upload.rs`, `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`). These are left to a separate PR; the CI toolchain `1.98.0` is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`Yes`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - **Widened:** the workspace path scan now accepts the existing safe-device redirect targets (exact `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, `/dev/zero`) when they appear inside a substitution or subshell. Before, those targets were refused only because a trailing `)` or backtick made them unrecognizable. No new device, path, or command is allowed, and lookalikes stay blocked (tested).
  - **Tightened:** commands inside `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, and subshells are now scanned and risk-classified as their own commands. A forbidden path inside a double-quoted substitution, previously unscanned, is blocked. A high-risk command inside a substitution now makes the whole command High, so under Supervised autonomy it requires approval. Medium-risk inner commands count too: `echo "Branch: $(git branch --show-current)"` is now Medium (`git branch` is classified as a write), so the default Supervised policy asks before running it.
  - **Strict allowlist:** unchanged. A new guard keeps rejecting unquoted POSIX `(`/`)`, so the split does not turn `(git status)` into an accepted `git status`. `$(`, `<(`, `>(`, and backticks were already rejected in strict mode.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Behavioral note: with `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`, and Supervised autonomy, a command that hides a high-risk command inside a substitution now asks for approval, and one that hides a medium-risk command (for example `echo "Branch: $(git branch --show-current)"`) is now Medium and asks under the default Supervised policy. Heredocs with a `$'...'` delimiter, a `<<` inside a bare `((`, and a heredoc body inside `$(...)` that never reaches its terminator are now refused (`unreadable heredoc delimiter`), because the shells disagree on or neither split can prove where the body ends.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. There is no config, data, or migration state to unwind.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None

The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. prs.title: ci(plugins): raise the cranelift runtime leg timeout to 30 minutes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - `check-plugin-backends` reads its timeout from the matrix, with a 20-minute fallback.
  - The `plugins cranelift runtime` leg gets 30 minutes. Its six serial test steps now take 18-20 minutes on ordinary runs, and it has been cancelled at the shared 20-minute limit, including in the merge queue.
- **Scope boundary:** No step, command, cache key, runner or required-gate change. The other four legs keep 20 minutes.
- **Blast radius:** CI only. A slow runtime leg now runs up to 30 minutes instead of being cancelled at 20.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10558. Related #10868, which split this leg out.

### What this does, simply

One required CI leg runs the plugin runtime tests and the root CLI plugin tests one after another. Those suites have grown, and the leg now often finishes just under its 20-minute limit or gets cancelled at it. A cancellation fails the required gate and drops a PR from the merge queue even when no test failed. This gives that one leg 30 minutes and leaves every other leg at 20.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the change is a workflow timeout, and this PR's own run exercises it.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** A `ci.yml` change makes `plugin_backend_change_filter.sh` select this job, so this PR's `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` runs under the new limit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Only a run longer than 20 minutes shows the higher limit taking effect; a shorter run shows only that the expression resolves.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
actionlint 1.7.12 + ShellCheck 0.10.0, .github/actionlint.yaml labels, on .github/workflows/ci.yml
  master:    exit 0, 0 findings
  this head: exit 0, 0 findings
  mutant (runtime leg timeout-minutes: thirty): exit 1

PyYAML comparison against master
  changed jobs: ['check-plugin-backends']
  steps and every matrix field except timeout-minutes identical
  per-leg timeout-minutes: runtime 30, others unset (fallback 20)

bash scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh
  windows test scope contract tests: pass
bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh
  plugin backend change filter tests: pass
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The duration history of this leg across master, merge-group and PR runs. Since 2026-10-20 its successful runs have p50 11.9, p90 18.5 and max 19.8 minutes (n=118). Nine runs were cancelled at 20 minutes: merge groups 39628892317, 39629027855 and 39638319027, master push 39669353771 attempt 1, and PR runs 39496300978, 39631677383, 39632217852, 39673663847 and 39687270391. The cranelift backend leg's one timeout in that window (39635156913) spent 10.8 minutes in checkout, so that leg keeps 20. An explicit per-leg version without a fallback was rejected because actionlint does not flag a leg that omits the field.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Commit `460bc56d3bb1911f9b6ad3623d8bc743818009bd`; workflow-only, no product interface.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The runtime leg's limit resolves to 30; the other legs resolve to 20.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No Rust build or test; the change touches only workflow timeout fields.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>` restores the shared 20-minute limit.

prs.title: ci(docker): bound arm64 build memory and add a dry-run dispatch to docker-publish
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Bounded arm64 memory.** Legs that build `linux/arm64` get the same 8 GiB of swap that the release workflow gives its Linux ARM64 build (`dist_runner_memory.sh prepare`, then `cleanup` under `always()`), and run Buildx with `max-parallelism = 1`, so the amd64 and arm64 release links never overlap. The arm64 build of the `dist` image runs out of memory in its final link. The same Dockerfile leg in `docker-image-pr.yml` was killed with `ResourceExhausted` on #11347's approved head ([run 39040526108](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39040526108)). The `publish` timeout goes from 60 to 120 minutes for the serial build, and because the `all-features` leg alone takes 41 to 64 minutes in `docker-image-pr.yml`.
  - **A manual dispatch is a dry run unless asked.** Dispatch gains four inputs: `release_ref`, `stems`, `push` and `floating`. On a dispatch, `push` and `floating` default to false. On `workflow_call` they default to true, so Release Stable keeps publishing and moving the floating tags. The variant's floating tag (`<stem>`) and the relay's `latest` move only on a tag push, on the release call, or on a dispatch with `floating` set, so rebuilding an older release can't move them back to it.
  - **Dry runs and publishes never share a queue.** Each dry run gets its own concurrency group (`docker-publish-dry-run-<run_id>`), so it can't queue behind a publish or cancel a pending one. Publishes are keyed on the release (`docker-publish-<release_ref or ref name>`), so the tag push and the release call for one release stay serialized.
  - **The memory helper comes from the workflow's own revision.** Arm64 legs fetch `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh` at `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA` into `RUNNER_TEMP`, so a `release_ref` that predates the helper (v0.8.5 and older) still builds. The image source stays exactly `release_ref`, because nothing is added to the build context.
  - **Unknown stems fail before building.** `stems=dist,all-feature` used to build only `dist` and pass. Now any unknown stem fails the `matrix` job, and the error lists every unknown name, escaped onto one line.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the Dockerfiles, Rust profiles, LTO or codegen settings (#11741 proposes per-variant LTO), runner classes, the tag matrix in `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, the release workflow, or `docker-image-pr.yml` (its default `Dockerfile` arm64 leg gets the same bounded-memory steps in #11925). Checking that `release_ref` is a real release tag before publishing is #11943. The maintainer CI docs (`docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md`) are not updated here.
- **Blast radius:** Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job, which calls this workflow at the release tag, and the tag-push trigger. Both resolve the same tags as before, and both still push, sign and scan. Their concurrency group is now named after the release instead of the caller's ref. Manual dispatches change behavior: they push only when `push` is set, and they move floating tags only when `floating` is also set.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11828. Depends on #11347 (merged; adds `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh`). Related #11741, #11943, #11925.

### What this does, simply

When a stable release is published, the release workflow calls `docker-publish.yml` to build four container image variants from source. The `dist` variant is built for both amd64 and arm64 on one hosted runner. With the v0.8.6 feature set, the arm64 build needs more memory than the runner has, and it is killed near the end. That left v0.8.6 without a `dist` image.

This change gives those builds the same extra swap the release workflow already uses for its own ARM64 build. It makes BuildKit run one step at a time, so the two links never overlap, and it doubles the time limit to cover the slower serial build.

It also makes a manual run safe to use as a rehearsal or a targeted rebuild:

- A manual run builds without publishing unless someone sets `push`. It can be limited to named variants, and a misspelled variant name stops the run instead of being skipped.
- Publishing an older release, such as v0.8.6 after v0.8.7 ships, updates only that release's own tags. The shared "current" tags like `dist` and the relay's `latest` stay on the newest release unless the person running it also sets `floating`.
- A rehearsal can no longer hold up or cancel a release that is waiting to publish.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A maintainer with write access runs the dry run below. The branch must be in this repository, because the build job only runs in `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None of the product surfaces. GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` of `docker-publish.yml` only.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Before dispatching, record the GHCR state the run could touch: the package version lists of `zeroclaw` and `zeroclaw-zerorelay`, and the digests of `dist`, `dist-v0.8.6`, `all-features` and `all-features-v0.8.6`.
- **Steps to run:** `gh workflow run docker-publish.yml --ref ci/docker-publish-arm64-memory -f stems=dist,all-features -f push=false -f floating=false`. Leaving `push` and `floating` unset gives the same result.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - The `matrix` job resolves only `dist` and `all-features`.
  - The `dist` leg fetches the helper, passes the 16 GiB free-disk check, turns on 8 GiB of swap, builds both platforms without SIGKILL, and releases the swap file.
  - Both legs finish within 120 minutes.
  - The build log tags only `dist-v0.8.6` and `all-features-v0.8.6`, and nothing is pushed.
  - "Sign container image", `publish-relay`, `scan`, `scan-relay` and both SARIF uploads are skipped.
  - The GHCR version lists and tag digests are unchanged afterwards.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Don't dispatch `master`'s version to compare. There, every dispatch pushes and signs all four variants and the relay, and moves every floating tag. On `master`, the comparable evidence is the `docker-image-pr.yml` arm64 Dockerfile leg, which is killed on `ubuntu-latest` (run 39040526108).

### How I tested

The workflow has **not run in GitHub Actions yet**. The checks below ran on Linux x86_64 at 517acede09 (master ece3b744e6 merged in). The dry run above is the first Actions check.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None run this workflow. The architecture tests in `tests/architecture/container_release.rs` and `xtask/src/generate/docker_tags.rs` assert strings in this file, and I ran both suites (below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The memory change only proves itself in Actions; that is the dry run above. Pushing, signing and the floating-tag move are exercised only by a real release, or by a dispatch with `push` (and `floating`) set.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  # actionlint 1.7.7 + shellcheck 0.10.0, docker-publish.yml linted together with its caller release-stable-manual.yml
  docker-publish.yml findings: 0 at 517acede09, 0 at 3380b9c99a, 0 at master ece3b744e6
  (release-stable-manual.yml findings are unchanged by this PR and identical on all three)

  # cargo test --test architecture
  test container_release::manual_stable_release_calls_container_matrix_at_release_tag ... ok
  test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  # cargo test -p xtask docker_tags
  test generate::docker_tags::tests::publish_relay_pins_release_ref_for_provenance ... ok
  test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 234 filtered out

  # matrix step run as written (yq output replaced by the same .tags JSON), before -> after
  stems='dist'                        exit 0 dist                 -> exit 0 dist
  stems='dist,all-features'           exit 0 both                 -> exit 0 both
  stems='dist,all-feature'            exit 0 dist only            -> exit 1 No docker-tags.toml stem named "all-feature"
  stems=','                           exit 1 (echoes input)       -> exit 1 stems lists no stem name
  stems='dist,'                       exit 0 dist                 -> exit 0 dist
  stems=$'dist\n::warning::x'         exit 1, 2 command lines     -> exit 1, 1 line (JSON-escaped)
  stems='100%,dist'                   exit 0 dist only            -> exit 1 ... named "100%25"

  # every changed condition evaluated from the file text (push / tags pushed / concurrency group)
  tag push v0.8.7                     push  <stem>-v0.8.7 <stem>; relay :v0.8.7 :latest   docker-publish-v0.8.7
  Release Stable call v0.8.7          push  <stem>-v0.8.7 <stem>; relay :v0.8.7 :latest   docker-publish-v0.8.7
  dispatch release_ref=v0.8.6         none (dry run)                                      docker-publish-dry-run-<run_id>
  dispatch v0.8.6 dist push           push  dist-v0.8.6                                   docker-publish-v0.8.6
  dispatch v0.8.7 dist push floating  push  dist-v0.8.7 dist                              docker-publish-v0.8.7
  (before: the tag lists of the first two rows were identical; the fourth also pushed dist;
   every master dispatch shared docker-publish-refs/heads/master with the release call)

  # helper fetch step run as written against GitHub, in a shallow v0.8.5 checkout (no helper at v0.8.5)
  * branch 3380b9c99a7fe15b7c53c8e43631c05035ac9d62 -> FETCH_HEAD
  RUNNER_TEMP/dist_runner_memory.sh sha256 f88032f7...e181 (= the helper in this branch)
  HEAD unchanged; 0 files added to the workspace
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job passes only `release_ref`, so `push` and `floating` take their `workflow_call` defaults of true.
  - An empty `tags:` line adds no tag. build-push-action v6.18.0 reads `tags` with `Util.getInputList` from @docker/actions-toolkit 0.61.0, which skips empty lines and filters empty items.
  - `actions/checkout` v6.0.2 refuses a `path` outside the workspace, and both `Dockerfile` and `Containerfile` `COPY . .`, so a second checkout would have entered the image build context. `git fetch` writes only under `.git`, which `.dockerignore` excludes.
  - `stems` reaches the shell only through `env` and `jq --arg`. It is never interpolated into the script.
  - `dist_runner_memory.sh` already runs on hosted runners. Its prepare and cleanup passed on the `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` legs of Cross-Platform Build [run 39001999557](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557).
  - Not verified: whether 8 GiB of swap is enough for the arm64 link inside BuildKit, the runner's disk headroom with the swap file in place, and the serial build time. The dry run answers all three.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 517acede09 (tree 910a5b96fb); checks above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The workflow itself hasn't run, because the dry run needs this branch pushed first. It is the next step, and its run and numbers will be added here.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Job permissions are unchanged. The swap file is created under `RUNNER_TEMP` with `sudo` on the hosted runner, by the script the release workflow already uses.
- New external network calls? Yes, to the existing origin. Each arm64 leg runs one `git fetch` of this workflow's own commit from the same GitHub remote and with the same read token the checkout already uses. The helper it fetches comes from the same commit as the workflow file itself, so it is trusted exactly as much as the workflow.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. A dry run still logs in to GHCR with the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, as before. It doesn't push.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: See the network-call answer. The fetch adds no new host, no new credential and no new code source.

**Please read the push and tag gating closely.**

- Pushing and cosign signing happen only when `inputs.push || github.event_name == 'push'` is true. The expression appears on both build steps (`push:`), both signing steps (`if:`) and both scan jobs, and the concurrency group uses the same expression to choose its queue.
- The floating tags (`<stem>`, relay `latest`) are added only when `inputs.floating || github.event_name == 'push'` is true.
- The release path keeps publishing and moving floating tags, because `workflow_call` defaults both `push` and `floating` to true.
- The tag-push path keeps both through the `push` event check.
- A dispatch with `push` set publishes only the pinned tags of the ref it builds. Without `release_ref`, those tag names come from that ref's `docker-tags.toml`; #11943 will restrict this.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the release and tag-push paths: same tags, same push and sign behavior. A manual dispatch no longer publishes, or moves floating tags, by default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Product config, env and CLI are unchanged. The workflow gains four optional dispatch inputs and one optional `workflow_call` input.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Maintainers who dispatch this workflow to publish must now set `push: true`. To move the floating tags, they must also set `floating: true`, and they should do that only when publishing the newest release.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. One workflow file; no state to migrate.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. A dispatch with `push: false` is the dry run, and `floating: false` keeps a published rebuild off the floating tags.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - In a release run, "Publish Docker Variant Matrix" legs show "Sign container image" or `scan` as skipped. Either means `push` resolved to false.
  - After a release, `ghcr.io/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw:dist` has a different digest from the new `dist-vX.Y.Z` (compare with `docker buildx imagetools inspect`). That means `floating` resolved to false on the release path.
  - "Fetch the build memory helper" fails, or "Prepare bounded build memory" fails with "Need 8 GiB for swap plus 8 GiB of build headroom".
  - The arm64 leg still ends with `signal: 9, SIGKILL` or `ResourceExhausted`.
  - The cleanup step prints "Swapfile retained" or "Refusing cleanup".
  - A leg hits the 120-minute timeout.
  - The `matrix` job fails with "Unknown stem" on a release call. That shouldn't be possible, because the release call passes no `stems`.

prs.title: fix(ci): run the crates.io preflight only for a pull request's own version bump
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `scripts/ci/crates_preflight_trigger.sh` decides whether a run needs the crates.io package preflight by comparing the workspace version against a base. For `pull_request` it used `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, which is the pull request's merge base, not current `master`. A branch that forked before `master`'s version bump therefore looked like a version bump itself. Once that version was tagged, the preflight's release guard correctly refused the existing tag, and `CI Required Gate` failed. #11234 hit this after the v0.8.6 tag: `Tag v0.8.6 resolves to c473221313…, but the release was built from 5a92aade76…`, where `5a92aade76` is the pull request's test merge.
  - For `pull_request`, the trigger now compares against the test merge's first parent, which is the base branch as it is now. A pull request that really changes the version still runs the preflight.
- **Scope boundary:** `merge_group`, which already gets the real base, and `push` behaviour are unchanged. The release guard in `scripts/release/resolve_crates_release.sh`, `pub-crates.yml`, the `ci.yml` call line and `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs` are not touched.
- **Blast radius:** CI only: when the `crates.io Package Preflight` job runs on pull requests. About 275 open pull requests currently record a merge base from before the v0.8.6 bump and fail `CI Required Gate` on their next push; after the v0.8.7 bump and tag, nearly all open pull requests would.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11966. Related #10814.

### What this does, simply

Pull requests that bump the version run an extra crates.io packaging check. The check that decides whether a pull request bumps the version compared it against the point where the branch was created. If `master` was bumped after that, every older pull request looked like a version bump, ran the packaging check against a release tag that already exists, and failed. This makes the comparison use `master` as it is now, so only pull requests that change the version themselves run the check. The release-time check itself is unchanged and stays strict.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

### How I tested

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for the trigger. The release-time path does not call this script.
- **Commands run and tail output:** throwaway worktree at `89bd18484b`, comparing `master`'s script with the fixed one:

| Case | `master` script | This change |
|---|---|---|
| Existing test | ok | ok |
| New test: branch forked before a bump, test-merged into the bumped base | fails: `expected run=false, actual run=true tag=v2.0.1` | ok |
| #11234's real test merge (`b350fcec00` into `89bd18484b`, event base `ceb1e11176`) | `run=true`, `tag=v0.8.6` (the reported failure) | `run=false` |
| `merge_group` with the true base | – | `run=false` (path unchanged) |
| A version-only 0.8.6 → 0.8.7 bump test-merged into `89bd18484b` | `run=true`, `tag=v0.8.7` | `run=true`, `tag=v0.8.7` |

```text
tag=v0.8.7

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the v0.8.7 release run is unaffected either way: it passes the tag it is about to create, which does not exist yet. Also that a missing event base still fails loudly, because the existing check runs first.

prs.title: fix(sop): keep a stale run copy from reviving or overwriting a run
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **A finished run's record is final.** On both store backends, two kinds of write to a run with a stored terminal record now fail with `StoreError::TerminalRun`: an active write, and a terminal write that differs from the stored one. A byte-identical terminal retry is still accepted. Before this change, SQLite's active upsert reset `terminal=0`, so one stale write put a completed run back into `load_active_runs`, and the next restore drove it again. The five SQLite run writes now run in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the guard and the write see the same row even when another engine writes through its own connection.
  - **A write must build on what the writer last saw.** Every persist used to be stamped "stored revision + 1", so the revision guard never refused an engine's write, however old its copy was. Each write is now stamped one past the revision this engine last read or wrote for the run. The existing `StaleRevision` / `RevisionConflict` guard then refuses a copy that another writer has moved on.
  - **A stale copy does not move the run forward.** Before starting a transition, the engine checks whether the store holds a newer record of the run. If it does, the engine adopts that record (a terminal record moves to `finished_runs`; an active one replaces the copy) and then:
    - **refuses** a step result or the next deterministic capability with a typed stale-copy error: the result is not recorded, and nothing is executed or dispatched;
    - **refuses** a gate decision unless the adopted record still presents the same gate, in which case the decision goes ahead;
    - **skips** the run in the approval-timeout sweep, without recording a refusal;
    - **decides** a cancel against the stored state;
    - **adopts the stored record** in maintenance retries of a refused terminal write, instead of retrying the same write every tick.

    A cancellation that another engine requested is finished at the driver boundary. If the stored run is still on the step that just ran, that step's result is recorded first. If it is on a later step, the late result is dropped and a `step_result_stale` row records that. Refusals add a `run_copy_stale` event. The persists that hand out a step or park at a gate refuse a stale write the same way, which covers a writer landing between the check and the write. Rollback paths no longer put the stale copy back after the stored record has been adopted.
  - **Two matching writes are not one write.** Each engine now marks the records it writes with a random writer id (a new optional `writer` field). Before this change, two engines that passed the stale check could build the same state from the same revision. Within one second, `now_iso8601()` made their records byte-identical, so the store accepted the second write as a retry, and both engines handed out the next step. Now the store's same-revision check refuses the second write, and that engine adopts the stored record. A retry from the engine that wrote the record still matches.
  - **A cancel that lands after the stale check is finished, not stranded.** At the two driver boundaries (`advance_step` and `advance_headless_deterministic_step`), a write can be refused because another writer moved the run on after the check. That covers the terminal write, the dispatch write and the park write. The engine adopts the stored record. If the record is a cancellation requested through another engine, the boundary finishes it. Otherwise the transition is refused, as at the check. Before this, a remote cancel that landed during a deterministic capability, or between the final step's check and its terminal write, left the run `Running` and claimed until a restart.
  - **Stale-copy refusals are localized.** The refusal text comes from Fluent keys (`cli-sop-run-copy-*`).
  - Together these close #10066 as widened in its status update. A finished run cannot go back to `running`, re-promote from an earlier step, or have its `step_results` replaced. Once a step's output-schema rejection is recorded, no out-of-date copy can promote past it.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Run ownership is unchanged: an agent turn still builds its own engine, and that engine restores daemon-owned runs. That ownership work is tracked with #9841. Such an engine can still write first when its copy is current. What it can no longer do is overwrite or revive a run from an out-of-date copy.
  - Claims, the approval ledger and the deterministic state file are not changed.
  - Not addressed:
    - repairing runs that an older build already revived (see Compatibility);
    - stale copies of runs that retention has already pruned;
    - recording the result of the step that ran when a cancel is finished after a refused write (#11948);
    - the follow-ups listed below.
- **Blast radius:**
  - SOP run persistence on both backends, and every engine path that starts a transition on a held run.
  - Where a stale copy used to return the next action, it now returns an error. Every production caller already stops on an error:
    - `sop_advance` returns it;
    - the headless LLM and deterministic drivers log it and exit;
    - the approval and cancel surfaces report it.
  - A store read failure during the staleness check now refuses the transition instead of proceeding.
  - A refused terminal write keeps today's retained semantics, so a stale copy never releases a claim that another engine holds.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10066. Related #10813. Related #9841.

### What this does, simply

A SOP run's saved record is meant to be the history of what the run did. Several engines can hold a copy of the same run: the daemon's, the one each agent turn builds, one left over from before a config reload, or a CLI command's. Until now, any of them could save its copy over the record, even a copy that was hours out of date.

On #10066, a review run finished all four steps. Then an older copy that still thought it was on step 1 saved over the record. The run went back to "running" and started the review again, and its record claimed only one step had run, holding another step's output.

After this change, a finished run's record cannot be changed. A save is accepted only if it builds on the latest saved version. An engine that finds its copy out of date takes the saved version instead and declines to move the run forward.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The race needs two engines over one store, and the new tests reproduce it deterministically.

### How I tested

- **Commands run and tail output:**

New tests. Unless a row says otherwise, each one runs two engines over one SQLite store.

| Test | Scenario |
|---|---|
| `stale_copy_cannot_reopen_a_terminal_run_in_sqlite` / `_in_memory` | The issue's controlled run: a copy restored at step 1 gets a result after the run completed. `_in_memory` runs the same scenario on the in-memory store. |
| `stale_copy_cannot_promote_past_a_recorded_schema_rejection` | The owner records step 2's schema rejection; a copy that missed it tries to promote 2→3. |
| `late_result_on_a_stale_copy_is_not_rejected_or_retried` | The issue's order: another engine promotes past step 2 first, then the owner's step-2 result arrives. |
| `cancel_requested_through_another_engine_finishes_at_the_driver_boundary` | A cancel lands through another engine while a step is in flight. |
| `stale_deterministic_copy_runs_no_capability_after_a_remote_cancel` | The same, between two deterministic capabilities; counts capability executions. |
| `stale_copy_of_a_finished_run_cannot_resolve_its_old_gate` | An approval reaches a parked copy of a run that has since finished. |
| `approval_timeout_skips_a_gate_another_engine_resolved` | The timeout sweep runs on a gate that the owner already approved. |
| `stale_copy_write_is_refused_by_its_revision` | The revision stamp alone, with no pre-check involved. |
| `stale_copy_is_refused_at_the_dispatch_write` | A writer lands between the pre-check and the write. Uses a store wrapper whose next read lags. |
| `sop::store::tests::terminal_run_is_final` / `sqlite::tests::terminal_run_is_final` | Store only, no engines: all five writes refuse a terminal record. |
| `sqlite::tests::terminal_run_is_final_across_connections` | Store only: two connections to one database file. |
| `remote_cancel_on_a_later_step_is_finished_at_a_stale_driver_boundary` | The other engine advanced and then cancelled the run; the stale driver's late result is not recorded. |
| `cancel_through_a_stale_engine_is_decided_against_the_stored_run` | A cancel through an out-of-date copy of a run that was approved elsewhere. |
| `decision_on_a_stale_copy_of_the_same_gate_goes_ahead` | The parked run was re-saved without changing its gate; the approval goes ahead and nothing is recorded as a refusal. |
| `stale_copy_is_refused_at_the_park_write` | A writer lands between the pre-check and a park write. |
| `maintenance_adopts_a_cancellation_another_engine_finished` | A cancellation this engine failed to finish was finished by another engine. |
| `maintenance_finishes_a_remote_cancel_instead_of_a_stale_budget_failure` | A step-budget failure is pending, and another engine requests a cancel. |
| `gate_resumed_step_records_schema_rejection_before_any_promotion` | Single engine: guards the approval-resume path the issue names. |

`cooldown_is_shared_across_engine_instances` used to re-finish an already-terminal run to age its completion time. That is now refused, so the test writes the aged completion as the run's only terminal write.

The new tests only use APIs that exist on `master`, so they also build against it.

**Before the fix**, on `master` `96da19523e` with only the new tests applied: 17 failed and 4 passed. The 4 that pass are tests already correct on `master`: the single-engine guard, the same-gate decision, the cancellation finished by another engine, and the rewritten cooldown test.

```text
  test sop::store::tests::terminal_run_is_final ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::cooldown_is_shared_across_engine_instances ... ok
  test sop::engine::tests::gate_resumed_step_records_schema_rejection_before_any_promotion ... ok
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_cannot_reopen_a_terminal_run_in_memory ... FAILED
  test sop::store::sqlite::tests::terminal_run_is_final ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::cancel_requested_through_another_engine_finishes_at_the_driver_boundary ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::decision_on_a_stale_copy_of_the_same_gate_goes_ahead ... ok
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_deterministic_copy_runs_no_capability_after_a_remote_cancel ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_cannot_promote_past_a_recorded_schema_rejection ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_is_refused_at_the_dispatch_write ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_write_is_refused_by_its_revision ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::cancel_through_a_stale_engine_is_decided_against_the_stored_run ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::remote_cancel_on_a_later_step_is_finished_at_a_stale_driver_boundary ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_is_refused_at_the_park_write ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_of_a_finished_run_cannot_resolve_its_old_gate ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::late_result_on_a_stale_copy_is_not_rejected_or_retried ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::approval_timeout_skips_a_gate_another_engine_resolved ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::maintenance_finishes_a_remote_cancel_instead_of_a_stale_budget_failure ... FAILED
  test sop::engine::tests::maintenance_adopts_a_cancellation_another_engine_finished ... ok
  test sop::engine::tests::stale_copy_cannot_reopen_a_terminal_run_in_sqlite ... FAILED
  test sop::store::sqlite::tests::terminal_run_is_final_across_connections ... FAILED
  test result: FAILED. 4 passed; 17 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5800 filtered out; finished in 0.04s
```

Each failure is on its behavioural assertion. On `master`:
- a stale copy hands out `ExecuteStep` for step 2 or step 3;
- a cancel through a stale engine cancels a run that is running elsewhere (`Some(Cancelled)` where `Requested` is expected);
- a stale step-budget retry overwrites a remote cancel with `Failed`;
- the timeout sweep cancels a gate that was already approved;
- a stale deterministic copy runs a second capability (2 calls where 1 is expected);
- an approval that reaches a stale parked copy of a finished run is accepted and deferred (`Resolved(DeferredAtCapacity)`) instead of refused.

**With the fix:**

```text
# the 21 tests above
test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5800 filtered out
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo test -p zeroclaw --bins
test result: ok. 543 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop::
test result: ok. 715 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5105 filtered out
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: FAILED. 5811 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The full `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw --bins` runs are from the first commit. The second commit only touches `sop/engine.rs`, and on it I re-ran the targeted tests, the `sop::` module, fmt, clippy and the layer checks. Before that commit, its two new assertions fail on the first commit: `remote_cancel_on_a_later_step_is_finished_at_a_stale_driver_boundary` (no `step_result_stale` row) and `approval_timeout_skips_a_gate_another_engine_resolved` (a `run_copy_stale` row from the sweep).

The runtime lib failures are all timing-sensitive tests outside the SOP code, and the set changes from one full run to the next:
- `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget` waits on a detached task for a fixed number of yields. It also failed in the one full run on `master` (`5792 passed; 1 failed`), and it passes alone on both `master` and this branch.
- `rpc::dispatch::tests::session_prompt_waits_for_queued_provider_update_transaction` and `config_set_for_other_agent_does_not_wait_on_busy_session` use 25 ms to 1 s wall-clock timeouts.
- The two `rpc::local::tests::*replacement_generation_waits_for_durable_session_prompt_local` tests failed with a refused local connection in one full run.

Across three full runs on this branch, the peer-turn test failed in all three. Each `rpc::` test failed in only one of the three runs. All of them pass when run alone on this branch, and none of them touches `sop/`.

**Each layer removed on its own.** The tests above were run with one layer of the fix disabled at a time, on this PR's head. The unmodified head passes all 21 first. These are the tests that fail when each layer is removed:

| Layer removed | Failing tests |
|---|---|

### Changes after the first review (head a42c300155)

| Test | Scenario |
